Title EN: Fostering cinematic excellence: empowering palestinian film industry and global collaboration
Goal: Achieve A Balanced Flow Of Cultural Goods And Services And Increase The Mobility Of Artists And Cultural Professionals
SDG: SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 10 - Reduce inequality within and among countries,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Flow of cultural goods and services,Mobility of artists and cultural professionals
Agency Implementation: Ministry of culture, ministry of foreign affairs, ministry of higher education
Main Feature: The policy aims to actively engage and collaborate with civil society organizations and film festivals within palestine. this includes providing resources, expertise, and support to foster a vibrant film culture and encourage participation in local and international film events. official recommendations and selections: the policy establishes a transparent and inclusive process for making official recommendations and selections for palestinian films. this ensures that deserving films receive recognition, exposure, and opportunities for further development and distribution. film grants: the policy introduces film grants to provide financial support to emerging and established filmmakers in palestine. these grants serve as an investment in talent, creativity, and the growth of the local film industry. they enable filmmakers to bring their visions to life, pushing the boundaries of storytelling and promoting diversity in palestinian cinema. networking and communication: the policy emphasizes the importance of networking and communication within the film industry. it facilitates connections and collaborations between palestinian filmmakers, producers, distributors, and international partners. this encourages knowledge sharing, exchange of ideas, and the establishment of valuable professional relationships that can drive the growth and global recognition of palestinian films. by implementing these key features, the policy strives to foster cinematic excellence, empower the palestinian film industry, and facilitate global collaboration. it aims to elevate palestinian films on the international stage, strengthen the local film ecosystem, and provide filmmakers with the necessary resources and support to thrive.
Results: Results achieved through the implementation of the policy: the implementation of the policy has yielded significant results, showcasing the growing success and recognition of palestinian films on the international stage: cairo international film festival (november 2022): the palestinian film "alam" directed by firas khoury received three prestigious awards, including best feature film, best actor, and audience award. this recognition highlights the talent and artistic excellence of palestinian filmmakers and their ability to captivate audiences worldwide. additionally, the film's selection for the cannes film festival's "l'atelier" program further solidifies its recognition by international film professionals. cannes film festival (may 2022): maha al haj's screenplay for "mediterranean fever" earned the best screenplay award in the "un certain regard" section. this accomplishment not only demonstrates the artistic daringness of palestinian cinema but also positions the film as palestine's submission for the 2023 oscars. with three awards and eight nominations across various festivals, "mediterranean fever" has garnered critical acclaim and further establishes palestinian filmmakers as masters of storytelling. "al garib" directed by ameer fakher eldin, palestine's submission for the 2022 oscars, has accumulated two awards and three nominations. the film received recognition at the asia pacific screen awards for best cinematography and was also honored with the edipo re award for social inclusion at the venice international film festival. its selection as the closing film at the arab film festival and recognition for best debut feature in san francisco exemplify the growing international acclaim for palestinian cinema. palestinian delegation and official participation at the clermont-ferrand international short film festival in france (february 2023) demonstrate the increased visibility and representation of palestinian filmmakers in prominent global film events. this participation opens doors for networking, collaboration, and exposure to international film professionals. the successful organization of the 9th edition of palestine cinema days 2022, featuring 58 films and attracting an audience of 3500, highlights the growing interest and engagement with palestinian cinema. this event, organized by film lab: palestine, serves as a platform for showcasing local talent and fostering cultural exchange. the red carpet human rights film festival - gaza, now in its 6th edition, has become a significant cultural event with 45 films presented and an audience of 2500. this festival, held in cooperation with the karama film festival in jordan, serves as a vital platform for promoting human rights through the medium of film, amplifying the voices of palestinian filmmakers and shedding light on important social issues. these remarkable achievements underscore the effectiveness of the policy in empowering the palestinian film industry, promoting global collaboration, and garnering international recognition for palestinian films.
Recommandations: The creation of a supportive environment for the creative sector necessitates concerted efforts across three key levels: policy interventions, a legislative foundation, and the establishment of an institutional structure. policy interventions: it is crucial to develop comprehensive policies that recognize and prioritize the needs of the creative sector. these policies should include measures to support artists, filmmakers, writers, and other creative professionals through funding programs, grants, and access to resources. additionally, policies should focus on promoting cultural diversity, fostering artistic freedom, and facilitating collaboration and networking opportunities within the creative community. legislative foundation: a strong legislative framework is essential to protect the rights and interests of creative individuals and organizations. this includes enacting copyright laws that safeguard intellectual property, ensuring fair compensation for creative works, and addressing issues related to licensing, distribution, and piracy. establishing clear regulations and mechanisms for resolving disputes can provide a secure foundation for the creative sector to flourish. institutional structure: the establishment of a robust institutional structure is vital to coordinate and oversee the development of the creative sector. this may involve setting up dedicated governmental bodies or agencies responsible for implementing and monitoring policies, providing support services, and facilitating collaborations between artists, cultural organizations, and relevant stakeholders. such institutions can also play a role in promoting the creative sector at national and international levels, facilitating partnerships and exchanges. by working simultaneously on these three levels—policy interventions, legislative foundation, and institutional structure—it is possible to create an enabling environment that nurtures the creative sector, encourages innovation, and fosters the growth and sustainability of creative industries. these efforts will contribute to the overall cultural and economic development of the country, while empowering artists and creative professionals to thrive and contribute to society.

Title EN: Introduction of a system of multifunctional cultural service centers
Goal: Integrate Culture In Sustainable Development Frameworks
SDG: SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: National sustainable development policies and plans
Agency Implementation: Ministry of culture and information policy of ukraine
Main Feature: The introduction of the system of cultural service centers is driven by the demand of territorial communities in ukraine to create multifunctional cultural institutions that will replace the extensive soviet network of cultural institutions and outdated cultural infrastructure that is unable to meet the needs and demands of the population for cultural services, is inefficient and expensive to maintain. the center for cultural services is: - modern architecture and interior design; - polite and qualified staff; - barrier-free space and services; - convenient location and opening hours; - multifunctional environment; - services that can be easily adjusted to meet the needs of residents.
Results: The legal basis for the establishment and operation of multifunctional cultural institutions - cultural service centers in territorial communities - was formed by introducing appropriate amendments to the law of ukraine "on culture" and the budget code of ukraine. at the initiative of the ministry of culture and information policy of ukraine and with the financial support of the swiss agency for development and cooperation (sdc), the project "cultural service centers as a community cohesion tool" was implemented in 2021. as a result of the project, a manual "cultural service center in a territorial community" was prepared and published, which explains in detail how to create a cultural service center so that it is effective and consistent with the original policy philosophy.
Financial Ressources: Expenditures from the state budget of ukraine (calculated at the average us dollar exchange rate for the respective year): 2021 - approximately 5.3 thousand us dollars expenditures at the expense of international technical assistance (government of the swiss confederation; project registration card no. 4777, state registration dated 13.07.2021) (calculated at the average us dollar exchange rate for 2021): approximately usd 83 thousand.
Recommandations: The policy is in great demand among territorial communities, which see cultural service centers as an opportunity to optimize the system of providing cultural services to the population, update the list of services provided by cultural institutions, the material and technical base of institutions, and attract more people to cultural practices. however, most territorial communities currently lack the ability to invest in the creation of modern and effective cultural service centers, and employees of ordinary cultural institutions are afraid of losing their jobs if a cultural service center is created. the solution to these problems is seen in financial support for territorial communities to create cultural service centers through the introduction of a subvention from the state budget to local budgets and the attraction of donor funds, as well as in training cultural workers in territorial communities to reorient them to new standards of work to focus on the quality of services and meet the needs of community residents.

Title EN: Music tourism strategy - belize tourism board
Goal: Integrate Culture In Sustainable Development Frameworks
SDG: SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: National sustainable development policies and plans
Agency Implementation: Belize tourism board
Main Feature: The belize tourism board and sound diplomacy, an international music policy consultancy and global expert in developing long-term and self-sufficient music strategies, have partnered to create the first-ever music tourism strategy for belize. this comprehensive strategy aims to assess the value of music and cultural ecosystems, identify growth areas, and establish an actionable plan to deliver measurable economic and social benefits. the primary objectives of this strategy are to equip local authorities and promoting agencies with the necessary tools to engage with music arts and the creative economy effectively. by doing so, they can develop a unified public policy that supports the cultural sector and establishes a strong link between music, culture, and tourism. additionally, the strategy will provide an economic baseline that showcases the value of music to the country, along with a set of benchmarks and case studies to learn from and adapt. it will also include a music tourism marketing framework to position belize as a globally recognized destination for music enthusiasts. the program began in 2023 and will span an 8-month period, during which information gathering will occur through roundtables and interviews. the research team will conduct benchmarking and comparative analyses to ensure a thorough and data-driven approach. as a result, a concise strategic plan will be developed, focusing on maximizing the value of music and music tourism in belize. the plan will revolve around four core frameworks, namely: music tourism development: identifying and promoting music-related attractions and experiences that can attract both domestic and international tourists. music production: enhancing and supporting the local music production industry to create a vibrant and diverse music scene. supporting artists and smes: implementing measures to support local artists, musicians, and small and medium-sized enterprises (smes) in the music sector. fostering live music and festivals: encouraging the organization of live music events and festivals across the country to boost cultural tourism. by adopting this music tourism strategy, belize aims to position itself as a hub for music and cultural experiences, further enriching its tourism offerings and fostering sustainable growth within the creative economy.
Results: The tentative expected completion for the policy is december 2023.

Title EN: National cultural policy of trinidad and tobago (2020 - 2025)

Area of Monitoring: Cultural and creative sectors
Agency Implementation: Ministry of tourism, culture and the arts
Main Feature: In may 2018, the draft national policy on culture and the arts was approved by cabinet for public consultation which were held during the period july to september 2018, and a revised policy was submitted for further interrogation by a cross-section of experts and practitioners in the field of culture. by november 2019, the policy went before cabinet for final approval, where comments were requested and received from ministries with responsibility for education, tourism, planning and development, sport and youth affairs, labour and small enterprise development, and trade and industry. the national cultural policy of trinidad and tobago (ncptt) 2020 – 2025 was approved by way of cabinet minute no. 1297 of july 23, 2020, and seeks to place the artist at the centre of cultural development, services and growth; stimulate cultural innovativeness and leverage all of our cultural products for economic potential and global penetration; and recognise and reward excellence. the overarching goals of the ncptt are to: 1. enhance cultural confidence by enriching the participation of all in cultural development that transforms the social and economic experiences of the nation 2. strengthen identities, national identity and the sense of belonging among all socials groups 3. secure and strengthen the infrastructure for cultural diversity, preservation, participation, exchange and expression 4. support artists, entrepreneurs and industry associations in the production of high quality output 5. establish and sustain an integrated institutional framework to support the cultural sector the ncptt has four (4) sub-sectors thematic areas for development of the cultural sector of trinidad and tobago which are: 1. the culturally confident citizen; 2. the arts; 3. heritage, legacy, and memory and; 4. the cultural and creative industries.

Title EN: National cultural policy of trinidad and tobago (2020 - 2025) – upgrade of cultural and arts facilities
Goal: Integrate Culture In Sustainable Development Frameworks
SDG: SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: National sustainable development policies and plans
Agency Implementation: Ministry of tourism, culture, and the arts
Main Feature: The national cultural policy of trinidad and tobago (2020 - 2025) aims to increase and improve the production and distribution of cultural goods and services. the construction of the desperadoes pan theatre in april 2023 fulfils the main themes of of the national cultural policy (2020 - 2025). at the cost of approximately us$ 2 million, the construction of this venue meets the main themes of the policy, namely: - it enables a more harmonised and strengthened cultural environment as an enabler of cultural growth as it provides a space for work and performance for members of the orchestra. - it promotes the exchange of cultural goods and services through the provision of commercial art/cultural spaces to conduct business thereby having a positive economic spill over effect in the community where it is situated. - it increases the exposure of artists to existing and new audiences thereby developing new hubs for creative activities in the city. - it contributes to the enhancement of cultural infrastructure in key municipalities. - it protects the right of all citizens to freely engage and express themselves culturally through the development of safe and habitable spaces. - it encourages community engagement and builds a platform for community place attachment through the brand recognition of excellence in performance. - it encourages the consumption of local music and is a source of pride and confidence among citizens.
Results: The construction of the facility was completed and handed over in april 2023. plans are underway to launch a music school for young persons in the area as the first project of the organisation. the principals have also sent out proposals for entrepreneurs to occupy the business spaces within the facility. this initiative will serve as a conduit of economic regeneration for the area.

Title EN: Ramallah the city of music
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture,Integrate Culture In Sustainable Development Frameworks
SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Cultural and creative sectors,National sustainable development policies and plans
Agency Implementation: Ramallah manucipality
Main Feature: Introducing the comprehensive music industry development policy in ramallah the ramallah municipality presents a visionary project aimed at mapping the music industry and formulating a strategic plan for its growth and development. this initiative recognizes the importance of identifying skills gaps within the sector and takes proactive measures to address them. one of the key objectives is to design and implement a specialized educational program that empowers ramallah artists and enhances their mobility within the industry. from 2017 to 2019, ramallah conducted an extensive analysis of available resources and identified the needs of the local music industry. through consultations with professionals, this groundwork led to the application for the unesco creative cities network, which further propelled the city's commitment to fostering a thriving music scene. an action plan was subsequently developed in collaboration with the ramallah music sector, outlining strategic steps to be undertaken from 2020 to 2024. the policy encompasses several main features, including: integrated cultural policy: ramallah aims to establish a comprehensive cultural policy that provides practical guidelines and resources for both government and non-governmental institutions operating in the city. this approach encourages the application of a cultural lens to their programs and projects, ensuring that culture remains a central aspect of their endeavors. culture integration in education: beginning with musical education, ramallah seeks to integrate culture into the educational curriculum. this progressive approach will later extend to other areas of culture, fostering an appreciation for the arts among students and nurturing their creative potential. creative-hub: a dedicated creative-hub will be established as a vibrant center for creativity and artistic expression, catering to residents and visitors alike. this space will facilitate intergenerational exchange through master classes conducted by esteemed palestinian artists from older generations, ensuring the transfer of knowledge and experiences. additionally, the policy comprises a range of specific activities, including: the jasmine festival: an annual festival celebrating classical, jazz, and world music. palestine sacred music festival: a festival highlighting the rich heritage of sacred music in palestine. palestine international festival for music and dance: a platform that transcends cultural barriers, fostering communication and connection with the outside world. wein a ramallah: an annual street festival that brings the community together through music and cultural performances. the palestine music expo: an annual showcase featuring educational programs, promoting palestinian music to a broader audience. pop-oriental music collaboration: a collaboration between mannheim's oriental music academy and the edward said conservatory, promoting cultural exchange and artistic collaboration. the virtual music archive: an online repository preserving the oral history of music, capturing the diverse musical traditions and narratives of ramallah. this forward-thinking policy endeavors to transform ramallah into a thriving music hub, empowering local artists, fostering cultural exchange, and ensuring the preservation and promotion of the city's rich musical heritage.
Results: The implementation of the music industry development policy in ramallah has yielded significant results. here are the achievements so far: mapping ramallah's music industry: the project successfully mapped the city's music industry, providing valuable insights that have contributed to more informed policymaking. this comprehensive understanding of the local music sector has raised awareness and fostered a deeper appreciation for its cultural and economic significance. evidence-based strategy and action plan: through meticulous research and analysis, ramallah has developed an evidence-based strategy accompanied by a comprehensive action plan. this strategy serves as a blueprint for the city's music development, outlining targeted initiatives and interventions to nurture a thriving music ecosystem in ramallah. "ramallah city of music" online platform: an online platform titled "ramallah city of music" has been created to promote and showcase the action plan of the music development strategy. this platform serves as a source of inspiration for other cities aspiring to harness the power of music in their own communities, fostering knowledge sharing and best practices exchange. skills identification study: a study was conducted to identify the specific skills required by artists and music industry professionals to participate in events and opportunities beyond the city's borders. this study helps artists better prepare themselves for external engagements, opening up avenues for collaboration and exposure beyond ramallah. recommendations for artist mobility: based on the findings of the skills identification study, a report was produced containing insightful recommendations to improve the mobility of artists. these recommendations aim to enhance artists' ability to participate in events, performances, and collaborations outside of ramallah, ultimately expanding their reach and impact on a broader scale. these achievements highlight the successful implementation of the music industry development policy in ramallah. by mapping the music sector, creating an evidence-based strategy, establishing an online platform, and facilitating artist mobility, ramallah has taken significant strides towards positioning itself as a vibrant city of music, contributing to cultural enrichment, economic growth, and cross-cultural exchange.

Title EN: Research on leisure time and cultural needs of urban youth in ukraine
Goal: Integrate Culture In Sustainable Development Frameworks
SDG: SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: National sustainable development policies and plans
Cultural Domain: Performing Arts,Visual Arts,Music,Publishing,Design,Cinema and Audiovisual Arts,Media Arts
Agency Implementation: Ngo cedos - centre for society research
Main Feature: In this study, cedos focused on the leisure and cultural needs of young people who live in kherson, ivano-frankivsk and khmelnytsky and work in the service sector, in information technology, and in culture and creativity. the focus group discussions also involved students in departments adjacent to these occupation spheres. in addition, cedos focused on the priorities and processes of development of these cities’ cultural and youth policies, and cedos described some features of the work of public and communal culture institutions. the study consisted of two parts: the desk stage, which involved an overview of regulatory documents that shape the cultural policies of the selected cities, an analysis of qualitative data from kantar ukraine, and a literature review; and the field stage, which involved using qualitative research methods and conducting focus group discussions and in-depth interviews. the field stage of the study took place in july-september 2020. during this part, cedos conducted 18 focus group discussions with young people from khmelnytsky, ivano-frankivsk, kherson. for each of the cities, cedos conducted 6 online focus group discussions with young people aged 18-35 who work in the service sector, information technology, and culture and creativity. cedos also conducted and analyzed 30 in-depth semi-structured interviews with representatives of government agencies, culture institutions and ngos that work in the field of culture, as well as ngos that work with vulnerable youth groups.
Results: Young people do not often associate leisure and rest with cultural events and institutions. focus group participants described rest as space for recuperation and restoring one’s mental health. they also mentioned that rest for them was an opportunity not to work and not to think about work. some young people who work in the service sector mentioned that rest for them meant satisfying their basic needs, such as sleep. young people who work in the sphere of it, for instance, noted that sometimes their work and rest were not that different from each other. in addition, young people barely distinguished between the concepts of “rest” and “leisure.” however, some said that rest was associated with recuperation and usually took place in a private space. on the other hand, young people associated leisure with public spaces in cities, and with cultural institutions. one of the factors that affect young people’s leisure is their sphere and type of employment and their labor conditions. the amount of free time which can be used for leisure depends on the length of the workday or the flexibility of hours, as well as on other labor conditions. for instance, people who worked remotely or were freelancers said that they often spent their leisure time at home because they could receive a new work task at any moment. the gender characteristics of young people’s leisure and free time. young men and women have different amounts of free time. for instance, women additionally engage in reproductive labor: domestic chores, childcare. they are more likely than men to associate leisure with time free not only of work, but also of domestic chores. the quantitative data analysis has demonstrated a significant difference between men and women in the ways they spend their free time. 78% of young women take care of their residence after work. at the same time, only 38% of young men perform similar duties. occupation, the amount of free time, income levels, having children, being involved in the city’s cultural life generally affect young people’s needs and requests in terms of leisure. young people of different occupations in all cities expressed the need for alternative culture. by this, they usually meant events or spaces whose thematic content or format would be different from the available public and communal institutions. sometimes by “alternative culture,” young people meant institutions’ openness to collaboration and opportunities to initiate and organize their own events.

Title EN: State support for ukrainian creative products on a competitive basis
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture
SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Cultural and creative sectors
Cultural Domain: Performing Arts,Visual Arts,Music,Publishing,Design,Cinema and Audiovisual Arts,Media Arts
Agency Implementation: Ministry of culture and information policy of ukraine, ukrainian cultural foundation, ukrainian book institute
Main Feature: One of the most prominent governmental arm-length institutions is the ukrainian cultural foundation. it is a state institution established in 2017 according to the law of ukraine “on the ukrainian cultural foundation”. the ucf is subordinated to the ministry of culture and information policy of ukraine. the ucf provides support to artists, cultural actors and cultural projects by distributing grants on a competitive basis in such sectors as: - visual arts, - performing arts, - cultural heritage, - design and fashion, - music sector, - audio-visual arts, - literature and publishing, - cultural and creative industries, etc. grant applications are submitted once a year. for most support programmes, the grant cycle begins in autumn. calls for proposals are open to ukrainian artists and to legal entities of all forms registered in ukraine. non-ukrainian artists, institutions, cultural organisations and ngos may apply as partners together with a ukrainian applicant. all applications undergo technical and expert selection. during the covid-19 pandemic, in 2020, the ukrainian cultural foundation launched an institutional support programme that covered payrolls, rent expenses, utilities and other expenses of the creative businesses that lost their income because of the pandemic. overall, during the four grant seasons of 2018-2021, the ucf received 10120 applications for grants, of which 2475 grants were awarded, totalling uah 2 billion 83 thousand. uсf has several grant programmes aimed at supporting: ● audio-visual art and cinema development (audio-visual art), ● a barrier-free society and artists with disabilities (inclusive art), ● creative industries and performing art (innovative cultural product), ● promotion of cultural studies, artistic mobility and exchange of artistic practices (training. exchanges. residencies. debuts), ● support of regional cultural initiatives and creation of local cultural hubs (culture. tourism. regions), ● support of significant cultural events (significant events), ● support of projects aimed at the preservation and promotion of cultural heritage (cultural heritage). the largest grant programme of the ucf is innovative cultural product. it covers almost all the sectors of ukrainian culture and is aimed at unleashing the potential and boosting the competitiveness of cultural and creative industries. under this programme, 268 creative projects were implemented during 2019-2021. programme training. exchanges. residencies. debuts. (short nord from ukrainian) aims to promote the exchange of knowledge, experience and ideas in the field of culture and arts, as well as open new artistic practices and ideas. in 2019-2021, 159 projects were supported as part of this programme. the main tools for cooperation and fundraising are: ● business angels club within the ucf, which promotes the involvement of sponsors, patrons, and investors in the ukrainian cultural space; ● cultural charity is a partnership programme aimed at attracting philanthropists and patrons to promote charity in the field of culture; ● creative accelerator is a comprehensive programme that provides training on business skills in creative industries so that the projects supported by the ucf remain sustainable; ● cultural business hub is a platform for communication and networking of businesses, cultural organisations and authorities to share experience, expertise, and study cases and find partners. in 2021, the european business association joined the project; ● the refuelling initiative increases the international visibility of ukrainian art residencies. it informs the international community about the opportunities available to various artists in ukraine, maintains professional standards of art programmes and attracts foreign artists, curators and art managers to ukrainian residences. expanding the geography of projects in 2021, the foundation supported projects from all regions of ukraine. as for the international projects, in 2021 the partners were from germany — 19 projects, the uk — 13, poland — 5 projects, france — 3, armenia — 1, georgia — 1, the netherlands — 1, spain — 1, sweden — 1. along with the state financial support for implementing cultural projects, ucf engages international partners. the british council, us agency for international development (usaid), international renaissance foundation, evz foundation, zagoriy foundation, netherlands embassy and other institutions actively participated in supporting the ucf grant programs. thus, ucf implemented the culture for changes programme in 2020-2021. this is an international cooperation programme aimed at supporting cultural dialogue and creating joint artistic projects. 9 international projects were implemented in 2020 (ukrainian-german cultural initiatives), 28 — in 2021 (ukrainian-german, ukrainian-british initiatives). moreover, to support ukrainian culture abroad, the ukrainian diaspora was given an opportunity to participate in a grant competition. in 2021, grant applications were submitted from sweden, germany, thailand, and finland. the ucf is a member of international networks, namely the international federation of arts councils and culture agencies (ifacca), european network of cultural centres (encc), culture action europe, international network for cultural mobility on the move, european network on cultural management and policy (encatc), etc. the foundation presents its opportunities and activity at international meetings, accelerators, events, etc. expansion of international relations and fundraising activities is one of ucf's priorities. there are also special support programmes in the field of literary creation and translation implemented by the ukrainian book institute (ubi). the ubi was established in 2016 in accordance with the law of ukraine "on amendments to certain laws of ukraine on improving the system of public administration in the book publishing sphere". the purpose of the ubi is to support book publishing, promote reading, encourage translation activities and promote ukrainian literature all over the world. the ukrainian book institute achieves these aims through several programmes. the libraries replenishment programme has been implemented by the ubi every year since 2018. the ministry of culture and information policy of ukraine and the ubi publicly announce the selection of books to be purchased and transferred to the libraries. the books are selected on a 177 competitive basis by an expert council formed by the ubi. after the selection procedure, the council drafts the list of books recommended for purchase to replenish ukrainian libraries. the draft list of recommended books is finally approved by the ministry of culture and information policy of ukraine. since 2020, the ubi has been implementing the translate ukraine programme. it partially reimburses the costs of publishing ukrainian literature in foreign languages, namely the acquisition of rights to translate a ukrainian book into another language and the payment of royalties as well as the reimbursement of translation services. the maximum amount of reimbursement for each project is equal to eur 4 000. the projects are selected on a competitive basis and are evaluated by the translation expert council established by the ubi. as part of the programme, in 2020, the ubi supported 53 translations of works of ukrainian authors into 21 languages (english, german, italian, french, slovak, polish, arabic, hebrew, mongolian, macedonian and others) in 24 countries. in 2021, the programme supported 71 translations into 23 foreign languages in 27 countries. there are also several prize programmes in the field of literature that are awarded annually in ukraine: ● oles honchar prize for the best literary works that affirm the ideals of humanism, the spiritual values of the ukrainian people, and the idea of independence of ukraine; ● sholem aleichem prize for the best literary and artistic works that promote the spiritual and cultural heritage of the ukrainian and jewish peoples; ● mykola gogol prize for the best literary and artistic works; ● taras shevchenko national prize of ukraine (in the category of literature) for the most outstanding works of literature, which are the supreme spiritual heritage of the ukrainian people, and affirm high humanistic ideals, enrich the historical memory of the nation, its national consciousness and identity, and are aimed at state formation and democratisation of ukrainian society.
Results: The ukrainian cultural foundation’s activities have significantly changed the ukrainian creative economy. in particular, the cultural market was replenished with new players with competitive ideas. ucf created a market niche for new professionals such as cultural managers and experts in creative industries. over four years of the foundation's activities, uah 1 billion 328 million 940 thousand were directed to the cultural sphere, which, in turn, created additional value-added, increased income and employment of cultural representatives, which through supply chains affected the government's tax revenues. moreover, the wider impact of the foundation lies within the creation of new meanings, dissemination of new ideas, knowledge, concepts and skills, which contributes to the competitive national cultural product, innovation, technological progress and, cultural growth and quality of life. for example, in 2021, 4513 people were involved in ucf-funded project teams. the gender composition of the teams is 43% (men) and 57% (women). 12% of the projects had people with disabilities among their team members, 24% of the projects had veterans, 26% — internally displaced persons, 50% — volunteers. 57% of teams chose for their public events a venue accessible to people with disabilities; 31% of teams organised their projects (public events) online; 42% of the teams involved people from different age groups while implementing the project; 54% of teams see the possibility of commercialising their project. the top project outputs for the period 2018-2021 were scripts — 58, printed editions — 54, festivals — 51. the state cultural institutions supported a wide range of cultural projects representing different regions, ethnicities, and cultural traditions of ukraine. this has helped to promote and preserve the cultural diversity of ukraine, as well as encourage intercultural dialogue and understanding.  moreover, they have been instrumental in promoting cultural management standards and best practices in ukraine. through their grant programmes and other initiatives, the ucf and ubi have supported the professional development of cultural managers and artists and encouraged them to adopt best practices in project planning, financial management, and audience engagement. the ucf has also helped to establish partnerships between cultural organisations in ukraine and abroad, providing opportunities for knowledge exchange and capacity building. finally, the institutions immensely supported the development of ukraine's independent cultural sector. by providing funding and other resources to independent cultural organisations and artists, the institutions have helped to create new opportunities for creative expression and cultural innovation in ukraine.

Title EN: Strengthening interinstitutional and intersectoral cooperation in creative industries
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture,Integrate Culture In Sustainable Development Frameworks
SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Partnering with civil society,Cultural and creative sectors
Cultural Domain: Performing Arts,Visual Arts,Music,Publishing,Design,Cinema and Audiovisual Arts,Media Arts
Agency Implementation: Ministry of culture and information policy of ukraine
Main Feature: Creative industries deal with a range of complex issues, such as intellectual property, education, access to finance, etc., that require close work with adjacent sectors, public bodies and non-governmental actors. therefore, the ministry of culture and information policy of ukraine came up with several measures to bridge the gap between various stakeholders in the policy-making and implementation process. one of the measures is the annual international creative ukraine forum. it is the largest platform in eastern europe aimed at discussing public policy in creative industries. every year, the event brings together several dozen speakers from upwards of 10 countries. politicians, creative entrepreneurs, international economic and cultural experts, and government representatives work closely to determine the most effective ways of forging an economy based on innovation, talent, and creativity. each year, the event focuses on central topics such as baukultur, digitalisation, the pandemic as a new normal, creative industries' retooling, etc. the forum has been held since 2017. in 2021, it was organised for the fifth time in a row. in 2021, the cabinet of ministers of ukraine launched the creative economy council (resolution of the cabinet of ministers of ukraine no. 501 dated may 19, 2021). it is an advisory body of the government for establishing a direct dialogue between the government and businesses on the development of creative industries, both at national and regional levels. since 2021, the council has started sectoral working groups (on design, art crafts, concert and music industry) that unite representatives of the respective creative sectors. groups' members discuss creative industries' problems and needs on a regular basis, prepare proposals for governmental policies and policy documents and organise information campaigns and creative education training sessions.
Results: Each year more than 600 participants and 100 speakers from 15+ countries attend the creative ukraine forum. over the years, almost 200 workshops on particular creative sectors, such as the film industry, design, fashion, marketing, concert and music industry, art crafts, etc., took place as part of the event. the forum also laid the foundation for numerous partnerships and cross-sectoral initiatives in creative industries, involved high-level politicians (ukrainian president, prime-ministers, vice-prime-ministers, ministers, etc.) and attracted attention to the creative industries issues in ukraine. the establishment of the creative economy council by the cabinet of ministers of ukraine is a positive step towards promoting the growth and development of the creative industries in the country. the council's sectoral working groups help identify specific challenges and opportunities within each sector and develop targeted policies to address them. by facilitating direct dialogue between the government and the business community, the council can help ensure that policies and initiatives are aligned with the needs and priorities of the creative industries.
Recommandations: In the long-term, to ensure the sustainable development of creative industries and provide better cross-sectoral and interinstitutional cooperation, the ministry of culture and information policy of ukraine intends to establish a state institution targeted specifically for the creative businesses support — the national creative industries office. the idea behind it is that creative industries are a sector that fits neither in the cultural policy (since creative businesses aim to profit) nor in the economic one (common economic measures for smes do not work for creative industries since they lack tangible assets and trust of banks and investors). therefore, it is envisioned that the national creative industries office will provide a set of targeted programmes tailored to the specificity of the creative sector. among them, there are: •	reimbursement of rent expenses for ukrainian fashion, design and crafts brands in the malls and shopping centres; •	support for ukrainian stands and booths taking part in the international exhibitions as well as fashion and design fairs – export promotion; •	support in establishing new business supply and marketing chains (trade missions, b2b meetings and platforms); •	stipends for young manufacturing workers in creative industries (tailors, cutters, furniture makers, etc.); •	launch of the creative backpack programme when the state funds the trips of school students and their acquaintance with contemporary creative professions and practices; •	grant support for r&d, new technology and innovation in creative industries, high-tech; •	grants/subsidies for capital expenditure: 	funds for the purchase of equipment and raw materials; funds for establishing local supply chains for raw materials, especially fabrics and paper; 	cross-sectoral programmes that integrate ukrainian ci in the reconstruction projects (industrial design, architecture, landscape design, urban planning, etc.). moreover, the national creative industries office will be designed to provide immediate support for creative businesses restarting their activities after the war (compensation of rent rates, utilities, and payrolls for a certain period of time: 3-6 months). creating the legal prerequisites for the establishment of the national creative industries office are envisioned in ukraine’s government priority actions plan 2022 and ukraine’s legal-drafting plan 2022.

Main Feature: In line with task 1449 "creating legal prerequisites for creative industries development in ukraine" of the action plan on implementation of the association agreement between ukraine and the eu, the ukrainian government and parliament adopted several legal acts to ensure that creative industries are well-established in the political agenda. •	the definition of "creative industries" was introduced by the ukrainian law "on amendments to the law of ukraine "on culture" regarding the definition of "creative industries" (no. 2458-viii dated june 19, 2018). this laid the foundation for further legislative and policy interventions to support the development of creative industries in ukraine. •	the cabinet of ministers of ukraine approved the types of economic activity that belong to creative industries in its order no. 265 dated april 24, 2019, which provided a clear understanding of what sectors fall under the creative industries category. •	the law "on state support for culture, creative industries, tourism, small and medium-sized business due to the measures to prevent the spread of covid-19" was passed in 2020, defining the concept of "creative product." this legislation paved the way for further state support of the creation of creative products. •	presidential decree no. 329/2020 contains measures to support the culture, preservation of cultural heritage, development of creative industries, and tourism, including arts and crafts and creative hubs.
Results: These legal acts have led to the further recognition of creative industries in the government's agenda and the allocation of the state budget to support creative industries. additionally, it has allowed for a unified statistical account of the sector, which is essential for evidence-based policy-making. the government can now take steps to support creative industries by implementing sectoral programs and initiatives that will lead to their sustainable development.
Recommandations: According to the «pulse of the agreement» online monitoring system, task 1449 “creating legal prerequisites for creative industries development in ukraine” of the action plan on implementation of the association agreement between ukraine and the eu was completely fulfilled (100%).
