Title EN: Amendments to the Law 'On Mass Media'
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture
SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Media diversity
Cultural Domain: Design,Performing Arts,Media Arts,Cinema and Audiovisual Arts,Music,Publishing,Visual Arts
Agency Implementation: Ministry of Information of the Republic of Belarus
Main Feature: An extensive network of print and electronic media of various forms of ownership and various orientations operate and develop in the Republic of Belarus. Foreign media are also widely represented in the country's media space (more than 4,000, including periodicals from Russia, Kazakhstan, China etc.). The principle of informational freedom in the Republic of Belarus is enshrined in such constitutional rights as the right to receive, store and disseminate complete, reliable and timely information about the activities of state bodies, public associations, political, economic, cultural and international life, the state of the environment, no monopoly on mass-media and censorship are allowed (Articles 33-34 of the Constitution of the Republic of Belarus). The fundamental normative legal act governing relations in the media sphere is the Law of the Republic of Belarus "On Mass Media", which takes into account the approaches of international legal regulation and experience in the field of mass media.  The Law "On Mass Media" establishes the basic principles of media activity in Belarus: reliability of information, equality, respect for human rights and freedoms, diversity of opinions, protection of morality, compliance with professional ethics. The law became the basis for introducing elements of self-regulation in the media sphere of Belarus - for this purpose, the Public Coordination Council in the Sphere of Mass Media was created, including representatives of the media, journalistic organizations, and the expert community. As of November 1, 2024, the following numbers of mass-media are registered in the country: 909 print media (366 newspapers, 528 magazines, 14 bulletins, 1 catalog), of which 397 are state-owned and 512 are non-state; 7 news agencies: 2 state-owned and 5 non-state-owned; 66 online publications (57 state-owned, 9 non-state-owned); 164 television and radio broadcasting media, of which 88 are state-owned (48 radio programs and 40 television programs) and 76 are non-state-owned (28 radio programs and 48 television programs). Printed publications are published mainly in Belarusian and Russian, however, there are certain publications in other languages. There are periodic specialized publications devoted only to cultural topics: “Kultura” (Culture) and “Litaratura and Mastatstva” (Literature & Arts) newspapers, “Art and Culture” and “Mastastva” (Arts) magazines. The Belarus-3 TV channel and the Culture channel of the Belarusian radio are completely devoted to cultural issues. The Ministry of Information of the Republic of Belarus allocates state subsidies to support certain publications promoting the national culture and publishing in the Belarusian language. For example, “Zvyazda” newspaper; “Maladosts”, “Polymya”, “Nyoman” literary and art magazines, and “Litaratura i Mastatstva” newspaper. They play a significant role in popularizing the best examples of the Belarusian literature. “Kultura” newspaper and “Mastatstva”, “Narodnaya Asveta”, “Belaruski Hystarychny Chasopis” magazines contribute to the methodological support of the scientific and educational process in the country and provide significant assistance to teachers. This list also includes certain newspapers and magazines in Belarusian for adolescents and children: “Byarozka” and “Vyaselka”.  Despite the growing competition in the information market, domestic media still remain the main source of information for Belarusians. The largest national media are Belteleradiocompany, CJSC "Second National TV Channel", CJSC "Stolichnoe Television", publishing house "Belarus Today", publishing house "Zvyazda", Belarusian Telegraph Agency. In the context of changing global information space and dynamic development of technologies, formats, methods of preparation and transmission of information, the media industry of Belarus today is actively moving towards digital transformation. There are 7 news agencies in Belarus, 5 of which are private. The largest news agency in Belarus is the Belarusian Telegraph Agency (BelTA), which has a correspondent network in all regions of the country. In Minsk, along with Belarusian news agencies, there are also correspondent offices of foreign news agencies - TASS, "Russia Today", "Xinhua".  As of January 1, 2024, 89 radio programs and 92 television programs were broadcasting in Belarus. Of these, 28 radio programs and 51 television programs are private. The high share of public radio programs is explained by the fact that most of them are regional radio, with local authorities acting as founders. About 30 radio stations broadcast in the FM range in Belarus, including Radius-FM, Radio Unistar (a Belarusian-German media project), Europe Plus and others. Radio station Belarus, which broadcasts in Belarusian, Russian, English, German, Polish, French, Spanish and Chinese, is designed for foreign audiences interested in events in our country. The first and only international satellite TV channel of Belarus – "Belarus 24" – which began broadcasting in 2005 ("Belarus TV"), today operates 24 hours a day. Its coverage area covers over 100 countries, and the audience is over 200 million people. The content is based on news and analysis of the most important events in the country and the world, interesting TV projects and high-quality film screenings. And, of course, the broadcasting grid includes many programs about Belarus: the unique history and culture of the country, the main attractions and tourist destinations, Belarusian cuisine, famous brands, outstanding people.
Results: 1) a variety of media content is provided; 2) the rights of independent and private media are ensured; 3) there are special media for youth audiences and children, as well as for various sub-cultural groups.
Financial Ressources: The data are not available
Recommandations: The variety of mass media and balance between control and editorial independence contribute to the freedoms of thouth and expression

Title EN: :  Urusaro International Women Film Festival
Goal: Promote Human Rights And Fundamental Freedoms
SDG: SDG 5 - Achieve gender equality and empower all women and girls,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels
Area of Monitoring: Gender equality
Agency Implementation: CinéFEMMES Rwanda
Main Feature: The Urusaro International Women Film Festival, like any successful film festival, can be measured and evaluated through various features to assess its effectiveness and impact. Here are the key features of the measure for the festival:  Attendance and Participation: The festival's success can be measured by the number of attendees, including filmmakers, industry professionals, and general audiences, as well as the diversity and engagement levels of these participants. Film Submissions and Screenings: Evaluating the quantity and quality of film submissions, the variety of genres and cultural backgrounds represented, and audience turnout and reception at screenings provides insight into the festival's reach and impact. Media Coverage and Publicity: The extent and quality of media coverage, social media engagement, and overall publicity efforts are crucial for assessing the festival's visibility and public awareness. Impact on Filmmakers: The festival's influence on the careers of participating filmmakers, including new projects, awards, networking outcomes, and feedback on the support provided, indicates its effectiveness in advancing women's roles in cinema. Workshops and Educational Programs: The number and variety of educational activities, along with participant feedback and their impact on skill development, measure the festival's contribution to filmmaker education and professional growth. Economic Impact: Revenue from ticket sales, sponsorships, and the economic benefits to the local community, including hospitality and tourism, highlight the festival's financial impact. Cultural and Social Impact: The festival's influence on perceptions of women in cinema, contributions to cultural exchange, and engagement with social issues reflect its broader cultural and societal impact. Awards and Recognition: The number and significance of awards given, their impact on recipients, and the festival's recognition in the film community showcase its role in promoting excellence and gaining prestige. Festival Growth and Development: Year-on-year growth in size, scope, and influence, along with innovations, improvements, and strategic partnerships, indicate the festival's development and long-term sustainability.
Results: Since its establishment in 2015, the Urusaro International Women Film Festival has made significant strides in promoting gender equality and supporting women filmmakers. Here are some of its main achievements: Increased Participation and Diversity: The festival has seen a steady increase in the number of film submissions  and attendees from diverse cultural and professional backgrounds,up to date we have received 415 films highlighting its growing international reach and inclusivity from just Africa to America, Asia and beyond. Prominent Platform for Women Filmmakers: Urusaro IWFF has become a significant platform for women filmmakers to showcase their work, gaining recognition and visibility in the global film industry. This has led to career advancements for many participants. Influential Educational Programs: The festival has conducted numerous workshops, seminars, and panel discussions, contributing to the professional development and skill enhancement of emerging women filmmakers. Enhanced Media Coverage: The festival has attracted substantial media coverage, both locally and internationally, raising awareness about gender disparities in cinema and promoting the work of women filmmakers. Successful Networking Opportunities: Urusaro IWFF has facilitated networking and collaboration opportunities for filmmakers, industry professionals, and other stakeholders, fostering partnerships and mentorship relationships. Recognition and Awards: The festival has awarded numerous films and filmmakers, boosting their profiles and helping them secure further opportunities in the industry. as of this year 2024 in June, we have awarded 11 outstanding films in the 8th edition of Urusaro International Women Film Festival Economic and Cultural Impact: The festival has positively impacted the local economy through tourism and related activities. It has also contributed to cultural exchange and understanding by showcasing diverse narratives. Advocacy for Gender Equality: Urusaro has been a vocal advocate for gender equality in the film industry, influencing discussions and policies aimed at supporting women’s participation and leadership in cinema. 8. Responsible agency:  The agency responsible for Urusaro International Women Film Festival is CinéFEMMES Rwanda ( www.cinefemmesrwanda.org  ) a non government organization created to empower women, youth and marginalised communities through the profession of cinema industry.

Title EN: ‘’ Do Your’S’’
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture
SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Cultural and creative sectors
Cultural Domain: Design,Performing Arts,Media Arts,Cinema and Audiovisual Arts,Music,Publishing,Visual Arts
Agency Implementation: Ministère de la jeunesse et des Sports
Main Feature: La stratégie du secteur notamment dans son volet jeunesse est fondée d’une part, sur la perspective de mettre en mouvement une dynamique de mobilisation de notre jeunesse pour sa pleine participation à l’élaboration d’une politique en mesure de capter et décrypter ses différentes demandes (demande politique, économique et sociale, culturelle et loisirs et d’activités et de divertissements et détentes, de tourisme et de mobilité…), et d’autre part,  sur son implication concrète et assumée dans le choix des actions à mettre en œuvre. L’objectif demeurant de donner du sens aux ambitions de notre jeunesse d’être un acteur plein dans la construction de son avenir.   Dans cette perspective, le secteur de la jeunesse et des sports considère que la promotion de la jeunesse à travers les activités qu’il propose est porteuse de développement, d’émancipation et surtout d’autonomisation.   C’est pourquoi des mesures et initiatives sont entreprises pour la redynamisation des activités de jeunesse à travers la diversification de l’offre en adoptant des programmes pédagogiques de loisirs, attractifs et innovants,  intéressant les jeunes dans différents domaines.   La mise en œuvre de ces programmes et activités s’effectue dans les établissements de jeunes encadrés par les professionnels de la jeunesse d’une part , et d’autre part, à travers l’organisation des manifestations de jeunesse,  festivals, concours, salons, expositions, sur les thèmes et slogans définis dans le plan d’action, qui concernera plusieurs activités à savoir,  arts et culture et l’audio-visuel, avec le concours des directions de la jeunesse et des sports des 58 wilayas et le mouvement associatif, permettant ainsi la détection des jeunes talents. Dans ce cadre, les Festivals nationaux de la Jeunesse, en tant que manifestations qui regroupent les jeunes des 58 wilayas dans un climat compétitif, ont pour objectifs la détection des jeunes créateurs dans les différents domaine d’activités. Les festivals sont organisé conformément aux disposition du Décret 85-67 du 06 avril 1985 portant l’organisation des Festivals Nationals de Jeunesse (FNJ), ainsi que l’arrêté Ministériel du31 décembre 2018(MICLAT – MJS) qui fixe les wilayas concernés par l’organisation de ces festivals nationaux , leur natures et leur durée.       Aussi, et en vue de la redynamisation des maisons de jeunes, et pour pallier au manque d’encadrement, le ministère de la jeunesse et des sports a mis en place, en 2020, un programme intitulé ‘’ Do Your’S’’ en direction des associations de jeunesse, pour la gestion totale ou partielle des activités au sein des maisons de jeunes, sur la base de conventions. A cet effet, une nomenclature des activités de jeunes a été élaborée pour le suivi et l’évaluation.  Dans le cadre de la promotion du partenariat avec le mouvement associatif et l’encouragement des initiatives de jeunes, et en adoptant une démarche consensuelle et participative, le ministère de la jeunesse et des sports lance chaque année, un appel à projet, en direction des associations de jeunes se basant sur plusieurs axes entre autre  : loisirs et mobilisation de jeunes, animation culturelles et artistiques  des espaces pédagogiques des établissements de jeunes, renforcement des capacités,  autonomisation de jeunes et entrepreneuriat … . La priorité est donnée aux projets innovants et mis en œuvre dans les maisons de jeunes à l’effet d’avoir plus d’impact dans le but d’atteindre les objectifs assignés notamment celui de la redynamisation des établissements de jeunes
Results: Concernant les activités de jeunesse : - l’année 2020 a connu une crise sanitaire à savoir le COVID 19 qui a touché pratiquement tous les pays du monde dont notre pays. Cette situation n’a pas empêché notre secteur de réaliser certaines opérations à travers des actions virtuelles permettant d’assurer une continuité des activités telles que :  Maison de jeunes virtuelle : -	Participation de 1500-3000 jeunes par activité et par établissement dans le cadre de la sensibilisation pour la lutte contre la Covid 19 au niveau des 58 wilayas, dans le domaines  des expressions culturelles et scientifiques ,audio visuel (film court métrage, affiches, spots publicitaires , …), et d’autres activités  de loisirs (dessins, musique, jeux, comtes, histoire…) .  Concours nationaux virtuels : -	Participation de 369 jeunes dans les domaines des arts dramatiques, audio visuel, littérature, musique, arts plastiques), 25 jeunes primés à raison de 05 lauréats  par domaine d’activité. -	Dans le cadre de partenariat  avec l’Unicef et le mouvement associatif de jeunesse,  405  jeunes ont pris part au concours national sur un spot publicitaire. Les 15 premiers lauréats ont été primés. -   Concours national virtuel sur la création d’un spot publicitaire « ElWabaa la Yahzimouna » (la pandémie ne nous vaincra pas), en partenariat avec l’UNICEF et les Scouts Musulmans, qui a vu la participation de 405 jeunes. Les 15 premiers participants ont été primés.  -  Concours national virtuel de jeunes créateurs، qui a vu la participation de 369 jeunes, 25 jeunes ont été primés à raison de cinq lauréats par domaine d’activité.  - Ainsi que différentes participations virtuelles arabes. Résultants à travers ces activités de programme de rencontres, concours de jeunes pour la détection des jeunes talents dans les différents domaines et créneaux d’activités :  4636 participants dont 212 lauréats. Concernant le partenariat avec le mouvement associatif de la jeunesse : 92 associations de jeunesse ont bénéficié de financement dans le cadre de l’appel à projet au titre de l’année 2020, dont 25 projets sont concernés par les activités culturelles.   l’année 2021 : a connu l’organisation de 27 Festivals nationaux de jeunes : -	Nombre de participants : 3013 jeunes dont 787 filles et 2226 garçons. 124 lauréats dont 47 filles et 77 garçons.  Concernant le partenariat avec le mouvement associatif de la jeunesse : 75 associations de jeunesse   ont bénéficié de financement dans le cadre de l’appel à projet au titre de l’année 2021, dont 17 projets sont concernés par les activités culturelles.   l’année 2022 : l’organisation de 27 Festivals Nationaux de la Jeunesse dans différents domaines : culturel ; scientifique ; littérature ; audiovisuel … . -	Nombre de participants : 3250 jeunes dont 2570 garçons et 680 filles  168 lauréats  Concernant le partenariat avec le mouvement associatif de la jeunesse : 84 associations de jeunesse   ont bénéficié de financement dans le cadre de l’appel à projet au titre de l’année 2022, dont 21 projets sont concernés par les activités culturelles.   Résultats atteints  1-	La redynamisation et la promotion des activités scientifique, technologique, culturelle et artistique en milieu de jeunes 2-	La Diversification de l’offre notamment en matière d’activités culturelles et artistiques 3-	La détection des jeunes talents dans les différents domaines d’activités. 4-	Valorisation des capacités créatives des jeunes et des enfants. 5-	Ayant touché un grand nombre d’enfants et de jeunes dans la mise en œuvre des actions du secteur.
Recommandations: L’importance de la promotion des activités de jeunesse en particulier dans les établissements de jeunes, considérés comme étant des leviers pédagogiques, appelle une diversification des offres de programmes et actions dédiés à la jeunesse, avec la participation du mouvement associatif partenaire du secteur de la jeunesse et des sports ; ainsi qu’un renforcement des capacités de l’encadrement pédagogique afin d’être à la hauteur des attentes des jeunes.  L’organisation des différents festivals et concours nationaux, notamment dans le domaine culturel, est un moyen privilégié de détection des jeunes talents, leur permettant de participer aux événements internationaux de jeunesse. A cet effet, il y a lieu : - De réfléchir en partenariat avec le Ministère de la Culture, sur la mise en place d’un mécanisme d’accompagnement favorisant la promotion des jeunes talents, leur permettant l’accès au professionnalisme.  -	De créer un fichier national numérique des jeunes talents issus des programmes et activités culturelles de la jeunesse. -	De créer un fonds national pour l’encouragement de la créativité des jeunes et la mise en place d’un système de contrôle avec la participation financière de chaque secteur concerné.

Title EN: “ALALAO” INTERNATIONAL WINTER THEATRE FESTIVAL 1995
Goal: Achieve A Balanced Flow Of Cultural Goods And Services And Increase The Mobility Of Artists And Cultural Professionals
SDG: SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 10 - Reduce inequality within and among countries,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Flow of cultural goods and services
Agency Implementation: MAGIA Space for Art and Culture EMAIL: jimmy_americol@hotmail.com PHONE: 73892818  Association of Agents in Art, Culture and Tourism of Oruro EMAIL: jimmy_americol@hotmail.com PHONE 72892818
Main Feature: In 1995 we decided to create this space, taking as a reference the Popular Educators Movement and the Popular Theatre Meeting, avant-garde movements of the “Collective Construction of Thought”, the fundamental basis of our proposal. The ALALAO International Winter Theatre Festival was created with the idea of rescuing the cold of the Bolivian Altiplano as an identifying feature of the event, where magic, colours and the harsh winter would be the reason for the existence of this aesthetic and ethical form that, in this way, inextricably linked its philosophy of existing in the city of Oruro as the headquarters and centre of cultural irradiation that it already was, but which requires constant effort to maintain, value and project it for the benefit of the inhabitants of the Department. With the firm purpose of involving the population in the art of theatre, we carry out many activities in the city centre and in peri-urban areas, getting the inhabitants to participate in a celebration of integration, but also in knowledge, criticism and analysis of the context in which we develop, based on training and formation workshops in the performing arts, the circulation of national casts through municipalities and neighbourhoods, carrying out thematic exhibitions to inform and educate and encouraging local casts to produce derivatives of their works such as audiovisuals, texts, costumes, puppets and others to exhibit at theatre fairs. What was once a five-day project on stage has now become a five- to six-month project in different formats over the course of the seventeen versions already carried out. Such a long-term duration can only mean the commitment and awareness that all serious, responsible and productive work that has real possibilities of impacting society must be developed from all the experience gathered in previous versions of the festival, capable of proposing truly sustainable long-term activities. This cultural event has generated the formation of new casts and the positioning of theater as an element of transformation and citizen regeneration, it has generated a social movement in the demand for the rights of theater artists, promoting the creation of the Oruro Theater Artists Association, the Association of Working Actors in Theater, Film and Creativity and has also strengthened the Oruro cultural movement by creating the Oruro Association of Agents in Art, Culture and Tourism. These are instances that make an impact and show the government and the population that the economic generation of the artistic sector is valuable and that it demands an economic conversion of "SUPPORT" as a government policy towards artists through CULTURAL INVESTMENT.

Title EN: “Re-imagined” Industrial Strategy
Goal: Integrate Culture In Sustainable Development Frameworks
SDG: SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: International cooperation for sustainable development
Cultural Domain: Design,Performing Arts,Media Arts,Cinema and Audiovisual Arts,Music,Publishing,Visual Arts
Agency Implementation: Department of Trade, Industry and Competition (DTIC)
Main Feature: South Africa’s recent Re-imagined Industrial Strategy specifically identifies the creative economy as a priority sector of focus. To this end, a Sectoral Master Plan for the Creative Industries is under development. South Africa’s trade policy and trade agreements are identified as an important lever in supporting the Master Plan process. This makes the analysis of the country’s CCI trade highly relevant to South Africa’s current growth and industrialisation strategy. Chapter 3 examined South Africa’s international trade in cultural goods and services, using local and international data sources. The focus is on the US/Mexico-Canada (USMCA) bloc and SADC in comparative perspective, and the impact of the COVID-19 pandemic  In 2020, South Africa’s cultural goods exports were worth US$316.46 million, and made up 0.37% of the value of all South Africa’s commodity exports. Until 2018, cultural goods exports had been growing strongly, making up 0.47% of South Africa’s total commodity exports (US$448.86 million) in that year. As with GDP growth and employment, the economic slow-down and the impact of COVID-19 have had a negative impact on cultural goods exports. Cultural goods trade contracted more sharply than total commodity trade on both the export and import side for 2018–2020.  Like many small, open economies, South Africa had a cultural goods trade deficit, with the value of cultural goods imports being more than the value of exports. However, cultural goods imports have been declining recently, and for the first time in 20 years, South Africa had a positive cultural goods trade balance for some quarters in 2020 and 2021 (Figure 18). While cultural goods exports initially appeared to recover more quickly after the hard lockdown, they have not yet reached pre-pandemic levels  The Reimagined Industrial Strategy aimed to focus more clearly on strategic value chains, including: •	Promoting localisation and sector masterplans, •	To ensure that more South Africans benefit directly from the industrialisation process through job creation and more broad-based ownership of businesses,  •	To promote the legal and other modalities required to increase trade within Africa, through the AfCFTA.  The Re-imagined Industrial Strategy incorporates key aspects of national policy documents:  •	National Development Plan,  •	New Growth Path framework,  •	Industrial Policy Action Plans •	Economic Reconstruction and Recovery plan. The South African strategy involves, inter alia: 1.	Building industrial resilience and competitiveness through workplace-level support for structural transformation. 2.	Developing partnerships based on mutual commitments from business, labour and government set out in sector masterplans or social compacts. 3.	 Applying competition policies to address some structural constraints to growth, including through measures by the competition authorities to enhance SMME participation and new entrants in markets. 4.	 Utilising trade policies directed to growing the industrial base, with an evidence-led approach. 5.	 Accessing markets through preferential trade agreements, particularly where there is industrial complementarity. 6.	 Pivoting to African-led trade and investment, through the AfCFTA. 7.	 Promoting economic inclusion and transformation in the economy, through measures that promote a wider pool of industrialists (the black industrialist programme);a deeper shareholding through worker ownership schemes; and a broader skills base. 8.	 Promoting greater levels of innovation and technological development, by linking research with commercialisation strategies. 9.	Greater levels of local procurement by the state and major firms, coupled with supplier development initiatives. 10.	 Identifying and backing new sources of growth (digital economy, green industrialisation) while retaining employment in traditional sectors. 11.	Adjusting strategy to contemporary pressures, eg implementation of the measures to deal with energy supply or logistics challenges
Results: The South African Re-Imagined Industrial Strategy seeks to achieve the following results: •	Deepen the domestic market by growing employment, increasing productivity and undertaking other measures to improve equity and income distribution, and widen the market for South African goods and services through a stronger focus on exports to the region and other rapidly growing economies. •	Supply-side measures seek to improve competitiveness, build resilience and strengthen the agility and innovation at firm-level.

Title EN: Basic Income for the Arts Pilot Scheme
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture
SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Cultural and creative sectors
Agency Implementation: Department of Tourism, Culture, Arts, Gaeltacht, Sport and Media
Main Feature: The Basic Income for the Arts is a three-year pilot scheme (2022 – 2025) to support artists and creative arts workers, providing 2,000 successful applicants with a weekly income of €325 each which incorporates a research programme to inform future Government policy. The Scheme was open to all eligible artists and creative arts sector workers. The overarching objective of the scheme is to address the earnings instability that can be associated with the intermittent, periodic, and often project-based nature of work in the arts.   Objectives:  • To enable artists and creative arts workers to focus on artistic and creative work during the period of the pilot, without having to enter into employment in other sectors to sustain themselves.  • To assesses if, during the period of the pilot, self-employment presents a viable pathway for artistic and creative work, by reducing income instability.  • To capitalise on investment in sectoral skills and expertise developed through education within the sector.  • To minimise the loss of skill and experience from the arts sector. • To reduce the need for artists and creative arts workers to avail of social protection supports including Jobseekers.  • To ensure participants retain a steady and predictable income during the period of the pilot.  • To measure any multi-dimensional well-being impacts of the scheme on participants.  • To give recognition to the value of time spent on developing a creative practice.  • To give recognition to the value of the arts and the role of creative practice in Irish society  The scheme is designed as a Randomised Control Trial (RCT). A treatment group of 2,000 is compared to a control group of 1,000. Both have been selected randomly from a pool of roughly 8,000 eligible applicants. The evaluation of the scheme will be conducted on an ongoing basis to determine the impact of the grant payment.   Background/ Development of the Policy The Arts and Culture Taskforce, established in September 2020, was tasked by the Minister of Culture with producing a report to include a set of recommendations on how best the arts and culture sector could adapt and recover from the COVID-19 pandemic.  The number one recommendation from the taskforce report "Life Worth Living Report" was to pilot a Basic Income scheme for a three-year period in the arts, culture, audio-visual and live performance and events sectors.  As part of the National Economic Recovery Plan, launched on 1 June 2021, the Minister of Culture secured a commitment from Government for a Basic Income Pilot Scheme for artists.  Throughout 2021, the Ministry of Culture engaged in a policy development process, which has involved discussions with the Life Worth Living Oversight Group, engaging with sectoral stakeholders, convening an inter-departmental working group to assess challenges, and reviewing international research and best practice. The Ministry used this work to inform its proposal for a pilot Basic Income for the Arts (BIA).  Stakeholder engagement has been core to the policy development process and this has included a stakeholder forum on 15th December 2021, where over 150 participants from 50 artists and arts workers resource and representative bodies came together to discuss the proposal.  A public consultation took place throughout the month of January 2022. The purpose of the consultation was to ensure that the general public, artists and creative arts workers, and those working in the arts and culture sector have the opportunity to contribute to policy development for the pilot scheme.  https://www.gov.ie/en/publication/29337-basic-income-for-the-arts-pilot-scheme-guidelines-for-applicants/#:~:text=in%20the%20arts.-,The%20scheme%20will%20research%20the%20impact%20on%20artists%20and%20creative,period%20(2022%20%E2%80%93%202025).   https://www.gov.ie/en/press-release/4769e-arts-and-culture-recovery-taskforce-report-published/   https://www.gov.ie/en/campaigns/709d1-economic-recovery-plan/
Results: Findings from the first year of the programme were published in May 2024. The findings indicated a number of very positive impacts on the lives and cultural practices of participants, including: Investment in creative practice: •	BIA recipients spend on average almost 8 weekly hours more on their creative practice than the control group.  •	Namely, compared to the control group, BIA recipients spend on average 3.5 weekly hours more making work, more than 2 weekly hours on research and experimentation, more than half an hour weekly on training, and more than 1 hour weekly on management and administration. Compared to the control group, BIA recipients invest on average €550 more monthly in their practice, namely on equipment and materials, advertising and marketing, workspaces, and work travel. This extra spending equates to almost 40% of participants’ BIA monthly payment. BIA recipients are 7.7 percentage points more likely to have completed new works in the previous six months compared to the control group. On average, they have completed 3.6 pieces of work more than the control group •	BIA recipients are 7.7 percentage points more likely to have completed new works in the previous six months compared to the control group. On average, they have completed 3.6 pieces of work more than the control group   Time spent working in other sectors: BIA recipients spend on average 2.7 weekly hours less than the control group working in another sector.  Wellbeing: •	Life satisfaction, measured on a scale of 1 to 10, is more than half a point higher for BIA  recipients compared to the control group. BIA recipients have increased their leisure time by almost one hour per week on average compared to the control group BIA recipients are on average 6 percentage points less likely to have felt downhearted or depressed, and over 8 percentage points less likely to have experienced anxiety compared to the control group Material deprivation: •	BIA recipients are on average 18.8 percentage points less likely to have difficulty making ends meet compared to the control group. The Enforced Deprivation Rate, as measured by the Central Statistics Office, declined by 20.2 percentage points for BIA recipients compared to the control group. •	BIA recipients experienced a decline in material deprivation across 10 out of 11 SILC indicators, meaning that they are more likely to be able to afford basic necessities compared to the control group. The decline ranges from -4 to -19.6 percentage points, depending on the item.  The full report can be accessed at www.gov.ie/pdf/?file=https://assets.gov.ie/294268/3555e53e-4882-403b-ab57-d09f31ffab9b.pdf#page=null
Financial Ressources: €35 million (approx. $38,034,500 USD) per year,  for a total of €105 million (approx. $114,103,500 USD) for the period 2022-2025 (i.e. until the end of the pilot).
Recommandations: The pilot is being evaluated continuously. Every six months, participants complete the survey. Survey data is sent to the research team and analysed. The analysis is then presented in a report. This far, two reports have been published. See above for impacts detected this far.  Final recommendations will be provided at the end of the trial in 2025.

Title EN: “WE ARE DIVERSE: Empowering and  encouraging workers from populational collectives belonging to women movie maker minorities, indigenous, afro, LGBTIQ+, migrants and cisgender in seven countries of Latin America"
Goal: Promote Human Rights And Fundamental Freedoms
SDG: SDG 5 - Achieve gender equality and empower all women and girls,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels

Agency Implementation: IBERO-AMERICAN FEDERATION OF ACADEMIES OF FILM ARTS AND SCIENCES
Main Feature: The "Somos Diversas'' project is a comprehensive initiative led by the Ibero-American Federation of Film Academies (FIACINE in Spanish), with the financial support of UNESCO and the International Fund for Cultural Development (FIDC in Spanish). Its main objective is to promote inclusion and diversity in the Ibero-American film industry, with a specific focus on supporting and empowering women filmmakers belonging to minority groups in Argentina, Chile, Colombia, Ecuador, Guatemala, Mexico, and the Dominican Republic.         The project seeks to identify and strengthen collectives of women filmmakers who belong to different minority groups, such as indigenous, Afro-descendant, LGBTIQ, migrants and cisgender. This is done to generate inputs that contribute to a publication with specific recommendations on the state of women workers in the audiovisual sector in each participating country. These recommendations aim to influence public policies related to cinema and promote quality jobs for women in the region.         The main objectives of the "Somos Diversas" project are the following:         1. Identification of Groups: The aim is to identify and map the groups of women belonging to indigenous, Afro-descendant, LGBTIQ, migrant, and cisgender minorities within the audiovisual industry in the seven participating countries. This step is essential to understand the diversity within the sector and design inclusive and specific strategies for each group.         2. Analysis of the Labor and Training Situation: The project aims to analyze the labor and training situation of working women belonging to the groups identified in each country. This analysis will allow us to identify the barriers and challenges that these women face in their professional development in the cinematographic field. Moreover, it seeks to develop capabilities and competencies that improve their access to national and international cultural markets and industries.         3. Report and Recommendations for Public Policy: From the data collected, a detailed report will be generated that maps the audiovisual sector in the seven participating countries from the perspective of minority women workers. This report will include specific recommendations addressed to film authorities and public policy makers to promote equal opportunities and inclusion in the sector.         4. SOMOS DIVERSO Forum: The project contemplates the organization of the "Somos Diversos" forum as a key space for the articulation of networks between identified minority groups. This forum will not only facilitate the exchange of experiences and good practices, but will also strengthen collaboration and mutual support between women filmmakers of diverse origins within Ibero-America. In summary, "Somos Diversas" not only aspires to make visible and empower women filmmakers belonging to minority groups in the Ibero-American region, but also seeks to influence public policies and practices in the film sector to build a more inclusive and equitable environment. Through research, training and networking, the project aims to generate a lasting impact that promotes significant cultural and structural change in the film industry.
Results: The "Somos Diversas" project is an initiative of the Ibero-American Federation of Film Academies (FIACINE), financed by UNESCO and the International Fund for Cultural Development (FIDC). Its objective is to promote inclusion and diversity in the Ibero-American film industry, focusing on empowering women filmmakers from minority groups in Argentina, Chile, Colombia, Ecuador, Guatemala, Mexico, and the Dominican Republic. It seeks to identify and strengthen groups of minority women filmmakers, such as indigenous, Afro-descendant, LGBTIQ, migrants and cisgender, to generate recommendations that influence public policies and promote quality jobs. The key objectives are:         1. Identification of Groups: Map and understand diversity in the audiovisual industry in the         participating countries, designing inclusive and specific strategies.         2. Analysis of the Labor and Training Situation: Evaluate the barriers and professional challenges of         these women, developing capacities to improve their access to cultural markets.         3. Report and Recommendations for Public Policy: Prepare a detailed report with         recommendations addressed to film authorities to promote equality of         opportunities.         4. SOMOS DIVERSOS Forum: Create a space for the articulation of networks between groups         minorities, facilitating the exchange of experiences and strengthening collaboration between         women filmmakers.         The project not only seeks to make these women visible and empower them, but also influence public policies and practices in the film sector to build a more inclusive environment. Through research, training, and networking, we aim to generate a lasting impact that promotes significant cultural and structural change in the film industry.         Additionally, the diversity in the size of the groups, ranging from 1 to 5 members to more than 21, influences the distribution of responsibilities and capacity for action. The majority work voluntarily, reflecting their commitment to the group's mission and objectives.         In terms of decision-making and financing, collectives usually adopt democratic practices and diversify their sources of financing, including self-financing, public funds, and private donations. This favors its sustainability and independence.         Audiovisual production and training are priority areas for these groups, reflecting their commitment to content creation and professional development of their members. However, they face technical and infrastructure challenges, especially in rural areas.         Finally, the groups show interest in cross-sector topics such as cultural public policies, project management, and intellectual property, and expanding networks of contacts and collaborating internationally. These interests and training needs are crucial for their development and professionalization in the audiovisual field.

Title EN: « SENTOO » : un projet de coopération sud-sud pour le cinéma africain
Goal: Integrate Culture In Sustainable Development Frameworks
SDG: SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: International cooperation for sustainable development
Agency Implementation: CNCI (Tunisie)
Main Feature: « SENTOO » signifiant « attendre quelqu'un ou quelque chose avec espoir » en langue wolove (Sénégal) est un projet fédérateur et structurant, conçu par et pour des professionnels africains, majoritairement financé par des opérateurs et des partenaires continentaux et/ou actifs sur le continent (OIF- UNESCO). Il vise à donner aux producteurs et auteurs les outils et les moyens matériels pour développer leurs films en préservant leur identité africaine et leurs droits à les exploiter. En particulier, il permet aux producteurs délégués Sud de conserver la maitrise d’ouvrage et la propriété des œuvres concernées. Pour la première fois en Afrique, un programme de soutien à la création cinématographique associe des résidences d’écriture, un atelier de production et de coproduction et une aide au développement, avec deux objectifs précis et concrets : •	Accompagner des auteurs africains porteurs d’un projet à fort potentiel, à l’étape de l’écriture, de l’idée au premier traitement ; poursuivre l’accompagnement des auteurs et des producteurs concernés pendant les phases suivantes de développement. •	Favoriser les coopérations sud-sud, en particulier les coproductions entre pays d’Afrique Subsaharienne et du Maghreb, en nombre et en qualité. « SENTOO » est une initiative du Centre national du cinéma et de l’image tunisien (CNCI) visant à impliquer le maximum de ses homologues du Maghreb, d’Afrique centrale et de l’ouest, (centres du cinéma et institutions équivalentes en matière de compétences et de missions ) avec pour ambition de créer un environnement favorable aux coproductions Sud-Sud et encourager tous les pays africains disposant d’un fonds de soutien à la production cinématographique à investir dans le développement des projets qui constitue une phase cruciale pour la qualité des films africains. Sont éligibles au programme les projets dont les auteurs-réalisateurs sont originaires de l’un des pays partenaires qui sont au nombre de: •	06 pour la première session : Tunisie, Maroc, Sénégal, Burkina-Faso, Mali, Niger •	07 pour la deuxième session : Tunisie, Maroc, Sénégal, Burkina-Faso, Mali, Cote d'Ivoire, Togo
Results: Le projet s’est déroulé en deux sessions sur la période 2019-2022 : •	La première session a bénéficié à 12 producteurs et 06 auteurs africains des pays partenaires. Elle a été marquée par l’organisation de 03 résidences d’écritures (avec une durée d’une à deux semaines) en Tunisie, au Sénégal et au Maroc.   Liste des projets bénéficiaires (par pays) :  1) BURKINA FASO : Djéliya (Documentaire), du réalisateur Boubacar SANGARÉ 2) MALI : Aida (Fiction), de la réalisatrice Hawa Aliou N'DIAYE 3) MAROC : Boom boom Sonata (Fiction), du réalisateur Mohamed Akram NEMMASSI 4) NIGER : Ville en mutation (Documentaire), du réalisateur Bawa KADADÉ RIBA 5) SÉNÉGAL : Mouton de Sada (Fiction), du réalisateur Pape Bouname LOPY 6) TUNISIE : L'aurore Boréale (Fiction), du réalisateur Oubeyd AYARI  •	La deuxième session bien qu’elle a été interrompue à plusieurs reprises en raison de la crise sanitaire covid-19, a bénéficié à 07 auteurs d’un projet de film en phase de développement :  -	TUNISIE : MAARA IS BACK (Fiction/Animation) de Nadia RAÏS  -	BURKINA FASO : LA GRAINE FERTILE (Fiction/Animation) de André Daniel TAPSOBA  -	MAROC : CEUX QUI VONT AU PARADIS (Fiction) de Nabil MERROUCH  -	SENEGAL : RÉPUBLIQUE, PÉTROLE, RÉVOLUTION (Documentaire) de Abdou LAHAT FALL -	CÔTE D’IVOIRE : LORENZO (Fiction) de Joël AKAFOU  -	TOGO : ETRE AIMÉ (Documentaire) de Justin KPATCHAA PALAKIYEM -	MALI : LE RETOUR DE WARAKORO (Fiction/Animation) de Gaoussou TANGARA  Elle a été marquée par : •	Des résidences d’écriture, encadrées par des professionnels africains chevronnés (Lieux des résidences : Bobo Dioulasso (Burkina Faso) - Saint Louis (Sénégal) -  Tunis (Tunisie) •	Un atelier de production et de coproduction destiné à mettre en contact (match-making) les porteurs des projets sélectionnés avec d’autres producteurs africains. Un coaching de ces producteurs, afin de leur donner les outils nécessaires pour conserver la production déléguée des projets qu’ils souhaitent accompagner. Cette troisième étape s’est prolongée par un événement de mise en réseau (networking) des binômes auteur/producteur délégué avec des décideurs internationaux. •	Des bourses d’aide au développement en numéraire (5000 euros) attribuées à chaque projet sélectionné. Cette initiative de coopération sud-sud qui a offert un cadre étendu de collaborations entre les pays en développement basé sur un concept de solidarité qui annule la dichotomie classique entre les donateurs et les bénéficiaires a contribué à développer : -	Le réseautage entre professionnels de la culture -	L’échange d’expertise et d’expériences -	Une dynamique de coproduction et mutualisation de ressources à l’échelle africaine -	Un partage des connaissances, des compétences, des savoirs –faire et des initiatives réussies dans les pays partenaires pour atteindre les buts du développement moyennant des efforts concertés.
Financial Ressources: 278150 Dinars tunisien soit 88900 dollars américains

Title EN: 421 Arts Campus
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture
SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Cultural and creative sectors
Cultural Domain: Design,Performing Arts,Media Arts,Cinema and Audiovisual Arts,Music,Publishing,Visual Arts
Agency Implementation: 421 Arts Campus
Main Feature: 421 Arts Campus is an independent platform dedicated to emerging artists and creative practitioners in the UAE and across the region. A site for research, learning and experimentation, 421 provides a nurturing environment for emergent creative practices and those who want to harness the arts as an agent for social inquiry and transformation. 421 encourages practitioners to explore the potential of public spaces as a means for progress and community engagement through a wide-ranging programmatic model that facilitates artistic exchange and critical dialogue. Previously known as Warehouse421, 421 was established in 2015 inside a renovated warehouse that was repurposed as an exhibition and community space featuring galleries, studios, courtyards, co-working spaces, a library and cafe, and a public, outdoor plaza that serves as a multipurpose venue for film screenings, symposia, performances, art installations, and other special programs. The 421 campus is also home to several permanent art installations commissioned for major exhibitions that were previously presented inside the 421 galleries. Since its establishment.
Results: 421 has organized over forty solo and group exhibitions, and more than 1000 public programs across a range of artistic and creative disciplines. PROGRAMS AND INITIATIVES � EXHIBITIONS Throughout the year, the 421 galleries see eight to ten exhibitions solo and group exhibitions that focus on a range of disciplines including visual arts, design and architecture, new media, literary arts and publishing, sound and sonic exploration, and performance. Many of the exhibitions presented are the result of other 421 programs such as the Artistic Development Program and the Curatorial Development Program. Several off-site exhibitions also take place at partner institutions, offering emerging artists and creative practitioners� access to new audiences and opportunities for engagement. � PUBLIC PROGRAMS Every season, the 421 public program presents an extensive calendar of workshops, courses, talks, film screenings, excursions, and special events that are designed to immerse audiences in hands-on experiences that develop artistic and creative skills and encourage cultural exchange. Responding to themes and topics addressed in the exhibitions on view, the 421 public programs promote deeper interaction and engagement with the arts. � CAPACITY BUILDING PROGRAMS The 421 capacity building programs support artists and creative practitioners who have a sustained artistic practice or interest in creative disciplines. Often involving juries made up of locally and regionally based arts professionals, as well as pedagogical partners that contribute to the curricula, the capacity building programs function as a launching pad for the career development of young and emerging practitioners. Those programs are open to participation of students, recent graduates and early-career practitioners interested in visual arts, design and architecture, film, new media, literary arts and performance. � HOMEBOUND RESIDENCY Originally conceived as an onsite initiative, the Homebound Residency Program emerged as a response to the challenges posed by the COVID-19 pandemic in early 2020. The program, which was created to support the work of artists and creative practitioners across the MENASA region, was reconfigured to address the needs of artists during the global crisis. Facing isolation from their communities, the 6-month-long online program provided a platform for artists to explore digital modes of connection and engagement. � RESIDENCY PROGRAM The Residency Program supports creative practitioners interested in experimenting with social and community engagement as part of their practice. The five-month program takes place in person at the 421 Art Campus artist studios and is designed for the creative community at large. The residency is multidisciplinary in focus and is open to practices in visual arts and curation, design and technology, music, literary arts, culinary arts, performance and theater, and other creative disciplines. The residency will bring together three successful applicants for each cohort of the program. � ARTISTIC RESEARCH GRANT The 421 Artistic Research Grant supports practice-based research investigating contemporary social questions through interdisciplinary methodologies and active engagement with the researcher�s community. While this is not an academic grant, a strong interaction with the historical, geographical, and intellectual context of a grantee�s topic and medium is expected. � ARTISTIC DEVELOPMENT PROGRAM The 421 Artistic Development Program is an exhibition process that emphasizes the professional and creative development of its participating artists. Conceived as a commissioning exhibition, participating artists are supported by experienced art educators and/or a senior curator from the region, along with the 421 team, through a structured educational model of production, towards a polished exhibition of high caliber. � CURATORIAL DEVELOPMENT PROGRAM The 421 Curatorial Development Program is an exhibition process that emphasizes the professional and creative development of its curators. Supported by the 421 team and an expert pedagogical partner, the program aims to support emerging local and regional curators who are pushed here to hone their practice holistically and to build a well-rounded skill set that aids them in crafting each facet of a successful exhibition.

Title EN: Abstraction and Calligraphy ? Towards a Universal Language"
Goal: Achieve A Balanced Flow Of Cultural Goods And Services And Increase The Mobility Of Artists And Cultural Professionals
SDG: SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 10 - Reduce inequality within and among countries,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Flow of cultural goods and services
Agency Implementation: Louvre Abu Dhabi
Main Feature: "Abstraction and Calligraphy ? Towards a Universal Language" exhibition at the Louvre Abu Dhabi, held from 17 February to 12 June 2021, is a remarkable journey into the interplay between Eastern calligraphy and Western abstract art. In collaboration with the Centre Pompidou, this exhibition uncovers the profound influence of Asian and North African scripts on Western artists' quest to create a universal visual language. Visitors are invited to explore the emotional depth and vibrant expressions behind the works of renowned artists such as Cy Twombly, Wassily Kandinsky, Henri Matisse, Paul Klee, Joan Mir�, Lee Ufan, Andr� Masson, Dia Azzawi, and Jackson Pollock. These masterworks are showcased alongside contemporary pieces by artists like Sanki King, Mona Hatoum, and a monumental installation by eL Seed, offering a rare chance to appreciate these diverse artworks in one space. The exhibition presents a fascinating dialogue between East and West, highlighting how calligraphy's raw precision and expressive restraint unlocked new modes of expression for abstract artists. Through this lens, visitors can see how symbols and signs from the Arab world fueled the imagination of Western artists, allowing them to convey complex emotions, empathy, and ideas in innovative ways. As the first exhibition of 2021, "Abstraction and Calligraphy" features masterworks from prestigious collections, including the Centre Pompidou and Guggenheim Abu Dhabi, many of which are being shown for the first time. This unique display offers a rich exploration of how diverse cultural influences converge on the canvas, celebrating the universal language of art.
Results: The initiative to present "Abstraction and Calligraphy: Towards a Universal Language" at the Louvre Abu Dhabi has yielded significant results in showcasing the intersection between two seemingly divergent artistic traditions and fostering cross-cultural dialogue. Through this initiative, visitors have been exposed to the fascinating convergence of abstraction and calligraphy, exploring how these two artistic forms have influenced and enriched each other across different cultural contexts. By juxtaposing artworks from diverse regions, including the Middle East, Asia, and the West, the exhibition has highlighted the universal language of art and the transcendent power of visual expression to communicate complex ideas and emotions. Visitors have been captivated by the innovative techniques and bold experimentation showcased in the artworks, gaining a deeper appreciation for the diversity of artistic traditions and the potential for cultural exchange to inspire creativity and innovation.
Recommandations: The "Abstraction and Calligraphy" exhibition offers several conclusions and recommendations for advancing cultural understanding and appreciation, particularly in the context of art and aesthetics. Firstly, the initiative underscores the importance of recognizing and celebrating the interconnectedness of artistic traditions from different cultures. By embracing cultural diversity and promoting dialogue and collaboration, cultural initiatives can contribute to building more inclusive and harmonious societies, where the richness of human creativity is celebrated as a universal heritage.

Title EN: Accessibility measures for the book sector
Goal: Integrate Culture In Sustainable Development Frameworks
SDG: SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: National sustainable development policies and plans
Agency Implementation: The Association of Canadian Publishers (ACP), the National Association of Book Publishers (ANEL), eBound Canada, Literary Press
Main Feature: In 2019, the government announced an investment of CAD 22.8 million over 5 years for the development of an initiative to support the sustainable production and distribution of accessible digital books by Canadian independent publishing houses. This investment therefore made it possible to put in place a number of initiatives aimed in particular at improving accessibility to Canadian literary works in the digital environment for people with cognitive or motor limitations. The Association of Canadian Publishers (ACP), the National Association of Book Publishers (ANEL) and eBOUND Canada therefore carried out a research project to determine the best practices to be implemented using this fund. The results of this project have been implemented over the past four years by independent publishers and their provincial or regional organizations, as well as by the Literary Press Group (LPG), in multiple projects aimed at converting independent publishing houses' back catalogs into accessible formats, and teaching independent publishing houses how to create accessible books upon release (born-accessible book), including EPUB-3 and audiobooks. Thus, publishing houses across the country have converted entire sections of their catalog into formats promoting accessibility, adding hundreds of Canadian titles to the accessible digital offering, and ensuring that people with disabilities or disabilities limitations can access high-quality Canadian books when they need them and in a format that suits them. Moreover, the Alberta Book Publishers Association, the Atlantic Book Publishers Association, and the LPG have all launched accessible digital marketing campaigns and catalogs highlighting their members' achievements in this field, demonstrating that Canada is a leader in accessible publishing in North America and around the world. In short, the initiatives grouped here strongly contribute to better accessibility of Canadian literary content to minority communities, promoting diversity in the dissemination of culture and promoting the right to freely take part in cultural life for all, as defined in the Universal Declaration of Human Rights.
Results: Many independent Canadian publishing houses have pursued and achieved globally certified accessibility status by Benetech Global, having developed and integrated accessible digital workflows into their normal production process. These publishing houses now publish their books in an accessible way upon release, allowing people with disabilities or limitations to interact with Canadian literary culture at the same time as everyone else and therefore having an impact on the availability of Canadian culture, even after the end of the federal funding program. More specifically, for Alberta during this period, 815 digital books were added to the catalogs of 15 ACP member publishers; 83 audiobooks were added to the catalogs of 21 publishers and 6 publishers received Benetech certification.  For their part, the members of LPG made 712 books from their catalog accessible; 35 publishers across the English-speaking part of Canada were involved in this project. Although government funding is coming to an end, Canadian independent publishing houses remain committed to making high-quality books available to all.

Title EN: Accords de coopération avec les pays africains et du Sud, amis et frères du Maroc (Sénégal, Djibouti, Burkina Faso, Côte d'Ivoire, Cap vert, Gambie, Congo Brazzaville )
Goal: Integrate Culture In Sustainable Development Frameworks
SDG: SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: International cooperation for sustainable development
Cultural Domain: Design,Performing Arts,Media Arts,Cinema and Audiovisual Arts,Music,Publishing,Visual Arts
Agency Implementation: Ministère de la Jeunesse, de la Culture et de la Coopération
Main Feature: La coopération culturelle entre le Maroc et l'Afrique s'est intensifiée au fil des années, se manifestant par la conclusion de plus d'une centaine d'accords de coopération. Ces accords visent à valoriser l'héritage culturel commun, en mettant en avant des initiatives axées sur plusieurs domaines clés.  L'un des aspects les plus importants de cette coopération est le transfert du savoir et du savoir-faire en matière de mise en œuvre de projets de développement humain. Le Maroc partage son expertise avec de nombreux pays africains, contribuant ainsi à l'amélioration des conditions de vie et au développement socio-économique à travers des projets culturels. Ces initiatives permettent non seulement de préserver le patrimoine culturel, mais aussi de favoriser la création de nouveaux emplois et de stimuler les économies locales.  La diplomatie spirituelle constitue également un pilier fondamental de cette coopération. En Afrique, le Maroc s'emploie à renforcer les actions de diplomatie spirituelle, en favorisant les échanges culturels et religieux. Cette approche contribue à promouvoir la tolérance, la compréhension mutuelle et la paix dans la région.  Le développement et la promotion des échanges culturels sont au cœur des accords conclus. Ces échanges permettent de renforcer les liens entre les peuples, de promouvoir une meilleure compréhension des diverses cultures et de stimuler la créativité artistique. Les festivals, les expositions et les échanges d'artistes sont autant de manifestations de cette dynamique culturelle.  La préservation et la mise en valeur du patrimoine culturel occupent également une place de choix dans ces accords. Le Maroc, riche de son patrimoine historique et culturel, partage ses techniques de conservation et de valorisation du patrimoine avec ses partenaires africains. Cela inclut des projets de restauration de sites historiques, la formation de professionnels du patrimoine et la mise en place de musées et de centres culturels.  L'échange de savoir-faire et d'expertise en matière d'industries culturelles et créatives est un autre domaine de coopération majeur. Le Maroc et ses partenaires africains collaborent pour développer des industries culturelles dynamiques, telles que le cinéma, la musique, l'artisanat et la mode. Ces secteurs offrent de nouvelles opportunités économiques et permettent de valoriser la richesse culturelle africaine sur la scène internationale.  Enfin, le renforcement des capacités dans les métiers du patrimoine, de la culture et des arts est un objectif primordial. Des programmes de formation et des ateliers sont organisés pour former une nouvelle génération de professionnels qualifiés, capables de préserver et de promouvoir le patrimoine culturel de leurs pays respectifs.  En somme, la coopération culturelle entre le Maroc et l'Afrique, soutenue par une centaine d'accords de coopération, est un vecteur puissant de développement humain et de rapprochement des peuples. Elle témoigne de l'engagement commun à préserver et à valoriser l'héritage culturel, tout en favorisant le progrès économique et social sur le continent africain.
Results: 1.Développement des industries culturelles et créatives des deux pays:  -Participation réciproque aux salons internationaux de livre, festivals, expositions, et manifestations culturelles ; -Échange de troupes musicales, folkloriques et artistiques ; -Échange de publications spécialisées dans les domaines du patrimoine, des arts et de la culture ; -Organisation des évènements culturels et artistiques visant la promotion des deux cultures ; -Mobilité des artistes entre le Maroc et les pays africains ; -Traduction réciproque des œuvres littéraires célèbres dans les deux pays. 2.Préservation et mise en valeur du patrimoine Culturel:  -Renforcement des capacités des gestionnaires du patrimoine culturel ;  -Échange d’expertise, d’expériences et des bonnes pratiques dans les domaines de la mise en valeur du patrimoine culturel matériel et immatériel, la préparation des dossiers d’inscription des biens et éléments sur les listes du patrimoine mondial de l’humanité de l’Unesco « Conventions 1972 et 2003 », méthodes d’inventaire national, la lutte contre le trafic illicite des biens culturels ; -Lutte contre le trafic illicite des biens culturels ; -Numérisation du patrimoine culturel immatériel et digitalisation des sites historiques ; -Échange entre les instituts de recherche et de formation dans le domaine du patrimoine  3.Renforcement des capacités des professionnelles de la culture:  -	Echanges de visite au profit des gestionnaires de infrastructures culturelles au Maroc et pays africains; -Echanges de programmes de formation et de stages professionnels ;  -Echanges d’expertises et de savoir-faire.

Main Feature: The Media Support Act is based on a proposal (Prop. 138 L (2019-2020)) by the Norwegian Ministry of Culture: https://www.regjeringen.no/no/dokumenter/prop.-138-l-20192020/id2714839/  (in Norwegian). The Act stipulates the purpose behind five grant schemes for direct media support. A new political  instrument comes in the form of a four-year governing plan for media support. A fixed, long-term financial framework for NRK, the state-owned public service broadcaster, as well as fixed, long-term frameworks for the direct grant schemes for media support is included in this four-year  governing plans. The Act also formalizes the roles of the Media Authority and the Media Appeals Board in the administration of the direct media support schemes. The Act also provides independence for the Norwegian Media Authority in managing the direct media support schemes. According to the Act, the King (the Government) cannot instruct the Norwegian Media Authority or the Media Appeals Board regarding decisions in individual cases, nor may the King change the Norwegian Media Authority’s or the Media Appeals Board’s decisions or make decisions in a case that comes under their authority according to regulations pursuant to this Act.
Results: The purpose of this Act is to ensure responsible, effective, and transparent collective management of copyright and related rights for both rightsholders and users. It also aims to safeguard rightsholders’ freedom of choice in collective rights management.

Title EN: Adoption du décret sur les droits de suite
Goal: Promote Human Rights And Fundamental Freedoms
SDG: SDG 5 - Achieve gender equality and empower all women and girls,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels
Area of Monitoring: Artistic freedom
Agency Implementation: Ministère de la Jeunesse, de la Culture de la Communication
Main Feature: Le gouvernement marocain a adopté un décret historique qui instaure le droit de suite pour les artistes plasticiens. Une mesure permettant aux artistes de bénéficier d'une compensation financière chaque fois que leurs œuvres sont revendues par des marchands d'art. Cette initiative renforce la protection des droits d'auteur des artistes et contribue à promouvoir leur reconnaissance et leur soutien économique à long terme. En alignant ces pratiques avec les normes internationales en matière de propriété intellectuelle dans les arts plastiques, le Maroc renforce son engagement envers ses créateurs et leur contribution culturelle. Le décret ne se limite pas seulement à renforcer la protection des droits d'auteur et à assurer une compensation financière équitable. Il joue également un rôle crucial dans la promotion de la liberté artistique. En garantissant aux artistes une rémunération continue à chaque revente de leurs œuvres, cette mesure leur permet de poursuivre leur pratique artistique de manière plus indépendante et durable. Elle encourage ainsi la créativité en offrant aux artistes une sécurité économique accrue, leur permettant de se consacrer davantage à leur art sans être uniquement dépendants des ventes initiales de leurs œuvres. Cette sécurité financière peut également stimuler l'innovation artistique en réduisant les pressions économiques souvent associées à la création. En alignant ces efforts sur les normes internationales en matière de propriété intellectuelle, le Maroc montre son engagement envers la liberté d'expression artistique et son soutien continu aux créateurs dans leur contribution culturelle essentielle.
Results: Protection accrue des droits d'auteur : Les artistes plasticiens bénéficient désormais d'une compensation financière à chaque revente de leurs œuvres, renforçant ainsi leur protection économique et leurs droits d'auteur.  Soutien économique aux artistes : Cette mesure offre aux artistes une source de revenus continue, ce qui leur permet de se concentrer davantage sur leur création artistique sans être exclusivement dépendants des ventes initiales de leurs œuvres.  Stimulation de la créativité et de l'innovation : En réduisant les préoccupations financières liées à la revente des œuvres, les droits de suite encouragent les artistes à explorer de nouvelles formes d'expression et à expérimenter, contribuant ainsi à dynamiser le paysage artistique marocain.  Reconnaissance sociale et culturelle accrue : Cette politique renforce la reconnaissance des artistes plasticiens au sein de la société marocaine, en valorisant leur contribution culturelle et artistique de manière tangible.  Alignement avec les normes internationales : En introduisant cette mesure, le Maroc se conforme aux normes internationales en matière de propriété intellectuelle, renforçant ainsi sa réputation dans le domaine culturel et artistique à l'échelle mondiale.

Ainsi, les œuvres soutenues (longs-métrages, courts-métrages ou œuvres audiovisuelles quel que soit le genre) affichent une ambition particulière et apparaissent comme des vitrines du savoir-faire technique et artistique de ces prestataires français.

This Charter was signed by the Minister of Arts and Culture on 25 May 2012 and was ratified by Cabinet and adopted by Parliament in 2013.
