Title EN: Agreement on Providing Radio Broadcasting and Television Broadcasting Services to the Public
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture
SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Media diversity
Agency Implementation: Ministry of Culture of the Slovak Republic
Main Feature: This Agreement was made with the aim to set a framework for system support and development of public services in the field of radio and television broadcasting through: •	creation and production of new original programs in the public interest,  •	public dissemination of these programs as part of the public service in the field of broadcasting, •	modernization of the technological base intended for the production and broadcasting of new original programs in the public interest and  •	foreign language broadcasting.  By entering into this Agreement, the contracting parties (the Slovak Republic represented by the Ministry, and Radio and Television of Slovakia (hereinafter referred to as "RTVS")) declare that they consider the support of the creation, production, broadcasting and preservation of Slovak audiovisual and cinematographic works and sound recordings and transmissions of artistic performances to be an integral part of the service public in the field of broadcasting, as well as part of the cultural heritage of the Slovak Republic. In relation to the sustainable development of audiovisual culture, RTVS has an irreplaceable historical, cultural, social and economic position. Ensuring this development with the use of public funds and in cooperation with RTVS and other entities operating in the audiovisual area is the fulfilment of public interest in the field of broadcasting, as well as in the field of development of audiovisual culture and industry in the Slovak Republic while fulfilling the values of humanism, ethics and education. In 2017, new Framework Agreement No MK – 57/2017/M on Providing Radio Broadcasting and Television Broadcasting Services to the Public was signed for the period of 2018 – 2022.  In 2022, Framework Agreement No MK 180/2022/M on Providing Radio Broadcasting and Television Broadcasting Services to the Public was signed for the period of 2023-2027. Each year, the contracting parties agree on the exact and binding scope and nature of mutual obligations arising under this Agreement, in the form of an addendum to the Agreement. The addendum is always made for a period of one calendar year. Based on the addendum, the Ministry shall annually provide RTVS an agreed amount of funds for the following purposes: •	program commitment of RTVS, the content of which is the realization of new original radio programs in the public interest and new original television programs in the public interest; the program commitment is always specified in more detail in the addendum for the relevant calendar year;  •	realization of specific investment projects according to the specification given in the addendum for the relevant calendar year, and  •	the foreign language broadcasting of RTVS, which is carried out as part of the Radio Slovakia International radio program service, broadcast via satellite and the Internet, for at least 30 minutes a day in each of the following broadcasting languages: Slovak, English, German, French, Russian and Spanish. Since 2013, the addendum to the Agreement with the State also contains State support for the area of special interest for the relevant calendar year and a minimum percentage of the amount of the contribution provided for the implementation of the program commitment, which will be used to implement new original programs in the public interest in the area of special interest of the State. The following areas of special interest of the State were agreed in 2020: •	Programs about important cultural institutions and personalities of Slovakia in the context of historical anniversaries •	Programs focused on raising awareness of and presenting Slovakia´s national cultural monuments •	Programs for children on applying their rights under the UN Convention on the Rights of the Child   The minimum percentage of the amount of the contribution provided for the implementation of the program commitment, used for the implementation of new original programs in the public interest in the area of special interest of the State under Article I (3)(e) of the Agreement: 5 %. The following areas of special interest of the State were agreed in 2021: •	Programs about important cultural institutions and personalities of Slovakia in the context of their historical anniversaries •	Programs focused on raising awareness of and presenting Slovakia´s national cultural monuments •	Programs focused on the 2021 Slovak Design Year   The minimum percentage of the amount of the contribution provided for the implementation of the program commitment, used for the implementation of new original programs in the public interest in the area of special interest of the State under Article I (3)(e) of the Agreement: 3 %. The following areas of special interest of the State were agreed in 2022: •	Documentaries on culture  •	Programs focused on combating disinformation  •	Programs to improve media literacy  •	Programs for national minorities and ethnic groups in the languages of national minorities and ethnic groups living in the Slovak Republic  •	Programs facilitated by multimodal access   The minimum percentage of the amount of the contribution provided for the implementation of the program commitment, used for the implementation of new original programs in the public interest in the area of special interest of the State under Article I (3)(e) of the Agreement: 10% of which at least 2% for programs aimed at combating disinformation, at least 1% for programs for national minorities and ethnic groups in the languages of national minorities and ethnic groups living in the Slovak Republic, and at least 4% for programs facilitated by multimodal access. The following areas of special interest of the State were agreed in 2023: •	Documentaries on arts  •	Programs focused on combating disinformation  •	Programs to improve media literacy   The minimum percentage of the amount of the contribution provided for the implementation of the program commitment, used for the implementation of new original programs in the public interest in the area of special interest of the State under Article I (3)(e) of the Agreement: 5% of which at least 3% for programs aimed at combating disinformation and programs aimed at media literacy.   On 1 July 2023, Act No 242/2023 Coll. amending Act No 532/2010 Coll. on Radio and Television of Slovakia and on amending certain laws as last amended and amending certain acts laws, by which the institution of the Agreement with the State was annulled. The validity of the Agreement with the State for the period of 2023 - 2027, including its addendum for 2023, was terminated as of 31 December 2023. Contribution from the state budget intended for the implementation of programs in the public interest, for the implementation of specific investment projects and for the payment of expenses of foreign language broadcasting agreed in these documents is provided in full for 2023.  Financial resources earmarked for politics: In 2020,  based on the Agreement with the State, RTVS received EUR 19,332,641 to fulfil its program commitment in the field of television broadcasting; EUR 3,000,000 to fulfil its program commitment in the field of radio broadcasting; EUR 1,000,000 for foreign language radio broadcasting, and EUR 3,000,000 specific investment projects. In 2021 based on the Agreement with the State, RTVS received EUR 22,875,645 to fulfil its program commitment in the field of television broadcasting; EUR 3,139,862 to fulfil its program commitment in the field of radio broadcasting; EUR 1,000,000 for foreign language radio broadcasting, and EUR 3,000,000 for specific investment projects.   In 2022, based on the Agreement with the State, RTVS received EUR 19,508,256 to fulfil its program commitment in the field of television broadcasting; EUR 3,000,000 to fulfil its program commitment in the field of radio broadcasting; EUR 1,000,000 for foreign language radio broadcasting, and EUR 3,000,000 for specific investment projects.   In  2023 based on the Agreement with the State, RTVS received EUR  20, 632,600 to fulfil its program commitment in the field of television broadcasting; EUR 3,000,000 to fulfil its program commitment in the field of radio broadcasting; EUR 1,000,000 for foreign language radio broadcasting, and EUR 3,000,000 for specific investment projects.
Results: Support for the audiovisual industry also recorded an increase in 2023. In it, last year the fund paid out support to a total of 68 projects in the amount of EUR 12,570,281, which is the highest amount since the creation of this program in 2016. In this context, it should be emphasized that with effect from January 1, 2020, the conditions for supporting the audiovisual industry were legislatively amended and the original subsidy rate of 20% of authorized expenses was changed to 33%. As a result, it occurred during the 2020s until 2023 to a significant increase in the number of registered film projects, as well as to a year-on-year increase in the total amount paid to support the audiovisual industry. In 2023, the fund registered a record 100 new film projects that are currently being implemented or will be implemented between 2023 and 2026. The benefit of this support according to basic measurable indicators continues to show a continuous increase, while another important indicator of the effectiveness of this method of support - the recalculated total amount of non-state investments spent on the realization of audiovisual works in Slovakia - also increased significantly year-on-year. Title EN: Identification, restoration and promotion of tribal and traditional art forms of Kolhan region in Jharkhand
Goal: Integrate Culture In Sustainable Development Frameworks
SDG: SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: National sustainable development policies and plans
Agency Implementation: KALAMANDIR
Main Feature: Kalamandir strides forward with the ambition to promote and restore cultural heritage. Through various initiatives and programs, Kalamandir aims to preserve traditional arts, crafts and performances that are at the risk of being wiped out. By organizing cultural worships, exhibitions, they provide a platform for artisans and performers to showcase their talents and share their knowledge with younger generations. The efforts not only revive endangered cultural practices but also foster a deeper appreciation and understanding of the cultural diversity within the community. Hence, the main features of the initiatives are:  1. 	To promote ethnic cultural experiences to urban educated people to create a space for indigenous culture. Amadubi Rural Tourism Center, run and managed by “AmadubiPanijiyaGraminParyatanSamiti” has been a unique blend of livelihood generation, safeguarding and promotion of tribal culture, vernacular architecture, ethnic festivals and an extinct scroll painting form Payatkar .  Tribal Dance ( Performing  form) Sarpha, Dasai and Baha have been revived along with art form of Pyatkar painting and Santali BhittiChitra ( Murals on mud houses) ( Visual forms) . The center has been developed under the mentorship of Kalamandir – CCAF to use rural tourism as a tool for sustainable initiative. Here the urban tourists/ visitors are taken to the cosy space of artisans in their village to have taste of their dances, music, craft, life style and cuisine. Concept has been replicated in a larger canvas at Chenjora heritage village with a concept of santal tribe’s governance system, art, culture, vernacular architecture and cuisine. Sarpha is a traditional dance of Santali, performed by the Santhali women. It is performed during Sohrai coinciding with the Kali Puja. The women are dressed in symmetric bordered saree, worship the community God- Kapila the cow. Dasai, a ritualistic dance of AdivasiSantal culture and traditions is performed on the day of Mahalaya. The dance form raises the spirit of war to free the innocent and good from the clutches of evil.  2. 	It also creates awareness to educate its younger generations about its culture and cultural experience. We hold regular workshops and Live demonstration of Tribal and traditional / folk dances (Performing form) ManbhumChhau, SeraikelaChhau, KharsawanChhau, Sarpha, Dasai and Baha have been held in schools of east Singhbhum and SeraikelaKharsawan to disseminate the Intangible Cultural Heritage. It incorporates cultural education into the younger generations and they grow up with a strong sense of cultural identity and appreciation.   3. 	Restoration and dissemination of extinct forms of Culture Heritages of different areas and community which protects the cultural expressions of its respective community. Kalamandir have been instrumental in restoration and preservation of extinct form of tribal dance Forms like Firkal ( Bhumij tribes, Martial art ) in Janumdih village , Potka block , East singhbhum, KharsawanChhau ( Folk Dance of Ho and Lohar community) inDeuridihvillage, Kharsawan block, serakelaKharsawan district , Rinjhain Ranikudar village, Potka block, East Singhbhum and Sing SingrayinKaliyam village, Dumaria block, East Singhbhum( Santal tribes , Folk story telling ) , Payatkar scroll paintingin Amadubi Village, Dumaria Block, East Singhbhum ( Chitrakars , Storytelling and painting with organic colours) through Dorabjitata Trust, eastern Zonal Cultural Centre, Kolkata and SangeetNatakAkademi, Nes Delhi  4. 	Restoration of Practices and making of traditional / tribal Musical Instruments like Banam We have helped to restore making and practice of playing almost extinct form of musical (string) instruments vizBanam( Durga Prasad  Murmu and Durga Prasad  Hansda)  andKendri ( Durga Prasad  Murmu)with the support from SangeetNatakAkademi.  5. 	Presentation and Performance of Dancers and Musicians Every year we organise more than 50 performance program for 30 dance teams at different places along with hosting Seminars, Workshops including school and colleges   Thus, the Foundation has, initiated a process of emotive integration of the primitive culture into the national main cultural stream without disturbing its own distinct grace and beauty.        	   Thus Kalamandir had been intervening in promotion, conservation and dissemination of the tribal / indigenous cultural issues since 1997. In its 27 years of journey, the initial focus was on supporting in all possible ways and generating eventually a continuing support base for three tribal / Indigenous communities, viz. the Bhumij (Mundas), the Santals, The Kudmis, the Hos, the Bhuinyas , Mal-Hors/Kansari /   Ranasengaged  in dokra/bell metal style. Our initiative was aimed at empowering these communities in their locations through education, training/dissemination in practice, cooperative economy and marketing etc. that allowed them to survive and carry on with the creative traditions freely. We also supported a tradition of stone carving and stone sculpture celebrating/discovering the lost history of a region, carried through a musical narrative practice by the Nachnis, and drawing on fragments still lying in ruins in the region.
Results: The results achieved so far through these implementations are impressive. Many traditional art forms have seen resurgence in popularity, with increases participation from both young and old community members.   Durga Prasad Murmu was awarded with coveted with SangeetNatak award. PrabhatMahato was invited to Bali and other places with his dance teams to showcase their talents and share their knowledge with younger generations.   Cultural festivals like the Bharat Parv, attracted larger audiences each year raising awareness and appreciations for rich cultural heritage. Bharat Parv, is a six day mega event organized by the GovernementofIndia as a part of Republic day celebrations. The event includes a food festival, a handicraft mela, folk and tribal dance performances, cultural trope performances. The program is a way to celeberate India’s unity in diversity.The Government of Jharkhand’s Tourism, Art & Culture, Sports, and Youth Affairs department entrusted Kalamandir to showcase the state’s traditions at Bharat Parv through Santali and Paika Dance of Jharkhand on 29th January, 2023.   The G20 event took place on 2nd and 3rd March 2023 in Patratu, Jharkhand in collaboration with Tourism, Art & Culture, Sports, and Youth Affairs departments. Kalamandir set up 8 stalls, showcasing various crafts such as Grass mats, Dokra, Pyatkar paintings, Terracotta, musical instruments, Santal wall paintings, Sohrai paintings, and mask making.   East Zonal Cultural Centre, Ministry of Culture, Government of India organised “ ShagunParv- Festival of Tribals” at SrijaniShilpagram, Santiniketan from 6th – 8th January, 2023. Representing Jharkhand, Kalamandir showcased Jharkhandi cuisine, Biponi crafts and traditional Sarpha dance from Jharkhand.   PurbanchaliyaLokMahotsav held from 14th – 17th December, 2023. It is the Signature Festival of East Zonal Cultural Center. Kalamandir participated in the Food, Craft & Exhibition.   Workshops have successfully trained new generations of artists and craftsmen, ensuring the continuity of these skills. These efforts have not only preserved cultural heritage but also strengthened community bonds and fostered a sense of pride and identity among participants.

Title EN: Alberta’s Arts Professions Recognition Act
Goal: Promote Human Rights And Fundamental Freedoms
SDG: SDG 5 - Achieve gender equality and empower all women and girls,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels
Area of Monitoring: Artistic freedom
Cultural Domain: Performing Arts,Media Arts,Cinema and Audiovisual Arts,Music,Visual Arts
Agency Implementation: Government of Alberta – Arts, Culture and Status of Women
Main Feature: The Arts Professions Recognition Act outlines how public entities, meaning the Government of Alberta and its public agencies, boards and commissions, are required to engage with artists. When contracting with or engaging the services of a professional artist, public entities must have a written contract with the artist. Public entities must also, as far as it considers reasonable and appropriate, respect, honour and in good faith abide by scale agreements of artists’ associations and respect the working conditions of professional artists.
Results: Alberta’s Arts Professions Recognition Act came into effect on December 2, 2021. This legislation: o	supports the recognition and rights of Alberta’s artists; o	promotes art as a profession and a career path to be respected like other fields of work; o	gives formal recognition to artists, their representative associations, their freedom of expression and their economic – including contractual – rights; o	formally acknowledges artists’ value and contributions to Alberta, promotes their work and their rights and provides them with resources to help make their artistic enterprises profitable; o	protects artists’ economic and contractual rights; o	enshrines in law Alberta’s continued commitment to freedom of artistic expression; and o	models the way for private and non-profit employers and contractors in Alberta’s economy and helps legitimize the professional nature of artists’ work.

Title EN: Ana Aslan, the woman who defeated time - story on afostodata.ro
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture

Area of Monitoring: Cultural and creative sectors
Agency Implementation: A fost odata/ Once Upon A Time
Main Feature: One of the most famous figures of Romanian science, Professor Ana Aslan dedicated her entire life to research, and her remarkable discoveries in gerontology, the science that studies the third age, had a great impact on the medical world. Her name went around the world, being one of the country's most significant ambassadors. That's why Ana Aslan can be an example for all young people and children who have a dream and are ready to fulfill it through courage, perseverance, devotion, curiosity.   To continue the story of the Romanian woman who defeated time, the team of storytellers Once Upon a Time created a podcast that can be listened to directly on afostodata.ro, Spotify or iTunes: https://afostodata.ro/ana-aslan-pagina/.  In addition, kids can complete the online interactive quiz with information like Did you know? Let's remember, Fun Facts. It is an initiative that supports the digital literacy for young kids, telling them the importance of Ana Aslan in the world science. The #afostOdata team aims to leave a strong and concrete imprint on people's consciousness on who was the woman who is said to have brought to reality the fairy tale of Youth without old age and life without death.   Approaching new technologies and bringing to the surface lesser-known stories about his life, the project is actually a dynamic realization of life events, social and historical contexts, as well as character traits.   We were very happy to make this content known along with CNR Unesco in their network of schools and other educational sites from all over Romania in  2024, the year dedicated to the personality of Ana Aslan. Ana Aslan, the story, is an awareness and advocacy project with long-term social impact: the discovery by the young public - through story, game and digitization - of a female scientist from Romania that they may not know much about, hoping that in this way we can grow an audience that is greatly needed in the coming years.
Results: The project makes the connection between the past and the present, instilling in teenagers the curiosity to relate to a model of a scientific personality of great value, increasing the level of literacy among young people and their proximity to a personality - an extremely important symbol for their identity and general culture. The content is accessible free of charge, considering that it is made within a cultural project financed by the Ministry of Culture. Among the quantifiable results, it can be mentioned: - an audio story about the life of Ana Aslan and an original illustration  - over 4000 listenings on site, 3278 on Spotify and iTunes.  - communication campaign supported by both Once Upon a Time and CNR Unesco (online posts, press release) - the translation of this story into English so that it can be used outside the country in specific UNESCO activities  The story is available online so the numbers and the results will increase. Newsletters are sent to all the schools almost monthly.

Main Feature: Arab Film Studio (AFS) is a comprehensive training program designed to identify, train, and develop the skills of aspiring filmmakers in the UAE and the broader Arab region. The program aims to provide participants with the necessary knowledge and practical experience to succeed in the film industry. AFS offers several specialized courses, including narrative, documentary, scriptwriting, and young filmmaker’s workshops. These courses are structured to mirror the real process of film production, from concept development and scriptwriting to directing, editing, and post-production. Participants gain hands-on experience and are mentored by industry professionals, ensuring they receive high-quality training and valuable insights into the filmmaking process. Over the years, AFS has launched a variety of programs to cater to different aspects of filmmaking. The narrative program focuses on storytelling and fiction filmmaking, while the documentary program emphasizes non-fiction storytelling. The scriptwriting program provides in-depth training in writing for films, enabling participants to develop compelling screenplays. The young filmmakers workshop targets high school students, offering them an introduction to filmmaking and the opportunity to create their own short films. These programs collectively help nurture a new generation of filmmakers by providing them with the tools, training, and support needed to tell their unique stories.
Results: AFS has successfully trained over 150 emerging filmmakers, many of whom have gone on to have successful careers in the film industry. Films created during the AFS programs have been showcased over 400 times at prestigious international film festivals, including the LA Film Festival, Melbourne Film Festival, and Beirut International Film Festival. These films have also won 25 awards, highlighting the high quality and impact of the training provided by AFS.  AFS has also been instrumental in creating job opportunities within the regional film industry. Many participants have secured full-time positions at Image Nation Abu Dhabi and other prominent production companies, further contributing to the growth and sustainability of the local film industry.
Recommandations: Over the years, AFS has introduced new specialized courses to cater to different aspects of filmmaking. The program now includes Narrative, Documentary, Scriptwriting, and Young Filmmakers workshops, each focusing on distinct areas of film production. This diversification allows participants to choose programs that best match their interests and career goals, enhancing their learning experience. The curriculum has been continually updated to incorporate the latest industry practices and technologies. Workshops, online tutorials, and assignments have been added to provide a more comprehensive learning experience. The inclusion of experienced industry professionals as mentors has further enriched the training process, ensuring participants receive current and relevant guidance. AFS has strengthened its collaborations with various industry partners, such as NYU Abu Dhabi, to offer more opportunities for participants. These partnerships have facilitated access to better resources, facilities, and networking opportunities, crucial for budding filmmakers. The program has also placed greater emphasis on hands-on experience. Participants now engage in real-world film production activities, including creating their own short films that are showcased at the end of the program. This practical approach helps participants gain the skills and confidence needed to succeed in the film industry. These improvements have resulted in significant achievements for AFS, including training over 150 filmmakers, showcasing films at over 400 international festivals, and winning 25 awards. Many participants have secured full-time positions in the film industry, contributing to the growth and sustainability of the local film sector.

Cultural Domain: Design,Performing Arts,Media Arts,Cinema and Audiovisual Arts,Music,Visual Arts
Agency Implementation: Cultures, Arts, Heritage and Public Diplomacy Division (DIRAC), Ministry of Foreign Affairs (MINREL).
Main Feature: One of the main opportunities to approach internationalisation of cultural and artistic practices undertaken by the Chillean Ministry of Foreign Affairs (MINREL), is carried out through the Cultures, Arts, Heritage and Public Diplomacy Division (DIRAC). Its mission is to promote and disseminate cultural aspects, according to interests, objectives and guidelines of the Chilean foreign policy.   The DIRAC Contest takes place through an annual call for cultural projects abroad for artists, be they individuals or legal entities that reside in Chile or abroad. The performing arts, visual arts, craftwork, design and architecture, literature, heritage, music, film and audiovisual content areas are available for applications. The cultural projects  that take part cannot be for profit.   Since 2023 and for the 2024 open call, new milestones have been incorporated into the application conditions to this contest, notably the addition, to the heritage area, of a sub-area for intangible heritage exclusively dedicated to indigenous peoples from the national territory and the promotion of their languages. Another addition included awarding 5 extra points to those projects that address gender and environmental themes in their description, as a tie breaker with regard to others with the same score.   Finally, in line with the monitoring framework of the 2005 Convention, this open call reports on the indicator on "policies and measures that support the outward and inward mobility of dynamic cultural and creative sectors".
Results: The open call has been an important tool to boost internationalisation of Chilean art and culture, significantly contributing to mobility, by affording the artists an opportunity to exhibit their works and collaborate with artists and audiences from other cultures. Connections and collaborations have been established with other artists, institutions and  galleries abroad, facilitating cultural and creative flows.   Support has been created for investment in the careers of Chilean artists, by offering co-financing to cover costs related to travel, accommodation, and other aspects of the project, alleviating the financial burden on the artists. Participating in exhibitions and events abroad has increased the visibility of Chilean artists on the international stage. With regard to the figures from the last edition of this contest, it is worth noting that 72 projects were selected, where music (18%), literature (11%), film and audiovisual (10%) and visual arts (8%) were the creative sectors that benefitted the most.   In terms of the countries where these projects were implemented, the United States (7), Peru (7), Spain (6), Italy (6) and France (4) stand out.
Recommandations: With the purpose of improving through recommendations for the correct management and refining of the DIRAC Contest, the wining projects must submit a final project implementation and management report, which includes a description of the activity carried out, that should indicate how the project performed, indicating the content, adecuate or inadecuate stage, quality of the attendees at the inauguration and during the exhibition period, interest shown by the public, among others.   In conclusion, there has been ongoing work towards improving the accountability process and the gathering of information on the impact of the funded projects.

Title EN: Annual International Convention
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture
SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Cultural and creative sectors
Agency Implementation: Fondazione Mondadori
Main Feature: Since 2022 FAAM has promoted an annual international conference to reflect on creativity and culture in relation to the themes of memory and its preservation and how these influence the development of cultural infrastructure, cities and active participation. What kind of cultural infrastructure do we need? What kind of space do we need to shape the identity of the city in order to promote community well-being through cultural participation? Libraries and archives are protagonists of this reflection, at a time when major projects are being implemented all over Europe. Yet the public perception of these spaces is full of contrasts, seemingly static and immobile in change. Libraries can decide to survive without being any more influential or they can try to survive by reinventing themselves, even redefining their influence. The idea of the conference, which aims to think about the cultural infrastructure of the future, as part of the well-being and quality of life system and the paradigm of human development, comes from these suggestions. Professionals from different fields - from philosophy to architecture, from economics to publishing, from art to neuroscience - will take part in the discussion. Thanks to the involvement of the City of Milan, the Lombardy Region, the Cariplo Foundation, BookCity Milano and leading Italian universities, FAAM has brought the debate on cultural aggregation, active participation and community well-being to the attention of the institutions.
Results: The organisation of an annual conference made it possible to create a network of debate with the institutions involved, also inviting policy makers to reflect and collaborate. At the conclusion of the conference Open City Book (2023) the Five Theses for the Libraries of the Future were presented 1. The library offers everyone an open, caring, inclusive, stimulating, welcoming, enabling space. The goal of libraries will not be enjoyment but participation through the vitality of services. The librarian is the trigger and activator of participation and vitality. 2. The library is the space of a regained time to be devoted to curiosity, to deepening, to cognitive and emotional development, to the articulation of slow thoughts and fast thoughts. Time is the most precious resource we have. 3. The library is a social organism that interacts with the environment, of which it is one of the components. It is a place that generates social ties and transforms the "space" of uncritical habit into the "place" of the possible. 4. The library has a social impact, it works to improve the quality of life of all people living in a place. It cannot do this on its own but in the systemic relationship with other realities, institutions and services operating in that same place. 5. The library produces culture. As a living organism, it is a generator of impulses, it offers space for new knowledge that arises from serendipity, from connections, from the unhinging of disciplinary boundaries that the library by its very nature generates. This work will give rise to a book that aims not only to preserve, by putting it in writing, that experience, but above all to mark a further step. The book is a further advance in what is being defined as a workshop of thought on the cultural infrastructure of the future, through the involvement of speakers from the conference as well as new voices.

Title EN: Appropriation de la Loi n° 2016-012 portant statut de l’artiste au Togo
Goal: Promote Human Rights And Fundamental Freedoms
SDG: SDG 5 - Achieve gender equality and empower all women and girls,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels
Area of Monitoring: Artistic freedom
Cultural Domain: Design,Performing Arts,Media Arts,Cinema and Audiovisual Arts,Music,Publishing,Visual Arts
Agency Implementation: Association Culture-Développement (CUL.DEV)
Main Feature: La mesure relative l'appropriation de la Loi N°2016-012 portant statut de l’artiste au Togo s'est traduite la conception et l'exécution du projet intitulé " Organisation de 05 ateliers régionaux regroupant 117 artistes des nouvelles Communes du Togo pour le renforcement de leurs capacités sur la Loi n° 2016-012 portant statut de l’artiste, pour une appropriation responsable afin de mieux orienter les politiques locales pour une pleine jouissance de leurs droits et un meilleur impact social national" Cette loi portant statut de l’artiste au Togo, promulguée en 2016, est destinée à professionnaliser les artistes et accroitre  leur contribution au développement socio-économique du pays en rapport avec la feuille de route gouvernementale du Togo 2025. Mais jusqu’ici, elle n'a pas été suffisamment vulgarisée ni opérationnalisée depuis son adoption.  La mesure comprend l'organisation de cinq ateliers régionaux qui consistent à informer les artistes sur les dispositions de la loi, à renforcer leurs compétences juridiques et à les préparer à plaider pour l'élaboration des textes réglementaires restants. Les artistes formés deviendront des ambassadeurs du statut de l'artiste, capables de sensibiliser et de mobiliser leurs pairs et les communautés locales pour la prise en compte du secteur culturel et créatif dans les plans de développement. Cette information sera publiée sous forme d’information de contact dans le rapport périodique et incluse dans la base de données de l’UNESCO. Les activités ont débuté en décembre 2023 avec des réunions préparatoires dans les chefs-lieux de région, impliquant les administrations communales et le ministère de la culture. Un lancement officiel de la politique a eu lieu à Lomé le 12 décembre 2023, avec une large couverture médiatique pour assurer la visibilité du projet. Le projet accorde une attention particulière à l'équité de genre, garantissant une participation équilibrée des hommes et des femmes parmi les 117 artistes sélectionnés.  En plus des ateliers, le projet prévoit des séances de suivi et d'évaluation pour mesurer l'impact des formations et identifier les besoins supplémentaires des artistes. La flexibilité et l'adaptabilité sont des principes clés de la mise en œuvre, permettant de répondre aux défis imprévus tels que les situations d'urgence. Le projet est financé par l'UNESCO dans le cadre du Programme Aschberg et s'inscrit dans les priorités globales de l'organisation en matière de promotion de la culture et de soutien aux artistes.
Results: À ce jour, cette politique d'appropriation de la loi portant statut de l'artiste a permis de réaliser les résultats suivants : - dix points focaux régionaux, cinq Directeurs régionaux des Arts et de la Culture et cinq Responsables culturels Communaux des cinq région sont désignés pour servir de relais en région , facilitant l'engagement des artistes bénéficiaires ;  - un total de 117 artistes issus des 117 Communes du Togo formés sur la Loi n° 2016-012 relative au statut de l’artiste ; - le grand public et les autorités locales sensibilisés à l'importance de la loi portant  statut de l'artiste ; - Un total de 1000 fascicules de 42 pages avec en préface l’extrait du discours du Ministre de la Culture et du Tourisme prononcé lors du Lancement le 12 Décembre 2023 et comprenant le recueil des textes organiques du Statut de l’artiste (Loi N° 2016-012 du 02 Juin 2016 et le Décret N° 2017-038/PR du23 Mars 2017) ont été produits ; - des kits pédagogiques et un accompagnement financier ont été remis aux artistes formés ;  - les artistes formés sont déployés comme Ambassadeurs du Statut de l’Artiste pour poursuivre et pérenniser les activités de sensibilisation dans leurs communautés ; - une participation équilibrée des hommes et des femmes a été assurée, contribuant ainsi à renforcer l'équité de genre en matière de développement culturel ;  -le projet a également favorisé une meilleure collaboration entre les artistes, les administrations communales et le ministère chargé de la culture, renforçant ainsi le réseau de soutien pour les initiatives culturelles ; -cinq documents de recommandations (un par région) ont été formulés sous forme de plaidoyer à l’endroit du ministre chargé de la culture, en vue de la signature rapide des 06 textes réglementaires en souffrance et qui freinent actuellement l’opérationnalisation complète de la Loi n°2016-012 - en outre, la mesure a contribué significativement à la réalisation des objectifs de la Convention de 2005, en soutenant des systèmes de gouvernance durables de la culture, en incluant la culture dans les cadres de développement durable des collectivités locales et en promouvant les droits de l'homme et les libertés fondamentales dans les secteurs culturels et créatifs.
Recommandations: Les organisations de la société civile (OSC) devraient se concentrer sur les priorités suivantes pour la mise en œuvre de la Convention durant les quatre prochaines années : -Renforcement des capacités et de la professionnalisation des artistes : Il est crucial de continuer à offrir des formations et des ressources aux artistes pour qu'ils comprennent, appliquent efficacement et jouissent pleinement des lois et réglementations culturelles. Cela permettra de professionnaliser davantage le secteur et de valoriser la contribution des artistes au développement socio-économique ; -Promotion de l'équité de genre et de l'inclusion sociale : Les OSC doivent garantir une participation équitable des femmes et des groupes marginalisés dans toutes les initiatives culturelles. L'équité de genre et l'inclusion sociale sont essentielles pour un développement culturel durable et équilibré ; -Plaidoyer pour des politiques culturelles efficaces : Les OSC devraient intensifier leurs efforts de plaidoyer auprès des gouvernements et des institutions pour l'élaboration et la mise en œuvre de politiques culturelles qui soutiennent les artistes et les industries créatives. Des textes réglementaires clairs et des mécanismes de soutien financier sont nécessaires pour favoriser un environnement propice à la créativité. En se concentrant sur ces priorités, les OSC pourront contribuer significativement à la réalisation des objectifs de la Convention, en soutenant des systèmes de gouvernance durables de la culture, en incluant la culture dans les cadres de développement durable, et en promouvant les droits de l'homme et les libertés fondamentales.

Title EN: Art Jameel creative initiatives

Area of Monitoring: Partnering with civil society
Agency Implementation: Art Jameel
Main Feature: Art Jameel, an independent organization dedicated to supporting artists and creative communities, has launched two significant initiatives aimed at promoting cultural diversity, sustainability, and artistic expression. These initiatives, "Down to Earth" and "Art Jameel Commissions: Arts Writing and Research," reflect a commitment to fostering a vibrant, inclusive, and sustainable cultural landscape in the UAE. The "Down to Earth" festival is free and open to the public. The festival aims to engage a wide audience with activities themed around botanical, sustainable, and eco-conscious living. It offers a diverse range of activities, including making workshops, tours, talks, and demonstrations. New interactive art installations and experiential performances are designed to educate and inspire participants about sustainable practices and eco-conscious living. By providing a platform for community interaction and learning, the festival promotes cultural and environmental awareness, encouraging participants of all ages to explore sustainable living through creative and interactive experiences. The "Art Jameel Commissions: Arts Writing and Research" program focuses on arts writing and research, supporting writers, critics, art historians, curators, and artists whose primary medium is writing. The program offers a three-month residency based at Jameel Arts Centre, Dubai, providing a supportive environment for developing innovative research and producing substantial writing projects. Open to participants from the Middle East, North Africa, Turkey, and those with meaningful connections to the region, the program’s jury, ensures a rigorous selection process. The thematic focuses include Confluence, inspired by the UAE’s role as an international meeting place; Museology, investigating contemporary modes of art production and exhibition making; and the GCC, exploring cultural narratives and experiences within the Gulf countries. The initiative aims to foster critical dialogue, support new creative works, and contribute to the broader development of cultural infrastructure, emphasizing the importance of innovative research and written material in evolving cultural discourse.
Results: Through these initiatives, Art Jameel continues to support and nurture the creative and cultural sectors, emphasizing sustainability, critical research, and international collaboration. These efforts contribute to the UAE’s vision of being a leading cultural hub, reflecting UNESCO's goals of promoting cultural diversity and sustainable development.
Recommandations: The positive reception and impact of the "Down to Earth" event at Jameel Arts Centre underlines the growing public interest in sustainability and environmental stewardship.

Il permet d’associer la création culturelle et artistique à la diffusion, en soutenant aussi bien les créateurs que les entreprises culturelles. Title EN: Arabic Language Summit 2022
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture
SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Cultural and creative sectors
Agency Implementation: Ministry of Culture. Abu Dhabi Arabic Language Centre. Department of Culture and Tourism – Abu Dhabi.
Main Feature: The Arabic Language Summit is an annual event designed to promote and celebrate the Arabic language's pivotal role in cultural identity and heritage. The Summit focuses on various aspects, including: •	Cultural Dialogue: Bringing together experts, academics, and cultural figures from across the Arab world and beyond to discuss the significance of the Arabic language in arts, literature, and science. •	Modernization and Preservation: Addressing contemporary challenges facing the Arabic language, such as integration in modern technology and media, and strategies for its preservation and promotion. •	Educational Impact: Examining the state of Arabic language education and proposing improvements to curricula and teaching methods. •	Creative Expressions: Highlighting the contributions of Arab poets, writers, and artists who use the Arabic language as a medium to express cultural and intellectual ideas. •	Workshops and Panels: Featuring sessions on topics such as the relationship between language and identity, the role of drama and arts in language promotion, and the future of the Arabic language in the digital age.
Results: The Summit has successfully fostered a deeper appreciation of the Arabic language, emphasizing its importance in cultural identity and intellectual heritage. It has brought attention to the need for modernizing Arabic language education and integrating it into contemporary media and technology. The event has also provided a platform for showcasing the work of Arab intellectuals and creatives, contributing to a renewed interest and pride in the Arabic language.
Recommandations: The evaluations emphasize the Summit's role in highlighting the Arabic language's cultural and intellectual significance. Recommendations include continuing to support initiatives that modernize Arabic language education, encourage creative expressions in Arabic, and foster cross-cultural dialogue. The Summit is also seen as a crucial platform for discussing the future of the Arabic language in a rapidly evolving global landscape.

Main Feature: Since 2022, Art Clubs have been implemented annually in public upper secondary education centers, a joint initiative of the National Administration of Public Education (ANEP), the National Directorate of Education and the National Directorate of Culture (the last two in the orbit of the Ministry of Education and Culture). These are four-month spaces that operate with a guiding teacher - selected through a public call - whose purpose is the presentation of an artistic proposal with a free theme and technique, starting from the creation of a show that can be performed in scene in a maximum of thirty minutes. In this, various artistic disciplines can be presented and integrated: theater, music, dance, circus, puppets, visual arts, audiovisual, etc. The proposals resulting from the Art Clubs are finally presented in instances open to the general public - held in different parts of the country - and with juries made up of prominent personalities in the artistic environment, whose task is to distinguish with first, second and third award to those shows that are considered outstanding based exclusively on their artistic quality and originality. The distinguished proposals are finally exhibited in a show with free admission and accessible to all audiences. In addition to the resources allocated for the remuneration of the guiding teachers and for the required materials, in the case of educational instances, the Art Clubs have access to training proposals on different artistic disciplines. During its period of operation, the National Institute of Performing Arts of the National Directorate of Culture makes available specific visits from theater, dance, circus or puppet teachers to advise the teams in achieving their creation and production objectives. Likewise, it enables interested students to apply for artistic training scholarships that the Ministry of Education and Culture contracts in member institutions of the Chamber of Artistic Education Schools of Uruguay.

Main Feature: The Swedish Arts Grants Committee launched the ArtNexus programme together with the Swedish International Development Cooperation Agency in 2020, commissioned by the Swedish government.  ArtNexus is an international cultural and development cooperation program with the aim to create synergies between cultural policy and international development cooperation initiatives. The programme’s objective is to strengthen the conditions and rights of artists and cultural practitioners in the programme’s partner countries Albania and Armenia.  The ArtNexus program aims to improve the conditions for artistic professionals to freely exercise and be able to make a living from their art, as part of increased democratization of the selected partner countries. Through education, public talks and advocacy and policy work, ArtNexus supports its partners in developing a strong art and culture sector.The overall objectives of the program are: •	 The public has access and ability to consume art •	Artists are empowered and have income security and self-reliance •	The national art scene enables local art and culture practitioners to operate nationally and internationally. By achieving these goals, the ArtNexus program will have contributed to a strengthened freedom of expression and increased democratization of the communities in which the program operated.
Results: ·	Approx. 300 cultural and creative professionals have received education in skills and knowledge essential for a career in the creative profession such as: IP-law, financial management for artists, promotion for artists, arts handling and shipping. ·	Approx. 45 actors have received education related to making art accessible to all, specifically covering disability inclusivity. ·	102 children in conflict affected regions in Armenia has been given access to arts education and a space to discuss human rights and democracy through art. ·	An online resource platform for Albanian creative professionals has been launched. The platform currently includes 35 publications, handbooks, podcasts and studies related to the artistic field in Albania and beyond, 33 of which have been produced by ArtNexus partners. Read more here: arca.al/en/toolbox/   ·	A new cultural policy strategy was adopted in Armenia, refencing the research and work of ArtNexus and local partner organization Katapult Creative Accelerator. Quote from the strategy:  •	Expanding cooperation with creative unions and public organizations operating in the Sector and creating conditions for the establishment of professional umbrella associations that will unite Armenian artists and creative unions. […] The proposal is based on the results of the research on the needs of the Creative Sector conducted by the Katapult Creative Accelerator Program, implemented by AGBU Armenia and funded by the EU. The establishment of the union is planned to be implemented within the cooperation framework of the Katapult Creative Accelerator Program and the Swedish ArtNexus Program.

Agency Implementation: Ethiopian Visual Artist Association
Main Feature: This impactful exhibition featured the work of 57 international artists and focused on Pan-African movements and soulful resistance. It provided a powerful platform for exploring and expressing resilience through art.  The symposium facilitated an exploration of cultural and historical narratives associated with the Nile, fostering cross-cultural artistic dialogue.  The exhibition showcased a wide range of artworks from international artists, emphasizing cultural impressions and the exchange of artistic perspectives. It offered a platform for artists to engage with Ethiopian audiences and present their work.  Unique anthology brought together poetry from Ethiopia and Romania, highlighting the rich literary traditions of both countries. The convergence of these poetic voices provided a deep cross-cultural dialogue through literature.  The inaugural Addis International Art Symposium marked a significant milestone in Ethiopia’s art scene. The event brought global artists to Addis Ababa, facilitating important discussions and showcasing their work to an international audience.  The Ethiopian  Visual Artist Association partnered with a dedicated artist whose commitment to inviting international artists and organizing major cultural events has significantly elevated the global profile of Ethiopian art.   Below is a summary of the major events 1. #NO MORE - Pan African Movements Soulful Resistance Venue: G.K. Desta Centre (Modern Arts Museum) 2. ORIGIN - International Arts Symposium 2023 3. The International Art Exhibition "Culture Impression" 4. Ethiopian & Romanian Poetry Converge in a Unique Anthology 5. The First Addis International Art Symposium
Results: #NO MORE - Pan African Movements Soulful Resistance: This exhibition featured 57 international artists and explored themes of Pan-Africanism and resistance, offering a platform for expressing resilience through art. It took place at the G.K. Desta Centre (Modern Arts Museum).  ORIGIN - International Arts Symposium 2023: This symposium focused on the cultural and historical narratives of the Nile, promoting cross-cultural artistic dialogue and showcasing global perspectives in art.  The International Art Exhibition "Culture Impression": This event displayed a wide range of artworks from international artists, emphasizing cultural impressions and facilitating artistic exchanges with Ethiopian audiences.  Ethiopian & Romanian Poetry Converge in a Unique Anthology: This anthology combines poetry from Ethiopia and Romania, highlighting the rich literary traditions and fostering a deep cross-cultural dialogue through literature.  The First Addis International Art Symposium: This landmark event brought global artists to Addis Ababa, marking a significant milestone in Ethiopia’s art scene and showcasing international art to a broader audience.  Contribution of Artist Tamirat Siltan: Siltan played a crucial role in promoting Ethiopian art on the global stage, organizing events and inviting foreign artists. His efforts have led to the inclusion of Ethiopian artworks in the Addis Ababa Museum for the first time.

Title EN: Art, gender, and digital environments
Goal: Promote Human Rights And Fundamental Freedoms
SDG: SDG 5 - Achieve gender equality and empower all women and girls,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels
Area of Monitoring: Gender equality
Cultural Domain: Design,Performing Arts,Media Arts,Cinema and Audiovisual Arts,Music,Publishing,Visual Arts
Agency Implementation: Karisma Foundation, Artists at Risk (Finland)
Main Feature: The Karisma Foundation held, together with Cartel Urbano and Artists at Risk, workshops in the city of Bogotá, with female artists from Latin America. For the development of these workshops, the foundation presented the results of the research carried out during the years 2022 and 2023 on cultural rights in digital environments and spoke with the women artists about the challenges they face in a context of high digitalization of their artistic and creative work. Within the framework of this participation, the Karisma Foundation presented the progress of research about to be published, which in an exploratory manner has reviewed human rights violations on the Internet, especially in relation to the right to freedom of artistic expression on the Internet. This research, which served as input for the workshop, also included an exercise of collecting testimonies from Colombian artists and artists' organizations that had suffered some type of censorship by the content moderation and curation practices carried out by digital platforms in which they share their creations and artistic content.
Results: Due to the workshops, experiences of women artists from the Latin American region were collected and practices that hinder the exercise of freedom of artistic expression on the Internet were analyzed. Likewise, valuable information was shared with the women artists to identify the scenarios in which the content moderation carried out by the platforms implies a violation of human rights and the cases in which it is possible to make an appeal to the digital platforms. Finally, due to the workshops, women artists were also provided with a series of digital safety recommendations to protect themselves from gender-based violence in digital environments. Over 30 women artists from Latin America attended this workshop.

Title EN: Artistic Residency Program for Artists from Belarus
Goal: Promote Human Rights And Fundamental Freedoms
SDG: SDG 5 - Achieve gender equality and empower all women and girls,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels
Area of Monitoring: Artistic freedom
Agency Implementation: The Zbigniew Raszewski Theatre Institute
Main Feature: The Artistic Residency Program for artists from Belarus, initiated in 2021, was a response to the dramatic situation of Belarusian artists related to the ongoing political crisis in the country. The aim of the program was to enable residents to work creatively by implementing a specific project or looking for new inspirations under the artistic supervision of Polish theaters and other cultural institutions, as well as to create conditions for establishing permanent cooperation between Polish cultural organizations/institutions (and their teams) and representatives theater competitions from Belarus. In addition to the possibility of maintaining the artistic work, the Program also guaranteed a package of activities providing support in the field of communication (an intensive and individualized Polish language course), psychological well-being (individual and group consultations for victims of the regime), as well as a series of workshops and training in the field of legal and formal, acquiring grants, self-presentation
Results: In the years 2021-2023, over 200 people were qualified to participate in the program, and 186 artists forced to work outside Belarus took advantage of it.  More than 100 Polish cultural institutions spread over 12 Polish cities expressed their willingness to accept Belarusian residents to their teams. In the years 2021-2023, thanks to the Program, performative projects of high artistic value were carried out in over 30 Polish theaters by creators of independent Belarusian culture. Several of them participated in international festivals and shows. Thanks to an intensive language course and substantive, legal and psychological support provided to them by the Theater Institute, the residents of the Program have the opportunity to stay in Poland and work related to their profession.
Recommandations: The evaluation showed great potential for intercultural rapprochement resulting from the Program. The opportunity for cooperation and exchange of experiences between Polish and Belarusian theater people was appreciated.  The recommendations focused on developing the training component so that residents could achieve independence faster in the previously unknown formal and cultural realities of Poland/European Union

The main emphasis in the program is placed on comprehensive projects, implemented outside the standard framework of the applicants' current educational activities, distinguished by an original, coherent concept that takes into account innovative ideas, both in terms of teaching methodology and the subject of the classes. The tasks enable students to have direct contact with top-class teachers and authorities. Interdisciplinary projects are co-financed - strengthening cooperation between different types of schools - enabling the exchange of experiences in order to create a coherent educational offer. Title EN: ARTISTIC NATIONAL ENCOUNTERS TO PROMOTE INTERCULTURAL DIALOGUE OF CHILDREN AND YOUTH THROUGH THE PRACTICE OF DIFFERENT ARTISTIC EXPRESSIONS OF NATIVE INDIGENOUS AND AFRO-BOLIVIAN PEOPLE
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture

Area of Monitoring: Cultural and creative sectors
Agency Implementation: MINISTERIO DE CULTURA, DESCOLONIZACIÓN Y DESPATRIARCALIZACIÓN (MINISTRY OF CULTURE, DECOLONIZATION AND DEPATRIARCHALIZATION)
Main Feature: The main purpose of this measure is to promote a meaningful dialogue between generations within the artistic and cultural world, placing special emphasis on children and adolescents, who represent the creative and social future of the country.  The aim is not only for these new generations to acquire tools and knowledge through artistic training meetings, but also to provide them with a space for the exploration and expression of their identity, talents and world views. These meetings focus on technical development in disciplines such as music, dance and visual arts, but are also aimed at strengthening values such as respect for cultural diversity, cooperation and empathy.  As part of the priority objectives, the full exercise of human rights, equal opportunities and social justice will be promoted through art, using music, dance and other cultural expressions as powerful ways to raise people's awareness of the importance of a more just and inclusive society. Art becomes a very important and strong medium to address social issues and generate a positive impact on the community, inviting reflection, dialogue and social transformation.
Results: Nine intercultural and intergenerational meetings were held in different cities of the Plurinational State of Bolivia, attracting more than 1,800 participants and direct beneficiaries. More than 1,000 children benefited from artistic training workshops in different cities of the Plurinational State of Bolivia. The creation of more than 30 exponents of Bolivian music with social content has been promoted in the two versions of the contest held to date, making visible their work that promotes the fight for the rights and dignity of the Bolivian people. The development of Cultural Industries has been contributed to by allowing contestants to emerge and generate economic movement with their art by making their work visible on a national platform. The participation of male and female artists has been equitable and has been framed within the strategic guidelines of the Ministry of Cultures, Decolonization and Depatriarchalization. Some 21,000 members of the public have been indirect beneficiaries. 60 professional musicians benefited from the event. 20 sound technicians and engineers benefited from the project.

In order to develop the artistic potential, we have collaborated with agencies and producers to develop a balance between local and international artists.  We have sought to boost the programming by inviting artists from different corners of the world to perform: India, China, Uk, France, South Africa, Senegal ,Madagascar, Germany, Switzerland, Hungary, Australia, Spain, Japan, Singapore, USA, Russia and islands of the Indian Ocean region. There have been several masterclasses conducted with local artists as well as some residences in a bid to create projects that are then staged in the theatre.  The genres have differed too: piano classical concerts, orchestra and chamber music, jazz concerts, Theatre, Dance and Magic shows. We have also started developing our Fine Arts department and have hosted a number of artists in our 2 galleries.
Results: This has helped to bring in new audiences. Artists with international reputation help to drive audiences and so, through such shows and performances, many have discovered the theatre and the arts centre. This also helps young learners of music and arts to develop a certain benchmark/level that they aspire to achieve.  Collaborations with local artists have been very successful. There have been artistic collaborations and workshops/masterclasses and these have received positive responses from local artists. This endeavour was driven by the need for capacity building.

Main Feature: The National Institute of Fine Arts and Literature (INBAL) aims to support the cultural and creative sectors while promoting the diversity of cultural expressions on a national scale. To achieve this, INBAL has strengthened its national vocation through collaborations and co-productions with various states of the Mexican Republic, tailored to their existing premises and capacities. These efforts encompass a range of artistic activities, workshops, conferences, discussions, and exchanges of best practices.
Results: From 2019 to 2023, INBAL has organized over 2,500 cultural activities across Mexico, fostering artistic expression and promoting cultural diversity. These initiatives span various regions and artistic disciplines, showcasing the richness of Mexico’s cultural heritage.  Key Highlights:  1.	National Theater Show: A showcase of theatrical excellence featuring national and international productions. 2.	Festival of Monologues – Theater with a Single Voice: Celebrating the power of solo performances. 3.	Great Theater Marathon for Girls, Boys, and Young People: Engaging young audiences through theater. 4.	National Dance Meeting: A platform for dance artists to collaborate and present their work. 5.	Chapultepec National Circuit of Performing Arts Call: Focused on dance and self-managed spaces. 6.	Fine Arts Everywhere: Expanding INBAL’s music initiatives to states across Mexico (since 2023). 7.	“Manuel Enríquez” International New Music Forum: A forum for contemporary music exploration. 8.	Fine Arts Literature Awards: Recognizing outstanding literary achievements. 9.	Catalog of Artistic Groups and Exhibitions: Disseminating information about artists and exhibitions to each state and relevant institutions. INBAL recognizes the cultural rights of the population and actively collaborates with independent and state artistic communities. Notably, the states with the highest activity levels during these five years are Guanajuato, State of Mexico, Jalisco, Michoacán, and Veracruz. While over 70% of the activities were in-person collaborations, the remaining 27% were virtual due to the pandemic (with 2020 and 2021 witnessing a surge in online events).  Across different states, specific artistic disciplines have flourished: •	Theater: Campeche, Jalisco, and Colima. •	Dance: Baja California Sur, San Luis Potosí, and Sinaloa. •	Music: Yucatán, Sonora, and Puebla. •	Opera: Nuevo León, Guerrero, and Sonora. •	Literature: Tabasco, Hidalgo, and Tlaxcala. •	Visual Arts: Oaxaca, Chihuahua, and Aguascalientes.  INBAL’s commitment to cultural enrichment remains steadfast, fostering creativity and artistic dialogue nationwide
