Agency Implementation: CSO NAME: Tajalla for music and arts                  EMAIL: info@tajalla.com                       PHONE:   065511007  CSO NAME: Medearts                                           EMAIL: info@medearts.org                   PHONE: +962777123456
Main Feature: Tahalofat  Al-Rass (Al-Rass Alliance) is a joint cultural project between Tajalla for Music and Arts and the Medeart Network. Tahalofat Al-Rass seeks to enhance forms of cultural research and create a state of solidarity among Jordanian cultural and artistic institutions. It also seeks to contribute to enhancing mutual learning, benefiting from existing experiences, and learning about pioneering cultural models from Jordan and the Arab region. This study comes within the Tahalofat  Al-Rass (Al-Rass Alliance) project implemented by Tajalla for Music and Arts and the Medeart Network with the support of the Cultural Resources Foundation. This study was worked on for six consecutive months, during which the methodological and implementation structure for it was designed, and then the research project was launched at multiple levels, starting with an extensive review of the legislative literature in the field of culture at the global level, the Arab world, and international legislation, and then based on the most important things we found. . In the context of cultural rights, welfare and development in cultural industries, a guide has been designed to conduct focus sessions with diverse groups of cultural actors and officials at the country level. Sessions were held in the south, north, and center of the Kingdom that attempted to monitor the most important ongoing interactions between cultural actors, the cultural legislation system, and cultural institutions. These sessions were accompanied by a series of in-depth personal interviews with legal and cultural experts. The research then concluded with broad comparisons between the best practices and desired functions of cultural organization and cultural work itself, on the one hand, and between the cultural legislative and institutional structure in Jordan and its position in relation to those practices. The best international standards and the extent to which cultural work achieves its goals. This study adopted the position that culture is a cross-sectoral function, and considers it a basis for achieving stability and advancing development. Hence, the study interacted in all its analyzes with culture contextually, taking into account its transcendent role, so it delved into the meanings carried by the legislative text instead of merely standing still. With regard to legislation and institutional structure from a technical standpoint, that is, the study attempted to monitor the extent of the effectiveness of the legislative system and the institutional situation in raising the efficiency of cultural work and pushing it towards achieving its goals and completing its meaning, and involving this in the societal and institutional mind in a way that achieves society’s stability and identity, and pushes and qualifies it for development and progress on various levels. Levels.  The initiative focuses on monitoring the effectiveness of the legislative system and institutional structure in enhancing cultural work. It aims to push towards achieving societal stability, identity, and development on various levels. The study emphasizes the importance of active participation in shaping society's future through legislative text and institutional arrangements. The study is divided into two main sections: Section One: Cultural Legislation In this section, we examine the cultural legislation in Jordan. This includes identifying the laws that regulate or directly impact cultural activities and their locations, according to the institutions responsible for their implementation. We also evaluate these legislations based on Jordanian legal standards, the experiences of cultural practitioners, and by comparing them with cultural practices in the Arab world and globally. Despite the lack of a definitive document outlining best legislative or administrative practices for organizing cultural work, our initial evaluation aimed to extract insights from various global and regional legislations to establish a reference framework for assessing Jordanian cultural laws. Section Two: Cultural Institutions This section highlights the importance of cultural institutions in organizing cultural activities and their expected roles. We analyze the major cultural institutions in Jordan, discussing their roles, effectiveness, and integration with each other. This analysis is based on the roles defined by law, strategies, and plans they set for themselves, or their expected roles in the organizational process. We have initiated the development of an online platform for our research. This platform aims to provide a convenient and user-friendly interface where all relevant information about our research will be easily accessible. In addition to the digital platform, following the completion of the study, we plan to launch a comprehensive awareness campaign at both local and regional levels. This campaign will present the study's findings in a clear and simplified manner, targeting the general public, artists, and cultural sector workers. The goal is to enhance understanding of the cultural landscape and its legislation through a series of messages disseminated via social media and a podcast series.
Results: The study on cultural regulation and institutions in Jordan is anticipated to yield several impactful consequences, extensively influencing the cultural sector. The key predicted outcomes are mentioned as follows:  Comprehensive Analysis of Current Cultural Legislation: This analysis will illustrate how those laws have an effect on cultural work and the institutions responsible for their implementation. By presenting a detailed review, the study will enable stakeholders to comprehend the current legal framework and its implications for cultural activities.   Identification of Strengths and Weaknesses: The study will highlight the strengths and weaknesses within the present-day legislative and institutional framework of the cultural sector. This evaluation will shed light on regions in which the system excels and in which it falls quickly, presenting possibilities to improve overall performance and boost effectiveness in the cultural field. Understanding those elements is critical for driving enhancements and fostering a more supportive environment for cultural endeavors.  Providing a Vision for the Next Generation Interested in Cultural Work: The study will provide a complete image of the cultural sector, detailing the relevant legislation and the present-day cultural landscape. These records could be invaluable for the next generation, assisting them to to produce content that aligns with current laws and suggesting campaigns to amend guidelines that won't shape their desires. By doing so, the study goals contribute to the continued development of the cultural sector, ensuring its growth and evolution.  Development of an Online Platform:  As part of the study's implementation, an online platform is developed. This platform aims to provide easy access to the research findings, recommendations, and other relevant information. The platform is intended to be freely available to all, promoting transparency and community involvement ,allowing for the sharing of facts and ideas among cultural actors and the general public. By improving transparency and community participation, the platform will play an extensive role in the improvement of the cultural sector.  Launch of an Awareness Campaign: Targeted at the overall public and mainly at artists and cultural workers, this campaign will help everyone apprehend the cultural landscape and its law in Jordan. The awareness  campaign aims to boost public engagement and knowledge about cultural issues and legal guidelines.  Enhancing Cultural Stability and Identity: The study reinforces cultural stability and identity through the enhancement of cultural regulation and establishments. By doing so, it seeks to make improvements that contribute to sustainable and complete improvement across numerous sectors.

This workshop, conducted in collaboration with UNESCO and SIDA, This workshop aimed to equip women visual artists with the tools and knowledge to thrive in the modern, digital art landscape and advocate for gender equality in the cultural and creative sectors. The workshop targeted 50 professional Ethiopian female visual artists, aiming to equip them with cutting-edge knowledge and tools to advance in the evolving art world and foster greater gender equality in the cultural and creative sectors. The workshop has raised awareness among Ethiopian female visual artists about gender equality issues within the cultural and creative sectors, encouraging greater advocacy and participation in discussions on these topics. Title EN: CDEA’s Creative Economy Incubator and Accelerator Initiative  for Animation Film and Fashion Design
Goal: Integrate Culture In Sustainable Development Frameworks
SDG: SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: National sustainable development policies and plans
Agency Implementation: Culture and Development East Africa (CDEA)
Main Feature: CDEA’s Creative Economy Incubator & Accelerator Programme is a platform that empowers creative entrepreneurs to implement their artistic and business ideas. Its niche is youth and women artisans and creative enterprises in the audio-visual and design industries, in the early stages of artistic development or market entry.  Since its launch in the year 2016, the Incubator has had activities that involve technical and business skills development provided to youth and women artisans from communities with rich biodiversity and fashion designers to make versatile products using traditional and modern skills for jewellery, leather, and hand-woven products.  Project aim and objectives:  CDEA’s creative economy incubator & accelerator  Initiative’s main objective is to promote inclusive economic growth for youth and women artisans and fashion designers through sustainable tourism and export trade.  In 2022, CDEA received a grant  TZS 463, 359, 000 to implement  the CDEA’s Creative Economy Incubator & Accelerator Programme between April 1, 2022 and April 30, 2024.   CDEA's Creative Economy Incubation and Accelerator Initiative aimed to provide industry skills for 10 Tanzanian   and 10 Ugandan fashion brands and 5 women in animation selected from East African countries with support from the Ignite Culture programme with funding support from The European Commission and capacity building support from HEVA Fund  and the British Council  The project began on April 1, 2022 and ended on April 30, 2024. CDEA provided overall project management and Monitoring and Evaluation (M&E) support for the project in Tanzania. CDEA  also provided business development training to the fashion brands. CDEA worked in partnership with other organizations in the two value chains ( animation film and fashion design) to achieve two goals aligned to two of the grant objectives namely: 1. Building appropriate, industry-ready skills and capacity for young people entering the creative and cultural sectors. 2. Improving the visual literacy of audiences, the visibility of makers and access to new markets for creative and cultural goods and services from Eastern Africa.
Results: What are the results achieved so far through the implementation of the measure/initiative? (400 words) Animation Film The Let Your Voices Roar project  had 3 segments namely:  The orientation  animation training of  8 women animators from Tanzania (4 from mainland  and 1 from Zanzibar);  5 women animators ( 3 from mainland, 1 from Zanzibar and 1 from Uganda) were then selected to move on to the incubation phase;  and later the acceleration  phases of the project. The project ended with the 5 women animators being provided with an Apple laptop sand software by the Ladima Foundation, so that they continue with their creativity.   The project was implemented as a collaboration between CDEA, the Ladima Foundation, the African Animation Network (AAN), Kwetu International Animation Festival (KIAFF), Naota Studios – a digital arts company (Kenya) and Creatures Animation Studio (Uganda).  Fashion design The project had three segments namely: training, incubation and acceleration. The project focused on providing technical and business skills development to 10 fashion brands in Tanzania. This information was packaged into an online e-learning platform and has been accessed by 557 fashion students in Dar es Salaam. In addition, the project hired a workshop space where the 10 brands and their in-house tailors would get training and also use the tailoring facilities to perfect their skills.  Other support service producers who were trained include Marketers and graphics designers who contribute to the fashion brands visibility. The project is still ongoing. The key implementation partners are: CDEA, Naledi Dream Centre , 360 Creative Hub, Endelea, Ndoto Hub and Sanaabiz. The acceleration project involves offering market linkages to the 10 fashion brands in Tanzania and 10 fashion brands in Uganda through Sanaabiz.shop. As part of providing market linkages for the 10 fashion brands in Tanzania, CDEA decided to organize a fashion and artisan fair that would bring the designers and their products closer to the domestic market in Dar es Salaam.   The Ghana Expo 2024 -Tanzania provided a suitable platform CDEA’s Fashion & ArtiSAN Fair to connect an intra-African platform by enabling the fashion designers and artisans to: Access new markets, networking opportunities, learning opportunities, product showcase and cultural exchange.   The maiden edition of the Ghana Trade Expo was held in Nairobi, Kenya, in East Africa in 2023. Ghana selected Tanzania to host its second Market Entry Expedition under the African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA) agreement from January 24- 28, 2024. This Expo was organized by Ghana National Coordinating office for AfCFTA and the Minister for Industry and Trade, United Republic of Tanzania.  CDEA was invited by the Ghana AfCFTA National Coordination Office to co-create the creative programme that was held on January 27, 2024. The programme had a showcase component, where seven fashion designers and artisans were among the 20 Tanzanian businesses showcased their products at the 5-day market entry expedition at Mlimani City Conference Centre from 24th-28th January 2024.  A panel discussion was held under the topic: Connect, Trade, and Collaborate: Reconstructing the Narrative of Africa's Creative Economy, a side event with stakeholders of the creative economy this event highlighted the connection between the creative economy and the AfCFTA and a  fashion show  showcased the  creativity of Tanzanian and Ghanaian Garment and Textiles.

Title EN: Cervantino International Festival
Goal: Achieve A Balanced Flow Of Cultural Goods And Services And Increase The Mobility Of Artists And Cultural Professionals
SDG: SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 10 - Reduce inequality within and among countries,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development

Cultural Domain: Design,Performing Arts,Media Arts,Cinema and Audiovisual Arts,Music,Visual Arts
Agency Implementation: General Directorate of Promotion and Cultural Festivals (DGPFC). Ministry of Culture.
Main Feature: The International Cervantino Festival (FIC), organized by the Ministry of Culture of the Government of Mexico, stands as the foremost cultural gathering in Mexico and Latin America. It ranks among the four most significant festivals of its kind globally. Held annually during October, the festival brings together a diverse array of national and international artists and groups, showcasing a rich tapestry of cultural expressions. These include music, opera, theater, dance, visual arts, literature, audiovisual media, and academic forums.  The festival takes place in the city of Guanajuato, fostering the mobility of artists and cultural professionals at both national and international levels. This federal government initiative collaborates with various governmental tiers, public institutions, and private organizations. Its primary aim is to engage the general public by designing diverse programming with accessible costs. Additionally, the festival offers a wide range of free artistic activities in street settings within public squares. It caters to specific audiences through presentations for children, master classes for students and artists, and other targeted events.  Among its core objectives are bridging artistic expressions to diverse audiences, contributing to a more inclusive society marked by plurality and empathy. The festival also serves as a platform for promoting national creativity, providing stages for both domestic and foreign artists. Furthermore, it seeks to distribute and equalize cultural wealth, cultivate new audiences based on varied interests, and underscore the profound relevance of art in society.
Results: In 2020, in response to the COVID-19 pandemic, the Cervantino International Festival adapted to the prevailing circumstances by hosting a virtual edition. This innovative approach involved participation from 12 countries, featuring delayed live broadcasts and experimentation with new online media formats. The festival provided a rich cultural experience entirely free of charge.  In 2023, “Historical Collection” of the Cervantino International Festival was established. Its purpose is to safeguard and preserve documents of historical, aesthetic, or testimonial significance related to the festival’s history. By doing so, it upholds the fundamental human right of access to culture and information. The collection serves as a repository accessible to the public, offering a virtual space for consultation. Within this repository, visitors can explore audiovisual collections spanning over 50 years of the Cervantino International Festival. Title EN: Challenges of cultural management and copyright in digital environments
Goal: Promote Human Rights And Fundamental Freedoms
SDG: SDG 5 - Achieve gender equality and empower all women and girls,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels
Area of Monitoring: Artistic freedom
Cultural Domain: Design,Performing Arts,Media Arts,Cinema and Audiovisual Arts,Music,Publishing,Visual Arts
Agency Implementation: Fundación Karisma, Creative Commons (United States)
Main Feature: The project was carried out with the financing of a grant awarded to the Karisma Foundation by Creative Commons, an international non-profit organization that promotes the action of sharing and the use of creativity and knowledge through free and legal instruments. The developed project aimed to unite the main actors within the GLAM community (Galleries, Libraries, Archives and Museums) at the local, district and national level to understand their main needs derived from: (a) the integration of new technologies in the daily operations of GLAMs as cultural managers at district and national levels, and the resulting implications for the national copyright system; and (b) the challenges faced by local communities in safeguarding their traditional cultural heritage. To this end, workshops were held at the national level with the main GLAMs of five cities and districts of the national territory and a methodology was designed for dialogue and collection of experiences from the institutions in charge of cultural management. Likewise, the existing exceptions and limitations that protect and promote the work of GLAMs and access to information, culture and knowledge in Colombia were made known. But, the conversation was also opened with the GLAMs to review what exceptions and limitations could be useful and are necessary for the development of cultural management activities in highly digitalized contexts such as the current ones.
Results: As a result, the project designed a collaborative dialogue methodology between stakeholders. The key findings have been presented as a roadmap for the library, archives, and museum community, accompanied by a series of recommendations designed to improve the capabilities of decision-makers. The document of systematization and collection of information on the experience is about to be published by the Karisma Foundation and is expected to serve as input for the debate to be carried out on the expansion of flexibilities to copyright before the National Directorate of Copyright. The experiences collected in the framework of the workshops highlight the need to comply with the public hearing contemplated in article 17 of Law 1915 of 2018 and provide arguments in favor of making modifications to the legislation that protects cultural rights, of access to the diversity of cultural expressions of Colombian citizens in digital environments.

Title EN: Chester Beatty Equality, Diversity and Inclusion (EDI) Policy
Goal: Promote Human Rights And Fundamental Freedoms
SDG: SDG 5 - Achieve gender equality and empower all women and girls,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels
Area of Monitoring: Gender equality
Agency Implementation: Chester Beatty
Main Feature: Describe the main features of the policy/measure:  The Chester Beatty is one of Ireland’s National Cultural Institutions, which receives Government funding and support. It promotes the appreciation and understanding of world cultures with holdings of manuscripts, rare books, and other treasures from Europe, the Middle East, North Africa and Asia.  A new Equality, Diversity and Inclusion (EDI) Policy was approved by the Trustees in February 2023, having been guided by the requirements of Section 42 of the Irish Human Rights and Equality Commission Act 2014. Throughout the year, a number of civic festivals supporting EDI were marked, including International Women’s Day (March), Bealtaine (May) and Pride (June).  The museum also engaged with Places of Sanctuary Ireland – a network of groups in towns, cities and local communities with the objectives of promoting a culture of welcome and inclusiveness, so that wherever people seeking sanctuary go they will feel safe, find people who welcome them, and understand why they are here. The resulting project at the Chester Beatty was co-ordinated by this organisation – linked to the wider City of Sanctuary movement – and the Education Authority of Northern Ireland. Young students from ten schools awarded with the title Schools of Sanctuary (five in Northern Ireland and five in Ireland) travelled to the Chester Beatty in May to explore the collections as well as meet Sanctuary Ambassadors. These ambassadors brought objects from their countries and explored their cultural heritage with the students, with the event being supported by the Department of Foreign Affairs.  Also in 2023, Faiths in Focus – an inter-faith dialogue initiative, enabled the exploration of objects from the Chester Beatty with members of the Dublin City Interfaith Forum (DCIF). Working in collaboration with DCIF, faith-based communities selected objects from the museum’s collections and explored what they meant to them, sharing their thoughts and experiences in a series of ten-minute films. These films were showcased online during National Heritage Week in August and the project was supported by the Heritage Council.  Audio-descriptive training was provided to staff in 2023, with the purpose of integrating it into museum tours and other public programme activities.  Health and Wellbeing at the Chester Beatty Throughout 2023, the Chester Beatty's Health and Wellbeing programme continued, providing a blend of onsite and online events designed to enhance the physical, mental, and emotional wellbeing of its participants.  The Conversations on Art initiative, a dementia-friendly programme, remained popular, offering engaging and accessible art discussions that cater to individuals with dementia. Additionally, the Slow Art Tour and Meditation series, introduced in the previous year, continued to attract participants interested in exploring art at a leisurely pace, combined with meditation practices to enhance mindfulness and relaxation.  International Yoga Day was celebrated on 24 June with a session that combined gentle yoga and meditation, and the monthly Qigong sessions held in the Rooftop Garden remained a popular feature, drawing attendees to experience a traditional Chinese meditation practice.  The Teen Wellbeing programme, supported by funding from the City of Dublin Youth Service Board, continued in 2023. A popular component of this initiative was the Nature Nurtures workshop, a two-day event specially designed for teenagers. This workshop emphasised the importance of the natural world and explored the multitude of benefits it offers for mental and physical wellbeing.

Title EN: CINeDUCATION Programme: Promoting Film Education among youth

Area of Monitoring: Cultural and creative sectors
Agency Implementation: A.E.I. Audiovisual Forum
Main Feature: The Non-Profit Cultural Organization A.E.I AUDIOVISUAL FORUM was founded in 2019 with the aim to organize cultural events and film education programmes for children, young people and professionals in the field of audiovisual production in Cyprus and abroad. Since 2018, the Organisation collaborates with the Cyprus National Commission for UNESCO to provide capacity building workshops for young people (in secondary or higher education institutions), for the production of short films on topics related to history and cultural heritage. The workshops are facilitated by archaeologists and professional film-makers, who provide training on the basic techniques to produce documentaries. The research and production of the films is entirely implemented by students. So far, more than 80 films have been produced through the program. All films are screened publicly during the annual festival and compete for 3 awards and a special award, funded by the National Commission, for the best student film about cultural and/or natural heritage of Cyprus. CINeDUCATION is recognized as an innovative programme of non-formal education subsidized by the Deputy Ministry of Culture, the Cyprus National Commission for UNESCO, and the Cyprus Radio Television Authority.
Results: CINEDUCATION has reached more than 1200 high school students, 200 university students and 200 teachers and university professors, enabling them to acquire skills in film production and especially in the documentary genre. Furthermore some of these films have been broadcast in Cyprus (CyBC) and Greece (COSMOTE HISTORY CHANEL) and participated in other film festivals.  The experience gained through this educational programme has laid the foundations to further develop the programme through synergies with similar organisations in other countries, to collaborate on film education for youth.

Main Feature: *Cultural domain covered by the measure: Culture and creative sectors          Main aims: recommendations for a unified pan-European and specifically tailored programme of measures to reinforce the innovative potential of the cultural and creative industries for the long term; maintaining strong structures for European dialogue (particularly in light of Brexit).  Target groups: European stakeholders, including from the UK, involved in the governance of the cultural and creative industries (in politics or administration at the European, federal or Land levels, and adjacent structures such as stakeholder groups, working groups/committees, federal, Land and international support structures for the sector, and foundations), academics, stakeholders of the cultural and creative industries.           Expected results:   •	Generating new knowledge about the cultural and creative industries, their impact and their potential for innovation, so that better evidence-based political strategies, measures and conditions can be put in place (“creative impact”) •	Gaining insights into and fostering (social and cultural) entrepreneurship in the sector by conducting 13 entrepreneurial innovation processes  •	Exploring and formulating recommendations for better governance structures in the realm of funding •	Building a network structure and lasting collaborations with academics, businesspeople, creatives and relevant experts •	Deriving insights from examining and comparing (political) strategies and parameters in the set-up of research and development structures and support programmes for the cultural and creative industries in the UK, Europe and Germany •	Drawing up a work plan or strategy paper with findings and recommendations for better support for the cultural and creative industries in Germany and Europe

Title EN: Circulation of Colombian authors, editors, and other cultural managers at regional and international book fairs.
Goal: Achieve A Balanced Flow Of Cultural Goods And Services And Increase The Mobility Of Artists And Cultural Professionals
SDG: SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 10 - Reduce inequality within and among countries,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Mobility of artists and cultural professionals
Agency Implementation: National Library, Ministry of Cultures, Arts, and Knowledge
Main Feature: The circulation strategy of Colombian authors, editors, and other cultural managers in regional and international book fairs, where the National Library and the Ministry of Culture, Arts, and Knowledge are present or supported, more than 24 national and 5 international fairs per year.                  In this framework, depending on the context and characteristics of each fair (size, region in which it takes place, etc.), a specific number of writers, booksellers, editors, or artists from different parts of the country are decided, with the purpose of supporting their mobility at a national or international level, guaranteeing their participation in the socialization of their work in spaces such as discussions and conferences and/or artistic presentations.                   As selection criteria, the National Library takes into account gender parity, balance between the different regions of Colombia, balance between commercial and independent publishing houses, and balance between commercial and independent bookstores.
Results: With this measure, in the last four years, the circulation of approximately 200 Colombian writers, 40 editors, 20 booksellers, and at least 60 musicians has been achieved. In the context of the current government, we have achieved a greater international presence and hence author mobilization. For 2023, Colombia was the guest of honor at the Havana International Book Fair (Cuba), at the Venezuela International Book Fair, and in 2024 at the Santa Cruz de la Sierra International Book Fair (Bolivia), at the Quito International Book Fair (Ecuador), and at the Sao Paulo Book Biennial. For each fair, around 20 authors, 5 editors, and 2 booksellers, and at least 12 artists were mobilized.                   1.	For 2020, the resources allocated for this first measure were COP$232,900,000 for the Bogotá International Book Fair. This year, invitations to be the guest of honor were not accepted because it was the year the Covid-19 pandemic began.          2.	For 2021, COP$465,045,000 were invested, which allowed the circulation of authors at the Bogotá International Book Fair, and support for regional book fairs in Colombia.          3.	For 2022, COP$1,200,000,000 was invested in Colombia's presence as a guest country at the Seoul Book Fair. Likewise, COP$195,000,000 were invested in supporting regional fairs in Colombia.          4.	For 2023, COP$700,000,000 were invested for the presence of the guest country of honor at the Havana Book Fair (Cuba), COP$700,000,000 for the presence of the guest country at the Venezuela International Book Fair, COP$200,000,000 for the organization of fairs in remote regions of the country, and COP$449,000,000 in support of regional fairs.          5.	For 2024, COP$400,000,000 will be invested in the presence of Colombia as a guest country of honor at the International Book Fair of Santa Cruz de la Sierra, COP$400,000,000 in the presence of Colombia as a guest country of honor at the International Book Fair of the Quito Book, COP$1,200,000,000 will be invested in the presence of Colombia as a guest country of honor at the Sao Paulo Book Biennial, COP$880,000,000 will be invested in supporting regional fairs in the country, and COP$300,000,000 in the creation of fairs in remote areas of Colombia.

Title EN: ÉCOLE DE LA DEUXIÈME CHANCE
Goal: Integrate Culture In Sustainable Development Frameworks
SDG: SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: National sustainable development policies and plans
Agency Implementation: Ministère de l'Enseignement Technique, de la Formation Professionnelle et de l'Apprentissage
Main Feature: L'École de la Deuxième Chance de Côte d'Ivoire vise à offrir une nouvelle opportunité d'éducation et de formation professionnelle aux jeunes déscolarisés et non scolarisés. Le programme comprend des formations techniques et professionnelles adaptées aux besoins du marché du travail, ainsi qu'un accompagnement socio-éducatif pour faciliter l'insertion sociale et professionnelle des bénéficiaires. il fait partir de la mise en œuvre du de la deuxième phase du programme social du Gouvernement intitulé "PSGouv2" qui s'étend sur la période 2021 -2024 avec un objectif d'insertion de 400 000 jeunes sur un total de 1000 000 de jeunes sans emplois ou mal insérés. Cette politique a pour objectifs spécifiques : - La formation sur les métiers correspondants aux besoins du secteur productif : Elle consistera à concevoir ou adapter les curricula de formation sur la base des besoins du secteur productif. Ceci aura l’avantage de doter les apprenants de compétences qui sont recherchées sur le terrain et ainsi à faciliter leur absorption dans le tissu économique. - La mise en stage pratique / apprentissage des apprenants chez des professionnels : Cette activité va permettre aux apprenants de mettre en pratique les compétences acquises à l’école dans un environnement professionnel. - L’appui à l’insertion : Il s’agira d’assurer un accompagnement individualisé des jeunes formés et de mettre en place un fonds de garantie d’insertion auprès des institutions financières.  Ainsi, dans le cadre du Contrat de Désendettement et de développement (C2D), un projet de formation par apprentissage d’environ 6 000 apprenants a été mis en œuvre. 2032 jeunes ont été déjà sélectionnés pour la première vague et 4000 autres à partir de juillet 2022. Tandis que 18 000 jeunes bénéficieront de formations qualifiantes et par apprentissage dans le cadre du Projet Emploi Jeune et Développement des Compétences (PEJEDEC). L’École de la deuxième chance s'est inscrit dans la certification à partir d’octobre 2022 de 1 500 maîtres artisans. Ce sont au total 10 000 maîtres artisans issus du secteur productif qui ont vu leurs capacités renforcées.
Results: Au plan juridique: l'adoption loi n° 2022 -795 du 13 octobre 2022 portant orientation de l’enseignement technique et de la formation professionnelle. cette loi a pour objet de fixer les dispositions régissant l'enseignement et la formation technique et professionnelle en Côte d'Ivoire. Elle en fixe les orientations fondamentales, vise à assurer leur qualité, leur performance et leur développement pour favoriser l'insertion professionnelle des formés et garantir l'efficacité et la compétitivité de l'économie Nationale.  - Au plan institutionnel : Transformation de plusieurs collèges en lycées et la réforme prévue de plusieurs institutions: dont l' Institut Pédagogique National de l'Enseignement Technique et Professionnelle (IPNETP), le Fonds de Développement de la Formation Professionnelle (FDFP), le Centre de Promotion des Nouvelles Technologies de l'Information et de la Communication (CPNTIC) : - Au plan infrastructurel et matériel : la construction de plusieurs établissements sur toute l’étendue du territoire nationale : Dabakala, Diabo, Ebimpé, Yopougon et Abobo. Pour illustration : le Lycée Professionnel multisectoriel Mohammed VI de Yopougon et le Garage-Ecole d’Abobo. - Sur le plan du partenariat : Plusieurs conventions conclues avec des partenaires internationaux : l'Agence Coréenne de Coopération Internationale (Koica Corée), la coopération ave la République populaire de Chine à travers le Projet AVIC, Contrat de Désendettement et de Développement( C2D), UNESCO-projet BEAR III vise à améliorer les opportunités d'emploi des jeunes et à renforcer les économies en Afrique Subsaharienne en répondant aux exigences du marché du travail en constante évolution il est financé par la République de Corée et sera mise en œuvre sur une période de 5ans de 2023 à 2027.  Depuis sa mise en œuvre, l'École de la Deuxième Chance a permis à de nombreux jeunes d'acquérir des compétences professionnelles et d'améliorer leur employabilité. De nombreux diplômés ont réussi à trouver un emploi ou à créer leur propre entreprise. Les taux de réinsertion scolaire et professionnelle ont augmenté significativement.
Financial Ressources: Plus de 318 627 451 USD
Recommandations: Les évaluations ont montré que le programme est efficace pour améliorer les perspectives d'emploi et l'inclusion sociale des jeunes bénéficiaires. Il a été recommandé d'étendre le programme à d'autres régions du pays et d'augmenter les ressources financières et techniques pour renforcer les capacités des centres de formation.

Title EN: CLUBS  IPL: CENTRES D'INCUBATION CINEMATOGRAPHIQUE AU SEIN DES ETABLISSEMENTS SCOLAIRES ET DES CENTRES SOCIOCULTURELS
Goal: Integrate Culture In Sustainable Development Frameworks
SDG: SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: National sustainable development policies and plans
Agency Implementation: ONG Inter Palm Lumière (IPL)
Main Feature: Les Clubs IPL, créés par l'ONG Inter Palm Lumière (IPL), sont des espaces de motivation pour les métiers du cinéma, visant à réduire le chômage tout en produisant un cinéma de qualité. Inspirés par des initiatives littéraires pour encourager la lecture, les clubs IPL servent de véritables centres d'incubation cinématographique au sein des établissements scolaires et des centres socioculturels. Contrairement à de simples clubs de cinéphiles, les membres des Clubs IPL reçoivent des formations approfondies dans divers aspects du cinéma, tels que l’écriture de scénarios, la réalisation, le cadrage, le montage vidéo, et le jeu d’acteur.  Les Clubs IPL encouragent la créativité en étudiant des œuvres cinématographiques et en les adaptant à des œuvres littéraires. Des rencontres avec des professionnels du cinéma sont organisées pour offrir des conseils et des formations spécialisées. Les clubs servent également de lieux de divertissement, permettant l’organisation d’événements sociaux comme des anniversaires et des projections de films suivis de débats.  Toutes les activités et créations des clubs IPL sont supervisées par l'ONG IPL et sont considérées comme son patrimoine. Les clubs peuvent collaborer avec d'autres institutions culturelles pour enrichir l'offre et élargir le réseau de soutien. Les espaces pour les clubs sont aménagés dans des établissements scolaires et des centres socioculturels, et l'ONG IPL s'efforce de mobiliser des ressources, des financements, du matériel et des bénévoles pour leur fonctionnement.  L’adhésion aux Clubs IPL est ouverte à tous ceux qui partagent les mêmes objectifs. L'impact et l'efficacité des activités des Clubs sont régulièrement évalués pour s'adapter aux besoins des membres. Les Clubs IPL, régis par des règles spécifiques, sont des lieux dynamiques et enrichissants pour les amateurs de cinéma.  Le premier Club IPL, situé à Bonoua, fonctionne très bien et sert de modèle pour d'autres clubs à venir. La vision de l'ONG IPL est de voir ces clubs s'implanter largement dans les établissements scolaires et les centres socioculturels, à l'image des bibliothèques.
Results: Les résultats atteints par cette mesure sont remarquables. En effet, avec l'évolution numérique et les Clubs IPL, de nombreux jeunes ont intégré des équipes de production et trouvé des emplois dans le tournage.  Par exemple, le Club IPL de Bonoua a formé plus d'une cinquantaine de jeunes, leur donnant de nouvelles compétences cinématographiques. La communauté "Face Lite Chanel", grâce aux services de l'ONG IPL, est désormais autonome en matière de reportage et de production de films de sensibilisation et d'évangélisation. Certains bénéficiaires de ce programme souhaitent poursuivre leur carrière dans le cinéma en renforçant leurs compétences par des ateliers et des séminaires de formation, et ceux qui n'avaient pas de métier apprécient cette opportunité.

Title EN: CODEPA CREATIVE AND CULTURAL DEVELOPMENT  PROGRAM (2020-2024)
Goal: Integrate Culture In Sustainable Development Frameworks
SDG: SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: National sustainable development policies and plans
Agency Implementation: COMMUNITY DEVELOPMENT PROGRAMME AGENCY
Main Feature: Describe the main features of the measure/initiative (800 words):     The CODEPA CREATIVE AND CULTURAL DEVELOPMENT  PROGRAM (2020-2024) has been conceived and coordinated by Mr. Boopen DOOBAH Founder -President of the NgO COMMUNITY DEVELOPMENT PROGRAMME AGENCY     ( CODEPA founded in 2021 . Registered Number 6544) and implemented in collaboration of different stakeholders namely public, private and civil society actors.  The main objective is to promote the development of Inclusive Creative and Cultural industries as per the guidelines and programme of UNESCO and the Ministry of Arts and Cultural Heritage ( Mauritius) CODEPA along with its strategic partners namely IOCDAFRICA and ARTA Indianoveanika  aim at alleviating poverty from socio- economic empowerment and women integration through a series of community based initiatives and self help programmes inclusive  of Creative and Cultural Empowerment of Artists of various diciplines. It covers not only Mauritius, Rodrigues ,  the Outer Islands , but also Indian Ocean, Africa , Europe and UN. CODEPA aims at developing integrated projects with main emphasis on socio-economic integration of vulnerable groups and poverty alleviation in a systematic way. Actions are being focused on empowering deprived women, families, artists groups ,elderly and young unemployed persons. The development philosophy is based on the UN  Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). CODEPA is also working with different stakeholders through a multi-disciplinary approach, thus, grouping competencies from the public, private, civil society, partners and collaborators.    The following activities constitute the CODEPA CREATIVE AND CULTURAL DEVELOPMENT  PROGRAM (2020-2024) namely: 1.	Establishment of a structure namely the CODEPA Mauritius Regional Creative and Cultural Interactive Network  for the promotion and consolidation of inclusive artistic and cultural  exchanges, as well as in the fields arts and cultural heritage, creative and cultural tourism , sustainable community development , social entrepreneurship poverty alleviation, well-being, ecological activities related to recycled arts and crafts; capacity building and empowerment  of vulnerable groups of artists with  women, youngsters, unemployed  ,  the elderly and the handicapped amongst others and community based arts media and  filmography  2.	Collaboration with the Ministry of Arts and Cultural Heritage , and the Bhojpuri speaking Union , Centre Nelson Mandela , Aaleemee Society, New China Town Foundation and the Mauritius Council of Social Service ( MACOSS to organise the CODEPA  Intercultural Exchange Programme with the involvement of stakeholders and artists working on consolidating the multicultural fabric of the Mauritian Society 3.	CODEPA- IOCDAFRICA joint initiative to organise the ARTA Indianoceanika Biennalede Arts de l’Indianoceanie , in partnership with the Mauritius National Commission for UNESCO ( NATCOM );  Municipal Council of Port  Louis, the Ministry of Arts and Cultural Heritage , Muncipalities of Quatre Bornes and Vacoas Phoenix,  Arts and Culture orgaisations and groups of the Indian Ocean , and the International  Movimento Arte Quantistika ( IAMAQ- Italy) 4.	CODEPA Creative Social Entrepreneurship Program   The teaching environment of CODEPA CODEPA Creative Social Entrepreneurship fuses theory and practice, utilizing conceptual framework, case studies and examples from the field and gives students the opportunity to design and develop Creative  social entrepreneurship initiative utilizing the arts and crafts training as an incubator and a breeding ground for creativity and inclusion . The introduction to the course grapples with two central questions. what is creative social entrepreneurship? And consequently who are creative social entrepreneurs? It uses the Community based Decentralised Methodology to bring together citizens, artists, CBOS, NGOs, as well as  public and private together to develop self help creative projects to sustain the socio- economic integration of artists and vulnerable groups,  elderly women, youth, school children, and handicaped    5.	CODEPA and Rodrigues Socio Economic and creative Integration   The Community Development Programme Agency (CODEPA) is considered a reference in terms of Creative and Green  development in Mauritius, Rodrigues and Africa by extension. Recipients of the Africa Leadership Award (NGO) and National Environment Award for Community Based Environmental Education for community leaders where representatives of Mauritius and Rodrigues have received capacity building in Organic Farming and related Creative and Cultural  Self help- Community based in Income Generating activities for the most vulnerable groups including planters, women involved in subsistence agriculture and youth leaders. For the sensitisation and implementation of Organic farming inclusive of food processing activities Rodriguans have been able to benefit greatly from  CODEPA's input which is in line with the Sustainable Development Goals (SDG's) whereby they have been able not only to cultivate Organic vegetables, citrus and Fruits with partial processing and pickles that was sold in Rodrigues and exported to Mauritius. Our coordinator, Mr Andre Augustin, Rodriguan subject has been assigned the task to conduct  follow up and monitoring, It should be noted that though Rodrigues has embarked on the Organic farming options, there is still much to be done in terms of capacity building, sensitisation in  order to clarify the difference between Smart Agriculture and Organic farming which at time brings some confusion with regard to execution of projects. Moreover, there is an urgent need to develop Rodrigues as a model for  Green Creative and Cultural Hub, taking into consideration of its constraints and limitations of access to creative and material / resources.  6.	CODEPA Rural Creative and Cultural Integration Program focuses on reducing the creative gap of  community groups and artists and performers in rural and peri urba regions. In this context we have organised capacity building  for schools and artists I northern, eastern, south( souillac) and west ( Le Morne Village) where the UNESCO World Artist Day and Green Creative camaigs have been implemented.
Results: OUTCOMES & RESULTS OF THE CODEPA CREATIVE AND CULTURAL DEVELOPMENT PROGRAM (2020-2024)  1.	CODEPA CREATIVE AND CULTURAL DEVELOPMENT PROGRAM (2020-2024) has yielded remarkable output and outcomes where hundreds of Artists, Performers, Women. Youth, Elderly and Handicapped, as well as vulnerable groups from Mauritius, Rodrigues and the region have experienced action based creative socio economic and cultural integration from various perspectives. During the last 5 years CODEPA has been able to contribute to enhance the social, creative, cultural and educational capacities of local and regional art and culture groups through diligent collaborative partnerships as well as community-based education and research  2.	CODEPAa- Arta Indianoceanika- is a not-for-profit community-based organisation in Mauritius that has succeeded with relatvelylittle means to develop, promote and produce high quality visual arts, writing, poetry, music and crafts through a range of arts access, workshops, art residencies, and education programs, community activities, exhibitions and events. It has therefore been able to collaboratiely contribute to the cultural life of the Mauritius, and Indian Ocean- Africa region by nurturing creative and cultural potential, supporting artists and encouraging people of all ages and background inclusive of women and youngsters to actively engage with various art forms.   Arta Indianoceanika is placing high value addition on creative and cultural initiatives, exhibitions that originate from the south-south region, as well as those that offer something new and stimulating to our local audience. It is encouraging exhibition and applications from emerging, mid-career and integrating artists across all art disciplines and visual art forms, as well as curatorial proposals.  ARTA IndianoceanikA Biennale de l'indianoceanie d'Afrique 2022-2023 is inspired and based on UNESCO Creative and Cultural program. The Biennale incorporated a virtual museum, of selected Artworks from different artistic and cultural disciplines. Additionally was organized in Mauritius as well as participating countries related live activities in the form of Art Festivals, exhibitions, Quantum Art and Science manifestations, performances, multi media creative videos and films, creative writing and poetry, amongst others. This Biennale was conceived and organized by Mr Boopen Doobah, Founder/ President of CODEPA in partnership with ARTA IndianoceanikA , IOCDAFRICA, Mr Doobah is also the director of International Art Institute Indianoceanika. The event that was a success from national, regional and international levels that positioned local Mauritian Artists and Cultural actors on the global regognition. Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture

Area of Monitoring: Partnering with civil society
Cultural Domain: Design,Performing Arts,Media Arts,Cinema and Audiovisual Arts,Music,Publishing,Visual Arts
Agency Implementation: Fédération des Industries Culturelles et Créatives (FICC)
Main Feature: Sous le haut patronage de Sa Majesté le Roi Mohammed VI, la première conférence des industries culturelles et créatives au Maroc s'est tenue récemment, rassemblant près de 600 participants de divers horizons culturels et partenariats public-privé. Cet événement historique, qui a eu lieu à Rabat les 4 et 5 octobre 2019, a été une tribune d'échange et de réflexion sur le rôle crucial de la culture dans le développement économique et social du pays. Les discussions ont mis en lumière l'importance de promouvoir les industries créatives, de développer une stratégie nationale inclusive, de relever les défis de la numérisation, de soutenir les petites et moyennes entreprises du secteur, et de créer un environnement fiscal favorable. La conférence a également souligné le potentiel des industries culturelles à générer des emplois et de la richesse, tout en valorisant l'identité culturelle et en promouvant la diversité culturelle et la créativité artistique. Parmi les participants figuraient des artistes, des auteurs, des réalisateurs, des producteurs, des distributeurs, des éditeurs, des intellectuels, des parlementaires, des ambassadeurs et des représentants des médias. Cette forte mobilisation témoigne de l'engagement envers le développement dynamique des industries culturelles et créatives au Maroc, ouvrant la voie à de nouvelles collaborations et à un dialogue continu dans le secteur.
Results: Les résultats de la mise en œuvre de cette action sont marqués par une sensibilisation accrue sur le rôle central de la culture dans le développement économique et social du pays, ainsi que par un engagement renforcé en faveur du soutien et de la promotion de ces industries. Des recommandations concrètes ont été prises pour développer une stratégie nationale inclusive, soutenir les petites et moyennes entreprises du secteur, créer un environnement fiscal adapté, et garantir l'accès à l'art et à la culture pour les jeunes. Cette dynamique a favorisé une collaboration renforcée entre les acteurs du secteur et les décideurs(Ministère de l’économie et des Finances, la Confédération Générale des Entreprises du Maroc-CGEM, Le Conseil économique, social et environnemental du Royaume du Maroc -CESE), ouvrant ainsi la voie à des initiatives innovantes et à des opportunités de croissance pour les industries culturelles et créatives au Maroc.
Recommandations: À l'issue de cet événement sur les industries culturelles et créatives au Maroc des recommandations cruciales ont été soulevé et sont comme suit : 1.	Élaboration d'un plan stratégique national en collaboration avec tous les secteurs concernés. 2.	Actualisation et renforcement de la législation et de la réglementation pour prendre en compte les évolutions du domaine culturel et créatif. 3.	Renforcement du cadre juridique relatif aux droits de propriété intellectuelle et artistique. 4.	Institutionnalisation du soutien aux industries culturelles et créatives par le biais de textes juridiques appropriés. 5.	Encouragement de l'entrepreneuriat culturel avec des définitions claires et un dispositif fiscal favorable. 6.	Création de fonds nationaux et communs public-privé pour soutenir les industries culturelles et les festivals. 7.	Mise en place de programmes de formation dans l'audiovisuel et le cinéma dans les institutions d'enseignement supérieur. 8.	Introduction de nouvelles initiatives artistiques dans les manuels scolaires. 9.	Implication des régions et des communes dans le renforcement des industries culturelles et créatives. 10.	Promotion des industries culturelles à travers le renforcement des programmes audiovisuels.

Title EN: Community outreach and engagement policies. University of Chile.
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture
SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Cultural and creative sectors
Cultural Domain: Design,Performing Arts,Media Arts,Cinema and Audiovisual Arts,Music,Publishing,Visual Arts
Agency Implementation: Vice-Rector's Office for Extension and Communications (VEXCOM), University of Chile.
Main Feature: "The extension and community outreach policy" (free translation), drawn up by the Vice-Rector's Office for Extension and Communications of the University of Chile, promulgated in 2020, serves the purpose of underlining the relationship with the communities as a university.   This role facilitates compliance with its public commitment and its critical point of view by creating, promoting and developing constant interactions between the university and the communities, both internal and external. The main goal is to strengthen the public role of the university, positively influencing social, cultural and economic development in thecountry. This policy was developed between 2015 and 2019, carrying out an internal participatory process for its formulation.   This policy proposes guidelines and strategies in order to establish effective collaboration with the community and other external groups of interest. The proposed actions encompass cultural initiatives, scientific dissemination, professional training and assistence, among others. The policy focuses on promoting, supervising and evaluating the main areas of action:  (a) culture and heritage, (b) production and services, and (c) social and community Diverse forms of intervention are adopted in each area, with reach that varies from the local to the international.   These areas are characterised by the actors involved and the type of cultural knowledge and production that is offered. It is essential to recognise and appreciate the singularity of each area in order to provide adequate support, to evaluate its initiatives and to promote structural changes.
Results: As a result of the implementation of the policy on extension and outreach with the environment, the following results are observed between 2020 and 2022. Of the total extension and outreach initiatives with the surroundings, the cultural and heritage sector represents 15.6%. The activities and events predominate with 70%.   The projects, which are more often long-term and require planning, make up 13%. The remaining 17% correspond to agreements and educational initiatives, demonstrating diversity in the way the institution connects with its surroundings. The following results specifically correspond to this area of action: During this period, 3,902,637 beneficiaries of the cultural and heritage initiatives were registered, indicating that facing the challenges presented by the public health situation, the institution managed to adapt and offer digital options, ensuring that a great number of people could benefit.   Moreover, even though the initiatives in the cultural and heritage areas represent a lower proportion of the total number of initiatives, they are the ones that register the largest participant base: 53% of the beneficiaries come from this area, compared to 28% from the community field and 18% from the productive and service areas.  For the organisation of these initiatives, 1,652 academics and 4,666 students from the university took part, which reflects an internal commitment towards these initiatives. The majority of the activities (73%) were aimed at the general public, which shows an inclusive approach. Followed by undergraduate and postrgaduate students, that represented only 5.7%.   Nevertheless, it is important to consider increasing the initiatives aimed at specific or priority groups: professionals, youth, children and women represented 3.2%, which suggests the opportunity to develop initiatives oriented towards these groups in the future. Of the initiatives, 43% had a national focus, which indicates the intention of contributing to the entire country. Twenty five percent was focused on a regional, local or micro-local level, demonstrating attention to the specific needs of different communities.  Twenty four percent had international reach. To conclude, we can highlight the importance of the university for developing artistic policies and activities for cultural diversity, and that it not only impacts tha student community, but also the general community. In turn, the connection with the environment and the special emphasis on policies on inclusion within the cultural extension of this tertiary education establishment, is a relevant aspect to highlight within the framework of the 2005 Convention.
Financial Ressources: Without information.

Title EN: CONCEPTION DES PROGRAMMES ET PROGRESSIONS, SUIVIE DE LA FORMATION
Goal: Integrate Culture In Sustainable Development Frameworks
SDG: SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: National sustainable development policies and plans
Agency Implementation: MINISTERE DE LA CULTURE ET DE LA FRANCOPHONIE (MCF)/Direction de la Formation Artistique et Culturelle / Sous-Direction de la Pédagogie et des Conservatoires
Main Feature: LA Direction de la Formation Artistique et Culturelle (DFAC) est régie par l'Arrêté n°045 MCF/CAB DU 07 MAI 2008 portant organisation et fonctionnement de la Direction de la Formation Artistique et Culturelle. 	 Une cellule pédagogique a été implantée au sein de ladite  Direction et des antennes de pédagogie en région restent à mettre à place. La création et la mise en œuvre de la Cellule pédagogique qui fonctionne depuis trois (03) ans est en train de procéder à la mise en place de mécanisme de contrôle et de gestion d’outils pédagogiques et didactiques adaptés à l’enseignement des Arts en vue d’un suivi-évaluation tout en harmonisant les curricula du secondaire artistique et culturel. La DFAC, à travers sa Sous-direction de la Pédagogie et des Conservatoires veille au suivi et à l’évaluation de la Pédagogie dans les établissements de formation artistique et Culturelle. Cette action menée par l’antenne pédagogique se traduit par la révision des programmes et progressions des enseignements mais aussi par l’évaluation des enseignants pendant des inspections pédagogiques. Au regard des conclusions de ces actions, un séminaire didactique et pédagogique de recyclage des enseignants du secondaire artistique et culturel s’est tenu du Mardi 29 au Mercredi 30 Août 2023 à la salle polyvalente du Musée des Civilisations de Côte d’Ivoire. Cet atelier qui découle d’un programme triennal d’inspection a permis de recycler une centaine d’enseignants issus du Centre Technique des Arts Appliqués (CTAA) de Bingerville, du Lycée d’Enseignement Artistique de Cocody (LEA) et du Conservatoire Régional des Arts et Métiers d’Abengourou (CRAMA) sur la méthodologie de préparation de la leçon en Arts Plastiques, en Art Dramatique et en Musique. Ce renforcement de capacités, le premier du genre depuis une trentaine d’années a été conduit par six (06) Inspecteurs Pédagogiques du Ministère de la Culture et de la Francophonie, des spécialistes de la didactique des Arts venus de l’INSAAC (Institut National Supérieur des Arts et de l’Action Culturelle), des experts en pédagogie du Ministère de l’Éducation Nationale et de l’Alphabétisation (MENA). L’ouverture des antennes pédagogiques à l’intérieur du pays dans les Directions Générales obéira à l’ouverture effective des établissements d’enseignement artistique sur toute l’étendue du territoire national (trois (03) LEA, neuf (09) CTAA, plusieurs conservatoires d’Arts et Métiers). L’antenne pédagogique basée au sein de la DFAC veille à l’application des pédagogies dans les Établissements d’Enseignement Artistique et Culturel fonctionnels sous la tutelle du MCF.
Results: Les mises en œuvre des programmes et progressions, ainsi que leur suivi dans le secondaire artistique et culturel a permis à la DFAC de progresser à plusieurs niveaux : - Il s’agit notamment de la tenue régulière d’ateliers d’ajustement et de mise à niveau des programmes et progressions dans les Établissement d’Enseignement Artistique et Culturel (EEAC), LEA, CRAMA, CTAA : - de collecter et de mettre à niveau des programmes et progressions dans les EEAC ; - de planifier l’implantation des antennes pédagogiques dans les directions régionales en collaboration avec les partenaires d’éducation-formation avec des écoles fonctionnelles ; - d’intégrer les inspecteurs des arts de la cellule pédagogique à tous les niveaux d’élaboration et de suivi de l’enseignement des arts tout en clarifiant leur statut et leur fonction ; - de coordonner l’organisation du séminaire de renforcement de capacité pour le recyclage pédagogique et didactique des enseignants du secondaire artistique et culturel quarante (40) CTAA, trente (30) CRAMA, soixante (60) LEA ; - de réviser les programmes d’enseignement au CTAA.  Elle a également entrainé la promotion des offres de formations artistiques et culturelles à travers la participation annuelle de la DFAC aux lancements des journées carrières du Ministère en charge de l’éducation nationale, chiffrée à 2.000.000 F CFA / 3.715 $ US ;  -l' installation des jeunes diplômés sur la base de ressources financières acquises du Ministère en charge de la culture via 5% du Fonds de Soutien à la Culture et à la Création Artistique (FSCCA) octroyé à la DFAC .  Dans ce cadre, un groupe d’élèves diplômés du CTAA ont déjà bénéficié , d’un financement de leur projet d’entrepreneuriat culturel à hauteur de 13.000.000 F CFA / 24.149 $ US. D’autres projets sont en attente de demande de financement du Ministère en charge de la culture via le FSCCA.

Main Feature: The priority directions of the Concept approved by the Decree of the President of the Republic of Uzbekistan are: ˗	consistent improvement of the legal framework for the development of civil society; ˗	providing assistance to civil society institutions and further improving the mechanism of their state support; ˗	creating the necessary conditions for the active participation of civil society institutions in state and public administration; ˗	further expansion of the participation of civil society institutions in the implementation of state social projects; ˗	ensuring openness of the activities of civil society institutions. It has been established that: The concept is being gradually implemented through a “Road Map”, separately approved by a resolution of the Cabinet of Ministers every two years and its Target Indicators include: ˗	increasing the volume of state support for NGOs, NPOs and other civil society institutions in the form of subsidies, grants and social contracts by at least 1,2 times in 2021 and 1,8 times in 2025; ˗	allocation of funds in the amount of 16 billion soums in 2021 and 70 billion soums in 2025 to public funds to support non-governmental non-profit organizations and other civil society institutions under the Jokargy Kenes of the Republic of Karakalpakstan, the Kengashes of people’s deputies of the regions and the city of Tashkent; ˗	bringing the number of members of the National Association of Non-Governmental Non-Profit Organizations of Uzbekistan to 10 percent in relation to the total number of operating non-governmental non-profit organizations in 2021 and up to 30 percent in 2025; ˗	bringing in the activities of public councils under each government body (in relation to the total number of representatives of non-governmental non-profit organizations included in public councils) the number of representatives of non-governmental non-profit organizations created on the initiative of citizens to 5 percent in 2021 and 25 percent in 2025 ; ˗	ensuring that the total number of proposals submitted by non-governmental non-profit organizations to higher organizations to improve legislation reaches 1,000 in 2021 and 5,000 in 2025; ˗	bringing the number of non-governmental non-profit organizations participating in the implementation of the state program of the announced year in our country to 30 in 2021, the state program of 2025 – to 50; ˗	reducing the number of offenses committed by non-state non-profit organizations (in relation to the total number of offenses committed in 2020) by 3,8 percent in 2021 and by 19,2 percent in 2025, by simplifying existing procedures and strengthening preventive measures; ˗	retraining and advanced training of 50 managers of non-governmental non-profit organizations in 2021 and 250 in 2025 at the Academy of Public Administration.
Results: The measures to support NGOs in our country are aimed at practical efforts to create appropriate conditions and strengthen the legal base of the sector. As of January 1, 1991, there were 9 NGOs operating in the field of culture and art in the republic, and by January 1, 2000, their number increased to 27, as of January 1, 2017, to 36, and now – to 222. Also the achievements of the measures are as followings so far: ˗	All government services related to the activities of the media have been transferred to electronic form; ˗	Analytical laboratories have been created for the scientific and theoretical study of civil society and constant analysis of its development; ˗	Applied and fundamental research on the development of civil society has been established; ˗	Retraining and advanced training courses were organized for representatives of non-governmental non-profit organizations and other CSOs; ˗	The practice of financing socially oriented projects has been expanded by providing CSOs with targeted social orders instead of state grants; ˗	The creation of legal mechanisms for the participation of CSOs in the development of important political, social and economic programs and monitoring their implementation has been achieved; ˗	Support is being given to the creation of SCOs dealing with problems of youth, children, employment, women, the elderly and the environment, culture, arts, etc.; ˗	There is an increase in the number and volume of state social orders submitted by government bodies to CSOs at the expense of extra-budgetary funds; ˗	The development of mechanisms for direction, coordination, support and encouragement, registration of volunteer activities, introduction of the practice of performing the tasks and functions of government bodies in a relatively effective and cost-effective form through volunteering;  ˗	and so on..

Title EN: CONECTA Service
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture
SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Cultural and creative sectors
Agency Implementation: General Directorate of Cultural Industries and Arts (Ministry of Culture)
Main Feature: The approval of the National Culture Policy for 2030, of the National Reading, Book and Library Policy, as well as the challenges identified in the CPI 2016-2019 and the problems exacerbated by the pandemic, highlighted the need to reinforce measures and strategies for capacity building. This is how in 2020, an exceptional budget allocation was made for the implementation of training with the aim of training cultural agents for greater resilience in the sector.   This is how, within the framework of the Recovery Plan for cultural industries and arts, one of its strategic objectives is defined as: Strengthening capacities for the development of cultural industries and arts.  Within the framework of this need, the CONECTA service arises, as a permanent training service. The service is aimed at artists and cultural agents in the cultural sector and creative sector, with the aim of strengthening the cultural management capabilities of artists, managers and entrepreneurs from all regions of the country, who contribute to the development of their creative processes and cultural management in the sector of cultural industries and the arts.  It consists of three axes:   • Conecta Creates: contemplates topics that aim to promote and develop creative processes and acquisition of knowledge about artistic languages, recognizing the diversity of cultural expressions and the symbolic values ​​present in them.  • Conecta entrepreneurship: aimed at strengthening the capacities of agents in the sector to develop, enhance and/or reactivate their cultural ventures and initiatives. Includes topics such as innovation and digital transformation, design and management of cultural ventures/business models, formalization and legal aspects, collaboration networks, cultural financing, management of social networks for cultural ventures • Connect Public: aimed at providing tools that allow the cultural agent to understand the various audiences to develop and generate connections between them and the cultural content they create, at the same time aiming at their formation of commitments with cultural communities. Topics include audience development, cultural mediation, and marketing and cultural communication.
Results: The main results stand out:  - Creation of the CONECTA web platform  - More than 60 national and international exhibitors have participated, forming a large team of specialists from the cultural sector. - More than 20 thousand users have benefited.  - More than 250 training activities (workshops, mentoring, discussions, online classes, courses and others) have been carried out nationwide.
Recommandations: • Expand strategic alliances with the educational sector to increase the training offer. • Design a training plan that addresses and prioritizes the needs identified in the National Registry of cultural and arts workers and organizations, as well as the entire value chain of the cultural and creative industries. • Establish proposals that address the different levels of training of cultural agents (initial, intermediate, expert level). • Implement a registration system for applicants and beneficiaries of the Conecta service, which allows monitoring and generating information and knowledge about the training needs of the beneficiaries.

Main Feature: Le mandat de service public de la Société suisse de radiodiffusion et télévision (SRG SSR) est décrit par la concession que lui a délivré le Conseil fédéral le 29 août 2018 pour la période allant du 01.01.2019 au 31.12.2024. Pacte_2020-2023_FR.pdf (srgssr.ch) -	La Charte de la musique, selon laquelle la SRG SSR s’engage à mettre en avant la musique suisse ainsi que de jeunes talents (cf. rapport de gestion 2022 SRG-GB-2022-fr.pdf (srgssr.ch) -	Sans avoir spécifiquement signé un accord avec les milieux littéraires, la SSR tient également compte de la littérature suisse. Results: L’autorité de régulation est régulièrement en contact avec le diffuseur pour l’évaluation de l’offre.

Cette enveloppe est globale et couvre toutes les missions de la SRG SSR dans les 4 langues nationales allemand, français, italien, etromanche. Les montants spécifiquement alloués au secteur de la production cinématographique et de la musique suisses sont négociés dans les accords passés avec la branche. Main Feature: For the Government of the Republic of Armenia to promote the import of products and services (including cultural), the Commission for Coordination of Charity Programmes operates in Armenia, which implements the state policy in the sector of humanitarian aid and charity. In the context of the policy for ensuring sustainable economic growth in the Republic of Armenia, the development of small and medium enterprises (SMEs) is called to ensure the stability of the economic growth of the country, giving the economy an innovative direction and flexibility. Each year, the Government of the Republic of Armenia discusses and adopts a programme for supporting small and medium enterprises, the development and implementation of which is based on the Law of the Republic of Armenia “On state support for small and medium enterprises”. The programmes are based on fundamental principles of economic policy adopted by the Government of the Republic of Armenia and contribute to the economic development of the country, especially its remote and borderline settlements, and the overcoming of disproportions. In this regard, the SME, with its features and development opportunities, has a significant impact on the economic development of the country, in general, and in particular, on the culture sector, where 95% of products and services are provided by the SMEs of the field. The Government of Armenia encourages the circulation of materials of cultural nature, which significantly increases the level of ensuring and disseminating cultural diversity in the country. In 2010, Armenia acceded to the Florence Agreement on the Importation of Educational, Scientific and Cultural Materials and the Nairobi Protocol to that Agreement, which contribute the free distribution of books, cultural, educational and scientific materials, access to customs and administrative processes related to the importation of such materials, as well as their free circulation. The application of the Agreement in Armenia has created favorable conditions for the establishment and awareness-raising of the cultural expressions.
Results: In fact, the State has a financial participation in all charity programs being implemented in Armenia, amounting to 20% and more of the value, exempting the programs from certain types of taxes and duties. This policy creates favourable conditions also for the charity import of cultural products and services. During the reporting period, the number of cultural charity programs increased dynamically, as a result of which the general basket of products and services of cultural diversity has been replenished.

Art 22 of the Constitution of the United Republic of Tanzania, Right to Work; Every person who is able to work, has the opportunity to engage himself/herself in any legitimate activity so as to earn a living. ARTICLE 17 of the Constitution of the United Republic of Tanzania, Right of Freedom of movement: All artists have the right to move from one place (or country) to another (mobility) to conduct their arts and culture activities.   ARTICLE 20 of the Constitution of the United Republic of Tanzania; Freedom of Association: Artists have the right to freely form associations and federations and take part in them.   ARTICLE 24 of the Constitution of the United Republic of Tanzania; Freedom to own properties: Artistic creations are recognized as properties (intangible). ARTICLE 29 of the Constitution of the United Republic of Tanzania; Formulation of Policies, Laws and regulations that do not contravene with freedom of artists. Article 21 of the Constitution of the United Republic of Tanzania; Right to participate in public affairs such as electing or being elected, appointing or being appointed to take part in governance.   Article 18 of the Constitution of the United Republic of Tanzania; Right to access information.   Article 11 of the Constitution of the United Republic of Tanzania; Right to education.
