Title EN: COVID-19 measures of the Austrian Federal States (Laender)
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture
SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Cultural and creative sectors
Agency Implementation: Austrian Federal States
Main Feature: Main features of the policy/measure: In Austria, extensive measures were implemented to mitigate the effects of the COVID-19 crisis on the arts and culture sector. The Austrian Laender (Federal States) have also implemented a number of measures and projects in this context. These include  Project development funding from the Federal State of Carinthia: After 2020 and 2021, the independent arts and culture sector was severely affected by the COVID-19 regulations. In response, the Federal State of Carinthia developed a new, forward-looking funding format: project development funding was put out for tender with the aim of enabling independent cultural initiatives to use their creative potential in the face of possible further restrictions on cultural life, even without direct events with an audience. The focus was on themes with high socio-political relevance, such as equal opportunities, climate change, digitalisation and its social impact or democracy, for which EUR 107,000 was spent in 2021.  Working Grants for Freelance Artists and Scientists (Federal State of Carinthia) In order to contribute to fast and uncomplicated support, 36 work grants for freelance artists and scientists were launched in May 2020. The aim was not only to support artists in financial need, but also to promote high-quality, creative, innovative or avant-garde cultural work. Due to high demand in the first round, the number of grants was doubled to 72, which was announced in autumn 2020. In 2021 and 2022, 72 working grants were awarded per year. A total of EUR 596,160 was spent on these activities.  Working Grant for artists (Federal State/City of Vienna) As a reaction to the COVID-19 pandemic the City of Vienna in 2020 launched a work grants programme that has become an integral part of Vienna’s cultural funding since then. Artists from all disciplines living in Vienna are eligible. Each year, the City of Vienna provides 84 work grants (EUR 18,000 each). In total, EUR 1,5 mio are invested yearly.  Funding Programme Kultur im Jetzt („Culture Now) (Federal State of Vorarlberg): In 2020, the Plattform Kultur und Tourismus (“Platform Culture and Tourism”) of the Federal State of Vorarlberg developed the funding programme Kultur im Jetzt (“Culture Now”). The programme supported (outdoor) events organised by municipalities in cooperation with local/regional artists. The funding was earmarked for artists’ fees. Between 2020 und 2022 363 projects were funded and a total of EUR 358,754 was spent.  Working and Studio Grants (Federal State of Vorarlberg) To support Vorarlberg's artists and cultural practitioners affected by the COVID-19 crisis a work and studio grants programme was implemented by the Federal State of Vorarlberg. Funding was provided for research, conception, contemporary writing or composition projects, film projects or digitisation measures. The decisive factor was not the specific result or output, but the programme was intended to support artists from all disciplines in their work processes. In 2020 and 2022 442 projects were funded with a total of EUR 1,007,860.  COVID-19 Support Package of the Federal State of Burgenland The support package included the possibility of work grants of EUR 2,500 each, for projects in the fields of literature, visual arts, media arts, music and film. With the "Culture Voucher" project, the state subsidised the purchase of products and services by Burgenland artists by 25%. In 2020, EUR 174,333 and in 2021, EUR 219,423 were spent on the special projects "Culture Vouchers" and "Work Grants".  Measures taken by the Federal State of Tyrol A total of EUR 8.25 million was made available to the arts and culture sector in 2020 and 2021 to overcome the COVID-19 crisis. The special funding programmes "Emergency Aid for Culture", "New Start" and "Digitalisation" provided support for the numerous cultural institutions and associations in Tyrol and enabled the successful implementation of important measures in the field of digital transformation, but also in the acquisition of new audiences and the creation of new event and mediation/participation formats. For individual artists, the work and studio grants in particular have been an important funding instrument. The work grants were created as a support measure to mitigate the negative effects of the COVID-19 crisis on the arts and culture sector. They were subsequently maintained as an important measure to support artists and are currently still in place. The aim of awarding work grants is to promote creative work processes, stimulate the development of new artistic concepts and projects and thus support professional artists and cultural workers in their living and working situation. The working grant is awarded within a defined period (15 April to 15 October) for a maximum of six months and is endowed with EUR 1,500 per month (in total a maximum of EUR 9,000 per grant). Grants are available in the following areas: Visual Arts, Music, Literature, Performing Arts and Film.  COVID-19 Investment Package – Upper Austrian Plan for Cultural Associations and Institutions (Federal State of Upper Austria) Cultural associations and institutions were eligible for funding for investment measures to help them cope with the COVID-19 pandemic. The investment package was part of the Upper Austria Plus package of measures and served as an impulse and start-up aid for 2021 and 2022. A total of EUR 3,916,951 was disbursed in the years 2021-2023.  Hardship Fund for Cultural Professionals in Upper Austria (Federal State of Upper Austria) The Upper Austrian Emergency Fund for Cultural Professionals was a support measure for artists and cultural actors who due to the COVID-19 Pandemic were unable or only partially able to pursue their artistic activities and were therefore in financial distress. The target group were primarily artists who did not receive support from the federal government through the Artists' Social Insurance Fund. The fund was accessible in 2020-2022 and grants totalling EUR 54,301.2 were paid out.  Funding Programme Art@Home (Federal State of Upper Austria) The special funding programme “Art@Home” provided support to artists in Upper Austria who were looking for new ways to present their projects online due to the limitations of COVID-19. A total of EUR 22,435 was distributed.  Funding for additional costs for festivals in case of postponement & Restart Bonus (Federal State of Upper Austria) In 2020, the Federal State of Upper Austria paid out full funding for festivals and festival-like projects that had to be postponed to 2021 due to the COVID-19 pandemic. Additional costs incurred due to the postponement (compared to the previous year's plan, e.g. additional rehearsals, new printed materials, etc.) could be applied for up to 50% of the costs. The total amount of payments was EUR 546,850. In 2022, the Restart Bonus replaced the programme. The Restart Bonus served to mitigate the financial impact of reduced events and declining audiences in 2021 and 2022. By increasing the regular annual funding of cultural event organisers in the form of a non-dedicated lump sum of 10% of the total costs in 2019 (the last regular financial year before the COVID-19 pandemic), losses were covered and the overall financial situation of cultural event organisers was stabilised. The total amount of grants was EUR 388,578.  Art Grants & Digital Call #keepincontact (Federal State of Lower Austria) As a dedicated measure to support artists in Lower Austria during the COVID 19 pandemic, art grants were distributed in 2020 and 2021 to mitigate the impact of emergency situations for artists due to cancelled events. Funding was also provided for digital projects under the motto '#keepincontact', via the YouTube channel 'Kultur Niederösterreich FREI HAUS'. A total of EUR 2.5 million in cultural funding from the Federal State of Lower Austria was allocated for the period 2020-2022.  COVID-19 Special Funding: Covering the Additional Needs of the Salzburg Art and Culture Scene (Federal State of Salzburg) For the period from 2020 to June 2021, the Federal State of Salzburg has allocated a total of around EUR 2,400,585 in special funding for the arts and culture sector. During the COVID-19 related closures in spring 2020, the Federal State of Salzburg awarded work grants to financially support artists in and from Salzburg and to enable cultural processes and productions. A second call for work grants followed in late autumn 2020, aimed primarily at freelancers who earn their living primarily from independent artistic or cultural activities. The grants could be awarded for a maximum of three months and were endowed with EUR 1,000 per month. A total of around EUR 815,000 was distributed to artists for working processes. In addition, various cultural institutions were supported with special Covid funding.  A total of EUR 28,000 was spent on pandemic-related protective measures in regional museums and in the field of folk culture. Two other support measures set up in connection with the COVID-19 crisis were continued as regular funding programmes due to their success: since 2020, regional museums in Salzburg have been able to draw on funds for the part-time employment of cashiers, supervisors, etc. (2020/21: EUR 42,040). Digitisation in national and regional museums has been prioritised and supported by appropriate funding programmes.  Measures by the Federal State of Styria  The Federal State of Styria implemented a range of measures to mitigate the effects of the COVID-19 pandemic on the arts and culture sector, including a COVID-19 Support Packages for Recipients of multi- year grants (EUR 129,866); a COVID-19 Sondereinreichtermin (“special call”) for the independent arts and culture sector (EUR 399,915), a Hardship Fund for Culture and Sport (Donations) (EUR 22,643); a Special Support Programme for Tours/Touring Artists and the resumption of projects that had to be postponed due to the COVID-19 pandemic (EUR 59,250) and a funding programme for regional museums (Museums-Call 2020/2021, EUR 291,000). Furthermore, the existing Kunstraum Steiermark Grants have been doubled for the years 2021 und 2022, resulting in an increase of EUR 72,000, and also the acquisition budget for art works has been significantly increased in order to support artists during the COVID-19 pandemic (EUR 193,523). In total, the Federal State of Styria has provided EUR 1,168,217 specifically for the arts and culture sector.
Financial Ressources: s. above

Title EN: CRADLE OF CREATIVITY FESTIVAL
Goal: Achieve A Balanced Flow Of Cultural Goods And Services And Increase The Mobility Of Artists And Cultural Professionals
SDG: SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 10 - Reduce inequality within and among countries,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Mobility of artists and cultural professionals
Agency Implementation: ASSITEJ SA
Main Feature: Cradle of Creativity 2023 was an International Dance and Performing Arts for Young Audiences festival which showcased local, continental, and international performances, and celebrated opportunities for intercultural exchange. The aim of the festival was to be an African event that provided a snapshot of the very best performing arts for young audiences from across the continent and the world. The platform is also intentional about building a rich legacy of diversity, creativity & opportunity that continues after the festival. The festival is meant to be biennial but was last performed live in 2019 due to COVID.  In 2023 the festival, hosted and organised by ASSITEJ South Africa, was supported by the Department of Sports, Arts and Culture, and the Department of Basic Education. Cradle of Creativity took place at the iconic Market Theatre in Johannesburg from 20-27 August, with satellite events taking place at the Windybrow Arts Centre, the National Children’s Theatre, and Sibikwa Arts Centre.  A total of 27 (18 local and 9 international) productions were staged in 86 separate performances across 11 different spaces in 4 venues, alongside an impressive conference, workshop and seminar schedule. There were 4 featured dance productions, and approximately 251 artists who performed across the festival. Cradle of Creativity reached over 8700 audiences of children, young people, their families and artists working in the field, as well as the general public. The festival also provided local arts organisations with a platform for child-centered activations, which included short performances, games, and story circles facilitated by authors of South African children’s books.  The festival attracted 200 official delegates which included the ASSITEJ International Executive Committee, and artist delegations from different programmes supported by British Council Wales, Pro Helvetia, and the Government of Flanders. The festival also had a delegation of African artists who participated in the Babel African Regional Workshop initiative, as well as artists, facilitators, and coordinators involved in the national Arts4Youth programme which is supported through the Social Employment Fund.  In total, there were artists and delegates from 32 countries that were represented at the festival: these included Argentina, Australia, Belgium, Botswana, Brazil, Burundi, Cameroon, Chile, Denmark, England, France, Germany, India, Italy, Kenya, Mexico, Mozambique, Namibia, Netherlands, Nigeria, Pakistan, Russia, Rwanda, Senegal, South Africa, South Korea, Swaziland, Switzerland, Uganda, Wales, Zambia, and Zimbabwe. Each day of the conference had a specific area of focus which included: Inclusivity and Accessibility in Theatre for Young Audience, Playwriting for Young Audiences, Performing Arts for Teens (14+), Performing Arts for Early Years (0-6 years), Dance for Young Audience, Arts as / in Education, Child/Youth Participation in the Arts, and The Art of Listening in Theatre for Young Audiences. In addition to the daily conference, there were 16 workshops attended by 209 participants over the course of the festival, as well as two workshops targeting children and young people, reaching 28 participants.  Throughout the festival more than 24 schools and community based groups were reached. The festival also attracted more than 30 volunteers. ASSITEJ South Africa was glad to have the support from the national government not only financially but also in presence. The opening ceremony held on 20 August 2023 was addressed by Deputy Minister Dr Regina Mhaule from the Department of Basic Education and attended by Mr Themba Luthuli, Deputy Director: Performing Arts and Festivals from Department of Sports, Arts and Culture. The closing ceremony was attended and addressed by Ms Seboko Maggie Tseka, the Assistant Director of School Sport and Enrichment, for the Department of Basic Education.  The theme for Cradle of Creativity 2023 was ‘The stories that move us’. Artistically the foundation of Cradle of Creativity has been about the alchemy that exists when different cultures and forms collide. We are currently living in a world where movement has become increasingly difficult. The pandemic was a shared moment of precarity; the feeling that life can change at any moment. In the past three years this has been paired with rising political instability, devastating natural disasters, and the deterioration of public services across the world. The festival theme was a deliberate recognition of theatre as a vehicle for traversing physical, social, and imaginative boundaries.  This year the festival had over 200 productions apply to be on the programme. The festival is proud of the diversity that the platform is able to attract. The Cradle of Creativity had productions and delegates from Rwanda, Burundi, Burkina Faso, Denmark, France, Switzerland, Germany, the Netherlands, Mexico, Argentina, as well as representation from all nine South African provinces.   The festival was committed to programming shows that sensitively broach difficult subject matter with children. Themes such as bullying, coming to terms with loss, social pressure in high school, understanding race, climate change, and ecological restoration were all themes that were addressed in the productions. ASSITEJ South Africa has long been an advocate for inclusivity. Two productions, The Stories We See, and Thandiwe wa Bantu, were created by/with young persons with disabilities. These young people were also intimately involved in the festival through the Young Critics programme.  In addition, Cradle of Creativity was a site for research as part of an EU-funded ASSITEJ international project called “Babel: the art of listening in TYA”. The African Regional Workshop at the festival brought together 25 artists from 13 African countries, for an intense period of reflection, exploration and exchange.
Results: • Making arts and culture accessible to children and young people. • Strengthened partnerships between ASSITEJ centres in a range of countries as well as with foreign missions and cultural agencies such as British Council, Goethe institute, Pro Helvetia, Government of Flanders. • Strengthened partnerships between different players in the SA cultural landscape including different festivals, community centres, theatre spaces, governmental and non-governmental entities etc. • Strengthened relationships between artists of different cultures, languages, ethnic and other identities leading to collaborative work. • Development of new work for children and young people. • New methods for the integration of children and young people into festival curation and Reception –Young Critics programme. • Heightened media attention for work for young audiences and for work of different cultures/languages in the mainstream. • African artists inspired by the opportunities for inter-continental exchanges and unprecedented levels of activity in theatre for young audiences on the continent, with new ASSITEJ centres becoming members of the association, and with new productions being created across the continent and collaborations being designed, coming out of Cradle of Creativity.

Title EN: création de clubs : « LIMITL’ESS generation » au sein des maisons de culture
Goal: Integrate Culture In Sustainable Development Frameworks
SDG: SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: International cooperation for sustainable development
Agency Implementation: Le Ministère des Affaires Culturelles (MAC)
Main Feature: L’union européenne (UE) est un partenaire stratégique de la Tunisie et un acteur de premier plan de la coopération internationale. Le dialogue politique entre l’UE et la Tunisie a permis de faire de la jeunesse une priorité transversale du cadre unique UE-Tunisie établi autour de 03 secteurs prioritaires qui cadrent parfaitement avec les objectifs de la convention 2005 sur la protection et la promotion de la diversité des expressions culturelles (article 13/intégration de la culture dans le développement durable et article14/coopération pour le développement) : -	La promotion de la gouvernance et de l’Etat de droit, -	La stimulation d’une croissance durable et inclusive,  -	Le renforcement de la cohésion sociale entre les générations et les régions, De plus, le partenariat UE-Tunisie dédié à la jeunesse est lancé autour d’une vision commune cherchant à promouvoir l’éducation, l’emploi, la croissance économique, le développement régional ainsi que la mobilité des jeunes notamment les jeunes créateurs et porteurs des projets innovants. Ce partenariat s’inscrit dans le cadre de politique publique tunisienne qui accorde une place importante aux jeunes et à leur inclusion sociale économique et culturelle : * Les plans de développent de la Tunisie pour les périodes (2016-2021), (2023-2025) ainsi que la vision Tunisie 2035 qui ont fixé des objectives en matière d’inclusion politique, économique, sociale et culturelle notamment des jeunes. * Le Ministère de la jeunesse et des sports avait initié un dialogue national sur la jeunesse visant à définir une stratégie plurisectorielle pour l’horizon 2035 qui vient d’être adoptée le 07 mai 2024 et qui s’articule autour de 05 axes : l’appartenance, la citoyenneté, le bien-être social, les modes de vie sains, l’intégration sociale et économique des jeunes, la créativité, l’innovation, la mobilité des jeunes et les loisirs. C’est dans ce contexte que le programme EU4Youth a été conclu pour s’établir sur la période 2019-2027 afin d’opérationnaliser le partenariat UE –Tunisie dédié à la jeunesse en soutien aux politiques publiques du pays. Ce programme se construit explicitement à partir du concept d’inclusion des jeunes et autour d’une approche transversale qui vise à dépasser les approches sectorielles classiques de l’action publique et de la coopération internationale, de sorte à pouvoir agir sur l’ensemble des leviers de l’inclusion permettant ainsi de maximaliser les perspectives d’impact et de changement. L’inclusion recouvre plusieurs dimensions qui correspondent à autant de composantes du renforcement du pouvoir d’agir des jeunes : une dimension socio-économique à travers l’auto-emploi et une dimension politique autour de la construction de la citoyenneté par l’accès à des services permettant leur implication dans la société et par leur participation à des mécanismes de dialogue avec les autorités leur permettant d’influencer ou de peser sur la conception, le suivi et l’évaluation des politique publiques.  En conséquence, l’objectif d’inclusion des jeunes d’EU4Youth se décline autour des axes suivants : -	L’inclusion économique des jeunes tunisien (nes) à travers l’amélioration d’accès à l’emploi par, notamment, le renforcement de l’employabilité et à travers la promotion de l’entreprenariat individuel et collectif dans le cadre de l‘Economie Sociale et Solidaire (ESS) autour des filières innovantes. -	L’inclusion des jeunes hommes et femmes à la vie publique par des activités associatives et communautaires dans des domaines tels que les arts, et la culture.  Trois principes directeurs sont véhiculés par le programme EU4Youth et qui s’alignent avec les principes directeurs de la convention 2005 (art 2 : Principe de la complémentarité des aspects économiques et culturels du développement/ Principe de développement durable/Principe d’accès équitable) : 1-	Principe de multisectorialité 2-	Principe de territorialité       3-	Principe de vulnérabilités et de lutte contre les discriminations Ainsi, ce programme cadre parfaitement avec la vision stratégique du Ministère des Affaires Culturelles (MAC) qui fait de la culture un catalyseur pour le développement économique et social. Le MAC s’est lancé à travers la DCI (Direction de la Coopération Internationale) et la DGAC (Direction générale de l’Action Culturelle) dans un projet de création/implantation de clubs ESS intitulés « LIMITL’ESS generation » qui s’inscrit dans le cadre du projet de promotion de l’économie sociale et solidaire et création d’emploi décent pour la jeunesse tunisienne: JEUN’ESS, mis en œuvre par l’organisation internationale du travail (OIT) (qui est une agence spécialisée des Nations Unis ayant pour mission de promouvoir les droits au travail, favoriser la création d’emplois décents, améliorer la protection sociale et renforcer le dialogue social pour résoudre les problèmes liés au monde du travail) en partenariat avec le Ministère de l’Economie et de la Planification (MEP) dans le cadre du programme EU4YOUTH (programme d’appui à la jeunesse tunisienne) financé par l’UE (convention de financement entre le gouvernement tunisien représenté par le MEP et l’UE ENI/2018/041-142) et ayant pour objectif la contribution à l’inclusion économique, sociale et politique des jeunes tunisiens les plus défavorisés à travers une approche de développement local en particulier dans les zones préalablement identifiés sur des critères de développement (07 gouvernorats cibles: Jendouba, Kef, Kairouan, Sidi Bouzid, Kasserine, Gabes et Kébili). Ces clubs ont pour vocation de sensibiliser et promouvoir l’Economie Sociale et Solidaire (ESS) auprès des jeunes et de contribuer à l’instauration d’une culture entrepreneuriale basée sur les valeurs et les principes de l’ESS.  La démarche générale du club consiste à offrir aux jeunes apprenants des opportunités de se familiariser avec l’ESS et de vivre une expérience « ESS » visant à apporter une réponse à une problématique économique ou sociale identifiée au niveau du centre ou dans leur environnement économique et social. Les jeunes bénéficient également dans le cadre des clubs d’un accompagnement spécifique pour développer leurs idées de projets ESS-Culture et les concrétiser à travers un fonds dédié par le projet JEUN’ESS : « le Social Innovation Fund (SIF) » (mis en place pour appuyer la création de nouvelles structures de l’ESS et/ou consolider des structures de l’ESS existantes ainsi que la promotion de la culture entrepreneuriale ESS chez les jeunes).  Dans le cadre de ce fonds, les clubs « LIMITL’ESS generation » sont créés et ont pour objectif de diffuser les valeurs d’entrepreneuriat social et solidaire auprès des jeunes tunisiennes et tunisiens fréquentant les structures dédiées au développement et à l’épanouissement de la jeunesse.
Results: Le Ministère des Affaires Culturelles a défini 07 maisons de culture (structures hôtes) dans les 07 gouvernorats cibles du projet pour accueillir les clubs ainsi que la liste des animateurs (au nombre de14 dont 07 Femmes et 07 Hommes), désignés pour encadrer les jeunes membres des clubs dont le nombre s’élève à 85 (40 Femmes et 45 Hommes) et les accompagner à développer leurs idées de projets culturels et ce, dans une logique de respect du principe de l’égalité des genres.  Des ateliers de renforcement de capacité sont organisés au profit des animateurs en collaboration avec l’équipe OIT- Tunis :  -	Un premier atelier sur le thème de l’ESS : gestion et animation des clubs ESS avec la participation des Commissariats Régionaux aux Affaires Culturelles (CRAC) dans les régions concernés (Mars 2023) -	Un deuxième atelier en matière de Soft Skills (communication et feedback / estime de soi / travail d’équipe et intelligence collective / créativité et innovation/techniques de négociation) (Décembre 2023) -	Un accompagnement et coaching au profit des jeunes et des animateurs (08 ateliers dont 03 en présentiel et 04 à distance) (Voir en annexe le rapport fourni par le bureau de l’OIT-Tunis). Après un processus de sélection effectué par des jurys régionaux, 02 idées de projets portées par des jeunes sont retenues et un appui financier et technique leur sera accordé à raison de 30.000 DT (dinar tunisien) par projet : •	Projet Discover Tunisia (application) •	Agence culturelle touristique/VR En perspective, la création de 07 radios web dans les 07 maisons de culture en tant que structures hôtes avec un budget estimatif de 210.000 DT (septembre 2024).
Recommandations: Une évaluation à mi-parcours du programme EU4Youth est en cours d’élaboration. Cependant, une évaluation concomitante est assurée durant toutes les étapes de mise en œuvre du projet de création des clubs via l’équipe OIT–Tunis et les services de la DGAC et en coordination avec la DCI afin de garantir l’engagement des animateurs et des jeunes porteurs d’idées de projets culturels innovants et ce à travers des réunions périodiques mais aussi dans le cadre de la rencontre des animateurs des clubs de recyclage artistique organisé par la DRAC en présence des représentants de l’équipe OIT-Tunis (le 02 mai 2024).  Pour le pilotage de l’ensemble du projet JEUN’ESS, en plus du MEP qui assure le lead, des représentants des différentes institutions engagées sur la thématique au niveau du pays (entre autres le MAC) ainsi que des organisations syndicales et patronales siègent au sein d’un comité de pilotage national chargé de veiller à ce que les activités soient mises en œuvre conformément au document du projet.  Par ailleurs, un comité régional d’appui basé dans chacun des gouvernorats d’intervention se charge de renforcer l’adhésion et l’appropriation pour la mise en place et le suivi des activités des projets dans les régions. L’objectif est d’inscrire les résultats dans la durabilité et de développer les compétences des acteurs régionaux (OSC-CRAC-jeunes créateurs et porteurs de projets culturels innovants …). Ce mécanisme de pilotage tel qu’il est conçu est pertinent car il permet une concertation au niveau national et régional entre les différentes parties prenantes et parties intéressées. Toutefois dans un contexte en évolution, la mise en application de ce dispositif a été confrontée à certains obstacles (la crise sanitaire (2020-2021) n’a pas été sans effet sur la régularité des réunions des comités- l’instabilité des membres- les changements institutionnels fréquents…). La durabilité des projets incubés est favorisée par l’implication des structures publiques dans la sélection des projets. En effet, la participation de ces acteurs spécialisés (CRAC, MAC…) aux jurys de sélection est un facteur de durabilité des projets d’autant plus que le projet JEUN’ESS a prévu que l’incubateur assure aussi le suivi post création notamment en collaboration avec les associations locales et les structures d’appui ce qui garantit durabilité de l’action.  Pour les clubs « LIMITL’ESS generation », le choix des maisons de culture (comme structures hôtes) qui sont dotés de personnel permanent spécialisée dans l’animation contribue à la pérennité des clubs.

Title EN: Create a map of cultural and creative industries
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture
SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Cultural and creative sectors
Cultural Domain: Design,Performing Arts,Media Arts,Cinema and Audiovisual Arts,Music,Publishing,Visual Arts
Agency Implementation: Ministry of Culture, Sport, and Youth
Main Feature: The “Cultural and Creative Industries Map” is the first initiative launched by the Ministry of Culture, Sports, and Youth to shed light on the cultural and creative industries in the Sultanate of Oman, coping with the Ministry's ambitious goals in its cultural strategy 2021-2040, which was developed and prepared to achieve the pillars of Oman Vision 2040. The map project was officially launched in November 2021 after appointing a team of (8) researchers and professionals in the cultural sector, and continued continuously for two years of systematic scientific research work to monitor the opinions and interventions of workers in the cultural and creative sectors in the Sultanate of Oman, based on the best global practices through international consultations with a group of specialists in the field of cultural and creative industries, and opening interactive communication channels from workers in these vital sectors to monitor their challenges and explore their ambitions, as more than (20) international experiences were analyzed on the cultural and creative industries in the world, on the basis of which the map's path was built, then the teams began collecting data on the ground by implementing the first laboratories in Muscat Governorate, which were supported by the General Directorate of Arts at the Ministry of Culture, Sports and Youth and included (144) of creative entrepreneurs and independent practitioners in the creative sectors, then continued its journey through the rest of the governorates, where (56) questionnaires were distributed across the various governorates of the Sultanate of Oman targeting a deliberate sample of creative entrepreneurs and independent practitioners in the cultural and creative sectors, and finally, interviews were employed, the number of which reached (30) interviews with a number of experts in the cultural and creative sectors, whether they were from the academic research sector or from the government and private sectors. Regarding the most important objectives of the research study project “Map of Cultural and Creative Industries," the creative cultural industries contribute to creating opportunities and achieving economic, social, cultural, and political gains and benefits. The creative cultural industries also help in sustainable development and work to increase the competitiveness of cities in finding creative solutions to the problems facing society and transforming their economy into a creative economy. This project aims to understand and study the cultural and creative industries sectors in the Sultanate of Oman, propose a methodological framework to monitor the creative economy in the Omani GDP, study the characteristics of workers in the cultural and creative industries sectors in the Sultanate of Oman, understand the legislative aspects and policies related to the cultural and creative industries sectors, study the reality of education, innovation, and skills and talent development in the creative sector in the Sultanate of Oman, and also aim to shed light on the role of digital infrastructure in developing cultural and creative industries, understand the reality of intellectual property and its role in protecting the creativity of the creative class, reveal the Omani society’s view of creative work and its readiness to adopt and enhance the creative economy, and also provide decision-makers with evidence-based data to support the cultural strategy in the Sultanate of Oman.
Results: Completion of the project and launch of the map in 2024.  In terms of analyzing secondary data to propose a framework for monitoring the economic contributions of creative industries to the economy of the Sultanate of Oman, the map team conducted a quantitative analysis of approximately (483) commercial activities, (1020) creative professions, and (411) creative goods and services. The study sought to provide a scientific analytical view of the reality of cultural and creative industries through seven main themes that stimulate the creative industries system in the Sultanate of Oman, which are as follows: policies and legislation, creative economy, national talents, education and creative professions, technology and innovation, intellectual property, creativity and society.
Recommandations: As stated in the speech of His Excellency the Undersecretary of Culture for the Ministry; the map achieved the desired results that are consistent with the directives of the Ministry’s cultural strategy. The recommendation was to take the results of the map and include it in future policies to develop the cultural industries sector. The efforts of the working team were praised and honored by His Highness the Minister of Culture, Sports and Youth.

Title EN: CreatiFI – Culture and Creative Industries Financing Initiative
Goal: Integrate Culture In Sustainable Development Frameworks
SDG: SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: International cooperation for sustainable development
Cultural Domain: Design,Performing Arts,Media Arts,Cinema and Audiovisual Arts,Music,Publishing,Visual Arts
Agency Implementation: European Commission (Directorate General for International Partnerships)
Main Feature: The CreatiFI programme is designed to unlock the economic and social potential of Cultural and Creative Industries. It is a financial instrument to support creative industries through blending (finance and technical assistance).  CreatiFI was designed to fill the gap by providing a dedicated instrument to address the specificities of the sector and to harness the visibility of the multiple benefits from the sector which reaches in particular a very large and young audience. It serves to build capacity and interest among Financial Institutions to include CCIs in “regular” guarantee and blending operations. The structure of the programme was built with lessons learned from the successful EU internal Cultural and Creative Sectors Guarantee Facility.  The overall objective of the action is to increase the contribution of culture to sustainable socio-economic development in the ACP countries.   The specific objective is improved access to finance for MSMEs from the culture and creative sectors.
Financial Ressources: Aprox. USD 22 million [EUR 20 million] Implementation period: 2019 - 2028

Title EN: Creating "Ciudad Sur" community networks and alliances. International Fund for  Cultural Diversity.
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture
SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Partnering with civil society
Cultural Domain: Design,Performing Arts,Media Arts,Cinema and Audiovisual Arts,Music,Publishing,Visual Arts
Agency Implementation: "Ciudad Sur" Municipalities Association (AMCS).
Main Feature: The measure, co-financed by the International Fund for Cultural Diversity, has the purpose of strengthening co-operation between dynamic cultural actors in developing countries. In this regard, the project “Creación de redes y alianzas entre agentes Culturales de Ciudad Sur” ("Creation of networks and partnerships between cultural agents of Ciudad Sur")  promotes associative life and collaboration between the cultural agents from eight communes of the Metropolitan Region of Chile, through coordinated action between public bodies and the citizens, carried out by the "Ciudad Sur" Municipalities Association (AMCS), the body responsible for the project.   The AMCS was founded in 1998 and has developed, over 25 years, a permanent commitment to building spaces for community participation, freedom of expression and equal access to cultural goods for the citizens. This shows its long standing organisational history in the southern sector of the Metropolitan Region, which comprises the San Joaquín, La Granja, El Bosque, Cerrillos, San Bernardo, San Ramón, Lo Espejo y Pedro Aguirre Cerda communes, representing a population of 1,119,982 residents.   The AMCS areas of action are social development, local economic growth, education, health, culture, public safety, urban development and environment. In the cultural sphere, the AMSC brings together the identity and heritage of a territory with extensive social and cultural history and citizen's cultural participation and self-managed organisation.   Lastly, this measure is characterised by the active participation of public entities (Municipal Divisions for Culture and Cultual Corporations) integrated with society in cultural agents at an intercommunal level during associative work, through the creation of thematic cultural networks, and the development of participatory diagnoses and strategic plans of action for thematic cultural network. With regard to the monitoring framework of the 2005 Convention, this measure responds to the "measures that strengthen the skills and capacities of civil society" indicator.
Results: The measure is ongoing and its implementation is planned between July 2023 and June 2024. To date, co-ordinating and contact with the culture representatives from the municipalities, members of AMSC, has been carried out. At the same time, the ComisiÃ³n Cultura Ciudad Sur (Ciudad Sur Cultural Commission) has been activated, with the participation of the representatives of culture from the 8 member communes, selecting a coordinator of activities and presenting the "Plan de Trabajo 2023-2024" working plan, whose main goal is to establish a connection with the community of cultural agents from the territory such as artists, managers, cultural organisations and local artistic entrepreneurs.   During this activity, municipal representatives of culture commit to a local call for cultural agents, in order to implement the measure. Continuing with the work, a positive response is seen with the information received from cultural artists and agents of the inter-city territory. These databases serve the purpose of building, in an associative manner, "Redes Culturales TemÃ¡tices" ("Thematic Cultural Networks") on the basis of four artistic disciplines such as music, dance, theatre and literature.   This call was carried out by municipal respresentatives of culture and a list of 191 cultural agents, surveyed by these municipal units, was received. Concurrently, an open call was made through the web page and social newrks of the AMSC, managing to incorporate 105 new cultural agents to the "Ciudad Sur".
Financial Ressources: 2023: USD 83,903 (total project cost).

Title EN: CREATION D’UNE TISSUTHEQUE A TIEBISSOU DANS LE CADRE DE LA MISE EN ŒUVRE DU PROGRAMME D’APPUI AU RENFORCEMENT DES POLITIQUES ET INDUSTRIES CULTURELLES (ARPIC)
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture
SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Partnering with civil society
Agency Implementation: Ministère de la Culture et de la Francophonie/ Direction de la Mode et du Design
Main Feature: Le programme ARPIC, œuvre au renforcement et à l’appui aux politiques des Industries Culturelles et Créatives (ICC). Le secteur des ICC ayant subi d’énormes dommages du fait de la COVID-19, ledit programme représente une opportunité pour hisser la culture dans toutes ses dimensions comme un réel facteur stratégique de développement économique, au bénéfice des créateurs et de la valorisation de la diversité des expressions culturelles. Cette mesure a pour objectifs de : - mettre en œuvre des politiques visant à promouvoir la créativité, la production, la distribution et la diffusion de biens et services culturels, ainsi qu’à consolider les industries culturelles et créatives ; - renforcer les capacités des acteurs concernés ; - formuler et mettre en œuvre des politiques et mesures culturelles ; - faire de la production et de la commercialisation des biens et services culturels des facteurs qui contribuent au développement économique et social de la Côte d’Ivoire ; - renforcer la prise en compte de la culture comme une dimension essentielle des politiques et des stratégies de développement durable ; - accompagner l’émergence d’une société civile culturelle professionnelle. Dans ce contexte a été crée la tissuthèque dans la région du Bélier à Tiébissou.  Logée dans les locaux du Centre culturel Hacandy Ackah de Tiébissou, cette Tissuthèque  contribue à la valorisation des pagnes traditionnels tissés et à l’ensemble des tissus spécifiques à la région. Cette initiative  aura un impact économique considérable pour la région et l’ensemble de sa population. Les principales activités de  la tissuthèque sont : la mise en place de programmes de formation continue et initiale pour améliorer les compétences techniques et professionnelles des artisans. -Partenariats avec des institutions nationales et internationales pour fournir des formations spécialisées; Facilitation de l'accès aux matériaux de base tels que les fils, colorants, et autres accessoires nécessaires à la production. L'Introduction d’outils de production modernes et numériques pour stimuler l’innovation et la productivité.  le Développement de stratégies marketing et de commercialisation pour promouvoir les produits textiles baoulé sur de nouveaux marchés. l'Organisation d’événements et de festivals pour accroître la visibilité des produits artisanaux.
Results: La mise en œuvre de cette initiative a pour résultats :  - Renforcement des Capacités et Formation: par l'amélioration de la formation technique et professionnelle pour les artisans baoulé, notamment dans le domaine du tissage artisanal. Cela pourrait se traduire par une meilleure qualité des produits, une préservation des savoir-faire traditionnels, et une capacité accrue à innover et à utiliser des outils modernes comme les machines numériques. - l'Accès aux Intrants et Modernisation:  par facilitation de l'accès aux intrants nécessaires tels que les fils, colorants, et autres fournitures. La modernisation des équipements et l'intégration d'outils numériques pourraient augmenter l'efficacité et la productivité des artisans. - le Développement du Marché et Marketing: Amélioration de la commercialisation des produits textiles baoulé, ce qui pourrait conduire à une augmentation des ventes tant sur le marché local qu'international. Le renforcement de la structuration du segment du tissage artisanal pourrait également contribuer à une meilleure visibilité et valorisation des produits. - les Infrastructure et Tourisme Culturel: Développement d'infrastructures telles que la tissuthèque et le Centre culturel de Tiébissou transformé en un centre technique et de promotion des arts du tissage. Cela pourrait stimuler le tourisme culturel basé sur les routes du pagne et renforcer l'économie locale par le biais de l'artisanat et du tourisme. - les Partenariats et Coopération:  l'établissement de partenariats solides entre les régions d'Auvergne Rhône-Alpes et le Bélier en Côte d'Ivoire, ainsi qu'avec des organisations internationales comme l'ONUDI, le PNUD, et l'UNESCO. Ces partenariats pourraient apporter un soutien financier et technique  pour la réalisation des objectifs du projet.

Title EN: Cycles de formation des musiciens
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture
SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Cultural and creative sectors
Agency Implementation: Orchestre Philarmonique du Maroc
Main Feature: Organiser des cycles de formation, des masters classes, des séminaires de formation des formateurs au profit des professeurs de musique relevant du Département de la culture;  Convier les élèves des conservatoires de musique relevant du département de la Culture aux répétitions et générales  offrir au profit des élèves des conservatoires de musique un concert pédagogique par saison
Results: La mise en œuvre de cette mesure, incluant des cycles de formation, des master classes, des séminaires de formation des formateurs, ainsi que la mobilité des musiciens, a produit plusieurs résultats positifs :  Amélioration des compétences des professeurs de musique :  Les cycles de formation, les master classes et les séminaires ont permis aux professeurs de musique de se perfectionner et d'acquérir de nouvelles compétences pédagogiques et techniques. La formation des formateurs a renforcé la capacité des enseignants à transmettre efficacement leurs connaissances. Renforcement de l'expérience éducative des élèves : L'invitation des élèves des conservatoires de musique aux répétitions et générales leur a offert une immersion dans des environnements professionnels, enrichissant leur apprentissage et leur compréhension des processus musicaux. Les concerts pédagogiques offerts chaque saison ont permis aux élèves de découvrir de nouvelles œuvres et styles musicaux, tout en bénéficiant d'explications et de contextes musicaux directement liés à leur formation. Encouragement à la pratique musicale :  Ces initiatives ont suscité un intérêt et une motivation accrus chez les élèves, les encourageant à s'engager davantage dans leur pratique musicale. L'exposition régulière à des musiciens professionnels et à des concerts de qualité a inspiré les élèves à poursuivre leurs études musicales avec plus de passion et de dévouement. Création d'une communauté musicale :  Les interactions régulières entre professeurs, élèves et musiciens professionnels ont favorisé la création d'une communauté musicale dynamique et solidaire. Les événements et les formations ont offert des opportunités de réseautage et de collaboration entre différents acteurs du secteur musical. Promotion de la culture musicale :  L'initiative a contribué à la promotion de la culture musicale au sein de la communauté, sensibilisant le public aux diverses formes et genres musicaux. Les concerts pédagogiques ont également servi à éduquer et à sensibiliser le public à l'importance de la musique et de l'éducation musicale. Évaluation et ajustement continus :  Les retours d'expérience des participants ont permis d'ajuster et d'améliorer continuellement les programmes de formation, assurant ainsi leur pertinence et leur efficacité. Soutien institutionnel :  L'engagement du Département de la Culture dans ces initiatives a renforcé le soutien institutionnel pour l'éducation musicale, démontrant une reconnaissance de l'importance de la formation musicale dans le développement culturel et artistique. Mobilité des musiciens :  La mobilité des musiciens a permis l'échange de pratiques et de savoir-faire entre différentes régions, enrichissant ainsi l'expérience musicale des participants. Les musiciens ont pu se produire dans divers contextes, partageant leurs talents et découvrant de nouvelles perspectives musicales, ce qui a contribué à leur développement professionnel et artistique. Cette mobilité a également favorisé les collaborations internationales, permettant aux musiciens d'établir des connexions et de s'inspirer de diverses cultures musicales.

Title EN: CREATION DU FONDS DE RETRAITE  AU BURIDA
Goal: Promote Human Rights And Fundamental Freedoms
SDG: SDG 5 - Achieve gender equality and empower all women and girls,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels
Area of Monitoring: Artistic freedom
Cultural Domain: Design,Performing Arts,Media Arts,Cinema and Audiovisual Arts,Music,Publishing,Visual Arts
Agency Implementation: BURIDA
Main Feature: Les principales caractéristiques de cette mesure sont, notamment :  - promouvoir une action sociale en faveur des créateurs d’œuvres littéraires ou artistiques et des titulaires de droits; - offrir une meilleure retraite aux artistes, membres du BURIDA;  - promouvoir et défendre les intérêts moraux et sociaux des artistes.  Cette mesure s’inscrit dans les mesures destinées à promouvoir les expressions culturelles notamment la promotion et la protection des droits d’auteurs et des droits voisins. La convention instituant un FONDS RETRAITE BURIDA au bénéfice des membres du BURIDA a été signée le 06 mai 2015 entre le BURIDA et un professionnel en assurance Vie la Compagnie d’Assurance BELIFE INSURANCE. La spécificité de cette convention se trouve dans le fait qu’elle est souscrite par le BURIDA (Souscripteur) au bénéfice de ses sociétaires (Adhérents), lesquels doivent obligatoirement y adhérer. Ce système se caractérise par l’externalisation de la gestion de la retraite, l’avancement de l’âge de départ à la retraite à 65 ans et surtout par la possibilité pour les adhérents d’effectuer par eux-mêmes des versements sur leur compte, en complément de ceux effectués par le BURIDA auprès de l’assureur. Les ressources du Fonds Retraite  du BURIDA sont alimentées par un prélèvement de 10% sur les répartitions individuelles au titre des droits d’exécution publique.
Results: Les résultats obtenus par cette mesure sont:   -Une action sociale en faveur des créateurs d’œuvres littéraires ou artistiques et des titulaires de droits est promue ;  - Une meilleure retraite est offerte aux artistes, membres du BURIDA ;  - Les intérêts moraux et sociaux des artistes sont promus et défendus. Au 31 décembre 2019, 879 sociétaires sur un effectif de 10 541, ont été pris en compte et leur cotisation globale est de 323 138 496 FCFA.
Financial Ressources: Les ressources du Fonds Retraite BURIDA sont alimentées par un prélèvement de 10% sur les répartitions individuelles au titre des droits d’exécution publique., soit 528 005 USD
Recommandations: La cotisation pour la retraite est opérée au moment de la distribution des droits aux artistes. Cette distribution ne bénéficiant pas systématiquement à tous les artistes, cela explique que tous les artistes ne sont pas encore couverts par ce système. Toutefois, la faculté est offerte à tout sociétaire de cotiser pour sa retraite, indépendamment des revenus de la distribution des droits. Mais la précarité des conditions de vie des artistes explique en partie qu’ils ne puissent s’offrir une retraite descente.

Title EN: Création du Ministère de la Transition Numérique et de la Digitalisation
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture
SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Digital environment
Cultural Domain: Design,Performing Arts,Media Arts,Cinema and Audiovisual Arts,Music,Publishing,Visual Arts
Agency Implementation: Le Ministère de la Transition Numérique et de la Digitalisation
Main Feature: Dans sa politique de répondre aux exigences des Nouvelles Technologies de Communication (TIC) l'Etat de Côte d'Ivoire a créé en 2023 un département ministériel spécifique à la transition numérique.   Le Ministère de la Transition Numérique et de la Digitalisation a été mis en place par le décret n°2023-820 du 25 octobre 2023 portant attribution des membres du gouvernement en son article 22.   Il est chargé de la mise en œuvre et du suivi de la politique du Gouvernement en matière de Transition Numérique et de Digitalisation. A ce titre, et en liaison avec les différents départements ministériels concernés, il a l’initiative et la responsabilité des actions suivantes : - élaboration et suivi de l’application de la réglementation en matière de Transition numérique et de Digitalisation ; - mise en œuvre de stratégies et de plans d’action pour le développement d’un environnement numérique ; - développement de l’accès au réseau numérique ; - contrôle de la programmation et de la réalisation des infrastructures et des équipements du secteur des télécommunications ainsi que leur maintenance ; -élaboration et suivi de l’application de la réglementation en matière de télécommunication ; - suivi des concessions dans les différents secteurs d’infrastructures de télécommunication ; - élaboration et mise en œuvre de la politique en faveur du développement et de la diffusion des usages du numérique ; -  élaboration et mise en œuvre de la politique d’informatisation de l’Administration et évaluation de son impact sur la modernisation de l’Administration et la qualité des Services Publics, en liaison avec les Ministres concernés ; - développement de la formation, de l'emploi, de la recherche, de l'innovation et de la compétitivité dans le secteur numérique ; - restructuration et modernisation de la Poste ; - élaboration et suivi de l’application de la réglementation en matière de Poste ; - mise en place et suivi du plan de sécurité numérique.   La politique de transition numérique et de digitalisation en Côte d'Ivoire vise à intégrer pleinement les technologies numériques dans tous les aspects de la société et de l'économie, y compris le secteur culturel. Les principales caractéristiques de cette politique incluent : - Infrastructure numérique : Développement de l'infrastructure numérique pour assurer une connectivité fiable et abordable dans tout le pays. - Éducation et formation: Programmes de formation en compétences numériques pour les jeunes, les artistes et les professionnels de la culture. - Soutien aux industries créatives : Encouragement à l'utilisation des technologies numériques dans la création, la production et la distribution de contenu culturel. - Accès aux ressources numériques : Promotion de bibliothèques numériques et d'archives en ligne pour faciliter l'accès aux ressources culturelles et éducatives. - Innovation et entrepreneuriat : Soutien aux start-ups et aux initiatives technologiques dans le domaine culturel, y compris le financement et les incubateurs. - Gouvernance numérique : Mise en place de cadres réglementaires pour protéger les droits d'auteur et encourager une utilisation éthique des technologies numériques.
Results: La mise en œuvre de la politique de transition numérique et de digitalisation a permis d'atteindre plusieurs résultats notables : - Augmentation de la connectivité : Amélioration significative de l'accès à Internet et à la technologie numérique dans les zones urbaines et rurales. - Capacités numériques : Formation de milliers de jeunes et de professionnels en compétences numériques, augmentant leur employabilité et leur capacité à contribuer au développement économique. - Innovation culturelle : Prolifération de nouvelles formes d'expression artistique utilisant des technologies numériques, telles que les arts visuels numériques, la musique électronique, et les films d'animation. - Accès à la culture: Accès facilité à des œuvres culturelles via des plateformes numériques, augmentant la participation et l'inclusion culturelle. - Soutien aux entrepreneurs : Création de plusieurs start-ups et projets innovants dans le secteur culturel, soutenus par des incubateurs et des financements publics et privés.
Financial Ressources: 55 649 125 870 milliards de FCFA soit 90 929 944,23 Usd
Recommandations: L'évaluation de la politique de transition numérique et de digitalisation a conclu que : - Réussite de l'infrastructure : Les efforts pour améliorer l'infrastructure numérique ont été largement couronnés de succès, mais des améliorations sont encore nécessaires dans certaines zones rurales. - Besoin de formation continue : Il est crucial de continuer à investir dans la formation et le développement des compétences numériques pour tous les groupes démographiques. - Renforcement des partenariats : Il est recommandé de renforcer les partenariats avec les secteurs privé et public pour maximiser l'impact des initiatives numériques. - Focus sur l'inclusion : Les futures initiatives devraient se concentrer davantage sur l'inclusion numérique, en particulier pour les groupes marginalisés et les zones sous-développées. - Innovation soutenue : Encourager davantage l'innovation en fournissant des fonds et des ressources aux entrepreneurs et aux start-ups dans le secteur des technologies numériques.

Title EN: Creation of popularization materials for the Convention
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture
SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Partnering with civil society
Agency Implementation: Coalition for the Diversity of Cultural Expressions ( CDCE ), International Federation of Coalitions for Cultural Diversity ( IFCCD )
Main Feature: In 2023, the Coalition for the Diversity of Cultural Expressions (CDCE) and the International Federation of Coalitions for Cultural Diversity (IFCCD) developed communications tools aimed at promoting and popularizing the 2005 Convention among historically marginalized or less aware populations to the convention and its potential, in particular by highlighting the impacts it can have specifically for these groups. Thus, the CDCE and the IFCCD have each created a new section on their website, “UNESCO Convention”. The texts were written in partnership with the Canadian Commission for UNESCO (see Popularization convention – CDCE and Popularization convention – IFCCD). The two sections explain in a simple way the foundations of the Convention and its impact on creators and cultural organizations in addition to answering frequently asked questions and giving concrete examples of the benefits that can result from the implementation of the Convention. The texts have been modified to respond to the different contexts of the two organizations: the examples and quotes put forward are exclusively Canadian for the CDCE, and from international sources for the IFCCD. This therefore contributes to democratizing the mechanisms governed by this convention which can be used to assert cultural rights, in addition to serving as a point of reference and being available in French and English. These two tools can help build bridges with new communities. For example, the CDCE was invited to an annual gathering for the transmission, expression, and preservation of indigenous heritage which was held in November 2023, in Wendake, and which welcomed nearly a hundred participants. During this event, the CDCE distributed a paper version of the section of the website to participants in the form of brochures. In addition, the programming of this gathering included a panel aimed at discussing the implications of the Convention for Indigenous peoples, thus contributing to raising its awareness.

Title EN: Creation of the first Key Indicators for the culture sector
Goal: Integrate Culture In Sustainable Development Frameworks
SDG: SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: National sustainable development policies and plans
Cultural Domain: Design,Performing Arts,Media Arts,Cinema and Audiovisual Arts,Music,Publishing,Visual Arts
Agency Implementation: National Institute of Statistic and Geography, Ministry of Culture.
Main Feature: The creation of the first Key Indicators for the culture sector is an important milestone. These indicators are now part of the National Catalog of Indicators.  The purpose of these Key Indicators is to provide a concise overview of the economic and social dynamics within Mexico’s cultural sector. By doing so, they support and advocate for the defense and assurance of cultural rights. This understanding allows the Ministry of Culture to advance its objectives, ensuring that no one is left behind. It also sheds light on the profound economic and social dimensions represented by Mexico’s rich cultural diversity and heritage
Results: The measurement of the economic impact of the cultural sector was previously limited to the Cultural Satellite Account of Mexico (CSCM). However, recognizing the need for more comprehensive data, efforts were made to gather additional information. This expanded dataset will allow greater utilization of statistical tools and instruments, enabling a deeper understanding of culture’s role and its significance in the country’s economic and social contributions.  Notably, in 2020, culture contributed approximately 2.9% to the national Gross Domestic Product (GDP) and accounted for 3.0% of the country’s jobs, according to the latest update from the CSCM.  The introduction of new indicators provides valuable insights: •	Real Growth of Gross Added Value in the Culture Sector: This indicator tracks the behavior of economic activities related to culture over time. By comparing year-on-year changes, it sheds light on the sector’s dynamics. When combined with the percentage of GDP attributed to cultural activities (as reported by the Mexican Culture Satellite Account), decision-makers gain a better understanding of cultural relevance and variability. This information informs cultural public policies. •	Growth in Cultural Sector Jobs: Monitoring workforce variations in the cultural sector between consecutive years is crucial. Contrary to the assumption that economic growth always correlates with higher employment rates, this indicator reveals nuances. For instance, it highlights cases where economic growth does not necessarily translate to increased employment.  Both proposals cover the entire nation and will receive annual updates.

Addresses the historical and structural inequalities faced by different nationalities and genders in Bolivia. Decolonization and depatriarchalization became central axis to its mission seeking to reverse the injustices that have marginalized indigenous communities and women in the cultural and social spheres. Leads the generation, implementation and supervision of public policies for the recovery, protection, preservation, restoration, promotion, socialization and appreciation of the cultures and artistic expressions of indigenous peoples and nations, intercultural communities and Afro-Bolivians, with processes of decolonization, depatriarchalization and cultural revolution to contribute to the consolidation of the Plurinational State and Living Well. Area of Monitoring: Cultural and creative sectors
Agency Implementation: Creative Ireland Programme (within the Department of Tourism, Culture, Arts, Gaeltacht, Sport and Media)
Main Feature: The Creative Ireland Programme was set up to enable the creative potential of all people living in Ireland, to enhance their wellbeing and the collective wellbeing across all areas of our society. The Programme focuses on encouraging and supporting new ways and opportunities to participate in creative and cultural activities. The Creative Ireland Programme is an all-of- government culture and wellbeing programme running until 2027. More information is available at www.creativeireland.gov.ie  A large part of the remit of the Creative Ireland Programme is to embed creativity across public policy. The Programme works in partnership with the Department of Health (Ireland), the Health Service Executive (HSE) and The Arts Council to demonstrate how creativity, be it through performing or visual arts, culture, and heritage-based activities, promotes positive health and wellbeing by helping people to connect socially, enhancing their self-esteem and resilience, enabling recovery and empowering them to manage their own health and wellbeing through their lives. This is backed up by research carried out internationally, for example the World Health Organisation’s (WHO) most recent report, and domestically, where the Creative Ireland Programme worked with Trinity College Dublin to participate in the most recent TILDA report, which found clear evidence of a positive association between creative engagement and health and wellbeing across all of the life course.  Working in partnership with Healthy Ireland and the Shared Island Initiative, the Creative Ireland Programme’s Health and Wellbeing Pillar aims to build on what we have learned from projects funded since 2021, which have supported the health and wellbeing of: •	Older people •	Traveller Communities •	Children with chronic conditions •	People at End of life and experiencing bereavement •	Social Prescribing activities  The Creative Ireland Programme is working with Healthy Ireland to advance its objectives of: •	bringing a concerted focus on life-long wellbeing and prevention of illness •	seeking to reduce health inequalities •	addressing the settings in which health and wellbeing is impacted, and •	empowering people and communities to better look after their own health and wellbeing.  Through collaboration with Healthy Ireland, HSE Local Health & Wellbeing and Sláintecare teams in Local Authorities, Creative Ireland will implement arts and health projects, in 2024 and 2025, to meet the health and wellbeing needs of communities throughout the country of Ireland leveraging the power of the Irish Government's Shared Island Initiative.   Support is also provided to Local Authorities in partnership with the Department of Health to provide Live Music Performances in Residential Healthcare Settings.  Details of initiatives funded under these schemes can be found here: https://www.creativeireland.gov.ie/en/blog/creative-ireland-awards-over-e1-2-million-to-creative-health-and-wellbeing-projects/
Results: Reports from the Creative Health and Wellbeing Pillar: https://www.creativeireland.gov.ie/en/publications/?_sft_category=creativity-health-wellbeing
