Title EN: Creative Export Strategy
Goal: Achieve A Balanced Flow Of Cultural Goods And Services And Increase The Mobility Of Artists And Cultural Professionals
SDG: SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 10 - Reduce inequality within and among countries,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Treaties and agreements
Cultural Domain: Design,Performing Arts,Media Arts,Cinema and Audiovisual Arts,Music,Publishing,Visual Arts
Agency Implementation: Department of Canadian Heritage
Main Feature: The Government of Canada launched the Creative Export Strategy in 2018, with a five-year mandate to help Canadian creative industries maximize their export potential and stand out in the global market.   The original Strategy (2018-19 to 2022-23) was organized around three distinct pillars:  1) Position creative industries for export and sales in foreign markets by increasing export funding in existing Canadian Heritage programs (e.g., Canada Arts Presentation Fund, Canada Book Fund, Canada Music Fund Canada, and Canada Periodical Fund) and Telefilm Canada.  2) Increase and strengthen the presence of Canadian creative industries abroad, with the objectives of promoting Canadian artists and culture internationally and increasing support for Canada's international priorities, and, providing direct services to businesses through Global Affairs Canada's Trade Commissioner Service.  3) Foster the growth of Canadian creative industries by financing export-ready projects through a creative export funding program (Creative Export Canada), building the relationships necessary to make business deals through trade missions, commercial activities, and partnerships, and leading Canada’s participation as guest of honor at the Frankfurt Book Fair, the publishing industry’s largest international event.   During the pandemic, the Creative Export Strategy received additional funding through Canadian Heritage’s Recovery Fund (2021-2022 and 2022-2023) to provide targeted support to Canadian creative businesses and organizations in achieving success in international markets by enabling them to be well-positioned to take advantage of international trade opportunities through:   1) Training and mentorship opportunities offered by the Trade Accelerator Program, run by Provincial Boards of Trade.   2) High-quality export services through the Trade Commissioner Service’s Canadian Creative Accelerator initiative, led by the Canadian Consulate in Los Angeles in collaboration with the Canadian Consulate in New York.   3) Top-up funding that allowed Creative Export Canada to support additional export-ready projects.  These measures, along with the many others undertaken by the Department of Canadian Heritage and its Portfolio organizations, helped stabilize the arts, culture and heritage sectors.  On March 15, 2023, the Minister of Canadian Heritage announced the renewal of the Canadian Heritage portion of the Strategy for three years beginning in fiscal year 2023-24 until 2025-26. Global Affairs Canada received separate funding over two years – 2023-2025 – for its portion of the Creative Export Strategy. The following components make up the renewed Creative Export Strategy:   1) Creative Export Canada – continue to deliver the export funding program for both for-profit and not-profit companies and organizations, which aims to heighten the exposure of Canadian creative works internationally and increase export profitability for Canada’s creative industries. The renewed funding program has been expanded to support both existing exporters and new and early-stage exporters.   2) Trade missions and events – continue to deliver multi-sector creative industries trade missions and expanded business programming for Canadian companies and organizations at key international creative industries trade events (e.g., Edinburgh Fringe Festival, FAME Week Africa and Gamescom).  3) Creative Export Navigator Service – deliver a new service to provide creative companies and organizations with a contact point in the department to help them navigate export supports for which they might be eligible.  4) Global Affairs Canada’s Trade Commissioner Service – continue to provide direct export services to Canadian creative industries companies worldwide, including through dedicated officers in key markets.
Results: The Creative Export Strategy supported more than 1,800 Canadian creative industries firms between fiscal years 2019-20 and 2023-24. Support was provided for export activities around the world, particularly in France, Germany, the United Kingdom, and the United States.   The Strategy has generated important results throughout fiscal years 2019-20 to 2023-24, including:  •	The Canada Periodical Fund funded 29 export projects (2019-20 to 2022-23), benefitting 26 periodical publishers. •	The Canada Arts Presentation Fund funded 102 export projects (2019-20 to 2022-23), of which 92 facilitated the participation of foreign presenters in activities in Canada and 10 facilitated the participation of Canadian presenters in activities abroad. •	Telefilm Canada supported 8 additional audiovisual co-production projects (2019-20 to 2022-23). •	The Trade Commissioner Service provided 4,500 services to Canadian creative businesses, generating 299 commercial deals signed or negotiated in 9 missions in the United States, France, the United Kingdom, India, Japan, China, Australia, and Mexico between 2019-20 and 2023-24 (up to December 2023). •	The 5 virtual trade missions (Netherlands, Germany, Sweden, Australia and New Zealand, and South Korea) and the 4 in-person missions (Europe, Dubai, Australia and New Zealand, and Japan) delivered between 2019-20 and 2023-24 have resulted in the signing (or negotiation) of 95 commercial agreements estimated at a total value of CAD 20 million for Canadian creative companies and organizations. •	The expanded business programming delivered at over 95 international trade and cultural events resulted in at least 170 trade agreements signed or under negotiation for Canadian delegates, not including results for 2022-2023 and 2023-2024, which are still being compiled. •	The Creative Export Canada program funded 75 export-ready projects totaling nearly CAD 36 million in funding during fiscal years 2019-2020 to 2022-2023. •	Canada's successful participation as the Guest of Honor country at the Frankfurt Book Fair in 2020 and 2021 generated more than 600 in-person and virtual events and activities in Germany and on the international stage between 2018 and 2022. During this period, nearly 500 Canadian titles were translated and published in German, and book sales in the German-language market increased by 120%.  Despite major disruptions during the pandemic, the Creative Export Strategy was able to continue supporting companies and organizations with the injection of additional funding generating the following results:  •	The Boards of Trade in Montreal, Toronto, and Vancouver helped 108 companies prepare for internationalization through the Trade Accelerator Program. •	The Canadian Trade Commissioner Service provided 98 Canadian creative industries companies with high-quality services to help them succeed in the Los Angeles and New York markets through the Canadian Creative Accelerator. The Canadian consulates in Los Angeles and New York delivered 15 cohorts from 2019-2020 to 2023-2024 across film, television and music, generating 70 business deals signed or under negotiation with reported commercial transactions valued at over CAD 3.3 million. •	The Creative Export Canada program was able to fund an additional 20 export-ready projects supported with nearly CAD 7.5 million in funding during fiscal years 2021-2022 and 2022-2023.
Financial Ressources: The original Strategy received CAD 25 million annually for 5 years for a total investment of CAD 125 million from 2018-19 to 2022-23. An additional CAD 9.2 million in funding was allocated to the Strategy to support companies and organizations during the pandemic through Canadian Heritage’s Recovery Fund.  The Canadian Heritage portion of the renewed Strategy was approved with a budget of CAD 19 million annually for 3 years for a total of CAD 57 million from 2023-24 to 2025-26.  Global Affairs Canada received approximately CAD 5 million in funding over two years (2023-24 to 2024-25) for its portion of the Creative Export Strategy.
Recommandations: An evaluation was conducted in 2022 of the Canadian Heritage-delivered portion of the Creative Export Strategy, namely, the Creative Export Canada program and the delivery of trade missions and events.   Overall, the evaluation confirmed the relevancy, efficiency, and effectiveness of the Strategy with recommendations to update the Strategy’s logic model and performance measurement indicators and implement measures to streamline and enhance the funding decision process of the Creative Export Canada funding program.

Title EN: Cultural and Creative Economy Satellite Account
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture
SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Cultural and creative sectors
Cultural Domain: Design,Performing Arts,Media Arts,Cinema and Audiovisual Arts,Music,Publishing,Visual Arts
Agency Implementation: National Administrative Department of Statistics-DANE in Spanish, Ministry of Cultures, Arts, and Knowledge and Secretariat of Culture, Recreation, and Sports of Bogotá.
Main Feature: The Satellite Account of the Cultural and Creative Economy is a focused, continuous, and comparable economic information system of cultural and creative goods and services, and the activities that generate them; which is methodologically registered within the System of National Accounts. Cultural and creative activities include sectors that combine the creation, production, and marketing of goods and services based on intangible content of a cultural nature and/or those protected by copyright. The activities that make up the cultural and creative economy are classified into three areas: arts and heritage, cultural industries and functional creations.                  For the purposes of the quadrennial report for the 2005 UNESCO Convention covering the period June 2020 to June 2024, the Cultural and Creative Economy Satellite Account - CSECC in Spanish, is an economic measurement of all cultural and creative activities, with which information is obtained on the behavior of these activities in a series of years (2020 - 2022 preliminary), as well as the contribution of this economic sector to the country's economy. It also offers information on the people employed in these activities, and the jobs generated. Therefore, the CSECC is a diagnosis of the behavior of the cultural and creative sector and is used for the development of public policies and market strategies by the economic agents involved in these activities.
Results: Measuring the added value of cultural and creative activities for the preliminary series 2014 to 2022.

Agency Implementation: ifa - Institut für Auslandsbeziehungen
Main Feature: *Cultural domains covered by the policy/measure: Cultural and creative   Main aims: Fostering intercultural dialogue and cooperation in the realms of culture, education, research, art and the media by means of work-related stays in host organisations in Germany or CCP partner countries; providing grants and mobility support, thereby reinforcing international understanding, civil society networks and capacity-building; developing professional knowledge and the fellows’ regional knowledge and networks  Target groups: CCP Fellowships: Professionals and volunteers aged 23 or over from more than 40 countries working in the fields of politics and society, education (particularly civic education), media, arts and culture, human rights and peace, or sustainable development; CCP Synergy: Two employees working in tandem, one from each of two organisations (operating in any of the following fields: politics and society, education (particularly civic education), the media, arts and culture, human rights and peace, or sustainable development that are planning a cooperative venture; alumni of CCP Fellowships. Title EN: Cultural and Creative Industries Strategies
Goal: Integrate Culture In Sustainable Development Frameworks
SDG: SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: National sustainable development policies and plans
Cultural Domain: Design,Performing Arts,Media Arts,Cinema and Audiovisual Arts,Publishing,Visual Arts
Agency Implementation: Ministry of Culture, Department of Culture and Tourism in Abu Dhabi, Dubai Culture and Arts Authority
Main Feature: The UAE government acknowledges the value of developing a cultural and creative strategy to ensure that culture contributes to the economy and trade. Below is a highlight of efforts at the federal and local governments to develop strategies to strengthen and nurture the cultural and creative industries (CCI): o National Strategy for the Cultural and Creative Industries: The National Strategy for the Cultural and Creative Industries aims to promote the growth of the cultural and creative industries sector and increase its contribution to 5 per cent of the national GDP by 2031. It also seeks to strengthen the UAE�s position on the global cultural and creativity map and inspire creative thinking and attract cultural talents and creative entrepreneurs from around the world amongst others. Launched in 2021, the UAE�s National Strategy for the Cultural and Creative Industries aims to promote the growth of the cultural and creative industries� sector and increase its contribution to 5 per cent of the national GDP by 2031. It also seeks to: � strengthen the UAE�s position on the global cultural and creativity map � inspire creative thinking and attract cultural talents and creative entrepreneurs from around the world � double the number of enterprises operating in the sector � create new jobs in the creative industries � raise the average income of those employed in this field � attract freelancers and creative start-ups to set up, live and work in the UAE. To achieve these objectives, it focuses on 40 initiatives covering three main segments: � talents and creatives � professionals and business environment � enabling the business environment. The strategy is based on partnerships between the public and private sectors to implement comprehensive programs. It will enhance the UAE�s position as a global destination for a knowledge-economy based on creativity, innovation, talent and technology. Abu Dhabi Culture and Creative Industries Strategy � 2020 � 2024: In 2019, Abu Dhabi developed a 5-year culture and creative industries strategy 2020-2024, working in collaboration with key sector partners. The Strategy seeks to strengthen Abu Dhabi�s position as a globally recognized center of creative talent and a leading regional producer and exporter of creative and cultural content. Five strategic pillars provide a framework for initiatives to be implemented over the term of the Strategy, which include: Governance, Talent, Innovation, Business Development, and Place. The Strategy will be implemented by the Government of Abu Dhabi and by sector partners. The vision is to position CCI as a critical contributor to livability and vitality in the community, and to economic development and diversification, including job creation. Culture Plan for Dubai: In October 2019, Dubai Culture and Arts Authority (Dubai Culture), announced a new cultural plan comprising of three overarching strategic objectives: (1) creating an effective and sustainable new cultural movement in Dubai, (2) making Dubai a premier destination for talent, and (3) developing the creative industries and economy. To implement the Cultural Plan, Dubai Culture will work with various cultural organizations. Transforming Al Quoz into A Creative Free Zone is one of the Culture Plan�s initiatives, and it aims to transform Al Quoz into a free zone for creative talent in the culture sector, providing comprehensive facilities and services from the conception stage through to design and production. The free zone will create an end-to-end system for creatives to produce, display and sell their works. This initiative will encourage the flow of cultural goods and services into and out of Dubai.
Results: Both Abu Dhabi and Dubai have launched their cultural and creative industries strategies and have begun implementing initiatives towards the realization of those strategies. The Ministry of Culture has also taken steps to support the creative industries in the UAE, even before the launch of the national strategy, some of those initiatives include: � Established the Cultural and Creative Industries Council in 2018 to ensure inclusive and collective policymaking for the cultural sector in the UAE � Started the assessment of the funding ecosystem for the cultural sector in the UAE in 2020 � Started the assessment of conditions for cultural freelancers in the UAE in 2020 and has collaborated with Ministry of Economy to provide the required support for freelancers � Started the assessment of the IP system in the UAE in 2020 to ensure that it provides the necessary protections for the cultural sector

Agency Implementation: Le théâtre de l’Opéra de Tunis (TOT) : établissement public à caractère non administratif (EPNA) placé sous tutelle du Ministère des Affaires Culturelles doté de l’autonomie administrative et financière.
Main Feature: La cité de la culture (qui s’étale sur une superficie de presque 9 Hectares au cœur de la capitale) est conçue comme une véritable plateforme pour la promotion de la diversité culturelle et artistique dans ses expressions diverses. Elle vient renforcer le maillage institutionnel assez développé qui caractérise l’infrastructure culturelle en Tunisie. Fédératrice d’un certain nombre de pôles culturels qui regroupent pratiquement toutes les disciplines et les spécialités culturelles et artistiques (musique et opéra, ballet et chorégraphie, théâtre et arts scéniques, livre.) ainsi que des institutions culturelles dotés de l’autonomie administrative et financière (CNCI, TICDCE, MACAM, CNM, ENPFMC…), la cité de la culture s’inscrit dans le cadre d’une vision stratégique du Ministère des Affaires Culturelles (MAC) qui s’articule autour de : -	La promotion de la création littéraire et artistique.  -	L’encouragement des productions dans tous les secteurs artistiques y compris les arts numériques qui ne cessent des de développer grâce au développement des nouvelles technologies de communication. -	La garantie de l’accès pour le grand public notamment les jeunes et les enfants à un produit culturel diversifié mais aussi à forte valeur identitaire. -	La création d’une dynamique culturelle non seulement à travers l’évènementiel mais aussi et surtout à travers les connexions et le réseautage entre artistes et professionnels de la culture qui pourra éventuellement se traduire par des projets communs, des partenariats et des co-productions.    Le théâtre de l’Opéra de Tunis (TOT) « vaisseau amiral » de la Cité de la Culture est un établissement public à caractère non administratif (EPNA) placé sous tutelle du MAC doté de l’autonomie administrative et financière, il a pour missions : -	La création de l’orchestre symphonique de l’opéra de Tunis et du ballet de l’opéra de Tunis ainsi que la mise à niveau et la réorganisation de l’orchestre symphonique tunisien, de la troupe nationale des arts populaires en ce qui concerne les aspects juridiques organisationnels et ressources humaines. -	La production et la présentation de spectacles et de grandes œuvres artistiques ainsi que l’encouragement à la diffusion des différentes expressions artistiques telle que l’opéra, l’opérette et le théâtre chantant. -	L’encouragement de la création et la médiation culturelle permettant la consolidation du rayonnement de la culture et l’impulsion du tourisme culturel autour de grands évènement et de grandes productions artistiques. -	La mise à disposition des opérateurs culturels des espaces techniques nécessaires à la production, l’exercice et la formation. -	L’Organisation de résidences artistiques et le développement des modalités de coopération avec et entre les créateurs. -	La commercialisation et la diffusion des œuvres artistiques.  -	L’organisation de festivals et manifestations culturelles et artistiques. -	Le renforcement de la coopération, l’échange et le partenariat international.  -	La consolidation du partenariat public privé (PPP) dans le domaine du développement de l’action culturelle et de la création artistique. •	Pour mener à bien ses missions, le TOT dispose de 03 salles de spectacles : -	La salle « Théâtre de l’Opéra » avec 1650 places  -	La salle « Théâtre des régions » avec une capacité de 680 places -	La salle « théâtre jeunes créateurs » avec une capacité de 194 places. •	Les pôles artistiques qui relèvent du TOT : -	Musique et opéra : unité de gestion et de coordination administrative et artistique constituée d’une équipe pluridisciplinaire qui par sa diversité assure la coordination entre les différents orchestres et veille au respect des procédures en vigueur. Avec une approche stratégique et évolutive le pôle a pour objectif le développement des orchestres de références. Il assure par ailleurs la diversité d’une programmation musicale ambrassent toutes les tendances susceptibles de renforcer la scène artistique tunisienne.  -	Ballets et arts chorégraphiques : Il veille sur la mise en place de manifestations et projets artistiques et culturels liés à la danse et aux arts chorégraphiques développés à la cité de la culture dans le but d’assurer le rayonnement national et international de la danse tunisienne. Il comprend le Ballet de l’Opéra de Tunis, la Troupe nationale des arts populaires, le Centre Chorégraphique Tunisien. -	Théâtre et Arts Scéniques : structure de création qui se distingue par son ouverture sur la scène théâtrale nationale plus particulièrement professionnelle, et son soutien aux projets novateurs. Fondé sur une stratégie d’exploration et d’expérimentation des formes théâtrales les plus innovantes, le Pôle Théâtre et Arts scéniques se veut également un espace de dialogue et de confrontation artistique ouvert à toute proposition de nature à enrichir et promouvoir la scène théâtrale nationale. Depuis son lancement, son action s’est concentrée sur les objectifs fondamentaux d’appui à la création théâtrale des secteurs aussi bien professionnel qu’amateur ; une action concrète sous forme de mise à disposition d’un cadre de travail adéquat doté des moyens techniques, logistiques et de communication nécessaires. Par ailleurs, en qualité d’interlocuteur de la profession, le Pôle Théâtre et Arts Scéniques construit des relations avec l’ensemble des acteurs du théâtre du pays et développe des liens à l’international pour élargir son réseau de partenaires étrangers. Title EN: Cultural backpacks
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture
SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Cultural and creative sectors
Cultural Domain: Design,Performing Arts,Media Arts,Cinema and Audiovisual Arts,Music,Visual Arts
Agency Implementation: Ministry of Culture
Main Feature: This financing measure has been implemented since 2022 to improve access to culture of basic school students (grades 1 to 9) regardless of their special needs, place of residence, financial situation, and other conditions. Schools can use it for study trips (visits to museums, theatres, concerts, cinemas, and exhibitions) that are related to the school’s curriculum. The money can be used to buy tickets for cultural institutions and events and to order special programmes, as well as to cover travel expenses.   An important consideration is to guide teachers not just to visit cultural institutions, but to choose from the wide variety of available educational programmes that engage young people, to show them things "behind the scenes" and to introduce different professions.    The measure helps children and young people to develop both the subject competencies prescribed by the national curriculum, as well as to become creative and versatile individuals. Thereby, the measure contributes to the development of both the creators and the audience.   The financial support for municipal schools is allocated through local governments. Support for students attending state and private schools is allocated through the Ministry of Education and Research.
Results: The measure has been well received by schools and is actively used.  In 2023, the evaluation survey was sent to all basic schools, of which 70 % responded. 97.6% of the respondents confirmed that they had made use of the support measure vs 2,4 % who had not done so.   The system is simple to manage, flexible enough and gives schools freedom of choice (for example, the performances, exhibitions, museum lessons to be visited, time or organisation thereof is left up to the schools).  The measure allows systematic integration of study tours and visits into the studies during the academic year, successfully combining formal and non-formal learning.
Financial Ressources: The budget for 2022 was 1 071 500 USD and for 2023 1 607 250 USD
Recommandations: There have been two evaluations of the measure (after 2022 cycle and 2023 cycle).    In general, schools regard the measure as much needed and long-awaited support for student development. Visits to cultural institutions are well received and the financial support provides an opportunity to do this in a more systematic way than in the past, shaping the student's cultural experience across the whole basic education curriculum. Schools also appreciate the fact that the measure does not impose any additional application or reporting obligations.    A bottleneck in the implementation of the measure is the high transport costs for schools and special needs students in remote areas, which are unavoidable when visiting cultural institutions. Due to rising ticket prices and high fuel and time costs, the support measure would clearly require additional funding (an average of €11 per pupil per year is not sufficient to ensure an annual cultural experience). There is a need to ensure better communication between schools and cultural institutions and to seek further feedback and input from pupils to improve the conditions of the measure in the coming years.   It would be good to expand the measure to also cover children in kindergarten and high school students, but it will depend on the possibilities of state budget.

Title EN: Cultural Exchange Programme/ Memorandum of Understanding on Cultural Cooperation

Area of Monitoring: Treaties and agreements
Agency Implementation: Ministry of Arts and Cultural Heritage
Main Feature: To foster artistic and cultural exchange, Mauritius has a policy in place for collaboration with friendly nations.  Under this policy, the sending country shoulders the airfare and travel insurance for their artists, while the receiving country takes care of their accommodation, meals, and local transportation. This facilitates artist exchanges and fosters cultural understanding. The Ministry of Arts and Cultural Heritage has established agreements, known as Cultural Exchange Programs (CEPs) or Memorandums of Understanding (MOUs), with several countries to implement this policy. Some examples of these partner nations include India, China, Seychelles, and Madagascar.
Results: This policy has proven highly successful. A significant number of Mauritian artists have been able to represent their country by participating in international cultural events abroad. This exposure has increased Mauritius' visibility on the global stage, fostering a greater international appreciation for its unique artistic heritage. Additionally, these exchanges have facilitated collaboration with foreign artists, leading to a valuable sharing of experiences and perspectives that enriches both sides. Title EN: Cultural Consultations in Denmark
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture
SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Partnering with civil society
Agency Implementation: Kulturelle Samråd I Danmark
Main Feature: The huge civil society sector of voluntary culture in the Nordic and Baltic Countries not only provide joy, friendship, and meaning for the participants, but it can also support and strengthen the added community values in the following four focus areas: 1. social inclusion & cohesion, 2. active citizenship & democracy, 3. environmental sustainability. Based on these considerations, the aim of the project is to support lifelong learning providers in the sector of voluntary culture to gain better tools and practice methods to assess the potentials of their activities to promote key societal benefits. Until now, learning providers in the sector can use many good practice examples as inspiration and support. However, there is a need of more systematic tools and methods for the learning providers on how to concretely assess their own activities and implement improved practice. Title EN: Cultural Pacts for Life and Peace
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture
SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Cultural and creative sectors
Cultural Domain: Performing Arts,Media Arts,Cinema and Audiovisual Arts,Music,Publishing,Visual Arts
Agency Implementation: Ministry of Cultures, Arts, and Knowledge of Colombia
Main Feature: The Cultural Pacts are a great agreement that seeks the protection of life and peace through the strengthening of the cultural sector. It arises from the common needs of the people in the territory. They are a roadmap that is drawn from the demands of the communities, an engine of popular strength, an amplifier of the culture of peace and an action that transforms the institutional logic towards the popular mandate.         Cultural pacts seek to strengthen the articulation between organizations, groups, and workers in the arts and cultures, to promote the governance process from the sector and strengthen social and cultural mobilization.         Its implementation began in 2023 with the I Cultural Pact for Life and Peace signed in the Nariño Pacific. To date, three Pacts have been signed, as follows:         I Cultural Pact for Life and Peace - Nariño Pacific (Tumaco, Barbacoas, El Charco, Olaya, Maguí Payan, Roberto Payan, Ricaurte, Santa Barbara de Iscuandé, Francisco Pizarro, La Tola, Mosquera)         II Cultural Pact for life and peace - Magdalena Medio: (Barrancabermeja, Yondó, Cantagallo, San Pablo, Santa Rosa, Simití Morales, Arenal).         III Cultural Pact for life and peace: ethnic, farmer, and amphibian cultures for the defense of life. (San Pelayo, Tuchin, Montelíbano, Magangué, San Benito Abad, San Marcos, Ayapel, San José de Uré).                  For the implementation of the Strategy, the following actions are considered:         Prioritization of territories: It is based on mapping and regionalization, carried out by the Ministry of Equality, categorizing the most excluded municipalities, taking into account high deficiencies in aspects such as: investment, access to public services, education, and violence. At the same time, this information is cross-referenced with internal data from the Ministry of Culture, Arts, and Knowledge, related to the development of institutional projects, cultural and community processes, intangible heritage, managers and artists (all through the Soy Culture platform and Planning Report)          Construction and diagnosis of collective needs: Once the municipalities have been selected, visits are made to significant experiences in the territories, and representatives of organizations, cultural managers, social leaders are invited to working groups and participatory dialogues who promote the construction of a culture of peace in the territories. In these working groups, a map of collective needs is built, a document that is sent to the different areas of the Ministry of Culture for their response. Here some processes are also identified that require immediate strengthening for the execution of their activities. This type of support has been called acupuncture.         Participatory dialogues: Meetings are held between different leaders and organizations for the          collective construction of a needs assessment document. Then the territorial team proceeds to structure a document on the pillars, current problematic situation, needs and proposals of the community. Finally, a collective document approval process is conducted with the community.         Visits and bilateral dialogues: Different immersive visits are made by the Ministry team to organizations,  leaders and groups of arts, cultures, and knowledge, and bilateral dialogues with organizations, local government, private sector, and cooperation.         Collective creations: Other ways of dialogue in the community of arts, cultures, and knowledge proposed by this strategy are based on the creative capacity of the communities. For this reason, it is proposed to develop a collective creation of short format works integrating the diversity of artistic and cultural practices of each municipality.         Signing of the Pact: To finalize the Pact construction process, a meeting is held between the territories prioritized by stage. This event also includes a cultural mobilization, a fair of popular economies and the presentation of different collective creations. The event also recognizes artists, experts, and cultural workers, highlighting older adults. Amidst this rich artistic and cultural activity, the Minister makes the public announcement of the commitments of the Ministry of Cultures to the region.         Implementation and monitoring: Once the Pact is signed, the internal administrative processes, pedagogy, and socialization sessions with the communities begin. After that, the different areas begin the execution of activities in the territory. As a process of accompaniment to the fulfillment of commitments, internal monitoring, and support working groups are periodically held with the different areas and communities of the Pact.
Results: To date we present the following advances: Cultural Pact for Life and Peace - Nariño Pacific:  46 commitments, 125 impacted organizations, and 677 participants.  II Cultural Pact for life and peace - Magdalena Medio: 40 commitments. The Pact signing event saw the participation of 370 people, including artists and experts, on stage. 50 popular economy ventures, 15 memory exhibitions, 8 collective creations, 12 recognitions and eight acupunctures worth COP$130 million. Also, 50 arts and cultural groups participated. III Cultural Pact for life and peace: ethnic, farmers and amphibian cultures for the defense of life:  175 commitments. More than 500 people from different regions and 9 acupunctures worth COP$172 million were mobilized at the Pact signing event.

It aims to enhance understanding and appreciation of India's cultural heritage while linking it to modern development goals, targeting a developed India by 2047. It emphasizes a holistic and inclusive approach to cultural exploration and serves as a platform for constructive dialogue, aiming to position India's cultural resurgence as a global knowledge contributor.
Results: Since its inception, the "Cultural Policy Chaupal: Culture for Development – Viksit Bharat@2047" has achieved significant milestones, including a successful inaugural session on February 23, 2024, which set a strong foundation for the series. The dialogues have facilitated direct conversations between the youth and experts, raising awareness about India's cultural heritage and its relevance to development.   The series has encouraged pride in India's cultural achievements and promoted the revival of ancient practices through efforts like the 'Ancient Stitched Ship Reconstruction Project.' By integrating diverse perspectives, the initiative has appealed to a wide audience and established a strong platform for future cultural discussions, setting a model for sustained efforts in promoting and preserving India's cultural heritage.

Electronic questionnaires and many documents, studies, and strategies related to cultural affairs were also used locally and internationally to investigate the Omani cultural scene with its challenges, needs, and aspirations.  11 Areas: The strategy covered 11 areas: identity and intangible cultural heritage, manuscripts, cultural festivals and exhibitions, libraries, cultural centers and clubs, translation and publishing, visual arts; cultural communication, cultural initiatives, literature, performing arts; and finally cultural events, competitions, and awards.  Themes and objectives: The cultural strategy is divided into seven themes that include a number of objectives: The first theme is “Creativity and Cultural Development”, which focuses on enabling and enhancing cultural production based on renewal, creativity, and innovation in the Sultanate of Oman, employing advanced technology to produce and publish Omani cultural content, supporting studies and research that enhance creativity and development, and sponsoring talented and creative people in cultural fields.  The second theme is represented by "Creative Cultural Industries,” whose objectives are achieved by enhancing the economic contribution of the cultural sector, providing facilities for projects in the field of creative industries, enhancing awareness of the importance of investing in the cultural field, and supporting and encouraging investment in sustainable creative cultural projects.   The objectives of the third theme in "Cultural Identity" are achieved by preserving and developing cultural knowledge related to identity, international cooperation in the fields of cultural identity and preserving intangible cultural heritage, spreading awareness and knowledge of the Omani cultural identity locally and abroad, anticipating renewed knowledge according to the constants of the national cultural identity, and also rooting the national cultural identity.  The fourth theme, "Culture and Society", addresses the following objectives: activating the cultural role of civil society institutions, encouraging the establishment of cultural initiatives to consolidate the community partnership system, raising awareness of the principle of local and foreign cultural diversity, dialogue and constructive criticism, culturally humanizing cities, and preparing the appropriate environment for cultural movement in the various governorates of the Sultanate.   The objectives of the fifth theme, "Cultural Development", are achieved by employing technology to support cultural sector programs and projects, enhancing the investment system in cultural assets, developing cultural structures that embrace cultural work, developing administrative and financial procedures related to cultural work, and also preparing and qualifying human cadres working in the cultural sector.   The objectives of the sixth theme, “Cultural Regulations and Legislation,” are represented in reviewing and developing the regulations and legislation governing cultural work, creating legislation, systems and regulations that enhance cultural work, and activating cultural agreements and treaties signed by the Sultanate of Oman with international organizations and institutions. The strategy concluded its objectives with the “Cultural Communication” theme, which is represented in investing in cultural diversity as a means of promoting and introducing the Sultanate, enhancing communication and cultural dialogue with countries of the world, exchanging expertise internally and externally in the cultural field, highlighting the role of the Sultanate of Oman in the global cultural map, and also achieving partnership and integration with local and international institutions in cultural fields.

Title EN: Culture and Gender Equality – EU Gender Equality Strategy
Goal: Promote Human Rights And Fundamental Freedoms
SDG: SDG 5 - Achieve gender equality and empower all women and girls,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels
Area of Monitoring: Gender equality
Cultural Domain: Design,Performing Arts,Media Arts,Cinema and Audiovisual Arts,Music,Publishing,Visual Arts
Agency Implementation: European Commission
Main Feature: The European Union Gender Equality Strategy adopted in March 2020 seeks significant progress towards a gender-equal Europe by 2025. The Strategy presents policy objectives and actions to deliver on the commitment of the von der Leyen Commission to achieve a Union of Equality.    It states that all citizens, regardless of their sex, gender identity and expression, sex characteristics, sexual identity; racial or ethnic origin, age, religion or belief and any disability, must be able to pursue their chosen path in life and have equal opportunities to thrive, participate and lead. It recognizes the role of the media and the cultural sectors in shaping people’s beliefs, values and perception of reality, and are thus further key channels for changing attitudes and challenging stereotypes.  In this document, the European Commission commits itself to continue supporting projects promoting gender equality under the Creative Europe Programme, including under the Music Moves Europe initiative.  Presidency Conclusions on gender equality in the field of culture adopted in December 2020, underline the potential of culture to advance gender equality and acknowledge persistent gender inequalities in the sector. The document refers in particular to obstacles related to:   •	equal access to the cultural and creative labour market; •	equal payment and representation in creative and decision-making positions; •	equal appreciation and recognition of work.   The report of EU Member States’ experts “Towards gender equality in the cultural and creative sectors” provides an overview on the discrimination of  women artists and creative professionals. The report focusses on the following key challenges: •	gender stereotypes; •	sexual harassment; •	access to the labour market and the gender pay gap; •	access to resources; •	access to leadership positions and female entrepreneurship. This report details extensive recommendations and good practices on how to implement these. It also collects over 250 practices from across the EU.   Creative Europe projects: Several projects promoting gender equality have received co-funding under the Creative Europe programme, including a flagship initiative in the music sector – the Keychange project.    Keychange is an international campaign that encourages music festivals, orchestras, conservatoires, broadcasters, concert halls, agents, record labels and music organisations to pledge their commitment to achieving a 50:50 gender balance by 2022.    The new Creative Europe programme foresees strengthening the role of gender equality across beneficiary projects.  The Culture Moves Europe mobility scheme offers special financial support to people having children below the age of 10. The mobility scheme has a particular focus on emerging artists and aims at maintaining gender balance among its grantees.

Main Feature: In line with the State's policy to implement the provisions of the International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights, the “Mada” (Assistive Technology Center) launched an accessible platform titled "Culture and Community Support Platform." These provisions include enabling every individual to enjoy their right to participate in cultural life, their right to science, and their right to protection of interests related to authorship rights. The platform was launched following the COVID-19 pandemic. It is specifically designed for persons with disabilities and contains vital information, resources, and electronic services in the cultural and community sectors. The goal is to ensure that all individuals, including those with functional limitations such as disabilities and the elderly, have access to resources and electronic services through a single platform. Mada Center has committed to continuously updating this platform and adding the latest programs and resources, selected by experts and specialists in cultural programs from Mada and its strategic partners. This is conducted through various communication methods indicated on its official website.    This initiative/measure is part of a series of parallel and subsequent efforts aimed at establishing a general framework for the inclusion of persons with disabilities in society and facilitating their participation in social life, including their right to participate in cultural life. For instance, Mada designed the "Inclusive Digital Education Support" platform, another initiative supporting remote learning, aimed at ensuring inclusive education for all students, including those with disabilities and functional limitations. In addition to these two platforms, Mada Center issued its first guide in 2022, which includes the latest methods and approaches in training persons with disabilities and creating an inclusive and accessible training environment. In 2023, a second guide was released, detailing how to access digital media (Annex No. 36).    The Assistive Technology Center “Mada” is a private institution of public benefit, established in 2010 as an initiative to support digital accessibility for persons with disabilities and to create a technological community that generally meets the needs of the elderly and particularly those with functional limitations, including persons with disabilities. Furthermore, the center provides consulting and training in key areas related to ICT accessibility policies and best practices (Annex No. 37).
Results: The Assistive Technology Center “Mada” won the UNESCO for Digital Empowerment of Persons with Disabilities for 2020-2021 in the organizations category. This award recognized Mada's achievements in strengthening digital inclusivity and building a technology-accessible community for persons with disabilities, as well as its significant role in supporting government strategies, legislation, and policies in this field. This UNESCO prize, valued at USD 40,000, was established in 2002 with support and funding from the State of Kuwait. It aims to reward contributions by individuals, groups, organizations, or specialized centers in fields related to the special educational needs of the mentally disabled, provided that the nominees have made outstanding achievements in research and practical studies related to enhancing the quality of education for persons with disabilities (Annex No. 38). -	Additionally, Mada won the ESCWA Arab Digital Content Award for 2023 for its project "Unified Arabic Braille Portal," the first initiative worldwide to provide eight-dot Braille tables in Arabic (Annex No. 38). -	Mada has become a model for the sustainable use of technology to integrate persons with disabilities into society. Its outstanding work in research and development, application, consulting services, standardization, and providing assistive technology to users with disabilities has set an example for various State institutions working to establish principles of digital accessibility. -	This initiative has enabled various institutions and agencies responsible for assisting persons with disabilities to organize numerous events aimed at facilitating the integration of this group of citizens. For instance: -	In 2022, the Qatari Media Center organized events titled "Digitization" for the members of the Qatari Social and Cultural Center for the Deaf. -	The Music Affairs Center held a cultural event in the same year for persons with disabilities to qualify and help them use their disability as a motivation to overcome their specific conditions and succeed in life. -	The Supreme Committee for Delivery and Legacy organized a conference on November 6, 2022, for this group of citizens to clarify the ways and procedures for their attendance at the Qatar World Cup events.

Title EN: Culture Collective
Goal: Integrate Culture In Sustainable Development Frameworks

Area of Monitoring: National sustainable development policies and plans

Agency Implementation: Creative Scotland
Main Feature: Culture Collective is a network of 26 participatory arts projects, shaped by local communities alongside artists and creative organisations. Funded by the Scottish Government through Creative Scotland, these projects took place across Scotland from March 2021-October 2023.    From Shetland to Inverclyde, Aberdeen to Hawick, each unique project is designed and driven by the community in which it is rooted, playing an important part in shaping the future cultural life of Scotland. Some projects are worked to creatively engage with older community members; some provide opportunities for young women and non-binary people to find their voices; and others address disconnection, loneliness and mental health in a post-lockdown world.    For the projects themselves, the Culture Collective provides a network: opportunities to share resources, learning and experiences. For the sector as a whole, the Culture Collective shines a light on the crucial importance of participatory arts projects for artists, for communities and for the future.
Results: The Culture Collective programme, supported initially through Scottish Government Emergency Funding, received £4.27m from the Scottish Government in March 2022 to support the existing network of 26 projects (supported with £6m of Scottish Government funds in 2021/22) to extend their work for up to a year. In 2022/23, the Scottish Government provided a further £230,000 to support the Network’s programme of peer learning, development, exchange and collaboration.    In September 2022, representatives from the Culture Collective Network were invited to present at The International Teaching Artists Collaborative (ITAC) in Oslo, highlighting the innovative Culture Collective model, and showcasing the work of artists and communities in Scotland. The ITAC programme is the world-wide network for artists who work in participatory settings to create positive social impact.
Financial Ressources: Since 2021, $13.51m worth of funding has been allocated to support the Culture Collective Programme.
Recommandations: In February 2022, an evaluation team from the Centre for Communication, Cultural and Media Studies at Queen Margaret University in Edinburgh was commissioned by Creative Scotland to undertake an evaluation of the Culture Collective. The evaluation states:    ‘It is clear that the unique, flexible, and long term support offered by the Programme has enabled the projects to make their work responsive to their place, with more meaningful community-centred engagement.     The Programme is developing what should be understood to be important cultural infrastructure – in terms of the networks and connections between the organisations, partners and artists in the project locations. Evidence from the projects shows that these (viable) networks are vital for places to be able to generate and continue this type of work.     There is evidence that projects are already maximising the value that comes from an investment of this scale. The value of the work taking place is multifaceted: for the cultural sector; for the communities they are working with; for local authorities seeking models of person-centred service provision and rapid, targeted responses to local need; and for policymakers seeking to fulfil Covid Recovery objectives by means of this Programme.     On the basis of the evidence presented in this report, we can also confidently state that the programme is already performing significantly across the aims of Scotland’s Culture Strategy.    The next part of our evaluation (currently unpublished) gathers more definitive figures at the close of the projects’ programmes of work, and presents a collection of case studies to illustrate the kind of outcomes created in the programme made possible as a result of the key enabling factors inherent in this unique funding approach.’

SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Cultural and creative sectors
Agency Implementation: Federal Ministry of Education and Research
Main Feature: Main aims: Fostering extracurricular culture and arts education projects for children and adolescents who would otherwise have limited access to culture and arts education.  Target groups: Children and adolescents between the ages of 3 and 18 years.  Expected results: •	Reducing worrying correlations between children’s educational attainment and their families’ socio-economic circumstances  •	Opening up new opportunities for education and development to children and adolescents who have limited access to culture and arts education  •	Boosting civil society engagement and mobilising local alliances •	Fostering the quality, diversity and attractiveness of provision  •	Contributing to more educational fairness and social participation as important prerequisites of social cohesion
Results: New in the 2020-2023 reporting period (Information on the previous funding period of this measure can be found in the third periodic report.):          Further development undertaken in four areas to reinforce the quality, outreach and sustainability of the programme: (1) ties generated among Culture is Strength players within each municipality to establish lasting educational provision, (2) high-quality involvement fostered in the development of all-day provision in schools, (3) alliance players in rural areas mobilised and empowered and (4) digital media, issues and/or expressions incorporated into the projects at a local level.
Financial Ressources: up to EUR 50 million a year (2023-2027)
Recommandations: The project is evaluated continuously. Facts, figures and data are available (in German) here: https://www.buendnisse-fuer-bildung.de/buendnissefuerbildung/shareddocs/downloads/files/210831_bmbf_kms_zahlen_2021.pdf?__blob=publicationFile&v=6  Final report (in German) on the evaluation and monitoring of Culture is Strength. Education Alliances in the second funding phase (2018-2022): https://www.buendnisse-fuer-bildung.de/buendnissefuerbildung/shareddocs/downloads/files/20230627_Evaluation.pdf?__blob=publicationFile&v=2  Key findings: During its first two funding phases, the programme achieved a vast reach nationwide and worked effectively in terms of mobilising alliances and initiating projects. The third funding phase has had a successful start. Since the launch of the programme in 2013, more than 17,950 education alliances have profited from the programme. Around 45,000 projects for children and adolescents have been conducted across the whole of Germany, reaching some 1.3 million participants.  The projects profit from a high number of volunteers being involved. Project implementation is focused on regions where the target group, educationally disadvantaged children and adolescents, is frequently to be found. The reach is greatest in the Eastern Länder and the city-states. By the end of the second funding phase, projects within the programme had been offered in 99% of Germany’s 401 districts and unaffiliated towns and cities.

Title EN: Cyprus Choreography Showcase
Goal: Achieve A Balanced Flow Of Cultural Goods And Services And Increase The Mobility Of Artists And Cultural Professionals
SDG: SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 10 - Reduce inequality within and among countries,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Mobility of artists and cultural professionals
Agency Implementation: Deputy Ministry of Culture
Main Feature: Launched in 2020, the Cyprus Choreography Showcase (CCS) takes place every two years at the Rialto Theatre and aims at showcasing the work of local choreographers abroad, as well as at creating greater visibility for the Cypriot contemporary cultural production. CCS has become an institutional event that presents selected choreographic pieces, conceived and created in Cyprus over the past two years. More specifically, the CCS offers the opportunity to Cyprus-based choreographers to present their works, within an organised context, to artistic directors and international contemporary dance festival representatives, thus fostering collaborations with global dance networks. In this way, the Showcase enhances the choreographers’ efforts for international promotion and presentation of their works abroad. At the same time, CCS offers the chance to the local audience to re-watch some of the most memorable choreographic productions.   Cypriot choreographers or permanent residents of Cyprus living and working on the island during the past five years have the right to participate in the CCS. A special Committee is responsible for selecting the choreographic works. After examining and evaluating the submitted proposals over a period of two years, the Committee proposes the projects that ARE INCLUDED in each CCS edition.

Goal: Achieve A Balanced Flow Of Cultural Goods And Services And Increase The Mobility Of Artists And Cultural Professionals

Agency Implementation: Danza Urbana ETS
Main Feature: It aims to support young authors in accessing programming circuits abroad for works designed or re-staged for unusual contexts, as well as training courses abroad in the field of urban dance.                   The program provides two mobility grants for foreign countries, which will be awarded by a Commission of experts in the field. The selected authors may use the mobility grant to cover travel expenses related to the programming of the selected show or to participate in training courses. In the latter case the grant can also be used to cover any registration costs. The winners have full choice both in terms of circuiting (squares/festivals/international exhibitions) and of training course (Schools/workshops/international seminars). Danza Urbana ETS also reserves the right to promote the winning works to the partners of the Dancescapes project and the international networks with which it collaborates, in order to evaluate any programming or participation in a training course in their own events.

Title EN: D—Arts – Project Office for Diversity
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture
SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Cultural and creative sectors
Cultural Domain: Design,Performing Arts,Media Arts,Cinema and Audiovisual Arts,Music,Publishing,Visual Arts
Agency Implementation: D—Arts - Projektbüro für Diversität
Main Feature: D—Arts is a project office and network of cultural institutions, initiatives and actors that promotes the diversification of the Austrian arts and culture sector and aims to fundamentally transform the sector. Based on a critical concept of diversity, decentralized strategies, and dialogical concepts, D—Arts’ goal is to encourage and support diversity-focused structural change in the Austrian arts and culture sector. The project office builds on a broad network; the cooperation between different actors (artists, cultural workers, cultural institutions, and cultural policy) is central. D—Arts was officially founded in 2023. 78 institutions have committed themselves to and are actively working towards the diversification of the arts and culture sector. The project office has established an expert network and offers diversity training for art practitioners and institutions. It supports transformations processes in cultural institutions through counselling and know how. A main goal is also to raise awareness for the importance of critical diversity and anti-discriminatory approaches in the arts and culture sector through promoting dialogue and public discourse on the topic.

Title EN: Database with works by women and gender minoritised composers in the genre of Western Art Music from the Nordic countries
Goal: Promote Human Rights And Fundamental Freedoms
SDG: SDG 5 - Achieve gender equality and empower all women and girls,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels
Area of Monitoring: Gender equality
Agency Implementation: KVAST (Swedish Association of Women Composers)
Main Feature: During 2023 KVAST (Swedish Association of Women Composers) started the work to establish a new database with works by women and gender minoritised composers in the genre of Western Art Music from the Nordic countries. The database is intended to be run by several institutions and represent all the Nordic countries. It will be marketed worldwide and will make repertoire by women and gender minoritised composers from the Nordic countries easily available to art musicians all over the world. KVAST also aims to provide sheet music. The database will thus function as a tool in a struggle for increased equality in terms of repertoire on the world’s classical music scene. The marketing will promote the common profile of the Nordic countries concerning gender equality, and it will hopefully increase performances by Nordic women and gender minoritised composers, as well promoting gender equality in the repertoire on the classical music scene in the Nordic region and in the rest of the world.

Title EN: Decentralization Fund
Goal: Integrate Culture In Sustainable Development Frameworks
SDG: SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: International cooperation for sustainable development
Cultural Domain: Design,Performing Arts,Media Arts,Cinema and Audiovisual Arts,Music,Publishing,Visual Arts
Agency Implementation: Ministry of Finance - national plan directorate
Main Feature: Grant instrument under 4th Indicative Cooperation Program Financed by Luxembourg cooperation was launched on 2022. More than 4 million euros has been made available by Luxembourg Cooperation in order to empower local communities and support municipalities themselves in their strategic plan of local development. The fund was developed on three fronts:  1. A plan to strengthen the capacity of municipalities and associations in the formulation, execution and justification of projects of which the Together for Local Transformation project aimed at community associations is part. 2. Proximity support to the beneficiary institution in the form of personalized coaching to ensure good management of the project from its identification, through formulation, monitoring and final justification; 3. A communication and information strategy for beneficiaries and the general public, through the creation of an interactive website that serves to provide information at all times and in an accessible and transparent way about the implementation status of projects financed by the FD. The program is aligned with the desire of national authorities to deepen the decentralization process with the purpose of reducing regional asymmetries and improving local populations' access to basic services.
Results: After three years of project implementation, which benefited more than 21 thousand people in the country's 22 municipalities. 22 projects were developed in the most diverse areas by the country's 22 municipalities within the scope of the Decentralization Fund implemented from April 2021 to February 2023.
Financial Ressources: 6 million euros: 2,800,000 euros for projects to associations and city councils: 2,300,000 euros divided among all 22 municipalities in the country; 500,000 euros divided for the 9 pilot municipalities of the Platform for Local Development and Objectives 2030 Cape Verde Program (the 3 of Santo Antão, the 3 of Fogo, São Salvador do Mundo and Ribeira Grande de Santiago).
Recommandations: The program recommends directing the focus of projects on a single essential and structural problem in the municipality in order to maximize the impact of interventions. A more active role is also recommended in the priority intervention areas indicated in the Municipal Strategic Sustainable Development Plans (PEMDS) and in the annual budgets, encouraging a higher municipal contribution (a minimum of 20%), as a way to promote greater involvement of municipal actors

Title EN: Decree Nº 11,336, of January 1, 2023, which approves the regulatory structure of the Ministry of Culture
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture
SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Cultural and creative sectors
Cultural Domain: Design,Performing Arts,Media Arts,Cinema and Audiovisual Arts,Music,Publishing,Visual Arts
Agency Implementation: Ministry of Culture
Main Feature: In Brazil, the body responsible for the cultural and creative sectors is the Ministry of Culture (MinC). According to Decree No. 11,336, of January 1, 2023, which approves the regulatory structure of the MinC, the Secretariat of Creative Economy and Cultural Promotion is responsible for: X - propose, conduct and support the elaboration, implementation and evaluation of plans and public policies for the development of the creative economy ; XI - plan, promote, implement and coordinate actions for the development of the Brazilian creative economy ; XII – formulate and support actions to train cultural professionals and entrepreneurs and qualify enterprises in the creative sectors ; XIII - formulate, implement and articulate lines of financing for actions in the creative sectors to strengthen their production chain ; XIV - establish programs and projects to support actions by the creative sectors, their professionals and entrepreneurs, to articulate and strengthen micro and small cultural enterprises ; XV - subsidize actions to promote Brazilian cultural goods and services at national and international events, in conjunction with the Special Advisory for International Affairs; XVI - support actions to intensify technical and management exchanges in the creative sectors with foreign countries ; XVII - articulate and conduct the mapping of Brazil's creative economy to identify vocations and opportunities for local and regional development ; XVIII - create mechanisms for institutional consolidation of regulatory instruments in the creative economy sector ; XIX - articulate with public bodies the inclusion of the theme of creative economy in their areas of activity; It is XX - subsidize other units of the Ministry and its related entities in the formulation of policies to promote the Brazilian creative economy.  Art. 26. The Directorate of Economic Development of Culture is responsible for: I - implement a program to promote and encourage cultural production chains; II - coordinate and implement the creative economy program, to incentives for micro and small companies in the creative sectors; III - coordinate, implement and manage, in conjunction with the FCRB, the National System of Information and Cultural Indicators; IV - plan , coordinate, supervise and prepare, in conjunction with the FCRB, technical studies and research of a statistical nature with a view to formulating public cultural policies; V - establish partnerships, nationally and internationally, with a view to improving the areas of research and information related to the Ministry's activities; It is VI - encourage cooperation between cultural observatories, with a view to exchanging methodologies, studies and statistical data.
Results: In line with the competencies established by Decree Nº 11,336 of 2023, the Ministry of Culture has, since its recent recreation, been making efforts to carry out actions aimed at developing and strengthening the creative economy in Brazil.
Financial Ressources: Not applicable

Title EN: Declaration of Intent of the Network of Colombian Creative Cities
Goal: Achieve A Balanced Flow Of Cultural Goods And Services And Increase The Mobility Of Artists And Cultural Professionals
SDG: SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 10 - Reduce inequality within and among countries,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Treaties and agreements
Cultural Domain: Design,Performing Arts,Media Arts,Cinema and Audiovisual Arts,Music,Publishing,Visual Arts
Agency Implementation: Ministry of Cultures, Arts, and Knowledge
Main Feature: The articulation of the different cities allowed the Annual Meeting of the UNESCO Network of Creative Cities in Media Arts to be held in Cali between October 31 and November 3, 2023, which brought together the delegations of 15 international and 7 national cities, and was carried out for the first time in Latin America.                   In the context of the Meeting, a Declaration of Intent was signed between the eight cities, the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, and the Ministry of Cultures, Arts, and Knowledge. The Declaration aims to:         ●	Ensure compliance with the mission of the UNESCO Creative Cities Network, that is, strengthen cooperation between cities, creativity as a strategic factor of sustainable development, in economic, social, cultural, and environmental terms, generating cooperation strategies in network with local initiatives of national and global articulation.         ●	Facilitate among Colombian member cities the exchange of experiences, knowledge, and good practices to guarantee competitiveness with respect to other cities both nationally and internationally.         ●	Create opportunities for inter-sectoral and cross-cutting collaboration and encourage the execution of joint creative projects to reinforce the creation, production, distribution, and dissemination of activities, goods and services that ensure sustainable urban development and social stability through the organization of events, exchange projects, and joint initiatives in different creative fields.         ●	Protect and promote cultural heritage, cultural diversity, and creative assets, especially in times of crisis, and enable the cultural and creative sectors to contribute to recovery and revitalization processes.         ●	Create/generate periodic spaces that allow the design and monitoring of work strategies to position cultural heritage and the local creative industry, at the national and international level, based on the work plans established in the application and the four-yearly reports delivered to UNESCO.         ●	Strengthen the cultural industries and the country's creative economies and practices, encouraging the generation of national and international projects as a potential source of investment to promote the diversification of markets and products produced in Colombian creative cities.         ●	Accompany and technically support future candidatures of other Colombian cities that wish to join the UNESCO Creative Cities Network (UCCN).         ●	Make visible the actions of Colombian Creative Cities in the national and international context.         ●	Constitute itself as a space for discussion to define a concerted strategy to reinforce the Colombian presence and experience within the UCCN and actively participate in the global network and networks for creative vocation.         ●	Contribute to the design of public policies that ensure urban creativity and citizen participation.
Results: Periodic meetings are being held between the 8 Colombian cities to exchange good practices and strengthen the network of Colombian creative cities.
