Title EN: DEFILE DE MODE POUR L’EXPANSION DU CENTRE DE FORMATION POUR TISSERANDES ABE APO ELISABETH DE MONTEZO
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture
SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Cultural and creative sectors
Agency Implementation: CENTRE DE FORMATION POUR TISSERANDES ABE APO ELISABETH DE MONTEZO
Main Feature: Le défilé de mode a été organisé pendant la Coupe d'Afrique des Nations(CAN) 2023. Il a conjointement été mis en œuvre par le Ministère de la Culture et de la Francophonie et l’organisation Africa Fashion International (AFI). Africa Fashion International est une Association Sud-Africaine dirigée par Mme Dr Precious Moloi –Motsepe. Ce défilé de mode  s’inscrit dans le volet culturel de cet évènement sportif, la CAN. Ces deux entités sont  à l’origine de la grande partie des fonds récoltés au cours de cette soirée. Avec notamment un chèque de 50 000 dollars offert sur les 70 000 dollars mobilisés.    Cette activité réalisée entre dans le cadre de la promotion du secteur de la mode en Côte d’Ivoire. Ainsi, le rendez-vous sportif  international , la CAN, a servi de tremplin à la mode. Un défilé de mode,  vitrine qui a réuni la diversité des expressions culturelles des créateurs de vingt-quatre pays participant à la trente quatrième édition de l’évènement sportif phare de la CAF.   Ce défilé caritatif avait pour objectifs, entre autres, de collecter des fonds, de  promouvoir la formation aux  métiers du tissage  et  de participer à l’autonomisation de la femme. Il a été l’occasion de mettre en lumière, le talent de plusieurs créateurs de mode des 24 pays participants à la Can 2023. Les fonds récoltés ont été  réversés au Centre Artisanal Abé Apo Élisabeth, à Montézo une ville située à une cinquantaine de km d’Abidjan, dans la région d'ALÉPÉ, créé  par la créatrice de mode et entrepreneure culturelle, Michèle Yakice, fille de  Montézo.  Ce centre se consacre à la formation des femmes et des jeunes dans l’art du tissage traditionnel, leur permettant d’acquérir des compétences dans le domaine et de gagner leur autonomie.  Cette activité a  participé au rayonnement de la culture ivoirienne à travers la promotion du pagne tissé. Ensuite, elle a  permis à de nombreuses jeunes filles et femmes d’apprendre un métier; cela  favorise leur autonomisation financière.  Le Centre s’inscrit également dans la logique de développement du village de Montezo par la création d’infrastructures. Une des  principales caractéristiques de cette mesure, vise à créer une synergie d’actions entre les entités concernées, notamment, le Gouvernement,  l'Association des Footballeurs Ivoiriens (AFI), les acteurs culturels  de Montezo  afin de  soutenir ledit centre.    Le Gouvernement ivoirien représenté par le Ministère de la Culture et de la Francophonie, et la Confédération Africaine de Football (CAF), par le biais de l’AFI, vont assurer la mise en œuvre du projet et son suivi. Un protocole d’accord a été signé entre les 2 parties. Le Centre Artisanal Abé Apo Elisabeth soutenu également par l’UNESCO, ambitionne d’agrandir, diversifier les activités  pour créer des richesses et soutenir les femmes vulnérables, offrant des opportunités d’emplois  et une garderie pour leurs enfants pendant les heures de travail. Le projet d’extension des tisserandes de Montézo tombe à point nommé et pourrait être considéré comme un projet avant-coureur de la possibilité d’étendre le métier de tissage aux femmes à toutes les aires géographiques de Côte d’Ivoire.
Results: cette  mesure a donné les résultats suivants:   -Autonomisation financière des femmes à travers les métiers du tissage;   -Intégration de la femme dans la filière du tissage en Côte d'Ivoire. En effet, en Côte d’Ivoire, la fabrication du pagne tissé ou l’art du pagne tissé s’étend sur 3 ou 4 principales aires géographiques occupés par les groupes ethniques Akan (Sud, Centre, Est), Krou (Centre-Ouest, Sud-Ouest, Ouest), Gour (Nord, Nord-Est), Mandé(Centre-Ouest, Ouest, Nord-Ouest) et les Dan (Ouest). Elle est en général dominée par les hommes qui interviennent tout au long de la chaîne de valeur. Mais aujourd'hui avec le Centre des tisserandes de Montezo, les femmes peuvent exercer le métier de tisserandes;  -L'extension du  Centre de Formation pour Tisserandes de Montézo, permet à long terme, de briser le plafond de verre plus efficacement, les barrières socio culturelles liées à la production du pagne tissé.   - En étendant le métier de tissage aux femmes, l’on assistera à une forte production du pagne tissé made in Côte d’Ivoire et partant, à une appropriation du pagne par les populations.

Title EN: Des partenariats pour promouvoir la diffusion du contenu culturel
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture
SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Media diversity
Agency Implementation: Le Ministère des Affaires Culturelles (MAC), La Radio Nationale Tunisienne, La télévision tunisienne, L'Union de Radiodiffusion des États Arabes (ASBU)
Main Feature: L’instauration d’une culture de proximité notamment à travers la diffusion d’un contenu culturel diversifié et accessible à tous les citoyens et répondant aux attentes de diverses catégories sociales sur tout le territoire national, figure parmi les priorités stratégiques du Ministère des Affaires Culturelles (MAC). Ces priorités s’alignent en la matière avec les dispositions de la nouvelle constitution tunisienne adoptée par referendum le 25 Juillet 2022 ayant consacré son chapitre 2 aux « droits et libertés » et garantissant aussi bien les droits civils et politiques que les droits économiques, sociaux et culturels. Plusieurs dispositions constitutionnelles s’inscrivant dans le cadre de la garantie de la liberté d’opinion et d’information et visant la promotion de la diversité des expressions culturelles à travers la stimulation de la création, l’encouragement de la production, la promotion de la diffusion, méritent d’être soulignés. A cet égard, l’article 37 dispose que «les libertés d’opinion, de pensée, d’expression, d’information et de publication sont garanties, aucun contrôle préalable ne peut être exercé sur ces libertés». L’article 38 ajoute que «l’état garantit le droit à l’information». L’article 44 garantissant le droit à l’enseignement dispose, notamment, que l’état «encourage l’ouverture sur les langues étrangères et les civilisations, il veille à la diffusion de la culture des droits de l’homme». Quant au droit à la culture, l’article 44 prévoit en particulier que «le droit à la culture est garanti, la liberté de création est garantie. L’Etat encourage la créativité culturelle et soutient la culture nationale dans son originalité, sa diversité et son innovation en vue de consacrer les valeurs de tolérance, de rejet de la violence et d’ouverture sur les différentes cultures». A la lumière de ces garanties constitutionnelles et dans le but d’appuyer davantage les efforts des autorités de tutelle concernant la présentation et la promotion des programmes culturels et artistiques nationaux lancés dans tous les domaines et couvrant les différentes expressions culturelles, le MAC a opté pour une démarche participative fondée sur la création de partenariats pour promouvoir la diffusion d’un contenu culturel diversifié et accessible à travers : •	La signature en Décembre 2019 d’un accord de partenariat et de coopération avec la Radio Nationale tunisienne ayant pour objectif principal de contribuer à consolider la coopération dans les différents domaines culturels entre le MAC et la Radio Nationale, en tant que service public qui dispose d’un réseau de stations radio dans plusieurs régions et améliorer les bases de l’action culturelle et médiatique commune.  L’accord porte sur la co-production des émissions culturelles radiophoniques, la couverture médiatique de différentes manifestations culturelles et artistiques qu’organise le MAC ainsi que les institutions et établissements sous tutelle et la promotion de spots publicitaires selon les moyens disponibles et dans le respect de la ligne éditoriale de la Radio Nationale comme celles des radios régionales. En vertu de cet accord, le Ministère des Affaires Culturelles appuie les productions de la troupe musicale et théâtrale de la Radio Nationale tunisienne par la programmation de spectacles dans les festivals et facilite à la Radio culturelle et à la Radio « Panorama » l’accès aux informations, produits et contenus culturels et médiatiques des différentes institutions culturelles et ce, par le biais d’une coordination préalable et dans le respect des droits de propriété intellectuelle et artistique. •	La signature en Février 2023 d’une convention tripartite entre le Ministère des Affaires Culturelles, la Télévision Tunisienne et l’ASBU (Arab States Broadcasting Union/ L'Union de radiodiffusion des États arabes) portant sur l’organisation à Tunis, de deux éditions successives (23 et 24) du festival Arabe pour la radio et la télévision : plateforme d’échange et de réseautage entre professionnels et spécialistes dans le secteur des médias ayant pour objectif de contribuer à promouvoir les productions médiatiques (Radio et Télévision) et les adapter aux nouvelles exigences et enjeux liés aux nouvelles technologies de l’information et de la communication (NTIC) et ce en encourageant les institutions médiatiques (Radio – Télévision) à développer leurs potentiels créatifs à travers des prix, des ateliers, des conférences et des expositions pour la diffusion des produits audiovisuels et l’ouverture sur les technologies innovantes dans le secteur de l’audiovisuel. La 23ieme édition du festival ayant pour thématique générale « célébrer la Culture et les Arts» a été organisée en Juin 2023 à la cité de la culture (qui abrité les expositions, les ateliers..) et l’amphithéâtre de Carthage (pour l’organisation du spectacle de clôture). La 24ième édition est en cours de préparation à la date de la rédaction de ce rapport.
Results: En application de l’accord entre le Ministère des Affaires Culturelles et la Radio Nationale qui a été actualisé en 2023, un studio permanent de la Radio culturelle est mis en place au sein de la cité de la culture.  Inauguré en Décembre 2023, ce noyau fédérateur de 12 Radios régionales et ouvert à tous les professionnels du secteur a contribué à assurer une couverture médiatique en temps réel de toutes les activités, projets et programmes culturels au sein de la cité de la culture. Ce qui a contribué à assurer : •	Une meilleure visibilité de la dynamique culturelle à l’échelle régionale et nationale. •	Un produit et des contenus culturels plus accessibles et plus proches du citoyen. •	Un produit médiatique radiophonique plus diversifié couvrant toutes les disciplines artistiques et ciblant un public plus large (jeunes, enfants, femmes, personnes à besoins spécifiques …).

Title EN: Design and Architecture Policy to 2030
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture
SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Cultural and creative sectors
Agency Implementation: Ministry of Culture and Business Affairs Iceland Design and Architecture
Main Feature: A new Design and Architecture Policy was published in 2023. The strategy was formulated in collaboration with a number of partners, and economic and professional partners through the Center for Design and Architecture. The center was established at the initiative of the government in 2008 in order to promote Icelandic design and architecture as art forms and their basis for job creation. The Center for Design and Architecture is directly connected to the grassroots and business life of design, but it is supported by nine professional associations with a total of 1200 members who own and operate it with the support of the government through the Ministry of Culture and Trade. The draft policy in matters of design and architecture was published in open consultation in the government's consultation portal by the Ministry of Culture and Business Affairs.  The new strategy contains a vision and goals intended to increase the quality of life, create value and increase sustainability with a targeted focus on issues of design and architecture.  The strategy is developed in broad consultation and across ministries. The Ministry of Culture and Business Affairs, in collaboration with the Center for Design and Architecture, has lead the work on formulating a policy in design and architecture.  Main Goals: 1.	Value creation that builds on design and architecture •	 Funding that supports diverse innovation  2.	Design as a driving force for change  •	Use of design thinking in solving projects and challenges  3.	Sustainable infrastructures •	Strategic planning for infrastructure design with a strong focus on sustainability and public health  4.	Education of progressive generations •	Knowledge sharing and diverse educational possibilities in the fields of design and architecture  5.	Promoting Icelandic design and architecture •	Maximize visibility and awareness of Icelandic design and architecture  One of the Goals is: A stronger support system for design disciplines. The ways to achieve this goal is to set legislation on design and architecture where their overall framework and role of the government is clarified. Increase the share of designers in the distribution of artists’ salaries. Define metrics and map the economic impact and added value of design.
Results: The Design Policy is important as a guide to how the government views its interaction with the design community. While it is fairly recent, the Policy is an important part of a continuing effort in supporting a growing design community in Iceland and recognizing its value to society both culturally and economically.
Financial Ressources: In 2024 1.013.323 USD was allocated to the Iceland Design Center (140.000.000 ISK)

Main Feature: Le foisonnement des actions artistiques et culturelles actuel du pays reste le signe le plus visible de la volonté des artistes et des acteurs culturels de s’approprier leur patrimoine, et cela, dans toute sa diversité. A travers les artistes et les professionnels de la culture, le Bénin est connu et apprécié du monde. Agency Implementation: The Ministry of Regional Development and Infrastructure of Georgia (MRDI)
Main Feature: Within the Pilot Integrated Regional Development Programme (PIRDP) for 2020-2022, approved by ResolutionNo628 of the Government of Georgia on December 20, 2019, projects have been implemented within integratedregional development measures in four pilot regions of Georgia - Kakheti, Imereti, Guria and Racha-Lechkhumi-Kvemo Svaneti. The PIRDP aimed to increase competitiveness in these regions and reduce socio-economic and infrastructuralinequalities compared to Tbilisi and Batumi to create a favourable environment in the pilot regions for balanced,sustainable socio-economic development through integrated territorial development initiatives. The PIRDP hasbeen technically and financially supported by the European Union. The total financial resources allocated to thePIRDP program was 76,304 million USD. The following projects related to the cultural infrastructure were implemented through integrated regionaldevelopment measures:Rehabilitated Lagodekhi Historical Museum; Rehabilitated Lagodekhi Music School, improved quality and delivery of local public services; The QR codes were placed on historical monuments and tourist information boards, and QR cubes and energy-efficient chairs were placed in the town of Telavi, strengthening the cultural and educational role of the town;Constructed Amphitheater and arranged recreational and entertainment spaces (attractions, sports facilities) atTelavi Nadikvari Park; Rehabilitated Georgian Cavalry History Museum named after John Malkhaz Shalikashvili in Gurjaani; Rehabilitated Gurjaani House of Culture, improved quality and delivery of local public services;Rehabilitated road and administrative building of Zinobiani Udi Ethno Village (Kvareli municipality) - unique touristproduct. Small museum set-up in the administrative building;Constructed a cultural and recreational park with an Amphitheater on Evdoshvili street in the town of Tsnori;Arranged recreational infrastructure, a multifunctional exhibition space in the central square of Kutaisi city; Rehabilitated Open-air Theater named after Varinka Tsereteli in Tskhratskaro, Zestafoni municipality village. Rehabilitated and arranged Amphitheater, facades of the surrounding buildings as well as the square adjacent tothe administrative building of Terjola City Hall, developed and modernized social infrastructure;Rehabilitated Youth Multifunctional Center in Gubi administrative unit, Khoni Municipality;Rehabilitated Nodar Dumbadze House-Museum and arranged ethnographic spaces in village Khidistavi,Chokhatauri Municipality; the Diverse tourist potential of Chokhatauri is supported.
Results: The projects mentioned above contributed to achieving the policy intervention (PIRDP) to increase regional competitiveness and reduce socio-economic and infrastructural inequalities, creating a favourable environment forbalanced, sustainable socio-economic development through integrated territorial development initiatives.

Title EN: Film and Stage Plays Act No. 4 of 1976

Area of Monitoring: Artistic freedom
Agency Implementation: TANZANIA FILM BOARD
Main Feature: "The amendment of the Film and Stage Plays Act No. 4 of 1976 aims to ensure artistic freedom in film development. The concept changed from strict regulation of the industry to introduce concept of development. Among the features amended to ensure freedom are changes from film censorship to film classification. Additionally, features related to film development, such as talents identification and promotion, are included to ensure professionalism."
Results: In the past four years, no film has been banned in Tanzania,  Establishment of film development programs like the Tanzania Film Festival Awards (TAFFA), which has run for three years from 2021 to 2023,  Introduction of programs to enhance professionalism, such as tailor-made training, film screening programs, upcoming film star programs, and symposiums. These initiatives have collectively benefited more than 1,171 film practitioners to date.

Title EN: Development and awareness-raising of the Armenian culture
Goal: Achieve A Balanced Flow Of Cultural Goods And Services And Increase The Mobility Of Artists And Cultural Professionals
SDG: SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 10 - Reduce inequality within and among countries,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Mobility of artists and cultural professionals
Cultural Domain: Performing Arts,Media Arts,Cinema and Audiovisual Arts,Music,Publishing,Visual Arts
Agency Implementation: Ministry of Education, Science, Culture and Sport of the Republic of Armenia
Main Feature: With a view to strengthening foreign cultural policy and raising awareness of national and contemporary Armenian creative sectors, competitive conditions were created for ensuring participation of the whole culture sector in international events. Equal conditions and transparent procedures were ensured for establishing competitive framework between the cultural organisations and individual creators. With a view to increasing the recognisability of the country and the culture, as well as ensuring additional quality and the necessary high profile to the events, targeted programmes (international and republican festivals and competition programmes, exhibitions, film screenings, other educational and cultural programmes) are being implemented in the Republic of Armenia every year with the participation of famous foreign artists, creative groups and sector specialists. With a view to raising awareness of the Armenian culture, support was provided to Armenian creative groups and individual performers for participation in international projects, in particular: - Cinema/Audiovisual arts: participation of Armenian films and individual creators in a total of 60 international film festivals, film markets and forums (every year); - Performing arts/Theatre: participation of 11 Armenian theatre companies and 16 individuals in 20 international projects; -Visual arts: participation of young creators in 12 international biennales, exhibitions and innovative programmes; - Music: participation of 15 Armenian musical groups and 70 individual performers in 90 international music festivals and projects; - Dance: participation of 4 dance ensembles and 9 individual performers in 14 international festivals and competitions; - Cultural education: participation of 120 individual performers and 1 choir in 40 international child and youth competitions, festivals and master classes. With a view to promoting the diversity of cultural expressions, during the reporting period, 100 diverse and multi-genre projects (competition-festivals) were implemented in the republic in the sectors of theatre arts, cinema/audiovisual arts, music, dance, visual arts, as well as cultural education, 120 of which only were international projects and 70- republican projects. FILM PROGRAMMES: Film weeks organised in Armenia, co-production of films, conclusion of international agreements, membership to international institutions, international festivals held in Armenia, etc. In the Republic a series of Republican and international festivals take place which ensure the communication of the citizens with multinational, multigenre, diverse cinema. “Golden Apricot” Yerevan International Film Festival continues to take place under the theme “Crossroads of Civilisations and Cultures” and is the major regional international film festival receiving state support. In the reporting period, taking into account the years of the Covid 19 pandemic, more than 305 films have been shown within the scope of the festival, 262 guests and 155000 viewers have been included. During the festival directors and films representing different ethnic groups, nations, religions and aesthetics are seen, telling the daily life, troubles and joys, domestic life and habits of ordinary people from unique perspective. During this period of time the renowned guests were François d'Artemare, Nadav Lapid, Florian Hoffmann, Romana Lobach, Mohammad Mehdi Asgarpour, Luc Hardy, Takeshi Kitano, Lav Diaz, Jan Luck, etc. The members included in the honorary board of the festival are: Atom Egoyan (Canada), Jos Stelling (Netherlands), Krzysztoof Zanussi (Poland), Godfrey Reggio (USA), Fanny Ardant (France), Asghar Farhadi (Iran), Alexander Sokurov (Russia), Lee Chang Dong (Korea). In the reporting period, during the film festival the following have been carried out: restrospective shows, opening of the stars of classics of Armenian cinema, international programmes, regional programmes, Yerevan premiers, workshops, master classes, Talent labs. In the reporting period, the initiatives promoting international cooperation progress and development of the film industry are the following: presenting to the Armenian audience a greater number of the best films by film directors of the Asian, regional countries, as well as by film directors of Armenian origin, inclusion of filmmakers enjoying greater international reputation in the competition juries, launch and development of GAIFF Pro industry platform, launch and development of the project of C2C co-production film market, launch and development of CineThink project, establishment of regional film market – Armenia, Georgia, Turkey, expanding the cooperation with Rotterdam IFF, EAVE, IDFA, Bozar (Belgium), Israel Film Fund, Estonian Film Institute, Polish Film Institute, Tribeca Film Institute, promoting co-production, expansion and development of In Focus programme, inclusion of new countries. Within the wider scope of the festival, animation films (“ReAnimania” International Animation Films Festival - 350 animation films from 40 countries), spiritual films (“Fresco” International Festival of Modern Art and Spiritual Films), ethnographic films (“Apricot Tree” International Documentary Film Festival) are also presented, creating diversity in the cinema. From the point of view of gender expression, importance is attached to the numbers of “KIN” (40 films from 14 countries) International Film Festivals. Events assisting to young and junior creatives include Yerevan Short Film Festival, “One Shot” International Short Film Festival for youth and “Rolan” International Film Festival for Children and Youth (284 films from 98 countries). Films of domestic production and creative staff have participated in a number of international film festivals and film markets with the support of the Ministry (the Cannes, Moscow, Prague, Annecy, Talin, Lisbon, Guangzhou, Zielona Gora, Targu Marus, Brussels, Netherlands, Berlin and Bucharest). Since 2020 the works of restoration of the Armenian film heritage have started jointly with FIXAFILM Company in Poland. The samples of the film heritage were shown in Roterdam, Cannes, Berlin International Film Festivals, 2020, at the Hong Kong International Film Festival, 2020, at “Cinemateket” Movie Theater of Copenhagen, 2020.  THEATRE PROGRAMMES: Within the framework of International Theatre Festivals held in 2020-2023, the global contemporary theatre arts have been presented – “High Fest”, “ArmMono” Mono Performances, Leonid Yengibaryan Mime and Shakespeare International festivals, Yerevan’s International.teatrical festival. Importance has been specially attached to the programmes implemented for children and youth groups and young beneficiaries, such as “Tumanyan Fairy Tale Day”, “Pomegranate Seed” Children and Youth Theatre Festivals. Famous artists from Russia, France, Germany, Israel, Lithuania, Egypt, the USA, the Great Britain, Switzerland, as well as from Iran have participated in “ArmMono” One Man Show International Festival. Directors of international festivals of well-known mono performances: Nina Mazur, theatre critic, Co-Chair of the International Monodrama Forum of UNESCO, Vetslav Geras (Poland), Director of Wroclaw Festival, Jolanta Sutowich (Germany), Maria Tanana (Lithuania) and other were among the honourable guests. Popular and young Armenian artists also participated in the festival. In recent years Armenian participants received invitations to participate in this or that prestigious mono festivals and returned with awards, Grand Prix. Since 2009, the festival is held not only in the capital city, but also in the marzes (regions) of Armenia: Syunik, Lori, Tavush and Kotayk. Տhe festival presented nearly 30 performances; it had 60 participants and around 2000 attendees. Leonid Yengibaryan International Mime Festival is held in the open air; all the performances are given both in the parks of Tsakhkadzor and on open stages placed in the central square. During the festival, a separate programme also engages the audience through master classes and lectures. Within the framework of the festival, 30 performances were given, 20 theatre companies of 6 countries, and it had more than 8000 attendees. In addition to Armenian theatre companies, the students and graduates of Yerevan State Institute of Theatre and Cinematography give performances during the festival, as well as pupils of the school for hard of hearing children also engage therein. Each year the “High Fest” International Theatre Festival has different titles, in particular: In 2020, it was “To be! That’s not a question”” (online format). 5 Remarkable performances form 5 countries: Russia, Norway, Germany and Italy. In 2022, in was "The next 20 years will be better" (more than 250 participants and guests from 10 countries, 26 performances). The remarkable performances of the festival included ballet “Roden: his eternal idol” (choreographer Boris Eifman, Russia). Other interesting performances were from Romania, Cyprus, Germany, Israel, Estonia and Iran. Within the framework of “High Fest”, the European Festivals Association (EFA) has implemented the programme entitled “Europe for festivals and festivals for Europe”. This programme was aimed at integrating the performing arts of the region into the European festival environment. The programme “Eastern Dance Partnership” took place, which pursued an aim to present the contemporary dance and dance arts, created by the best Polish artists, teachers and professionals.  MUSIC PROGRAMMES: In the past four years in the field of music а concert programme was implemented in collaboration with foreign and Armenian ensembles, musicians, conductors, which included diversity of genres and traditions - classics, folk, ethnographic, jazz, avant-garde, etc. In music, the diversity in genre and participation is ensured also by “Yerevan Perspectives”, “Aram Khachaturian” International Festival of Classical Music, Yerevan’s international music festival, “Armenia” festival, “Yerevan, as well as Viola and Cello festival named after Henrik and Geronti Talalyan, Armenian and Foreign Contemporary Composition Art (Armenian Contemporary Music, Armenian Composition Art) Festivals”. In 2020-2023, “Yerevan Perspectives” International Music Festival has presented a range of events and initiatives which left indelible mark on our cultural life. High-ranked musicians and singers of the world visited Armenia, they had joint performances with their Armenian counterparts, meetings of minds in a special format were organised, concerts - in marzes, master classes – on different platforms. Concert “The roads of friendship”- conductor Riccardo Muti, Gospel Choir form London, renowned tenor Rolando Villazon, harp Xavier de Maistre, pianist Maya Ohanyan, Gil Marsala with performance “Formidable Aznavour”, orcrestra Roma Simfonietta and conductor Andrea Morricone, two-time Grammy Award-winning musicen Georg Benson, pianist Evgeny Kissin, Vienna Boys Choir, Japanese pianist Nobuyuki Tsuji blind from birth, Quatuor Eben, flutist Jasmine Choi, renowned sopranos Veronica Dzhioeva and Hibla Gerzmava, tenor Alessando Safina, cellist Stefan Hauser, violinist and conductor Leonidas Kavakos, pianists Arcadi Volodos and Denis Matsuev, violinist Sergey Khachaturyan,  performed during the festival. Master classes and meetings of minds took place at Byurakan Art Academy, Music College named after Romanos Melikyan, Gyumri branch of Komitas State Conservatory of Yerevan, Music School No 1 in Vanadzor. GilThe International Festival named after Aram Khachaturian has its unique place in the cultural life of the Republic, which, by its nature, is the only one in the region and it also expands beyond the limits of the country: CIS countries (Russia, Kazakhstan, Belarus), Italy, Belgium, France, Germany, China, Japan - the non-exhaustive list of the countries where the festival concerts were presented. Each year, in the autumn in Yerevan, the brightest stars of the world of the classical music- Alexander Romanovsky, Karen Shahgaldian, Narek Hakhnazaryan, Mayu Kishima, Maria Domashenko, Nin Fen, Zakhar Bron, Maxim Vengerov and others come together to jointly create a platform for establishment and strengthening of international and cultural ties, which is the basis for fruitful dialogue of not only different nations, but also the entire civilized world. The Khachaturian festival had 90 concerts taken place, including 28 Armenian and 6 world premieres. Since 2023 the Khachaturian festival is also held in China, with the support of the Ministries for culture the boths countries. The festival is truly a classical music holiday; simultaneously its doors are open to jazz and other genres of world music. It offers the audience a wide range of music impressions, starting from symphony concerts to chamber evenings. Each autumn the Khachaturian festival hosts more than 18.000 concert-goers. The “Contemporary Classics” Composers’ Festival is a one-of-a-kind music event presented to the audience a whole constellation of world-famous composers in one place. Within the framework of the festival, legendary composers of our age from across the world, such as China, Georgia, Poland, Malta, Russia, Latvia, the United Kingdom and, of course, Armenia, visited Armenia. “Contemporary Classics” Composers’ Festival gave the music-loving audience an exclusive opportunity to enjoy the works of acclaimed composers of our age by the live performance of the Armenian State Symphony Orchestra and world-famous virtuosos. The beautiful compositions of contemporary classics composers were performed by world-famous musicians, such as Maurio Brunello, Gidon Kremer, Boris Berezovsky, Darya Chaykovskayan, Yuri Bashmet and others. One of the forms of musical diversity is the jazz music. In November 2011, the United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organisation (UNESCO) declared 30 April as the International Jazz Day. Starting from 2012, that event has been organised each year and it has been celebrated grandly in Yerevan and in the other marzes of Armenia. Armenia is officially considered as a member country of the international network. Each year the International Jazz Day is celebrated in Yerevan, within the framework of which world-famous artists and famous Armenian groups and individual performers (four-time Grammy Award-winning Gonzalo Rubalcaba, Tavitjan Brothers Trio, Goran Gesovski, Richard Bona, Chico Freeman and others) performed. The mission of development, popularising of jazz music is carried out by “Yerevan Jazz Fest” Annual Jazz Festival. Within the framework of the festival Grammy-winning artists visited Armenia, such as Dee Bridgewater, Marcus Miller, Gonzalo Rubalcaba, Artur Sandoval, Stanley Clarke, etc; around 27 concerts, more than 25 000 concert-goers, more than 90 popular musicians from more than 15 countries, and representatives in 3 countries of the world. The festival includes movie screenings, master classes, and exchange of experience, concert performances, official meetings, and visits to historical and cultural centers. The primary aim of the festival is to develop the cultural tourism, restore the reputation of Yerevan as the capital of jazz, and cooperate with tour agencies and institutions, thus ensuring the tourist inflow during the festival. When drawing up the programme emphasis is placed on the joint performances of invited artists and Armenian jazzmen, thus presenting to the audience unique and special performances. In this musical mosaic a special place is given to the programmes for young audience, in particular “Jazz for children” concert programme. This interactive concert event was accompanied by classical jazz music educational and informative stories. Other programs for young audience are: “The philharmony for children”, “Musical marathon-fest”.  PROGRAMMES IMPLEMENTED IN THE FIELD OF VISUAL ARTS: The programmes for popularising and developing Armenian contemporary visual arts are aimed at creating new exhibitions, presenting the Armenian contemporary art on international prestigious platforms, organising designated events in Armenia, organising exhibitions dedicated to individual and jubilee, as well as memorable dates of renowned artists. In particular: “Armenian Palette” Armenian-Chinese Plenary exhibition in the Tumanyan region of Lori Marz, Armenian-Georgian painting plein air in the Shorja of Gegarqunik Marz, “International Print biennale”, International festival-exhibition "Literary art and calligraphy" in Gumri։ More than 20 individual exhibitions of a number of artists were held, including “Abrahamians” exhibition, Retrospective Exhibition dedicated to the 20th death anniversary of sculptor Benik Petrosyan, individual exhibitions dedicated to the 100th anniversary of sculptor Sargis Baghdasaryan and artists Mkrtich Sedrakyan and Suren Safaryan, to the 75th anniversary and 80th anniversary of artists Valmar and Pharaon Mirzoyan, The catalogue of works presented in the above-mentioned exhibitions were published. The aim is to popularise the works of artists ensuring today’s artistic development, so that the art-loving public and particularly our young generation could see them.  PROGRAMMES FOR CULTURAL EDUCATION: In 2020-2023, the programs launched and successfully implemented in previous years, which were implemented in the field of cultural education for public school students, continued, among them are: “DasA” (ClassA), “Your Art at School”, “Class+Classics”. “Zardagir”, “Zardarvest”, “Im simphonic”. The aims of these programs are to introduce pupils to classical music through specially prepared interactive materials. These programs are intended for pupils of high schools of Yerevan and marzes of Armenia. According to the format of the Programme, meeting-classes were held at schools and “Aram Khachatruian” Concert Hall, which were conducted by Sergey Smbatyan, Artistic Director and Principal Conductor of the Armenian State Symphony Orchestra, orchestral musicians, as well as invited soloists performing with the orchestra. Within the framework of the programme, around 13300 pupils of 35 schools participated in 18 concerts, and around 2000 returned to the concert hall. The monitoring of the return was implemented by “DasA” application specially created for the programme. Then, a gala-concert was organised solely for the participants of the programme. The Programme “Your Art at School” is aimed at developing critical, analytical and creative thinking, increasing interest in classical music and visual arts, appreciating contemporary artists, popularising their activities, establishing direct contact and communication between artists and pupils. Within the framework of the programme, 43 artists and theorists, by drawing lots, had the opportunity to bring to life their projects at around 1290 schools of general education in Yerevan and marzes of the Republic of Armenia (each participant in 30 schools). The Programmes covers three main dimensions — classical music, visual arts and literature. The programme “Class+Classics” solely refers to the theatre arts, and 250 pupils submitted an application for participation in it. The participants were given time to write an essay on the topic dedicated to the Armenian theatre arts. As a result of summarization of the results of the essay 60 pupils were selected, of which 55 received a certificate for participation in the programme. They had the opportunity to participate for free in the seminar-lectures on the topics “The history of theatre”, “The art of acting”, “Stage direction”, “Engagement of other types of the art in the theatre”, “Organisation of theatrical business”, which were conducted by the best specialists of the field: Henrik Hovhannisyan, theatrologist, corresponding member of the National Academy of Science of the Republic of Armenia, Merited Artists of the Republic of Armenia Ruben Babayan, Nelli Kheranyan, Davit Hakobyan, People’s Artist of the Republic of Armenia Armen Elbakyan and other famous theatrologists and other cultural figures. The five-day lectures were also accompanied by seeing performances. The above-mentioned programs were included in the long-range programmes of the Ministry as effective projects. In 2023, the directions of the program were expanded and now include also the nomination-musical performance and pantomime. In the field of music, 26 international and republican competitions-festivals are organized each year (16 international, 10 republican), which give creators and groups the opportunity to present themselves on an equal footing in public and professional orders The best young musicians having participated in the competitions held in the Republic joined the creative staff of not only national, but also foreign leading opera houses and orchestra. Such names already ensure the impartiality of the competition and serve as a guarantee of high reputation and good name. Due to international reputation growing every year, the competition has been included in the composition of the World Federation of International Music Competitions (WFIMC), constituting a part of big and prestigious family, to which world-famous competitions have joined, such as the International Chaykovski Competition, the Queen Elizabeth Competition (Brussels) and Montreal International Competition. Spendaryan National Opera and Ballet Academic Theatre, as well as comprehensive development and improvement of soloists in the art of vocal. To date, some of them perform oh the world’s leading opera scenes (Metropolitrn opera, Huston Opera, Prague opera, La Scala etc). The educational and cultural programme was implemented with the support of the Ministry of Education, Science, Culutre and Sports of the Republic of Armenia, which was considered to be concerts and master classes for students of music, general education and cultural centres of the Republic of Armenia. Title EN: Development of Cultural and Creative Industries
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture
SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Cultural and creative sectors
Agency Implementation: Enterprise Estonia https://eas.ee/en/
Main Feature: Development of cultural and creative industries (CCI) is part of the Estonian Culture Development plan 2021-2030 (Culture 2030). Under the third objective it is stipulated that the role of culture and creativity in the development of society is valued. Culture and creativity shall contribute to Estonia’s competitiveness, to the growth of economic and social well-being and country’s international image.    The main objective of the measure is to bind the potential of CCI with entrepreneurship and the rest of the economy in order to increase the number of companies and institutions with new, ambitious and viable business models in CCI, increase the export potential and capacities of CCI companies and institutions, increase the value-added and productivity of CCI companies and institutions, and increase the value provided by CCI to the rest of the economy and society.   The CCI development measure includes six activity lines:   1) Grant for implementation of development plans of ambitious SMEs with growth potential;  2) Grant for supporting the growth of export capacity of CCI SMEs with growth potential;  3) Grant for providing incubation, accelerator and development services to startups and SMEs in CCI;  4) Support for facilitating cooperation within CCI and with other sectors;  5) Support for raising awareness about creative economy;  6) Support for developing entrepreneurial, export, innovation, etc knowledge and skills.
Results: SMEs who have received monetary or non-monetary support have more sustainable business models, they enter new export markets or expand in existing ones and increase their export revenues, are innovative users of digital solutions and other technologies, increase their value-added per employee, have better access to different funding options, and have more crossovers and spillovers with other sectors.
Financial Ressources: Ca 11,9M USD (11M EUR) for 2021-2027
Recommandations: The activities of CCI development measure have contributed to the productivity of workforce and the growth of value added. The highest increase (on average 2,8 times) in value added per employee was demonstrated among beneficiaries who used incubation services. Linking the CCI with other sectors also had a significant impact on the growth of added value. These activities did not result in employment growth, as the purpose of the support was primarily to increase the value added of products and services and to increase the resource efficiency of economic activity. Also, the activities on CCI development measure had a statistically significant positive effect on the growth of corporate sustainability. Almost all respondents (91%) of the companies surveyed during the evaluation in 2020 found that export development project supported by the grant helped to increase their competitiveness and according to 77% of the respondents it helped to increase their turnover. 60% of the respondents mentioned the increase in value added and 57% increase in profit. Export turnover increased on average for every other company responding to the survey. 68% of the respondents used the support to start their exports and 85% to export to new target markets.   As a conclusion, CCI development measure activities have proven to be relevant, efficient and effective and have had a positive impact on the sector’s employment, total income and other economic indicators. It is necessary to encourage and guide CCI companies and organisations to use other financing options than the state budget, including guarantee measures and private funding.

Title EN: Digital Poland Operational Programme and igital Culture Programme
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture
SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Digital environment
Agency Implementation: Ministry of Culture and National Heritage
Main Feature: The aim of the programme is to make available and enable the reuse of digital resources for promotional, educational and scientific purposes, taking into account the development and digitisation of cultural heritage resources. In the years 2020-2023, the digitization of cultural resources in Poland was carried out using funds:  - EU (Operational Program Digital Poland dedicated to state institutions, co-run institutions and archives, and to a lesser extent - Regional Programs).  - at the disposal of the Minister of Culture and National Heritage, as part of the Minister's Digital Culture Program, the beneficiaries of which may be local government cultural institutions, non-governmental organizations, churches and religious associations).  - own budgets of cultural institutions  In order to carry out the digitization of archival resources of libraries, music, theatre and film institutions, museum collections and cultural heritage, 5 Digital Competence Centres were appointed:  National Digital Archives, in the scope of digitisation of archival materials  National Film Archive – Audiovisual Institute, in the scope of digitisation of audiovisual materials  National Library, in the scope of digitisation of library materials  National Cultural Heritage Institute, in the scope of digitisation of monuments  National Institute of Museums, in the scope of digitisation of museum exhibits.
Results: Institutions operating as Competence Centers implement technological changes concerning the digitization and storage of digital data as part of their own activities, and digitize and make their own collections available. All Competence Centers develop the so-called Catalogs of good practices and standards for the digitization of individual types of objects for the purpose of implementing the above-mentioned Program, and also educate the staff of cultural institutions and archives and other entities conducting digitization, as well as perform tasks related to technical verification and storage of master copies of digitized resources under the Program.  From the European Regional Development Fund, as part of the Digital Poland Operational Programme, sixteen (16) projects were implemented in the years 2020-2023 concerning the digitisation of cultural resources, including archival materials, increasing accessibility and improving the quality of cultural resources made available digitally. The list of projects is available at: https://www.gov.pl/web/popcwsparcie/poddzialanie-232-popc. The total number of digitised and made available documents containing public sector information amounted to: 2,762,733 and 2,802,270, respectively. Among the most interesting are: https://wmuzeach.pl/ implemented in partnership by 5 state museums, as a result of which: information on over 9.5 thousand collections was made available. (images with descriptions in both Polish and English, including the GIS system), and 2D and 3D digitization of cultural heritage objects was carried out using advanced photogrammetric methods (https://inmuseums.pl/).  Noteworthy project was the initiative of the Feature and Documentary Film Studio, which used artificial intelligence algorithms to present digitized film heritage. In addition, the project reconstructed: 160 feature films, 71 documentaries, 474 animated films, including 10 full-length animated films. All of the above-mentioned film materials (a resource of almost 4,000 film items) are available on the streaming platform  https://35mm.online/en   Polish Music Publishing House set up the site with Polish Music Library - https://polskabibliotekamuzyczna.pl/ This is a portal that provides access to unique resources of musical cultural heritage collected over the years by the Polish Music Publishing House. Among the collections available online, we can distinguish: - Musical materials of solo, chamber and orchestral pieces; - Iconographic materials, including reproductions of photographs, engravings, press clippings, correspondence; -Entries of the PWM Music Encyclopedia.  The Zbigniew Raszewski Theatre Institute provides an Encyclopedia of Polish Theatre on its website: https://encyklopediateatru.pl
Recommandations: The assessment of the scale of digitization in cultural institutions in Poland is an extremely complex matter. Different categories of cultural institutions measure the size of the digitization of their collections in different ways. Nevertheless, statistical sources of the Central Statistical Office indicate that by the end of 2022, cultural institutions had digitized over 16 million collections (in the report for 2021, the institutions reported 13,839,294, and for 2020 - 12,628,957 digitized objects). This data includes the resources of libraries, museums, theaters and music institutions, as well as cultural centers.  As part of the Programme of the Minister of Culture and National Heritage entitled "Digital Culture" in the years 2020-2023, 285 projects were co-financed, which included the digitization of over 316 thousand collections (of which almost 274.5 thousand were made available). The Programme also includes tasks supporting national and ethnic minorities, as well as people with disabilities. More and more projects also concern the digitization of monuments.  This report does not fully exhaust the scale of digitization of Polish cultural resources, but only draws attention to the enormous scope of this process, which is the digital sharing of cultural resources in Poland.

Title EN: Diagnostic/assessment of Law 502-08 of Books and Libraries and its application regulation (No. 511-11)
Goal: Integrate Culture In Sustainable Development Frameworks
SDG: SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: International cooperation for sustainable development
Agency Implementation: Ministry of Culture and its dependencies relevant to the policy
Main Feature: In mid 2024 the Ministry of Culture identified the need to start working on 2 diagnostics:  1.	Law 502-08 (2008) of Books and Librairies and its application regulation No. 511-11 (2011): For this process, key areas of the Ministry were summoned to take part (Pedro Henriquez Ureña National Library, General Direction for Books and Reading and the Viceministry of Cultural Identity. 2.	The theatre sector: This sector does not have any sectoral rule. The Viceministry for Creativity and Arts Education was summoned to steer this process, with the help of previous polls and civil society feedbacks gathered in an open dialogue held at an open dialogue in 2022.  Both diagnostics suggest the need to draft new legal instruments. In the case of Law No. 502-08, it is insufficient for the sector and requires a transformation, both structural and in its institutional scope, specially considering the user. The results confirm grave preoccupations in the implementation and execution of the law. Regarding the theatre sector, the diagnostic highlights great needs gathered in 2022, one of them being that the sector wishes to be recognized and represented as an artistic and cultural sector within the legal framework, bringing opportunities and growth. Both diagnostics will be presented to the National Culture Council, the sectoral advisory body, in its next session, to gather feedback and proposals for the subsequent drafting of the preliminary bills, ordinances and provisions for both instances. Additionally, the diagnostic pertaining to book and libraries will be presented to another existing body, the Intersectorial Council for Book, Reading and Libraries Policy (CONLIBRO).
Results: Two diagnostics, serving as a base to start the drafting of new norms.

SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Digital environment
Agency Implementation: Arts Council England
Main Feature: The Digital Culture Network (DCN) provides free and practical support to the arts and culture sector to develop organisations' digital skills and explore the benefits of technology. It provides specialist support in digital strategy, digital marketing, social media, eCommerce, data analytics and insight, search engine marketing, websites, content creation, CRM and ticketing, and email marketing. The Network is led by a team of specialist Tech Champions supporting individuals and organisations from the creative and cultural sector including museums and libraries. The DCN provides a range of learning resources, events and webinars, and free one-on-one support for organisations.
Results: In 2023-2024, the DCN delivered more than 2,000 one-to-one support cases to almost 700 organisations and individuals in the creative and cultural sector. 3000+ attendees have attended events, train days, workshops or webinars on a diverse range of topics including Grow Your Digital Content Skills in partnership with Google Arts and Culture.
Recommandations: The DCN were given a 96% rating in their 1:1 satisfaction survey, with 97% of participants reporting to have felt that the information / advice received would have a positive impact on their organisation.

Title EN: Digital is culture: Convergent narratives for change
Goal: Promote Human Rights And Fundamental Freedoms
SDG: SDG 5 - Achieve gender equality and empower all women and girls,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels
Area of Monitoring: Artistic freedom
Agency Implementation: Ministry of Cultures, Arts, and Knowledge
Main Feature: Strengthen spaces for reflection, training, creation, and circulation around digital culture, interactive and immersive media based on collaborative processes, which lead to the understanding of territories and their cultural diversity from digital narratives; as well as, in the appropriation of creation tools for innovation and content production, which contribute to the growth of the country's creative ecosystem.
Results: Since 2020, the Digital is Culture strategy has achieved the following progress as a strategy to promote artistic freedom and the guarantee of fundamental rights of various social groups: Within the framework of “Convergent Narratives for Change” the production has been achieved of more than 120 digital and new media content in the context of the Stimulus calls and in particular the Convocatoria Crea Digital, carried out in agreement with the Ministry of ICT, the development of more than 10 sectoral meetings that allowed the generation of synergies in the digital content sector, through dialogue with representative agents of animation, video games, and transmedia and XR narratives. From these dialogues, it was possible to recognize the current state of the sector and the needs of its agents regarding incentives, circulation, scholarships and calls, and the development in 2023 of the first (1) Transmedia Clinic of Digital Content distribution.

Title EN: Equipo Praxis actions
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture
SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Partnering with civil society
Agency Implementation: Equipo Praxis para la investigación y desarrollo de la danza
Main Feature: The Praxis Annual Gala of Traditional Dance is a showcase of the best performances of Traditional Dance and Tango casts of each year in the civil association "Equipo Praxis para la investigación y desarrollo de la danza", presented in a Gala show at the Teatro Sala Verdi in Montevideo on August 25th of each year. Initiated in 2011, this annual event continued to take place during the last quadrennium. "Traditional or Folkloric Dance is an art form with low presence in the main communication and exhibition spheres and suffers a long process of deterioration and discrimination in our society that is evident in the contrasted number of shows, supports and sponsorships. From our NGO we believe that it is a fundamental form of construction and preservation of our cultural identities and we struggle to sustain its best practices". Likewise, since 2022 Equipo Praxis has been promoting the annual giving of awards to the best artists (individuals or casts) dedicated to traditional dance, with the understanding that there is a lack of awards, incentives and policies in Uruguay that favor and stimulate the development of this sector of culture and the arts. Like the Annual Gala referred to above, the Praxis Awards for Traditional Dance are an action based on the assumption that it is an artistic expression that is not widely disseminated and lags behind in terms of support and sponsorship. Between February 2022 and December 2023, Equipo Praxis developed the project "Reconocer Radio", a weekly radio program -through a community Internet radio- that aimed to address traditional Uruguayan popular culture, dealing with topics related to folklore, tango, candombe and other indigenous musical and choreographic forms.
Results: Maintaining a stage presence of Traditional Dance and Tango casts in an important hall of the city, building and expanding the relationship with new audiences.  Awarding of several prizes to Traditional Dance in various categories and consolidation of the prestige and recognition of the distinguished artists, at least in their sector of reference.  More than 100 Reconocer Radio programs carried out, with an audience valued at an average of approximately 1,500 weekly connections and the production of content considered to be of high quality.

Title EN: Digital Participation Policy
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture
SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Digital environment
Agency Implementation: Telecommunications and Digital Government Regulatory Authority
Main Feature: The Digital Participation Policy in the UAE government is a strategic framework designed to enhance and streamline the engagement of citizens, businesses, and other stakeholders through digital platforms and services. This policy reflects the UAE's commitment to leveraging technology to improve governance, accessibility, and public services. The policy aims to increase citizen participation in government processes by providing accessible and user-friendly digital platforms. This includes online portals for feedback, public consultations, and digital voting systems that make it easier for the public to engage with and influence government decisions. The policy focuses on digitalizing government services to make them more efficient and user-centric. This includes integrating online services across different government departments, reducing bureaucratic processes, and enhancing the speed and convenience of service delivery. The policy encourages the adoption of emerging technologies such as artificial intelligence, blockchain, and big data analytics to improve service delivery and operational efficiency. It supports the development of innovative digital solutions to address various public sector challenges.
Results: The implementation of the Digital Participation Policy has led to significant improvements in public engagement and governance. There has been a marked increase in the number of citizens participating in policy discussions and providing feedback on governmental initiatives. The policy has facilitated quicker and more effective responses to public queries and concerns, thereby enhancing trust and accountability. Additionally, the integration of digital tools has streamlined administrative processes, reduced bureaucratic delays, and improved service delivery. The Ministry reports a higher satisfaction rate among citizens regarding their interaction with government services.
Recommandations: To effectively implement the Digital Participation Policy in the UAE government, it is crucial to develop a comprehensive digital infrastructure that supports seamless integration of online services across departments and ensures reliability and scalability. Platforms should be designed with a user-centric approach, incorporating feedback to create intuitive and accessible experiences. Enhancing digital literacy through extensive training programs for both government employees and the public is essential for effective use of digital tools.

Title EN: Digital theater
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture
SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Digital environment
Agency Implementation: Afroteatro Digital de Tumaco or Tumaco Digital Afrotheater
Main Feature: Tumaco Digital Afrotheater is an innovative initiative whose main objective is the dramaturgical and scenic production inspired by the life and culture of the men and women of Tumaco and the Colombian Pacific. This initiative stands out for the pioneering use of new technologies to make visible and preserve the rich Afro-Colombian cultural heritage.          This initiative seeks to rescue, preserve, and disseminate the culture and ancestral knowledge of the Afro-descendant communities of the Colombian Pacific through theater and dance. The initiative seeks to create a space where art, communication, and cultural diversity mix, using digital tools to reach a broader and more diverse audience.          The creation of plays and dance shows are inspired by the stories, legends, and daily life of the Afro-descendant communities of Tumaco. In addition, traditional elements such as songs, dances, and rituals are incorporated that reflect the cultural richness of the region.          The initiative uses digital platforms to disseminate productions, allowing access to global audiences. Implementing interactive and multimedia technologies helps enrich the theatrical experience and encourage greater audience participation.           The initiative runs training programs in performing and digital arts for young people in the community, promoting the development of new skills and job opportunities. Likewise, it conducts workshops and seminars on Afro-Colombian history and culture, with a focus on preserving ancestral knowledge.          Afroteatro Digital de Tumaco also addresses environmental issues, recognizing the close relationship between Afro-Colombian culture and the natural environment. The black communities of the Colombian Pacific have a deep knowledge of their territory, which is reflected in their traditional practices and their worldview.
Results: Since its implementation, Tumaco Digital Afrotheater has achieved several significant results that reflect its positive impact on the community and the dissemination of Afro-Colombian culture. Below are the main achievements achieved to date:          1. Colombian Pacific Network: A solid collaboration network has been created between artists, communicators and community groups in the Colombian Pacific. This network allows the exchange of ideas and experiences, strengthening cohesion and mutual support among its members. Thanks to the network, local capacities have been strengthened through the exchange of tools and knowledge in areas such as theater, dance, and visual arts.          2. The support of the Ministry of Culture has been crucial for strengthening the Create Peace program, allowing greater dissemination and scope of the activities of the Digital Afroteatro of Tumaco.          Community communication groups have worked together with people who carry out community work in areas such as arts, literature, and theater, creating synergies and joint projects that benefit the community.          3. Various publications have been made that document and disseminate the initiatives of Afroteatro Digital of Tumaco, contributing to the visibility and recognition of Afro-Colombian culture.          Meetings and Events: Cultural meetings have been held that bring together artists and community members, promoting cultural exchange, and strengthening Afro-descendant identity.         4. Through its productions and activities, Afroteatro Digital of Tumaco has spread messages of respect and care for women, promoting gender equality and the creation of healthy environments.          5. The works and activities of the Afroteatro have raised awareness about the importance of protecting the territory and valuing natural resources, understanding how they work and how they can be preserved.          6. The initiative has given a voice to people from rivers and seas, creating bridges so that those who do not have access to the media can be heard and valued. The dissemination of ancestral knowledge and Afro-Colombian culture has been promoted, valuing the cultural richness and diversity of the Colombian Pacific.

Title EN: DISPLAY
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture
SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Digital environment
Agency Implementation: Fondazione Caritro
Main Feature: 2022 marked the 30th anniversary of Caritro, a foundation of banking origins created in 1992 from the merger of Cassa di Risparmio di Rovereto and that of Trento. On this occasion the Foundation has carried out an accurate work of cataloguing all its works of art and created a catalogue. Subsequently, in order to make the Art Collection more accessible to the community, the Foundation has decided to visually illustrate the artistic heritage through a digitized archive of pieces. This is how Display was created, in collaboration with Campomarzio, a collective of architects from Trento. This is not a traditional exhibition, there are no works physically exhibited, but rather a path of accessibility and digital exploration. The visit path is divided into three rooms precisely as there are three moments in the project: Reflection, Immersion and Creation. The first room is a story of the Collection in numbers. The second room represents the interactive moment: you will be able to virtually explore the digitized heritage and choose six works to create a personal catalogue, which you will physically create in the last room. The artistic heritage of the Foundation spans 5 centuries, from the 16th century to a final work acquired in 2022, and consists of over 300 works. There are 100 artists, including 14 female artists. The characteristic that all the works have in common is the fact that they are Trentino art or produced in relation to the Trentino territory.
Results: INSTRUCTIONS FOR THE DIGITAL ACTIVITY: In order to discover the Art Collection, you can: - Enter keywords in the “Ricerca” (Search) box - Select the author by surname initial - Use the proposed filters: artist movement, technique, colour, subjects The works that meet the entered criteria will appear on the screen: - click on the work to read the caption and use the zoom - click on the heart to save the work - click “Reset” (to the right of the filters) for a new search To create your personal catalogue: - click on the “Preferiti” (Favourites) section (top right) and select up to 6 works - click “Invio e stampa il tuo catalogo” (Send and print your catalogue) - enter your name and your email, accept the notice In the last room, the cover and the index of the selected works are printed with the corresponding code, which serves to identify them more easily in the cells. This way you will be able to take paper postcards of the works home with you.

Title EN: Digitalized Audio Description in Theatre – Accessible Theatre for Blind and Visually Impaired
Goal: Integrate Culture In Sustainable Development Frameworks
SDG: SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: National sustainable development policies and plans
Agency Implementation: NOTA
Main Feature: Audio description plays a crucial role in making visual content accessible to audiences with visual impairment, by providing detailed descriptions of visual elements, therefore enhancing understanding, increasing engagement and fostering inclusion and accessibility. Today, audio description in theatres typically involves hiring a live interpreter for special showings to provide real-time audio descriptions of the visual elements happening on stage. Live audio description in theater is both costly and inflexible for audience members with visual impairments, as an interpreter must be hired for each showing, and because audience members who rely on audio description must attend the theatre at the time of the special showing with audio description. This initiative aims to make audio description digitalized, thus making it possible for visually impaired people to attend the theater when it suits them and on their own terms, receiving the audio description on their smart phone and similar devices.
Results: So far, the importance of automatic, digitalized audio description has been identified, and Nota is now, in collaboration with The Royal Theatre (Det Kongelige Teater) and the Danish Association for the visually impaired, (Dansk Blindesamfund) in the process of exploring digital solutions for the implementation of digitalized audio description

Title EN: Digiteket
