Area of Monitoring: Digital environment
Agency Implementation: National Library of Sweden (Kungliga Biblioteket)
Main Feature: Digiteket is a national library service operated by an editorial team at Malmö City Library on behalf of the National Library of Sweden (Kungliga Biblioteket, KB). Digiteket is a platform for digital professional development and inspiration, with the primary goal of increasing the competence of library staff in digital skills, media and information literacy (MIK), democracy and participation, and promoting reading and literature. Digiteket aims to disseminate knowledge from library-related research and monitoring of trends, focusing on digital professional development and reading promotion. The content consists of both courses, articles, and resources.  After being part of the national initiative ‘Digitalt först med användaren i fokus’ (Digital First with User Focus) from 2018 to 2020, the National Library was given the assignment by the government to continue running “Digiteket”. In 2022, KB and the Swedish Arts Council decided to collaborate on Digiteket with the aim of strengthening the national structure for competence development in public libraries.
Results: The National Library´s assessment of the work with Digiteket is that it´s well functioning. A new version expanded with research-based material on reading promotion in collaboration with the Swedish Cultural Council has been launched during the year, which increased the opportunities for knowledge sharing.
Financial Ressources: Digiteket is financed through an annual operating grant from the National Library of USD 353 541. The basic grant has been unchanged for the past three years. During 2023, The Arts Council has contributed extra funding to Digiteket of USD 88 385 and during 2022 the Arts Council contributed an extra grant of USD 321 723 .

Title EN: Digitisation of cultural heritage
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture
SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Digital environment
Agency Implementation: The national/central museums (museums that are authorities and as such funded by the government)
Main Feature: The government allocated additional funding to the central museums that are authorities in order to secure digitally accessible collections and for the development of digital services. The overarching goal of the government’s digitalization strategy is for Sweden to be the best in the world at utilising the opportunities of digitalization. The pandemic has clarified the importance of having the museums’ collections digitally available with qualitative metadata. This is a prerequisite for both national and international research and knowledge development, as well as a matter of accessibility and equal access for everyone to the common cultural heritage. Organising and digitising (converting information from analogue to digital form) the collections is also necessary to conduct a secure and active collection management.
Results: All authorities have reported results of the work due to the reinforcement. Special digitization projects have been implemented during the year. Hundreds of thousands of objects have been photographed and published, object records have been enriched with information and metadata and made searchable in collection databases. In connection with this work, the condition of the collections has been assessed. The amplification has also been used to develop new digital displays. The work has also resulted in increased accessibility to the collections for, among other things, people with disabilities. However, it appears from the authorities' reports that digitization operations and digital mediation cut through many parts of the museal work which are largely integrated with each other. Separate reporting of costs and results can therefore be difficult to do. The museums' increased digital presence has resulted in more searches in collection databases and a larger number of followers in social media compared to previous years.
Financial Ressources: 1 975 410 USD (20 million SEK) per year during the years 2020-2024

Since 2020, the Diploma has been offered virtually, first due to the Covid 19 pandemic. However, this initial challenge made it possible to adapt to the demands of new forms of cultural projects, new languages, and the exploration of other forms of design and programming in virtuality. In addition, virtuality also made it possible to reach other latitudes and the training space has been enriched not only with Peruvian experiences from other countries.

Title EN: Double Taxation Avoidance Treaty
Goal: Achieve A Balanced Flow Of Cultural Goods And Services And Increase The Mobility Of Artists And Cultural Professionals
SDG: SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 10 - Reduce inequality within and among countries,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Mobility of artists and cultural professionals
Cultural Domain: Performing Arts,Media Arts,Cinema and Audiovisual Arts,Music,Visual Arts
Agency Implementation: The Ministry of Finance of Georgia
Main Feature: Georgia currently has 58 OECD Model Tax Conventions on Income and on Capital in force. It's important to note that Georgia has a Double Taxation Avoidance Treaty (DTA) in force with all EU countries. These DTA treaties include Article 17 (Entertainers and Sportspersons), supporting the mobility of artists and cultural professionals.  The article states that "income derived by a resident of a Contracting State as an entertainer, such as a theatre, motion picture, radio or television artist, or a musician, or as a sportsperson, from that resident’s personal activities as such exercised in the other Contracting State, may be taxed in that other State."
Results: Article 17 (Entertainers and Sportspersons) of the OECD Model Tax Convention on Income and on Capital addresses the practical difficulties that often arise when taxing artists and cultural professionals performing abroad.

Title EN: Directory of agents in the publishing sector developed under the Pacific Alliance.
Goal: Achieve A Balanced Flow Of Cultural Goods And Services And Increase The Mobility Of Artists And Cultural Professionals

Area of Monitoring: Flow of cultural goods and services
Agency Implementation: Ministry of Cultures, Arts, and Heritage of Chile; the Ministry of Culture of Colombia; the Ministry of Culture of Mexico; and the Ministry of Culture of Peru.
Main Feature: In the context of the Integration Mechanism of the Pacific Alliance in which Colombia is a part, a study was carried out on the Characterization of the circulation of the book network, the agents and the cultural agendas, in December 2021 in the countries that make up the Pacific Alliance, whose main objective is to contribute to strengthening commercial and book circulation networks, agents, and cultural agendas, through the mapping and characterization of publishing agents of the AP in Spanish.
Results: In this document, part of the findings contributed to generating primary information about the behavior of agents by link of the chain in the four countries of the Alliance, and in the identification of actions that strengthened labor networks and book circulation. The incentives or difficulties that book agents and organizations have to establish an international flow of trade were carefully analyzed, exposing experiences of the creation of networks between countries, studying the role of each of the agents of the value chain within the countries, and exposing a general overview of the current state of the publishing sector in each country as of 2021.

Title EN: Diversity of cultural expressions in educational establishments. Ministry of Education arts  workshops.
Goal: Integrate Culture In Sustainable Development Frameworks
SDG: SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: National sustainable development policies and plans
Cultural Domain: Design,Performing Arts,Media Arts,Cinema and Audiovisual Arts,Music,Publishing,Visual Arts
Agency Implementation: Ministry of Education (MINEDUC).
Main Feature: This measure is related to the implementation of art workshops in educational establishments throughout Chile since 2015, which are jointly carried out by teaching artists and teachers from the establishments. The most important pedagogical objectives developed by the arts workshops are to broaden and diversify art experiences for students in different areas and modalities, to offer opportunities for students to express themselves creatively and to appreciate and respond critically to art, to strengthen self-esteem and sense of self-identity, to strengthen teaching skills in implementing arts workshops with the students.  Among the guiding parameters for implementation of arts workshops during the period 2020-2022, we can highlight socioemotional support for students and educational community considering the impact of the public health situation, adaptating the implementation of workshops to online, hybrid and face-to-face format, support and enhancement the work of teachers and directors from benefiting establishments.  Lastly, considering the monitoring framework of the 2005 Convention, the arts workshops report on the "policies and measures that support equity in the distribution of cultural resources and inclusive access to such resources" indicator.
Results: During this year (2023), 540 workshops have been carried out in 291 educational establishments. The workshops lasted 52 teaching hours each and were carried out during the first semester of this year. Each workshop was attended by 20 students, reaching a national coverage of 10,800 participants distributed around all the regions of the country.  On the other hand, the results of arts workshop implementation, based on systematisation of reports, interviews, focus groups, satisfaction surveys, among others, for different actors involved in these lines (in particular directors, teachers, students, external companies that carry out arts workshops and teaching artists), show that more than 90% of the survey respondents stated that:  (1) the workshop helped students in developing specific art skills,  (2) it helped the expansion of opportunities for the students to experiment artistic experiences,  (3) the workshop strengthened the pedagogical skills of the head teacher,  (4) the workshops contributed to improve school co-existence,  (5) the workshops helped with socioemotional support of students/ teachers. On the other hand, more than 90% of the directors from the selected schools stated that they would again include art workshops in their School Improvement Plans.
Recommandations: In 2022, a satisfaction survey was conducted for the different agents, management team or  people in charge of arts workshops, students, teaching artists and cultural management  companies, which was systematised and led to the following recommendations related to implementation:   (1) positive assessment of management teams from the establishments participating in the workshops, considering each of the evaluated parameters, especially those referring to objective observance and assessment of the effects of these initiatives.   (2) In the case of teaching artists, the results presented also show a positive evaluation. This evaluation, as in previous years, was better in terms of obtained results and effects than in terms of workshop implementation.   (3) In general terms, at implementation level, a higher rating was obtained for the role of the contracted company in providing information or acting in a timely manner to deal with problems presented during the workshop, and for the contact made with the teacher in charge of the workshop.   (4) A lower rating was observed in relation to timely delivery of materials by the contracted company and their relevance. Differences were identified in the score, between different regions.   (5) Regarding observance of objectives and effects,, favouring development of art skills, its contribution to socialemotional support and the interest it created in students were highlighted to a greater extent.   Similarly, lower ranking scores were obtained by the contribution of the workshops to strengthening students' learning skills, satisfaction with the quality of achievements reached and the observance of their objectives. In this case, there were small differences between the regions where the teaching artists came from.

Area of Monitoring: Digital environment
Agency Implementation: Documentary Association of Canada (DOC)
Main Feature: In September 2021, the Documentary Association of Canada (DOC) announced a partnership with Tënk as part of the DOCs From The Vault initiative.  The DOC is a member of the Coalition for the Diversity of Cultural Expressions and represents the interests of independent documentary filmmakers in Canada. For its part, Tënk is a solidarity cooperative specializing in the promotion and distribution of documentaries. This distribution platform originates from France, but a Quebec service presenting a distinct catalog and sharing the same cloud infrastructure was created in 2020. Tënk operates with a subscription formula, giving access to its entire catalog, but with particular attention paid to the frequent renewal of the offer and the curation of content.  DOCs From The Vault was created to provide a window of visibility for documentaries that did not benefit from much exposure upon release and have never been broadcast online. Thus, DOC launched a call for projects from September 27 to October 21, 2021, in order to collect applications from its 1,100 members. Ten documentaries were selected and made available on the Tënk viewing platform in two waves, the first from January 28, 2022, and the second from March 25, 2022. The films selected for the DOCs From The Vault project, in addition to being digitized and made available via Tënk, have all been translated in order to make them bilingual thanks to the addition of subtitles (French-speaking content, into English, and vice versa).  The films broadcast explore a diversity of subjects and points of view, focusing on underrepresented communities, such as First Nations in several communities in Canada or people living with HIV.
Results: This initiative made it possible to contribute to the promotion and discoverability of 10 documentaries which only benefited from minimal exposure upon their release, and therefore made it possible to respond to a key objective of the Convention by contributing to promoting a diversity of content, in this case documentaries. Even more, by encouraging the translation of works, DOC has contributed to strengthening the pan-Canadian cultural social fabric by opening dialogue between two communities of practice: French-speaking and English-speaking creators. Members were therefore able to discover documentaries that were not produced in their ¬¬-mother tongue and expose themselves to a diversity of points of view which only contributes to better cultural diversity. In itself, documentary practice is a strong vector of diversity of cultural expressions: the executive director of DOC reports that 50% of the members of her organization come from diverse backgrounds. This diversity is reflected in the films mentioned above, since the documentary, due to the much lower initial investments it requires compared to other types of audiovisual productions, allows a certain economic equity. It allows people from underprivileged backgrounds to make their first steps as directors, creators, etc., who can act as a lever allowing them to ultimately access more attractive funding in government subsidy structures. The DOCs From The Vault initiative, in addition to promoting 10 pre-existing documentaries, above all allows us to highlight the richness of Canadian documentary practice, its diversity of form and subject, and ultimately, to open dialogue between different communities. Indeed, DOC, particularly through partnerships with the Network of Independent Canadian Exhibitors (NICE), greatly encourages member documentary filmmakers, once their project has been broadcast, to go to broadcast locations (such as NICE member theaters) in order to enter into dialogue with the public, to share, to exchange, and to contribute to a richer Canadian culture anchored in openness towards others. With DOCs From The Vault, it is the entire documentary that is valued and put forward as a vector of cultural diversity.

Title EN: E-culture: Romania's Digital Library
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture
SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Digital environment
Agency Implementation: Ministry of Culture/ Project Management Unit
Main Feature: "E-culture: Romania's Digital Library" is a pilot project implemented at the level of the Ministry of Culture through the Project Management Unit, dedicated to the digitisation of mobile cultural heritage and which resulted in the creation of the Romanian Digital Library (culturalia.ro), the national counterpart of the European Digital Library (europeana.eu).  Implemented between 2018 and 2023, the project was co-funded by the European Union from the European Regional Development Fund, through the Competitiveness Operational Program 2014-2020, Priority Axis 2, Action 2.3.3 "Improving digital content and systemic ICT infrastructure in the field of e-education, e-inclusion, e-health and e-culture".  The overall objective of the project was to streamline the public services offered by the Ministry of Culture by harnessing the potential of IT&C in the process of digitisation of mobile cultural heritage, in order to increase accessibility to cultural resources.  The specific objectives of the project were:  -To increase the number of cultural heritage items digitised and exhibited online in a single access point; -To increase the degree of interoperability between institutions holding cultural heritage items; -To promote national cultural heritage by showcasing digitised cultural resources on europeana.eu. Thus, the project responded to the need to create a national infrastructure for the digitisation of cultural content that will ensure the viability of cultural heritage by facilitating the documentation, research, promotion and transmission of information / knowledge on cultural goods to a wide range of audiences and where access to digitised resources will be online, free of charge.  The project also responded to the objective of digitising 750,000 cultural resources, undertaken by Romania according to the Digital Agenda 2020, and to create, as a consequence, the Digital Library of Romania, which is the largest national contribution to europeana.eu, the European platform for digital cultural heritage.
Results: The project  contributed to the protection, transmission, promotion and enhancement of mobile cultural assets at national and European level by:  - The creation of an online digital library and shared catalog (culturalia.ro), available free of charge to cultural institutions and the general public; - Digitalisation of at least 560,640 cultural resources (texts, images, audiograms, videograms, objects) and making them available  in the Romanian Digital Library. By the end of the project, at least 200,000 of these were also displayed in the European Digital Library.
Financial Ressources: The approximative value of the project was 11,369,570.34 USD (current exchange rate RON/USD)
Recommandations: E-culture: Romania's Digital Library programme over-achieved its goals and results.

Title EN: E-culture campaign
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture
SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Digital environment
Agency Implementation: Ministry of Culture
Main Feature: The "E-Culture" campaign is being implemented in two stages, focusing on four main goals. The primary objective is to facilitate evidence-based policy decisions and establish a unified industry registration and information system. During the first phase, the plan includes the establishment of a registration and information system within the cultural sector. This system aims to utilise data-driven analysis for decision-making, enable electronic monitoring, and provide services to users electronically.
Results: The integrated management system for internal operations within state cultural and artistic institutions, along with a system for planning, monitoring, and evaluation, has been successfully implemented and is currently in operation. Furthermore, efforts are underway to develop a robust data management and statistical system for the cultural sector. This initiative aims to establish a unified data warehouse that will facilitate various analytical and forward-looking visual information capabilities. The system will also enable the generation of implementation results and provide monitoring opportunities. In addition to these advancements, a portal site has been launched. This portal adheres to unified standards to ensure easy and accessible access to information. It covers details about the selection programs of the Fund for Culture and Arts, the Fund for Film Art, and various cultural products and services within the industry. Moreover, in the pursuit of promoting universal cultural education, a cultural heritage registration information system, a library registration information system, and an art and repertoire database have been integrated. This collaborative initiative, known as the GLAM shared system, facilitates user access across Galleries (G), Libraries (L), Archives (A), and Museums (M). This integration enhances the availability and accessibility of cultural resources for educational and research purposes.

Title EN: E-culture Platform (since 2022)
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture
SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Digital environment
Agency Implementation: Martynas Mažvydas National Library of Lithuania
Main Feature: E-culture – is a unified platform for digitized and digital cultural and audiovisual content, electronic services and dissemination. The digitized cultural content is sought to be preserved and disseminated as a value-creating resource of knowledge and information for the public, actively consumed for leisure, exploration, learning, scientific research, CCI and tourism development purposes.  The problem addressed by the project: The main problem is the low level of digitisation of culture and the insufficient or unattractive accessibility of digital/digitised cultural content.  Main tasks from the policy side: 1.	Set a clear regulatory framework ensuring sustainability of the E-culture Platform, therefore developing digital skills and competencies, and provide conditions for sustainable financing of digitization activities of cultural content. 2.	Improve and enlarge diversity, quality, dissemination and accessibility of digitized cultural content. Prioritize creation of audiovisual and curated digital cultural content and digitized cultural content, also considering needs of the people with disabilities. 3.	Develop and present digitized cultural heritage as a recourse which generates cultural, social and economic value.  The challenges addressed: • rapid technological development, • changing demand for cultural content of the contemporary society, • consequences of the global pandemic.
Results: Expected results and benefits of the project:   • Digital and digitized cultural resources scattered through different systems are systematized. • The one-stop shop principal increases the availability of cultural resources and services. • A unified user interface adapted to the needs of persons with disabilities is created. • The support costs of different systems are optimized, data is transferred and protected in the state cloud (700 TB + 150 TB/year). • Contemporary technologies for metadata processing, search and navigation are implemented. • Centrally aggregated data for opening and further use. • Strengthening of basic systems to smoothly deliver data to the E- culture Platform. • Unification of data standards (handover to international DBs, data opening). • Dissemination of attractive cultural content that meets the needs of the contemporary consumer.  It is envisaged that the E-culture Platform will benefit as follows: • Increase in the number of views of digitized and digital cultural resources – up to 20% in 2030. • Digital (electronic) publishing resources adapted for persons with disabilities, in percentages from 15% (2020) to 20% (2030). • Percentage of population using e-services related to cultural heritage – from 16% (2017) to 20% (2030).  Project duration: 5 October 2023 - 30 April 2026.
Financial Ressources: The project is funded by the European Union (Next Generation EU) and the Economic Recovery and Resilience Plan "Next Generation Lithuania".   The value is approx. USD 26.4 million (EUR 23.8 million).

Title EN: EEA Grants
Goal: Integrate Culture In Sustainable Development Frameworks
SDG: SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: International cooperation for sustainable development
Agency Implementation: EEA Grants
Main Feature: The EEA Grants aim to reduce social and economic inequality, in addition to strengthening bilateral cooperation among the EEA countries and the beneficiary countries. The EEA Grants are jointly funded by the three donor countries, Iceland, Liechtenstein and Norway, with each contributing according to their size and GDP. Eligibility of the Grants mirrors the criteria set for the EU Cohesion Fund aimed at Member States where the Gross National Income (GNI) per inhabitant is less than 90% of the EU average. Recipients of allocations from the fund during the current funding period are Bulgaria, Croatia, Czech Republic, Cyprus, Estonia, Greece, Hungary, Latvia, Lithuania, Malta, Poland, Portugal, Romania, Slovakia and Slovenia. Allocations from the Grants are decided by the Financial Mechanism Office, a committee composed of representatives of the Foreign Ministries of Iceland, Liechtenstein and Norway. The Grant currently has five priority sectors that allocations are channeled through, focusing on such things as innovation, youth employment and environmental considerations. Culture plays a significant role in the work that the Grants engage in. The vital role of culture in countries’ economies, its role in uniting individuals, increasing stability and innovation is recognized. The Grants follow the Europe 2020 strategy and contribute to smart and sustainable growth, supporting cultural activities such as cultural heritage management, cultural entrepreneurship and artistic activities contributing to sustainable development and social cohesion.
Results: The EEA Grants have supported an incredibly large number of projects in a wide variety of fields in the last 28 years. Since the beginning of the 2014-2021 funding period, over 110 stakeholder consultations have been held, with 95 concept notes finalized by year end 2019, 80 program agreements signed and 149 calls for proposals launched since the first release in 2017. The Grants have provided significant assistance to recipient countries economically, socially and culturally. During the previous funding period of 2009-2014, the EEA Grants allocated 86,754,967 USD (78,600,000 EUR) to the 16 recipient countries at the time, with a large portion of that assigned to projects involving protection of cultural heritage, as well as climate change and energy. During that funding period, Iceland partnered with 181 organizations in 15 countries to work on 401 projects in various fields.
Financial Ressources: In 2019, 4,474,223.78 USD was allocated to the fund from the Icelandic State Treasury (611 million ISK).

Main Feature: The UAE offers many education and training opportunities to support cultural professionals and youth to acquire more experience, skills, and knowledge in media sectors. The courses and programs are provided by different institutions as follows: The Mohammed Bin Rashid School for Communication (MBRSC): at the American University in Dubai, is the first academic institution in the region to offer world-class and specialized undergraduate courses in various communication fields. The MBRSC offers a Master of Arts in Leadership and Innovation in Contemporary Media (M.A.) and a Bachelor of Communication and Information Studies (B.C.I.S) with two majors; Digital Production and Storytelling, and Journalism. MBRSC boasts 98% employability rate within the first year of students’ graduation and offers annual scholarships to select undergraduate students, removing barriers to participation and enabling students to gain access to education and training in the media field. In5: an initiative launched by TECOM group, is an innovation center and hub for media freelancers, and entrepreneurs to work collectively on media related endeavors. In5 incubates, trains and guides aspiring entrepreneurs to conduct successful businesses in the media. It offers its members an educational program that includes both international as well as in-house training programs and workshops to develop the latest skills and knowledge and offers creatives spaces including editing suites, green rooms, multimedia and meeting rooms. New Media Academy: is an academic institution offering a broad range of career-oriented educational programs to nurture innovation and creativity in the field of digital marketing. The educational programs include social media professional programs, youth youtuber program, storytelling program, open content creator program and impact digital creator program. The learning experience includes mentorship, e-learning, and on-demand online learning along with opportunities to apply skills.  The Media National Youth Programme (MNYP):  is an annual training programme that aims to develop a new generation of Emirati journalists that are equipped with the tools and skills needed to excel in the media industry. The programme is held in partnership with leading media and academic institutions and includes specialised workshops designed to improve the analytical and professional skills of participants.  Arab Film Studio: Image Nation, in collaboration with local, regional and international partners, offers training and education opportunities for the film industry. These include internship opportunities on the set of TV series, one year film programs involving making a movie, a 5-month in-depth program for scriptwriters, online filmmaking workshops for high-school students, online scriptwriting courses, and online media content development courses for marketing and communications executives.
Results: The implementation of education and training programs in the UAE’s media sector, such as those offered by the New Media Academy, has yielded several significant outcomes. These initiatives have notably enhanced the skills and competencies of media professionals, equipping them with advanced expertise in digital content creation, media management, and emerging technologies. This has led to increased innovation in industry, with professionals adopting new tools and techniques to produce high-quality and creative content. The programs have also strengthened the local talent pool, contributing to career advancement and the growth of a skilled workforce capable of taking on leadership roles. Additionally, the training has improved the media sector’s competitiveness by aligning with global standards, enhancing the UAE's reputation as a media hub and attracting international interest. Networking opportunities and industry partnerships fostered by these programs have further facilitated collaboration and knowledge exchange within the sector. Furthermore, the increased public engagement and improved media literacy resulting from more effective content creation have positively impacted audience interaction with media.
Recommandations: Expanding the range of training topics to include emerging fields such as artificial intelligence in media and advanced data analytics would ensure that professionals stay ahead of industry trends. Increasing collaboration with global media institutions and incorporating international best practices into the curriculum can enhance the relevance and effectiveness of the training programs. Providing more opportunities for hands-on experience through internships and live projects can bridge the gap between theoretical knowledge and practical application, helping participants apply their skills in real-world scenarios.

L’Ensemble Artistique National a pour missions la mise en œuvre de la politique nationale de la promotion de la diversité artistique et culturelle au plan national et international ainsi que la valorisation des cultures ancestrales en perdition. A ce titre, l’organisme est chargé de : 	Mettre en place le Ballet National, l’Orchestre National et la Troupe Nationale de Théâtre ; 	Créer, diffuser et promouvoir les arts du spectacle ; 	Devenir l’ambassadeur itinérant de la culture centrafricaine ; 	Former les artistes dans les disciplines du théâtre, de la musique et de la danse ; 	Renforcer les capacités des acteurs culturels ; 	Valoriser le patrimoine immatériel du pays ; 	Donner les représentations artistiques dans les manifestations officielles de l’Etat ; 	Procéder à des recherches permanentes dans les domaines de la chorégraphie, la musique et la dramaturgie ; 	Favoriser les échanges nationaux et internationaux dans le domaine des arts scéniques ; 	Favoriser la transmission authentique des œuvres centrafricaines en matière d’arts musicaux et d’arts chorégraphiques, tendant à l’affirmation de l’identité culturelle centrafricaine, face aux progrès artistique, scientifique et technique, en vue de l’épanouissement du génie créateur de la personnalité centrafricaine ; 	Vulgariser le répertoire symphonique de l’entité sur toute l’étendue du territoire national ; 	Mener une politique dynamique en matière d’audiovisuelle ; 	Elaborer des actions éducatives et créatives qui place la jeunesse au centre du projet pédagogique en vue de vulgariser les savoir-faire culturel centrafricain.
Results: 315 artistes et Cadres de formation sont recrutés et formés sur la chorégraphie, les techniques de chant ancestrales, et l’oralité à la centrafricaine par le théâtre. Depuis deux ans, l’Ensemble artistique National, par le Ballet National, l’Orchestre National et la Troupe Nationale de Théâtre mis en place, participe aux cérémonies officielles de l’Etat.  Des répertoires riches et variés dans les domaines de la musique, du Théâtre et de la Danse sont constitués.

Title EN: eEnsure cultural diversity in public radio
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture

Area of Monitoring: Media diversity
Agency Implementation: Radio Education / Radio Educación
Main Feature: Radio Educación broadcast 17 cultural festivals, during which the institution made its signal available for free to public, cultural, and community radio stations across the country. Through live coverage and broadcasts, Radio Educación brought cultural expressions closer to a wider audience, featuring some of the most significant cultural festivals in Mexico. These festivals included the Cervantino International Festival, the Huasteca Festival, the Son Jarocho Special Forum, the Alfonso Ortiz Tirado Cultural Festival, the Riviera Maya Jazz Festival, the Jazzbook Festival, the Sinergia Festival, and the Guadalajara International Book Fair.  In support of indigenous peoples, languages, and culture (PEPIA 2019-2023), Radio Educación transmitted 3,694 radio programs during this period. Notably, they began airing the series “Canto de cenzontles” as part of a collaborative effort with the Red de Comunicadores Boca de Polen, S.C. This series explores stories and themes from indigenous and Afro-descendant communities, highlighting their worldviews, struggles, and teachings.  To showcase Afro-descendant culture in Mexico, Radio Educación disseminated 80 programs during the same timeframe. Key highlights in this area include: •	A radio marathon celebrating Afro-Mexicanness, multiculturalism, and the contributions of the Afro-descendant community. This event coincided with the 190th death anniversary of Vicente Guerrero. •	The transmission of materials produced for the 25th anniversary of the “First Meeting of Black Peoples” in Mexico.  Furthermore, Radio Educación actively participated in the design of public policies to support indigenous and community radio stations in Mexico. This initiative aimed to incorporate indigenous content into public and commercial media. The project was led by the Federal Government and the Office in Mexico of the United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organization (UNESCO), with support from the European Union. The goal was to strengthen community and indigenous radio stations as cultural and creative industries, ensuring their legal constitution and long-term sustainability.  As part of this effort, Radio Educación contributed to the preparation of the Declaration of Principles for Cultural and Linguistic Diversity in the Media. This document outlines actions for diverse programming and fosters collaborative relationships between various media entities, community communication, art, and culture projects. It emphasizes the cultural and social expressions and rights of indigenous peoples, Afro-descendants, and other diverse communities, including migrants, peasants, rural populations, neighborhoods, and the LGBTQ+ community.  The First Monitoring Committee was established to oversee the implementation of the Declaration of Principles for Cultural and Linguistic Diversity in the Media. This committee comprises representatives from public media, government institutions, civil society organizations, and indigenous and community media, including Radio Educación.  Lastly, in alignment with the International Decade of Indigenous Languages 2022–2032, the Secretariat of Native Peoples and Neighborhoods and Resident Indigenous Communities (SEPI), along with Radio Educación, launched the “Sounds of Diversity” contest. This contest aims to promote the cultural and linguistic diversity of Mexico City through oral stories in indigenous languages and Spanish, created by citizens

As part of this effort, Radio Educación contributed to the preparation of the Declaration of Principles for Cultural and Linguistic Diversity in the Media. This document outlines actions for diverse programming and fosters collaborative relationships between various media entities, community communication, art, and culture projects. It emphasizes the cultural and social expressions and rights of indigenous peoples, Afro-descendants, and other diverse communities, including migrants, peasants, rural populations, neighborhoods, and the LGBTQ+ community.  The First Monitoring Committee was established to oversee the implementation of the Declaration of Principles for Cultural and Linguistic Diversity in the Media. This committee comprises representatives from public media, government institutions, civil society organizations, and indigenous and community media, including Radio Educación.  Lastly, in alignment with the International Decade of Indigenous Languages 2022–2032, the Secretariat of Native Peoples and Neighborhoods and Resident Indigenous Communities (SEPI), along with Radio Educación, launched the “Sounds of Diversity” contest. This contest aims to promote the cultural and linguistic diversity of Mexico City through oral stories in indigenous languages and Spanish, created by citizens

Title EN: Égalité hommes-femmes dans l’encouragement du cinéma
Goal: Promote Human Rights And Fundamental Freedoms
SDG: SDG 5 - Achieve gender equality and empower all women and girls,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels
Area of Monitoring: Gender equality
Agency Implementation: Office fédéral de la culture OFC
Main Feature: Diverses études internationales et nationales ont montré que, par le passé, les projets de films de femmes ont été soutenus moins fréquemment et avec moins de moyens. Pour cette raison, l’OFC a pris des mesures depuis 2016 pour promouvoir l’égalité dans l’encouragement du cinéma, en soutenant notamment les projets de films des deux sexes de manière équilibrée. Cependant, la parité étant loin d’être atteinte, l’OFC a maintenu ses mesures pour la période d’encouragement 2021-2024.   Outre la question de l’encouragement du cinéma, la représentation des sexes devant et derrière la caméra est de plus en plus mise en avant. Diverses études ont montré que les femmes ainsi que les minorités en termes d’orientation sexuelle, d’appartenance ethnique ou religieuse sont sous-représentées dans les médias audiovisuels, ou que leur apparition à l’écran est souvent stéréotypée.  Il existe une forte corrélation entre la part d’hommes et de femmes en charge de la réalisation et du scénario (derrière la caméra) et la part de rôles principaux masculins et féminins (devant la caméra). La présence de femmes dans les rôles principaux dépend en grande partie du fait que ce soit une femme qui ait écrit ou réalisé le film. La répartition des sexes devant la caméra (à l’écran) et derrière la caméra (hors écran) est mesurée statistiquement au niveau européen et la Suisse collecte des données depuis 2017 dans le cadre du relevé statistique « Gender Map ».  Pour chaque film achevé et tourné avec des fonds publics en Suisse, la « Gender Map » collecte en effet les données relatives à la répartition des sexes devant et derrière la caméra.  En complément de la « Gender Map » des critères de sélection concrets et impératifs pour l’égalité des genres sont introduits dans le soutien à la production cinématographique.
Results: Au total, 155 longs métrages suisses (y compris des coproductions) sortis entre 2020 et 2022 ont été examinés, parmi lesquels 55 étaient des films de fiction, 98 des films documentaires et 2 des films d’animation.  Continuité dans les résultats : par rapport à la période précédente (2017-2019), on ne relève aucun changement majeur sur la période 2020-2022. À noter toutefois quelques hausses statistiquement significatives : la proportion de productrices est passée de 34 % à 42 % et celle des scénaristes femmes de 34 % à 41 %. Dans le domaine des films documentaires, la part de réalisatrices est passée de 29 % à 39 % et celle des protagonistes femmes de 34 % à 42 %.  Répartition des sexes dans les équipes cinématographiques : quelque 42 % des longs métrages suisses sont produits par des femmes. 34 % des films ont été réalisés par une femme, tandis que 41 % des scénarios ou des documents servant de base aux films documentaires ont été écrits par une femme. Dans 16 % des films, la photographie a été assurée par des femmes. On observe, dans les salles de montage, une représentation parfaitement équilibrée des hommes et des femmes.  Rôles principaux dans les films de fiction : dans les films de fiction, on compte à peu près le même nombre de rôles principaux féminins que masculins ; cependant, les personnages féminins de moins de 40 ans sont surreprésentés. Par ailleurs, chez les 51-65 ans, on compte deux fois plus de rôles principaux pour les hommes que pour les femmes.  Rôles principaux dans les films documentaires : bien que la proportion de femmes apparaissant comme une protagoniste centrale dans les films documentaires ait progressé, passant de 34 % à 42 %, celles-ci restent sous-représentées. Ce type de rôle revient dans 35 % des cas à des hommes de plus de 40 ans.
Recommandations: Il est prévu de reconduire la « Gender Map », qui a fait ses preuves en tant qu’outil statistique. La liste des principaux métiers de la production cinématographique a été élargie début 2023 : outre la production, la réalisation, l’écriture du scénario, la photographie et le montage, toutes les fonctions impliquées dans la création d’un film sont désormais prises en compte.

Title EN: Elaboration d’une feuille de route pour le développement des Industries Culturelles et Créatives (ICC) en Tunisie
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture
SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Cultural and creative sectors
Cultural Domain: Design,Performing Arts,Media Arts,Cinema and Audiovisual Arts,Music,Publishing,Visual Arts
Agency Implementation: - Le Ministère des affaires culturelles (MAC) : Unité d’encadrement des investisseurs (UEI) dans le cadre du programme Tfanen-Tunisie créative financé par l’UE (axe initiative services publics- ISP)
Main Feature: Les Industries Culturelles et Créatives (ICC) sont des secteurs d'activité ayant comme objet principal la création, le développement, la production, la reproduction, la promotion, la diffusion ou la commercialisation de biens, de services et activités qui ont un contenu culturel, artistique et/ou patrimonial.  Elles ont comme matière première la créativité individuelle, la compétence et le talent, devenue aujourd’hui le levier de croissance de l’ensemble de l’économie. Elles intègrent le consommateur et/ou le producteur dans les chaines de valeur et de l’innovation et elles sont considérées comme :  •	Une source décisive d’avantages compétitifs  •	Un moteur de l’économie de la connaissance  •	Un levier pour développer les politiques nationales et locales A cet égard et vu la nécessité d’intégrer le nouveau modèle de développement mondial dans lequel l’économie et la créativité sont liés et englobent des aspects économiques, culturels et sociaux et afin de développer l’écosystème culturel et créatif en Tunisie, le Ministère des Affaires Culturelles (MAC) a lancé en 2021, une mission au profit de l’Unité d’encadrement des investisseurs (UEI) visant à créer un cadre stratégique et opérationnel adéquat permettant de promouvoir les ICC et ce, dans le cadre du programme Tfanen-Tunisie créative (axe initiative services publics- ISP) financé par l’UE et mené par le British Council (BC) au nom du pôle EUNIC (réseau des instituts culturels européens établis en Tunisie). L’objectif général de cette mission est de proposer au MAC une approche stratégique de soutien aux ICC en Tunisie qui s’articule autour de 04 grands axes : -	Mise en place d’un cadre conceptuel et normatif des ICC (la définition des grandes filières des ICC en Tunisie et de leurs nomenclatures). -	Diagnostic des chaines de valeur de chacune des filières ICC. -	Panorama de l’économie culturelle et créative en Tunisie (la production d’indicateurs chiffrés pour chacune des filières). -	Production d’une feuille de route pour le développement des ICC en Tunisie.
Results: La feuille de route pour le développement des ICC couplée à une étude/panorama du secteur des ICC en Tunisie élaboré par le cabinet privé Matine Consulting selon une démarche inclusive, participative et interactive (impliquant presque 70 entretiens avec 8 experts sectoriels - 22 entretiens avec des acteurs publics et privés couvrant l'ensembles des 11 filières des ICC - un questionnaire en ligne avec 720 réponses) a permis de dresser le diagnostic du marché des ICC en Tunisie qui génère 1,5 milliards de dinars par an (soit 500 millions d’euros) dont 36% dans le secteur informel. Les entreprises ICC sont au nombre de 14.000 et emploient 70.000 personnes (soit 1,6% de la population active) dont 40.000 sont dans l’informel (soit 56% des employés). Le domaine employant le plus de personnes dans les ICC est la musique avec 27.000 employés et 40% des emplois, viennent ensuite le design avec 9000 personnes et 12% des emplois et les arts visuels avec 8000 employés et 11% des emplois. La feuille de route pour le développement des ICC en Tunisie élaborée selon une vision/approche qui considère les ICC comme vecteur de développement et de relance économique décline les ICC en 108 activités selon un plan de développement échelonné sur 03 horizons temporels : le court terme 2022, le moyen terme 2023-2025 et le long terme 2030. Elle est structurée sur 04 niveaux du général au spécifique (vision globale- effet/changement direct recherché - produit/ résultat à atteindre - Activité/Actions concrètes à entreprendre). Les objectifs spécifiques autour desquels s’articule cette feuille de route sont : 1.	Un cadre institutionnel modernisé et favorisant le développement du secteur culturel et créatif. 2.	Un accès au financement plus fluide et aisé pour les créateurs et porteurs de projets ICC.  3.	Une infrastructure physique et digitale mise à niveau permettant d’exploiter le potentiel des ICC.  4.	Des métiers de la culture adaptés aux exigences actuelles et futures du marché du travail. 5.	Une scène culturelle dynamique favorisant l'accès du public notamment les jeunes et les femmes au produits culturels. Ces objectifs spécifiques se déclinent en produits (18) et activités (108), une analyse détaillée de ces produits et activités est disponible en annexe 2. Néanmoins, parmi les produits/résultats recherchés à travers l’élaboration de cette feuille de route : -	La mise en place d’une batterie d’outils d’incitations à l’investissement privé dans les ICC (notamment à travers le Creative ACT à l'instar du startup ACT) -	La numérisation des œuvres culturelles et créatives et la création de plateformes digitales  -	Le renforcement de l’accès du public notamment les jeunes aux produits culturels  -	La restructuration du système d’aides et subventions publiques afin d’améliorer l’efficacité, l’efficience et l’équité. Ces résultats recherchés cadrent parfaitement avec les objectifs et les principes directeurs de la convention 2005 notamment en termes d'accès équitable au biens et services culturels, la mise en exergue du volet numérique et son importance en tant qu’enjeux majeur pour le développent des ICC etc .. L'élaboration de cette feuille de route a dévoilé la nécessité pour le MAC de disposer d'une stratégie nationale des ICC à l'horizon 2035 (en stade de validation) ayant comme vision les ICC, vecteur de développement et de bien-être social et qui s'articule autour des axes suivants : •	La consommation des ménages : un levier essentiel du développement des ICC. •	L’investissement privé : des mécanismes incitatifs à repenser et un écosystème à améliorer. •	L’exportation des biens et services culturels : un créneau à exploite. •	Les compétences : un renforcement indispensable pour l’éclosion des ICC.
Financial Ressources: La mesure s’inscrit dans le cadre du renforcement institutionnel, objectif principal du programme « tfanen » financé par l’UE (Initiative Services Publics dont le budget global s’élève à 0,6 M€)
Recommandations: Cette mesure en elle-même, en tant que travail de recherche basé sur des données récentes émises sur le secteur des ICC en Tunisie, élaboré selon une approche participative inclusive et interactive, est considérée comme un instrument d’orientation stratégique pour le MAC pour concevoir sa politique en matière de développement des ICC et prioriser ses objectifs en matière de réformes législatives et structurelles. Cependant, cette feuille de route a été présentée et débattue lors d’une conférence-débat intitulée « Quel soutien aux industries culturelles en Tunisie ? » en présence d’un groupe de responsables du Ministère des Affaires Culturelles et de plusieurs acteurs et opérateurs du milieu culturel.

Title EN: Elèves conservateurs du patrimoine engagés dans les actions d’éducation artistique et culturelle
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture
SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Cultural and creative sectors
Cultural Domain: Design,Performing Arts,Media Arts,Cinema and Audiovisual Arts,Music,Publishing,Visual Arts
Agency Implementation: Ministère de la Culture
Main Feature: Tous les ans, les élèves conservateurs se rendent dans des structures où l’accès à la culture est difficile afin de mener des actions d’éducation artistique et culturelle.
Results: En 2024, les élèves se sont rendus à l’hôpital universitaire Avicenne de Bobigny pour un atelier artistique avec les patients. Ils se sont également rendus au lycée Marcel Rudloff de Strasbourg où une table ronde avec les élèves s’est tenue, complétée de la visite des réserves du musée zoologique de Strasbourg. Enfin, Les « Cordée de la réussite » sont une initiative éducative française lancée en 2017 dont l’objectif principal est de favoriser la réussite scolaire et l'orientation vers l'enseignement supérieur de jeunes issus de milieux sociaux défavorisés. A la tête de la cordée « A nous le patrimoine ! » depuis 2021, l’Inp concourt à ce dispositif d'entraide et de solidarité par le biais d’actions d’EAC menées par les élèves conservateurs et restaurateurs. Des lycées des académies de Paris, Créteil et Versailles se sont alors rendus au musée des arts décoratifs.

Title EN: ELF Youth Advisory Group
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture
SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Cultural and creative sectors
Agency Implementation: Emirates Literature Foundation
Main Feature: The program is open to individuals aged 18�22 who are residents of the United Arab Emirates and will remain so for the program's duration. Applicants should demonstrate a genuine interest in learning about the publishing industry, the creative sector, and the work of cultural organizations such as the Emirates Literature Foundation. During the application review process, we seek candidates who can commit to self-directed and collaborative learning, as well as demonstrate the ability to reflect and problem-solve within a diverse group of peers. Each monthly session will include a book group discussion, opportunities to inform the Emirates Airline Festival of Literature program, and some sessions will include a workshop or discussion led by an industry professional from the publishing or creative sector. In between sessions, participants will be encouraged to read widely (and may even gain access to advanced copies of books not yet published), write book reviews, or other content, which will be shared through Emirates Literature Foundation channels, and support the Emirates Airline Festival of Literature marketing team in creating original content for social media to promote the 2025 Festival.
Results: The program has provided participants with a platform to explore promising career trajectories within the publishing, arts, and culture sectors. Through monthly gatherings, participants will have the invaluable opportunity to interact with industry professionals specializing in publishing, marketing, and related fields. By engaging in insightful discussions, reviewing advanced reader copies of forthcoming books, and actively contributing to the shaping of events for the 2025 Emirates LitFest, participants will gain practical experience and invaluable insights that will pave the way for their professional growth and development.

Title EN: Empowering the cultural and creative sectors for international cooperation (Creative Europe Desk Slovenia)
Goal: Achieve A Balanced Flow Of Cultural Goods And Services And Increase The Mobility Of Artists And Cultural Professionals
SDG: SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 10 - Reduce inequality within and among countries,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Mobility of artists and cultural professionals
Cultural Domain: Design,Performing Arts,Media Arts,Cinema and Audiovisual Arts,Music,Publishing,Visual Arts
Agency Implementation: The European Commission and Ministry of Culture
Main Feature: Creative Europe is a transnational programme of the European Union running from 2021 to 2027. It is the EU's flagship and the only instrument to support the cultural and creative sectors in Europe. It promotes cultural and linguistic diversity, heritage and the competitiveness of the cultural and creative sectors. EU funds are earmarked for actions that strengthen cultural diversity and address the needs and challenges of the cultural and creative sectors. The programme will contribute to the recovery of these sectors by strengthening their efforts to promote digitalization, environmental protection, resilience and inclusion. The tasks of the Creative Europe Desk (CED) Slovenia primarily include promotion and information about the Creative Europe programme, as well as technical and expert support for users who wish to submit their projects to Creative Europe calls. The Centre also works closely with the Ministry of Culture in preparing the call for proposals for co-financing successful projects of Slovenian applicants under the Creative Europe programme. In addition, CED Slovenia organises regular consultations with civil society, in which the Ministry of Culture also frequently participates.
Results: The CED team has an excellent track record, having carried out CED tasks for many years. The CED programme is credited with providing accurate and up-to-date information and support for applications for co-funding of challenging international projects involving or led by Slovenian cultural organisations. The list of Slovenian beneficiaries of Creative Europe support, which is very high, confirms the success of the CED office.
Financial Ressources: $323.996,00 from the Ministry of Culture and the same amount provided by the European Commission
Recommandations: The Expert Commission for International Cooperation and Promotion of the Ministry of Culture assessed the work of the CED as extremely successful.

Title EN: Ensuring integration among all policies and measures of governmental and non-governmental entities with the national vision for the FIFA World Cup (2022)
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture
SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Cultural and creative sectors
Cultural Domain: Design,Performing Arts,Media Arts,Cinema and Audiovisual Arts,Music,Publishing,Visual Arts
Agency Implementation: Supreme Committee for Delivery and Legacy
Main Feature: Reviewing the cultural events that have taken place in the State of Qatar over the past four years highlights that the country has undoubtedly become a leading global hub for organizing events, whether related to cultural events themselves or organized tangentially to other non-cultural events. On this occasion, it is possible to focus on reviewing events with an international character due to their significance, such as the State of Qatar organizing the Doha Capital of Culture events in the Islamic world (2021), or hosting the Qatar Airways Grand Prix for Formula 1 (October 6-8, 2023) alongside the Geneva International Motor Show, which is held for the first time outside Switzerland (October 5-14, 2023), the Doha Expo (October 2, 2023, to March 28, 2024), the Qatar International Tourism and Travel Exhibition (November 20-22, 2023), the Web Summit (February 26-29, 2024), the World Aquatics Championships (February 2-18, 2024), the Qatar International Food Festival (February 7-17, 2024), and the Doha Design Exhibition (February 24-28, 2024). These are all international events around which several cultural events have been organized, intersecting with the objectives of the Convention on the Protection and Promotion of the Diversity of Cultural Expressions. However, the State of Qatar's organization of the FIFA World Cup in 2022 under the supervision of the Supreme Committee for Delivery and Legacy, with the participation of all State agencies, represented the most significant event in the country, embodying the achievement of the goals of the mentioned Convention. The uniqueness imposed by the nature of the event and its success conditions made it essential to ensure that sustainability of developmental aspects must be considered. Thus, the responsibility of verifying the fulfillment of this condition was entrusted to the Supreme Committee for Delivery and Legacy, which supervised the organization and execution of the Qatar World Cup (2022). This Committee was specifically established to achieve the best conducive conditions for organizing and executing the mentioned sports event, considering the enhancement of comprehensive development plans in the country across all sectors, leading to the creation of a legacy for the State of Qatar that extends beyond the tournament and through generations. According to Article 4 of Emiri Decision No. (27) of 2011, which established the "Supreme Committee for Qatar 2022" and later changed its name to its current form under Emiri Decision No. (03) of 2014, its competencies include that the State “ is responsible for developing strategies and general policies related to the World Cup (2022). It prepares and monitors the implementation of developmental, economic, and infrastructural plans for the event. It approves necessary plans and programs for their implementation. The State supervises and monitors the implementation of these plans and programs. It also determines frameworks to support and encourage various activities and events related to the World Cup (2022). Additionally, it coordinates with governmental and non-governmental ministries, agencies, local, regional, and international committees, organizations, initiatives, activities, and projects in all fields related to the World Cup (2022). The State ensures integration between the strategies, plans, decisions, and activities of the referred entities and the national vision for the World Cup (2022). It accomplishes them in the best manner, including identifying, monitoring, and executing projects implemented by governmental and non-governmental ministries and agencies.” (Annex No. 39). Given the scope of this report, it is not feasible to delve into all the cultural events and activities held on the sidelines of the World Cup Qatar 2022 for several reasons. Firstly, examples of the most significant events have already been mentioned throughout this report. Secondly, it's impossible to exhaustively list these activities as they originate from various State institutions involved in cultural affairs. Thirdly, the focus of this periodic report primarily centers on policies and measures rather than mere events. Therefore, the focus in this area will be on measures that fall within the scope of this report, particularly those that consider the sustainability of developmental aspects:  1.Supporting Governance Systems: The primary aim of organizing the World Cup Qatar 2022 was to present an authentic image of the Qatari people, introduce their culture and features, and showcase the State’s prosperity and progress. Therefore, it was imperative to ensure that the presented image remained stable and continuous beyond the event by ensuring its sustainability. To achieve this goal, all parties in the State of Qatar, whether political authorities, private sectors, or civil society, unified their efforts to utilize all available resources and strive to provide what was necessary to create a sustainable cultural environment. The integration of all state institutions' efforts has occurred, including the initiative of the supervisory authorities to invite all relevant entities in the State's cultural affairs to prepare the necessary infrastructure. This includes providing suitable physical cultural spaces to hold accompanying events such as seminars, concerts, art, and cultural exhibitions, as well as logistical spaces by creating a digital environment that utilizes the advantages of technological advancement. Regarding the provision of physical cultural spaces, the supervisory authority has undertaken to allocate the space known as "Beit Al-Sulaiti" for cultural events intended by communities and various guests of the "2022 Qatar World Cup" on the sidelines of the sporting event. Additionally, the cultural space located in the Umm Salal Muhammed area, known as "Darb Al Saai", is being prepared and allocated as a permanent venue for cultural events starting from November 2022. Furthermore, the "Qatar Museums Authority" renovated the Museum of Islamic Art to improve its facilities and keep pace with development, reopening it in 2019. In 2022, it inaugurated "Flag Plaza" (Flags Square), a new community destination launched by the Cultural Years program for international cultural exchange. It features 119 flags representing countries with diplomatic missions in the State of Qatar, along with the European Union, the United Nations, and the Gulf Cooperation Council flags. Additionally, the "DADU, CHILDREN’S MUSEUM OF QATAR" was established, covering an area of 14,500 square meters, focusing on children's play artifacts and traces, such as footprints and rock engravings. Another initiative involved dedicating a historical building dating back to the mid-twentieth century in the Msheireb Downtown Doha to open studios and design laboratories named "Lewan Design Studios and Labs." These spaces aim to support the creative community in the State of Qatar and enhance its connections. In this context, it is worth noting that these spaces fall within the framework of projects related to sustainability, as per the requirements of the Supreme Committee for Delivery & Legacy (SC), including "Green Building Practices" endorsed by the Global Sustainability Assessment System (GSAS) in design, construction, and operational processes. *Regarding digital infrastructure, since 2019, in partnership with the Qatar Financial Center, the Group ONE Holdings, and the Bloomberg Media Group, the "Media City" has been established to provide business incubators supporting initiatives in the digital and technological media fields. Additionally, in 2022, the Ministry of Transport and Communications established the "Digital Excellence Center" in partnership with Microsoft and Elev8 to be a center for knowledge and innovation providing digital skills programs for students, professionals, and business leaders in the State of Qatar. Furthermore, the Supreme Committee for Delivery & Legacy launched the "Qatar Media Portal" to broadcast comprehensive media materials about the 2022 FIFA World Cup (Annex No. (40)). It also serves as an integrated digital platform for obtaining entry permits to the State of Qatar and photography permits for all journalists and representatives of broadcasting entities covering the tournament. This includes those holding host country permits or FIFA permits, including media representatives with and without FIFA broadcasting rights. It works on facilitating customs clearance procedures for equipment and portable devices (excluding requests related to drones or unmanned aircraft). In the same context, "Qatar Tourism" launched the mobile application "Visit Qatar" in 2021 to provide all tourist offers and a cultural events agenda for exploring activities throughout the State of Qatar. This step is part of Qatar Tourism's comprehensive digital transformation strategy to enrich visitors' experiences. Following suit, the Qatar Museums Authority launched the digital cultural portal "One Pass" in 2022 to align with the "Qatar Creates" initiative. This portal allows everyone to explore a series of community events and programs celebrating art, fashion, design, culture, and architecture over a week. It also facilitates visits to museums, cultural events, festivals, and theatrical performances across the State of Qatar, in addition to sharing entertainment, adventure experiences, and fashion shows.  2.The mobility of artists and cultural professionals and the flow of cultural goods and services: It is essential to refer to the exceptional law issued concerning the organization of the World Cup Qatar 2022. Law No. (10) of 2021, issued on July 29, 2021, on measures to host the FIFA World Cup in Qatar (2022), included guarantees that the State of Qatar is committed to providing, whether regarding the procedures for granting entry and exit visas, working in relation to the World Cup and its associated activities, or regarding tax exemptions and ensuring intellectual and literary property rights (Annex No. 41). It is worth noting that these guarantees apply to officially organized events and matches in the tournament, those approved or sanctioned by FIFA, and other activities related to or accompanying the tournament, such as various cultural events. These guarantees benefit all parties involved in this sports event, whether directly or indirectly, including individuals and legal entities that have entered into any contractual relationships with FIFA or any person or entity licensed by FIFA regarding the mentioned activities. This includes FIFA's commercial partners, suppliers, contractors, service providers, and broadcasters of FIFA-organized events, as well as subcontractors with these entities. This means that the provisions of this law and the guarantees it provides cover all those involved in cultural matters and falling into one of these categories. Among the guarantees relevant to this report are: -Article 2 of the referenced law obligates official entities in the State to establish a rapid and simplified mechanism for issuing entry permits, usage permits, work licenses, company registration, and any other permits or licenses required by this law, as circumstances dictate, without any restriction, condition, or discrimination.  -Article 8 provides for a full exemption from all fees and partial exemption from taxes due on activities carried out during the specified period in the referenced law.  -Article 13 stipulates the facilitation of cash and banking operations to lift restrictions and facilitate exchanges, even before the time period of the tournament and not exceeding ninety days after its conclusion.  -The sixth and seventh chapters of the law include provisions regarding rights related to the production, distribution, and exchange of cultural goods and services, including artistic, musical, literary works, and intellectual innovations related to neighbouring rights, and any content or audiovisual, auditory, visual, textual, or other materials related to hosting the World Cup Qatar 2022, followed by the right to enjoy copyright protection. Based on the above, the State of Qatar ensured that, in organizing the World Cup Qatar 2022, a space is provided where all stakeholders in the cultural sector, including artists and cultural professionals, can move freely. There should also be a spontaneous flow of cultural goods and services, in accordance with the Convention on the Protection and Promotion of the Diversity of Cultural Expressions. It is worth noting that the right to intellectual property protection mentioned in this law aligns with the objectives of several other laws issued in Qatar, which are beyond the scope of this report, such as Law No. (7) of 2002 on the Protection of Copyright and Related Rights (Annex No. 42), and Law No. (17) of 2011 on Border Measures for the Protection of Intellectual Property Rights (Annex No. 43). It also aligns with certain agreements entered into by the state, such as the Arab Agreement to Facilitate the Transfer of Arab Cultural Productions (Regional Agreement) (Annex No. 44), signed on 22/04/1987 and ratified by Qatar under Decree No. (124) of 1990 dated 10/11/1990, and the Framework Agreement on the Trade Preferences System among the Member States of the Organization of the Islamic Conference, signed on 12/08/2007 (Annex No. 45) and ratified by Qatar under Decree No. (32) of 2007 dated 10/06/2007. All these legislative texts include provisions ensuring the right to enjoy intellectual and literary property protection, creating a cultural environment that fosters creativity and innovation sustainably.  3.Gender equality and the promotion of artistic freedom: Gender equality is State policy and is not affected by any temporary or regular events. Therefore, all policies and initiatives taken in organizing the World Cup Qatar 2022 benefit both genders, with positive discrimination towards women in empowerment matters. However, the institutional fabric aimed at ensuring gender equality was strengthened on the occasion of organizing the World Cup Qatar 2022 by transforming the "Generation Amazing Community Club" launched in 2010 with a group of sports volunteers and coaches working to leverage the benefits of football to achieve Qatar's National Vision 2030 and the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals, including Goal 5 on gender equality, into a standalone foundation aimed at launching sustainable programs that will generate great opportunities for community development beyond the World Cup Qatar 2022, including a focus on enhancing gender equality. In conclusion, the organization of the FIFA World Cup Qatar 2022 was an opportunity where the desired goals of the Convention on the Protection and Promotion of the Diversity of Cultural Expressions were achieved in its fullest sense, especially since the measures taken on this occasion were characterized by sustainable development. It is a matter of pride for the State of Qatar to share this achievement with the rest of the international community within the framework of exchanging best practices.
