Title EN: Establishment of an Advisory Committee on the Representation of Women and Women’s Stories within the context of the National Cultural Institutions and National Collections
Goal: Promote Human Rights And Fundamental Freedoms
SDG: SDG 5 - Achieve gender equality and empower all women and girls,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels
Area of Monitoring: Gender equality
Agency Implementation: Department of Tourism, Culture, Arts, Gaeltacht, Sport and Media
Main Feature: An Advisory Committee on the Representation of Women and Women’s Stories within the context of the National Cultural Institutions and National Collections has been established in Ireland during the reporting period. Coinciding with International Women’s Day on the 8th March 2024, the Minister of Culture appointed this new Advisory Committee to examine how the diverse experiences and voices of women, particularly historically marginalised women, are represented in the context of the national cultural institutions and the national collections.  The committee is embarking on a significant programme of work, which will consider best practice models within cultural policy internationally, undertake a broad public consultation, support the national cultural institutions in reviewing the national collections, and consider feasible options for developing a dedicated presentation of women’s stories.  The culmination of the committee’s work will be to make specific recommendations to assist the Government in enhancing the representation of women’s experiences, contribution, and voices in Irish cultural organisations and within the national collections.    The committee will also explore the possibility of creating a dedicated space for women’s stories through options such as a women’s museum or through the National Collection.  It is further proposed that the advisory committee oversee a review of the National Collection, and identify best practice models that can support the National Cultural Institutions to ensure that women’s stories are appropriately reflected in the programming and presentation of cultural heritage.    It is expected that this review would identify any significant gaps in the representation of women and that the committee may propose recommendations on actions to address these gaps.   The advisory committee includes members from national cultural institutions in Ireland and abroad, historians, experts in gender and equality studies, representatives from the National Women’s Council of Ireland and from relevant Government departments, and those with a range of other experiences and expertise. It represents a diverse cross-section of women in Ireland, across generations, socio-economic status, geographic locations, abilities, religions, ethnicities and sexual orientations.  The Committee held its first meeting in May 2024.
Results: This Advisory Committee held its first meeting in May 2024 and recommendations will be made to government during the course of its work.  It should be noted that other areas of the Department’s work i.e. the Decade of Centenaries Programme have highlighted the role of women in the country’s revolutionary period and in the foundation of the State.  Dedicated exhibitions took place on the role of the women in 2016 and 2018 and a dedicated platform www.mna100.ie was established in 2020 to highlight the role of many forgotten women in our history through a range of innovative programmes, partnerships and initiatives.

Title EN: ETUDE DE FAISABILITE D’UN PROJET DANS LE SECTEUR DES INDUSTRIES CULTURELLES ET CREATIVES (ICC)
Goal: Integrate Culture In Sustainable Development Frameworks
SDG: SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: International cooperation for sustainable development
Cultural Domain: Design,Performing Arts,Media Arts,Cinema and Audiovisual Arts,Music,Publishing,Visual Arts
Agency Implementation: Ministère de la Culture et de la Francophonie / Fonds d’Etudes et de Pilotage AFD
Main Feature: Cette étude de faisabilité vise à évaluer les opportunités et les défis liés à la mise en œuvre d’un projet ambitieux destiné à développer les Industries Culturelles et Créatives (ICC) en Côte d'Ivoire. L’étude comprend une analyse approfondie des besoins du secteur, des ressources disponibles, des potentiels de marché, et des impacts socio-économiques. Elle propose également des recommandations pour le cadre institutionnel, juridique et financier nécessaire à la réalisation du projet. Les principaux axes de cette étude incluent le renforcement des capacités des acteurs culturels, l'amélioration des infrastructures culturelles, la promotion de l'entrepreneuriat créatif, et la mise en place de mécanismes de financement durables.  Cette  étude est en cours en réalisation entre le Ministère de la Culture et de la Francophonie et l’Agence Française de Développement (AFD) afin de financer le 3ème Fonds Etudes et Pilotage (Convention d’Affection N°CCI 1749 01R) à hauteur de 35 M FCFA, pour la réalisation d’une étude de faisabilité d’un projet dans le secteur des industries culturelles et créatives. Les Industries et Culturelles et Créatives (ICC), en tant que le levier de développement local inclusif, ont un impact positif évident sur l’activité économique et sociale des pays et constituent un gisement d’emplois, en particulier pour la jeunesse et les femmes.  Dans le cadre des négociations les parties ivoirienne et française ont convenu de dégager un financement  pour le développement du secteur des ICC. Quatre (4) axes d’intervention prioritaires ont ainsi été identifiés dans ce secteur stratégique : -	Les infrastructures et équipements culturels ; -	Le développement de l’entrepreneuriat ; -	La formation aux métiers des ICC ; -	La gouvernance et les droits d’auteurs. La présente prestation a pour objectif de préparer l’instruction et la mise en œuvre de ce projet dédié aux ICC, permettant d’atteindre les ambitions sectorielles en termes d’impacts sur la jeunesse, l’employabilité, la croissance économique et la cohésion sociale. L’objectif du volet culture est donc de construire un projet, qui prendra en compte des besoins identifiés, et dont l’enjeu principal serait d’accompagner le développement d’activités liées aux ICC autour d’un tiers lieu pilote emblématique à Bouaké (centre Jacques Aka) et de favoriser la création d’emplois et l’insertion professionnelle, et ce faisant la création de richesse à l’échelle nationale. Le projet s’articule autour de deux (2) axes qui devront contribuer au développement de trois (3) filières des ICC prioritaires par le ministère comme étant celles représentant le plus d’enjeux et d’opportunités en termes de création d’emploi des jeunes et de professionnalisation : (1) audiovisuel / cinéma ; (2) musique et (3) mode et design. -Axe 1 : création d’un tiers-lieu estimé à 7,9 milliards FCFA : ce lieu pourrait regrouper différentes activités liées à la création, à l’accompagnement et à la diffusion de contenus et aurait vocation à dispenser des formations courtes et qualifiantes et à accompagner les entrepreneurs des trois (3) filières identifiés (fonction d’incubation). -Axe 2 : l’appui institutionnel au MCF estimé à 3,4 milliards FCFA : ce deuxième axe pourrait contenir des activités d’accompagnement et de renforcement de capacités (diagnostics, assistance technique, formation etc…) permettant d’accompagner au mieux le ministère à mettre en œuvre ses orientations stratégiques et à favoriser l’attractivité économique du secteur des ICC en Côte d’Ivoire. L’objet de ce marché est de réaliser une étude de faisabilité pour le développement du future culture. Cette étude doit permettre d’affiner et de détailler le contenu du projet de faire des propositions à la fois sur les activités et sur les modalités de mise en œuvre des deux axes envisagées du projet. Les livrables de cette étude doivent permettre à la Côte d’Ivoire et à l’AFD d’instruire le projet et de procéder à l’octroi des 35 milliards de F CFA . Une étude complémentaire technique, centrée sur les aspects architecture et urbanisme du projet, sera menée en complément.
Results: L'étude de faisabilité  permettra  de : -Identifier les principaux acteurs des ICC et cartographier leurs besoins en formation et en ressources. -Évaluer le potentiel économique des ICC et leur contribution possible au PIB national. -Proposer des modèles de financement innovants pour soutenir les initiatives créatives. -Recommander des réformes législatives pour mieux encadrer et protéger les droits des créateurs. -Sensibiliser les décideurs politiques et le public sur l'importance des ICC pour le développement économique et social du pays.

Title EN: EU Research and Innovation for Culture – Horizon Europe Programme (2021-2027)
Goal: Integrate Culture In Sustainable Development Frameworks
SDG: SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: National sustainable development policies and plans
Cultural Domain: Design,Performing Arts,Media Arts,Cinema and Audiovisual Arts,Music,Publishing,Visual Arts
Agency Implementation: European Commission – Directorate General Research and Innovation
Main Feature: The Horizon Europe Research and Innovation Framework Programme (2021 to 2027) encompasses a dedicated part which supports research in cultural heritage and cultural and creative industries, accounting for around 0.8 billion euros for the period 2021-2027.      The specific cluster priorities are the following:  -	Green cultural heritage;  -	Intangible cultural heritage;  -	Cultural tourism;  -	Illicit trafficking of cultural goods;  -	Cultural literacy;  -	Crafts & Design;   -	Digital transformation for the cultural sector.    Moreover, cultural heritage and Cultural and Creative Industriess research and innovation projects can also be funded under other parts of the Horizon Europe programme (e.g. the European Research Council, Marie-Sklodowska Curie Actions, the European Institute for Innovation and Technology.)
Results: In the context of EU funded Research and Innovation, results and success stories are long-term endeavours, as projects last between 3 and 5 years. Much of HE funded research projects presented in this document are still ongoing.   Details on projects relevant to the Convention can be found here:  -	The CORDIS result pack: CORDIS Results Pack on cultural tourism: https://publications.europa.eu/resource/cellar/9e481375-02be-11ef-a251-01aa75ed71a1.0001.01/DOC_1  -	The booklet on Destination 2 with 2021 and 2022 open calls: https://op.europa.eu/en/publication-detail/-/publication/9e16c9a5-5cdf-11ee-9220-01aa75ed71a1/language-en/format-PDF/source-293355247     Moreover, EU funded Culture and Creativity research has achieved concrete results in these transversal priorities:    1. Strengthening capacity building for cultural diversity:  The European Collaborative Cloud for Cultural Heritage is a new cutting-edge collaborative platform that aims to support cultural heritage researchers and professionals to take full advantage of the many opportunities in the digital transition. It is an inclusive platform that will enable also small institutions with limited resources to become digitally adept. Horizon Europe will invest € 110 million in 2023, 2024 and 2025 to establish the Cloud.  2. Encouraging intercultural dialogue through R&I: the Horizon Europe programme demands collaboration between organisations from at least three different countries, the number being usually higher for most projects. Moreover, the HE programme is open to participants from non-EU countries.    3. Supporting resilience and sustainability in and through culture: HE supports research and innovation on the protection of artefacts and cultural goods from anthropogenic threats.  A new European Partnership for Resilient Cultural Heritage, potentially mobilising € 250 million, should be launched in 2025.
Financial Ressources: Over USD 0.9 billion [EUR 0.8 billion] for the period 2021-2027.

Title EN: Freedom of Artistic Expression through Equitable and Inclusive Approaches in the Ethiopian Circus Sector
Goal: Promote Human Rights And Fundamental Freedoms
SDG: SDG 5 - Achieve gender equality and empower all women and girls,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels
Area of Monitoring: Artistic freedom
Agency Implementation: Ethiopian National Circus Association Consortium (ENCAC)
Main Feature: In the past four years, there has been no censorship on the freedom of artistic expression in circus art production from the government. A colorful first Ethiopian Circus Arts festival was organized in Addis Ababa and participants came from different parts of Ethiopia and presented their production without any restriction in collaboration with EFDR Ministry of Culture and Sport.   ENCAC actively participated in the promotion of gender equality, peace, and security issues in collaboration with Selam Ethiopia, regional, zonal & city women & children affairs, and other partners, and 38 events were organized in the past four years with 1,520,000.00 ETB. During the event there were a total of 241 (173 female & 68 male) circus artists actively participated, 72 % of the artists who participated in the event were female. ENCAC has created a working opportunity for all associated artists in Ethiopia through festivals and different occasions. Promoting the circus arts by collaborating with all relevant groups, organizations, agencies, and institutions was one of the major activities undertaken in the past four years. ENCAC highly encourages members' association on women's leadership, four years ago there were not more than 10 women in the circus leadership but now there are 54 female circus artists who participated actively in the circus leadership. This means there is one female circus leader in the circus clubs on average. 33% of female artists were in the international circus market in the past four years. Out of four World Guinness Records one of the records was broken by a female artist from Africa Dream Circus. One deaf female professional circus artist from Circus Debrebrhan is a role model for women currently working in the international circus company.  Recently, the Amhara Region Circus Association with all circus artists’ and leaders’ active participation and decision-making process a bylaw was developed and approved, which ensures the movement of circus artists from one circus club to other circus clubs without limiting their movement. The approved bylaw was an important tool for monitoring the movement of circus artists by respecting their fundamental freedom of the circus artists. In addition to this, the bylaw came up with a solution for circus clubs and reduced conflicts that happened among circus clubs during a transfer of circus artists. Currently, Addis Ababa and Tigray Circus Associations are in the process of adopting the bylaw.
Results: •	There is no problem with the freedom of expression in circus production  •	ENCAC documented the biographies of all the circus artists in Ethiopia  •	54 female circus artists participated actively in the circus leadership (on average there is one female actively participating in the circus leadership) •	1 deaf female professional circus artist from Circus Debrebrhan is working in the international circus company •	241 (173 female & 68 male) circus artists have actively participated in an awareness creation campaign on gender equality and 72 % of the artists who participated in the event were female •	Amhara Region Circus Association was developed and approved bylaw to ensure the movement of circus artists  •	33% of female artists were in the international circus market in the past four years.  •	Out of 4 World Guinness Records one of the records was broken by a female artist from Africa Dream Circus. •	Addis Ababa and Tigray Circus Associations are in the process of adopting the bylaw.

Area of Monitoring: Cultural and creative sectors
Agency Implementation: SboNdaba Dance NPC
Main Feature: Provide professional dance training and generate employment in the performing arts industry for youth from under-resourced communities.  • Choreograph original, uniquely South African works of art in the field of African Contemporary Dance and Integrated Arts  • Create employment opportunities in the dance/music/arts/theatre/film industries, public performances, community, extra-mural education and tourism • Initiate projects, events, and collaborations with other artists and organisations, locally, nationally and internationally • Increase accessibility to the arts by taking our live performances to the people where-ever they are, and making arts products available digitally.
Results: Over the past 4 years 15 professional dancers have been trained per year in dance and integrated arts and sustainably employed. This includes SAQA accredited teacher training. 150 vulnerable youth per year, from communities at risk, have been provided with weekly basic dance, singing and performance skills training, led by the SboNdaba Dancers.  This has enabled exposure to positive role models and public performance spaces such as professional theatres, urban spaces and parks. A professional dance company has been developed that performs in a broad range of contexts including theatres, community hubs, outdoor spaces, festivals and educational institutions in urban and rural areas, taking the arts to people wherever they are.  Since 2022 they have given 70 performances to over 10 million people including on television.  The SboNdaba Dance Company has been invited to perform in The Netherlands, Shanghai, and Australia.  The company works in collaboration and in partnership with other artists, companies and environmental NGOs. During Covid we developed a number of documentaries. The choreography by award winning choreographer Sbonakaliso Ndaba focuses especially on social and environmental justice. We have recently tackled pressing climate change issues in partnership with Environmental NGO’s with productions such as “Who stole our Oceans?”, ‘Our Oceans, Our Future’ and ‘Our Mother the Earth’. Other recent productions include ‘Locked Doors, Behind Doors’ during lockdown and “If Only Our Ancestors Could Speak’ performed at Afrovibes in The Netherlands in 2023. We have received support for the past 4 years from the Presidential Employment Stimulus Programme (PESP) which kept us alive and developing through the Covid pandemic. We received a grant this year from the Mzansi Golden Economy for a highly acclaimed production titled “! ke e: /xarra //ke, Diverse People Unite” celebrating Africa Day and 30 years of democracy. We hope to tour this production around the country if we can find the funding. We are also supported annually by the City of Cape Town and the provincial department of Cultural Affairs and Sport. We have been unsuccessful in our applications to the National Arts Council.

Title EN: Evaluation de la mise en oeuvre de la politique culturelle du Togo
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture
SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Cultural and creative sectors
Cultural Domain: Design,Performing Arts,Media Arts,Cinema and Audiovisual Arts,Music,Publishing,Visual Arts
Agency Implementation: Ministère de la culture et du tourisme
Main Feature: La présente mesure se caractérise par la collecte et l’analyse des données sur la mise en œuvre de la politique culturelle nationale de 2011. Son objectif est de présenter les grands résultats de l’état de mise en œuvre de la politique culturelle et d’identifier les priorités pour les années à venir.  La collecte s’est déroulée du 20 au 30 mars 2023 dans les cinq (05) régions économiques du Togo, auprès des acteurs culturels impliqués directement ou indirectement dans la chaîne de la culture togolaise.
Results: La mesure a permis d’obtenir les résultats suivants : - les populations dans l’ensemble reconnaissent la culture  comme « base de toute action de développement culturel au niveau local » ;   - large implication des populations dans les pratiques ;  - la politique culturelle togolaise a pris en compte la question du genre qui est en vigueur dans les pratiques endogènes ; - le budget alloué à la culture est largement insuffisant pour soutenir des projets  structurants pouvant impacter durablement les communautés.
Financial Ressources: non disponible
Recommandations: L'évaluation du projet de collecte est parvenue aux conclusions suivantes : - la  politique culturelle nationale n’a pas été suffisamment vulgarisée ;  - les populations en ont une faible connaissance  ; - la durée de l’enquête était courte et insuffisante pour obtenir la disponibilité de tous les acteurs identifiés ;  - les moyens logistiques et financiers mis pour la réalisation de cette mesure étaient en deçà des besoins sur le terrain. Comme recommandations pour la prochaine politique, il faudra : - vulgariser davantage la politique culturelle nationale auprès de toutes les couches socioprofessionnelles; - mobiliser des ressources suffisantes ;  - faire une évaluation à mi-parcours à terme réviser cette politique.

Title EN: Evaluation of the Impact of Covid-19 on Cultural and Creative Industries
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture
SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Cultural and creative sectors
Agency Implementation: Secretariat of Culture
Main Feature: The project “Evaluation of the Impact of COVID-19 on the Cultural and Creative Industries” was an initiative promoted by the Secretariat of Culture of Argentina, in coordination with the Meeting of Ministers of Culture of MERCOSUR (MERCOSUR Cultural), and the collaboration of the United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organization (UNESCO), the Inter-American Development Bank (IDB), the Ibero-American General Secretariat (SEGIB) and the Organization of Ibero-American States for Education, Science and Culture (OEI). The main objective of the project was the macro and microeconomic estimation of the impact of the restrictions imposed by the COVID-19 pandemic on the region's Cultural and Creative Industries (CCI). This involved the identification, collection and systematization of information and cultural statistics at the regional level, as well as the generation of new data.  The activities were carried out between July and November 2020, through collaborative work with the public institutions of the eleven States that took part in the project: Argentina, Brazil, Bolivia, Colombia, Costa Rica, Chile, Ecuador, Mexico, Paraguay, Peru and Uruguay.  This joint exercise contributed to the dimensioning of the size of the CCIs at regional level, and allowed for a survey of the public policies implemented in response to the emergency and an in-depth dialogue with sector representatives on the characteristics of the crisis and the opportunities in the short and medium term.   At the same time, two online surveys were carried out aimed respectively at workers and entrepreneurs of the cultural and creative sector. The purpose of this component of the project was to make an approximation of the microeconomic impact of the restrictions imposed by the pandemic on the sector, as well as other dimensions that are not usually covered by official sources.   At the same time, the “Strengthening and Training Workshop on Cultural Indicators” was held, which promoted the review of methodological alternatives for the generation of indicators on the contribution of culture to the different dimensions of development, taking as a reference UNESCO's Culture 2030 Indicators, and promoted the exchange of experiences and peer learning through collaborative exercises of reflection and analysis.   Does the policy/measure specifically target youth? No Does the International Fund for Cultural Diversity (IFCD) support the implementation of the policy/measure? No
Results: In its various components, the project yielded the following results:   - Macro and microeconomic estimation of the impact of Covid-19 on CCIs. - Characterization of public policies and opportunities in the face of the emergency. - Survey of the perception of workers and companies of the CCIs.  - Identification of opportunities for the generation of cultural statistics  In order to face the new challenges of the global order in the CCIs, the study presented five keys for their reactivation in the region that compile some of the main ideas and strategies for strengthening the sector in the post-pandemic period, which can be summarized in the following points:  -Strengthen physical and digital infrastructures, and promote the development of digital and technical capabilities. -Organize and strengthen the labor and production market of the CCIs and promote labor formalization. -Update regulatory frameworks and financing paradigms. -Promote cultural diversity and encourage the consumption of local and regional content. -Promote public-private collaboration and networking as a strategy.
Recommandations: research left as a first major result the potentiality of regional cooperation. In this regard, it synthesized a joint work agenda which expresses the need for collaboration between international organizations and States, with the aim of strengthening capacities and resources along the CCI value chain.  This work also emphasized the importance of deepening and consolidating a system of cultural indicators at the regional level. In this regard, it is not only necessary to strengthen current regional experiences such as SICSUR, but also to advance in the process of convergence and harmonization of methodologies and indicators to assess, among other things, the impact of migration to digital technology and the generation of new products and new professions, levels of informality, gender (in)equality and the cultural and creative diversity of the region.  The cultural and creative industries can guide economic recovery, not only because they provide jobs and occupy a prominent place in our economies, but also because they have a very positive impact on other economic sectors and generate a multiplier effect on them. In addition, cultural industries can contribute to sustainable development in the region, helping to maintain cultural diversity from a rights-based approach.

Title EN: Exemplary CSO Initiatives that Support the Mobility of Artists and Cultural Professionals
Goal: Achieve A Balanced Flow Of Cultural Goods And Services And Increase The Mobility Of Artists And Cultural Professionals
SDG: SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 10 - Reduce inequality within and among countries,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Flow of cultural goods and services
Agency Implementation: Ministry of Education, Culture, Research, and Technology (Kementerian Pendidikan, Kebudayaan, Riset, and Teknologi; Kemendikbudristek)
Main Feature: In the past four years, exemplary CSO initiatives that support the mobility of artists and cultural professionals include: 1. Solo International Performing Arts (SIPA);  2. Indonesia Dance Festival (IDF); 3. Art Jakarta; 4. ArtJog; 5. Lake Toba Traditional Music Festival and  6. Indonesian Music Expo (IMEX).  SIPA, IDF, Art Jakarta, and ArtJog were reported in the 2020 QPR and are still being organized annually while drafting this report. Of the four events, only ArtJog was not disrupted during the COVID-19 pandemic. Meanwhile, the other three events could only be held virtually or postponed during the pandemic. For example, SIPA was held virtually in 2020, and since 2021, it has been held in a hybrid manner, combining virtual presentations and live performances at Fort Vastenburg Solo.   The IDF was held virtually in 2020. In the latest development, in 2023, the Loka Tari Nusantara Foundation (Yayasan Loka Tari Nusantara, YLTN) was launched as a legal entity to ensure the sustainability of the IDF. Friends of the IDF was also launched in 2023, which functions as a fundraising partner to support the creation of works and program implementation, as well as the growth and career development of dance performers, performing arts managers, and dancers and artists both on stage and behind the scenes.  Art Jakarta was held virtually in 2020 and 2021. Then, in 2022 and 2023, it was back to normal, but at a more extensive exhibition venue at the Jakarta International Expo in Kemayoran. As additional information, one of the unique features of this exhibition is the availability of on-site services for overseas shipping and customs clearance for artworks sent from and to overseas. This event has the central vision of being an art exhibition focusing on Southeast Asia and one of the most prominent art exhibitions in the region.   One of the new initiatives in the past four years is the Lake Toba Traditional Music Festival, which is part of the Indonesian Traditional Music Festival. Rumah Karya Indonesia initiated this festival and has been supported by Kemendikbudristek since 2021. This festival involves local communities and musicians in the Lake Toba area, North Sumatra, and it also invites traditional music composers from other regions in Indonesia. This festival carries the concept of traditional music used for rituals and uses a variety of musical instruments originating from the areas of participating musicians. The output from this activity is in the form of video clips, online festivals, and song recordings, which are then broadcast on online platforms. Winning participants receive recording facilities in their respective cities amounting to IDR 5,000,000 / 306,43 USD video clip-making facilities in Lake Toba, and a composer/group appreciation award amounting to IDR 15,000,000/ 919,29 USD.  Another exemplary event that has not been reported in the 2020 QPR but is still being organized while preparing this report is IMEX. IMEX was first held virtually in 2019 with support from Kemendikbudristek. This annual event aims to introduce world music or types of music rooted in Indonesian traditions and ethnicity, such as gamelan, keroncong, or dangdut, to the world of music abroad. Apart from that, IMEX is also a music market inviting stakeholders from the world music ecosystem with the hope that they will be interested in inviting the groups that perform on the IMEX stage to their respective countries. The stakeholders include music promoters, booking agents, producers, label owners, festival directors, art center directors, TV, radio, and online media, members of organizations and music associations, and musicians from other countries interested in collaborating. In 2023 and 2024, IMEX was held live in Bali.   In general, exemplary CSO initiatives that support the mobility of artists and cultural professionals are aimed at contributing to achieving the following agenda(s) of the National Strategy for Culture: 1. Provide space for the diversity of cultural expressions and encourage cultural interaction to strengthen the inclusiveness of culture (Agenda 1); 2. Protect and develop values, expressions, and practices of traditional culture to enrich national culture (Agenda 2); and 3. Develop and utilize cultural resources to strengthen the position of Indonesia internationally (Agenda 3).
Results: SIPA: It is watched by more than 10,000 viewers every year.  IDF: IDF has continually involved cultural institutions from other countries, such as the Goethe Institute (Germany), Institut Francais Indonesie (France), Istituto Italiano di Cultura (Italy), British Council (England), Japan Foundation, and Korean Cultural Council.  2023 Art Jakarta: Sixty-eight artworks from Indonesian and foreign artists, such as Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand, Philippines, Vietnam, Taiwan, South Korea, China, Japan, Russia, and Australia, were presented. One foreign artist who participated in this exhibition is Park Jihyun from South Korea.  2023 ArtJog: Brought together 73 artists consisting of 51 adult artists and 22 child artists and presented the annual Young Artist Award.  Lake Toba Traditional Music Festival: Twelve traditional music composers from other regions in Indonesia participated in this festival after being selected through an open call and strict curation by the organizers.  2024 IMEX: Of the 124 groups across Indonesia who registered for the IMEX 2024 Open Call, 15 performers were selected to perform live.
Recommandations: IDF: The internal evaluation in 2023 by YLTN and IDF resulted in the following conclusions/recommendations. 1. A series of YLTN activities from October 2022 to March 2023 were organized smoothly, safely, and comfortably according to the plan of the YLTN and IDF working teams.  2. The 2022 IDF event, 2022 Focus Group Discussion, Mapping of Contemporary Dance, Launching of YLTN and Friends of IDF, and Rebranding of YLTN-IDF were carried out by the schedule and plans that have been prepared.  3. The YLTN-IDF programs implemented in 2022 shall become benchmarks for implementing the programs in 2024 and beyond. By maintaining synergy and sustainable activities, it is hoped that program implementation in the coming years will be better and provide more significant benefits for the Indonesian Contemporary Dance ecosystem.  ArtJog: The evaluation carried out in 2023 by Emmanuel Kurniawan, Yulianus Febriarko, and Tri Subagya specifically aimed to explore the impact of ArtJog on the knowledge production process, especially related to cultural education and cultural diplomacy. The results of this research produced the following conclusions/recommendations. 1. From the cultural education perspective, ArtJog introduces the public to the world of fine arts, even becoming a "showcase" and benchmark for developing contemporary Indonesian arts. Various forms of fine arts are presented in two or three dimensions, as well as multimedia. As a "showcase" for contemporary arts in Indonesia, ArtJog provides fairly up-to-date information regarding emerging ideas, styles, techniques, and trends, especially among young artists in Indonesia. The selected themes contribute positively to public knowledge regarding social, political, economic, and environmental issues. In the exhibition, people are helped to understand the artworks and issues presented through curatorial tours, discussions, and meetings with the artists. More than that, education on how to behave in exhibition spaces or galleries is also carried out.   2. From a cultural diplomacy perspective, ArtJog brings together many people from various social backgrounds and interests. Therefore, ArtJog becomes an arena for interaction that forms relationships or refreshes social networks that have been formed. Some make new friends, and quite a few continue to work together or collaborate to create work together. Things that are often discussed by art observers and educators about ArtJog are generally related to (a) ideas/themes, (b) event management, including communication and branding strategies, and (c) technical matters such as display techniques, exhibition space management, etc.

Title EN: Exhibition compensation - grants to cover fees to artists
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture
SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Cultural and creative sectors
Agency Implementation: Ministry of Education and Culture   The Finnish Heritage Agency
Main Feature: It is a compensation paid to an artist for work done for a museum exhibition.    The Ministry of Education and Culture carried out a three-year experiment on exhibition fees in 2017-2019, and an impact assessment required by Parliament's Education and Culture Committee was carried out on the experiment.    In 2020, the Ministry of Education and Culture appointed a working group to draw up a proposal for an exhibition fee model for visual artists. According to the final report of the working group published in 2021, the comprehensive implementation of the system requires additional funding in addition to exhibition fees paid through museums.     The appropriation of one million euros for exhibition fees was made permanent in the 2022 budget.
Results: The primary objective of the exhibition fee system is to take into account the importance of visual artists as producers of exhibition content and to improve their chances of making a living from artistic work. The system of exhibition fees also helps museums and other exhibition organisers to act as strong advocates of the livelihood of art and artists in their areas, thus ensuring long-term artistic work and the development of visual arts.   Experience has shown that the model has improved the artist's financial position and facilitated the drafting of contracts.   1) In 2022, awards were granted to 187 exhibitions, and in 2023 to 400 exhibitions.   2) In 2022, approximately 650 artists received awards, while in 2023, awards were granted to 826 artists.   3) The average amount of exhibition awards granted in 2022 was around 5300 euros per exhibition (with multiple recipients possible per exhibition), whereas in 2023, the average was 3600 euros per exhibition, with an average artist award of 1700 euros.
Financial Ressources: 1,1 million USD
Recommandations: According to the three alternative calculations presented in the evaluation report from 2020 (Taide maksaa: assessment of the exhibition fee experiment for artists, publications of the Ministry of Education and Culture 2020:19), establishing the exhibition fee model requires an appropriation of between EUR 675 000 and EUR 1 300 000 per year. The amount of the required appropriation depends on the extent to which museums will apply for the appropriation in the future and how the exhibition fee model will be formed. If the model were to apply to exhibition organisers other than museums, such as exhibitions organised in libraries or other municipal exhibition facilities, the amount of the required appropriation would be higher than estimated in the evaluation report, as they were not taken into account in the calculations.

Main Feature: Le Burkina Faso est réputé dans l’organisation régulière de grandes manifestations culturelles diversifiées et d’envergure internationale. Lesdites manifestations connaissent un engouement de la part des artistes et des professionnels internationaux de la culture. Leur déplacement à destination du Burkina Faso est soutenu par plusieurs actions notamment le statut de participants de « pays invité d’honneur », l’opérationnalisation du E-visa et l’existence d’infrastructures et sites de promotion de la diversité des expressions culturelles accueillant des artistes étrangers en résidence artistique.   La participation de pays en qualité d’invité d’honneur lors des événements et manifestations culturelles nationales d’envergure internationale constitue une pratique visant à renforcer les échanges culturels par le biais de la diplomatie culturelle. Cette initiative favorise la mobilisation des ressortissants des pays invités, en particulier des artistes et des professionnels de la culture, qui deviennent ainsi des ambassadeurs culturels du Burkina Faso dans leurs pays d’origine.   Généralement, la participation de la délégation officielle, composée d’autorités gouvernementales et de professionnels de la culture, est entièrement prise en charge (voyage, hébergement, déplacement). Les autres participants, notamment les artistes et les professionnels de la culture ne faisant pas partie de la délégation officielle, bénéficient de facilités transfrontalières pour leurs déplacements ainsi que d'accréditations pour participer aux événements concernés.   L’introduction de l’E-Visa Burkina, représente une avancée significative dans l’univers des titres de voyage et de séjour au Burkina Faso. Opérationnelle depuis début 2023, la plateforme E-Visa Burkina permet de faciliter l’accès des artistes aux documents d’autorisation pour entrer sur le territoire national.  L’opérationnalisation de l’E-Visa Burkina a amélioré la mobilité entrante des artistes et professionnels de la culture. Title EN: Fairness Process for Arts and Culture
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture
SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Cultural and creative sectors
Agency Implementation: Federal Ministry for Arts, Culture, the Civil Service and Sport; all nine Austrian Federal States (Bundeslaender)
Main Feature: The COVID-19 pandemic has highlighted challenges in the arts and culture sector, some of which already existed before the crisis, but which have been exacerbated by the pandemic. In response, the Federal Ministry for Arts, Culture, the Civil Service and Sport launched a fairness process in autumn 2020 in cooperation with the Federal States and with the intensive involvement of CSO and interest groups in the arts and culture sector.  The Fairness Process is an exemplary federal-state cooperation; a number of measures were developed in the first few months and presented at a Symposium in 2021. These measures included -	a joint commitment to greater fairness in the arts and culture, summarised in the Fairness brochure, -	increased coordination meetings between the funding bodies of all participating regional authorities -	and standardised criteria for awarding multi-annual contracts.  In addition, a Fairness Codex for Art and Culture was developed. This codex was drawn up by a working group consisting of representatives of the federal government, the Laender (federal states) and CSO/interest groups in a one-year participatory process. With this codex, the Austrian arts and culture scene has for the first time received a codified cooperation standard that is intended to pave the way for more fairness in the cultural sector – through respect and appreciation, sustainability, diversity and transparency. The document aims to strengthen the resilience of the entire sector and at the same time contributes to increased public awareness of fairness in art and culture.  Fair pay for all those working in the arts and culture sector is a key issue in the fairness process. In June 2022, a historic commitment was made by all federal states, the Austrian Association of Cities and Towns, the Association of Austrian Municipalities and the federal government with the signing of the joint Fair Pay Strategy. In this joint Fair Pay Strategy they emphasised their responsibility for the financing of art and culture as well as their willingness to make a greater contribution to fair pay in future.  The fairness process in Austria will be continued in the coming years. Moreover, the Arts and Culture Section of the Federal Ministry for Arts, Culture, the Civil Service and Sport was also involved in the EU working group on the Status and Working Conditions of Artists and Cultural and Creative Professionals (2021-2023).  The Austrian Federal States are an integral part of the Fairness Process as described above. They have actively implemented Fair Pay measures and provide federal state funds for this purpose.
Results: As part of a pilot phase in 2022, the Federal Ministry for Arts, Culture, the Civil Service and Sport provided earmarked funding totalling EUR 6.5 million for "Fair Pay" for the first time. Overall, in the period 2022- 2024, the Federal Ministry for Arts, Culture, the Civil Service and Sport has provided € 25.5 million in funding for fair pay measures.  A direct result of the Fairness Process is the expansion of IG Netz (“IG Network”). IG Netz, founded in 1991, supports independent groups in the field of performing arts through subsidising social security contributions so as to provide an incentive for employment. As a first measure under the Fairness Process, IG Netz was expanded in cooperation with the Laender and the interest group Freie Theaterarbeit. The total budget of this support fund was stepped up from EUR 300,000 to EUR 700,000 (in 2024), also with funds provided by the Laender. Not only have more persons become eligible for funding as a consequence, the amount of subsidies per person and month has increased from EUR 200 to EUR 300.   The establishment of the vera* trust centre for persons affected by violence, harassment and the abuse of power in the arts, culture and sport (see also separate measure) represents a further milestone in the Fairness Process. The confidential counselling centre supports people from the fields of art and culture who have experienced harassment and violence and points out possible courses of action.
Financial Ressources: s. above

Area of Monitoring: Cultural and creative sectors
Agency Implementation: Knowledge Economy Forum
Main Feature: The first part of the study discusses the situation of cultural education in Lithuania. The first part of the study focuses on one-off cultural education in Lithuania. Activities (cultural passport) and long-term cultural education interventions. Based on this analysis, five key elements of the current challenges of the current cultural education system.  These challenges become the basis for the selection of the best practices from foreign countries and the Lithuanian educational initiatives that could create synergies with cultural education. This analysis and the recommendations based on it are presented in the second part of the study.  The third part of the study is devoted to presenting the proposed national framework for cultural education for the schoolchildren system and the roles of the actors involved, their responsibilities and interrelationships. Title EN: Federal Digitalization offensive / Measures for the digital transformation of the arts and culture sector
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture
SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Digital environment
Agency Implementation: Federal Ministry for Arts, Culture, the Civil Service and Sport
Main Feature: Main features of the policy/measure: The digital transformation has profoundly changed the arts and culture sector as well as artistic processes. Cultural and creative work is influenced by digital advancements and change, providing among other things opportunities for the development of innovative forms of artistic expressions and new ways of cultural participation.  In its government programme 2020-2024, the federal government of Austria has set itself the goal of establishing innovative platforms for the arts, culture, technology and the digital world, as well as promoting interdisciplinary cooperation between the cultural and tech scene, start-ups, universities and research institutions. A digitalization offensive provides the necessary prerequisites for a sustainable digital transformation of the sector. The Federal Ministry for Arts, Culture, the Civil Service and Sport has thus provided extensive financial means to support the digital transformation of the arts and culture sector during the reporting period. In 2020, EUR 1,1 Mio were provided for the development and implementation of digital projects and formats that open up new ways for individuals and cultural institutions to engage in artistic engagement and knowledge transfer as well as exchange, participation and interaction with the public.  In 2021, the Federal Ministry for Arts, Culture, the Civil Service and Sport and the Federal States (Laender) jointly developed and funded digital projects through the funding call Kunst und Kultur im digitalen Raum (“Arts and Culture in the digital space”). A total of EUR 2.5 million were provided for 85 projects. Those projects included artistic projects, digital strategies, apps, games, digital platforms, interactive websites and virtual and augmented reality projects.  In 2022, 38 projects that contributed to the digital transformation of the arts and culture sector were funded with a total sum of approx. EUR 900,000.  In 2023, 32 projects were funded with a total sum of approx. EUR 850,000.

Title EN: IMMA (Irish Museum of Modern Art)’s A Creative Catalyst for Change – Strategic Plan 2024-28
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture
SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Cultural and creative sectors
Agency Implementation: IMMA (Irish Museum of Modern Art)
Main Feature: The Irish Museum of Moderm Arts is Ireland's National Cultural Institution for Modern and Contemporary, which receives funding from the Department of Culture. IMMA’s A Creative Catalyst for Change – Strategic Plan 2024-28 was launched this year and sets out the strategy for strengthening the institution over the next 4 years. It includes the goals that over the next five years IMMA will be: 1. A Catalyst for Change 2. A Radically Public Space 3. A Centre for Research and Innovation 4. A Global Connector  A Catalyst for Change IMMA will be a catalyst for motivating and mobilising actions for climate positive change and social progress by showcasing artwork that raises awareness, challenges mainstream narratives, and encourages sustainable practices. Over the period of this strategy, we will:  •	Host exhibitions that address current social and political issues around identity, honouring our commitment to diversity in our curatorial practices and programming.  •	Host an annual ecological ‘Earth Rising’ festival, with major new commissions to imagine a sustainable future.  •	Lead sectoral thinking around carbon consumption, inclusive audience engagement, and diversity in the arts.  •	Promote conversations on ecology and encourage innovation in art-ecology prototypes that demonstrate good environmental practice.  •	Play a leading role in the practice, advocacy, and access to the arts for young people and their concerns for the future.  •	Support artistic risk-taking and experimentation.  IMMA’s strategy goal to be a Catalyst for Change includes the programming and delivery of a major climate action festival, Earth Rising. IMMA are now programming year three of the festival which attracted over 16,000 visitors last year including international artists, scientists and climate action researchers creating a platform for to affect behavioural change.  IMMA is working to be a regenerative museum.   A Radically Public Space Over the period of this strategy, IMMA will:  •	Increase the impact of outdoor artistic programming using the full 48-acre site to create an exciting and accessible place for all visitors.  •	Develop the Courtyard as a convivial space with live events.  •	Build on the success of our Art & Ageing Programme by creating a new broader strand of programming to support Art & Wellness enhancing the mental and physical wellbeing of our communities both onsite and online.  •	Develop the IMMA residency programme to increase its emphasis on experimentation and international research and exchange.  •	Transform our Project Spaces into a Creativity Hub, placing learning, innovation and creativity at the heart of the Museum.  •	Develop new engagement themes with an emphasis on community and new audiences.  An Equality, Diversity and Inclusion Executive has been appointed to support the museum in implementing this goal. This includes cooperation between national and local/regional government authorities.  https://imma.ie/wp-content/uploads/2024/02/IMMA-STRATEGY-2024-2028.pdf  https://imma.ie/about/policies-and-reports/public-policies/gender-equality-policy/   Key programmes for diversity and inclusion also include IMMA Horizons, a programme for the lifelong curious building out extensive art and wellness programmes including the Azure programmes for people with dementia and their carers. IMMA also have specific programmes to support Ukrainian asylum seekers, and art and oral language support programmes in partnership with DCU (Dublin City University) for asylum seekers.  https://imma.ie/learn-engage/imma-horizons/   A Centre for Research and Innovation Invest in the digital transformation of institutional collections and best practice in digital treatment of archive materials.  A Global Connector The strategy also outlines how IMMA will strengthen its ties with international partners through collaborative projects, touring exhibitions and also includes plans for staff mobility for peer learning across museums in Europe.  •	Strengthen IMMA’s ties with international partners through collaborative projects and touring exhibitions.  •	Produce research into connections between Ireland’s culture and important simultaneous international developments. •	Increase access to international art across Ireland. •	Promote the IMMA Collection internationally to a global audience •	Purchase international art to emphasise the global scope of contemporary art practice. •	Programme a more diverse global art history. •	Establish a visiting curators programme to support the visibility of Irish artists abroad. •	Highlight Dublin as an increasingly global city.  The Strategy also outlines how IMMA will work to promote human rights and fundamental freedoms including through exhibitions, talks and screenings.

Title EN: FESTIVAL DE CINEMA "Clap Ivoire"
Goal: Achieve A Balanced Flow Of Cultural Goods And Services And Increase The Mobility Of Artists And Cultural Professionals
SDG: SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 10 - Reduce inequality within and among countries,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Flow of cultural goods and services
Agency Implementation: Office National du Cinéma de Côte d’Ivoire (ONAC-CI)
Main Feature: Le festival de cinéma CLAP Ivoire est un concours de courts métrages des jeunes réalisateurs de 08 pays membres de l’Union Economique et Monétaire Ouest Africaine (UEMOA). Après trois (3) éditions nationales, CLAP IVOIRE s’est ouvert à cet espace sous régional en 2004. Dans la phase pratique le festival s’organise en deux (02) étapes : -La Phase Nationale se déroule dans chaque pays membre de l’UEMOA;  -La Phase Internationale réunit quant à elle, les 16 finalistes des Etas membres d’Abidjan. Le concours concerne deux genres cinématographiques d’une durée de 13mn : la Fiction et le Documentaire. LA PHASE NATIONALE Le jury décerne quatre prix -	Dans le genre Fiction 1.	Le premier prix 2.	Le deuxième prix Il est  à noter que cette année au niveau de la Côte d’Ivoire deux (2) prix ont été  décernés. 1.Le prix  de la meilleure interprétation masculine ; 2.Le prix de la meilleure interprétation féminine.  -Dans le genre Documentaire 1.Le premier prix 2.Le deuxième prix Les deux premiers de chaque genre représentent leurs pays respectifs lors de la phase finale internationale. LA PHASE INTERNATIONALE Une table ronde des Directeurs de la cinématographie des pays participants s’organise autour d’un thème ; -Des ateliers de formation sont animés par des experts ; -Les films en compétition sont projetés ; -Un concours de pitch est organisé. L’objectif du festival est de contribuer au développement du cinéma en Côte d’Ivoire  et dans l’espace UEMOA par la promotion des métiers du cinéma et de l’audiovisuelle auprès  de la jeunesse afin qu’elle fasse du cinéma un moyen d’expression et de lutte contre la pauvreté. Un instrument dédié au soutien de la création cinématographique avec les objectifs clairement définis :  -Soutien aux réalisateurs et formation des professionnels ; -Formation à l’écriture scénaristique et aussi la formation des jeunes réalisateurs.    Le Clap Ivoire permet de créer un cadre de réflexion et d’échanges entre les différents directeurs cinématographiques de la zone UEMOA pour apporter des approches de solutions pour reconquérir et créer une économie cinématographique dans la zone pour bénéficier des retombées économiques. Cette rencontre des directeurs permet de créer une plateforme commune afin de partager des idées communes et d’élaborer des projets communs dans le cinéma et de l’audiovisuel et la libre circulation des œuvres dans la zone l’UEMOA. L’organisation d’un concours de pitch qui permet de déceler des jeunes talents, des acteurs et des amateurs qui pourront assurer la relève dans ce domaine qui suscite autant d’engouements et d’intérêt au sein de la jeunesse. Ce concours à travers des films documentaires et des films de fictions permet de déceler des réalisateurs et de promouvoir l’intégration culturelle sous régionale. Elle permet aussi une promotion et une coproduction entre les différents Etats. Le Festival Clap Ivoire  amène à développer l’esprit de créativité des jeunes réalisateurs par la mise en place et l’implication à des scénarios sur dimensionner et surréaliste pour remporter ou être l’un des meilleurs lors de cette compétition. Pendant le Festival Clap ivoire, il y a l’organisation des Master class pour amener les jeunes à se familiariser à des techniques nouvelles du cinéma et de l’audiovisuel. C’est aussi une vitrine pour faire connaître à la jeunesse les différents secteurs d’activités dans le cinéma pour promouvoir les métiers du cinéma et de l’audiovisuel. Cette année  Clap Ivoire indique une place de choix du cinéma dans le développement et à sa participation pour l’éducation d’une nation et aussi apporter une plus- value au  culte de croyance au cinéma local.
Results: le festival clap ivoire  a permis de:  redynamiser le secteur cinématographique  tout en pérennisant et aussi en valorisant le patrimoine cinématographique Africain; -créer l’émulation au sein de la jeunesse pour la proposition des thèmes cinématographiques attrayants.  -participer à un nouvel instrument de relance du cinéma africain  par le soutien aux jeunes réalisateurs.  - faire  sortir des jeunes cinéastes de la précarité en leur permettant de participer à des concours et à des festivals à l’international; -d'ouvrir un carnet d’adresse par des échanges plus fructueux dans ce domaine cinématographique.  Il a aussi permis l’engouement des jeunes réalisateurs à la création de films plus attractifs dans la zone de l’UEMOA et aussi l’intégration culturelle entre les différents acteurs. Il a développé une collaboration franche et permanente entre les différents directeurs  de la zone UEMOA par  échanges interminables et participatifs sur des sujets d’actualité dans le domaine cinématographique. Il a renforcé la coproduction sous régionale par le biais d’accords bilatéraux et multilatéraux à travers les différentes sociétés de production et de distribution de l’espace UEMOA.  Il a permis de développer la formation et de valoriser les différents  corps de métiers de la chaine de valeur cinématographique.
Financial Ressources: Budget de l’Office National du Cinéma de Côte d’Ivoire (ONAC-CI) et l’appui du FONSIC à hauteur de 200 000 USD
Recommandations: L'évaluation a montré que le Festival Clap Ivoire est un outil efficace pour la promotion des cinéastes africains et la diversité culturelle. Il a été recommandé de renforcer les partenariats internationaux pour élargir la portée du festival et d'augmenter les financements pour soutenir davantage de projets cinématographiques innovants.; d'intégrer des programmes de mentorat pour les jeunes réalisateurs et d'améliorer la visibilité du festival à l'échelle mondiale.

Title EN: FESTIVAL INTERNATIONAL DU FILM POUR ENFANT (FESTIFE)
Goal: Integrate Culture In Sustainable Development Frameworks
SDG: SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: National sustainable development policies and plans
Agency Implementation: ONG Inter Palm Lumière (IPL)
Main Feature: L’Objectif de l'ONG Inter Palm Lumière (IPL) est : Eduquer, former et sensibiliser les individus par le biais du cinéma, le théâtre et  le sport. Cette ONG IPL  a un projet : festival international du film sur l’enfant. Cette activité a pour objet de faire la promotion de l’éducation et les droits de l’enfant à travers le cinéma, le théâtre et le sport’’ Les motivations de l'ONG Inter Palm Lumière (I.P. L) à l'initiation du Festival International du Film sur l'Enfant (FESTI.FE) sont multiples :   l'enfant représente la pépinière de demain, et investir dans son éducation et son bien-être est essentiel pour bâtir un avenir meilleur pour toute l'humanité. Le Festival International du Film sur l'Enfant s'inscrit ainsi dans cette noble mission de valorisation et de protection de l'enfance, offrant une plateforme essentielle pour la diffusion d'œuvres cinématographiques engagées et inspirantes.  Concernant les activités prévues lors du festival, il est prévu une programmation diversifiée pour divertir et éduquer les participants :  - Compétition cinématographique dans cinq catégories distinctes : long métrage, court métrage, série, feuilleton et documentaire projetés dans les Clubs IPL; -Une plateforme de rencontres professionnelles dédiée au cinéma, ainsi qu'un forum de discussion abordant divers sujets liés au bien-être des enfants. -Rencontre d'écrivains célèbres, dont les ouvrages sont utilisés comme manuels scolaire avec les élèves. - Rencontre d’un enfant acteur avec les enfants, offrant ainsi une occasion unique d'échange et d’inspiration. -Activités récréatives variées pour les enfants, comprenant défilé des pompons girls accompagnées avec la fanfare, des concours de danse, de chant, de poésie, sketch et des démonstrations de karaté; -Des stands mis à disposition pour les différentes structures promouvant l’éducation et les droits de l’enfant, afin de présenter leurs activités et projets; -Atelier de formation aux métiers du cinéma, offrant aux participants la possibilité d’acquérir des compétences pratiques et théoriques dans divers domaines Cinématographiques. Le festival se déroulera autour du 20 novembre de chaque année, en lien avec la journée mondiale de l’enfance et s’étendra sur 5 jours. Les  cibles principales sont les cinéastes professionnels produisant des œuvres qui respectent les normes cinématographiques et qui mettent en avant l'éducation et les droits de l’enfant. En somme, le Festival International du Film sur l’Enfant (FESTI. FE) promeut l’éducation et les droits de l’enfant à travers le cinéma, le théâtre et le sport, avec des impacts significatifs sur les plans social, culturel et éducatif. Éducativement, il sensibilise le public aux questions d’éducation et de droits de l'enfant via des films, pièces de théâtre et événements sportifs qui suscitent discussions et réflexions critiques. Il expose les spectateurs aux défis mondiaux des enfants, encourageant la prise de conscience et la résolution de ces problèmes. Sur le plan des droits de l’enfant, le festival met en lumière les violations et promeut leur protection, encourageant le respect des droits des enfants, y compris une éducation de qualité et la protection contre l’exploitation.
Results: Les résultats attendus par cette mesure sont:  -Générer un intérêt passionnant autour de ce festival à l'échelle internationale; -Favoriser un espace d'échanges entre les cinéastes et les défenseurs de l'éducation et des droits des enfants; -Stimuler la production de films visant à promouvoir l'éducation et les droits de l’enfant.

Title EN: Friends of Jordan Festival
Goal: Achieve A Balanced Flow Of Cultural Goods And Services And Increase The Mobility Of Artists And Cultural Professionals
SDG: SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 10 - Reduce inequality within and among countries,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Mobility of artists and cultural professionals
Agency Implementation: Friends of Jordan Festivals (FJF), Amman TV Media Company, Jordan Tourism Board (JTB), Departmetn of Antiquitites
Main Feature: The Al-Adha Festival, held from Friday, July 31, to Monday, August 3, 2020, was a virtual celebration designed to highlight Jordan's rich cultural heritage and support Jordaninan artists during the pandemic through a series of performances at four historic sites around the country. The festival was conducted with the slogan "Eidkom El Sana Eina - Urdunna Janna, Urdunna bekheir" (عيدكم السنة عنا.. أردننا جنة…أردننا بخير), emphasizing the message that Jordan is a paradise and remains in good health.  Program Highlights:  Date: Friday, July 31, 2020 Location: Amman Citadel, Historic Section, Omeyyade Palace Performance: An evening of Classical Music with Old Favorites and Famous Movie Tracks Featuring: National Music Conservatory Orchestra with soloists Hind Hamed and Ady Naber, conducted by Mohamad Othman Sediq  This opening night set a refined tone for the festival, blending classical music with popular film scores to create an accessible yet sophisticated experience for audiences. The performance by the National Music Conservatory Orchestra showcased Jordan's talent in classical music and celebrated local soloists, emphasizing the country's musical heritage.  Date: Saturday, August 1, 2020  Location: Kerak Castle Performance: An enchanting evening of Oriental fusion music titled "Whispers and Tunes" Featuring: Haleem Music Band  The second evening featured the Haleem Music Band, known for their innovative fusion of classical Arabic compositions with various musical forms. This performance highlighted the diversity within Jordan's musical landscape, blending traditional sounds with contemporary influences.  Date: Sunday, August 2, 2020 Location: Jerash, North Theatre Performance: An evening of Arabic Tarab and Classical Music with a Tribute to Arab Idols Featuring: Amman Arabic Ensemble with soloists Natalie Samaan, Atallah Hindeleh, and Bisan Kamal, conducted by Sakher Hattar  This tribute concert honored iconic Arab musicians such as Umm Kulthoum, AbdelHalim Hafez, and Abdel Wahab. By featuring renowned local soloists and the Amman Arabic Ensemble, the performance connected contemporary audiences with the timeless legacies of these music legends, fostering a deep appreciation for Arabic classical music.  Date: Monday, August 3, 2020 Location: Dead Sea Panorama Performance: Autostrad Indie Band with Bedouin Electronic music Theme: Music derived from the everyday life in Jordan, its slang, and traditional songs  The final night of the festival featured Autostrad, an indie band known for their unique blend of Bedouin electronic music. Their performance reflected the everyday experiences and cultural narratives of Jordanian life, offering a modern take on traditional themes and resonating deeply with local and international audiences alike.  The Al-Adha Festival exemplified FJF's commitment to promoting the diversity of cultural expressions and supporting the mobility of artists and cultural professionals. By leveraging a virtual format, the festival not only celebrated Jordanian heritage but also demonstrated the resilience and adaptability of the cultural sector in the face of global challenges, through:  Virtual Format and Accessibility: Due to the COVID-19 pandemic, the festival adopted a virtual format with no physical attendance. This innovative approach allowed the performances to reach a global audience through online streaming, facilitated by Amman TV. The virtual format ensured the safety of all participants while maintaining a vibrant cultural exchange.  Cultural Significance and Impact: The Al-Adha Festival successfully promoted the diversity of Jordanian cultural expressions by featuring a wide range of musical genres and traditions. Each performance was strategically placed in a historic site, enhancing the cultural and historical context of the event. This not only showcased Jordan's rich heritage but also highlighted the importance of preserving and celebrating cultural diversity.  Promoting Mobility and Engagement: The festival provided a platform for local artists and cultural professionals to gain visibility and engage with a broader audience. By streaming the events online, FJF facilitated the virtual mobility of Jordanian artists, enabling them to connect with international audiences and cultural professionals. This initiative aligned with UNESCO's Goal #2 by enhancing the flow of cultural goods and services and increasing the mobility of artists, even in a virtual setting.  Advocacy for Cultural Goods and Services: Through the festival, FJF advocated for the recognition of cultural goods and services as essential components of trade and investment agreements. By highlighting the economic and cultural value of the arts, the festival underscored the need for policies that support the mobility and sustainability of cultural expressions.
Results: The Al-Adha Festival has achieved significant results in enhancing the visibility of Jordanian cultural expressions, promoting cultural diversity, facilitating cross-cultural exchange, strengthening cultural infrastructure, advocating for the economic value of cultural goods and services, and increasing audience engagement. These outcomes align closely with the objectives of the UNESCO 2005 Convention, demonstrating FJF's commitment to protecting and promoting the diversity of cultural expressions. Namely through:  Enhanced Visibility and Global Reach: The virtual format of the Al-Adha Festival enabled FJF to reach a significantly larger audience than traditional in-person events. With online streaming facilitated by Amman TV, the performances were accessible to viewers not only within Jordan but globally. The festival garnered thousands of views across various digital platforms, demonstrating its wide reach and impact. This increased visibility has elevated the profile of Jordanian artists and cultural professionals on an international stage, fostering greater appreciation and recognition of their work.  Promoted Cultural Diversity: By featuring a diverse lineup of performances, the festival successfully showcased the rich tapestry of Jordanian cultural expressions. The variety of musical genres - from classical and Arabic Tarab to Oriental fusion and Bedouin electronic music - highlighted the country's cultural diversity. This not only celebrated Jordan’s heritage but also reinforced the importance of preserving and promoting diverse cultural expressions as outlined in the UNESCO 2005 Convention.  Facilitated Cross-Cultural Exchange and Professional Development: The festival provided a platform for Jordanian artists to collaborate and engage with local audiences and showcasing Jordanian talent to international audiences.   Strengthened Cultural Infrastructure: The use of historic sites such as Amman Citadel, Kerak Castle, Jerash North Theatre, and Dead Sea Panorama as performance venues underscored the importance of cultural heritage sites in contemporary cultural life. The festival highlighted the potential of these sites as vibrant spaces for cultural events, encouraging their preservation and use in promoting cultural expressions.  Advocated for the Economic Value of Cultural Goods and Services: Through the festival, FJF effectively advocated for the recognition of cultural goods and services as significant contributors to the economy. The event demonstrated how cultural initiatives can generate economic activity and support the livelihoods of artists and cultural professionals.   Increased Audience Engagement and Cultural Participation: The online format and diverse programming of the festival led to high levels of audience engagement. Viewers were able to interact with the performances through comments and social media, fostering a sense of community and participation. This interactive element was particularly important during the COVID-19 pandemic, as it provided a means for people to connect and engage with cultural content despite physical distancing measures.
