Title EN: Film Curating Workshop for Seniors “Kino kelionės”
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture
SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Cultural and creative sectors
Agency Implementation: Lithuanian shorts
Main Feature: "Kino kelionės" is a "Lithuanian Shorts" initiative – a film curating workshop program primarily focused on Lithuanian seniors, aimed at promoting professional short films to this demographic. The program consists of a two-day workshop in November, where selected participants watch the latest Lithuanian short films, learn about the short film industry in Lithuania, and become familiar with Lithuanian film festivals and how their repertoires are curated. After a brief theoretical session and film screenings, the seniors, together with mentor Ieva Šukytė – Vilnius Short Film Festival programmer and film journalist – discuss each film in a group, select their favorites, and curate a program of 5–6 short films. The official release of this curated program occurs in January during the Vilnius Short Film Festival, where the films are screened as part of the festival’s repertoire. Workshop participants attend the screenings, present the "Kino kelionės" initiative, and introduce the short film program. After the screening, the senior curators have the opportunity to hold a Q&A session with the filmmakers in front of the audience. The second part of the initiative takes place in the spring when the same program is showcased for elderly audiences in cultural centers across various regions of Lithuania. The target audience of the "Kino kelionės" program includes Lithuanian seniors, residents of care homes in regional areas, members of employment centers, senior citizens' communities and clubs, and visitors of the University of the Third Age.
Results: The successful results of "Kino kelionės" are shown by the implemented workshops, the interest from seniors to attend this program, the creation of two curated film programs, the large number of spectators, and the positive feedback from cultural centers that organized screenings. In its first edition, the program had 6 participants from Vilnius who curated a short film program. All participants learned about the program during a special presentation of the initiative at a screening for elderly people at the “Skalvija” Film Center. The second edition had 7 participants from Kaunas. These participants heard about “Kino kelionės” through various channels such as the University of the Third Age in Kaunas, Kaunas Public Library, and other senior clubs. Each year, participants watched around 20 short films and selected 5 for the program. In the spring, the programs were screened in cities such as Vilnius, Kaunas, Klaipėda, Šiauliai, Anykščiai, Varėna, Radviliškis, Jonava, Alytus, Kėdainiai, Lentvaris, Šilutė, among others. In 2023, the program was showcased in 40 cultural centers and attracted more than 700 spectators, whereas in 2024, it was screened in 25 venues and drew over 900 visitors. The increase in spectator numbers and the positive feedback from cultural institutions that organized the screenings have only strengthened the significance of "Kino kelionės". Cultural institutions are pleased to offer seniors a cinema experience, allowing them to connect with the stories depicted in the films, ask questions, and discuss them with their peers. This program provides a valuable platform for seniors – both the program participants and elders in the regions – to explore the world of short films, engage in a communal activity, and embrace Lithuanian culture in smaller towns. This initiative contributes to sustainable development by promoting social inclusion, cultural participation, and lifelong learning among seniors, ensuring that cultural experiences are accessible and enriching for all members of society, including those in smaller towns and regions.

Title EN: Fonds Culturels Sud

Main Feature: Au nom de la Direction suisse du développement et de la coopération (DDC), artlink gère le programme de subventions Fonds culturel Sud, qui facilite l'accès au marché culturel suisse et aux réseaux professionnels pour les artistes et les praticiennes et praticiens de la culture basées et basés en Afrique, en Amérique latine, en Asie du Sud-Est et du Sud-Ouest, et en Europe de l'Est (pays non-membres de l'UE). Le Fonds culturel Sud soutient les artistes individuelles et individuels, les groupes et collectifs artistiques ainsi que les promotrices culturelles et les producteurs culturels, et les institutions travaillant dans le domaine des arts visuels, des arts du spectacle, des arts écrits et des arts culinaires. Le Fonds culturel Sud encourage tout particulièrement les projets et les collaborations transdisciplinaires. Il soutient uniquement des projets d'artistes originaires de pays et de territoires éligibles à l'aide publique au développement (APD). Les artistes des pays partenaires de la DDC sont prioritaires pour l'obtention d'un soutien.  Le Fonds culturel Sud propose deux formes de soutien :  1) Ongoing Grant Programme (Demandes en cours) destinées aux projets présentés en Suisse en collaboration avec un lieu ou un partenaire suisse.  2) Call for Proposals Programme (Appels à propositions), selon plusieurs types d’appel à proposition, chacun de ces appels cible, une région, un thème et une pratique artistique.
Results: Depuis plus de 30 ans, le Fonds culturel Sud soutient, par des garanties de déficit et des contributions à des projets, des productions et des manifestations d’artistes et de praticiennes et praticiens de la culture d'Afrique, d'Asie du Sud-Est et du Sud-Ouest, d'Amérique latine et d'Europe de l'Est (pays non-membres de l'UE). Chaque année, le Fonds culturel Sud a soutenu en moyenne environ 700 représentations de 370 artistes, praticiennes et praticiens de la culture, groupes et collectifs différents dans les domaines de la musique, des arts visuels, de la danse/du théâtre, du cinéma et du théâtre. Les artistes et les praticiennes et praticiens de la culture ont ainsi généré des recettes, élargi leurs réseaux et, pour certaines et certains, obtenu des engagements ultérieurs et une présence médiatique en Suisse et dans l'Europe proche. De nombreux événements qui marquent la diversité du paysage culturel suisse n'auraient pas pu avoir lieu sans le Fonds culturel Sud.

Title EN: Film Festival on Disabilities
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture

Area of Monitoring: Cultural and creative sectors

Main Feature: The Film Festival on Disabilities is an annual cinematic event that takes place around the International Day of Persons with Disabilities (3rd December). So far, Center for Social Innovation – CSI (Cyprus) who is the organiser of the event, has organised three consecutive festivals.  The Film Festival on Disabilities, the only one of its kind in Cyprus film festival stands for inclusion, accessibility, solidarity and social cooperation aims to bring the wider public into contact with the issues of disability, accessibility, equal opportunities, respect for human rights and diversity.  The Festival’s programme includes film screenings (featuring films related to disabilities, diversity, social inclusion, solidarity etc.), a special Children's Zone and parallel activities like music concerts, panel discussions and activities for children.   FFD applies a sustainability plan in order to secure viability and seamless repetition each year. One of the sustainability aspects is the co-organisation of the festival with running relevant EU-funded projects that seek dissemination or space for reaching their target groups. Another aspect is the synergies strategy: through the mobilization of its vast network, CSI brings together various organisations with diverse backgrounds, thus, multiplying the impact in the local community.
Results: The Film Festival on Disabilities (FFD) organized by the Center for Social Innovation (CSI) in Cyprus has made several notable achievements since its inception. Below are some key results and impacts of the initiative:  •	Increased Awareness and Sensitization: The festival has successfully brought issues of disability, accessibility, and diversity into the public spotlight, raising awareness and fostering greater understanding among the general population. •	Community Engagement: The FFD has engaged a broad audience through its diverse program, which includes film screenings, panel discussions, and music concerts. This engagement helps to create a more inclusive and supportive community. •	Educational Impact: The inclusion of a special Children's Zone and activities for children ensures that younger generations are educated about disabilities and inclusivity from an early age. This helps in building a more inclusive society in the long term. •	Sustainability and Viability: The festival’s sustainability plan, which includes co-organization with EU-funded projects and creating synergies with various organizations, has ensured its continuous success and repetition each year. This strategic approach has secured necessary resources and support, making the festival a sustainable event. •	Enhanced Visibility for EU Projects:By partnering with relevant EU-funded projects, the festival has helped these initiatives reach their target groups more effectively, increasing their visibility and impact within the community. •	Multiplying Local Impact: Through mobilizing its vast network, CSI has brought together organizations from diverse backgrounds, which has multiplied the festival’s impact on the local community. This collaborative approach has strengthened the community's capacity to support people with disabilities. •	Promotion of Human Rights and Diversity:The festival has been a strong advocate for equal opportunities, respect for human rights, and diversity, promoting these values through its varied programming and outreach efforts.  Overall, the Film Festival on Disabilities has not only provided entertainment and educational opportunities but has also made significant strides in promoting social inclusion, solidarity, and cooperation within the local community. Its continued success and growing impact demonstrate the effectiveness of its sustainability and synergy strategies.

Title EN: Freedom of Expression in the Constitution
Goal: Promote Human Rights And Fundamental Freedoms
SDG: SDG 5 - Achieve gender equality and empower all women and girls,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels

Cultural Domain: Design,Performing Arts,Media Arts,Cinema and Audiovisual Arts,Music,Publishing,Visual Arts
Agency Implementation: Icelandic State
Main Feature: In Iceland, the freedom of expression is a constitutional right guaranteed, along with other human rights, by the Icelandic Constitution. The general public, including artists and the press, is thereby guaranteed the freedom to their opinions and convictions, as well as the right to express those. The freedom of expressions is an incredibly important right for both individuals and society as a whole, providing individuals with the ability to freely express themselves. This has a direct impact on society as a whole, providing a legislative foundation upon which laws, regulations and policies are built. It should be noted that the freedom of expression does not protect individuals’ rights to hate speech and other forms of discrimination.

Title EN: Film Policy 2020-2030
Goal: Integrate Culture In Sustainable Development Frameworks
SDG: SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: National sustainable development policies and plans
Agency Implementation: Icelandic Film Centre
Main Feature: The Ministry of Education and Culture, the Ministry of Finance, the Association of Icelandic Film Producers, the Association of Filmmakers and the Association of Film Directors have for decades made an agreement for a certain period of time on the orientation of Icelandic filmmaking. In the spring of 2019 the Minister of Education and Culture, appointed a working group with representatives of the government and film associations and industry to formulate a comprehensive policy for filmmaking and film culture in Iceland, which should apply until 2030.  The five main goals of the policy are: 1) create a rich film culture, which strengthens the identity of the nation and strengthens the Icelandic language, 2) offer a more diverse and ambitious film education, 3) strengthen the competitive position of the industry and 4) Iceland becomes a well-known international brand in the field of filmmaking. Ten actions are identified in the strategy that support its stated goals. The goal of the policy is that Icelandic filmmaking can flourish and prosper in the coming decade. It is intended to strengthen Icelandic culture and language and the nation's identity, promote the economy and promote Iceland's strong reputation. The task force was tasked with drawing up an action plan based on the strategy, covering film culture, film education, development and production of film material and international promotion, including Iceland as a filming location. It was requested that the group specifically examine the institutional and support system of filmmaking with regard to simplification and strengthening, but also how filmmaking could support Iceland's goals in the field of sustainability

Main Feature: The FILMar project, operated by the Portuguese Cinematheque within the framework of the EEAGrants funding mechanism, aims to broadly showcase Portuguese film heritage related to the sea. Developed in collaboration with partners in Norway, Iceland, and Liechtenstein, the funding countries, it seeks to digitize ten thousand minutes of films of various genres and formats, ensuring their visibility through retrospectives and cycles, DVD editions, and publications. By 2024, the FILMar project is responsible for the dissemination of film heritage related to the sea, starting a digitization process from copies deposited in ANIM - National Archive of Moving Images, in coordination with partners in the areas of exhibition, programming, distribution, and research or education, both in heritage cinema and in related fields such as visual anthropology, museology, inter-arts, film literacy promotion, and film and historical analysis.  The primary objective is to return cinema to the communities depicted in it, whether through fiction, documentary, or animation. This is achieved through close dialogue, creating suitable presentation contexts for a film heritage that requires reading and interpretation, given the multiple sources of origin and layers of analysis that may arise.  A strategy accompanies the digitization process, carried out in a laboratory by a dedicated team. Programs involve the areas of programming, archiving, exhibition, and publishing of the Portuguese Cinematheque, including Cinematheque Junior, integrating various intervention areas of the institution.  Additionally, the program maintains a hybrid presence, with programming actions in theaters in Lisbon and various parts of the country, in collaboration with festivals, film clubs, and cine-theaters. These actions are extended through an online page accessible via the link www.filmar.cinemateca.pt, where complementary and contextual content of the selected and programmed films is regularly presented, along with a digital image archive and a podcast.
Results: The FILMar project, developed by the Portuguese Cinematheque – Museum of Cinema since February 2, 2020, concludes on April 30, 2024, after digitizing 267 titles of film heritage related to the sea. Operationalized within the framework of the European Financial Mechanism EEAGrants 2020-2024, FILMar aimed to identify, preserve, digitize, and disseminate Portuguese cinema, establishing national and international partnerships, notably with the Norsk Film Institutt and the Cinematheque in Oslo, Norway.  FILMar has significantly transformed and influenced the way the Portuguese Cinematheque digitizes and promotes film heritage, creating conditions for a more fluid and transversal approach to film preservation and shared knowledge. By establishing a digital laboratory at the National Archive of Moving Images, the Cinematheque increased the number of available titles on digital platforms and in public screenings. This internalized laboratory facilitated the digitization of 267 films, surpassing the original goal of 70 titles, and increased the number of minutes from the initially determined 10,000 to 10,511.  Over more than three years, with a budget of €981,324.81, FILMar contributed to the digitization of 119 short films (3,804 minutes) and 68 feature films (6,707 minutes). Since the first public session on June 12, 2021, with MARIA DO MAR by José Leitão de Barros, FILMar has presented nearly 180 films in around 40 national cities through thematic cycles, special sessions, extensions, and mediation programs. These efforts involved collaboration with festivals, film clubs, exhibitors, museums, art galleries, universities, educational projects, and cultural mediation. A notable partnership was also established with the RTP program Cinemax.  Despite the temporal coincidence with the COVID lockdown, the public presentation of the results marked a significant change in the Cinematheque’s public engagement, allowing for 502 public screenings in 45 cities instead of the original 25 screenings in 6 cities. This extensive public interaction led to active participation in programming for major film festivals in Portugal and foundational programming for festivals in partner countries such as Iceland and Norway.  FILMar’s impact extended to film mediation and education programs in cooperation with state-run projects, reaching territories previously unserved by the Cinematheque. The project’s broad approach to sea-related film heritage and contemporary perspectives also resulted in organizing five exhibitions, publishing five books, and releasing one DVD. Furthermore, FILMar maintained a regular presence on public television, with 14 programs showcasing 21 films, reaching 200,000 viewers.  The cooperation between the Portuguese Cinematheque and the Norsk Film Institutt, under the framework of the International Federation of Film Archives (FIAF), involved sharing copies and exchanging best practices in film preservation and mediation. Due to renovation works at the NFI building and the impact of the COVID lockdown, a different strategy was devised for presenting the results. Regular programming of Norwegian films in Portugal, always in dialogue with Portuguese films digitized under the project, included the participation of Norwegian specialists. Special programs were also developed under Icelandic and Norwegian initiatives, with professionals from these countries invited to visit the digital laboratory and share expertise.  Field trips and specific screenings for professionals from donor countries, as well as interactions with professionals from other European and South American countries, were organized. Cooperation with the Norwegian partner is set to continue through regular screenings, exchange of digital practices, and collaboration on film history and identification.  FILMar has established a new paradigm for presenting and promoting film heritage, creating opportunities for film historians, educators, curators, exhibitors, museums, and public institutions to integrate cinema into best practices for historical learning and collective memory awareness.

Main Feature: The goal of this measure, which as call begins in 2023, is to strengthen micro and small creative enterprises, by supporting activities that promote an increase in sales, improvement in skills and innovation capacities, an increase in competitivity and sustainability of their economic activity, strengthening stability of their business in the medium and long term, by granting co-financing for their "business strengthening" which considers a strategy for increasing their sales, basing them on activities that promote innovation, on increasing skills of human capital and on business models and, on the other hand, the development of a "portfolio" with activites that strengthen goods, services, creative content and/or experiences and performances, among others that the business has. This contest has two calls for proposals: “Factoría Inicia” and “Factoría Escala”. Individuals and legal entities can apply to these opportunities.   The cofinancing covers up to 80% of the total cost of the project, with the recipient contributing the remaining amount. In the “Factoría Escala” section the amount can be up to $35,000,000. The expected result is an early stage scale-up, a prototype and/or an innovative business model. This measure, in accordance with the monitoring framework of the 2005 Convention, is part of the "policies and measures that support the development of dynamic cultural and creative sectors" indicator. In turn, it is a means of verification as "job creation and entrepreneurship measures".
Results: Of a total of 125 applications received, in August 2023, 83 projects were identified as meeting the criteria to pass onto the evaluation stage. Of these, 88% are from legal entities (72% micro and 16% small businesses) and 12% are from individuals. Of these applications, 25.3% belonged to the female gender, which translates to 21 eligible applications.   Regarding the national distribution of eligible projects, and following the tendency from previous years, the highest volume of projects corresponds to applications from the Metropolitan Region, reaching a little more than half of eligible projects (50.6%), followed by the Maule Region, (10.84%) and the Valparaíso Region (8.43%).   From the selected projects, we can highlight the following projects in "Factoría Escala": "Playmestudio, from video games to film and series” (free translation), “Immersive sounds: driving the music industry through innovation and technology" (free translation) and "Business strengthening and training in new immersive audio technologies" (free translation).   Lastly, regarding projects selected for "Factoría Inicia", we can highlight the following: "XR STAGE in Chilean theatres" (free translation), "Productora trino: AI service in production services" (free translation) and "Quijote films. Expansion and strengthening of disruptive technologies" (free translation).

Recommandations: European Project IR-CREA âStrategici ma vulnerabili. Relazioni industriali e lavoratori delle industrie culturali e creativeâ is a researching project         focuses on industrial relations in creative industries ( http://www.ties-unifi.eu/ircrea/about/) . Creative workers are a highly heterogeneous group,         which is internally highly differentiated. On the one hand, there are workers employed in large enterprises with high wages, good employment         conditions and stable contracts. On the other, there are vulnerable workers who contract out their skills to various organizations in project based         labour markets, straddling between self-employment and economically dependent conditions, with medium-low wages and a professional         environment characterised by a high level of uncertainty. The research project regards the latter, namely highly skilled workers that play a key role         in the knowledge economy but that are also more vulnerable. The action has three main goals: a) providing a general overview on industrial         relations in creative industries across Europe; b) investigating practices in different countries with heterogeneous traditions in industrial relations         and social dialogue; c) disseminating projectâs results among social partners, policy makers and other stakeholders at national and international         level. IR-CREA will especially study how trade unions and employersâ representatives include creative workers in collective bargaining activity and         what kind of services they provide. The project also aims to disclose the presence of alternative forms of association of creative workersâ interests         (such as informal professional communities and co-working spaces). The digitization of the economy has resulted in the rise of new activities         within the creative industries (as the case of gaming industries) and it transformed the others (as the case of graphic designers). The project IRCREA will explore the dynamics of the two sectors, analysing the major changes, and highlighting the relationships with the representative         organizations. Title EN: Form a Regional Cultural Alliance for Sustainable Cultural Development and Consolidate community action to Protect and Promote the diversity of cultural expression in Lautem Municipality

Area of Monitoring: Cultural and creative sectors
Cultural Domain: Design,Performing Arts,Media Arts,Cinema and Audiovisual Arts,Music,Publishing,Visual Arts
Agency Implementation: Many Hands International
Main Feature: The concept for this initiative is to create a cultural alliance consisting of representatives from government, communities and civil society that promotes, protects and supports culture as a foundation, driver and enabler of development in Timor-Leste. The role of a cultural alliance is to support and sustain cultures and creative activities within and across communities. This means creating a sustainable foundation, including robust planning and funding, to allow communities to practice and economically benefit from their cultures and creative pursuits as Timor-Leste develops into a modern and vibrant nation.   Formation of the regional Lautem Cultural Alliance is the first step in a longer process to create regional-level alliances across Timor-Leste and eventually a National Cultural Alliance. This first step includes formation and registration of the Lautem Cultural Alliance, training in cultural development planning, the development of a Lautem cultural development plan and guidance in advocating for national government engagement and support.  The initiatiave also supports decentralisation by supporting strengthened regional development planning and implementation. The development of the Lautem Cultural Alliance and the Lautem Cultural Development Plan contributes to the creation of opportunities for local democratic participation by all citizens and establishing more effective, efficient and equitable public service delivery to support the nation’s social and economic development. It does this by bringing government, civil society and community together to plan for and allocate resources to the delivery of cultural services.  Thorough this initiative, the Lautem Cultural Alliance actively contributes to Timor-Leste meeting its obligations under the Convention on the Protection and Promotion of the Diversity of Cultural Expressions, to which Timor-Leste is a signatory and which both government and civil society have a role to play in implementing.
Results: A survey of community cultural, public administration and CSO leaders, as well as cultural practitioners and young people in Lautem municipality was conducted to guage their a) understandings and perspectives regarding the protection and promotion of the diversity of cultural expressions in Timor-Leste, and b) interest and support for the creation of Lautem Cultural Alliance. A total of 63 people were interviewed. The results revealed high levels of community support for the creation of Lautem Cultural Alliance. The respondents believed that there is benefit in supporting and being involved in the Lautem Cultural Alliance and receiving training on cultural development planning. The Lautem community and its local government agreed to support and be part of Lautem Cultural Alliance and develop a strategic plan for culture in the Lautem municipality. From the respondents who wanted to be part of the Alliance, Working Groups have been formed to supervise the creation of the Lautem Cultural Alliance Constitution and development of a Cultural Development Plan for Lautem. The Constitution has been drafted and work is under way to understand the process and prepare the necessary paperwork for the Alliance to be legally registered. The Cultural Development Plan is in the final drafting phase after workshops in cultural development planning with the participants and other community members were delivered. This Plan will be used in the creation of an MoU with the government to implement the Plan. A Steering Committee comprising high-level national and local government officials has also been formed to provide advice and other support in the formation of the Lautem Cultural Alliance and in the development of an MoU with the Government of Timor-Leste.  The national media has been very supportive in providing coverage of this initiative, including of meetings with the President of Timor-Leste.

Main Feature: As part of the State institutions' efforts to monitor and implement decisions aimed at enhancing gender equality in various fields of life and work, a national committee called the “National Committee for Women, Children, the Elderly, and Persons with Disabilities” was established by Council Resolution No. (26) of 2019 dated (16/09/2019), as amended by Council Resolution No. (16) of 2023 (Annex No 29) This committee is chaired by the Minister of Social Development and Family and includes representatives from various ministries, Qatar University, the National Human Rights Committee, the Qatar Foundation for Social Work, and the Qatar Foundation for Education, Science, and Community Development.  The committee aims to protect and promote the rights of women, children, the elderly, and persons with disabilities. Among its key responsibilities and tasks related to the Convention on the Protection and Promotion of the Diversity of Cultural Expressions are the following: -	Monitoring the status of women's rights, -	Proposing necessary measures to enhance and follow up on the achievement of objectives stated in international conventions and treaties related to women's rights, which the State has joined, and recommending the State's accession to other relevant conventions and treaties. This means that achieving the goals of the Convention on the Protection and Promotion of the Diversity of Cultural Expressions concerning gender equality falls within its scope of work. -	Studying legislation related to women and proposing amendments to align them with international conventions the State has joined. -	Contributing to the preparation of national reports to be submitted by the State to international bodies and organizations concerned with women's rights, regarding conventions the state has joined, including the Convention on the Protection and Promotion of the Diversity of Cultural Expressions. To further emphasize, the same resolution stipulates that when preparing legislative tools related to women, the competent authorities should coordinate with the committee to assess the compliance of these legislative tools with the provisions of international conventions to which the state is a party and to express their views on them.

Title EN: Fortalecimiento de jóvenes a través de la música
Goal: Integrate Culture In Sustainable Development Frameworks
SDG: SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: National sustainable development policies and plans
Agency Implementation: Estudio Urbano (Directorate General of Music, Ministry of Culture, Government of the City of Buenos Aires)
Main Feature: The program seeks to strengthen the capacities of young residents in vulnerable neighborhoods of the City of Buenos Aires to develop themselves through music, and offers training to promote access to the labor market through the trades that are part of the music industry.
Results: Musical projects from popular neighborhoods of the City of Buenos Aires have access to a professional recording, receive training in project management and dissemination of their work. Beneficiaries: 30  Target population receives training in trades and tools required by the music industry. Beneficiaries: 195
Recommandations: 1. Musical projects from working class neighborhoods in the City of Buenos Aires have access to a professional recording, receive training in project management and dissemination of their work.  The people interviewed agree in valuing the constant accompaniment of Estudio Urbano, their suggestions and dedication. They say that the project helped considerably to professionalize their career, to strengthen the band, giving it sequentiality and continuity. They take with them as tools the technical knowledge of each workshop, the network of contacts generated, the possibility of creating and doing with other artists, having clear objectives. Also, some "soft skills" can be highlighted as they say that the project restored their confidence, restored their identity as artists and made them grow in personal t e r m s . Related to the technical side, some highlight their learning in song writing - "with a more poetic language"-; learning how to break down a video clip with its scenes and shots; learning about photography, production and developing coordination skills.  On the other hand, it was also important to survey the criticisms and contributions made by the bands/soloists, thinking about the future development of the program. Among the arguments developed, we highlight that some indicated that the workshops were too general and long because all the bands participated and, in this sense, they proposed more personalized instances. Others felt that the workshops were too demanding, especially considering that many participants were teenagers finishing high school. In this regard, a closer accompaniment is suggested, such as through the deepening of tutoring spaces. If necessary, explain the main conclusions and recommendations that emerged from this evaluation, as well as the challenges encountered.   2. Target population receives training in trades and tools required by the music industry.  A survey was also carried out on the participants' evaluations of the different aspects of their time at Estudio Urbano. A first reading shows that the evaluation was positive insofar as the expectations and objectives previously mentioned were met. In this sense, it was specifically highlighted how the participants gave a positive feedback on the impact it had on the development of skills and professional training. It is worth mentioning that, in the perceptions of the participants, the training had little or no impact when it came to getting a job, although it is necessary to clarify that the survey was carried out as soon as the training was completed and it would be pertinent to ask this same question after a longer period of time had elapsed. We also identified a very positive overall assessment of the courses and the numbers that reflect this perception follow the same trend when focusing on the contents, the course modality, the teaching performance and the organization.  Finally, it has been identified that the training correlates with significant changes in some key identificators, which gives a guideline of the impact that participating in Estudio Urbano has on the trajectories of the subjects. Thus, when comparing the initial situation - before starting the courses - with the final one - once they are finished - we see that the number of students who have jobs related to music increases, as well as the number of people who get paid for their jobs related to music. At this point we observe a notable gender inequality, as men have greater access to jobs and remuneration than women. Although this phenomenon is not exclusive to the field analyzed, but is transversal to the entire labor market, a greater disparity can be seen, which is an invitation to design strategies from the institution that translate into corrective policies.  However, one fact that emerges from the study is that the scholarship policy does not follow a progressive criterion in economic-distributive terms, but rather is identifies a notable mismatch between the scholarships requested and those granted if they are discriminated by income. Thus, the training of individuals who, presumably, do not need this economic aid is funded, while the training of other individuals who, presumably, would not be able to access the training without it, is not funded. This point marks an important dimension to consider w h e n evaluating the institution's scholarship policy.  In short, the data from this evaluation show a positive and significant impact in terms of professional training and the trajectories of the subjects who participate in the Urban Study courses. It also provides a series of elements to be taken into account for the design of future actions, with special emphasis on the training modality, inclusion and gender policies.

Le Forum sur l’économie culturelle est un ensemble d’événements culturels et économiques, soit l’aboutissement de vingt-deux (22) séances de travail tenues pendant trois (03) mois ayant réuni l’ensemble des acteurs intervenants en matière de culture et autres partenaires économiques, et la participation de vingt (20) départements ministériels. Recommandations: Les principales recommandations du forum consistent en : •	L’encouragement de l’entrepreneuriat et la création de startups dans le but de contribuer à des idées généreuses qui créent le spectacle et appellent à la justice, à l’égalité et à toutes les valeurs humaines et nobles ; •	L’intégration de programmes de formation spécialisée impliquant une vision économique du produit culturel ; •	La facilitation de l’accès aux moyens et aux assiettes foncières pour la création d’entreprises artistiques, et l’allègement fiscal et douanier au profit des entreprises d’investissement culturel émergentes ; •	La mise en place d’une stratégie globale pour promouvoir la production culturelle par, entre autres, l’intégration  du théâtre en milieu scolaire et la création de villes dédiées à la production cinématographique, d’ateliers pour les professions associées à la production cinématographique et théâtrale, et la mise en place de formations continues et spécialisées dans les professions associées à la production culturelle (son, image, numérisation, design numérique, effets, déco, costumes, etc.) ; •	La sollicitation des banques à l’effet d’accompagner les projets proposés par les startups et les financer sur la base de prêts bancaires selon des ratios et/ou à titre de contribution ; •	La mise à disposition d’espaces vacants ou à réaffecter, au profit des artistes visuels à l’effet de leur permettre la création artistique ; •	La création de studios de tournage dans les villes du sud ; •	La réactualisation de tous les accords conclus avec les Ministères de l’Éducation et du Tourisme.

Title EN: Frauen*-Literatursymposium 2022 – Symposium Femmes dans le milieu littéraire
Goal: Promote Human Rights And Fundamental Freedoms
SDG: SDG 5 - Achieve gender equality and empower all women and girls,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels
Area of Monitoring: Gender equality
Agency Implementation: AdS
Main Feature: L'A*dS (Association Autrices et auteurs de Suisse) a organisé un symposium de deux jours, les 18 et 19 juin 2022, au Centre Paul Klee à Berne, sur la question des femmes dans le milieu littéraire. En effet, les femmes sont toujours désavantagées en termes de visibilité, de reconnaissance, de pertinence et d'influence, ce qui se répercute à tous les niveaux depuis les canons littéraires à la rémunération des écrivains féminins. Au cours de ces deux journées, des autrices, des organisatrices, des journalistes, des éditrices ainsi que des expertes de la recherche et de la promotion littéraire des quatre régions linguistiques de Suisse se sont penchées avec les participantes sur les questions spécifiques des discriminations des femmes dans le monde littéraire : autopromotion, travail de care, honoraires, structures de pouvoir ou l'image (hétéronormative) de la femme dans la littérature. L'industrie littéraire est issue de structures patriarcales, ce qui fait que les femmes sont encore aujourd'hui structurellement désavantagées, notamment au niveau des honoraires, des rubriques, de la promotion, des prix et des canons littéraires ; du point de vue d’un plan de la carrière, il est également préférable de faire une thèse sur Franz Kafka plutôt que sur Erika Burkart, par exemple. Les réseaux, la transparence et les statistiques permettent de lutter contre ces structures patriarcales : « Comblez le fossé des données. Comptez les femmes sur les podiums, dans les jurys, dans les bourses, dans les critiques, en tant qu'expertes interrogées dans les journaux, dans les canons de lecture des manuels scolaires, en tant que personnes agissant dans des œuvres textuelles ou cinématographiques, comptez également combien d'argent les femmes reçoivent pour la même prestation (lecture, participation à un panel, animation, etc.) par rapport aux hommes, etc. »  Le premier jour a été marqué par quatre exposés d’ouverture, sont intervenues Nina George, présidente du Conseil européen des écrivains, Nicole Pfister Fetz, Secrétaire générale de l’A*dS, l'autrice Pascale Kramer qui a rappelé que « pour le Prix Goncourt, le prix littéraire le plus renommé en France, le jury est composé de trois femmes et de dix hommes et que seules deux femmes ont été récompensées au cours des dix dernières années », ainsi que l’éditrice Dana Grigorcea.  Le samedi était placé sous le signe de l'état des lieux dans les différents domaines de l'exploitation, au-delà des frontières linguistiques. Cinq tables rondes ont permis de débattre et de discuter en deux temps : 1.	critique littéraire, formation, recherche : avec Martina Läubli (journaliste culturelle Bücher am Sonntag, NZZ am Sonntag) et Sabine Haupt (Professeure en littérature à l'Université de Fribourg et écrivaine) 2.	théâtre : avec Julia Reichert (co-directrice du Theater Neumarkt) et Anne-Christine Liske (directrice du far° Nyon) 3.	librairie et maisons d'édition : avec Lucia Lanz (lectorat/relations publiques, Lenos Verlag) et Noémi Schaub (éditrice, Paulette éditrice) 4.	promotion de la littérature : avec Christine Chenaux (Office fédéral de la culture, secrétariat du jury des Prix suisses de littérature) et Reina Gehrig (responsable du département Littérature, ProHelvetia) 5.	manifestations : avec Flurina Badel (autrice, artiste et organisatrice) et Marguerite Meyer (journaliste, animatrice, poetry slammer).  Des questions et des thèmes dans tous les domaines ont été regroupés en vue d’établir une liste de revendications répartie en dix ateliers pour le deuxième jour. Le samedi soir a eu lieu la lecture publique, polyphonique et multilingue, « Panorama ! » avec Zaher Al Jamous, Carin Caduff, Laura di Corcia, Friederike Kretzen, Dragica Rajčić et X Schneeberger.
Results: Ce symposium de deux jours a permis d’établir une liste de discriminations entre les autrices et les auteurs et de proposer, en réponse, une liste de revendications réparties en dix domaines : quotas, rapports de pouvoir, #metoo, modérations/interviews, attentes, travail de care, honoraires, canon littéraire, réseaux, organisation d’un symposium mettant en avant les angles morts. Cette dernière revendication est en voie d’aboutir. Un deuxième symposium est en préparation sous le titre de Féminisme, intersections & littérature est en préparation « Car la littérature est plus qu’un divertissement ou un secteur économique ; la littérature est un art – et un outil politique. Un instrument qui permet de dénoncer et dépasser les représentations ». Féminisme, intersections & littérature se concentrera sur deux questions : comment surmonter le sexisme et la cishétéronormativité du milieu littéraire ? Et qui sont les invisibilisées et les indésirables en littérature ? Le symposium est prévu les 7 et 8 juin 2024 à Bâle.

Agency Implementation: National Culture Fund (Ministry of Culture)
Main Feature: IFACCA is the global network of arts councils under the ministries of culture and governmental organizations in support of arts and culture, with nearly 70 member states, including the Republic of Bulgaria, represented by the National Culture Fund, with a mission to create and promote international dialogue and exchange in a spirit of solidarity, inclusion, reciprocity and mutual learning. The Ninth Summit pays special attention to the rebuilding of the Culture Sector on a local level, given the last three difficult years for artists and art operators.
Results: Procedures and long-term strategies have been developed and presented to the global public for adaptation in the post-covid environment, restoring, redefining and reforming public support for the arts and culture towards sustainability and security, integrating the Culture Sector into the expanded perimeter of social activities, creating international preconditions for affirming the ubiquitous opportunity for all people to participate in cultural life and thus creating sustainability for the cultural and creative sector in society. The Stockholm meeting is taking place under the motto ‘Safeguarding Creative Freedom’, recognized by and under the protection of international law as ‘the freedom to imagine, create and disseminate diverse forms of cultural expression without censorship by the state, political interference or pressure from non-state actors’ (UNESCO Report 2019). The National Culture Fund (Bulgaria), is actively involved in the work of the world organization, and the Federation, for its part, offers know-how for the development of structures for the expenditure of public funds mainly in Europe through mechanisms of self-management and distribution through de facto decentralization of funds. As a result of the participation of the Bulgarian delegation in the Stockholm Forum, sustainable relationships have been established and are being further developed in a bilateral project between the National Culture Fund and the Arts Council of Norway (Arts and Culture Norway) with the support of the Ministry of Culture and the Sofia Municipality towards integration and exchange of experience in the challenging environment of the development of the Culture Sector. The project activities start in January 2024.  Parallel to these relationships, the National Culture Fund is establishing a working cooperation between the National Culture Fund and Cultur|LX, the Council for Culture of the Grand Duchy of Luxembourg, in January 2023 and a follow-up workshop in May 2023 of the two funding institutions on programmes of financial support for the cultural sector, focus and objectives, evaluation of project proposals and the possibility of exchange between Bulgaria and Luxembourg. Problematic aspects of the work in the two cultural institutions are discussed, as well as strategies for the effective and efficient spending of the increasing cultural budget in both countries, including the Recovery and Sustainability Plan. Specific steps towards the interaction between the National Culture Fund and its Luxembourg counterpart to develop a unified strategy for the development of independent culture and arts operators at pan-European level are also discussed. The need for dialogue in an international context is linked to the growing interest in the National Culture Fund and its importance for Bulgarian culture. And as one of the main cultural funding institutions in Bulgaria, the National Culture Fund has the responsibility to carry out its activities in the relevance of the times and with a mission to promote and preserve cultural diversity and development, while not relenting in its efforts to consolidate Bulgaria's rightful place in the European family of cultural values and high creative potential.

Title EN: Fund for the Development Cooperation and Humanitarian Aid (since 2022)
Goal: Integrate Culture In Sustainable Development Frameworks
SDG: SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: National sustainable development policies and plans
Agency Implementation: The work of the Fund's Governing Board is organised by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Lithuania. The Central Project Management Agency (CPMA) acts as the administrator and secretariat of the Fund.
Main Feature: Lithuania's development cooperation policy aims to achieve the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals by 2030, to ensure peace, promote economic growth and social stability in the world, reduce disparities between developed and developing countries and integrate developing countries into the global economy.  In order to ensure the proper implementation of the Law on Development Cooperation and Humanitarian Aid of the Republic of Lithuania https://e-seimas.lrs.lt/portal/legalAct/lt/TAD/TAIS.449238/asr, the Strategic Directions for Development Cooperation for the period 2022-2025 were approved by the Order of the Minister of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Lithuania of 27 December 2021( https://ltaid.urm.lt/en/doclib/wzul6ssdrk9j49dd6gpbx1rggnft8nu8).   In 2022 a systematic reform of development cooperation policy took place in Lithuania, which led to the establishment of the Fund for the Development Cooperation and Humanitarian Aid (henceforth, the Fund).    The Fund aims to support the implementation of a flexible, responsive and results-oriented development cooperation policy and to empower Lithuanian public and private sector institutions to implement large-scale, high added-value projects in partner countries.  The decision on the allocation of the Fund's financing is taken by the Governing Board, in accordance with the Description of Activities of the Fund, approved by Order No V-197 of the Minister of Foreign Affairs of 9 June 2022 (https://e-seimas.lrs.lt/portal/legalAct/lt/TAD/95ebb451e7b211ec896de0b71e988500). By the decision of the Fund’s Governing Board, funding is allocated to projects and programmes in 3 possible ways:  1. Through a competitive process. The Central Project Management Agency (CPMA) is responsible for preparing the documentation for calls for applications. Ministry of Foreign Affairs is responsible for preparation of the concepts. 2. Direct funding projects or programmes. 3. Co-financing of programmes or projects financed by international donors. The natural or legal person submits the request for co-financing directly to the Board (via CPMA). If the Board decides to allocate the funding, CPMA concludes the agreement.  The Fund's Governing Board is composed of 7 members delegated by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, the Ministry of Finance, the Central Project Management Agency, the Lithuanian Information and Communication Technology Association "Infobalt", the Association of Lithuanian Municipalities, and non-governmental organisations active in the field of development cooperation.   The Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Lithuania, in accordance with the Strategic Guidelines for Development Cooperation, prepares concepts for the consideration of the Fund's Board, which are included in the Call for Proposals.  Applications for national co-financing for the implementation of a programme or project financed by international donors can be submitted to the Fund‘s Governing Board directly through the Fund secretariat – CPMA. Among the priority themes of the Fund from 2022 to 2024 were 1. Resilience of the public to disinformation and prevention of hybrid threats; 2. strengthening national and regional media capabilities; 3. spreading democratic ideas through the empowerment of independent media.
Results: Projects to be mentioned that have been implemented or continued to be implemented in the areas: democracy, civil society, media  Year 2022 (11 concepts in total): Concept 5 "Supporting the development of Belarusian citizenship"  Project "Belarusian independent cinema: revival" (cooperation area: democracy and civil society). For more detail: https://ltaid.urm.lt/projektai/zemelapis/85/baltarusija-17;  Concept 8 "Strengthening resistance to disinformation in the Eastern Partnership countries of the European Union, with a special focus on independent media"  Project "Challenges of modern disinformation in the face of occupation" (cooperation area: Democracy and civil society, Media, Multilateral projects). Countries: Armenia, Azerbaijan, Belarus, Moldova, Sakartvelo, Ukraine. Project manager – Delfi UAB. Duration: 2022 – 2025. Allocated funding – approx. USD 99187 (EUR 88 607). For more detail: https://cpva.lt/programa/lietuvos-vystomojo-bendradarbiavimo-ir-humanitarines-pagalbos-fondas/veiklos-sritys or https://ltaid.urm.lt/projektai/zemelapis/85  Project "Challenges of modern disinformation in the face of occupation" Project objective – to train the media in Ukraine, Georgia and Armenia and the wider public to choose reliable sources and create truthful narratives, to identify and counter disinformation. Project manager – Civic Resilience Initiative. Countries: Armenia, Sakartvelo, Ukraine. Duration: 2022 – 2024. Allocated funding: approx. USD 66 703 (EUR 59 589).  Year 2023 (9 concepts in total): Concept 8 "Strengthening Strategic Communication in Moldova"  Project "Strengthening strategic communication to counter Russian disinformation in Moldova” (cooperation area: Democracy and civil society). Periodic Subsidy refers to the financial allocation disbursed to selected cultural public benefit associations. Its purpose is to contribute towards covering a portion of their operational expenses to facilitate them achieving their objectives. Disbursement Frequency: The subsidy is disbursed once annually to each eligible beneficiary. Objective: To ensure the sustained operations of eligible associations in the cultural landscape, with the minimum expected level of activities and events. The value of the periodic subsidy ranges from AED 20,000 to AED 100,000. Programme and Projects Subsidy is disbursed once a year to cultural public benefit associations, either individually or collectively, for a specific cultural programme or project presented to secure financial support from the Ministry. Disbursement Frequency: The subsidy is disbursed once annually to each eligible beneficiary, with the right to apply for only one project subsidy once a year. Objective: To motivate and encourage deserving cultural public benefit associations to execute more effective and impactful programmes benefiting their respective segments. The maximum subsidy for programs and projects is AED 200,000.
Results: Funding for cultural public benefit associations from the UAE Ministry of Culture is anticipated to yield several key results that will significantly impact the cultural and creative landscape of the country. Firstly, increased financial support is expected to enhance the capacity of these associations to execute high-quality projects, such as cultural festivals, art exhibitions, and heritage conservation programs. This, in turn, will help to enrich the cultural experiences available to the public and promote greater appreciation of the UAE�s diverse heritage. Secondly, funding will enable these associations to expand their outreach and impact, allowing them to engage more effectively with different communities and foster cultural participation across various demographics. It will also support the development of new programs and initiatives that address emerging cultural needs and interests. Additionally, by providing financial resources, the Ministry aims to strengthen the sustainability of these associations, ensuring that they can continue to operate and contribute to the cultural sector over the long term. This support is likely to result in enhanced organizational capacity, including improved infrastructure and administrative capabilities. Lastly, the funding is expected to drive innovation and creativity within the cultural sector, as associations can invest in new technologies, artistic practices, and collaborative projects. Overall, these results will contribute to a more vibrant, inclusive, and dynamic cultural environment in the UAE.

Title EN: Funding Programme Klimafitte Kulturbetriebe (“Investment fund for climate- friendly cultural businesses”)
Goal: Integrate Culture In Sustainable Development Frameworks
SDG: SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: National sustainable development policies and plans
Agency Implementation: Federal Ministry for Arts, Culture, the Civil Service and Sport; Climate and Energy Fund Austria
Main Feature: The arts and culture sector is increasingly concerned with ecological change and the need for environmental action. On the one hand, there is a growing awareness of social responsibility at institutional level. On the other hand, institutions also expect cost savings in the medium to long term by optimising energy efficiency and recycling management.  Transformation and innovation towards climate neutrality involve considerable investment and often cannot be financed by the cultural institutions themselves. The Ministry for Arts, Culture, the Civil Service and Sport has therefore provided incentives for green investments in the cultural sector with EUR 15 million from the European Union's Recovery and Resilience Facility - NextGenerationEU.  The aim is to promote sustainability and, in particular, to contribute to achieving the environmental and climate protection targets of the European Green Deal and the Austrian Energy and Climate Plan. In particular, investments to reduce CO2 emissions were supported, which are being implemented as part of a comprehensive sustainability concept:  - Climate-friendly heating, ventilation and cooling systems - Use of renewable energy sources - Energy-efficient interior and exterior lighting - Thermal refurbishment of buildings - Measures to save natural resources and CO2 emissions  The programme ran two calls for proposals in 2022 and 2023, with around 125 projects receiving funding and the available budget (EUR 15,000,000) being fully utilised.
Results: Around 125 initiatives were supported with the available budget. These range from small associations in rural areas to large cultural institutions run by the federal and state governments. The individual projects are equally diverse, ranging from the installation of photovoltaic systems, the replacement of heating systems and the construction of green roofs and facades to the widespread use of LED lighting. By implementing these measures, the supported institutions make a tangible contribution to reducing CO2 emissions and annual energy consumption, as well as to generating renewable energy.
Recommandations: Ongoing evaluation

Title EN: Future Vision Minimum Standards – first social partners’ recommendation for independent cultural work in Austria // Zukunftstraum Mindeststandards – erste Sozialpartnerempfehlung für freie Kulturarbeit in Österreich
Goal: Promote Human Rights And Fundamental Freedoms
SDG: SDG 5 - Achieve gender equality and empower all women and girls,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels
Area of Monitoring: Artistic freedom
Cultural Domain: Design,Performing Arts,Media Arts,Cinema and Audiovisual Arts,Music,Publishing,Visual Arts
Agency Implementation: IG Kultur Österreich, GPA Union
Main Feature: While 98 per cent of employees in Austria are covered by collective agreements that ensure minimum wages and other essential labour law provisions (such as arrangements regarding pay, flexible working hours and the termination of the employment relationship, etc.), there is still no collective protection for workers/employees in the independent cultural sector. The consequences are precariousness, the risk of poverty and a lack of social security and pension prospects for many cultural workers. Therefore, GPA Union and IG Kultur Österreich started a cooperation in 2023 to jointly improve working conditions in the independent cultural sector. The result of this cooperation is the first recommendation by the Austrian social partners for the independent cultural sector in Austria. The recommendation defines standards for the remuneration of employees (fair pay), creates a common frame of reference for working conditions in the sector and provides transparency and legal certainty through the clarification of labour law provisions. For the first time, the social partners have agreed on defining goals for improving working conditions for employees in the independent cultural sector. However, due to the precarious economic situation of many cultural institutions (employers), the practical implementation of the suggested improvements is a challenge. The social partners' recommendation is thus accompanied by two further measures: Firstly, in the framework of the Austrian Fair Pay Process, efforts to consider fair pay in the evaluation of funding applications need to be continued, without restricting the diversity of cultural offerings. Secondly, IG Kultur Österreich has developed the Kultur recht praktisch (“culture – law – practice) project that aims at capacity building for cultural initiatives as employers, providing them with tools (e.g. model contracts, training programmes on practical legal questions) and supporting them in their daily work.

Title EN: GEAR UP: Gender Equity in Audio Recording and Music Production, Manitoba Taskforce
Goal: Promote Human Rights And Fundamental Freedoms
SDG: SDG 5 - Achieve gender equality and empower all women and girls,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels
Area of Monitoring: Gender equality
Agency Implementation: Manitoba Film and Music
Main Feature: "In response to the need for improved representation and inclusivity in the local audio recording and music production sector, Manitoba Film & Music and Manitoba Music partnered to establish a taskforce. The main purpose of this collaboration was to evaluate the current state of gender equity and inclusivity in the industry and gather recommendations for necessary enhancements.  The Gender Equity in Audio Recording and Music Production Manitoba Taskforce (GEAR UP) was established in 2022 to address the needs in Gender Inequity in Audio Production in Manitoba for women and gender diverse people working in audio recording and music production in Manitoba.  The taskforce dedicated to the recording and production communities in Manitoba consists of eight members who identify as women or gender diverse. It is designed to represent the diverse voices within the community, including Black, indigenous, and people of color (BIPOC). The taskforce comprises individuals with a range of skills, genres, and experience, including artists, songwriters, beat-makers, business owners, freelance workers, educators, as well as experienced producers and audio engineers. Their primary focus is to engage in discussions and offer guidance and recommendations on matters of equity, discrimination, oppression, bias, and harassment that impact women and gender diverse individuals in the industry."
Results: "In a study cited in the GEAR UP report titled, “Inclusion in the Recording Studio?” which examines the representation of women and underrepresented racial/ethnic groups in the music industry, the University of Southern California Annenberg Inclusion Initiative found that women are still underrepresented in the music industry, with only 22.4% of artists, 12.6% of songwriters, and 2.1% of producers being female. The study also found that underrepresented racial/ethnic groups are also underrepresented in the music industry, with only 7.4% of artists, 6.2% of songwriters, and 3.1% of producers being from underrepresented racial/ethnic groups (Annenberg Inclusion Initiative’s annual report on popular music reveals little progress for women | USC Annenberg School for Communication and Journalism).  The GEAR UP Manitoba Taskforce conducted an assessment to identify the challenges and barriers encountered by women and gender diverse individuals in the audio production and recording field. The assessment also highlighted the strengths and opportunities available to address the underrepresentation of these groups. The identified challenges include pay disparity, issues related to funders and finances, lack of educational support, limited representation in music sector awards and arts service organizations, and a scarcity of women and gender diverse individuals working in studios. The GEAR UP Manitoba Taskforce provided ways to address gender oppression in audio recording and production to ensure safer, respectful, and increased participation of women and gender diverse producers and engineers such as: • Increase opportunity and representation throughout the sector • Ensure equitable remuneration • Ensure women and gender diverse people are credited for their work • Increase opportunities for connection • Enhance current educational spaces and opportunities • Improve recording studio working conditions • Affordable means of accessing equipment • Commit to ongoing research and data collection • Create supports for survivors of sexual assault and harassment  The recommendations form the basis of the taskforce’s ongoing work, re-evaluation, and future recommendations. The taskforce sponsors will keep track of the progress in the audio recording and production sector in Manitoba, both new and ongoing, and update the successes, achievements, and challenges in the sector to promote the progress of women and gender diverse people. Manitoba Film & Music and Manitoba Music are dedicated to embracing the recommendations put forth by the taskforce, disseminating them within the community, and making efforts to integrate them into their own policies and programming."

Title EN: Tartu UNESCO City of Literature residencies
Goal: Achieve A Balanced Flow Of Cultural Goods And Services And Increase The Mobility Of Artists And Cultural Professionals
SDG: SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 10 - Reduce inequality within and among countries,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Mobility of artists and cultural professionals
Agency Implementation: Estonian Literary Society
Main Feature: During the recent years, residency programmes for writers and translators have been a rapidly evolving aspect of Tartu City of Literature. In 2017, the Estonian Literary Society as the coordinator and official Focal Point for Tartu UNESCO City of Literature launched its first residency for writers and translators of Estonian Literature. Under the title Tartu UNESCO City of Literature International Residency Programmme for Writers and Translators seven writers with different cultural backgrounds have been hosted as a result of global calls for applications: Andrej Tomažin (Slovenia), Darran Anderson (Ireland), Gabi Csutak (Hungary),  Ron Whitehead (USA), Andy Willoughby (UK), Olena Huseinova (Ukraine), and Christiane Vadnais (Canada).  The global pandemic naturally had an effect on the program and there was a pause in hosting residents during 2020-2022, yet at the same time further developments in the strategic planning took place and in addition to the main residency program, other activities and projects related to supporting the mobility of writers took place. During 2020-2022 a writers exchange program with Norwich UNESCO City of Literature took place: the late Estonian novelist and poet Vahur Afanasjev stayed in Norwich in March 2020; and novelist and poet Penny Boxall went to Tartu in August 2022. In 2022, the Estonian Creative Residencies Network was established, with the Estonian Literary Society as one of the 11 founding members. In 2023, 8 members of LOORE launched a residency program (the project is funded by the Nordic Culture Point) for Ukrainian artists, during which Tartu City of Literature hosted the Ukrainian poet Sophia Lenartovyh. In the same year a recidency designed exclusively for the translators of Estonian literature was organised as a result of which, the Hungarian translator Mónika Segesdi spent a month in residency in Tartu. In 2023, a regional residency project was also launhched - funded by the Nordic Culture Point, Tartu City of Literature Nordic-Baltic residency includes five 2-month residencies during 2023-2025 for writers connected to Cities of Literature in the Nordic and Baltic countries.   Our residency programs aim to enhance international exchange and communication, diversify the local literary scene, and allow local readers, writers, and cultural organisers to become acquainted with new foreign authors and their works. Our goal is to create a nurturing and inspiring environment where writers can focus on their work and generate fresh creative ideas. These programs also enable writers to introduce their work to Estonian readers. Additionally, we seek to establish enduring connections, fostering a willingness for future collaborations beyond the residency period.   In addition to the abovementioned residencies, a special project took place in the recent years, connecting residencies with transversal collaboration between writers and artists of other fields. As part of Tartu International Literature festival Prima Vista, the largest international project undertaken by Tartu City of Literature so far, "Bring Your Own Utopia," was prepared during the years 2022-2024, the results were shown at Prima Vista 2024 Futures Better and Worse. Five UNESCO Cities of Literature - Heidelberg, Lviv, Manchester, Norwich, and Reykjavik - each found a writer willing to dive into the unknown: coming to a residency in Tartu and working here with a local creator so that by the time of the festival, a completely new work could emerge from this collaboration, embodying utopian or dystopian themes in one way or another. The project was also part of the main program of European Capital of Culture Tartu 2024. The results of the project included an installation titled "Once was mire. Siin oli soo" by Norwich poet Penny Boxall,Estonian writer Maarja Pärtna, and musician and (sound) artist Liis Ring; a verbal and musical city walk  titled “Walk through the times of you, me and us” led by Heidelberg writer Anne Richter and Estonian musician Argo Vals; an installation called “Crossing” attached to a traffic light in the city centre, created by. Ásta Fanney Sigurðardóttir, a poet, visual artist, and musician from Reykjavik and Estonian artist Timo Toots; an installation called "Safe Place" by the poet and video artist Olga Povoroznyk from Lviv and Estonian artist Eike Eplik, and a storytelling event "The Forest of Ink and Skin" created by Manchester writer David Hartley and the  interdisciplinary Estonian artist Henri Hütt.
Results: The residencies have resulted in deepened understanding of the literary heritage and contemporary cultural scene of the cultures the residents have represented and at the same time the programme has increased awareness about the Estonian culture and literary heritage and enhanced further interest in it. Personal connections between the residents and the local creatives have been an important aspect of the residencies and several writers who have participated in the programme have developed further collaborations with writers and cultural managers of Tartu. The Bring Your Own Utopia experiment attracted the attention of both local and international audiences and demonstrated the strong creative impact of collaborative residencies and the potential of of possible further projects of the kind.

Main Feature: As part of the implementation of the Future of Media Commission’s recommendations, the State’s new media regulator, Coimisiún na Meán (CnaM) are developing a Gender, Equality, Diversity and Inclusion strategy for the media sector. This is reflective of the fact that the media sector plays a key role in shaping public opinion and culture and therefore has an obligation to ensure that it is representative and inclusive – both in the content it produces, but also within the sector itself.  The strategy will seek to implement EDI monitoring, data and research, to ensure all Public Service Media and Public Service Content Providers play a role and are accountable for implementing same. Coimisiún na Meán will be responsible for co-ordinating these activities.  Following the publication of the strategy the following actions will commence: • Coimisiún na Meán will focus on developing and resourcing an in-house strategic research unit focused on EDI matters including gender equality, and will review funding scheme criteria with a view to the potential inclusion of appropriate standards/criteria to ensure the collection of consistent and comparable EDI data; • Coimisiún na Meán to develop data standards metrics to be aligned with the National Equality Data Strategy, to ensure to collection and publication of consistent and comparable baseline EDI data by PSMs and PSCPs; • Following publication of the GEDI strategy Coimisiún na Meán will carry out stakeholder consultation via the Stakeholder Consultation Group to examine the feasibility of diversity boards across the sector, and will research to examine current status of diversity strategies within the media sector.

Title EN: Georgian Women Composers Web Portal
Goal: Promote Human Rights And Fundamental Freedoms
SDG: SDG 5 - Achieve gender equality and empower all women and girls,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels
Area of Monitoring: Gender equality
Agency Implementation: NNLE Acoustics 2023
Main Feature: The primary goal of the initiative is to highlight and promote the contributions of female composers from Georgia in the professional and academic music field. In accordance with the project guidelines, each phase will focus on a composer from each decade, totaling ten composers. The selection process is based on a comprehensive evaluation of historical records, musical accomplishments, and cultural significance.  The contributions and achievements of Georgian female composers remain largely unrecognized, as many operated in obscurity with their names scarcely acknowledged. However, this platform will contribute to greater recognition for this integral facet of Georgian culture: Georgian women composers and their works.  The content featured on the portal is designed to be a valuable educational resource for research, classroom discussions, and as supplementary material in music textbooks. Additionally, the availability of digital sheet music pieces will enhance the performance of musical compositions, infusing them with vitality during live presentations.
Results: The first phase of the project was implemented in 2022. It faced challenges due to the limited availability of information on female composers, including scarce archival resources, language barriers, and the need for extensive cross-referencing to ensure accuracy. However, even the discovery of minute details during the research process, which proved significant, underscored the importance of the project's team mission. The project also utilized related materials such as photos, theatre history, documentaries, radio and TV archives, and press.    The project team is constantly working on the project. To promote it, they use various media to inform the public. The team also organizes presentation events on the project's website for each stage of the project, where live musical performances play an important role.   As of June 2024, the web portal features comprehensive data on 30 female composers, offering detailed and easily accessible information about each composer's body of work.
