Title EN: Golden Visa and Artistic Freedom
Goal: Achieve A Balanced Flow Of Cultural Goods And Services And Increase The Mobility Of Artists And Cultural Professionals
SDG: SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 10 - Reduce inequality within and among countries,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Mobility of artists and cultural professionals
Cultural Domain: Design,Performing Arts,Media Arts,Cinema and Audiovisual Arts,Music,Publishing,Visual Arts
Agency Implementation: UAE Cabinet; Emirates Science Council; Ministry of Economy; Ministry of Culture
Main Feature: In 2018, the UAE issued the Golden Visa, which is a new system for granting 10-year residence visa to researchers in the fields of science and knowledge and those with specialized talents such as doctors, specialists, scientists, inventors, as well as creative individuals in the field of culture and arts. The visa extends to the spouse and children of the recipient and can be renewed after 10 years. The new system allows the UAE to attract top talents and creatives in the cultural sector and to contribute to the development of a vibrant creative sector. This allows recipients flexibility, as their residence in the UAE is no longer tied to their employment with an organization and gives them the stability to be able to innovate in the UAE.
Results: The UAE's Golden Visa program, introduced in 2019, has significantly impacted artist mobility in the region. This long-term residency visa offers a 10-year renewable residency to investors, entrepreneurs, and skilled professionals, including artists. Since its implementation, the Golden Visa has attracted a diverse range of global talents to the UAE. This influx has led to an increase in the number of international artists participating in UAE-based exhibitions, festivals, and cultural events. Furthermore, the program has enhanced the UAE's cultural landscape, fostering a vibrant arts scene and boosting the local creative economy by providing artists with long-term stability and opportunities for collaboration.
Recommandations: The introduction of the Golden Visa for artists in the UAE has had a profound impact on the country's cultural landscape. By attracting a diverse array of international artists, the initiative  has significantly enriched the UAE's artistic scene, leading to a more vibrant and eclectic cultural environment. International participation in major cultural events, such as the Dubai Art Expo and Abu Dhabi Art, has increased, reflecting a more globally connected art scene. The long-term residency provided by the Golden Visa allows artists to undertake extended projects and deeper engagements with the local community, fostering ambitious creative endeavors. This influx of international talent has also stimulated economic growth within the creative sector, driving demand for art-related services and contributing to the local economy. Additionally, the presence of prominent artists has enhanced the UAE's reputation as a global cultural hub, strengthening its role in international cultural diplomacy. Collaborative opportunities between local and international artists have flourished, leading to innovative artistic partnerships. Moreover, the increased focus on the arts has prompted investments in artistic infrastructure, such as new galleries and cultural centers, further cementing the UAE's status as a leading destination for the arts.

Title EN: Identity Building and Sharing Business Initiative: an Ethical and Glocal Approach to Job Creation and Sustainable Development
Goal: Integrate Culture In Sustainable Development Frameworks
SDG: SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: International cooperation for sustainable development
Cultural Domain: Design,Performing Arts,Media Arts,Cinema and Audiovisual Arts,Music,Publishing,Visual Arts
Agency Implementation: European Commission (Directorate General for International Partnerships)
Main Feature: The project Identity Building and Sharing Business started in December 2018 and ended in July 2023.  The initiative contributed to socio-economic development through human capital investment in the cultural and creative sectors, which are mobilized as factors of business development and identity building. The project addressed the root causes of irregular economic migration and displacement by strengthening the identity building sectors in countries with fragile situation and address the lifestyle market’s value chains.    The project used the methodology developed by the Ethical Fashion Initiative (EFI), a flagship programme of the International Trade Centre (ITC) that enables artisans living in urban and rural poverty to connect top luxury lifestyle brands, and that supports the rising generation of fashion talents. The Identity Building and Sharing Business Initiative expanded the EFI approach to a wider number of countries and  range of creative industries through an integrated, comprehensive approach investing simultaneously in market access and in identity building, with special attention to fragile countries.   The project was implemented in Kenya, Uganda, Tajikistan, Uzbekistan, Iran, Ivory Coast, Mali and Eritrea. The project produced increased investment in human and social capital in the creative economies and in marginalized segments of the society, with value of human capital investment in target countries equal to 20.000.000 USD.
Results: Main activities carried out include:  1. Production activities aimed to support microenterprises, designers and social enterprises from creative industries and the heritage sector to access international value chains and trade. Activities were implemented in all the project countries and included: capacity building for artisans, brands and producers in technical, artisanal and marketing skills; facilitation of networking, partnership and access to international contacts and value chains; support in participation to international trade shows; support in development of B2B businesses; capacity building in circularity and ESG procedures.   2. Designer Accelerators: the project set up several editions of designer accelerators aimed to support emerging designers. - Kenya Designer Accelerator (Jan 2020 – Dec 2021) - West Africa Accelerator (June 2021 – June 2023) - Homeware Accelerator Central Asia (Dec 2021 – Dec 2022) 3. Opportunities are Here – Project X – was a special strand of activities designed to support young emerging African talents in creative industries. It took a format of a reality show competition where young professionals applied and went through a series of trainings and mentorships, including incubators programmes. The activities also focused on fostering connections and networking. The editions included activities in Uganda (2020), Kenya (2021) and Ivory Coast (2021/22).  4. Marketing support – the project team developed a sales platform, Hands of Fashion, to support B2C sales of the social enterprises involved in the project.   5. Environmental, Social and Governance (ESG) support – a new set of ESG due diligence was developed under the project and applied to all social enterprises.   Among the main achievements: ·	Number of jobs consolidated (sustained) for artisans from marginalized communities: 782 (of which 633 women) ·	Number of supply chains managed by social enterprises, enabling artisans from marginalized communities to be involved: 67 ·	Number of creative talents, artisans and designers involved in the value chains of the lifestyle market: 3506 (of which 2006 women) ·	Number of emerging designers mentored and exposed to the market: 66 ·	Number of international cultural events promoted: 13 ·	Number of local talents mentored and exposed for the market: 1666
Financial Ressources: Aprox. USD 11.9 million [EUR 9.830.000,00 ]   (USD 11.700.00 EU Contribution [EUR 9.700.00,00]; USD 158.000,00 ITC Contribution [EUR 130.000,00 EUR)
Recommandations: The excellent outcomes of specific activities, allowed several areas of work to continue beyond the programme, allowing many involved in the project to sustain and expand their skills and business activities. The Accelerator Alumni have continued to present at fashion events in Paris and London following the Paris Fashion Week event, which was a first for all of them. The Central Asia Homeware Accelerator designers engaged with other institutions (British Council, Swiss Embassy) following their highly publicized presence in Milan and Paris. OAH finalists all started their own ventures. There are several examples of how the programme provided the confidence to develop creative businesses. The training materials and equipment acquired during the project have been handed over to social enterprises who are continuing to provide work for hundreds of artisans.

Title EN: IMMA (Irish Museum of Modern Art) Strategy Goal to become ‘A Global Connector’
Goal: Achieve A Balanced Flow Of Cultural Goods And Services And Increase The Mobility Of Artists And Cultural Professionals
SDG: SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 10 - Reduce inequality within and among countries,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Flow of cultural goods and services
Agency Implementation: IMMA – Irish Museum of Modern Art
Main Feature: The Irish Museum of Modern Arts is Ireland's National Cultural Institution for Modern and Contemporary, which receives funding from the Department of Culture. IMMA’s A Creative Catalyst for Change – Strategic Plan 2024-28 was launched this year and sets out the strategy for strengthening the institution over the next 4 years. Further details on the overall plan are included under Goal 1 Culture and Creative Sectors. The Strategy includes a goal that over the next five years IMMA will be ‘A Global Connector’  Under this goal IMMA outlines how it will strengthen its ties with international partners through collaborative projects, touring exhibitions and also includes plans for staff mobility for peer learning across museums in Europe. IMMA are driven to increase the presence of Irish creativity on the international stage, by actively engaging in an international network of like-minded partners, through collaborative projects and touring exhibitions, and by inviting international curators and artists to collaborate with Irish practitioners. Over the period of this strategy, IMMA will:   •	Strengthen IMMA’s ties with international partners through collaborative projects and touring exhibitions.  •	Produce research into connections between Ireland’s culture and important simultaneous international developments.  •	Increase access to international art across Ireland.  •	Promote the IMMA Collection internationally to a global audience.  •	Purchase international art to emphasise the global scope of contemporary art practice. •	Programme a more diverse global art history.  •	Establish a visiting curators programme to support the visibility of Irish artists abroad. •	Highlight Dublin as an increasingly global city.

Title EN: Implementation of digitisation activities and application of information technologies in the culture sector
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture
SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Digital environment
Agency Implementation: Ministry of Education, Science, Culture and Sport of the Republic of Armenia
Main Feature: In 2020-2023, Armenian state symphonic orchestra concert-courses with the application of new technologies were broadcast online which had 3200 followers from regions and the Diaspora. The National Аcademic Тheatre of Opera and Ballet named after Alexander Spendiaryan performed 3-D projections of Mozart’s “The Magic Flute", Donizetti’s "Elisir of Love", Puccini's "Tosca" operas and Khachaturian "Masquerade", "Spartacus" and "Gayane" ballets were broadcast during a tour in France dedicated to the 120th anniversary of Aram Khachaturian. 12 concerts of Armenian National Philharmonic Orchestra were also broadcast. With a view to being a part of the contemporary processes through introduction of newest technologies, in 2022, were broadcast online the concert "Hover" State Chamber Choir, dedicated Nerses Shnorhali. In 2020-2023, Armenian State Symphony Orchestra made more than 20 live performances, which were broadcast by "Medici" and “Mezzo” leading classical music TV channels. The Armenian State Symphony Orchestrа digitised the works of Armenian composers (Tigran Mansuryan, Haro Stepanian, Edvard Mirzoyan, Edgar Hovhannisyan and others). In 2023 were broadcast by “Mezzo” the films about Aram Khachaturian, Khachaturian competitions and concerts of Armenian state symphonic orchestra, dedicated to Khachatryan's 120th anniversary. Within the framework of the jubilee programs, the Khachaturian radio platform and Khachaturian music reingtons were created. With a view to preserving and disseminating Armenian and world contemporary cultural heritage, digitisation of musical works, films, "Golden Fund" of the Public Radio was carried out: replenishment of different cultural funds /music, theatre/; awareness-raising of the Armenian culture through online platform; creation of contemporary cultural products through introduction of newest technologies. In particular, kept in “Golden Fund" of the Public Radio were restored and digitised. With a view to ensuring appropriate level of TV airtime, with the support of the Ministry of Education, Science, Culture and Sport of the Republic of Armenia, public television and other television companies were prepared and broadcast the series of cultural television programs “On the Roads of Armenia” and “Cultural Armenia” (programs of Public television and Armenia TV), covering Armenian historical and cultural monuments, cultural centers and cultural events, national traditions, rituals and celebrations. Another television company, Bun TV, produced and broadcast a series of artistic educational programs, and ZUM LLC produced the «TV Encyclopedia» project. In cooperation with Deutsche Grammophon, the State Symphony Orchestra of Armenia prepared and broadcast the music of famous Armenian singer Charles Aznavour and composer Tigran Mansuryan.With a view to identifying and promoting creative potential in the republic, information databases оf educational items for talented teens with and without disabilities, were established. Another interesting project is an online concert by the famous Armenian pianist Hayk Melikyan on the theme of the Armenian epic Davit of Sasun with illustrations and an online concert dedicated to the 80th anniversary of the installation of the Main Clock of Armenia.
Results: Preservation and dissemination of Armenian and world contemporary cultural heritage, replenishment and preservation of cultural funds, awareness-raising of the Armenian culture, creation of contemporary cultural products through introduction of newest technologies.
Financial Ressources: every year 50 000
Recommandations: As a result, the international audience has expanded.  Thanks to the use of the newest technologies, communication of age groups with different cultural preferences has been simplified, access to culture has been ensured, the quality of life has been improved, cultural life has been enriched and new forms of entertainment were created.

Title EN: International festival of contemporary arts City of Women
Goal: Promote Human Rights And Fundamental Freedoms
SDG: SDG 5 - Achieve gender equality and empower all women and girls,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels
Area of Monitoring: Gender equality
Agency Implementation: City of Women, Association for the Promotion of Women in Culture
Main Feature: The International Festival of Contemporary Arts – City of Women has been held every October since 1995 in different venues across Ljubljana. Uniting amazing women* and gender non-conforming people from all over the world, the festival offers a unique experience, blending exciting art with inspiring talks and workshops. Since its establishment, the festival has welcomed over 1400 Slovenian and international artists, collectives, curators, theoretician, and activists, ranging from emerging to well-known names. By cooperating with local and international partners and taking place at a range of institutional and alternative venues in Ljubljana and around Slovenia, the festival offers a variety of events from all artistic disciplines which reach broad and diverse audiences and enjoy wide media exposure.  Situated in material feminisms, the City of Women festival exposes the social reality in which art is produced and in which artists live and work. It draws attention to discrimination in art and culture, and aims to improve conditions for women* in the arts and culture. The City of Women encourages social reflection, awareness, solidarity, and acceptance of diversity. Since its foundation, the City of Women festival has been nurturing an intersectional approach to feminism by looking at how gender overlaps with class, race, sexual orientation, physical ability and other nodes of oppression. Over the years, the festival has always posed questions of major relevance for today's life with the help of art and feminist critique. Learning from our own herstory, each edition of the festival tries to imagine the future of feminist art and thought in dialogue with different communities and audiences.  Every festival edition is curated by the program director and associated selectors. We present local and international authors/artists and collectives of mainly women's* authorship. As an interdisciplinary festival we present all art genres, showcasing innovative and breakthrough formats and ideas which engage in a critical dialogue with the present. The festival is curated and without a public call. To participate, please contact us.
Results: •	Higher visibility of women and gender non-conforming artists;  •	Visibility of gender related issues (e.g. care work, pay gap, reproductive health rights); •	Raised sensibility for gender equality and LGBTQ+ rights; •	Raised sensibility about working conditions in precarious cultural sector; •	International circulation of artists and art works

Main Feature: The annual celebration is held at Chedwin Park in St. Catherine, the parish where Indian indentured labourers arrived in Jamaica between  1845 and 1917.  The event features traditional Indian cuisine, and the music of the tassa bands (a drumming ensemble drawn from an amalgamation of various North Indian folk drumming traditions).. Indian fashion is also on display. The event promotes mutual respect and dialogue among the Jamaican citizenry (mostly of 90% African heritage) and the Indian community which currently comprises 1.2% of the Jamaican population.

Title EN: International Festivals and Resdidencies
Goal: Achieve A Balanced Flow Of Cultural Goods And Services And Increase The Mobility Of Artists And Cultural Professionals
SDG: SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 10 - Reduce inequality within and among countries,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Mobility of artists and cultural professionals
Cultural Domain: Design,Performing Arts,Media Arts,Cinema and Audiovisual Arts,Music,Publishing,Visual Arts
Agency Implementation: Association of Non-governmentalOrganizations of Contemporary Culture
Main Feature: Various non-governmental cultural organizations organize festivals to which guest artists are invited. They are organized by such organizations as the Latvian New Theater Institute, Serde, RixC etc. At the same time, the residences of artists and writers are maintained, which allows you to work creatively both in the Dubulti Writers' House, International Writers and Translators House in Ventspils, Serde etc.   The mission of RIGA IFF is to create an internationally recognised cinema event that promotes Riga, enriches the northern European cultural space, and advocates for the development of an intelligent, open and active society. The Riga International Film Festival was established in 2014 and has quickly become one of Latvia’s premier cultural events. It is a celebration of cinema that introduces the international film industry to the current body of work coming out of the Baltic Sea region and the Nordic countries, and in turn, introduces local audiences to the latest happenings in world cinema. The festival advances public interest in current events taking place in the contemporary cinema landscape and encourages dialogue between viewers and filmmakers. In the RIGA IFF programme, contemporary cinema meets the classics, and assertive debut works mingle with festival hits. Moreover, the industry section of the festival provides a platform for film professionals from around the world in which to develop sustainable collaborations as well as discuss the future challenges facing the world of film. (https://rigaiff.lv/en/)   Riga International Short Film Festival 2ANNAS 2024 will take place for the 28th time and as usual offers original, innovative, challenging, socially active short films and medium-length films to viewers. 2ANNAS exists in a context in which the short-film format is not only a step to the first full-scale work but also a deliberate, consistent choice resulting in high-quality art. Similarly, the festival is known as crazy parties in unaccustomed places, a free atmosphere, and creative manifestations, not only in the form of cinema. 2ANNAS offers four tender programs each year: the International Short Film Competition, the Baltic Short Film Competition, the International Small Film Contest, and the competition for films for children and young people. Also, in 2024 the festival will take place on-site and online. (https://2annas.lv/en)   Skaņu Mežs is a festival for adventurous (innovative, experimental, avant-garde, etc.) music. It happens in Riga, Latvia since 2003. The festival usually happens in the beginning of October, whereas one-off events by Skaņu Mežs happen more often. Seeing as all forms of modern music have an experimental dimension, there is always a wide variety of musical genres represented at the festival – from electro-acoustic music, free improvisation, contemporary composition, and noise to interesting shifts in dance music, hip-hop and rock or metal. Skaņu Mežs is a member of festival network ICAS (International Cities of Advanced Sound) and a co-founder of the SHAPE platform as well as one of its two coordinators. SHAPE platform for innovative music and audiovisual art is supported by the „Creative Europe” programme of the EU. Among many others, Skaņu Mežs has presented Autechre, Merzbow, Swans, Liars, Blixa Bargeld, Battles, Bernard Parmegiani, Pierre Henry, Roscoe Mitchell, Christian Wolff, Francois Bayle, Wadada Leo Smith, Laurel Halo, Julia Holter, James Holden, Zebra Katz, Shabazz Palaces, Evan Parker, AMM, Peter Brötzmann and Lustmord. (https://www.skanumezs.lv/en/)   The International Artist Residency “Pedvale” started operating in the renovated Master’s house of Fircks-Pedvale Manor in April 2020. Residency invites artists to present themselves and their work to the local community. The Residency also offers a possibility to teach a public workshop, to perform or make an exhibition during the residency. (Open call for Spring and Summer Residency 2024 – Pedvale Art Park)   Since 2009 the association “Culture and Art Project NOASS” started artists in residence program. The resident house is located on NOASS second floor and studio type apartment on Zaubes street. The main objective is to enable artists to get acquainted with Riga as one of the most beautiful cities in the Baltic States, it’s diverse cultural life, giving new impulses to new creation in the field of visual art, art criticism, writers. more about residence >> Since 2007, “Culture and Arts Project NOASS” has operated within the TEH- Trans Europe Halles – European Network of Independent Culture Centres. THE supports a range of creative initiatives in the European Union and has a membership comprised of 49culture and arts organizations from 25 countries. more about TEH and projects >> The second largest European network where NOASS actively participates is European Network of Cultural Centres (ENCC). Since 2008, “Culture and Arts Project NOASS” has functioned as a EVS – European Volunteer Services sending and hosting organization, thus promoting the mobility of young people who are interested in cultural and arts events among various public organizations. Also, NOASS is registered in PADOR database which is managed by EuropeAid. PADOR or “Potential Applicants Data Online Registration” is a recent applicant processing system introduced by European Commissions through EuropeAid to understand and maintain extensive information about NGOs requesting funds from it for collaboration projects with worldwide organizations. In addition to the mobility and residency programmes and the opportunities for European volunteer work and its participation in TEH, “Culture and Arts Project NOASS” is continuing the partnerships it has begun with other foreign organizations, representing the Latvian Video Art Archive and selections of the very best works from the well-established contemporary arts and video festival, “Water pieces”, as well as the Latvian contemporary art scene at international level. Festivals of national significance, which include the participation of foreign artists, are implemented with the help of the State Cultural Capital Fund. For example, New Theatre Institute of Latvia (NTIL) is a project based organisation working in the field of contemporary performing arts. Since 1995 NTIL has been organizing the International Festival of Contemporary Theatre Homo Novus, which is the largest performing arts platform in Latvia. NTIL also produces and presents projects and long-term collaboration programmes together with local and international partners, strongly believing in the necessity to explore the contemporary performing arts field together with artists and audiences. http://theatre.lv/eng/ Serde (an association whose goal is to promote the development of professional art in Latvia by developing regional and international cooperation between cultural and artistic organizations of various fields and individuals by offering a real functioning environment and infrastructure outside the usual central urban environment)http://www.serde.lv/?q=lv/node/11.   RIXC is the centre for new media culture, art gallery and artist collective, that initiates projects in intersection of art, science and emerging technologies. RIXC's activities include: running an art gallery, production of artworks and innovative art, science and technology projects, organising of the annual RIXC Art Science festival, exhibitions, publishing of Acoustic Space journal series.(http://rixc.org/en/center/)   The contemporary art festival Survival Kit, comprised of a curated exhibition and an event programme, was initiated in 2009 as a response to the economic crisis affecting Latvia at the time. Each year, the festival's appointed curator (or curators) carefully selects the themes explored, inviting artists from around the world to offer alternative scenarios of survival. The festival's mission to critically investigate and reflect on the evolution of contemporary society has made it a key platform for the Latvian Centre for Contemporary Art (LCCA) to showcase its commitment to research, creation, and development of contemporary art processes in Latvia and internationally since 2000. Survival Kit's choice of venue is an integral part of the festival's identity, as it inhabits empty buildings in Riga, exploring their potential and possible development strategies that could be used to revitalize them. Despite the often challenging nature of these spaces, the festival emphasizes the importance of accessibility, assisting people with disabilities. ( https://lcca.lv/en/survival-kit/ )
Results: Taking into account the Latvian Cultural Capital Fund, the support of the non-governmental sector and local governments, every year it is possible to continue the activities of artists and writers’ residencies, as well as organize festivals that introduce Latvian audiences to the performance of foreign professionals in the cultural sector. This positive trend is expected to continue.

Title EN: Inauguration of the College of Cultural and Creative Industries at the University of Technology and Applied Sciences
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture
SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Cultural and creative sectors
Agency Implementation: University of Technology and Applied Sciences
Main Feature: The College of Creative Industries includes four academic programs and these programs are divided into ten different specializations. The programs of the College of Creative Industries are the Mass Communication Program, the Design Program, the Fashion Design Program, and the Photography Program.  The Mass Communication Program:  The Mass Communication program is one of the most popular and vital disciplines demanded by the job market. The program focuses in general on human communication and communication through print, electronic, and new media. It aims to provide students with the knowledge, skills, and values that enable them to prepare and analyze media content and study its various effects on the public. The program is offered in the colleges of Nizwa, Sur, and Salalah, and it is currently offered at the bachelor level only.  The program provides the following five specializations:  •	Public Relations •	Journalism •	Digital media •    	 Media management •	Advertising  The Public Relations specialization aims to prepare empowered public relations specialists who are aware of their professional and social responsibilities, especially in the field of institutional promotion, human resources management, organizational and strategic communication with clients and stakeholders, organizing campaigns, media crisis management in accordance with the ethical framework of public relations, and building content to meet the needs of diverse audiences.  The Digital Media major specialization aims to prepare professionals in the field of digital media, radio and television, capable of innovation and creative thinking to convert ideas into digital media and creative productions and can manage and develop websites and build interactive content in accordance with client requirements and the cultural and ethical framework.   The Journalism major specialization aims to prepare journalists who are proficient in the field of journalistic production for various media, including print and electronic and new media. It prepares journalists who are able to prepare and convey news with full professionalism, honesty, and competence and who search for the truth and give voice to the voiceless. They are appreciative of the value of the journalistic news in enlightening the society.   The Media Management specialization aims to prepare professionals who are aware of the role of culture in determining the institutional formation and social identity. It prepares specialists who can analyze the internal and external forces that shape creative industries, establishing and managing media projects, employing effective marketing strategies, analyzing the political and cultural contexts in which policies are formed and managed, and defining organizational strategies. They are also able to oversee and inspire media organizations and drive organizational change.  The Advertising specialization aims to prepare specialists who are able to think in a unique and innovative way, and use different techniques, equipment and advertising programs in order to produce different types of advertisements and advertising campaigns in light of the choices of the target audience.  The Design Program:  The Design Program at the College of Creative Industries at the University of Technology and Applied Sciences offers students a unique opportunity to excel in the fields of creativity and innovation. It is a program that has been prepared to keep pace with the needs of the job market and the future aspirations of the country. The program takes into account the future skills that students acquire through the practical application of solving problems in creative and innovative ways, with a focus on the academic side and applied side of the industry, as well as keeping pace with modern technologies. The design program is currently being offered at the Bachelor level in at the university branch in Nizwa only.  The design program offers 3 Specializations: •	Graphic Design •	Multimedia Design •	Interior Design  The Graphic Design major aims to prepare students to become professional and communicative visual designers, able to practice and follow the design process and problem-solving to create printed or digital design outcomes, which will serve and impact the industry and their community and environment.  The Multimedia Design major aims to provide the market with graduates who are able to demonstrate sufficient knowledge in all aspects of multimedia design and technologies, acquire problem-solving skills, critical thinking, creativity, and innovation, in addition to demonstrating competence in leadership, teamwork, and ethical responsibilities for their professional life.  The Interior Design major aims to provide the labor market with highly qualified interior designers who are equipped with the required skills and knowledge, and who are able to communicate their ideas using advanced technology and supported by modern project management skills.    The Fashion Design Program:  The Fashion Design program aims to provide students with a high-quality education in the field of fashion design in accordance with global business requirements, local market needs, and adapting them to local social norms. To help students learn and practice the skills necessary for graduates to be able to integrate into the professional industry. To create a bridge between young entrepreneurs and local fashion industry professionals. This program accepts females only, and students can study it in three stages: diploma, advanced diploma, and bachelor's degree. The program is available at the university branch in Muscat only.  The Photography Program:  The photography program aims to provide high-quality technical education as well as an advanced level of creativity and aims to produce graduates with the professional and personal skills to work in the global media and advertising market or to enter the business with confidence, and to contribute effectively to the creative and economic development of the Sultanate of Oman. The program is available at the university branch in Muscat only at a diploma level.
Results: 1.	Offering five sub-specializations in the mass communication program, including:  •	Public Relations:  •	Journalism  •	Digital Media  •	Media Department  •	Advertising   •	 2.	Offering 3 sub-specializations in the design program, namely:  •	Graphic Design •	Multimedia Design •	Interior Design.

Title EN: Incorporating the Cultural Enrichment Policy into the National Development Strategy for the period (2018-2022).
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture
SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Cultural and creative sectors
Agency Implementation: National Planning Council (formerly the Planning and Statistics Authority)
Main Feature: One of the key aspects of this strategy is to define the medium-term direction of the culture sector, stemming from the Qatar National Vision (2030). This vision sets out the country's development path and its long-term objectives, aiming to balance the challenges of modernization with the need to preserve identity, traditions, and culture. This strategy acknowledges that cultural development is intertwined with other pillars of progress. The Second National Development Strategy (2018 - 2020) (Annex No. 6) adhered to the principle of integrating cultural development by defining mandatory programs and projects. This remains one of the significant steps taken by the state to incorporate culture into public policy, ensuring the achievement of desired cultural goals.
Results: In light of the state's efforts to implement the cultural enrichment policy in the National Development Strategy (2018-2022), significant milestones have been achieved across various facets of the cultural sector, including:  1.	A comprehensive review of legislation related to the culture and sports sector, especially Emiri Decree No. (7) of 2016 on the organizational structure of the Ministry of Culture and Sports. 2.	Initiating the formulation of a modern sectoral policy. 3.	Taking practical measures towards enhancing cultural community participation. 4.	Strengthening regional and international cooperation and communication. 5.	Assigning relevant state bodies with preparing necessary studies to position culture as a vital component of economic resources.
Recommandations: Following the evaluation of the Cultural Enrichment Policy in the National Development Strategy (2018-2022), the real challenges impeding the realization of sustainable cultural governance objectives have been identified, the most important of which are: -	The structural linkage between culture and sports at the decision-making and managerial levels -	The lack of focus on the specificities and characteristics of the cultural sector. It has thus become imperative to concentrate on how to overcome these challenges in the preparation of the Third National Development Strategy (2024-2030).

Title EN: Incentive Model for Austria as a film location
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture
SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Cultural and creative sectors
Agency Implementation: Austrian Film Institute
Main Feature: Incentives are an important part of the increasingly global and competitive film industry. They make financial resources available to production companies and are a decisive factor in the determination of the production site. Many European countries are therefore using incentives as a strategic tool to increase local value creation, attract inward film investment, create skilled jobs and develop production infrastructure and digital expertise in a key growth area of the cultural and creative industries. The sustainable strengthening of Austria as a film location is ensured through the adoption of the Film Location Act and the amendments to the Film Subsidies Act and the KommAustria Act. The new incentive system for all film productions came into force on 1 January 2023.  In order to ensure maximum appeal for international productions and maximum planning security for domestic productions, the subsidies are granted in all sectors without a budget cap. The model provides for an automatic, non-repayable grant based on a catalogue of criteria of up to 35% of the expenses incurred in Austria for film productions. 5% of this amount is earmarked for climate-friendly criteria. The maximum subsidy amount is EUR 5 million per film and EUR 7.5 million for series. For the first time, support is also provided for streaming productions.  The film incentive model is based on three pillars:  -	International service productions (FISAplus): Grants for international non-Austrian productions (streaming, cinema, TV) and production services (postproduction, music recording, VFX) are administered by Austria Wirtschaftsservice GmbH (aws). Independent production service providers based in Austria who have been commissioned to produce a film or part of a production are entitled to apply (service processing). -	Austrian television and streaming productions (FISAplus, television productions in coordination with the RTR-GmbH): Grants for Austrian productions that have not been commissioned by broadcasting organizations or video-on-demand services in the areas of television, streaming and virtual reality with a total budget of more than EUR 1.8 million are also processed by the aws. Eligible to apply are independent producers (production companies) based in Austria. Productions below the budget limits will remain in the Television Fund. -	Austrian cinema films (ÖFI+): The Austrian Film Institute is responsible for funding Austrian independently produced films for their first theatrical release as well as international co- productions of the same status. Applications are open to independent producers (production companies) based in Austria. The grant replaces the cinema film grants previously awarded by Filmstandort Austria (FISA). Austrian cinema films will thus have a single point of contact instead of having to rely on a number of different federal funding agencies (Austrian Film Institute, FISA).  Overall, the measure aims at:  •	strengthening Austria as a film location •	attracting film productions from abroad •	promoting jobs in the sector •	strengthening the cultural and creative industries in Austria  In 2023 EUR 15,5 Mio. EUR were spent for ÖFI+ and approx. EUR 22 Mio. for FISAplus.
Results: •	Strengthening of location attractiveness, especially through the "value-added bonus" for international co-productions: The inflow of foreign funds will be subsidised with a bonus (+25%) => (Parts of) film shoots that were not originally planned for Austria have moved to Austria. •	Increased number of international co-productions •	Increased international exchange, transfer of know-how and development of strategic alliances to strengthen domestic film production and infrastructure •	Enhancement of competitiveness through an increase in the revenue share of productions •	An increase in the creation of skilled jobs
Financial Ressources: s. above

Key features of the policy include showcasing traditional and contemporary Islamic art forms, fostering cultural exchange and dialogue among artists and audiences from diverse backgrounds, and emphasizing the historical and spiritual significance of Islamic artistic traditions. The festival typically features a curated selection of artworks, including calligraphy, painting, sculpture, and digital media, reflecting both classical aesthetics and modern interpretations. It also includes panel discussions, workshops, and lectures aimed at deepening understanding and appreciation of Islamic art. By offering a platform for both emerging and established artists, the IAF supports the preservation and innovation of Islamic artistic heritage, while enhancing public awareness and cultural enrichment within the community.
Results: The 25th edition of the Islamic Arts Festival (IAF) was a diverse and captivating showcase of artistic talent from around the world. Artworks officially endorsed by the Supreme Committee during a meeting at the Department of Culture in Sharjah highlighted the theme of "Tajaliat (Manifestations)" through a range of interior artworks. Title EN: Indonesian Dance Festival

Agency Implementation: Yayasan Loka Tari Nusantara office@indonesiandancefestival.id +62 813-8583-8254
Main Feature: Indonesian Dance Festival (IDF) is an international biennial contemporary dance festival founded in 1992 in Jakarta and since 2019 under the auspices of Yayasan Loka Tari Nusantara (YLTN). The next festival will be held on November 2-6, 2024. The IDF was established as a presenting platform for young Indonesian choreographers, and an incubator providing space and support for the creation of new contemporary dance works.  Entering its 32nd year, IDF is the longest held international contemporary dance in Southeast Asia and among the only few similar festivals in the world. A women-led organization, they have held 18 festival editions, presented more than 270 performances and premieres, 150 works by Indonesian choreographers, and 90 works by international choreographers. The festival has involved around 400 dance and multidisciplinary artists and has both commissioned and reconstructed around 45 dance pieces.  IDF aims to map, dialogue, understand the dynamics of the development of dance practice and choreographic discourse, strengthen the dance networks in various regions in Indonesia while connecting it with the network and dynamics of regional and global practices.  The festival’s programs include: ● Evening Performances — full dance numbers by mid-career & established choreographers ● Kampana — matinee, work in progress presentations by emerging choreographers ● Workshop and Masterclasses — dance techniques available for the public ● Lifetime Achievement Award — award given to Indonesian dance maestros ● Young Potential Choreographers — observation program for young dance makers from various Indonesian regions ● Public Discussions — discussions on topical theme in performing arts sectors ● Archive Exhibitions — exhibition of IDF’s 32 years archive showing trajectory of Indonesian contemporary dance  YLTN-IDF also carries out various development and educational programs throughout the year external to the main festival to contribute to the production of knowledge, and the development of the Indonesian performing arts ecosystem
Results: ● Entering its 32nd year, IDF is the longest held international contemporary dance in Southeast Asia and among the only few similar festivals in the world. ● A women-led organization, its committee has transitioned from its co-founder to the new generation. Since 2022 the festival is being led by a new young director at the helm of a young festival team. ● Since 1992, 18 festival editions have been held, presenting more than 270 performances and premieres, 150 works by Indonesian choreographers, and 90 works by international choreographers. ● The festival has involved around 400 dance and multidisciplinary artists and has both commissioned and reconstructed around 45 dance pieces. ● Each festival edition is attended by 30-50 international producers, directors, festival programmers, curators, etc. ● IDF functions as a launching pad for discovering contemporary dance pieces from Indonesia and in extension, Southeast Asia. Many Indonesian choreographers have been discovered through the IDF and later toured internationally through the exposure that the IDF has been able to provide. ● IDF’s program, KAMPANA, is an incubator program offering time, space, funding and mentorship to 6 young choreographers (4 Indonesians, 2 SEA) to create new contemporary works, which culminates in a matinee presentation during the festival time frame. This program is one of the very few incubator programs existing in Indonesia. ● IDF has been continuously contributing to the discourse of the contemporary dance and performing arts sector in Indonesia and Asia, and by extension globally, both in the arts aesthetics implementation/production and the academic fields. ● IDF has been engaging with a wider audience community by utilizing technology through the festival’s regular programming on its YouTube channel, allowing accessibility to communities outside of Jakarta and Java (National central points)

The inclusion of the works in this Catalog does not imply any expenditure. The Catalog has a digital format and is hosted on the institutional website. Main Feature: The Ethiopian Visual Art Association has played a pivotal role in advancing the visibility and influence of Ethiopian visual art. By participating in international exhibitions, hosting significant events, and engaging in advocacy, EVAA has strengthened Ethiopia's cultural presence on the global stage. The association's efforts have not only promoted Ethiopian artists but also contributed to broader cultural and economic objectives.  This report outlines the significant activities and achievements of the Ethiopian Visual Art Association (EVAA) from 2020 to 2024. During this period, EVAA has engaged in various international and national art events, showcasing Ethiopian talent and contributing to cultural diplomacy. The report highlights key exhibitions, symposiums, and initiatives undertaken by EVAA, alongside the outcomes achieved.  International Engagements International Invitations (2020-2024) EVAA facilitated the participation of 30 Ethiopian artists in international exhibitions across countries, including the USA, Greece, France, Italy, Egypt, Germany, and the Czech Republic. These events provided a platform for Ethiopian artists to display their work globally, fostering cross-cultural exchanges and enhancing the visibility of Ethiopian art.  60th Venice Biennale (2024) Ethiopia was represented for the first time at the 60th Venice Biennale. The event, held from April 20th to November 24th, 2024, took place in the Pavilion at Palazzo Bollane in Venice, Italy. This prestigious participation marked a significant milestone for Ethiopian contemporary art, allowing for greater international exposure and recognition.  Notable Exhibitions and Symposiums Soul for Resistance #NoMore Art Movement (2022) Hosted at the Modern Art Museum Gebrekirstos Desta Center in Addis Ababa, this international exhibition featured artists from 25 countries and ran from February 20th to March 4th, 2022. The exhibition focused on themes of resistance and solidarity, reflecting on contemporary socio-political issues through visual art.  Origin International Art Symposium (2023) Held at Sheger Park, Addis Ababa, from January 26th to February 24th, 2023, this symposium included 25 artists from 18 countries. The central theme, "The Great Renaissance Dam," explored the intersection of art and national development projects.   The symposium also fostered dialogue and collaboration among international and Ethiopian artists.
Results: Image Building and Cultural Diplomacy  Through these international and local engagements, EVAA has significantly contributed to the image building of Ethiopia as a center of cultural and artistic expression. Participation in global events like the Venice Biennale has positioned Ethiopian art within the broader global artistic discourse.  Networking and Collaboration The association's activities facilitated networking and attachment opportunities with artists from different nations. These interactions have paved the way for future collaborations, enriching the artistic landscape of Ethiopia and beyond.  Promotion and Sales The exhibitions and symposiums provided platforms for promoting Ethiopian artists and their work. These events not only showcased the talents of the artists but also created opportunities for the sale of artworks, thereby supporting the economic empowerment of artists.  Advocacy and Workshops EVAA has also been active in advocacy, utilizing workshops to promote and address national agendas through visual art. These efforts underscore the role of art in societal transformation and public discourse.

Law "On Amending the Civil Code of the Republic of Armenia".. 5.	Armenia's accession to international IP treaties, including the Marrakesh Treaty and the Beijing Treaty, the Protocol "On Protection of Industrial Designs" and Agreement "On Trademarks, Service Marks and Places of Origin of Goods of the Eurasian Economic Union". Title EN: INTERNATIONAL FESTIVAL OF AMERICAN RENAISSANCE AND BAROQUE MUSIC “MISIONES DE CHIQUITOS”
Goal: Achieve A Balanced Flow Of Cultural Goods And Services And Increase The Mobility Of Artists And Cultural Professionals
SDG: SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 10 - Reduce inequality within and among countries,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Flow of cultural goods and services
Agency Implementation: APAC  EMAIL: info@festivalesapac.com PHONE: 781-16658
Main Feature: The main objective of the International Music Festival is to preserve and spread the beauty of the ancient Jesuit Missions, as well as to show internationally the cultural wealth of the musical archives of Chiquitos and Moxos. This project is unique because it revolves around the living and dynamic cultural heritage of its people who keep their traditions alive. Music arranged or created by the local indigenous people is often performed, so cultural identification plays a fundamental role. The ancient Jesuit missions of Chiquitos in the department of Santa Cruz and Moxos in the department of Beni constitute one of the main treasures of the regional and national cultural heritage. During the restoration process of the Jesuit temples of these missions, a great musical wealth was discovered: in Chiquitos 5,500 and in Moxos 7,000 sheets of sacred music written between the 17th and 18th centuries, both by European musicians and by the indigenous people of the area, which was played daily in these towns until the mid-19th century. Added to this treasure is the UNESCO declaration in 1990 that grants the title of Cultural Heritage of Humanity to six towns in Chiquitos as "living towns", since unlike other ancient Jesuit towns of which only ruins remain, in Chiquitos their beautiful churches, musical scores, customs, clothing, festivals, ceremonies, instrument making and in many of them the musical tradition are preserved. In 1996, the Asociación Pro Arte y Cultura, APAC, emerged as a visionary initiative of cultural managers, giving life to the International Festival of American Renaissance and Baroque Music “Misiones de Chiquitos” that would embrace the task of reviving, preserving and disseminating the musical heritage of the missions. This project is unique because it revolves around the living and dynamic cultural heritage of its peoples who keep their traditions alive. Often, music arranged or created by the indigenous people of the place is performed, so cultural identification plays a fundamental role. One of the Festival's characteristics is that it encourages the artistic growth of music schools, orchestras and choirs. In recent versions, co-productions have been made between national and international groups, which demonstrate that local musicians have the technical level to perform with internationally known groups. Also, in these more than 20 years of festivals, the number of music schools, orchestras and choirs has grown significantly. The “Misiones de Chiquitos” Music Festival, held every two years, is hailed as the most relevant cultural event in Bolivia, ranking among the most prestigious in its category worldwide. It is an event that disseminates and celebrates the rich historical-cultural legacy of Chiquitos, projecting its influence beyond its borders. APAC becomes a bridge that connects the past with the future, and, through Chiquitos, promotes Bolivian cultural wealth on the global stage. This festival is made possible thanks to the financial support of the Autonomous Departmental Government of Santa Cruz, the Autonomous Municipal Government of Santa Cruz, the Autonomous Governments of San Xavier, San José de Chiquitos, Concepción, San Rafael, Roboré, San Ignacio, Cotoca, Porongo and Ascensión de Guarayos, and Embassies, Consulates and private companies.
Results: The International Festival of American Renaissance and Baroque Music "Misiones de Chiquitos" has shown a remarkable trajectory through its latest editions, each one reflecting significant adaptations and achievements in its development.  In 2018, the festival featured 58 groups performing 140 concerts in 18 different venues, attracting 52,000 attendees. This year also saw a notable international presence, with representatives from 17 countries contributing to the diversity and richness of the event. In 2022, the festival featured 57 groups performing 132 concerts at 14 different venues, bringing together 50,000 attendees. This year also saw a notable international presence of 14 country representatives. In 2024, the festival saw the participation of 61 groups offering 134 concerts in 18 different venues, bringing together 50,000 attendees. This year also saw a notable international presence of 15 country representatives. The economic impact generated in the different Festival venues: generation of sources of employment, increase in tourism. Promotion and dissemination of the Chiquitos Missions as a World Heritage Site.

Two macro-areas are focused on cultural and creative industrial: textile and fashion industry and crafts, and tourism. Creativity in the textile sector frequently goes hand in hand with the production of raw materials, from cotton to vegetable fibers to semi-finished leather. 38 African Nations are producers of high-quality cotton. The international fashion weeks in Nigeria, Ghana and South Africa attract, every year, a vast audience of high economic; in this context the "Made in Italy" can play a strategic role both to supply ideas and raw materials to transfer skills and create new growth opportunities in Africa.                   Africa’s environmental and cultural characteristics and landscapes represent an opportunity to improve the economy through tourism. There are many Italian companies that, in this area, have achieved experiences of quality and important economy in the country in which they have settled.

Title EN: KALINGA INSTITUTE OF SOCIAL SCIENCES
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture

Main Feature: The Kalinga Institute of Social Sciences (KISS) is a renowned educational institution in India that has played a significant role in protection and promotion of the diversity of cultural expressions through its distinctive approach rooted in three pillars : Educate, Empower, and Enable. Committed to delivering quality education to Indigenous children, KISS integrates traditional knowledge, creativity and cultural practices into its curriculum, fostering an innovative pedagogical model that ensures students receive a comprehensive education encompassing social, cultural, economic, emotional, and environmental well-being. By bridging the connection between tradition and modernity, KISS addresses contemporary challenges from an Indigenous perspective to help protect and promote the diversity of cultural expressions. KISS believes that Indigenous people are the true custodians of their traditions and culture. KISS engages its 80,000-strong Indigenous/Tribal student body (30,000 at the KISS Bhubaneswar campus, 10,000 across 10 satellite centres, and 40,000 alumni) (65% female) through immersive learning methods aimed at fostering the protection and promotion of the diversity of cultural expressions. These methods include : ●        Elevating awareness and understanding of Indigenous culture through immersive workshops and curriculum integration. ●        Cultivating skills and confidence in students through hands-on experiences in Indigenous practices, such as music, dance, visual arts, performing arts, storytelling, and language. ●        Establishing and nurturing relationship-based networks within Indigenous communities, connecting students with local people, elders, and traditional practitioners. ●        Showcasing the contemporary relevance and adaptability of Indigenous traditions in today's world through innovative programs and events. ●        Empowering students to take individual and communal 'ownership' of their Indigenous culture, encouraging active participation and celebration of their living cultures and creativity. At KISS, students become practitioners and true custodians of their traditions and culture by engaging in experiential learning modes that are purposively immersive, participatory, and co-created, fostering a sense of ownership and promoting informal cultural transmission. Language and Cultural Immersion Programs : KISS's language and cultural immersion programs enrich lives by promoting Indigenous languages and creativity. Through Mother Tongue Based Multilingual Education (MTBMLE), Indigenous languages, stories, and performing arts are integrated into education, fostering dynamic cultural continuity and creativity. The Language Lab enhances language learning, while workshops standardize Indigenous languages and promote STEM education. International Mother Language Day celebrations and academic events deepen appreciation for linguistic and cultural diversity and Indigenous culture and expression. Indigenous Culture-Based Schools and Research Centres :KISS has introduced seven Indigenous culture-based schools focusing on Comparative Indic Studies, Indigenous Science, Indigenous Languages and Literatures, Indigenous Knowledge, Science and Technology, Culture, Philosophy and Eco-spiritualism, Heritage and Indology, Legal Studies and Rights, and Resource Management at University level. We purposively create opportunities for our student body to provide a platform to know about their creativity and heritage, share their traditions, and educate others about their cultural practices. KISS also encourages research and documentation of creativity, languages, narratives, oral traditions, sacred groves, Indigenous techniques and technology, traditional knowledge, practices, and skills through its seven innovative centres. Community Engagement and Consultation :This is exemplified by the Professors of Practice (PoP) concept, where KISS appoints practitioners of various Indigenous knowledge, art forms, vocational skills, and practices, who bring the first voice of  Indigenous narratives into the teaching and research programs. Their experiential knowledge enriches the KISS pedagogy, making learning more relatable and engaging for students, and ensures the transmission of cultural knowledge from one generation to another, protection, promotion of the diversity of cultural expressions and promoting creativity. Cultural Festivals, Events, and Performing Arts :KISS actively celebrates various cultural festivals, events, and ceremonies showcasing the rich diversity of Indigenous cultures. It has a central cultural body that facilitates the safeguarding and appreciation of Indigenous performing arts, creative minds, and knowledge systems, creating a more inclusive and culturally sensitive educational environment. ●        Sarhul ●        Mage Parab ●        Baa Parab ●        Chaiti Parab ●        Vija Pandum Promotion of Indigenous Sports &Games :KISS's sports tournaments, like the Janjatiya Khel Mahotsav, enrich lives by celebrating Indigenous athleticism and culture. Hosting 5,000 athletes and 1,000 officials from 26 states, KISS provides a platform to showcase traditional sports nationally, fostering pride and unity among Indigenous communities while promoting physical well-being and living vultures. Protection and promotion of the diversity of cultural expressions occurs at KISS via exposure and participation through : ●        Immersive workshops and integration that elevate awareness and understanding of the diversity of Indigenous cultural contents andexpressions and narratives among its student body. ●        Active participation and hands-on experiences in traditional practices, which cultivate skills and confidence in students. ●        Direct engagement with local individuals, artists, elders, and traditional practitioners by building relationship-based networks within Indigenous communities. ●        Showcasing the contemporary relevance and adaptability of Indigenous traditions through innovative programs, events, and celebration of Indigenous creativity and living cultures. ●        Empowering students to take individual and communal 'ownership' of their Indigenous culture, encouraging active participation and celebration of their arts, culture and heritage, fostering a sense of pride and responsibility among the student body. Title EN: JEUX DE LA FRANCOPHONIE
Goal: Integrate Culture In Sustainable Development Frameworks
SDG: SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: International cooperation for sustainable development
Cultural Domain: Design,Performing Arts,Media Arts,Cinema and Audiovisual Arts,Music,Publishing,Visual Arts
Agency Implementation: Commission Nationale de la Francophonie (CNF)
Main Feature: Les Jeux de la Francophonie sont un événement international qui combine des compétitions sportives et des concours culturels, rassemblant des jeunes talents des pays francophones du monde entier. Ils visent à promouvoir les échanges culturels et la solidarité entre les pays de la Francophonie, tout en mettant en avant les talents artistiques et sportifs. Les Jeux incluent des disciplines telles que l’athlétisme, le football, la lutte, la musique, la danse, la peinture, la photographie, et la littérature. Ils offrent une plateforme unique pour la promotion de la diversité culturelle et la valorisation des jeunes talents.  En 2017, la Côte d'Ivoire a organisé et abrité les jeux de la Francophonie à Abidjan. depuis lors, la Côte d'Ivoire  participe chaque année  aux jeux de la Francophonie, notamment à la dernière édition de l'année 2023 à Kinshasa, en République Démographique du Congo, en faisant participer les acteurs culturels dans toutes les disciplines.
Results: -Mettre en lumière les talents artistiques et sportifs des jeunes francophones. -Promouvoir les échanges interculturels et renforcer les liens entre les pays francophones. -Stimuler l’intérêt pour les arts et les sports au sein des communautés locales. -Contribuer à la diffusion des œuvres des artistes francophones et à la reconnaissance internationale de leurs talents. Encourager le développement des infrastructures sportives et culturelles dans les pays hôtes.
Recommandations: L'évaluation a révélé que les Jeux de la Francophonie sont un outil efficace pour promouvoir la diversité culturelle et renforcer la coopération internationale. Les principales recommandations sont :  -Continuer à soutenir l’organisation des Jeux et à mobiliser les ressources nécessaires pour leur succès. -Renforcer les programmes de formation et de préparation des jeunes talents participants. - Améliorer la couverture médiatique pour accroître la visibilité des événements et des participants. - Développer des partenariats avec le secteur privé pour assurer une plus grande durabilité financière. - Évaluer régulièrement l'impact des Jeux sur le développement culturel et sportif des pays participants.

Title EN: Kania Soly
Goal: Integrate Culture In Sustainable Development Frameworks
SDG: SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: National sustainable development policies and plans
Agency Implementation: Association Kania Diyé / Email : associationkaniadiye@gmail.com
Main Feature: En République de Guinée, toutes les sociétés s’identifient à travers une culture, des traditions, des coutumes et mœurs. Le Soly est une danse traditionnelle qui exprime la bravoure des initiés à l’école sécrète (LAGA). Cette danse au couleur des hommes forts est une parfaite transmission du savoir-faire de la société africaine qui mérite d’être connue par la transmission générationnelle. Cette pratique est exercée par des personnes appelées Yongoyeli. Le Soly a évolué avec le temps pour être reconnu comme danse traditionnelle de Kania, d’où le nom (Kania Soly). C’est une danse de duel et d’affrontement pour exprimer la joie de la communauté suite à l’initiation des filles et fils du Kania.  L’Association Kania Diyé composée des ressortissants de Kindia vivant en Guinée et à l’étranger, amis et sympathisants, organise le Kania Soly depuis 2020 au lendemain de chaque fête de tabaski sur une place publique et avec toutes les tranches d’âge. L’objectif général est de promouvoir le patrimoine culturel, agricole, touristique et artisanal de la Préfecture de Kindia. Il vise spécifiquement à : -	faire connaître le Kania Soly à la nouvelle génération, ses valeurs, ses enseignements et ses pratiques ; -	faire connaître l’identité artistique et culturelle du soly ; -	promouvoir la diversité des danses traditionnelles du terroir ; -	former et renforcer la capacité  des hommes/femmes de Kindia en entreprenariat (saponification, teinture, tissage, etc.) ; -	construire et rénover des infrastructures scolaires ; -	réaliser des forages, latrines publiques pour le développement de la localité ; -	faire le reboisement pour lutter contre le réchauffement climatique ; -	faire un plaidoyer auprès du Gouvernement pour la construction des infrastructures publiques (pistes rurales, maison des jeunes, électrification des zones des communautés, etc.) et la modernisation du textile local.
Results: Depuis 2020 jusqu’à nos jours, les résultats suivants ont été atteints : -	les enseignements et les pratiques du Kania Soly ont été promus ; -	l’identité artistique et culturelle du soly est connu ; -	la diversité des danses traditionnelles du terroir est promue ; -	200 hommes/femmes de Kindia ont été formés en technique de l’entreprenariat, en teinture, en saponification, en technique de conservation alimentaire ; -	6 forages et 10 latrines publiques ont été réalisés dans les quartiers et districts de Kindia ; -	5 000 arbres ont été plantés ; -	8 pistes rurales ont été réalisées ; -	une grande partie des quartiers urbains et districts ruraux ont été électrifiés ; -	la restauration des têtes de source de 10 marigots des villages environnant ; -	6 écoles ont été rénovées et équipées.
