Title EN: Le Pass Culture
Goal: Integrate Culture In Sustainable Development Frameworks
SDG: SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: National sustainable development policies and plans
Cultural Domain: Design,Performing Arts,Cinema and Audiovisual Arts,Music,Publishing,Visual Arts
Agency Implementation: La SAS Pass Culture
Main Feature: Dans le cadre des missions qui lui sont dévolues, le ministère de la Culture, sous l’impulsion du Président de la République, a créé un nouvel espace public de partage et de rencontre, une plateforme digitale, de service dénommée « pass Culture ». Cette application géolocalisée et éditorialisée est destinée en premier lieu aux jeunes de 18 ans, bénéficiant d’un crédit de 300€, pour faciliter leur accès à la culture, favoriser leur participation autonome à la vie artistique et culturelle au moment de leur accession à la majorité, et promouvoir la qualité et la diversité des offres culturelles sur l’ensemble du territoire national.  Une mission d’intérêt général pass Culture a ainsi été créée par décret n°2019-66 du  1er février 2019. Le ministère de la Culture et la Caisse des Dépôts se sont associés afin de constituer une société par actions simplifiée – la SAS pass Culture – pour porter la gestion et le développement du pass Culture. Nouvelle forme de service public à portée de la main et pleinement inscrit dans les usages contemporains, c’est un outil privilégié pour enrichir et prolonger le parcours d’éducation artistique et culturelle des jeunes et faciliter leur pleine participation à la vie culturelle diversifiée, partout et quelle que soit leur situation.  Depuis 2021, le dispositif étendu comprend deux volets complémentaires : la part individuelle, à destination des jeunes de 15 à 18 ans et la part collective, à l’attention des établissements scolaires. Ces deux volets participent au même objectif : permettre à 100 % des jeunes de bénéficier d’un parcours d’EAC de qualité leur permettant ensuite de participer de façon autonome et éclairée à la vie artistique et culturelle. Part individuelle et offres individuelles La part individuelle permet à tous les jeunes de 15 à 18 ans sur l’ensemble du territoire national de découvrir des propositions culturelles de proximité et d’y accéder : places et abonnements, livres, CD, visites, cours et ateliers, matériel de beaux-arts, services numériques, etc La part collective est exclusivement dédiée au financement d’activités d’EAC effectuées en groupe et encadrées par des professeurs : ateliers de pratique artistique et scientifique, représentations, concerts, projections, rencontres, visites guidées ou libres, conférences, festivals, salons.  Les activités sont organisées en partenariat avec les acteurs culturels, associatifs, publics ou privés. Elles sont animées par des professionnels des arts et de la culture.   Dans sa mise en œuvre, le pass Culture répond à trois freins identifiés pour le déploiement tant de l’EAC que des pratiques autonomes des jeunes adultes :  -	La difficulté d’accès à l’information et la ressource, par le développement d’une application géolocalisée et éditorialisée ; -	Le frein financier, par la mobilisation de crédits inédits ; -	La complexité d’organisation et de validation en ce qui concerne les projets éducatifs, pour les établissements scolaires. Par ailleurs, encourageant la diversification et la régularité des pratiques culturelles des jeunes, il constitue un soutien à l’économie culturelle, avec plus de 35 000 partenaires culturels, associatifs, publics et privés venant de tous horizons, et de tous domaines.  Le fonctionnement du pass Culture : Un contrat d’objectifs et de performance (COP) et une convention de gestion ont été conclus entre le ministère de la Culture et la SAS afin d’arrêter les orientations stratégiques et déterminer les moyens alloués à cette dernière. La gouvernance du pass Culture est assurée par un comité stratégique : il est consulté sur toutes les orientations, est tenu informé de l’activité de l’établissement qu’il peut orienter et délibère sur les grandes orientations budgétaires. Il est le lieu où se débattent et se définissent les orientations que le président de la SAS devra mettre en œuvre. Le comité est composé de 13 membres : un représentant de l’Etat (ministère de la Culture) nommé par arrêté ; sept membres nommés par les deux associés sur proposition de l’Etat ; trois membres nommés par les deux associés sur proposition de la Caisse des Dépôts ; deux représentants des salariés de la Société élu par eux.  Le Président de la SAS, nommé par décret du Président de la République, est un président exécutif : il est responsable juridiquement de tous les actes de gestion de l’établissement dont il est le mandataire social.
Financial Ressources: 224 708 750 Dollars
Recommandations: L’évaluation est en cours, menée d’une part L’IGAC Inspection Générale des affaires culturelles, d’autre part par la cour des comptes et le département des études de la prospective et des statistiques du ministère de la Cuture (DEPS).

Title EN: Le programme national « Dialogues Culturels »
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture
SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Partnering with civil society
Cultural Domain: Design,Performing Arts,Media Arts,Cinema and Audiovisual Arts,Music,Publishing,Visual Arts
Agency Implementation: Le ministère des affaires culturelles (MAC)
Main Feature: Lancé en 2022, le programme national « Dialogues Culturels » s’inscrit dans le cadre de la réforme du secteur culturel visant à développer un modèle de l’action culturelle fondé à la fois sur la protection de la spécificité et la production d’un contenu culturel à forte valeur identitaire et la promotion de la diversité des expressions culturelles et ce, en partant d’une conviction selon laquelle « la richesse culturelle du monde, c’est sa diversité en dialogue. Chaque culture puise à ses propres racines mais ne s’épanouit qu’au contact des autres cultures ». Un tel équilibre ne peut être atteint qu’à travers l’instauration d’une culture de dialogue entre les différents acteurs/opérateurs de la scène culturelle et artistique (institutionnels – OSC – artistes – intellectuels.). Ce programme est initié au niveau central par les établissements sectoriels sous tutelle du Ministère des Affaires Culturelles et à l’échelle régionale par les institutions de l’action culturelle établies sur tout le territoire national (maisons de culture -  Centres culturels.) formant un tissu institutionnel exceptionnel et une plateforme de diffusion et de jouissance assez importante. Le suivi est assuré par les CRAC (commissariats régionaux aux affaires culturelles) et la DGAC (Direction générale de l’action culturelles) afin d’assurer des dialogues/rencontres culturelles de qualité notamment en termes de thèmes abordés, d’engagement des intervenants. L’objectif étant de rapprocher les créateurs, artistes (qui en quelque sorte forment l’élite intellectuelle de la société et de la scène culturelle nationale) aux jeunes et aux enfants ce qui contribuera à stimuler leurs potentiels créatifs et développer l’esprit critique et forger sur le long terme leur personnalité sur la base de principes universels de tolérance, d’acceptation de la différence et d’appartenance.
Results: Selon le rapport fourni par la DGAC, l’année 2023 a été marquée par l’organisation de 1409 dialogue/rencontres culturelles au profit de 88.493 participants parmi les jeunes et les enfants. Les 1409 actions sont réparties selon des thèmes très variés : -	Technologies – culture numérique – économie culturelle 27 -	Le rôle de la femme dans l’action culturelle 38 -	Programmes d’incitation à la lecture 50 -	L’éducation artistique 85 -	Les valeurs de la citoyenneté 107 -	Valorisation du patrimoine matériel et immatériel 140 -	Les Arts 150 -	Renforcement des capacités critique artistique et échange d’expériences 150 -	Littérature : 199  -	Divers 463

Title EN: Les Bonnes Pratiques
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture
SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Partnering with civil society
Agency Implementation: Syndicat Suisse Romand du Spectacle (SSRS)
Main Feature: Cette initiative s’adresse dans un premier temps, aux porteuses et porteurs de projets des arts de la scène. Elle vise à sensibiliser aux problématiques liées aux conditions de travail et à la durabilité au sein des pratiques professionnelles de la culture par le biais d’un processus d’autoévaluation non contraignant.  Prendre le temps de questionner son projet grâce aux Bonnes Pratiques, permet d’identifier d’éventuelles faiblesses et d’agir en conséquence, de manière fondée et argumentée. C’est faire le premier pas vers une amélioration significative de la manière de construire des projets, de les conduire.  Basée sur la bonne foi, l’auto-évaluation se compose de trois questionnaires. Chacun d’eux pose 10 questions ouvertes aux porteuses et porteurs de projets, à trois temps forts du processus de création.  Des outils et des exemples complètent les questions dans le but d’accompagner les participantes et participants dans leurs prises de décisions.  Les questions interrogent les projets sous l’angle des conditions de travail, de l’écologie, de la gouvernance, de la santé et de l’égalité, en accord avec les Objectifs de Développement Durable développés par l’ONU et l’agenda du Canton de Vaud (Suisse).  Méthode Pour élaborer la méthode d’auto-évaluation, une « matrice » a été créée. Elle se compose, d’un côté, des « temps forts » d’une création et, de l’autre, des objectifs de développement durable. Le croisement de ces données permet de créer la grille de la check-list et de l’auto-évaluation.  1. Environnement Objectifs : promouvoir une consommation et un « style » de production durables dans le cadre des arts vivants. Favoriser tout type de mesure permettant de limiter la consommation d’énergie et la production de gaz à effet de serre. Promouvoir le local et le bio, et encourager le circuit court.  Indicateurs : – Type de moyen de transports utilisés – Consommation d’énergie – Émissions de gaz à effet de serre – Quantité de déchets produits  2. Gestion de projet Objectifs : adopter, autant que possible, une attitude exemplaire aux différents échelons de la structure (bureau/plateau…). S’engager à analyser son projet sous l’aspect de la durabilité. Offrir des conditions de travail attractives et rendre possible la conciliation famille-travail.  Indicateurs : – Transparence – Transmission des informations – Opérations de sensibilisation à la durabilité  3. Égalité et formation Objectifs : sensibiliser les équipes à la durabilité. Promouvoir la recherche permettant de mettre en place des solutions novatrices. Valoriser la diversité et renforcer l’intégration. Promouvoir activement l’égalité entre les hommes et les femmes. Développer des activités culturelles diversifiées. – Diversité au sein de l’équipe – Formations proposées, favorisées – Recherches, innovation dans le travail  4. Économie Objectifs : favoriser le développement d’une économie circulaire. Développer des synergies entre les acteurs et actrices culturelles et encourager les activités commerçantes de proximité (costumes, décors). Améliorer les conditions salariales.  Indicateurs : – Niveau des salaires (au minimum les salaires recommandés par le SSRS) – Durée et type d’engagement – Utilisation (optimale) des ressources – utilisation de technologie innovante – Pourcentage de l’approvisionnement en circuit court  5. Santé Objectifs : Créer des espaces de travail libres de harcèlement et autres atteintes à la personnalité. Développer des types d’engagement offrant un cadre de travail protégeant la santé (durée des contrats, horaires de travail, pauses). Promouvoir une alimentation saine.  Indicateurs : – Engagement d’une Personne de Confiance en Entreprise – Dépenses de prévention des maladies et promotion de la santé – Type d’alimentation favorisée (sain, varié, de saison, bio, local)
Results: Le site internet a été diffusé auprès de nombreux réseaux, le retour des compagnies qui l’ont utilisé ont été très favorables. Néanmoins, le projet n’a pas eu assez de répercussions par manque de ressources.

Title EN: Let Them Schools Arts Festival
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture
SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Partnering with civil society
Cultural Domain: Design,Media Arts,Cinema and Audiovisual Arts,Music,Visual Arts
Agency Implementation: Let Them Trust
Main Feature: Let Them Trust (LTT) is a local non-profit organisation based in Harare and Domboshava. Its mission is to promote creativity and artistic expression with the aim of preserving African culture and good cultural practices. It is a creative, educational and cultural initiative for children and the youth that aims to create platforms for young people to learn about the arts and also showcase their artistic talent. LTT incorporates themes in its programming that educates participants on how they can deal with issues that affect them. HIV/ AIDS, Sexual Reproductive Health Rights, Abolition of social evils (such as child marriage, child labour etc.), Mental Health, Children’s Rights, Gender Based Violence, Drug Abuse Climate Change, Adolescence Development and Zimbabwean Culture & Heritage are some issues that have been tackled over the years. Let Them Trust has conducted workshops in over 400 schools impacting on the lives of over 202,000 children over the past decade. At its inception in 2010, LET THEM Trust intended to preserve traditional and cultural heritage through Ngano (traditional folk tales) and theatre performances in education centres. Since then, and now in its 11th year, it has evolved into a multifaceted cultural arts promotion and preservation organisation. The organisation has responded to changes in the current generation of youths who are exposed to more external influences and habits through the prevalent global digital connectivity. This access to all information from all over the world, though positive in bringing humanity together, has inevitably altered their cultural expression. LTT engages all children and youth nationwide to progressively adapt and embrace change while maintaining Zimbabwean culture. It also paves a way for them to sustainably pursue careers in the arts.   The festival is the organisation’s flagship program. It has been running for the last 11 years and it has adapted during the Covid pandemic to online platforms. It was held mostly in Harare but has now moved to Domboshava, a rural countryside setting which offers natural surroundings. More than 300 schools have participated in the festival over the years. This  year Let Them Trust is celebrating its 12th edition of the Schools Arts Festival under the theme Tamuka. The two  day event will be packed with performances and interactive activities. In line with the UNESCO 2005 convention goal number 4 the poetry category participants have been asked to curate content around the conexus between youth unemployment and drug abuse. Those performing in theatre have also been asked to create story lines around the challenges women are facing in the society in trying to further their careers particularly in the art industry. Let Them Schools Arts festival continues to provide a platform for the children to be knowledgeable and proactive in advocating for their human rights and fundamental freedoms using their artistic talent.
Results: The festival has managed to reach over 500 000 people across the world over the years. It has managed to host more than 300 schools around Zimbabwe. Young artists have had the opportunity to be paired with mentors across many disciplines. 20 Students have managed to at least get recording deals and roles in local production as a result of the festival’s exposure. A  few examples are  Tendai Mavengeni who is now a professional musician after having been discovered at the festival.  Through our partnerships with organisations like Afrikera  one of our students,  called Jevas graduated in 2016 with a professional certificate, he  is now a dance instructor and has come back to mentor a number of children since. Jevas has also extended his art portfolio by enrolling with the Zimbabwe Theatre Academy, another partner of the Let Them Trust.  There is also an artist by the name Solution whose talent was identified during the Let Them Schools Arts Festival, he went on to represent Zimbabwe in China under the Chinese Bridge Competition that hosted over 107 countries from all over the world. He managed to get into the quarter finals. Our partnership with Africalia in 2021 was also very instrumental in driving the art for change campaign that was implemented across the country.

Title EN: Let’s Create
Goal: Integrate Culture In Sustainable Development Frameworks
SDG: SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: National sustainable development policies and plans
Cultural Domain: Design,Performing Arts,Media Arts,Cinema and Audiovisual Arts,Music,Publishing,Visual Arts
Agency Implementation: Arts Council England
Main Feature: Let’s Create is Arts Council England’s organisational strategy for 2020-2030. It was developed over the course of two years, informed by research and evidence and extensive consultation with members of the public, the arts and culture sector and other stakeholders.     The strategy’s vision wants England to be a country in which the creativity of each of us is valued and given the chance to flourish, and where every one of us has access to a remarkable range of high-quality cultural experiences by 2030.    To achieve this, the strategy is structured around three main Outcomes. Creative people focuses on how the public can engage with and develop personal creativity at every stage of their lives. Creative communities considers how the professional and voluntary sectors can work together to help shape stronger cultural provision in places. A cultural and creative country looks at the professional cultural sector, supporting innovation, international work and cooperation, and talent development.   This is supported by four investment principles, which describe what “fit for the future” and well-run arts and culture organisations look like and sets out how organisations will need to develop. These are: ambition and quality, dynamism, environmental responsibility, and inclusivity and relevance.
Results: A delivery plan for 2021-2024 has been drafted to help bring the strategy to life.

Title EN: Lifting Restrictions on Foreign investment in cultural, sports and entertainment services
Goal: Achieve A Balanced Flow Of Cultural Goods And Services And Increase The Mobility Of Artists And Cultural Professionals
SDG: SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 10 - Reduce inequality within and among countries,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Flow of cultural goods and services
Agency Implementation: Ministry of Commerce and Industry
Main Feature: One of the key features of encouraging foreign investment in the fields of cultural, sports, and entertainment services is the cancellation of the investment cap. Relevant legislation and laws have been reviewed, particularly Law No. (13) of 2000 regulating the investment of foreign capital in economic activity, which has been repealed and replaced by Law No. (1) of 2019 concerning the regulation of non-Qatari capital investment in economic activity (Annex No. 17), and the adoption of associated executive regulations. Article 2 of the new law stipulates that, without prejudice to the legislation regulating the practice of non-Qataris in commercial activities and professions, and the provisions of Article (4) of the same law, the Minister of Commerce and Industry may allow non-Qatari investors to exceed their specified contribution limits of 49%. They may be allowed to contribute up to 100% of the project’s capital. This applies to certain exceptional fields listed in the executive regulations attached to the law, including cultural, sports, and entertainment services.
Results: The Covid-19 pandemic that swept the world during the years 2020 and 2021 and led to a sharp contraction in trade and investment on the one hand, and the focus of most foreign investors on investing in the services sector accompanying the State of Qatar’s preparation to host the World Football Championship in 2022 on the other hand, justify the failure of this measure in achieving the results expected from it, despite the positive statistical indicators that have begun to appear little by little, such as the increase in the percentage of activities and demonstrations of a cultural nature, and the increase in national production in fields related to culture.

Title EN: Lithuanian Capital of Culture
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture
SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Cultural and creative sectors
Cultural Domain: Design,Performing Arts,Media Arts,Cinema and Audiovisual Arts,Music,Publishing,Visual Arts
Agency Implementation: Ministry of Culture of the Republic of Lithuania
Main Feature: Continuing the idea of the project "Vilnius – European Capital of Culture" (2009), the Ministry of Culture of the Republic of Lithuania has been implementing the project "Lithuanian Capital of Culture". The aim of the project is to promote cultural activity, participation in culture, creative initiatives and their diversity, to strengthen the creative potential of the local community, to develop culture and art, to make culture more accessible to population, to develop cultural services that improve the local cultural, social and economic environment and satisfy the cultural needs, to promote the local cultural heritage and the attractiveness of the local identity, as well as to increase the project's visibility and its awareness to the public. The project also seeks to stimulate and promote the long term co-operation of the state, municipal institutions and bodies, municipalities, communities, NGOs, and artists.  Until 2024, any city in Lithuania, except Vilnius, could become the Lithuanian Capital of Culture. Since July 2024, following new amendments to the document –  "The Description of the Procedure for the Partial Financing of the Project "Lithuanian Capital of Culture" from the State Budget Funds“ approved by the Order No.ĮV-580 of the Minister of Culture of the Republic of Lithuania, dated 5 July 2024, no restrictions to the applicants (municipal institutions) have been applied.  The provisions of a new document encompass the following new evaluation criteria to the applications: -	Relevance and innovation (creativity) of the project to identity and image of the city and its long-term benefits for the local community, city, region (cultural, social, educational, economic (tourism);  -	inclusion and promotion of professional art activities in cultural programme;  -	initiatives that promote and strengthen local/regional identity and cultural traditions;   -	initiatives that strengthen national identity and citizenship;  -	initiatives that strengthen the preservation of Lithuanian identity and traditions, historical memory;  -	cooperation, networking, cultural entrepreneurship (joint creative projects with the local community, individual creators and/or performers, municipal and cultural and other organizations (e.g. educational, social), national and international cultural organizations, NGOs); -	contribution to increasing the accessibility of cultural services to different groups of population.  The new application must comply with the horizontal principles: - sustainable development, including avoiding significant harm (sustainable activities that respect climate and environmental standards, promoting employment, reducing poverty and social exclusion, preserving cultural identity, promoting sustainable consumption, etc.);  - equal opportunities and non-discrimination (on grounds of sex, race, nationality, citizenship, language, origin, social status, religion, beliefs or opinions, age, sexual orientation, ethnic origin, religion, disability, etc.); - innovation (creativity) (applying new technologies, developing or implementing innovative and creative solutions, etc.); - accessibility for all (accessibility solutions for service infrastructures, physical and e-environmental accessibility, universal design solutions, etc.).  The title of Capital of Culture is a responsibility not only for local communities, but also for municipalities. According to the new provisions of the   project financing rules, the amount of state budget funds allocated by the Ministry of Culture of the Republic of Lithuania for the implementation of the project shall not exceed 50 % of the total amount of the project's costs. The amount of funds to be allocated from the municipal budget and other sources of funding to be indicated at the time of application must be at least 100 % of the amount allocated by the Ministry of Culture of the Republic of Lithuania.
Results: The programme contribute  to strengthening cultural activities in the regions, promoting participation of local communities, cultural institutions, NGOs in cultural life, developing cultural tourism, creating and providing a variety of new cultural services and cultural products in the regions.
Financial Ressources: From year 2020 until 2026 approx. USD 111240 (EUR 100 000) partial support will be allocated for the implementation of the project by the Ministry of Culture. Pursuant to "The Description of the Procedure for the Partial Financing of the Project "Lithuanian Capital of Culture" from the State Budget Funds”, since year 2026 cities that will be granted the status of the Lithuanian Capital of Culture will receive partial allocations from the Ministry of Culture for the implementation  of the project approx. USD 167 000 (EUR 150 000). The project's funding intensity will be up to 50% of the funding needed to implement the project. The amount of funds to be allocated from the municipal budget and other sources of funding to be indicated at the time of application must be at least 100 % of the amount allocated by the Ministry of Culture.

Title EN: Lithuanian Shorts Mentorship and Baltic Women in Film Mentorship
Goal: Promote Human Rights And Fundamental Freedoms
SDG: SDG 5 - Achieve gender equality and empower all women and girls,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels
Area of Monitoring: Gender equality
Agency Implementation: Lithuanian shorts
Main Feature: For the past several years, the Lithuanian Short Film Agency "Lithuanian Shorts" has been organizing two mentorship programs: “Lithuanian Shorts Mentorship” and “Baltic Women in Film Mentorship”. The inspiration for these initiatives came from the active European movement "Women in Film and Television" (WIFT), which unites women working in film and television. Additional motivations included research on women in the Lithuanian film industry by Lina Kaminskaitė-Jančorienė and Dr. Jelena Šalaj, as well as international examples such as “EWA Network Mentoring for Women Producers”, “Women Go TECH,” “ProPro – The Producers’ Programme for Women”, and the “Creative Europe MEDIA” research “Supporting Gender Balance.” It was observed that, until now, there were no such mentoring programs for women in the film/TV industry in Lithuania, and later, the same gap was identified in the Baltic States. “Lithuanian Shorts Mentorship” is an eight-month program dedicated to Lithuanian women from all areas of the film and television industry, regardless of their disciplines. Through this program, selected participants are paired with experienced industry professionals who are highly motivated to share their knowledge and guide them through career challenges, helping them delve deeper into specific industry areas. The goal of the Lithuanian Shorts Mentorship program is to help women discover their talents, fill knowledge gaps, explore new professional development opportunities, and motivate them to pursue successful careers in the film and television industry. The target audience of the "Lithuanian Shorts Mentorship" includes professionals from various fields within the Lithuanian film and television industry (e.g., producers, directors, screenwriters, operators, sound and editing directors, animation creators, festival organizers and program curators, film critics, TV show producers, etc.). These individuals seek to deepen their professional knowledge in their field or expand their horizons in other areas of the film/TV industry, learn from experienced industry representatives, and work individually with an appointed mentor. The "Lithuanian Shorts Mentorship" selection committee consists of organizing agency’s representative and human resources (HR), personnel selection professionals Laura Hamidova, Deimante Grybauskaitė and Justina Jančiauskaitė, who help to evaluate the motivation of the candidates for the mentoring program. The structure of this mentorship program includes around 12 on-site and online meetings between organizers and mentees, as well as individual meetings between mentees and their mentors (the number of meetings depends on the pair). Each month, mentees meet online for a catch-up discussion on how the program is progressing. Occasionally, these meetings feature guests – such as successful alumni like filmmakers Marija Kavtaradzė, Irma Pužauskaitė, and producer Greta Akcijonaitė – motivational speakers, or representatives from the Lithuanian Film Center and Vilnius Film Office. Additionally, mentees and mentors have the opportunity to attend various seminars and workshops on creativity, feedback, and more. Alongside formal events, the program also includes informal networking events for the entire mentorship community. “Baltic Women in Film Mentorship” is the first mentorship program exclusively for women in all areas of the film and TV industries across the Baltic States. Through its activities, BWiFM seeks to enhance the exchange of best practices, knowledge, contacts, and interest in Baltic film culture while addressing gender equality. The core of the mentorship program is building an effective contact-exchange and matchmaking marketplace where women working in the Baltic audiovisual industry can be mentored by industry experts. Fifteen participants (five from each country) are selected to take part in the program. It welcomes women from Estonia, Latvia, and Lithuania who are already working in these industries and wish to deepen their professional knowledge and expand their networks. Since 2022, the mentorship program has been dedicated to developing young talents and is intended for women under 30 years of age. The structure of this mentorship program differs slightly from the previous one. It consists of matchmaking between mentees and mentors, followed by their individual meetings, monthly online gatherings with mentees and industry guests, self-education webinars and workshops on topics like mental health, leadership, self-promotion, and more. The program also includes visits to industry events during Estonian, Latvian, and Lithuanian film festivals. The entire program lasts for seven months. The program is organized by the Lithuanian Short Film Agency “Lithuanian Shorts” in collaboration with the “Women in Film & Television Lithuania” association, in partnership with the Vilnius International Film Festival, Riga International Film Festival, Tallinn Black Nights Film Festival, EWA European Women’s Audiovisual Network, AVAKA, and Creative Europe MEDIA Desk Lithuania. It is sponsored by Nordic Culture Point.
Results: Since its inception, the “Lithuanian Shorts Mentorship” and “Baltic Women in Film Mentorship” programmes have achieved remarkable results, both quantitatively and qualitatively.  Every year, the “Lithuanian Shorts Mentorship” programme receives an increasing number of applications, highlighting its continued relevance and growing recognition. This consistent interest indicates the program's significant potential for the future. The programme has cultivated a strong community of mentee alumni, now reaching over 100 professionals from various fields within the film and television industry. This community has not only fostered numerous collaborative ideas but has also led to the formation of valuable professional partnerships. The programme has a sustainable, long-term impact, both on the participants' professional development and on the Lithuanian film industry as a whole. In the international market, "Lithuanian Shorts Mentorship" is named and considered as an example of good practice. The idea of the "Baltic Women in Film Mentorship" marked a significant step towards creating a sustainable regional network of like-minded organizations. Through this network, the practice of professional mentoring in the fields of film and television has been successfully applied and developed. In 2022, the second season of the "Baltic Women in Film Mentorship" confirmed the program's necessity and importance in the professional journeys of young women. Many program alumni have successfully completed ongoing projects, submitted applications for project funding, or initiated new co-production ventures. In the spring of 2023, this mentorship program was recognized and evaluated by the experts at Nordic Culture Point, a significant entity in the region, and was awarded substantial three-year funding for the program's development and the expansion of the organizing network. This achievement is a significant milestone for the Lithuanian audiovisual sector, as the "Lithuanian Shorts" project is one of only four cooperation network projects in the Nordic and Baltic countries to receive funding and the only one representing the Baltic region.

Title EN: Local Art Show
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture
SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Cultural and creative sectors
Agency Implementation: Ethiopian Visual Art Association
Main Feature: 1. Big Art Sale at Hilton Addis The Big Art Sale, an annual event held in collaboration with Cactus Showcase at the Hilton Addis, serves as a significant platform for Ethiopian artists to present and sell their works. This event attracts a diverse audience, including art collectors, enthusiasts, and the general public. The Big Art Sale has been instrumental in promoting local artists and providing them with an opportunity to reach a broader market. The event not only facilitates the sale of artworks but also fosters networking among artists, collectors, and art professionals, enhancing the overall visibility of Ethiopian art.  2. African Union: "Unite Africa" Exhibition (May 22-25, 2023) The "Unite Africa" exhibition, held at the African Union headquarters, was a special event that aimed to celebrate African unity and diversity through visual art. This exhibition featured works from artists across the continent, with a focus on themes of unity, peace, and cultural heritage. The event provided a platform for dialogue on the role of art in promoting peace and social cohesion. It also highlighted the potential of visual art as a medium to address pan-African issues and foster a sense of solidarity among African nations.  3. Raddison Blue: Memorial of Famous Ethiopian Tember Designer (January 22-27, 2020) The memorial exhibition at Raddison Blue honored the legacy of a renowned Ethiopian Tember designer. This exhibition showcased the designer's significant contributions to Ethiopian art and culture, offering a retrospective of their most iconic works. The event attracted art historians, cultural enthusiasts, and the general public, serving as an educational experience about the importance of traditional Ethiopian design in contemporary contexts. The memorial provided a platform for reflecting on the evolution of Ethiopian art and design, celebrating the rich cultural heritage of the country.  4. Fendika Culture Center: Monthly Event Fendika Culture Center hosts a monthly event that focuses on showcasing the works of local artists. These events are designed to engage the local community and provide a consistent platform for emerging and established artists to display their creations. The center has become a hub for cultural exchange and artistic expression, offering workshops, live performances, and discussions that promote the understanding and appreciation of Ethiopian art. The monthly events have helped to cultivate a loyal audience and stimulate interest in the local art market.
Results: Promotion and Sales of Artworks: These events have significantly boosted the visibility and sales of Ethiopian art, providing artists with a vital platform to showcase and sell their works.  Audience Engagement: The diverse audiences attracted to these events have included local art enthusiasts, international visitors, collectors, and cultural stakeholders, helping to broaden the market for Ethiopian art.  Local Market Development: The regularity of these events, particularly the monthly showcases at Fendika Culture Center, has helped develop a vibrant local market for art, encouraging local investment in the arts.  Workshops and Advocacy: The workshops and discussions held in conjunction with these events have focused on advocating for peace and addressing national agendas through visual art. This has positioned art as a powerful tool for social change and dialogue, highlighting its role in promoting national unity and cultural identity.

Title EN: Local Cultural Strategies and Plans
Goal: Integrate Culture In Sustainable Development Frameworks
SDG: SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: National sustainable development policies and plans
Agency Implementation: Department of Culture and Tourism in Abu Dhabi Dubai Arts and Culture Authority Sharjah Department of Culture
Main Feature: Many of the local departments and authorities of culture in the different Emirates of the UAE, have developed local cultural strategies and plans to ensure the growth of the cultural sector at the local level, ones that complement efforts in the Federal level, but also build on the strengths of each Emirate and the priorities at the local level. The UAE has 7 Emirates, and each Emirate contributes greatly to the development of the cultural sector in the country. Below is a list of some local authorities that have developed and implemented cultural strategies and plans:  •	The Department of Culture and Tourism in Abu Dhabi (DCT): DCT regulates, develops and promotes culture and tourism in Abu Dhabi. Its cultural mandate is to preserve and promote Abu Dhabi’s cultural heritage, to increase awareness and engagement with cultural heritage and the arts, to stimulate creativity, to build and enable capacity in Abu Dhabi’s cultural sector and t   and creative industries. Below are a few more specific priorities for DCT in Abu Dhabi: o	Heritage: Historic monuments, ancient buildings, oases and natural heritage are the essential elements that constitute Abu Dhabi’s historic environment. It is part of DCT’s mandate to uncover traces of Abu Dhabi’s ancient civilizations, as well as to document, preserve and ensure the maintenance of historic buildings. their responsibility extends to the management and development of culturally significant locations, including oases and archaeological sites.  DCT’s responsibility is to collect, safeguard, and document the intangible cultural heritage and history of the citizens of Abu Dhabi as well as the modern heritage. Initiatives under the intangible heritage preservation mandate are supported through constant collaboration with other local and federal departments, authorities, ministries and civil society.  o	Museums: Positioned at the forefront of Abu Dhabi’s continued advancement into a leading global arts and cultural hub, DCT is mandated to develop and shape Abu Dhabi’s historical and evolutionary narrative. DCT is responsible for the creation of a diverse array of world class museums and international cultural platforms of expression presented in the capital’s Saadiyat Cultural District. The location already features Louvre Abu Dhabi and will feature additional major museums – all of which will bring to the world a distinctive canvas of artworks and installations steeped in history, heritage, modernity and contemporary appeal. From housing artistic expressions transcending cultures and civilizations, to creating vibrant platforms for educational, cultural exchange, stage performances and artistic dialogue, the museums on Abu Dhabi’s Saadiyat Cultural District are poised to become the heart of sustained multicultural exchange between local, regional and international art landscapes. Existing museums such as Al Ain Museum and the Dalma Museum allow visitors to journey into the UAE’s proud national history, offering a glimpse into the inspirational values of the UAE’s Founding Father, Sheikh Zayed bin Sultan Al Nahyan, as well as the nation’s rich history, culture and heritage. Al Ain Palace Museum, Al Jahili Fort and Qasr Al Muwaji in Al Ain also offer insights into the historical buildings of the United Arab Emirates, having been preserved, maintained and renovated into museums which form some of the mythical wonders of Al Ain.  o	Promoting the arts: DCT seeks to offer a vibrant program of cultural, artistic and educational events to provide visitors with a unique cultural experience. By leveraging a series of lectures and seminars in collaboration with museums in Abu Dhabi, DCT reaches and engages the community through a wide range of cultural initiatives including exhibitions, performances, Artscape’s and other cultural events. DCT strives to foster a cultural environment for Abu Dhabi by supporting UAE-based artists as they pursue their professional careers, promoting cultural tourism and a deepened understanding of Abu Dhabi’s artistic, cultural and historic institutions.  o	Education and outreach: DCT is dedicated to expanding their cultural education programs to engage with audiences both resident in and visiting the UAE. A range of programs and outreach initiatives have been designed to enhance the accessibility of Abu Dhabi’s culture and heritage. These initiatives prepare the community for a vibrant future full of artistic accomplishment, engaging with the next generation, with teachers, and with aspiring individuals by offering a range of educational materials and academic programs. Moreover, as part of their commitment to engaging with members of the community and creating platforms for knowledge sharing and skills development, DCT offers a series of training programs for young Emirati students. o	Abu Dhabi’s Culture and Creative Industries Strategy 2020 – 2024: In 2019, Abu Dhabi developed a 5-year culture and creative industries strategy 2020-2024, working in collaboration with key sector partners. The Strategy seeks to strengthen Abu Dhabi’s position as a globally recognized center of creative talent and a leading regional producer and exporter of creative and cultural content. o	Dubai Arts and Culture Authority (Dubai Culture): Dubai Culture supports and inspires local and international creative talent, ensuring that art and creativity can be practiced and enjoyed by anyone, anywhere. It empowers the growth of Dubai’s creative sector as a key contributor to the emirate’s economic growth and position on the global cultural map. Finally, it celebrates and safeguards Dubai’s cultural heritage, with the overarching aim of positioning the emirate as a global center for culture, an incubator for creativity and a thriving hub for talent. The key strategic pillars underpin the Authority’s mandated role as a policymaker and planner, regulator, enabler and operator – one that seeks to facilitate and promote the development and sustainability of the city’s cultural ecosystem and creative economy. Dubai Culture’s Strategic Pillars •	Encouraging and supporting the public and private sectors and non for profit organizations to contribute to the creation of various cultural events and activities to enrich the cultural content within the community. •	Confirm the cultural heritage values and activate them through school curricula •	Encourage and support creative writers and artists, supporting their literary and artistic activities and works and nurturing young talents in the field of cultural, literary and artistic creativity •	Preserve the emirate’s folklore and folk arts. In 2021, the wise leadership approved three strategies relating to the cultural and creative sector. It was the first time that three strategies were approved in one year since te launch of Dubai Culture: Dubai Creative Economy Strategy: Aims to transform the emirate into a preferred destination for creatives and the global capital of the creative economy by 2025. Rehabilitation and Revitalization of Al Fahidi Historical Neighborhood Strategy: Aims to transform the neighborhood into a leading cultural destination, offering creative artistic experiences amid an authentic architectural and urban fabric, raising artistic taste, and devoting the spirit of cultural innovation to fuel the creative movement, and support the growth of the creative economy. Public Art Strategy: Includes three pillars: economic growth by stimulating cultural tourism, developing cultural infrastructure by encouraging youth to contribute to improving technical infrastructure, and sustainable urban and community development. o	The Department of Culture in Sharjah: The Department focuses its efforts in the areas of culture and media in Sharjah. The main objectives of the Department are:  •	Deliver high quality cultural programs and activities.  Preserve national culture and arts.  Contribute to national development goals.  Preserve and promote awareness about the local heritage.   Cooperate with local, Arab, and international cultural organizations to promote and strengthen culture.
Results: Over the years, the cultural sector in each of the UAE’s seven Emirates has grown.
Recommandations: The implementation of different local cultural strategies and plans in the UAE highlights several key conclusions and recommendations. Promoting coordination and integration across emirates is essential to avoid duplication and ensure a cohesive national cultural policy, maximizing resource utilization and creating a unified cultural vision. It is crucial for these strategies to reflect the UAE unique heritage and traditions, emphasizing cultural identity through preservation initiatives, community-based projects, and heritage programs. Enhancing community engagement is also vital; developing accessible programs, workshops, and events tailored to various demographics will encourage active participation in cultural activities. Supporting cultural innovation and creativity is equally important; local strategies should foster contemporary art forms, creative industries, and cultural entrepreneurs to drive economic growth and enrich the cultural scene. Encouraging collaboration and partnerships between local cultural institutions, government bodies, and the private sector can enhance the effectiveness of cultural plans, leading to shared resources and expertise. Additionally, investing in cultural infrastructure, such as museums and performance spaces, and capacity building for cultural professionals will improve the quality and impact of cultural initiatives. Finally, regular monitoring and evaluation of cultural strategies are necessary to assess their effectiveness and impact, ensuring that they remain relevant and responsive to the evolving needs of the community.

Title EN: Mar del Plata International Film Festival
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture
SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Cultural and creative sectors
Agency Implementation: INCAA (National Institute of Cinema and Audiovisual Arts /  Secretariat of Culture
Main Feature: The Mar del Plata International Film Festival, organized by the National Institute of Cinema and Audiovisual Arts (INCAA), promotes cinematographic activity in all its forms, and its screens show films of diverse origins, themes and styles. In it coexist the tradition of classic cinema with new trends, new voices and new technologies.   The Mar del Plata Festival - the only one in Latin America with Category "A" - has been held every year since 1954, and it has been reflecting the universe of Argentine and international cinema and consolidating itself as a platform for the development and exchange of the film and audiovisual industry.   The Festival is historically organized in different sections:   The first of these is the Competition: with juries carefully selected for each edition, awards are given to films in the International Competition, Latin American Feature and Short Film Competition, Argentine Feature and Short Film Competition, Altered States Competition and Work in Progress.   The second section is Panorama, where spectators will find the best of the most recent international productions. Established directors coexist with new talents and different thematic focuses such as Mar de Chicas y Chicos -aimed at children-, Banda Sonora Original -for films with music as the protagonist- or Super 8 - 16mm -dedicated to these historic formats-, among others such as Hora Cero, Generación VHS and Las Venas Abiertas.   The third section is dedicated to Tributes and Retrospectives and seeks to update the trajectory of prestigious directors with the aim of bringing them back into circulation. In addition, this section makes it possible to give rise to new cinematographic trends from various focuses on current filmmakers who otherwise would not reach the theaters. This is a key section for evaluating works in terms of their cultural heritage for the cinema of the present and the future.   A fourth section concentrates on Restorations, where the national and international cinematographic cultural heritage is brought back into value so that the public can enjoy the old glories of the history of cinema.  Outside the screens, the Festival is also characterized by the attractiveness of its Special Activities; among them, talks with Masters, round tables, book presentations, special screenings and seminars on new criticism. Over the years, the Festival has become a space for reflection on new film movements and has welcomed theorists, journalists and filmmakers from all over the world. With the seaside city of Mar del Plata as a framework, the International Film Festival also represents a relevant platform to exhibit Argentine production, and is fertile ground for the meeting between professionals, the circulation of works and the creation of new audiences.
Results: According to the report made in 2023 by the INCAA, the Mar del Plata Film Festival contributed to position the Argentine film and audiovisual industry among the best in the world with great international recognition.
Recommandations: The initiative has a great impact at the national, federal and international levels. Year after year, the prizes awarded gained prestige and the Festival grew to become the most important in Latin America.  Its continuity over time contributed significantly to the positioning of Argentine Cinema as a showcase of our country in the world.

Title EN: MA CITE SANS CHOMEUR : PROGRAMME D'INSERTION PROFESSIONNELLE DES JEUNES DANS LE DOMAINE DE LA MODE , DE L'ARTISANAT ET DU TEXTILE.
Goal: Integrate Culture In Sustainable Development Frameworks
SDG: SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: National sustainable development policies and plans
Agency Implementation: Fondation Roger Bango pour le Développement  -Association des Créateurs de Mode et de Textile de Côte d’Ivoire ; -Association des Volontaires pour le Service International (AVSI-CI) ; -Union des Fédérations Nationales des ICC ; -ABC construction ;others
Main Feature: La Fondation "Roger Bango" est une organisation ivoirienne dédiée au développement économique et social à travers divers programmes, notamment dans le secteur culturel et artisanal. Elle vise à réduire le chômage, particulièrement parmi les jeunes, en leur offrant des formations professionnelles et des opportunités d'emploi. Un de ses projets phares est "Ma cité sans chômeurs", qui se concentre sur l'insertion professionnelle des jeunes dans le domaine de la mode et de l'artisanat textile. La fondation travaille en partenariat avec le gouvernement et d'autres organismes pour mettre en œuvre des initiatives qui contribuent au développement durable et à l'amélioration des conditions de vie en Côte d'Ivoire.  Ce programme vise à réduire le chômage et à fournir une main-d'œuvre qualifiée dans le secteur artisanal textile, le plus grand employeur artisanal en Côte d'Ivoire. Il englobe les couturiers, stylistes, tisserands et maroquiniers, avec environ 10 à 15 entreprises semi-industrielles et plus de 5000 entreprises artisanales traditionnelles. Avec une croissance des besoins vestimentaires estimée à 5,2 % par an, la réorganisation et l’industrialisation des PME de ce secteur sont essentielles pour améliorer l'offre et la compétitivité internationale. Des programmes de formation et de renforcement des capacités dans les métiers de la couture et les métiers supports au développement d'entreprise sont nécessaires. Le projet "Ma cité sans chômeurs" vise à insérer professionnellement 400 jeunes dans la mode, répondant aux besoins de formation et d’employabilité des jeunes. Il s'aligne sur la vision du Président de la République de Côte d'Ivoire, qui a désigné 2023 comme l'année de la jeunesse. Les districts d’Abidjan, des Lacs, du Sassandra-Marahoué et des Savanes ont été choisis pour ce projet, basé sur les besoins des artisans et le potentiel régional dans le secteur textile. Des projets pilotes entre 2017 et 2019 ont déjà formé et inséré 45 jeunes, démontrant que ce projet à plus grande échelle pourrait générer de nombreux emplois et réduire le chômage, contribuant à une cité sans chômeurs.
Results: Les résultats atteints par la mesure sont :  -Un répertoire des métiers de la mode et du textile (métiers techniques et métiers connexes) est disponible; -Les 400 bénéficiaires aux métiers identifiés dans le secteur de la mode et du textile sont formés en 6 mois ; -De nouveaux métiers dans le domaine de la mode et du textile sont créés avec un profil de carrière; -Les ateliers employeurs améliorent leur gestion administrative et comptable; -Les ateliers employeurs présentent un bilan financier positif un an après la fin du projet; - Plusieurs projets pilotes ont déjà été réalisés de 2017 à 2019 sur une période de 6 mois et ont permis de former puis d’insérer 45 jeunes dont 35 jeunes filles et 10 jeunes hommes

Agency Implementation: 1. Ministry of Education, Culture, Research and Technology 2. Ministry of Tourism and Creative Economy
Main Feature: In the past four years, main policies and measures that contain strategies and frameworks for the development of an integrated culture and creative economy sector include:  1. Presidential Regulation 142 of 2018 on the 2018-2025 National Creative Economy Master Plan (PR on the 2018-2025 RIPEKN);   2. Presidential Regulation 114 of 2022 on the Strategy for Culture (PR on Strategy for Culture); and  3. Draft Presidential Regulation on the 2025-2045 Culture Advancement Master Plan (Rencana Induk Pembangunan Kebudayaan) (2025-2045 RIPK).   Regarding the culture sector, the 2020 QPR reported that the National Strategy for Culture document was successfully developed at the 2018 Indonesian Culture Congress. The Strategy for Culture has now been enacted through the PR on Strategy for Culture. Following the provisions of the Law on Culture Advancement (see Goal 1, Specific Policies that Regulate the Culture and/or Creative Economy Sectors), the Strategy for Culture is currently being reviewed by Kemendikbudristek as a reference in the preparation of the 2025-2045 RIPK. It is hoped that the RIPK could be stipulated in a Presidential Regulation in 2024 to be included in the Final Draft of the 2025-2045 National Long-term Development Plan (see Goal 3, Policies on Sustainable Medium- and Long-term Cultural Development Plans).  Regarding the creative economy sector, the 2020 QPR reported on the stipulation of the PR on the 2018-2025 RIPEKN, which is still valid at the time of the drafting of this report. As a follow-up effort, Kemenparekraf is conducting a review process for the preparation of a new Master Plan for Creative Economy Development to accommodate the latest developments after the enactment of the Law on Creative Economy (see Goal 1, Specific Policies that Regulate the Culture and/or Creative Economy Sectors).
Recommandations: PR on Strategy for Culture:  Evaluations conducted by Koalisi Seni on the process of preparing the PR on Strategy for Culture have resulted in the following conclusions/recommendations.  1. According to Gumay (2022a), until the fifth year since the Law on Culture Advancement was enacted, not all derivative regulations for its implementation have been completed, including those directly related to the legal basis for the management of the Cultural Endowment Fund/Dana Indonesiana (see Goal 1, Measures that Provide Funds for CSO Capacity Development), even though the fund had been successfully established since 2022.   2. According to Gumay (2022b), it took four years for the President to ratify the Strategy for Culture as a Presidential Regulation, even though the draft National Strategy for Culture had been submitted to the President since the 2018 Indonesian Culture Congress. Title EN: MAIs - Women farmers in the inner territories

Main Feature: Support for Women as Creators, Producers, and Distributors of Cultural Activities, Goods, and Services. This project aims to foster civil and cooperative participation among women farmers from inland countryside of Portugal, through their empowerment, so as to contribute to their social visibility and enhancing equality between women and men. The intervention-oriented project is based on the Theory of Change, a methodology which carries participation in its core.
Results: The project has facilitated the creation and dissemination of cultural knowledge through the production of manuals such as the 'Manual de Práticas Agroecológicas' and the 'Manual: Entre feijões e outras espécies das hortas de S. Pedro do Sul.' These publications support women in agriculture, recognizing their role as cultural stewards and promoting their knowledge and practices. Women's Access to Decision-Making Positions: By involving women in the planning and execution phases of the project, including participation in workshops and training sessions, the project has empowered women to take on leadership roles within their communities. The creation of local associations and the inclusion of women in policy-making discussions further highlight this effort. Support for Women's Full Participation in Cultural Life: The MAIs project has created opportunities for women to participate in cultural and educational events, such as the Workshop on Gender Equality in Agriculture. This initiative, organized in collaboration with UMAR (Portuguese women's rights association), ensures that women are actively involved in cultural activities and have a platform to share their experiences and knowledge.
Recommandations: - Empowerment through Knowledge and Skill Development: The production and dissemination of manuals have been effective in recognizing and promoting women's roles in agriculture. This has empowered women by enhancing their knowledge and cultural practices, positioning them as cultural stewards within their communities. - Increased Female Leadership and Participation in Decision-Making: The project has successfully facilitated women's involvement in decision-making processes. By including women in the planning and execution phases and promoting their participation in workshops and training sessions, the initiative has enabled women to assume leadership roles. The creation of local associations and women's inclusion in policy-making discussions underscore the project's impact on increasing female leadership. -Enhanced Participation in Cultural and Educational Activities: The initiative has provided significant opportunities for women to engage in cultural and educational events, such as the Workshop on Gender Equality in Agriculture. Collaborations with organizations like UMAR have ensured that women have a platform to share their experiences and knowledge, fostering their full participation in cultural life. - Promotion of Gender Equality in Agriculture and Beyond: By addressing gender equality in agriculture and supporting women's involvement in various cultural activities, the project has contributed to the broader goal of promoting gender equality. This has had a positive impact not only on women's personal and professional development but also on the cultural and social fabric of their communities. Overall, the initiative demonstrates the importance of targeted support for women in cultural and agricultural sectors, highlighting the positive outcomes of empowering women through education, leadership opportunities, and active participation in cultural life.

Title EN: Malacate
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture
SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Cultural and creative sectors
Cultural Domain: Design,Performing Arts,Media Arts,Cinema and Audiovisual Arts,Music,Publishing,Visual Arts
Agency Implementation: Cultural Heritage, IP and DGARTES - Directorate General of Arts
Main Feature: Malacate was a multidisciplinary artistic intervention project created specifically for the São Domingos Mine (Mértola): a place with a remarkable history of mining exploration, as evidenced by the industrial building of impressive aesthetic value that still exists. Malacate aimed to be the vector of a contemporary and innovative artistic work, emerging from the encounter between locals and a community of national and international artists, supported by a wide process of community mediation. The project sought to become an agent of territorial and community regeneration, affirming itself as an unavoidable place for cultural fruition on a regional scale, with an impact on the attractiveness for locals, as well as for external visitation flows. It also aimed to improve the quality of life of the residents and broaden their horizons, creating a unique place of cultural enjoyment.
Results: Access and support to/for contemporary arts in low-density municipalities through, inter alia: programming of artistic productions, involvement of residents in creative processes and audience development activities. The project has contributed to boosting the artistic offer in the region, as well as bringing audiences closer to a multitude of cultural domains, through a wide range of creative processes, programming, and audience development activities. Malacate was the vector for a contemporary artistic endeavor, which arose from the encounter between locals and a wide community of artists, sustained by a community mediation process. The participatory artistic creation processes involved local communities as active agents of creation and/or public presentation, considering the direct participation of specific community groups and the creation of dynamics of proximity and involvement. Audience development was prominent, as a way of responding to the objectives of involvement and transformation through the valorization of identity, fostering the development of a long-term project based on the will of the residents. During its EEA Grants financing period, Malacate contributed to the mobility of artists and cultural professionals, promoting several artistic exchanges within the region. Additionally put down roots for further international institutional co-operation, by partnering up and bringing together both a Portuguese and a Norwegian municipality within the scope of the project. Malacate also started a community curatorial group created with residents of Mina de S. Domingos and the region, with responsibilities for monitoring and deciding on the artistic projects to be developed in the future, promoting an effective and relevant legacy in the community.

SDG: SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: National sustainable development policies and plans
Cultural Domain: Design,Performing Arts,Media Arts,Cinema and Audiovisual Arts,Music,Publishing,Visual Arts
Agency Implementation: Department of Arts
Main Feature: MIP-1 aims at raising the country's income status to lower-middle level by 2030 and to meet most of the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) whose end-line target is 2030.  Developing a Creative Arts and Heritage Industry is another strategies for the Urbanization Pillar of MIP-1. Among interventions for this strategy is the organization of promotional events, festivals, groupings and awards for the youth in creative arts and sports.
Results: The Department of Arts has encouraged and supported the organization of arts festivals by creative civil society organizations in different locations in the country including towns, cities, beaches of Lake Malawi and related venues.  The festivals during the reporting period (2020-2024) included Blantyre Arts Festival, Sand Music Festival, Tumanini Festival, Likoma Festival, Easter Theatre Festival, Art in The Park, Malawi Film Festival, Zomba City Festival.  All these festivals involved the movement of artists from one part of the country to another while others, like Sand Music Festival and Easter Theatre Festival, brought in other artists from both the Southern African Development Community (SADC) Region and  Europe.
