Title EN: Manitoba’s Francophone Tourism Strategy
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture
SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Cultural and creative sectors
Cultural Domain: Design,Performing Arts,Media Arts,Cinema and Audiovisual Arts,Music,Publishing,Visual Arts
Agency Implementation: Travel Manitoba
Main Feature: The Manitoba Francophone Tourism Strategy was launched in 2022 to increase the development and promotion of Manitoba’s Francophone tourism experiences and showcase the province’s distinct minority Francophone and Métis heritage and culture to Manitoban, Canadian, and international tourists. It is an implementation plan that envisions a collaboration led by Travel Manitoba between the public sector, the private sector, and civil society organizations to meet the targets highlighted in the broader Manitoba Tourism Strategy, namely: 1) Increase visitation to Francophone experiences and communities; 2) Increase visitor spending in Francophone experiences and communities.  A preliminary Francophone tourism business inventory conducted in 2020 and cited in the strategy document, identified a total of 368 Francophone tourism businesses operating in the province including events, culinary experiences, cultural attractions, outdoor recreation experiences, and accommodations. The 2017 provincial visitation data also reveals that Manitoba greeted 3,800 visitors from France and 51,000 visitors from Québec.  The Manitoba Francophone Tourism Strategy defines three strategic goals to enhance and position the sector: 1) Foster collaboration and build support for tourism; 2) Lead brand and market positioning; 3) Advance destination management.
Results: The Manitoba Francophone Tourism Strategy has led to a 2022 Travel Manitoba commissioned report on the economic impact of Francophone-inspired tourism in the province, which estimates that the sector generates between CAD 4.6 million and CAD 13.6 million per year. In 2023, Travel Manitoba released and update of their Francophone Marketing Plan, which responds to part of the “Lead brand and market positioning” strategic goal outlined in the strategy. The drafting of the Manitoba Francophone Tourism Strategy has also resulted in the creation of the Francophone Tourism Advisory Committee, which continues to consult Travel Manitoba on the Francophone tourism sector. The advisory committee unites representatives of the Manitoba Francophone tourism industry, the Francophone cultural and heritage sector, Métis associations, Francophone business development organizations, and provincial as well as municipal tourism agencies.  The measure drives awareness of French culture in St. Boniface and the 17 Francophone communities across the province, allowing to promote respect for the diversity of cultural expressions and raise awareness of its value at the local, national, and international levels.

Title EN: Marketing Guide for French-speaking Quebec music (MQF Guide)
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture
SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Cultural and creative sectors
Agency Implementation: Quebec Association of the Recording, Entertainment and Video Industry (ADISQ)
Main Feature: The Marketing Guide for French-speaking Quebec Music (MQF Guide) initiative, launched in 2022, represents an invaluable resource for professionals in the music industry, as well as for anyone interested in consumption habits of music in Quebec. This comprehensive guide offers a detailed overview of the behaviors and musical preferences of the French-speaking Quebec population, based on a large-scale survey conducted among 4,003 people in Quebec. One of the main characteristics of this initiative is its inclusive scope. Although designed primarily for music industry professionals, the guide is also accessible to everyone, making it a valuable resource for understanding the Quebec musical landscape as a whole. It offers a wealth of information on various subjects, ranging from the consumption of recorded music to attendance at performance halls, including sources of musical discovery. It also brings together a large number of resources available on the web aimed at promoting the discovery of musical content online and facilitating their marketing.  The MQF Guide also stands out for the richness of its data and the diversity of the analyses it offers. Survey results are presented in a clear and concise manner, allowing users to quickly grasp observed trends and behaviors. Additionally, in-depth analyses are available for those who wish to further explore specific topics. The development of marketing segments and targets brings real added value to the guide, by facilitating market research work for cultural actors who may not have the necessary resources to do so internally. Such tools can also serve as a basis for discussions with certain important players in the sector — for example, commercial radio stations, streaming platforms, and entertainment presenters. Presenting them with convincing data that demonstrates that Quebecers appreciate local music can help promote better visibility of Quebec music on the airwaves, online and in theaters, in the region and even beyond.  Another important feature of this initiative is its rigorous methodology. The survey was carried out by a professional firm in collaboration with ADISQ, thus guaranteeing the reliability and representativeness of the data collected. In addition, the results were weighted according to various demographic criteria to ensure an accurate portrait of the French-speaking population of Quebec, adding certain credibility to the data that can be used in audience studies, for example.  Finally, the MQF Guide is distinguished by its evolving nature. Thanks to financial support from the RadioStar Fund and the Quebec Ministry of Culture and Communications, this initiative is expected to develop and improve over time. Users are encouraged to share their comments and suggestions to continually enrich this valuable resource. It is therefore a guide, but above all a reference point allowing the gathering and popularization of essential data and knowledge for marketing that promotes the discoverability of the diversity of French-speaking musical cultural expressions.
Results: Since the publication of the first version of the guide, ADISQ has been regularly contacted by decision-makers, university researchers and journalists who claim to use this tool. The new edition of the guide has already interested several media who have presented it and several academics have already announced that they will integrate it into their courses. In the particular legislative and regulatory context that the Quebecer/Canadian music industry is going through (Bill C-11 and policy on commercial radio to name a few), this data is very important in contributing to the reflections of political decision-makers. Several data were also presented during hearings in which ADISQ participated (House of Commons, Senate, CRTC), allowing for political structuring that better takes into account musical cultural reality. Finally, the content of the guide was the subject of presentations at various conferences bringing together industry professionals or students as part of university presentations.  More concretely, the impacts can be observed through the different social network pages in this guide. For the Facebook page, publications relating to the guide receives around 100 interactions per publication with an engagement rate of 10% and for the LinkedIn account, so-called organic impressions amount to 400 impressions. Since the release of the guide, ADISQ has published articles on a regular basis in the perspective section of the website; these benefit from a similar commitment. Specifically, regarding the publication of the guide release announcement, for the Facebook page, it received 170 interactions with an engagement rate of 15% and for the LinkedIn account, the so-called organic impressions numbered 800. In short, this guide has had, and will continue to have, notable impacts on the literacy of music users and creators in Quebec, contributing to a richer and more easily discoverable cultural diversity.

Title EN: Mauritius Music Research Project by 3M
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture
SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Cultural and creative sectors
Agency Implementation: MOMIX (Moris Music Expo)
Main Feature: 3M (Moris Music Museum) MOMIX, as the project developer, establishes and implements the first music museum in Mauritius : 3M.   Located in the heart of the island, in Moka, this space is dedicated to the promotion of artists and cultural workers for music creation and production. In a dual momentum, both for the museum and production scopes, 3M aims at the conservation and transmission of the musical heritage of Mauritius island, as well as the structuring and professionalisation of the music industry in Mauritius. The musical heritage of Mauritius island is deeply rooted in the Mauritian cultural knowledge. A musical heritage from the past, but also from the present which gradually runs out each second. Then, by exhibiting this heritage, 3M is committed to promoting this cultural knowledge so as to democratise its access to the Mauritian population. This mandate opens the doors to knowledge that deserves to be shared, but above all, to be lived. The images, texts and sounds in the museum will enable people to experience what they have not experienced and to understand what has always existed. For the purpose of this reporting, the focus will be on action taken for the structuring and professionalisation of the music industry in Mauritius.
Results: MOMIX has launched the Mauritius Music Research project aimed at collecting music consumption and other industry-related data in the country. The study, spearheaded by the Department of Research and Development at MOMIX, will form part of the 3M (Music Museum Moris) project. By applying established research methods, the project seeks to collect representative data to provide relevant cultural statistics of the Mauritian music industry. The theoretical framework and methodological approach of the research were unveiled last year by MOMIX director Stephan Rezannah and the organisation’s research and development manager, Kimberly Oxide. This was followed by fieldwork to gather data earlier this year, with MOMIX research assistants Laëticia Botte and Stephan Ravaton going on the road to collect information from both public and private institutions across the island nation.  Online questionnaire Recently, MOMIX launched an online questionnaire intended for people living in Mauritius to collect information on music consumption in the country.  “We wish to collect and collate relevant data on music consumption in Mauritius, by approaching consumers present at concerts and festivals, among others,” MOMIX said. “Subsequently, we aspire to offer cultural statistics in the music industry in Mauritius. “It’s important to note that this research is fully funded by MOMIX for now and that there is a sponsorship call for the continuity of the research project.

Title EN: Measures that Facilitate Dialogue Mechanisms between CSOs and the Government regarding Policies
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture
SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Partnering with civil society
Cultural Domain: Design,Performing Arts,Media Arts,Cinema and Audiovisual Arts,Music,Publishing,Visual Arts
Agency Implementation: Ministry of Education, Culture, Research, and Technology (Kementerian Pendidikan, Kebudayaan, Riset, and Teknologi; Kemendikbudristek)
Main Feature: In the past four years, measures that facilitate dialogue mechanisms between CSOs and the government regarding policies include: 1. National Culture Week (Pekan Kebudayaan Nasional, PKN); and 2. Indonesian Culture Congress (Kongres Kebudayaan Indonesia, KKI).  PKN, held every two years since 2019, has been reported in the 2020 QPR. PKN is an implementation of Law 5 of 2017 on Culture Advancement (see Goal 1, Specific Policies that Regulate Culture and/or Creative Economy Sectors). In 2021, PKN was held online due to the COVID-19 pandemic, while in 2023, it was held offline in Jakarta with the theme "Caring for the Earth, Caring for Culture."  As in the 2018 KKI, which produced the Indonesian National Strategy for Culture document then later was adopted as a Presidential Regulation, the 2023 KKI had formulated the 2025-2045 Culture Advancement Master Plan (Rencana Induk Pemajuan Kebudayaan) (RIPK 2025-2045; see Goal 1, Policies on Cooperation Among Government Institutions) which is planned to be stipulated in the form of law. The formulation of RIPK 2025-2045 is a form of implementing the National Strategy for Culture, which has been specified in Presidential Regulation 114 of 2022 on the Strategy for Culture (see Goal 1, Main Policies and Measures that Contain Strategies and Frameworks for the Development of an Integrated Culture and Creative Economy Sector).   In general, measures that facilitate dialogue mechanisms between CSOs and the government regarding policies are aimed at contributing to achieving the following agenda(s) of the National Strategy for Culture: 1. Provide space for the diversity of cultural expressions and encourage cultural interaction to strengthen the inclusiveness of culture (Agenda 1);  2. Protect and develop values, expressions, and practices of traditional culture to enrich national culture (Agenda 2); and 3. Strengthen the role of the government as a facilitator of culture advancement (Agenda 7).
Results: PKN: In 2023, around 700 artists, 600 communities, more than 1000 cultural actors, and 223 residency points will participate.  KKI: The results of the 2023 KKI panel point to the urgency of forming a ministry that specifically handles culture in an integrated manner.  Here are the 10 points from the 2023 KKI results: 1. Affirming culture as the leading force in realizing Indonesian transformation. 2. The 2024-2029 period is a crucial stage in cultural advancement. 3. Freedom of expression that is safe and comfortable. 4. Cultural education is a "school of life." 5. Transformation of the governance of the Arts Council and/or Cultural Council into an institutional priority. 6. Cross-border cultural bonding at village and city levels in a participatory and inclusive manner. 7. Utilize digital technology to process data on the Regional Cultural White Papers, the Culture Development Index, the Indonesiana Program, and various community cultural harvests. 8. Indigenous and other local communities are sovereign subjects over their culture. Indonesia needs a body mandated for the promotion of culture. 9. The APBN/APBD model is aligned with the cultural framework.  The ideas in the KKI were then prepared as the 2025-2029 National Action Plan for Culture Advancement, which will become a blueprint for Indonesia's national cultural policy for the next five years.

Title EN: Measures to further improve the efficiency of the field of fine and applied arts

Area of Monitoring: Cultural and creative sectors
Agency Implementation: Uzbekistan Art Academy
Main Feature: At the Academy of Arts of Uzbekistan, the Workshop of artistic excellence (higher art courses, as a preparatory stage in the postgraduate education system) and the Center for retraining and advanced training of teachers and specialists in the areas of art education have been established. The main objectives of the Center are: ˗	retraining and advanced training of teachers and specialists in the fields of fine, applied arts and design, art history, museology of state higher and professional educational institutions, specialized schools of art and culture, as well as boarding schools, children's music schools and art; ˗	ensuring the educational process is conducted at a high level with the widespread use of modern forms and methods of teaching, effective pedagogical technologies, electronic information resources aimed at developing the knowledge and skills of talented young professional artists; ˗	improvement on a systematic basis of curricula and programs for retraining and advanced training courses, taking into account the widespread introduction of modern pedagogical and information and communication technologies into the educational process; ˗	formation of an educational and methodological base and coordination of the activities of retraining and advanced training courses for teachers and specialists in the areas of art education with the implementation of organizational and methodological management. The Workshop is entrusted with the following tasks: ˗	ensuring high quality works of fine art, full realization of the potential of creative artists in the fine arts; ˗	development of advanced teaching methods and introduction into the educational process of the experience of creative workshops while preserving the traditions of “ustoz-shogird” and art education; ˗	selection and improvement of the aesthetic level and skill of talented creative figures working in the fields of fine art (easel painting, graphics, monumental art, miniatures and sculpture); ˗	achieving reflection of national and universal traditions in works of art at a high level; ˗	organizing creative trips to foreign countries for young creators of higher art courses in order to make copies, exchange experiences and familiarize themselves with unique works stored in foreign museums and exhibitions; ˗	promoting the regular enrichment of the collections of museums in our country with works of fine art that have high artistic value.
Results: Activities were implemented in accordance with the Program of additional measures to further improve the efficiency of the field of fine and applied arts. In particular, the anniversary of Kamaliddin Bekhzod was held, measures were taken to strengthen the material and technical base and create the necessary conditions for students of specialized art schools and boarding schools of the Uzbekistan Arts Academy, measures were taken to stimulate employees of the system, the Investment programs provide for the necessary capital investments for construction on the territory adjacent to the main building of the National Institute of Arts and Design named after Kamаliddin Bekhzod, an auxiliary building, which includes an additional educational building, a modern information and library center and an exhibition gallery.
Recommandations: The action plan has been completed successfully, and the remaining planned tasks are being implemented.

Title EN: Measures to further improve the level of cultural services provision to the population
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture
SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Cultural and creative sectors
Cultural Domain: Design,Performing Arts,Media Arts,Cinema and Audiovisual Arts,Music,Publishing,Visual Arts
Agency Implementation: Cabinet of Ministers of the Republic of Uzbekistan
Main Feature: The main directions of state policy in the field of cultural activities are: ˗	state support for the development of culture; ˗	ensuring the integrity and safety of historical and cultural heritage, as well as supporting folk art; ˗	introduction of public-private partnerships into the field of cultural activities; ˗	meeting the cultural needs of the population and improving the quality of cultural services; ˗	creation and improvement of conditions for the realization of the creative potential of the population, including youth; ˗	improving the system of training young talents, training highly qualified personnel and improving their qualifications; ˗	creation of necessary conditions and a healthy competitive environment in the field of cultural activities; ˗	development of international cooperation.   In accordance with the Law of the Republic of Uzbekistan “On cultural activities and cultural organizations”, the basic rights and responsibilities in the field of cultural activities are defined. Thus, citizens of the Republic of Uzbekistan have the right: ˗	enjoy cultural achievements and participate in the cultural life of society; ˗	engage in creative activities on a professional or non-professional (amateur) basis as part of creative teams or independently; ˗	freedom to choose areas of cultural activity in accordance with one’s needs, interests and abilities (capabilities); ˗	own, use and dispose of cultural property in their ownership in the manner prescribed by law; ˗	use various symbols and other means of open expression of one’s opinion not prohibited by law during cultural events; ˗	to visit cultural objects, access to museum objects and museum collections included in the National Museum Fund, as well as access to information and library institutions and to information and library resources, as well as to archival documents in the manner prescribed by law. Foreign citizens and stateless persons on the territory of the Republic of Uzbekistan enjoy rights and bear responsibilities in the field of cultural activities on an equal basis with citizens of the Republic of Uzbekistan. Legal entities and individuals, in the manner prescribed by law, have the right to export outside the Republic of Uzbekistan and import into the territory of the Republic of Uzbekistan the results of their creative activities for the purpose of exhibiting, other forms of public presentation, as well as their sale. Concert and entertainment activities on the territory of the Republic of Uzbekistan and abroad are carried out by individuals and legal entities on the basis of a license for the right to carry out concert and entertainment activities issued by the Ministry of Culture of the Republic of Uzbekistan. On the territory of the Republic of Uzbekistan, touring activities of creative groups and individual performers are carried out on the basis of an agreement concluded with the customer. The main directions of international cooperation in the field of cultural activities are: ˗	international cultural exchange; ˗	cooperation with international cultural organizations; ˗	popularization of cultural objects and works of art. The Republic of Uzbekistan promotes the development of international cultural exchange, the main forms of which are: ˗	creation and development of national cultural centers; ˗	sending cultural workers for training (internship); ˗	creation and practical implementation of modern innovative technologies and technical means in the cultural sphere; ˗	demonstration of national customs and traditions; ˗	organizing and holding days of national culture, shows and competitions, festivals, exhibitions, conferences, literary seminars, tours and other cultural events; ˗	establishing mutual exchange of experience among cultural workers and other types of cooperation. The procedure for carrying out international cultural exchange is determined by international treaties and legislation of the Republic of Uzbekistan. In order to popularize cultural objects and works of art, the Ministry of Culture of the Republic of Uzbekistan, in collaboration with interested ministries, departments and institutions: ˗	organizes international competitions, festivals and exhibitions in all areas of culture and art; ˗	takes part in international competitions, festivals and exhibitions held outside the Republic of Uzbekistan; ˗	organizes “Days of Culture of Uzbekistan” in foreign countries. In order to popularize cultural objects and works of art, non-governmental non-profit organizations can also organize competitions, festivals and exhibitions. The government gives priority to work on the development of culture, establishing the activities of cultural organizations, strengthening their material and technical base, satisfying aesthetic needs and improving the quality of cultural services provided to the population in remote and inaccessible areas.
Results: In order to increase the level of provision of cultural services to the population, especially citizens living in remote areas and tourists, systematically organize tours of creative groups in the regions of the republic, effectively use the capabilities of cultural centers, expand the scale of support for talented young creative figures, and widely attract the private sector to the field, as well as the consistent implementation of the “Uzbekistan – 2030” Strategy, a calendar plan for cultural, mass, concert and entertainment events held at the republican level in 2024-2025 was approved, as well as regional calendar plans for 2024, including the regular holding of concerts entertainment programs by artistic groups operating on their territory, in government agencies, organizations and enterprises, in alleys and squares, in cultural and recreation parks, cultural centers. Organizational issues necessary to carry out the events defined in the plans at a high level are resolved in a timely manner. Target indicators for strengthening the material and technical base of amateur art groups are also being met. At the same time, all issues with the mobility of Uzbek and foreign art and cultural workers in the country and abroad will be comprehensively resolved. Also, according to the decision of the Cabinet of Ministers of the Republic of Uzbekistan dated 30.05.2019, the Directorate of International Festivals operates under the Ministry of Culture, and its main tasks are to train culture and art workers in all areas of Uzbek art for international festivals, pageants, as well as exhibitions, conferences, scientific-practical conferences and ensure participation in all other state events; to promote it widely in Uzbekistan and abroad, to preserve the most unique examples, to pass them on to the future young generation, and to carry out further popularization Also, based on the decision of the President of the Republic of Uzbekistan dated 09.12.2021, the Culture and Art Development Fund operates under the Cabinet of Ministers. The main tasks of this institution are as follows: expansion of international and interstate cultural relations, development of cooperation with international cultural organizations and charity funds in the field of culture and art, attraction of foreign investments and grants, support for the development of patronage of culture and art in our country; to establish intercultural creative dialogue and support the integration of Uzbek art into the world artistic and cultural space, as well as to demonstrate aspects related to the cultural, scientific and technical potential and competitiveness of our country; improvement of the system of training, retraining and improving the skills of personnel in the field of culture and art, at the same time, providing culture and art institutions with the necessary literature and periodicals.  According to the Decree of the President of the Republic of Uzbekistan in 2023 "On measures for effective organization of state management in the field of culture and tourism within the framework of administrative reforms", "ERP culture" is preparation of preliminary project estimates for the introduction of the management system has begun. This web portal is planned to start its operation in September 2025, and the platform "Training and online education" and its mobile application will be introduced in this electronic system. Based on the decisions of the President of the Republic of Uzbekistan on the international promotion of the art of Maqam and Bakhshi, crafts, dance art, and music at the international level, every year since 2018, the International Maqam Art Conference in the city of Shahrisabz and Zomin district, the International Festival of Bakhshi Art in the cities of Termiz, Nukus and Gulistan have been held every, "Sharq Taronalari" International Music Festival in Samarkand, International Crafts Festival in Qoqand, Lazgi International Dance Festival in Khiva, International Film Festival in Tashkent are held. More than 2,700 foreign participants from 87 foreign countries, well-known culture and art workers have systematically participated in these events in recent years.
Financial Ressources: In 2023-2024, the amount equal to 684,000 USD has been spent on stimulating the creative activities of artists and culture professionals and sending them to local and foreign tours.
Recommandations: Organization of cultural events related to the mobility of artists and culture requires careful preparation, including analysis of the situation, determination of the topic, objectives, choice of the form of implementation of the plan, collection of information, formulation of goals and drawing up cost estimates. For policies and measures implemented at the state level to be effective, all aspects of this activity must be taken into account.

Main Feature: The Romanian Cultural Institute supports the participation of artists and cultural professionals of Romanian expression in relevant European and international events (major festivals, book fairs, art fairs and exhibitions etc) through specific mobility and creation funds and through financial support like grants and allowances. The financial support and the partnership for cultural projects are based on criteria of international visibility.  Examples: -	Funding: The Romanian Cultural Institute provides funding for artists to participate in international exhibitions, workshops, festivals, or conferences. This financial support enables artists to travel and showcase their work globally, both in the countries where the Romanian Cultural Institute is represented, as well as in countries where they are proposed by Romanian embassies or in different contexts where Romanian artists are invited. In countries where the Romanian Cultural Institute has branches (representations), funding is ensured through the Directorate General Representations Abroad and historical communities, based on the annual workplans put forward by the representations abroad. The essential elements for a cultural project to be eligible for support are: high value content; traditional cultural content; new/original cultural elements; cultural content produced by young artists; a reasonable ratio between investment and impact; integrated promotion; segmentation of audiences before the proposal of cultural content; attractiveness for families (children, parents); the prestige and renown of local partners and of the area where the event takes place. The branches of the Romanian Cultural Institute pursue the establishment/continuation/consolidation of the relations with the bilateral organizations, the Romanian cultural organizations, the honorary consulates, the Romance languages departments in the respective cultural areas, to ensure the proportional cultural presence of Romania on the territory of the host country.  Another funding programme of particular importance, that provides non-refundable grants for cultural initiatives in the field of visual arts (plastic arts, decorative arts, science/research and architecture, design, new media, photography, performance) and performing arts (theatre, music, dance) is the CANTEMIR Programme. This programme targets events organized exclusively abroad (outside Romania) and not in partnership with the local branches of the Romanian Cultural Institute.  This ensures a balanced approach, to allow as many independent actors as possible to organise cultural projects worldwide.   Every year, the cultural operators are invited to submit grant applications. Any Romanian or EU-based Natural Person, individual entity, family enterprise or private or public legal entity can participate to the selection process, provided that such entities are cultural operators, have no debts to the state central or local budget and have complied with their obligations under the previous non-refundable sponsorship contracts. The projects are assessed by a selection commission. The CANTEMIR Programme aims for artistic excellence, originality, encouraging the fusion of innovative and experimental artistic forms; the European dimension, the international cooperation / co-productions; the contribution to an improved visibility of Romanian culture and of the interest for the same on the international cultural markets, by facilitating the access to representative Romanian artistic works; attracting the audience by the project artistic/cultural value and relevance; supporting the partnerships of Romanian and foreign cultural operators, on one side, and on the other side the International cultural organizations.  Networking and Partnerships: the RCI facilitates connections between Romanian artists and their counterparts abroad. It supports cultural events, exhibitions, and collaborations, allowing artists to build networks and explore new artistic horizons (examples: participation in international art fairs like: Art Paris, Paris Photo, Art Basel, Art Brussels, ARCO Madrid, Supermarket Stockholm Independent Art Fair, Drawing Now Art Fair – Paris, ARCOlisboa, viennacontemporary, etc. as well as present with their own stand at the most important international book fairs or at international film festivals where Romanian films are screened:  -Residencies and scholarships: RCI collaborates with international cultural centres and organizations to offer artist residencies. These residencies provide artists with the opportunity to live and create in different countries, fostering cross-cultural exchange and creativity (examples: Constantin Brâncuși Scholarships - art,  George Enescu Scholarships - music,  Woodrow Wilson Scholarships – research, Scholarships in Romania for Foreign Cultural Journalists  and scholarships in Romanian for foreign researchers).  These initiatives provide an important basis for international exchanges.  - Cultural seasons – the most recent one is the Romanian – Polish season, developed by the Romanian Cultural Institute in collaboration with the Ministry of Culture.  -Romanian language courses for foreigners and the Brașov Summer School (annual programme).
Results: -	Projects funded by the Cantemir programme in 2023: 26 projects  -	11 scholarships in 2022 -	22 scholarships in 2023
Financial Ressources: Budget for the Cantemir programme in 2023: approximatively 500 000 USD Budget for scholarships in 2022: 35.500 EUR + 42.000 USD Budget for scholarships in 2022: 80.000 EUR + 28.000 USD
Recommandations: The programmes and actions have good results in ensuring a balanced flow of artists and cultural professionals.

Title EN: Methodology for Determining the Level of Consumption of Illegal Content in Lithuania
Goal: Promote Human Rights And Fundamental Freedoms
SDG: SDG 5 - Achieve gender equality and empower all women and girls,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels
Area of Monitoring: Artistic freedom
Agency Implementation: Ministry of Culture of the Republic of Lithuania
Main Feature: In June 2023, under the initiative of the Ministry of Culture of the Republic of Lithuania, a methodology was designed to determine the level of illegal content consumption among the Lithuanian population and a pilot study to test methodology was carried out.   The methodology enables consistent monitoring of digital piracy trends and related dynamics. The methodology allows for periodic surveys to monitor the consumption of illegal content (films, series, videos, TV programmes, sports broadcasts, music, e-books and audiobooks, magazines, sheet music, video games, educational content and software) by the Lithuanian population, to determine the public's attitude towards digital piracy, and to monitor the public's illegal content consumption habits and attitudinal changes. Such monitoring will provide a basis for evidence-based policy in this area, help assess the effectiveness of such policy and periodically adjust its directions and objectives.  The Methodology considers the following legal, political and administrative measures in the area of protection of copyright and related rights: -	legislation of the Republic of Lithuania. -	European Union legislation. -	The Copyright and Related Rights Protection Programme administered by the Lithuanian Council of Culture. the powers granted to the Lithuanian Radio and Television Commission to block websites and their copies that unlawfully publish copyright-protected content, and the powers to issue binding instructions to a payment, financial or other institution to stop payments or other financial transactions to an entity conducting copyright infringing activities on the Internet. The main aim of the study to test the methodology (for more detail look: https://www.kulturostyrimai.lt/wp-content/uploads/2023/10/Nelegalaus-turinio-vartojimo-metodika-ir-tyrimas_2023.pdf) was to assess  attitudes and habits of the population  towards the illegal use of copyrighted content (piracy), and to monitor changes in such  attitudes. The questionnaire consisted of a series of questions: consumption habits of legal and illegal content, reasons for choosing such content, consumption patterns and negative consequences of its consumption, public knowledge, beliefs and attitudes towards illegal content, communication in the social space and in the family, as well as ancillary questions.  This tested methodology will be used to calculate a piracy index in a biennial survey.  The index is a derivative of two groups of indicators: one describing illegal content consumption habits and the other describing attitudes of acceptance and tolerance of illegal content consumption.  The target group of the survey is the Lithuanian population aged 14-64 who use the Internet, with an additional distinction between the population aged 14-29.
Results: The results from the pilot study show the following: 45% of the population consume pirated content in some category at least sometimes.  29 % of the Lithuanian population consume pirated content regularly. 48 % of the population consider at least one method of accessing or disseminating pirated content online to be acceptable. 38 % of the population are tolerant of piracy by at least one of the aspects measured.  24 % of the population report being unable to distinguish between legal and illegal access to online content. 59 % of the population lack information about the harm caused by pirated content and legal access to online content.  62 % of the population consume legal paid content.
Financial Ressources: Development of Methodology for Determining the Level of Consumption of Illegal Content in Lithuania and Pilot Survey  - approx. USD 27700  (EUR 24 829)

Area of Monitoring: Media diversity

Main Feature: The UK Government is committed to a pluralistic media landscape, where citizens are able to access information from a range of sources in order to form opinions. The public’s ability to access a wide range of news, views and information about the world in which we live is central to the health of our democracy.    Under the Enterprise Act 2002, the DCMS Secretary of State has a quasi-judicial role in considering whether mergers raise media public interest concerns. They can intervene in a merger where she believes there may be a public interest concern.    The media public interest regime has two broad purposes. Firstly, it allows for action to be taken in cases which (notwithstanding any competition concerns) may narrow the range of media providers or restrict the public’s choice of media e.g. the coverage of news and current affairs. Secondly, it enables action to be taken if there are significant concerns about whether an acquirer of a significant UK media company will respect the UK’s traditions for accuracy in news and free expression of opinion or (in TV and radio cases) have a less than genuine commitment to broadcasting standards.

Title EN: Mise en place du Programme d’appui à l’entrepreneuriat et à l’autonomisation des filles et femmes
Goal: Promote Human Rights And Fundamental Freedoms
SDG: SDG 5 - Achieve gender equality and empower all women and girls,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels
Area of Monitoring: Gender equality
Agency Implementation: Centre d’Autonomisation et d’Entrepreneuriat Féminin (CAEF)
Main Feature: En République de Guinée, le Centre d’Autonomisation et d’Entrepreneuriat Féminin (CAEF) a mis en place en août 2021 un programme d’appui à l’entrepreneuriat et à l’autonomisation des filles et femmes. L’objectif global de ce programme est de contribuer à l’autonomisation des filles/femmes à travers leur implication, leur participation, et partage accru des dividendes de la croissance économique. Il est axé sur quatre objectifs spécifiques, à savoir : 1-	Renforcer l’insertion socio-économique de 6.000 filles/femmes ; 2-	Promouvoir et renforcer l’entrepreneuriat féminin ; 3-	Contribuer à la réduction des pesanteurs socioculturelles liées au rôle de la femme dans la société guinéenne ; 4-	Renforcer les capacités opérationnelles et institutionnelles des bénéficiaires y compris l’Equipe de Coordination du Programme. Le programme s’investit fortement dans l’amélioration de l’employabilité des filles et femmes à travers la formation et le développement des compétences qui visent leur insertion dans les bassins d’emploi au niveau local et/ou l’auto-emploi par des interventions ciblées : -	la formation professionnalisant de qualité et aux stages en entreprises pour les filles/femmes ; -	Les filles/femmes évoluant dans les Centre d’Autonomisation et d’Entrepreneuriat Féminin (CAEF), les groupements et dans les Micro, Petites et Moyennes Entreprises (MME) actives dans l’agriculture, la pêche, les mines, l’artisanat, le commerce, l’assainissement, etc. seront accompagnés afin d’augmenter leur revenu et d’assurer la durabilité de leurs activités au fils du temps ; -	les filles/femmes bénéficieront de l’assistance technique et organisationnelle dans les organisations de base à vocation économique (CAEF, groupements, associations, ONG et organisations faîtières). -	les filles et femmes bénéficieront d’un accompagnement rapproché pour la réussite de leur projet d’Entrepreneuriat individuel et collectif. Dans la phase de mise en œuvre du programme, des actions sont envisagées pour faciliter l’accès au financement et à sa bonne gestion assortie de la mise en place d’un fonds de garantie en partenariat avec les Institutions de Micro Finance (IMF) et les banques primaires de la place à l’effet de réduire les coûts de financement. Dans le cadre de l’appui aux approches d’idées comportementales (behavioral insights), le programme a mis en place des activités de recherche et a testé des modèles d’intervention pour promouvoir des changements d’attitude relatifs aux Violences Basées sur le Genre (VBG).
Results: La mise en œuvre de la mesure a permis d’atteindre les résultats suivants : -	6.000 filles/femmes ont bénéficié d’une formation professionnalisant de qualité et aux stages en entreprise ; -	Les filles/femmes évoluant dans les CAEF, les groupements féminins à vocation économique et dans les Micro, Petites et Moyennes Entreprises (MME) actives dans l’agriculture, la pêche, les mines, l’artisanat, le commerce, l’assainissement ont été accompagnées afin d’augmenter leur revenu et d’assurer la durabilité de leurs activités au fil du temps. Une approche portant sur la chaine de valeur a été mise en place afin de mieux organiser les filières en mettant un accent particulier sur la transformation, le conditionnement, la conservation et la commercialisation sous des labels spécifiquement guinéens ; -	100 000 filles/femmes ont bénéficié d’une assistance technique et organisationnelle dans les organisations de base à vocation économique (CAEF, groupements, associations, ONG et organisations faîtières) ; -	50 filles et femmes ont bénéficié d’un accompagnement rapproché pour la réussite de leur projet d’Entrepreneuriat individuel et collectif.

Title EN: National Workshop Schools [Escuelas Taller] Program of Colombia
Goal: Integrate Culture In Sustainable Development Frameworks
SDG: SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: National sustainable development policies and plans
Cultural Domain: Design,Performing Arts,Media Arts,Cinema and Audiovisual Arts,Music,Publishing,Visual Arts
Agency Implementation: Ministry of Cultures, Arts, and Knowledge - Directorate of Heritage and Memory
Main Feature: The National Workshop Schools Program aims to train different sectors of the population, particularly young people, using the non-formal methodology of “learning by doing,” creating job connections and promoting cultural entrepreneurship. It establishes a link between teachers of cultural crafts and traditional skills recognized by their communities, for their empirical knowledge of the particularities of their region, and apprentices between fourteen and thirty-five years old who become peace builders by learning a skill or craft, seeking to transform their situation of vulnerability. Therefore, the program is aimed at: allowing the qualification of cultural trades, thus improving employment opportunities. Priority is given to young people exposed to the effects of armed conflict, lack of opportunities, educational attrition, and unemployment. Moreover, training is combined with work, guaranteeing the future employability of apprentices. The strategy thus aims to promote civil society's access to cultural training as a tool for social inclusion, employment, and cultural entrepreneurship.
Results: With the learning-by-doing model, more than 6,000 young people during the period 2020-2024 have acquired skills and knowledge in cultural trades, and have also accessed technical and complementary training courses, such as cooking, filigree jewelry, gardening, pottery, blacksmithing, furniture making, luthiery, galope de piedra, riverside carpentry (boat building), and traditional construction techniques (tread wall, adobe, acacia, and mud).

Title EN: Ministerial ordinance (resolution) No. 17-2024 publishing general guidelines of conduct for the media in public performances, radio or television
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture

Area of Monitoring: Media diversity
Agency Implementation: Ministry of Culture and National Commission for Public Performances and Radio Broadcast (CNEPR)
Main Feature: The ministerial ordinance published the general guidelines of conduct for the media in public performances, radio or television, both in live, recorded or retransmitted broadcasts, in accordance with national regulations. Some key aspects of the ordinance are: 1.	Every broadcast (radio or television) should avoid the use of foul language, considered a harmful and perturbing influence for the harmonic development of children and youth. 2.	Every radio or television broadcast should promote, be based on, and proyect good civic and citizen values, and the respect to the principles of social morality, human dignity and family links. 3.	Every radio or television broadcast should avoid malicious expressions, perverse words or imagery, dual meaning phrases, the vindication of crime or violence, and all that may be degrading to the civic cult of national heroes or any person. 4.	Every radio or television broadcast should try to elevate the cultural level of the society, the preservation of the national character, customs and traditions, the purity of the language and exalt Dominican values. 5.	Every radio or television broadcast should have educational objectives within articles 63, 64, 8 and 38 of the Constitution of the Dominican Republic, and thus 6.	Every radio or television broadcast should entertain, educate, inform and promote arts and culture. The ministerial ordinance also encourages alternative communications and media platforms to emulate the general guidelines, under numeral 11 of article 63 of the Constitution that states that media outlets, private and public, should contribute to civic education.
Results: The measure has been celebrated by traditional media outlets. Some newcomers hace approached the Ministry for guidance on the implementation of the guidelines.

Title EN: Minority language broadcasting in community radio services
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture

Area of Monitoring: Media diversity
Agency Implementation: Ofcom
Main Feature: The Community Radio Order 2004 outlines how community radio services are local services that provide for particular communities in order to deliver social gain. The Order therefore indirectly makes provisions for community radio to serve minority language communities (e.g. Cornish-speaking radio services such as Radyo An Gernewegva).   Community radio stations of this kind are not-for-profit entities and use any profit that is produced in the provision of the service exclusively for securing or improving the future provision of the service, or for the delivery of social gain to members of the public or the community that the service is intended to serve.  As noted previously, the Community Radio Order 2004 outlines how community radio services are local services that provide for particular communities in order to deliver social gain. Community radio stations play a central role within communities and cater directly to their needs. Often they are wholly reliant on the work of a small number of volunteers. Many of these stations broadcast content that works to address local issues in an accessible way. This often takes the form of targeted programmes for young people or for people of specific cultural heritage. E.g. The Beat 103.6 is a community radio station in North-West London that produces content for local young people that directly deals with the issues facing them, such as knife crime or registering to vote. It also provides volunteering opportunities for young people within the community and offers them training in areas such as radio production, broadcasting, researching etc.

Title EN: Mise en place d’un cadre institutionnel pour la protection et la promotion de la femme au Bénin Identification et catégorisation des artistes par discipline
Goal: Promote Human Rights And Fundamental Freedoms
SDG: SDG 5 - Achieve gender equality and empower all women and girls,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels
Area of Monitoring: Gender equality
Cultural Domain: Design,Performing Arts,Media Arts,Cinema and Audiovisual Arts,Music,Publishing,Visual Arts
Agency Implementation: Institut national de la Femme
Main Feature: Créé en République du Bénin par décret No 2021_391 DU 21 JUILLET 2021, l’Institut national de la Femme est un établissement public à caractère social et scientifique dénommé « lnstitut national de la Femme ». Il est chargé d’œuvrer à la promotion de la femme aux plans politique, économique, social, juridique et culturel aussi bien dans la sphère publique que privée et de lutter contre toutes les formes de discrimination et de violence à l'égard de la femme. L'Institut national de la Femme est le cadre de concertation avec les organisations de la société civile qui œuvrent à la protection et à la promotion de la femme.  A ce titre, il :  -	dresse un état des lieux sur la problématique de toutes les formes de violences et plus généralement de toutes les formes de discrimination à l'égard de la femme et de la fille, initie et conduit des études et de la recherche en la matière ;  -	évalue I'impact de toutes les formes de violences et discriminations sur l'inclusion des femmes dans le développement durable, leur participation à la vie publique et politique, et leur épanouissement au sein de leur famille ;  -	assure la production, la diffusion et l'actualisation de toutes informations, toute documentation, toutes archives, et toutes données à caractère statistique, législatif et réglementaire outillées par sexe en général, et relatives à la femme et à la fille au Bénin en particulier ; -	participe à l'élaboration des politiques, stratégies, plans et programmes d'action visant à la protection et la promotion des femmes et des filles au Bénin ; -	participe à la supervision et à la coordination de la mise en œuvre de ces politiques, stratégies, plans et programmes d'action et y apporte son concours technique et opérationnel ;  -	propose des outils et donne des avis techniques pour faciliter cette mise en œuvre et notamment élabore des codes de conduites, des guides, manuels, protocoles, à l'usage aussi bien des acteurs publics que des acteurs privés ;  -	participe à l'évaluation des résultats de la mise en œuvre de ces politiques, stratégies, plans et programmes d'action ;  -	évalue les actions initiées dans le cadre de la protection et de la promotion des femmes et des filles par les acteurs des secteurs publics, privés et par les organisations de la société civile ;  -	appuie l'intégration d'une démarche soucieuse de l'égalité homme-femme dans tous les secteurs ;  -	œuvre à l'amélioration du statut juridique de la femme et notamment évalue la législation en vigueur, et propose des réformes ou de nouvelles lois ;  -	organise la lutte contre toutes les formes de discrimination à l'égard de la femme : violence physique, psychologique, économique, harcèlement sexuel, lévirat, mutilations génitales féminines, exploitation et traite, mariage forcé, mariage précoce, etc... et mobilise I'appui en faveur de cette lutte ;  -	organise un dialogue social sur l'élimination des attitudes traditionnelles, coutumières, religieuses et stéréotypées qui perpétuent la violence et les autres formes de discrimination à l'égard des femmes et des filles avec les acteurs politiques, religieux, ceux de la société civile, les autorités traditionnelles, les élus locaux, en vue :  •	de mener la réflexion sur l'influence que certaines traditions, coutumes et pratiques religieuses exercent sur les mentalités de la collectivité, et sur leur rôle dans la perpétuation de la violence à l'égard de la femme ;  •	de travailler à I'identification de valeurs culturelles promouvant le statut de la femme et interdisant toute discrimination à son endroit, en vue de leur valorisation;  •	de faire jouer l'influence de ces acteurs auprès des communautés pour l'élimination des coutumes et pratiques relatives à la succession et aux biens matrimoniaux qui ont une incidence négative sur le statut des femmes ;  •	d'amener ces acteurs à soutenir et faciliter les efforts déployés en vue d'éliminer l'exclusion des femmes de la vie politique et publique ; -	anime un cadre de concertation avec les organisations de la société civile qui œuvrent à la protection et à la promotion des femmes ; -	d'amener ces acteurs à soutenir et faciliter les efforts déployés en vue d'éliminer l'exclusion des femmes de la vie politique et publique ; anime un cadre de concertation avec les organisations de la société civile qui œuvrent à la protection et à la promotion des femmes ;  -	fournit des informations, des conseils et offre une assistance à toute personne concernant la législation en vigueur et les moyens de faire valoir ses droits en cas de violence et de toutes formes de discrimination ;  -	mène en concertation avec le ministère en charge de l'Action sociale des actions de sensibilisation pour le grand public et certains groupes cibles ;  -	identifie et propose des actions en renforcement des capacités des acteurs intervenant dans la chaîne de la prise en charge holistique des victimes de violences basées sur le genre et d'autres formes de discrimination ;  -	propose ou contribue à la conception d'un module pour une formation diplômante à caractère universitaire sur les questions liées au genre, à l'égalité de droits et d'opportunités entre les femmes et les hommes dans le secteur privé, public, militant et associatif, et l'organisation de cette formation dans les universités du Bénin ;  -	veille à la disponibilité des services publics d'accueil, d'hébergement à titre transitoire, et de prise en charge médicale, sociale, psychologique et juridique des victimes de violences basées sur le genre et d'autres formes de discrimination ;  -	œuvre à l'intégration des hommes dans les stratégies de sensibilisation et de levée de barrières sociales, culturelles et religieuses;  -	participe à l’élaboration et à la validation des rapports périodiques dus au titre des instruments régionaux et internationaux ratifiés par le Bénin ainsi qu'à leur présentation devant les comités et autres mécanismes compétents ;  -	participe activement à tous les débats internationaux et régionaux relatifs à la protection, la promotion des femmes et leur participation au développement ;  -	assure la vulgarisation de toutes les lois, de toute la réglementation et des instruments internationaux ou régionaux de protection et de promotion des femmes et assure une communication sociale permanente à leur sujet ;  -	organise les journées internationales, africaines et nationale relative à la protection et la promotion des femmes ;  -	identifie et propose à la Grande Chancellerie des hommes et des femmes qui se sont distingués dans la protection et la promotion des femmes, pour des récompenses ou distinctions honorifiques ;  -	anime un service d'écoute, veille à la disponibilité d'une ligne d'assistance pour tout signalement et reçoit les dénonciations de victimes ou de personnes ayant connaissance de faits de violence ou de discrimination ; -	soutient les victimes de façon optimale et notamment les assiste face à toute structure ou administration accusée ou soupçonnée de discrimination à leur endroit;  -	exerce des actions en justice, se constitue partie civile devant les juridictions ordinaires et également devant toutes juridictions spécialisées.  -	veille à la dotation conséquente de lignes budgétaires affectées à la mise en œuvre des attributions de l'institut, par l'autorité de tutelle, les ministères et les communes.
Results: -	des communautés impactées et sensibilisées sur les droits des femmes ;  -	engagement des leaders religieux et têtes couronnées en faveur des droits des femmes ;  -	accroissement des  dénonciations de cas de  Violences Basées sur Genre (avant il y avait plus de peur et de pudeur même à dénoncer au regard du poids des traditions, etc.), -	accroissement du nombre de décisions de justice rendues depuis la création de l'Institut avec parfois de très lourdes condamnations.

Title EN: Minsk International Film Forum "Listapad"
Goal: Achieve A Balanced Flow Of Cultural Goods And Services And Increase The Mobility Of Artists And Cultural Professionals
SDG: SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 10 - Reduce inequality within and among countries,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Mobility of artists and cultural professionals
Agency Implementation: Ministry of Culture of the Republic of Belarus  Festival Directorate
Main Feature: The first Listapad Film Forum was held in Minsk in 1993, until 2002 it was called the International Film Festival of the CIS Countries and Baltic States. In 2013, the Minsk International Film Festival Listapad received permanent accreditation from the International Federation of Film Producers Associations and entered the list of the most prestigious film forums where such world-famous film forums as Berlin, Venice, Warsaw, and Moscow festivals are included. There are six international jury panels at the "Listapad", each of which determines the winners and awards prizes in the nominations. The most prestigious awards of the festival are the Grand Prix "Listapad Gold" ("For the best film"), "Listapad Silver" ("Film as an art phenomenon", awarded by the International Film Press Jury), "Listapad Bronze" (audience award for the best feature film). Prestigious awards are presented in documentary film competitions, the children's and youth film competition "Listapadzik". The Prize of the President of the Republic of Belarus A.G. Lukashenko "For Humanism and Spirituality in Cinema" has also been established. More than 30 thousand spectators attended the events of the XXX Minsk International Film Festival "Listapad", which was organized in November, 2024. The festival was filled not only with film screenings, but also with various cultural and educational events. A total of 24 such events were held, the venues for which were the Academy of Arts, the Belarusian State University of Culture and Arts, the Belarusfilm film studio, the House of Moscow, and the All Saints Memorial Church. These were film screenings, meetings with celebrity guests, and master classes. They were attended by more than 1.7 thousand spectators. The festival continued to confirm its international status. It featured films from India, China, Iran, Russia, Zimbabwe and other countries. The main themes of the anniversary "Listapad" are the 100th anniversary of Belarusian cinema and the 30th anniversary of the festival. During the festival, about 130 films from more than 40 countries were shown. The 30th film festival collected a record number of applications – more than 3.5 thousand. The geography of the participants is also impressive – films were presented by 120 countries, including China, Brazil, India, Iran. Over the course of a week, the forum covered dozens of Belarusian cities. More than 600 screenings took place.
Results: 1) effective implementation of the state cinema policy; 2) increase in the domestic film production and audience; 3) the best visibility and recognition of the Belarusian film industry; 4) strengthening the position of cinema in the national cultural and educational system; 5) ensuring mobility of Belarusian cinematographers and promoting their art; 4) an acquaintance with the best foreign practices in the film industry and the transfer of experience; 5) formation of a high social and cultural status of the cinema and the involvement of young filmmakers in the industry.
Financial Ressources: No data available
Recommandations: The Ministry of Culture of the Republic of Belarus with the wide participation of the civil sector carries out the evaluation of the results of the festival constantly. Based on monitoring, the recommendations have been developed for improving management, expanding the capabilities and the geography of the festival, attracting additional funds and new stakeholders.

Title EN: Mis-and-disinformation hub. Chile leads OECD group against disinformation.
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture
SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Media diversity
Agency Implementation: Ministry General Secretariat of Government and Ministry of Science.
Main Feature: In November 2022 the Ministry General Secretariat of the Presidency (SEGPRES) incorporated Chile in the working group of member states of the Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD), whose goal is to address disinformation and fake news, understanding that they constitute a threat to the country's democracy. The Mis-and disinformation Hub ecomprises Chile, Norway, Greece, Lithuania, Luxembourg and Finland.   One of the objectives of this working group is to provide a space where countries can develop an exchange around their policies and regulations on the matter, identifying good practices and effective measures around the so-called fake news that emerge on different platforms and media within society. Its work places special attention on digital literacy, as well as around the effects of disinformation on children and youth.   The group, or Mis-and-disinformation Hub, is the first of its kind in the history of the OECD and will operate for two years. Chile is the only Latin American country involved. We can note that the inclusion of Chile in the Mis-and-disinformation Hub is part of the "policies and measures that support diversity of content in the media" indicator within the monitoring framework of the 2005 Convention.
Results: As part of the implementation of the policy, in May 2023, a presidential decree was published in the Diario Oficial (Official Journal), that creates a ministerial advisory commission named "Advisory Commission against Disinformation", of a temporary nature and with the aim of guiding the minister of Science, Technology, Knowledge and Innovation and the Minister Secretary General of the Government on matters related to the analysis of the global disinformation phenomenon and its development within the national territory.   The "Advisory Commission against Disinformation" has the duty of focusing on the following topics: impact of disinformation on the quality of democracy, education and disinformation, digital literacy, disinformation on digital platforms, good international practices and comparative experience, public policy and disinformation. The commission is composed of 9 experts that represent public universities, private universities, regional universities, civil society organisations and organisations dedicated to fact-checking.   The commission presented two reports. The first*, published towards the end of August 2023, was a general assesment about the disinformation phenomenon around the world and in the Chilean context. The final report**, released on 4 December, highlights the threat of disinformation on social networks and makes 72 recommendations, among them: to strengthen co-operation with international governance bodies that are dealing with the problem; guidelines for the State regarding electoral processes, cyber-security and public health; diverse measures on information, media and digital literacy and measures for strengthening the media and research around disinformation.  * Available at: https://www.minciencia.gob.cl/noticias/informe-desinformacion/  ** Available at: https://minciencia.gob.cl/uploads/filer_public/f5/fc/f5fc81c1-a990-4eec-87bef3b43108beeb/informe_ii-comision_contra_la_desinformacion-04-12-23.pdf
Financial Ressources: Without funding.

Title EN: Mladi Levi International Festival
Goal: Achieve A Balanced Flow Of Cultural Goods And Services And Increase The Mobility Of Artists And Cultural Professionals
SDG: SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 10 - Reduce inequality within and among countries,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Mobility of artists and cultural professionals
Agency Implementation: Bunker, Ljubljana
Main Feature: International festival Mladi Levi is one of the more prominent annual events of the Bunker Institute, bringing the most current stage performers from all over the world to Ljubljana every end of the summer, since 1998. It bears a mark of a demanding artistic profile, placed within the arena of contemporary progressive theatre and takes pride in its reputation for discovering young talents. The Festival has a distinctive atmosphere, marked with curious audience of all generations and encourages social connection. Festival Mladi Levi inhabits a place of encounters and surprises, continuously opening up to foreign artists and guests, who take pleasure in art and spread contemporary artistic or social topics in front of one another. It is a place of exchange as well as a source of new ideas, friendships and co-operations, which frequently extend beyond the local concepts or borders in the process of their growth. During the Mladi Levi festival we are hosting around 45 events yearly, presenting a very diverse array of forms of artistic expression– from innovative contemporary theatre performances to contemporary dance performances, from contemproary circus performances to musical scores, from performative installations and artistic walks to actions in public space. The invited works are often critical, socially engaged, dealing with important societal, political, environmental and artistic topics.  To provide ample space for developing the topics that artists explore through their works, we also organize traditional festival discussions in public spaces, international forums and conferences, various workshops, and a festival school for the elderly. Additionally, we offer cultural education programs for teachers and students, numerous social events in public spaces that attract families and young people, and international gatherings of cultural workers and project partners. These gatherings include networking meetings, discussions, and artistic events. Each year we host around 200 foreign artists and international cultural workers or journalists that come to participate at the festival. We collaborate with the artists from numerous countries – most of the artists are coming from the wider Europe, and some from Asia as well as Northern America.Our priority area of interest is the Western Balkans – we host artists from the Balkan countries in different capacities every year, with their artistic performances or as participants in debates and workshops or as a part of our collaborations in numerous international projects, which very often have meetings during the Mladi Levi festival in Ljubljana. We are interested in building connections and collaborations also with the artists of Eastern Europe, Ukraine, Turkey, Georgia, Armenia and Azerbaijan. With artists and cultural operators from the above mentioned countries we collaborate through various international projects (such as Balkan Express or Create to Connect, Create to Impact or Act, Climate, Transition …). Our collaborations with the artists and artistic organisations from Africa and South America are more sporadic (we feel there is a need for more approachable sources of financing for nurturing connections with these parts of the world). We are collaborating with the artists from these countries through international research and artistic projects (such as Transkmaking) and consequentially we are able to invite them to present their work or participate in conferences and discussions that we organize within the Mladi Levi festival.  In the programme of Mladi Levi festival we are presenting well established artists and young artists side by side, so they can meet each other, see each other’s work and build connections. Since the beginning of the festival, we have also had a strong focus on supporting younger artists at the beginning of their professional careers by presenting them at the Mladi Levi festival (where international curators and artists can see their work), and thus giving them a strong push in starting their international careers and touring.
Results: Throughout the years, Mladi Levi festival hosted more than 1000 international events, in the last four years alone more than 160, ranging from performances to installations, from concerts to actions in public space, artistic walks, immersive projects, artistic protests and various other forms of artistic expression.  Only in the last four years, the festival hosted more than 700 international guests – artists, cultural operators, journalists, students of arts studies, and so on.  The festival organised various discussions, forums and conferences which tackled important social topics (with a strong focus on environmental issues, the issues of social and gender equality and the role of arts in the changing society, trying to reimagine and reshape a fairer and better functioning world) as well as educational programmes for various groups of people – young people, the elderly, professionals, high school kids and students.
