Title EN: National Film Board of Canada’s Support of Emerging Filmmakers
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture
SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Cultural and creative sectors
Agency Implementation: National Film Board of Canada (NFB)
Main Feature: To foster skills development and knowledge transfer in the fields of filmmaking and the audiovisual arts, the NFB allocates a portion of its production budget every year to projects by emerging filmmakers and other emerging creators. Filmmakers and creators are regarded as emerging if they are in the process of directing their first, second, or third work in a given category of production (films, interactive works, etc.). In addition to providing this ongoing support, each year the NFB carries out initiatives specifically targeting emerging artists.   The main initiatives carried out during the past four years include:  NFB XP (2nd edition): a lab that the NFB has launched to test new ideas and find technological solutions to the challenges of animating and producing films. NFB XP seeks to encourage more experimentation by animators, as well as by creators and innovators from related disciplines. NFB XP gives creators the freedom to explore an idea, a particular issue, a method, a technique or a new tool related to their field and is aimed at creators who do not have access to the resources that they need to conduct such experiments and have not yet had the opportunity to work with the NFB.  5 Shorts Project (4th edition): an NFB initiative to explore the short documentary genre in collaboration with artists’ centres and production centres from Quebec’s various regions. Presented in partnership with the Paralœil production centre in Rimouski, Quebec, the 4th (2020) edition of the NFB’s 5 Shorts Project cast the spotlight on talented emerging documentary filmmakers from Quebec’s Bas-Saint-Laurent region.  The new NFB creative lab called Alambic, offering to three emerging directors/craftspeople of any age the opportunity to create an animated film of less than three minutes during a six-month period. It’s an initiative that’s aimed at the next generation of French-speaking animators.  Hothouse (13th and 14th editions): an intensive mentorship program, supported by the NFB English Program Animation Studio, that offers emerging animation filmmakers opportunities to receive training and create their own projects. In keeping with the NFB’s established practice, these two editions of Hothouse provided paid, three-month apprenticeships in the NFB’s professional animation film production environment.   The Jeunes pousses digital apprenticeship program (4th edition) at the NFB’s Interactive Studio: open to all students at all universities in Canada, as well as to all students in the final year of a trade program at a CEGEP in Quebec. Delivered in partnership with Akufen, an award-winning, Quebec-based digital-production studio, the 4th edition of Jeunes pousses gave students the opportunity to explore new storytelling formats and to test their knowledge, skills and initiative in a real-world production environment.   The Repêchage initiative (3rd edition): launched in 2015 by the NFB’s Documentary Studio in collaboration with the Université du Québec à Montréal (UQAM), gives graduates of UQAM’s Media School the opportunity to produce their first professional films at the NFB.   The NFB’s Filmmaker Assistance Program (FAP): provides technical services and support to emerging independent filmmakers to help them complete their films or videos. FAP does not provide cash funding. It provides assistance in the form of technical services, with a maximum value of CAD 3,000 or CAD5,000 (equivalent to USD2,268 and USD3,781 respectively using the Bank of Canada exchange rate on December 29, 2023), depending on the region where the filmmaker lives, to support the production of documentary, animation and short fiction works in film or video format.
Results: As a result of the projects, initiatives and ongoing support that the NFB offers, many emerging filmmakers and other emerging creators have been able to develop their skills and acquire practical production experience by creating original, innovative animated, documentary and interactive works in a real-world production environment, with the support of professional teams. These programs offer a great springboard for their professional careers and provide them with relevant, persuasive credentials. Overall, in fiscal year 2022–2023, 65% of the productions completed at the NFB were the work of emerging creators.
Financial Ressources: In fiscal year 2021–2022, 37.7% of the NFB’s production spending—CAD 5,730,541 (equivalent to USD 4,332,862 using the Bank of Canada exchange rate of December 29, 2023)—was allocated to works by emerging creators. This amount includes spending on the ongoing commitments to emerging artists and the targeted initiatives described above.  This measure directly supports cultural and creative sectors and protects and promotes the diversity of cultural expressions at the creation and production levels of the cultural value chain.
Recommandations: The NFB will continue to invest, in order to pass its rich legacy on to future generations of creators, contribute to the training of emerging talent and support the development of film, animation and digital culture in Canada and around the world.  The various creative opportunities that the NFB offers to emerging filmmakers propel their careers and increase their chance of success in the Canadian audiovisual sector. Most of these initiatives allow emerging creators to gain the necessary experience in a high-level production environment, with the support of professional teams. The NFB also supports participating creators in terms of distribution and broadcasting. The opportunities to develop one's expertise, know-how and confidence, to build one's portfolio and professional network through the NFB's various initiatives intended for emerging artists are all guarantees of a successful creative career.

Title EN: National Handcrafts Export Strategy
Goal: Achieve A Balanced Flow Of Cultural Goods And Services And Increase The Mobility Of Artists And Cultural Professionals
SDG: SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 10 - Reduce inequality within and among countries,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Flow of cultural goods and services
Agency Implementation: Ministry of Investments, Trade and Industry
Main Feature: The global market value for handicrafts is estimated at US801.8billion and is projected to grow to USD 855.7 billion by 2020. These estimates are extrapolated from the home accessories market often used to estimate the demand for handcrafted goods. According to the NEDPS Handicraft Sector Working Group, Kenya’s share of this market is quite small, given the country’s annual average exports of USD 15 million. The untapped export potential of Kenya’s handicraft industry compared to the magnitude of global handicraft trade paint a bright future for the handicraft sector. This prospect is to be exploited through strategic interventions that have been proposed in this strategy to address a myriad of constraints that have hitherto impeded handicraft export growth. The handicraft products targeted for export trade under the NEDPS, based on existing and potential capacity for their production are as follows: Handmade/hand-decorated fabrics, Leather crafts, Basketry, Woodwork & Crafts, Metalwork & Crafts, Jewellery, Soap Stone carving, Pottery and Ceramics, Beads, and Traditional Artefacts. A review these products’ current exports values reveal a decline of 58% over a four-year period, from USD 67.2 million in 2012 to USD 28.3 million in 2016. The hardest hit was handmade and decorated fabric handcrafts which had accounted for 79% of total handicraft exports in 2012. The immediate goal under the NEDPS framework will be Integrated National Export Development and Promotion Strategy Plus Implementation Plan 11 to support the development and promotion of these products’ exports targeting to increase the exports to the 2012 level as a minimum. This will require handicraft exports to grow at an average of 25% over the four-year period 2018-2022. The Projected export growth is contigent on constrints and challenges that have limited handicraft export performance in the past being addressed. The strategy has proposed various interventions which are designed to address these constraints and to stimulate handicraft production for export. The resource requirement to implement intervention activities foreseen under the NEDPS is estimated at KES 5.2 billion over the period 2018 to 2022. Out of these required resources, 88% is to go into supporting new products development and production of handicraft products designed for specific exports markets and promotion of the handicraft products in the identified destination markets. The prospects for handicraft export growth are quite bright going by the target destination country annual market size estimates that over the period 2014-2016 were estimated at USD 353 billion. These target market countries and regions are as follows: USA, EU, Middle East, Japan, China, EAC, COMESA, and Gulf Cooperation Countries (GCC). Kenya’s exports to these markets over the same period averaged USD 57 million or 0.02% of these countries’ combined market size. Therefore, if Kenya were to aim at taking a 5% share in these target markets, Kenya’s handicraft exports would increase in value to USD 17.6 billion per year. This is the horizon of Kenya’s handicraft export possibilities that will be pursued under the NEDPS.
Results: Improved  participation by crafts enterprises in international trade Capacity of Crafts men and women  improved through training and branding of their products (Made In Kenya)

Proigualdad coordinates efforts among various agencies and entities of the Mexican government, in collaboration with all three branches and levels of government, to respond to the needs of women citizens and ensure their rights and well-being. This specialized program represents a pivotal shift through its six primary objectives, 37 strategic priorities, and 267 targeted actions.  Annually, public sector entities in Mexico, as part of the National System for Gender Equality (SNIMH), commit to executing strategic public policy actions promoting gender equality. To promote productive activities among women across sectors such as education, culture, economics, environment, labor, and tourism, the Federal Government has implemented various initiatives through social programs. Several public awareness campaigns have been launched targeting the general public, government officials, and strategic sectors like education and health. National Programme on Equal Opportunities for Women and Men 2015–2021 supported: - promoting employment and work opportunities for women and men; - seeking balanced participation of women and men in decision-making and high-ranking positions; - improving the efficiency of institutional gender equality mechanisms; - promoting gender mainstreaming in education and research, culture, healthcare, environmental protection, the national defence and access to justice; - implementing EU and international gender equality commitments. Commission on Equal Opportunities for Women and Men set up by Resolution No 266 of 7 March 2000 of the Government of the Republic of Lithuania oversaw coordination of implementation.  Municipalities, women’s organizations, gender studies centres, social partners and other relevant bodies were encouraged to cooperate in implementation of the Programme to reduce inequalities of different situations of women and men. Different ministries, including the Ministry of Culture of the Republic of Lithuania, were responsible for the implementation of the concrete measures.  In the field of culture following tasks were envisaged to be implemented: - promoting adherence to the gender equality principle when assessing contributions of country’s artists to culture and arts and allocating financing for cultural projects; - encouraging a stronger involvement of men in cultural initiatives.

Artistic Freedom: 'Study on Social Conditions of Artists'). Main Feature: The National Recovery and Sustainability Plan is a recovery and resilience mechanism - part of the Next Generation EU (2021-2024) instrument of the Recovery and Sustainability Plan (RSP).  The plan aims to contribute to the economic and social recovery from the crisis caused by the COVID-19 pandemic, to restore and develop the growth potential of the economy and to achieve resilience to negative externalities.  Investment c11.I7 Digitalisation of museum collections, libraries and archives Operating Agreement SPOR-43/04.05.2023 for the implementation of Investment C11.I7 Digitalisation of museum collections, libraries and archives (Project 43) of the Recovery and Sustainability Plan of the Republic of Bulgaria is programmed by the Ministry of Culture (MoC) and is currently being implemented by the Ministry as lead partner with final beneficiaries (see below). The investment is the only initiative at national level so far with a policy claim and a longer impact horizon in the field of management of our cultural heritage - digitization, preservation, conservation and promotion, as well as to ensure broad access of users at national and international level to the cultural wealth of our country. So far, individual institutions or municipalities have worked on different programmes to offer their own solutions for digitisation and access to their cultural assets. Alongside this investment, the National Culture Fund (NCF) participates in specific measures related to the implementation of the cultural policy foreseen in the Plan, namely the Development of the cultural and creative sectors investment (C11.I6), Project 42, with implementation period 2022-2026. Responsibility for the implementation of the investment is assigned to the National Fund for Culture, which is designated as the Monitoring and Reporting Entity (MRE) and the Final Recipient (FR) for the Development of the Cultural and Creative Sectors Investment (C11.I6) by the PPA No. 157 of 2022. The planned resource is EUR 96.8 million.  In terms of the structure under the NRSP, the National Culture Fund is recognised as an integral part of the process.
Results: The policy area of the NRSP: social inclusion. Objective: to comprehensively reform the state's policies on digitization, preservation, conservation and promotion of cultural heritage, and to ensure free access to our country's cultural wealth for all stakeholders at national and international level.   In Bulgaria, there is some, but definitely unsatisfactory, experience in the field of digitization, as well as available digitized cultural content. The types of cultural content are in various forms and varying degrees of digitisation depending on the category to which they belong. Each of the final recipients of the investment is at a different stage of digitisation, with some of the institutions having their own platform. The need for a common platform to synchronise these digital content management systems has been identified. The aim is to bring the information from the different institutions together in one place, to create a common environment to enable intelligent search across different types of cultural heritage. is 2023 - 2026.  mobilising the expertise of various stakeholders to give our country a chance to authoritatively find a way out of the situation it is in regarding the topic under discussion. The project has the following specific objectives: •	To introduce 	uniform standards for digitization (capture, storage, description and processing) of the different types of movable heritage stored in the collections of museums and art galleries, libraries, BNF, BNT, BNR, and BNA. Title EN: National recovery and resilience Plan/ “Capacity building per gli operatori della cultura per gestire la transizione digitale e verde”

Area of Monitoring: National sustainable development policies and plans
Agency Implementation: Ministry of Culture- General Directorate "Creatività Contemporanea"
Main Feature: The entire value chain of the national cultural and creative sectors has been heavily affected by the COVID-19 pandemic both by the uncertainties generated by the forced closure of cultural events and venues and by the alarming and consequent reduction of cultural habits. In this context, the intervention aims to support the recovery and innovation of the cultural and creative sectors.          Targeted for investment are the cultural and creative sectors which are based on cultural values,  and artistic and  creative expressions, whether,  or not,  market-oriented.
Results: 113 capacity-building projects have been selected to access grants put out by the Ministry of Culture and will be implemented throughout the country, with the aim of supporting the activities of cultural workers to manage the ecological and digital transition of the entire cultural and creative supply chain.
Recommandations: (Objectives and expected impacts)          The overall objective is to support the recovery and revitalization of the cultural and creative sectors as defined by the Creative Europe program, i.e., all sectors whose activities are based on cultural values and artistic and other individual or collective creative expressions, whether market-oriented or nonmarket-oriented, including the following areas: architecture, archives, libraries and museums, artistic crafts, audiovisual (including film, television, video games and multimedia), tangible and intangible cultural heritage, design (including fashion design), festivals, music, literature, performing arts, (including theater and dance), books and publishing, radio and visual arts. In particular, the specific objective is to foster the generation and establishment of new models of cultural offerings supported by digital technology, which help reach new audiences in safe conditions while ensuring the fair remuneration and social security of operators and the economic sustainability of cultural and creative enterprises.                  The specific objective is to foster the generation and establishment of new models of cultural offerings supported by digital technology, increasing managerial and economic knowledge and skills that help reach new audiences in safe conditions while ensuring the fair remuneration and social security of operators and the economic sustainability of cultural and creative enterprises.                  Capacity building projects must involve the implementation of activities aimed at the development and transfer of skills and knowledge aimed at upgrading the value chain from a digital and technological perspective. Specifically, the projects will aim to accompany and guide cultural operators (public and private) in the retraining of the value chain in a digital and technological key, helping and guiding them in adopting and increasing the application and use of digital and innovative solutions within their cultural production, management and organization processes, providing supporting tools and knowledge.                  Capacity building projects may include:                  - training activities;                  - exchange of best practices;                  - peer learning moments;                  - adoption of cooperative strategies.

Title EN: The project BOOST
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture
SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Cultural and creative sectors
Agency Implementation: Kulturelle Samråd I Danmark
Main Feature: During the last years, an increased European interest in the potential of amateur arts, voluntary culture, and heritage to foster social inclusion can be witnessed. This is reflected in a range of publications and projects focusing on this interconnection. Based on this data, own research, and results of the former Erasmus+ development project BRIDGING, the partnership circle shares the view that the huge civil society sector of amateur arts, voluntary culture, and heritage in the European member states not only provide joy, friendship, and meaning for the participants, but it also supports and promotes added community values, such as social inclusion, social cohesion, and active citizenship. We are aware that most leaders, learning providers and volunteers in the sector know of the potential of their work to support added community values. Yet, how this can be done and what categories and practical questions need to be considered when working on this objective is often unclear. Therefore, we think this potential for fostering added community values can be improved by a more conscious development work. Until now, the leaders and learning providers in the sector can use many good practice examples as inspiration and support. However, there is a need for more systematic tools and methods on how to concretely assess their own activities and implement improved practice; and the overall aim of the BOOST project is to develop new tools and methods to support the actors in the sector of amateur arts, voluntary culture, and heritage to work more consciously and systematically in promoting the added community values of their cultural activities.
Results: The Programming and thus the target groups have been expanded in all four partner countries. The Danish Practice Partner wants to work with children/young people as well as adults in the future and to address them through the programme initiated by an action plan. Take A Part Carlow wants to involve the community more in order to increase engagement and participation. Glej, the Slovenian Practice Partner, through the use of BT, has found that new target groups with different backgrounds can be addressed, included and also equipped with social skills: “We also saw that the programme enables a rise in social competences which can be then used in everyday life of participants.” The Polish Practice Partner Spichlerz has also made adaptations in this category through the project partnership: “In programme planning we paid attention to offering content, activity etc. to every social and age group. We want to offer something to everyone interested in participating in our events.”

Title EN: National Survey of Cultural Consumption (ENCC)
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture
SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Cultural and creative sectors
Cultural Domain: Design,Performing Arts,Media Arts,Cinema and Audiovisual Arts,Music,Publishing,Visual Arts
Agency Implementation: Secretariat of culture
Main Feature: The National Survey of Cultural Consumption is consolidated as a public policy for the production of information on the population's cultural practices and consumption. Due to the outbreak of the Covid-19 pandemic, the third edition of the ENCC had to be postponed for a year in order to maintain statistical rigor and guarantee the comparability of the data with previous editions. In addition, with the conviction that such a survey would provide valuable and accurate information on the time after the infection, the approach of the study was expanded and updated, incorporating both academics from the field of culture and communication, as well as the Ministry's management teams. In turn , by generating information on the territorial distribution of cultural practices and consumption, it becomes a fundamental tool for planning and implementing federal public cultural policies.   Objectives:   To learn about the habits, practices and cultural consumption of the Argentine population, and the different regional scenarios of the country. To generate information for the design of public policies and evidence-based decision making. To promote academic research and the development of the private sector linked to the cultural industries, to detect access gaps and trends that allow for the generation of more precise and effective public policies.
Results: It was applied to the population aged 13 and over, residing in private households in urban agglomerates with more than 30,000 inhabitants.   Field work was conducted between November 2022 and January 2023. The questionnaire kept 93 questions from previous editions and included new queries suggested by academic researchers, public cultural managers and cultural industry professionals.  It was carried out through home interviews and personal application, the format adopted was structured and the extension reached around 179 questions. Stratification was considered in seven regions of the country: CABA, GBA, Centro, NOA, NEA, Cuyo and Patagonia. As in previous editions, within each stratum a random selection (with probability proportional to size) of census radii and blocks of dwellings was made; for the final selection of the respondent within the household, a strategy combining a random selection of dwellings through systematic sampling (with an oversample to compensate for non-response) and a selection by sex and age  (adjusted by census parameters) was used.  The sample size was 3,380 effective cases and the margin of error for the main indicators of the study was +/-3%.
Recommandations: The editions carried out provide information on various sectors of the cultural industries, the transformations of their production and monetization modalities from the point of view of demand; digital practices, mass consumption, the use of platforms, access and participation in the field of tangible and intangible heritage, and practices related to artistic training and community culture. Its sample design makes it representative at the national level, allows for regional readings and allows segmenting the information according to age, educational and socioeconomic level, gender, and so on.   The ENCC data can also be used by other public agencies that, for example, require the characterization of consumer groups or that attend to the planning of sectorial economic policies, such as the Ministry of Social Development, ANSES (National Social Security Administration)  the Ministry of Production, among others. In addition to public agencies, the ENCC information is used by business chambers, entrepreneurs and cultural managers to, for example, define cultural circuits, programming lines and characterize entrepreneurial sectors, among other actions. Universities and researchers are also frequent users of the data collected in the cultural consumption surveys. The results of this edition call especially for studies and research derived from the cultural consumption patterns of the population, the role of recommenders, the determinants of consumption.   The press and data journalism or journalism specialized in cultural issues is also a user of the information gathered in the ENCC and is a fundamental actor for the development of content and data analysis on cultural consumption and habits.  Future editions will improve the diagnosis by incorporating information over time, since the differences between the results of one edition and the next may respond to temporary issues or to permanent changes in habits, so that only periodic surveys can produce series and identify lasting changes in cultural consumption habits.

Main Feature: In the past four years, policies and measures that support the supply of data and information trends on media diversity include: 1. Law 16 of 1997 on Statistics (Law on Statistics); 2. Law 14 of 2008 on Open Public Information (Keterbukaan Informasi Publik) (Law on KIP);  3. Draft Law on Amendments to Law 16 of 1997 on Statistics (Draft Law on Statistics); 4. Draft Law on the Integration of Development Data (Draft Law on the Integration of Development Data); 5. Presidential Regulation 39 of 2019 on One Indonesian Data (Satu Data Indonesia); 6. Minister of Communication and Informatics Regulation 2 of 2021 on the 2020-2024 Ministry of Communication and Informatics Strategic Plan; and 7. Ministry of Communication and Informatics One Data Portal (Satu Data Kominfo).  Two fundamental policies related to the provision of data and information that have not been reported in the 2016 and 2020 QPR are the Law on Statistics and the Law on KIP (see Goal 1, Policies and Measures on Information Systems and Cultural Statistics Used in Policy Development). In recent developments, stakeholders have identified a real need to update the Law on Statistics to be more responsive to current developments and all its challenges and opportunities. In the National Legislation Program (Program Legislasi Nasional, Prolegnas), the Draft Law on Statistics is one of the priorities for completion in 2024. At the time of drafting this report, it has already entered the drafting stage. Another relevant draft law related to providing data and information trends about media diversity registered in Prolegnas is the Draft Law on the Integration of Development Data. However, unlike the Draft Law on Statistics, the Draft Law on the Integration of Development Data is not yet a priority for completion in 2024. Title EN: New European Agenda for Culture
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture
SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Cultural and creative sectors
Cultural Domain: Design,Performing Arts,Media Arts,Cinema and Audiovisual Arts,Music,Publishing,Visual Arts
Agency Implementation: European Commission
Main Feature: In 2018 the Commission adopted a New European Agenda for Culture, to reflect the evolution of the cultural sectors since the 2007 European Agenda for Culture. This also responded to calls from the Leaders of the EU27 for “a Union where citizens have new opportunities for cultural and social development and economic growth, a Union which preserves our cultural heritage and promotes cultural diversity”.     The New European Agenda for Culture Communication COM (2018) 267 and its accompanying Staff Working Document provide the framework for cooperation on culture at the EU level.  The Agenda has three strategic objectives: -	Social dimension – harnessing the power of culture and cultural diversity for social cohesion and well-being -	Economic dimension – supporting culture-based creativity in education and innovation, and for jobs and growth -	External dimension – strengthening international cultural relations. These three pillars focus on the positive contribution that culture brings to Europe’s society, its economy and international relations. The Agenda also sets out enhanced working methods with Member States, civil society organisations and international partners.   The New European Agenda for Culture also refers to the UNESCO 2005 Convention.
Results: (See specific actions under the Annual Work Plans for Culture)
Recommandations: In 2022, the European Parliament published a Report on the implementation of the New European Agenda for Culture and the EU Strategy for International Cultural Relations.  The report was drafted following intensive consultations with stakeholders and based on numerous written contributions and sources, including the European Parliamentary Research Service (EPRS) study published in September 2022 entitled “Culture: in or out?” and the Commission’s report of 29 June 2022 on the Work Plan for Culture 2019-2022. In addition to this, meetings of the Shadow Rapporteurs with stakeholders were organised in June, July and September 2022, where experts from academia, civil society and representatives of the Czech Council Presidency were invited to share their perspective on the implementation of the two documents and give recommendations on the way forward, particularly in view of the adoption in Council of the Work Plan for Culture 2023-2026.  The report addressed most of the themes outlined in the New Agenda for Culture, with a special focus on the accessibility of culture in an inclusive way, the availability of funding opportunities at EU level, the engagement of civil society in the co-designing and co-creation of cultural policies and projects, and the contribution of culture and tangible and intangible cultural heritage to social cohesion, sustainable development and the fight against climate change.  The report acknowledges the overall satisfactory implementation of the New European Agenda for Culture.

Title EN: Nouvelle loi relative à l’activité audiovisuelle
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture

Area of Monitoring: Digital environment
Agency Implementation: •	Ministère de la Communication
Main Feature: La loi n° 23-20 du 2 décembre 2023 relative à l’activité audiovisuelle a été promulguée et a pour « objet d’organiser l’activité audiovisuelle et de fixer les règles relatives à son exercice ».  Elle encourage le libre exercice de cette activité et stipule que « l’activité audiovisuelle est librement exercée dans le respect des principes énoncés par les dispositions de la Constitution, de la loi organique relative à l’information, de la présente loi, de la législation et de la réglementation en vigueur ». Vu l’importance de l’activité audiovisuelle, sa pratique est associée, dans le présent texte de loi, à un nombre de principes, notamment le droit du citoyen à une information objective et transparente, le respect de l’expression plurielle des courants de pensée et d’opinion, le respect de la dignité humaine et la protection de l’enfant et de l’adolescent. Au plan national, l’on dénombre aujourd’hui plusieurs chaines audiovisuelles dites « off-shore », dont le siège social est établi en dehors du territoire national. Ainsi, il est indispensable de les intégrer au paysage médiatique national en étendant dans la présente loi sur l’audiovisuel, l’activité des services de communication autorisés aux chaines généralistes. Une modification significative portant sur les procédures d’octroi des autorisations qui sont les mêmes et pour les chaines audiovisuelles dites classiques et pour les chaines audiovisuelles en ligne. Au plan du contenu, la présente loi introduit une série de dispositions dont les plus importantes portent sur :  •	La mission concédée à l’établissement public de télédiffusion d’Algérie, d’assigner les fréquences destinées aux services de communication audiovisuelle, après attribution par l’Agence Nationale des Fréquences ;  •	La consécration de l’exclusivité de la télédiffusion à l’établissement d’Algérie par tout moyen technique approprié ; •	L’extension de l’autorisation des services de communication audiovisuelle thématique aux services de communication audiovisuelle généraliste ; •	L’obligation de détention d’un capital social exclusivement national ; •	La possibilité d’autoriser la création d’un service de communication généraliste ou audiovisuelle en ligne et/ou thématique ;  •	L’élargissement des missions de l’Autorité Nationale Indépendante de Régulation de l’Audiovisuel ; •	L’alignement des Web TV et Web radio sur les services audiovisuels autorisés ; •	L’obligation pour les services de communication audiovisuelle de se conformer à un cahier des charges (charges générales et particulières) ; •	L’octroi aux seules autorités judiciaires le pouvoir de suspendre ou de retirer les autorisations de création des services de communication audiovisuelle ; •	La mise en place d’un cadre juridique pour l’exercice des activités de production, de tournage et de diffusion de contenus audiovisuels sur tout support ; •	La création d’un organisme public chargé de préserver, de conserver et de mettre en valeur le patrimoine audiovisuel national.
Results: La loi n° 23-20 du 12 décembre 2023 relative à l’activité audiovisuelle fixe les droits et obligations de toutes les parties concernées. L’Etat algérien reconnaît expressément une liberté de communication audiovisuelle et affiche une franche volonté de stimuler davantage les investissements privés et publics pour rendre ce secteur compétitif au niveau national et international. En Algérie, la politique nationale de communication vise à consolider les droits des professionnels des médias et à tracer de nouvelles perspectives pour la mission de l’information et de la communication. L’intérêt de l’Etat pour le secteur de la communication s’articule autour de plusieurs thèmes indépendants visant à renforcer le paysage médiatique national par la création de nouvelles chaines thématiques.

Title EN: Nyanga Arts Festival
Goal: Integrate Culture In Sustainable Development Frameworks
SDG: SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: National sustainable development policies and plans
Agency Implementation: Nhimbe Trust
Main Feature: Established in 2022, the Nyanga Arts Festival is an initiative of Nhimbe Trust, in partnership with Montclair Hotel & Casino, aimed at enhancing the leisure industry in Nyanga by amplifying its eco-friendliness through culture, creativity and cultural expressions. The festival in an effort of contributing to target 8.9 of the SDGs which calls on stakeholders to devise and implement policies to promote sustainable tourism that creates jobs and promotes local culture and products. The location of Nyanga in the mountainous Eastern Highlands promotes tourism suitable for both local and international consumption. The entry point of the festival therefore is to draw visitors in through vibrant artistic programming that makes the rural district an attractive tourism prospect for music lovers and tourists seeking a richer tourism experience. The festival also acts as a platform that brings awareness to important social and environmental issues with an end goal of improving lives, preserving natural resources and sustainably benefiting the Nyanga community. The overall vision is for Nyanga Rural District to become the leading eco-friendly heritage tourism destination in Zimbabwe, and a leader in sustainability and climate action. The festival enjoys the approval and cooperation of the Ministry of Sport, Recreation, Arts and Culture and the National Arts Council of Zimbabwe, as well as the partnership of corporate companies.  The festival is built on four main strands; free live performances for rural communities to facilitate their access to cultural life, paid live performances, golfing, and capacitation trainings on various subjects. Community performances are attended and officiated by the Chief and traditional leadership, signalling a cultural celebration of dance, music and drinking festivities. Local artists, schools and community members are programmed for performances, in addition to artists from surrounding towns.
Results: Through cooperation with the Zimbabwe Tourism Authority, the first edition of the festival housed a capacitation seminar for hoteliers, tour operators and event organisers, with Nhimbe Trust facilitating training on destination festivals. The training focused on how Nyanga Rural District can be co-created through cultural policy making, with those in the value chain of tourism playing a key role in destination festival designing.  Alongside 9 diverse acts staged for rural communities in 2022, was inclusion of an enthralling one-man theatre piece titled AN ACT OF MAN, raising awareness of climate change, rain making ceremonies, and the importance of preserving culture and conserving natural heritage. The festival brought to the attention of the locals the need to sustainably conserve and preserve the climate in a world engulfed by climate change and global warming. Such conservation coupled with artistic performances presented a formidable force in tackling climate change while promoting artists and celebrating culture. In its two years of existence the Nyanga Arts Festival has enjoyed a global online footprint in 71+ countries.

Title EN: Obligations d’investissement indirect dans la production : le système de taxes affectées au financement des aides
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture
SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Cultural and creative sectors
Agency Implementation: Centre national du cinéma et de l’image animée (CNC)
Main Feature: Tel que détaillé dans la mesure précédente, le financement de la création cinématographique et audiovisuelle en France repose sur un principe selon lequel « l’aval finance l’amont ». Deux mesures servent cet objectif, les obligations d’investissement direct dans la production (voir mesure 1 ci-dessus) et les contributions fiscales au fonds national de soutien au cinéma, à l’audiovisuel et à l’image animée administré par le CNC.  Ce fonds est exclusivement financé par trois taxes affectées :  1.	La taxe sur la vidéo et la vidéo à la demande (TSV) : elle est assise sur le chiffre d’affaires des secteurs de la distribution de vidéo physique (DVD, Blu-ray) et de la vidéo à la demande (VàD). Elle est également due par les plateformes établies hors de France mais visant le marché français. Son assiette intègre par ailleurs les recettes publicitaires tirées de la diffusion de vidéos en ligne. Des exonérations sont prévues pour les sites qui ne diffusent pas de la vidéo à titre principal, pour les sites d’informations et de presse et pour les sites dédiés à la promotion du cinéma et aux bandes annonces. Son taux est de 5,5 %.  2.	La taxe sur les services de télévision (TST) : elle comporte un volet éditeur (TST-E) et un volet distributeur (TST-D).  •	La TST-E est assise sur les recettes de publicité et de parrainage (y compris sur la télévision de rattrapage), des appels surtaxés et SMS, ainsi que sur les ressources publiques des chaînes de télévision. Les éditeurs de services de télévision ne diffusant pas de programmes aidés par le CNC ne sont pas assujettis à la taxe. Son taux est de 5,15 %.  •	La TST-D est assise d’une part, sur les abonnements et autres sommes acquittées par les usagers en rémunération d’un ou plusieurs services de télévision (avec un abattement de 10 %). Elle est assise d’autre part sur les abonnements et autres sommes acquittés par les usagers en rémunération d’une offre internet, dès lors que celle-ci permet de recevoir des services de télévision (en pratique les offres haut débit). Un abattement de 66 % est alors appliqué pour tenir compte de la pluralité des usages de ces abonnements.
Results: Ces taxes affectées abondent chaque année le fonds de soutien au cinéma, à l’audiovisuel et à l’image animée du CNC (voir ci-après les chiffres pour l’année 2023). Elles permettent de financer, d’une part, le fonctionnement du CNC et, d’autre part, la quarantaine de dispositifs d’aides qu’il administre en faveur du soutien aux œuvres cinématographiques et audiovisuelles européennes. Plusieurs segments de la chaîne de valeur sont ainsi financés et à différents niveaux dont voici les axes principaux :  -	Soutien à la création cinématographique et à la diffusion en salle ;  -	Soutien à la création audiovisuelle et multimédia ;  -	Soutien à la diversité de la création et à la diffusion auprès des publics ;  -	Soutien aux actions en faveur du patrimoine cinématographique ;  -	Soutien à la diffusion vidéographique et à l’innovation technologique ;  -	Soutien à la coopération et à la diffusion internationale et européenne.  Ce système, lié aux obligations d’investissement directes (mesure 1) et à la chronologie des médias (mesure 3), a prouvé son efficacité en bénéficiant aux secteurs cinématographiques et audiovisuels sous différents aspects :  -	Activité économique au global : les secteurs couverts par le CNC, impacts directs, indirects et induits confondus, ont généré 38 milliards de dollars (35,5 Mds€) de chiffre d’affaires, 16,38 milliards de dollars (15,3 Mds€) de valeur ajoutée, soit 0,7 % du PIB et 149 400 ETP, soit 0,6 % de l’emploi en France ou 244 500 effectifs totaux, intermittents inclus (non convertis en ETP).  -	Audience : avec 181 millions d’entrées, la France est le pays où la reprise post-Covid est la plus forte au monde. Le marché du film français est le premier de l'Union européenne en termes de fréquentation. En ce qui concerne l'audiovisuel, 97 % des audiences françaises de fiction concernent des productions françaises.  -	La part de marché pour les films français s’élève à 40 %.  -	Export : dans l'audiovisuel, les ventes de programmes atteignent un niveau record (230 millions de dollars, soit 215 M€, soit 5 % de plus que le précédent record de 2017). En cinéma, la somme des ventes internationales et des préfinancements étrangers des films français atteint 431,36 millions de dollars, soit 403 M€, soit 6,3 % de plus qu'avant la crise.
Financial Ressources: 819,14 millions de dollars (764,7 M€).
Recommandations: Succès critiques : en 2022, les films français représentaient 25 % des sélections des dix plus grands festivals.

Results: •	In 2021-22, the AcceleratiON Program provided 32 companies with CAD 300,000 in support to grow their businesses and build capacity in the Black and Indigenous music communities. •	The Access CMW activation at Canadian Music Week provided a safe space within the conference for networking and mentorship opportunities for emerging Black, Indigenous and people of color music reps (the "Access CMW Lounge”) in addition to an exclusive "meet and greet" with CMW Social Justice Award recipient and rap music icon Chuck D for 24 participants. •	Ontario Creates supported industry organization Canadian Independent Music Association in co-presenting industry Anti-Black Racism discussion series entitled Breaking Down Racial Barriers: Next Steps, to individuals and companies in the music industry.
Financial Ressources: •	CAD 2.15 million in 2022-23 for the Diversity Enhancement, AcceleratiON: Black and Indigenous Entrepreneurship, and other strategic, time-limited initiatives.  •	CAD 1.775 million in 2023-24 for the Diversity Enhancement and AcceleratiON: Black and Indigenous Entrepreneurship programs.

Main Feature: The Open Fund for Individuals is one of Creative Scotland’s key funding programmes, supporting the wide range of activity initiated by artists, writers, producers and other creative practitioners in Scotland.     The Open Fund will support a period of research, development and/or delivery of creative activity for up to 24 months. This fund is designed to support creative activity such as a specific project, production or a period of research and development. It can support an individual’s time where this is related to specific creative outcomes.
Results: Creative Scotland received 1,474 eligible applications for Open Funding between 1 April 2022 and 31 March 2023 and made 708 awards through this route, distributing a total of £15.7m. Of these awards 69% were made to individuals (490) and 31% to organisations (218).     The overall success rate for the Open Fund in 2022/23 was 48%. The success rate for applications from individuals was 46% and the success rate for organisations 52%.     The number of awards made through the Open Fund increased from 627 in 2021/22 to 708 in 2022/23, and the overall funding level increased from £13.8m to £15.7mm. The average award through this funding route has remained broadly the same (£22,030 in 2021/22 and £22,160 in 2022/23).     While £15.7m represents the commitment from Creative Scotland, the total predicted budget for the activity we funded through these programmes was £33.7m. Successful applicants drew on partnership funding from a range of sources including Local Authorities, Trusts and Foundations and the Private Sector, as well as earned income. In 2021/22, the total predicted budget for projects funded through the Open Fund was £29.2m.

Title EN: Opérationnalisation du fonds d’appui aux acteurs culturels face à la Covid 19
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture

Area of Monitoring: Cultural and creative sectors
Cultural Domain: Design,Performing Arts,Media Arts,Cinema and Audiovisual Arts,Music,Publishing,Visual Arts
Agency Implementation: Ministère de la Communication, de la Culture, des Arts et du Tourisme (MCCAT)
Main Feature: La maladie à corona virus (covid 19) a eu des conséquences sur l’économie nationale induisant une baisse des recettes publiques, estimée à 572 969 700 USD (306 milliards de FCFA) et le ralentissement général des activités économiques, tous secteurs confondus.   S’agissant du secteur de la culture, il a été durablement affecté par les mesures barrières dont l’interdiction de rassemblements et de manifestations conduisant à l’annulation ou au report des événements culturels et artistiques majeurs tels que la Semaine nationale de la culture (SNC) éditions 2020 et 2022, le FESPACO 2021, le SIAO 2020, les concerts, les festivals, etc.   En réponse à la crise sanitaire, des mesures ont été prises par le Gouvernement du Burkina Faso parmi lesquelles figurent la détaxation de certains produits et services, la mise en place d’un comité de réflexion ainsi que le renforcement du cadre juridique de protection sociale.    Pour ce faire, et pour soutenir la résilience socioéconomique des acteurs culturels, le Fonds de soutien des acteurs culturels face à la Covid-19 a été mis en place et assorti d’un comité de gestion participative et inclusive.    La société civile culturelle et le secteur privé de la culture ont été responsabilisés dans la détermination des critères de répartition des ressources du fonds ainsi que le choix des bénéficiaires. À travers leurs faîtières, les acteurs culturels ont fait des propositions et formulé des recommandations à l’endroit du Comité, afin d’apporter une réponse globale à l’ensemble des filières culturelles ayant subies des préjudices.
Results: Les résultats atteints sont :    la relance de la filière arts plastiques et appliqués à travers l’acquisition de 136 œuvres auprès de 88 artistes plasticiens et l’appui à la filière pour un coût de 280 868 USD (150 000 000F CFA). Ces œuvres ont été destinées à la décoration des édifices publics ;   la réparation financière des préjudices de la filière art de la scène à hauteur de 692 807 USD (370 000 000F CFA), à travers le remboursement des cachets des artistes, des subventions et le sponsoring perdus. A cela s’est ajoutée la prise en charge des charges fixes à titre de régularisation ;   l’appui financier à la filière cinéma et audiovisuel à hauteur de 468 113 USD (250 000 000F CFA), soit 25% du montant global dudit fonds ;   l’appui de la filière livre à hauteur 93 622,5 USD (50 000 000F CFA) ;   L'affectation à la caisse du Bureau Burkinabè du Droit d’Auteur (BBDA) pour soutenir les membres et non membres à hauteur de 337 041 USD (180 000 000 F CFA) ;   les frais de gestion, l’appui à la filière patrimoine culturel, à hauteur de 468 113 USD (250 000 000F CFA).

Après leurs intégrations dans les EEAC, les apprenants après 3 années de formation sont sanctionnés par un diplôme ; le bac H pour le LEA, le BTA pour le CTAA ainsi que le Certificat d’Aptitude pour le CRAMA. Par conséquent elle doit :  Proposer un calendrier annuel des examens et concours ;  Coordonner l’organisation des examens du Brevet Technique des Arts Appliqués (BTAA et du CRAMA ;  Coordonner la préparation des états financiers pour la rétribution des acteurs des examens et concours Coordonner l’organisation des concours d’entrée au Lycée d’Enseignement Artistique (LEA) et au Centre technique des Arts Appliqués (CTAA) et du test du CRAMA ; Coordonner l’organisation le concours du Master professionnel de l’IRES-RDEC de Lomé ; Préparer   les dossiers des attributions et des renouvellements des bourses des apprenants du LEA, CTAA, et de l’IRES-RDEC ;  Proposer au DFAC les membres des jurys (recensement des enseignants et professionnels, répartition et affectation en jurys, Élaborer les arrêtés portant organisation des examens et concours chaque année ; Coordonner le choix des sujets des examens et concours ; Conditionner les sujets des examens et concours ; Acheminer les sujets sur les sites de compositions ; Assurer le suivi des dossiers des bourses auprès des agents du trésor en charge des boursiers des établissements artistiques et culturels (TGAS) ; Participer aux journées de l’orientation des bacheliers organisés par le MESRS; transmettre les procès-verbaux et la liste des admis au DFAC ; Coordonner la préparation des états financiers pour la rétribution des acteurs des examens et concours ; Produire les guides des examens et concours.

Title EN: Organisation de la Grande Nuit du Conte en République de Guinée
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture
SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Cultural and creative sectors
Agency Implementation: Maison de l’Oralité et du Patrimoine Koumakan
Main Feature: Le conte, en tant que puissant vecteur de transmission des connaissances, des valeurs et des enseignements, joue un rôle essentiel dans la préservation de la mémoire collective d’un peuple. En Afrique, particulièrement en Guinée dans les différentes communautés, où l’oralité occupe une place prépondérante dans les traditions, il s’agit d’un pilier central de la culture et de l’identité. La Grande Nuit du Conte Guinée incarne cette essence en célébrant la richesse et l’authenticité des récits africains. Depuis son lancement en 2019, la Grande Nuit du Conte s’est imposée comme un rendez-vous incontournable. En seulement cinq éditions, cet évènement a su séduire un public de plus en plus large, en offrant une expérience immersive où se mêlent tradition et modernité. Les spectateurs, jeunes et moins jeunes, guinéens et étrangers se retrouvent pour revivre ou découvrir les veillées traditionnelles, ces moments magiques où les conteurs ou Maîtres de la parole, racontaient des récits au clair de la lune. Plusieurs artistes et acteurs culturels venus du Sénégal, Mali, Côte d’Ivoire, Togo, etc. y prennent part. La Grande Nuit du Conte en Guinée transcende le simple cadre d’un évènement culturel. Elle incarne une stratégie globale visant à renforcer l’identité culturelle africaine, en s’appuyant sur l’éducation, la technologie et l’art. Ce projet est une source d’inspiration pour d’autres pays du continent, démontrant que les traditions orales, loin d’être figées, peuvent évoluer et s’adapter aux réalités contemporaines. En réunissant passé et présent, cet évènement nous rappelle que la culture est un levier essentiel pour construire une société résiliente et harmonieuse. Grâce à des initiatives comme celle-ci, les traditions orales africaines continuent de rayonner sur la scène internationale, inspirant des générations tout en célébrant leurs racines profondes.
Results: Les résultats atteints sont les suivants : -	Participation de 500 spectateurs par édition depuis 2019 ; -	les récits traditionnels ont été découverts par la nouvelle génération à travers la narration de 5 conteurs venus du Sénégal, du Togo, du Mali, y compris de la Guinée ; -	l’identité culturelle guinéenne et africaine sont renforcées via l’éducation, la technologie et l’art ; -	un espace dédié à l’oralité guinéenne (Maison de l’oralité et du patrimoine Koumakan) a été créé.

Title EN: Organisation du Salon international des jeux vidéo
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture
SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Digital environment
Agency Implementation: Ministère de la Jeunesse de la Culture et de la Communication
Main Feature: Le Ministère de la Jeunesse, de la Culture et de la Communication a organisé la première édition du « Morocco Gaming Expo » à Rabat Morocco Gaming Expo  est le premier salon du genre au Maroc. Son but est de promouvoir l’industrie du Gaming au Maroc et plus particulièrement Rabat Gaming City, qui vise à mettre en place un cluster d’entreprises, nationales et étrangères.  Rabat Gaming City est destinée à devenir un gisement d’emplois de qualité, mais aussi un foyer de créativité culturelle et sociale dans la capitale, et l’un des plus grands hubs du secteur du Gaming en Afrique et dans la zone Mena. Le salon est ouvert au public ainsi qu’aux professionnels et présentera l’industrie du Gaming avec ses différentes composantes, techniques, artistiques, créatives, pédagogiques et financières. - Mission Morocco Gaming Expo  est une occasion pour les entreprises et les startups marocaines de rencontrer d’autres entreprises mondiales du Gaming, de nouer des partenariats nationaux et internationaux et de participer à des sessions de formation dans toutes les filières du Gaming. Morocco Gaming Expo  est une occasion aux jeunes entrepreneurs passionnés du Gaming de participer à plusieurs activités : Réseautage professionnel, Veille concurrentielle, Accès aux nouvelles opportunités d’affaires, Formation et apprentissage. - Objectifs Faire de Morocco Gaming Expo, un rendez-vous annuel, reconnu à l’international dans le secteur du Gaming. Développer l’industrie du Gaming au Maroc. Consolider les liens entre les différents acteurs de la chaîne de valeur du Gaming. Promouvoir et encourager les initiatives de création d’entreprise dans le secteur du Gaming Etablir des rencontres entre les jeunes entrepreneurs, les créateurs, les startups et les opérateurs nationaux et internationaux de toute la chaîne de valeur. Promouvoir le secteur du Gaming comme gisement d’emploi et de création de valeur pour les jeunes.  -Plateformes Destinée à exposer l’ensemble de l’écosystème du Gaming eu Maroc et regroupant : Un stand central de Rabat Gaming City, qui présentera la future cité du Gaming à Rabat et toutes les institutions qui œuvrent autour de cette cité ; Les startups et les incubateurs du gaming ; Les opérateurs de formation du gaming ; Les banques et les opérateurs de financement ; Les fournisseurs d’infrastructures (matériel, communication numérique (fibre et mobile), data center, cloud, …). Destinée aux B2B, son accès est réservé et elle est aménagée et équipée pour des échanges et rendez-vous entre professionnels. Cette plateforme est destinée à encourager les collaborations et à atteindre les objectifs des participants en terme de networking jusqu’à la signature de conventions de partenariat et de coopération. Destinée à présenter les nouveautés en matière de Gaming dans le cadre de conférences, de tables rondes et de sessions de formation qui sont animées par des intervenants de haut niveau. Liste non exhaustive des thèmes abordés: Rabat Gaming City – Presentation of the Moroccan offer ; The video games industry – Trends and outlooks; Video Games in the Entertainment Industry: A New Paradigm ; Building a gaming ecosystem in Morocco – Keys of success ; Music in video games; E-sport MENA – Perspectives ; Indie Incubation and Game Development – Fostering Growth in Morocco ; Education – Training in gaming industry ; XR, VR, …. ; IA & Gaming. En Partenariat avec la Fédération Royale Marocaine des Jeux Electroniques (FRMJE), cette plateforme est une première au Maroc avec deux espaces : Une vraie Aréna qui abritera la finale de 3 compétitions ; Espace de divertissement F2P (Free to Play).
Results: Un échange savant  Le Moroccan Gaming Expo a été marqué par de nombreuses conférences et ateliers qui ont offert une richesse de connaissances aux participants. Ces sessions ont couvert un large éventail de sujets, notamment le développement de jeux, la réalité virtuelle, l’intelligence artificielle et les dernières tendances du marché. Les échanges avec des experts de renommée ont permis de découvrir des perspectives riches sur les enjeux et les possibilités de développement dans le domaine du gaming. Takaya Imamura a été l'une des figures de proue de cette première édition. Une intervention qui a tenu l'audience en haleine, où il a partagé des conseils précieux avec les jeunes créateurs marocains. La légende de Nintendo a insisté sur l'importance d'utiliser la culture locale comme source d'inspiration pour créer des jeux uniques et innovants. Pour Imamura, «chaque culture possède des éléments uniques et fascinants qui peuvent inspirer de nouvelles créations. Les jeunes créateurs marocains ont une opportunité extraordinaire de se démarquer en utilisant leur patrimoine culturel pour concevoir des expériences de jeu captivantes». Title EN: Overcoming Stereotypes
Goal: Promote Human Rights And Fundamental Freedoms
SDG: SDG 5 - Achieve gender equality and empower all women and girls,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels
Area of Monitoring: Gender equality
Agency Implementation: Council for Electronic Media
Main Feature: The Council for Electronic Media is a member of the National Council for Gender Equality. Pursuant to the National Strategy for the Promotion of Equality between Women and Men 2021-2030, as well as the adopted National Action Plan for the Promotion of Equality between Women and Men 2021-2022 and the National Action Plan for the Promotion of Equality between Women and Men 2023- 024, the CEM is committed to monitoring the presence or absence of balance in the participation of men and women in programmes, to monitor the existence of stereotypes in the programmes of media service providers.
Results: 2020 A focused observation was conducted on the topic of women's and men's participation/representation in commercial announcements in television programmes. The monitoring covers TV commercials across four programmes produced by the two most influential commercial media service providers in a total of 32 hours of content. Two of the programmes have a general (poly-thematic) profile, two are niche, with a specialised film profile. The scope of the monitoring is narrowed in time and content due to the fact that for the first time in the Council a methodology for assessing television commercial speech from a gender perspective is being applied. The methodology is based on European experience in similar observations, but is applied to a smaller volume of content compared to foreign practices. Overall, the monitoring reports as a positive trend the absence of discriminatory commercial practices by gender, as well as the absence of negative gender stereotypes in the monitored programmes and advertisements. Television advertisements are based on stereotyped images and social roles, reflecting objective social and cultural relations based on gender differences, which cannot be qualified unequivocally with a negative sign. The representation in commercial messages of women as housewives and mothers, or of men as workers and husbands, are images that reflect human daily life and attract the relevant social groups to the advertising message. Considering the great influence of short and highly memorable advertising images of women and men, the observation highlights the cultural views of our consumer society on gender roles. The change in the social participation of both sexes in economic and family life is also reflected on screen, including in commercial messages in television programmes. Advertising plots, unthinkable until recently, are now perceived as normal by the audience, precisely because of the cultural changes that have occurred in the social participation of both sexes in postmodern society. More about the results of the observation:  https://www.cem.bg/files/1617192413_otchet_cem_2020.pdf  2021 In 2021, elections were held for MPs - three times, as well as elections for the President of the Republic. Within the framework of the specialized monitoring of electoral campaigns, the participation of men and women in them was also tracked.  April 2021 - elections for Members of the European Parliament   For yet another election campaign, CEM's observation reports a preponderance of men over women in election content. According to information from the CEC, of those running for the 45th National Assembly, women accounted for 2,073 or 29.67% and men 4,913 or 70.3%. The data on the participation of men and women in radio and television programmes also shows a significant predominance of men over women.  More details on programmes in the monitoring report at the following link - https://www.cem.bg/controlbg/1362  July 2021 - Extraordinary elections for MPs In this campaign, too, the monitoring found a preponderance of male over female participants in radio and television programmes during elections. According to the CEC, there were 3,585 male candidates for the special election and 1,494 women. There were 181 male and 59 female elected deputies, a ratio that is also a result of the picture of gender participation in pre-election media content. It can be concluded that achieving equality between women and men in the legislature remains a good wish, but also an important goal for a democratic Bulgarian society.  More details on programmes in the report at the following link -https://www.cem.bg/controlbg/1371  November 2021 - two-in-one elections - presidential and vice-presidential elections and special parliamentary elections  Men's participation in electoral content here again outweighs women's participation quantitatively. According to the publicly announced presidential and vice-presidential candidacies (23 pairs), there are 191 male candidates for head of state and 4 female candidates. The candidates for vice-president are 9 men and 14 women.  According to the CEC data for the parliamentary elections, out of a total of 5,068 candidates for MP (6,306 candidates as one person can be registered in two lists), there are 1,515 female candidates against 3,553 male candidates. More details on programmes in the report at the following link - https://www.cem.bg/controlbg/1402   2022	 In 2022, a specialized observation of an election campaign for parliament was conducted. Traditionally, CEM also monitors the participation of women and men in election content and reflects the participation rates of female and male candidates by media services. Inequalities in the representation of both genders in the campaign are reported.  At the request of the CEC, a long-standing practice has now been established for the CEC to disclose the participation of men and women in the lists of MPs and this data is widely reported in the media.    https://www.cem.bg/controlbg/1447  The Council has also implemented a focused monitoring of commercial messages in audiovisual media services for the presence of gender stereotypes. The monitoring covers programmes re programmes of the two largest and most influential commercial providers - BTV (with a poly-thematic profile); BTV LADY (with a specialised profile aimed at female audiences) and NOVA TV (with a poly-thematic profile); DIEMA FAMILY (with a specialised film profile).  This is the second time the Council has conducted such a study. In summary, the monitoring now finds that there is no gender discrimination in the advertisements distributed. The advertisements reflect people's everyday lives and the social participation of both sexes in work, family life and leisure. In the case of the main characters on screen, there is a predominance of female representation, while in the case of the secondary characters there is some competition for the top spot (in some programmes women dominate, in others men dominate, but the results are almost similar). In the case of behind-the-scenes voices, male voices dominate. In the case of age, young people of working age dominate the commercials.  Stereotypical gender roles are inevitably reflected in advertisements - the woman is a housewife, she does the shopping; the woman is a mother and takes care of the house, the children, the whole family - the health, the food; the man does sports, keeps fit; the man does repairs in the house, maintains the garden.    There is also a growing presence of advertisements in which there is a change in gender stereotypes - it is not only women who take care of the home and children. The man is a caring father, husband. He is also the householder who cleans and does the washing. Both men and women are featured in advertisements for dietary supplements and pharmaceuticals, and the emphasis is on maintaining a healthy lifestyle, exercising and improving health.

Title EN: Pacific Regional Culture Strategy 2022-2032 (PRCS)
Goal: Integrate Culture In Sustainable Development Frameworks
SDG: SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: International cooperation for sustainable development
Cultural Domain: Design,Performing Arts,Media Arts,Cinema and Audiovisual Arts,Music,Publishing,Visual Arts
Agency Implementation: Manatū Taonga Ministry for Culture and Heritage
Main Feature: The Pacific Regional Culture Strategy (PRCS) is the progression of a long-term goal to improve cultural outcomes across the Pacific. It replaces the initial 10-year strategy (2010-2020) with a revised 10-year horizon (2022-2032). The PRCS is non-binding and intended to provide guidance and support to member countries; build opportunities for partnership, sharing information and strengthen accountability for cultural development. The Vision for the PRCS is a future where ‘Pacific cultures are vibrant, visible and valued for the empowerment, wellbeing and prosperity of our people’. It provides five priorities for the region:  ·	Priority Area 1: Cultural Policy Frameworks - Our national legislation, strategies and policies amplify the value of culture and heritage. ·	Priority Area 2: Cultural Heritage - Our cultural heritage, arts and languages are protected and thriving. ·	Priority Area 3: Cultural Wellbeing - Our cultures are treated as an integral component of economic, environmental, social, spiritual, and emotional wellbeing. ·	Priority Area 4: Cultural Innovation - We are advancing culture in innovative ways for future generations. ·	Priority Area 5: Cultural Statistics - Cultural statistics are current, accessible, and used for effective, targeted decision-making.  The Secretariat of the Pacific Community (SPC) leads the development of the PRCS and is overseen by the Council of Pacific Arts and Culture (CPAC) and Pacific Ministers of Culture. SPC is an international development organisation owned and governed by its 27 Pacific Island countries and territories. New Zealand is a founding member of SPC. The Minister for Arts, Culture and Heritage, and the Ministry for Culture and Heritage, supported by the Arts Council of New Zealand and Creative New Zealand, represented New Zealand in several CPAC and MCM meetings to consider and take decisions on the PRCS, Festival of Pacific Arts and Culture (FestPAC) and relevant regional and international cultural policy matters.   In June 2023, New Zealand endorsed the PRCS including its first five-year Implementation Plan 2023-2027 at the 6th Pacific Ministers of Culture Meeting.  New Zealand also participated at the 13th FestPAC hosted by the Federal Government of Hawai’i in Honolulu from 6-16 June 2024. FestPAC is the world’s largest festival of indigenous Pacific peoples and cultures which was launched in 1972 by SPC to safeguard traditional practices through ongoing cultural exchange.  It is a key deliverable of the PRCS. The 13th FestPAC brought together approximately 2000 indigenous artists and cultural practitioners, traditional leaders, Pacific Ministers of Culture and youth leaders representing 27 Pacific Island countries and territories.  The Ministry for Culture and Heritage led New Zealand’s engagement at the Government-to-Government Strategic Agenda at FestPAC for the Meetings of the 40th CPAC and 7th Pacific Ministers of Culture. The Arts Council and Creative New Zealand led Aotearoa New Zealand Delegation of Māori and Pasifika artists to FestPAC with an 85-person artistic delegation participating at the 13th FestPAC. This continues New Zealand’s tradition of continuous participation since the first FestPAC in Fiji in 1972 (including hosting in 1975 in Rotorua), ensuring our ongoing collaboration across the Pacific family of nations.
Results: The first country reports on the implementation of the PRCS are due to the Secretariat of the Pacific Community in June 2025.

Results: 1.	Gender equality:  - Presidency Conclusions on gender equality in the field of culture (policy guidelines) adopted in 2020 (with support from 24 of the 27 EU member states), initiated by Germany in the context of its Presidency of the Council of the EU, represented by the Federal Government Commissioner for Culture and the Media and with the involvement of the Länder; - The above initiative sparked by the Commissioner’s and German Commission for UNESCO’s finding that women’s lack of equal access, participation and visibility in the cultural sector leads to the persistence of gender discrimination and the loss of cultural diversity and talents (in both qualitative and quantitative terms); - Topic of gender equality in the field of culture addressed at an EU-wide policy level for the first time, with the Conclusions containing numerous recommendations and calling on EU member states and the European Commission to implement them; topic kept on the agenda in the context of the trio presidency with Portugal and Slovenia in 2021 and subsequently with France in 2022 and embedded in the Council’s new Work Plan for Culture 2023-2026.  2.
