Support for the cultural and creative sectors during the COVID-19 pandemic: - Dialogue continued between EU member states about national measures to support the cultural and creative sectors badly affected by the pandemic; - Findings of the dialogue continuously updated, the aim being for states to gain an overview of pilot projects demonstrating best practice and extrapolate ideas for measures of their own; - Discussions held at ministerial level, at a working meeting between EU member states, in Berlin in September 2020, about countries’ different experiences and successful strategies, particularly with regard to the resumption of cultural activities restricted by the pandemic.  4.	Specialist and cultural programme: - A wide-ranging specialist and cultural programme of more than 30 individual events arranged by the Federal Government Commissioner for Culture and the Media, despite pandemic conditions, during Germany’s Presidency of the Council of the EU, including the concert Europe – Remembering and Hoping as part of the Young Euro Classic festival, European Theatre Forum 2020: European Performing Arts in Focus and the workshop Missing Gender Data in the Creative Sector and How to Bridge the Gap.

Title EN: Participation des faitières du secteur culturel (société civile culturelle) à l’élaboration et la mise en œuvre de la nouvelle politique culturelle de la République de Guinée
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture
SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Partnering with civil society
Cultural Domain: Design,Performing Arts,Media Arts,Cinema and Audiovisual Arts,Music,Publishing,Visual Arts
Agency Implementation: Ministère de la Culture, du Tourisme et de l’Artisanat
Main Feature: La culture guinéenne est caractérisée par des activités, des acteurs et des ressources spécifiques. Elle est aussi un domaine transversal, ayant des liens étroits avec les autres domaines de l’activité humaine et sociale, touchant à la fois l’économie, la santé, l’environnement, l’éducation, les relations internationales, les sciences et les techniques, etc. La nouvelle politique culturelle de la République de Guinée engage des acteurs de tous ces domaines qui doivent œuvrer tous ensemble, à des degrés divers et avec des responsabilités définies et reconnues de façon consensuelle, à son élaboration, à sa mise en œuvre et à son évaluation. L’élaboration de cette politique a été faite suivant une démarche transversale, participative et inclusive.  Dès l’entame du processus d’élaboration de la nouvelle politique, des concertations préliminaires ont été organisées avec les faitières (OSC culturelle sur l’utilité d’élaboration de ce document afin de recueillir leur appréciation et leur adhésion au processus. Pour une meilleure participation de ces organisations, le ministère en charge de la culture a organisé à leur attention des journées régionales de concertation en vue de leur permettre de s’approprier du canevas d’élaboration de la nouvelle politique.  Après cette phase préliminaire, les faitières (OSC culturelle) ont désigné leurs représentants devant participer aux groupes de travail qui devaient être mis en place. De l’étape du diagnostic à la rédaction du document, des représentants des faitières (OSC culturelle) ont activement participé aux travaux des groupes.  Pour la validation de la nouvelle politique, les représentants des faitières ont d’abord restitué les résultats au sein de leurs faitières respectives en vue d’une pré validation avant une participation plus élargie des OSC culturelle à l’atelier de validation qui s’est tenu en novembre 2017.  La nouvelle politique culturelle, adoptée en Janvier 2018, a tenu compte de toutes les préoccupations des faitières (OSC culturelle), notamment : -	la création, la production, la distribution/diffusion des biens et services culturels ;  -	la création et la gestion de manifestations et d’événements culturels ;  -	le respect des normes et standards de la législation et de la règlementation en matière culturelle ;  -	la formation des acteurs culturels ;  -	la construction et la gestion d’infrastructures culturelles ;  -	le plaidoyer pour la mobilisation de ressources financières ;  -	leur implication dans la mise en œuvre et le suivi-évaluation des programmes et projets, etc.
Results: L’implication des faitières (OSC culturelles) dans la mise en œuvre de la Politique Culturelle a permis d’atteindre des résultats significatifs dans les secteurs de l’économie, la santé, l’Artisanat, le Tourisme, l’environnement, l’éducation, les relations internationales, les sciences et les techniques, la communication, etc. Le partenariat entre l’Etat et les faitières (OSC culturelles) a permis d’atteindre les résultats majeurs suivants :  -	l’adhésion des faitières  (OSC culturelles) aux orientations contenues dans la nouvelle politique culturelle ; le renforcement de la coordination, de la synergie d’actions et de la complémentarité entre les interventions de l’Etat et les faitières (OSC culturelles).

Title EN: Partenariat avec le Cerav, Centre Régional pour les arts vivants en Afrique
Goal: Integrate Culture In Sustainable Development Frameworks
SDG: SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: International cooperation for sustainable development
Cultural Domain: Design,Performing Arts,Media Arts,Cinema and Audiovisual Arts,Music,Publishing,Visual Arts
Agency Implementation: Ministère de la Jeunesse, de la Culture et de la Communication-Département de la Culture
Main Feature: Le Centre régional pour les arts vivants en Afrique (CERAV/Afrique) est un centre de catégorie 2 créé en 2010 suite à un accord signé entre le gouvernement du Burkina Faso et la Directrice générale de l'UNESCO. Il a pour mission de promouvoir la diversité et la richesse des arts vivants africains à travers une série d'actions et de mécanismes spécifiques. Ces initiatives incluent l’assistance aux États membres pour créer des conditions propices au développement des capacités créatrices, la collecte de données et l’échange de bonnes pratiques, le soutien aux politiques visant la protection et la promotion des arts vivants, ainsi que le développement d’activités de formation.  Un partenaire clé dans cette mission est le Maroc, qui a démontré un engagement continu et substantiel envers le CERAV/Afrique depuis sa création. Le Maroc apporte chaque année une contribution financière significative au budget global du centre, ce qui est essentiel pour la réalisation des projets et des programmes de promotion des arts vivants africains. Cette contribution permet de financer des projets spécifiques, de soutenir les activités de formation et de renforcement des capacités, de faciliter la collecte et la diffusion de données sur les arts vivants, et de promouvoir les échanges culturels entre les artistes africains.  Au-delà de l'apport financier, le Maroc s'engage activement dans la réalisation des objectifs du CERAV/Afrique. Cet engagement se manifeste par la participation à des initiatives de coopération culturelle régionale et internationale, l’organisation et la participation à des événements et des festivals mettant en valeur les arts vivants africains, le soutien à la création et à la diffusion d’œuvres artistiques, ainsi que la promotion de politiques culturelles visant à protéger et à valoriser le patrimoine immatériel africain.  Ce partenariat avec le Maroc s'inscrit pleinement dans le cadre de la coopération Sud-Sud que le Maroc promeut dans sa politique étrangère. En effet, le Maroc met un accent particulier sur la solidarité et la collaboration avec les pays africains pour favoriser un développement mutuel et durable. Cette stratégie vise à renforcer les liens entre les pays du Sud, en partageant des expériences et des ressources pour surmonter les défis communs.  L'engagement du Maroc envers le CERAV/Afrique illustre parfaitement cette approche de coopération Sud-Sud. En soutenant le développement des arts vivants en Afrique, le Maroc contribue non seulement à la valorisation de la culture africaine mais aussi à la création de conditions favorables à l’épanouissement des capacités créatrices sur tout le continent. Ce soutien renforce les échanges culturels et permet de mettre en place des réseaux de collaboration entre les artistes et les institutions culturelles africaines.  Grâce à cet engagement, le CERAV/Afrique peut continuer à jouer un rôle central dans le développement et la valorisation des arts vivants sur le continent africain, contribuant ainsi à l'épanouissement des capacités créatrices et à la diffusion de la richesse culturelle africaine. Cette action reflète la vision du Maroc d'une Afrique unie et prospère, où les pays travaillent ensemble pour atteindre des objectifs communs et créer un avenir meilleur pour tous.
Results: L'engagement du Maroc dans le cadre de la coopération Sud-Sud a été déterminant pour le succès du CERAV/Afrique. Les contributions financières et l'appui technique du Maroc ont permis au centre de mener à bien ses missions et d'atteindre ses objectifs. Cette coopération a renforcé les capacités du CERAV/Afrique à agir efficacement et a consolidé les relations entre les pays africains, démontrant l'importance de la solidarité et de la collaboration pour le développement culturel du continent et ce à travers un certains nombres d’initiatives permettant la promotion et la protection de la diversité des expressions culturelles en Afrique à savoir ; le renforcement compétences des acteurs culturels africains et d'améliorer la qualité des productions artistiques sur le continent, le développement et la mise en œuvre des politiques culturelles visant à créer un environnement plus favorable à l'épanouissement des artistes et à la diffusion de leurs œuvres, le soutien à la création et à la diffusion d’œuvres artistiques en Afrique et enfin le centre joue un rôle clé dans la promotion des échanges culturels entre les pays africains. Il organise et soutient en étroite collaboration avec les pays un nombre importants de festivals, d’ateliers, d’expositions et d’événements artistiques, facilitant ainsi la rencontre et la collaboration entre les artistes de différents pays. Ces échanges ont non seulement enrichi la scène artistique africaine, mais ont aussi renforcé les liens culturels entre les nations.

Title EN: PARTIS - Práticas Artísticas para a Inclusão Social
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture
SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Partnering with civil society
Cultural Domain: Design,Performing Arts,Media Arts,Cinema and Audiovisual Arts,Music,Publishing,Visual Arts
Agency Implementation: Calouste Gulbenkian Foundation
Main Feature: PARTIS is an initiative of the Calouste Gulbenkian Foundation that supports, through funding and training actions, organizations that develop projects that use artistic practices (plastic, audiovisual and/or performative) as a privileged tool to promote social inclusion. In this context, PARTIS seeks, through the projects it makes possible, to find new languages of communication between groups/communities that don't usually cross paths and to provoke meetings of interests that contribute to the reduction of social inequalities and to greater autonomy for the most disadvantaged people and communities. There were three editions: 2014-2016; 2016-2018; 2019-2022.
Results: From 2014 to 2019, PARTIS opened three calls for proposals and enabled 48 projects, in different regions of the country, in the areas of music, visual arts, theater, circus, dance, photography and video. The first PARTIS edition took place in the 2014-2016 period and supported 17 artistic projects with social impact, selected from more than 200 applications from across the country. The projects that made up this first edition involved 7,900 direct participants, the majority of whom were children and young people between the ages of 6 and 25, and worked on a range of social issues, such as: children and young people at risk, imprisonment/deprivation of liberty, immigration/ ethnic minorities/asylum, disabilities, social and/or geographic isolation, among others. Over the three years, a total of 472 employees and 384 partner organizations were involved in these projects. There were 9,399 activities (workshops, rehearsals, classes, among many others) and 466 public events (especially shows/performances and concerts) attended by 57,112 spectators. These projects involve 181 full-time professionals, 104 volunteers and 287 partner organizations (public and private – for-profit and non-profit).

Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture
SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development

Cultural Domain: Design,Performing Arts,Media Arts,Cinema and Audiovisual Arts,Music,Publishing,Visual Arts
Agency Implementation: UNESCO Regional Office for Culture in Latin America and the Caribbean
Main Feature: The participation and integration of several institutions of the Ministry of Culture and other institutions related to the Transcultura Program, coordinated by the UNESCO Regional Office of Culture in Havana, whose initiative covers four years (2022-2025), demonstrates the will of the Cuban State to turn young people into agents of change and development. The training and support programs for entrepreneurship provide artists with the necessary tools to develop creative projects from the country and the region, since mobility and networking complement the training. It is considered a substantial contribution to the professional path of the cultural and creative sectors and contributes to sustainable development and inclusive socioeconomic transformation.
Results: It is considered the largest UNESCO program in Latin America and the Caribbean, and is aimed at young cultural professionals, artists and entrepreneurs from 17 Caribbean countries. From Cuba, young people linked to museum work have participated in courses on topics of collections and heritage fortifications. It has been implemented in three languages. It has provided opportunities for the future in the region and in Europe, through training, support for entrepreneurship, creation of professional networks and mobility.
Recommandations: The Transcultura Program has had a transformative impact on the young people who have participated. These have been empowered and have contributed to the development in their communities through culture and creativity. Faced with the challenges faced by Small Island Developing States, it is demonstrated that culture contributes to the development of communities and social cohesion, employment, economic growth and creativity and innovation. The Program won the United Nations Award for Partnerships in Small Island Developing States in the Social category (2024). It is recommended to design new training programs from creative sectors that address the values and potential of Cultural Heritage in the participating countries. , not only movable and immovable property, but also intangible cultural manifestations.

Title EN: PARTICIPATION IN THE VENICE BIENNALE
Goal: Achieve A Balanced Flow Of Cultural Goods And Services And Increase The Mobility Of Artists And Cultural Professionals
SDG: SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 10 - Reduce inequality within and among countries,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Flow of cultural goods and services
Agency Implementation: MINISTERIO DE CULTURAS DESCOLONIZACIÓN Y DESPATRIARCALIZACIÓN (MINISTRY OF CULTURES, DECOLONIZATION AND DEPATRIARCHALIZATION)
Main Feature: The participation of the Plurinational State of Bolivia in the Venice Biennale has been a significant process that reflects its commitment to promoting cultural diversity and recognizing national artistic expressions.  The presence of different national pavilions allows countries to exhibit not only works of art, but also cultural products that represent their cultural identity. Collaboration between nations, such as the transfer of the Russian pavilion to Bolivia, illustrates how political and cultural dynamics are intertwined in this event, generating opportunities for cultural exchange. Bolivia's first formal participation in the Venice Biennale with a pavilion was in 2022. Before this, it had been present in previous editions without its own space, which limited the visibility of its artistic production. At the 59th Venice Art Biennale, Bolivia presented the project "Wara Wara Jawira". At the 2024 Biennial, the 60th Biennial, Bolivia presented its pavilion entitled "Looking to the past, moving beyond the future." This project seeks to highlight ancestral knowledge and skills and make visible ancient cultures that have been historically marginalized, presenting works by 25 Bolivian and Latin American artists.
Results: Participation in the Biennial has allowed Bolivia to showcase its cultural and artistic wealth to a global audience, contributing to greater international recognition of its traditions and contemporary expressions, achieving global visibility for cultural markets.  The exhibitions have served as platforms to reaffirm Bolivian cultural identity and promote intercultural dialogue. The presentation of ancestral knowledge in a setting as prestigious as the Biennial is an important step towards recognition and respect for indigenous worldviews. At the level of cultural impact, the participation has also generated a renewed interest in visual arts within the country, inspiring new generations of artists to explore and express their cultural identities through art.

Main Feature: "Pay the artist now! - Infotour" is a series of information events in several Austrian Federal States (Tyrol, Carinthia, Styria, and Upper Austria). It has runs since November 2023. Each venue hosts a public event and a workshop with invited participants from the independent (visual) arts scene, artists, and cultural workers from local institutions, as well as representatives from local funding bodies.  The main objective is to provide information on the current status of the Austrian “Fairness Process” (see separate measure) and to share experiences with actors from local visual arts institutions in order to evaluate and contribute to the further development of Fair Pay measures. In addition, the project aims to collect experiences from different stakeholders and to build links with local/regional organizations and initiatives from the independent visual arts sector. Ultimately, the project will strengthen efforts to implement Fair Pay as a condition for funding.

Title EN: Participatory design of a National Arts Education Policy.
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture
SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Partnering with civil society
Cultural Domain: Design,Performing Arts,Media Arts,Cinema and Audiovisual Arts,Music,Publishing,Visual Arts
Agency Implementation: Ministry of Cultures, Arts and Heritage (MINCAP).
Main Feature: The National Arts Education Policy forms part of the five policies to be jointly developed between the Ministry of Education (MINEDUC) and MINCAP, by means of a cooperation agreement signed during the 2022 Arts Education Week. This initiative seeks to guarantee the right to arts education for all people throughout their lifetime, promoting access to quality training experiences in formal and non-formal education.  Its implementation will allow guiding and evidencing actions of different actors that comprise the arts education ecosystem, integrating children and youth, teachers and artists in the process. Considering “cultural democracy50” model and the importance for the National Arts Education Policy to be designed with citizens. For this, during 2023, MINCAP and MINEDUC implemented a participatory process in order to gather observations and suggestions that would serve as input for the policy's design, establishing a focus, related actors and areas of action.  It should be pointed out that the definition of the areas of the National Arts Education Policy were based on the results from the "Voices and proposals for the future of arts education in Chile" forum, that took place in 2021, with technical support from UNESCO.  Using the ten topics that emerged at the forum, a participatory exercise took place through more than 60 working groups in all the regions of Chile, with the idea of defining the areas of action. In this exercise, with the participation of more than 600 people, five priority areas were identified, designing regional and national participatory processes for policy mapping: Arts education in the educational system, Arts education outside the school system, Initial and continuous education, Specialised arts education and Arts education sustainability.  Based on this participatory process, a draft policy will be developed, that will be validated by the authority between November 2023 and March 2024. The implementation of the policy in our country will begin in May 2024, during the arts education week. Lastly, following the monitoring framework of the 2005 Convention, this policy responds to the "civil society is involved in the implementation of the Convention at national and global levels" indicator.  In line with this indicator, this measure seeks to strengthen cultural collaboration as a fundamental value of cultural participation.
Results: N/A.

Title EN: Participo! / I participate! - Civic and political participation of women
Goal: Promote Human Rights And Fundamental Freedoms
SDG: SDG 5 - Achieve gender equality and empower all women and girls,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels
Area of Monitoring: Gender equality
Agency Implementation: CIG - Commission for Citizenship and Gender Equality
Main Feature: The Participo! Project aligns with Objective 10 by promoting gender equality through increased civic and political participation of women and girls in local communities. 1. Support for Women as Creators, Producers, and Distributors of Cultural Activities, Goods, and Services: - The project facilitated the creation and dissemination of cultural narratives through initiatives such as the 'Theater of the Oppressed' workshops and performances. These activities allowed women to express their stories and challenges, thereby acting as producers and distributors of cultural content. 2. Women's Access to Decision-Making Positions: - Through various training sessions and the creation of local working groups, the project empowered women to take on leadership roles. For instance, the creation of a 'Mapping of Obstacles' and subsequent 'Proposal of Solutions' involved women in identifying issues and formulating policy recommendations, thereby enhancing their decision-making capabilities. Support for Women's Full Participation in Cultural Life: - The project organized 35 numerous events, such as webinars, academies, and the TEDxPorto Salon, which provided platforms for women to actively participate in cultural and civic life. The engagement in these events fostered a sense of community and inclusion among participants. Efforts to Generate Data on Progress Made Towards Gender Equality: - Throughout its 24-month duration, the project collected extensive data on its impact. This included 201 completed questionnaires and six focus group evaluations, which contributed to a comprehensive impact report. The findings showed that 75% of participants demonstrated learning in gender equity and opportunities. Addressing Special Circumstances and Needs of Women: - According to Article 7 of the Convention, the project specifically targeted the unique circumstances of women in the local communities of Aldoar, Foz do Douro, and Nevogilde. By focusing on these areas, the project addressed the local needs and barriers faced by women, providing tailored support and opportunities for their participation.
Results: Training and Capacity Building: The project conducted two editions of a B-learning course with 13 modules each, focusing on transversal skills such as self-awareness, public speaking, and political and civic commitment. A total of 65 participants were enrolled, with 37 completing the course successfully.- Publications and Resources: Development of a digital platform that hosted forums, webinars, and various resources, facilitating communication and knowledge sharing among women.- Networking and Collaboration: Establishment of a Local Help Network and the organization of multiple forums and academies to foster collaboration and mutual support among women.

Several policies reported in the 2020 QPR, namely (1) Law on Broadcasting (see Goal 1, Policies and Measures that Support Media Freedom), (2) Guidelines for Broadcasting Behavior, and (3) Standards for Broadcast Programs, are still valid while drafting this report. In recent developments, stakeholders have identified a real need to update the Law on Broadcasting to be more responsive to current developments and all its challenges and opportunities. The Draft Law on Broadcasting has been prioritized in the National Legislation Program to be completed in 2024. At the time of drafting this report, it had already entered the drafting stage. As an additional note, while waiting for the completion of the Draft Law on Broadcasting, several regulations in the Law on Broadcasting have been amended with the enactment of the Law on Job Creation (see Goal 1, Policies and Measures that Encourage Job Creation and Entrepreneurship in Culture and Creative Economy Sectors and Goal 1, Policies and Measures that Demand Media Accountability).  Two policies that were reported in the 2020 QPR, namely Government Regulation 12 of 2005 on the Public Radio Broadcasting Institution of the Republic of Indonesia and Government Regulation 13 of 2005 on the Public Television Broadcasting Institution of the Republic of Indonesia, have been replaced with the enactment of GR on RRI and GR on TVRI. In essence, the passage of these two GRs strengthens the role of RRI and TVRI in broadcasting things essential to the public and regional cultural diversity in Indonesia without partisan and political interests. This aligns with the 2020-2024 Kemenkominfo Strategic Plan (see Goal 1, Policies and Measures that Support the Digital Transformation of Cultural and Creative Industries).   Meanwhile, the Minister of Communication and Informatics Regulation 43/PER/M.KOMINFO/10/2009 on the Implementation of Broadcasting via Network Station Systems by Private Broadcasting Institutions with Television Broadcasting Services has been replaced most recently by the issuance of the Minister of Communication and Informatics Regulation 11 of 2021 on Amendments to Ministry of Communication and Informatics Regulation 6 of 2021 on the Broadcasting Operations. One of the reasons for the issuance of this regulation is the prolonged COVID-19 pandemic, which has resulted in delays in preparations for the implementation stages of stopping analog television broadcasts (Analog Switch Off).  One of the measures reported in the 2020 QPR is Indiskop. On March 23, 2020, Indiskop temporarily closed its operational activities due to the COVID-19 pandemic. Then, from August to October 2021, Indiskop Festival was held online. Based on the latest information obtained, Indiskop signed a memorandum of understanding with the Indonesian Chamber of Commerce and Industry and State Film Productions to collaborate in developing the national film and animation industry. At the time of drafting this report, there was no further information. With these considerations, coupled with reconsideration by the Drafting Team regarding the relevance of this section, starting from QPR 2024, reporting on Indiskop will discontinue.  In general, policies that support the diversity of government media content are aimed at contributing to achieving the following agenda(s) of the National Strategy for Culture: 1. Provide space for the diversity of cultural expressions and encourage cultural interaction to strengthen the inclusiveness of culture (Agenda 1); 2. Protect and develop values, expressions, and practices of traditional culture to enrich national culture (Agenda 2); and 3. Strengthen the role of the government as a facilitator of culture advancement (Agenda 7).

Title EN: Photo exhibition “ Libano. Sospesi. In Bilico.” - 2022
Goal: Promote Human Rights And Fundamental Freedoms
SDG: SDG 5 - Achieve gender equality and empower all women and girls,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels
Area of Monitoring: Artistic freedom
Agency Implementation: Università degli Studi di Padova - UNESCO Chair Human Rights, Democracy and Peace
Main Feature: The exhibition "Libano. Sospesi. In bilico." draws attention to some of the human rights issues that Lebanon faces today. Following the 2019 Revolution, the deadly explosion at the port of Beirut in 2020, a religiously-divided society, the crushing ongoing financial and economic crisis, and the consequent increasing levels of poverty, the country finds itself in a highly precarious position.  The photographs display some of these afflictions that jeopardise the fragile coexistence between the country’s refugee and Lebanese communities. The images tell a story of Lebanon’s ongoing social, political and economic instabilities, and the consequences of these crises on the lives of Lebanese citizens, Syrian refugees and immigrant female domestic workers. With people’s livelihoods ‘suspended’ in a void, the exhibition underlines Lebanon as a country ‘on the brink’ (‘in bilico’) of a chaotic and devastating future.  The exhibition took place on two occasions. The first at the Villa Borromeo (San Giorgio in Brenta, PD) on November 25, 2022 and the second at the University Center of Padua on December 20, 2022. The exhibition was organised by Osteria Volante with the contribution of the Veneto Region and the City of Padua and the collaboration of Centro di Ateneo per i Diritti Umani "Antonio Papisca," Jardin de los Ninos ONLUS and Spaccature APS.
Results: By interweaving photography and storytelling, the exhibition was able to engage visitors and to achieve the main goal of unveiling some of Lebanon’s critical issues concerning Human Rights. Presenting events such as the 2019 revolution, the ongoing popular protests,  the disastrous explosion at Beirut's port in August 2020 and the plight of migrant domestic employees, the exhibition brought to light the issues gripping the country and threatening the already fragile balance in the coexistence between Syrian and Lebanese communities.

Title EN: Pilot internship scheme for people with disabilities
Goal: Integrate Culture In Sustainable Development Frameworks
SDG: SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: National sustainable development policies and plans
Agency Implementation: Arts and Culture Norway
Main Feature: Lack of special provisions and prejudice can constitute obstacles to the recruitment of people with disabilities in artistic and culture-related professions. In 2021, Arts Council Norway and Arts and Culture Norway (ACN) jointly developed a pilot scheme whereby cultural enterprises could receive funding if they hired candidates with disabilities. This pilot scheme aims to counteract structural discrimination by encouraging the employment of candidates with disabilities in the arts and culture sector. The experiences of these candidates serve as a valuable resource for the employing enterprise, benefiting from their different perspectives and networks. Professional companies in the arts and culture sector can apply for funding to hire an intern. The candidate must have experience and interest in arts and culture, preferably having studied an arts or culture-related subject or received equivalent training. The scheme covers all art forms and creative industries, and the internship can be linked to artistic, technical, and administrative functions. The grant must be used entirely to pay the intern’s salary, and the intern will be employed under normal terms and conditions. The company must provide duties that ensure professional and artistic development, enhancing the intern’s future employment prospects in the arts and culture sector. These tasks should align with the company’s goals and needs.
Results: As of 2023, 12 grants have been awarded, and funds have been appropriated for this purpose until 2026.

Title EN: Policies that Support the Diversity of Media Ownership
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture
SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Media diversity
Cultural Domain: Media Arts,Cinema and Audiovisual Arts,Music,Publishing,Visual Arts
Agency Implementation: 1. Press Council of Indonesia 2. Ministry of Communication and Information Technology 3. Indonesian Broadcasting Commision
Main Feature: In the past four years, policies that support the diversity of media ownership include: 1. Law 5 of 1999 on the Prohibition of Monopoly Practices and Unfair Business Competition; 2. Law 40 of 1999 on the Press (Law on the Press);  3. Law 32 of 2002 on Broadcasting (Law on Broadcasting); 4. Law 6 of 2023 on the Stipulation of Government Regulation in Lieu of Law 2 of 2022 on Job Creation into Law (Law on Job Creation); 5. Draft Law on Amendments to Law 5 of 1999 on the Prohibition of Monopoly Practices and Unfair Business Competition; 6. Draft Law on Amendments to Law 32 of 2002 on Broadcasting (Draft Law on Broadcasting); 7. Presidential Regulation 32 of 2024 on the Responsibility of Digital Platform Companies to Support Quality Journalism (PR on Publishers Right); 8. Press Council Regulation 1/Peraturan DP/I/2023 on the Data Collection of Press Companies; and 9. Indonesian Broadcasting Commission Regulation 07/P/KPI/2020 on the Guidelines for Annual Evaluation of Broadcast Program Requirements for Private Broadcasting Institutions.  Draft Law on Amendments to Law 5 of 1999 on the Prohibition of Monopoly Practices and Unfair Business Competition is the only policy regarding diversity in media ownership reported in the 2020 QPR. Even though it has been included in the National Legislation Program list, this bill has not yet become a priority for completion in 2024. Law 5 of 1999 on the Prohibition of Monopoly Practices and Unfair Business Competition was still in effect when this report was drafted.  Two central policies that support diversity in media ownership but have not been reported in this section in the 2020 QPR are the Law on the Press (see Goal 1, Policies and Measures that Support Media Freedom) and the Law on Broadcasting. For the Law on Broadcasting, some regulations have been replaced with the Law on Job Creation (see Goal 1, Policies and Measures that Encourage Job Creation and Entrepreneurship in Culture and Creative Economy Sectors). Efforts to update it are already underway in the National Legislation Program, where the Draft Law on Broadcasting has become one of the priority bills to be completed in 2024. At the time of drafting this report, it has already entered the drafting stage.  Three other relevant policies are (1) PR on Publishers Rights; (2) Press Council Regulation 1/Peraturan-DP/I/2023 on the Data Collection of Press Companies; and (3) Indonesian Broadcasting Commission Regulation 07/P/KPI/2020 on the Guidelines for Annual Evaluation of Broadcast Program Requirements for Private Broadcasting Institutions. For more detailed information on these three policies, see Goal 1, Policies and Measures that Demand Media Accountability.  In general, policies that support the diversity of media ownership are aimed at contributing to achieving the following agenda(s) of the National Strategy for Culture: 1. Provide space for the diversity of cultural expressions and encourage cultural interaction to strengthen the inclusiveness of culture (Agenda 1); and 2. Protect and develop values, expressions, and practices of traditional culture to enrich national culture (Agenda 2).
Results: Press Council Regulation 1/Peraturan-DP/I/2023 on the Data Collection of Press Companies: See Goal 1, Policies and Measures that Demand Media Accountability.
Recommandations: Evaluations carried out in 2020-2024 by KPI, the Press Council, and the Ministry of Communication and Informatics on the diversity of media ownership resulted in the following conclusions/recommendations. 1. KPI supervises media conglomerates to prevent uniformity in media content and bias towards particular political, social, and cultural views. 2. One of the media's challenges during the 2024 election is media conglomeration, which can be very dangerous in influencing the media's function as a transmitter of objective information. 3. The Press Council stated that media conglomerates inevitably influence the market, advertising, and the function of the press in the public through the intervention of owners who have background members and political party administrators who will ignore the disclosure of information to the public.  Evaluations carried out separately by Masduki (2014), Karman (2014), Darmanto (2020), and Aulia and Raffles (2021) produced the following conclusions/recommendations. 1. Mass media in Indonesia tends to be owned by certain business groups and generally has affiliations with power or political parties. 2. Media conglomeration has created a media ownership model with capitalistic tendencies. 3. Even though ownership of mass media is part of the expression of (some elite) citizens in carrying out tasks guaranteed by the constitution, restrictions on ownership need to be sought because this business sector uses limited public space to carry out its business and the democratization function attached to it. 4. In situations and conditions where mass media ownership is centered among certain business actors or conglomerates, citizens do not get a variety of information choices (plurality of content), even though it seems there are many media for citizens to choose from. 5. Press monitors (for example, KPI and the Press Council) are expected to be more critical in assessing media behavior and content so that media content is oriented towards the general interest, not the interests of certain groups.  References: Aulia, M.Z. & Raffles, R. (2021). Pemusatan kepemilikan media massa di Indonesia: tinjauan aspek hukum. Jurnal Hukum & Pembangunan: Vol. 51: No. 1, Article 10. Title EN: Plan RescArt
Goal: Integrate Culture In Sustainable Development Frameworks
SDG: SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: National sustainable development policies and plans
Agency Implementation: Art Direction (Ministry of Culture)
Main Feature: The Ministry of Culture, through the RecatARTE plan, seeks to reduce the rates of violence and insecurity through cultural and artistic activities, enriching the lives of citizens, through art, culture and the fight against racism and ethnic discrimination. -racial, promoting social cohesion and strengthening identity in communities.  This plan promotes access to public spaces accessible to all people through artistic interventions. Likewise, it will develop workshops and training programs in art and culture which contribute to the development of a civic culture and strengthening of cultural identities.  With the implementation of the plan, the Ministry of Culture develops direct actions for the benefit of citizens, as it considers that it is possible to consolidate a nation in which, through our arts, we build a great community.  Within the framework of the Rescatarte Plan, the following programs and contests are developed:  ●	Playground: mechanism that, through the holding of artistic workshops, seeks to promote the development of socio-emotional and intercultural skills in adolescents and young people, generating creative spaces, in regions where there is a great challenge regarding citizen insecurity. ●	Do it yourself: mechanism that provides training workshops on audiovisual communication tools and socio-emotional support, as well as artistic and cultural workshops, aimed at women from neighborhoods and/or towns with high rates of family violence and social vulnerability. ●	Orchestra in the Neighborhood: musical training program aimed at young people and adults who reside in vulnerable areas of the Peruvian territory, obtaining as a final result an orchestra made up of the beneficiaries.  ●	ItinerArte: this line of action proposes the development of urban artistic interventions with the purpose of promoting the use (activation and/or recovery) of public spaces, in neighborhoods with a high incidence of crime, involving the participation of the community and its local authorities.  A little more than 5 million soles (1,340,483 dollars) were allocated for the execution of the aforementioned mechanisms.  Economic incentives:  ●	“Safe neighborhood with culture” contest: The “Safe neighborhood with culture” contest for Culture Points, which aimed to provide greater access to artistic practices and cultural development programs for populations and sectors focused on situations of risk and vulnerability, with emphasis on children and youth, as tools for the practice of a culture of peace that contribute to citizen security. At the national level, they financed 134 projects for a maximum amount of 15 thousand soles for cultural interventions in neighborhoods with a high index of insecurity.  ●	Non-competitive fund “Cultural House”: non-competitive fund that seeks to transform communities through culture and art, through the creation and improvement of cultural spaces, providing training in cultural management, operational management, among others, empowering communities so that they become agents of change in their own environments, promoting coexistence, creativity and citizen participation. 40 thousand soles (10,724 dollars) were allocated for each beneficiary project in all regions of the country.
Results: The Rescatarte 2023 Plan has managed to benefit 34,138 people and 184 cultural organizations, at the national level it has affected the 25 regions, through its 6 mechanisms. In addition, 492 interventions have been implemented directly through the mechanisms Itinerate, Playground, Orchestra in the Neighborhood and Do It Yourself.  ●	Safe neighborhood with Culture: At the national level, there were 134 projects from cultural organizations that benefited from the fund. 20% of the total culture point organizations benefited from the delivery of the monetary fund within the framework of Safe Neighborhood with Culture. On average, 5 projects benefited from the fund per region.  ●	Cultural House: At the national level, there were 50 projects to improve, condition and/or implement cultural spaces that benefited from the Cultural House economic stimulus. The average of 2 cultural space improvement projects per region have received the monetary fund.  ●	Do It Yourself: The Do It Yourself mechanism has benefited a total of 1,974 people, through 46 interventions developed in 9 regions of the country (Lima, Huánuco, Piura, Puno, Cusco, Ancash, Apurímac, Cajamarca and Madre de Dios)   ●	Orchestra in the Neighborhood: The Orchestra in the Neighborhood mechanism has benefited a total of 2,402 people, through 10 interventions developed in 4 regions of the country (Lima, La Libertad, Callao and Piura).  ●	Itinerarte: The Itinerarte mechanism has benefited a total of 20,303 people, through its 37 interventions developed in 8 regions of the country (Lima, Arequipa, Callao, Huancavelica, Junín, La Libertad, Loreto and Piura).  ●	Patio de Recreo: The Patio de Recreo mechanism has benefited a total of 9,459 people, through its 399 workshops (dance, theater, drawing and painting) developed nationwide in all regions with the exception of Ica.

Title EN: Platform for the Cultural and Creative Industry (hereinafter also "PCCI")
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture
SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Cultural and creative sectors
Cultural Domain: Design,Performing Arts,Media Arts,Cinema and Audiovisual Arts,Music,Publishing,Visual Arts
Agency Implementation: Ministry of Culture
Main Feature: In August 2020, the Ministry of Culture established a working group focused on multi-level cross-sectorial cooperation and support of the cultural and creative industry in the Slovak Republic called the Platform for the Cultural and Creative Industry (hereinafter also "PCCI"). Through it, the Ministry of Culture seeks to continue the dialogue established with the representatives of the temporary working group to address the consequences of the spread of the disease COVID-19 in the Slovak Republic in the field of culture. The goal is also to systematically coordinate the conceptual and strategic direction of the cultural and creative industry through multi-level and cross-sectorial cooperation between its actors, which should lead to synergies and multiply the positive effects of the measures for the entire creative ecosystem in Slovakia. Almost seventy representatives of organizations involved in cultural and creative industries in various contexts, not only theoretically, but also practically, confirmed their participation on the platform. With regard to the extent and diversity of actors, the members were divided into four subgroups: state administration and other bodies and institutions of state administration, territorial self-government; research and educational institutions; sector associations, and other entities operating in various sectors of the cultural and creative industry and its related sectors. The first activity of the platform was an online discussion on the approach and cooperation of selected departments in the field of supporting the cultural and creative industry in Slovakia, which took place on 15 December  2020 at the Ministry. As part of PCCI activities, conferences were organized annually in 2021-2023 on relevant topics in the field of supporting culture and the creative industry.  On 29 April  2021, the Ministry organized the Platform's first online conference on the strategic support of the CCI (hereinafter "CCI") at the level of departments and municipalities. The first point of the program was a moderated interdepartmental discussion, to which representatives of the departments of the economy, foreign and European affairs, transport and construction, and the environment accepted the invitation. Its aim was to point out the necessity of inter-ministerial cooperation in this area, as well as to emphasize the contribution of the cultural and creative industry in the context of the economy, social affairs, environmental stability or sustainable development. The discussion was followed by a lecture given by foreign expert Ragnar Siil from Estonia on a strategic approach to CCI at the level of local and regional self-government and a presentation of two examples of good practice from the European environment (from CREADIS3 project partners). The end of the conference was dedicated to the second moderated discussion on the strategic approach of local and regional self-government to the cultural and creative industry in practice. The invitation was accepted by representatives of the Slovak and Czech municipalities, specifically representatives of the Trnava self-governing region, and of the cities of Nitra, Trnava, Trenčín, Košice, Žilina, Ostrava, Plzeň  and Brno. The conference was broadcast via the YouTube website. As part of the activities of the Platform for the Cultural and Creative Industry (hereinafter referred to as the "Platform"), the Ministry organized on 16 and 17 May 2022 under the title Culture and Our World (Visions and Contexts - Challenges and Priorities). The conference offered participants different scales of view of culture in the contemporary world, from a global view to narrowly specialized approaches. The aim of the conference was mainly to enable discussion, participation of the professional public and obtaining of important inputs and contributions to the prepared Strategy of Culture and Creative Industry of the Slovak Republic 2030 (hereafter referred to as the CCI 2030 Strategy). During the first day, the program focused on clearly depicting the context in which culture and the creative sector in Slovakia are located, and the vision of culture in the contemporary world. Afternoon panel discussions and presentations were devoted to the creation of the CCI 2030 Strategy focused on cooperation and the possibilities of connecting various strategic documents, and finally, at the end of the day representatives of the preparatory team of the strategy presented the philosophy and methods of its creation. The second day belonged to working groups that discussed current needs and challenges in the cultural and creative industries, in the context of current social, political and environmental changes. Together, they identified cultural policy priorities for the coming years and outlined their ranking according to importance/urgency. On September 18 and 19, 2023, the Ministry organized a conference named Well-managed Culture. The first day of the conference took place in three blocks. The content of the first block was public interest in the field of culture, a topic framing the environment - a view of culture and the role it fulfils or should fulfil in society. The second subsequent block dealt with the goals of cultural policy and their use for defining accessible and high-quality culture and its social impacts. The third block discussed the theme of the need and importance of cooperation of all key actors operating in the field of culture and creative industry at various levels. On the second day, key topics related to the improvement of conditions for actors and actresses in the culture and creative industry were discussed in the form of round tables for the invited participants, focusing on the definition of natural and legal persons in culture, or methods of financing in this area, etc.. As part of CCI activities, a Platform Newsletter has also been regularly published in two-month intervals since 2021. The newsletter presents a selection of news and activities of interest in the field of cultural and creative industry support carried out by members of the Platform from the field of state administration, individual sectors, regions and universities. The newsletter enables not only the Ministry, but also other members of the Platform to present their activities and inform each other about interesting support activities in the field of CCI. Anyone can subscribe to it, and therefore it represents an effective tool for positive communication of the resort towards the public. At the same time, for the needs of better information, a social network profile and a separate website were also established, making available relevant information in the field of supporting culture and the creative industry.

Title EN: Poesia YA!
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture
SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Media diversity
Agency Implementation: Secretariat of Culture of Argentina
Main Feature: This is a call to promote, encourage and stimulate the poetic literary production. This event seeks to value poetry as an artistic expression as well as to give a sample of the rich poetic production that has been developing in recent years in the country. With a federal stamp, the Festival brings together established and emerging voices from all over the country, offering reading workshops (face-to-face and online), book presentations, readings, lectures, talks, performances, exhibitions, fairs and even activities for children related to poetry. Other activities included the Master Encounters, a proposal that brought together readings, talks and the projection of video poems. This cycle included emerging talents, such as the video-artists from the open call.
Results: The Festivals (Edition 2022, Edition 2023) bring together established and emerging voices from all over the country, offering reading workshops (in person and online), book presentations, readings, lectures, performances, exhibitions, fairs and even activities for children related to poetry.  With the participation of renowned national and international artists, the third edition of the largest Poetry Festival in the continent was held. It included nine days of activities that brought to the forefront the poetic production that has been developed for decades in our territory and the most current creations.  The Festival Poesía Ya! 2023 had exceptional characteristics: an active and diverse program that this year adds three more venues (the Centro Cultural Borges, the Casa Patria Grande Néstor C. Kirchner and the Museo Nacional del Cabildo de Buenos Aires y de la Revolución de Mayo); a federal imprint as a result of an open call; the confluence of new voices with others with extensive experience; crossings of poetry with other disciplines, audiovisual and performative works; the launching of the Storni Poetry Award 2023; training activities such as reading and writing workshops in classroom format; and the permanent meeting between authors and readers through master classes, readings and tributes.   As part of the 2023 Festival, the third edition of the Storni Poetry Prize (for unpublished books) was launched. In its first two editions, more than 4,000 books were submitted. During the launching, which took place at the Kirchner Cultural Center, an anthology edited by Eudeba was presented, which gathers a selection of the winning books of the 2021 and 2022 editions.   As in its previous edition, the Festival Poesía Ya! made part of its program from an open and federal call. The winners were participating in various events: readings of Poetry Out Loud and Novísimes in the Hall of Honor, reading and writing workshops for adults and children and Videopoems that are available on the Youtube Channel of the Kirchner Cultural Center and in a permanent exhibition in the Sala Sonora. The activities took place at: Centro Cultural Kirchner, Centro Cultural Borges, Museo Nacional del Cabildo de Buenos Aires y de la Revolución de Mayo, Casa Patria Grande Presidente Néstor C. Kirchner.

Title EN: Policies and Measures for Culture Regeneration
Goal: Integrate Culture In Sustainable Development Frameworks
SDG: SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: National sustainable development policies and plans
Cultural Domain: Design,Performing Arts,Media Arts,Cinema and Audiovisual Arts,Music,Publishing,Visual Arts
Agency Implementation: Ministry of Education, Culture, Research, and Technology Ministry of Manpower  National Professional Certification Agency  Education Fund Management Institution State Film Productions Televisi Republik Indonesia
Main Feature: In the past four years, policies and measures for culture regeneration include:  1. Law 20 of 2003 on the National Education System (Sistem Pendidikan Nasional) (Law on Sisdiknas);  2. Law 13 of 2003 on Manpower (Law on Manpower);  3. Draft Law on Amendments to Law 20 of 2003 on the National Education System (Sistem Pendidikan Nasional) (Draft Law on Sisdiknas);   4. Draft Law on Amendments to Law 13 of 2003 on Manpower (Draft Law on Manpower);  5. Minister of Education, Culture, Research, and Technology Regulation 56 of 2022 on Teacher Education Standards (Teacher Education Standards);  6. Indonesian National Work Competency Standards (Standar Kompetensi Kerja Nasional Indonesia, SKKNI);  7. Second-party Professional Certification Institute for Culture (Lembaga Sertifikasi Profesi Pihak Kedua Kebudayaan, LSP-P2 for Culture);  8. Linearity of Teacher Profession Education;  9. Dana Indonesiana;  10. Special Allocated Funds for Culture;  11. Scholarships for Cultural Practitioners;  12. Movement for Artists to Enter Schools (Gerakan Seniman Masuk Sekolah, GSMS);  13. Learning with the Maestro;   14. Mini-Seminar Series: Meeting of Minds;   15. Arts Institutions Standardization and Certification in Bali;   16. Indonesia Film Content Academy (IFCA);  17. We Love Children Songs (Kita Cinta Lagu Anak, KILA);   18. Marasante Traditional Music Festival (MTMF);   19. The Never-ending Blue Scarf (Slendhang Biru Tak Pernah Usai);   20. Archipelago Rhythm (Irama Nusantara); and  21. INDONESIANA.TV.   All measures reported in the 2020 QPR, namely: (1) Cultural Endowment Fund (now Dana Indonesiana, see Goal 1, Measures that Provide Funds for CSO Capacity Development); (2) Special Allocation Fund for Culture; (3) National Education Development Fund; (4) GSMS; and (5) Learning with the Maestro, are still ongoing at the time this report was drafted. Regarding the National Education Development Fund, the specific program in question is the Scholarships for Cultural Practitioners program (see Goal 1, Policies and Measures for Education and Training Programs in Culture and Creative Economy Sectors), which at the time of drafting this report was still ongoing but has been merged into the Dana Indonesiana program. As additional information, the Learning with the Maestro program is also under Dana Indonesiana.  Formal and non-formal education and training are essential vehicles for cultural regeneration. The 12-year national compulsory education program ensures that children of primary and secondary school ages (grades I-XII) are continuously introduced to a curriculum that contains arts and culture learning materials, including local and national arts and culture. Many educational units also offer opportunities for students to explore their interest in arts and culture through extracurricular activities. As explained in Goal 1, Policies and Measures for Education and Training in the Culture and Creative Economy Sector, the Law on Sisdiknas and the Law on Manpower are the statutory regulations that underlie Indonesia's education and training sector. In recent developments, stakeholders have identified a real need to update the Law on Sisdiknas and the Law on Manpower to be more responsive to current developments and all their challenges and opportunities. Although the Draft Law on Sisdiknas and the Draft Law on Manpower have been registered with the National Legislation Program, neither has been prioritized for completion in 2024.  Furthermore, several good policies and measures related to cultural regeneration have not yet been reported in the 2020 QPR. For policy development, there is the Mini-Seminar Series: Meetings of Minds (see Goal 2, Exemplary Higher Education Institution Initiatives that Support the Mobility of Artists and Cultural Professionals), while for education and training, there are several, such as (1) Teacher Education Standards; (2) Linearity of Teacher Profession Education; (3) SKKNI; (4) LSP-P2 for Culture; (5) Arts Institutions Standardization and Certification in Bali; and (6) IFCA. For more detailed information about SKKNI, LSP-P2 for Culture, Arts Institutions Standardization and Certification in Bali, and IFCA, see Goal 1, Policies and Measures for Education and Training Programs in Culture and Creative Economy Sectors. Then, there are several activity events organized by the Central Government, regional governments, and/or CSOs, such as (1) KILA, (2) MTMF, and (3) the Slendhang Biru Tak Pernah Usai concert. Lastly, there are efforts to archive music digitally through the Irama Nusantara website (see Goal 1, Policies and Measures that Support the Digital Transformation of Cultural and Creative Industries) and cultural broadcast programs.  One of the critical factors in implementing sustainable cultural regeneration is preparing quality teaching staff for subjects with arts and culture content in numbers that match real needs in the field. Kemendikbudristek has established Teacher Education Standards and Linear Requirements for Teacher Profession Education, including for Arts and Culture Teachers, to guarantee the quality in question. Teacher Education Standards aim to meet graduate learning outcomes, implementation aspects, and instruments for developing internal and external quality assurance systems for Bachelor of Education Programs and Teacher Profession Education Programs. The Bachelor of Education Program is an academic education program to produce education graduates organized by the Education Personnel Educational Institution, while the Teacher Profession Education Program is an educational program held after the undergraduate or applied undergraduate program to obtain an educator certificate in early childhood education, primary education, and/or secondary education. These two programs are path options that can be taken to become a prospective professional teacher.   For linearity requirements, Cultural Arts Teachers must graduate from one of the following undergraduate or applied undergraduate study programs, namely: (1) Arts Education; (2) Drama, Dancing, and Musical Arts Education; (3) Dancing Arts Education; (4) Musical Arts Education; (5) Performing Arts Education; (6) Dancing and Musical Arts Education; (7) Hindu Religious Dancing Arts Education; (8) Hindu Religious Arts and Cultural Education; (9) Arts and Religious Education; (10) Hindu Religious Karawitan Arts Education; (11) Dance Education; (12) Theatrical Arts; or (13) Angklung and Bamboo Music. Several leading higher education institutions that provide these study programs have joined the Indonesian Arts Higher Education Cooperation Agency (see Goal 2, Exemplary Higher Education Institution Initiatives that Support the Mobility of Artists and Cultural Professionals).  In terms of activities, there is KILA, which is an event from the Directorate of Film, Music, and New Media, Kemendikbudristek, which seeks to revive national values ​​from an early age in a simple and easy-to-understand way, namely through songs and music. Songs and music are considered a universal language readily accepted and understood by all levels of society, especially children. In 2023, KILA competed in 2 categories: a song-singing competition for children ages 5-7 years and 8-13 years. Meanwhile, in 2024, KILA will present five competition categories, including (1) children's song-singing competition for ages 5-7 years; (2) song-singing competition for children ages 8-13 years; (3) children's songwriting competition for ages 5-7 years; (4) children's songwriting competition for ages 8-13 years; and (5) regional children's song arrangement competition. Apart from the competition, KILA also carries out awareness-raising activities for songs written by winners of the KILA competition to various schools in several regions in Indonesia.  Another activity area that can be reported is MTMF. This festival is part of the Indonesian Traditional Music Festival program under the Directorate of Film, Music, and Media, Kemendikbudristek, in collaboration with Wildhouse Production. MTMF was held to strengthen the Indonesian traditional music ecosystem and build the young generation's love for cultural identity. "Marasante" was chosen as the diction because it represents a philosophical concept to explain a shared vision in the efforts and ideals of preserving and developing traditional music. In Tidore's language conversation, marasante means "selfless courage." Marasante is also sung in local artistic poetry to describe the ideals and civilization of Tidore. At the 2023 event, youth from 4 Sultanates in North Maluku, namely Ternate, Bacan, Jailolo, and Tidore, were encouraged to collaborate with the theme "music of spices."  Then there is the Slendhang Biru Tak Pernah Usai event, specifically the Gondong Gunarto music concert, which brought back Ki Nartosabdo's work in collaboration with Imoeng Mulyadi (Tresnawara Chamber Orchestra) and two rising millennial artists, Kunto Aji and Fanny Soegi. The main aim of this concert is to preserve and develop the great works of Javanese Karawitan gending on the broader community and across generations so that they can be enjoyed by various groups in the context of cultural regeneration. The ten best songs by Ki Nartosabdho, which also complemented the excitement of this concert, were Lesung Jumengglung, Mawar Kuning, Ibu Pertiwi, Iki Saputanganmu, Adja Dipleroki, Slèndang Biru, Santi Mulya, Sarung Jagung, Adja Lamis, and Dara Muluk.   The last cultural regeneration effort can be reported through cultural broadcast programs. Along with the outbreak of the COVID-19 pandemic in 2020, Kemendikbudristek invited TVRI to work together to broadcast the Learning from Home (Belajar dari Rumah, BDR) program. BDR contains educational, cultural, and entertainment programs for all levels of education, starting from PAUD and equivalent, elementary school and equivalent, middle school and equivalent, and high school and equivalent, as well as parenting programs for parents. During prime time, selected children's and national films were shown as educational shows for children aged 4-13. National films also included educational films that showed typical Indonesian stories. On weekends, this program showed educational and cultural programs for all ages. In 2021, BDR moved to the TV Edukasi television channel owned by Kemendikbudristek. TV Edukasi will close in 2023 and eventually be replaced by INDONESIANA.TV (see Goal 3, Programs and Events to Increase Participation in and Access to Diversity of Cultural Expressions). Apart from the BDR program, Kemendikbudristek and TVRI also worked together to broadcast an annual program, namely National Culture Week (see Goal 1, Measures that Facilitate Dialogue Mechanisms between CSOs and the Government regarding Policies), which at the time of drafting this report had also moved to broadcast on INDONESIANA.TV.  In general, policies and measures for culture regeneration are aimed at contributing to achieving the following agenda(s) of the National Strategy for Culture:  1. Provide space for the diversity of cultural expressions and encourage cultural interaction to strengthen the inclusiveness of culture (Agenda 1);  2. Protect and develop values, expressions, and practices of traditional culture to enrich national culture (Agenda 2);  3. Utilize objects of culture advancement to improve people’s welfare (Agenda 4);  4. Culture advancement that protects biodiversity and strengthens ecosystems (Agenda 5);  5. Institutional reform and culture budgeting to support the culture advancement agenda (Agenda 6); and  6. Strengthen the role of the government as a facilitator of culture advancement (Agenda 7).
Results: SKKNI: See Goal 1, Policies and Measures for Education and Training Programs in Culture and Creative Economy Sectors. The List of SKKNI related to Culture and Creative Economy per Main Group in the Annexes section provides a complete list with document links.  LSP-P2 for Culture: See Goal 1, Policies and Measures for Education and Training Programs in Culture and Creative Economy Sectors.  Arts Institutions Standardization and Certification in Bali: See Goal 1, Policies and Measures for Education and Training Programs in Culture and Creative Economy Sectors.  Dana Indonesiana: See Goal 1, Measures that Provide Funds for CSO Capacity Development.  KILA: In 2023, socialization activities were conducted in Semarang, Surabaya, Makassar, and Medan. A total of 358 participants took part in the competition, while the KILA Performance in Jakarta involved 500 participants, with an audience of 2,956 people  In 2024, socialization activities will be conducted in Surakarta/Solo, Denpasar, Jakarta, and Palembang.
Financial Ressources: Dana Indonesiana: See Goal 1, Measures that Provide Funds for CSO Capacity Development.
