Title EN: Programme for the Promotion of Mexican Cinema (FOCINE)
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture
SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Cultural and creative sectors
Agency Implementation: Mexican Institute of Cinematography
Main Feature: Commencing in 2021, the Programme for the Promotion of Mexican Cinema (FOCINE) was launched with the primary goal of allocating resources to boost film projects and cultivate high-quality, diverse, inclusive, gender-equitable, and accessible Mexican cinema for all citizens. This initiative serves as an administrative framework that emerged from extensive dialogue held in July 2020 through 13 working groups with the film community. It builds upon and expands the support previously provided by the Fidecine and Foprocine trusts. FOCINE operates through three core components: support for production, exhibition, and the preservation of collections. The production support component encompasses nine distinct modalities: •	Experimental cinema •	Production of fiction feature films •	Production of documentary feature films •	Pre-production and production of short films and animated features •	Production of films targeted at children •	Debut films from film schools or specialized programs •	Short films focused on regional themes and established trajectories •	Post-production services for feature films and shorts •	Collaborative productions with Mexican states  In addition, FOCINE includes an exhibition component with two specific calls for proposals. The first, "Support for equipment and/or conditioning of film exhibition spaces and projects," aims to provide economic subsidies to enhance and professionalize exhibition venues and projects. This initiative ensures that Mexican cinema remains accessible to all, thereby safeguarding the constitutional right to culture. The second call, "Support for Mexican film exhibition programs," offers financial subsidies to diversify film exhibition options, thereby expanding audiences and bolstering the appreciation of Mexican cinema nationwide.  Lastly, FOCINE's "Support for the creation and preservation of collections" is designed to fund projects focused on researching, cataloging, digitizing, restoring, and facilitating access to audiovisual and cinematographic materials. This initiative underscores FOCINE's commitment to preserving Mexico's rich cinematic heritage while facilitating broader public access to these cultural assets
Results: During the three-year period under FOCINE, significant strides were made in bolstering Mexican cinema across production, exhibition, and preservation fronts. The program facilitated the production of 232 film projects through nine calls for production support. These initiatives encompassed a wide spectrum, including animation, debut films from film schools, children's films, experimental cinema, and collaborations with various states. FOCINE's support for exhibition proved instrumental as well, with 142 projects funded from 2021 to 2023. This included 49 grants for equipment and 93 for exhibition programs, crucially enhancing the accessibility and diversity of Mexican cinema in theaters across the country. Independent cinemas were particularly supported, helping to broaden the range of films available beyond mainstream commercial offerings and reaching all 32 states, thus contributing to decentralization efforts.  Additionally, the initiative to create and preserve film collections marked a significant milestone, providing 53 grants from 2021 to 2023. These grants supported projects ranging from research to restoration, ensuring the longevity and accessibility of Mexico's audiovisual heritage for future generations.  IMCINE's concerted efforts through the Program for the Promotion of Mexican Cinema under FOCINE spurred economic activity related to the film industry nationwide. This not only amplified the expression and visibility of local realities but also led to a historical high in film production. The years 2022 and 2023 saw record-breaking numbers of Mexican feature films produced, surpassing the prolific era of the country's golden age of cinema. Notably, around half of these productions received public support, underscoring FOCINE's pivotal role in sustaining and diversifying Mexican cinematic output
Financial Ressources: In 2021, FOCINE allocated  $9,507,660.96 dollars. The following year, in 2022, the allocation increased to ($11,283,753.29 dollars. In 2023, FOCINE disbursed  $9,909,232.48 dollars- Altogether, over the past three years, FOCINE has distributed a total of   $30,700,646.74 US dollars.
Recommandations: From 2020 to 2023, the National Council for the Evaluation of Social Development Policy conducted an analysis of the Programme for the Promotion of Mexican Cinema (FOCINE). The evaluation identified several key findings:  Strength: The program's ability to support film production was highlighted as a significant strength, reflecting its popularity among producers.  Weakness: A noted weakness was the program's tendency in the project selection process to favor proposals with optimal production conditions or delivery processes.  Recommendation: The evaluation recommended that FOCINE review the timeline established in its call for proposals to allow registered projects more time for necessary documentation corrections. This adjustment is aimed at enhancing the selection process and increasing the number of selected film projects.

Title EN: Sharjah Calligraphy Biennial
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture
SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Cultural and creative sectors
Agency Implementation: Sharjah Department of Culture
Main Feature: Launched in 2004, the Sharjah Calligraphy Biennial is a prestigious event that celebrates the art of Arabic calligraphy in both its traditional and modern forms. Organized by the Cultural Affairs Department at the Department of Culture in Sharjah and under the patronage of His Highness Dr. Sheikh Sultan bin Muhammed Al Qasimi, Supreme Council Member and Ruler of Sharjah, the Biennial invites renowned calligraphers and practitioners from around the world to showcase their art, engage in workshops, seminars, performances, and participate in award ceremonies. The event attracts global participation, with calligraphers from various countries showcasing a wide spectrum of traditional and modern calligraphic styles. The Biennial offers numerous educational opportunities through workshops and seminars, promoting technical, aesthetic, and intellectual advancement in Arabic calligraphy. Significant prizes are awarded to outstanding works, with a main prize of $15,000 and several other prizes for both traditional and modern calligraphic arts. Each edition of the Biennial has a specific theme, with the 11th edition themed "Taraqim," encouraging artists to explore and innovate within the realm of Arabic calligraphy. The general exhibition is divided into two sections: Traditional Calligraphy, adhering to classical artistic and aesthetic traditions, and Modern Calligraphic Arts, including contemporary, letter-based, and conceptual works. The Sharjah Calligraphy Biennial plays a significant role in preserving and promoting Arabic calligraphy as a vital cultural and artistic practice. It serves as a global platform for cultural exchange, innovation, and the dissemination of knowledge related to Arabic calligraphy. The Biennial fosters appreciation for this art form, encouraging both historical continuity and contemporary reinterpretation.
Results: This prestigious event attracts a diverse array of artists from around the world, emphasizing the global appreciation and practice of calligraphy. By opening submissions, the Biennial fosters an inclusive platform for artists of various cultural backgrounds to showcase their work, thereby promoting cross-cultural dialogue and artistic exchange. The anticipated participation of both renowned and emerging calligraphers highlights the Biennial's role in supporting artistic talent and enhancing the cultural landscape of Sharjah. The submission phase is expected to yield a rich collection of calligraphic works that reflect a multitude of styles, traditions, and innovations, underscoring the event's commitment to cultural diversity and artistic excellence.

Title EN: Programme of Cooperation between the Ministry of Culture of the Republic of Lithuania and the Ministry of Culture and Information Policy of Ukraine
Goal: Integrate Culture In Sustainable Development Frameworks
SDG: SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: International cooperation for sustainable development
Cultural Domain: Design,Performing Arts,Media Arts,Cinema and Audiovisual Arts,Music,Publishing,Visual Arts
Agency Implementation: Ministry of Culture of the Republic of Lithuania and Ministry of Culture and Information Policy of Ukraine
Main Feature: Programme of Cooperation between the Ministry of Culture of the Republic of Lithuania and the Ministry of Culture and Information Policy of Ukraine was signed on 18 March 2021.   The two countries have focused on sharing experience in cultural policy development and implementation, exchanges of experts and creative partnerships. The two countries have long been linked by the movable and immovable cultural heritage in their territories, exchange of expertise, exhibitions and publications.  The two sides agreed to further develop cultural cooperation in the fields of theatre, music, choreography, fine and amateur arts, film, literature, creative industries, libraries and museums, the preservation and effective use of monuments and other objects of cultural and historical heritage.   There is also a commitment to cooperate in the field of preservation of national minority culture and to promote initiatives of the Lithuanian national minority in Ukraine and the Ukrainian national minority in Lithuania.   The Programme provides more opportunities for young cultural professionals from both countries for exchanges, visits, joint creative initiatives and ambitious projects.
Results: Since the beginning of Russia's war against Ukraine, Lithuania's cultural sector has focused on supporting Ukrainian art and culture workers who have come to Lithuania to ensure their decent living conditions and provide them with opportunities to create and work in Lithuania.  From year 2022 The Lithuanian Council for Culture has been allocating Grants for Ukrainian cultural and professional artists who have temporary residence permits to stay in Lithuania. The purpose of this grant for Ukrainian artists who have been forced to flee from Russian invasion is to support the creative activities of those who have found refuge in Lithuania and to promote their cooperation with the Lithuanian cultural community in the fields of architecture, libraries, circus, art, design, ethnic culture and folk art, photography, cultural heritage, literature, museums, music, dance, interdisciplinary art and theatre. The amount of the grant is approx. USD 1980 (EUR 1 800), and it is awarded for a period of 3 months.  The Lithuanian Film Centre under the Ministry of Culture since 2022 has been allocating grants to Ukrainian citizens, film culture or art creators. The purpose of the grants is to support the creative activities of Ukrainian citizens, film culture or art creators (artists), and to promote their cooperation with the film community of the Republic of Lithuania in the fields of film culture and art or the dissemination of art and film culture. Adult citizens of Ukraine, film culture or art creators, who have been granted temporary protection in the Republic of Lithuania are entitled to receive grants.The amount of the grant is EUR 1 800 and it is awarded for a period of 3 months.  The Lithuanian Council for Culture: in year 2022 - 2023, 210 grants were funded. The Lithuanian Film Centre:  in year 2022 – 2023, 16 grants were funded.  For more information: https://www.lkc.lt/finansavimas/stipendijos-ukrainos-pilieciams-kino-kulturos-ar-meno-kurejams  Ukrainian war refugees with temporary residence permits can visit Lithuanian museums free of charge. Public libraries also offer free Lithuanian language training and designated spaces for Ukrainian children to play, read literature in Ukrainian, watch films, or engage in other creative activities.   A close mutual cooperation is going on between Lithuanian museums (Lithuanian National Museum of Art, The National Museum – Palace of the Grand Dukes of Lithuania, National Museum of Lithuania, Trakai History Museum, The Lithuanian Ethnocosmology Museum, Open-air Museum of Lithuania) and partners from Ukraine (The National Museum of the History of Ukraine, Lviv Historical Museum, Zaporizhzhya Regional Museum of Local Lore, Lviv National Art Gallery of Boris Voznicki, the Lviv History Museum, Klimentis Szeptycki Museum of Architecture and Household in Lviv, the Serhiy Pavlovych Koroliov Museum of Cosmonautics in Zhytomyr and others) implementing the Lithuanian-Ukrainian bilateral projects.  In June 2023, the Association of Lithuanian County Public Libraries organised the first Ukrainian-Lithuanian librarians' forum “The role of libraries in strengthening democratic society”. Media and informational literacy was the main topic of the forum. Other topics – the role of academic and librarian institutions in the development of a democratic society, bibliotherapy, and art therapy were also discussed. The forum took 3 days, main libraries in Vilnius, Kaunas, and Klaipėda were visited. The second forum took place in 2024, with topics, relevant to Ukrainian librarians (institutional preparedness for extreme situations, cooperation network, and networking practices; integration, promotion of active citizenship, ensuring access to services, and use of libraries in building emotional and mental wellbeing and resilience; and media and informational literacy education, cultural heritage preservation, and actualization in libraries) and with sharing of good practices, presentation of product and services as well as librarian tools.   Since 2018, the Ministry of Culture, together with the Ministry of Education, Science and Sport, has been implementing the "Culture Passport" programme for cultural education for children and young people. All pupils studying in Lithuania under the general education curriculum (including Ukrainian children from 2023) are allocated funds for the Culture Passport services, which can be accessed by pupils (teacher coordinators) logged into the Cultural Education Information System (hereinafter – KEIS). Ukrainian schools relocated to Lithuania have also been allocated the funds for Culture Passport. All-Ukrainian International School have joined the KEIS.  On June 7, 2024, an international conference was held in Vilnius, Towards the Recovery of the Culture Sector of Ukraine, highlighting the importance of the culture sector for reconstructing Ukraine after the war. This was clearly stated in the conference’s concluding document (Vilnius Call for Action on the Recovery of the Culture Sector of Ukraine). The conference endorsed the updated Action Plan for Culture in Ukraine, developed by Ukraine and UNESCO together with international partners. Conference participants committed to contributing to implementation of the Action Plan. Representatives of 31 countries (Austria, Belgium, Bulgaria, Canada, Croatia, Czechia, Denmark, Estonia, Finland, France, Germany, Greece, Iceland, Ireland, Italy, Japan, Latvia, Lithuania, Luxembourg, the Netherlands, Norway, Poland, Romania, Sakartvelo, Slovakia, Spain, Sweden, Switzerland, Ukraine, the United Kingdom, the USA) and international organisations and non-governmental organisations approved the conference’s concluding document.   Six priorities for the recovery of the cultural sector in Ukraine were identified in the updated Action Plan, along with interventions needed to implement the priorities in the following areas: 1) monitoring, assessment, and documentation of damage to cultural heritage in Ukraine; 2) preventive and urgent measures, repairs, reconstruction, and recovery of cultural heritage; 3) revival of institutional capacity of cultural institutions and cultural education; 4) strengthening cultural and creative industries of Ukraine; 5) strengthening resilience through culture; 6) digital transformation of cultural heritage management, development of digital infrastructure, creation of digital cultural heritage inventories for integration and interoperability with international databases.  In this respect, Lithuania will make commitments to implement specific measures addressed to a more sustainable, economically viable restoration of Ukraine’s culture and its heritage.
Financial Ressources: In 2022- 2023, the Lithuanian Council for Culture allocated over USD 420 000 (EUR 378 000) in total and The Lithuanian Film Centre allocated over USD 32 000 (EUR 28 800)) accordingly.

Title EN: PROJECT “PROMOTION OF CULTURAL AND CREATIVE INDUSTRIES IN THE CITY OF LA PAZ, BOLIVIA”
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture
SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Cultural and creative sectors
Cultural Domain: Design,Performing Arts,Media Arts,Cinema and Audiovisual Arts,Music,Publishing
Agency Implementation: Cultural Vision Foundation, Plurinational Coordinator of Cultural Spaces
Main Feature: The Plurinational Coordinator of Self-Managed Cultural Spaces (PCSCS)(CPECA), through its La Paz Regional Office and the Visión Cultural Foundation, executed between June 2022 and January 2024 the project “Promotion of Cultural and Creative Industries in the city of La Paz, Bolivia”, which was the winner of the 12th version of the International Fund for Cultural Diversity (IFCD). This project was characterized by having a broad and even ambitious vision, based on responsible co-management, interculturality and collaborative work. It focused on:  a) Helping to generate conditions and capacities to promote cultural entrepreneurship and the development of cultural and creative economies. b) Promoting the socialization and full implementation of regulations and public policies as a decentralized entity for the full exercise of cultural rights, mainly in the municipality of La Paz. c) Strengthening the management and sustainability capacities of the Self-Managed Cultural Spaces (SCS), as well as enhancing the actions of articulation, coordination, communication, representation, proposal and political influence of the Plurinational Coordinator of Self-Managed Cultural Spaces (PCSCS). It involved carrying out a variety of activities such as: mapping and diagnostics, training, education and advisory processes, creating spaces for exchanging experiences, discussion, socialization and proposals, and preparing guides, directories, manuals and protocols, in addition to advocacy, coordination, alliances and networking actions with more than fifty cultural institutions and organizations, both public and private, and from civil society. The project activities were grouped into three components: a)	Cultural and Creative Economies - Strengthening Cultural Entrepreneurship: It was aimed at contributing to the reactivation, development, innovation, competitiveness and collaborative work of the cultural and creative industries sectors, collaborative economies and community production systems of the municipality of La Paz and its projection at a national level, through the mapping and visualization of successful cultural entrepreneurship experiences, the creation of spaces for meeting, exchange, transfer of knowledge and information, processes of formation and incubation of projects and the accompaniment of cultural entrepreneurships, as well as the development of cultural markets at a decentralized level and, from them, the promotion of the consumption of cultural goods and services, mainly from the SCS of the PCSCS. b)	Cultural Rights - Dissemination and deepening of the regulatory framework in favor of the cultural development of the municipality of La Paz and Institutionality and Political Influence: It focused on promoting the socialization and full implementation, as decentralized, of municipal public regulations and policies for the promotion of cultural and creative economies and the strengthening of self-managed cultural spaces in the municipality of La Paz, through socialization, training processes and the proposal for the creation of Cultural Information, Advice and Guidance Points in different macro-districts, as well as the participatory evaluation of the status, degree of compliance and results of Municipal Autonomous Law 265/319 for the Promotion, Safeguarding, Development and Promotion of Cultures and the Arts and its regulations. c)	Strengthening the cultural management and articulation capacities of the PCSCS and its member SCS: it was focused on strengthening the capacities of articulation, coordination, representation, proposition, communication and political incidence of the Plurinational Coordinator of Cultural Spaces, as well as sustainability, self-management, entrepreneurship, collaborative work and interaction with other social, cultural and territorial actors of its members to constitute them as agents of structural change, through normative and operational institutional strengthening, enhancement of spaces for transfer and exchange of knowledge and expertise as well as collaborative work for access to benefits, incentives and funds established by law, and the improvement of its mechanisms as tools for planning, monitoring, communication, evaluation and interaction with other networks, organizations and sociocultural actors at local, national and international levels. Furthermore, these components have been strengthened through the implementation of a cross-cutting Communication Strategy. This was focused mainly on social media and aimed at promoting content that showed the progress, development and results of the project to the target audiences and cultural sectors identified as beneficiaries.  Three levels of information and content management were developed:  1. On the development of the project 2. Regarding general information related to the cultural field  3. strengthening of the PCSCS.  Each level included the creation of information material, development of concepts, development of themes in various areas of cultural communication and the creation of visual, written and audiovisual products for dissemination in the media and virtual platforms .
Results: The main results of the project for each of its components are: 1.	Cultural and Creative Economies -	Mapping 50 successful cultural ventures -	Directory of Cultural Enterprises -	A National Meeting of “Self-Managed Cultural Enterprises” -	Handbook for the development of cultural enterprises -	Ten workshops on Introduction to Cultural Entrepreneurship -	Six training processes for the incubation of 51 cultural ventures in music, performing arts, visual and plastic arts, audiovisual arts, alternative fashion design and sociocultural ventures -	Decentralized Cultural Market and Business Roundtable in six creative sectors 2.	Cultural Rights -	A training process for promoters of the Municipal Autonomous Law 265/319 -	Information booklet on the contents of Municipal Autonomous Law 265/319 -	24 workshops to disseminate the Municipal Autonomous Law 265/319 -	12 artistic interventions to raise awareness and appreciation of the rights and roles of cultural workers in society for children and youth -	A digital media communication campaign on Law 265/319 -	Participatory evaluation of Law No. 265/319 and proposed amendment. -	Cultural Information, Advice and Guidance Points Project (IACOP)(PIAOC), aimed at providing information, advice and guidance on issues related to the cultural field and citizen participation. 3.	Institutionality and Political Incidence -	PCSCS Strengthening Plan 2023-2026 -	Two National Meetings of Self-Managed Cultural Spaces -	Management of legal status of two PCSCS Regional Offices -	A communication campaign in digital media providing information about the PCSCS and its SCS. -	Diagnosis of the current situation of self-managed cultural spaces at the national level . -	Guide to Self-Managed Cultural Spaces members of the PCSCS -	Bank of ECA projects members of the PCSCS -	Manual for the preparation and management of projects and resources in the public, private and international sectors -	Training process to strengthen the self-management and sustainability capacities of cultural spaces that are members of the PCSCS -	National mapping of 50 territorial sociocultural organizations and 10 national and international Cultural Networks -	Directory of 185 Socio-Cultural Organizations at the national level -	Strategy to improve the relationship and joint work of the PCSCS, as well as the member SCS, with territorial sociocultural organizations -	Management to establish relationships and work spaces of the PCSCS with public institutions in the cultural field and with national and international networks in the cultural field.

Agency Implementation: Ministry of education, science, culture and sports of the Republic of Armenia
Main Feature: The Ministry of education, science, culture and sport of the Republic of Armenia reaize co-financing projects related to the mobility of artists, cultural and art professionals. The goal of this cultural policy measure is systemic support for promotion of international cultural cooperation and armenian culture and art abroad; for exchange and networking through the participation of artists and professionals from Armenia in international festivals, competitions, biennalle, exhibitions, events, seminars, workshops, conferences, master-classes, as well as through study and residency programs, and the similar, which are related to all fields of culture and the arts. The program is intended for bilateral and multilateral cultural cooperation and cover costs of international flights and accommodation only for artists and professionals in the field of arts, cinema and culture. Priority is given to individuals who are recipients of recognitions and/or awards in the fields of culture and the arts, members of international bodies and professional networks, art associations, and participants in prominent international cultural events. The professional commission formed by the Ministry of education, science culture and sport decide to approve or refuse participant.
Results: The number of applications is increasing every year, which proves the effectiveness and demand of the program. In 2020-2023, 350 applications were submitted for the movement of artists and specialists in the field of culture and art, and 240 received co-financing support, the pass rate of which was 68,5%.

Recommandations: The reports of participants and department’s report is the basis for an annual evaluation of the given policy/measure and the assessment of the call’s success. In the period 2020- 2023, there was a lot of interest in the program, therefore funding for the project has been increased. Projects supported within the call included co-financing artists’ mobility in a large number of countries. The majority of the applicants were associations of music artists, painters, performing artists, as well as cultural and art societies, and cultural institutions.

Goal: Promote Human Rights And Fundamental Freedoms
SDG: SDG 5 - Achieve gender equality and empower all women and girls,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels

Cultural Domain: Design,Performing Arts,Media Arts,Cinema and Audiovisual Arts,Music,Publishing,Visual Arts
Agency Implementation: Ministère de la Jeunesse de la Culture et de la Communication-Département de la Culture
Main Feature: Le gouvernement marocain a récemment adopté un projet de décret visant à mettre en œuvre un régime obligatoire d'assurance maladie et de retraite pour les artistes travaillant à leur compte. Cette mesure impose une cotisation mensuelle de 18 dollars au régime d'assurance maladie de la CNSS, bénéficiant à environ 10 000 artistes détenteurs de cartes professionnelles. Les artistes du secteur public ne sont pas inclus, étant déjà affiliés à un régime de couverture sociale de la fonction publique. Le ministre Mohamed Mehdi Bensaid a souligné l'engagement royal à développer l'économie culturelle, assurant que cette initiative vise à améliorer les conditions de travail et de création des artistes tout en garantissant une couverture médicale à 70% des dépenses, complétée prochainement par une assurance complémentaire.
Results: Ce Projet de décret constitue une base solide donnant le coup d’envoi à la création imminente d'une fondation dédiée à la protection sociale des artistes marocains. Cette fondation sera spécifiquement orientée vers la résolution des problèmes sociaux des acteurs culturels, notamment en matière de santé et de logement, en proposant des solutions durables et efficaces. Par ailleurs, le ministre a souligné que le ministère apporte déjà son soutien aux artistes en prenant en charge discrètement les frais d'hospitalisation, garantissant ainsi la confidentialité pour préserver la dignité des artistes.

Main Feature: -	Mettre en place des structures de collecte des statistiques ; -	Identifier les statistiques, notamment les statistiques culturelles ; -	Collecter les statistiques, notamment les statistiques culturelles ;   -	Harmoniser les statistiques, notamment les statistiques culturelles   -	Améliorer les statistiques, notamment les statistiques culturelles ;  -	Evaluer les statistiques culturelles ; -	Déterminer l’apport des statistiques issues des différents domaines d’activités dans le PIB.
Results: La mise en œuvre du Projet a commencé à des périodes différentes dans les pays d’Afrique de l’Ouest et du Centre. Pour ce qui concerne le Mali, on peut noter : -	Renforcement des capacités du personnel de la Cellule de planification et de statistique (CPS) ; -	Dotation de la CPS en matériels et équipements en vue d’améliorer les conditions de collecte des statistiques ; -	Amélioration des statistiques collectées au plan quantitatif et qualitatif ;  -	Harmonisation des concepts et du contenu des fiches avec les autres pays de l’Afrique de l’Ouest ; -	Disponibilité, stockage et conservation des statistiques collectées.

Main Feature: La principale mission d’Africadoc en Côte d’Ivoire est le Développement et la Promotion du cinéma documentaire de création, en Côte d’Ivoire et en Afrique. Il contribue au renforcement de compétences des professionnels du secteur, au développement  les échanges et les réseaux professionnels dans des relations Sud-Sud et Sud-Nord. Il intensifie la diffusion des films documentaires, il fédère des partenaires œuvrant aux mêmes objectifs en Afrique et au-delà, et  contribute ainsi  à la croissance du secteur du cinéma documentaire au niveau économique, social et culturel. Le projet Impala comprend une innovation. Il  vise à renforcer le secteur du cinéma documentaire de 11 pays d’Afrique en diffusant des films documentaires africains pour des lycéens et étudiants, en renforçant les capacités de 40 jeunes professionnels dont au moins 16 femmes, en incubant des projets de films dont l’accès aux marchés sera facilité par l’organisation de Rencontres internationales de coproduction.  Africadoc à travers ce projet  contribue à la structuration du secteur du film documentaire en Afrique. En formant, les jeunes aux métiers du cinéma documentaire (la réalisateur, le montage, la prise de son et d’image, un accompagnement à l’écriture du cinéma à travers des ateliers, des formations sur les fondamentaux de la production, créer un cadre de rencontre entre le professionnel du Sud et du nord enfin promouvoir les films en faisant de la diffusions.
Results: La cible a été atteinte en termes de nombre de personnes et d’âge. Les femmes sont un peu moins représentées que souhaité. C’est également le cas pour le nombre de pays : 8 pays sont représentés au lieu de 11 dans le projet. La qualité des projets et surtout leur potentiel à aller à leur terme ont été privilégiés afin d’assurer le plus d’impact au projet. L’ensemble des porteurs de projets a travaillé sérieusement 18 projets sur 20 ont respecté l’échéance et présenté une dernière version afin de participer au processus de sélection pour les rencontres de coproduction.  14 sur ces 18 ont été retenus par le comité pédagogique pour participer aux rencontres de coproduction       29 participants aux Rencontres de coproduction, 8 rendez-vous individuels par projet, Qualité des pitchs jugée excellente par les participants notamment l’OIF 20 articles publiés (presse et web), 4 émissions radio et télé / 12 projets sur 14 sont en passe de trouver des partenaires

Title EN: PROJET UNESCO-ARSCHBERG L'ELABORATION DU PROJET D’ARRETE FIXANT LES CONDITIONS ET MODALITES D’ATTRIBUTION DE LA CARTE PROFESSIONNELLE D’ARTISTE
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture
SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Cultural and creative sectors
Cultural Domain: Design,Performing Arts,Media Arts,Cinema and Audiovisual Arts,Music,Publishing,Visual Arts
Agency Implementation: Direction des Affaires Juridiques et de la Coopération (DAJC)
Main Feature: Le projet UNESCO-Aschberg vise à promouvoir la diversité des expressions culturelles et à renforcer les capacités des professionnels de la culture à travers le monde. Il soutient des initiatives visant à développer des politiques culturelles durables et inclusives. Le projet offre des bourses, des formations, et des opportunités de mobilité pour les artistes et les professionnels de la culture, afin de favoriser le dialogue interculturel et la coopération internationale. Les activités tournent autour des ateliers, des résidences artistiques, et des programmes de mentorat. La Côte d'Ivoire a bénéficié en 2023 du fonds UNESCO -Aschberg dans le cadre de l'élaboration du projet de décret portant modalité d' attribution de la carte professionnelle de l'artiste. En effet, l’État de Côte d’Ivoire à travers le Ministère de la Culture et de la Francophonie a alloué plus de cinquante millions (50 000 000) Francs CFA à l’adoption du décret relatif au statut de l'artiste en application de la loi N° 2016-555du 25 juillet 2016 relative aux droits d'auteurs et droits voisins. Cela s’est traduit par l’organisation d’ateliers de rédaction et de validation ainsi que des tournées de sensibilisation. Aussi le Ministère en charge de la Culture, à travers la Direction des Affaires Juridiques et de la Coopération (DAJC) a vu son projet (projet d’arrêté fixant les conditions et modalités d’attribution de la carte professionnelle d’artiste) approuvé par le programme UNESCO-ASCHBERG pour les artistes et les professionnels de la culture. Le budget alloué s’élève à 30 000 $, soit environ dix-huit millions (18 000 000) Francs CFA
Results: Le projet UNESCO-Aschberg a permis de : -Renforcer les capacités des artistes et des professionnels de la culture dans divers pays. -Promouvoir la diversité culturelle et la liberté artistique. -Faciliter des échanges interculturels et des collaborations internationales. -Soutenir la création et la diffusion de projets artistiques innovants. -Contribuer à l'élaboration de politiques culturelles plus inclusives et durables. - rédiger le projet d’arrêté fixant les conditions et modalités d’attribution de la carte professionnelle d’artiste en Côte d'Ivoire.
Recommandations: L'évaluation a révélé que le projet UNESCO-Aschberg est efficace pour promouvoir la diversité des expressions culturelles et renforcer les capacités des acteurs culturels. Les principales recommandations sont: -  =Augmenter le nombre de bourses et d'opportunités de mobilité pour toucher plus d'artistes et de professionnels de la culture. -Renforcer les partenariats avec des institutions locales pour assurer une mise en œuvre plus efficace des programmes. - Développer des outils de suivi et d'évaluation pour mesurer l'impact des activités et améliorer les futures initiatives. - Promouvoir davantage les réussites et les impacts du projet pour attirer plus de soutien et de financement. Encourager l'intégration des résultats et des bonnes pratiques dans les politiques culturelles nationales.

Title EN: Promoting Cultural and Artistic Exchange and Cooperation between Viet Nam and the International Community, Bridging Local Artists to Regional and Global Art Market
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture
SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Partnering with civil society
Cultural Domain: Design,Performing Arts,Media Arts,Cinema and Audiovisual Arts,Music,Publishing,Visual Arts
Agency Implementation: Vincom Center for Contemporary Art (VCCA)
Main Feature: The Vincom Center for Contemporary Art (VCCA), established in June 2017, is a non-profit art center fully funded by Vingroup. Its mission is to connect artists with the community, artworks with art enthusiasts, and Vietnamese fine arts with global fine arts, contributing to the sustainable development of Vietnamese arts. VCCA's main activities include: (1) Organizing art exhibitions to showcase the works of local and international artists to bring Vietnamese and global art closer to the public, (2) Discovering, suppporting, and nurturing young talented artists through the young talented artist incubation program and various support activities, assisting Vietnamese artists to get access to and participate in regional and global art markets, (3) Conducting regular art education and experience programs for the community, including talks, discussions, performances, workshops, art tours, and more, aiming to shape aesthetic orientation and spread art knowledge widely among the public. The center has been developed based on diverse and professionally organized art activities, supported by international standard infrastructure and equipment, with a total area of nearly 4,000 square meters. The management and advisory board of VCCA includes reputable, experienced experts, and dedicated and talented artists from both Viet Nam and abroad to build a systematic and sustainable professional orientation that keeps pace with global trends, with the goal of positioning VCCA as one of the key art centers in the region and the world.
Results: During the period 2020-2023, VCCA organized 40 exhibitions and 159 art education programs and events, bringing together 800 artists from both Viet Nam and abroad, displaying over 2,150 artworks, and welcoming more than 1.8 million visitors. Notably, many of VCCA's exhibitions were large-scale, involving collaborations with renowned regional and global artists and curators who gain significant acclaim in the professional community and are well-received by the public. Prominent exhibitions included "TỎA" (2020, 2022), the "ASEAN Graphic Arts Exhibition – Viet Nam 2020," "The 5th Hanoi Art Connecting International Exhibition" (2022), and the "Emotional Tides" installation by Japanese conceptual artist Chiharu Shiota (2023). Through each exhibition, VCCA contributed to honoring and fully expressing the artistic language, personality, and philosophy of the exhibiting artists. VCCA also played a pioneering role in introducing masterpieces by world-renowned artists through digital exhibitions. Notable exhibitions included "Images and Distance: The Works of Gustav Klimt and Egon Schiele in Transition" (2020), "Radiant Silence," a digital exhibition on Claude Monet and Pierre Bonnard (2021), "Empathic Void," a digital exhibition of Piet Mondrian and Wassily Kandinsky's works (2022), and "This is Not a Dream," a digital exhibition of classic works by René Magritte and Frida Kahlo (2023). In June 2023, Hanoi Grapevine’s Finest, an annual event honoring cultural and artistic activities,  recognized VCCA as an active organizer. Additionally, the "TỎA IV" exhibition with the theme "Methods of Dialogue with Nature" of VCCA was selected by Hanoi Grapevine’s Finest to be listed in the category of Finest Projects of the Year. This exhibition was also highlighted as one of the must-see exhibitions worldwide by ArtForum magazine (USA). With the aim of supporting and nurturing young artistic talents, in the period 2020-2023, VCCA discovered, selected, and supported 276 promising young artists through various forms and programs. A notable initiative was the 2022 Talent Support and Development Program, aimed at identifying and supporting potential young Vietnamese artists on their professional creative journeys. This program included travel grants, creation grants for young artists' art projects in Viet Nam and abroad, and a series of capacity-building activities for young artists through thematic seminars, personal consultations for orientation, and workshops led by well-known artists and experienced experts from Viet Nam and around the world. Additionally, VCCA organized exhibitions to provide opportunities for young artists from various regions across the country to display and introduce their works and receive feedback and evaluation from professionals and the public. Some exhibitions included "What are we playing?" (2021), "Midpoint" (2022), "The Gardeners" (2023), "The Glory Heights" (2023), and "The Dreamers" (2023).

Title EN: Promoting the goals and principles of the 2005 Convention and the 2030 Agenda in the preparation of the new resolution on the National Programme for Culture 2024–2031
Goal: Achieve A Balanced Flow Of Cultural Goods And Services And Increase The Mobility Of Artists And Cultural Professionals
SDG: SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 10 - Reduce inequality within and among countries,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Treaties and agreements
Cultural Domain: Design,Performing Arts,Media Arts,Cinema and Audiovisual Arts,Music,Publishing,Visual Arts
Agency Implementation: Ministry of Culture
Main Feature: In 2023, the Ministry of Culture prepared a new National Programme for Culture for the period from 2024 to 2031. (The resolution on the National Programme for Culture was adopted on July 10, 2024) The Program cites the 2005 Convention on the Protection and Promotion of the Diversity of Cultural Expressions as one of the main documents from which it drew inspiration. Specifically, it refers to: - articles 1 and 2 (Objectives, Guiding Principles) when defining the goal of protecting cultural diversity. This includes support for cultural activities of ethnic minorities and cross-policy internationalization, through which the country aims to integrate culture into international flows and contribute to intercultural tolerance. The main directions of this cross-cutting policy include the promotion of dialog, the promotion of coexistence between different communities and the advocacy of comprehensive intercultural exchange. - article 7 (Measures to promote cultural expressions) when emphasizing the need to understand culture as a public good that requires stable public funding and support to be accessible to all inhabitants regardless of their status or personal circumstances. The content of Article 7 is also in line with the three objectives of the resolution: high-quality and diverse arts and autonomous evaluation, a developed system for disseminating cultural content and ensuring its accessibility, and independent and high-quality media, including investigative journalism. - article 11 (Participation of civil society), when emphasizing a sustained dialog with stakeholders and a rapid response to challenges. As the name suggests, this approach defines a modern way of policy making by involving different stakeholders in the policy development process. - article 10 (Education and public awareness) to promote the goal of recognizing the importance of culture and its impact in the public sphere and committing to raising public awareness of the importance of culture and its contribution to a more egalitarian society, as well as supporting the media and cultural research through public funding. In the chapter dedicated to intersectoral cooperation, three goals - the role of culture in health and well-being, the role of culture in sustainable cities, human settlements and communities, and the role of culture in reducing inequality - relate directly to three goals of the 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development: - goal 3 (Good health and well-being): the programme recognises the importance of culture in improving mental and physical health. It emphasises integrating cultural activities into health and social care systems, supporting community-based cultural projects that promote mental health, and ensuring access to cultural experiences for all ages. - goal 10 (Reduce inequalities): the programme emphasises the need to promote equal access to cultural activities and resources, especially for disadvantaged groups, people with disabilities, and local communities. It advocates measures that eliminate cultural inequalities, improve access to buildings for people with reduced mobility and facilitate decentralisation. - goal 11 (Sustainable cities and communities): the programme emphasises the role of culture in urban development and community cohesion. It promotes the inclusion of cultural aspects in urban planning and public funding for sustainable cultural initiatives, as well as a more environmentally friendly approach to cultural heritage.
Results: The first results will be seen in the next few years.

Title EN: Promoting the integration of culture into sustainable development policies
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture
SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Cultural and creative sectors
Cultural Domain: Design,Performing Arts,Media Arts,Cinema and Audiovisual Arts,Music,Publishing
Agency Implementation: Ministry of Education, Science, Culture and Sport of the Republic of Armenia
Main Feature: In the reporting period, consistent works have been carried out to value and appreciate culture as sustainable development potential. The role of culture in economic stability, preservation of national identity, formation of the civil society and social capital in the country, preservation of peace, cultural diversity is studied. The Government Programme 2021-2026 of the Republic of Armenia which includes provisions concerning the economy, urban development, healthcare, nature protection, culture and other sectors, and is aimed at the development of tax policy and administration, institutional modernisation and development of infrastructures of the country. “The Strategy of promotion, preservation and development of culture in the Republic of Armenia for 2023-2027” also emphasizes the role of culture in sustainable development. The success of implementation of the cultural policy firstly depends on the principle of state budgeting. The financing of the cultural sector is carried out on the basis of programme budgeting, the priority areas of which derive from laws of the Republic of Armenia in force, decisions of the Government of the Republic of Armenia, as well as the system of measures designated by the sustainable development programme. The whole chain of “drafting - planning - budgeting” of those policies is implemented through triennial medium-term state expenditure frameworks, in the elaboration, financing, organisation, monitoring of which the civil society representatives in the composition of sectoral professional boards of the Ministry of Education, Science, Culture and Sport of the Republic of Armenia are engaged. In the field of culture the revenues geared down to the potential of economic growth are the revenues received from cultural services rendered to the public that mostly generate from the sales of tickets to treatre goers, concert goers and to exhibition visitors, lease of halls, premises, bailment of drawings, bibliographic and indexing services, sales of books, newspapers, etc. In 2023, the Armenian government has started to apply a new model of financing theater and concert organizations, according to which the organization is financed in the amount of twice its own income. The new financing model was implemented at the National Opera and Ballet Theater after Spendiaryan as the pilot project. From the point of view of building the capacities of national minorities and human capital, ensuring their education, importance is attached also to many non-governmental organisations and cultural centres of national minorities operating in the Republic of Armenia, the aim of which is to nurture national consciousness, preserve and develop the mother tongue, literature, history and culture. Inclusive creative measures and targeted educational programmes for full-fledged integration of vulnerable groups into the cultural life, providing conditions for their further creative development and progress, creating self-manifestation opportunities, as well as building a climate of tolerance in the public are implemented in the sector.
Results: Promoting the integration of culture into sustainable development policies has allowed to ensure sector stability, which is displayed in economic and social results. Consistent works for increasing the number of cultural goods and services are being carried out, which will result in growth in the number of the employed, will allow to essentially increase the money flow and reproduction capacities.  In Armenia live 11 national minorities and they have more than 50 non-governmental organizations. Part of whose work is a preservation and development of native languages. In addition to Assyrian, Yezidi, Russian, Greek, Kurdish ethnic communities, non-governmental organizations of Ukrainian, Jewish, Polish, Georgian, Belarusian and German ethnic communities are also active.  State care for the languages of national minorities is of great importance for the continuation of the process of democratization of the Republic of Armenia and the development of civil society. The languages of national minorities in Armenia are under state protection and enjoy special recognition. Article 41 of the Constitution of the Republic of Armenia stipulates the linguistic right of national minorities. Newspapers, school and fiction literature are published, programs are broadcast։ For the publishng of newspapers in the languages of national minorities (Yezidkhana, Rya Taza, Lalash, Dnipro, etc), an amount of 25000 $ USA (10 mln AMD) is allocated annually. In 2021 By the RA government's decision N 599 of April 15, the elements "Yezdi wedding ceremony" and "Assyrian New Year's celebration" were included in the list of intangible cultural heritage of RA that needs immediate protection. On November 4 of the same year, by the RA government's decision N 1825, the "Pontian dialect of the Greek population of Armenia" was included in the list of intangible cultural heritage of RA that needs immediate protection. In 2023 On November 30, the value of the "Buka barane" rainmaking ritual" of the Yazidi community was included in the same list by the RA government's decision N 2097-N. The process continues. 2020 the Helsinki Committee of Armenia prepared the research report “Rights of the largest national minority of the Republic of Armenia, the Yazidi community” which enjoyed the advisory support of the Ministry of education, science, culture and sport of the Republic. of Armenia (see link: https://armhels.com/publications/%d5%b0%d5%a1%d5%b5%d5%a1%d5%bd%d5%bf%d5%a1%d5%b6%d5%ab%d5%b0%d5%a1%d5%b6%d6%80%d5%a1%d5%ba%d5%a5%d5%bf%d5%b8%d6%82%d5%a9%d5%b5%d5%b8%d6%82%d5%b6%d5%b8%d6%82%d5%b4-%d5%a1%d5%b4%d5%a5%d5%b6%d5%a1/)  2020-2023 the process of installing trilingual signs in the territories of monuments belonging to national minorities continued. With respect to preservation of the national culture of national minorities, a series of events have been held, in particular, national participation in national holidays, national days and concerts of classical vocal music (Yezidi soloist, soprano Diana Amiryan (Germany) and Kurdish soloist, soprano Yulia Karatash (German). In 2020-2021 in Aragatsotn Marz, was implemented the program "Meeting with the Mountaineers", during which celebrations, performances of national music, song and dance, donations of books and newspapers were organized. 60-70 people of different ages and genders participated in similar events every year, the purpose of which is to ensure the vitality and continuity of traditional Yazidi holidays, to preserve national customs, manners, song and dance, food tradition, and to pass them on from generation to generation. In 2022-2023, from April to June, focusing on the participation of national minorities in educational, cultural and public life, educational programs for 60 Yazidi children from the Tashir community of the Lori region were organized. In December 2022-2023 the ministry was organized a cultural festival of national minorities residing in Armenia "The Roof: Armenia". The festival took place in the "Arno Babajanyan concert hall. Music and dance groups of all 11 minorities performed at the concert. Booths were set up in the foyer of the concert hall, where each community presented handicrafts, newspapers, books, etc.  22 representatives of national minorities work in cultural organizations under the RA Ministry of Education and Culture. Inclusive programs:  In the reporting period, in diverse fields of art (theatre, concert, film, visual arts, cultural education) various inclusive programmes have been implmented and events have been held, support has been provided to cultural programmes for creative groups and individuals having limited physical capacities. 900 children with disabilities, left without parental care and disadvantaged children have been included in the system of aesthetic education, the database of gifted children with disabilities has been replenished, support has been provided to their participation in many Republican and international projects, events dedicated to the International Disability Day have been held. Every year by support of the ministry NGOs realize 18 programs were implemented in the field of cultural education and 6 inclusive programs (Children and Youth Creative Summer School for children from vulnerable groups, “The taking works”, “Film School without Borders”, “Together” Inclusive Children and Youth Exhibition, “Side by Side” Inclusive Music Festival). The majority of the mentioned programmes were implemented in the marzes of the Republic of Armenia, including in border communities.  For the purpose of ensuring the participation of retired citizens in the cultural life, supporting the tradition of access of pensioners to cultural institutions, promoting active lifestyle of the aged, increasing the level of self-realisation and self-sufficiency, around 2000 retired beneficiaries were provided with free tickets in 2020-2023.
Financial Ressources: every year 208250 USD
Recommandations: Organizations functioning within the Ministry analyse their performances, make revenue forecasts generating from the provision of cultural services and approve the schedule for submission of monthly reports. Non-financial indicators are developed for each cultural programme, through which the effectiveness of use of funds, including the quanity or number, become measurable. As regards national minorities, opportunity was provided to unlock and promote the creative potential of certain strata of society, as well as their integration into the society was ensured through culture, with the targeted support of certain strata and creative programs of non-governmental organizations dealing with their issues.

Title EN: Promotion du droit à la pratique artistique inclusive
Goal: Integrate Culture In Sustainable Development Frameworks
SDG: SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: National sustainable development policies and plans
Agency Implementation: Association SOARBA;    Association Art au-delà du handicap (ADH) et Association Coiffure Solidaire du Boulkiemdé
Main Feature: La liberté d’expression artistique fait partie des droits culturels et humains et est consacré par plusieurs traités et conventions internationaux. L’activité artistique améliore la qualité de vie et contribue à l’épanouissement et à l’intégration sociale.     Au Burkina Faso, plusieurs organisations de la société civile culturelle prennent en compte la promotion des droits de l’homme et des libertés artistiques dans leurs interventions, particulièrement au profit des jeunes, des femmes et des enfants vulnérables ou vivants avec un handicap. Ces initiatives contribuent globalement à la création des conditions favorables à leur développement et à leur épanouissement, à leur insertion socioprofessionnelle. De façon spécifique, leurs actions permettent de lutter contre les formes de discrimination, d’assurer la formation artistique, de promouvoir des talents artistiques et culturels des personnes en situation de handicap et celles vulnérables.    Plusieurs initiatives ont été enregistrées sur la période 2020-2023 :   Le projet « Coup de pouce » consiste en une formation en arts plastiques, en cinéma et audiovisuel organisée par l’association SOARBA au profit d’enfants déficients auditifs. La 1ère édition a porté sur l’initiation à la peinture, la 2ème édition sur le renforcement de leurs capacités en peinture et sur leur initiation en cinéma d’animation.    Le projet « Lônni » consiste en la tenue de formations en danse, théâtre, musique, langage de signes et en informatique. Il est mis en œuvre par l’Association Art au-delà du handicap (ADH) au profit de 60 jeunes dont la majorité est en situation de handicap dans la ville de Bobo-Dioulasso. Les bénéficiaires ont été répartis par catégorie de handicap et de filière.    Le projet de formation en art capillaire de jeunes filles défavorisées et/ou vivants avec un handicap porté par l’Association coiffure solidaire du Boulkiemdé visait la promotion de l’entreprenariat créatif et l’autonomisation du public cible. Il a consisté en la tenue d’ateliers de formation en art capillaire, en esthétique et en gestion de micro-entreprises dans les provinces du Boulkiemdé et du Sanguié.
Results: La mise en œuvre de la mesure a permis d’atteindre plusieurs résultats.   Concernant le projet « Coup de pouce » :   contribution à l’expression et au développement des capacités des enfants déficients auditifs issus du Centre d’Education et de Formation Intégré des Sourds et Entendants (CEFISE);    14 enfants déficients auditifs initiés à la peinture sur la toile et au cinéma d’animation.   S’agissant du projet « Lônni » :   20 jeunes dont 10 en situation de handicap auditif ont participé aux ateliers de danse ;    20 jeunes dont 10 pensionnaires non-voyants de l’Union nationale des associations burkinabè des aveugles et malvoyants ont participé aux ateliers de musique ;   20 jeunes, dont plusieurs en situation de handicap auditif, moteur ont participé aux ateliers de théâtre ;   des cours d’informatique ont été dispens à tous les participants au projet pour maitriser les outils et pouvoir écrire eux-mêmes leurs projets artistiques ;   la formation des participants en langage de signe, devenue l’outil de communication de tous les participants et qui facilite l’inclusion du public en marge.   Pour le projet de formation en art capillaire de jeunes filles défavorisées et/ou vivants avec un handicap : 12 jeunes filles défavorisées formées en art capillaire, en esthétique et en gestion de micro-entreprises.   Coût des initiatives : 50 290,1 USD.

Title EN: Promotion du paysage audiovisuel national
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture

Area of Monitoring: Media diversity
Agency Implementation: Ministère de la Jeunesse de la Culture et de la Communication –Département de la Communication
Main Feature: 1.	La loi n° 77-03 relative à la communication audiovisuelle La loi n° 77-03 relative à la communication audiovisuelle promulguée par le Dahir n°1-04-257 du 7 janvier 2005 telle qu’elle a été modifiée et complétée a joué un rôle crucial dans la libéralisation du paysage audiovisuel au Maroc. Elle a constitué un jalon important dans le processus visant à mettre en place le cadre juridique de la libéralisation de ce secteur et qui a débuté avec la promulgation du dahir n° 1-02-663 du 31 août 2002 relatif à la création de la Haute autorité de la communication audiovisuelle et le décret-loi n° 2-02-663 du 10 septembre 2002 portant suppression du monopole de l’Etat en matière de radiodiffusion et de télévision, ouvrant ainsi la voie à la libre entreprise de communication audiovisuelle. Cette loi se fonde, dans sa philosophie générale et ses objectifs, sur les constantes et les référents constitutionnels du Royaume, la garantie de l’exercice de la liberté d’expression et d’opinion dans un esprit de responsabilité, ainsi que la consécration des valeurs de pluralisme, de modernité, d’ouverture, de respect des droits de l’Homme, tels que reconnus au niveau international.  L’article 4 de cette loi stipule que les opérateurs de la communication audiovisuelle conçoivent librement leurs programmes. L’indépendance éditoriale des opérateurs exige qu’ils définissent leurs contenus éditoriaux en dehors de toute influence, notamment celle des groupements idéologiques, politiques ou économiques.  Enfin, ce texte donne à la Haute Autorité de la Communication Audiovisuelle, dans le cadre des prérogatives et des attributions que lui confère le dahir qui l’a instituée, et aux différents pouvoirs publics compétents, les outils nécessaires pour réguler le secteur et accompagner son développement, en prévoyant les différents mécanismes et procédures à mettre en œuvre. 2.	Les cahiers de charges des opérateurs audiovisuels publics Les sociétés nationales de l’audiovisuel public (SNRT et SOREAD-2M), sont tenues par la loi 77-03, au respect d’un cahier des charges fixant leurs obligations particulières. Ces cahiers de charges sont établis par le gouvernement et approuvés par la Haute autorité de la communication audiovisuelle dans un délai de soixante (60) jours et publiés au Bulletin officiel. Ils définissent les obligations des sociétés nationales de l’audiovisuel public, notamment celles relatives à leurs missions de service public.  Les cahiers des charges stipulent que la liberté d'expression et le droit à l’information sont considérés comme éléments essentiels de la fonction publique de la communication audiovisuelle. Pour cela, les sociétés nationales de l’audiovisuel public s'appuient sur les principes de l'indépendance éditoriale et de la diversité d'expression de l’ensemble des courants de pensée et d'opinion, tout en garantissant les droits de l'opposition, dans le cadre des contrôles juridiques appliqués. Ils assurent le respect de la diversité linguistique et culturelle de la société marocaine et le maintien de la diversité des domaines tout en respectant les valeurs fondamentales et lois du Royaume. Dans ce cadre, la chaîne « AL Aoula » consacre 70% du temps de sa grille de référence aux programmes en langue arabe, sahraoui hassani et les autres dialectes et expressions marocaines et 20% à langue amazighe elle peut également proposer des programmes dans les langues étrangères les plus utilisées dans le monde. La chaîne « 2M » consacre 80% du temps de sa grille de référence aux programmes en langue arabe et langue amazighe et la langue sahraoui hassani et 20% aux programmes en langue étrangère. Depuis 2021, le Maroc a entamé un chantier de restructuration des sociétés nationales de radiodiffusion et de télévision à travers la création d’une société « Holding » du pôle audiovisuel public, La finalité de ce projet de restructuration est d'ériger un pôle audiovisuel public plus efficient, animé par les soucis d'optimisation et de synergie et disposant d'un modèle économique pérenne à même de lui permettre de répondre aux ambitions du Royaume.  Les principaux objectifs sont les suivants : •	L’amélioration de la qualité de la production nationale; •	La concentration sur les médias de proximité et les informations nationales ; •	L’accélération de la transformation digitale; •	Le maintien du financement du secteur audiovisuel national, et la rationalisation de l’intervention de l’Etat pour renouveler le capital…
Results: Le paysage audiovisuel marocain est composé d’une pluralité d’opérateurs aussi bien publics que privés.  Les sociétés nationales de l’audiovisuel public (SNRT et SOREAD 2M) assurent, dans l’intérêt général, des missions de service public tendant à satisfaire les besoins de culture, d’éducation, d’information et de divertissement du citoyen.  En termes de services édités, le paysage audiovisuel national compte :  	Une offre publique regroupant dix (10) services télévisuels, et (17) services radiophoniques :  	Quatre (04) généralistes à vocation nationale (Al Aoula, 2M, Tamazight et Medi1 TV) ;  	Une (01) télévision généraliste à vocation régionale (Laâyoune) ; 	Cinq (05) télévisions thématiques (Arriyadiya, Arrabiâ, Assadissa, Aflam et Al- Maghribiya) ;  	Six (06) radios à couverture nationale (Alwatania, Amazighe, Radio-2M, Chaine-Inter, Medi1 Radio et Mohammed VI du Saint Coran) ; 	Onze (11) radios à couverture régionale (Casablanca, Fès, Meknès, Tanger, Dakhla, Laâyoune, Marrakech, Agadir, El Hoceima, Oujda et Tétouan). La Société Nationale de Radiodiffusion et de Télévision (SNRT) a lancé au mois d’avril 2024 la première plateforme marocaine publique de vidéo à la demande (VOD),  « forja.ma » ayant pour objectif de mettre à la disposition des utilisateurs un catalogue de contenu audiovisuel 100% marocain. Ce nouveau service non linéaire est dédié exclusivement à la diffusion d’œuvres marocaines diffusées sur Al Aoula et 2M. Il vise à promouvoir le patrimoine culturel national, constitué de séries, films, pièces de théâtre et documentaires.  	Une offre privée constituée de : 	Une (01) télévision (Chada TV) ; 	18 radios diffusant sur la bande FM, dont (08) à couverture nationale, (04) à couverture multirégionales (Atlantic Radio, Cap radio, Luxe Radio et Radio Azawane) ; 	Un réseau de cinq (05) radios à couverture régionale (Radio plus) ; 	Une (01) radio à couverture multi-villes (U-Radio).  Sans compter deux télévisions satellitaires (Jeunesse et Documentaire) ayant obtenu licence et qui, et qui ne sont pas encore opérationnelles.
Financial Ressources: •	Société Nationale de Radiodiffusion (SNRT) en 2023 ; -	Investissement : 300 MDH ; -	Fonctionnement : 800 MDH ; -	FPPAAEP : 120 MDH ; •	SOREAD-2M : 65 MDH en 2023 ; •	Association des Radios et Télévisions Indépendants (ARTI) :  -	20 MDH depuis 2020 ; -	05 MDH annuelle.
Recommandations: La Cour des comptes a effectué une mission d’évaluation du paysage audiovisuel national. Au titre de l’année 2018, la Cour des comptes a réalisé deux missions de contrôle de la gestion des organismes publics et d’évaluation des programmes publics, concernant la Société nationale de radiodiffusion et de télévision « Diffusion terrestre et satellitaire des chaines de Télévision et de Radio » et la Société d’études et de réalisations audiovisuelles (SOREAD-2M).

Main Feature: As one of the challenges included in the last compliance report with respect to the 2005 UNESCO Convention, the need to have an Organic Law on Culture (LOC) that guarantees "cultural diversity, interculturality and cultural rights" and on which the sectoral public policy is legitimized and the institutional scheme related to its implementation is rationalized, was pointed out as one of the challenges included in the last compliance report with respect to the 2005 UNESCO Convention. On December 30, 2016, the new Organic Law of Culture was published in Official Gazette No. 913; its regulations were issued through Executive Decree 1428, published in Official Gazette Supplement 8, June 6, 2017.  This Law orders the National Culture System through two Subsystems: Subsystem of Social Memory and Cultural Heritage and the Subsystem of Arts and Cultural Innovation. This second subsystem aims, on the one hand, to renew the institutionality from the State, through the creation of two institutes (The Institute of Cinema and Audiovisual Creation ICCA-Ministerial Agreement No. DM-2017-052 dated August 09, 2017 and The Institute for the Promotion of Arts and Innovation and Creativities IFAIC-Ministerial Agreement No. DM-2017-053 dated August 09, 2017 and The Institute for the Promotion of Arts and Innovation and Creativities IFAIC-Ministerial Agreement No. DM-2017-053 dated August 09, 2017. DM-2017-053 dated August 09, 2017); and, on the other hand, to strengthen the use of the Fund for the Promotion of Arts, Culture and Innovation, established in Article 110 of the LOC, regulated by Ministerial Agreement DM-2018-046 dated April 04, 2018. Subsequently, these two institutes were merged by Presidential Decree 1039 dated May 8, 2021, into an entity called Instituto de Fomento a la Creatividad e Innovación IFCI, based on the Organic Statute of Organizational Management by processes contained in Ministerial Agreement MCYP-MCYP-2021-0044-A promulgated on May 16, 2021. These institutes and subsequently the IFCI are the ones called upon to establish lines of promotion that arise from the Fund for the Promotion of Arts, Culture and Innovation. From this fund, non-refundable resources are allocated to creators, producers and cultural managers, in accordance with the regulations issued for this purpose, seeking the artistic, cultural and creative strengthening of our society, with criteria of quality, diversity, territorial equity and interculturality.  The Fund for the Promotion of Arts, Culture and Innovation will have the following lines of financing:  (a) The Arts and Creativity Financing Line, administered by the Institute for the Promotion of Arts, Innovation and Creativity;  b) The Line of Financing for Cinematographic and Audiovisual Creation, administered by the Institute for Cinematographic and Audiovisual Creation; and,  c) Other lines of financing that may be established by the governing body of culture, aimed at the areas of Social Memory and Heritage or others, in accordance with its competencies. Each year public calls are opened for the free application of the citizenship.

Title EN: Promotion of creative cultural industries
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture
SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Cultural and creative sectors
Agency Implementation: Ministry of Culture
Main Feature: In the period from 2020 to 2023, the Ministry of Culture launched 3 public calls to finance the development of innovative projects and companies in the cultural and creative sectors. The funds were allocated for: - development of innovative ideas, companies or projects, - promoting the establishment and operation of companies, - promoting cooperation between the cultural and creative sector and the economy and the transfer of new ideas to the economy, - promoting entrepreneurship and entrepreneurial skills in the CCS sector through collaboration with mentors and inclusion in mentoring programs, - new jobs within the projects. The call supports creatives and businesses in the idea and prototype development phase, creative businesses in the growth and expansion phase and businesses from other sectors of the economy looking to restructure their work and offering with the help of creatives, designers, "design management" or other creative processes. Grants of between €15,000 and €40,000 are available for individual entrepreneurial phases. The public call for proposals is divided into three areas. The Concept Check area is used to develop/test a business idea prior to market launch. The aim is to create an innovative product or service, to promote innovation and new ideas in companies by funding tests and feasibility studies of innovative ideas, concepts and designs before the final development of the product/service or before market launch. Creative Start UP is designed to support companies operating in the cultural and creative sectors that are in a phase of rapid growth (to improve their business processes, promote ambitious innovative development projects and expand into international markets). It promotes products that have already proven themselves on the market but need capital for market entry, growth and expansion as well as professional organization of the company. Small and medium-sized enterprises are given the opportunity to grow, develop new production lines and thus create new jobs. The Creative CONNECTOR area is intended to promote cooperation between the economy and the cultural and creative sectors. The funding is aimed at small and medium-sized enterprises that operate outside the cultural and creative sector and have a long-standing presence in the market and intend to restructure their processes, products or services through collaboration with the cultural and creative sector in order to expand their markets at home or abroad. It promotes a) the integration of CCS into the economy in the development of high-tech products, b) the revitalization of traditional economic sectors with the help of CCS, c) the use of traditional crafts, skills, technologies and materials, and d) the enhancement of brands, including those related to culture and protected values, such as cultural landscape, knowledge, techniques and folk customs.
Results: The total number of applicants for all three public calls (in the period from 2020 to 2023) was more than 600. As part of the three public calls, The Ministry of culture supported the development of 166 innovative ideas within three program sections with financial incentives amounting to 4,590,000.00 euros, supported companies, products and services from the cultural and creative sector, stimulated 42 new collaborations between cultural workers and the economy and enabled 62 new jobs in creative companies.
