Title EN: Promotion of film distribution: The Slovenian Film Database
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture
SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Digital environment
Agency Implementation: Slovenian Film Centre
Main Feature: The Slovenian Film Database (Baza slovenskih filmov, BSF) is the national online platform providing information on Slovenian filmography from its beginnings to the present. It covers professional and amateur productions, commercial and experimental projects, and includes films and music videos. In addition to basic data, BSF provides access to photos, written material and videos that are essential for understanding the broader cultural and historical context of Slovenian filmmaking. BSF serves as a basic reference site for both experts and the general public, and is aimed at film lovers, connoisseurs and those who discover Slovenian cinema through BSF. At the end of October, BSF expanded its offer to include films on demand. In cooperation with Slovenian libraries, the Slovenian Public libraries Association and the Institute of Information Science (IZUM), members of partner libraries can also borrow films to watch online.
Results: The Slovenian Film Database (Baza slovenskih filmov) is an important first step towards better information for domestic and international audiences. Its further development in the coming years will also contribute to the popularization of Slovenian film. Loans and rentals of Slovenian films within the database are increasing - in the first full year of broadcasting, users rented 945 films, while in 2022 this number almost doubled to 1,717. Online access to Slovenian films (video on demand) is also possible through the service Filmoteka - RTV 365, which was launched in 2021 by RTV Slovenija (public broadcaster; however, it is a separate database), as well as through commercial video stores (commercial streamers, VOD, commercial TV networks, cable and digital providers). The total number of rentals of Slovenian films (via Baza slovenskih filmov, RTV-365 and two commercial streaming services) doubles from 2021 to 2023 (2021: 75,162 rentals - 2023: 144,598 rentals).

Title EN: Promotion of the Film industry in Cambodia

Area of Monitoring: Cultural and creative sectors
Agency Implementation: Department of Cinema and Cultural Diffusion of the Ministry of Culture and Fine Arts
Main Feature: This measure was adopted in 2017 to promote Cambodia’s emerging film industry, and to create an enabling environment for young filmmakers in Cambodia to be able to take part in film competitions at the national and international levels. The measure consists of two activities: short film training program and annual film festival.  Since the establishment of the program in 2017, the short film program has been designed to engage and encourage young people to take part in film industry. The program includes script writing, directing and cinematography. To date 133 trainees have been trained; and some of them now are able to produce high quality films, which are able to take part in the completions at national and international film festivals.  With film production skills, the young filmmakers can produce short films to take part in the Ministry of Culture and Fine Arts’s annual short film festivals. This short film festival is designed as a bridge for filmmakers to produce feature film to compete in Cambodia International Film Festival organized annually with participation of filmmakers from around the world.  In addition, to encourage the local film production, the Ministry of Culture and Fine Arts and the Ministry of Information signed an inter-ministerial agreement to create a “golden slot” from 7 p.m. to 8 p.m. for Cambodian films to be screened on the national televisions at a prime time (7 pm-8pm).
Results: To date 133 trainees have been trained; and some of them now are able to produce a quality film which can compete at the international film festivals.  Short and feature film festivals have alternately been organized every year along with Cambodia International Film Festival (2024 is the 13th International Film Festival. See https://cambodiaiff.com/).
Financial Ressources: Annual Financial resources allocated for the measure is about 122, 000.00 USD which can be broken down as the following:  -	Short film training program in 2023 was about 13000 USD. -	Financial resources allocated for the Short Film Festival in 2022 was 24000 USD. -	Financial resources allocated for the Feature Film Festival in 2021 was 50000 USD. -	Financial resources allocated for Cambodia International Film Festival in 2023 was about 35000 USD

Title EN: Promotion of the Government Scholarship Program for students to pursue cultural majors
Goal: Achieve A Balanced Flow Of Cultural Goods And Services And Increase The Mobility Of Artists And Cultural Professionals

Area of Monitoring: Mobility of artists and cultural professionals
Cultural Domain: Design,Performing Arts,Media Arts,Cinema and Audiovisual Arts,Music,Publishing,Visual Arts
Agency Implementation: -Ministry of Education and Higher Education -Ministry of Labour
Main Feature: The Government Scholarship Program for Students is a measure established by the State of Qatar for students wishing to pursue pre-university (diploma), university, and postgraduate studies at the State's expense, either within the State or abroad. This program is based on a set of policies and strategies that regulate the scholarship process to ensure effective contributions to the nation's development across all levels and sectors. In this context, the Ministry of Education and Higher Education is responsible for guiding, advising, and sponsoring students in collaboration with the Ministry of Labor, which is tasked with preparing the general policy for scholarships, coordinating with government entities to develop scholarship plans based on their needs, and then sending these plans to the Ministry of Education and Higher Education. Additionally, the amendment of the Ministry of Labor pursuant to Emiri Order No. (4) of 2021 has directly and indirectly encouraged students interested in benefiting from the Government Scholarship Program to enroll in universities specializing in cultural fields, whether national or foreign, due to the clear demand in the job market for national competencies in this area.

Title EN: PROMOTION OF THE PERFORMING ARTS - NUNA ESPACIO y ARTE
Goal: Achieve A Balanced Flow Of Cultural Goods And Services And Increase The Mobility Of Artists And Cultural Professionals
SDG: SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 10 - Reduce inequality within and among countries,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Flow of cultural goods and services
Agency Implementation: Luis Daniel Iturralde  EMAIL: Teatronuna@gmail.com PHONE: 69720355
Main Feature: Nuna Espacio Arte was founded in 2013 in the city of La Paz with the aim of providing high quality technical services for artists (considered clients who use our space to generate profits) and at the same time give comfort to different audiences to achieve a permanent and dynamic activity within the performing arts and music in the southern part of the city.  Nuna Espacio Arte has always sought to attract different artistic proposals by charging an affordable cost (quality/price ratio) and without neglecting the development of sustainability through the sale of food and drinks, subleases for courses, private corporate events, and external financing. On the other hand, it aims to maintain a schedule with as many presentations as possible per month to be a benchmark of dynamism within the performing arts and music. NUNAFEST is a festival produced by Nuna Espacio Arte. It has been in existence for 10 years and promotes artistic mobility to the city of La Paz from Cuba, the United States, Cameroon, Senegal, France, Spain, Argentina, Chile, Brazil, China, Romania, etc. Thanks to this festival, Nuna Espacio Arte is part of a network of music producers in the region that includes 11 countries and in this way, it manages to bring world-renowned artists at lower costs by joining tours coordinated by this network called Conexiones Culturales Latinoamerica CCLA. On the other hand, through alliances with producers of performing arts (Teatro.bo and Plataforma 1), Nuna Espacio Arte has managed to generate a project called Yvyrasacha, which promotes theatrical works by emerging authors from creation to staging of the works (physical and virtual). This project also promotes the inclusion of low-income audiences by managing financing from private companies to open free functions to public schools. Nuna Espacio Arte has managed to finance, through the Goethe Institute, a platform with online ticketing, which allows greater control over income and more convenience for the public who can purchase tickets on our platform or at the physical box office of the theater. This is not common to any cultural center in Bolivia since normally the ticketing is outsourced, generating a higher cost for the artist. In terms of training, there is a permanent acting workshop led by the renowned Bolivian-Spanish actress Patricia García, where students train for 6 months and then present a play in the same space. Promising actors and actresses have emerged from this workshop who are now part of the city's performing arts ecosystem. However, work must be done to formalize this course and deepen its content in order to obtain a diploma that endorses the knowledge gained by the students.  Besides our Runatiña percussion school, directed by me, is a place of recreation where more than 100 students learn the art of group percussion from basic to complex levels. This school allows many people to enter the world of music who would never have thought of making music due to advanced age or a mild mental condition.  We honor the popular origins of Afro-Bahian percussion by welcoming a variety of people of different ages and backgrounds, helping them achieve collective rhythmic goals that are very stimulating and healing, as strong bonds are often created between participants. It should be noted that 80% of our students are women and there is a women-only branch of the school called Warmitiña that supports events related to gender equality. Finally, we also offer temporary workshops in different artistic and technical disciplines (lights, sound, scenography, etc.), the latter to contribute to the development of the professionalization of the arts. The current space of the cultural center is rented, so the Teatro Nuna Espacio Arte plans to build the CCI-NUNA (Iturralde Cultural Center) by 2025, financed by the Kantutani Foundation in order to own a proper space that will have a theater for 500 spectators and one for 120, built to host works with high demands and at the same time taking into account self-sustainability through various spaces available for rent for restaurants and boutiques, parking service and a hall for multiple events (corporate, graduations, weddings, fairs, etc.) all this with the aim of generating surpluses for artistic and cultural production. This project aims to mark a before and after in the cultural sector at a national level, with the objective of promoting the professionalization of the performing arts and music through the management of resources generated by the same undertaking, without leaving aside the possibility of external financing to generate greater proposals and opportunities.  Finally, it is worth highlighting that this project will promote the inclusion of diverse artistic expressions (both classical and popular) and will provide opportunities to artists or casts from different backgrounds.
Results: Since its founding, Nuna Espacio Arte has inspired several initiatives around the country, all with similar business models. Some concrete examples include: Teatro Meraki (Santa Cruz), Complejo Cultural Llajtaymanta (Oruro), Utópica (La Paz), Casa Grito (La Paz), Teatro Kuu (La Paz). In all of these cases, people have approached us for advice or have investigated us thoroughly, as they are several years more recent than our space. Obviously, each space has developed its own style and has positioned itself differently and according to its possibilities. However, we can say that the influence of Nuna Espacio Arte has been an important factor in the performing arts and music sector in the country, and we are pleased that there are more private spaces that generate greater movement and decentralize cultural activity towards their neighborhoods. These spaces seek sustainability through the sale of drinks and food, they work with a fixed rent that ensures technical service, they offer training workshops in the arts and have generated festivals by obtaining external financing. This model is not something invented by Nuna Espacio Arte, however, there really was no private initiative in Bolivia that had proposed this way of working and had lasted more than a decade demonstrating sustainability. We believe that this is the result of constant work, despite the adversities that have occurred in Bolivia and in the world in all these years.  Finally, we can mention that through conversations between these private cultural spaces and the Secretariat of Cultures of the Autonomous Municipal Government of La Paz, specific certifications for private cultural centers were generated, which although they do not satisfy all the demands of the sector (the most important being the debureaucratization of the application of Law 2206 that exempts national artists from paying taxes) , they have managed to categorize these spaces in a specific way and separately from certifications granted to bars, restaurants or event halls, which have a purely commercial logic and do not necessarily work for culture. Nuna Espacio Arte has not been the initiator of this approach, but it is part of these new private cultural agents for which -conscious government actors- have generated this type of policies thinking about the development of the cultural area and the creative economy.

Title EN: Promotion of the performing arts in Chile. Santiago a Mil International Theatre Festival.
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture
SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Cultural and creative sectors
Agency Implementation: Teatro a Mil International Festival Foundation (FITAM).
Main Feature: The Santiago a Mil International Theatre Festival has the goal of reclaiming public spaces for the citizens, improving access to culture, strengthening the performing arts and increase their visibility both in Chile and the world.   The Santiago a Mil International Theatre Festival has promoted artistic creation though its co-productions, supported national and international circulation of national performing arts companies, and developed training and mediation, and democratisation of access to arts and culture.   These lines of work, part of the organisation's mission, contribute to the public good and align with the policy objectives and the acquired commitments as a State collaborating institution (receives funding by law through MINCAP) The Foundation's projects, mainly the festival, are decentralised, reaching more than 25 communes of the Metropolitan Region and all Chilean regions every year, reaching a transversal audience, with a focus on communities and people who, due to socioeconomic and territorial conditions have less access to cultural offering and participation. Its management model is based on the coordination and collaboration with public and private institutions and organisations at an international, national, regional and local level.   Every year the festival mobilises a network of more than 100 spokespeople and partners such as exhibition space and theatre circuits, cultural centres, theatre, dance, circus, music companies, embassies and bilateral institutes, ministeries and public services, media, municipalities and territorial and community organisations. Eighty percent of the Teatro a Mil Festival audience accesses the free programme. The Festival is an important driver for dynamising the performing arts in Chile, as it creates employment for diverse theatre companies, both national and international, as well as reaching a wide audience.
Results: The Santiago a Mil International Theatre Festival, in its long history since 1994, has reached 12 million spectators, presenting, since its creation, 1,265 national shows and 568 international shows. Through its decentralisation policies, every year it presents performing arts shows par excellence in more than 40 communes throughout Chile.   Together with the festival extensions throughout the country: “Antofagasta a Mil”, “Valparaíso a Mil” and “Concepción a Mil”. Three years ago the "Territorios Creativos - Creative Territories" programme was initiated in order to support artistic creation in the regions, through collective performing arts curation undertaken by local representatives, premiering to date, with free access, a total of 44 performances throughout Chile.
Recommandations: The Santiago a Mil International Theatre Festival resently developed its first impact study, undertaken in 2022 by the Centre for Public Policy of the Pontifical Catholic University of Chile *.   * Study available at: https://politicaspublicas.uc.cl/publicacion/estudio-de-medicion-de-la-incidencia-delfestival-internacional-teatro-a-mil-en-el-bienestar-social-y-la-economia/   This publication demonstrates the importance of the festival for Chile, transforming January into the month of performing arts for Chile, instilling itself in the country's cultural memory and the history of theatre in Chile. Moreover, the festival has a positive impact on the surroundings, making the city not only dynamic in cultural terms, but also from a local economic growth perspective: commerce, services, suppliers, etc.   At an economic level, the same study reveals that the festival's economic impact in the Metropolitan region reached USD 5,181,011 in its 2022 post-pandemia edition. Lastly, those who attended a great French show with free access and presented in different communes of the Metropolitan Region were surveyed with the goal of quantifying the benefits generated by the festival. One in 4 attendees had not seen a cultural performance in the past 12 months, and 36% had never seen an international performing arts show.  Among the primary motives for not attending cultural shows were time constraints (47%), lack of money (26%) and distance (11%). The study conducted shows that the most evident contribution of Santiago a Mil International Theatre Festival can be evidenced in the access, where 80% of the audience attends free performances, meaning that the Festival provides a direct subsidy to cultural consumption, given the presentation of shows of international standards in multiple territories of our country.

Title EN: PROTECTION AND PROMOTION OF THE CULTURAL DIVERSITY OF CH'UTILLOS, THE FESTIVITY OF SAN BARTOLOMÉ AND SAN IGNACIO DE LOYOLA - POTOSÍ
Goal: Integrate Culture In Sustainable Development Frameworks
SDG: SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: National sustainable development policies and plans
Agency Implementation: Association of Folkloric and Native Fraternities of Potosí Safeguarding Committee of the Chutillos Festival Lyndon Santiago Cruz Llanos EMAIL: santiago_don@hotmail.com PHONE: 72415580
Main Feature: The Ch'utillos Festival has pre-Columbian roots. Today it is a religious celebration that begins in the town of San Antonio, in the place called Mullu Punku ravine, also called San Bartolomé ravine, La Puerta, or Devil's Cave, located 10 km from the city of Potosí, located in the Tomás Frías province of the Department of Potosí, south of Bolivia. The Association of Folkloric and Native Fraternities of Potosí (AFFAP) organizes a great demonstration of native and folkloric dances from different towns in the department and the country. The celebration is characterized by a cultural parade that links several streets, where dancers parade demonstrating dances while groups of musicians play lively rhythms; the costumes for each dance are different, they wear outfits that are made by artisan embroiderers, who make objects and artifacts with their own specialized techniques.  The San Bartolomé Chutillos Festival in Potosí, Bolivia, is part of a policy aimed at protecting and promoting cultural diversity, with the aim of preserving its rich cultural heritage and strengthening its recognition at national and international levels. A series of actions have been implemented to protect, disseminate and promote the festivity. This plan includes educational activities, workshops and events that encourage community participation and intergenerational learning about the cultural traditions linked to Chutillos. Promotion of Cultural Tourism: The festival is promoted as a tourist attraction, encouraging the arrival of national and international visitors. This not only generates economic income, but also helps to make Potosí's cultural wealth visible. Community Participation: The organization of the festival involves various fraternities and local groups, promoting social cohesion and collaborative work among the inhabitants. This reinforces the sense of belonging and cultural pride among the participants. Cultural diversity: Chutillos is an example of cultural syncretism, where indigenous and Catholic elements are combined. The festival reflects this diversity through dances, music and rituals that are an integral part of the local cultural identity.
Results: Results achieved: Direct Economic Impact: The Chutillos festival has become one of the main sources of income for the city of Potosí. In 2023, the event was reported to have generated approximately Bs 60 million (around $us 8.5 million) in a single day, demonstrating its ability to mobilize large sums of money in the local economy, through the cultural industries and their different stages of the cultural value chain. The festival benefits multiple sectors, including hospitality, transportation, and local commerce. Services related to the festival, such as restaurants and craft shops, experience a significant increase in demand during the event. Temporary jobs are generated in areas such as costume making, food and beverage sales, and tourism services. This not only helps the local economy, but also provides job opportunities for many people during the festival. Benefit to the Tourism Sector: The festival attracts thousands of national and international tourists, which contributes to diversifying Potosí's tourist offer. It is estimated that more than 59% of visitors come attracted by cultural tourism, which highlights the importance of the event for the tourism sector. The promotion of Chutillos has allowed it to reach a global audience, increasing its international visibility through digital media and live broadcasts. This not only helps to position Potosí as a cultural destination, but also encourages cultural exchanges. Strengthening Cultural Identity: The festival allows communities to express their cultural identity through dances and traditions that combine indigenous and Catholic elements. This contributes to a sense of belonging, memory and the transmission of cultural legacy to new generations. The organization of the event involves various fraternities and local groups, promoting social cohesion and collaborative work. This strengthens community ties and fosters a sense of unity among the inhabitants.

Title EN: Protection of Films from Piracy and Theft
Goal: Promote Human Rights And Fundamental Freedoms
SDG: SDG 5 - Achieve gender equality and empower all women and girls,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels
Area of Monitoring: Artistic freedom
Agency Implementation: Ethiopia Film Producers Sectoral Association
Main Feature: Introduction  The Ethiopian Film Producers Sectoral Association (EFPSA) was established 14 years ago and currently boasts 254 permanent members. One of the primary objectives of the association is to collaboratively address the challenges faced by film producers.  Achievements and Developments To tackle copyright issues during film distribution, EFPSA has implemented an updated encrypted system operational across 42 cinemas nationwide. This system facilitates the weekly uploading of films for audiences and showcases selections from various film festivals. Over the past four years, the association has successfully distributed 257 films to these cinemas, contributing significantly to the revival of the stagnant cinema sector.  Audience Engagement The revival efforts have resulted in a notable increase in cinema attendance, with films shown three times daily in each cinema. However, security issues have impacted visibility in certain regions. In total, 228 films have been screened in cinemas, and an additional 1,244 films have been released online, particularly on YouTube.  The EFPSA continues to play a vital role in promoting and protecting the Ethiopian film industry, enhancing the viewing experience for audiences while addressing the ongoing challenges within the sector.
Results: The association has achieved several key milestones:  Protection Against Piracy: Implemented digital monitoring and management systems to safeguard film distribution.  Successful Distribution: Distributed 257 films through the digital platform over the last four years, with only one incident of theft recorded.  Legal Action: Took legal action against the cinema involved in the theft and won the case, demonstrating a commitment to protecting producers' rights.  Safe Distribution: Ensured safe film distribution across 42 cinemas in the country.

Title EN: Public Art Abu Dhabi

Main Feature: The Department of Culture and Tourism (DCT) – Abu Dhabi launched Public Art Abu Dhabi, a comprehensive initiative aimed at embedding art and culture into the fabric of the emirate’s society. The initiative seeks to enhance the cultural landscape of Abu Dhabi through a series of public art projects and programs designed to foster community engagement, creativity, and artistic expression. One of the key components of the initiative is Manar Abu Dhabi, an annual light art platform that highlights the natural beauty of Abu Dhabi’s archipelagos and mangroves. Manar Abu Dhabi offers immersive experiences through light projections, sculptures, and installations, celebrating the emirate’s unique landscapes. It aims to create a surreal and magical visual narrative, enhancing the public’s connection to the natural environment. The initiative also includes a series of yearly direct commissions across the emirate's landmarks, such as tunnels, roundabouts, bridges, and parks. These commissions will involve significant contributions from artists, drawing inspiration from the UAE capital’s distinctive traits and modern heritage. The artworks will enhance the public’s everyday life, making art accessible to all and cementing Abu Dhabi’s position as a leading cultural destination. Public Art Abu Dhabi emphasizes the conservation of significant architectural and urban spaces, contributing to the preservation of their historical, aesthetic, social, scientific, and technological value. The initiative aligns with DCT Abu Dhabi’s Modern Heritage Conservation Initiative, which aims to safeguard and maintain sites that narrate the country’s more recent past. The community engagement aspect of Public Art Abu Dhabi is crucial, acting as a catalyst for creativity and artistic expression in the public domain. The initiative offers numerous opportunities for residents and visitors to interact with art, fostering a sense of belonging and civic pride. By integrating art into public spaces, the initiative seeks to transform Abu Dhabi into a global center for culture and creativity, enhancing the city’s livability and attractiveness to visitors. Overall, Public Art Abu Dhabi represents a significant effort to embed cultural expression into the daily lives of the emirate’s residents, promoting a vibrant, diverse, and inclusive cultural environment. The initiative reflects Abu Dhabi’s commitment to advancing its creative industries and preserving its rich cultural heritage for future generations.
Results: Since its launch, Public Art Abu Dhabi has significantly enhanced the cultural landscape of the emirate, achieving several notable results. The initiative began with the unveiling of WAVE, a digital media artwork by district at Abu Dhabi’s Cultural Foundation, which attracted considerable public interest. Various art projects and programs have actively engaged residents and visitors, deepening their connection to Abu Dhabi’s cultural heritage. The annual light art platform, Manar Abu Dhabi, has become a highly anticipated event, celebrating the emirate’s natural beauty and establishing Abu Dhabi as a cultural hub. Additionally, a series of direct commissions across landmarks such as tunnels, roundabouts, bridges, and parks have enhanced public spaces and made art accessible to the public. The initiative has also contributed to the preservation of significant architectural and urban spaces, aligning with DCT Abu Dhabi’s Modern Heritage Conservation Initiative. By integrating art into public spaces, the initiative has strengthened the cultural identity of the emirate and fostered civic pride. Public Art Abu Dhabi has attracted international attention, showcasing Abu Dhabi’s commitment to culture and creativity on a global stage, and fostering international collaboration and cultural exchange.
Recommandations: The implementation of Public Art Abu Dhabi has demonstrated the significant impact of public art on urban environments and community well-being.

After its revision, the Scheme is now more inclusive, by extending eligibility to not only the oldest and historically significant theatres of Cyprus but also to the newly established theatres, which do not own their own venues. Title EN: Public Information System for Producers and Disseminators (VIRSIS)
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture
SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Digital environment
Agency Implementation: The data controller of VIRSIS is the Ministry of Culture of the Republic of Lithuania, whereas the data processor of VIRSIS is the State Enterprise Centre of Registers.
Main Feature: On 1 January 2023, the Information System for Public Information Producers and Disseminators (VIRSIS) has been launched, which allows any user of the system to monitor and analyse, free of charge, the data of media organisations and other public information producers and disseminators on their governance, participants, media outlets they manage, donations by natural and legal persons, political advertising, budget funds from state and municipal (public sector) bodies, irregularities and other relevant information. A transitional period was foreseen until 30 June 2023 to register and submit data to VIRSIS. Until then, VIRSIS training was provided.  In order to implement Article 5(1)(51) of the Law on the Right to Information and the Re-Use of Data, VIRSIS has implemented an additional functionality that allows the display of funds allocated by the public institutions to specific producers and disseminators of public information. Technical measures have also been implemented, with the help of which the data provided by the institutions to VIRSIS can be published on the websites of institutions by means of a special link.
Results: Benefits of VIRSIS 1.	Better transparency of the activities of producers and disseminators of public information and the processes related to the provision of information to the public; 2.	Lower probability of drivers of corruption in the public and private sectors; 3.	Greater compatibility, reliability and security of the declared data; 4.	Reduced administrative burden for the producers and disseminators of public information; 5.	Greater critical thinking of the public, more effective protection of individual rights and legitimate interests.
Financial Ressources: More than USD 467 000 (EUR 419 907) was allocated for the implementation of VIRSIS project, costs of yearly maintenance and development are  over USD 66 700 (EUR 60 000).
Recommandations: Ministry of Culture of the Republic of Lithuania and  State Enterprise Centre of Registers evaluate the VIRSIS project continuously and ensure that the system is efficient to the users. The Parliamentary control is also conducted to ensure the proper functionality of the VIRSIS project.

Title EN: Regulations of the Audiovisual Fund
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture
SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Cultural and creative sectors
Agency Implementation: Ministry of Cuklture of the Slovak Republic
Main Feature: On 21 May 2020, Act No 129/2020 Coll. amending certain acts within the competence of the Ministry of Culture of the Slovak Republic in connection with COVID-19 entered into force. This Act unified the regulation of selected procedural deadlines in the activities of the Audiovisual Fund (hereinafter “the Fund“), the Fund for the Promotion of Arts and the Fund for the Promotion of National Minority Culture, as well as the regulation of administrative processes and formalities in the abovementioned Funds with a view to simplify them in order to allow for a more effective responses to a crisis situation. As a result of the situation linked to the spread of COVID-19, the production of films included in the Fund's support mechanism for the audiovisual industry was also suspended. Accordingly, the Act allowed, upon written notice from the applicant, to suspend the expiration of the term of the registration certificate of a film project for a specified period. On 1 November 2020, Act No 300/2020 Coll. amending certain acts within the competence of the Ministry of Culture of the Slovak Republic in connection with the second wave of the COVID-19 pandemic entered into force. The Act enabled the Fund to become a provider for the use of the European Union funds and a financial institution for the implementation of financial instruments. At the same time, the definition of two new specific areas of the Funds support activities, namely the operation of audiovisual technical facilities (cinemas) and the establishment or maintenance of creative, research, educational, artistic, artistic-craft, craft, technical or support professions or professional, technical or technological capacities and services in the field of audiovisual culture and the cinematographic arts, was added. The Act systematically addresses the situation of the emergence and duration of a crisis situation outside the time of war and a state of war, specifically with regard to the provision of a mechanism for financial compensation as a result of the emergence and duration of crisis situation and the immediate period thereafter (six months). It is a temporary waiver of the obligation to fulfil certain conditions for the provision of financial resources from the Fund. On 1 January 2021 Decree of the Ministry of Culture of the Slovak Republic No 398/2020 Coll. amending Decree of the Ministry of Culture of the Slovak Republic No 165/2014 Coll. on film projects, as amended by Decree of the Ministry of Culture of the Slovak Republic No 193/2017 Coll., entered into force,  adjusting the minimum time scale of a film project and the minimum amount of eligible expenses paid in connection with the creation of a film project, individually for a single feature audiovisual work, a multi-part feature audiovisual work with a maximum of 26 parts, a single documentary audiovisual work, a multi-part documentary audiovisual work with a maximum of 26 parts, and a single or multi-part animated audiovisual work. The minimum amount of eligible expenses was also differentiated. The minimum amount of eligible expenses paid in respect of the creation of a film project is EUR 50 000 if the film project is a stand-alone documentary audiovisual work with a running time of at least 50 minutes or a stand-alone animated audiovisual work or a multi-part animated audiovisual work with a total running time of at least 26 minutes. The minimum amount of eligible expenses paid in respect of the creation of a film project is EUR 100 000 if the film project is a stand-alone audiovisual work of fiction with a running time of at least 70 minutes or a multi-part documentary audiovisual work with a maximum of 26 parts and a running time of at least five minutes for each part. The minimum amount of eligible expenses paid in respect of the creation of a film project shall be EUR 300 000 if the film project is a multi-part audiovisual work with a maximum of 26 parts and a running time of at least 40 minutes for each part. The minimum amount of eligible expenses paid in connection with the production of a film project may not exceed 50% of the total budget for the production of the film project. The content of each supported film project must comply with the content requirements, which means that the content of the audiovisual work complies with the relevant legislation (evidenced by a cultural test or co-production statute issued by an authorised person), the legal regulations of the Slovak Republic, is not pornographic in nature, and does not condone violence or openly offend human dignity. The starting point of the support system in question remains the basic requirement for a minimum amount of non-public funds to be invested by the producer of an audiovisual work in the Slovak Republic. This amount must consist of eligible expenses, which are, on the one hand, the payment for goods or services to a person who has a registered office or place of business in the Slovak Republic and who is registered in the Slovak Republic with the tax administrator, or the payment of remuneration or the total cost of work to a natural person, if such remuneration or wages, which are part of the total cost of work, are taxable in the Slovak Republic.  On 1 August 2022 Act No 264/2022 Coll. on media services and on amendments to certain acts (Media Services Act) entered into force. The most significant change brought about by the Media Services Act is the inclusion of video-sharing platforms in the regulatory framework for audiovisual media services. The Media Services Act regulates the rights and obligations of broadcasters, providers of on-demand audiovisual media services, retransmission operators, multiplex providers, rights and obligations of video-sharing platform providers, content service providers who are not one of the aforementioned entities, and also regulates the rights and obligations of a signal distributor.  In connection with the new conditions of regulation, it also regulates the status and scope, including broader competences, of the national independent regulatory authority, which in the Slovak Republic is the Media Services Council (formerly the Broadcasting and Retransmission Council.   The new legislation does not change the distinction between linear and non-linear services, but in many respects it unifies the requirements for individual entities, e.g. in the area of protection of minors, protection against hate speech, etc.. The Media Services Act preserves public access to information in the broadcasting of program services, complemented by guaranteeing access to pluralistic, objective and impartial information; guarantees multimodal access in television broadcasting (in relation to the public service broadcaster, it foresees a significant increase in the proportion of programs that are provided with multimodal access, and there is also an increase in relation to private broadcasters) and in the provision of on-demand audiovisual media services; quotas for Slovak music, European works and independent productions continue to apply, while a new obligation to give due prominence to European content is introduced in relation to on-demand audiovisual media services.  The area of plurality of information and transparency of property and personal relationships also underwent a significant change. The Media Services Act makes it compulsory for all media to register as public sector partners, whether or not they do business with the State. Making information on the ultimate owners of the media available through a public register should bring greater transparency of media ownership.  Following the new legal regulations provided for by the Media Services Act, Act No 532/2010 Coll. on Radio and Television of Slovakia and on amendments to certain acts, as amended (hereinafter referred to as "Act No 532/2010 Coll.") was also amended. Act No 532/2010 Coll. modified the definition of a program in the public interest (for more information see the section Media Diversity).  The obligation to broadcast content- and regionally balanced programs for national minorities and ethnic groups in radio broadcasting, through a stand-alone website that reflects current digital capabilities and public demand (through a dedicated program service), as well as television broadcasts of at least 120 minutes on weekdays, so that at least 500 hours of such broadcasts are provided annually across all television program services combined. In relation to this obligation, there was a transitional period until 2024 during which Radio and Television of Slovakia was obliged to reach a set number of hours.  At the same time, the Media Services Act extends the legislation concerning the public funds - the Audiovisual Fund, the Fund for the Promotion of Arts and the Fund for the Promotion of Culture of National Minorities - with a provision stipulating that, when providing financial support, the funds will also take significant account of the fair remuneration of authors, co-authors and performers, in accordance with the Copyright Act.   On 1 August 2022, Act No 125/2022 Coll. on publishers of publications and on the media and audiovisual register and on amendments to certain acts (the Publications Act) entered into force. It reflects current developments and new requirements in the area of dissemination of information, not only through the traditional periodical press, but also through electronic periodical publications and news web portals. The subject of the Publications Act is, among other things, the regulation of the system of registration of periodical publications, which was enshrined in Act No 167/2008 Coll. on periodical press and agency reporting and on amendment and supplementation of certain acts (the Press Act), as last amended. Electronic periodical publications and news web portals are also part of the register under the Publications Act.   Part of the Publications Act also regulates the obligations of publishers of periodical publications, press agencies and operators of news web portals in the dissemination of information. The obligation for publishers of non-periodical publications to publish mandatory data in relation to the dissemination of these publications is also new. The Publications Act introduces a new obligation for the publisher of a periodical publication and the operator of a news website to register in the register of public sector partners.  The Publications Act also regulates transparency of financing, distinguishability of advertising and explicitly excludes the publisher's liability for the truthfulness of published advertising or other forms of promotion. It is proposed to regulate specifically sponsorship in relation to a non-periodical publication, a communication of a periodical publication or part of an agency service.  In order to raise awareness of fundamental rights and freedoms, information pluralism of minorities, local communities or disadvantaged groups, the Publications Act introduces the notion of a community periodical and, at the same time, some obligations arising from its position in the market. The Publications Act also regulates the obligations of publishers of periodical publications, publishers of non-periodical publications and operators of news web portals for the purpose of building a preservation fund and a digital deposit fund. In addition to reflecting current digitisation trends, the intention is also to modify the system of handing over depositories of publications to authorised entities, so-called depositories.   With effect from 1 July 2023, Act No 59/2023 Coll. amending Act No 145/1995 Coll.  on administrative fees, as last amended, and on amendments to certain acts repealed Act No  340/2012 Coll. on fees for public services provided by Radio and Television of Slovakia and on amendments to certain acts, which means that also fees as one of the main incomes of RTVS were cancelled. The fees and the contribution from the State budget under the State Budget Act for the relevant financial year, provided on the basis of a contract with the State for the implementation of programs in the public interest, for the implementation of special-purpose investment projects or for the reimbursement of expenses for the provision of foreign language broadcasting, were replaced by a claimable contribution from the State budget (hereinafter referred to as the 'claimable contribution') intended for the financial provision of the core activities of RTVS. Act No 242/2023 Coll. amending Act No 532/2010 Coll. on Radio and Television of Slovakia which entered into force on 1 July 2023, stipulated that the eligible contribution is provided annually from the State budget in an amount equal to 0.17% of the gross domestic product of the Slovak Republic expressed in current prices for the calendar year two years preceding the calendar year for which the eligible contribution is provided.  Act No 530/2023 Coll. amending certain acts in connection with the consolidation of public finances with effect from 1 January 2024 reduced the amount of the eligible contribution from 0.17% to 0.12% of the gross domestic product of the Slovak Republic.

Title EN: Reggae  Sunfest
Goal: Achieve A Balanced Flow Of Cultural Goods And Services And Increase The Mobility Of Artists And Cultural Professionals
SDG: SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 10 - Reduce inequality within and among countries,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Flow of cultural goods and services
Agency Implementation: Downsound Records
Main Feature: Reggae Sumfest is the island's summer reggae festival started in 1993 and is held over a week with its main nights from Thursday to Saturday in Montego Bay. Activities include, an All White Blitz party, Sound System Explosion, Beach Party and the main concerts.  Sumfest is a cultural experience, featuring delicious Jamaican cuisines, arts and crafts vendors, and is renowned for its electrifying musical performances by both  local and international reggae artists. From legendary icons to rising stars, Reggae Sumfest showcases the diverse spectrum of reggae music, uniting fans from around the globe in a joyous celebration of Jamaica’s rich musical heritage.  It attracts crowds of all ages from all over the world, and has featured a variety of Jamaican reggae artistes such as Damion 'Junior Gong' Marley, Ziggy Marley, Toots and the Maytals, Buju Banton, Chris Brown, Rihanna. Kanye West, Usher, Beres Hammond, Freddie McGregor, Sean Paul, Spice, Chronix and many others.  This year international recording artiste, Babyface, is set to perform.
Results: Dubbed the largest festival on earth, Reggae Sumfest continues to be the island’s most anticipated summer show. It is the launching pad for numerous local talents who went on to achieve international fame. Legendary acts like Beenie Man, who received just 15 minutes on the stage at the debut show, and many Jamaican artistes credit Reggae Sumfest as a pivotal moment in their careers. As the years went by, Reggae Sumfest began to attract bigger names and international acts, further cementing its reputation as a premier music festival. The festival has hosted the like of Rihanna, Lionel Richie, and Destiny’s Child, making it a truly universal event. The Sumfest also gives substantial economic benefits to Montego Bay and Jamaica at large. The festival directly employs around 200 individuals and supports numerous families through indirect services, making it a significant contributor to the local economy.

Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture
SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Media diversity
Agency Implementation: New Zealand On Air  Manatū Taonga Ministry for Culture and Heritage
Main Feature: The NZD$55million Public Interest Journalism Fund (PIJF) was made available by the government in 2020 to support news media through the COVID-19-induced downturn. Funding was provided to New Zealand On Air to administer until 30 June 2023. The PIJF was a specific ring-fenced fund that was designed to provide targeted, short to medium-term support for roles, projects and industry development.
Results: The PIJF provided seven rounds of funding, with funding for 73 projects, 219 roles and 22 industry development projects in total, and supporting journalism across New Zealand. As at April 2023, it has seen more than 60,000 pieces of news content created that have had more than 134 million total views.
Financial Ressources: Approximately $USD34.5 million (NZD$55 million)
Recommandations: A Public Interest Journalism Fund (PIJF) Interim Report 2021-2023 - Te Puna Whakatongarewa was completed in August 2023. This report was collated by the New Zealand On Air Journalism team and covers PIJF-allocated funding across 26 months – from May 2021 to June 2023. The report comes after the allocation phase of the PIJF concluded at the end of June 2023. Note that while allocation of the NZD$55m PIJF was completed at the end of June, the outputs of the funding will continue through until early 2026. The interim report found that: The investment of NZD$55m of taxpayer funding has resulted in an injection of journalists and journalism and a move towards greater diversity across the sector. Audience engagement has surpassed expectations, reviving areas like court and local democracy reporting that had been dwindling in many regions. New Zealand On Air is confident that the fund’s support for a wide range of journalism and journalists has made a compelling case for ongoing subsidies to safeguard at-risk public interest journalism and sustainably contribute to the future of the fourth estate.

Title EN: Public media
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture
SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Media diversity
Agency Implementation: Bulgarian National Television and  Bulgarian National Radio
Main Feature: The Bulgarian National Television and the Bulgarian National Radio are the national public media service providers whose activity, management and financing are defined by the Radio and Television Act. Both providers are entrusted by the law and by the licences issued by CEM with obligations to fulfil certain public service obligations. The Law on Radio and Television provides that, including (but not limited to) BNT and BNT shall provide media services to all citizens; provide access to national and world cultural values and promote scientific and technical achievements through the dissemination of Bulgarian and foreign educational and cultural programmes and broadcasts for all age groups; contribute to the development and promotion of Bulgarian culture and the Bulgarian language, as well as the culture and language of the citizens in accordance with their ethnicity; contribute to mutual understanding of the Bulgarian culture and the Bulgarian language; and contribute to the development of the Bulgarian language. According to the law, BNT should allocate 10% of the state budget subsidy for Bulgarian film television works, BNR, in turn, allocates for the creation and performance of Bulgarian musical and radio drama works not less than 5% of the subsidy.  The Council for Electronic Media has issued BNT with 3 licences for the provision of audio-visual media services (distributed over the air, via multiplex) - one with a general (poly-thematic) profile, one with a general (poly-thematic) profile implemented in the field of culture and education and one with a specialised (sports and entertainment) profile. BNT also holds one registration (cable and satellite).   BNR holds 11 individual licences for the provision of radio services. 2 of the programmes have a national territorial coverage and a general (poly-thematic) profile, one with an information and music format and the second with a culture and education format.  9 radio programmes have a regional territorial coverage and a general (multi-thematic) profile. BNR has a licence for programmes in languages other than Bulgarian (Albanian, English, Greek, Spanish, German, Russian, Serbian, French, Turkish). For several years, the content has been available through the provider's website.  According to the licenses issued, BNT and BNR have obligations for a certain volume of broadcasts (on a daily, weekly, monthly or annual basis), namely: news; current affairs; educational and scientific broadcasts; cultural, religious, etc. Programmes intended for Bulgarian citizens for whom Bulgarian is not their mother tongue, European and Bulgarian production; Own production; Programmes created by independent producers.    The Council for Electronic Media monitors annually compliance with the law and the programming parameters set out in the licences of the two public service media providers.
Results: The public commitments assigned to BNT and BNR by the Broadcasting Act and the individual licences require that the content provided by the public service providers be monitored with particular care.  During the period 2020 - 2023, focused monitoring was conducted to both comply with the requirements of the law and to meet program characteristics.  2020  BNT  Two observations were made on compliance with the requirement to reflect different ideas and beliefs in society through pluralism of viewpoints in each of the news and current affairs programmes with political and economic themes. The results of the monitoring show that for the monitored period there was pluralism of viewpoints, both by discussing topical issues on society's agenda and by including interlocutors expressing different opinions - political forces, civil society organisations and experts. There were also two observations of compliance with the programme characteristics in the individual licence for the BNT1 programme. It was found that while fulfilling the licence conditions on a number of parameters - such as news, current affairs, cultural, scientific and religious programmes, entertainment programmes, children's and youth programmes are in deficit. The pandemic year of 2020 is proving even more challenging in terms of putting resources into realising new original projects. Positive, but still too weak, is the tendency to include animated series with an educational element and Eurovision documentaries for children in the programming schedule. In November 2020, during the peak of morbidity and mortality in Bulgaria, the national television, in view of the increased cases of infected and in the television teams, undertook changes in the programming schedules of BNT1 and BNT2.   BNR Two observations of the main BNR programme, HORIZONT, have been carried out to assess the pluralism of viewpoints in each of the news and current affairs programmes with political and economic themes. The monitoring found compliance with the provision of the RTI. The monitoring takes into account the broadcasting of audio content providing information and commentary on important topics on the agenda of the Bulgarian society, with the active participation of various subjects expressing positions of institutions, parties, authorities, organizations, citizens, etc. on the issues discussed. Where the points of view are not included in the content with voice, there the journalistic teams have reflected some positions through retelling, which further enriches the information and guarantees pluralism of views. Two focused observations on compliance with the license for the program HORIZONT have been carried out, which show that the public provider complies with the set parameters in terms of the volume of news and programs in the content of the program, according to its universal information and music format.  2021  BNT - the monitoring of compliance with the conditions of the licence for BNT1. shows implementation for a large part of the programmes, but the planned volume for children's and youth programmes has not yet been reached. As a positive programming measure, it is noted that, following the monitoring period, the volume of children's feature and animation films broadcast in BNT1's summer schedule has increased, as have a number of other programmes and features.  BNR From the monitoring of the HORIZONT and HRISTO BOTEV programmes, it was found that the conditions of the licenses issued were met. The programme HRISTO BOTEV is unique for the Bulgarian air, which reflects various events in the field of culture and education. Particular attention is paid to genre diversity. Topical programmes discuss themes related to common human values, education, spirituality, culture, purity of language and religious issues. The monitoring found an increase in the volume of Bulgarian music production broadcast on air. The monitoring of one of the regional programmes of BNR, RADIO SOFIA, also established compliance with the licence; the programme is broadcast under the slogan The Voice of the Capital, there is a development towards reaching a larger and younger audience not only through topical music content but also in terms of topics, guests and presenters.  2022  BNT Bulgarian National Television executes an individual license for the delivery of audio-visual media service BNT1. The main parameters have been met on a weekly basis. In one of the weeks, given the fulfilment of the public function of providing information to all citizens and due to extraordinary live broadcasts of the then important political events in the country - the start of the 48th National Assembly and the start of the consultations with the parties in the Presidency on the establishment of a regular government, some of the parameters showed a minor deviation. On the positive side, there has been sustained provision of sign language interpretation in the Around the World and at Home central news bulletin on a daily basis (including Saturdays and Sundays).  Another observation - on the requirement for pluralism of viewpoints in news and current affairs programmes - found compliance with the law.  BNR BNR's current affairs programmes are subject to focused scrutiny to reflect different ideas and beliefs. No violations of the law have been found. The licence conditions of the HORIZONT programme licence are met.   2023  BNT Monitoring of the implementation of the licence of BNT1 shows compliance with the programme characteristics The monitoring reports the new cognitive programme aimed at children and youth audience as a significant progress for the programme. For the first time, together with the verification of the fulfilment of the programme characteristics, a study was carried out on the representation of both genders - women and men as presenters and guests in the current affairs programmes of BNT1. Over a two-week period, the observation recorded an equal number of male and female presenters in 33 programmes, with a male preponderance in the case of guests (68% vs. 32%).  BNR Observation of the core polythematic program indicates compliance with licensing requirements.  At the same time as checking the implementation of the programme characteristics, the monitoring also for the first time reports on participants and presenters by gender, given the commitments of the CEM to the National Council for Equality between Women and Men of the Council of Ministers. The results by programme show the strong presence of women as presenters in the current affairs programmes of the HORIZONT programme, as well as a stronger male presence among the guests in the programmes.   More information on supervision can be found in the CEM reports for the respective years: https://www.cem.bg/activitybg/2108 https://www.cem.bg/activitybg/2185 https://www.cem.bg/activitybg/2276 https://www.cem.bg/activitybg/2347
Financial Ressources: The financing of the activities of the national public media service providers BNT and BNR is through subsidies from the state budget.  BNT and BNR also have the right to broadcast advertisements, but to a limited extent compared to commercial providers. The total duration of advertising for each individual programme may not exceed: 1/ for BNT - 15 minutes per day and 4 minutes per hour; 2/ for BNR - 6 minutes per hour. BNT shall be entitled to use up to one third of the total advertising time per day in the time zone from 19:00 to 22:00.

Main Feature: As far as Sahitya Akademi is concerned, it is a premier institution that is engaged in preserving, promoting and enriching the literatures of India.   Towards this end, the Akademi publishes large volumes of material, confers a number of awards and grants, and conducts numerous programmes, seminars, workshops, lectures, symposia, readings, discussions and performances in all the 24 languages recognized by it.   Over the past seven decades, the Akademi has published over 7000 books in 24 languages.  The Akademi publishes original works and also works in translation – fiction, poetry, drama and criticism – covering classical, medieval, pre-modern and contemporary literature. The Akademi is also involved in promoting quality children’s literature.   Sahitya Akademi Award, awarded to the most outstanding book(s) of literary merit published in the 24 Indian languages recognized by the Akademi, Bhasha Samman (given to writers / scholars / editors / collectors / performers / translators who have made considerable contribution to the propagation and enrichment of languages that have not been recognized by the Akademi), Translation Prize (given to outstanding translations in all the 24 languages recognized by the Akademi),Bal Sahitya Puraskar (annual awards given to outstanding contributions to children’s literature in 24 languages) and Yuva Puraskar (annual award given to young Indian writers in 24 languages)are some of the major awards instituted by the Akademi.   Every year the Akademi holds a number of seminars at regional, national and international levels in addition to nearly 200 other literary gatherings, workshops and lectures.  Meet the Author (where a distinguished writer talks about his/her works and life), Samvatsar lectures (given by a distinguished writer / creative thinker who has a thorough understanding of Indian literature), Kavi Anuvadak (provides opportunity for the audience to enjoy poetry in both the original and in translation), People and Books (where distinguished persons from interdisciplinary areas deliver lectures), Kathasandhi (a programme where a novel in the process or recently published short stories are read and discussed), Kavisandhi (providing  poetry lovers an opportunity to hear the poetry being read out by the poet herself / himself), Loka: The Many Voices (a programme consisting of lectures as well as demonstrations, to celebrate folk art of dancing and singing), Literary Forum, Through My Window, Panel Discussion, Symposium, programmes specially under Ek Bharat, Shreshtha Bharat, Nari Chetna (a programme to provide platform for women writers writing in Indian languages), Yuva Sahiti (a new programme to encourage young writers writing in different Indian languages), Purvottari (a platform aimed at providing opportunities for writers from North-East to showcase their talent), Book Discussion (a platform where Akademi publications are discussed), Gramalok (an initiative of the Akademi for village outreach), Dalit Chetna (a platform devoted exclusively for the Dalit writers of India), Bhashantara Anubhava (Multilingual poetry readings) and Translation workshops (bringing together translators from different parts of the country) are some of the popular programmes  of the Akademi.  The Akademi holds a Festival of Letters every year to celebrate the glories of Indian writing.  The Akademi’s literary programmes are held from across the nation, obviously including the state of Punjab.  The Akademi confers Fellowships on eminent Indian writers and foreign scholars who have served Indian literature. The Akademi also has Ananda Coomaraswamy Fellowship for scholars from Asian countries to pursue literary projects and Premchand Fellowship for scholars doing research on Indian literature from SAARC countries are two other prominent Fellowships of the Akademi.   The Akademi has also an exclusive scheme of translating all its award-winning books into other Indian languages thus bridging the gap between different language communities and integrating one culture into another.   The Akademi also has a series of publication called ‘Makers of Indian Literature’ under which the Akademi publishes biographical sketch and information about outstanding literary contribution of the Indian literary legends who are considered to be the makers of Indian literature, and has many a monograph on distinguished Rajasthani writers. Also, the Akademi published Encyclopedia of Indian Literature which has been referred to by generations of students, scholars, and literary connoisseurs. It is proved to be one of the most authentic, academic, and scholarly information about Indian writers, literature as well as literary movements in Indian languages. Furthermore, the Akademi brought out the History of Literature Series to make available the general readers as well as to the students of literature standard histories of literature in various languages of India.   The Akademi offers travel grants to young writers (age 40 or below) under which a writer is offered to take a travel to a State other than his/her own to get acquainted with literary ambience of another language.   Besides above, the Akademi has compilation of works on eminent Indian writers called ‘Sanchayan’, in addition to bringing out anthologies and readers on literary stalwarts carrying the compilation of their work, its literary evaluation, research articles, etc. which also is of high research value.   The Akademi has a series of programmes called Cultural Exchange through which it conducts literary exchange with different countries and sends and receives several writers’ delegations every year besides taking part in literary festivals and book fairs abroad.
Results: The Akademi, in collaboration with Ministry of Culture, Government of India, organized an International Literary Festival, from 16 to 18 June 2022, in Shimla, in which 425 eminent writers, both Indian and foreign, took part. This was the biggest literary festival ever held, and boosted up the literary milieu of the nation.  The second edition of UNMESHA – the International Literary Festival, was held from 3 to 6 August 2023 in Bhopal.  In this festival, more than 575 writers, Indian and foreign, took part in 85 literary programmes, and almost 103 languages were represented.  Smt. Droupadi Murmu, Honorable President of India, inaugurated the second edition of UNMESHA.   Sahitya Akademi and the Ministry of Culture organized three literary programmes –   1. Literary and Cultural Heritage of Kashmir on 28 January 2023 in collaboration with Kalakshetra Foundation, Chennai; 2. Godavari and Vitasta : A Cultural Journey on 1 & 2 April 2023 in collaboration with WZCC in Pune, Maharashtra; and 3. Buddhism and Kashmir on 24 & 25 June 2023 in collaboration with NZCC in Srinagar, J&K   With the theme of Vitasta and Kashmir under the Vitasta Kashmir Festival.   The Akademi also published a collection of papers presented at these three literary programmes, titled Vitasta: Uniting Cultures.  The book was released by Sri Amit Shah, Hon’ble Home Minister, Government of India and Sri Manoj Sinha, Hon’ble Lt. Governor, Jammu and Kashmir.   In association with the Ministry of Culture, Government of India, Sahitya Akademi published an Anthology of Poetry from the countries belonging to G20 titled Under the Same Sky.   As such, the Akademi plays a major role in promoting art and culture in the country.

Title EN: Quebec Digital Cultural Plan 2014 to 2023
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture
SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Digital environment
Agency Implementation: Ministry of Culture and Communications (MCC)
Main Feature: The year 2022-2023 marked the last year of implementation of the QDCP. Originally accompanied by funding over 7 years, the QDCP benefited, as part of the Quebec Government Action Plan on Culture 2018-2023, from a two-year extension.  The objectives of the QDCP remained the same as those mentioned in Quebec's last quadrennial report, including the two major files "Support and appropriation" and "Visibility and influence of culture".  The cultural sector has been one of the sectors greatly affected by the COVID-19 pandemic. Beyond the financial issues linked to the health crisis, this situation also had the effect of stimulating creativity in the community to offer original content to the population, and further of demonstrating the need for a transformation of the cultural network so that it is more in line with digital practices. So that the cultural network can seize the opportunities offered by digital practices to flourish further and reach as many people as possible, here and abroad, the MCC has set up, as part of the QDCP: Digital Ambition and Support for Digital Outreach programs.  The Digital Ambition program aimed to carry out structuring, collaborative and lasting initiatives focusing on a profound and lasting transformation of business (and/or economic) models, the possibility of taking advantage of the digital environment, the influence of the Quebecer culture online, here and abroad, and the exemplary and optimal exploitation of data, both upstream (descriptive metadata) and downstream (usage data) of the project. Under this program, MCC's minimum financial contribution to a project was CAD 300,000 and could not exceed CAD 1 million.  The Support for Digital Outreach program aimed to increase initiatives for the creation, adaptation, dissemination, and promotion of online events and content, to stimulate innovation with regard to the approach and broadcast formats, and to develop the skills necessary for the broadcasting of events and cultural content online. The maximum financial contribution from MCC to a project was CAD 45,000.
Results: During the 9 years of the QDCP, the MCC, state cultural corporations and its partners have led the largest multi-sector digital transformation project in culture in its history. This project made it possible to invest more than CAD 167 million in the implementation and completion of 136 measures.  This vast project has enabled the Ministry to lay the foundations for digital adaptation for the development of all fields of activity in the cultural sector, which involves in particular the adequate use of descriptive and usage data as well as strengthened collaboration between the different cultural actors, with a view to having greater impact.
Financial Ressources: CAD 6.486 million in 2022-2023. This equates to approximately USD 4.774 million.
Recommandations: Four general observations emerge from the learning accomplished and the testimonies collected over the years of the QDCP: 1.	Far too many organizations and businesses in the field are subordinate to tech firms which do not have detailed knowledge of the issues specific to the cultural sector. 2.	In a digital context favoring large players (GAFAM), the digital transformation of the environment requires too many changes for it to take place effectively through one-off projects arising from calls for projects. Cohesion and a long-term vision in government actions are necessary. 3.	Digital technology is an essential tool for cultural development. However, the environmental impact is not negligible. This issue must now be at the heart of discussions in the community. 4.	In the digital universe, the economic model of culture, protected by laws, regulations, quotas, and customs controls linked to geographic tags, no longer exists. Markets are now open, with the competitive, commercial, technical, and cultural implications that this implies. The Quebecer state should continue to take note of the repercussions of these changes on the environment and make strategic decisions, by producing reliable and robust data and modernizing its regulatory frameworks so that the environment can benefit from the distribution of content on major transnational digital platforms.

Main Feature: Queer Museum Vienna aims at establishing an anchor point for queer urban history and contemporary queer art in Vienna. The institution is first and foremost a place for queer history and queer art, as well as a platform for mediation, conversation, and experimentation. All visitors are welcome and encouraged to engage with the museum through visiting exhibitions, public lectures, film screenings, educational programmes etc. to learn more about Vienna’s queer community. Queer Museum Vienna is a non-profit, self-organized collective that believes in the power of art, is actively committed to the equality of LGBTIAQ* persons (lesbian, gay, bi, trans, intersex, asexual, aromantic, queer*) and has an anti-patriarchal mindset. It understands queer both as an umbrella term for the LGBTIAQ* movement and as a label in its own right. However, queer is also a theoretical and activist approach. It questions various forms of oppression, especially when they are based on gender and sexuality. The collective actively promotes diversity, inclusion, and self-determination by creating a museum with queer structures and a non-normative internal form of organization.  Queer Museum Vienna is focused on Research / History, Art, Education, Community Building, fostering virtual spaces and inclusivity. It is a place of mediation, exchange, and experimentation and collects marginalized narratives and underrepresented artistic positions to make them more visible through creative experimentation and collaboration. The museum is a place that researches, collects, preserves, interprets, and exhibits queer art, theory and culture, material and immaterial heritage, and makes it a node in the cultural network through collaborations with local and international organizations.

Results: During 2023, it was possible to meet the certification requirement for its training process in the Territorios AL AIRE diploma course through ASENRED in Spanish, which is a training institution for work and human development.         • The training component of Territorios AL AIRE introduced tools, concepts, methodologies, and invited radio stations and their managers to think about strategies in the scenarios of management, content production, and the transition to the world of transmedia.
