Title EN: Residency Programme
Goal: Achieve A Balanced Flow Of Cultural Goods And Services And Increase The Mobility Of Artists And Cultural Professionals
SDG: SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 10 - Reduce inequality within and among countries,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Mobility of artists and cultural professionals
Agency Implementation: pARTage Contemporary Artists Association
Main Feature: We have two main initiatives:  1.	The artists-in residency program, a long-term non-prescriptive residency, the artist is free to do undertake any project. 2.	The international residential workshop- short-term production residency  pARTage runs artists-in-residence programs focused on artists from the islands of the Indian Ocean and Africa. However, artists must pay their residency fees.   We organize workshops, conferences, and international exhibitions. Our international workshop brings together a diversity of local, regional, and international artists to live and work together for 2 weeks. Artists only need to pay for their international flight, we cover all ground costs (food, accommodation, equipment, transportation). We ensure a balance between genders, age groups, geographical locations, and the techniques used. All these events create opportunities for local artists to interact with international artists. The workshop ends with an exhibition of the works produced to allow the public and art lovers to see the results of the workshop. The workshop is more about working together and learning from each other. A real intercultural dialog takes place. As part of the workshop, an outreach community arts program involving slide presentations, video screening, and open discussion/conference also takes place. During the workshop, we organize specialist activities for children and young artists.
Results: Our initiatives have allowed local and international artists to meet and work together. They created incredible works. They have enriched the local art scene and brought a better understanding of contemporary art. We have created opportunities for many young artists. As artists, we always like to push the boundaries. Most of us have the same dream, the dream to fly like a bird freely. For birds, one of the main reasons for traveling is food. As much as birds need to travel for food, artists also have this vital need to travel, almost for the same reason, to feed their souls and quench their thirst for discoveries, exchanges, new knowledge, ideas. and visions. Discovering new things, and new places reaffirms our existence on this planet and gives us a sense of empowerment, freedom, clarification, and understanding. This is what our artists-in-residence program has achieved. Even if today, we have internet and virtual reality, the need to travel and to be there physically is very important for an artist, for his fulfillment and the development of his work.  Our workshops: We have organized more than 10 international workshops with participants from different corners of the world which sparked a rich cultural dialogue. They have produced incredible art, enriched their practice, and expanded their professional network. This has created more opportunities for local artists to be invited to workshops and residencies in other countries.

Title EN: Résilience endogène face à la crise sécuritaire
Goal: Integrate Culture In Sustainable Development Frameworks
SDG: SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: National sustainable development policies and plans
Cultural Domain: Design,Performing Arts,Media Arts,Cinema and Audiovisual Arts,Music,Publishing,Visual Arts
Agency Implementation: Ministère de l'économie, des finances et de la prospective Ministère de la Communication de la Culture des Arts et du Tourisme (MCCAT)
Main Feature: Depuis quelques années, le Burkina Faso est confronté à une crise sécuritaire particulièrement éprouvante qui a eu des répercussions humanitaire, sociale et économique sans précédent. Cette situation s’est superposée à une crise de gouvernance qui a conduit à des changements institutionnels dans la gestion du pouvoir d’État. Pour la conduite de l’action publique, les autorités ont souhaité fédérer les énergies de l’ensemble des Burkinabè afin de poser les bases d’un Burkina Faso nouveau, libre et souverain qui assume avec dignité et intégrité la construction d’une nation solidaire, de paix, de sécurité et de stabilité pour un développement partagé au bénéfice de tous les filles et fils du Burkina Faso.  Cette volonté s’est traduite par l’élaboration des projets de chartes (constitutionnelle et des valeurs) adoptés par les forces vives de la nation. La charte du 14 octobre 2022 a assigné à la Transition six missions principales : (i) rétablir et renforcer la sécurité sur l’ensemble du territoire national ; (ii) apporter une réponse urgente, efficace et efficiente à la crise humanitaire ; (iii) promouvoir la bonne gouvernance et lutter contre la corruption ; (iv) engager des réformes politiques, administratives et institutionnelles en vue de renforcer la culture démocratique et consolider l’Etat de droit ; (v) œuvrer à la réconciliation nationale et à la cohésion sociale et (vi), assurer l’organisation d’élections libres, transparentes et inclusives.  Les actions prioritaires à mener pour réaliser les missions sont reparties dans quatre (04) piliers : (i) lutter contre le terrorisme et restaurer l’intégrité territoriale ; (ii) répondre à la crise humanitaire ; (iii) refonder l’État et améliorer la gouvernance et (iv) œuvrer à la réconciliation nationale et à la cohésion sociale. En vue de mettre en œuvre ces priorités, le Gouvernement a mis à jour un Plan d’action pour la stabilisation et le développement (PA-SD), de manière participative et itérative avec l’implication de l’ensemble des départements ministériels.  Le premier pilier "lutter contre le terrorisme et restaurer l’intégrité territoriale", a fixé comme objectif de libérer les zones occupées par les groupes terroristes et de créer les conditions sécuritaires nécessaires au retour de l’État et des populations dans ces zones. Le deuxième pilier "répondre à la crise humanitaire" vise à assurer une réponse urgente et efficace à la crise humanitaire et aux drames socio-économiques et communautaires provoqués par l’insécurité et les aléas climatiques. Le troisième pilier "refonder l’État et améliorer la gouvernance" concentre les priorités d’action à mener afin d’améliorer différents domaines de gouvernance, de consolider la dynamique du développement du capital humain et d’améliorer la production des secteurs porteurs pour l’économie en vue de répondre efficacement aux besoins des populations. Le quatrième Pilier "œuvrer à la réconciliation nationale et à la cohésion sociale", a été consacré à la poursuite du chantier de la réconciliation nationale dans le but de recoudre le tissu social mis à mal par les préjugés, les rancœurs et les accusations.  Dans cette dynamique, le Gouvernement a accompagné plusieurs initiatives d’organisations de la société civile qui a permis d’impacter positivement les différentes filières culturelles. En effet, les acteurs culturels on fait preuve de résilience à travers plusieurs initiatives mises en œuvre pour encourager les forces combattantes et semer les graines du vivre ensemble et de la cohésion sociale.
Results: Le soutien populaire, l’approvisionnement continu du Fonds de soutien patriotique, l’engagement citoyen et l’adhésion massive des Burkinabè ont permis d’engranger d’importants résultats. La libération de plusieurs localités sur l’ensemble du territoire national, la diminution de la fréquence des attaques terroristes, la réinstallation de populations déplacées, la réouverture de nombreuses écoles pour la rentrée scolaire 2023-2024 témoignent de l’efficacité des actions mise en place. Ces acquis sont la résultante d’une politique volontariste de recrutement massif au sein des Forces de défense et de sécurité (11 000 environ) et des Volontaires pour la défense de la patrie (plus de 90 000), de leur formation stratégique et technique pour la défense opérationnelle du territoire et de l’acquisition d’équipements performants répondant aux besoins actuels de la guerre  L’adoption du décret No20023-0021/PRES-TRANS/PM/MDAC/MATDS/MEFP du 23 janvier 2023 dont l’objectif est de collecter et de centraliser les contributions financières des patriotes et des citoyens pour lutter contre le terrorisme. La mise en place d’un fond de soutien patriotique a permis de mobiliser auprès des Burkinabè et des amis du Burkina Faso 130 041 715 418 FCA pour la période du 31 décembre 2023 au 12 mars 2024. Cette enveloppe a permis de renforcer les capacités opérationnelles des Volontaires pour la défense de la patrie qui, aux côtés des FDS, abattent un travail formidable de reconquête et de restauration de l’intégrité territoriale.  L’organisation d’ateliers de pratiques artistiques dans les filières suivis de restitution du spectacle, l’organisation de concerts impliquant et d'actions sociales au profit des populations à travers une remise de dons aux personnes déplacées internes, l’organisation de Nuits du sursaut patriotique ayant mobilisées plus de 4 000 personnes et qui a permis de collecter la somme de 4 618 925 FCFA en faveur des personnes déplacées internes, l’éditions de recueils de poèmes et de nouvelles en 1000 exemplaires.

Title EN: SALON DU LIVRE POUR ENFANTS ET ADOLESCENTS (SALEA)
Goal: Integrate Culture In Sustainable Development Frameworks
SDG: SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: National sustainable development policies and plans
Agency Implementation: MINISTERE ENCHARG DE LA CULTURE /DIRECTION DE L’INDUSTRIE DU LIVRE ET DE LA PROMOTION DE LA LECTURE (DILPL)
Main Feature: L’organisation du Salon du Livre pour Enfants et Adolescents se justifie par la nécessité d’intéresser les enfants et adolescents au livre dès leurs plus jeunes âges, de ne pas limiter l’activité de lecture au seul cadre scolaire et, surtout de développer le secteur de la littérature enfantine et de jeunesse pour notre pays. En effet, le Salon du livre pour Enfants et Adolescents (SALEA) se présente comme un cadre idéal qui permet à la famille de jouer un rôle auprès de leurs enfants en les intéressant au livre et à la lecture. Même si l’école offre de multiples occasions de lire, dont certaines pour le simple plaisir de lire, l’enfant qui n’a pas bénéficié d’une familiarisation précoce avec le livre et qui n’a de rapport à la lecture qu’à l’école, est plus à risque de n’associer strictement la lecture qu’au contexte scolaire. Il sera alors moins porté à lire à l’extérieur de ce cadre, et ce, tout au long de son cheminement. Le Salon du Livre pour Enfants et Adolescents est là pour pallier cette situation et montrer aux enfants et adolescents qu’il existe d’autres raisons et d’autres endroits pour s’intéresser au livre et à la lecture.  En plus, la découverte du livre à l’école peut se révéler une expérience quelque fois traumatisante pour les jeunes qui l’ont découverte à l’école dans un contexte contraignant. Ces derniers n’ont souvent pas bénéficié d’une initiation à la lecture plaisante et douce à la maison. Le S.A.L.E.A est une occasion de leur permettre de découvrir le côté ludique du livre. Le Salon du Livre pour Enfants et Adolescents (SALEA) se justifie aussi par le fait que le plaisir de lire décline à mesure que les jeunes avancent dans leur scolarité. Il importe donc de souligner qu’il n’est pas seulement ici question de la lecture de livres, mais aussi de la lecture sous toutes ses formes et sur différents supports, c’est-à-dire des magazines, des blogues, des paroles de chanson, des courriels, des bandes dessinées, des affiches, le livre numérique etc. Si la pratique de la lecture est un facteur essentiel à la réussite scolaire, lire pour le plaisir est l‘élément qui déterminera toute la portée de ce facteur. En résumé, les élèves ayant une attitude positive envers la lecture réussissent mieux à l’école, voire dans la vie.  Par ailleurs, les nombreux auteurs et illustrateurs ivoiriens d’ouvrages pour enfants et de jeunesse, connaissant un succès au plan national et international profiteront de ce SALEA pour se faire connaitre des jeunes, et peut être susciteront des vocations en leur sein.  Enfin, le Ministère de la Culture et de la Francophone veut par ce SALEA qui est une expérience inédite dans la sous-région, renforcer le leadership de la Côte d’Ivoire en Afrique au Sud du Sahara en matière de littérature de jeunesse. L’objectif principal de ce Salon du Livre pour Enfants et Adolescents est de faire de la Côte d’Ivoire un haut lieu de visibilité et un important marché du livre pour enfants et de jeunesse. De façon spécifique, ce Salon vise à : -Susciter l’intérêt des éditeurs pour le livre pour enfants et de jeunesse ;  -Offrir aux acteurs nationaux une plate-forme de promotion du livre pour enfants et de jeunesse ;  -Rapprocher les publics scolaires du livre et de la lecture ; -Renforcer les échanges professionnels et commerciaux entre les acteurs du livre pour enfants et de jeunesse ; -Renforcer la promotion des auteurs confirmés et promouvoir les nouveaux et jeunes auteurs du livre pour enfants et de jeunesse ; -Susciter l’amour du livre et de la lecture au sein des populations enfantines et de jeunesse ; -Offrir aux illustrateurs et professionnels de la bande dessinée (BD) et des arts graphiques une plate-forme d’expression de leur art ; -Inscrire Abidjan dans l’agenda culturel international du livre pour enfants et de jeunesse ;  -Renforcer le leadership de la Côte d’Ivoire dans le domaine du livre de jeunesse.
Results: Les résultats du Salon du Livre pour Enfants et Adolescents 2023, atteints sont les suivants : -L’amour du livre et de la lecture au sein des populations d’enfants et de jeunes est renforcé ;  -Le niveau de langue des enfants et adolescents est rehaussé ; -Les éditeurs nationaux renforcent leur intérêt pour le livre pour enfants et de jeunesse ; -Les acteurs nationaux du livre pour enfants et de jeunesse ont une plate-forme de promotion du livre pour enfants et de jeunesse ; Les échanges professionnels et commerciaux entre les acteurs du livre pour enfants et de jeunesse sont renforcés ; -La promotion des auteurs confirmés et des nouveaux auteurs de livres pour enfants et de jeunesse est renforcée ; -Une plate-forme d’expression est offerte aux illustrateurs et professionnels de la bande dessinée (BD) et des arts graphiques ; -La Côte d’Ivoire est inscrite dans l’agenda culturel international du livre pour enfants et de jeunesse; -Les jeunes et enfants manifestent plus d’intérêt pour les métiers de la chaine du livre.

Title EN: Status and working conditions of artists and cultural professionals
Goal: Promote Human Rights And Fundamental Freedoms
SDG: SDG 5 - Achieve gender equality and empower all women and girls,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels
Area of Monitoring: Artistic freedom
Cultural Domain: Design,Performing Arts,Media Arts,Cinema and Audiovisual Arts,Music,Publishing,Visual Arts
Agency Implementation: EU Member States, European Parliament, European Commission
Main Feature: Artists’ and creative sector professionals’ working conditions are high on the EU agenda. The European Commission issued an EU study end-2020, launched a “Voices of Culture” civil society dialogue, which presented the result of its discussions in June 2021, and facilitated a working group composed of experts from EU Member States’ ministries of culture and employment/social affairs, which issued its report in July 2023. Further activities are foreseen in the current EU Work Plan for culture, such as thematic workshops and a special section on the CreativesUnite platform on artists‘ and creative professional working conditions, based on data gathered by the group of EU Member States’ experts.  As part of its support for European social dialogue, the European Commission also supports and organises relevant meetings of two Sectoral Social Dialogue Committees - Live Performance and Audiovisual - https://ec.europa.eu/social/main.jsp?catId=480&langId=en&intPageId=1825 and https://ec.europa.eu/social/main.jsp?catId=480&langId=en&intPageId=1842  On 21 November 2023, the European Parliament adopted an INL (own initiative legislative) resolution with recommendations for an EU framework for the social and professional situation of artists and workers in the cultural and creative sectors [2023/2051(INL)].
Results: The main achievements include:  • The report of the Member States’ expert group on the Status and Working Conditions of Artists and Cultural and Creative Professionals: https://culture.ec.europa.eu/news/eu-experts-publish-recommendations-to-improve-working-conditions-of-artists-and-cultural-and-creative-professionals • As foreseen in the Council Work Plan for Culture 2019-2022, the study on artists’ and creative sectors professionals’ working conditions end-2020, which is available here: 07b74a1edf6f782478c55bd85899219c.pdf (eenc.eu) • The “Voices of Culture” civil society dialogue results were presented in June 2021, it is available here: https://voicesofculture.eu/2021/07/06/brainstorming-report-status-working-conditions-for-artists-cultural-and-creative-professionals/ • Artists’ working conditions platform on CreativesUnite, taking up and updating the results of the survey and findings of EU Member States’ expert group, with a section on artists’ working conditions: https://creativesunite.eu/work-condition/

Title EN: Revision of the Interstate Agreement on Media (Medienstaatsvertrag) – second and third amending agreements, 2021 and 2023
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture
SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Media diversity
Agency Implementation: All 16 Länder of the Federal Republic of Germany
Main Feature: Main aims: Creating legal parameters for a digitalised media sector which foster diversity of opinion and equal opportunities for communication, particularly online; raising the profile of quality journalism and strengthening the internet community’s sense of responsibility for its actions; adapting the remit and output of public-service broadcasters to changes in media consumption and the realities of people’s lives and enhancing flexibility  Target groups: People and institutions creating, providing, distributing or making accessible broadcast media and/or telemedia in Germany          Expected results: •	Safeguarding and fostering media diversity online •	Reinforcing independent personal and public opinion-forming, particularly in the areas of political messaging and social media •	Improving journalistic standards by obliging particularly influential telemedia providers to uphold them •	Enhancing the transparency of media content as regards how it is selected and ordered by algorithms •	Curbing discriminatory media content by regulating algorithms •	Enhancing the discoverability and visibility of media services, e.g. regional, local and accessible provision in the context of cable television networks and streaming services •	Creating more flexibility between consumption platforms and ensuring a high quality of standards
Results: New in the 2020-2023 reporting period (Information on the previous funding period of this measure can be found in the third periodic report.): •	Revision of the 2020 Interstate Agreement on Media and its 2021 amendments adopted (Second Interstate Agreement on Media) •	Four instruments put in place by the Second Interstate Agreement on Media to improve media provision in Germany: (1) transparency rules, (2) discrimination prohibitions, (3) rules on the discoverability and visibility of media provision and (4) enhanced significance of journalistic standards •	Third Interstate Agreement on Media adopted, its chief amendments relating to expanded powers for oversight bodies, the option of converting linear channels into online services, greater accessibility in the media, and flexibility in distribution options in public-service broadcasting in the interests of adapting media provision to the changes in media consumption resulting from the advance of digitalisation •	Fourth Interstate Agreement on Media drafted, for entry into force on 1 January 2024, intended to create unified legal provisions on transparency, compliance, oversight and control for the Land broadcasters comprising the Association of Public Broadcasting Corporations in Germany (ARD), Second German Television (ZDF) and Deutschlandradio
Financial Ressources: The Land media authorities for private broadcasters responsible for overseeing the new provisions are partly financed by broadcasting fees.
Recommandations: The provisions have been evaluated in liaison with the Land supervisory authorities for private broadcasters responsible for overseeing them.

Title EN: Roadmap for Jazz Federation’s Carbon-Neutral Touring 2030
Goal: Integrate Culture In Sustainable Development Frameworks
SDG: SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: National sustainable development policies and plans
Agency Implementation: Finnish Jazz Federation
Main Feature: In autumn 2022, The Finnish Jazz Federation will organise seven pilot tours in addition to its basic tour activities to explore different more sustainable ways of producing jazz tours. Tours t by different modes of travel and production gather information and participants' experiences and disseminate information on climate-friendly choices. Drawing on the information from the pilot tours, the The Finnish Jazz Federation will draw up a roadmap towards carbon neutral tour operations in 2023. The expert partners in the project are Puuni Oy and positive impact Oy.   In addition to the federation tour bus, the pilot tours also include trains and electric cars, and in addition to the ring routes, one tour is used to work in the neighbouring areas from the perspective of resilience. One tour combines school concerts with evening concerts to reach as many different audiences as possible with the same transportation. One of the tours is directed to coastal and archipelago areas. One tour takes place in Sweden. It examines emissions from flying out of Finland in relation to low-carbon local mobility. The Finnish Jazz Federation has developed more sustainable recycling practices in cooperation with its Nordic partners since 2020.  At concert venues, the Finnish Jazz Federation encourages more sustainable choices with the help of “green riders”. In riders, i.e. the wish lists sent by artists to gig venues, concert organisers are asked to ensure, among other things, that public transport options are presented to the audience for movement to the concert venue, energy saving, waste reduction and the availability of vegan food for artists and audiences. Through its project, theFinnish Jazz Federation participates in extensive sustainable development work in the field of live music.
Results: The development project measured the carbon footprint of the Finnish Jazz Federation's tour activities and drew up an action plan towards the Federation's carbon neutral tour activities. The climate impacts of Finnish live music were also examined as part of the project package in cooperation with organisations in the field of live music.

Title EN: Sharjah Art Foundation Film Program

SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development

Main Feature: Sharjah Film Platform (SFP) is an annual festival organized by the Sharjah Art Foundation, celebrating independent cinema, documentary filmmaking, and moving image art. The ten-day event features regional and international films, talks by filmmakers and industry professionals, musical concerts, and mixers, centered around the open-air Mirage City Cinema in Sharjah’s historical quarter. Film Screenings and Events: SFP focuses on films not shown in mainstream cinemas, including award-winning works by emerging directors, world cinema classics, and curated series exploring specific themes or genres. Screenings are held in the outdoor Mirage City Cinema and are free and open to the public. Productions and Partnerships: Sharjah Art Foundation has supported film artists through commissions and production grants, promoting the creation of new works. Film Club: Dedicated to film and filmmaking, the SAF Film Club offers screenings, workshops, discussions, and opportunities to engage with the local film community. Members can submit their films for screening consideration and access a fully equipped editing suite.
Results: The Sharjah Film Platform provides a diverse array of cinematic experiences and fosters a vibrant film community. By showcasing independent and experimental films, SFP has offered audiences new perspectives and elevated emerging voices in filmmaking. The festival’s free and accessible screenings have promoted cultural inclusivity, while the Film Club has nurtured local talent through workshops, discussions, and practical resources. These initiatives have not only increased public engagement with the arts but have also supported the development of the local film industry, contributing to a dynamic and culturally rich environment in Sharjah. Through these efforts, the Sharjah Art Foundation has reinforced its commitment to artistic innovation and community engagement, aligning with broader goals of cultural development and sustainability.

Title EN: Safe Spaces culture
Goal: Promote Human Rights And Fundamental Freedoms
SDG: SDG 5 - Achieve gender equality and empower all women and girls,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels
Area of Monitoring: Artistic freedom
Agency Implementation: Syndicat Suisse Romand du Spectacle (SSRS)
Main Feature: Le Syndicat Suisse Romand du Spectacle s’engage à la création de structures qui protègent les créatrices culturelles et les créateurs culturels contre toutes les formes de harcèlement, sexuel ou mobbing. Il contribue au développement du dispositif Safe Spaces Culture, dispositif de conseils en cas de harcèlement au travail.  Safe Spaces Culture a comme ambition de mettre sur pied des moyens d’action pour les lieux de travail et de formation libres de harcèlement, de mobbing et de discriminations dans le secteur de la culture.  Depuis 2023, Safe Spaces Culture propose aux employeuses intéressées et employeurs intéressés un service de « Personne de Confiance en Entreprise ». Cette structure permet ainsi à l’ensemble des professionnelles et des professionnels de la culture d’avoir accès à un soutien externe en cas de harcèlement, de mobbing, etc.  Que propose la cellule ressource ? Le mandat a été confié à la Clinique du Travail et a pour but « d’offrir un soutien externe neutre et bienveillant en cas de souffrance ou de difficulté sur la place de travail (harcèlement psychologique ou sexuel, pression, etc.) ». La confidentialité est garantie. Il ne s’agit pas d’une écoute passive mais d’offrir un soutien concret en proposant des mesures préventives et d’indiquer les moyens d’action.  Ce service est complémentaire aux dispositifs de « Personne de Confiance en Entreprise » que certaines employeuses et certains employeurs de la culture ont actuellement mis en place. Ce service est disponible lorsque les indépendantes et indépendants ou salariées et salariés n’ont pas accès à une « Personne de Confiance en Entreprise ».  Comment joindre la cellule ? La cellule ressource est joignable par mail ou par téléphone. Ce service est gratuit et l’anonymat est garanti.  Le dispositif Safe Spaces Culture s’adressant à toutes les actrices culturelles et à tous les acteurs culturels est particulièrement utile, voire nécessaire, dans le secteur culturel fortement touché par les différentes formes de harcèlements et de mobbing.
Results: Mise rapidement en place dès sa création en 2021, la cellule ressource de Safe Spaces Culture est toujours active en 2024. Elle propose aux professionnelles et aux professionnels en activité ou en formation des conseils personnalisés lors d’entretiens téléphoniques. Les indépendantes et les indépendants, les employées et les employés, les étudiantes et les étudiants qui se retrouvent en difficulté sur leur lieu de travail ou de formation peuvent ainsi faire part de leurs souffrances en toute confidentialité et obtenir gratuitement un soutien tel qu’une analyse de la situation (harcèlement psychologique ou sexuel, épuisement, pressions, conflits, etc.), une assistance dans l’identification des ressources mobilisables ou des recommandations en lien avec le démarrage d’une procédure judiciaire.  Selon les bases légales en vigueur, l’employeuse ou l’employeur se doit de prendre toutes les mesures nécessaires pour améliorer la protection de la santé et garantir le bien-être physique et psychique de ses employées et employés. Pour ce faire, disposer d’un service de Personne de Confiance en Entreprise est une mesure jugée efficace. Ce dispositif est à l’heure actuelle encore peu répandu dans le milieu culturel, majoritairement composé de microstructures. C’est pourquoi Safe Spaces Culture a mis en place un dispositif mutualisé de « Personne de Confiance en Entreprise ». Des contrats de prestations sont proposés aux employeuses et aux employeurs de la culture pour répondre à leurs besoins spécifiques. Grâce à l’engagement financier des collectivités publiques, cette prestation leur est proposée moyennant l’acquittement d’une cotisation à prix modique et devient ainsi financièrement accessible. Avec le service « Personne de Confiance en Entreprise » de Safe Spaces Culture, les employeuses et les employeurs s’assurent de répondre aux exigences légales en matière de protection des employées et des employés. Les structures culturelles des cantons et/ou des villes partenaires désireuses de mettre en place ce service peuvent adresser leurs demandes par mail à pce@safespacesculture.ch.  À noter qu’à cette étape du projet pilote, ce service s’adresse prioritairement aux plus petites structures, soit celles qui cumulent un temps de travail en contrat à durée indéterminé équivalant à un maximum de 4 employées et employés à plein temps.

Title EN: SALON INTERNATIONAL DU LIVRE D'ABIDJAN (SILA)
Goal: Integrate Culture In Sustainable Development Frameworks
SDG: SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: International cooperation for sustainable development
Agency Implementation: MINISTERE EN CHARGE DE LA CULTURE /DIRECTION DE L’INDUSTRIE DU LIVRE ET DE LA PROMOTION DE LA LECTURE (DILPL)
Main Feature: Le Salon International du Livre d'Abidjan (SILA) est un événement annuel qui vise à promouvoir la littérature, la lecture et l'édition en Côte d'Ivoire et dans la sous-région. Il rassemble des auteurs, des éditeurs, des libraires, des bibliothécaires, des enseignants, et des lecteurs de divers horizons. Les principales activités incluent des conférences, des ateliers, des séances de dédicaces, des expositions de livres, et des rencontres professionnelles. Le SILA met également un accent particulier sur la littérature jeunesse et l'éducation, en organisant des activités spécifiques pour les enfants et les jeunes lecteurs. La 14e édition du Salon international du livre d’Abidjan a eu lieu du 14 au 18 mai 2024 au Parc d'Expositions à Abidjan, avec pour thème "Le livre, un pari toujours gagnant". Le SILA est aussi l’occasion pour ses acteurs d’afficher les ambitions du secteur de l’édition mais aussi ses défis pour continuer à grandir, notamment à l’international.  Pour le président de l'Association des éditeurs de Côte d'Ivoire (ASSEDI) et Commissaire Général du SILA, le premier indicateur de la vitalité du secteur est la multiplication des maisons d’édition.
Results: Le SILA a contribué à l’augmentation de la visibilité des auteurs ivoiriens et africains, à la promotion de la lecture et à l’essor du secteur de l’édition en Côte d'Ivoire. Il a également favorisé la création de partenariats entre les éditeurs locaux et internationaux, et stimulé l'intérêt des jeunes pour la littérature. La participation croissante des visiteurs et des exposants chaque année témoigne du succès et de l'impact positif du salon sur le développement de la culture littéraire dans le pays.  Le SILA a permit également aux éditeurs de multiplier les maisons d'éditions. De sept maisons d’édition au départ,  aujourd’hui il y a une trentaine de maisons d’édition qui sont  membres de l’Association des Editeurs de Côte d’Ivoire.
Recommandations: L'évaluation a révélé que le SILA joue un rôle  important dans la promotion de la littérature et de la lecture en Côte d'Ivoire. Il est recommandé de renforcer le soutien financier et logistique pour permettre une plus grande participation des acteurs du livre, notamment ceux des zones rurales. Il est également suggéré de développer des programmes de sensibilisation à la lecture tout au long de l'année et d’intégrer davantage les technologies numériques pour atteindre un public plus large. Enfin, l’accent devrait être mis sur la promotion de la littérature en langues locales pour préserver et valoriser le patrimoine linguistique du pays.

Title EN: Sharjah Folklore Poetry Festival
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture
SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Cultural and creative sectors
Agency Implementation: Sharjah Department of Culture
Main Feature: The Sharjah Folklore Poetry Festival, which began its first edition in 1983 and is traditionally a prominent platform for popular poetry at the beginning of each new year, provides a rich opportunity for creative engagement and discussion around this literary genre. Popular poetry represents a living memory in the UAE, the Gulf region, and the wider Arab world, embodying feelings of longing for the land, attachment to roots, and identity. Sharjah Folklore Poetry Festival is a prominent cultural event dedicated to celebrating and advancing Traditional poetry. This annual festival, featuring poetry readings, discussions, and a special award, the "Al Hira Award for Folklore Poetry," highlights the significance of this traditional literary form. By recognizing outstanding poets and their contributions, the festival not only honors their achievements but also fosters a deeper appreciation for Traditional poetry within the community. The event, which includes participation from renowned poets from the UAE and all over the Arab countries, serves as a platform for cultural exchange and strengthens the cultural fabric of Sharjah and the broader Arab world, reaffirming the city's role as a center for literary and cultural excellence.
Results: Sharjah Folklore Poetry Festival has successfully celebrated the rich tradition of Folklore poetry, showcasing the talents of poets and promoting cultural heritage. Through poetry recitations, competitions, and workshops, the festival has provided a platform for poets to share their work and connect with audiences.
Recommandations: This festival plays a significant role in fostering positive competition among Nabati poets, encouraging further refinement and development of their work in terms of form, content, and imagination. This emphasis on literary quality and critique can offer valuable insights and details for those interested in studying and documenting folk poetry.  Consequently, the Sharjah Festival of Traditional Poetry has become an important cultural event for folk poets in the UAE, the Gulf region, and the wider Arab world. Poets compete vigorously for the honor of being featured in its sessions, motivating them to continually deliver exceptional work.

Title EN: Sankofa Danzafro Tour
Goal: Achieve A Balanced Flow Of Cultural Goods And Services And Increase The Mobility Of Artists And Cultural Professionals
SDG: SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 10 - Reduce inequality within and among countries,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Mobility of artists and cultural professionals
Agency Implementation: Ministry of Cultures, Arts, and Knowledge
Main Feature: Tour of several European countries by the Sankofa Danzafro dance group. The Sankofa group is a Colombian group that disseminates the African diaspora throughout the world. The group went on a world tour, which had 35 performances, and artistic exchanges, workshops, and conferences in North America, Europe, and Africa (5 countries, 11 cities). This tour represented the opportunity to continue expanding the dance discourse to enable communication with other cultures and encourage reflections on social justice, racial equality, anti-racism, and dance.                  Sankofa means “return to the root”. More than a word, it is an African philosophy that proposes knowing the past as a condition for understanding the present and being able to dimension the future. The Teathre de la Ville, who led the tour, is known as the place of dance in the world, it is a high-quality reference. Scheduling agents from other European countries were invited to learn about the proposal and take it to their spaces.
Results: The tour ran through March and April 2024. There were a total of 21 performances in Lyon, Paris, Annemasse, Aix en Provence, Girona, Barcelona, Tenerife.

Title EN: Screen Ireland’s audience-engagement strategy
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture
SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Digital environment

Main Feature: Screen Ireland is the development agency for the Irish film, television and animation industry. Goal: Promote Human Rights And Fundamental Freedoms

Main Feature: AFRICAN DREAMERS is a documentary film that tells the story in a life passage of five African girls. Five young women, in 4 countries in that Africa from where many flee in search of a better life. Wangare and Grace, Deborah, Marveille and Mariam decided to stay and try to change their difficult lives, struggling against prejudices, beliefs, violence and ancient cultures that too often deny universal rights.  So traveling along dusty tracks, shantytowns and breathtaking landscapes, their stories over the course of three years have come to us and amidst small and great difficulties each of them is trying to navigate toward their dream. A dream of redemption.
Results: The documentary wants to give voice to that part of African society that has even less of a voice: girls and women. It does it through a documentary that rather than only words lets the images, sounds, and colors speak for themselves. The five intertwining stories of the girls show bravery and freedom, making the public empathize so much that the story becomes their own.

Key features of the festival include a focus on traditional desert performances, such as folk plays and storytelling, alongside contemporary theatrical works that incorporate desert themes. The festival provides a platform for both established and emerging artists, encouraging the exploration and innovation of desert-inspired narratives and techniques. It also offers workshops, panel discussions, and cultural exchanges to engage audiences and participants in a deeper understanding of desert culture and performing arts. This initiative provided a platform for visitors to immerse themselves in the natural beauty and cultural heritage of the desert. Through various exhibits, interactive displays, and educational programs, the park offered valuable insights into the biodiversity and conservation efforts in the region. The establishment of the park contributed to raising awareness about the importance of desert ecosystems and fostering a sense of environmental stewardship among visitors.

Its primary features include providing a dedicated platform for young poets to showcase their work and gain recognition, fostering their development through workshops, mentoring sessions, and collaborative opportunities with established poets. The forum emphasizes the importance of cultural and literary education by offering resources and training aimed at enhancing participants' poetic skills and understanding of literary traditions. It also aims to encourage creativity and self-expression among youth, contributing to the preservation and innovation of Arabic poetry. By creating an inclusive environment for young poets to engage with their peers and the broader literary community, the forum supports the growth of a new generation of poets and strengthens the cultural landscape of Sharjah and the UAE.
Results: The Sharjah Young Poets Forum has achieved notable success in nurturing and promoting young Emirati poets. The forum provided a dynamic platform for these poets to showcase their talents and engage with a broader audience. This initiative has not only enriched the local cultural scene but also highlighted the importance of poetic expression in preserving Emirati heritage. Young poets have gained visibility and recognition, contributing to a deeper appreciation of poetry within the community. The forum has also facilitated cultural exchange and dialogue, enhancing the cultural diversity of Sharjah and the broader UAE.
Recommandations: The Sharjah Young Poets Forum emphasizes the critical importance of continuous support and development for young poets to sustain and enhance Emirati cultural heritage. One of the key recommendations is the expansion of educational programs. This involves organizing more workshops and mentorship opportunities to further develop the skills and confidence of young poets. Inviting established poets and literary figures to conduct masterclasses and provide guidance would also be beneficial. Another recommendation is to ensure ongoing financial and institutional support. This will help maintain the forum's activities and expand its reach. Increased funding could facilitate more frequent events, competitions, and public readings, ensuring a vibrant and active poetic community. Broadening the forum’s outreach is also crucial. Extending activities to include poets from different cultural backgrounds within the UAE would foster a richer, more inclusive cultural dialogue. Strengthening community and school engagement is another key recommendation. Collaborating with schools, universities, and community organizations can help integrate poetry more deeply into educational curricula and community activities. Initiatives such as poetry clubs, inter-school competitions, and literary festivals can cultivate a greater appreciation for poetry among the youth. Financial prizes and substantial recognition are granted to winners, furthering their influence and encouraging ongoing contributions to Arab culture and literature.

It has also motivated writers, translators, and intellectuals to produce high-quality works, contributing to the enrichment of cultural heritage. The initiative has fostered greater appreciation and understanding of Arabic literacy and intellectual traditions both within the Arab world and internationally. The initiative had 71 participating countries and 113 award winners.
Recommandations: Key conclusions drawn from the initiative emphasize its role in elevating the standards of Arabic literary and intellectual production. The awards have successfully stimulated a vibrant cultural scene, inspiring both established and emerging voices in the literary community.

Title EN: Shifting Places
Goal: Promote Human Rights And Fundamental Freedoms

Main Feature: Shifting Places est une initiative qui aide les artistes touchées et touchés par la guerre à poursuivre leur travail en Suisse. L'initiative s'adresse aux artistes qui ont fui la guerre vers la Suisse ou qui vivent encore dans des pays touchés par la guerre. Elle s'articule autour de trois grands piliers de travail artistique : la mise en réseau, la création, le partage. Shifting Places donne aux artistes professionnelles et professionnels et aux praticiennes et praticiens de la culture (dans les domaines du design, des médias interactifs, de la littérature, de la musique et des arts du spectacle) la possibilité de poursuivre leur activité professionnelle et d'exercer leur pratique sur la scène artistique suisse.  Shifting Places vise à : -	Aider les artistes, qui ont fui la guerre ou qui résident encore dans des pays en guerre, à poursuivre leur travail. -	Mettre ces artistes en contact avec le paysage culturel de la Suisse et leur fournir des plateformes pour présenter leur travail sur la scène artistique.  Shifting Place est mise en œuvre en collaboration avec divers partenaires culturels.  Shifting Place se décline en trois sous-programmes : Meet! Work! Share! (Rencontre ! Travail ! Partage !) chacun s’adressant à différents partenaires et groupes cible :  -	Meet! : Une impulsion, un élan donné aux artistes réfugiées et réfugiés en Suisse pour découvrir le paysage culturel suisse et construire un réseau en Suisse grâce à des pairs dans le monde de l'art, par une plateforme numérique et des points physiques pour se connecter et échanger. -	Work! : L'étape suivante après Meet! pour développer d'autres connexions et commencer à travailler dans la nouvelle scène culturelle grâce à deux possibilités de positions : Observateur (les partenaires culturels invitent les artistes dans leur pratique quotidienne) et Artistes Associés (les institutions offrent des résidences, des bourses ou des collaborations). -	Share! : Des présentations virtuelles numériques par les artistes dans les zones touchées par la guerre, afin de pouvoir développer et partager leur travail artistique en collaboration avec des partenaires suisses.
Results: Nombre de participantes et participants selon les trois sous-programmes entre août 2022 et décembre 2023 : Meet! -	11 rencontres physique (dans différents théâtres, festivals, musées à Lausanne, Bâle, Berne, Zurich, etc.) pour un total de 243 participantes et participants. -	4 rencontres sous forme digitale pour un total de 72 participantes et participants -	Les participantes et participants étaient originaires d’Ukraine, Syrie, Ghana, Guatemala, Mexique, Iran, Afghanistan, Colombie, Brésil, Inde, Turquie. Work! -	Artistes associées et associés : 12 artistes ont été accueillies et accueillis en résidence, 10 venaient d’Ukraine, 1 de Turquie et 1 d’Iran -	Observatrices et observateurs : 6 artistes invitées et invités à suivre les pratiques de leurs pairs, 5 venaient d’Ukraine et 1 de Russie.  Share! -	Mise en place d’un partenariat avec Videocity, plateforme numérique basée à Bâle qui promeut au niveau international un large réseau d’artistes travaillant dans le domaine de la vidéo.  Shifting Places, mesure initiée par artlink est soutenue par la Fondation suisse pour la culture Pro Helvetia, pour un projet pilote, août 2022-mars 2024. L’objectif d’artlink est de faire de cette mesure une offre durable à plus long terme. L'initiative Shifting Places a vu le jour en réaction immédiate à la guerre en Ukraine ; artlink entend pouvoir y inclure des artistes et des praticiennes et praticiens de la culture de toutes les autres régions et pays en guerre.

Title EN: Shorts Critics
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture
SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Cultural and creative sectors
Agency Implementation: Lithuanian Shorts
Main Feature: The SHORTS CRITICS programme is designed for emerging film critics, journalists, and cultural communication specialists who are looking to expand their knowledge in film criticism, enhance their creative writing skills, and learn how to write compelling critical articles about short films. The primary aim of this program is to help emerging Lithuanian film industry professionals establish themselves in the market by developing their writing and critical analysis skills. However, the program not only focuses on that, but also provides a platform for emerging professionals to gain recognition in the industry by publishing their work on both national and international film, culture, and news portals. During the "Shorts Critics" program, selected participants take part in two workshops that provide not only theoretical knowledge on film criticism, journalism, short film history, creative writing, film festivals, and film curation, but also offer opportunities to practically improve their skills. Participants prepare film reviews and conduct interviews with short film filmmakers, all while consulting with the program's mentors—film critics Mantė Valiūnaitė and Monika Gimbutaitė. The program structure is as follows: ●	September: First film criticism workshop ●	October–January: Visits to Lithuanian film festivals ("Nepatogus kinas" / "Inconvenient Films", European Film Forum "Scanorama", and Vilnius Short Film Festival) and practical activities (writing reviews and interviews) ●	January: Second film criticism workshop Every year we invite experts to be programmes speakers and present different topics. A few of the regular speakers are: Rasa Paukštytė, Teklė Kavtaradzė, Austėja Kuskienė, Aistė Račaitytė, etc. Participants' texts are published on the Lithuanian national broadcaster LRT's news website, 15min.lt, lfc.lt, and lithuanianshorts.com, as well as on the websites of the festivals that the participants attend. In its second edition, "Shorts Critics" partnered with the European film criticism workshop "The END" to host a joint lecture on "Film Criticism: Essayistic, Local, and Global." Participants from both workshops had the opportunity to network during breaks, which allowed them to compare their experiences, discuss the state of film criticism in different countries, and connect with other film critics.
Results: Over the past two years, the program has confirmed the importance and necessity of film criticism training. During this period, nearly 30 candidates applied to the program, eager to explore the field of film criticism and enhance their professional skills. Ten emerging film critics participated in the program, producing 37 critical texts, including interviews and reviews. All these texts were successfully published on news portals such as lrt.lt, 15min.lt, and lfc.lt. This dissemination of short film cinema critiques and the promotion of future film critics' names is particularly important for the entire Lithuanian film industry. As film production continues to grow, raising the qualifications of film critics who write about these projects is crucial. The "Lithuanian Shorts" agency, as the organizer, created a dedicated webpage titled "Shorts Critics Texts" to showcase all the reviews and interviews published by program participants. This page serves not only as a centralized hub for these texts but also as a platform for high-quality film reviews and interviews with filmmakers. The organizational experience and results of the workshops were shared with colleagues from other film festivals and organizations that organize film criticism workshops. Those are the European film criticism workshop “The END” and the film criticism workshop organized at the Riga International Short Film Festival 2ANNAS. The experience and achievements of the participants were shared not only on the agency's communication channels, but also on the participants' personal social media. Participants express their gratitude, share their own experience and confirm that the “Shorts Critics” programme helped them to start writing reviews, interview or improve their writing skills. Furthermore, several program participants continued their practice, independently writing and publishing short film reviews by contacting press representatives. One participant, in particular, decided to delve deeper into film criticism and applied to the European film criticism workshop “The END”, where she was accepted to further improve her skills.

Title EN: SIGNATURE DE DEUX ACCORDS DE PARTENARIAT POUR LA PRÉSERVATION DU PATRIMOINE CULTUREL NATIONAL À TRAVERS LA PROTECTION DE LA PROPRIÉTÉ INTELLECTUELLE
Goal: Achieve A Balanced Flow Of Cultural Goods And Services And Increase The Mobility Of Artists And Cultural Professionals
SDG: SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 10 - Reduce inequality within and among countries,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Treaties and agreements
Agency Implementation: Ministère de la Jeunesse de la Culture et de la Communication-Département de la Culture
Main Feature: Deux accords de partenariat portant sur la préservation du patrimoine culturel national à travers la protection de la propriété intellectuelle ont été signées, lundi 15,04,2024  à Rabat, entre le ministère de la Jeunesse, de la Culture et de la Communication, le ministère de l’Industrie et du commerce et l’Office marocain de propriété industrielle et commerciale (OMPIC) Signés par le ministre de la Jeunesse, de la Culture et de la Communication, Mohamed Mehdi Bensaid, le ministre de l’Industrie et du commerce, Riad Mezzour et le Directeur général de l’OMPIC, Abdelaziz Babqiqi, ces accords représentent un nouveau cadre pour la protection des créations des artisans contre les pratiques pouvant porter atteinte à leurs droits et au patrimoine culturel national. Le premier accord vise à sensibiliser autour de l’importance de la protection de la propriété industrielle et intellectuelle du patrimoine marocain, et de son rôle en lui conférant plus de rayonnement, tout en associant les professionnels, les artisans et les opérateurs concernés par ce patrimoine à sa protection. En vertu de cet accord, le département de la culture fournira l’expertise nécessaire au ministère de l’Industrie et du Commerce et à l’OMPIC pour garantir la protection du patrimoine marocain. Le deuxième accord, tend, quant à lui, à financer les opérations réalisées par le Royaume dans le domaine de l’inscription, à travers l’OMPIC, du patrimoine culturel auprès des institutions internationales, en mettant en place un plan d’action pour organiser les opérations d’inscription des éléments du patrimoine marocain dans le monde.  Ces accords constituent un autre outil légal pour la protection du patrimoine culturel marocain, a ajouté le ministre, estimant qu’ils contribueront au renforcement de la protection de la création des artisans. Ils visent également à renforcer la contribution du patrimoine culturel au développement socio-économique du Royaume, à travers la création des opportunités d’emploi et de la valeur ajoutée.
Results: Les deux accords de partenariat pour la préservation du patrimoine culturel national au Maroc visent dans un premier plan à  établir un cadre solide pour protéger les créations des artisans marocains contre toute violation de leurs droits et pour sauvegarder le patrimoine culturel du pays. De plus, en associant les professionnels, les artisans et les opérateurs concernés à cette protection, ces accords ont favorisé une sensibilisation accrue à l'importance de la protection de la propriété industrielle et intellectuelle du patrimoine marocain. En fournissant une expertise spécialisée, le département de la culture contribue activement à assurer la protection efficace du patrimoine marocain. En outre, le deuxième accord prévoit le financement des opérations d'inscription du patrimoine culturel marocain auprès des institutions internationales, renforçant ainsi la visibilité et la reconnaissance internationales de ce patrimoine. Dans l'ensemble, ces accords renforcent la protection du patrimoine culturel marocain, stimulant ainsi son rôle dans le développement socio-économique du pays en créant des opportunités d'emploi et en ajoutant de la valeur.

This was on the sidelines of the closing of the Digital Cultural Exchange Week between the youth of the Sultanate of Oman and the People's Republic of China.  The agreement was signed on behalf of the Ministry by His Excellency Sayyid Said bin Sultan Al Busaidi, Undersecretary of the Ministry for Culture, and on behalf of Omantel by Eng. Sami bin Ahmed Al Ghassani, Chief Operating Officer of the company, while on behalf of Huawei, it was signed by Stephen Yi, President of the Middle East and Africa region for the company.  The agreement aims to enhance and support the talents and skills of Omani youth in the field of information and communications technology and to keep pace with emerging technological developments, with the contribution and cooperation of the private sector according to plans, policies, and programs organized by the three parties to the agreement. The agreement also represents a strategic partnership to support ICT talents and develop technology for society in the Sultanate of Oman.
Results: ▪ Building bridges of communication between public and private sector institutions.  ▪ The Memorandum of Understanding presented a cultural model for cultural rapprochement between peoples.  ▪ Encouraging creativity and technical cultural innovation.  ▪ Supporting and sponsoring artists in various fields of multiple arts and promoting contemporary artistic production.  ▪ Increasing opportunities for cultural participation and interaction for Omani youth at various local and international levels.
Recommandations: • Emphasis on developing future cadres as the agreement will provide more training opportunities on the latest technologies that will enable the target groups to participate in developing the digital society and contribute to the social and economic development process of the Sultanate of Oman.  • These agreements establish a new phase of cooperation between the Ministry of Culture, Sports, and Youth and private sector institutions in order to contribute to the development of various cultural and youth activities in the Sultanate of Oman.  The CEO of Omantel stated: “We will work together to advance the gains of the Sultanate of Oman in terms of the digital information sector and innovative solutions through several projects that will support the Omani society and attract the latest advanced electronic devices and systems and modern technologies in the Fourth Industrial Revolution, artificial intelligence, and the Internet of Things, which in turn will contribute to achieving the national program for the digital economy.  A joint innovation platform will be established between the parties to support the Sultanate of Oman in embracing innovative solutions and the fifth-generation network to activate the terms of this agreement. This platform is located in the main building of Omantel. • Based on this agreement, there will be a training program for employees of the Ministry of Culture, Sports and Youth in the fields adopted by the Memorandum of Understanding, and the live broadcast of the 5th generation network will be adopted for use in the events implemented by the Ministry.  The agreement will also support the establishment of the Innovation Week and the Innovation Competition that the Ministry will launch with the aim of developing the child’s perceptions and awareness in the technical and electronic field, in addition to the development of advanced devices and systems such as virtual reality and augmented reality devices, and providing technical and technological support and facilitating communications services and providing electronic devices and systems to the sectors supervised by the Ministry.

Title EN: Study "Evaluation of Measures and their Impact for the Promotion of Lithuanian Culture Abroad" (since 2022)
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture
SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Cultural and creative sectors
Cultural Domain: Design,Performing Arts,Media Arts,Cinema and Audiovisual Arts,Music,Publishing,Visual Arts
Agency Implementation: Ministry of Culture of the Republic of Lithuania
Main Feature: In 2022, the study "Evaluation of Targeted Measures for the Dissemination of Lithuanian Culture Abroad and their Impact" was carried out at the request of the Ministry of Culture with the participation of the Lithuanian Council for Culture.   The key objective of the research – to analyse the ongoing measures for the promotion of Lithuanian culture and their impact on the promotion of culture abroad in the period 2018–2021, and to provide conclusions and recommendations on a strategy for the dissemination of Lithuanian culture abroad in various cultural fields and geographical areas.  The key focus was on the targeted funding measures of the Lithuanian Film Centre, the Lithuanian Culture Institute, the Cultural Attaché and the Lithuanian Council for Culture related to the promotion of culture abroad. The study showed that the resources allocated to targeted measures for the promotion of Lithuanian culture abroad are limited.   The data showed that the most international sectors are cinema, with its institution – the Lithuanian Film Centre, and visual arts (including visual art, photography and interdisciplinary arts). Meanwhile literature and publishing, theatre, dance, circus and music are about one third less active. Low activity in internationally targeted measures for the promotion of culture abroad could be observed in the fields of design, archives and libraries.  In terms of the geography of cultural outreach, the most important countries for the various cultural sectors, are the European Union countries: Germany, Italy and France, followed by neighbouring Poland, the Baltic States and the English-speaking United Kingdom, the United States and Canada. The potential for further expansion is seen in the strengthening of existing trends and a greater focus on Scandinavia, with the Netherlands, Spain and Japan often mentioned as potential markets.   The study also discussed strategic events for the promotion of culture abroad, with the Venice Biennale (art and architecture), the Frankfurt and London Book Fairs, the Cannes Film Festival and the Berlinale, Milan Design Week and Tallinn Music Week being the most frequently mentioned.
Results: The study provided 7 recommendations on objectives, priorities and implementation principles for the promotion of culture abroad: • Identify the growth of a network of international channels and partners as a key objective for promoting  culture abroad. • Systematically monitor and measure the impact of culture promotion  abroad. • Strengthen existing and develop new destinations for promoting culture abroad. • Harness the potential of culture to build soft power. • Apply the principles of sustainable development to the promotion of  culture abroad.  • Provide the necessary competences for promoting culture abroad.  • Build trust between the institutions that fund cultural promotion abroad  and the actors who implement it. Also 5 recommendations on improving the effectiveness of culture promotion abroad: • Combine commercial and cultural objectives in the projects of promotional nature abroad. • Encourage different formats and themes for participation in projects of  promotional nature abroad. •	Support the continuity of the activities of cultural attaches and the diversity of the cultural and artistic fields they promote. • Combine the promotion of culture abroad in remote and physical formats. • Promote a variety of themes and genres of publicity at trade fair-style event. 4 recommendations for strategic actions: • Develop the Lithuanian Film Centre’s programmes for more effective film promotion abroad. • Strengthen an effective Lithuanian Culture Institute study visit programme with focus on long-term results. • Identify the priorities of the Lithuanian Culture Institute translation grant programme and promote long-term partnerships. • Enhance development cooperation between Lithuanian and international memory institutions. 2 recommendations on functions and pilot programmes for the promotion of culture abroad: • Institutionally support the functions of participation in the Venice Biennale. • Institutionally support the functions of implementing culture promotion abroad.
Financial Ressources: The study was commissioned by the Ministry of Culture of the Republic of Lithuania with the participation of the Lithuanian Council for Culture. The Cost of the study over USD 30300 (EUR 27 225)

Title EN: STRATEGIC PLANNING DEVELOPMENT IN CULTURES (Municipal Strategic Plan for Cultures and the Arts 2021-2025 “Thakhisawa-Our Path” )
Goal: Integrate Culture In Sustainable Development Frameworks
SDG: SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: National sustainable development policies and plans
Cultural Domain: Design,Performing Arts,Media Arts,Cinema and Audiovisual Arts,Music,Publishing,Visual Arts
Agency Implementation: Municipal Autonomous Government of La Paz/Secretariat of Culture and Tourism
Main Feature: The Autonomous Municipal Government of La Paz, within the framework of compliance with the Municipal Autonomous Law 265-319 on the Promotion, Safeguarding, Development and Promotion of Cultures and the Arts in 2017, prepared between 2019 and 2021 the Municipal Strategic Plan for Cultures and the Arts for management 2021-2025 - “Thakhisawa-Our Path”, which aims to complement the attention to the needs of the cultural sector and integrate cultural policies with other public policies to solve the central problems faced as a society from the implementation of nine strategic axes.  This Strategic Plan is a management tool that guides municipal action in the cultural field, adapting to the context; it establishes the strategic vision, objectives, policies and projects based on knowledge management, innovation and entrepreneurship; it relates development planning with administration and territorial planning, and focuses on a multidisciplinary, transdisciplinary and comprehensive approach to the analysis of inputs, sectoral needs and the generation of a development proposal.  This plan, the first of its kind in the country, not only at the municipal level, constitutes a tool for articulating diversity, the exchange of values and knowledge to nourish the common heartbeat of coexistence in difference, the right to imagine and build possible futures in the same shared territory in pursuit of living well (suma jakaña) based on responsible co-management and the articulation of cultural development with sustainable development, economic growth, protection of the environment, social inclusion, the generation and recovery of knowledge and expertise, the promotion of intercultural health and human rights, the decentralization and democratization of the cultural fact from the Territories and the promotion of intercultural citizenship and cultural governance.  In this sense, the Municipal Strategic Plan for Culture and the Arts attempts to become a management instrument for the Autonomous Municipal Government of La Paz, which, due to its comprehensive, intersectoral and inter and intra institutional nature, requires the involvement and participation of the different organizational bodies of the municipality.  It will be established jointly with the Territorial Comprehensive Development Plan and the Institutional Strategic Plan as the basis for management planning, not only for the Municipal Secretariat for Culture, but also for the rest of the areas and organizational units related to its implementation. It pursues the vision of: being a municipality proud of its ancestral roots, intercultural, creative, innovative, inclusive, resilient and critical, which generates comprehensive sustainable development and improves the quality of life of its citizens through the safeguarding of cultural rights, the promotion of diversity, the promotion and dissemination of its cultures and arts, the consolidation of a network of cultural spaces, the strengthening of cultural economies, artistic cultural education and training, as well as the appreciation, respect, protection and conservation of its cultural heritage, based on the principles of responsible co-management, intercultural dialogue, democratization, decentralization, equity and transparency.  Its purpose is to address new fields of action in cultural policies to transcend from the sectoral to a comprehensive and inter-institutional view of strategic planning of the municipality from the perspective of sustainable development, also, from a comprehensive diagnosis, which merges the sectoral and territorial areas, complement the attention to the needs of the cultural sector and integrate cultural policies with other public policies to solve the central problems faced as a society from the implementation of 9 strategic axes linked to sustainable development.  The nine strategic axes are:  1.	JAKÄWISA: Cultures, inclusion and care for life 2.	SARATUTI: Cultures, testimonies, memory and identities 3.	TAYPI: Cultures to promote diversity and intercultural creativity 4.	UTJIRI: Cultural and creative economies 5.	YATXATÄWI: Cultures and comprehensive education 6.	ARUSKIPASIÑA: Cultures, knowledge, know-how and information 7.	LURAWINAKASA: Cultures and technologies 8.	YUPAYCHATA: Territory and cultural citizenship 9.	AYNI: Cultures, citizenship and governance  From the 9 axes with their objectives (OE), 27 sub-axes with their Objectives (OSE), 81 programs with specific strategic objectives (OPE) and impact indicators, and 209 strategic actions are generated.  Its implementation is based on a participatory and co-responsible approach, both in the identification and analysis of the problem, as well as in the generation and execution of proposals through dialogue and consensus in a flexible and dynamic vision that seeks feedback and adjustment every two and a half years, evaluating the processes and results achieved for the fulfillment of the goals. Thus, in the 2023 management, within the framework of the Cultural Days, the sustainable development guidelines established in this planning document were analyzed for their adjustment under criteria of applicability and concordance with the territorial comprehensive development plans.
Results: -	The Municipal Strategic Plan for Culture and the Arts was the first experience of comprehensive, multidisciplinary, multi-sectoral and inter-institutional participatory strategic planning in the cultural field and in public cultural management at the municipal level. -	It constitutes a management tool that organizes, provides coherence, prioritizes and establishes horizons for the cultural public management of the Municipality of La Paz. -	It is an attempt to link the cultural sphere with other areas of municipal development through its articulation with the 20240 Plan and to position cultural development as a strategic factor in municipal management. -	With the experience of its execution, it is expected to move from a municipal cultural management with a purely sectoral view to an integral one that will seek to contribute to the integral and sustainable development of the municipality through culture. -	It establishes a system of indicators and goals for monitoring the implementation of the Plan, which attempts to generate an experience of evaluation of cultural public policies.
Financial Ressources: DOES NOT INCLUDE BUDGET
Recommandations: The 2021-2025 “Thakhisawa-Our Path” project was evaluated in a dialogue process established in the 2023 Cultural Conference Days, where it was concluded that the proposal must be adjusted under criteria of applicability, specific intersectoral work with other areas of sustainable development and establish a mechanism for approving this planning instrument at the municipal regulatory level, in accordance with the regulations and planning tools at the municipal and national level, including the TERRITORIAL INTEGRAL DEVELOPMENT PLAN.

Title EN: State of the ART(ist)
Goal: Promote Human Rights And Fundamental Freedoms

Area of Monitoring: Artistic freedom
Agency Implementation: Federal Ministry for European and International Affairs, Ars Electronica
Main Feature: State of the ART(ist) was launched jointly by Ars Electronica and the Federal Ministry of European and International Affairs in 2022 – as a reaction to the Russian war of aggression against Ukraine and as a way of showing solidarity with and support for artists in Ukraine who are unable or barely able to visibly exercise their callings due to political or social circumstances. In 2023, the initiative was broadened.  State of the ART(ist) addresses artists around the world who are working under existential uncertainties and risks. As different as the global threat scenarios are – oppression, lack of freedom of expression, political persecution and acts of war, exploitation, climate crisis and natural disasters –they all impose precarious and dangerous living and working situations on artists. Moreover, they limit the artists’ capacity for critical reflection and prevent them from fulfilling their role in society. State of the ART(ist) wants to set an example by providing threatened artists with financial support and, above all, by giving them visibility and space for their work.  The project is open to: •	Artists / creative professionals (no matter if individuals or groups) that live in politically oppressive systems, where freedom of speech is not guaranteed or that suffer from natural catastrophies linked to the climate crisis •	associations, public institutions, NGO and private enterprises clearly demonstrating artistic collaborative practices and that address artistic ways to empower communities and individuals (through digital technologies)  In the framework of an open call, a total of 357 submissions from 40 countries were received in 2022. The 2023 call resulted in a total of 564 artworks, actions, projects, and collaborative activities at the intersection of human rights and art submitted from 58 countries.  Yearly two main prizes of EUR 3,000 each and eight honorary mention prizes of EUR 750 each are awarded. The Digital Deal Award offers the opportunity to win an additional EUR 2,000.  In 2022, the Federal Ministry for European and International Affairs provided EUR 40,000 for the project. In 2023, EUR 48,000 were allocated to the project.  The project is co-funded by the European Union (Digital Deal).
