Title EN: Statutory measures to promote content diversity in programming
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture
SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Media diversity
Cultural Domain: Media Arts,Cinema and Audiovisual Arts,Music,Visual Arts
Agency Implementation: Manatū Taonga Ministry for Culture and Heritage Television New Zealand  Radio New Zealand New Zealand On Air  Whakaata Māori (Māori Television) Te Māngai Pāho
Main Feature: Government-owned broadcasters and funding bodies are required by their enabling legislation to provide a range of programming that caters for a diverse range of interests and audiences including linguistically diverse programming, community interest programming, programming for different ethnic groups and programming for children and young persons. Section 36 of the Broadcasting Act 1989 requires New Zealand On Air (amongst other things) to promote Māori language and Māori culture and to provide funding to ensure a range of programming is available to provide for the interests of women, youth, children, disabled persons, minorities and ethnic minorities, and ethical and religious beliefs of New Zealanders. Section 53 of the Broadcasting Act also establishes an autonomous Crown entity (Te Reo Whakapuaki Irirangi known as Te Māngai Pāho) to specifically to promote Māori language and Māori culture by making funds available for broadcasting, transmitting on demand, producing programmes and archiving content. Section 8 of the Radio New Zealand Act 1995 requires Radio New Zealand to provide a range of radio services that (among other things) reflect New Zealand’s cultural identity, including Māori language and culture; provide comprehensive, independent, accurate, impartial, and balanced regional, national, and international news and current affairs; provide programmes which balance special interest with those of wide appeal, recognising the interests of all age groups; include an international service to the South Pacific in both English and Pacific languages. Section 12 of the Television New Zealand Act 2003 requires TVNZ to provide high-quality content that is relevant to, and enjoyed and valued by, New Zealand audiences; and encompasses both New Zealand and international content and reflects Māori perspectives.
Results: New Zealand On Air carries out regular research which measures: the diversity within creative sectors that produce local media, the public attitudes and awareness towards New Zealand On Air and the content that it funds, television ratings of funded programming and audience preferences and behaviour. Overall, there is good uptake and appreciation of the diverse programming funded by New Zealand On Air and broadcast by government-owned entities in accordance with their statutory obligations. Te Māngai Pāho also carries out research on public attitudes towards Māori culture and programming.
Financial Ressources: New Zealand On Air distributes approximately USD$99.54m in funding each year. Te Māngai Pāho distributes approximately USD$51.91m in funding each year.
Recommandations: A 2012 evaluation of New Zealand On Air found that that “for the most part the institution has found ways to achieve its goals and thus its remit… It is an extraordinary, enduring, success story, in the face of the challenges arising from the [wider media environment] around it”.

Cultural Domain: Design,Performing Arts,Media Arts,Cinema and Audiovisual Arts,Music,Publishing,Visual Arts
Agency Implementation: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Lithuania
Main Feature: Lithuania pays particular attention to the support of the Lithuanian culture and traditions among its diaspora members, ensuring coordinated and effective implementation of the Lithuanian diaspora policy. The Lithuanian diaspora is an integral part of the Lithuanian population, which can use its creative potential to participate in the civic, political, economic, cultural, scientific and other aspects of Lithuanian life.  The main strategic document of Lithuania's diaspora policy is the Strategic Guidelines of Lithuania's Diaspora Policy "Global Lithuania" for the years 2022-2030 (Strategic Guidelines "Global Lithuania"), approved by the Order of the Minister of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Lithuania of 27 December 2021 No V-550 (https://e-seimas.lrs.lt/portal/legalAct/lt/TAD/2ea18920b3df11ec9f0095b4d96fd400). The aim of the Strategic Guidelines "Global Lithuania" is to strengthen and expand the relationship, dialogue and partnership between the Lithuanian public and the Diaspora with a view to promote the preservation and promotion of national identity, to create favourable conditions for more active participation of Diaspora in Lithuania related matters,  enablingthe Diaspora to return to Lithuania.   The implementation of the Strategic Guidelines "Global Lithuania" is guided by a three-year Action Plan (the "Action Plan"), which is updated annually and renewed for one year, with the aim of ensuring a coordinated and effective implementation of Lithuania's diaspora policy. The implementation of the three-year Action Plan is coordinated by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Lithuania. The Action Plan is being developed with the active participation not only of the Lithuanian state institutions (including the Chancellery of the Government of the Republic of Lithuania, the Ministries of Culture, Education, Science and Sports, Defence, Economy and Innovation, Social Security and Labour, Justice, Interior, Agriculture) and municipalities, but also of the World Lithuanian Community, the World Lithuanian Youth Union, the Public Institution Global Lithuanian Leaders, the Lithuanian Language Schools Association, Diaspora LT and other diaspora organisations.  In the Strategic Guidelines "Global Lithuania“ a special attention is paid to the promotion of national identity – language, culture and traditions, historical memory, cooperation with other Lithuanian organisations. To achieve the aims the state supports Lithuanian organisations abroad and their activities promoting Lithuanian identity, the sense of community and cooperation with other Lithuanian organisations, as well as initiatives maintaining the Lithuanian traditional culture, Lithuanian schools.   The Ministry of Culture of the Republic of Lithuania and institutions under the ministry (the Lithuanian National Centre for Culture, the Lithuanian National Museum, the Lithuanian Council for Culture, the Office of the Chief Archivist of Lithuania) are actively involved in the implementation of the measures of the Strategic Guidelines "Global Lithuania" and the respective three-year action plans in the field of culture.
Results: Action Plan of the Strategic Guidelines of the Lithuanian Diaspora Policy "Global Lithuania" 2022-2030 included the following tasks on culture:   1.	To increase state attention and support for measures to promote traditional culture abroad by providing diaspora organisations, cultural organizations and art collectives with methodological assistance (including remotely), seminars, educational workshops and methodological consultations on traditional culture. Approximately 200 to 300 diaspora representatives from 10 to 15 countries take part in the seminars organized by the Lithuanian National Centre for Culture every year.  2.	The Lithuanian National Centre for Culture also organises educational workshops "Lithuanian National Costume", "Lithuanian Christmas Eve and Christmas Traditions. Straw toys", etc. for cultural representatives of the Lithuanian diaspora organisations and teachers of the Lithuanian educational institutions that operate abroad.  3.	Promote and help organise events and other activities promoting traditional culture. In cooperation with the Lithuanian communities abroad, the Lithuanian National Centre for Culture assisted in organising gatherings of members of the Lithuanian schools "Draugystės tiltas" (The Friendship Bridge): 2021 - in Italy, 2022 - in Greece. The Centre also provided methodological assistance in organising the Lithuanian diaspora dance festivals in Argentina and Philadelphia (the USA). Since year 2022, the Lithuanian National Centre for Culture has been organising the European Lithuanian Culture Days – an event that promotes and fosters cultural activities of the European Lithuanian communities.  4.	Develop incentives for the promotion of Lithuanian traditional culture among the diaspora abroad. The Lithuanian National Centre for Culture coordinates the activities of arts groups working abroad, organises competitions for directors and cultural specialists, pays salaries and other expenses to selected specialists under service contracts. In 2020, 14 artistic directors and 1 museum staff member were paid, and in 2024, 16 artistic directors and 2 cultural specialists. 5.	Lithuanian Council for Culture runs annual calls for funding projects targeted at Lithuanian Diaspora. Under promotion of the idea "Global Lithuania" in year 2020 – 2024 in total 75 projects were funded, allocated amount – approx. USD 825 000 (EUR 749 000).  6.	During the reporting period, the Office of the Chief Archivist of Lithuania continued and strengthened the management of the archives of diaspora organisations and included 40 identified fonds descriptions in the search tool of the website www.archyvai.lt. In 2023, the Office of the Chief Archivist of Lithuania created the website www.diaspora.archyvai.lt, which transferred the information gathered in the previous search engine www.archyvai.lt and enabled external users not only to search for information on the archives but also to provide information on the diaspora archives. 7.	In 2023, the National Museum of Lithuania prepared an exhibition "Lithuania the Size of the World. Our Migration Story", which aims to bring together compatriots living in Lithuania and abroad through the story of the country's mass migration. The exhibition was organised in cooperation with various diaspora organisations and individuals. Around 160 diaspora members contributed to its preparation by lending exhibits, telling stories, organising meetings and sharing information.

Title EN: Strengthening Intellectual Property Enforcement in Viet Nam (SIPE)
Goal: Promote Human Rights And Fundamental Freedoms
SDG: SDG 5 - Achieve gender equality and empower all women and girls,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels
Area of Monitoring: Artistic freedom
Cultural Domain: Design,Performing Arts,Media Arts,Cinema and Audiovisual Arts,Music,Publishing,Visual Arts
Agency Implementation: National Institute of Culture and Arts Studies (Ministry of Culture, Sports and Tourism) Viet Nam and Copyright Office (Ministry of Culture, Sports and Tourism)
Main Feature: The Project “Strengthening Intellectual Property Enforcement in Viet Nam” includes implementing a series of activities aimed at improving the protection and enhancing the effectiveness of intellectual property rights enforcement in the Viet Nam’s Cultural Industries Development Strategy to 2020, with a vision to 2030, fulfilling the tasks outlined in the National Strategy for the development of cultural industries in Viet Nam by 2020 with a vision to 2030, and contributing to the sustainable development of domestic cultural and creative industries.  The project has three specific objectives: - Conduct a comprehensive assessment of the current state of intellectual property rights protection in Viet Nam to build common awareness and practical understanding of the legal framework on intellectual property for the cultural and creative industries. - Enhance institutional capacity in protecting intellectual property rights for the cultural and creative sectors through a series of training courses for government officials at various levels and relevant agencies. - Promote and raise awareness and strengthen the enforcement of intellectual property rights for the cultural and creative industries in Viet Nam through basic intellectual property training courses for artists and practitioners in the creative field.
Results: The project has achieved the following outcomes: Outcome 1: Strengthening the capacity of state management officials The project, through the activity "Reviewing and analyzing laws and regulations on intellectual property rights in the fields of culture and creativity in Viet Nam," has provided an overview assessment of the current legal framework and the status of intellectual property rights enforcement in these fields. It has also imparted a general understanding and knowledge of the protection and enforcement of Viet Nam's current legal framework on intellectual property to relevant stakeholders operating in these industries. Officials in charge of state management in some areas have become better at managing and enforcing intellectual property rights in Viet Nam by taking part in project activities like symposia and training courses on how to enforce intellectual property rights in the creative and cultural sectors. These activities were made possible by basic teaching materials created by the project's team of domestic and international experts. Outcome 2: Enhancing intellectual property rights protection capacity for artists and creative practitioners  The project has developed basic guidelines on intellectual property for artists and creative practitioners to support them in acquiring knowledge and understanding for the protection and exploitation of the values of their intellectual assets.  Additionally, the project has organized capacity-building training sessions on implementing, protecting, and exploiting intellectual property rights in the fields of culture and creativity for numerous artists, practitioners, and enterprises operating in the cultural, artistic, and creative sectors in Ha Noi, Ho Chi Minh City, and Da Nang. Through practical and updated case studies, the workshop participants gained fundamental knowledge of the legal framework of intellectual property. They were also equipped with skills to protect their creative works in the rapidly changing digital platforms and the development of cultural industries, drawing from the practical knowledge of the expert team, particularly experts from Phan Law Vietnam, one of the leading legal consulting organizations in Viet Nam for artists and enterprises, and providing policy advice to state management agencies.
Financial Ressources: The International Fund for Cultural Diversity (IFCD): USD86,219.28; Viet Nam National Institute of Culture and Arts Studies: USD4,455
Recommandations: After the completion of the project activities, central and local state management officials have improved their institutional capacity and enforcement of intellectual property rights, as well as their ability to protect and exploit the intellectual property assets of artists and creative practitioners in Viet Nam. In the long run, these are the core forces that will bring about positive changes for the sustainable development of the cultural and creative industries in Viet Nam. Specifically, cultural and artistic experts and management officials at both central (at departments under the Ministry of Culture, Sports and Tourism) and local levels (at provincial and municipal state management units) have gained a deeper understanding of the current legal framework for intellectual property rights protection, particularly copyright and related rights. As a result, they have improved their cultural management. Intellectual property experts and state managers, through direct engagement with practitioners in cultural and creative fields via a consultation meeting for Activity 1.1, Research Assessment, and Activities 1.4 and 2.2, have gained a better understanding of the status of intellectual property rights enforcement in these fields and the intellectual property issues faced by cultural practitioners to better update intellectual property laws in the future. Furthermore, the direct beneficiaries of the project, including artists, cultural professionals, practitioners, and creative entrepreneurs who are key factors in numerous communities/groups, creative spaces, or creative enterprises in cities such as Ha Noi, Ho Chi Minh City, Da Nang, Hoi An, Da Lat, now have improved capabilities to protect and exploit their intellectual assets for the development of the domestic creative industry and participation in regional and global markets.  The project has also contributed to enhancing multi-stakeholder cooperation between various organizations and sectors in implementing project activities. Cross-sector coordination includes the participation of both the Viet Nam Copyright Office under the Ministry of Culture, Sports and Tourism and the Intellectual Property Office under the Ministry of Science and Technology. In terms of sectors, project participants come from various fields, including design, visual arts, film, music, photography, theater, performing arts, museums, cultural heritage, publishing, etc. This has created opportunities for cross-sector collaboration and long-term partnerships among project beneficiaries. 49 media outlets, including newspapers, national and local television have disseminated information about the project activities, thereby enhancing the visibility of the IFCD and the 2005 Convention in Viet Nam, and increasing public awareness of the importance of protecting and enforcing intellectual property rights in the cultural and creative sectors.  The cultural and creative community in Viet Nam has recognized and highly appreciated the efforts and contributions of the project "Strengthening Intellectual Property Enforcement in Viet Nam". Therefore, in 2023, the SIPE project received a nomination for the Hanoi Grapevine's Finest 2023 award, which recognizes contemporary art projects in Viet Nam. Hanoi Grapevine organizes the event and solicits nominations from the public. The event aims to honor individuals, organizations, projects, creative and artistic activities, and artists aged 35 years and younger who have a significant impact on the community. It also aims to encourage the development of creative arts locally, promote communication, and further spread the influence of arts and culture within the community.

The Strategy for promoting freedom expression in the Norwegian foreign- and development policy was launched in 2021.  This strategy aims to promote and to create safe environments for freedom of speech. A strategic objective/goal is protection of artistic freedom, where the two action, points are:   1) Defend the right to express opinions and ides through the arts, and support cooperation between international, regional, and local organisations working to promote freedom of artistic expression and cultural rights.  2) Support international and national safety nets for artists who are at risk and in need of legal assistance, protection and psychological support. The programme has swiftly mobilized support to artists, cultural professionals and culture institutions affected by emergency situations. Amon them particular assistance has been given to Afghanistan, Sudan and Ukraine. Two projects will be implemented in a crisis context in Yemen and Palestine.   The Aschberg Programme actively participates in the UNESCO culture sector working group where cultural and creative industries will be strengthened, and the diversity of cultural expressions as well as artists and cultural professionals at risk, will be protected.  For strengthening the economic and social rights of the artists the UNESCO World Forum on Cultural Policies – Mondiacult 2022 Declaration was enshrined. Its scope focuses on music, dance, singing, the interpretation and manufacture of typical instruments and popular folk traditions.  • Conducts historical-cultural workshops and seminars with different experts on the subject (anthropologists, historians, folklorists, researchers) with different audiences, both urban and rural. The modality is that of autonomous and individual workshops.  • It carries out temporary acts and events of cultural training within official spaces, such as the “Teatro de la Casa de la Cultura” and the patio of the Historical Archive Building of Tarija, open to the public. • The Government of Tarija is dedicated to supporting artists and cultural managers, through the contracting modality for events and workshops. This measure allows the cultural economic movement to be energized within the department of Tarija, at different levels.  • Prints books, CDs and DVDs of the work of local artists, including access to recording and audiovisual production studios.  • Funds audiovisual production and research related to the history and cultural tradition of the Tarija region.  • Promotes activities to link rural communities with urban centers, both for the participation and dissemination of their traditional festivals and festivities, based on support for traditional artists and cultural managers. • Logistically supports the holding of festivals, pictorial exhibitions and all types of events of local cultural managers and organized civil society. • Supports the implementation of autonomous and self-managed initiatives of artists, local cultural managers and organized civil society. It has been possible to generate an investment in technological resources and the provision of instruments to teachers and students. Books, CDs and DVDs published, like “Historical, cultural and festive schedule of the Department of Tarija” [2022], “Cancionero - Acordes Tarijeños” [2023], “Pozo Bermejo-002, 100 years of history” [2023], and “Aguayrenda - Notes on its history” [2024]).  Realization of events, editorial production and consolidation of specific festivals. 25-50 people (artists) per month with interprovincial and interdepartmental cultural mobility.

Main Feature: In 2023, the Ministry of Culture launched two important public calls for proposals, opening up a new field of project funding. The first, in spring 2023, allocated $183,600to strengthen the cultural sector by developing the skills of NGOs and cultural workers, fostering professional networks and supporting NGOs engaged in various areas of the "support environment." The program aims to improve the infrastructure of cultural organizations, provide resources for skills development and strengthen the cultural environment as a whole by promoting activities such as archiving, education and knowledge transfer. In the fall 2023, the ministry issued another call with a budget of $648,000 for 2024-2025, focusing on ensuring long-term support for cultural initiatives and promoting projects that would have a lasting impact on the cultural landscape.
Results: Projects selected through these calls include training programs, mentoring initiatives, research studies, legal and administrative support, and educational workshops. One project, for example, focuses on training contemporary art curators, improving their professional development and expanding their curatorial practices. Another initiative addresses the gap in knowledge transfer among journalists by introducing a mentoring program that combines the skills of experienced journalists with the needs of younger colleagues. A comprehensive study on the challenges faced by cultural workers is underway, providing valuable insights for advocacy and policy planning. There is also a project on legal and administrative support for cross-border mobility of artists and cultural workers, providing free information and advice on issues such as visas, social security and taxes. A project on theatre education will provide free, continuous and high quality training for theatre professionals and educators, including hands-on workshops, networking events and debates. Twenty projects have been selected for the period 2023 and thirty-three for the period 2024-2025, with significantly higher funding for the latter projects.

Title EN: Supporting better access to and greater participation in cultural life for disadvantaged groups
Goal: Integrate Culture In Sustainable Development Frameworks
SDG: SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: National sustainable development policies and plans
Cultural Domain: Design,Performing Arts,Media Arts,Cinema and Audiovisual Arts,Music,Publishing,Visual Arts
Agency Implementation: Ministry of Culture
Main Feature: In 2023, the implementation of the projects selected for co-financing under the public call for the selection of actions to promote the social inclusion of members of disadvantaged groups in the field of culture under the European Social Fund for the years 2021 – 2023 was completed. The public call aimed at employment or ensuring greater employment opportunities in the labor market, raising the level of skills, cultural creation and creativity, as well as strengthening the self-confidence and social inclusion of members of ethnic minorities and people with disabilities in the wider social environment. Eleven projects were funded in which people with disabilities and/or members of ethnic minorities were involved.  Example of a project for people with disabilities: The limits of my language are not the limits of my world. The project "The limits of my language are not the limits of my world" was organized by Beletrina publishing house. The project was carried out for deaf and hard of hearing participants who are members of three associations for the deaf and hard of hearing. It was led by a deaf coordinator and her assistant. The aim of the project was to promote the use and development of Slovenian sign language in the field of literature. Deaf and hard of hearing participants were encouraged to understand, interpret and create literature – short prose and poetry in Slovenian and Slovenian sign language. The project took the form of workshops and participation in cultural events. In the workshops (which lasted just over 80 hours), the participants explored different genres of poetry and other texts and developed their understanding and expression. They also got to know the artistic expression technique of the deaf – Visual Vernacular, which consists of gestures, facial expressions, body movements, pantomime and various signs. Under the professional and adapted guidance of an interpreter, the participants visited museum and gallery exhibitions and dance performances. The participants also created their own literary contributions and presented them at the First Festival of Poetry, Mime and Visual Vernacularity for the Deaf and Hard of Hearing, organized by the Slovenian Association of the Deaf and Hard of Hearing at the end of the project. Almost 50 deaf and hard of hearing participants took part in more than 80 hours of workshops. The project had a positive impact on the participants, as many of them came into contact with artistic literature for the first time. Participation in the project enabled the deaf and hard of hearing participants to improve their employability and social inclusion. The project developed a methodology for training deaf and hard of hearing people to become authors, interpreters and translators of artistic texts.  Example of a project for immigrants: Creative Bodies in Movement  The Creative Bodies in Movement project (https://www.pekinpah.com/ktg) was aimed at immigrants living in Slovenia who are interested in contemporary performing arts. The project was implemented by the non-governmental organization Pekinpah in cooperation with the pLjubljana Public Education Center - Cene Štupar. The project implementers prepared various performing arts workshops for the project participants – costume design, scenography, dance and music (each workshop lasted 40 hours), followed by individual consultations. The project was designed to encourage immigrants to be productive and creative, develop their skills and increase their chances of employment in Slovenia in the field of performing arts. With this project, they promote the creative potential of immigrants and intercultural and intergenerational dialog. Most programs aimed at immigrants usually focus on solving their most basic problems in the new environment, such as learning the Slovenian language or dealing with administrative procedures. In contrast, the Creative Bodies in Movement project focused on fostering immigrants' creativity and helping them to build a network of acquaintances and connections that newcomers lack for their further creative journey. Therefore, the project was partly open to participants from Slovenia. The training programs were designed by the project organizers together with established Slovenian artists from the field of performing arts, who also acted as mentors for the workshops. A total of 51 immigrants from 30 countries took part in the project. The project ended with the performance "Creative Bodies, Movements and Live - Vulnerable Performance"," in which 17 immigrants and 6 participants from Slovenia took part.
Results: A total of 147 people with disabilities were included in 11 projects, each of whom completed at least 40 hours of training. Of these, 118 were either looking for work, had a job, gained a qualification or continued their education or training after completing the project.

Main Feature: The operators of private media service in Iceland have for some time held that the conditions for the operation of media outlets and media services are extremely difficult due to various external factors. In December 2016, the Minister for Education and Culture appointed a committee to examine the matter and make proposals for measures to address the challenges currently faced by these operators. The committee delivered a report in January 2018 on the conditions for the operations of media outlets.  It concluded that even though the conditions for the operation of media services in Iceland are in many ways diverse considering the limited population, it is obvious that there are difficult conditions for the operation of private media. The committee concluded that this should be of concern for the public and a reason for enacting measures to create better conditions for the operation of media service providers. The objective of the scheme is to address market failure and to support media pluralism in Iceland and the dissemination by private media outlets of news, culture, current affairs and material covering social issues.
Results: In 2023 25 Icelandic independent media outlets were allocated grants to support media pluralism in Iceland. The total amount allocated was 3.441.131 USD and this support has proved to be very important for private media outlets of news, culture, current affairs and material covering social issues

Main Feature: The Ministry of Culture carried out activities between 2020 and 2023 to support digitalization and information services in the field of performing arts. These activities included the publication of three public calls for proposals (for the periods 2020-2021, 2022 and 2023-2024). In this way, the ministry aims to achieve long-term goals such as improving access to public cultural goods and information, modernizing existing systems through the use of new technologies, providing a wide range of information on music and the performing arts, and introducing comprehensive services for cooperation between cultural institutions, the government, citizens and other organizational structures within the information society. Co-financing is intended to support cultural operators whose previous work has been recognized as outstanding at national level and whose programmes are in keeping with cultural policy objectives. In the field of performing arts, co-financing supports a web portal for performing arts activities. This portal allows the simultaneous exchange of information, research, education, reviews and the archiving of digital and digitized content. It guarantees unlimited, multilingual access to content, services and databases (www.veza.sigledal.org). In the field of music, the co-financing of the digitalization program supports the creation and dissemination of digital and digitized content in the field of music. It aims to continuously increase the amount of digitally accessible cultural content, improve digital preservation, enable public access to contemporary copyrighted works and promote Slovenian music creation (www.sigic.si).
Results: In the field of performing arts, where the main objective is to support a web portal for performing arts activities, the portal provides information, research, education, reviews and archiving of digital and digitized content. It ensures unlimited, multilingual access to content, services and databases. Between 2020 and 2023, the portal was visited by a total of 812,556 unique visitors, including the general public as well as performing arts professionals and experts. The web portal not only serves as the main information hub but has also developed into a central critical platform for the performing arts (in cooperation with the public institution The Slovenian Theatre Institute – the Theatre Museum) and an online catalog of productions by professional and semi-professional theaters in Slovenia.  In the field of music, the almost half a million visitors to the website, the regular digitization of physical materials on Slovenian musical heritage (sheet music, photos) and the public funding of the digitization and archiving of sound recordings should be highlighted. These recordings are then published in the Slovenian digital library https://www.dlib.si/ (https://www.dlib.si/results/?query=%27source%3dnotno+gradivo%40OR%40source%3dkoncertni+sporedi%40OR%40source%3dzvo%C4%8Dni+posnetki%27&sortDir=ASC&sort=date&pageSize=25) and in Europeana, thus ensuring public accessibility for non-commercial, scientific, and educational purposes

Area of Monitoring: Cultural and creative sectors
Agency Implementation: Selam Ethiopia
Main Feature: Ethiopian Culture and Arts Council Establishment  The establishment of a Culture and Arts Council in Ethiopia was a major intervention supported by Selam as part of its capacity-building efforts. Selam recognized that the culture council could help address underlying issues related to arts and culture in the country and better understand how arts and culture are supported, led, and function at different levels. Selam Ethiopia has supported the Ministry of Culture and Sport in establishing the first-ever Culture and Arts Council in Ethiopia. The council aims to support, promote, and develop arts and culture at national, regional, and community levels by identifying needs, developing policies and programs, and advocating for the importance of arts and culture in society. Selam’s involvement in this process has been significant, as it played a prominent role in drafting a legal document that has been submitted to the council of ministers for approval.   Moreover, Selam organized workshops with key stakeholders to contribute ideas and held final validation workshops. Working in collaboration with the legal department of the Ministry of Culture and Sport, Selam supported the development of two key documents: a regulation to be issued by the Council of Ministers and an explanatory document that outlines the need for a Culture and Arts Council in Ethiopia. Establishing the council is a major step towards addressing underlying issues related to arts and culture in Ethiopia. Selam believes that it will enable the development of long-term strategies, define goals and objectives, build a strong diversified network, and take on other creative initiatives.
Results: So far, all the necessary steps to realize the council have been accomplished. However, the Ethiopian Council of Ministers has not ratified it yet.

The call is announced for the category of preservation cultural heritage and promotion, popularization and development of Contemporary arts, including digitization. 1. Strengthening participants’ capacity in the process of digitization of cultural heritage; 2. Purchase of equipment (necessary equipment for the implementation of projects covered by the Call, which will be used long-term in all segments of the process of digitization of cultural heritage and contemporary arts), as well as programs, software solutions, and information systems that are widely used in cultural heritage and contemporary arts, in order to process and manage digital material and ensure its availability; 3. Development of applications, platforms, and other multimedia solutions related to cultural heritage and contemporary arts; 4. Presentation and promotion of digitized material as well as popularization of the process of digitization of cultural heritage and contemporary arts. The call is open for institutions, art, and other associations registered as engaging in cultural activities, legal entities operating in the field of information and communication technologies, natural persons, and other cultural entities. The objective of the call is to finance or co-finance projects related to the digitization and promotion of national cultural values. For example: the presentation of digital materials, digital art, the use of information technologies to promote national cultural values and the purchase of equipment necessary for the ongoing process of digitization.

The call is evaluated at the level of Ministry. Regarding the digitization of contemporary art, the most common projects approved for funding were those related to the digitization of music, fine arts, audiovisual arts, performing arts, books, collections and archives

Title EN: The Omani Society for Writers and Literati Competition for Literary Creativity Award for School Students
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture
SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Partnering with civil society
Agency Implementation: Omani Writers and Literati Society
Main Feature: The Omani Writers and Literati Socity, in cooperation with the Ministry of Education, organized the first edition (2023) and the second edition (2024) of the Omani Society for Writers and Literati Award for Literary Creativity aiming school students.   The award aims to stand as a pioneering national project in its content and levels of consolidating the values of literary beauty and developing it among talented and creative students in the literary field. The award conditions are that the works in all areas of the competition take into account the specificity of Omani society and its religious, social, moral, and political systems, that the participation is individual creativity, and no attention will be paid to any work done or implemented by more than one student, and that the participation is new and has not been previously published in any capacity, or participated in a specific event. The areas of the award for the youth category include classical poetry, literary research, critical reading, short stories, and literary articles, while for the youth category it will be in the literary article, promising speaker, poetic recitation, and young reader.  The award aims to enhance channels of cooperation and communication between the association and the Ministry of Education, educational institutions and schools, highlight the importance of literary work among all segments of society, especially students and youth in schools, and develop a spirit of competition among students in winning literary awards;  This contributes to improving their literary productions and enhancing their talents and creativity, encouraging literary writings among youth and young adults, working to publish distinguished literary productions for the winners of the competition, enhancing the association's role in serving the community, and enhancing awareness of the importance of literature among segments of society, specifically the youth.  The Omani Society for Writers and Literati, in cooperation with the Ministry of Education, developed the award in the second edition, dividing participants into three categories, each with specific areas that suit the age group in which they participate. The award targeted students from public and private schools and special education students in the young category from 6-9 years, the youth category from 10-13 years, and the adolescent category from 14-17 years.   The award fields are: poetry recitation, promising speaker for the young category, poetry recitation, speaking in standard Arabic, and analysis of literary texts "poetry field" for the adolescent category.
Results: The number of schools participating in this literary competition for the competition reached (60) schools, with 1,400 male and female students.
Recommandations: The award evaluation committee issued a number of recommendations to improve the competition's objectives and outcomes, which is necessary for the continuation of the partnership between the two institutions. The aim is to ensure the continuation of the competition for years to come and develop its fields and objectives in a way that serves the student and develops his various skills, and to invite the committee to invest in holding workshops for schools on the participation mechanism. The evaluation committee also recommended urging students to make an effort to compete in the next edition, diversifying the fields of participation to include larger study groups than the categories that were in the first edition, and the need to intensify media coverage of the competition, whether official media or social media platforms, in a way that benefits the competition from the promotional aspect.

Title EN: Supporting cultural projects through Cultural Endowment of Estonia
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture
SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Cultural and creative sectors
Agency Implementation: Cultural Endowment of Estonia
Main Feature: Outside of the Ministry of Culture, the main institution distributing state money for cultural purposes is the Cultural Endowment of Estonia - a legal person governed by public law. It supports mainly creative individuals, artistic associations and project-based initiatives in literature, dramatic art, music, audio-visual art, visual and applied arts, folk culture, architecture, and sport. Additionally, it also funds the construction and renovation of cultural buildings of national importance.     The Cultural Endowment operates with a minimum of bureaucracy under its own regulations and independently from political interests as the biggest share of the funding is automatically allocated from tax revenues.    The detailed breakdown of the income of the Cultural Endowment is as follows:   - proceeds in the state budget from the excise duty on alcohol and tobacco 3.5%  - proceeds in the state budget from gambling tax 47,8% (whereof 60,6% is allocated to finance cultural buildings which are of national importance and 39,4% is allocated to award grants and support and for administrative expenses)  - property donations and bequests made in favour of the Cultural Endowment  - income received from investment of the assets of the Cultural Endowment  -income from other economic activities   The structure of the Cultural Endowment of Estonia includes eight endowments and fifteen county expert groups.   An endowment is a structural unit of the Cultural Endowment with the function to distribute financial support allocated by the supervisory board of the Cultural Endowment to a specific field of culture. Funds are distributed through application rounds or based on the endowments’ initiative. The activities are organized by an endowment panel consisting of seven persons who are active in the corresponding field of culture and who are nominated by organizations representing this field of culture. The Minister of Culture approves the membership of an endowment panel. The mandate of a panel is two years and one person may serve two consecutive mandates.   A county expert group is a structural unit of the Cultural Endowment, which acts in every county with the function to distribute financial support allocated by the supervisory board of the Cultural Endowment to the fields of culture within the county. Funds are distributed through application rounds or based on the expert groups’ initiative. An expert group consists of five members that are persons active in the cultural field at the county level, the supervisory board of the Cultural Endowment approves the membership for two years. One person may belong to two consecutive memberships of an expert group.
Results: The funds that Cultural Endowment of Estonia distributes through its independent expert bodies to a wealth of different projects play a significant role in the overall finances of the culture sector. This makes the Cultural Endowment one of the most important sources of income for many creative individuals in Estonia. More than 17 000 applications are submitted yearly and due to limited budget, approximately 64-70% of them get financial support.
Recommandations: While it has been evaluated before, no external evaluation has been conducted in the period of 2020-2023. The Cultural Endowment operates under public law that has not been changed during the reporting period.  Like all undertakings operating in Estonia, the Cultural Endowment is obliged to submit an annual report that confirms to the form established in legislation. It consists of management report and the annual accounts and is reviewed by auditors.

Title EN: Supporting digital Transformation in Egypt
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture
SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Digital environment
Agency Implementation: The Supreme Council of Culture
Main Feature: Perhaps not since Gutenberg invented the printing press has humanity experienced such a qualitative shift as the one in the current era, with the emergence of the information age. It is developing rapidly and has brought together people from all parts of the world in a collection of networks and gatherings unobstructed by natural barriers, national borders, language, and so on. The world is rapidly moving from the real world to the virtual (digital) world, where traditional tools for communication, learning, therapy, commerce, culture, entertainment, and work in general are replaced by newer tools that rely on databases, technical systems, and high-speed communications networks. This has paved the way for what has come to be known as the fourth industrial revolution, where artificial intelligence techniques and massively-scaled data analysis are coupled with smart devices and ubiquitous internet connection in what has come to be known as the Internet of Things (IoT), and the development of new mechanisms for file exchange, file saving, and moving files across networks, such as blockchain technology, in addition to expanding digital financial inclusion to create encrypted digital currencies that can be used for buying, selling, and exchanging goods and services. All of the above has led to the growth of what is known as the digital economy, which has prompted everyone – ‘everyone’ here meaning governmental and private institutions, civil society organizations, research and academic institutions, and individuals – to integrate themselves into this new economy, to speak through its available tools, and to look forward to everything that is new, as well as setting out visions and plans to accelerate digital transformation processes in all aspects of life. Due to the Egyptian state’s belief in the importance of this digital transformation and the resulting development of strategies and implementation of digital transformation plans, the Egyptian Ministry of Culture, represented by the Supreme Council for Culture, has created the Committee for Digital Culture and Digital Information Infrastructure to contribute to accelerating these efforts and to function as one of the points of communication and activation for the desired digital transformation, in addition to attempting to outline a vision for culture in the digital world and the information and technical infrastructure it requires. This is being achieved within the framework of Egypt’s Vision 2030 and Sustainable Development Goals, as well as the government’s action plan “Egypt Begins” 2018-2022, where the COVID-19 pandemic ramped up efforts to accelerate this trend and to emphasize the inevitability of digital transformation and its indispensable importance for the continuation of business and other activities, including of course cultural activities related to building up the Egyptian citizen. The committee aims to implement a strategy for digital culture that revolves around monitoring and stimulating the level of digital culture at the strategic level within the Egyptian state to bring about the desired positive changes, as well as communicating these goals to the public and spreading awareness of digital culture. This strategy is based on implementing the following: •	Cultural Monitoring Segment: Preparing a report on the current status of efforts related to digital culture, including government efforts and private experiences, highlighting best practices and work priorities, while taking into account international experiences in this context. •	Digital Legislation Segment: Preparing a report on proposals for amending laws and regulations related to the Ministry’s efforts concerning digital transformation, digital culture, and the use of current technologies in performing various works and services, in cooperation with the People’s Assembly and the Council of Elders. •	Research Focus: Preparing public opinion questionnaires and polls regarding the extent of demand and interaction with these services and collecting citizens’ opinions on ways to improve them. •	Activities & Events Focus: Continuing the plan for virtual seminars on activities and fields related to various aspects of digital culture, taking into account the flexibility of these seminars, and participating with various committees to review these committees’ most important mandates and how to activate them in the digital world.  Examples: o	Contributing to refining public taste in the arts and literature using tools of modern digital technology  o	Raising awareness of the importance and role of startups in supporting and developing digital cultural products in a manner appropriate to our era, while devising participatory business models that suit the new digital economy. o	Raising awareness of the importance of new digital industries such as the digital exhibition industry o	Digital media, its morals and ethics o	Digital entrepreneurship Activities related to digital culture or other council committees from 2020 to 2024: -	Number of seminars: 132 -	Number of videos: 58 -	Number of competitions: 24 (including committees, the National Center for Children’s Culture , and the Young Creatives program). -	Number of relevant policy papers or memos: 12
Results: There is a remarkable increase in the number of creative products and cultural manifestations appear in digital form.
Financial Ressources: Not Applicable
Recommandations: Expanding the availability of cultural content Introducing private-sector investment into digital culture  Cultural equity and outreach to the provinces and remote regions Raising cultural consciousness, particularly among youth and young people

Area of Monitoring: Media diversity
Agency Implementation: twofour54 Dubai Studio City
Main Feature: The UAE supports the production of films and TV shows through major production hubs in Dubai and Abu Dhabi’s Free Zones. The free zones provide a strong regulatory environment and streamlined services for obtaining permits and visas, thereby streamlining the production process.  TwoFour54, which is Abu Dhabi’s Media Free Zone, offers high quality production and post-production facilities and services for the creation of everything from corporate videos, TVC’s and music videos to large scale television dramas, entertainment shows and feature films. Twofour54 offers studios, backlot and the UAE’s only Dolby Vision certified post-production facility as well as a creative team that has experience and contacts to enable a seamless production experience. Dubai Studio City is a collaborative media production hub and the region’s leading business community for film and television production with state-of-the-art infrastructure and purpose-built facilities including the largest sound stages in the Middle East. Since its establishment in 2005, Dubai Studio City has grown into a community that fosters creativity and nurtures filmmakers and producers in its world class production and post-production facilities.
Results: The initiative to support the production of media content through free zones and media cities in the UAE, such as Dubai Media City and Abu Dhabi’s twofour54, has achieved several notable results. These free zones and media hubs have been pivotal in fostering a dynamic media and creative sector in the UAE. The media free zones have created thousands of jobs in various sectors, including production, broadcasting, marketing, and digital media. This has contributed to the UAE’s economy and provided career opportunities for a diverse workforce. he media zones have fostered an environment conducive to innovation and creativity, encouraging media professionals to experiment with new formats and technologies. This has led to the development of cutting-edge content and media solutions.    - Dubai Media City Has become a regional hub for major global media companies, including CNN, BBC, and Reuters. This has attracted significant international investment and bolstered the UAE's position as a leading media center in the Middle East.    - twofour54 Located in Abu Dhabi, this media zone has similarly attracted numerous international media organizations and production companies, contributing to its status as a key player in the region’s media landscape.
Recommandations: As a result of these initiatives, media free zones such as Dubai Media City and twofour54 have seen a significant enhancement in their impact. The diversification of media programs and services has led to a broader range of content formats and the adoption of emerging technologies, keeping these zones at the cutting edge of the industry. Increased investment in infrastructure has bolstered competitiveness and attracted high-quality projects. Strengthened support for local talent through targeted training and funding has fostered the development of the next generation of media professionals. Greater collaboration and networking between international and local entities have spurred innovation and knowledge sharing. Additionally, the promotion of sustainable practices within media production has underscored a commitment to environmental responsibility. Strategic marketing efforts have expanded global outreach, drawing further international interest. Regular evaluation and adaptation of policies have ensured that the media zones remain aligned with evolving global trends and challenges.

Title EN: Supporting the creation and dissemination of journalistic content which balances the Russian-language information space and shapes a common media sphere by Estonian independent private media
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture
SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Media diversity
Agency Implementation: Ministry of Culture
Main Feature: The aim of the measure is to strengthen the editorial teams of existing Estonian private Russian-language publications in order to make the content of Estonian Russian-language journalism more professional, balanced and diverse. Private legal entities eligible for support provide media services throughout the territory of Estonia and must be Estonian journalism code of ethics-compliant. The produced and published media content is entirely local in nature, i.e. aimed exclusively at the Russian-speaking population living in Estonia and is available to the public free of charge.     The need to bring Russian-speaking Estonian residents into a common communication and information space has become especially urgent since 2022 when Russia intensified war against Ukraine. Due to incitement of war and propaganda, several Russian TV-channels and access to a number of Russian websites has been banned following the full-scale invasion and war of aggression against Ukraine, but there are still people in Estonia who are following Russian propaganda channels despite their ban. Therefore, high-quality Russian-language journalism free of propaganda needs to be provided for Russian-speaking Estonian residents as an alternative.       The described measure helps Estonian independent private media to create and disseminate journalistic content which balances the Russian-language information space and shapes a common media sphere, in so doing supporting the cohesion of Estonian society.       The funding for 2022 totalled €1,300,000 and for 2023 €1,000,000, while grants to any one entity were capped at €300,000. Four media houses received the financial support in 2023. After the grant period, recipients will submit a report to the ministry detailing how the funds were used.
Results: As a result of the support, Estonian private Russian-language media companies have increased their capacity to create and broadcast information that balances the Russian-language information space and shapes the common information space. The journalistic content is more diverse, balanced and better meets the needs of different target groups.
Financial Ressources: The funding for 2022 totalled 1 389 180 USD and for 2023 1 068 600 USD . It is planned to continue the measure until 2027.

Title EN: The Piano Tour: Promoting music in public spaces through digital means
Goal: Achieve A Balanced Flow Of Cultural Goods And Services And Increase The Mobility Of Artists And Cultural Professionals
SDG: SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 10 - Reduce inequality within and among countries,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Mobility of artists and cultural professionals
Agency Implementation: Avantgarde Cultural Foundation
Main Feature: The Piano Tour is promoting concerts in outdoor spaces, taking talented pianists to unconventional urban or natural spaces to perform, while streaming it live on Facebook so that the event is also attended both by audience present in the location as well as audience through digital means.  The inaugural concert was held at GSP; the capital city’s main football stadium, on the evening of the Cyprus Football Cup Final, in 2019. A grand piano and two classical musicians made their way into a busy, bustling football stadium for a 4-hand piano recital. Since then, The Piano Tour has continued to voyage around the island bringing classical music to all corners of the country. Performances have taken place in the most unconventional and sometimes inaccessible locations, including modern, ancient, rural and urban sites; from the rooftop of Nicosia’s tallest building to the Neolithic Settlement of Choirokoitia (a UNESCO World Heritage Site) and from a shipwreck in Paphos to a medieval bridge amidst one of Cyprus’ largest forests.   The Piano Tour aims at supporting local pianists, helping them also to gain publicity and enhance their mobility since the concerts are broadcasted live on Facebook and uploaded on YouTube. It also contributes immensely towards the so-much-needed audience development.
Results: The results are phenomenal, as the project has managed to make an impact on the local community and beyond. The videos so far have circulated the web with increasing views each time and have caught the attention of international pianists, foreign media and even a couple of the world’s most reputable piano manufacturers who shared images from some of The Piano Tour’s concerts on their social media pages.  Equally impressive is the attention that the project has received from the local community. Many artists have contacted the Foundation, asking to play in one of the future concerts. Some of them are not even pianists but they would like to be included as the project is piano-orientated yet offers opportunities to all and has presented so far concerts with one piano (solo and 4-hands), two pianos (4-hands and 8-hands), pianos and voice, piano and saxophone, piano and clarinet - even five pianos together!  The project travels all around the country and has managed to gain the attention from all due to its inclusivity. For this reason, many small villages and/or remote communities have contacted the Foundation asking for The Piano Tour to visit them.

Main Feature: The Teatrines cycle is an initiative of the Ministry of Culture and the National Theatre Institute (INT), which includes around 800 performances in various locations throughout Argentina. These are popular activities with easy accessibility, aimed especially at children and young audiences, with the objective of making visible the work of theater artists who generate productions for children, adolescents and families.  Teatrines aims to strengthen ties with audiences in different cities, both in open and closed spaces, squares, canteens, neighborhood centers, schools, neighborhood centers and clubs where the objective can be achieved to increase audiences, encouraging participation and making possible the encounter between the community and the theater sector.  The programming of the scenic interventions generated by the INT not only seeks to make visible the work of Argentine theater artists, who throughout the length and breadth of the country generate theater productions aimed at children, adolescents and families, but also to strengthen ties with audiences eager to reconnect with theater, puppetry, circus shows, etc.    Teatrines is a system of co-production with provincial and municipal governments and institutions, health authorities, civil associations and third sector organizations which made it possible to adapt each performance, activity or festival to the local realities of each stage of compulsory preventive social distancing, in addition to making human, technical and logistical resources available.
Results: Through this programme, in particular, the replenishment of the productive system of the national independent theater continued its implementation in order to guarantee the exercise of the right to cultural consumption by children. These were popular, accessible activities, with events and festivals in different cities of the country aimed especially at children, both in open and closed spaces, respecting the health protocols in force. This was another way of gradually bringing about a new strengthening of the relationship between audiences who wanted to come back into contact with theater, puppet and circus performances, and Argentinean groups and casts that produce creative shows and activities aimed at children, adolescents and families. During 2021, more than 600 theater performances were held, involving more than 350 shows, reaching 240 locations throughout the country; while during 2022, the Teatrines programme continued in the same popular spirit, with easy accessibility, free admission and a focus on children and young people and families. Around 200 more performances and activities took place than the previous year, thus exceeding 800 in the different regions of the country.  Teatrines strengthened ties with children and youth audiences in different cities, both in open and closed spaces, squares, dining halls, neighborhood centers, schools, neighborhood centers and clubs where the aim of increasing audiences, encouraging participation and enabling the meeting between the community and the theater sector can be achieved.

This program aims to highlight the film industry in the State of Qatar and embody support for local talents by providing an important platform for Qatari and resident filmmakers to showcase their creativity and realize their unique ideas through films.  The Doha Film Institute (DFI) was established on April 25, 2010, with the goal of empowering and enhancing the capabilities of screenwriters and storytellers, especially those with global content and themes. The Institute aims to be a key player in the global film industry by offering training and development initiatives, film financing programs, and organizing film-related festivals and forums, such as the “Qumra Film Festival”. Qumra provides guidance, mentorship, and practical support to filmmakers in the State of Qatar and around the world, reaching its tenth edition in 2024. These measures, although beyond the timeframe of this report, are crucial and closely linked to achieving the objectives of the Convention on the Protection and Promotion of the Diversity of Cultural Expressions.    Additionally, the Doha Film Institute complements other active institutions in the field of cinema and films, such as “Qatar National Cinema and Film Distribution Company” (1970) (Annex No. 31), “Qatar Film Production Center” (2009) (Annex No. 32), and the “Doha Film Festival Foundation” (2010) (Annex No. 33).
Results: This program is still new, making it difficult to quantify all the results achieved for this report. However, it can be noted that the jury selected 14 short films in the official competition of the program during this cycle, four of which won awards as follows:  -	The film "The Chandelier" directed by Karim Amara won the Best Film Award. -	Nadia Al-Khater won the Best Director Award for her film "A Proposal". -	Faisal Al-Balushi won the "Abdulaziz Jassim Award for Best Performance" for his role in the film "Sanad". -	The films "Above the Tamarind Tree" by Buthaina Al-Mohamedi and "When It’s Time" by Awad Karar received special mentions from the jury. All participating films were broadcast during the week following the conclusion of the competition.  Additionally, the Doha Film Institute Grants Program has contributed to the success of many films that benefited from its mechanisms. Main Feature: In 2023, the Act on Amendments and Supplements to the Act on RTV Slovenia came into force, with the principal objective of guaranteeing the institutional and programmatic autonomy of RTV Slovenia and safeguarding the editorial and journalistic independence of the organisation. The most significant alterations pertain to the appointment of members of the Board and the Management, who are no longer appointed by political bodies but are instead nominated by civil society and professional associations. A more comprehensive revision of the Act on RTV Slovenia is forthcoming, which will regulate the financing of public RTV in addition to the administration and redefinition of the public service.
Results: By amending the act, the government has addressed some of RTV Slovenija's most pressing problems by removing party politics from RTV Slovenia and placing the governance of the largest public media outlet entirely in the hands of civil society and employees.

Title EN: The Árni Magnússon Institute for Icelandic Studies
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture
SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Cultural and creative sectors
Agency Implementation: The Árni Magnússon Institute for Icelandic Studies
Main Feature: The Árni Magnússon Institute for Icelandic Studies is an independently funded academic research institute at the University of Iceland under direct supervision of the Ministry of Culture and Business Affairs. Its role is to conduct research in the field of Icelandic studies and related scholarly disciplines, in particular Icelandic language and literature; to disseminate knowledge in these fields; and to preserve and augment the collections entrusted to its care. The Institute serves the role of teaching Icelandic and providing services to university professors of Icelandic at foreign universities on behalf of the Icelandic government. The Institute is a member of the Nordic Cooperation Committee for teaching Nordic studies abroad. It also offers a popular international summer course in Icelandic. One of the Institute’s main goals is safeguarding Icelandic manuscripts. The Institute also works on practical and theoretical research on the Icelandic language, literature, history and culture. It employs a number of full-time scholars as well as guests who are provided with facilities for researching, either in the short or long term. Several doctoral students have research facilities at the Institute and work on their projects in close cooperation with the Institute’s staff and guests. The Institute provides grants to foreign writers, translators and scholars through the Snorri Sturluson Icelandic Fellowships. These are awarded to individuals who seek to reside in Iceland for a few months specifically to acquaint themselves with the Icelandic language, culture and the local way of life.
Results: The Institute has provided a valuable service in terms of supporting scholars and those studying the Icelandic language. The Institute’s website hosts a publicly accessible list of endorsed projects. Some of the research projects endorsed have led to the development of continuously usable products, such as the Icelandic Vocabulary Network, a collection of over 200,000 various Icelandic phrases.
Financial Ressources: In 2024 7.653.486 USD was allocated to the Institute ((1.057.400.000 ISK)

Title EN: The Gender Balance Guide: Actions for UAE Organizations
Goal: Promote Human Rights And Fundamental Freedoms
SDG: SDG 5 - Achieve gender equality and empower all women and girls,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels
Area of Monitoring: Gender equality
Agency Implementation: UAE Gender Balance Council
Main Feature: The Gender Balance Guide: Actions for UAE Organizations is a comprehensive policy measure aimed at promoting gender equality and enhancing the representation of women in the workforce across all sectors in the UAE. The main features of this guide include actionable steps for organizations to implement gender balance, such as setting clear gender diversity targets, establishing mentorship and sponsorship programs for women, ensuring equal pay for equal work, and creating a supportive work environment that accommodates work-life balance. The guide also emphasizes the importance of leadership commitment and accountability in driving gender balance initiatives.
Results: The UAE has made significant progress in gender equality, as reflected in its ranking in the Gender Inequality Index (GII) 2024 issued by the United Nations Development Program (UNDP). The country advanced from 49th place in 2015 to 11th in 2022, and now to 7th globally and 1st regionally in 2024. This leap signifies substantial improvements in gender balance across various sectors including economic, political, and social domains. This achievement was highlighted during the 68th session of the Commission on the Status of Women in New York, where the UAE Gender Balance Council actively participated. The Council attributes this success to the visionary leadership and the supportive environment created for women's empowerment by initiatives and legislative measures.
Recommandations: The main conclusions from this achievement emphasize the critical role of leadership commitment and strategic initiatives in advancing gender balance. The UAE's approach, which involves comprehensive legislation and the creation of supportive environments for women, has been effective in promoting gender equality.
