Title EN: The Centre for Creativity
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture
SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Cultural and creative sectors
Agency Implementation: Museum of architecture and design – Centre for creativity
Main Feature: The Center for Creativity (CzK), managed by the Museum of Architecture and Design, is the national platform for the development of the cultural and creative sector (CCS) in Slovenia. With its programs, it promotes the strengthening of the social and economic potential of the sector and actively connects it with business, science, education and other sectors. Together with the public calls of the Ministry of Culture for the "Promotion of Creative Cultural Industries"," it creates a supportive environment for the development of the cultural and creative sector in Slovenia. The center promotes the development of activities that emerge at the intersection of art, culture, experimentation, market and entrepreneurship and whose results are also commercially exploitable, add value or aim to solve social problems and contribute to social progress and prosperity. CzK is active in the fields of architecture, advertising, design, visual arts, cultural heritage, archiving, libraries, books, cultural and artistic education, music, performing and intermedia arts, media, software and games, film and audiovisual activities, cultural tourism and other artistic creation. The programs are complemented by the CzK partner network, which connects more than 38 organizations from various creative fields. CzK manages various programs for the development of innovative products and services, organizes and promotes education, internationalization and networking, research and (online) promotion. Together with the tenders of the Ministry of Culture of the Republic of Slovenia for the promotion of the creative industries, it supports projects that emerge at the intersection of various creative fields and entrepreneurship and contribute to economic and social progress. The CzK partner network comprises no less than 38 partners, which you can find via the link https://czk.si/skupnost/partnerji/?fwp_vrsta_partnerstva=partnerska-mreza.  The members of the CzK partner network come from different areas of the cultural and creative sector, who with their visions and programs help shape a national support environment for the development of the creative ecosystem in Slovenia. CzK creates a supportive environment for the Slovenian creative sector based on six program pillars: 1.	Development of products and services: by promoting cooperation between the creative sector, businessesand the public and private sectors. By 2020, 115 projects and companies had already been supported with more than 2,9 million euros as part of the Ministry of Culture's "Promotion of the Creative Cultural Industries - CzK" call for proposals. A total of 5.3 million euros has been allocated to creative artists from funding alone until 2022. 2.	Education and mentoring: The center has helped more than a thousand participants through training, conferences, lectures, workshops, mentoring and advice on applying for CzK tenders: Cultural practitioners, creative businesses, producers, cultural managers, creative intermediaries, entrepreneurs and employees in the private and public sectors. The center runs educational programs such as the Creative Incubator, Creative Accelerator and Skillshare. 3.	Networking at home and abroad: Together with many partners from Slovenia and abroad, the center has organized a number of international presentations of Slovenian artists from the fields of architecture, design, music, visual arts and cultural heritage and have appeared at important international fairs and events, such as Milan Design Week, Vienna Contemporary, Maison & Objet in Paris, etc. In addition, the center has established several partnerships within the framework of European projects and platforms aimed at artists from various fields. 4.	Analysis and research: For a better insight into the economic and social potentials and needs of the cultural and creative sector with the aim of developing recommendations, supportive measures and programs. 5.	Online platform: www.czk.si is a national contact point for creatives and creative seekers - a solution that informs about and presents creative products and services and provides information about opportunities and training. 6.	Promotion and communication: The center promotes Slovenian creatives and their work through media partnerships, “pop-up” stores, events and exhibitions. The Center for Creativity works on a national and international level, bringing together various organizations and individuals from the CCI sector. CzK also brings together individuals and organizations from the fields of architecture, design and other areas through the projects listed below: 1.	MADE IN Platform: a research, design and heritage initiative that promotes collaboration and knowledge exchange between traditional craftspeople and contemporary designers and other cultural and scientific experts. 2.	Capacity2Transform: a capacity building project addressing skills shortages in the creative and cultural industries and sustainable tourism of small and medium-sized enterprises in Central Europe. 3.	Distributed Design Platform: brings together a wide range of members from cultural and creative institutions and offers pan-European programmes and opportunities to support emerging creatives working in the emerging field of distributed design. 4.	Biennial of Design: an international collaborative process where designers and creatives from diverse backgrounds question design as a creative discipline and develop alternatives to the established systems.
Results: From 2017 to 2022, CzK 1.0 networked and supported thousands of creatives, creative entrepreneurs and organizations together with public calls for the promotion of the creative industries by the Ministry of Culture. The project fostered new collaborations between creatives and the economy, facilitated new jobs in creative businesses and promoted the sector at home and abroad. The need for this type of project was great, as evidenced by the numerous awards, successes and indicators of the project. More than 500 programs were created to develop the sector and connect it with the economy, with the active participation of 500 companies from the creative and private sectors, more than 2,000 creative professionals and 248,000 participants and visitors. Together with public calls from the Ministry of Culture, over 200 innovative products and services were developed and at least 62 new jobs in creative companies were financed. CzK 1.0. cooperated with more than 200 partners from Slovenia and abroad, more than 60 presentations were held in 24 countries, more than 100 products received the CzK Made in Slovenia seal of quality. CzK 1.0. conducted the first national study on the importance, potential and needs of the creative sector. Most importantly, in just 5 years, the Center for Creativity (CzK 1.0) project has become a recognized player in various European networks and initiatives that provide Slovenian creatives with access to additional European funding.  From 2024 to 2029, the National Platform Center for Creativity 2.0 will aim to create a high-quality and efficient business and innovation environment for activities in the field of CCIs. CzK 2.0 represents a further development of CzK 1.0, i.e. the establishment of the National Platform Center for Creativity, which in the future will take care of the upgrading and implementation of measures for the development of the cultural and creative sector in Slovenia and its integration with other sectors, the development of technological and non-technological innovations and will contribute to the strengthening of CCIs as well as decentralization and internationalization.

Title EN: The Children’s Culture Fund of Iceland
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture
SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Partnering with civil society
Agency Implementation: Ministry of Culture and Business Affairs
Main Feature: The Children’s Culture Fund of Iceland was established by the Icelandic Parliament (Althing) in accordance with a resolution made at a parliamentary session conducted at Thingvellir in celebration of the centennial of Iceland’s sovereignty. The Fund is a public initiative intended to support diverse cultural activities for the benefit of children and youths. The Fund finances projects that support the democratic participation of children in society or take special measures according to the United Nations Convention on the Rights of the Child. The Fund works to fulfil the main goals of the government’s National Cultural Policy about cooperation between schools, civil groups and individuals, as well as the goal of equal access for children and youth to diverse and quality art events despite their living and financial situation. Eligible applicants to the Fund are artists, arts and culture organizations, NGOs, and others engaged in cultural activities for children and youth in accordance with the Cultural Policy. Children's culture refers to projects in the field of art and culture that are prepared for children and/or with the active participation of children. The fund enjoyed a contribution from the state budget for five years (2019-2023), 100 million ISK a year. Hence, it is a public initiative, intended to support diverse cultural activities for the benefit of children and young people. With the Parliamentary resolution on an action plan for the promotion of children's culture for the years 2024–2028 the fund is established for the long term.
Results: The fund supported 34 excellent projects in 2022 and 41 ambitious projects in 2023 and the total amount allocated that year was ISK 96.8 million. A total of 105 applications were received and almost four times the amount that the fund had for distribution was applied for, or over ISK 373 million.  An allocation from the Children's Culture Fund of Iceland has been announced for the year 2024. The fund supports 41 ambitious projects and the total amount of the allocation is 102.4 million ISK. A total of 117 applications were received and 383 million ISK was applied for. The allocation was announced at a ceremony in the Museum on Children's Day, Sunday 26 May 2024.
Financial Ressources: In 2024 794.735 USD was allocated to the Children´s Culture Fund (109.800.000 ISK)

Main Feature: Implemented by the National Institute of Music and Dance, the programme of the Minister of Culture and National Heritage "Composing commissions" is the first project in Poland which systemically supports latest musical production. The programme annually endorses approximately one hundred new pieces by Polish and foreign composers, enabling a wide audience to access valuable contemporary music compositions. The programme was launched in 2012 as an initiative of Polish musical milieu. The annual competition attracts applications form musical organizations willing to commission a work from a (Polish or foreign) composer or group of artists. The subsidy includes co-financing the work along with its world premiere and recording which is later rendered available online, free of charge, as part of the National Audiovisual Institute collection (Ninateka.pl). The programme implements projects representing a wide array of genres, from the so-called contemporary classical music and music theatre performances through pieces combining different musical genres (e.g. popular and traditional music) and interdisciplinary projects verging on music, performing and visual arts. The music created thanks to Composing commissions is intended to resound not only in major concert halls, where it will add to the latest chapter of artistic music, but also in minor centres and among non-specialist audiences, acting as an important vessel of artistic education
Results: The programme subsidizes the creation those main types of commissions: - chamber works - vocal / vocal and instrumental works - symphonic works - other works in which sound is the main composition element - electroacoustic works - full-length and chamber stage works - multimedia works in which sound is the main composition element. The programme co-financed 316 projects in the 2020-2023 period

Title EN: The Construction of Library and Archive Complex
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture
SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Cultural and creative sectors
Agency Implementation: Ethiopian National Archives and Library Service
Main Feature: Overview  The Ethiopian National Archives and Library Agency (ENALA) has undertaken a major infrastructure project with the construction of a state-of-the-art library and archive complex. This project was made possible through significant capital investment from the Ethiopian government. The new complex represents a pivotal development in the country's efforts to modernize its library and archival services, particularly in the areas of digitization, preservation, and accessibility of cultural and historical documents.  Key Objectives and Achievements Enhancement of Library and Archive Services: The new complex is designed to significantly improve the quality and scope of services provided by the Ethiopian National Archives and Library Agency. It offers advanced facilities for the preservation, display, and registration of various art documents, manuscripts, and publications. This infrastructure supports the agency's mission to systematically collect, organize, and make accessible Ethiopia's rich cultural heritage.  Advancement in Archiving Through Digitization: One of the core objectives of the new facility is to drive the digitization of archival materials. The complex will be equipped with modern technology to enable the digital preservation of valuable records, thus ensuring their protection from physical deterioration and making them more accessible to researchers and the public.  Improvement in Service Delivery: The construction of this complex is expected to elevate the overall service delivery of the Ethiopian National Archives and Library Agency. By providing a modern and efficient environment for both staff and users, the complex will facilitate better management of library and archival resources, contributing to the agency's goal of enhancing public access to Ethiopia's historical and cultural documents and space for the library.  The construction of the new library and archive complex marks a significant milestone in the development of Ethiopia's cultural infrastructure. It not only strengthens the capabilities of the Ethiopian National Archives and Library Agency but also positions it to better serve the public and preserve the nation's cultural heritage for future generations.
Results: Enhanced Library Service Excellence: The library has significantly improved its service delivery, emphasizing customer service excellence. This enhancement ensures a more responsive, user-friendly environment that better meets the needs of its patrons.  Improved Archiving Services: Archival processes are being upgraded to ensure more efficient management and retrieval of documents. This improvement in archiving services facilitates better organization and accessibility of historical and cultural records.  Access to Art Documents: Efforts have been made to increase the accessibility of art-related documents within the library's collection. This initiative supports researchers, students, and the public by providing easier access to valuable cultural resources.  Ensured the Safety of Art Products and Archives: The library is implementing enhanced safety measures to protect its collections and archival materials. These measures ensure that the integrity and preservation of these important cultural artifacts are maintained.  Supported Digitization of Archives: The library has advanced its digitization efforts, converting a significant portion of its archives into digital formats. This support for digitization not only preserves the materials but also makes them more widely accessible to a global audience.

Title EN: The creative salaries instrument as a way of supporting artists and writers with a state salary
Goal: Promote Human Rights And Fundamental Freedoms
SDG: SDG 5 - Achieve gender equality and empower all women and girls,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels
Area of Monitoring: Artistic freedom
Agency Implementation: Ministry of Culture
Main Feature: The creative salaries instrument was first introduced in 2016 as a way of supporting artists and writers with a fixed-period salary from a state. The funding is allocated by the Ministry of Culture in the form of a grant to the respective Artistic Association. The salary is paid by the Artistic Association for a period of three years to writers and artists at their creative peak who are selected through open competition. Each creative salary will be the 1.1 times the minimum wage for a cultural worker with higher education, including taxes. The number of selected salary recipients has gradually grown. The salary does not impose any obligations on its recipients, they are just asked to provide an annual overview of their creative activities. Awarding the creative salary is a recognition for the recipient. It provides much needed social benefits and sends a clear message to the society that the artists and writers are doing a valuable job that is as important as anyone else’s.
Results: Since 2023, a total of 15 writers and 20 artists receive yearly the creative salary from the state. The measure creates the conditions and security that enables outstanding creators to focus on their creative work for three years. The social guarantees for freelancers in the arts has been a long-standing problem and the measure helps to improve the situation.
Recommandations: Final report of the study by Civitta AS “Remuneration of Creative Work in Estonia and Assessing the Impact of Creative Salaries Instrument” was published in 2023 (in Estonian only).     The study found that a very large number of the problems are the same across different cultural sectors (notably lack of professional jobs, unstable incomes, lack of market demand, problem of social guarantees).   The creative salaries instrument for writers and artists is quite good and effective. Although it does not solve a large number of the problems that exist in the sectors, it does improve the working conditions of creators receiving a creative salary during the time they are receiving it, to a very significant extent.   The creative salaries measure should continue to be targeted at the top, i.e. creators who are professionally active and in top form.    If the conditions of the measure are changed, this should mean increasing the number of beneficiaries rather than increasing the amount.    By extending the measure to areas where there is no creative salary measure today, a similar system to the writers' and artists' salary would be appropriate.

Throughout the years, the Festival has championed the joy of reading, shining a spotlight on books in the UAE and worldwide. Title EN: The Digital Environment Ecosystem of the Music Sector in Zimbabwe
Goal: Integrate Culture In Sustainable Development Frameworks
SDG: SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: National sustainable development policies and plans
Agency Implementation: National Arts Council of Zimbabwe Ministry of Sport, Recreation, Arts and Culture
Main Feature: Establishing a baseline assessment of the digital music sector in Zimbabwe. Finding solutions for the sub optimal functioning of the digital music sector in Zimbabwe by identifying priority areas and detailing best practice case studies.  Mobilizing and engaging local stakeholders in identifying priority areas for music development and growth in a digitized environment. Providing the music sector with a baseline understanding of the digital music sector in Zimbabwe from which to develop further support.
Results: The requisite priority areas for music development in a digitized environment identified for immediate attention and these are: Implementing a music export strategy Professional development and education in the music sector Capacity building for creatives in intellectual property rights Updating of copyright legislation Availing of affordable internet data bundles Accessible and affordable recording and production houses Establishing accessible and apt digital infrastructure nation-wide

Title EN: The Female Filmmaker Project
Goal: Promote Human Rights And Fundamental Freedoms
SDG: SDG 5 - Achieve gender equality and empower all women and girls,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels
Area of Monitoring: Gender equality
Agency Implementation: National Film and Video Foundation (NFVF)
Main Feature: The Female Filmmaker Project is a programme developed by the NFVF to increase opportunities for emerging writers and directors to have their work developed by reputable production companies. The concept for the female filmmaker project is a valuable intervention by the NFVF, to provide recent female entrants into the industry, particularly those from historically disadvantaged backgrounds, with an opportunity to make a film in collaboration with other women. The initiative also assists production companies in identifying and producing films that demonstrate audience awareness in the South African and international markets. The aim of the project is: • To nurture, support and promote female filmmakers in South Africa through strategically developed training laboratories and workshops; and • To seek out remarkable storytellers and develop regionally based filmmaking talent, which will bring new perspective to the South African and ultimately the African global audience. Currently, it is the only programme with the aim of correcting the disparity between men and women within the film industry through up-skilling of female filmmakers, particularly writers and directors from a previously disadvantaged background, and mentoring them through their first short films.
Results: The National Film and Video Foundation (NFVF), in partnership with Yellowbone Entertainment, KZN Film Commission (KZNFC), and the South African Broadcasting Corporation (SABC), have launched a call for submissions for the NFVF Female Filmmaker Project. The initiative aims to bring together ten talented women from underrepresented backgrounds annually for the next three years to collaborate on film projects. By participating in the program, female filmmakers will have the opportunity to enhance their skills, broaden their knowledge, and establish important industry connections under the mentorship of Yellowbone Entertainment. Filmmakers have an opportunity to explore parallel realities in imaginative and creative ways, whether through science fiction elements or grappling with issues across multiple universes. For 2022/23 financial year, a cohort of 12 filmmakers have been selected to be upskilled through development and production workshops. A total of ten films were produced at the end of Year 1 of the programme.

Title EN: The Hong Kong SAR provides access to the public to diverse cultural expressions
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture
SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development

Cultural Domain: Design,Performing Arts,Media Arts,Cinema and Audiovisual Arts,Music,Publishing
Agency Implementation: Cultural, Sports and Tourism Bureau (CSTB) and Leisure and Cultural Services Department (LCSD) of the Hong Kong SAR Government
Main Feature: Performance venues and cultural programmes: 16 performance venues are managed by LCSD, which include three territory-wide performing arts venues, 11 district venues as well as two indoor stadia. In 2023, over 5000 performances were held in the relevant venues. LCSD presents a variety of cultural programmes annually, which include large-scale arts festivals.  LCSD also provides funding support for the Hong Kong Arts Festival.  Major performing arts groups that receive subvention from the Culture, Sports and Tourism Bureau, and arts groups which are Venue Partners of LCSD, present quality performances as well.  To further support the growth and development of local artists, LCSD has been organising programmes in GBA cities since 2018-19.  In addition, LCSD organises free arts education and audience building events at schools and in the local community to promote arts and culture in all walks of life.  Museums: There are 15 museums and two art spaces managed by LCSD.  They are professionally managed to provide an ideal environment for the conservation and display of collections.  Large-scale thematic exhibitions are held every year to add variety to the permanent exhibitions with the ultimate goal to attract more people to visit museums.  Extension activities such as film shows, demonstrations, workshops and travelling exhibitions are organised to stimulate interest and popularise museum services.  Libraries: The Hong Kong Public Libraries (HKPL) managed by LCSD now provides a network of 71 static libraries and 12 mobile libraries with a comprehensive collection of library materials, including books and multimedia materials.  As at 31 December 2023, HKPL had 4.86 million registered borrowers.  HKPL aims to serve the public in the ways as manifested in the “UNESCO Public Library Manifesto”. HKPL has continued to fulfill its commitment in promoting a knowledge-based community through reading and literary arts by organising a diversity of cultural activities by partnership with different organisations.
Results: Through a variety of cultural programmes and arts education activities, as well as museum and library services, the general public could access to the diverse cultural expressions in the community. In 2023, around 5 400 performances were staged at the 16 performance venues managed by LCSD, which attracted about 2.9 million audiences. About 29.6 million items have been borrowed from the 83 public libraries in Hong Kong. An attendance of about 6.35 million was recorded in the 15 public museums and two art spaces.
Financial Ressources: In 2023-2024, the Government's total expenditure on culture and arts around 789 million USD, where around 553 million USD were allocated to performing arts services, museum and public libraries services under LCSD.
Recommandations: The number of users of the resources have been recorded by the Census and Statistics Department of the Hong Kong SAR Government. The measures were effective in providing access to the public to the diverse cultural expressions in the society.

Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture

Area of Monitoring: Media diversity
Agency Implementation: The Icelandic Media Commission
Main Feature: The Icelandic Media Commission is an independent administrative committee which reports directly to the Ministry of Culture and Business Affairs. The Commission conducts surveillance in accordance with the media law and other relevant legislation. Its role is to promote media literacy, diversity and pluralism in the media, as well as safeguarding the freedom of expression and the right of the public to information. The Commission regulates both public and commercial media services in Iceland in accordance with the media act (38/2011) and the Icelandic National Broadcasting Service act (23/2013). The Commission additionally monitors children’s access to films and video games in accordance with the act on the monitoring of children’s access to films and video games (62/2006). The Commission monitors and conducts surveillance of a variety of both public and private media in Iceland. It monitors the Icelandic National Broadcasting Service (RÚV) and annually reviews its performance to determine if its operations are in line with legislation and guidelines. The Media Commission thus monitors advertising, sponsorship and product placement in Icelandic media. Furthermore it monitors programming that can be harmful for a child’s development and the use of advance warnings in television programming. The Media Commission also issues broadcasting licences in Iceland. Certain information about the media market and media companies must be available to the public according to the Media Law. This information is gathered by the Media Commission and made available on its website. This includes information about media ownership, list of media service providers and their rules on editorial independence. The Media Commission is intended to promote media literacy, diversity and pluralism in the media, protect freedom of expression and the public's right to information.
Results: Since the Commission was formed in 2011 it has been an instrumental part of monitoring and reviewing media related issues, for example reviewing and providing commentary on seven bills undergoing the Parliamentary process throughout this timeframe. The Commissions main task is monitoring and conducting surveillance of the media, ensuring that both public and private bodies work in accordance with the media act (38/2011). The Commission takes suggestions from the general public and is able to determine whether a media organization is in breach of relevant legislation following a review.
Financial Ressources: In 2024 813.554 USD was allocated tot the Icelandic Media Commission (112.400.000 ISK)

Title EN: The impact of AI and the digital transformation on the CCSI
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture
SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Digital environment
Cultural Domain: Design,Performing Arts,Media Arts,Cinema and Audiovisual Arts,Music,Publishing,Visual Arts
Agency Implementation: European Commission
Main Feature: Artificial Intelligence (AI) is disrupting the cultural and creative sectors and industries (CCSI). From architecture to book publishing, from film to music, from news media to videogames, from fashion to cultural heritage and visual arts, AI offers tremendous opportunities to understand and reach out new audiences, inspire new arts, save costs, increase efficiency and open new markets. However, the acceleration of Generative AI raises important challenges as regards copyright and personality rights, skills and jobs, fairness and transparency, cultural diversity, and the long-term impact for the market of cultural and creative products and services.  The European Commission has shown strong leadership in positioning Europe at the forefront of digital and AI regulation and policymaking. Several initiatives have been put in place to set up an enabling framework for a fair digital market and to allow cultural diversity to flourish, e.g. copyright reform, digital services package (see Digital Environment section of this report). Furthermore, the Artificial Intelligence Act will support the enforcement of the EU copyright rules and ensure transparency on the AI training content and marking/labelling content generated with AI. (see AI Act entry in the Digital Environment section of this report). Important flagship initiatives such as the Common Data space for Cultural Heritage or the European Collaborative Cloud for Cultural Heritage are on their way to ensure that the European cultural heritage sector takes full advantage of the potential of data and advanced technologies (see relevant entry in Digital Environment section). Furthermore, various resolutions from the European Parliament call to undertake action notably as regards transparency of algorithms, preservation of cultural diversity in the digital realm and the implications of AI on CCSI jobs, working conditions and skills, among others.  Besides, a number of studies have been carried out to better understand the changes brought by the digital transformation as well as to assess the link between AI and the CCS, among which the 2022 Expert study on (re)-engaging with digital audiences, providing key recommendations to cultural operators and policymakers to make the most of the technologies and data management, the comprehensive 2022 report Opportunities and challenges of Artificial Intelligence Technologies for the Cultural and Creative Sectors (CCS) exploring existing or potential business opportunities and the challenges that need to be addressed, such as how AI can be developed in ways that respect Europe’s cultural diversity and ethical values; or the complementary study Copyright and New technologies regarding the implications of the use of AI technologies for copyright, also published in 2022. In a continued effort to gather data and research evidence, the European Commission launched in Spring 2024 a study on discoverability of diverse European cultural content in the online environment with a view to promote European cultural diversity online. Results are expected in Autumn 2025.  In addition, different EU programmes, from Creative Europe to Cluster 2-Horizon Europe, Digital Europe, and the Recovery and Resilience Facility (RRF) have been mobilised to support the sector to undertake the digital transition.

Title EN: The project on development of the Slovenian language in a digital environment
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture
SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Digital environment
Agency Implementation: Ministry of Culture
Main Feature: The project Development of the Slovenian language in a digital environment is a reaction to the current social changes in connection with digitalization, as this influences the transformation of cultural identity. Language, as one of the fundamental elements of cultural identity, must be digitized in today’s world to ensure one of the most important prerequisites for the long-term preservation of cultural identity in an increasingly globalized and rapidly changing digital environment. The Slovenian language, with its smaller number of speakers, is even more exposed to the trend of its use giving way to the uniform adoption of English as the global language in the digitized society. The development of modern language resources and technologies for Slovenian ensures effective use of the language in the digital environment. It is essential that the country already has a partially established research and development environment and actors (public organizations and companies) for the development of language infrastructure. Consequently, the digital transformation of language (speech recognition, text recognition and processing, speech generation, translation, etc.) also implies the digital transformation of cultural and creative industries and institutions. This fosters positive links between culture, creativity, innovation, and the economy in general, as culture can directly contribute to exemplary solutions in new services and products.  The project consortium consisted of 12 institutions, including the largest educational and research institutions in Slovenia – 3 universities (University of Ljubljana, University of Maribor, University of Nova Gorica), 3 public research institutions (Jožef Stefan Institute, Scientific Research Centre of the Slovenian Academy of Sciences and Arts, Institute of Contemporary History) and 5 companies (Slovenian Press Agency, Post of Slovenia, Amebis, Aikwit, Alpineo, Vitasis).
Results: In the field of digitization of the Slovene language, some of the most urgent gaps related to open access resources, technologies and services for modern Slovene have been filled. The training datasets and and procedures for automatic linguistic annotation of modern Slovene have been renewed, the central language resources have been upgraded and the methodology for their future development has been revised. Progress has been made above all in the development of speech databases and speech technologies, especially in speech recognition for Slovenian. Semantic resources and technologies have also been developed, including the creation of a central digital dictionary database, a knowledge database, and resources for various semantic tasks. The methodology for machine translation has been improved and specific language resources and technologies have been developed that are a central part of language digitization. These include a machine translation engine for the EN-SL and SL-EN language combination, a speech recognizer (automatic transcription of audio files), a terminology portal for the management of Slovenian terminology and various e-tools for:  - the recognition of named entities (identification of names of persons, organizations, toponyms and proper names), - relation extraction (identification of names in the text and relations between them), - the resolution of coreferences (identification of names in the text and their coreferential relationships), - answering questions (finding answers to questions posed in the text) and for word sense disambiguation (identifying - the meaning of a word with several meanings used in a particular communication situation), - the automatic labeling of Slovenian texts and a tool for the manual correction of texts, - common-sense reasoning (automatic generation of coherent descriptions in natural language), - the recognition of semantic shifts (recognition of changes in word usage).  The results are not only useful in the field of culture, but also in a broader sense – for research institutions, companies and the general public.
Recommandations: The main recommendation is to ensure stable and continuous funding at national level. Co-funding the development of language resources and technologies through individual/sporadic public calls is not enough.

Area of Monitoring: Artistic freedom
Cultural Domain: Design,Performing Arts,Media Arts,Cinema and Audiovisual Arts,Music,Publishing,Visual Arts
Agency Implementation: Ministry of Culture/ Project Management Unit
Main Feature: The Statute of the Professional Cultural Workers  was elaborated as part of the National Recovery and Resilience Plan of Romania 2021-2026 and received technical support as well as through UNESCO - Aschberg Programme for Artists and Cultural Professionals.   The Statute provides for a coherent and unified legal and fiscal regime for the professional cultural workers in Romania and for a strengthening of the rights of cultural workers: collective representation, professional association memberships, social security, recognized work experience, and unemployment benefits meeting specific conditions. Moreover, cultural workers may benefit from protection in case of events similar to work accidents, medical leaves and temporary work incapacity, maternity or child sickness.  A National Mobility Program has been put in place that offers funding and support for career development and professional growth. The National Mobility Program shall support expenses regarding the international and national mobility, the acquisition of new skills, with priority for the development of digital skills or the costs of transport and insurance of the works and other protected objects. A Professional Cultural Workers’ Registry is in process of implementation and it will allow for a voluntary inscription of the cultural workers.
Results: - The approval of the Government Emergency Ordinance no 21/2023  concerning the Status of the Cultural Professional Worker. - The legal framework is under last stages of implementation of administrative preparatory measures .

Title EN: The World Conference on Creative Economy 2021
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture
SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Cultural and creative sectors
Agency Implementation: Ministry of Culture
Main Feature: The World Conference on Creative Economy (WCCE) has been established to discuss issues and challenges with global stakeholders so that the CCI can achieve their full potential. The first World Conference on Creative Economy (WCCE) was organized in Indonesia in 2018. The inaugural WCCE in 2018 mapped the creative economy ecosystem, including the regulatory, marketing, and financial aspects. It was a forum for policymakers and industry stakeholders to exchange ideas, resolve challenges, and identify opportunities within the creative economy. The next year, in 2019, the UN General Assembly declared that 2021 would be the International Year of Creative Economy for Sustainable Development. The proposal recognized the need to promote sustained and inclusive economic growth, foster innovation, and provide opportunities, benefits, and empowerment for all and respect for human rights. The WCCE baton has been passed from Indonesia to the United Arab Emirates, a country that has nurtured creativity and human expression over the past 50 years since its founding. The ambition has alwaysbeen to nourish the creative economy for a collective, cohesive, and thriving society. As the host of WCCE 2021, the UAE also launched a National Strategy for Cultural and Creative Industries in the same year. As part of the UAE’s mission to encourage global discourse on the creative economy, the country hosted the WCCE 2021 between 7 and 9 December at the Dubai Exhibition Centre at Expo 2020 Dubai with the theme ‘Inclusively Creative – Cultivating the Future’. WCCE 2021 took place alongside the global cultural phenomenon of the first World Expo being held in the Middle East, Africa, and South Asia region, with the participation of 192 nations. WCCE 2021 made a powerful statement on the importance of the CCI to humanity’s shared future. Positioned as the closing event of the United Nations’ International Year of Creative Economy for Sustainable Development, the conference united stakeholders in imagining a better future and laying the foundations to shape it. This was reinforced by a ministerial meeting held on the third day of WCCE 2021, where the primary stakeholders of the creative economy from 22 countries approved and adopted a 21-point UAE WCCE 2021 Agenda on the development of the global creative economy.
Results: WCCE 2021 in the UAE captured the innovative policymaking, entrepreneurial insight, and imaginative flair that connect global thinkers, policymakers, creative pioneers, and other changemakers. Through more than 65 sessions exploring 6 themes in depth and from diverse perspectives: 1- Future Sustainable Developing new thinking for responsible living 2-Technology Transformation Applying creativity to release the positive power of technology 3-Education Unleashed Liberating potential through cross-disciplinary learning 4- Reworking Work Connecting people, ideas, and places 5- Inclusivity and Diversity Harnessing creativity to help build inclusive, diverse societies 6- Elevating the Media and Communications Landscape Showcasing new ways to share and consume creative content WCCE 2021 inspired and equipped its delegates to make culture and creativity central forces in the drive towards a better tomorrow. WCCE 2021 in numbers: 3,600 Physical & virtual attendees 67 Sessions 39 Workshops 160 Local, regional & international speakers 19 Performances.
Recommandations: The next steps include the planning of practical ways in which to build on and deliver the ideas and inspiration generated during WCCE 2021. The WCCE needs to be part of visible action that includes government policymaking, the expansion of an effective regulatory base, and the streamlining of business activity in the CCI. As a guide on how to steer the CCI in a sustainable direction, WCCE 2021 provided actionable insights in two key areas – inclusivity and regeneration. Building on the themes, agendas, and case studies outlined at the conference, these action points provide the sector with an opportunity to promote sustainable growth, build international partnerships, and inspire both today’s creatives and those of the future.

Title EN: The year of Digital Culture 2020
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture
SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Digital environment
Agency Implementation: Ministry of Culture
Main Feature: The Ministry of Culture named the year 2020 the year of Digital Culture. The activities of this thematical year were organised by The National Library of Estonia, The National Heritage Board of Estonia, the Estonian Film Institute and Estonian Public Broadcasting. The goal of the year was for new generations to embrace our living culture and heritage, and for digital solutions to support this.  In addition to various discussions, events and competitions that took place all over Estonia, several initiatives were launched whose long-term impact extends far beyond the borders of a calendar year. Due to Covid-19 pandemic, the Year of Digital Culture could not have taken place at a better time, as the society was forced to test in a very short time many ways of creating and consuming digital culture. Lots of new ways to reach the audience were discovered and some of them are here to stay. E-book loan numbers grew 20 times, the planned introduction of audiobooks was given fresh impetus. Exhibitions, galleries, theatres and festivals had to discover innovative ways to share their art and performances online.
Results: The "Digital Culture Report" was published, which described the current state of digital culture. The "Digital Culture Manifesto" was published, which brings together 20 essays on digital culture.   Due to the special situation caused by the pandemic, 2020 became a year when digital culture was almost the only available cultural form in the whole country. Commercial audiobook offering was all but non-existent until 2020, but when the Spring lockdown set in, a list of 50 books by Estonian authors for all age groups was assembled, rendered into audiobooks by professional actors who had little to do during the closure. The audiobooks have since been launched by two commercial publishers, and two platforms — https://www.digiread.ee/ and https://mybook.me/ee/ - have been launched. The number of audiobooks on sale has doubled during the year and we are looking forward to strong long-term growth in the sector in the years ahead.   Although we have world-class museums, a digitally extended museum experience, and joint digital marketing has been missing. We commissioned a study on the business prospects of creating a joint digital Estonian museum card for visitors that provides live statistics, allows the creation of joint digital marketing campaigns, and adds new layers to the country’s digital museum experience. The card launched in 2023.   All festivals and event organisers were stranded with the COVID lockdown and had to quickly realign their plans for the year. We experimented with new forms of hybrid festivals, including the Intsikurmu music festival and the A-list Black Nights Film Festival or ‘PÖFF’, which duplicated their live content and international industry events online. The main takeaway from the experience is that hybrid festival formats are here to stay for a long time, and this may not be so bad after all.

Suite à cette prise de conscience par l’Artiste musicienne centrafricaine IDYLLE MAMBA, elle a mise en place avec les autres, une structure de « Promotion, de Création et de Développement Culturel », Duke’Ziki.  Selon les Promoteurs de cette organisation, le peuple centrafricain qui a longtemps souffert de stéréotypes et d’une image de violence a envie que le monde le découvre sous un autre angle, celui d'un peuple de paix, généreux, intelligent et avec une grande variété de richesses culturelles encore trop méconnues qui ne demandent qu’à s’ouvrir au Monde. La Centrafrique a énormément à donner. Dès lors, depuis maintenant plusieurs années, DUKE’ZIKI travaille pour sensibiliser la jeunesse africaine en général et centrafricaine en particulier, à mieux valoriser ses cultures et à prendre conscience de la richesse qu’elles constituent. C’est ainsi qu’elle a mis en place en 2017, un festival dénommé « Tî-Ï FESTIVAL » qui veut dire : NOTRE FESTIVAL, dédié à la promotion des musiques et des artistes centrafricains en particulier et du continent africain en général, tout en restant ouvert sur le monde pour que chaque année, le festival donne la possibilité aux musiciens centrafricains de rencontrer leurs homologues musiciens venus d’autres pays d’Afrique et d’ailleurs. Le succès de l’activité organisée pour la première édition au Cameroun en 2017  et  qui a reçu l’adhésion du public, a motivé les organisateurs à ramener le festival à la source même, c’est-à-dire en République Centrafricaine, précisement à Bangui,  pour en faire profiter les premiers concernés en 2022. Les objectifs du festival consistent à : - Promouvoir le patrimoine culturel centrafricain au-delà des frontières ; - Utiliser le patrimoine comme vecteur de création artistique et de paix ; - Créer une plateforme d’échanges entre les artistes et les professionnels de la culture ; - Renforcer la capacité des jeunes artistes au développement de leurs carrières. Le paquet des activités est composé de :	 	Les sessions BIRI NA LASSO qui permettent de réunir le temps d’une chanson les voix d’artistes d’hier et d’aujourd’hui, de Centrafrique et d’ailleurs, pour des duos, trio, uniques ; 	Ballets et contes : danses et contes agrémentées pendant 3 jours, avec les spectacles d’artistes de tous les horizons et de diverses tendances (Montégéné, rumba, danse traditionnelle, DJs, afro danse, etc.). Les contes et têrê ont encore une portée immense pour transmettre les récits et légendes. Certains s'appuient sur des instruments, quand d'autres comptent sur l'humour ou la sagesse...; 	Jeux et convivialité : passer un bon moment en famille et entre ami(e)s autour des jeux traditionnels à travers les jeux tels que le Kissoro ou le gbagba. Afin de rassembler la grande famille centrafricaine ; 	Formations : avec les partenaires comme Excellence Académia, Tî-ï Festival offre aux artistes amateurs des formations animées par des artistes expérimentés pour donner un lustre professionnel à leurs projets artistiques.
Results: Le festival est à sa troisième édition consécutive.  La quatrième édition est en préparation.

Title EN: Time for games – the Government’s gaming strategy 2024-2026
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture
SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Digital environment
Agency Implementation: Norwegian Ministry of Culture and Equality
Main Feature: The Norwegian Government presented a new gaming strategy in December 2023. The new strategy has the following objectives: -	A diverse and impactful selection of high-quality computer games -	Equality and diversity in Norwegian games and the Norwegian gaming industry -	Professionalism and growth in the Norwegian gaming industry -	An inclusive, safe and accessible gaming culture  Norwegian computer games and the Norwegian gaming industry are experiencing a positive development characterized by economic growth, an increased proportion of female developers, and the release of high-quality games. Simultaneously, there is significant untapped potential for the Norwegian games and gaming industry in terms of equality, commercial growth, and cultural impact within Norway.  One of the strategy’s main initiatives is to strengthen the Norwegian Film Institute’s (NFI) grant schemes for the development and launch of Norwegian computer games. Additionally, the strategy introduces a new automatic marketing scheme under the Norwegian Film Fund for finalizing computer games that have received development grants.  The strategy recognizes the strengths and potential of gaming culture as a leisure activity, an expression of art and culture, for e-sports, and as a tool for learning. However, it also highlights significant challenges related to hate speech, insults, and harassment within gaming culture. To address this, the strategy aims to enhance knowledge, expertise, activity, and content, as well as create safe and inclusive meeting places, both physical and digital.  A crucial measure is the establishment of a national competence center for gaming culture under NFI, in collaboration with Kulturtanken and the Norwegian Media Authority. The center’s mandate is to collect, strengthen, and share knowledge about computer games and gaming culture, primarily focusing on cultural expression, leisure activity, and e-sports.  To further strengthen content and activity in public spaces and events, the Government will introduce a trial scheme under the NFI. This scheme provides grants for the purchase of computer games and licenses to be used by children and young people in public spaces (such as libraries and leisure clubs). The grant can also support the organization of physical and digital public events. Overall, the scheme aims to promote computer games as both a cultural expression and a leisure activity, including e-sports.
Results: To soon to say, as the strategy’s effective period is starting from 2024

Title EN: Tours of the National Casts: “Bicentennial Tours” and “Culture Tour”
Goal: Achieve A Balanced Flow Of Cultural Goods And Services And Increase The Mobility Of Artists And Cultural Professionals
SDG: SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 10 - Reduce inequality within and among countries,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Flow of cultural goods and services
Agency Implementation: National Cast Directorate (Ministry of Culture)
Main Feature: The National Cast Directorate manages 6 national casts: the National Symphony Orchestra, the National Choir, the National Ballet, the National Folkloric Ballet, the Bicentennial National Youth Symphony Orchestra and the National Children's Choir. With the aim of forming audiences, diversifying the cultural offering in the country by promoting decentralization, appreciation and enhancement of the performing arts, as well as the sense of belonging to our cultural heritage and national identity, the Directorate of National Casts of the Ministry of Culture implemented “Bicentennial Tours” and “Culture Tour”.  The Bicentennial Tours are carried out within the framework of the celebrations for the Bicentennial of Peru (2021-2024), in coordination with the Special Bicentennial Project, which are staging of shows and free complementary activities carried out by the National Casts. Culture Tour, implemented in 2023, was born as an initiative from the Peruvian State to promote the active participation of citizens in various cultural and artistic expressions, recognizing the fundamental importance of the arts in comprehensive training and the strengthening of identities. Likewise, its focus is oriented towards the expansion of cultural offerings in those areas of the country with limited access, providing shows of high professional quality with the aim of reducing disparities in the appreciation of cultural rights.
Results: Within the framework of the “Bicentennial Tours” presentations were made in 11 regions of Peru, with an attendance of 18,400 people. Each of the shows flew a flag (EJE) of the Special Bicentennial Project. In that sense, the tour in the north of the country celebrated the cause of "Equal Opportunities", while the tour in the south focused on "Dialogue and Reconciliation". Finally, the tour to the east contemplated the cause of "Sustainability". Within the framework of Culture Tour, 17,600 citizens were able to benefit, allowing them to fully exercise their cultural rights, expanding and diversifying the cultural offer, in the regions of Ayacucho, Amazonas, San Martín, Piura, Iquitos and Puno.

Title EN: Trade Agreements for export of Cultural Goods
Goal: Achieve A Balanced Flow Of Cultural Goods And Services And Increase The Mobility Of Artists And Cultural Professionals
SDG: SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 10 - Reduce inequality within and among countries,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Treaties and agreements
Agency Implementation: Ministry of Commerce and Consumer Protection Mauritius Revenue Authority (MRA)
Main Feature: Mauritius actively promotes the export of cultural goods and services through various trade agreements. This allows duty-free access to a range of cultural products and digital services for e-commerce.  Agreements with COMESA, SADC, the European Union, the UK, China (Free Trade Agreement), and India (CECPA) provide preferential market access for these Mauritian exports.  Examples of cultural goods and services benefiting from this policy include: books, magazines, multimedia products, software, recordings, films, and videos. Additionally, digital services like telecommunication services, trade fair organization, translation, photography, and computer reservation systems are included.  The policy extends further to cover recreational, cultural, and sporting services, alongside services provided by artists, authors, and traditional medicine practitioners.  This focus on duty-free cultural exports fosters a vibrant Mauritian cultural industry and strengthens its presence in the global marketplace.
Results: Despite Mauritius' focus on duty-free cultural exports through various trade agreements, a key concern has emerged. Artists haven't fully capitalized on these preferential agreements to export their work. This underutilization limits the potential of the Mauritian cultural industry to reach a wider global audience. To address this gap, initiatives are needed to raise awareness among artists about these trade agreements and equip them with the knowledge and resources necessary to navigate the export process. By empowering artists to leverage these opportunities, Mauritius can further strengthen its cultural industry and its international presence.
Financial Ressources: Not available

Title EN: Traditional Skills Training Program

Area of Monitoring: National sustainable development policies and plans
Cultural Domain: Design,Performing Arts,Media Arts,Cinema and Audiovisual Arts,Music,Publishing,Visual Arts
Agency Implementation: Ministry of Culture and Fine Arts
Main Feature: The Royal Government of Cambodia laid out its Pentagonal Strategy for the next 25 years to achieve Cambodia Vision 2050, “the high-income economy country”. One of the strategies is to provide vocational training to 1.5 million less privilege youth from the poor or near poor families. Overall project is run by Ministry of Labor and Vocational Training. However, Ministry of Culture and Fine Arts was tasked to provide vocational training on the Traditional Skills from about 30, 000 to 60, 000 youth. The aim of the training is to first safeguarding the traditional skills passing down for generations, and to enrich cultural products while promoting cultural Industries in Cambodia. The training classes runs by Masters at their locations with technical supports from the staff of the MCFA.
Results: 185 students have been trained for the 6 different traditional skills including mask making, copper and silver sculpture, Krama weaving, pottery silk weaving, leather sculpture, stone sculpture and smith sculpture. The student from the poor and at-risk family received the monthly allowance approximately 70$ from the government.

Title EN: Training Program in Copyright and Related Rights
Goal: Promote Human Rights And Fundamental Freedoms
SDG: SDG 5 - Achieve gender equality and empower all women and girls,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels
Area of Monitoring: Artistic freedom
Cultural Domain: Design,Performing Arts,Media Arts,Cinema and Audiovisual Arts,Music,Publishing,Visual Arts
Agency Implementation: National Directorate of Copyright
Main Feature: The National Directorate of Copyright is committed to the dissemination of knowledge regarding Copyright and Related Rights. It offers training opportunities designed to provide a sound understanding of the general aspects of Copyright, collecting management organizations, and the registration of works and contracts.         These trainings are offered both virtually and in person, through conferences, self-managed virtual courses, and through open trainings that are broadcasted on YouTube.                  The virtual courses that are available on our virtual campus are: 1. Basic Copyright Course; 2. Entrepreneurship Course; 3. Observance Course; 4. Conciliation Course; 5. Software Course; 6. Audiovisual Course; 7. Editorial Course; 8. Musical Course.         Our portfolio of conferences has various topics all focused on Copyright and Related Rights, among which are: Basic aspects, contractual situations, collective management, civil aspects, criminal aspects, internet and software, university scope, and creative industries (Audiovisual, scenic works, literary works, works of art and music).
Results: From 2020 to 2023, 79,711 people have been trained. This figure includes both people who attend the training and those who enroll and complete the self-managed courses and obtain their respective certificates.
Recommandations: An effort should be made to increase the number of citizens benefiting from training activities on copyright issues, to achieve a greater presence in the regions in order to provide training and dissemination services on copyright and related rights throughout the country; as well as the permanent improvement in the provision of services of the Sub-Directorate of Training, Research, and Development for all citizens interested in making use of them.

Objectives - Skill Development: The primary goal was to develop writers who could leverage their skills to create impactful works. These works were aimed at addressing various societal issues across social, economic, and political domains. - Support for Emerging Writers: Special attention was given to young writers, helping them refine their abilities and advance their careers. Results: The initiative successfully produced writers with a solid understanding of literature. This effort facilitated the entry of young and novice writers into the profession.

Title EN: Traités et accords
Goal: Achieve A Balanced Flow Of Cultural Goods And Services And Increase The Mobility Of Artists And Cultural Professionals
SDG: SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 10 - Reduce inequality within and among countries,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Treaties and agreements
Cultural Domain: Design,Performing Arts,Media Arts,Cinema and Audiovisual Arts,Music,Publishing,Visual Arts
Agency Implementation: Ministère de la Culture et des Arts
Main Feature: Plusieurs accords de coopération, de mémorandums d’entente, protocoles d’accords, programmes d’échanges culturels et conventions ont été signés, entre 2020 et 2023, par les différentes institutions de l’Etat s’intéressant notamment au domaine de la culture toutes déclinaisons confondues (arts, arts visuels, livre, musique, théâtre, cinéma, etc.), s’inscrivant dans la stratégie insufflée par l’Etat algérien avec pour perspective la diversification des échanges culturels.  Cette stratégie a enregistré l’adhésion de plusieurs institutions étrangères de diverses nationalités notamment tunisienne, sahraouie, jordanienne, tanzanienne, italienne, française, portugaise, allemande, tchèque, ukrainienne, vénézuélienne et cubaine.   Cette politique a été à l’origine de la signature des accords de coopération, mémorandums d’entente, protocoles d’accords, programmes d’échanges culturels et conventions suivants :  Au titre de l’année 2020 :  •	Protocole d’accord pour le programme d’échange académique entre l’Institut National Supérieur de Musique et l’Académie des Arts de la Scène à Prague, République Tchèque, signé le 13 janvier 2020 ;  •	Mémorandum d’entente entre l’École Nationale de Conservation et de Restauration des Biens Culturels (ENCRBC) et la Faculté de Restauration de l’Université de Pardubice, République Tchèque, signé le 18 octobre 2020 à Alger. Au titre de l’année 2021 :  •	Mémorandum d’Entente entre la Bibliothèque Nationale Algérienne et la Bibliothèque Nationale d’Histoire Ukrainienne, signé le jeudi 1er avril 2021 à Alger ;  •	Convention entre le Centre National de Recherches Préhistoriques, Anthropologiques et Historiques et le Musée National de la République Tchèque, portant sur des recherches archéologiques sur le site de Tiddis, Algérie, signée le 03 mai 2021 ;  •	Reconduction de la Convention-Cadre de Coopération Scientifique et de Formation en Archéologie entre le Centre National de Recherche en Archéologie (CNRA) et l’Université des Etudes de Trento (Italie), signée le 06 novembre 2021 à Alger. Au titre de l’année 2022 •	Programme de mise en œuvre de l’accord de coopération dans le domaine de la culture entre l’Algérie et l’Italie pour les années 2022-2025, signé le 26 mai 2022 à Rome ;  •	Accord de coopération culturelle et scientifique algéro-allemand, signé le 13 juin 2022 à Alger.  Au titre de l’année 2023 •	Signature du programme d’échanges culturels algéro-cubain pour les années 2023-2027, le 15 février 2023 à la Havane lors de la 23ème session de la commission-mixte algéro-cubaine, tenue du 12 au 15 février 2023 ;  •	Accord de coopération culturelle entre l’Algérie et la RASD (République Arabe Sahraouie Démocratique) le 18 mars 2023 ; •	Programme d’échanges culturels algéro-portugais pour les années 2023-2025 signé le 24 mai 2023 à Lisbonne, Portugal ;  •	Programme de Coopération culturelle algéro-vénézuélien pour les années 2023-2025, signé le 08 juin 2023 à Caracas ;  •	Programme d’échanges culturels algéro-russe pour les années 2023-2025 signé à Moscou, le 15 juin 2023 ;  •	Mémorandum d’Entente sur la coopération dans le domaine de la culture et des arts, signé entre le Ministère de la Culture et des Arts Algérien et le Ministère de la Culture, des Arts et des Sports Tanzanien, le 1er août 2023 à Alger ;  •	Programme exécutif de coopération culturelle entre l’Algérie et la Jordanie pour les années 2023-2026, signé le 10 juillet 2023 à Amman ;  •	Accord de coopération dans le domaine de la culture entre l’Algérie et la Tunisie, signé le 04 octobre 2023 à Alger ;  •	Accord de coproduction cinématographique entre l’Algérie et la Turquie le 21 novembre 2023 à Alger ;  •	Mémorandum d’entente entre la Bibliothèque Nationale d’Algérie et la Bibliothèque Nationale de Turquie le 21 novembre 2023 à Alger.  Ce sont là autant de traités et accords initiés ou signés par l’Etat algérien dans la perspective d’un épanouissement culturel intercommunautaire.
Results: Cette mesure a permis la promotion d’un échange équilibré de biens et services culturels entre les nations avec élargissement du champ de prospection culturelle intercommunautaire, favorisant par la même l’accroissement de la mobilité des artistes et professionnels de la culture, ce qui est en soi l’esprit même des recommandations de l’UNESCO.
Recommandations: La signature d’autres traités et accords avec d’autres nations du monde serait de nature à enrichir cette entreprise et permettre ainsi l’extension de la diversité culturelle. Encourager la promotion d’un plus large échange de biens et services culturels entre les nations avec pour mot d’ordre une extension de la mobilité des artistes et professionnels de la culture, ainsi que les échanges culturels toutes disciplines confondues.

Title EN: Vers une nouvelle approche de l’espace culturel : Les hubs créatifs, les clubs numériques et créatifs
Goal: Integrate Culture In Sustainable Development Frameworks
SDG: SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: National sustainable development policies and plans
Agency Implementation: Le Ministère des affaires culturelles
Main Feature: L’amélioration de l’infrastructure culturelle et son adaptation aux besoins et aux attentes des nouvelles générations (les jeunes) notamment en termes d’innovation et de conception de l’espace est une composante fondamentale du programme des réformes adaptées par le Ministère des Affaires Culturelles. C’est ainsi que le hub créatif « Ennejma Ezzahra » a été mis en place en partenariat avec « Créative Tunisia » projet de soutien au secteur de l’artisanat financé par l’union européenne avec une contribution de l’agence italienne pour la coopération au développement et mis en œuvre par l’ONUDI (organisation des nations unies pour le développement industriel) et qui s’inscrit dans l’objectif du programme européen « Tounes wejhatouna » qui vise à soutenir la diversification de l’offre touristique par la création de synergies entre les secteurs des services touristiques, de l’artisanat des produits locaux et du patrimoine culturel. Ce Hub a été conçu pour combler une des composantes manquantes dans les différentes activités du centre des musiques arabe et méditerranéenne (CMAM) à savoir le design et l’artisanat. Il a pour objectif de devenir un pôle d’activité et de création réunissant les jeunes talents dans le domaine du design et de l’artisanat. Le hub créatif comprend trois parties : • Un lieu de création ou « working space » pour la conception créative et l’incubation des artistes et des artisans. • Un concept store : une boutique qui valorise les créations du Hub. • Une cafétéria : un lieu de détente mais aussi et surtout de discussion, de réseautage et de partage des idées innovantes. A travers cette conception, le Hub se positionne comme un vecteur de développement de l’entreprenariat dans les secteurs du design et de l’artisanat et a un certain nombre d’objectifs clés à réaliser : • Mettre en place un laboratoire d’expérimentation et de création pour les produits dérivés inspirés du patrimoine du palais Ennejma Ezzahra ainsi que les produits inspirés de la manufacture d’instruments de musique. • Réunir les acteurs des secteurs du design et de l’artisanat dans un espace de travail collaboratif permettant de renforcer les compétences créatives et l’expertise dans le domaine. • Renforcer les relations au sein de l’écosystème créatif (artisans, designers, étudiants, artistes, associations culturelles …) à travers une offre de services qui répond à leurs besoins. • Soutenir les porteurs de projets culturels et créatifs innovants à fort impact social et faciliter leur accès à l’écosystème de l’artisanat tunisien et aux différents équipements afin de leur assurer les meilleures conditions pour l’innovation. • Mettre en valeur les bâtiments du palais, son histoire et ses collections d’objet d’art. • Mettre en valeur le savoir-faire artisanal tunisien particulièrement en rapport avec le palais • Développer une programmation culturelle et artistique diversifiée. Ainsi la diversification des services et activités offerts par le Hub lui confère la qualité d’un véritable centre de formation technique, d’un laboratoire d’innovation et d’un espace d’exposition de produits culturels. Par ailleurs le MAC s’est engagé, à travers l’OTDAV (organisme tunisien pour la protection des droits d’auteurs et droits voisins), dans un programme national de mise en place de « clubs de créativité » pour la diffusion de la culture du respect des droits de la propriété littéraire et artistique auprès des jeunes et des enfants (au sein des institutions de l’action culturelles notamment les maisons de culture et les centres culturels avec un budget de 1,5 million de dinars. On note aussi entre 2022 et 2024: La création de 195 clubs pour la culture numérique ayant bénéficié à presque 2500 adhérant parmi les jeunes et les enfants au sein des maisons de culture ainsi que la création de 52 club de lecture numérique. La mise en place d’une compétition nationale pour encourager le développement de contenus numériques par les jeunes créateurs couplée d’un accompagnement à travers des sessions de formation et de renforcement des capacités dans le domaine de la création culturelle numérique.
Results: Le Hub créatif « Ennejma Ezzahra » a été inauguré officiellement le 29 Novembre 2022. Une étude a été menée par les deux partenaires (CMAM et Créative Tunisia), elle a permis de fixer les modalités d’implémentation et de pérennisation du Hub et de ses activités à travers l’analyse des aspects suivants : - La pertinence des services offerts par le hub - Sa capacité à devenir financièrement autonome - L’analyse des formes juridiques les plus appropriées pour ce type de structures - La réflexion sur un modèle de gouvernance basé sur la collaboration publique privée. L’étude a inclus également un benchmark international qui a dressé les meilleures pratiques issues de hubs Créatifs à l’international et a permis ainsi de présenter des recommandations stratégiques et opérationnelles pour la pérennisation du Hub. A l’issue de cette étude, deux appels publics ont été élaborés et lancés par le CMAM avec le concours de créative Tunisia en vue d’identifier une association pour gérer le Hub en tant que centre de service. Une association a été retenue et est en cours de contractualisation et ce, dans le but d’atteindre les objectifs culturels du CMAM et créative Tunisia qui consistent à développer l’entreprenariat à travers le soutien et l’accompagnement des artisans, designers et jeunes créateurs porteurs de projets innovants en leur offrant des services à la carte à des prix accessibles.
Financial Ressources: Concernant le hub créatif « ennejma ezzahra » :  Appui financier de l’ONUDI (organisation des nations unies pour le développement industriel) : 292.000 DT Pour le projet de mise en place de « clubs créatifs » par l’OTDAV : Un budget de 1,5 million de dinars.
