Area of Monitoring: Cultural and creative sectors
Agency Implementation: General Directorate of Cultural Industries and Arts (Ministry of Culture)
Main Feature: The Public Management Network in Cultural Industries and Arts (hereinafter, Network) is a territorial articulation mechanism between the General Directorate of Cultural Industries and Arts (DGIA) of the Ministry of Culture, regional and municipal governments, approved by Ministerial Resolution N °179-2021-DM/MC, July 14, 2021. The Network is aligned with the National Culture Policy, with guideline 6.4, which establishes that the Ministry of Culture must “Implement sectoral, intersectoral and intergovernmental coordination mechanisms, for the development of cultural policies throughout the national territory.” In this sense, the Network seeks to promote the development of public policies based on coordination, cooperation and mutual support between entities at different levels of government. To do this, act around the following 3 guidelines: 1. Articulation: is aimed at generating coordination and cooperation mechanisms between public entities at the three levels of government, as well as the private sector for the benefit of cultural governance. 2. Training and technical assistance: aims to expand the capacities of the servers and officials of regional and local governments, as well as the Decentralized Directorates of Culture for the implementation of public policies. 3. Development of local cultural policies: aimed at promoting management and information instruments for the implementation of public policies and services in favor of the arts and cultural industries. All regional governments and municipal governments (provincial and local) at the national level, which formally adhere to the Network, can be part of the Network. To this end, the Regional Governor or Mayor, as the case may be, sends an official letter addressed to the General Directorate of Cultural Industries and Arts, where they express their willingness to be part of it, designated representatives by institution. With each change in municipal management the commitment must be renewed. The designed articulation mechanisms are:  -	National Meetings: they are articulation spaces where all members of the Network participate at the national level. -	Capacity-building workshops: their objective is to provide practical tools in cultural management and public management. -	Meetings of the Executive Committee: to discuss and agree on the actions to be carried out within the framework of the Network, prioritizing the needs expressed by its members.
Results: In municipal management (2019-2022) the main results were: • 136 regional and local governments actively participated in the NETWORK. • 216 active participating public servants and officials. • 21 National Meetings held • 11 training workshops undertaken by the DGI, with a total of 218 beneficiaries. • Coordination with public institutions was achieved in order to strengthen management in cultural management and public management, as well as with the purpose of serving the agents of the sector in the face of the health emergency. Regarding the new municipal management (its mandate begins in 2023), to date, 163 subnational governments (regional and local) have formally joined the Network; a total of 33 requests have been received for the preparation of their culture plans; and work has been done to identify the needs of its members through the design of a diagnostic survey that each government must complete for its integration.
Recommandations: Among the main conclusions found are: - Work with a characterization of the 1800 subnational governments in order to prioritize and particularize the actions to be carried out based on the identified needs. - Promote the management and dissemination of information and knowledge. - Promote responsible citizen participation in decision-making at the territorial level. - Achieve greater impact that strengthens the commitment and political will of subnational governments that allow the sustainability of the initiatives undertaken.

Results: D’après le rapport d’évaluation annuelle élaboré par la DGAC, le total des subventions accordées au titre de l’année 2023 s’élève à 1478.500 millions de dinars ayant bénéficié à 94 associations actives dans pratiquement la quasi-totalité des disciplines artistiques (théâtre et arts scéniques, arts visuels, édition et livre, musique et danse, métiers du patrimoine, arts numériques.) et ciblant différentes catégories sociales (femmes rurales, artisans, jeunes créateurs, enfants..) contre un total de 2066.550  millions de dinars profitant à 106 associations en 2022. Cette mesure a, entre autres, contribué à réaliser un certain nombre de résultats : •	Un maillage associatif opérant dans les secteurs culturels et artistiques plus solide et plus développé, •	Une offre culturelle plus diversifiée, •	Un meilleur accès à des contenus culturels à la fois ancrés dans la spécificité et l’identité locale et ouverts sur l’environnement régional et international (notamment par le biais de connexions/ réseautages et partenariats), •	Une scène culturelle plus inclusive, •	Des projets culturels plus adaptés aux besoins des populations cibles.
Recommandations: Comme tout mécanisme de financement public, ce mécanisme d’aide publique aux associations œuvrant dans le secteur culturel et artistique fait l’objet d’une évaluation ex post dans le cadre des rapports annuels élaborés par les services compétents du MAC ( la DGAC). Les principales conclusions sont : •	La pérennisation et la durabilité de certaines manifestations portées par des OSC sont en grande partie tributaires des subventions accordées par le MAC. •	La mise en place et l’application de critères d’éligibilité est fortement recommandée afin de rationaliser les aides publiques et les orienter vers des actions qui cadrent avec les objectifs et les priorités stratégiques dans le secteur culturel qui s’inscrivent pleinement dans les principes et les lignes directrices de la convention 2005. •	La nécessité d’engager une réflexion sur les mécanismes appropriés pour mener vers une autonomisation financière progressive des associations dont la viabilité dépend largement des subventions publiques.

Title EN: Universal access and service policy for information and communication technologies
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture
SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Digital environment
Agency Implementation: Communications Regulatory Authority of Namibia (CRAN)
Main Feature: The CRAN Universal Access and Service Policy aims to provide all Namibians with equitable access to ICT services, especially in underserved and rural areas. It focuses on expanding ICT infrastructure, promoting digital inclusion, and enhancing access to internet, broadcasting, and telecommunications. The policy emphasizes capacity-building, digital literacy, and collaboration with stakeholders to drive investments. CRAN oversees the policy's implementation, ensuring compliance and safeguarding consumer rights, while sustainable funding mechanisms support ongoing universal service initiatives to bridge the digital divide in Namibia.
Results: The Ministry of Information and Communication Technology (MICT) has undertaken significant steps to review and update Namibia’s ICT policies, addressing the shortcomings of outdated frameworks and aligning them with current trends in the sector. This review process aims to create a more responsive and robust National ICT Policy that mainstreams all ICT sub-sectors, including telecommunications, broadcasting, and postal services. Here are the key results achieved so far:  Stakeholder Engagement and Input Collection: MICT invited ICT stakeholders to review and provide comments on the proposed ICT Policy. This inclusive approach ensures that the views and expertise of various players in the sector are considered, creating a policy that reflects the needs and aspirations of the industry.  Development of a Review Matrix Tool: A review matrix tool was developed and distributed to stakeholders to assess the extent of policy implementation. This tool aids in systematically evaluating which policy objectives have been achieved, highlighting gaps and areas needing improvement.  Identification of Policy Shortcomings: The review has identified critical gaps in the existing ICT-related policies, particularly the lack of Action Implementation Plans and monitoring and evaluation mechanisms. Recognizing these issues sets the groundwork for developing targeted, actionable policies in the future.  Alignment with Emerging Trends and Drivers: The review process aims to update the policies to address modern megatrends, such as digital transformation, cybersecurity, data protection, and the evolving needs of the ICT sector, ensuring that Namibia’s ICT framework remains relevant and forward-looking.  Cabinet Approval for Policy Review: Cabinet approval of the policy review highlights government support and commitment to overhauling ICT policies. This approval enables MICT to proceed with updating policies that cater to all ICT-enabled sectors.  Progress Towards a Consolidated National ICT Policy: The process has set the stage for finalizing a consolidated National ICT Policy that integrates all ICT sub-sectors. The new policy is expected to address current challenges, outline clear implementation targets, and provide a coherent framework for the growth and regulation of Namibia’s ICT sector.  Foundation for Future Policy and Action Plans: The ongoing review will aid in capturing new policy pillars, which are crucial for setting Namibia’s ICT sector on a path of sustainable development. The expected outcome is a comprehensive policy that includes implementation action plans, facilitating more effective monitoring and evaluation.

Title EN: Updating social protection schemes for freelance artists and freelance cultural professionals
Goal: Promote Human Rights And Fundamental Freedoms
SDG: SDG 5 - Achieve gender equality and empower all women and girls,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels
Area of Monitoring: Artistic freedom
Cultural Domain: Design,Performing Arts,Media Arts,Cinema and Audiovisual Arts,Music,Publishing,Visual Arts
Agency Implementation: Ministry of Culture
Main Feature: Freelance artists and other freelance cultural professionals, if their creative contribution is excellent (they have excellent references) and their personal income does not exceed a certain threshold of the income census, can obtain a five-year right to have their social security contributions covered by the state budget. They can reapply for this right after five years. There is no limit to the number of renewals, but the right becomes permanent (until the artist is entitled to an old-age pension) when they reach the age of 55 and have used the right for a total of 20 years. In 2023, the Government of the Republic of Slovenia amended the regulation that governs this area in order to facilitate eligibility by 1) raising the income limit (maximum income required for eligibility) and 2) lowering the criteria related to the scope of work (e.g. number of exhibitions, films, literary works), by 50% for those artists whose assessment period also covers the period from March 12, 2020 to May 31, 2022. (This is a period in which protective measures against COVID were in force and the exercise of cultural activities was restricted.) Freelance artists and other freelance cultural professionals can apply once a year for compensation for extended periods of sick leave. If they are on sick leave for more than 31 days, they can apply (retroactively) for compensation for the first 30 days of sick leave. (Under Slovenian law, the state covers the costs of sick leave exceeding 30 days; the first 30 days are the responsibility of the employer or, in the case of self-employed, the person themselves). In December 2022, the government increased the daily sickness allowance for self-employed artists and cultural professionals from 25 to 37 euros for 2023. Retired artists and other cultural professionals who have made a significant contribution to Slovenian culture, but whose pension is low or does not correspond to their contribution to Slovenian culture, can receive a so-called "recognition payment from the Republic". The Republic's recognition payment corresponds to the difference between a certain amount and the amount of the applicant's pension paid in the Republic of Slovenia and in other countries. This amount is adjusted annually to the development of pensions in Slovenia. In 2023, the Republic's recognition payment corresponded to the difference between the amount of the claimant's regular pension and 1,018.14 euros. In cases of exceptional contributions and highest artistic achievements at the national level, an individual can receive a "special pension". This is a retirement pension for special merits in the field of culture, which may not, however, exceed the amount of the highest pension for a full pension period. The artist receives the difference between their regular pension and the amount of the special pension.
Results: The number of people who are entitled to have their social security contributions paid from the state budget is increasing. From 2020 to 2023, an average of around 2,000 people per year had this entitlement. Compensation for extended sick leave (beyond 31 days), for the first 30 days of sick leave, averaged 66 per year from 2020 to 2023. In the years 2020 to 2023, 62 new recognition payments were granted by the Republic, making a total of 264 payments. In the period from 2020 to 2023, 10 special pensions were granted. There are around 100 beneficiaries in total.
Recommandations: The amendment of the Act on the Implementation of the Public Interest in Culture (ZUJIK) and the decree regulating the status and rights of freelance artists and other freelance cultural professionals is currently underway. The amendments to the two legal frameworks will further enhance the conditions for freelance artists and cultural professionals. The introduction of the so-called career dynamic is intended to elevate the socio-economic status of the freelancers. Furthermore, modifications to the legal framework for the Republic’s recognition payment and special pensions in the arts are being considered to improve the prospects of obtaining these rights.

Title EN: Upskilling Cultural Workers (since 2023)
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture
SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Cultural and creative sectors
Agency Implementation: Martynas Mažvydas National Library of Lithuania, National Museum of Lithuania, Lithuanian National Culture Centre, Office of the Chief Archivist of Lithuania.
Main Feature: In 2023, "Upskilling Cultural Workers" activity under the Progress Measure No. 08-001-04-01-01 "Increasing Access to High Artistic Value, Diverse and Inclusive Cultural Content" was launched. The key objective of the activity – to ensure systematic, targeted and long-lasting development of competences of cultural sector staff, enhancing their motivation and directly contributing to qualitative changes of cultural services provided.  With the ambitious target of developing qualifications (general and/or professional competences) of at least 65% of public, municipal and private cultural workers by 2030, the Ministry of Culture started coordinating the implementation of a systematic skills development model for cultural workers in 2023. Under this model, the general competences are handled by a single competence centre – Martynas Mažvydas National Library of Lithuania. This institution is responsible for the development of general and managerial competences of cultural sector staff, as well as for the development of professional competences of library staff.   Pursuant to this model, the training of professional competences in other cultural fields is handled by competence development centres, depending on the sector: for museums (and the Centre for Contemporary Art) by the National Museum of Lithuania, for cultural centres by the Lithuanian National Culture Centre, and for state archives – by the Office of the Chief Archivist of Lithuania.  The specific nature of the functions performed by the staff of professional performing arts organizations require a different way of organising the development of professional competences. The professional development of the professional competences of these staff members is organised by means of a competitive tendering procedure.   It should be noted that the Law on Cultural Policy Framework adopted by the Seimas of the Republic of Lithuania in 2024 contains provisions related to the continuous and systematic development and acquisition of competences, abilities and practical skills of cultural workers in order to ensure the provision of high quality cultural services to the Lithuanian public.
Results: In 2023, 4 projects were implemented by Martynas Mažvydas National Library of Lithuania, the National Museum of Lithuania, the Office of the Chief Archivist of Lithuania and the Lithuanian National Centre for Culture. All these competence development centres organized and coordinated the development programmes for staff in the respective cultural field.  In 2023, 93 training courses of general, managerial and professional competences were carried out, more than 2310 unique participants were trained, more than 120 participants took part in traineeships, and over 700 trainees were trained. In order to develop the competences of cultural sector staff in a systematic way, Professional Competence Inventories have been developed in the areas of archives, libraries, museums and cultural centres.  In order to efficiently organise and coordinate the training process, a learning management platform and a learning environment – the Library of Competences – has been implemented. The virtual learning environment will be used by more than 300 cultural institutions and more than 10 000 users in the first phase (2023 – 2025).   The National Museum of Lithuania has launched MARTA Muziejinių kompetencijų ugdymo programa „Marta“ -  https://lnm.lt/muziejiniu-kompetenciju-ugdymo-programa-marta/, a centralised museum competency development programme for national and state museum professionals.  Given the complexity of establishing a single and comprehensive process for the professional development of cultural sector staff, the new qualification model is being implemented gradually. In the first phase, the staff of state cultural institutions and municipal cultural centres are invited to take part in the qualification development of cultural workers. In the second phase, the qualification development for cultural workers will be extended to include employees of municipal cultural institutions (except cultural centres) and state cultural institutions whose ownership rights and obligations are exercised by other ministries or state institutions.   From 2026 onwards, the model will apply to all cultural workers, both public and private, as well as to those working individually in the cultural sector.  By 2030, at least 15,000 unique cultural workers (65% of all cultural workers) in the cultural sector (state, municipal institutions, NGOs and the private cultural sector) are expected to develop their qualifications (general and/or professional competences).  The quality of cultural services directly depends on the skills and motivation of cultural workers. Better trained and motivated staff can create more interesting and inclusive activities, events and programmes that meet the needs of different groups in society. Moreover, competent staff enable better and more effectively foster and disseminate information about cultural heritage, museum exhibits and other cultural assets. More qualified staff can design and implement innovative projects that enrich cultural life and promote social inclusion, strengthening the role of culture in society.
Financial Ressources: In 2023, USD 1,1 million (EUR 1 million) was allocated for the Action "Improving Qualification of Cultural Sector Workers".   A total of approx. USD 12,2 million (EUR 11 million) is earmarked for the qualification of cultural employees by 2030.

Title EN: Production of interactive plays and capacity building trainings in drama in education and theatre arts, Amman Contemporary Dance Festival
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture
SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Cultural and creative sectors
Agency Implementation: CSO NAME: The National Centre for Culture and Arts EMAIL: Lina.attel@ncca.org.jo    PHONE: +962-777460146
Main Feature: The National Centre for Culture and Arts (NCCA) implements various measures to promote cultural diversity through its capacity-building trainings programs in theatre and drama and produces interactive play that focus on socio economic issues that are toured by NCCA professional National Interactive Theatre Troupe and the touring of interactive plays in collaboration with the Ministry of Education, Ministry of Culture and different CBOs covering all governorates in Jordan. These initiatives focus on strengthening the resilience of youth, raising awareness of social issues, and fostering cultural understanding among different nationalities residing in Jordan. Interactive Play Productions: NCCA produces interactive plays that feature Syrian refugees, highlighting their stories and experiences. These productions aim to raise awareness of the value of social cohesion and coexistence amid the challenges posed by the influx of Syrian refugees. The plays address cultural diversity, tolerance, acceptance, and the plight of women. Developed through extensive research and community engagement, these plays resonate with local and international audiences. The interactive nature of these plays engages the audience directly, fostering deeper understanding and empathy. These plays are performed in various settings, including refugee camps and community centers, reaching a wide audience and promoting social awareness and cohesion.  Capacity Building Trainings. NCCA implements comprehensive capacity-building workshops designed to enhance the resilience of Syrian youth and raise awareness about the negative impacts of extremism. The training involves theatre-based techniques, psychosocial awareness training, and Maslow's hierarchy of needs. Syrian and Jordanian mentors are trained to deliver these workshops in Zaatari and Azraq refugee camps. The workshops focus on building the resilience of youth against violent extremism and recruitment, engaging them in activities that promote civic engagement and leadership. By empowering the youth and providing them with the skills to address grievances constructively, these trainings foster a sense of belonging and community cohesion. This initiative not only empowers the youth but also reaches a broad audience, including community leaders and decision-makers, fostering a community-wide understanding of the issues at hand. Creative writing workshops. NCCA facilitates creative writing workshops that involve directors and actors from different nationalities residing in Jordan. These workshops aim to foster cross-cultural understanding and collaboration by bringing together diverse perspectives. Participants, comprising vulnerable male and female youth, engage in creative writing workshops that allow them to express and reflect on their personal stories, challenges, solutions, and aspirations. The stories and monologues created by the participants are edited, published, and distributed nationwide. Additionally, these stories are adapted into theatre plays, which are then performed by a group of young artists who have received training in Drama, Music and vocals and toured the plays in different cities across Jordan. This initiative not only promotes creativity and literary skills but also helps participants articulate their experiences and aspirations, fostering empathy and mutual respect among different cultural groups. Theatre Based Techniques training:  This specialized training program is based on the Theatre Based Techniques for Peer Education Manual produced by UNFPA in 2005. The manual was translated into Arabic by NCCA and developed to reflect the Arab culture and traditions in addition to creating an advanced level training manual in collaboration with the founder of the project Dr. Alexandar Sasha Bodiroza and the original authors: Dr. Cydelle Berlin and Mr. Ken Hornbeck. The program acquired accreditation from the International Theatre Institute (ITI) – UNESCO. TBT is intended for program managers, youth educators, teachers, university students, activists and artists who are interested in adding a theatre component to their awareness and advocacy activities, with a focus on facilitation and scene creation to impact the target audience and beneficiaries. TBT is the only training program in the region that utilizes theatre skills and participatory drama methodology to enable youth peer educators to deliver effective dynamic messages through performing arts towards appropriate change of attitudes and behavior and raise awareness on issues related to Reproductive Health and Rights (RHR), Human Rights, Gender Based Violence (GBV), Prevention of Violent Extremism (PVE), Peace Building, Cultural Diversity and Civic Engagement. The trainees acquire skills and practical knowledge related to facilitation, audience participation and creation of interactive theatre pieces based on improvisation and how to respond to the audience questions as actors remaining in their characters. NCCA conducted numerous regional TBT training courses for participants from: Algeria, Egypt, Sudan, Morocco, Yemen, Oman, Palestine, Libya, Djibouti, Somalia, Tunis, Syria, Saudi Arabia, Lebanon, Iraq, Kurdistan and Bulgaria. Drama in Education:  The National Center for Culture and Arts, in partnership with the Ministry of Education, implemented the "Classroom Creativity" project. This project aims to provide teachers from grades 1 to 12 with theater-based techniques, drama in education, facilitation methods, and interactive theater over a period of three years. The goal is to empower public school teachers in targeted areas to conduct creative activities to enhance their personal skills and provide them with rich educational experiences beyond the curriculum, ensuring comprehensive development for students. This extensive training program enables students to achieve the 4 Cs of the 21st Century Skills: Critical Thinking and Problem Solving, Communication, Collaboration, Creativity and Innovation. More than 300,000 students benefit annually from the implementation of these activities by teachers in the classroom nationwide. Amman Contemporary Dance Festival (ACDF) ACDF established in 2009 as part of Masahat Dance Network; a regional network comprising of Maqamat ‎Dance ‎Theatre in Lebanon and Sareyyet Ramallah in Palestine ACDF is an annual festival organized by the National Centre for Culture and Arts (NCCA). ACDF invites cutting edge performances by renowned international choreographers and companies to perform in Jordan with a wide range of movement styles, techniques, and influences, allowing audiences to explore the boundaries of physicality, emotion, and storytelling. ACDF mission:  Promote dance as a tool for communication and address contemporary social issues. Develop public awareness of the value and aesthetics of contemporary dance in Jordan. Provide the Jordanian audience with an opportunity to experience creative themes and concepts. Overall Impact: Through these initiatives, NCCA facilitates cultural exchange and collaboration, empowering youth and educators through creative expression. The programs raise social awareness about the challenges faced by marginalized groups, promoting social cohesion and proactive engagement. Recognized both nationally and internationally, NCCA demonstrate the power of performing arts in driving social change. Approximately 100,000 beneficiaries are reached annually, showcasing the extensive impact of NCCA’s initiatives in promoting cultural diversity and social development. This comprehensive approach emphasizes NCCA’s commitment to fostering a culturally diverse, resilient, and cohesive society through the performing arts, education, and creative expression.
Results: The Training and Creative Plays Productions Programs by NCCA have yielded significant results: Enhanced Skills and Knowledge: Teachers from diverse backgrounds have gained valuable skills in drama education, enhancing their teaching methodologies. Participants have developed a deeper understanding of how to address social issues through performing arts, creating a more inclusive and educational environment. Build a network with dance companies with the aim of collaborating in future projects to allow young Jordanian artists to expand their experience in contemporary dance techniques. Provide workshops for aspiring Jordanian dancers to interact and exchange experiences with renowned choreographers and dancers.  Capacity Building Trainings:  The capacity-building workshops have significantly enhanced the skills and resilience of Syrian youth and their mentors. Over 200 Syrian and Jordanian mentors have been trained in theatre-based techniques, psychosocial awareness, and basic human needs, equipping them to support youth in Zaatari and Azraq refugee camps. These mentors have conducted over 100 workshops, directly engaging more than 2,000 Syrian youth. The training has led to noticeable improvements in participants' leadership skills, emotional resilience, and civic engagement.

Title EN: Program – Digital platforms – Continuous online broadcast
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture
SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Media diversity
Agency Implementation: NAME: Coalition for the Diversity of Cultural Expressions (CDCE) EMAIL: coalition@CDCE-cdce.org TELEPHONE: (+1) 514-277-2666
Main Feature: The Program – Digital platforms – Continuous online broadcast aims to monitor, popularize, consult and advocate on the subject. Introduction [November 2020 – April 2023] Bill C-11 (successor to Bill C-10), led to the adoption by the Parliament of Canada of the Online Streaming Act (LC 2023, c. 8) . The latter received royal assent on April 27, 2023. The CDCE actively participated in all stages of the study of Bill C-11 by the Parliament of Canada . She also participated in the process relating to Bill C-10 (which was succeeded by C-11), that was unable to pass the third reading stage in the Senate of Canada before the prorogation of Parliament. The text of the Online Streaming Act (LC 2023, c. 8) amends the Broadcasting Act of 1991 to update Canadian broadcasting policy. The changes made are intended in particular to protect, and support, programs, films and music that meet the needs and highlight the diversity of cultural expressions, for all Canadians. Any company carrying out broadcasting activities in Canada will now have to comply with regulations providing for mandatory financial contributions to the development of Canadian content as well as obligations regarding the promotion of this content. The new Act also places emphasis on the following groups, communities and programming: •	Canadians who represent diversity and among them: -	Those who come from black or other racialized communities By  -	their ethnocultural background; -	their socio-economic status; -	their abilities and disabilities; -	their sexual orientation; -	their gender identity or expression; -	their age; -	the official language minority communities in Canada. •	Programming -	in indigenous languages that reflects indigenous cultures; -	accessible to people with disabilities and free of obstacles; -	of original programs in one or other of Canada's official languages.  The Online Streaming Act strengthens, as a corollary, the regulatory and supervisory power of the Canadian Radio-television and Telecommunications Commission ( CRTC ) relating to the Canadian broadcasting system. The contribution of the CDCE and its members to the process as well as to its positive results in terms of the protection and promotion of cultural and creative industries in the context of continuous distribution on digital platforms is multiple. The initiatives listed below were designed and implemented including in partnership with other sectors of civil society and the business and academic community. Their objectives included: -	strengthening knowledge and advocacy capacities; -	to deepen reflection and consultation; -	as well as the achievement of consensus – within the cultural community and between cultural stakeholders and those responsible for Canadian legislative and policy decision-making processes.  List of activities carried out under this program (non-exhaustive): •	[March 2020] Brief from the CDCE for the revision of the Broadcasting Act (bill C-10). | W  •	[June 2021] Answers to the most frequently asked questions about Bill C-10 to help counter the high level of misinformation related to this bill in the media and on social networks. | W  •	[ November 2021] CDCE round table on the supervision and responsibilities of the CRTC in the new legislation – allowing discussions between six experts and 22 representatives of CDCE members.  •	[November 2021] CDCE round table on content enhancement, discoverability, and transparency of platforms – bringing together 10 experts and 19 representatives of CDCE members.   •	[March 2022] Deployment of tools and launch of a campaign of the CDCE in favor of Bill C-11. | W  •	[March – April 2022] Holding regional meetings to discuss Bill C-11 in partnership with members and allies of the CDCE: Saskatchewan (March 2022) Manitoba and British Columbia (April 2022).  •	[February 2023] Bill C-11 , Streaming Act online , after the study by the Senate: analysis of the CDCE | PDF  •	[July 2023] Comments from the CDCE as part of the Government of Canada's consultation on the Proposed Order to Implement the Streaming Online Broadcasting Act. | W  •	[2022-2023] CDCE campaign to send letters to MPs and senators of the Canadian Parliament organized in the fall and winter to illustrate support for the bill and to counter minority, but noisy, discourse spreading misinformation about him.
Results: The CDCE's actions under this program led to the publication of several articles in Canadian newspapers and enabled a large number of people – both from the cultural and creative industries and from the general public – to mobilize in favor of the Bill C-11 on online streaming, despite its complexity.  The CDCE applauded the adoption of Bill C-11 and was pleased to note that the requests it brought to the attention of parliamentarians during the process were accepted – and in particular with regard to the need to act to finance and promote Canadian shows, films and music on all platforms carrying out broadcasting activities in the territory.  The actions of the CDCE, and the attention paid by parliamentarians to its recommendations, led to the formulation of provisions strengthening Canadian legislation on online streaming, in favor of the diversity of Canadian cultural expressions in the digital environment.  The Online Continuous Broadcasting Act contributes to Canada's positioning among the growing number of countries with laws aimed at regulating digital platforms in order to protect and promote the diversity of their cultural expressions.

Title EN: Program Related to the Mobility of Artists and Cultural and Art Professionals

Main Feature: The Ministry of Education, Science, Culture and Sport of the Republic of Armenia realizes co-financing program related to the mobility of artists, cultural and art professionals. The goal of this cultural policy measure is systematic support for the promotion of international cultural cooperation and armenian culture and art abroad; for exchange and networking through the participation of artists and professionals from Armenia in international festivals, competitions, biennales, exhibitions, events, seminars, workshops, conferences, master-classes, as well as through study and residency programs, and the similar, which are related to all fields of culture and the arts. The program is intended for bilateral and multilateral cultural cooperation and cover the costs of travel (ticket) and accommodation only for artists and professionals in the field of arts, cinema and culture. Priority is given to individuals who are recipients of recognitions and/or awards in the fields of culture and the arts, members of international bodies and professional networks, art associations, and participants in prominent international cultural events. The professional commission formed by the Ministry of Education, Science, Culture and Sport decides to approve or reject the applicant։
Results: The number of applications is increasing every year, which proves the effectiveness and demand of the program. In 2020-2023, 350 applications were submitted for the movement of artists and specialists in the field of culture and art, and 240 received co-financing support, the pass rate of which was 68,5%.
Financial Ressources: For the period 2020-2023, a total of approximately 27 763 USD (111,052,000 AMD) was allocated for the mobility of artists and cultural and art professionals, as follows: in 2020-2022 - 112,565 USD (45 026 000 AMD); in 2023 - 82,532 USD (33,013,000 AMD).
Recommandations: The reports of participants and department’s report are the basis for an annual evaluation of the given policy/measure and the assessment of the call’s success. In the period 2020- 2023, there was a lot of interest in the program, therefore funding for the project has been increased. Projects supported within the call included co-financing artists’ mobility in a large number of countries. The majority of the applicants were associations of music artists, painters, performing artists, as well as cultural and art societies, and cultural institutions.

Cultural Domain: Design,Performing Arts,Media Arts,Cinema and Audiovisual Arts,Music,Publishing,Visual Arts

Main Feature: Since March 2020, the Portuguese Government has tried to approve measures to support families, workers, the economy and the culture sector, which were being progressively deepened and adapted, aiming to mitigate the effects of the health crisis caused by COVID-19. This program aimed to reinforce support mechanisms for the culture sector, taking into account the emerging economic and social effects of the epidemiological situation, in order to contribute to ensuring that the cultural and artistic fabric can not only face short-term commitments, but also contribute to the maintenance and relaunch of the respective activities during and after the pandemic outbreak. The Guarantee Culture Program was a universal (non-competitive), financially non-refundable support. This program supports artistic creation or programming activities, carried out in physical or digital formats and contexts. The artistic areas covered by the Guarantee Culture Program were performing arts, visual arts, disciplinary crossover, books, cinema and museology. The Program aimed at - Individual and collective artistic entities that pursue activities of a non-commercial nature (including individual entrepreneurs under a simplified regime); - Business sector (micro, small and medium-sized companies, including sole traders with organized accounting) in the cultural and artistic sector. The allocation for the Guarantee Culture Program – without prejudice to funding increases that took place until the end of 2021 – was 45,56 M USD, distributed across the two subprograms mentioned above. The Guarantee Culture Program was only applicable to entities domiciled or headquartered in Mainland Portugal.
Results: Attending to the demand after this program was launched it was financially reinforced. For instance, the initial 13,02 M USD financial line for artistic entities that pursue activities of a non-commercial nature was almost doubled to 23,65 M USD using European financing.  In February 2023 the number of entities who executed their projects and were fully supported already closed in the universe of 1095 who benefited from this support program allocated to the GEPAC subprogram, aimed “at singular and collective artistic entities that pursue activities of a non-commercial nature”, increases to 931. In 2023, there were 101 projects that have not yet submitted the report, a necessary condition for payment of the second tranche (50% of the support). Of the allocation allocated to this subprogram, of 21.8 million euros, 20 million have already been executed, which corresponds to 92 percent of the total (21,69 M of 23,65 M USD).

The program is aimed at artists of all disciplines and from all over the country. They gain access to the residency by registering to the calls for research and/or creation projects. Title EN: Presidential Economic Stimulation Programme (PESPus d
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture
SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Cultural and creative sectors
Cultural Domain: Design,Performing Arts,Media Arts,Cinema and Audiovisual Arts,Music,Publishing,Visual Arts
Agency Implementation: Department of Sport, Arts and Culture and related entities such as National Film and Video Foundation (NFVF), National Arts Council (NAC), and Performing Arts Centre of the Free State (PACOFS).
Main Feature: Presidential Economic Stimulation Programme (PESP) is a special government initiative geared towards employment creation for artists, creatives, heritage sector workers and cultural workers following the effects of the COVID- 19 pandemic in the sector. In October 2020, South Africa launched the Presidential Employment Stimulus (PES) in response to the pernicious impact of the coronavirus pandemic on employment. The PES aimed to protect jobs and livelihoods while the labour market recovers, while creating new jobs and supporting people to create work of their own.   The PES provided support to the arts and culture sector, through a stimulus to create employment managed by the National Arts Council (NAC) and the National Film and Video Foundation (NFVF) on behalf of the Department of Sport, Arts and Culture (DSAC). This is known as the Presidential Employment Stimulus Programme (PESP) which is a special government initiative geared towards employment creation for artists, creatives, heritage sector workers and cultural workers following the effects of the COVID- 19 pandemic in the sector. PESP has had multiple phases, including PESP 1 and PESP 2 which were launched to mitigate the economic impacts of the COVID-19 pandemic by creating employment opportunities and supporting various sectors. More than 30 000 people in the arts and culture sector have benefitted directly from the PESP, which has provided opportunities to continue to work, as well as for new creative work in a sector badly affected by lockdown. PESP is based on the following main objectives: •	Job Creation and Retention: It aims to create new jobs and retain existing ones, providing economic stability and growth. •	Economic Stimulus: By injecting funds into various sectors, it stimulates economic activity and supports businesses. •	Skills Development: Participants often receive training and skill development, enhancing their employability. •	Community Development: Projects funded by PESP can lead to improved infrastructure and services in communities. •	Support for Vulnerable Groups: It often targets vulnerable populations, providing them with opportunities and support. •	Job Creation and Retention: It aims to create new jobs and retain existing ones, providing economic stability and growth. •	Economic Stimulus: By injecting funds into various sectors, it stimulates economic activity and supports businesses. •	Skills Development: Participants often receive training and skill development, enhancing their employability. •	Community Development: Projects funded by PESP can lead to improved infrastructure and services in communities. •	Support for Vulnerable Groups: It often targets vulnerable populations, providing them with opportunities and support.
Results: The Presidential Stimulation Programme has supported more than 100 000 Jobs and livelihood, provided opportunities through National Art Council (NAC), National Film and Video Foundation (NFVF) and the Performing Arts Center of the Free State (PACOFS). The programme supported our societies through diverse contributions-film production, striking murals, language preservation, craft markets, museum exhibition, etc.  The National Heritage Council (NHC) and NAC supported a series of projects aimed at preserving, documenting, and celebrating indigenous identity and culture while simultaneously creating jobs and livelihood opportunities. The following were projects supported by PESP: •	Kalahari Arts and Heritage Festival: It was held in the Northern Cape’s Philandersbron, to celebrate the Khoi and San communities’ rich heritage. Supported by the PESP, the festival extended beyond entertainment. Set against the mystical backdrop of the Kalahari Desert, and aimed to reshape narratives around these indigenous communities, often misunderstood in mainstream arts. It featured an ambitious showcase of 20 short films by first-time filmmakers from these historically marginalised groups. With activities including workshops and panel discussions, vibrant performances and exhibitions, the event fostered a sense of unity and cultural exchange among participants from South Africa, Namibia, and Botswana. By supporting such initiatives, the PESP created livelihood opportunities and invested in the preservation and empowerment of a vital cultural heritage, ensuring the Khoi and San communities’ stories continue to be told and celebrated. •	Umkhumbane Music Heritage project: This project was Funded by the PESP through the NAC, Kunene set out to reignite a love for Irabi Jazz – a blend of 1950s Afro-American and local South African sound. The first part of the project included a music business masterclass for young musicians, covering music development and the business aspects of the music industry. This revival culminated in a concert where the original Umkhumbane Jazz Ensemble played alongside the young musicians they mentored. In total, the project created 77 jobs and livelihood opportunities for artists, technicians, and vendors.  The NFVF was one of the vehicles used to disburse the PESP funds. NFVF joined the management team as continue to implement the rollout of PESP3 and plan PESP4 and managed to provide guidance and leadership for the successful implementation of PESP3 and the targets envisioned by the Department of Sport, Arts and Culture (DSAC), were exceeded. The main highlights for PESP3 included notable: •	An increase in the number of applications received, which can be attributed to a robust marketing and public awareness strategy that included roadshows across all provinces and partnerships with media houses. •	NFVF also managed to successfully implement the 3-Tier Funding Model.  •	The overall targeted number of jobs (a target of 9 000 jobs) that PESP3 projects were supposed to achieve was exceeded. To date, a total of 16 155 jobs have been created across all three streams. This exceeds the 8 101 jobs created in PESP1, even though PESP1 had four streams.

Title EN: Presse écrite et électronique
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture
SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Media diversity
Agency Implementation: Ministère de la Communication
Main Feature: La loi n° 23-19 relative à la presse écrite et à la presse électronique a été promulguée le 2 décembre 2023, la présente loi « a pour objet de fixer les principes régissant l’activité de la presse écrite, de la presse électronique et leur libre exercice ». La loi concernant la presse écrite et électronique encourage le libre exercice des activités de la presse. Elle stipule « que l’activité de la presse écrite et de la presse électronique est librement exercée dans le cadre du respect des principes prévus par les dispositions de la Constitution, de la loi organique relative à l’information, de la présente loi ainsi que la législation et la réglementation en vigueur ». La présente loi veille à mettre de l’ordre dans le secteur de l’information et organise l’exercice de l’activité de presse en fixant les modalités de l’édition, distribution, colportage et importation des publications périodiques (de l’article 5 à l’article 25).  La présente loi organise et encadre l’activité de la presse électronique, notamment l’hébergement et la mise en ligne du site, l’actualisation du contenu, la cessation injustifiée de la presse électronique et la responsabilité du contenu du site. La loi fixe également les prérogatives de l’autorité de régulation de la presse écrite et de la presse électronique qui veille au respect des dispositions de la loi et au libre exercice de l’activité de presse écrite et/ou électronique.
Results: Cette loi consolide la liberté d’expression à travers la dépénalisation du délit de presse et l’exclusion de peines privatives de liberté contre le journaliste, ce qui constitue une grande avancée et un acquis majeur en matière de protection des journalistes. Ce mécanisme juridique inclusif et intégré émane d’une volonté politique en faveur d'une presse libre, indépendante et pluraliste, et ce, par la consécration effective de la liberté du journaliste et la consolidation de ses capacités professionnelles.

Title EN: Printemps de la ruralité
Goal: Integrate Culture In Sustainable Development Frameworks
SDG: SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: National sustainable development policies and plans
Cultural Domain: Design,Performing Arts,Media Arts,Cinema and Audiovisual Arts,Music,Publishing,Visual Arts
Agency Implementation: Ministère de la Culture
Main Feature: L’offre culturelle dans les zones rurales, où un tiers des Français habitent, est bien moins dense que pour le reste de la population. Ainsi, le Ministère de la Culture recueille durant deux mois mes idées et les propositions des acteurs concernés et de l’ensemble des citoyens sur la vie culturelle dans les territoires ruraux. A l’issue de ces consultations, se tiendront des  Assises nationales de la culture en milieu rurale afin de palier au difficile accès aux ressources culturelles.
Results: Afin d’être au plus près des réalités du terrain, une consultation nationale en ligne a été menée pendant deux mois auprès des habitants, élus, associations et acteurs culturels. En parallèle, les directions régionales des Affaires culturelles (DRAC/DAC) ont organisé au sein des territoires des rencontres, des débats et des ateliers autour de la place de la culture en ruralité. Cette grande concertation a permis de souligner les dispositifs déjà existants dans les territoires ruraux et de mettre en valeur de nombreuses propositions. Les ressources constituées tout au long, en libre consultation, ont servi d’appui à l’élaboration des 23 mesures du Plan culture et ruralité.

Title EN: PRODUCTION AUDIOVISUELLE A DES FINS EDUCATIVES
Goal: Integrate Culture In Sustainable Development Frameworks
SDG: SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: National sustainable development policies and plans
Agency Implementation: ONG Inter Palm Lumière (IPL)
Main Feature: L’ONG IPL incarne pleinement son engagement en faveur de l'éducation et les droits de l'enfant à travers le pouvoir du cinéma. Pour concrétiser cette noble mission, l’ONG IPL se spécialise dans la création de films de fiction et documentaires visant à sensibiliser et à éduquer le public sur ces thématiques cruciales.                                                                                                                                                                                                              Au cœur de cette initiative réside une équipe de production constituée de techniciens et d’acteurs formés au sein des incubateurs de l'ONG IPL. Chaque étape importante de la chaîne de production, depuis l'élaboration du scénario passant par la réalisation, techniciens et acteurs, jusqu’à la post-production, bénéficie de la contribution des membres issus des centres d’incubation IPL. Ainsi, le processus créatif est enrichi par leur expertise et ils gagnent en expérience. Il est important de souligner que tous ceux qui sont formés dans les clubs IPL auront la primauté de travailler sur les plateaux de tournage de l’ONG IPL, dès lors que celle-ci est engagée dans des films. Aussi est-il que l’ONG IPL n’empêche pas ses membres à exercer sur autre plateau de tournage que le sien. C’est ainsi, de plateau de tournage, à plateau de tournage, expériences accumulés, ils seront comme ces professionnels sélectionnés avec rigueur et dotés de compétences nécessaires qui donnent vie aux messages essentiels des grandes maisons de production. Les œuvres cinématographiques produites par l’ONG IPL peuvent aller à des festivals ou autres programmes de diffusion si besoin est fait. L’ONG IPL ayant son propre festival, ne fera pas passer ses films en compétition, mais les fera passer en information. Toujours fidèle à son principe d’objectif Principal, c’est-à-dire : faire la promotion de l’éducation et les droits de l’enfant à travers le cinéma, le théâtre et le sport, l’ONG IPL a réalisé, en 2022, deux courts-métrages sur ces thèmes. Les courts-métrages “Maltraitance" et ‘‘Drogue en milieu scolaire’’ illustrent bien cet engagement qui met en lumière ces deux thèmes. En effet, pour le premier court-métrage, ‘‘Maltraitance’’, qui a juste sa première séquence tournée qui ne dure que 3,44 Mn, met en scène une jeune enfant brillante dans ses études dans son milieu de vie au village et même de toute la sous-région, sera retirée pendant l’année scolaire de l’école par sa tante, une citadine, veuve ayant hérité de tous les biens de son mari défunt, sous prétexte qu’on ne peut pas aller à l’école au village et réussir dans ses études. Pour mieux impressionner les parents du village, la tante fait une promesse disant que la petite sera inscrite dans une école d’excellence dans la ville. Ce film a pour but d’alerter les parents du village qui accepte l’exode de leur progéniture sans savoir les conséquences. Pour le deuxième court-métrage, ‘‘Drogue en milieu scolaire’’ ce film met en scène 4 jeunes élèves d’un collège de la place, face à leur destin. Ce sont : Franck, Koniba, Grégoire et Kalifa.  Franck, Koniba, les deux premiers, challengent sur leurs études. Ils achètent des anales pour étudier. Ils font des parie entre eux sur leurs moyennes de classe pour mieux se mettre au travail. En somme, ils mettent en question leurs études.  Tandis que les deux autres, Grégoire et Kalifa, cherchent des astuces pour faire passer la drogue dans les écoles. Ils ont leur ravitailleur, Abou, loin des écoles et caché dans une maison inachevée.  Ils arrivent même à entrainer les enseignants dans leurs sales besognes.   Ce film exhorte les jeunes scolarisés à s’éloigner des addictions que sont le tabagisme, l’alcool, la drogue, les parie aux jeux et même les discussions inutiles autour de la vie des célébrités. L’ONG IPL prévoit d’organiser des caravanes de sensibilisation avec ses deux films dans les établissements scolaires et les sociaux culturels des communes.
Results: Grâce à la mise en place de cette cellule, l’ONG IPL mène aisément ses activités de sensibilisation et d’éducation du public sur les thématiques cruciales inscrites dans ses objectifs à travers ses propres créations. L’ONG IPL a pu former des jeunes à travers les centres d’incubations cinématographiques, les formations cinématographiques personnalisées et les accompagnements de jeunes talents. Ainsi, pour les productions au sein de l’ONG IPL, ces jeunes ont la primauté d’être retenus afin de mettre leur compétence en valeur. Aussi est-il que, tous ces jeunes qui étaient destinés à la rue, à la délinquance juvénile, ou au chômage, sont désormais nantis de compétences. Ils expriment leurs talents en menant leurs activités avec passion.

Title EN: Producing handicrafts from driftwood, recycled wood, and sustainable plantation wood, contributing to the restoration and preservation of the Kim Bong traditional carpentry and fostering sustainable and green tourism in Hoi An.
Goal: Integrate Culture In Sustainable Development Frameworks
SDG: SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: National sustainable development policies and plans
Agency Implementation: Làng Củi Lũ (Driftwood Village)
Main Feature: Cui Lu Village, founded by Mr. Le Ngoc Thuan, a local amateur artist and owner of a renowned chain of restaurants, villas, and homestays in Hoi An. Cui Lu was established with the aim of providing livelihoods for artisans in the craft village, ensuring stable monthly incomes for various laborers (carvers, guardians, janitors, shop assistants, young apprentices, interns, etc.), raising awareness, and fostering the development of artistic creativity among artisans to meet market demands for decorative carving products with practical applications in daily life. Additionally, Cui Lu opens carving courses for both domestic and international tourists to experience and practice carving to create their unique artworks, thus contributing to creating sustainable and green tourism products in Hoi An.
Results: Cui Lu Village, which was founded in 2020 with only a few skilled carvers who lost their jobs due to the COVID-19 pandemic, now has over 20 staff members engaged in various tasks, from carving to painting and finishing sculptures, as well as taking care of visitors. Cui Lu is a workshop area specializing in wood carving and the production of artistic wooden products, gathering dozens of skilled craftsmen and sculptors from Quang Nam province to create beautiful, artistic, and unique works from driftwood (wood washed down from upstream Thu Bon River to Hoi An City), recycled wood, and other sustainable natural materials. After over three years of operation, Cui Lu has produced thousands of products with diverse designs from sustainable plantation wood. Notably, Cui Lu has displayed over 300 artistic works with unique cultural meanings crafted from driftwood in a special exhibition area for visitors. Cui Lu regularly organizes workshops on wood carving and decorating carved wood products, using sustainable forest timber. These workshops offer tourists the opportunity to create handicraft artworks, deepen their understanding of local culture, and raise awareness about sustainable use of recycled materials and environmental preservation.  Cui Lu also organizes monthly interactive art fairs as a gathering event to connect craftsmen, creators, and the community to share art experiences through interactive activities, workshops, and community building. Visitors to the fairs have the opportunity to experience various entertainment and learning activities, such as participating in crafting handmade artworks, interacting with artists and craftsmen, exploring and enjoying unique local dishes, shopping for environmentally friendly products, and reinforcing community pride and cohesion. Cui Lu Village is also a place to support, inspire, and nurture new craftsmen and young local creators to develop their skills and talents by providing free counseling programs for Vietnamese youth interested in learning about wood carving art and aspiring to continue the local tradition of carpentry and wood carving. Cui Lu Village, the wood carving workshop and  Hoi An Interactive Art Fair are gradually receiving community attention and creating meaningful, memorable, and unique experiences. After years of construction and development, Cui Lu Village has become an attractive destination for domestic and international tourists visiting Hoi An, the UNESCO-recognized World Heritage Site, and the favourite choice for cultural exchange tours from many countries around the world. In addition, the handicraft products created by skilled local craftsmen have gained the affection of many tourists and become meaningful souvenirs, and preferred decorative items in modern living spaces. Cui Lu has participated in some domestic and international cultural activities, thereby contributing to spreading messages, and raising awareness about the use of recycled materials, environmental protection, and the preservation of local culture. The founder of Cui Lu was honored to be one of 100 craftsmen participating in a meeting with the President at the "Viet Nam Craft Village Conservation and Development Festival 2023." Representatives from Cui Lu also continuously participated in the "National Startup Forum - National Tourism Industry Congress," and local exhibitions with the message of protecting the marine environment. Additionally, Cui Lu participated in various international cultural exchange events, such as the Viet Nam - Poland Colors Convergence in 2023, the Hoi An Cultural Festival in Paris in 2023, the "Seminar Project on Asean Green Cultural Entrepreneurship" in Thailand in 2023, etc. Cui Lu village also has artworks to be displayed at Hoi An Garden, Wernigerode City (Sachsen-Anhalt state, Germany) in 2023 to commemorate the 10th anniversary of the establishment of friendly relations between Hoi An and Wernigerode City (2013 - 2023), etc. Aligning with the motivation and aspirations of Hoi An as a member of UNESCO's Creative Cities Network, Cui Lu Village continues to aim at conserving and promoting the value of the traditional Kim Bong carpentry village in the locality, promoting exchanges, and learning experiences with creative cities in the UNESCO Creative Cities Network, thereby creating more new values to improve the quality of life for artisans, while contributing to building Hoi An as a cultural, ecological, tourism, creative, green, and sustainable city.

Title EN: PRODUCTION ET DIFFUSION DES STATISTIQUES DE ROUTINES CULTURELLES (DPSEC)
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture
SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Cultural and creative sectors
Cultural Domain: Design,Performing Arts,Media Arts,Cinema and Audiovisual Arts,Music,Publishing,Visual Arts
Agency Implementation: Ministère en charge de la Culture / Direction de la Planification, des Statistiques et de l’Economie Culturelle (DPSEC)
Main Feature: L’information statistique se présente comme une matière première essentielle à la vie de l’administration culturelle. Elle permet d’avoir la situation actuelle du secteur sur une base objective en faisant un état des lieux et se projeter sur des résultats tangibles, ce qui évite de naviguer à vue. L’information statistique permet également d’améliorer la communication institutionnelle en étayant les propos par des chiffres. Elle permet en outre d’assurer la comparabilité de nos performances avec les autres pays de l’UEMOA. C’est pourquoi, ayant pris conscience de la situation et du dynamisme culturel, « la mise en place du système informatisé de collecte et de gestion des données statistiques culturelles » est le projet du Ministère de la Culture et de la Francophonie pour une gestion rationnelle et optimale de toutes les informations relatives à la culture. Il s’agit, d’être en adéquation avec les autres services de l’Etat ayant opté pour la numérisation des données et rendre performant nos services afin qu’ils soient efficaces comme ceux des pays développés.  Par ailleurs la mise en œuvre de ce projet viendra résoudre les manquements suivants qui sont entre autres :  -l’absence d’une cellule dédiée à la production de statistiques ; -la méthode dépassée de collecte de données à travers l’administration de questionnaire ; -la méconnaissance de l’importance des statistiques de certains administrateurs ; -l’absence de formation des producteurs de données statistiques et  -l’insuffisance de matériel informatique pour le traitement de données et le stockage.  -le renseignement du Système Informatique Régional pour la Culture (SIRC) mis en place par l’UEMOA Par ailleurs, l’objectif clé de ce projet qui est la production des Annuaires des Statistiques Culturelles permettra plus aisément d’avoir des données sur la dimension économique et industrielle de la culture et des arts notamment : (i) la contribution de la culture à la formation de la richesse nationale (PIB) ; (ii) l’évolution des emplois culturels ; (iii) l’évolution du nombre d’entreprises culturelles.
Results: - La production de trois (03) annuaires statistiques : 2018, 2020 et 2023 - La Mise en place du système informatisé de collecte et de Gestion de Données Statistiques Culturelles (SIG-DSC) (en cours) - L’étude impact économique sur la Culture (IUCD) en 2014 - Participation à l’atelier régional pour l’harmonisation des statistiques culturelles de l’UEMOA (SIRC) depuis 2016.
Financial Ressources: Le Budget de l’Etat alloué à la Direction chargé de la planification est de 106 209,15 USD en 2024
Recommandations: Les résultats cette étude d'impact économique de la culture dans le Plan National de Développement a contribué à l'augmentation du budget du Ministère en charge de la culture. L’atelier régional pour l’harmonisation des statistiques culturelles de l’UEMOA a permis a d'harmoniser les données statistiques des pays de  l'espace UEMOA et de créer une plateforme  ou chaque Etat  publie ses données statistiques   En raison de la pertinence de son modèle, la Côte d'Ivoire  a été invitée à un partage d'expérience et à une assistance technique avec le Togo et le Benin dans l'élaboration de leur politique et leur système d'évaluation statistiques.

Main Feature: !kauru contemporary art project began in 2012 as a vehicle for educating the public about the role of art in society. it was conceptualised as a platform for cross-border/cross-regional engagement and discourse between south african creatives and their counterparts across the african continent. the project is focused on dialogue around social and economic cohesion, transformation and access within the creative sectors in south africa but also across the continent to strengthen engagement and build sustained relationships with creatives on the african continent.
Results: The results expected through the implementation of the measure? •	to showcase the finest of african contemporary art. •	sensitize and mobilize south african/african audiences and media to appreciate african visual art. •	promote inter africa/diaspora cultural exchange in a direct and meaningful way. •	create a network and visibility for artists, artist promoters, academia, and cultural institutions. •	skills transfer, empower young and up coming local artists through skills development workshops and community outreach programs. •	!kauru not only recognizes the visual arts as a means to celebrate heritage, but it strives to position the visual arts as an important contributor to the economy of the region and stimulate ongoing investment in this field.

2016 the former cnca (current, mincap), through the national subdirectorate of indigenous peoples, launched the "program for the promotion and dissemination of the arts and cultures of indigenous peoples". this instrument is developed from a territorial approach, in compliance with ilo convention no. 169, and responds to the programmatic commitments reached in the prior consultation developed by the cnca between 2014 and 2015, a process that, in addition to incorporating the opinion of indigenous peoples around the new cultural institutionality, it welcomed their views on the promotion of indigenous arts and cultures. as a result, today indigenous organizations throughout the country and the afro-descendant community of arica, and parinacota are executing the "revitalization plans", biannual instances that were agreed upon in the different dialogue processes between indigenous organizations, and the regional directorates. the "program for the promotion and dissemination of the arts and cultures of indigenous peoples" has a biannual execution and is made up of three components: -	indigenous cultural participation: it translates into the definition of the themes that will be addressed in the cultural revitalization plans with territorial relevance, of the cultures and the arts of the native peoples. this definition results from the dialogues developed in a first stage between the former cnca and indigenous organizations in the country and the afro-descendant tribal people of arica and parinacota. -	promotion of indigenous arts and cultures: at this stage, a plan will be executed per region, through which three biannual instances of cultural revitalization with a territorial approach will be implemented. this execution is carried out as defined by each region and may be carried out in collaboration with institutions validated by local indigenous organizations or through the body defined jointly. -	diffusion and cultural exchange: through this component, actions, experiences and artistic and cultural expressions of native peoples that are carried out in component 2 and others that are relevant to the peoples in their territories are supported and implemented.
Results: As of december 2019, the program has been implemented by the national sub-directorate of indigenous peoples in the 15 regions of the country, in addition to the rapa nui territory. in the first cycle of the program, in the years 2016-2017, 96 linguistic revitalization actions were carried out with indigenous organizations. in the second cycle 2018-2020, which is underway, 138 actions have been carried out in 94 communes of the country.

Main Feature: The development of digital culture has been the object of attention by the state since the 1990s, with various actions, which are strengthened from the year 2000 onwards with the 2004-2006 digital agenda and the 2007-2012 digital strategy, where the former cnca reports actions for the fulfillment of measures committed by the different public institutions. in 2017, the "onda media platform" was also presented, with free access and with a catalog exclusively dedicated to national audiovisual creation, which seeks to bring cinema, television and other local content closer to the public. for its part, among the main initiatives of former dibam (directorate of libraries, archives and museums, now the national cultural heritage service) on digital culture are: chilean memory, digital resource center that makes available original documents and content related to chilean cultural identity; memories of the 20th century, program of social participation and patrimonial rescue; chile for children, digital blog of cultural, heritage and historical content for boys and girls; digital public library, it is an initiative developed by the national system of public libraries of chile of the former dibam that consists of a free digital book loan service; chilean plastic artists digital platform, site dependent on the digital area of the national museum of fine arts. by 2020, on the occasion of the pandemic caused by covid-19 and the key role that digital content has come to play, the ministry of cultures, arts and heritage has proceeded to create a new culture unit digital.
Results: Within the framework of strengthening actions that contribute to public policy for digital culture, favoring the promotion of creation and facilitating access to cultural goods by citizens, in june 2017 the launch of the "platform ondamedia" of audiovisual content, which through the use of new technologies provides access to citizen content, live broadcasts of artistic activities and a wide catalog of national tapes, short films and cultural programming. this experimental digital project arises in response to the profound transformations are having in society in relation to the  information and communication technologies, offering a platform of freely available cultural content, specially designed for current digital devices and in which users play a role. protagonist, becoming creators of their own content, reaffirming the creative power of citizens. as of 2017, the platform had 120 feature films, which include the most relevant and awarded films on the national scene; 95 short fiction, animation, documentary and experimental titles; 750 academic candidates with degrees in science, arts and humanities; and 176 audiovisual content created by artists, intellectuals and citizens. so far there are 45 thousand registered users. in 2018, the fourth "seminar on digital culture: city, creativity and digital arts" was held. the meeting took as its thematic axis the unesco creative cities network, an initiative that was born to contribute to the development and enhancement of the urban and cultural impact of different disciplines of culture and the arts at the territorial and city levels. another recent milestone in the matter of digital culture, developed in october 2020, has been the realization of the "ii international seminar on public development and digital culture". in this instance reflected on the participation of the public in a scenario of pandemic, confinement and post-confinement; the new challenges that organizations and cultural spaces will face to develop and involve the public; the impact of digital culture, big data and artificial intelligence on the expansion, training and loyalty of the public; and, the learning of organizations and cultural spaces during the confinement by covid-19.
