Main Feature: Over the years, the private and public sector in the uae have launched several cultural awards to encourage and promote artists and creators and to provide support in the form of exposure and financial reward. some of the awards that are currently active in the uae are the following:   *	arab social media award: the award, launched in 2014 by dubai executive office, highlights the most important initiatives of social media in the arab world and honors individuals and institutions that have creatively used social media channels to increase awareness of issues of concern to the arab community and have had a positive impact on the development and prosperity of the community. there are 20 categories for the award, including categories for arts, media, youth, tolerance, and technology. in 2018, 31 social media influencers and organizations received the award.  *	arab journalism award (aja): launched in 1999, is the region's most prestigious award recognizing journalistic excellence. the award's main goal is to reward talent, inspire, and stimulate creativity and enhance the constructive role of the press in serving the community. it rewards talent under 13 categories including investigative reporting; young talent in journalism; photojournalism; economic journalism; outstanding cartoon artwork; sports journalism; best press interview; best columnist; media personality of the year; political journalism; cultural journalism; smart journalism and humanitarian journalism. the award's main goal is to reward talent, inspire, and stimulate creativity in journalism. the award has had 19 editions, has received 68,300 submissions from 43 countries and has been awarded 275 journalists   *	happiness film award: the award is organized by the ministry of community development and aims to support the development of positive and purposeful content by providing an innovative platform to engage community members. people are invited to provide creative content that promotes positive values and habits, and innovatively cements concepts of happiness and quality of life in society. the competition consists of short 1 minute film submissions. the award gives participants the freedom to choose the most appropriate film format to convey their ideas such as drama, documentary, advertisement, educational material, theatrical sketch, or any of the other filming styles they prefer.   *	sheikh zayed book award: the sheikh zayed book award is organized by the department of culture and tourism in abu dhabi and is presented annually to outstanding writers, intellectuals and publishers, as well as young talent whose writing and translation enriches the arab intellectual, cultural, literary and social life. each prize consists of a gold medal bearing the sheikh zayed book award logo, a certificate of merit, and a cash reward, comprising a total prize value of seven million uae dirhams (us $1.9m) annually. the cultural personality of the year receives a prize of one million uae dirhams, while the winners of the other categories receive 750,000 uae dirhams each.   *	international prize for arabic fiction (ipaf): ipaf is supported by the department of culture and tourism in abu dhabi and was launched in april 2007. it is the most prestigious and important literary prize in the arab world, and if often referred to as the "arabic booker prize". its aim is to reward excellence in contemporary arabic creative writing and to encourage the readership of high-quality arabic literature internationally through the translation and publication of winning and shortlisted novels in other major languages. one of the main aims of the ipaf is to encourage the translation of arabic literature into other languages. the shortlisted authors each receive $10,000 us. the winning author goes on to receive a further $50,000 us, with a commitment that ipaf will meet the cost of translation of the winning novel into english. novels associated with ipaf can look forward to increased readership and sales both within the arab world and internationally through translation.  *	little writer competition: the competition is organized by the department of culture and tourism in abu dhabi. it is a series of competitions for children called 'little writer' which focuses on the arabic language as an intellectual and cultural component that support social values. the winning stories are included in a volume called "little writer in the big book" which is distributed to all schools' libraries and maktaba's branches across the abu dhabi. *	sheikh mohammed bin rashid patrons of the arts awards: the awards is organized by dubai culture and arts authority honor and recognize individuals, business, organizations, and government entities that have provided financial and in-kind support for the promotion of artistic activity in dubai. contributions are recognized in the visual arts, film, literature and performing arts. in 2019, this award was replaced by the sheikh mohammed bin rashid al maktoum arts awards.  *	mansoor bin mohammed award for short films: the community development authority in dubai delivers this award, and its objective is to encourage creativity and innovation among young people. the award aims to (1) raise community awareness of human rights issues, (2) encourage youth to employ creative skills to portray human rights and thus to develop their creative artistic capacities and (3) to promote the values of tolerance, cultural diversity, and to combat discrimination and extremism. to date 30 films have won this award.  *	jameel prize for contemporary artists and designers: organized by the victoria and albert museum, london, in partnership with art jameel, the vision of the jameel prize is to recognize the influence of islamic tradition on contemporary culture and celebrate contemporary practitioners inspired by islamic design and visual culture. the artists and designers short-listed for the jameel prize are invited to show examples of their artwork in a special exhibition, which debuts either at the v&a or another notable international museum, before travelling to other venues around the world. there have been five editions since the prize began in 2009.  *	sharjah prize for arab culture - unesco: funded by the department of culture in sharjah, the award was established under the directives of his highness, ruler of sharjah, in cooperation with unesco, when sharjah was named capital of arab culture in 1998. the award is given in recognition of the efforts of cultural figures, or institutions that contribute to the intellectual and artistic promotion of arab culture and its appreciation and understanding around the world.   *	sharjah award for theatre creativity: the department of culture in sharjah organizes the award, which was established in 2007. the award encourages and honors arab playwrights who have shown their dedication to theatre over the years and created effective platforms for arab theatre.   *	sharjah award for arab creativity: the annual sharjah award for arab creativity is brought by the department of culture in sharjah and was established in 1996. it supports talented writers in the uae and across the arab world. categories of the award are: short stories, poetry, playwriting, children's literature, and essays.   *	sharjah international prize for cultural heritage: a merit award established in 2016 and granted annually by the sharjah institute for heritage to individuals, groups, or projects in honor of the efforts made in the field of heritage preservation and has completed its third cycle. the award works to appreciate the various efforts exerted at the local, arab and international levels in the field of heritage preservation and documentation of successful experiences and practices in order to ensure its continuity. the award aims to spread the spirit of theoretical and practical scientific competition between those interested and working in the field of scientific and field research in preserving and codifying heritage. the award also honors human treasures and emphasizes the effective role of narrators carrying oral literary masterpieces, traditional knowledge and craft skills in preserving the cultural heritage of man and ensuring its permanence.   *	sharjah international book fair awards: the annual sharjah international book fair awards which is brough by the sharjah book authority , promotes the production of good quality publications and recognize and appreciate distinguished individuals and organizations for their contribution to the social, cultural and literary fields. the breakdown of the awards include: turjuman award, award for an emirati book, award for the best international book, award for the best arabic novel, publisher recognition award, and cultural personality of the year award.  *	sharjah award for arab photo: the sharjah award for arab photo honors arab photographers who contribute and enrich the arab photography scene globally, with valuable photographs that reflect the arab world.   *	sultan bin ali al owais cultural award: the sultan bin ali al owais cultural award is granted to a number of outstanding arab innovators and intellectuals in recognition of their significant contributions in the following categories of (1) poetry (2) short story, novel and drama (3) literary studies and criticism (4) humanities and future studies.   *	fujairah international monodrama festival awards: the fujairah international monodrama festival awards was established in 2003 and brought by fujairah authority for culture and media. it aims at encouraging the presence of monodrama in the arabic theatre in general, and in emirati theatre in particular, and supporting the young and talented artists who can contribute to its growth.   *	fujairah photography award: brought by the fujairah culture and media authority and established in 2007, the award was launched with the aim of upgrading the intellectual, cultural and aesthetic scene in fujairah in particular, and the uae in general. it also aims at presenting creative works that reflect reality, spark the creative interest and curiosity of the public and enrich the world of visual arts.   *	ibda'a media student awards: the aim of the ibda'a awards is to discover, showcase and develop the talents of media students attending university or college. the etisalat award for arabic children's literature: the award was launched in 2009 and aims to provide an incentive for publishers, authors, and illustrators to publish arabic children's books and apps that are of the highest quality in both form and content. it is one of the richest awards of its kind in the world and is considered among the most important literary awards for children's literature in the arab region.
Results: There are many cultural awards in the uae, and many of them are regional and international awards. many people and organizations participate in these awards and competitions, some of those accomplishments are highlighted below: *	sharjah department of culture manages 7 domestic, regional and international cultural awards in areas such as poetry, drama, fine art critique, arabic culture, innovation and creativity. *	many of the organizations in the uae which manage awards and competitions ensure student engagement and participation in these awards. for example, the knowledge and human development authority (khda), the authority responsible for education in dubai, facilitated student participation in the following: international prize for arabic fiction, emirates airlines literature festival, and other awards. *	the happiness film award received nearly 200 creative participations over a period of 2 months, and 22 films qualified for the semi-finals. the first three winners won the opportunity to attend the 2019 cannes film festival, in an award presented by the ministry of the interior, in addition to financial prizes worth 5,000 uae dirhams for the 22 finalists. in addition, majid al futtaim group offered financial prizes of 50,000 aed dirhams to the first place winner, 30,000 aed dirhams for the second place winner, and 20,000 aed dirhams for the third place winner. *	the sheikh zayed book award is organized by the department of culture and tourism in abu dhabi and is presented annually with the following results in the last few years: o	2016 - 46 countries, 1,169 nominations o	2017 - 45 countries, 1,175 nominations o	2018 - 41 countries, 1,191 nominations o	2019 - 49 countries, 1,502 nominations o	2020 - 49 countries, 1,900 nominations *	international prize for arabic fiction (ipaf): 1,781 writers from 24 countries participated in the 13 editions of the international prize for arabic fiction, from its inception in 2008 to 2020. *	sheikh mohammed bin rashid patrons of the arts awards: the second edition of the awards, held recently recognized 40 patrons for contributing over aed 130 million in financial or in-kind contribution towards the arts. this followed the first edition where 59 organizations and individuals were recognized for their financial and in-kind support of about aed 250 million from 2007 to 2009.

Title EN: L’engagement des cinéastes dans la promotion des droits humains
Goal: Promote Human Rights And Fundamental Freedoms
SDG: SDG 5 - Achieve gender equality and empower all women and girls,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels
Area of Monitoring: Gender equality
Agency Implementation: Association CINEACTIF;   Association Taafé vision;   Djiguiya productions;    Média Afrique.
Main Feature: Au Burkina Faso, la crise sécuritaire a entrainé ces dernières années une recrudescence des phénomènes sociaux comme la délinquance juvénile, les mariages précoces/forcées, les grossesses non désirées/précoces, la prostitution, les viols, etc. Pour faire face à cette situation, plusieurs mesures et initiatives ont été développées par les acteurs publics, les organisations de la société civiles et les partenaires.  Le cinéma a un impact réel sur la société et constitue un moyen de communication et d’expression qui permet de promouvoir les droits humains. A travers des actions de formation et de projections de films, les OSC sensibilisent sur des thématiques liées à la violence basée sur le genre, l'extrémisme violent, la radicalisation, la cohésion sociale ainsi que les droits des enfants.  Dans le cadre de la commémoration de la Journée internationale pour l'élimination des violences à l'égard des femmes (25 novembre) et de la Journée des droits humains (10 décembre), l'Association TAAFE VISION a organisé dans le cadre de ses 16 jours d'activisme, « Le festival 16 Films 1 Cause ». Il a consisté en la projection sur grand écran de films d'ici et d'ailleurs. Ce festival se veut être un cadre d'échanges et de dialogue sur les thématiques des violences basées sur le genre mais aussi de dénonciation du phénomène et de vulgarisation des bonnes pratiques par le biais des films diffusés. Le projet « Écrans Citoyens » porté par l’association CINEACTIF est né de la volonté d’un groupe de professionnels en vue d’outiller les jeunes et à les sensibiliser sur la paix, le respect des droits et l’autonomisation. Il a consisté en des formations aux métiers du cinéma et de l'audiovisuel, avec une attention particulière à la sensibilisation sur l'extrémisme violent et la cohésion sociale. Des formations spécifiques sont orientées vers la paix et l'entrepreneuriat féminin.  L’initiative “Journées cinématographiques du cinéma amateur”, a consisté à installer au sein de certains lycées et collèges, des clubs cinéma. Les jeunes ont été formés dans les métiers du cinéma et de l’audiovisuel dans le cadre des activités parascolaires. Les modules dispensés concernent le scénario, la réalisation, le montage, l’image, le maquillage, etc.  L’objectif de ce projet était d’encourager les élèves à l’éducation aux médias, à la production de contenus pour sensibiliser leurs pairs sur les maux qui minent la jeunesse et des messages à l’adresse des parents et de la société pour que les droits et la parole des jeunes soient pris en compte.
Results: La mise en œuvre de ces initiatives a permis d’atteindre quelques résultats. Concernant le festival « 16 FILMS 1 CAUSE » : 16 films projetés, 2500 personnes enregistrées au cours des projections et des débats. S’agissant des initiatives "Écrans citoyens" et « Clap en Herbe » : 3300 jeunes formés ,115 courts métrages réalisés et 3500 cinéphiles enregistrés.  Coût des initiatives :  154  698 USDPartenaires : Ministère de la communication, de la culture, des arts et du tourisme, Equipop, Ambassade du Canada, Africalia Belgique

Title EN: Amendments to the Code of the Republic of Belarus on Culture
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture
SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Cultural and creative sectors
Cultural Domain: Performing Arts,Visual Arts,Music,Publishing,Media Arts,Design,Cinema and Audiovisual Arts
Agency Implementation: Ministry of Culture of the Republic of Belarus
Main Feature: The Code of the Republic of Belarus on Culture was adopted by Decree No. 413-Z of the President of the Republic of Belarus dated July 20, 2016, and it came into force on February 3, 2017. It was developed in accordance with the global core principles of cultural policy. The Code aims to establish the legal, institutional, economic, and social basis for cultural activities, in order to preserve and use the cultural heritage, to develop cultural institutions, and to ensure the accessibility of the cultural goods. In 2022, the amendments where introduced into the Code of the Republic of Belarus on Culture. The Code continues to determine the basic principles of civil relations in this field (Article 2), including the provisions of the Convention on the Protection and Promotion of the Diversity of Cultural Expressions. Thus, under the Code on Culture, the core principles of the cultural policy of the Republic of Belarus are as follows: recognizing the culture as one of the main factors of the identity of the Belarusian people and other ethnic communities residing in Belarus, as well as the basis for the formation and development of individuality; ensuring the accessibility of the cultural goods and the protection of the rights and opportunities of everyone, including people with disabilities, to participate in the cultural life; asserting the freedom of creativity; preventing unlawful advantages or privileges and the monopolization of cultural activities; promoting and protecting the copyright and civil rights of cultural workers and artists; ensuring the interaction of the Belarusian national culture with other cultures and its integration into the global cultural space.  The amendments into the Code helped to raise up the salaries of employed and the field, as well as developed further measures to protect the national and cultural heritage of the Republic of Belarus. The Ministry of Culture established the Consultative Council to facilitate its dialogue with civil society organizations.  New governmental programme ‘Culture of Belarus’ for 2021-2025 was approved. The programme emphasizes the necessity to preserve the historical memory of the Belarusian people, its national and cultural identity and traditions, as well as to actively involve people of Belarus into cultural life of the country. Among the positive changes in legal regulation in the field of culture we should mention the changes in the rules of state financial support to various cultural establishments. Now, the amount of this support is stronger connected to the quality of provided services and fulfillment of other key performance indicators.  The Special Fund of the President of the Republic of Belarus for supporting young talented people introduced new rules concerning the rewards and support. The amounts of rewards were significantly raised up, while the application conditions became stricter. It contributed to a higher status of rewards and support provided by the Fund, raised up the public awareness about young talented people in Belarus and their contribution to the development of national culture.
Results: 1) The further codification of legislation on culture made it possible to systematize disparate laws on a higher level, to identify the duplication, inconsistency of certain requirements, to fill in some gaps in legal regulation, and ultimately resulted in more effective governance in the field of culture and transparency in the implementation of legal norms. It is important that these further improvements in the Code of Culture were made after wide public discussions and through analysis of the existing practices and problems, which were not solved by the first variant of the Code of culture. 2) The Ministry of Culture succeeded in raising up salaries in the field of culture. The gap between incomes in this field and incomes in other sectors of economy was significantly reduced. These measures helped to save qualified personnel in cultural establishments and hire young talented people. 3) A special Council on Culture was established as an advisory board under the Aegis of the Ministry of Culture. This step helped to conduct further board discussions about the cultural policy in the country and raised the status of non-governmental sector in policy formation in the field of culture. 4) New regulations concerning the organization of cultural and public events helped to secure them from any possible fraud or low-quality and unexperienced organization.
Financial Ressources: The funding of the cultural sector is ensured by annually allocated government investments, sponsorship funds and funds of the State Program “Culture of Belarus”, other state programs, and as well as from the Special Fund of the President of the Republic of Belarus for Supporting Talented Youth. Also, state grants for major cultural programmes, projects and events are available. The annual state budget for culture is 0.38-0.41% of GDP.
Recommandations: The effectiveness of the implementation of the cultural policies and the practical application of the main provisions of the Code on Culture, as well as other legal regulations, is annually monitored by the Ministry of Culture of the Republic of Belarus and independent experts. The monitoring results are reviewed by the annual reporting panels of the Ministry of Culture and widely covered by the national media. Throughout the reported period wide publiccampaign were held to discuss changes and proposal to the national legislature in the field of culture. Some of these proposals, as for example, the proposal to raise up salaries in the field of culture, were implemented by the Ministry of Culture. Among the changes that should be made to this legislative act, the most important ones are as follows: 1) to work more thoroughly on the further implementation of the main provisions of the ratified international treaties, including but not limited to the UNESCO Conventions. Besides the 2005 Convention, great attention was paid to intangible and material cultural heritage of Belarus.  2) to link the existing provisions of the Code with the implementation of the Sustainable Development Goals, ratified by the Republic of Belarus in 2019, to pay particular attention to such issues as creating a supportive and diverse environment for the development of the local cultural and creative industries, protecting and promoting the social status of an artist, promoting the cultural expression and traditions of the local communities 3) to revise the budget financing of cultural erstablishment in order to stimulate them for a more active position in the market 4) to promote patriotic and national cultural activities, safeguarding the national values and traditions of the Belarusian people.

Main Feature: The ministry of culture created a team in 2017 to evaluate and prepare a new strategy and structure. in 2022, the team concluded its work and made several recommendations that were implemented, including the creation of a new public administration called the administration of digital content. this administration is focused on the importance of digital culture and aims to promote it nationally, regionally, and globally, especially in light of the pandemic. the ministry also established an administration of cultural industries, which has three departments and is responsible for developing policies and initiatives to support the cultural sector. these measures are expected to enhance the role of culture in society, improve the cultural sector's economic contribution, and promote the development of cultural industries.
Results: The ministry of culture has established two new public administrations: the general management of digital content and the general administration of cultural industries. these administrations have been activated and are currently working on implementing a range of conferences and activities related to their respective areas of focus. the general management of digital content is concerned with digital culture on a national, regional, and global level, particularly in light of the increased importance of digital content following the pandemic. meanwhile, the general administration of cultural industries is responsible for developing policies and programs related to cultural industries, and is comprised of three departments.
Recommandations: In partnership with the general personnel council in palestine, the ministry of culture discussed the significance of having these new public administrations within the ministry. the focus was on how these general departments will play a crucial role in implementing the new policies of the ministry of culture, which are centered around cultural industries and the advancement of culture through digital platforms.

Title EN: Carifesta xiv trinidad and tobago
Goal: Achieve A Balanced Flow Of Cultural Goods And Services And Increase The Mobility Of Artists And Cultural Professionals
SDG: SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 10 - Reduce inequality within and among countries,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Flow of cultural goods and services,Mobility of artists and cultural professionals
Agency Implementation: Ministry of community development, culture and the arts
Main Feature: Carifesta is a regional forum where artists, performers and other persons in the field of culture meet and exchange ideas through presentations of music, dance, drama, exhibitions on art, sculpture, poetry and symposia, among others. this regional creative festival was first held in georgetown, guyana in 1972, attracting creative artistes from over 30 caribbean and latin american countries. it is a celebration of the ethnic and racial diversity which separately and collectively created cultural expressions that are wonderfully unique to the caribbean and is intended to be a mixture of the states of the caribbean community (caricom); the wider caribbean, latin america; and a representation of africa, asia, europe and north america. carifesta xiv was hosted by trinidad and tobago from 16th - 25th august 2019. the host country management committee comprised representatives of ministries and state agencies; ministry of community development, culture and the arts, ministry of tourism, ministry of trade and industry, ministry of foreign and caricom affairs, ministry of public administration and communications, ministry of works and transport, ministry of national security, ministry of sport and youth affairs, tobago house of assembly, airports authority of trinidad and tobago, port authority of trinidad and tobago and a select group of creative and cultural sector advisors. the theme for carifesta xiv was the tangible and the intangible: connect, share, invest. it focused on both the tangible and intangible aspects of cultural heritage and development and sought to find the ways and means for caribbean people, artists, and cultural practitioners to connect with each other, share ideas and information, and invest in the development of our cultural explorations, products and exchanges thus building stronger national, regional and creative industries.
Results: The fourteenth edition of the festival catered to over 1,600 participants from within the region, including twenty-two (22) country delegations as well as independent participants. carifesta xiv attracted large audiences during the ten-day festival period, estimated at over 130,000 patrons and artists. numerous events were scheduled each day with many shows taking place in the capital city – port-of-spain in trinidad, and satellite events in communities around trinidad and in tobago. these included the opening and closing ceremonies, country nights, community festivals, the grand market, visual arts showcases, an underground series, symposia, a youth village and the island beats super concert. the carifesta xiv grand market attracted more than 112,593 visitors, while the super concert attracted over 6,000 patrons. the festival was supported by thirty-one (31) sponsors and a total of five hundred (500) volunteer workers were engaged at various levels in the organisation of the event.
Financial Ressources: 8,900 (trinidad and tobago’s contribution)
Recommandations: It is important to note that in order for the caribbean countries to continue to either host or participate in carifesta, they must be cognizant of the changing market dynamics in relation to social, economic, political, technological, environmental and cultural factors. additional consideration must be given to the trends in the global arts, entertainment, and tourism industries. evolving consumer tastes must also be monitored in order to anticipate the possible impact of this variable on future festivals. carifesta is the only regional arts and culture festival which can potentially bring the caribbean creative sector and industry together, therefore the legacy and future of this arts festival must be preserved.

Title EN: Full dance scholarship
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture
SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development

Main Feature: Modern dance movement provides full dance scholarships to selected dancers from ages 3 to adults. these scholarships are awarded based on the dancers' commitment to attending classes consistently and demonstrating respect towards the teacher and other dancers. the main goal of full scholarships is to alleviate the financial burden associated with dance education for talented individuals who may not have the means to pursue it otherwise. by offering scholarships to dancers ranging from 3-year-olds to adults, the scholarships ensure that individuals of all ages can benefit from this opportunity. this promotes a diverse and multi-generational dance community, fostering a sense of inclusiveness and mutual support among dancers of different age groups. rather than solely focusing on talent or skill level, the scholarship opportunity acknowledges the importance of dedication and the ability to work well with others in the dance environment. this approach encourages dancers to not only develop their technical abilities but also cultivate positive attitudes and values that contribute to a healthy and supportive dance community. financial relief is a significant aspect of this program. by offering full dance scholarships, the initiative aims to alleviate the financial burden associated with dance education. dance classes, costumes, shoes, and other related expenses can accumulate over time, making it challenging for many individuals and families to afford quality dance training. the scholarships provided can make dance education accessible to those who may have otherwise been unable to afford it, ensuring that talent and passion are not hindered by financial constraints. furthermore, this measure/initiative promotes the development of a supportive dance community. by awarding scholarships based on commitment and respect, it fosters an environment where dancers encourage and uplift one another. this can create a positive and inspiring atmosphere in which dancers can thrive, motivating each other to reach their full potential. additionally, the financial relief provided by the scholarships helps eliminate any sense of competition or disparity among dancers based on financial resources, fostering a sense of unity and camaraderie within the dance community. in summary, full dance scholarships focus on the values and qualities exhibited by the dancers, ensuring equal opportunities for all who meet the selection criteria. this commitment to inclusivity promotes diversity and encourages individuals from all walks of life to pursue their passion for dance.
Results: Selected dancers on full scholarships have increased access to dance education. by providing full scholarships, the initiative opens doors for talented individuals who might have otherwise been unable to afford dance classes. this results in increased access to quality dance education for a wider range of participants, including those from disadvantaged backgrounds or with limited financial resources. dancers on scholarship have the opportunity to develop their skills, refine their technique, and explore their artistic potential to a greater extent. this can lead to the emergence of exceptional dancers who may go on to achieve notable accomplishments in their dance careers locally and internationally. the requirement of consistent class attendance and commitment to the scholarship can help instil discipline and dedication in the recipients. knowing that their attendance and commitment are being recognized and rewarded, dancers may be more motivated to prioritize their dance training and actively participate in classes. this, in turn, can contribute to improved skill development and overall progress. engaging in dance education through full scholarships can have a transformative effect on the lives of the recipients. dance provides an outlet for self-expression, promotes physical fitness, and cultivates discipline, teamwork, and perseverance. by participating in the scholarship program, dancers may experience personal growth, increased self-confidence, and enhanced social skills. the scholarship initiative can foster a sense of camaraderie and mutual support among the dancers. recipients can form connections and friendships, encouraging and inspiring each other and fellow dancers in their dance journeys. this collaborative and inclusive environment can contribute to a positive dance community that nurtures talent and fosters a lifelong love for dance. by providing opportunities to dancers from various backgrounds, the scholarship initiative promotes diversity and inclusivity within the dance community. this enriches the dance field by bringing together individuals with different perspectives, experiences, and cultural influences, leading to a more vibrant and dynamic dance landscape.

Main Feature: Xe'il, meaning "true to our roots," is a fashion brand designed and developed to provide economic empowerment to indigenous maya women and showcase in southern belize. xe'il was established in october 2019 by the sarstoon temash institute for indigenous management (satiim) with financial support from the caribbean development bank (cdb) through its cultural and creative industries innovative fund (ciif). the primary goal of xe'il is to position maya women as national artists and bring their creative products to a wider market, starting with new fashion designs adorned with xokbil chuy, an endangered art of counted cross stitch embroidery. maya women, are among the most marginalized people in belize, often relegated to ethnic stereotypes outside of their communities. xe'il, has cultivated a growing network of maya women entrepreneurs by providing them with business training and unprecedented economic opportunities.  historically, maya women have been entrepreneurs who grow and create products to support their families. xe'il serves as a platform to offer them the support, recognition, respect, and incomes they have long deserved and ensure the cultural survival of traditional art forms through fashion. every purchase from xe'il directly supports elder maya women master artists and their apprentices, thereby ensuring the intergenerational transmission of knowledge forms, along with empowering a network of maya women entrepreneurs. xe'il products are designed for the conscious consumer and are not mass-produced in large factories. instead, they are meticulously hand-embroidered thereby retaining the traditional embroidery practice among the mopan maya people of southern belize. furthermore, the brand aspires to connect buyers both locally and internationally, fostering appreciation and support for the artistic expressions and cultural heritage of maya women.

Main Feature: The Antigone Project was created to raise awareness about and prevent Gender Based Violence (GBV) through school theatre workshops. Based on participatory theatre techniques, the project aims to enable and empower secondary school teachers across Europe to organise theatre workshops in order to raise awareness on GBV. To achieve this goal, the project has developed a manual in relation to the organisation of school workshops with all the necessary information, enabling teachers to use the theatre method independently in their schools. Based on this manual, training material was produced and online and face-to-face courses for teachers were organised in all partner countries. Beside Italy, represented by Fondazione AIDA, participating in the project are: Udrujenije Gragdana Dah Teatar - Centar Za Pozorishna Istrajivanja, Serbia (project leader); Theatro Aeroploio - Ena Theatro Giapaidia (Greece); Action Synergy SA (Greece); Association of Young Psychologists in Bulgaria (Bulgaria); Insite Drama Oktatasi, Kulturalis es szolgatato non-profit korlatolt Felelossegu Tarsasag (Hungary); Hogskulen Pa Vestlandet (Norway); RealStars (Sweden)          The project is supported by Erasmus+ / European Union

Main Feature: International co-production in ukraine is regulated by the law of ukraine “about state support of cinematography in ukraine”, rules of the european convention on cinematographic co-production, bilateral treaties and other related legislation. ukraine aims to create favorable conditions for the development of film production, establish transparent procedures for state funding of projects in the field of cinematography, and develop new initiatives to support international cooperation in film production. subsidy for film production. every year, the ukrainian state film agency holds pitching sessions in various categories of film projects (feature, non-fiction, amateur, debut films, children's, tv series, etc.) and, among other things, supports co-production projects with maximum funding of about 800,000 euros. categories for competitive selection: •	international co-production – a film of any kind, produced (created) and funded by two or more film producers, with at least one foreign producer among them. there are majority and minority international co-productions; •	majority international co-production is an international co-production in which the share of the ukrainian film producer is the largest in the total budget of the film; •	minority international co-production is an international co-production in which the share of the ukrainian film producer is not the largest in the total budget of the film. apart from the financial support of production, the state cinema also supports the promotion of ukrainian films and films created in co-production with other countries that are recognized as national in accordance with international agreements. cash rebate. foreign film productions starting 2020 can apply for a 25%-30% cash rebate. feature films, documentaries, and animated films are eligible, as well as tv feature films or animated series, commercials, and music videos. the obligatory condition for receiving a cash rebate is the absence of residents of ukraine among its owners, participants, shareholders, including the ultimate beneficial owners (controllers), as well as officials of this foreign subject of cinema. films that have passed the cultural test are the object of state support in the form of a cash rebate. eurimages. on december 19, 2019, the ukrainian parliament adopts the law on ukraine joining the european fund for support of joint production and distribution of artistic cinematographic and audiovisual works "eurimages", which promotes independent film production by providing financial support for the feature, animated, and documentary films and boosts international cooperation.
Results: Film projects supported by eurimages: ukrainian projects created with the support of the ukrainian state film agency «spas» by maxym nakonechnyi and «rhino» by oleh sentsov received 395 thousand euros of financial support. ukrainian-italian co-production film project directed by andrea magnani long run received 180 thousand euros of total financial support from the fund. the film project of director roman bondarchuk the editorial office, one of the winners of the 14th competition run by the ukrainian state film agency, received 140 thousand euros of total financial support from the eurimages foundation.

Title EN: Music schools in the community
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture
SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Cultural and creative sectors
Agency Implementation: Ministry of tourism, culture and the arts
Main Feature: From as early as 2012, the music schools in the community (msic) programme began as music education camps in communal spaces like pan yards in at-risk communities. the programme was conceived as a response to the dearth of trained musicians, underserved community spaces, extant music centres, dormant institutional programmes, and lack of access to tutors and instruments for those interested in music. msic operates as a partnership between the ministry and music educators. over the course of seven (7) years, msic has evolved with the goal of creating a cadre of musicians for the future, introducing participants of all ages to music literacy and instruments, inclusive of the steelpan, alto and tenor saxophone, trumpet, trombone, clarinet, guitar, sitar, tabla, harmonium, violin, and the recorder. the programme also served to increase music literacy among the steelband community, expose them to other instruments, and support their institutional strengthening.
Results: The major achievements of the music schools in the community programme include the hosting of its “dream big” concerts in 2017 and 2018 at the national academy for the performing arts (napa) featuring graduates from the music schools, and its initiation of the first-ever caribbean youth orchestra (cyo) during carifesta xiv in 2019, in trinidad and tobago. the music schools in the community / caribbean youth orchestra programme ran from june to august 2019 for ten consecutive weeks. music schools were allowed to adjust the times of the classes in order to facilitate the varying circumstances in each community. the caribbean youth orchestra was designed to include young musicians from the caribbean region. the following countries were able to send representatives to participate in the cyo: belize, cayman islands, grenada, guyana, st. kitts, st. lucia, st. vincent and the grenadines, and turks and caicos islands. the programme received an influx of students from the existing music schools as well as the wider community in trinidad and tobago. given the additional carifesta xiv ingredient in that year’s programme, provisions were made for over one hundred and fifty (150) young local and regional musicians.

Title EN: Palestinian national theatre festival
Goal: Achieve A Balanced Flow Of Cultural Goods And Services And Increase The Mobility Of Artists And Cultural Professionals
SDG: SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 10 - Reduce inequality within and among countries,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development

Agency Implementation: Ministry of culture
Main Feature: An annual measure organized by the palestinian national theatre festival in collaboration with the arab theater institute. this noteworthy event, initially established on the 25th of october, has now become a biennial festival due to recent circumstances caused by the global pandemic. the upcoming edition of the initiative is set to take place this year and promises an exceptional gathering of talented artists from arab and latin american countries, alongside renowned performers from various regions within palestine. this vibrant forum aims to foster a profound appreciation for theatre culture among the younger generation while simultaneously enhancing the professional capabilities of individuals involved in the field. the theater cultural exchange initiative strives to bridge diverse artistic traditions and facilitate meaningful exchanges of ideas, experiences, and techniques. by creating an environment conducive to cross-cultural collaboration, it enriches the theatrical landscape and empowers practitioners to further their artistic endeavors.
Results: The implementation of the policy has yielded remarkable achievements, contributing to the recognition and success of palestinian films in the international arena. here are some notable results: cairo international film festival (november 2022): the palestinian film "alam" directed by firas khoury received three prestigious awards, including best feature film, best actor, and the audience award. this accolade highlights the exceptional quality of palestinian cinema and its ability to captivate audiences globally. additionally, "alam" was selected as one of about 15 feature-length projects from around the world by the cannes film festival "l'atelier" program, providing the director with valuable networking opportunities with industry professionals. cannes film festival (may 2022): maha al haj's "mediterranean fever" achieved the best screenplay award in the "un certain regard" section, which focuses on artistically daring and thought-provoking films. this recognition at cannes further solidifies the film's artistic excellence and serves as palestine's submission for the 2023 oscars. "mediterranean fever" has also garnered three additional awards and eight nominations at various film festivals. it premiered on the opening night of the palestine cinema days 2022 in ramallah, showcasing its cultural significance. "al garib" by ameer fakher eldin, palestine's 2022 oscar submission, received two awards and three nominations. the film was honored with the asia pacific screen award for best cinematography (november 2022) and the edipo re award for social inclusion at the venice international film festival (september 2021). it was presented as the closing film at the arab film festival (december 2022) in san francisco, where it received the award for best debut feature. these achievements highlight the compelling storytelling and technical excellence of palestinian cinema. palestinian delegation's official participation in the clermont-ferrand international short film festival in france during february 2023 demonstrates the growing presence and representation of palestinian filmmakers on the global stage. this participation provides a valuable platform for showcasing palestinian talent and fostering international collaborations. the 9th edition of palestine cinema days 2022, organized by filmlab: palestine, presented 58 films to an audience of 3500. this annual event celebrates palestinian cinema and provides a platform for filmmakers to showcase their work to a diverse audience, further establishing the palestinian film industry's cultural impact. the 6th edition of the red carpet human rights film festival in gaza featured 45 films and attracted an audience of 2500. this festival, held in cooperation with the karama film festival in jordan, focuses on promoting human rights awareness through the medium of film. its success reflects the power of cinema to address social issues and advocate for change. these remarkable outcomes exemplify the effectiveness of the policy in fostering the growth, recognition, and international acclaim of palestinian films, elevating the voices and stories of palestinian filmmakers on a global scale.
Financial Ressources: 300000 usd from ministry of culture
Recommandations: Our goal is to significantly increase the number of theatre visitors in palestine by revolutionizing the way theatre is experienced. to achieve this, we are developing exciting and accessible tools that aim to capture the attention of theatre lovers, making their journey to the theatre more enjoyable, entertaining, and convenient. by harnessing the power of innovation, we seek to create a vibrant theatre scene that appeals to a broader audience base. through these new tools, we aspire to infuse performances with a greater sense of fun and excitement, drawing in both existing theatre enthusiasts and those who may not have previously explored the world of theatre. the innovative features we are developing will make it easier than ever for individuals to connect with the theatre scene in palestine. we are committed to ensuring that theatre experiences are easily accessible and enjoyable for all, breaking down barriers and inviting individuals to immerse themselves in the magic of live performances. by employing these new tools, we envision an increase in theatre attendance, with audiences eagerly anticipating each performance. our aim is to cultivate a vibrant and thriving theatre culture in palestine, where laughter, excitement, and entertainment are at the forefront, creating memorable experiences that inspire and captivate audiences of all ages.

Title EN: Omweleso

Main Feature: Omwoleso is an e-commerce platform designed to provide comprehensive support and empowerment for creatives across various artistic disciplines. through an array of tools, resources, and networking opportunities, omwoleso aims to nurture the talents of artisans, designers, and other creative individuals, enabling them to thrive in their respective fields. features and offerings 1. portfolio showcasing: omwoleso offers creatives a user-friendly interface to showcase their work, helping them build a captivating online portfolio that effectively communicates their unique style and skills. 2. collaboration hub: the platform facilitates collaboration between creatives from diverse backgrounds. users can discover potential collaborators, share ideas, and work together on projects, fostering a vibrant creative community. 3. resource library: omwoleso provides an extensive library of resources, including tutorials, guides, and industry insights. these resources cover a range of topics such as marketing, project management, copyright, and self-promotion, empowering creatives with the knowledge needed to succeed. 4. marketplace: a dedicated marketplace allows artists to sell their creations, whether it's physical crafts. the platform offers secure transaction processing, ensuring a seamless experience for both buyers and sellers. 5. educational workshops: omwoleso organizes virtual workshops and webinars featuring industry experts. these sessions provide valuable insights into current trends, techniques, and best practices within the creative world. 6. networking events: regular virtual events and meet-ups connect creatives with peers, mentors, and potential clients. these interactions foster meaningful relationships and open doors to new opportunities. 7. feedback and critique: the platform encourages a constructive feedback culture, allowing users to request feedback on their work from a community of peers and experts. this promotes growth and improvement within the creative process. 8. customizable profiles: creatives can tailor their profiles to reflect their brand identity. this personalization enhances their visibility and credibility among potential clients, collaborators, and fans. 9. market days: these are physical exhibitions that enable creatives to showcase their products as they interact with clients and get instant feedback. omwoleso stands as a groundbreaking platform that supports and empowers creatives on their artistic journeys. by offering a rich array of features and resources, the platform nurtures a dynamic creative community where individuals can learn, grow, and thrive in their respective creative endeavours.
Results: Omwoleso has created a significant impact during its operation. it has served as a transformative platform connecting artisans and creative entrepreneurs with a global audience, fostering economic growth, empowerment, and cultural exchange. empowerment of artisans: omwoleso has empowered over 700 artisans by providing them with a digital space to showcase their unique creations. through its user-friendly interface and support mechanisms, artisans gained the confidence to navigate the online marketplace, manage their product listings, and effectively communicate their brand stories. economic growth: the platform played a pivotal role in driving economic growth within artisan communities. by facilitating the sale of handmade products and creative works, omwoleso has enabled over 400 artisans to reach a broader customer base, resulting in increased sales and income. this, in turn, contributed to the economic well-being of individual artisans and their local communities. cultural exchange: omwoleso has become a hub for cultural exchange, where artisans from diverse backgrounds shared their traditional crafts and artistic expressions with a global audience. this not only enriches the platform's offerings but also promotes cross-cultural understanding and appreciation. skills enhancement: through omwoleso, over 200 artisans have acquired valuable skills beyond their craft. they learned about digital marketing, photography, and customer engagement strategies. this knowledge has equipped them to create compelling product listings, enhance their online presence, and connect with customers effectively. innovation in marketing: the platform's features, such as the customizable storefronts and integrated social sharing options, have allowed artisans to market their products creatively. as a result, they leverage social media and word-of-mouth referrals to drive traffic to their omwoleso stores, leading to increased sales. access to new markets: omwoleso has expanded artisans' market reach beyond geographical boundaries through our monthly market days across ugandan regions, thereby diversifying their customer base and reducing dependence on a single market. networking and collaboration: omwoleso facilitates networking and collaboration among artisans. through the platform's community forums and events, artisans share insights, learn from each other's experiences, and even form partnerships for joint ventures or collaborations. quality assurance: omwoleso's reputation for curating high-quality products has instilled trust among customers. this trust has led to increased customer satisfaction and loyalty, further enhancing the platform's credibility as a reliable source for unique and well-crafted goods. environmental impact: by promoting handmade and sustainable products, omwoleso has contributed to environmental consciousness. the platform has encouraged consumers to choose products with a lower ecological footprint, aligning with the growing global demand for eco-friendly choices.

Title EN: Mise en place du Programme National de Développement des Industries culturelles et créatives.
Goal: Integrate Culture In Sustainable Development Frameworks
SDG: SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: National sustainable development policies and plans
Cultural Domain: Performing Arts,Visual Arts,Music,Publishing,Design,Cinema and Audiovisual Arts,Media Arts
Agency Implementation: Bureau Central du Ministère de la Culture et de la communication
Main Feature: En juillet 2019, le Ministère de la Culture et de la Communication a mis en place le « Programme National de Développement des Industries Culturelles et Créatives » afin d’intégrer la créativité et les expressions culturelles en tant qu’éléments stratégiques dans la planification nationale et les politiques de développement durable. L’initiative résulte de l’analyse des difficultés et des besoins dont fait face le secteur culturel. La description du contexte national des politiques culturelles publiques met en évidence les difficultés du secteur culturel. Tout d’abord, la mise en place des politiques culturelles dépend du contexte national global du pays. La culture a été victime de plusieurs catastrophes dont les impacts continuent à se faire sentir notamment le séisme du 12 janvier 2010 et celui de 2021, le cyclone Matthew 2016, l’instabilité politique et ministérielle, la contestation populaire, le phénomène de « lock down » de cette même période. Ensuite, les faiblesses institutionnelles caractérisées par l’absence de loi-cadre, la désuétude de certaines lois culturelles, l’insuffisance budgétaire. D’autres problèmes minent la mise en place effective des politiques culturelles, notamment : (i) l’absence de coordination des aides bilatérales et multilatérales à la culture (absence de cadre de régulation de la coopération culturelle) ; (ii) le manque de ressources humaines qualifiées ou spécialisées pour certains domaines ; (iii) la faiblesse au niveau des infrastructures culturelles marquées par la concentration des équipements culturels à la capitale ; (iv) l’absence de données statistiques fiables sur les filières de la culture ; (v) l’absence de collaboration structurée entre les départements ministériels ; (vi) l’absence de cadre de dialogue, de concertation et de coordination pour réguler les interventions dans le secteur culturel et créatif. Cette mesure a pour objectif général la reconstruction du système culturel national. Elle visait spécifiquement à : 10) définir une politique publique de la culture et de politiques sectorielles ; 20) redéfinir le cadre législatif et règlementaire ; 30) élaborer et adopter les mécanismes institutionnels de financement des initiatives et activités culturelles ; 40) encourager l’entreprenariat culturel ; 50) contribuer 87 à la professionnalisation et à la mobilité des créateurs ; 60) renforcer la communication globale. L’estimation budgétaire est de l’ordre de : 1,085,750.00 USD. Ce budget devrait être ventilé à travers le budget national de la culture sur différents exercices. La stratégie de mise en oeuvre s’articule tout d’abord autour de la structure de gestion. Cette dernière comprend d’abord un Secrétariat technique de pilotage, composé de cadres techniques ayant participé à la conception du document de programme, de tous autres cadres compétents, de cadres des organismes sous tutelle, avec la participation de représentant de l’OIF, ensuite d’un Comité intersectoriel de consultation regroupant de représentants des secteurs public, privé, de la coopération internationale et des acteurs organisés du champ culturel (Conférence des bailleurs sur les priorités et le financement des actions) aussi d’un Comité Interministériel de consultation pour harmoniser les interventions en fonction des champs définis par le secteur. Ce comité est composé de différents ministères. Des groupes thématiques ou soussectorielles de travail complètent le dispositif de mise en place. Ces groupes de travail sont composés des représentants des différentes filières des industries culturelles et créatives et du secteur public sous le leadership des organismes sectoriels du Ministère. Ces structures renforceront les dispositions pour associer au projet les organisations professionnelles de la culture et d'autres partenaires de la coopération internationale. L’autre élément primordial de la stratégie de mise en oeuvre est la stratégie de financement. La stratégie de financement s’articule autour de : 1. Mobilisation des fonds à trois niveaux : Ministère de la Culture et de la Communication secteur privé des affaires, du mécénat, fonds internationaux mobilisés auprès des différentes structures de coopération dans le secteur sur la base de conventions et d’accords de partenariat multilatéral et bilatéral. 2. Mise en place d’un fond fiduciaire pour le secteur culturel regroupant les fonds provenant du secteur public, du privé et de la coopération internationale sous la gestion d’un Conseil d’Administration mixte nommé par le ministre de la Culture et de la Communication susceptible de garantir l’efficacité des dépenses et la bonne gestion du programme. Pour la mise en place de la stratégie de financement, le Ministère de la Culture et de la Communication a soumissionné à un appel à projet de l’Organisation Internationale de la Francophonie et a obtenu une promesse de financement. Ensuite, un budget présentant la contrepartie nationale a été introduite dans le budget national.
Results: Le « Programme National de Développement des Industries Culturelles et Créatives » a été lancé au cours de l’année 2019 et les discussions ont continué avec la coopération internationale notamment le Bureau de l’UNESCO à Port-au-Prince et les responsables de l’Organisation Internationale de la Francophonie. La mise en place du programme et l’atteinte des résultats ont été entravées par la grave crise qui est survenue dans les années ultérieures. Un avant-projet de loi sur la condition des artistes a été élaborée et l’entame de l’élaboration d’une politique culturelle a été faite. Une équipe de travail a été formée pour travailler sur la transformation numérique et l’introduction de ce dernier dans le secteur culturel. Des données statistiques sur la condition des artistes étaient en phase d’être collectées durant la période du Covid- !9. La contrepartie nationale a fait l’objet d’une proposition au Parlement Haïtien. Mais, depuis cette période, l’exercice même d’adoption a été bloqué au niveau du parlement haïtien et depuis lors, ce ne sont que des budgets rectificatifs qui sont mis en place. L’instabilité politique et sécuritaire minent la continuité de la mise en place du programme et l’atteinte des résultats. Le Ministère de la Culture et de la Communication travaille en vue d’atteindre les différents objectifs tout en essayant de faire face aux contraintes sécuritaires et à l’instabilité politique. En ce sens, depuis l’année de 2019 jusqu’à ce jour, il travaille avec la Commission Nationale de Coopération avec l’UNESCO à la formation et à la diffusion du texte de la Convention de 2005. Dans cette même stratégie, il travaille à conscientiser les différents acteurs des industries culturelles et créatives à se regrouper en vue de créer des plateformes professionnelles qui pourront servir d’interface dans la gouvernance de la culture. Depuis 2022, dans ce changement de stratégie pour atteindre les résultats, le Ministère de la Culture et de la Communication fait des appels à projets pour près de 21 associations sur tout le territoire dans le secteur des industries culturelles et créatives pour une enveloppe de101 000.38 usd (10,500,000.00 gourdes) à raison de 4809.54usd (500,000.00 gourdes) par association afin de favoriser la dynamisation de ce secteur.
