Main Feature: L'accord Culturel entre la République de Côte d'Ivoire et le Royaume du Maroc a été signé à Rabat, le 22 Septembre 1973. Dans ce accord, les parties ce sont engagées à développer et consolider les relations entre les deux pays dans les domaines universitaire , culturel, artistique, scientifique et technique.  un Programme d'Application de l'Accord Culturel entre le Gouvernement du Royaume du Maroc et le Gouvernement de la République de Côte d'Ivoire a été  pour les années 2010, 2011 et 2012 Ainsi les parties ont  convenu de ce qui suit: -Chacune des Parties organise sur le territoire de l'autre Partie des manifestations culturelles destinées à faire connaître les aspects de sa culture, notamment par des représentations théâtrales, musicales et de danse, des expositions d'œuvres  d'art, patrimoniales, de livres et de photographies. -Les Parties encouragent l'échange d'informations et de publications dans les domaines du patrimoine, des arts, du livre, des bibliothèques et des institutions culturelles. -Les Parties encouragent la coopération dans le domaine de l'édition et la promotion de partenariat entre les éditeurs marocains et ivoiriens. -Les Parties encouragent les expositions artistiques réciproques dans chaque pays. -Les Parties échangent les expériences dans le domaine de la médiation culturelle.  Les Parties favorisent la coopération directe entre la Bibliothèque Nationale du Royaume du Maroc et' la Bibliothèque Nationale de Côte d'Ivoire, notamment par l'échange de publications nationales et des listes bib1iographiques. -Les Parties encouragent la participation réciproque aux manifestations culturelles internationales et régionales, organisées dans chacun des deux pays et procèdent à l'échange d'informations et de documentations relatives à ces manifestation. -Les Parties encouragent et facilitent le séjour de leurs artistes sur le territoire de l'un ou de l'autre. Sur la base de cet accord et depuis lors, deux coopérations se sont développées. Il s'agit de:  -l'Accord de coproduction et d’échanges cinématographiques entre le Centre Cinématographique Marocain et l’Office National de Cinéma de Côte d’Ivoire (ONAC-CI) ; -la  Convention de Coopération entre la Bibliothèque Nationale du Royaume du Maroc et la Bibliothèque Nationale de Côte d’Ivoire. Ii ressort de cet accord les actions suivantes: - les échange d’experts dans le domaine de la technologie électronique pour la réalisation des travaux du fonds documentaire, conservation et restauration des documents ; -les parties mettent en œuvre les moyens nécessaires à la réalisation de programmes de formation ainsi que des activités scientifiques, pédagogiques et culturels ; - le développement de l’assistance technique dans le domaine de l’ingénierie informatique, du catalogage et de la numérisation de leur fonds documentaire et cinématographique. II est prévu en septembre 2024 la participation à la semaine du cinéma ivoirien au Maroc dans le cadre de cette coopération bilatérale.
Results: Les résultats atteints jusqu’à présent grâce à la mise en œuvre de la politique sont : - La consolidation des relations entre le Royaume du Maroc et la République de Côte d’Ivoire, a permis au Centre Cinématographique Marocain et l’Office National de Cinéma de Côte d’Ivoire de réaliser la 4ème édition de la Semaine du Film Ivoirien au Maroc, précisément à Tanger ;  -Rencontre des festivaliers ivoiriens au Maroc, opportunité pour les professionnels des deux pays de se rencontrer et de discuter des futurs projets de coopération et de coproduction.
Financial Ressources: Environ 57 190 USD par an.
Recommandations: La mise en œuvre de cette politique a permis d’améliorer le secteur de l’audiovisuel et cinématographique. Aussi, elle a également permis de moderniser et professionnaliser l’industrie cinématographique à travers l’harmonisation de la politique culturelle ivoirienne avec le Maroc. Elle a en plus favorisé le progrès et le renforcement de la formation aux outils numériques  et informatiques  favorable pour les deux parties.

Title EN: ACCORD DE COOPERATION CULTURELLE ENTRE LA REPUBLIQUE DE COTE D'IVOIRE  ET LE BURKINA FASO
Goal: Achieve A Balanced Flow Of Cultural Goods And Services And Increase The Mobility Of Artists And Cultural Professionals
SDG: SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 10 - Reduce inequality within and among countries,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Treaties and agreements
Cultural Domain: Design,Performing Arts,Media Arts,Cinema and Audiovisual Arts,Music,Publishing,Visual Arts
Agency Implementation: MINISTERE DE LA CULTURE ET DE LA FRANCOPHONIE DIRECTION DES AFFAIRES JURIDIQUES ET DE LA COOPERATION (DAJC)
Main Feature: dans le cadre de la mise en œuvre de cet Accord, un programme d’Echanges Culturels pour les années 2021-2024 entre le Gouvernement de la République de Côte d’Ivoire et le Gouvernement du Burkina Faso a été établit.  Il ressort de ce programme les activités suivantes : -organisation d’une foire culturelle et artistique (exposition-vente de produits artisanaux, défilés de mode, projection de films, gastronomie) destinée à faire connaitre les aspects de la culture de chaque Partie à travers une conférence en marge du sommet du Traité d’Amitié et de Coopération (TAC) ; -échanges d’informations et de publications dans les domaines du patrimoine, des arts, du livre, de l’archéologie, des industries culturelles et créatives, bibliothèques, festivals et manifestations à caractère national et international ; - collaboration et les échanges entre les réseaux de lectures publiques des deux pays et le renforcement de capacité et le partage d’expérience ; -organisation de journées cinématographiques et facilitation des coproductions cinématographiques, télévisuelles et audiovisuelles.  dans le cadre de cette coopération, plusieurs autres accord ont été signés dans les années 2018_2019 :  il s'agit  des quatre (04) accords suivants signés à Yamoussoukro, le 27 juillet 2018,   -l’accord de coopération dans les domaines de l’économie numérique et de la poste permet aux parties de partager les expériences et de procéder à l’interconnexion des infrastructures de communication électronique;  -l’accord concernant la Jeunesse est relatif à l’opérationnalisation du Fonds de l’amitié et de la coopération ivoiro-burkinabè pour l’insertion des jeunes (FACIBIJ, d’une valeur de 200 millions de FCfa. Chacun des deux pays apportant 100 millions de FCfa.  -Un autre accord porte sur la mise en œuvre du Fonds de l’amitié et de la coopération ivoiro-burkinabè pour la promotion de la femme (FACIBF). Pour alimenter ce fonds, il est prévu une contribution annuelle de 250 millions de FCfA par pays soit .408 496,73 Usd   -Enfin, l’accord dans le secteur de l’audiovisuel met l’accent sur la co-production, la formation et les échanges cinématographiques et audiovisuels. Ces accords ont été signés lors du sommet de  7ème Conférence du Sommet du Traité d’Amitié et de Coopération (TAC) ivoiro-burkinabè
Results: La mise en œuvre de cette politique a favorisé des interactions entre les administrations publiques des Etats et des acteurs privés. Elle a favorisé le partage des savoirs, des savoirs faires dans les domaines cinématographiques (productions communes, échange d’acteurs…), des arts plastiques (participation des artistes burkinabés au Salon International des Arts Plastiques ; le livre (participation d’écrivains burkinabé au Salon International du Livre d’Abidjan). Du côté du Burkina, on retiendra les premières journées culturelles à Ouagadougou ; la présence d’une forte délégation ivoirienne au Festival Panafricain du Cinéma de Ouagadougou (FESPACO) ; participation effective des artisans, acteurs du monde de la culture et des arts ivoiriens aux différentes éditions du Salon International de Ouagadougou (SIAO).
Financial Ressources: Plus de 408497 USD
Recommandations: La mise en œuvre de cette politique a renforcé davantage la coopération culturelle entre les deux Etats. Elle a également  contribué au renforcement des capacités en matière de culture  tout en suscitant la solidarité mutuelle.

Title EN: Action Plan for Gender Equality
Goal: Promote Human Rights And Fundamental Freedoms
SDG: SDG 5 - Achieve gender equality and empower all women and girls,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels
Area of Monitoring: Gender equality
Cultural Domain: Design,Performing Arts,Media Arts,Cinema and Audiovisual Arts,Music,Publishing,Visual Arts
Agency Implementation: Commission for Citizenship and Gender Equality (CIG)
Main Feature: Ensure governance that integrates the fight against gender discrimination and the promotion of equality between women and men (IMH) into policies and actions. In 2023, three fundamental Action Plans were approved in the National Strategy for Equality and Non-Discrimination which will be in force in the period 2023-2026. This national strategy follows from the one approved in 2018, which had its first cycle until 2021 and which was subject to an external evaluation in 2022. Thus, in addition to the Action Plan for equality between women and men (PAIMH) two more action plans were created (for the prevention and combat of violence against women and domestic violence and for combating discrimination on grounds of sexual orientation, gender identity and expression, and sexual characteristics). The PAIMH aims to guarantee governance that integrates the combat against discrimination based on sex and the promotion of equality between women and men (IMH) in policies and actions. This includes strengthening the mechanisms that promote this perspective in Public Administration, guaranteeing statistical information disaggregated by sex, integrating the IMH perspective in international relations and cooperation, guaranteeing conditions for education and training free from gender stereotypes, supporting production of scientific knowledge that allows expanding and deepening (multi)disciplinary knowledge about women and men and about the level of equality between each other, in all social areas, guaranteeing the conditions for full and equal participation of women and men in the labor market and professional activity, promoting IMH in the labor market, prevention and combat violence and harassment in the labor market and professional activities, produce and disseminate knowledge and information about conciliation policies and programs, ensure protection and empowerment of women and people in situations of social and economic vulnerability, promoting IMH and nondiscrimination in culture and communication sectors, preventing sexist content in all public spaces of formal and informal communication and promoting IMH and non discrimination in culture and in the creative industries.
Results: The plan is still being implemented. It was the subject of an external evaluation in 2022 albeit no hard data was presented. The preliminary conclusions are as follows: ‘In short, this policy cycle represented a paradigmatic leap in gender equality and non-discrimination policies, whether in the challenges and directions highlighted, or in the ways in which they were actions to comply with them. It is therefore important to continue this commitment and investment, providing the CIG with greater capacity for implementation and monitoring and maintaining recognition and appreciation of the need to move towards a fairer, more egalitarian and exempt Portuguese society any form of violence or discrimination.

Title EN: Accord de co-production audiovisuelle avec le Canada
Goal: Achieve A Balanced Flow Of Cultural Goods And Services And Increase The Mobility Of Artists And Cultural Professionals
SDG: SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 10 - Reduce inequality within and among countries,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Treaties and agreements
Agency Implementation: Office fédéral de la culture OFC
Main Feature: Cet accord signé le 3 novembre 2023 (et qui entrera prochainement en vigueur) actualise les conditions de coproduction entre la Suisse et le Canada. Les films coproduits dans le cadre de cet accord bénéficient d'un financement facilité et de meilleures modalités de diffusion dans les deux pays. L'accord permet par ailleurs de financer de nouveaux modèles de coproduction, par exemple pour les séries, et améliore les échanges et la collaboration des professionnelles et des professionnels du cinéma sur des projets communs. L'accueil de tournages de coproductions en Suisse est également facilité, ce qui aura des répercussions favorables pour différents secteurs. L'obligation d'investissement applicable dès 2024 aux plateformes de streaming et aux chaînes de télévision, avec l'entrée en vigueur de la loi révisée sur le cinéma, devrait également favoriser le financement des coproductions helvético-canadiennes
Results: Ce nouvel accord remplace l'accord de coproduction signé le 7 avril 1987 et consolide les relations culturelles et linguistiques entre les deux pays. Au cours des dix dernières années, la Suisse et le Canada ont réalisé six coproductions, pour un budget total de plus de 21,3 millions de dollars américains.

Goal: Achieve A Balanced Flow Of Cultural Goods And Services And Increase The Mobility Of Artists And Cultural Professionals
SDG: SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 10 - Reduce inequality within and among countries,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Treaties and agreements
Agency Implementation: Centre national du cinéma et de l’image animée (CNC)
Main Feature: La conclusion de ces accords contribue à développer la coopération culturelle bilatérale entre la France et ses partenaires afin d’encourager la coproduction d’œuvres sur la base d’une coopération artistique et financière ainsi que la coopération dans différents domaines comme la conservation du patrimoine cinématographique, l’éducation à l’image, la lutte contre le piratage, la formation, l’expertise, la diffusion, etc.  •	7 accords de coproduction cinématographique conclus depuis 2020 avec : le Canada (nouvel accord couvrant le cinéma, l’audiovisuel et les services de médias audiovisuels à la demande) et la Macédoine du nord en 2021, la Grèce, l’Irlande, le Kosovo et le Sénégal en 2022, et le Maroc (nouvel accord) en 2024, portant à 61 le nombre total d’accords bilatéraux de coproduction de la France.  •	19 accords de coopération conclus depuis 2020 avec : le Québec (nouvelle convention) et le Nigeria en 2020, la Tunisie en 2021, l’Albanie, le Kazakhstan et les Philippines en 2022, l’Albanie, la Corée et Taïwan en 2023, l’Arménie, l’Arabie Saoudite, le Brésil, la Corée, la Chine, Hong Kong, le Kazakhstan, le Kirghizistan, le Monténégro et l’Ouzbékistan en 2024

Title EN: Ibero-American Cultural Cooperation
Goal: Integrate Culture In Sustainable Development Frameworks
SDG: SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: International cooperation for sustainable development
Cultural Domain: Design,Performing Arts,Media Arts,Cinema and Audiovisual Arts,Music,Publishing,Visual Arts
Agency Implementation: Ministry of Culture
Main Feature: Ibero-American Cooperation is the way in which political agreements and commitments made by Ibero-American Heads of State and Government at Summits are transformed into concrete actions. It is a unique model of cooperation, thanks to its multidimensional and multi-actor regional approach and a flexible and horizontal project in which participation is voluntary and countries participate according to their national priorities. Furthermore, it is based on solidarity, which strengthens the community formed by the 22 countries and which, through joint actions, contributes to the socioeconomic and sustainable development of the region.  Ibero-American Cooperation is characterized by seeking concrete results that directly affect the strengthening of national sectoral public policies. These results are achieved through intergovernmental political dialogue based on technical cooperation (exchange of good practices, creation of networks, participation in political dialogue with those who make decisions, training) and financial cooperation (through, for example, competitive funds) to provide more and better responses to the needs of Ibero-American citizenship.  Among the main instruments of Ibero-American Cooperation are the Adscribed Programs, Initiatives and Projects, fundamentally focused on three priority areas: knowledge, culture and social cohesion. In the Culture and Sustainable Development Axis, the Ibero-American Cultural Space of the Ibero-American General Secretariat (SEGIB) articulates 14 existing Cultural Cooperation Programs and Initiatives, of which Brazil participates in nine, namely:  IberArchives - Support Program for the Development of Ibero-American Archives. Created in 1998, it is an initiative of cooperation and integration of Ibero-American countries to promote access, organization, description, conservation and dissemination of documentary heritage. The program, which currently has the participation of 16 countries, strengthens the capabilities of professionals in the field, and has a financial fund that supports projects submitted to annual competitions for aid for archival projects.  IberLibraries – Created in 2000 and reformulated in 2011, the Program brings together 11 countries around the objective of promoting free access for all citizens to reading, information and knowledge. Actions are developed to modernize and strengthen libraries in Ibero-America, make the most of technology and promote democratic access to support the development of public library networks or systems, as well as give visibility to the impact that libraries have on building societies democracy and strengthening the social fabric.  Ibercena – Created in 2006, the Program currently brings together 17 participating countries and its mission is to promote the exchange, creation and professionalization of Ibero-American performing arts, stimulating their circulation, co-production, research and dissemination. Among its objectives is also the effective consolidation of gender equality in the field of performing arts in the Ibero-American space.  IberCultura Viva – Created in 2013 and currently covering 11 countries, the Program’s objectives are: promote the development of public policies that strengthen community cultures; promote consensus, alliances and exchanges for joint action between the various governmental social agents; promote the creation and dissemination of cultural content, preferably multilingual; expand and guarantee access to the means of production, enjoyment and dissemination of culture; favor the development of a cooperative, supportive and transformative culture, by strengthening the capacity for community organization; and use artistic languages, symbols and cultural living spaces to stimulate critical reflection and the construction of citizenship.  Ibermedia – With 21 countries, the Program was created in 1995 with the aim of promoting the integration of Ibero-American companies in order to contribute to the creation of its own audiovisual space in the region. Actions are developed to support the exchange of industry professionals, through financial aid and technical assistance for the co-production of films for cinema, TV and other media, with independent producers as the main beneficiaries. Other actions support the initial assembly of projects, the distribution and promotion of audiovisual products in the regional market, as well as the training of human resources.  Ibermuseums – Created in 2007, the Program has the participation of 14 countries and aims to contribute to the articulation of public museological policies in Iberoamerica, favoring the sustainable development and regional integration of museums.  IberMusic – Ibero-American Music Promotion Program. Aiming to foster the presence and knowledge of Ibero-American musical diversity, stimulate the formation of new audiences in the region, and expand the job market for professionals in the sector, the IberMúsicas Program was created in 2011 and has the participation of 15 countries.  Iber-Routes – Strengthening Routes of Rights and Interculturality in Ibero-American Migration. Created in 2010, the Program brings together nine countries around the proposal to contribute to the promotion of cultural diversity in Ibero-America through the creation of a common space to protect the rights of migrants, from a cultural perspective.
Results: IberArchives: Between 2020 and 2022, the Program supported 63 projects aimed at archives and documentation centers in Ibero-America, with an investment of more than 500 thousand Euros (USD$548,050.00).  IberLibraries – Since 2012, the Program has held an annual Call for Help aimed at public, popular and community libraries in member countries and cities. In 2019, 12 projects were supported; 18 in 2020 and 4 projects in 2021. Each year, the Program selects an event of interest to Ibero-American librarians and supports the visit of participants from each of the member countries, as well as selecting a member country to carry out internships. In 2022, IberBibliotecas supported the participation of 12 librarians in the 7th Meeting of Popular and Community Libraries, held in Medellin, Colombia. In 2023, the Program supported the participation of 20 librarians in the 5th Iberbibliotecas International Internship, held in Bogotá, Colombia.  Ibercena – The Program has a Support Fund for Ibero-American Performing Arts, with three lines of support: Support for the Co-production of Performing Arts Shows; Support for Creation in Residence; and Support for the Programming of Festivals and Scenic Spaces. In 2023, of a total of 605 applications submitted, 136 received support, of which: 31 for creation in residence; 46 for co-production of shows; and 59 for programming festivals and scenic spaces. The sum to be distributed by the program is 1,092,073.57 Euros (USD$1,197,021.8401).  IberCultura Viva [Living Culture] – The Program works with several lines of action: scholarships, mobility support, competitions, knowledge bank and synergies. In the period from 2020 to 2023, 367 scholarships were awarded through a public notice for the International Postgraduate Course in Community-Based Cultural Policies at the Latin American Faculty of Social Sciences – FLACSO. In the same period, 129 supports were granted, totaling USD$464 thousand, to networks and collaborative work projects of community cultural organizations, indigenous peoples and Afro-descendant communities interested in holding events with at least two other organizations or collectives from Program member countries. Still in the same period, the Program promoted the “Community Migrant Flavors” competition every year, through which 56 stories of recipes and culinary practices from migrant communities in Ibero-America were awarded, with a total investment of USD$2,200. In 2022, the Mobility Notice supported the participation of 61 representatives of civil society organizations in Latin American Living Community Culture congresses, covering the costs of airline tickets, travel insurance and registration fees. The amount of resources was USD$57.5 thousand.  Ibermedia – Since its creation, the Program has supported, through calls for proposals, around 2,500 films that received funding for co-production, development and cinematographic promotion and dissemination. The Program also allowed a large number of women to join the cinema industry in key creative, directing and producing positions. In the area of training, Ibermédia granted more than three thousand scholarships to Ibero-American filmmakers to participate in workshops and development courses for screenwriters and directors, as well as specialization programs for producers and entrepreneurs, which contributed to strengthening and expanding the audiovisual sector in Ibero-America.  Ibermuseums – The Program operates on three axes: research, action and promotion. The Ibero-American Museum Observatory encourages research and improvement in the management of institutions and museum processes in the region. The Observatory's work resulted in the production of five major projects, generating publications, courses and the Registry of Ibero-American Museums, a repository that collects data from the museological panorama of 19 countries and plans, in the medium term, to involve the more than nine thousand museums that make up the museum heritage of 22 Ibero-American countries. In 2022, the 10th edition of the Ibero-American Meeting of Museums was held, which contributes to regional integration by promoting the exchange of experiences between museums and strengthening actions to preserve cultural heritage and memory. In the area of Training and Training, the Program enables the strengthening of professional capabilities, exchange and dissemination between museums, in addition to promoting an important incentive: the Ibermuseum Training Scholarships, which since 2016 has been offering economic aid to museum workers of the Program's member countries, can carry out training activities in other museums throughout the Ibero-American region. The main project of the Education line is the Ibermuseums Education Award: in 10 editions, 114 projects carried out by education teams from public, private or mixed museums in Ibero-America were recognized and promoted.  IberMusic – In 2023, the Program granted aid, through a notice, among others, to: 113 projects in the music sector from 14 countries for circulation in Ibero-American countries, with a total investment of USD$474,557; three musical projects for circulation in the United States (USD$15 thousand); 23 projects for programming, totaling USD$94,562); 16 composers for residency (USD$36,302.00); support for 5 institutions, organizations and groups for artistic residencies for composers (USD$12 thousand); assistance to 17 musicians for specialization and artistic and technical improvement (USD$58,631).  Iber-Rotas – Through its Program Assistance Fund, called Maleta Aberta, the Iber-Rotas Program promotes the development of socio-cultural activities that involve migrant communities, as well as the strengthening and respect for the diversity of cultural expressions. Between 2016 and 2020, 33 projects were supported. The Program seeks to facilitate the cultural diversity of Ibero-America through artistic calls, and awarded 14 prizes and 11 mentions in photography competitions between 2013 and 2018, and 18 prizes and 6 mentions for essays between 2014 and 2020.

Title EN: ADR - The Atlantic Drums Route
Goal: Achieve A Balanced Flow Of Cultural Goods And Services And Increase The Mobility Of Artists And Cultural Professionals
SDG: SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 10 - Reduce inequality within and among countries,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Treaties and agreements
Agency Implementation: Camões - Institute for Cooperation and Language
Main Feature: The Atlantic Drums Route (ADR) project aims to foster intercultural dialogue and inclusion through the creation of a cultural, educational, and tourism route centered around Atlantic drums. The project seeks to revive, preserve, and renew the symbolic capital of these traditional percussion instruments while promoting the socioeconomic development of associated communities. Focusing on the shared intangible heritage between Africa and Latin America, ADR endeavors to create significant social impacts. This initiative includes gathering historical, musical, and cultural data, developing community and organizational networks, and enhancing income opportunities, especially for women, through tourism and craftsmanship. The project is implemented in pilot regions of Angola, Guinea-Bissau, Brazil, and Colombia, with funding from an agreement between OEI Portugal and Camões, I.P., and is designed to span two years. By integrating these cultural practices into broader tourism and educational frameworks, ADR aims to establish sustainable cultural routes that benefit both local communities and international visitors.
Results: The Atlantic Drums Route has made notable progress since its inception. The project has successfully gathered and mapped extensive historical, social, and cultural information on Atlantic drums, creating a rich repository of knowledge that supports the project's objectives. In the pilot regions, community engagement and sensitization initiatives have been well-received, with local authorities and communities actively participating in the project's activities. Training programs have been conducted, enhancing the skills and capacities of local artisans, musicians, and community organizations. Moreover, initial partnerships with cultural and tourism operators have been established, laying the groundwork for sustainable tourism routes. Although still in its early stages, the project has already fostered greater awareness and appreciation of the cultural heritage of Atlantic drums, and has begun to create new economic opportunities for local communities, particularly for women involved in the production and sale of traditional crafts.

Title EN: Achèvement des travaux de création de l’Institut national supérieur de musique et des arts chorégraphiques
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture
SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Cultural and creative sectors
Agency Implementation: Département de la Culture
Main Feature: Le Département de la Culture a lancé en 2019 les travaux de construction  de l'Institut National Supérieur de Musique et des Arts Chorégraphiques qui constitue un véritable programme qui englobe un site, une culture et un pays. Ce projet a réussi à relever le défi de s'adapter à un site riche en contraintes positives grâce à sa morphologie, sa situation et son patrimoine historique. Il s'intègre également harmonieusement dans une ville, Rabat, connue pour sa capacité à marier tradition et modernité architecturale. L'Institut se veut un lieu dédié à la liberté du corps et de l'esprit, abritant l'Institut National Supérieur de Musique et des Arts Chorégraphiques, l'Institut Supérieur de Formation des Cadres en Musique, ainsi que la Recherche Musicale et Chorégraphique. Conçu pour accueillir 300 élèves, l'Institut est organisé en trois catégories d'espaces : les espaces d'enseignement et de formation, les espaces artistiques et musicaux, et les espaces logistiques. Le bâtiment se compose de différentes entités regroupées en un îlot convivial, capable d'accueillir diverses manifestations culturelles. En plus de son architecture inspirée de l'histoire locale, le projet intègre des espaces verts abondants, dissimulant deux niveaux de parkings ventilés et éclairés naturellement par des puits de lumière. Ce projet est une synthèse de fonctionnalité, technicité et spiritualité, ancrée dans un profond respect de l'histoire de la région.
Results: Lancement du décret de création et d'organisation de l'INSMAC

Title EN: Arts Council’s Policies relating to Human Rights, Equality, Diversity and Inclusion
Goal: Promote Human Rights And Fundamental Freedoms
SDG: SDG 5 - Achieve gender equality and empower all women and girls,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels
Area of Monitoring: Gender equality
Agency Implementation: Arts Council
Main Feature: In 2019, the Arts Council published its Equality, Human Rights, and Diversity (EHRD) Policy and Strategy. The policy is designed to build on a range of existing Arts Council work areas, including an Arts and Disability Policy, a Cultural Diversity and the Arts policy and a Dignity at Work policy. Title EN: Act Relating to the Sale of Books (the Book Act)
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture
SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Cultural and creative sectors
Agency Implementation: Norwegian Ministry of Culture and Equality
Main Feature: In June 2023, the Norwegian Parliament adopted a new Book Act. The legislation entered into force on 1 January 2024. The purpose of the Act is to facilitate breadth, diversity and quality in Norwegian literature and to ensure good accessibility to literature. The act shall also contribute to facilitating freedom of speech and the written culture in Bokmål, Nynorsk, the indigenous Sami languages and the national minority languages (Kven, Romani and Romanes).  The Book Act includes measures such as mandatory fixed prices for new books, the use of standard contracts for authors, illustrators and translators, and an obligation for retailers and suppliers to procure and supply all books which are available for sale. The measures aim to facilitate the production of a diversity of books in Norway, as well as ensuring that literature is accessible to consumers in all parts of the country. The core of the Book Act is the establishment of a fixed price for each publishing format of new books, such as hardcover, paperback, e-book, and audiobook. The fixed price, determined by publishers, will apply for 12 months from the first time the book format is published. The fixed price ensures the financial basis for the authors and the industry, so that they can create, publish and sell a wide variety of quality literature. The fixed price also ensures the existence of booksellers in smaller places, where selling books might otherwise not be profitable.   Furthermore, the Book Act aims to facilitate access to the latest audiobooks during the fixed-price period, as streaming services will also be required to offer audiobooks for individual sale. While audiobook sales have witnessed substantial growth, not all audiobooks have been available on the different streaming platforms. The selection has varied from platform to platform. The new act will make it easier to access all books, including those subject to fixed prices.
Results: The Act introduced a change in the book market as it introduced rights and obligations which apply to all retailers and suppliers on the Norwegian market trading books within the scope of the Act. This is a change to the previous agreement based conditions (the Book Agreement), which only applied to retailers and suppliers belonging to one of the two largest trade organisations for publishers and book sellers. As the act regulates the book market, the provisions of the act concerns all stakeholders in the market i.a. writers, illustrators, translators, publishers, book sellers and consumers. The act balances the interests of the various stakeholders and will provide predictable and stable economical conditions for authors, publishers, and booksellers
Financial Ressources: The Book Act is a legislative initiative, intended to regulate the book market. No financial resources have been allocated directly towards the measure.  However, several other measures intended to fulfil the same policy aims as the book act have been allocated financial resources. Examples are purchasing schemes, where the Government purchases a certain number of copies of selected titles every year, for distribution to Norwegian libraries. Other important instruments are exemptions from value-added tax, and compensation for the use of works through the Public Lending Right. Additionally, the state support various promotional activities connected to literature and reading and grants for authors.

Title EN: Action plan on universal design  2021 - 2025
Goal: Integrate Culture In Sustainable Development Frameworks
SDG: SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: National sustainable development policies and plans
Agency Implementation: Ministry of Culture and Equality/ The Norwegian Directorate for Children, Youth and Family Affairs (Bufdir)
Main Feature: The Norwegian government's vision is a society in which everyone can participate. Opportunities for everyone and the freedom to live their own lives are only ensured through a fair and sustainable society. Universal design strengthens and frees human resources with positive results for the individual and for society. It is a strategy that ensures a sustainable and equal society through the design of physical and technical surroundings. Universal design is important for the daily life of all residents, both as consumers of transport, housing and communication. People with functional impairments particularly benefit from the increased accessibility and usability of the surroundings that universal design provides.   The current Action plan on universal design  2021 - 2025 is the fourth in a series of action plans on universal design. There has been a significant and positive development of both policy and practice since the first plan was launched in 2004. Universal design has been established as a desired and necessary quality that affects people's everyday life through simpler, safer and more comfortable environments that contribute to a sustainable society both socially, economically and environmentally.    Within cultural environment management, universal design means that cultural monuments and cultural environments are made accessible to as many people as possible. This involves among others physical arrangements for visits. Important cultural monuments and cultural environments are universally designed as far as this can be done without significant architectural or cultural historical values being lost.  The Norwegian Directorate for Cultural Heritage has guidance material with several examples of universal design of cultural-historical buildings and facilities. The Directorate published a new guide on the universal design of interiors in 2021. Several municipalities also have their own guides on the universal design of buildings and cultural environments. Universal design in a listed building must be assessed based on the individual building's tolerance for change.

Title EN: Adhésion au programme Europe Créative : une locomotive pour la promotion de la diversité des expressions culturelles en Tunisie
Goal: Integrate Culture In Sustainable Development Frameworks
SDG: SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: International cooperation for sustainable development
Cultural Domain: Design,Performing Arts,Media Arts,Cinema and Audiovisual Arts,Music,Publishing,Visual Arts
Agency Implementation: Le Ministère des affaires culturelles, Le desk Europe Créative -Tunisie
Main Feature: Europe Créative est un programme phare de l’Union Européenne (UE) pour les secteurs culturels et créatifs. Avec un budget de 2.44 Mds d’euros pour la deuxième phase (2021-2027) contre 1,46 Mds d’euros pour la première phase (2018-2020), il investit dans des actions qui renforcent la diversité culturelle et répondent aux besoins et aux défis majeurs des secteurs de la culture et de la création et se compose de trois sous-programmes : ▪ Sous-programme Culture dédié aux professionnels de la culture et de la création (spectacle vivant, art contemporain, musiques, patrimoine, etc.). Il soutient, à travers la coopération, la mise en réseau et le développement de plateformes, des projets innovants portés par des structures professionnelles;  ▪ Sous-programme media visant à encourager le développement de l’industrie de l’audiovisuel, du cinéma et des jeux vidéo. Il soutient financièrement le développement, la distribution et la promotion de projets portés par des professionnels (producteurs, distributeurs, agents de vente, organismes de formation et d’évènements...);  ▪ Volet intersectoriel : il englobe le réseau des bureaux Europe Créative ainsi qu’un mécanisme de garantie financière.  Les principaux objectifs du programme sont les suivants : •	Préserver, développer et promouvoir la diversité et le patrimoine culturels, •	Stimuler l’émergence et le développement de la diversité artistique et culturelle, •	Accroître la compétitivité et le potentiel économique des secteurs de la culture et de la création, •	Développer davantage la création transnationale et l’innovation, •	Garantir un accès plus aisé au financement de projets culturels grâce à des mécanismes de cofinancement, •	Promouvoir la mobilité des artistes, professionnels et praticien (nes) de la culture, •	Accroitre les actions ciblant les besoins de secteurs créatifs spécifiques, tels que la musique, l’architecture et le patrimoine culturel. La Tunisie est le seul pays arabe et africain du bassin méditerranéen qui a adhéré au programme Europe Créative en 2017 et ce en vertu de la loi organique n° 2017-56 du 10 août 2017, portant approbation de l’accord conclu le 11 mai 2017, entre la République Tunisienne et l’union européenne sur la participation de la République Tunisienne au programme de l’union «Europe créative pour le soutien aux secteurs culturels et créatifs » et sur la coopération entre la République Tunisienne et l’union européenne concernant le sous-programme MEDIA du programme Europe créative.  Les dispositions de ce partenariat international avec l’UE, stipulent que la Tunisie bénéficie, exclusivement et pour la première année d’adhésion (2018) du privilège d’adhérer à ce programme pour la somme symbolique de 1 euro, au lieu des 250.000 euros que chaque pays membre est appelé à payer, comme ticket d’entrée, pour faire partie de l’Europe créative. Par ailleurs et en vertu d’un accord entre la DUE et le MAC, la DUE effectue une ristourne annuelle équivalente à 50% du ticket d’adhésion de la Tunisie à Europe Créative. Cette ristourne prend la forme d’un appui budgétaire à l’Etat tunisien. Ce privilège peut être considéré comme un traitement préférentiel en vertu de l’article 16 de la convention 2005 (qui stipule que « Les pays développés facilitent les échanges culturels avec les pays en développement en accordant, au moyen de cadres institutionnels et juridiques appropriés, un traitement préférentiel à leurs artistes et autres professionnels et praticiens de la culture, ainsi qu’à leurs biens et services culturels ».) En 2022 la Tunisie a renouvelé son adhésion au programme dans sa deuxième phase 2021-2027 (signature par le MAC de convention en 2022). Les acteurs culturels tunisiens (les associations, les organisations de la société civile et les entreprises créatives) bénéficient des mêmes avantages que leurs homologues européens en matière d’appels d’offres et subventions dans le cadre de ce programme. Les objectifs spécifiques du programme pour la Tunisie sont les suivants: •	Promotion de la diplomatie culturelle tunisienne •	Renforcement de l’apport économique des industries culturelles et créatives en Tunisie •	Appui aux projets internationaux pour la société civile tunisienne  Par ailleurs, des bureaux d’information Europe Créative (Creative Europe Desks) ont été constitués dans tous les pays participants au programme. Ils ont pour mission d’informer les acteurs des secteurs culturels et créatifs (Culture, média) sur les possibilités offertes par le programme et de les accompagner dans leurs démarches. Creative Europe Desk -Tunisie auprès des professionnels dans le domaine culturel et créatif a été lancé le 8 février 2018 ; il a pour mission la promotion des programmes communautaires ouverts à la culture et à l’audiovisuel, principalement Europe Créative. Il assure une aide technique pour la confection des dossiers de candidature et à la recherche de partenaires. Un lien est assuré par ce desk avec le réseau européen des Creative Europe Desks (CED), ainsi qu’avec d’autres institutions et acteurs culturels. Des séances d’information et de travail sont organisées sur le programme Europe Créative et la coopération européenne. Le desk Tunisie a également pour mission la diffusion d’informations sur l’actualité culturelle et sur les programmes communautaires.
Results: Le bilan du programme Europe Créative Tunisie (2018-2020) totalise 12 projets sélectionnés (parmi un total de 46 projets présentés) et 39 structures issues de 15 pays européens qui ont collaboré avec la Tunisie.  Ces douze projets, ont bénéficié de financements de l’ordre de 2 millions DT pour la période de 2018 à 2020 (soit 655.196 €) avec un taux de réussite des dossiers présentés de 26%. Ces projets appartiennent au sous-programme «culture» et au programme «média» qui sont les principaux sous-programmes d’Europe créative Tunisie et sont détaillés comme suit : •	2018: 03 projets retenus avec participation tunisienne (sur 16 présentés) avec un montant total des financements de 48.995 euro. •	2019: 05 projets retenus avec participation tunisienne (sur 16 présentés et dont deux chef de fil) avec un montant total des financements de 427.167 euro. •	2020 : 04 projets retenus avec participation tunisienne (sur 14 présentés) avec un montant total des financements de 179.033 euro.  Le bilan du programme Europe Créative Tunisie (2022-2023) totalise 07 projets sélectionnés (parmi un total de 35 projets présentés) ayant bénéficié d'un financement de l'ordre de 537.941€ détaillés comme suit : •	2022: 04 projets retenus avec participation tunisienne (sur 13 présentés) avec un montant total des financements de 335.495 euro. •	2023: 03 projets retenus avec participation tunisienne (sur 22 présentés) avec un montant total des financements de 202.446 euro. Au-delà des subventions reçues, l’adhésion de la Tunisie au programme Europe Créative a permis aux structures culturelles tunisiennes (OSC, secteur privé…) d’accéder, au même titre que les structures européennes:  ▪ À 51 réseaux professionnels visant à renforcer la capacité des structures culturelles à opérer au niveau transnational et international et à s’adapter au changement ;  ▪ À plus de 20 plateformes visant à présenter et promouvoir les créateurs et artistes des pays membres, tout particulièrement des talents émergents, grâce à une véritable programmation ;  ▪ À la plateforme européenne de diplomatie culturelle ;  ▪ Au programme de mobilité des artistes i-Portunus  L’intégration du volet écologique dans les projets culturels, la valorisation de la liberté d’expression, la participation à la cohésion sociale et l’appui à la digitalisation sont des valeurs prioritaires pour l’UE, partagées avec la Tunisie et renforcées dans le cadre du programme Europe Créative. Ce sont aussi des volets préconisés par la convention de 2005 qui incite les états membres à mettre en place des mesures dans le but de : •	Réaffirmer l’importance du lien entre culture et développement pour tous les pays, en particulier les pays en développement, et d’encourager les actions menées aux plans national et international pour que soit reconnue la véritable valeur de ce lien ;  •	Renforcer la coopération et la solidarité internationales dans un esprit de partenariat afin, notamment, d’accroître les capacités des pays en développement de protéger et promouvoir la diversité des expressions culturelles  Le bilan des actions du desk en 2019 totalise 04 sessions d’information et 30 réunions Front desk ayant profité à plus de 150 acteurs culturels.
Financial Ressources: 2 millions DT pour la période de 2018 à 2020 (soit 655.196 €) et 537.941€  pour la période 2022-2023
Recommandations: Au-delà d’un simple mécanise de financement, Europe créative s’avère comme une véritable locomotive pour la promotion de la diversité des expressions culturelles en Tunisie ayant permis à travers la cible, les mécanismes de mise en œuvre et les moyens alloués de : •	Diversifier les sources de financement des projets culturels internationaux •	Renforcer la capacité des acteurs culturels tunisiens au niveau de la création, production, diffusion en vue d’une bonne mise en œuvre des projets culturels à impact économique et social durable •	Renforcer le réseautage professionnel pour la Tunisie en Europe

Main Feature: Suisseculture Sociale et la Fondation suisse pour la culture Pro Helvetia se sont données pour objectif de dresser l’état de la situation des actrices culturelles et des acteurs culturels en Suisse en matière de revenus, en portant une attention particulière à la protection sociale des différentes formes de travail au regard du droit suisse des assurances sociales. Il s’agit de mettre en évidence les difficultés que le système actuel des assurances sociales pose aux actrices culturelles et aux acteurs culturels lorsque celles-ci et ceux-ci cumulent de petits engagements, travaillent comme intermittentes et intermittents ou comme indépendantes et indépendants, ou pratiquent de multiples formes de travail, et d’élaborer des pistes de solution. Pour mener à bien cette analyse de la situation des actrices culturelles et acteurs culturels en Suisse, un mandat a été donné à Ecoplan, bureau de recherche et de conseil indépendant qui a rendu son rapport en juin 2021.
Results: L’étude d’Ecoplan s'est basée sur les données collectées à l’aide d’une enquête en ligne (auprès de quelque 1500 participantes et participants) et de neuf entretiens qualitatifs, afin d’analyser la situation des actrices culturelles et des acteurs culturels en matière de revenu et au regard du droit des assurances sociales. Les résultats de l’enquête ont montré que la situation des actrices culturelles et des acteurs culturels de Suisse était parfois précaire en raison du bas niveau des revenus et d’une protection sociale insuffisante.     L’analyse d’Ecoplan a permis d’identifier ou de confirmer les priorités suivantes :   -  Améliorer l’information et le conseil : il faut garantir la mise à disposition de davantage d’informations et de conseils plus ciblés concernant la protection sociale des actrices culturelles et des acteurs culturels ; de plus, les institutions telles que les caisses de compensation devraient mieux prendre en considération les conditions de travail spécifiques des actrices culturelles et des acteurs culturels.    - Assortir les subsides de conditions : l’octroi de subsides publics, à tous les niveaux, devrait être assorti de la condition que les actrices culturelles et les acteurs culturels soient tenus de payer des cotisations sociales sur tous leurs revenus, et puissent le faire, et que des directives contraignantes en matière de rémunération des actrices culturelles et des acteurs culturels soient définies et respectées.    - Trouver de nouvelles solutions pour les assurances sociales, et faire du secteur de la culture un secteur pilote : en raison du bas niveau des revenus dans le secteur de la culture, beaucoup d’actrices culturelles et d’acteurs culturels, mais aussi de plus en plus de travailleuses et de travailleurs d’autres secteurs, ne sont pas (ou plus) en mesure de payer des cotisations sociales, ou parfois s’en abstiennent délibérément.

Title EN: AI Act
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture
SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Digital environment
Cultural Domain: Design,Performing Arts,Media Arts,Cinema and Audiovisual Arts,Music,Publishing,Visual Arts
Agency Implementation: The Member States of the European Union; their relevant national authorities and the EU AI Office
Main Feature: The AI Act completes the EU regulatory toolbox with the aim to build an ecosystem of trust and promote uptake of human-centric and trust-worthy Artificial Intelligence. In this context, its provisions seek to guarantee the safety and fundamental rights of people and businesses when it comes to AI, by managing the risks and promoting innovation. The AI Act promotes innovation and uptake of AI tools that can support human creativity, while ensuring human-centric approach to AI and respect of European values.   The AI Act includes notably measures to facilitate enforcement of the EU copyright legislation. In particular, for general-purpose AI models, which are often trained on copyrighted material, the AI Act requires a policy to respect Union copyright law and transparency about the content used for the training. For general purpose AI models that have most impact on the market and pose systemic risks, the AI Act also requires providers of those models to address systemic risks, including biases. Furthermore, the AI Act  requires deployers of generative AI systems to clearly label ‘deep fakes’ as well as AI-generated text that is published for professional purposes on matters of public interest unless the text has been reviewed by a human and a natural or legal person holds editorial responsibility for the publication. Providers of generative AI systems should also implement in their systems state-of-the-art technical solutions such as watermarks, content provenance etc. that enable the marking and detection of the content in a machine-readable format.
Results: The AI Act entered into force on 1st August 2024 and its various provisions will start to apply in a staged approach. The rules on general-purpose AI models, including the copyright-related provisions, will become applicable on 2 August 2025, while the transparency and labelling obligations for generative AI systems and ‘deep fakes’ will apply as of 2 August 2026. To facilitate the implementation, the AI Office will provide a template for the public summary of the data used for the training of general-purpose AI models and coordinate the drafting of a code of practice for the implementation of the obligations with the involvement of general-purpose AI providers, other industry representatives, civil society organisations, rightsholders and academia. The AI Office has just launched a process for stakeholders’ expression of interest to participate in the drafting of the code and a multi-stakeholder consultation to provide stakeholder input to the process. The first Code of Practice must be finalised in April 2025 after which it will be assessed by the Commission and, if deemed adequate, the Commission can approve it and give it a general validity within the Union by means of an implementing act.For the rules on transparency of AI-generated content, the Commission will also provide guidance and facilitate the drawing up of a code of practice on identification of AI-generated content to be ready before the relevant rules becomes applicable on 2 August 2026.  The newly established EU AI Office as part of the European Commission (DG CNECT) will be solely responsible for the supervision and enforcement of the new rules on general-purpose AI models. It will have sufficient staff for these tasks and access to appropriate technical means, expertise and testing infrastructure.  In the exercise of its tasks, the EU AI Office will also be supported also by a scientific panel of independent experts, an AI Advisory forum with stakeholder representatives and an AI Board composed of Member States representatives, thus building on a holistic and strong governance framework at EU level for the effective and inclusive implementation of the AI Act.

Title EN: Andares de Paz or Paths of Peace
Goal: Integrate Culture In Sustainable Development Frameworks
SDG: SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: National sustainable development policies and plans

Agency Implementation: Ministry of Cultures, Arts, and Knowledge of Colombia
Main Feature: Strengthening popular economy initiatives in the sector of arts, cultures, and knowledge of peace signatories of the agreement between the national government and the FARC.                  This project is in administrative processes and hopes to begin its implementation in the second semester of 2024.                   It seeks to recognize and strengthen the organizational, management and self-management capacities, to contribute to the sustainability of the initiatives of 15 groups or organizations of signatories of the peace agreement between the National Government and the FARC – EP, of the following urban and/or rural territories: Bogotá D.C., Cundinamarca, Boyacá, Tolima, Huila, Meta, Caquetá, Antioquia, and Sucre. The project is then aimed at popular economy initiatives related to trades, cultures, arts, and knowledge around diverse productive community processes of creation, transformation, circulation, exchange, commercialization, communication, education, productive reconversion, and use and sustainable use of biodiversity, among others. This is to strengthen and consolidate their skills and productive capacities, promote the construction of collaborative work networks, build bridges to prepare and circulate their cultural initiatives, and, in addition, explore the social fabric from a symbolic cultural perspective that, together, leads to having a significant impact on the quality of life of the signatories.                  Group selection ended May 24. Two hundred and ten (210) groups were represented nationally, of which 138 met the criterion of departmental territorialization. Of the one hundred and thirty-eight (138), 15 groups of signatories were selected; three (3) in Bogotá D.C., two (2) in Caquetá, one (1) in Cundinamarca, two (2) in Sucre, two (2) in Tolima, one (1) in Huila, two (2) in Antioquia, one (1) in Boyacá, and one (1) in Meta.                  The scope of Andares de Paz will be oriented towards the fulfillment of the missionary activities programmed in the action plan, mainly in the activities to be developed within the framework of the agreement:                   Public invitation to groups: this phase was carried out by the team from the Directorate of Strategy, Development, and Entrepreneurship of the Ministry of Cultures, Arts, and Knowledge; who, through the social networks of the Ministry, and allies, invited initiatives led by groups of signatories in the departments of Bogotá D.C., Cundinamarca, Boyacá, Tolima, Huila, Meta, Caquetá, Antioquia, and Sucre, to participate in the Project Andares de Paz.                   Selection of groups: this phase was in charge of the team from the Directorate of Strategy, Development, and Entrepreneurship of the Ministry of Culture, Arts, and Knowledge, who made a selection based on these criteria with the information of the groups registered in the previous phase: relationship with the cultural, artistic, knowledge, or craft sector; associativity for social cohesion, strengthening of territorial, and community ties; networking or working with other local and regional organizations or groups.                   Information collection: the implementation of this phase is in charge of the ESAL, in Spanish, who, after the selection of the groups, builds and applies in person the information collection instruments to systematize through a SWOT analysis (Strengths, Weaknesses, Opportunities, and Threats) the state of the fifteen (15) popular economy initiatives, which makes it possible to demonstrate the current situation of the groups.                   Strengthening phase implementation: it is in charge of the ESAL, who develop actions to strengthen the economic initiatives of the groups in person, through training processes, advice, technical support, and development of soft skills, with a focus on culture of peace, popular economy, and territorial articulation. The thematic axes can link topics such as cultural management, management of groups and associations, marketing, territorial coexistence, internal democracy and planning, among others. However, the definition of the topics must respond to the results obtained by the SWOT carried out in the previous phase and to the contents guided by the Management.                   Evaluation of results and socialization of experiences: the implementation of this phase is in charge of the ESAL, who compiles the experiences (note: define in agreement with the Ministry team whether it is an editorial or audiovisual product, among others) and socializes the product with the fifteen (15) beneficiary initiatives and their immediate communities and environments.
Results: The project is being implemented.

Title EN: Ajman Folklore Festival
