Area of Monitoring: Cultural and creative sectors
Agency Implementation: Ajman Department of Tourism Development; Ministry of Culture; Ousha Bint Hussein Cultural Hall
Main Feature: The Ajman Folklore Festival featured a diverse and extensive program designed to celebrate and preserve the rich cultural heritage of the Emirate of Ajman. The festival included folkloric performances, concerts, cultural showcases, and workshops highlighting traditional Emirati arts and crafts. Art exhibitions displayed vintage collectibles and various artistic works, along with interactive activities such as workshops on wicker painting and candle making. Additionally, the festival promoted cultural exchange by showcasing folk dance performances from various Arab and international groups and exhibiting traditional costumes from different countries. Competitions for traditional costumes and poetry, as well as an Emirati artist gathering and a symposium on Nabati poetry, were integral parts of the event, aimed at deepening heritage comprehension and fostering cultural interaction among diverse communities. A key focus of the festival was to spotlight the ancient heritage of the Emirate of Ajman, utilizing the festival as a platform to exhibit its distinctive cultural and artistic legacy. These events played a vital role in preserving Emirati heritage and passing it down to younger generations, thereby reinforcing national identity and nurturing cultural exchange within the community. On the festival's inaugural day, there was a lineup of Emirati folklore activities, featuring the opening of an art exhibition and a display of vintage collectibles both indoors and at external kiosks. Workshops on wicker painting and candle making, also took place. Furthermore, there was an Emirati artist gathering and a symposium on Nabati poetry, concluding with the announcement of the winners of the competition for the most captivating Nabati poem about Ajman. The second day featured an enchanting display of Arab folklore, with lively folk dance performances representing countries like Palestine, Egypt, Iraq, Morocco, and Yemen. Attendees also explored an exhibition showcasing folkloric costumes from various Arab countries tailored for adults, as well as a competition highlighting the most exquisite folkloric costume for children. On the third day, the festival showcased captivating folk-dance performances featuring multiple international groups, including Circassian, Chinese, Indian, Korean, Turkish, and others. There was also an exhibition of international folklore costumes. Finally, the festival welcomed an Uzbek artist and announced the winners of a competition for the most beautiful international or Arab heritage painting.
Results: The festival has achieved significant milestones in its planning and organization stages. It has successfully brought together key cultural and governmental entities, including the Ministry of Culture, the Ajman Department of Tourism Development, and the Rewaq Ousha Bint Hussein Cultural Center, demonstrating strong collaborative efforts. The festival has generated considerable interest and excitement within the community, highlighting Ajman's commitment to preserving and promoting its cultural heritage. By providing a comprehensive platform for cultural expression and exchange, the festival is poised to enhance cultural awareness and foster deeper connections among diverse communities, aligning with the goals outlined in Ajman Vision 2030.
Recommandations: The Ajman Folklore Festival plays a vital role in preserving cultural heritage by showcasing traditional arts, music, dance, and crafts, thereby ensuring that these practices are maintained and passed on to future generations. It also promotes cultural understanding by bringing together diverse cultural groups and fostering appreciation and unity among audiences. Supporting local artists and artisans is a key focus of the festival, providing them with a platform to display their talents and contribute to the vitality of traditional arts. Additionally, the festival enhances tourism by attracting visitors both within the UAE and internationally, boosting the local economy and raising Ajman’s profile as a cultural destination. Community involvement is encouraged through active participation in festival activities, strengthening local ties and pride in cultural heritage.

Title EN: Article 101 of the Media Services Act
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture
SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Media diversity
Agency Implementation: Ministry of Culture of the Slovak Republic
Main Feature: Under Article 101 of the Media Services Act, the Regulator assesses the influence of the content service provider and media group on the plurality of information on the media market and the advertising market and evaluates the risk of disrupting the plurality of information that threatens the application of this influence. A provider with a decisive influence on the disruption of the plurality of information is defined as a provider of a content service whose market share, either alone or together with other content services of the media group, exceeds the share of 60% in the entire advertising market of the Slovak Republic. The provider with relevant influence on the disruption of the plurality of information is the content service provider, whose market share, either alone or together with other content services of the media group, exceeds the share of 30% in the entire advertising market of the Slovak Republic. A provider with a low impact on the disruption of the plurality of information is a content service provider whose market share, either alone or together with other content services of the media group, does not exceed a share of 30% in the entire advertising market of the Slovak Republic.   The Regulator shall not grant a consent that would lead to the acquisition of a decisive influence on the disruption of the plurality of information, or shall reject the request for a consent under the Media Services Act. The Regulator shall proceed likewise if the acquisition of relevant influence on the disruption of the plurality of information would be immediately capable of endangering the plurality of information provided to the public. The Regulator assesses the property connection and personnel connection of the content service provider in order to examine whether the property and personnel relations meet the following conditions: a) The transparency of ownership relationships or the transparency or trustworthiness of the financial resources intended to finance the provision of the content service is ensured;   b) There is no obvious risk that the content service could be misused directly or in connection with a foreign power to threaten the constitutional establishment, national security or the democratic system of fundamental rights and freedoms guaranteed by the Constitution of the Slovak Republic, to discriminate or incite intolerance or violence;   c) There is no obvious risk that the plurality of information and media content could be disrupted;   d) The content service provider is not directly or indirectly financed by a terrorist organization or a person or State that is on the sanctions list of the United Nations or the European Union.  In accordance with Article 70 (1) of the Media Services Act, the provider of an on-demand audiovisual media service is obliged to reserve at least 30% of the total number of programs offered in the program catalogue per calendar month for European works, in each on-demand audiovisual media service separately, and to ensure their proper emphasis.
Results: In accordance with Article 5 of Act No 532/2010 Coll. on Radio and Television of Slovakia and on amendments to certain acts, as amended, the main activities of Radio and Television of Slovakia include, among other things, the support and development of the cultural and creative industries, especially in the area of program creation, digital and multimedia content, broadcasting of program services, provision of audiovisual on-demand media services and provision of digital and multimedia content.  In 2011, the Slovak Film Institute implemented the National Digital Audiovisual Project in cooperation with Radio and Television of Slovakia as part of the Operational Program Informatization of Society - Priority Axis 2, Development of memory and fund institutions and renewal of their national infrastructure. The financial completion of the project took place on 22 June  2016, and the project reached a 5-year sustainability period, during which the Slovak Film Institute undertook to digitize at least 50 film objects per year.  The sustainability of the Digital Audiovisual Project finished on 22 June 2021, but activities related to the digitization of audiovisual heritage continue to be ensured by the National Film Archive in the premises of the digitization workplace of the Slovak Film Institute, where new digital distribution copies of digitized films are also being prepared for cinemas and film events in Slovakia and abroad. The total number of digitized film works within the National Project and its sustainability is 1,380 film works (more than 1 Petabyte of data). In 2020, 70 film works (documentaries, feature films, news films) were digitized. In January and February 2020, the exhibition of digitally restored films under the name of Digital Cinema 1955-1975 was also continued at the Lumière Cinema Filmoteque, which began in September 2019 and continued in July and August 2020 after the interruption of cinema screenings. In 2021, 71 film works were digitized, and in 2022, 54 film works. The activities of the digitization workplace were interrupted in September 2022 due to a fire in the cinema´s premises. After the fire, it was necessary to proceed with the reconstruction of the premises and technologies and their subsequent renewal, as well as the rescue of film data, and these activities continued in 2023. In order to make film heritage accessible, digital copies were produced (in some cases also with subtitles) and their control was carried out for various methods of digital access, especially for digital cinemas (D-Cinema and E-Cinema), digital television broadcasting, audiovisual media services on demand or materials for blu-ray media.

Title EN: Al Burda
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture
SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Cultural and creative sectors
Agency Implementation: Ministry of Culture
Main Feature: Launched in 2004, Al Burda is an international initiative by the Ministry of Culture focused on supporting and fostering creativity, as well as raising awareness about Islamic art and culture both locally and globally. The initiative aims to introduce and engage younger generations to the diverse disciplines of Islamic art and culture. By doing so, Al Burda establishes broad intergenerational links that encourages the advancement of Islamic art on the global cultural map. The 18th edition of the Burda Award celebrates the aesthetics of Islamic culture by honoring the life of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) through the concept of 'Al-Noor (light) which embodies guidance and direction towards the path of truth and goodness.  By celebrating the honorable biography and character of Prophet Mohammed (PBUH) on the anniversaries of his birthday, the Al Burda Award aims to: 1-Spread public awareness, and appreciation for Islamic art beyond the traditional formats and encourage contemporary interpretations. 2-Recognize and celebrate outstanding achievements of the past 20 years of the award. 3- Celebrate Islamic arts as a gateway to cultural communication with the world and as part of global heritage. 4- Highlight values and principles of tolerance through celebrating the aesthetics of Islamic arts. 5- Discover and recognize established as well as emerging talent and showcase their work. 6- Support knowledge development by creatives and professionals through residencies, workshops, writing and other initiatives. Award Category: poetry: Al Burda Award recognizes poetry as a medium that highlights the life and character of the Prophet Mohammed (PBUH) through the art of language and the power of verbal expression. Receiving submissions for both classical and Traditional poetry, the award simultaneously celebrates the beauty of the Arabic language and the literary heritage of the Arab and Islamic world. In a sense, the poetry category is a literal reflection of the award’s namesake, ‘Al Burda’, derived from Qasidat Al Burda, or Ode of the Mantle, which is an epic poem for the Prophet Mohammed (PBUH), authored by the 12th century Sufi mystic Imam Al Busiri. Arabic Calligraphy: Calligraphy is one of the most versatile, disciplined and rich practices of Islamic art, and has rooted itself as a highly respected tradition in Islamic culture. Islamic calligraphy has paid tribute to the Arabic language, the revered language of the holy Quran; thus, it is not only a form of writing but also a form of spiritual expression. Al Burda Award has long recognized masterful work of both classical and modern Islamic calligraphy, embracing the traditional, contemporary, and typographic. Ornamentation: in Islamic art includes four forms; the three non-figural forms that are calligraphy, vegetal patterns, geometric patterns and figural representation. Al Burda Award has awarded works showcasing these forms, which depict the aesthetic range of Islamic culture. As with the other award categories, submission guidelines respect the intricate materials and approach used in the Classical and the Contemporary ornamentation practices. Does it specifically target young people?  No Does the International Fund for Cultural Diversity (IFCD) support the implementation of the policy/measure?  No What are the results achieved so far through the implementation of the policy/measure? Over the years, the Al Burda Award has honored numerous distinguished artists and scholars, contributing to the global appreciation of Islamic arts. It has played a significant role in bringing attention to Islamic artistic traditions and contemporary interpretations. The award is typically accompanied by exhibitions and events that showcase the winning works and promote dialogue about Islamic art and culture. These events provide a platform for artists and scholars to engage with a broader audience. The Al Burda Award has had a substantial impact on the global appreciation and understanding of Islamic arts. It has helped to foster a greater recognition of the diversity and richness of Islamic cultural expressions and has supported the ongoing development of traditional and contemporary Islamic art forms.
Financial Ressources: The Al Burda Award allocates significant prizes across several categories to recognize excellence in Islamic arts. For poetry, the award features a tiered prize structure with the first prize set at 70,000 AED, followed by the second prize at 50,000 AED, and the third prize at 40,000 AED. Additionally, the fourth and fifth prizes are awarded 30,000 AED and 20,000 AED, respectively. In the Arabic Calligraphy category, the top prize is also 70,000 AED, with the second and third prizes valued at 50,000 AED and 40,000 AED, respectively. Similarly, in the Ornamentation category, the first prize is 70,000 AED, the second prize is 50,000 AED, and the third prize is 40,000 AED, while the fourth and fifth prizes are 30,000 AED and 20,000 AED, respectively.
Recommandations: Al Burda Award underscore its vital role in advancing the appreciation and preservation of Islamic arts. It is evident that the award significantly enhances the visibility of traditional art forms, including poetry, Arabic calligraphy, and ornamentation, by providing substantial financial incentives and recognition.

The focus areas in the action plan include: •	Reducing prices and cost drivers for activities. •	Providing good and accessible information about activities and offerings. •	Making a greater variety of activities available to more people. •	Strengthening the voices and local participation of children and young people in leisure and cultural activities. •	Encouraging more and new forms of collaboration. •	Gaining more knowledge about social inequality and the effects of measures.
Results: The effects of the grants have not yet been evaluated. In total, over 4,000 sports clubs received additional funds in 2023 to encourage more children and young people to participate in leisure activities. The sports clubs report that the money has enabled them to start new activities, collaborate better with neighbourhoods and schools, cover training fees, and purchase equipment.

Title EN: An example of youth-oriented measure at local level: The Youth Center Velenje
Goal: Integrate Culture In Sustainable Development Frameworks

Main Feature: The Youth Center Velenje is a public cultural and educational institution dedicated primarily to youth and (youth) culture. It organizes cultural activities throughout the year at the eMCe plac club, including concerts, exhibitions, performing arts and creative workshops, and in the warmer months, events at the open-air cinema on Škale Lake. The center's largest cultural project is the Kunigunda Festival of Youth Culture, which has been held for 27 consecutive years. The theme of the festival is human rights, equality, tolerance and solidarity. In the past, the center has organized events such as Svatba, a performance celebrating love, where a male couple got married in the center of Velenje. The center founded the ARK - Autonomous Republic of Kunigunda, drafted a constitution and even created a flag, anthem and personal documents to show the possibility of a more tolerant, solidary and inclusive alternative to the social order. Artists are given free rein to express themselves and are encouraged to make their content effective and critical. The center's work is primarily about connecting with young people, facilitating the transmission of informal knowledge across generations, and providing ongoing opportunities for young people to gain skills and credentials through their participation in all aspects of culture. Throughout the year, the center engages young people in informal mentorship programs, both programmatic and technical, such as lighting and sound engineering, graphic design, filming, photography, and editing. Those involved in the preparation and delivery of cultural content throughout the year also become part of the festival team, with the condensed program schedule allowing for mentoring at a higher level. The goal is for the young people to be able to work independently as soon as possible. Therefore, the focus of the center is on learning by doing and peer-to-peer training, with mentors acting as advisors and helping with challenges. The goal is for young people to be able to work independently as soon as possible. Therefore, the center focuses on learning by doing and peer-to-peer training, with mentors acting as advisors and helping with challenges. In addition to informal knowledge transfer between generations, the center is also a partner of the konS platform for contemporary investigative art, where it has run mentoring programs. Over the course of four years (2020, 2021, 2022, 2023), the Center conducted intensive training sessions once a week for an average of four months. The future mentors were introduced to a variety of contemporary investigative arts content (mechatronics, programming, 3D design and printing, etc.) and pedagogical approaches. The center is also actively involved in the preparation of the local youth development program in the municipality of Velenje. Currently, the 3rd local program for 2021 - 2025 is in force. In 2024, the center will start intensive preparations for the 4th Local Youth Development Program. It is preparing this youth strategy thoroughly and in close cooperation with various youth organizations. To ensure that the strategy is responsive to the needs of the community, it organizes workshops where young people discuss what they would like to see, what would be beneficial to them, and what we should focus on in the future. For each local program, several workshops are organized for different groups: elementary and high school students, unorganized and organized youth, and workshops with disadvantaged youth. In these workshops, they are encouraged to reflect on topics such as environmental protection and sustainable mobility, active citizenship, arts, culture and heritage, sports, leisure and entertainment, tourism, education, information and training, entrepreneurship and employment, and the inclusion of disadvantaged young people with special needs. In these workshops, young people express their needs and aspirations and work together to develop objectives to be included in the programme. This document serves as the basis for the Velenje Municipality Public Youth Grant, which enables young individuals or associations to obtain funding for their projects.
Results: The results of the informal training that the center provides to young people are evident in the requests that other local organizations often make to the center to recommend students to work on their projects or even to hire them after they complete their training. The center's staff is also sought after and appreciated by other organizations in the local community. The result of the development of the local youth program is a strategic document adopted at the level of the Municipality of Velenje, which also secures funding for various public calls. This document allows the center to influence local youth policy.

Main Feature: At the initiative of the Ministry of Culture and Heritage, regulations were drafted for the validation of careers in the field of the arts to obtain a university degree for those with outstanding experience.   In 2016, the plenary of the Higher Education Council (CES), through Regulation RPC-SO-25-No. 433-2016, resolved to acknowledge in first debate the draft Regulation for the Validation of Professional Trajectories in the Field of the Arts, presented by the Permanent Commission of Higher Institutes and Conservatories of the CES.  The validation of professional trajectory is contemplated in Article 99 of Chapter I Recognition or Recognition of the Academic Regulations of the Council of Higher Education (CES), which determines that there are three mechanisms of recognition, one of which is the validation of professional trajectories.  The validation consists of the recognition of an outstanding professional career or work, artistic or cultural experience of the applicant, which may be equivalent to the approval of certain courses, subjects or their equivalents, or the entire career. On September 14, 2021, the "Specific Cooperation Agreement between the Ministry of Culture and Heritage and the Universidad de las Artes" was signed, in order to "Plan and execute joint actions and inter-institutional cooperation, in order to consolidate the processes of higher education in the arts and the granting of third level degrees, through the Validation of Professional Trajectories in the field of Arts", for a period of ONE (1) year from the transfer of funds and financial availability for its execution. Title EN: Appui à la mobilité sortante des artistes et professionnels de la culture en République de Guinée
Goal: Achieve A Balanced Flow Of Cultural Goods And Services And Increase The Mobility Of Artists And Cultural Professionals
SDG: SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 10 - Reduce inequality within and among countries,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Mobility of artists and cultural professionals
Cultural Domain: Design,Performing Arts,Media Arts,Cinema and Audiovisual Arts,Music,Publishing,Visual Arts
Agency Implementation: Ministère de la Culture, du Tourisme et de l’Artisanat
Main Feature: Les artistes guinéens produisent un nombre important d’œuvres artistiques. Cependant, la promotion et la commercialisation de leurs œuvres sur les plans national et international demeurent difficile ; ce qui ne leur permet pas de vivre du fruit de leur travail et de contribuer efficacement au développement économique du pays. Malgré de nombreuses opportunités qui leurs sont offertes à travers les foires, les salons, les festivals, … l’insuffisance de moyens financiers et la difficulté d’accès à certains marchés du Nord réduisent leur mobilité et l’écoulement de leurs produits tant au niveau régional qu’international. Le Ministère de la Culture, du Tourisme et de l’Artisanat (MCTA), conformément à sa mission régalienne, soutient la mobilité des artistes par le biais d’un dispositif d’accompagnement financier mis en place à travers le Fonds de Développement des Arts et de la Culture créé par décret D/00303/PRG/CNRD/ SGG du 20 juin 2022. Ce fonds contribue à hauteur de 25% du budget alloué chaque année à son fonctionnement, soit 289 957 USD. Quelques fois, le département en fonction de l’importance des évènements accompagne des artistes et professionnels de la culture à travers le Budget National de Développement (BND). A cela s’ajoute l’accompagnement des partenaires techniques, financiers et mécènes. L’objectif général de cette mesure est de contribuer à la promotion extérieure des œuvres artistiques des artistes guinéens. Elle vise spécifiquement à :  -	faciliter la circulation des artistes et de leurs œuvres ;  -	favoriser des échanges d’expériences à travers des mécanismes d’accompagnement technique et financier ;  -	faciliter la participation des artistes et acteurs culturels dans toutes les rencontres internationales à travers des festivals, des foires, des stages, des programmes de diffusion artistique.
Results: Le Ministère de la Culture, du Tourisme et de l’Artisanat a soutenu de 2022 à 2024 au moins trois cent (300) artistes et acteurs culturels dans leur mobilité. Cela a permis aux bénéficiaires de participer à des manifestations à l’international dont entre autres en Côte d’Ivoire (MASA), en Gambie (Hero’s Awards), au Sénégal (Festival International Panafricain de Nguèkhohh, Salon de pagne tissé à Dakar), au Burkina Faso (FESPACO, Journée Nationale de la Culture),  en France (JO, Kania soli de Paris), en Allemagne, au Canada, etc. A cet effet, on retient que : -	16 artistes et acteurs culturels ont participé aux Hero’s Awards en Gambie (du 24 au 27 mai 2024) ; -	Le Festival International Panafricain de Nguèkhohh a enregistré la participation de 5 acteurs culturels en 2024 ; -	En 2024, 80 artistes et acteurs culturels ont pris part au Marché des Arts du Spectacles d’Abidjan (MASA) et ont intervenu dans les domaines de la musique, du théâtre, du Slam ; -	Les Jeux Olympiques (JO) à Paris ont connu la participation de 100 artistes et acteurs culturels en 2024 ; -	13 artisans ont participé au Salon de pagne tissé à Dakar, Sénégal en 2024 ;  -	En 2023, 25 artistes et acteurs culturels ont pris part au FESPACO ; -	20 artistes ont participé au Kania Soli de Paris en 2022 ; -	En 2023, 5 artistes ont participé à l’expo Dubaï 2023.

Main Feature: The Austrian Museum for Black Entertainment and Black Music was established in 2022 during one of Vienna’s most renowned festivals (Wiener Festwochen). Its comprehensive and constantly growing multimedia collection focuses on the artistic work as well as biographies of Black entertainers and musicians in the German-speaking entertainment industry from the 1940s to the early 2000s. Special focus is put on the presentational strategies of black entertainers, their reception by a predominantly white audience and empowering strategies of subversion. The project aims at: •	establishing a space for Black artists, activists and journalists currently living and working in Austria •	presentation of evidence of the biographical and artistic work of Black entertainers and artists •	opening up a new field of Austrian and German historiography

Area of Monitoring: Cultural and creative sectors
Agency Implementation: Ministry of Culture
Main Feature: The Arabic Language Summit, organized by the Ministry of Culture, is designed to promote and preserve the Arabic language through various initiatives and discussions. The summit aims to enhance the use of Arabic in different fields, foster linguistic and cultural exchange, and address the challenges faced in the modernization and digitization of the language. Key features include expert panels, workshops, and collaborative projects aimed at developing educational resources, integrating Arabic into digital platforms, and promoting its use in contemporary contexts such as science, technology, and media.
Results: 'The implementation of the Arabic Language Summit has led to several significant achievements. These include the creation of new educational programs and resources that support Arabic language learning, increased collaboration between institutions and experts across the Arab world, and the development of digital tools and platforms that facilitate the use of Arabic in modern technology. Additionally, the summit has successfully raised awareness about the importance of preserving and promoting the Arabic language, resulting in greater community engagement and support for related initiatives. "Programs: 1- Arabic Language and Identity 2- Arabic Language, identity and drama 3- Identity makers in other languages 4- Future of the Arabic language 5- Review of the curriculum status report 6- Arabic Calligraphy and Modernist Patterns 7- A poetic shade 8- Arabic language in new worlds 9- Arabic Language and Music
Recommandations: The main conclusions from the Arabic Language Summit highlight the need for sustained efforts to integrate Arabic into various modern contexts and technologies. Recommendations include expanding the development of digital tools and resources, increasing funding for Arabic language research and education, and fostering international collaboration to address common linguistic challenges. The summit also emphasizes the importance of government support in implementing policies that protect and promote the Arabic language, as well as the need to engage younger generations in these efforts through innovative and interactive approaches.

Title EN: Argentine Cultural Industries Market  ( MICA)
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture
SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Cultural and creative sectors
Agency Implementation: Secretariat of Culture of Argentina
Main Feature: The Mercado de Industrias Culturales Argentinas (MICA) was born as the central event of the public policy system created for the commercialization of products and services and for the strengthening of the cultural industries sectors at national and international level. Since its first edition in 2011, MICA has aimed to foster regional integration, internationalization, export of goods and services, boost production, make cultural industries visible, generate employment and promote commercialization through business rounds. In addition, the program offers conferences aimed at the various sectors, workshops for the development of portfolios, live shows, entrepreneurs fair and exclusive events, among other activities. Finally, MICA has sought the federalization of culture as a democratizing measure, aimed at expanding existing capacities and resources.  MICA has held 8 editions: 2011, 2013, 2015, 2017, 2019, 2019, 2021, 2022 and 2023.  In addition, during the year 2021, the launching of its website was carried out in a joint action with Empresa Argentina de Soluciones Satelitales - ARSAT S.A. This digital platform sought to make visible and promote the commercialization of cultural industries. The MICA website promotes the participation of professionals and companies associated with the following sectors: Video Games, Visual Arts, Publishing, Design, Audiovisual, Circus, Theater, Dance, Tango, Folklore, Hip-Hop, Children, Music, Academic Music, Crafts and Gastronomy. At the beginning of 2024, the platform has 23,300 registered users and 6,600 published portfolios. It also has a catalog of 7,000 exhibited cultural products and services.  MICA is currently the most important cultural market in the region, with a constant activity through its platform where the economic side of culture is articulated with the aesthetic enjoyment.  During 2023, MICA has been guest of honor of the Brazil 2023 Cultural Industries Marketplace and the Canelones International Creative Industries Forum.  Is the policy/measure specifically targeting youth? No  Does the International Fund for Cultural Diversity (IFCD) support the implementation of the policy/measure?  No What are the results achieved so far through the implementation of the policy/measure? MICA 2023  MICA event at the Centro Cultural Kirchner - More than 45 thousand attendees participated in this edition.  - There were 21 countries invited.  - Brazil was the guest of honor at this edition of MICA.  - Approximately 15,000 formal business rounds have been held  - 150 international buyers from 27 countries  - 225 domestic buyers  - 2000 vendors from all over the country  - Trade delegations from Brazil, Chile and Uruguay  - About 150 showcases  - It included a Gastronomy Fair in which entrepreneurs from all over the country participated.  MICA 2022  MICA event at the Centro Cultural Kirchner Duration: 4 days  - More than 12,000 business rounds were held with the participation of some 90 buyers from 23 countries.  - There were also around 1,500 cultural managers, artists and producers of cultural goods and services from the 23 provincial states.  - Business opportunities were also generated and cultural production was boosted throughmore than 30 master classes, 20 showcases, 4 fairs, forums and workshops.  - The program funded airfare and lodging for 744 producers of cultural industry goods and services from all provinces of Argentina. - Special activities were carried out to deepen international cooperation between the Republic of Argentina and Mexico, since Mexico was the guest of honor at this edition of MICA.  In addition, MICA Nodes were held throughout the country, which were regional meetings with different sectors aimed at strengthening provincial cultural industries.  MICA 2021  Due to the severe restrictions that existed due to the Covid-19 pandemic, the digital platform "MICA 2021" was launched, a virtual space where companies and different sectors were linked to generate business relationships and form partnerships to expand their cultural offerings. As of October 2023, the platform has 23,300 registered users and 6,662 portfolios (perfiles) were uploaded. It also has a catalog of 7039 exhibited cultural products and services.  In 2021 there were more than 50,000 meetings and business rounds with more than 2,000 international attendees.  Financial resources allocated to the policy/measure in U.S. dollars. 1,000,000 USD (2023 edition)
Recommandations: This program achieved: SOUGHT- It encouraged MSMEs in the cultural sectors by promoting the consumption of cultural products at the local level, strengthening the internationalization of Argentine culture, building state areas at the provincial level dedicated to the subject, contributing to the professionalization of cultural agents, generating specific agreements between the countries of the region and serving as a model to consolidate an ecosystem that transcends borders.   - It promoted the creation and consolidation of different associative work formats such as cooperatives, formal associations, mutuals, clusters and unions to achieve the sustainability of projects at the social level.   - It contributed to the economic recovery of the post-pandemic cultural industries, redesigning the proposal in its digital version. It consisted of the creation of virtual spaces where companies and different sectors could link up to generate commercial relations and form partnerships that expanded their cultural offerings.   The 2023 edition was also evaluated during the month of June with a self administered online survey for those who participated as buyers in the business rounds.   The purpose of this survey was to know the commercial profile of the buyers, the volume of agreements reached during the MICA event and the business projection in the medium term.  Profile of participating buyers  25.6% are sole proprietors, 22.7% belong to  an SME/SME,  10.5% participated representing public bodies, 9.9%  belonged to a non-formalized grouping,  7% belong to a cooperative and  24.3% belong to other types of legal formations, in many cases without commercial purposes (foundations, networks, civil associations, among others).  Spaces where buyers carry out their activities  Almost 55% of the company's activities are carried out mainly in Argentina, and the rest in the 27 participating countries, especially in Europe (with a greater presence of Spain, France and Portugal), South America (with a greater presence of Brazil and Colombia) and the United States. Participation in previous editions of MICA and in business linkage spaces.  60.5% of buyers participated for the first time in a MICA, of which 47% participated for the first time in business rounds.  Characterization of the MICA 2023 Business Rounds  68% of those consulted mentioned having offered some type of agreement during the business rounds.  The types of agreements most frequently offered are:  ● linkage with third parties (36.6%)  ● direct purchase of goods and services (23.8%),  ● programming of functions (22.1%),  ● visibility actions (20.9%),  ● pre-agreement/pre-contract (18.6%),  ● co-productions (17.4%),  ● orders/ pre-order (12.2%),  ● tours (10.5%) and exhibition (10.5%).  Sales arranged during the MICA event  Concerted sales were agreed with producers from other provinces (59.3% of the total agreements were combined with producers from other provinces, different from the origin of the entrepreneur) and also with producers from another country (51.7%).   In monetary terms, almost 41.9% of the agreements in Argentine pesos are for a maximum value of $50,000. In the case of international buyers who offered agreements/contracts in USD, in almost 50% of the agreements the average amount offered exceeds USD 10,000, in 25% of the agreements the average amount offered is USD 3,000 and the other 25% offered agreements for approximately USD 500.   The various agreements made with international buyers are for the following destinations:  ● 75% in Europe,  ● 25% in the United States,  ● 25% Argentina  ● 25% Asia.   Regarding the MICA Gastronomy Fair, a total of 30 Argentine companies exhibited and marketed their products during the event, selling 100% of their products. of the mobilized merchandise. Most of these companies are MSMEs and SMEs with up to 10 members from the provinces. The sales made at MICA were retail sales during the fair. In addition, almost all the producers generated agreements through orders placed in the framework of the business rounds, an instance in which the Gastronomy sector participated for the first time.  As a result, products were sold for a total estimated value of  $9.000.000.   Finally,  was asked about interest in participating in MICA again, and the buyers stated the following:   ● 54% said that they were interested in participating in future virtual business rounds on the MICA virtual platform.   ● 94.8% said that they would be interested in participating in a new MICA face-to face event.   ● 76.2% said that their experience at business rounds was VERY productive and ● 55.8% said they wanted to participate in business rounds in other sectors

Title EN: Art Jameel Research and Practice Program: Climate Change Edition
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture

Area of Monitoring: Partnering with civil society
Cultural Domain: Design,Performing Arts,Media Arts,Cinema and Audiovisual Arts,Music,Visual Arts
Agency Implementation: Art Jameel
Main Feature: The Art Jameel and Dubai Culture and Arts Authority program represents a significant initiative to support UAE-based artists and multidisciplinary creative practitioners in addressing climate change through their practice. This comprehensive program incorporates a variety of features designed to foster innovation, sustainability, and collaboration within the creative community. The initiative is open to a wide range of creative practitioners, including artists, filmmakers, writers, curators, illustrators, designers, performers, and others, encouraging diverse approaches to sustainability and environmental issues. Projects submitted must address or include a conceptual or material focus on sustainability and the environment, aligning with the UAE Year of Sustainability and supporting the global dialogue on climate action leading up to COP28 in Dubai. Applications are welcomed from UAE nationals and long-term residents, with the submission period running from October 4, 2023, to December 15, 2023, ensuring a wide array of creative voices can participate. The program is supported by Dubai Culture and Arts Authority and is associated with the Al Quoz Creative Zone, an integrated creative hub in Dubai, highlighting the commitment of local cultural institutions to fostering creativity and sustainability. The Research and Practice Platform runs concurrently with the MENA-wide Anhar: Culture and Climate Platform, a collaboration between Art Jameel and the British Council, extending the impact of the program across the region. Building on the success of the 2020 Research and Practice Platform program, this second edition continues the joint commitment to supporting and nurturing the artistic and cultural landscape of the UAE, initially responding to the challenges posed by the COVID-19 pandemic. The program underscores a commitment to fostering sustainability within the creative community, exploring the intersection of culture and climate change, and contributing to pressing global conversations about our shared future. In addition to individual practitioner grants, the program encourages organizations to submit proposals for decarbonization strategies and collaborative projects under the Anhar program, extending the program�s reach and impact on institutional practices. The Art Jameel and Dubai Culture and Arts Authority program is a forward-thinking initiative that leverages financial support, multidisciplinary engagement, and collaborative efforts to address climate change through creative practice. By providing substantial grants and fostering a diverse array of projects focused on sustainability, the program not only supports the UAE�s cultural and environmental goals but also contributes to the broader international dialogue on climate action and sustainable development
Results: The collaborative initiative between Art Jameel and Dubai Culture has launched a UAE-wide grants program aimed at supporting creative projects that address the climate crisis. This initiative, aligned with the UAE Year of Sustainability and in the lead-up to COP28, aims to foster innovation and raise awareness about environmental issues through the arts. Since its inception, the program has successfully engaged a diverse array of artists, designers, and cultural practitioners from across the UAE. The grants have enabled the development of numerous projects that creatively explore sustainability and environmental stewardship. These projects include visual art installations, performance pieces, digital media works, and community-focused art initiatives that highlight the urgent need for climate action.
Recommandations: The Art Jameel and Dubai Culture grants program has demonstrated a strong impact by merging artistic creativity with environmental advocacy, effectively engaging the community and contributing to the broader discourse on sustainability

Agency Implementation: Direction for the Arts and Culture, Office of the Vice President for Research, Office of the Vice President for Communication and Cultural Outreach, Faculty of Arts, UC Institute of Music, Pontifical Catholic University of Chile.
Main Feature: A broad measure from the Pontifical Catholic University of Chile (UC Chile) for fostering and carrying out arts and culture research, creation and permeation into all segments of this educational space and the general community. This educational community is host to more than 35,000 people, between professors and students.   Its Direction for the Arts and Culture has calls for research and creation in speacialist and interdisciplinary areas of culture within the academic, student and administrative divisions and the "Artifying Programme" for dissemination of the arts through diverse lines of action: "Artifying the UC", "Artifying your Home", "Artifying your Neighborhood".  Along these lines, the arts created, researched and practiced at the UC Chile connect with the internal and external communities. In turn, the Office of the Vice President for Communication and Cultural Outreach is the entity that has defined culture outreach and communications strategies towards society. This organisation prepares an annual programme of initiatives, distributed through the three outreach centres located within different communes of the Metropolitan Region and in the different University campuses, and are often coordinated with the work ot the MAVI UC museum (Museum of Visual Arts); Beethoven Radio; the Teatro UC; the different initiatives from the Direction for the Arts and Culture of the Office of the Vice President for Research; the Factulty of Arts, the Faculty of Communication and the Faculty of Literature from the same institution.   In turn, an important part of the work relates to mediation and itinerancies, prioritising training and enriching individuals with a strong feeling of cultural identity, promoting environments that foster reflection, exploration, dialogue, appreciation, creativity and interaction with the vast universe of the arts and culture, encompassing expressions such as film and audiovisual expressions (UC Chile Cinema project check previous translation), programming created between UC Chile Media * and the 13C television channel, studio and podcast production), the visual arts (permanent collection exhibitions, contemporary art exhibitions, Indigenous Peoples Classroom, visual arts fairs), reading (Ediciones UC and University Magazine), music (UC Music Season of the UC Institute of Music and interfaculty orchestra activities), performing arts (Teatro UC and performative educational activites) and other spheres of outreach.   * UC Chile Media is an audiovisual platform at the Pontifical Catholic University of Chile which seeks to make a social contribution, showing the knowledge that it generates and providing a space for reflection for its academics.  In accordance with the monitoring framework of the 2005 Convention, this measure is part of the actions that "support the development of dynamic cultural and creative sectors", through "measures and policies that support the development of dynamic cultural and creative sectors".
Results: Through the "Artifying Programme", between 2012 and 2020 close to 220 community outreach events took place, which included music, visual arts, dramatic arts and visual arts. Moreover, through contests, between 2010 and 2022 close to 500 projects have been funded in investigation and creation within disiplines such as Architecture, Audiovisual arts, Visual arts, Design, Arts Education, Aesthetics, Literature and Poetry, Music and Theatre, as well as many other initiatives of interdisciplinary nature.  The UC Music Season from the UC Institute of Music. With more than 5,300 attendees over 35 concerts during 2019, until the in-person activities were cancelled due to the social uprising (2019), the pandemic restricted the possibility of public gatherings in 2020. Nevertheless, new formulas were developed in order to give continuity to the UC Music Season and its periodicity, providing, without interruption, a concert each week.   The 2022 edition began with reduced capacities and live streaming at the opening performances: there were more than 4,900 attendees over 44 concerts, inside and outside the University. In 2023, the audience fully returned to the halls: nearly 3,400 attendees were accounted for in the first 31 concerts of the 59th UC Music Season.   These events have strongly impacted the student community access to diverse cultural expressions, as well as supporting the university's own future artists in training. In turn, the great offer of outreach activities creates a relevant platform for artistic activities oriented towards the general public, given that the university is a relevant entity for the programming of cultural activites in the country.
Financial Ressources: 2023: USD 287,533 (Direction for the Arts and Culture). 2023: USD 32,000 (UC Chile Cinema project). 2023: USD 64,400 (Outreach centres). 2023: USD 50,000 (Internationalisation of books). 2023: USD 102,173 (UC Institute of Music).
Recommandations: In 2021 a survey was conducted on the impact of the contest instrument between 2011 and 2020, on the target academic community. The selected academics from the different academic units of the artistic and creative degrees were consulted. All the creation and/or research activities reached their target audience, amounting to hundreds of throusands beneficiaries. The implementation of the projects, has shown to be an effective platform for involving students in research/creation processes, as well as for connecting with other institutions.   Regarding the impact of the arts on the people's well-being, there is a general consensus that these have a positive impact on people's lives, both in aspects of personal satisfaction, and in the emotional sense and the meaning of life. Finally, as far as recommendations are concerned, the suggestion is to foster research and creation in the arts; the survey respondents show interest in the organisation of conferences and []_discussion panels with external guests.

Title EN: Assessing the impact of COVID-19 on the cultural and creative industries: a joint MERCOSUR initiative.
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture
SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Cultural and creative sectors
Cultural Domain: Design,Performing Arts,Media Arts,Cinema and Audiovisual Arts,Music,Publishing,Visual Arts
Agency Implementation: Countries participating in MERCOSUR (including Colombia), UNESCO, IDB, SEGIB and OEI
Main Feature: The study's objectives were to generate indicators to evaluate the impact of COVID 19 on the cultural sector of the region, and to promote technical cooperation in the generation and consolidation of cultural statistics.
Results: The document showed that at least 2.6 million jobs were affected due to the restrictions implemented in the countries, according to data from the Assessment of the impact of COVID-19 on the cultural and creative industries.                           The social distancing measures associated with confinement especially affected the creative and cultural sector, with effects on its entire value chain, further weakening the situation of cultural professionals, mainly workers in micro, small, and medium-sized companies, and artists and independent workers, many of them informal. This project also made it possible to bring together governments and international cooperation organizations to systematize cultural information and statistics at the regional level, an alarming situation was confirmed and made visible.                  Half of the workers and companies participating in the regional survey of this project estimated an 80% loss in income/sales. Activities linked to Heritage, Performing Arts, Training, and Music were the most affected, with drops of more than 20% in the generation of Gross Added Value. At least 71,817 CCI spaces or facilities have been affected by the pandemic: among them, 21,928 libraries, 11,304 cultural centers, 7,516 museums, and 6,908 theaters closed in 2020.                  This document sought to reverse a latent weakness in MERCOSUR by generating valid and updated statistics on the cultural economy through the generation of cultural indicators to support the management of cultural public policies; the production of regional cultural cartography; the socialization of public policies implemented by the cultural institutions of the member states; and the dissemination of studies and research. The document can contribute to promoting a common analysis of the sector through the generation of comparative data in the region and estimating the impact of the pandemic on the cultural goods and services of the countries.

Ces assises ont eu lieu suite à la tenue de plusieurs rencontres et réunions préparatoires de concertation  avec les différents services et acteurs dans le domaine du cinéma, selon qu’ils soient de l’intérieur ou de l’extérieur du pays, durant la période comprise entre le 11 mars 2023 et le 17 avril 2023, dans six (06) wilayas(Départements) pôles qui sont : Constantine, Oran, Biskra, Bejaia, Tipaza et Alger, qui, à leur tour, ont touché et concerné plus de vingt-neuf (29) wilayas à travers le pays, ainsi que les acteurs et intervenants dans le domaine du cinéma en Algérie, résidant dans plus de sept (07) pays en Europe, Amérique du nord et dans le monde arabe.   Le débat intéressant ledit projet de loi sur l’industrie cinématographique, s’est déroulé en ateliers à savoir : •	atelier mécanismes de soutien et de financement du cinéma, •	atelier création cinématographique, •	atelier investissements et industrie du cinéma, •	atelier formations et métiers du cinéma,  •	atelier exploitation et distribution. Les intervenants ont pu, en l’espace des assises nationales, exprimer leurs aspirations et attentes dans un esprit collaboratif avec un sens du devoir national. Les débats ont reflété l’engagement à relancer cette industrie de sorte à répondre aux attentes des différentes générations de public.
Results: Les principaux résultats atteints jusqu’à présent grâce à cette mesure sont : •	Vers la création d’un Centre National Intégré s’intéressant au cinéma et aux arts de l’audiovisuel ; •	Promulgation de la nouvelle loi sur l’industrie cinématographique. .       Identification de  79 terrains d'assiette proposés, relevant du domaine de l'Etat destinées à la réalisation de projets d'investissement  dans l’industrie cinématographique, reparties sur 27 Wilayas (départements),et  24 autres espaces reparties sur 08 Wilayas (départements).
Recommandations: Atelier de mécanismes de soutien et de financement du cinéma : S’agissant du rabattement fiscal : •	Exonération d’impôts pour les établissements de production cinématographique ; •	Exonération de taxes douanières pour les équipements et moyens de production audiovisuelle importés. S’agissant des investissements privés : •	Encouragement de l’investissement privé en matière de production et de distribution cinématographiques par des bonifications fiscales, avec un seuil maximal pour les droits de sponsoring financier ; •	Encouragement des stations et chaines de télévision en Algérie à opter pour une politique de : - Préacquisition des droits ; - Aide à la production de films algériens ; •	Agir de sorte à ce que la télévision devienne un soutien pour les œuvres cinématographiques ; •	Création d’une plateforme de commercialisation et de promotion des films à l’étranger et en faire une ressource en devises ;  •	Création d’un fond destiné à aider les jeunes producteurs et réalisateurs de courts métrages et de films documentaires ; •	Opter pour un guichet unique pour toutes les formalités administratives aux fins de permettre le financement de tout projet cinématographique dans un seul et même centre ; •	Dématérialiser les propositions de projets de manière électronique sur la plateforme du Ministère de la Culture et des Arts dédiée à cet effet ; •	Décentraliser pour répondre aux demandes des sociétés de production cinématographique et leur éviter de se déplacer à Alger pour toute formalité administrative et à la demande croissante dans ce domaine ;  •	Relancer les clubs cinématographiques qui constituent une plateforme importante pour la promotion du cinéma et le renforcement de la prise de conscience culturelle du public à travers la garantie de la liberté de la création cinématographique qui constitue un droit fondamental pour les artistes et créateurs dans l’industrie du film, en ce sens qu’elle leur offre la possibilité d’exprimer leurs idées, avis et créations artistiques de manière libre et indépendante.

Main Feature: Overview  The Ethiopian National Association of the Deaf (ENAD) provided specialized training to 20 members in the fields of music, theatre, and dance. This initiative aimed to equip participants with both technical skills and the broader applications of art for personal and professional growth.  Training Focus 1. Technical Skills: The training covered the fundamental techniques in music, theatre, and dance, ensuring that participants gained a solid grounding in these art forms.  2. Overcoming Challenges: In addition to technical training, the program addressed how individuals with disabilities could use arts as a mechanism to overcome personal and societal challenges. This included strategies for dealing with common obstacles and leveraging artistic expression as a form of empowerment.  3. Art as a Source of Income: The training emphasized the potential of arts as a means of economic empowerment. Discussions included how to build, promote, and sustain a career in the arts, using it as a viable source of income.  4. Global Perspectives: The program incorporated international experiences and case studies from other deaf and disabled communities. This provided valuable insights into how similar challenges are addressed globally and how these lessons could be applied locally.  Goals Achieved Empowerment: Participants developed skills and strategies to utilize arts for personal development and economic benefit.  Encouragement and Promotion: The training fostered a supportive environment for artistic expression and career development.  Global Learning: Exposure to international experiences enriched the participants' understanding and application of arts in overcoming disabilities.  Conclusion The training program significantly contributed to the development of participants by enhancing their technical skills and providing practical solutions for integrating arts into their lives and livelihoods.   The incorporation of global perspectives and practical applications ensured a comprehensive and impactful learning experience.
Results: The art capacity-building program provided significant benefits to 20 members of the Ethiopian National Association of the Deaf (ENAD). This initiative focused on enhancing the artistic skills of individuals with disabilities, with particular emphasis on practical applications in music, theatre, and dance.  Key Benefits: 1. Skill Development: Participants gained technical proficiency in various art forms, contributing to their personal and professional growth. 2. Empowerment: The training offered tools and strategies for overcoming challenges associated with disabilities, using arts as a mechanism for empowerment. 3. Economic Opportunities: Insights were provided on leveraging artistic skills as a source of income, and promoting sustainable livelihood options.  Overall, the program was tailored to address the specific needs of individuals with disabilities, facilitating their engagement in the arts and enhancing their quality of life.

Title EN: Arts Council of Northern Ireland’s Annual Business Plan for 2023-24

Main Feature: The Arts Council of Northern Ireland’s Annual Business Plan for 2023-24 sets out the organisation’s strategic objectives and corresponding actions for the current financial year.    The Business Plan reflects the delivery of the fifth and final year of the Arts Council’s five-year Strategic Framework for developing the arts, 2019-2024, entitled ‘Inspire, Connect, Lead’. It considers the specific strategic context for the arts in 2023-24, including recovery from the pandemic, the impact of the cost of living crisis, Governmental priorities, the implications of the UK’s withdrawal from the European Union, responding to environmental challenges, and reflecting the increasing diversity of Northern Ireland society in the audiences, leaders, producers and creators of a progressive and dynamic arts sector.    Under the Framework’s headings of ‘Inspire’, ‘Connect’ and ‘Lead’, the Business Plan outlines the key actions to be undertaken by the Arts Council this year in regards to: programmes to support reach, artistic quality and innovation; developing the creative workforce; commitment to equality, diversity and inclusion; connecting to strategic partners; national and international representation; engaging with the sector, and; valuing the creative sector.
Results: The Arts Council’s annual programme of funding and research for 2022–23 reflect a return to more normal circumstances, following the extraordinary upheaval caused in the preceding years as a result of the pandemic.
Recommandations: The report states ‘that serious challenges remain for the sector [...] due to, for example, the legacy of the pandemic, the implications of withdrawal from the EU and the significant additional pressures associated with the current cost of living crisis. Despite the many challenges, artists and arts organisations nevertheless continued throughout 2022–23 to demonstrate their resolve and ambition, inspiring audiences throughout Northern Ireland with great art.’    ‘The Arts Council will develop its 2024–29 strategic framework with the creative sector throughout 2023–24. We reviewed our progress against the 2019–24 strategic framework and as of Q2 year four — 66% of actions were completed. In the FY22-23, Arts Council Northern Ireland had 24 dedicated business plan actions that were monitored quarterly. At the end of FY22-23, 22 were on target, 1 was on hold, and 1 was completed. The Hub focuses on nurturing a community of young artists passionate about effecting change and fostering dialogue around thematic societal issues. The primary objective of the ACTION Hub is to provide a platform for young creatives to connect, ideate, and receive mentorship in producing critical audio-visual content that addresses pressing societal issues. By fostering a supportive and innovative environment, the project aims to empower emerging artists into independent creatives while amplifying their voices and contribute to meaningful conversation on thematic societal issues affecting them. Through mentorship and skill-building opportunities, the ACTION Hub seeks to cultivate a new generation of artists with a disruptive mindset, fueling their creativity and passion for driving social transformation. By equipping young creatives with the tools and resources to create critical audio-visual content, the ACTION Hub aims to spark dialogue, raise awareness, and inspire action towards achieving sustainable development goals. By engaging with diverse forms of performing arts such as music, poetry and theatre, the Hub strives to stimulate dialogue, provoke thoughts, and mobilize action within communities and beyond. Overall, the ACTION Hub is a dynamic space that harnesses the power of creativity and collaboration to empower young artists, amplify their voices for change, and catalyze a movement towards sustainable community development. Through this innovative approach to arts and activism, the Hub exemplifies EDZAI ISU’s commitment to using the arts as a tool for social transformation and positive impact on society.

Title EN: ATELIERS DE FORMATIONS DES ACTEURS CULTURELS (AFAC) ET FORUM DES ARTS VIVANTS D’AFRIQUE (FAVA)

Cultural Domain: Design,Performing Arts,Media Arts,Cinema and Audiovisual Arts,Music,Publishing,Visual Arts
Agency Implementation: Le Collectif des Acteurs Culturels (CAC)
Main Feature: Le Collectif des Acteurs Culturels  (CAC) est une association, un groupe de travail, de réflexions apolitiques, culturelles et artistiques dont les travaux et actions visent à promouvoir la structuration et le professionnalisme des acteurs culturels vivants en Côte d’Ivoire.  Les acteurs culturels et professionnels des Industries Culturelles et Créatives (ICC) de Côte d’Ivoire ont décidé de fédérer leurs forces et énergies pour mettre en place des projets de formations, d’information, de sensibilisation, d’échanges, de réseautage et de diffusion.  Cette initiative est née du constat suivant: l’inexistence de structure de formation, le manque de savoir-faire et la méconnaissance des métiers liés aux Industries Culturelles et Créatives (ICC). Ces faits ont amené à mettre en place cette lucarne de rencontre et d’apprentissage avec les acteurs culturels les plus expérimentés en Côte d’Ivoire et dans la sous-région.  Le projet AFAC (Ateliers de Formations des Acteurs Culturels), initié le 20 Avril 2022, répond au besoin de professionnaliser les acteurs culturels et de les rendre compétitif. Les AFAC se déroulent sur un programme qui prend deux années successives en compte d’où chaque deux mois une session de formation se tient en une journée en présentiel et distantiel généralement au Goethe-Institut à Abidjan sur un thème transversal pour permettre aux acteurs de toutes disciples des Industries Culturelles et Créatives de pouvoir bénéficier de cette formation ou de ce renforment de capacité. Ce qui voudrait dire sur un programme de deux (2) ans on comptabilise douze sessions de formations et d’ateliers de haut niveau. Et chaque programme AFAC est couronné par le Forum des Arts Vivants d’Afrique (FAVA).    Le programme  de l'année 2022-2023  a connu une grande réussite et un engouement considérable, avec l'instauration du Forum du droit d’auteur en Côte d’Ivoire qui est devenu une activité majeure des AFAC. La notion du droit d’auteur étant méconnue jusqu’à ce jour et sujet à polémique sous le tropique.  Cette activité devient majeure dans le déroulé du programme, qui se tient chaque mois d’Avril en Côte d’Ivoire, vu que le 26 Avril est consacré à la journée de la propriété intellectuelle, pour ne pas rester en marge de cette journée nous avons à notre tour dédié ce mois important pour notre Forum du Droit d’Auteur.  Il convient de rappeler que les AFAC, le Forum du droit d’auteur en Côte d’Ivoire et le FAVA sont impulsés par le CAC, avec pour leader  l'acteur culturel " SOLDAT JAHBOY" et pour parrain l'acteur culturel "KAJEEM", sans oublier l’implication de partenaires techniques et culturels clés de l’écosystème. Les intervenants, sont des acteurs des Industries Culturelles et Créatives. Ils apportent leurs expertises techniques et leurs expériences au service des projets de chaque participant. Les AFAC ont pour objectifs spécifiques de : -offrir des programmes de formation et des ressources pour aider les artistes et acteurs culturels des Industries; Culturelles et Créatives à développer leurs compétences techniques, leur entrepreneuriat et leur gestion d'entreprise; - Favoriser les échanges, les partenariats et la collaboration entre les participants, ainsi qu'avec d'autres professionnels, experts et institutions; - Analyser les enjeux artistiques du développement de carrière et les problématiques actuelles des Industries Culturelles et Créatives; - Mesurer les aspects juridiques et administratifs du développement de carrière
Results: Les résultats atteints par les AFAC sont:  l' Organisation et la  planification de plus en plus de leurs activités et leur carrière par les artistes ;  - la Coopération entre les associations, les acteurs et les entités culturels; - l' Intérêt pour l’amélioration des conditions des acteurs culturels - l'usage, l'interprétation et la  bonne relation avec la législation en vigueur au plan culturel.

Title EN: ETUDE RELATIVE A LA FISCALITE ET AUX DROITS DE DOUANE APPLICABLES AU SECTEUR  DES INDUSTRIES CULTURELLE ET CREATIVES EN COTE D’IVOIRE
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture
SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Cultural and creative sectors
Cultural Domain: Design,Performing Arts,Media Arts,Cinema and Audiovisual Arts,Music,Publishing,Visual Arts
Agency Implementation: MINISTERE DE LA CULTURE ET DE LA FRANCOPHONIE /Direction de la Promotion de l’Industrie de la Mode et du Design
Main Feature: La présente étude est relative à la fiscalité et aux droits de douane applicables au secteur des Industries Culturelles et Créatives (ICC) en Côte d’Ivoire. Elle été réalisée à la demande du Ministère de la Culture et de Francophonie en juillet 2022. Elle intervient dans le prolongement des négociations du CD2, ou un financement a été alloué au secteur des ICC en octobre 2021, en réponse aux demandes portées par les parties ivoiriennes et Françaises et aux objectifs du PND 2021-2025. Les ICC en Côte d’Ivoire, envisagé par les autorités ivoiriennes et l’Agence Française de Développement (AFD). Cette étude répond à plusieurs préoccupations nécessaires à évaluer la faisabilité du projet et s’inscrit à ce titre dans l’étude de faisabilité du projet de financement du secteur des ICC en Côte d’Ivoire envisagé par les autorités Ivoiriennes et l’Agence Française de Développement (AFD). Les principales caractéristiques de cette initiative sont axées sur trois objectifs spécifiques fixés par le Ministère : - Etablir un état des lieux général du secteur des Industries Culturelle et Créatives en Côte d’Ivoire et spécifique en matière de fiscalité et de droits douane ; - Présenter un aperçu de la fiscalité et des droits de douane existant d’un échantillon de pays ayant des politiques en faveur des ICC volontaires ; - Proposer des mesures fiscales et douanières qui pourraient être envisagées pour améliorer le développement des ICC en Côte d’Ivoire. En Côte d’Ivoire, la Politique Culturelle Nationale définie par la loi n° 2014-425 est mise en œuvre par le Ministère de la Culture et de la Francophonie. Elle a pour objectif de garantir la sauvegarde du patrimoine culturel national, de professionnaliser les secteurs des arts et de la culture et de mettre la culture au centre des stratégies de développement. Pour cela, le pays s’est doté d’un cadre institutionnel et juridique abouti et adapté aux enjeux du secteur des ICC, d’instruments de financement dédiés et d’outils de lutte contre la fraude. En matière fiscale, le secteur des ICC ne bénéficie pas d’un régime particulier et le pays est confronté à une économie sectorielle encore très largement dans l’informel. Pour dynamiser ce secteur certaines mesures existent, notamment, les choix de politique fiscale ont porté sur la dépense fiscale à travers l’octroi d’exonérations fiscales qui représentent des enjeux financiers important pour l’Etat et la compétitivité des entreprises du secteur. En matière douanière, le secteur des ICC s’inscrit dans un environnement interne et externe régi par l’adhésion de la Cote d’Ivoire à la CEDEAO et à l’UEMOA, les règles édictées par l’Organisation Mondiale du Commerce (OMC). Ainsi que l’Organisation Mondiale des Douanes (OMD) et l’instauration de zones de libre-échange. Cependant, bien que constituant un levier favorable à la facilitation et à la globalisation des échanges, ce cadre institutionnel et juridique limite les marges de politique douanière qui restent également sujettes aux dispositifs de réciprocité. Par ailleurs, les ICC se caractérisent par la nécessité d’importer des intrants taxés à des droits de douane élevés qui ont pour effet d’alourdir les couts de productions et de pénaliser les filières de l’édition ,du cinéma, de la musique et de la mode. Malgré les outils institutionnels et juridiques de lutte contre la contrefaçon, l’économie sectorielle reste encore marquée par un niveau de piratage élevé.
Results: L’étude montre que les pays où les industries culturelles et créatives se développent mettent en application des politiques publiques fortes, pour faciliter les échanges, et obtenir des avantages douaniers et fiscaux et en appliquant des régimes douaniers spécifiques. La Côte d’Ivoire dispose des leviers propices au soutien et au développement des ICC qu’il conviendrait de compléter ou optimiser par des mesures de simplication, d’application ou d’adaptation. En matière fiscale, l’institution d’avantages temporaires à la création d’entreprises, la promotion de l’adhésion aux centres de gestion agrée et l’accélération du remboursement de crédits de TVA contribueraient à Soutenir et structurer le secteur par des avantages fiscaux. Il s'agit de : -Créer un instrument incitatif de régularisation des structures évoluant dans l’informel ; -Instaurer des zones franches ciblées aux activités dépendantes des marchés internationaux ; -Favoriser l’installation en Côte d’Ivoire d’activités pérennes en contreparties d’exonérations douanières. L’optimisation des mécanismes fiscaux existants et le soutien aux entreprises des ICC pourrait aussi porter sur la mise en place d’un crédit d’impôt. En matière douanière, le soutien à l’action économique et à la promotion des exportations pourrait contribuer à renforcer le cadre environnemental des entreprises des ICC. La Côte d’Ivoire pourrait enrichir son dispositif en créant des pôles de soutien économique, des Cellules de conseil aux entreprises et un bureau national de promotion des exportations de la culture. Cela passe par : -Optimiser au profit des entreprises des ICC , les régimes d’exonération et de ristourne de droits existants qui permettraient aux entreprises exportatrices de bénéficier d’un remboursement total ou partiel des droits de douane payés sur les intrants importés. - Créer des entrepôts en douane spéciaux spécifiques aux ICC comme instrument de facilitation du développement des exportations - Améliorer l’accès aux mécanismes de garantie existants au profit des entreprises du secteur des ICC en favorisant l’usage des lettres de crédit, l’octroi de garantie publique auprès des établissements de crédits, la création d’un fonds de garantie pour les jeunes entrepreneurs et l’amélioration des conditions d’obtention du label « operateur économique agréé ».
