Title EN: Awareness-raising and promotion of the UNESCO 2005 Convention in Chile.
Goal: Integrate Culture In Sustainable Development Frameworks
SDG: SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: National sustainable development policies and plans
Cultural Domain: Design,Performing Arts,Media Arts,Cinema and Audiovisual Arts,Music,Publishing,Visual Arts
Agency Implementation: Ministry of Cultures, Arts and Heritage (MINCAP).
Main Feature: Chile's commitment regarding the implementation of the 2005 Convention has been reasserted with the recent creation of a cultural state organisation in line with the principles of the Convention, as well as with the delivery of quadrennial periodic reports on its implementation in 2012, 2016, 2020 and the current (2023) year.   These participatory report preparation processes have great importance as they have detected the measures aimed at protecting and promoting the diversity of cultural expressions in the country, thus being a useful instrument for decision-making and the formulation of cultural policies for sustainable development.   At the same time, these reports are mechanisms that provide relevant information for organised civil society, which constantly monitors compliance with the obligations assumed by the State and cultural policies that promote and protect creative work, cultural diversity and heritage within their different meanings.   In this sense, the efforts to implement the 2005 Convention also serve as a contribution to the 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development and the Sustainable Development Goals, highlighting the value of culture as a key factor for inclusive development. Within the 2005 Convention monitoring framework, we can report that this measure gives account of the indicator on “development cooperation strategies that include lines of action supporting diverse cultural expressions”.
Results: Actions implemented by MINCAP as focal point for the 2005 UNESCO Convention, are described below. In 2021, this commitment became established with the implementation of the 2005 Convention, generating a series of actions for diffusion and raising awareness about this international instrument, in collaboration with UNESCO.   In this way, more than 120 people, civil servants from different ministries and services, were trained in scope and content of the Convention, through regional workshops led by Alfonso Castellanos Ribot, member of UNESCO bank of experts in cultural governance. As a conclusion of this training activity, an International Seminar was also held.   These activities led to the creation of an institutional website, specially designed for the dissemination of the 2005 Convention. In 2022 dissemination activities were also caried out to raise awareness about the 2005 Convention, through International Seminars and Training Workshops all over the country, led by Lázaro Rodríguez Oliva, member of UNESCO bank of experts.   A project was also carried out, which included the organisation of the “International Seminar on Intercultural Policies for Plurilingualism in Comparative Perspective” (free translation) and another seminar called “Plurilingualism: A glimpse into the future from the public policy perspective” (free translation)

Title EN: Azadi Ka Amrit Mahotsav
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture
SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Cultural and creative sectors
Agency Implementation: Ministry of Culture, Government of India
Main Feature: Azadi Ka Amrit Mahotsav commemorates 75 years of India's independence with nationwide celebrations, focusing on historical milestones, cultural achievements, and socio-economic progress. It involves various cultural activities, competitions, and events across diverse domains.  1. Duration and Commencement: The Mahotsav officially began on March 12, 2021, marking the start of a 75-week countdown leading up to India's 75th Independence Day on August 15, 2022. It concluded on August 15, 2023.  2. Themes and Objectives: The initiative was structured around five key themes: - Freedom Struggle: Highlighted historical milestones and unsung heroes of India's independence movement. - Ideas 75: Celebrated ideas that have shaped India's socio-cultural fabric. - Achievements@75: Showcased progress across various sectors over 75 years. - Resolve@75: Reinforced commitments to specific goals and targets. - Actions@75: Highlighted current initiatives to implement policies and realize commitments.  3. Nationwide Celebrations: Azadi Ka Amrit Mahotsav involved extensive participation from ministries, states, union territories, corporate houses, NGOs, students, and volunteers across India and globally.   4. Involvement of Various Sectors: The Mahotsav covered multiple cultural domains including cinema/audiovisual arts, design, media arts, music, publishing, visual arts, and performing arts. This breadth ensured a comprehensive representation of India's cultural expressions and achievements.  5. Promotion of Cultural Heritage: Special emphasis was placed on commemorating unsung heroes of the freedom struggle. Activities such as the recording of the National Anthem by over 1.5 crore Indians, competitions on Rangoli making and patriotic songs (Deshbhakti Geet), and initiatives like the Digital District Repository (DDR) for documenting freedom fighters' stories highlighted the cultural richness and historical depth celebrated during the Mahotsav.  6. Youth Engagement: The Mahotsav specifically targeted young people through school and college engagements, competitions, and events like the Bhagat Singh Kabaddi Competition and Khudiram Bose Essay Competition. This engagement aimed to instil a sense of pride and awareness about India's cultural heritage and freedom struggle among the younger generation.  7. Governance and Monitoring: A National Committee headed by the Prime Minister and a National Implementation Committee headed by the Home Minister oversaw the formulation and implementation of various programs. This ensured effective governance and continuous monitoring of activities under Azadi Ka Amrit Mahotsav.  8. Continued Engagement and Future Phases: Beyond the initial celebration phase, future campaigns under themes such as Women and Children, Inclusive Development, and Atmanirbhar Bharat were planned. These campaigns further integrated cultural pride, unity, and sustainable development into the Mahotsav's framework.  In essence, Azadi Ka Amrit Mahotsav not only celebrated India's journey over 75 years but also served as a platform to promote cultural diversity, historical consciousness, and socio-economic achievements across the nation. Its structured approach and extensive participation made it a significant cultural governance initiative under the 2005 Convention on Protection and Promotion of Diversity of Cultural Expressions.
Results: - Cultural Events and Participation: By December 31, 2023, more than 17,000 events were organized across India under the Mahotsav. These events encompassed a wide array of cultural activities, including exhibitions, performances, workshops, and competitions, promoting active participation and engagement from diverse cultural stakeholders.  - Promotion of Cultural Diversity and Heritage: The Mahotsav played a pivotal role in celebrating India's rich cultural diversity and heritage. It highlighted various cultural expressions, traditions, and artistic practices from different regions of India, fostering mutual understanding and appreciation among communities. Support for Cultural Professionals and Performers: The initiative provided a platform for cultural professionals, performers, artists, and artisans to showcase their talents and skills. It facilitated their recognition and contributed to the sustainability of cultural practices by creating opportunities for their artistic expressions to reach broader audiences.  - Capacity Building and Skill Development: Through workshops, training sessions, and mentorship programs, Azadi Ka Amrit Mahotsav also focused on capacity building among cultural professionals. It aimed to enhance their skills, strengthen their networks, and empower them to contribute actively to India's cultural landscape.  - Legacy and Sustainability: Beyond immediate celebrations, the Mahotsav aimed to leave a lasting legacy by encouraging ongoing cultural activities and initiatives. It promoted intergenerational dialogue and transmission of cultural knowledge, ensuring the continuity and sustainability of India's cultural heritage.

Main Feature: La filière des arts dans l’enseignement secondaire a été créée au terme d’une convention conclue entre les deux ministères, Ministère de l’Éducation Nationale et Ministère de la Culture et des Arts, le 15 mars 2022 en application du programme d'action du gouvernement concrétisée par la création d’un Lycée National Artistique « Ech Chahid Ali Maâchi » à Alger comprenant quatre (04) options : •	Théâtre ; •	Arts plastiques ; •	Musique ; •	Cinéma et audiovisuel. La création de cette filière répond à certains besoins et certaines exigences, notamment : •	la promotion des arts, •	la mise en valeur des talents artistiques des élèves, •	la contribution au développement économique du pays. Les élèves inscrits en première année de tronc commun Lettres et Sciences, peuvent être orientés en deuxième année secondaire vers la filière Arts suivant leurs penchants artistiques, à travers : •	l’exploitation des appréciations des enseignants à l’intérieur et à l’extérieur des classes pour identifier et renforcer leurs talents,  •	l’exploitation de questionnaires destinés aux élèves à même de révéler leurs penchants, •	l’organisation d’une journée d’information au profit des élèves ayant exprimé leurs vœux en matière d’options artistiques, •	la préparation de supports médias et papiers pour faire connaître les quatre (04) options proposées dans la filière Arts, •	la remise d’une fiche de vœux aux élèves qui expriment le désir de poursuivre le cursus scolaire dans la filière Arts avec le concours des parents, •	l’élaboration d’une liste préliminaire de ces élèves au niveau de la Direction de l’Education, •	l’encadrement des élèves de la filière Arts par des enseignants du secondaire et des enseignants spécialisés dans la filière artistique des établissements placés sous la tutelle du Ministère de la Cultures et des Arts. La sélection des élèves se fait après étude minutieuse étant donné la forte demande suscitée par cette filière. Cette étude est menée comme suit : •	formation de commissions paritaires interministérielles compétentes chargées de la sélection des candidats proposés au niveau des directions de l’éducation, •	l’admission des élèves à la filière art se fait sur la base de leurs vœux puis soumis à délibération des commissions interministérielles (Ministère de la Culture et des Arts et Ministère de l’Education Nationale), •	établissement d’une liste définitive des élèves de deuxième année secondaire, filière Arts et leur répartition selon leurs vœux, sur les quatre (4) options, en tenant compte de l’équilibre entre les cohortes pour éviter toute surcharge.
Results: Les résultats attendus de cette mesure apparaitront au long terme. Cependant certains d’entre eux peuvent d’ores et déjà être mentionnés, notamment : •	le taux de réussite obtenu pour l’année scolaire 2022-2023, quatre (04) options confondues, est supérieur à 90% ce qui laisse présager un avenir prometteur ; •	les premières épreuves pratiques du baccalauréat artistique session 2024 ont eu lieu au mois de mai 2024 et les épreuves écrites sont programmées pour le mois de juin 2024 ; •	Certaines manifestations nationales ont été relancées par un groupe d’élèves de la filière.
Recommandations: Les perspectives relatives à la filière Arts dans l’enseignement secondaire sont prometteuses et peuvent être résumées en ce qui suit : •	Extension de la filière des arts d’une école secondaire nationale « Ech Chahid Ali Maâchi » à des écoles secondaires régionales au titre de l’année scolaire 2024-2025 ; •	Mise en place de toutes les procédures opérationnelles pour la préparation du « Bachelor of Arts » 2024-2025 ; •	Projet d’ouverture d’instituts nationaux des arts, quatre (04) options confondues, en vue d’accueillir les bacheliers retenus, à concrétiser à partir l’année universitaire 2024-2025 ;  •	Pour garantir une formation de qualité, des mesures ont été retenues, notamment : -	Faire bénéficier les élèves de stages internes et externes pour leur permettre de bénéficier des expériences nationales et internationales dans ce domaine ; -	Approfondir la formation dans le domaine des arts en les reliant à l’histoire de l’Algérie et à son patrimoine culturel ; -	Intégrer cette catégorie dans des postes permanents dès obtention du diplôme.

Title EN: Beyond Borders

SDG: SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 10 - Reduce inequality within and among countries,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Mobility of artists and cultural professionals
Agency Implementation: PRS Foundation
Main Feature: Beyond Borders stimulates and strengthens cross-border collaborations between music creators, performers and presenters. It supports the creation, touring and promotion of innovative and high-quality new music across all genres and encourages engagement with audiences across England, Scotland, Wales, Northern Ireland and the Republic of Ireland through multiple performances and digital activity.    Funding of up to £15,000 is available for projects that include new commissions, recordings and repeat performances of music written in the past five years. Support is given to up to 8-10 projects per year that represent: innovation and quality within the music, programming and performances, and potential for national/international profile; strength and depth of collaboration between cross-border organisations/ensembles/bands and potential for partnership legacy; and potential audience reach and impact and the strength of plans for public engagement.
Results: Beyond Borders was established in 2010 to support high quality co-commissions and tours, stimulating collaboration between composers, performance groups and music organisations across the four UK countries and, since 2014, the Republic of Ireland.    Previous Beyond Borders successes have included Songs of Separation, a collective of 10 female English and Scottish folk musicians whose album won ‘Best Album’ at the BBC Radio 2 Folk Awards 2017, and David Fennessy's ‘Panopticon’, commissioned by Hebrides Ensemble and Psappha, which won the Scottish Award for New Music for Small Scale work. Martin Green’s ‘Flit’, combining live music and animation which reflects on first hand stories of migration, also won over audiences and critics nationwide in 2016, and was funded through Beyond Borders.

Agency Implementation: Mohammed Bin Rashid Al Maktoum Knowledge Foundation
Main Feature: Launched in 2013 by the Mohammed bin Rashid Al Maktoum Knowledge Foundation, the Bil Arabi initiative aims to encourage Arabs to use their mother tongue online and on social media. The initiative focuses on celebrating the Arabic language and its rich cultural heritage, especially on its international day. In November 2021, the initiative was rebranded under the slogan �Arabic is a language of science and knowledge,� emphasizing the role of Arabic in contemporary scientific and knowledge-based contexts. Bil Arabi leverages digital media channels and social media to present various events, spread awareness about the beauty and historical significance of the Arabic language, and strengthen Arab identity among youth.
Results: Since its inception, Bil Arabi has made significant strides in promoting and preserving the Arabic language. The initiative has successfully reached 3.5 billion views of the #Arabic hashtag, indicating widespread interaction and engagement across several countries. By encouraging the continuous use of Arabic on social media platforms, Bil Arabi has helped reinforce the language's relevance in modern communication, contributing to the preservation of cultural heritage and identity. The initiative has also fostered a sense of belonging among Arabic speakers and non-native learners globally, thereby enhancing the visibility and appreciation of the Arabic language in both local and international communities.

Title EN: BOLIVIA LAB
Goal: Integrate Culture In Sustainable Development Frameworks
SDG: SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: National sustainable development policies and plans
Agency Implementation: Viviana Saavedra Del Castillo EMAIL: redbolivialab@gmail.com PHONE: +591 77233662  Cecilia Salazar  EMAIL: redbolivialab@gmail.com PHONE: +591 76982574  Rodrigo Quiroga Castro  EMAIL: rquirogac@gmail.com PHONE +59170675974
Main Feature: Bolivia Lab is an annual film training platform that has been strengthening the Ibero-American film industry since 2009. It provides specialized support in scriptwriting, development, post-production, distribution and exhibition to emerging and senior talents with fiction, documentary, animation and audiovisual innovation projects.  Bolivia Lab strengthens collaboration ties and strategic alliances between Ibero-American countries, enhancing co-production and exchange possibilities for the productive and cultural development of the region. In 2025, it will have 4 sectors (specialized training, industry, community and exhibition) that integrate 15 spaces.  Its main events are: International Screenwriting Workshop, Project Development Laboratory and Finaliza WIP Incentive, strategically designed to strengthen Ibero-American audiovisual production at all stages. In addition, Bolivia Lab is projected as a key space to contribute to strengthening the Sustainable Development Goals (SDG) through film and audiovisual, backed by 15 years of experience in film development in the region.  In its seventeenth edition, Bolivia Lab 2025 is committed to promoting principles of gender equity, diversity, accessibility and respect for the environment. The initiative benefits from a collaborative network that includes management with production houses, embassies, festivals and filmmakers from Ibero-America, creating a network that respects the identities and cultural visions of the continent.  Bolivia Lab seeks to improve the quality and reduce inequality in access to film training, facilitating co-production between emerging countries and those with greater development, in line with the principles of the IBERMEDIA PROGRAM from which it receives support to cover part of the 21 scholarships for project development and 1 for the international scriptwriting workshop.
Results: The Bolivia Lab has generated a significant impact on the film and audiovisual industry in Latin America, standing out as a space for training, development and networking in Bolivia.  Ibero-American Development Laboratory and Film Project Clinic: Over the course of its 15 editions in La Paz and Santa Cruz, the laboratory has supported 314 projects in development, of which 70% have won incentives and completed production. With the support of 224 international advisors, the laboratory has organized 280 master lectures and roundtables. In addition, there are 45 institutions and 35 agreements with festivals and programs, which expand access to funds and networks, including programs such as Ibermedia.  International Screenwriting Workshop: Based in Cochabamba, the workshop, in its 12 editions, has strengthened 183 scripts, many of which have already been turned into films. Complemented by the Screenwriting Incubator, the latter has supported 231 emerging scripts.  FINALIZA Bolivia Lab: In its final phase, Bolivia Lab has evaluated 36 films, supporting the editing and distribution of 24 of them. Of these, 12 films were incentivized with services valued at $10,000 USD and three received supports from the Dolby Atmos fund of $20,000 USD each.  Cinema, Community and Diversity (CCD): This initiative has promoted alliances with 20 institutions to strengthen community and gender cinema, in support of the Sustainable Development Goals (SDG).  Digital Seedbeds: In its five editions, they have involved 1,200 young people in advanced audiovisual technology, including animation and augmented reality.  Bolivia Lab Film Festival: With 14 editions, both in person and online, it has allowed the circulation of Ibero-American cinema, promoting the formation of audiences.  Celumetrajes Festival: Held in Bolivia, Ecuador, Brazil and Chile, this festival has trained students in mobile cinema, in alliance with festivals in Arica and Mambe.  “Bolivia Lab en Corto” Short Film Festival: In its first edition, aimed at film and audiovisual students, it supported everything from the script to post-production, in collaboration with festivals such as Bogoshort and Bamfest. International Pitch Rally: It has trained 40 projects in pitching, offering visibility and co-production opportunities.  Meeting of Communication and Audiovisual Students: In its first edition, it brought together 15 universities to create short content.

Title EN: BUREAU IVOIRIEN DU DROIT DAUTEUR (BURIDA)
Goal: Promote Human Rights And Fundamental Freedoms
SDG: SDG 5 - Achieve gender equality and empower all women and girls,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels
Area of Monitoring: Artistic freedom
Cultural Domain: Design,Performing Arts,Media Arts,Cinema and Audiovisual Arts,Music,Publishing,Visual Arts
Agency Implementation: BURIDA
Main Feature: Le BURIDA est la société de gestion collective des droits d'auteurs et des droits voisins en Côte d'Ivoire. Il veille à la protection des droits des auteurs et des créateurs dans divers domaines artistiques et culturels. Il assure la gestion collective des droits d'auteur, perception et répartition des droits générés par l'utilisation des œuvres protégées.  Il soutien la création artistique et littéraire en offrant des services et des conseils aux auteurs et artistes. Il organise  des ateliers de sensibilisation et de formation pour informer les créateurs sur leurs droits et sur les moyens de les protéger. Il est régit par le décret n°2015-271 du 22 avril 2015 fixant les attributions, l'organisation et le fonctionnement du Bureau Ivoirien du Droit d'Auteur.  Le décret de 2015 est bâti autour d’une idée majeure, à savoir la mise en place des mécanismes susceptibles de garantir une gestion efficiente, transparente et responsable. Cette démarche consiste à intégrer des règles correctives de toutes les faiblesses qui paralysent le fonctionnement normal du BURIDA. Par exemple, le projet de décret institue une Assemblée Générale exceptionnelle pour garantir le respect de l’obligation de reddition des comptes des dirigeants. En effet une première réforme du BURIDA a permis de modifier le décret N° 81-232 du 15 avril 1981, par le décret N° 2008-357 du 20 novembre 2008. Cette nouvelle réforme à son tour permet de remplacer le décret précité. Le décret 2015 comporte 5 chapitres. Le chapitre 1, intitulé dispositions générales est consacré aux définitions des concepts, à l’objet du décret, aux conditions d’adhésion au BURIDA et à la perte de la qualité de membre. Le chapitre 2 traite des attributions du BURIDA. Il présente la mission principale du BURIDA ainsi que ses missions spécifiques. Le chapitre 3 est relatif à l’organisation et au fonctionnement du BURIDA qui est administré par 4 organes. Il fait mention du personnel qui est composé de fonctionnaires et d’agents recrutés. En dehors de ce personnel, il existe des commissions et des agents assermentés qui sont utilisés pour des tâches spécifiques. Le chapitre 4, énumère les sanctions auxquelles s’exposent les associés en cas de violations des règles régissant le fonctionnement du BURIDA. Le chapitre 5 a trait aux dispositions finales. Une innovation dans ce décret, c’est qu’il permet au BURIDA de promouvoir des actions sociales en faveur des artistes sociétaires du BURIDA, de promouvoir et de défendre les intérêts matériels et moraux des sociétaires, de leurs ayants droits, des artistes interprètes et de tous les titulaires de droits voisins.
Results: Les résultats atteints dans la gestion des droits d'auteurs et des droits voisins sont:  -l'amélioration de la protection des droits d'auteur par une meilleure reconnaissance et protection des droits des auteurs et créateurs.; -l' augmentation des revenus pour les artistes  qui passe par la perception et la redistribution efficace des droits d'auteur, augmentant ainsi les revenus des artistes; -le renforcement de la Gouvernance Culturelle  par le renforcement des structures de gouvernance culturelle grâce à une gestion plus efficace des droits d'auteur. la sensibilisation accrue  à travers l'augmentation de la sensibilisation des créateurs et du public sur l'importance des droits d'auteur. la gestion  collective du BURIDA a permis également  les actions suivantes:  -l'adoption des décrets d’application de la loi n° 2016-555 du 26 juillet 2016 relative aux droits d'auteurs et aux droits voisins,   notamment la mise en œuvre de la perception de la rémunération pour copie privée et de la rémunération pour reproduction par reprographie; -l'adoption du décret  relatif droit de suite; - la sécurisation des outils de membres (carte de membre de type visa, attestation de membre avec hologramme) -l'implémentation d’une solution intégrée ERP;  -signature de conventions de réciprocité avec des organismes d’auteurs;  - les campagnes de sensibilisation et de formation des titulaires de droit et de certaines parties prenantes.

Main Feature: L'initiative (Café Culturel/Dialogue des Arts) consiste en un collectif culturel de jeunes dans la ville de Bordj Bou Arreridj, une ville de l'est algérien, initiative placée sous la direction d'une association civile indépendante dénommée Réseau Culturel Kaffaa, cette dernière a des partenariats avec des associations similaires dans de nombreuses wilayas d'Algérie. En plus d’une session principale mensuelle, l’on retrouve les activités suivantes :  le café littéraire pour personnes handicapés, le café pour enfants, le café El Barari qui propose des déjeuners artistiques en plein air (au pied des cascades, dans les forêts, sur les plages, dans les stations touristiques), le lancement de bibliothèques populaires (dans les cafés, les bus, les jardins, les hôpitaux, les salons de coiffure, etc.), la supervision des prix littéraires tels que le prix du récit, la littérature de voyage, les textes humanitaires, organisation d’ateliers de formation pour débutants dans les enceintes théâtrales et cinématographiques et dans les domaines littéraires, l’organisation de festivals de théâtre, etc. L'initiative vise, à travers les activités susmentionnées, à créer des ponts entre les différents arts, ce qui a été son slogan (Dialogue des Arts), dans le but de :  •	Créer des œuvres artistiques communes et des partenariats professionnels entre artistes ; •	Former des artistes débutants dans les domaines artistiques de leur choix ; •	Encourager les jeunes écrivains en leur accordant diverses récompenses grâce notamment à ses réseaux de relations avec les maisons d'édition en Algérie et à l'étranger, initiative qui a été publiée par une vingtaine de jeunes écrivains, dont la plupart pour la première fois ; •	Créer un lien direct entre le monde culturel et les citoyens, loin des espaces clos et isolés, lesquelles activités ne souffrent pas de manque d’audience, mais d’une incompréhension récurrente du grand public ;  •	Offrir un modèle vivant et un espace qui permette à l’activité culturelle de s’exprimer de manière synchrone avec les profondes mutations que connait la société algérienne ; •	Diffuser les valeurs des droits de l'homme, des libertés fondamentales, du dialogue et de la coexistence humaine, à travers la production et la consommation artistiques. Pendant quatre (04) années (2020 – 2023), l’initiative s’est appuyée sur les efforts bénévoles des personnes impliquées, ayant relevé les différents défis liés notamment au manque de financement et aux terribles conséquences de la pandémie du COVID 19. Cependant, l'initiative a su persévérer et récolter de bénéfices conséquents dans la perspective d’un changement de la vision ambiante de l’art, de la littérature et de la créativité culturelle.
Results: Cette mesure a permis de réaliser les résultats suivants : •	organisation de dizaines de séances littéraires et artistiques dans des salles et espaces ouverts, •	lancement de petites bibliothèques dans les cafés, •	organisation des prix de la nouvelle, •	lancement de prix littéraires,  •	organisation du Festival du Théâtre, •	organisation de deux résidences de création pour les jeunes (court métrage, écriture littéraire, dessin, rap), •	réalisation d'un court métrage, •	lancement de quatre spectacles de théâtre où une centaine d'artistes ont été honorés.
Recommandations: Pour atteindre ses objectifs, l'initiative se doit d’approfondir les programmes de formation, sous forme d'ateliers, de camps, de sorties et de résidences de création, de sorte à permettre aux artistes débutants d’acquérir une expérience, des compétences et une technicité qui leur permettra d’évoluer du rang d’amateur au rang de professionnel.

Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture

Area of Monitoring: Cultural and creative sectors
Cultural Domain: Performing Arts,Media Arts,Cinema and Audiovisual Arts,Music,Publishing,Visual Arts
Agency Implementation: CULTURAL FOUNDATION OF THE CENTRAL BANK OF BOLIVIA, CENTER OF THE CULTURAL REVOLUTION
Main Feature: The Cultural Foundation of the Central Bank of Bolivia annually promotes a call for proposals and a public promotion program for the development of arts and culture in the Plurinational State of Bolivia. These initiatives democratize access to state resources, are free, annual and have a national scope. These initiatives have benefited gender equality and artistic freedom in a significant quantitative and qualitative way in recent years, and their results present challenges to continue building ideal conditions to increase the participation of women in the artistic-cultural space.  “Letras e Imágenes de Nuevo Tiempo”  is a call for proposals from the Cultural Foundation of the Central Bank of Bolivia (FC-BCB) which, through the Center for the Cultural Revolution (CRC), focuses on promoting publishing, stimulating creativity, and encouraging critical thinking to strengthen the memory and identity of the Plurinational State of Bolivia. The call promotes the participation of emerging and long-standing artistic-cultural sectors, with the aim of boosting cultural, artistic, and research creation in the country.  Starting in 2021, the FC-BCB, through the CRC, made the decision to acquire (for two years) the rights to the selected works and thus, in addition to publishing and disseminating them, was able to economically recognize the cultural contribution of 67 authors. The theme of the seventh edition was “Women: resistance, cultures, memories and struggles”, with the aim of promoting contemporary political, cultural and social debate and reflection, for the creation of a depatriarchal culture and within the framework of the Comprehensive Law to Guarantee Women a Life Free of Violence (Law No. 348 of March 9, 2013).  The project Promotion of Cultural Productivity and Artistic Creation is focused on promoting artistic creation and cultural production in the following areas of expression: visual, performing, musical and audiovisual arts. It has been developed in the 2023 and 2024 administrations within the framework of the CRC's vocation as an itinerant space for the promotion and stimulation of cultural production and artistic creation, which aims to promote the management of cultural activities and spaces at a national level to foster meetings and dialogue with sectors, cultural organizations, casts, individual and collective artists, among others, within the framework of democracy and interculturality, through research, training, dissemination and cultural promotion of the different artistic and literary expressions in the Plurinational State of Bolivia.
Results: Through the Letras e Imágenes de Nuevo Tiempo call for entries, 66 works have been published since 2021 in the genres of essays, short stories, poetry, drama, photography, comics and audiovisuals. Of these works, 35 have been created by women and 31 by men. The seventh version of the call, focused on women, aroused great interest in the nine departments of Bolivia, which is expressed in the 339 proposals received, which mark a milestone in the most important national development contest of the FC-BCB. Title EN: Campaign "Health insurance for all!"
Goal: Promote Human Rights And Fundamental Freedoms
SDG: SDG 5 - Achieve gender equality and empower all women and girls,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels
Area of Monitoring: Artistic freedom
Cultural Domain: Design,Media Arts,Cinema and Audiovisual Arts,Music,Publishing,Visual Arts
Agency Implementation: Estonian Artists' Association
Main Feature: On August 15th 2022, the Estonian Artists' Association launched an open-ended reminder campaign "Health insurance for all!" with the aim of drawing attention to people without social protection. The campaign highlighted the widespread problem in the creative sector and the changing forms of work, which have made the social problems associated with freelance work very widespread in society.  With more than a thousand members, the Estonian Artists' Association is one of the largest creative associations in Estonia, bringing together artists, designers, art professionals and art scholars from many disciplines. It also has 18 sub-associations and is a member of several local and international associations. As an advocacy organisation, it works on a daily basis to address the concerns of artists and art professionals and supports its members on a wide range of issues.  The campaign is based on outdoor advertising, social media posts and communication with the media, political parties and politicians. A key part of the campaign is the involvement of freelance creators, people and institutions working in the cultural field in raising awareness and finding solutions to the problems.  According to various surveys, 86% of the Estonian working-age population has permanent health insurance and the number of freelance artists in Estonia is estimated to be at least 10 000. It is estimated that more than 100,000 people of working age are without permanent social protection due to freelance work and other forms of work that have changed. The number of freelancers, whatever their field, is difficult to estimate. Existing laws and accounting practices treat freelance work differently or not at all. However, the situation with regard to the availability of social guarantees and the livelihoods of freelancers is worrying.  Due to dispersed employment and low wages, freelance artists do not have access to health insurance, unemployment insurance, parental benefits and a retirement pension that will allow them to support themselves in the future. The employment situation has changed over time as a result of the various crises, and the forms of employment have also become much more flexible. Freelance work and the problems that go with it are no longer confined to creatives.  In the light of ever-changing forms of work and industrial relations, the health insurance system and the system of social guarantees more generally need an urgent change. Wage insecurity is increasing by the day, and the changed forms of work do not guarantee workers health insurance and social guarantees. As a result, tax revenues are falling, and the number of people excluded from the labour market and in need of assistance is increasing. The lack of social guarantees and of preventive and timely access to health care leads to increased medical costs for the sickness insurance funds and livelihood problems for individuals in retirement.  The campaign has now been joined by all the creative associations operating in Estonia, many theatres and cultural institutions, as well as cultural magazines. The campaign has received extensive media coverage and its follow-up activities continue to attract attention. The issues raised by the campaign to improve the situation of creators were included as election pledges in the pre-election platforms of the four political parties. At the same time as the coalition negotiations, an creatives' demonstration took place in Toompea, bringing together representatives from many fields.  Within the framework of the campaign, the Estonian Artists' Association has also created a special edition to accompany the four issues of the magazine Kunst.ee, which the association also distributes to members of the Riigikogu in the Parliament building in 2024. In 2023, the association participated in the Paide Arvamusfestival (Paide Opinion Festival) by organising a public debate on "The livelihoods of freelance artists". The discussion was attended by Tanel Kiik, Member of the Riigikogu, former Minister of Social Affairs and Minister of Health and Labour; Kaupo Koppel, Senior Analyst at the research company Civitta Estonia, artist Paul Kuimet; Õnne Pillak, Chair of the Social Affairs Committee of the Riigikogu and Riina Sikkut, Minister of Health.  Traditionally, major changes in society are only possible when election promises are included in a coalition agreement, so the Estonian Artists' Association started its campaign with seven months to go until the parliamentary elections in Estonia. The campaign, which started in 2022, is open-ended and will continue through various activities until the situation of freelance artists has improved significantly compared to the current situation.
Results: Through campaign activities and information, the understanding and awareness of the complex situation of freelancers and the problems associated with the freelance form of work has improved. This applies to the creative sector, politicians and officials, as well as society at large.  As a result of the campaign's activities, the biggest change to date is the amendment of the Estonian Cultural Endowment Law, which allows for the payment of existing creative work grants as creative work salaries. Summaries of the problems faced by creators have also been included in the election platforms of the four political parties ahead of the 2023 Estonian Parliament elections.  A paradigm shift in the definition of creative activity as work is also important, both with the amendment of the Cultural Endowment Law and in society at large. Defining creators and their activities as work, rather than as hobbies, leisure activities or activities done in the evenings and at weekends after 'real work'. Work that is remunerated and paid for, with taxes that provide the employee with social guarantees, equal rights with other workers and also the opportunity to rest.

Agency Implementation: Cultural Heritage, IP and DGARTES - Directorate General of Arts
Main Feature: “Campilhas” and “International” are two words that evoke two contrasting scales: the scale of a place in the Municipality of Santiago do Cacém, where there is a dam, and the scale of the world. These are the two scales that define this project that intended, on one hand, to implement itself from micro-contexts – avoiding being a foreign body and entering symbiosis with what is “local” – and, on the other hand, to establish ties with what is far away. The project sets to reinvent radio theatre, which is 100 years old, as a “virtual show”, through the participation of writers, musicians and sound technicians with a declared experimental vocation; the work of a group of unemployed people is transformed into dance – a “labor ballet”; the observation of reality is transcended through its fictionalization audiowalks; the artists follow what the audience determines; the work processes are be exposed and demystified before everyone's eyes. Far from understanding the circumstances of its set mission as an adversity, the project uses them as an opportunity to reinvent the very own models of artistic production: “who”, “how” and “what”.
Results: Access and support to/for contemporary arts in low-density municipalities through, inter alia: programming of artistic productions, involvement of residents in creative processes and audience development activities. Mala Voadora and its partners have devised a plan in which the plurality of activities is deduced from the plurality of the municipality's population: both their specificity (age, cultural, social) and the challenges to be overcome. The plan operated on the territory: it intervened socially, increased, and qualified the cultural offer, liaised with the municipality, integrated local structures, and agents, promoted the region, generating new flows with a cultural, social, and economic impact. Reaching the population via radio helped to overcome territorial dispersion, as well as the mobility difficulties of senior citizens. The mediation work was carried out systematically. Various sectors of the population have been captivated and drawn into the artistic practices, through artistic programming and audience development activities. Some had an active voice in the work processes: the school audience on the show to be performed; the senior audience on the radio narrative, boosting, in the various layers of the population targeted, namely the younger layer, a transformation beyond short-term enjoyment. As part of the project, many national and international artists have passed through the municipality, gaining a familiarity that will enhance the future development of other projects. A network of relationships was created between audiences, local cultural agents, and the national and international artistic fabric, which not only underpins the future, but will continue to be intensified and expanded through the activities programmed by Mala Voadora at the Campilhas Dam.

Title EN: Canada’s Policy on Audiovisual Coproduction
Goal: Achieve A Balanced Flow Of Cultural Goods And Services And Increase The Mobility Of Artists And Cultural Professionals
SDG: SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 10 - Reduce inequality within and among countries,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Treaties and agreements
Agency Implementation: Department of Canadian Heritage
Main Feature: An audiovisual treaty coproduction is a feature film or television production that has been created by pooling creative, technical and financial resources of Canadian and foreign producers. Governed under the terms of a treaty, these productions are granted national status, and as such, are also eligible for federal tax credits and provincial tax credits and additional funding sources such as the Canada Media Fund and the Canada Feature Film Fund.  Canada’s Policy on Audiovisual Coproduction outlines Canada’s new approach to Audiovisual Coproduction Treaty negotiation with the ultimate goal of modernizing old treaties and signing of new treaties in order to stimulate investment in Canada, generate employment for Canadians, and establish or expand international markets for Canadian talent and audiovisual productions. The modernized treaties also refer to the UNESCO Convention on the Protection and Promotion of the Diversity of Cultural Expressions, which encourage the conclusion of coproduction treaties as one of the means to promote international cooperation.  Canada was one of the first countries to recognize the advantages of audiovisual treaty coproductions.
Results: Since 2020, Canada has signed two modernized coproduction treaties with France and Switzerland. In this timeframe, the treaties with Switzerland and France have yielded 43 coproductions and approximately CAD 278 million in total budgets. These signings are part of the ongoing implementation of the Coproduction Policy that has produced nine treaty signings since its inception.   It remains too early to provide a clear picture of the impact of these treaties (the Swiss treaty, for example, has yet to be ratified) but other recent coproduction treaty modernizations have deepened ties between the Canadian audiovisual industry and those of its partners and have often led to higher levels of production with those partners and/or higher budgets.
Financial Ressources: The implementation of Canada’s Policy on Audiovisual Treaty Coproduction does not require the investment of financial resources, other than human resource expenditures by the Department of Canadian Heritage.

Title EN: Canadian Commission for UNESCO: Connecting Culture and Sustainability
Goal: Integrate Culture In Sustainable Development Frameworks
SDG: SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: National sustainable development policies and plans
Cultural Domain: Design,Performing Arts,Media Arts,Cinema and Audiovisual Arts,Music,Publishing,Visual Arts
Agency Implementation: Canadian Commission for UNESCO (Canada Council for the Arts)
Main Feature: Connecting Culture and Sustainability was an online event that was co-hosted with the Canada Council for the Arts, and which included guests from a range of stakeholders in arts and culture. This was the first time that the Canadian Commission for UNESCO (CCUNESCO) brought together its partners in culture to discuss the 2030 Agenda. The event tackled questions concerning the ways the culture sector as a whole can significantly impact sustainable development. These included: -	What is the link between culture and sustainability? -	How is culture an asset for sustainable development – especially when faced with global challenges? -	How can we ensure that culture is represented in sustainable development plans?
Results: The event was well received and is influencing ongoing efforts for the greening of the arts sector in Canada.  With the creation of the 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development, culture was included in the global development agenda as part of the 17 Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) in an unprecedented, cross-cutting way. Although no single goal is devoted to culture, cultural aspects are weaved throughout the different goals and targets, such as those related to climate action, sustainable cities, poverty reduction, and food security.  CCUNESCO will continue to engage with its partners on connecting culture, climate, and the SDGs.
Recommandations: Key findings from the conversation included:  •	Culture and the arts connect people to place and to one another; they hold the potential to raise awareness about climate issues and to be a generator of climate action. •	Mobilization for climate action is happening across the arts and culture communities. Ongoing movements can be better connected to the international frameworks on climate change and sustainable development. •	Among the 17 goals, Climate Action (SDG 13) is essential and will have an impact on all other elements. Action needs to be taken now. •	Indigenous peoples must be at the heart of conversations about culture and the SDGs in Canada. •	Methods must change for systems to change: implementing inclusive and participatory governance is a form of climate action. •	Reporting and monitoring are key to demonstrating the impact of the arts and culture in sustainable development and developing action plans. •	Youth must be engaged and empowered as a source of action and change. •	Existing networks, such as the UNESCO Creative Cities Network, should be harnessed for raising awareness and sharing wise practices.

En 2021, l’opérateur a notamment soutenu le projet « Égalité femmes-hommes : les nouvelles voix féminines coréennes » en Corée du Sud. Title EN: Certification of competencies, innovation and productivity. Transforma Economía Creativa - Chilecreativo.
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture
SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Cultural and creative sectors
Cultural Domain: Design,Performing Arts,Media Arts,Cinema and Audiovisual Arts,Music,Publishing,Visual Arts
Agency Implementation: Production Development Corporation (CORFO).
Main Feature: Transform Creative Economy aims to improve the competitive edge of cultural economics in Chile, by strengthening human capital, innovation and productive capacity, with the goal of resolving coordination failures and removing obstacles in strategic productive sectors like the Chilean creative economies.   A proposed target for 2025 is the full integration of the Chilean creative sector into the global economy, exporting goods and services based on individual and collective creative talent. In this way, the aim is for the Chilean creative sector to be recognised as a consolidated productive activity that, beyond its social and cultural importance, creates wealth and jobs in a sustainable and inclusive manner.   The goals of this measure are to increase exports of creative goods and services, to instill and certify business skills, to incorporate funding sources specific to the creative sector and to gather market intelligence in order to guide strategic decisions on commercial matters, on content development and technology investment. In practice, these actions lead to scholarships awarded for training courses, training with a sector-specific approach, as well as providing resources for strategic initiatives outlined in a road map.   This measure, in accordance with the monitoring framework of the 2005 Convention, is part of the indicator on "measures and policies that support the development of dynamic cultural and creative sectors".
Results: Goals were set in 2017, as a long-term vision of the Transform Creative Economy Programme. For Chilecreativo, the CORFO project that is host to the programme, specific targets were defined regarding the impact of the creative sector on the Chilean economy (technological, territorial and industrial development) In the case of the creative industries' contribution to the Gross Domestic Product (GDP), that in Chile corresponds to 12 productive sectors, the measurements obtained showed that this sector had a 1.6% share of national GDP (measurements published in 2016 using data from 2014).   The inital target at the beginning of the programme was to have a 3.6% share of GDP by 2026 (the previous measurements carried out on the contribution of the creative sector to GDP, from 2019, indicated a 2.78% share). In the case of creative goods and services exports, which were USD 45 billion in 2017, the inital proposed target was to double these, reaching USD 90 billion.   In the last measurement carried out, the creative goods and services exports reached approximately USD 83 billion. Another target was to establish an enabling platform for the regions, that is, a meeting place where territorial gaps and strategic initiatives can be gathered together with funding, hand in hand with the regional governments. In this respect the National Network of Creative Territories was developed and is currently being funded, which at the moment has members from eight of the country's regions.
Recommandations: In total for this period, activities on the roadmap have managed to leverage 44.7 times the baseline budget of Chilecreativo reaching a total investment of more than $56 thousand million which represents $64 million dollars approx. At present, the programme is in the formalisation phase of its recently approved renewal for three more years (2023-2026 period).   The goals for this new stage will be on three areas (and not on sectors as was initially done). Work will be done in a dimension around technological development, territorial development and industrial development. There are 22 initiatives in these three areas and where the strengthening of intelectual property component will be the fundamental pillar, as well as the professionalisation of the sector and the creation of technological Sandbox (isolated testing environments where software and application experimentation, development or testing can take place without affecting existing systems or the main infrastructure) related to artificial Intelligence (AI).   An important part of the challenges of the programme at this stage will be to design a continuity model for when the project ends in 2026.

Title EN: CARTOGRAPHIE DES INDUSTRIES CULTURELLES ET CREATIVES (ICC) EN COTE D’IVOIRE
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture
SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Cultural and creative sectors
Cultural Domain: Design,Performing Arts,Media Arts,Cinema and Audiovisual Arts,Music,Publishing,Visual Arts
Agency Implementation: Ministère de la Culture et de la Francophonie
Main Feature: Dans le cadre du troisième contrat de développement et de désendettement (C2D3) le ministère en charge de la culture de Côte d’Ivoire a commandité une étude de marché du secteur des industries culturelles et créatives (ICC) ivoiriennes. Cette activité consiste à mener une étude approfondie sur les ICC en Côte Ivoire, en vue d’actualiser les données existantes, de cartographier les différents secteurs des ICC, d’analyser leur poids économique, et de formuler des recommandations stratégiques pour le développement de ce secteur. Cette étude revêt une grande importance dans le cadre de l’instruction du projet C2D culture et a pour objectif d’informer les autorités et les acteurs économiques sur le potentiel du secteur des ICC. Les négociations pour le troisième contrat de désendettement et de développement CD2 ont permis à la Côte d’Ivoire et à la France de dégager une enveloppe de 17,2 milles euro (11 MILLIADRS de FCFA ) pour le développement du secteur des ICC. Considérant ce secteur comme stratégique, les interventions vont cibler 4 axes prioritaires, que sont: -les infrastructures et équipements culturels ; - le développent de l’entreprenariat ; - la formation aux métiers des ICC et la gouvernance et les droits d’auteurs. En effet le secteur des ICC en Côte d’Ivoire est dans une dynamique ascendante à l’international est considéré comme un secteur stratégique par les autorités ivoiriennes. Elles en ont fait une priorité nationale eue égard aux implications des plus hautes personnalités dans la promotion de ce secteur et à la part consacrée à la culture dans le budget de l’Etat, qui reste cependant faible. Il n’en demeure pas moins que le potentiel économique du secteur des ICC de la Côte d’Ivoire est très fort. Estimé à 2,43% du PIB en 2012, l’objectif des autorités ivoiriennes est de doubler le poids économique de ce secteur en le hissant à 4,4% à l’horizon 2025. Cet objectif ne peut être atteint que si la structuration de son écosystème et le renforcement de sa chaine de valeur se poursuivent. Des études préliminaires ont mis évidence des insuffisances telles que le manque de compétence, le difficile accès au marché international, les frais liées au cadre normatif et le manque de financements. Pour mener à bien cette mission, les étapes suivantes sont prévues: -effectuer une revue documentaire des ICC en Côte d’Ivoire -établir une cartographie des filières ICC et de leur poids économiques respectifs; - effectuer une analyse comparée du dispositif institutionnel ivoirien relatif aux ICC en se basant sur les expériences du Sénégal, du Bénin, du Maroc et la France; - réaliser une analyse croisée de l’étude de faisabilité du projet.
Results: Les résultats attendus par cette mesure sont : - décrire les différentes filières des ICC; - mettre en évidence l’évolution historique récente et la tendance du marché (y compris les possibles scénario futurs) ; - identifier les enjeux du développement durable, l'impact économique et social (PIB culture, emploi et consommation des ménages ); - identifier les enjeux de la Règlementation /gouvernance - mette en évidence la représentation des femmes et des jeunes - établir la typologie des emplois (stables ou précaires), niveau de salaire et de formation; -établir la typologie des entreprises pour chaque filière des ICC (entrepreneur individuel, petite ou moyenne entreprise, multinationale, association, société privée ou informelle) -décrire leur modèle d’affaire (profil détaillé des cous et des revenus, vitalité financière); -identifier les capacités et expériences des différents acteurs à générer des partenariats avec des ONG, et des bailleurs de fonds; -décrire les associations professionnelles existantes -décrire les besoins et les freins au développement de chaque filiale.

Goal: Integrate Culture In Sustainable Development Frameworks
SDG: SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: International cooperation for sustainable development
Cultural Domain: Design,Performing Arts,Media Arts,Cinema and Audiovisual Arts,Music,Publishing,Visual Arts
Agency Implementation: Commission Nationale de  la Francophonie (CNF)
Main Feature: La Journée Internationale de la Francophonie, célébrée le 20 mars chaque année, est une occasion pour les pays francophones de célébrer leur langue commune et leur diversité culturelle. Cette journée est marquée par une série d’événements culturels, éducatifs et festifs organisés dans les pays membres de l'OIF. Les activités incluent des concerts, des expositions d’art, des projections de films, des conférences, des concours littéraires et des événements sportifs. L'objectif est de promouvoir la langue française et les valeurs de solidarité et de diversité culturelle au sein de la communauté francophone.
Results: La célébration de la Journée Internationale de la Francophonie a permis de : - Renforcer les liens culturels et linguistiques entre les pays francophones. - Promouvoir la langue française et la diversité culturelle à travers des événements variés. - Sensibiliser le public aux valeurs de la Francophonie, telles que la solidarité et le respect des droits de l’homme. - Mettre en lumière les talents artistiques et littéraires des jeunes francophones. - Encourager l’apprentissage et l’utilisation du français comme langue de communication internationale.
Recommandations: L'évaluation a montré que la  célébration de la Journée Internationale de la Francophonie est un événement efficace pour promouvoir la langue française et la diversité culturelle. Les principales recommandations sont  : -Accroître la portée des activités de la Journée Internationale de la Francophonie pour toucher un public plus large, notamment dans les zones rurales. -Renforcer les partenariats avec les organisations locales et internationales pour diversifier les sources de financement et les ressources disponibles. -Développer des programmes éducatifs et de sensibilisation pour encourager l’apprentissage du français chez les jeunes. -Utiliser les nouvelles technologies et les médias sociaux pour promouvoir les événements et atteindre une audience plus jeune et connectée. -Assurer un suivi des activités et des résultats pour mesurer l'impact et améliorer les futures éditions de la célébration.

Title EN: Cinema development cooperation between Viet Nam and France
Goal: Achieve A Balanced Flow Of Cultural Goods And Services And Increase The Mobility Of Artists And Cultural Professionals
SDG: SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 10 - Reduce inequality within and among countries,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Flow of cultural goods and services
Agency Implementation: Ministry of Culture, Sports and Tourism, French Institute in Ha Noi
Main Feature: During the period 2020–2023, through the French Embassy and the French Cultural Institute in Viet Nam, Viet Nam and France have seen many cooperative activities in the field of cinema, as follows:  - Since the end of 2022, every year, the French Embassy and the French Cultural Institute in Viet Nam have introduced over 40 French movies to audiences in three major cities in Viet Nam including Ha Noi, Ho Chi Minh City, and Da Nang. Additionally, an event introducing French cinema is held annually on two leading digital video platforms in Viet Nam including Danet and FPT Play.  - France has regularly sent representatives to attend Vietnamese cinema events such as Ha Noi International Film Festival, Da Nang Asian Film Festival etc., and has nominated and sponsored film experts to attend and deliver speeches at seminars, conferences, and forums related to policy development and film industry development in Viet Nam such as the Forum "Viet Nam’s Tourism and Cinema - Connect to Fly high" within the framework of the Joint Program to develop Vietnamese tourism through cinema, hosted by the Ministry of Culture, Sports and Tourism in 2023 etc.  - In 2022, the French National Cinema Center (CNC) established the CNC Prize with the worth of 8,000 Euro for the best Southeast Asian film project within the framework of Autumn Meeting, an annual film event organized by a number of Vietnamese directors and producers. The Autumn Meeting aims to bring together a community of young Vietnamese and international independent filmmakers to participate in a workshop lasting more than a week with classes on directing, art design, acting, film production, etc., as well as seminars among the film-making community on cinema-related issues, sharing experiences, and looking for opportunities to introduce the works of young filmmakers to audiences and international film festivals, etc.  - CNC and the French Institute in Paris have also provided financial support for a number of projects by young and independent Vietnamese filmmakers, including two films in the period 2020-2023.  - In 2023, the 45th Three Continents Film Festival (from November 24 to December 3) in Nantes, France, in collaboration with the Viet Nam Film Institute (Ministry of Culture, Sports and Tourism) screened 21 classic Vietnamese films for free in a special program, introducing Vietnamese cinema to French and international viewers.
Results: In cinema development, cooperation and support activities between France and Viet Nam in the period 2020–2023 have played a significant role in strengthening and consolidating cultural relations between the two countries and made meaningful contributions to the development of Viet Nam's film industry. French cinema introduction programs are held every week in major cities of Viet Nam, contributing to increasing opportunities to access and enjoy culture for Vietnamese people. In 2023, the annual event introducing French cinema on two Vietnamese digital video platforms attracted more than 1.6 million views. The film "Inside the Yellow Cocoon Shell," sponsored by CNC, won the Golden Camera Award for Best First Feature Film at the 2023 Cannes Film Festival.

Main Feature: The Cinema in Prisons program integrates film exhibition to the activities of the country's Penitentiary Units, accompanying the policies of social inclusion and expansion of rights and understanding access to culture as an indispensable right for human development. It is a public policy carried out by INCAA in conjunction with ENERC and the NATIONAL PENITENTIARY PROCURATE and has been operating since 2017. It is carried out from training in prisons as well as the screening of films and audiovisual cultural goods in such establishments for the population in the context of confinement. In this way, we continue to support the policies of social inclusion and expansion of rights, understanding access to culture as an indispensable right for human development.

The program, of federal scope, reached establishments of the Federal Penitentiary System in Misiones, La Pampa, Chubut, Neuquén, Salta and Buenos Aires. More than 700 inmates participated in the program.  The INCAA's program of access to culture, Cinema in Prisons, held two screenings as part of the commemoration of International Women's Day in the cities of Villa María, Córdoba, and Los Hornos, Buenos Aires.  On March 8, 2023, in Córdoba, a day of film debate was held with "Gilda, no me arrepiento de este amor", by Lorena Muñoz, together with the program Gafas Violetas, the Espacio INCAA Villa María, and the collaboration of the Penitentiary Service. The screening took place in a specially prepared room in the chapel of Unit No. 5 of Villa María, and was attended by more than fifty women who actively participated with opinions, comments, reflections and questions. The debate revolved around the struggle of women to carry out their dreams, overcoming social and family mandates.   On March 15, in Los Hornos, province of Buenos Aires, the Women's Week function was organized jointly with the Buenos Aires Penitentiary Service. Fifty-five people participated in this event, which was held in the SUM of Unit No. 8 of the women's prison.

Title EN: Cinema in Education
Goal: Promote Human Rights And Fundamental Freedoms
SDG: SDG 5 - Achieve gender equality and empower all women and girls,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels
Area of Monitoring: Gender equality
Agency Implementation: CSO NAME: Ma3mal 612 Think Factory EMAIL: Ma3mal612@gmail.com    PHONE: +962795858188
Main Feature: Cinema in Education Project’s grand aim is to create a Module to ​”Support to film and audiovisual schools & organizing series of film screenings addressing youth and women in the Maghreb-Mashreq region” ​to achieve this the module will contain full range of information that the user needs to successfully implement the gender sensitive method. It aims to create an impact on the way that film students plan their future films and their projects. The devising of the module and structure will contain teaching content that includes: (exercises) about creating messages and sub-messages aim to enhance the image of women, avoiding common stereotyping, and showing different roles of women in a positive structure, highlight the main obstacles and struggles that women face.  The formulation of the module and its structure included educational content incorporating exercises focused on creating messages and sub-messages to enhance the portrayal of women. Emphasis was placed on avoiding common stereotypes and presenting diverse roles of women in a positive light, thereby spotlighting the primary obstacles and struggles faced by women. In essence, the module aimed to establish specific criteria, provide guidance on gender-related topics, furnish instructions, propose assessment methodologies, and offer examples of activities and materials conducive to leading gender-related initiatives.  The intention was to employ impactful and persuasive mechanisms to address gender disparity. Consequently, it became imperative to train students and professors in the methodology of screenings, enabling them to effectively target audiences and position gender issues through systematic discussions.  About the curriculum:  This educational curriculum aims to address and challenge stereotypical images of women in cinema by adopting a more objective gender approach. Targeted at higher education students in Arab universities from Jordan to Morocco, it engages them both theoretically and practically. The curriculum begins by diagnosing the stereotypical portrayals of women in cinematic imagination and reconstructing these portrayals rationally through descriptive and synthetic analysis. Cinema, as a convergence of past and contemporary arts and a subject around which social, psychological, political, and cognitive sciences revolve, provides a rich foundation for this curriculum. It examines degrading images of women, exploring their historical causes, formal and thematic manifestations, and their impact on cinematic reception. This exploration is conducted through various textual and extra-textual approaches, such as structuralism, semiotics, sociology, and psychology. The curriculum builds upon the legacy of women's studies in cinema, particularly in the United States and the United Kingdom. These studies emerged in the early seventies as part of cultural studies and women's movements, addressing issues such as the marginalization of women's roles in cinema and the effort to replace classical cinema with committed cinema. The goal was to push for women to play new roles in all expressive forms inside and outside cinema. This curriculum seeks to create a communication platform between the contemporary roles of women (both inside and outside cinema) and their representation on the big screen. It aims to prevent dominant cinema from continuing to display derogatory female images and to promote women's cinema as an alternative to counter-cinema, experimental, or independent cinema. This cinematic experimentation relies on deconstructing the iconic dimension of women in dominant cinema, which has traditionally reduced women's representation to a single, mythological image that is fixed and eternal, thus outside history. This practice has provided the world with a singular explanatory model despite the multiplicity and diversity of events. In contrast, the images and roles of men in cinema are more precise and diverse, especially in terms of iconic narration. The curriculum ultimately presents a set of lessons developed by a group of academic researchers. These lessons are distributed between the analytical and interpretive approaches, with the gender approach at their core. However, this gender approach is from a new perspective, breaking away from past views and necessitating a breach of the viewer's previous knowledge or a shift from their expectations (from narrative schemes and mental characteristics). The curriculum opens up to questions such as: Who makes the film and why? Who watches the film and how? And why is it watched in one way and not another? These questions address reactions closer to superficial viewing than to analytical viewing that produces a knowledgeable discourse. This superficial viewing, which does not separate itself from its subject, is one of the reasons for the decline in the artistic level of cinema and the escalation of cinematic clichés, including harmful representations of women. The success or failure of this curriculum depends on surpassing previous ontological theories and relying on modern and more effective theories and methodologies. The objective is to achieve the results and goals for which this curriculum was created. The curriculum is titled: "The Curriculum in the Impact of Gender Awareness on the Educational Outcomes of Film Students in Mashreq and Maghreb Universities." In summary, this curriculum is designed to confront and deconstruct the stereotypical and often harmful portrayals of women in cinema, particularly in the Arab world. By leveraging modern theoretical frameworks and analytical approaches, it aims to educate and empower students to recognize, analyze, and ultimately challenge these stereotypes. The curriculum emphasizes the importance of understanding the historical and cultural contexts of these portrayals and promotes the creation of a new cinematic narrative that accurately and respectfully represents women's diverse roles and identities. It seeks to bridge the gap between contemporary women's roles in society and their representation in cinema, striving for a more inclusive and equitable cinematic landscape. Through this curriculum, students will be equipped with the critical tools necessary to engage with and transform the dominant cinematic narratives that have long perpetuated gender stereotypes.
Results: Curriculum Formulate that targets students of universities written by experts and academic stakeholders on gender and cinema. https://drive.google.com/file/d/13CD_PPpje-7nsIfG3yQSpHk8Xo-Z6EoS/view  Multiple talks and events at universities to advocate and explain the curriculum and its various recourses and exercises. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=qHo1r_VGWiY&feature=youtu.be  An expert symposium in the Karama Human Rights Film Festival: Cinema in Education Seminar by the support of UNESCO and the European Union (a project of Ma3mal 612 Think Factory) To advance a gender-responsive film sector in The Maghreb region and the Levant.  About the Project: Cinema in Education (CIE) is a project that is implemented in the Maghreb-Mashreq region, in support of film and audiovisual educational institutions. The Project is working in order to create a systematic approach that introduces a gender sensitive and responsive ideological framework for audiovisual teachings and production. The methodology of the project integrates formal and informal education, advocacy and curriculum writing, with a heavy focus on young creators and audiences. The process of implementation is as follows; A drafting committee of professors, in Jordan and Morocco, collectively create gender responsive curricula, followed by a nuanced validation process and experimental implementation in film and art institutes. During the validation process, round tables with professors and professionals are set up to integrate feedback and development into the project. The final curricula will be distributed to several universities and audiovisual schools around the MENA region for implementation. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=cRCrjNZXfaw&feature=youtu.be

Specific objectives include:         •	Promote peace and reconciliation in communities affected by violence.         •	Provide training in circus arts and other cultural disciplines.         •	Promote the personal and social development of participants.         •	Create a sense of belonging and community. Since its inception, the program has had the active participation of 60 to 70 people per group, mainly children and young people.         2.One of the most notable results is the development of circus and artistic skills among the participants. Children and young people have learned to handle circus instruments, such as juggling and acrobatics.         3. By creating murals and urban art projects, the program has contributed to the visual and functional improvement of previously abandoned public spaces. These projects not only beautify the environment, but also promote a sense of belonging and community pride.         4. The cultural presentations made by the participants have enriched the cultural life of their communities. These events not only demonstrate the talents developed, but also encourage appreciation of art and culture among viewers.

Title EN: Collaboration of BÍL - Federation of Icelandic Artists with the Icelandic Government on the issues of arts and culture
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture
SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
