Title EN: Cultural Passport
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture
SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Cultural and creative sectors
Agency Implementation: Ministry of Culture of the Republic of Lithuania;  Ministry of Education, Science and Sports of the Republic of Lithuania; Martynas Mažvydas National Library of Lithuania
Main Feature: Cultural Passport – a tool intended for every student from 1st to 12th grade and provides each student with an amount of money (11 EUR per student in 2024) to spend on cultural education activities. It was initiated in 2018 with EU funds, and since 2020, the project has become an ongoing activity funded by the state. After updating the Cultural Passport regulations, the aim is that each of the provided educational activity is adapted for participants with at least one special (individual) need.  On 21 November 2022 the Minister of Culture approved a new thematic priority of the Cultural Passport for 2023-2026, to promote the conscious involvement of children and young people in cultural activities that ensure coexistence, sustainability, citizenship and social equality. For more information: ĮV-921 Dėl Kultūros paso tematinio prioriteto tvirtinimo (lrs.lt);   During the period 2022-2024, the priority project of the XVIII Government of the Republic of Lithuania "Sustainable Interaction of Culture and Education" was implemented, part of which was dedicated to the improvement of Cultural Passport services.   Achieved benefits of the project: Strengthened students' cultural competencies. After using the services of the Cultural Passport, all students strengthen at least one of the competencies: critical thinking, cultural (cultural awareness, cultural expression), creativity. And at least one of the general competencies: communication, cognition, citizenship, digital, social, emotional and healthy lifestyle.  More inclusive evaluation of applications. Each submitted application providing cultural service is evaluated by 3 experts, among whom must be cultural and educational experts. In total, the commission consists of 30 experts: 17 according to the field of art or genre, 10 experts in the field of education and 3 experts from the Lithuanian School Students' Union, Lithuanian Disability Forum, NGO Confederation for Children. Expert representation of arts fields allows for a more accurate assessment of applications and the provision of quality services.  Better quality cultural education services provided by cultural institutions and artists. The integrated feedback tool in Cultural Education Information System (CEIS) allows teachers and students to evaluate the visited Cultural Passport activities. Continuous monitoring of feedback is carried out, during which 90 percent of visited and evaluated educations are evaluated as good, very good and excellent. The project made it possible to create a solid foundation for further cooperation and growth between culture and education, ensuring that cultural education becomes an integral part of student education, and cultural institutions become an important, reliable and quality content-providing educational partner in formal and informal education.
Results: Project results: Successfully implemented Cultural Education Information System (CEIS). The system is based on the blockchain technology and allows schools and cultural institutions, educators to cooperate more easily; helps service recipients (students coordinated by teachers) to easily use the benefits of cultural education services offered by service providers. The created system contributed not only to the improvement of the quality of the offered cultural services, but also to the strengthening of the development of cultural competences, ensuring that more than 80% of Lithuanian students strengthened their cultural competences. Cultural Passport has been expanded. This development is important to ensure that cultural education reaches an even wider audience, including pre-school students and Lithuanian communities abroad. The inclusion of Lithuanian schools abroad helped to strengthen the Lithuanian identity and cultural connection among Lithuanians living abroad and encouraged their more active participation in the cultural life of Lithuania. Competence Development and Education Centre (CDEC) was established in Martynas Mažvydas National Library of Lithuania. From 2024, CDEC is also responsible for funding Cultural Passport. This helped to ensure that the project's objectives were achieved and ensured further development and continuity of operations. In 2025, the inclusion of pre-school education students is planned. 170 education services have been created for them in the CEIS system.  Cultural Passport statistics: In 2023 CEIS had more than 3,000 educational activities (services), over 1,400 service providers, 36 000 of educations held, 925 000 participations in activities. In 2024, 6 Lithuanian schools abroad used the services, 50 educational activities took place with 1040 participating students.  In order to ensure the smooth use of the system, from year 2022 consultations, trainings for Culture Passport service providers, school community members, Culture Passport coordinators have been carried out. In total, 22 virtual consultations were held – trainings for Culture Passport service providers, school communities, in which about 1,600 participants took part.  Based on 2024 data, there are 3847 services offered on the Culture Passport system. It includes: 1,596 services adapted for individuals with mobility disabilities. 433 services adapted for individuals with visual impairments. 758 services adapted for individuals with hearing impairments. 1,088 services adapted for individuals with intellectual disabilities. 170 services adapted for preschool-age students. 295 services adapted for independent visits for students from the age of 16.
Financial Ressources: The Cultural Passport started in September 2018, it was intended only for elementary school students (USD 5,5 (EUR 5) per student) and was financed by EU funds. In 2020, after the end of EU funding cycle, the project was continued using the state budget funds. in 2020 – allocated about USD 3.8 million (EUR 3.5 million) state budget funds; in 2021 – allocated about USD 4.4 million (EUR 4 million) state budget funds; in 2022 – allocated about USD 4.4 million (EUR 4 million) state budget funds; in 2023 – allocated about USD 4.4 million (EUR 4 million) state budget funds (approx. USD 12,3 (EUR 11) per student).

Title EN: Cultural, Creative, and Knowledge Territories Project - transition of the previously called Orange Development Areas (ADN in Spanish)
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture
SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Cultural and creative sectors
Cultural Domain: Design,Performing Arts,Media Arts,Cinema and Audiovisual Arts,Music,Publishing,Visual Arts
Agency Implementation: Ministry of the Interior, Ministry of Finance and Public Credit, Ministry of Labor, Ministry of Commerce, Industry, and Tourism, Ministry of Education, Ministry of Culture, Arts, and Knowledge, National Department of Planning
Main Feature: "With the commitment of the Cultural, Creative, and Knowledge Territories – TCCS in Spanish, we will seek to strengthen territorial dynamics, samples of traditional crafts and ancestral knowledge, and neighborhood environments with differential exercises, for women, young people, and ethnic populations. At the same time, they must promote the circulation, articulation, and generation of associative projects between agents in the cultural, artistic, and knowledgeable sectors, as well as the strengthening of cultural governance exercises, appropriation of cultural rights, community participation, and the recognition of cultural, heritage, and educational identity of each territory.                  To delimit the scale of the territories, population studies have usually established generation periods in periods of 20, 25 or 30 years.  Additionally, it must be taken into account that living heritage is that which generates collective emotional harmony for more than one generation, such as the music of the Caribbean and the Pacific, ancestral dances such as cumbia, porro, joropo, carnivals such as Barraquilla or Blancos and Negros, ecosystems like the Sierra Nevada, the Tatacoa Desert, parks like Los Nevados, sanctuaries like the Juan Tama Lagoon, photographs and paintings that are not forgotten, lakes like La Coha or Tota, among others. Thus, the regulatory decree contemplates categories of TCCS (consolidated, in consolidation, and potential), taking into account the role that practices, expressions, and knowledge have played in the collective soul over generational periods.                  On the other hand, it is important to mention that according to the nature of the territories, the coexistence of traditions and cultural practices that are their own and distinctive; likewise, the relationship between these and the different geographical features (mountains, roads, rivers, paths), elements that are related to the goals of the National Culture Plan, 2024-2038: ‘Culture for the care of the diversity of life, territory, and peace' adopted by Resolution 0118 of 2024 of the Ministry of Cultures, Arts, and Knowledge, in which it proposes biocultural as one of its approaches, defining it as:                   “This transdisciplinary approach is based on the importance of the links between linguistic, cultural, and biological diversity, as manifestations of the diversity of life to inspire presents and futures that call for other forms of relationships with environments. Furthermore, it takes up various forms of knowledge that have been strengthened through collective work between ethnic communities and researchers.”                   In this sense, biological diversity is articulated with linguistic and cultural diversity, coinciding in that the first elements become geographical spaces, these being the limits of territories and ecosystems, with the understanding that they usually house traditions and identities linked to their configuration. E.g.: paramuna, amphibious, riverine, mountain culture. There is no territory without geography.         Related regulations         ●	Article 179 of Law 1955 of 2019.         ●	Decree 697 of 2020.         ●	Article 34 of Law 2155 of 2021.         ●	Decree 1208 of 2022.         ●	Draft decree underway that regulates the Cultural, Creative, and Knowledge Territories and the National Council of Cultural and Creative Economy.
Results: Expedition of ninety-eight (98) Orange Development Areas in Colombia, which, according to the Colombia Development Plan, World Power of Life (2022-2026), may be recognized as Cultural, Creative, and Knowledge Territories once they comply with the criteria established by the current transitional regulatory regime.
Recommandations: Balance of ADN, in Spanish, Orange Development Areas                  Deficiencies         ●	The reduction to a relationship with precise geographical spaces that are delimited and recognized through administrative decisions of territorial entities or through territorial planning instruments. These delimitations have been called polygons. Globally, however, very diverse forms of relationships are identified between the districts and the spaces in which they are deployed. This relationship can be as precise as a building, a street, a block, or a neighborhood; or be as large as a city, a region, or even an entire country.         ●	These territorial figures were approached from an eminently economic perspective, ignoring that they imply a multidimensionality that must also be recognized, identified, and studied in terms of symbolic capital, networks, relationships and social, artistic, cultural and heritage dynamics.         ●	Insufficient regulations: Total autonomy to the territorial entities without review and prior authorization from the Ministry of Cultures, Arts, and Knowledge, since under these ADN regulations, this ministry did not have the legal power to issue a technical concept of relevance of the delimitation of these spaces; nor did they have the ADN monitoring and impact mechanisms that ensures compliance with the objectives proposed in the delimitation of each space.          ●	Misinformation about the process and benefits: AND was delimited without knowing its benefits and the correct way to do it.         ●	A differential offer was not consolidated: It was never possible to articulate the entities of the National Orange Economy Council, nor the Directorates of the Ministry of Culture to establish an institutional offer that would support the ADN processes. The reason why, through the regulations that are in progress, the National Council of Cultural and Creative Economy is created, whose purposes are to contribute to this differential offer.         ●	Absence of effective public policies at the territorial level: The majority of territorial entities did not design support and strategies to strengthen the processes in the ADN’s. They assumed as an achievement the issuance of the administrative act of delimitation.         ●	Notable milestones         ●	Networking: With the aim of generating spaces for cooperation, networking, and knowledge exchange, two face-to-face meetings were held, in which leaders of the country's ADN’s and cultural agents who are established in these territories participated.         ●	Interest from the mayor's and governor's offices in the cultural sector: Interest was generated and in a few cases support from territorial entities to support the cultural and artistic sector.         ●	Scholarships focused on ADNs: The 2022 National Incentives Program included for the first time the ADN Scholarship ($600 million Colombian pesos), in order to support the creation of projects in the cultural and creative sector aimed at activating, making visible, and circulating local goods and services that are produced in the country's creative districts.                   By virtue of this, the transition of the figure of the ADN is being carried out, to the Cultural, Creative, and Knowledge Territories, where the cultural, economic, social, political, geographical, and historical spheres are covered, opening to interdisciplinarity. In accordance with article 187 of the National Development Plan 2022-2026: "Colombia World Power on Life", the Cultural, Creative, and Knowledge Territories define them as meeting spaces that promote the permanent activity of creation, circulation, and appropriation of cultural, artistic, and knowledge practices and content, respecting the logic, dynamics, and cultural institutions of each territory, where culture is a fundamental axis for the construction of peace, social transformation, and protection of the environment in the country."

Strong investment in cultural sector should improve conditions for artists and culture professionals, especially in the country's regions. It is envisaged to strengthen the heritage management system, and to make the renovation of cultural sites more efficient.   The programme also provides the basis for the development of measures that respond to the specific needs of cultural and creative industries (CCI) sector, that are oriented towards the artist / creative person as the main target group, and that promote the growth and transformation of CCIs themselves. This is in response to the growing importance of CCIs in the economy, a trend that has been further highlighted by the pandemic of the growing demand in the global market for the production of innovative goods and services of high quality, based on cultural content.  The programme also aims at a breakthrough in the digitisation of cultural resources, with €30 million from the "Next Generation Lithuania" plan going towards the development of an E-Culture Gateway, consolidating existing systems and registers to open up all cultural resources and promote their use by the public (for more detail about E-Culture Programme look 1 Goal. Digital Environment).  The Programme places great emphasis on national minorities, their integration and the further development of the Lithuanian language. The programme also aims to mobilise the resources of different policy sectors for better and more efficient use of cultural potential, adding value to other public policies.

HP –Equal opportunities for all). 08-001-04-07-01 (PP) Creating conditions for the vitality and prestige of the Lithuanian language; 08-001-04-03-01 (PP) Promoting participation and inclusion of national minorities in public life and reducing the information divide (HP – Equal opportunities for all); 08-001-04-05-01 (PP) Actualization of the content and forms of communication on historical memory; 08-001-04-01-04 (PP) Development of critical thinking skills, responsibility for the legal consumption of content, media and information literacy.
Financial Ressources: A budget of approx. USD 321 million (EUR 290 million) has been envisaged for the implementation of the Culture and Creativity Development Programme for the Period 2021-2030. Title EN: CULTURE FROM THE NEIGHBORHOODS
Goal: Integrate Culture In Sustainable Development Frameworks
SDG: SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: National sustainable development policies and plans
Agency Implementation: Potosi Writers and Performing Arts Network (ReedPotosi) Roberto Arancibia López EMAIL: roberticodux@gmail.com PHONE: 77868914
Main Feature: The Culture from the Neighborhoods initiative seeks to revitalize neighborhood spaces as centers of cultural activity and social development through an inclusive and decentralized approach. Its main objective is to create and repurpose cultural spaces in neighborhoods, facilitating artistic training and developing cultural infrastructure based on the social, tourist and cultural needs of the community. This project contributes to urban and social regeneration, promoting a development model where culture is at the center of community life.  One of the key aspects of this initiative is its link to the POA Vecinal (Annual Operating Budget), which allows for a commitment to sustainability and active community collaboration. Through this program, neighbors, students, and artists actively participate in cultural opportunities and take on roles in the management and sustainability of the spaces. This approach fosters social cohesion and turns cultural consumption into a participatory experience, where the community plays a decisive role in decision-making and the creation of a shared sense of belonging.  In addition, Culture from the Neighborhoods turns these areas into decentralized cultural points of interest, complementing the traditional cultural spaces served by the municipality and allowing greater accessibility for residents. The initiative also promotes the exchange and circulation of local and national artistic talent, functioning as a meeting point and mutual learning between artists and cultural promoters.  The neighborhood, in this context, becomes a pilot neighborhood where culture is applied as a fundamental pillar for social, personal and community development. This approach not only improves the quality of life and reinforces local cultural identity, but also establishes a replicable model in other neighborhoods, promoting community empowerment and cultural sustainability. Ultimately, Culture from the Neighborhoods represents an innovative strategy that integrates art and culture into everyday life, strengthening the notion that access to culture is a fundamental right and a tool for inclusive development.
Results: Since 2021, the Culture from the Neighborhoods initiative has expanded its cultural activities and impact on the community through a management model that includes neighbors, youth, and children in artistic and cultural activities. Each year, the budget and variety of events have increased, reflecting growing commitment and greater neighborhood participation.  In 2021, with a budget of Bs. 5,000, a musical activity was organized with the participation of 46 spectators and 6 musical groups.  In 2022, the budget increased to Bs. 10,000, allowing for four activities that included music and book exhibitions, with an attendance of 180 people and the participation of 9 artist groups.  For 2023, the budget amounted to Bs. 20,000, with five activities (music, book exhibition and theater) that brought together 285 spectators, involved 12 artistic groups, and had the participation of 5 schools and 4 neighborhood councils, which replicated the cultural model in their neighborhoods.  In 2024, with a budget of Bs. 3,000, seven activities were developed that included music, literature, theater, declamation and a theatrical tour, bringing together 350 spectators, 11 artistic groups and 7 educational institutions benefited.  This initiative promotes culture as a pillar of social and community development, creating a sense of belonging and cohesion among neighbors. In addition, by addressing issues of social relevance, it encourages critical reflection on the community and makes visible the needs for urban improvement, such as the request for better lighting, maintenance of facades and cultural and tourist spaces in the neighborhood. Neighborhood cultural management has not only encouraged cultural consumption but has also strengthened the values of respect for older adults and developed artistic and leadership skills among young people.

Main Feature: Culture Moves Europe provides mobility grants for artists and cultural professionals in all 40 creative Europe countries. It covers the sectors of architecture, cultural heritage, design and fashion design, literature, music, performing arts and visual arts. The scheme follows the successful i-Portunus pilot project that took place between 2018 and 2022.     The scheme consists of two action lines: individual mobility (for individuals and groups of up to five persons) and residencies.      The individual mobility action offers financial support to individuals who travel between 7 and 60 days or groups of up to 5 persons who travel between 7 and 21 days.   The residency action is aimed at organisations and established individual artists who regularly organise residencies and are interested in hosting artists and cultural professionals. It supports them to welcome up to 5 international artists and cultural professionals for a residency project lasting between 22 and 300 days.
Results: With a budget of EUR 21 million, Culture Moves Europe offers mobility grants to around 7,000 artists, cultural professionals and host organisations from 2022 to 2025.    During the reporting period 2021-2024, there have been: -	Two calls for individual mobility of artists and cultural professionals – in 2023 (deadline 31 May 2023) and in 2024 (deadline 31 May 2024) -	Three calls for residency hosts – in 2023 (deadline 15 June 2023), in 2024 (16 January 2024) and in 2024 (31 May 2024)  During this period, 4672 artists and cultural professionals received a mobility grant to implement their project abroad. For a total budget of EUR 8,8 million.    In residency action, there have been three calls further to which 289 organizations hosting 1037 artists and cultural professionals have been selected.
Financial Ressources: Aprox USD 23,2 million [EUR 21 million]

Main Feature: Decolonization and depatriarchalization in Bolivia have been framed in a context of significant political change since 2006 and gained greater strength with the promulgation of the new Political Constitution of the State in 2009, which establishes their eradication as a central objective of the Plurinational State, recognizing cultural diversity and the need to repair historical injustices suffered by indigenous communities and other marginalized socio-cultural groups. In the country, through a public agenda, the search for a solution and an end to all expressions of violence, discrimination, racism and intolerance towards diversity, which were exercised primarily against native indigenous nations and peoples, other historically excluded populations and Mother Earth, was addressed. The Plurinational Policy of Decolonization and Depatriarchalization – PPDD “Bolivia of Equals from Our Diversities” aims to deepen the processes of decolonization and depatriarchalization in public management and in society; in such a way that it allows contributing to the consolidation of the Plurinational State, the Productive Community Economic Social Model for Living Well and the plural identity, generating conditions for the full exercise of the rights of the Bolivian population, without any type of exclusion or discrimination and contributing to the reduction of poverty and inequalities.
Results: In 2023 and 2024, management operations were adjusted towards capacity building in Decolonization and Depatriarchalization through the training of public servants and society, within the framework of the Plurinational Decolonization and Depatriarchalization Policy (PPDD); the implementation of the Decolonization and Depatriarchalization Policy in public management; Implementation of the training program in official State languages; community economic empowerment of women from Native Indigenous Nations and peoples, and the inter-cultural and Afro-Bolivian communities by revitalizing their ancestral knowledge and know-how; formation of a Council of Elders (Wise Men and Wise Women); revitalization of the cultural expressions of native indigenous nations and peoples, and the inter-cultural and Afro-Bolivian communities.

Title EN: DENTES DE LEÃO
Goal: Integrate Culture In Sustainable Development Frameworks
SDG: SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: National sustainable development policies and plans
Cultural Domain: Design,Performing Arts,Media Arts,Cinema and Audiovisual Arts,Music,Publishing,Visual Arts
Agency Implementation: Cultural Heritage, IP and DGARTES - Directorate General of Arts
Main Feature: The Dentes de Leão (Dandelions) project is an original coproduction by Materiais Diversos, Pó de Vir a Ser, Academy of the Senses, Municipality of Sardoal and Culturgest, within the scope of participatory arts, investing in the young population of Sardoal and Évora for the qualification and sustainability of these territories. The project set up a collaborative space centered on contemporary arts and integrated, in a multidisciplinary programme presented in Sardoal and Lisbon and, in open studio regime, in Évora, original creations developed, with the participation of groups of youngsters and young artists. In addition to the investment in Creation and Programming, the project had a strong component of audience development and provided training, betting on research, monitoring, and evaluation, in an original model forged in collaboration with the academy.
Results: Access and support to/for contemporary arts in low-density municipalities through, inter alia: programming of artistic productions, involvement of residents in creative processes and audience development activities. The project's polyhedral design was concretely developed from three types of action: audience development, artistic creation, and programming. Through youth encounters, the project involved young people in artistic processes of active, non-instrumentalized participation and co-authorship and broadened their horizons of reference and possibilities (social and professional), either through the exchange of experiences with young people of the same age or through direct contact with artists in processes of collaborative artistic creation. The creation axis focused on collaborative and multidisciplinary creation processes. The artistic residencies, articulated between the low-density territories, offered a group of young artists time for learning and research, as well as the opportunity to produce artistic proposals selected by the groups of young people. The results of the residencies were then incorporated into the programming axis, promoting the visibility of the process, the young artists, and the contribution of the youth groups from the various territories. The programming axis also included a Participatory Arts Course, contributing to the training of participants and cultural agents, the visibility of practices and the dissemination of results. The transversal involvement of researchers and academia produced knowledge and good practices disseminated through a publication, contributing to the project's recognition and sustainability.

Title EN: Design and Craft Joint Project Đây đó (Here/There)
Goal: Achieve A Balanced Flow Of Cultural Goods And Services And Increase The Mobility Of Artists And Cultural Professionals
SDG: SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 10 - Reduce inequality within and among countries,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Mobility of artists and cultural professionals
Agency Implementation: Viet Nam National Institute of Culture and Arts Studies (Ministry of Culture, Sports and Tourism), RMIT University Melbourne
Main Feature: Project “Here/There” aimed to develop long-term collaboration and exchange between craftsmen and designers in Australia and Viet Nam. Through mentoring programs from Vietnamese and Australian experts, discussions, community interactions, and work exhibitions, the project brings together different design and craft knowledge to (i) address the skills gap between emerging designers and traditional artisans in Viet Nam; (ii) showcase the skills and talents of artisans and designers in Viet Nam to an international audience; (iii) create income and trade flows across Vietnamese and Australian markets; and (iv) support the professional and long-term development of the craft and design industry in Viet Nam and Australia.  Project activities include improving the capacity of young Vietnamese designers through professional mentoring activities from Vietnamese and Australian experts and community connection activities such as workshops, discussions, and activities to display, introduce, and promote the project's design products.
Results: This project is an extension of "Skilled Hands: Shared Culture," a multicultural exhibition that RMIT Gallery, VICAS, and Vietcraft organized in 2020 during the COVID-19 period. The online exhibition featured works by 10 Australian and 10 Vietnamese artists, designers, and craftsmen who explored the connections between artistic creativity, craft, design, and community.  The 2021–2022 period of the Project Here/There focused on four collaboration activities in design and craft by four emerging designers in Viet Nam, including Pham Phan Hoang Linh, Tom Trandt Minh Dao, Luu Nhu Ngoc, and Dam Nha Han. With advice from leading Vietnamese and Australian experts and designers like Dewi Cooke, Managing Director of The Social Studio (Melbourne), Vu Thao, Founder and Artistic Director of Kilomet109, Outland Denim, Material Assembly (MatA), Mr. Le Ba Ngoc, Vice President of Vietcraft, Dale Hardiman, and Nguyen Phan Thuy Duong, Editor of Elle Decoration Magazine, the emerging Vietnamese designers developed and presented new works of art, craft, and design. The results were introduced on the project's website and exhibited at the Viet Nam Creativity and Design Festival 2022 in November 2022, along with other workshops and activities.  The 2023-2024 period of the Project Here/There comprised four components, including a creative residency in Melbourne, participating in Melbourne Fashion Week, and displaying works at the design exhibition at First Site Gallery for Pham Phan Hoang Linh and Tom Trandt Minh Dao in October 2023 and for Vo Ngoc Thanh Tien in Australia in 2024; the Business Development Consulting Program in Viet Nam for three young Vietnamese designers, including Dao Manh Khang, Do Trang, and Vo Ngoc Thanh Tien; the New Design Talent Award with advice from Australian industry mentors for Dao Manh Khang, Do Trang, and Vo Ngoc Thanh Tien; and the Product Exhibition in Viet Nam in 2024.
Financial Ressources: The project is sponsored by the Australian Embassy in Viet Nam and RMIT University; the Viet Nam National Institute of Culture and Arts Studies (Ministry of Culture, Sports and Tourism) contributes to project management in Viet Nam; and the finance, human resources and expertise support from other creative partners.
Recommandations: With the cooperation of many creative partners between Viet Nam and Australia, the project has:  - Supported and promoted the intersection between traditional craft and professional design/fashion to bring about sustainable economic and cultural development for 15 Vietnamese creative designers.  - Promoted contemporary design, sustaining traditional art forms and crafts in the context of rapid development and global challenges in Viet Nam and Australia for sustainable development and climate change after COVID-19.  - Created cultural, economic, and knowledge exchange between manufacturers and designers in Australia and Viet Nam, in which two Vietnamese designers had the opportunity to display and sell products in the Australian market.  - Celebrated ethical and environmentally conscious fashion, design, and craft in Viet Nam and Australia.

Title EN: Development of methods for increased digital outreach by the Royal Dramatic Theatre, the Royal Swedish Opera and the Swedish National Touring Theatre (Riksteatern)
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture
SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Digital environment
Agency Implementation: Royal Dramatic Theatre, the Royal Swedish Opera and the Swedish National Touring Theatre (Riksteatern)
Main Feature: The government believes that performing arts institutions need to continue the development and use of digital channels to reach their audiences. The government allocated extra funds for the Royal Dramatic Theatre, the Royal Swedish Opera and the Swedish National Touring Theatre (Riksteatern) in 2018-2020 to develop accessible digital solutions for performing arts, in collaboration with other theatres. The aim being an increased access for people living in all parts of the country.  The outbreak of the corona pandemic led to an increased use of digital platforms by performing arts actors and development of new interesting ways to interact with their audience digitally. The previous measure had provided the institutions with an infrastructure, which meant they were well prepared when theatres had to close down.
Results: The development of digitalization has been an essential tool for performing arts institutions to reach a broad and diverse audience throughout the country. With additional funding between 2018 and 2020, the Royal Swedish Opera, the Royal Dramatic Theatre and the Swedish National Touring Theatre (Riksteatern) were able to intensify their work to develop new digital solutions to communicate with their audiences, reach out to audiences across the country and to new and diverse groups in society.   As a result, these institutions were well prepared at the outbreak of the pandemic in 2020. When they were not able to welcome their audiences to live performances, they could still present high quality productions to audiences all over the country.   Notable and permanent results are the development of play-channels: Operan Play, Dramaten Play and Riksteatern Play, which were used as digital stages throughout the pandemic, offering free streamed theatre, opera and ballet performances to the public. This is an infrastructure that serves the purpose of broad outreach of high-quality performing arts.    The Swedish Post and Telecom Authority (PTS), commissioned by the government, has mapped KB's assessment of the work with Digiteket is good as a new version expanded with research-based material on reading promotion in collaboration with the Norwegian Cultural Council has been launched during the year, which increased the opportunities for knowledge sharing and analysed experiences and needs related to digital transformation due to COVID-19, including within the performing arts sector. The PTS report (Digital Transformation Due to COVID-19 PTS-ER-2021:1) highlights challenges faced by cultural institutions and creators in monetizing their productions. This is because institutions have not yet adapted payment models for digital broadcasts. The study also shows that the availability of digital cultural content within the performing arts has increased during the pandemic.  According to the report Performing Arts, the Pandemic, and the Future by Swedish Performing Arts Association (Svensk Scenkonst) the rapid digital transformation during the pandemic meant that organisations facilitating performing arts did not had time to establish structures and models to address these new needs. Additionally, the new expenses related to digitalization could not be covered due to revenue losses from cancelled performances. Swedish Performing Arts Association therefore entered into temporary crisis agreements during the pandemic in collaboration with relevant trade unions to enable a temporary opportunity to make performing arts productions accessible.
Financial Ressources: 4, 26 million USD (1,42 million USD/year) 2018-2020 (45 million SEK (15 million SEK/year)).

Main Feature: Industries and Handicrafts have been one of the Royal Government’s priority areas for  the national economic development. The Royal Government of the 7th Legislature of the National Assembly (2023-2028) reiterated the policy in its priority platforms. Thus, the policy is implemented by all related Government’s ministries and agencies. The most relevant among them are the Ministry of Industries, Science, Technology and Innovation, Ministry of Economy and Finance, Ministry of Commerce, Ministry of Tourism, Ministry of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation, and the Ministry of Culture and Fine Arts.  Stated in the Priority Platforms of the Royal Government of Cambodia of the Seventh Legislature of the National Assembly for Nation Building and Defense 2023-2028, is: •	to promote industries, handicrafts, and SMEs, as well as support the works of science, technology, and innovation in enhancing production, with a focus on the feasibility study on technology transfers to gradually participate in the global trends of the Fourth industrial revolution (IR 4.0).  •	to enhance the quality and productivity of SMEs and handicrafts, based on the 5-S principle, namely "Sort, Set in order, Shine, Standardize, and Sustain," and promote research and development, as well as protect the new inventions by patent and provide trainings on industrial property right. Provide support to SMEs and handicrafts in terms of training and investment in machinery or production equipment, as well as other incentives, by linking production to local raw materials, improve product quality and modernization of production chains, and foster links to multinational enterprises. (Source: Royal Government of Cambodia, Political Platform of the Royal Government of Cambodia of the Seventh Legislature of the National Assembly for Nation Building and Defense 2023-2028, pp. 8-9.)   Cultural and creative sectors are also supported by the policy, along with the  National Policy for Culture (NPC) adopted by the Government in 2014. Moreover, the Ministry of Culture and Fine Arts is updating the NPC to suit with current global fast-moving situation.
Results: A number of sector specific policies and frameworks have been promulgated, which include: -	Cambodia Industrial Development Policy 2015-2025 -	Cambodia Digital Economy and Society Policy Framework 2021-2030 -	National Strategy for Informal Economic Development 2023-2028 -	National Policy on Culture adopted in 2014.   There are also program and policies set forth to support “the Micro-, small and Medium-sized enterprises to achieve the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) in Cambodia through Streamlining Business Registration Policies (see “UNDESA-Supporting MSMEs to Achieve the SDGs in Cambodia through Streamlining Business Registration Policies,” link: Supporting MSMEs to Achieve the SDGs - Search (bing.com) )
Financial Ressources: According to the National Strategic Development Plan 2019-2023, points out that “in the period of 2015-2018, a total of 604 million USD in financing supported the implementation of the Cambodian Industrial Development Policy.
Recommandations: According to the report in the National Strategic Plan 2019-2023 point out major challenges and solution covering Industrial Development Policy as following: -	“Cambodia's integration with the Asean Economic Community including global trade relations, will require cooperation and coordination between governments and other development actors in strengthening national capacities and systems to improve service delivery and strengthen competitiveness of economic trade and build capacity for monitoring trade trends in all sectors. Cambodia's competitiveness is low labor costs due to unskilled labor. In order to maintain this competitiveness, it is necessary to upgrade skills to the workforce to strengthen productivity.”  -	“Reviewing and restructuring financial incentives that provide incentives for investment in sectors as set out in the IDP are limited.”  -	“Understanding the application procedures for establishing and obtaining the certificate for the operation of the factory or handicraft is limited.” -	“Lack of human and financial resources and equipment in the process of enterprises registration.”  -	“Lack of means of transport with 20 tons standard”  (Sources: National Strategic Development Plan 2019-2023, p. 27 and 67)

Title EN: Development of markets and enhancement of Quebec’s culture profile internationally
Goal: Achieve A Balanced Flow Of Cultural Goods And Services And Increase The Mobility Of Artists And Cultural Professionals
SDG: SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 10 - Reduce inequality within and among countries,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Flow of cultural goods and services
Agency Implementation: Quebec Ministry of Culture and Communications
Main Feature: The government of Quebec wishes to consolidate the development of markets for the Quebecer culture, as well as ensure to enhance its international profile. As part of measure 40 of the Government Action Plan on Culture 2018-2023 , the Ministry of Culture and Communications of Quebec aims to stimulate the export, profile, and discoverability of works as well as productions of Quebec cultural heritage. Among the actions envisaged to this end are the following: strengthening support for tours as well as the dissemination and export of Quebec cultural productions; increasing support for mobility outside Quebec for artists and cultural businesses and organizations; creating cultural showcases and accentuating collective presences abroad; strengthening the services offered to cultural circles by Quebec representations abroad (mainly through its network of cultural attachés within these representations), and more.  To do this, the Ministry of Culture and Communications (MCC) works in close collaboration with the Conseil des arts et des lettres du Québec (CALQ), the Society for the Development of Cultural Enterprises (SODEC), the Ministry of International Relations and de la Francophonie (MRIF) and representations of Quebec abroad, ensuring a role in coordinating international action in cultural matters.  In addition, one of the priority axes of the International Vision of Quebec , adopted in 2019, is to promote Quebec’s culture and artists on the international scene, in particular through the development of markets for Quebecer culture in the territories and sectors deemed priorities. The government of Quebec intends to support the important network of Quebec stakeholders in the field of culture.
Results: In 2023-2024, it is 663 activities contributing to the marketing outside Quebec of Quebecer cultural productions that have been financed by the MCC, including 606 cultural activities supported via the market development budget (network of Quebec representations in the foreign), which further made it possible to support the travel of 445 foreign broadcasters, programmers or journalists. There were 147 Quebec showcases and collective presences that took place outside Quebec, and 36 financial support for Quebec festivals aimed at welcoming foreign programmers and presenters, presenting Quebec works and organizing professional meetings.  Since the start of the COVID-19 pandemic in March 2020, the cultural universe has undergone various transformations which have made it possible to continue to reach not only the local public, but also foreign audiences, as well as buyers of cultural content outside Quebec. The Ministry has also made it one of its priorities to support the cultural sector in its initiatives to develop foreign markets in a context of recovery, following the effects of the pandemic. To do this, several modifications were launched in order to adapt the main action levers to the post-pandemic reality.  -	For example, the support program for international initiatives has been reviewed, expanded, and made more flexible in order to give exporters all the necessary leeway to continue their activities in the post-pandemic context. The network of cultural attachés (30 attachés in 21 representations in 18 countries, representing just over 23 full-time employees dedicated to culture) constitutes an exceptional lever of action for the dissemination and export of Quebec cultural productions.
Financial Ressources: The network of cultural attachés working within Quebec representations abroad had a budget of approximately CAD 650,000 (USD 474,904) per year and nearly CAD 1.5 million (USD 1,096,046) from 2023-2024.  The Ministry has export support programs with expenditures of approximately CAD 2.2 million per year, with an exceptional additional contribution of CAD 1 million in 2023-2024.

Main Feature: Ce projet a trois composantes essentielles : 1 -La réhabilitation du centre culturel jacques Aka de Bouaké Le Centre Culturel Jacques AKA de Bouaké fut ouvert au public en 1971 et inauguré le 16 février 1974. C’est un don de la coopération française à la Cote d’Ivoire qui aura été pendant plusieurs décennies un lieu emblématique pour toute la Côte d’Ivoire et singulièrement pour Bouaké sa ville d’implantation géographique. Il a traversé le temps et les épreuves avec force et résilience. Cependant force est de constater qu’il pâtit de son manque d’équipements modernes et de la vétusté généralisée de ses infrastructures causée par le manque manifeste d’’entretien et de suivi.  Cinquante ans plus tard il bénéficie d’un important projet de réhabilitation dans le cadre du Contrat de Désendettement et de Développement (C2D3) d’une valeur globale de 17 millions d’euros qui lui permettrait l’amélioration-transformation de ses infrastructures d’une part et la création de nouveaux espaces pour répondre efficacement aux attentes des populations. C’est une ambition forte portée par Mme le Ministre de la Culture et de la Francophonie à l’initiative de ce projet.  2 -L’appui au développement de l’écosystème des ICC Cette phase du  projet entend placer le Centre  Culturel Jacques Aka au cœur du dispositif de déploiement des Industries Culturelles et Créatives et prioritairement les filières de la mode et du design, du cinéma et de l’audiovisuel et de la musique. Ces filières ont été identifiées comme principales pourvoyeuses de richesses et d’emplois pour la jeunesse au profit de laquelle une activité d’incubation sera également déployée.  Par ailleurs ce projet a eu un enjeu de réplicabilité en tant que futur modèle de réussite qui pourrait être déployé à l’échelle du territoire national.  3- La mise en œuvre du projet   Cette phase concerne la mise en œuvre du projet en identifiant et définissant les acteurs, qu’ils soient partenaires financiers comme l’AFD, ou technique, le Secrétariat Technique du C2D3. La maitrise d’ouvrage relève du Ministère de la Culture et de la Francophonie. Une Cellule de Suivi du Projet sera mise en place pour coordonner les actions dans le cadre de ce projet.
Results: Projet en phase d’instruction

Main Feature: TContinuation of processes related to digitisation, storage and making availabie of various types of digital heritage resources in Poland (museums, libraries, archives, audiovisual and historical monuments), including for re-use, where digitisation should be understood as a modem form of conservation and preservation of the most valuable cultural resources. It also remains extremely important to continuously improve the digital competences of the staff of cultural institutions and archives, to modernise services along with strengthening their technological facilities and to disseminate digital solutions among cultural institutions.  The above efforts are carried out with national (e.g. Government „Digital Culture” Programme) and EU funds (Digital Poland Operational Programme), in cooperation and support of 5 so-called Competence Centres for Digitisation.
Results: Within the framework of the Programme of the Minister of Culture and National Heritage entitled „Digital Culture”, 285 projects have been subsidized so far from 2020 to 2023, which included the digitisation of over 316,000 collections (of which almost 274,500 were made available). The Programme also includes tasks supporting national and ethnic minorities, as well as people with disabilities. Projects concerning the digitisation of monuments (3D, gigapanoramas), mainly historic churches and monuments from the Polish UNESCO World Heritage list, are becoming increasingly popular. In the reporting period, the Historic Centre of Krakow and the Kalwaria Zebrzydowska Sanctuary were digitised. As part of the Digital Poland Operational Programme, 16 projects have been subsidized so far from 2020 to 2023. The total number of heritage collections made available online was 2,802,270. One of the most interesting was a project of the Documentary and Feature Film Studios, which used artificial intelligence algorithms to present digitised film heritage.
Financial Ressources: Within the framework of the Minister of „Digital Culture” Programme in 2020-2023, more than 5 million USD were allocated for the implementation of digital projects during the reporting period, while more than PLN 93 million was allocated from EU funds for this purpose
Recommandations: Continuation of policies and financial support programmes focused on digitisation, accessibility and re-use of cultural heritage resources including digital archiving, together with the provision of mechanisms to improve the digital competences of cultural staff.programs aimed at the digitization, accessibility, and reuse of cultural heritage resources are continued.

Title EN: Digitization of the collection of the Documentation Center of the National Arts Foundation
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture
SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Digital environment
Agency Implementation: National Arts Foundation
Main Feature: Digitization and dissemination projects of the CEDOC collection of the National Arts Foundation - Funarte, through the software SophiA , AtoM and the application of the free software Tainacan with the CEDOC Digital project.  The Documentation and Research Center (CEDOC) is the sector responsible for preserving, organizing and providing access to Funarte's documentary heritage. CEDOC was initially formed by gathering documentation from extinct cultural institutions in 1990 (Fundação Nacional de Artes Cânica, Fundação Nacional de Arte e Funarte and Fundação do Cinema Brasileiro), and today it already has more than 1 million items including books, periodicals, photographs, sound recordings, posters, show programs, plays, video tapes, in addition to the Institution's administrative documents. Since the beginning of the 2000s, the National Arts Foundation (Funarte) has been adapting its collection to become accessible to an increasing number of Brazilians. To democratize access and expand the reach of this heritage, made up of the most diverse types of documents such as photographs, sound files, textual documents and scores, belonging to the bibliographic collections and personal archives of great personalities in the arts, Funarte has been increasingly committed to more about digitizing your collection. CEDOC DIGITAL is a showcase for Funarte's digitized collection. It is continually fed with exhibitions and information about the memory of the arts in Brazil. The technical areas of CEDOC, responsible for processing documentation, are: the Edmundo Moniz Library, Iconographic and Audiovisual Collection, Private Archives and Institutional Archive. The Edmundo Moniz Library is the gateway for citizens who wish to consult Funarte's documentary heritage.
Results: Provision of historical content from the memory of the arts produced in Brazil, which can be found in the CEDOC Funarte collection, through the use of free Tainacan software , with editorial lines for the dissemination of exclusive content produced by Funarte throughout its almost 50 years, such as radio programs, testimonials, documentaries, musical performances and other content to promote Brazilian memory and artistic diversity.  Presentation of a vast digital universe with thematic exhibitions of performing arts, music and visual arts collections in Brazil. For example, the series “Achados do Cedoc ” allows you to learn a little more about the history of arts in Brazil, through selected treasures from the Foundation's collection. Furthermore, through Edições Funarte, unique printed and digital content is produced for the field of arts, which, commonly, do not find acceptance in the publishing market, such as Cadernos Técnicos and other training projects in specific areas of the arts (such as technical areas of shows and scenic equipment, photography and photographic conservation, records of concert and traditional popular music, music books, dramaturgical texts, biographies, translations of works), research projects, reflection and other products that promote the recording and dissemination of knowledge for the arts.

Cultural Domain: Design,Performing Arts,Media Arts,Cinema and Audiovisual Arts,Music,Publishing,Visual Arts
Agency Implementation: Uruguay XXI Dirección Nacional de Aduanas Dirección Nacional de Cultura
Main Feature: The Single Window for Foreign Trade (VUCE) is a foreign trade facilitation instrument that allows all procedures linked to import, export and transit operations to be carried out electronically and from a single point of entry. This project began in 2011 and the platform went into operation in 2013, under the management of the Uruguay XXI agency. Its main service is the electronic management of licenses, permits, declarations, certificates and other authorizations, documents and information required before and by the organizations to carry out the import, export and transit procedures of merchandise. The system works in interconnection with the National Customs Directorate, sending the pertinent authorizations once they have been managed and approved. The 2020-2023 four-year period has been about capitalizing on experiences and strengthening the tool. VUCE agreement with DNC: Since 2021, the National Directorate of Culture has maintained an agreement with the Single Window for Foreign Trade (VUCE) through which the DNC acts as an institution that authorizes the temporary exit and entry of cultural goods and services, established by decree 86. /007; through a procedure that users carry out through the VUCE portal. This procedure is a necessary requirement to be able to subsequently carry out the procedures before the National Customs Directorate. This work is carried out by the Department of Internationalization of Uruguayan culture. On the other hand, under literal D of art. 15 of the Customs Code; Law 19276; The Ministry of Education and Culture acts as Dispatcher, being exempt from some of the frequent fees in these procedures; when the cultural goods or services are for activities directly supported by the DNC.

Title EN: DRIS – Co-creating intercultural societies
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture

Area of Monitoring: Partnering with civil society
Agency Implementation: ECCOM
Main Feature: DRIS is a project funded by Creative Europe programme that aims at promoting intercultural dialogue and new anti-racism narratives through artistic participatory processes involving social and cultural agents. The project was implemented by a consortium of three partners: Interarts in Barcelona, ECCOM in Rome, and ITZ in Berlin, from November 2020 to October 2022. The project pursued the following objectives: â¢	To increase the participation of cultural institutions, public authorities, CSOs working in the cultural, education and social fields, and train them in audience development and management of pilot cultural projects; â¢	To enhance the opportunities of different minorities of migrant origin to collaborate and participate in the social and cultural life of their cities with the aim of co-creating intercultural projects and artistic products with new narratives, avoiding negative stereotypes. â¢	To co-create transnational projects and artistic co-productions to be showcased across Europe, with the active participation of communities of migrant origins and representatives, using cultural institutions and organizations as contact zones, spaces for intercultural dialogue and mutual learning. â¢	To disseminate counter-narratives and storytelling to raise the awareness of both public institutions and people in the 3 target countries on the value of cultural diversity, intercultural dialogue and peaceful social relations. The activities of the project â" training programmes, three international pilot projects, mobility schemes â" focused on developing tools and opportunities to enhance cultural participation of migrant communities at risk of exclusion.
Results: In 2022, the DRIS – Co-creating intercultural societies project partners from Spain, Italy and Germany, carried out a mapping of local projects/organisations focused on enhancing cultural diversity and intercultural dialogue leading to the release of a collection of 23 best practices: 5 in Rome, 5 in Berlin, 7 in Barcelona and 6 in other European countries such as France, Portugal, Austria and the Netherlands.  One of the main outputs of the project is the DRIS Intercultural Dictionary 5 languages (English, Spanish, Italian, German, Arab) that incorporates words that might be useful to better understand and enhance intercultural competences. These competences are pivotal in European multicultural societies since they contribute to the development of a social framework based on equality, growth, and social justice. DRIS was aimed to fostering intercultural dialogue and create new anti-racist narratives through participatory and artistic co-creation processes, involving actors from social and cultural fields. Projects addressing these issues should develop competencies that provide recommendations for cultural professionals and policy makers. Taking into account the need for guidance, the DRIS project has produced as a result the final recommendations, now available in four languages (English, Spanish, Italian and German).

Title EN: Dynamisation de la mise en marché des biens et services culturels
Goal: Achieve A Balanced Flow Of Cultural Goods And Services And Increase The Mobility Of Artists And Cultural Professionals

Area of Monitoring: Flow of cultural goods and services
Agency Implementation: Collectif Wékré,    Association Nationale des Artistes Professionnels des Arts Plastiques,    BIZ’ART Productions
Main Feature: Au Burkina Faso, l'un des défis majeurs du développement des Industries Culturelles et Créatives (ICC) demeure la question de la mise en marché des biens et services culturels. En effet, les produits culturels burkinabè rencontrent d'importantes difficultés à pénétrer les marchés intérieurs et extérieurs. Cette situation est de nature à maintenir leur fragilité et à faire de la question de conquêtes des marchés un défi majeur à relever impérativement.    Conscients de cette difficulté, des organisations de la société civile ont développé plusieurs initiatives en vue d’améliorer l’accès des produits culturels burkinabè aux marchés nationaux, régionaux et internationaux et de favoriser la mise en réseau des acteurs.   Le Collectif Wékré a créé depuis 2020, dans la capitale burkinabè, un marché des arts contemporains dont l’objectif est d’encadrer des artistes et des jeunes talents, de promouvoir les arts plastiques à travers des exposition-ventes et de favoriser le réseautage par le biais de rencontres professionnelles.   Dans le but de créer le besoin et d’inciter les populations à la consommation des œuvres d’art, l’Association Nationale des Artistes Professionnels des arts plastiques (ANAPAP) a initié en 2021, un projet d’embellissement des bâtiments publics et privés à travers la location-vente d’œuvres d’arts plastiques dans les villes de Ouagadougou et de Bobo-Dioulasso. Sur une période de trois (03) mois, le projet a permis de décorer différents cabinets ministériels et édifices publics et privés.    BIZ’ART Productions a organisé les 10 et 11 mai 2023, un cadre de rencontres professionnelles dénommé « Kundé Music Export » avec l’appui financier de l’Union Européenne. L’objectif de cette initiative était de créer un cadre de rencontre entre acheteurs internationaux de musique et artistes burkinabè en vue d’accroitre la présence de la musique burkinabè sur la scène et les médias internationaux. En marge de l’activité, il a été organisé « Les Showcase Kundé Music Export », concerts promotionnels d’artistes burkinabè devant des tourneurs, des directeurs et programmateurs de festivals ainsi que des directeurs de labels et de médias internationaux en vue de promouvoir les artistes burkinabè programmés et de renforcer la diffusion des spectacles de musique burkinabè sur les marchés nationaux et extérieurs.
Results: La mise en œuvre de ces initiatives a permis d’atteindre divers résultats .    Concernant « Wékré », marché de l’art contemporain :   promotion et commercialisation d’œuvres d’arts plastiques : 600 œuvres exposées, plus de 45 000 000 FCFA générés par la vente des œuvres ;   participation d’artistes et de professionnels : 150 artistes nationaux et 50 internationaux.   S’agissant de « Kundé Music Export » :   participation de professionnels : 03 Majors mondiaux de la musique, plus de 10 directeurs et programmateurs de festivals, 02 directeurs de labels et 02 médias internationaux enregistrés ;   mobilisation des populations : plus de 14 000 festivaliers enregistrés.   Coût total des initiatives : 204 097 USD   Partenaires: Union Européenne; MCCAT, autres Ministères et institutions financières

Title EN: EU support to culture in Ukraine
Goal: Promote Human Rights And Fundamental Freedoms
SDG: SDG 5 - Achieve gender equality and empower all women and girls,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels
Area of Monitoring: Artistic freedom
Cultural Domain: Design,Performing Arts,Media Arts,Cinema and Audiovisual Arts,Music,Publishing,Visual Arts
Agency Implementation: European Commission
Main Feature: The European Commission has increased its support to Ukraine’s cultural and creative sectors since the start of Russia's military aggression against Ukraine in February 2022. The various policy and programming initiatives are evidence of a cross-department approach under the steering of the Commission President, all the more since Ukraine became an official candidate country in June 2022. All Commission’s initiatives have promoted the diversity of cultural expressions at all levels.  1. Fostering the diversity of Ukrainian culture: The European Commission provided micro-grants under a dedicated call for proposals on Ukraine in 2022 under its Creative Europe programme, as well as under its flagship House of Europe programme run by the EU Delegation in Kyiv. The purpose of these micro-grants is to showcase Ukrainian culture in the country and in the EU, as well as to foster the resilience of displaced persons through culture. Second, the European Commission is supporting the Ukrainian cities of Vinnytsia, Rivne and Odesa in developing their cultural strategies, through the EU4Culture programme.  2. Safeguarding Ukrainian cultural heritage. The European Commission has funded the ALIPH Foundation to provide emergency equipment for cultural heritage, and has coordinated in-kind donations from EU Member States through the EU Civil Protection Mechanism. Second, the Commission has also set up an expert group tasked with identifying good practices and formulating recommendations in relation to safeguarding Ukrainian cultural heritage. Moreover, the Commission is partnering with ICCROM to set-up a Ukrainian team of cultural heritage first aiders.  3. Capacity building to the Ukrainian Ministry of Culture and Information Policy. First, the Commission launched the “Rapid Expert Support for Culture and Media Policies in Ukraine” action which aims to enhance strategic leadership of the Ministry. Second, the Ukraine Facility, the Plan for the reconstruction of Ukraine (“the Ukraine Plan”) includes the adoption of a Strategy for the development of Ukrainian culture.  4. Fostering the resilience of Ukrainian cultural and creative sectors. The European Commission organised a double set of activities with Ukrainian cultural and creative sectors in 2022 and 2024. Those were comprised of a quantitative survey, online consultations and a physical workshop, and identified needs and challenges of the sectors with the view to better support them in the future.
Results: · Mapping of the needs and challenges of Ukrainian cultural and creative sectors has been carried out. · Local cultural strategies developed in Vinnytsia · Recommendations formulated by the expert group on cultural heritage · Delivery of emergency protection to safeguard movable and immovable tangible cultural heritage in Ukraine · Setting up of the first team of cultural heritage first aiders in Ukraine · Small-scale projects supported that showcased Ukrainian culture
Financial Ressources: Aprox. USD 28 million [EUR 26 million] committed since February 2022

Title EN: Education and Training for Cultural Professionals
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture
SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Cultural and creative sectors
Agency Implementation: Mohammed Bin Rashid Al Maktoum Knowledge Foundation, Salama Bint Hamdan Al Nahyan Foundation, Dubai Design District, TECOM Group, Dubai Institute of Design and Innovation, Image Nation Abu Dhabi, Tashkeel, The Cultural Foundation
Main Feature: The UAE offers many long-term education and training for cultural professionals and is provided by different organizations, as follows: National Public and Private Universities and Institutions of Higher Education: The UAE has several public and private universities and institutions of higher learning that provide degrees in various cultural specialization, some of these universities are Zayed University, UAE University, University of Sharjah, American University of Sharjah, New York University Abu Dhabi, Sorbonne Abu Dhabi and many other universities.  Scholarships to international universities: Through the Ministry of Education, the UAE offers fully funded scholarships for Emiratis to study abroad in top universities. These scholarships include programs mapped under the cultural sector and a collaboration between the Ministry of Culture and the Ministry of Education tries to ensure wider coverage of cultural programs are available for students applying for scholarships. The Dubai Institute of Design and Innovation (DIDI): The Institute is a private, not-for-profit education institution established in 2018 in collaboration with two of the world’s leading universities for design innovation, teaching and research: Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT) and Parsons School of Design. The institute offers bachelor’s degrees in Product Design, Multimedia Design, Fashion Design and Strategic Design Management.  Master of Science in Conservation Management of Cultural Heritage: The program is offered by the University of Sharjah in collaboration with the International Centre for the Study of the Preservation and Restoration of Cultural Property (ICCROM). This program looks at cultural heritage from a comprehensive point of view, taking into consideration technical, cultural, historical and management aspects. The main objective of this program is to enhance conservation practices among specialists and experts in the region. The program has been designed to include the importance of a multidisciplinary perspective and to provide students with a strong theoretical background, as well as practical training necessary to develop their conservation and heritage management skills. Salama Bint Hamdan Emerging Artists Fellowship (SEAF): SEAF is a program delivered by Salama Bint Hamdan Foundation and is an intensive 10-month artistic education and development program for promising UAE-based artists. The program is operated in partnership with the US-based Rhode Island School of Design (RISD). The SEAF program identifies and nurtures emerging artists in the UAE and provides them with artistic and technical knowledge and professional skills. The program is consistent with the Foundation’s ambitions to establish a more connected community of emerging artists in the UAE and encourage graduate studies in the arts. Upon completion of the program, selected artists who are also able to gain admission to the Rhode Island School of Design are provided with a full scholarship to pursue a master’s in fine arts. Graduates join a growing community of emerging artists in the UAE, and many have taken advantage of opportunities to participate in the Foundation’s various other arts initiatives.  Image Nation’s Arab Film Studio: Image Nation, in collaboration with local, regional and international partners, offers training and education opportunities for the film industry. These include internship opportunities on the set of TV series, one year film programs involving making a movie, a 5-month in-depth program for scriptwriters, online filmmaking workshops for high-school students, online scriptwriting courses, and online media content development courses for marketing and communications executives.  Bait Al Oud Abu Dhabi: Bait Al Oud Abu Dhabi was established in 2008 and is one of the region’s leading music academies. It preserves the songs and techniques of the oud but also other Arabic instruments such as the qanun, cello, violin, rebabah and Arabic voice. As a center of teaching and research, the academy aims to preserve Arabic musical heritage while also nurturing a new generation of professional musicians. The center also encourages craftsmanship, making ouds by hand and even developing new adaptations of the oud, one of the oldest string instruments in the world.  School level Arts and Cultural Education:  The UAE education system provides many specializations that align with the abilities and personal interests of students. UAE schools focus on building 21st century skills through the curriculum especially in subjects that relate to technology, engineering, and mathematics. Further, to ensure freedom of expression amongst students, the Ministry of Education has provided programs and platforms to encourage expression. Some of those include dialogue clubs that have been established in schools and local/international competitions in science, arts, music, theater and culture.  The UAE also encourages students to participate in activities organized by UNESCO and other regional and international organization. UAE students participate in international programs and competitions in fields such as culture, debate, arts, and science. Moreover, students in UNESCO associated schools in the UAE participate in international exhibitions and scientific fairs that engage with the concept of cultural diversity. Furthermore, youth level education programs focus on international cultural awareness and the meeting of culture and education to engage youth in ideas related to arts, cultural exchange, cultural diplomacy, and cultural and social entrepreneurship. The Ministry of Education implements extra-curricular programs to ensure cross-cultural dialogue, specialized volunteering opportunities, teaching of UAE traditions and heritage, and programs implemented in collaboration between students from different schools. WOZO Vacances est une émission culturelle de jeux et de distraction destinée aux enfants de trois (03) à quinze (15) ans, issus des différentes communes, qui vise à promouvoir la diversité culturelle en Côte d’Ivoire. Développement des compétences : Amélioration des compétences artistiques : Les participants bénéficient de formations et de conseils de professionnels, ce qui améliore leurs compétences artistiques. Opportunités professionnelles : Les meilleurs talents se voient offrir des opportunités pour des collaborations et des contrats professionnels dans le secteur culturel. Impact économique : - Création d'emplois : L'émission génère des emplois pour les techniciens, les producteurs, les animateurs et autres professionnels du secteur audiovisuel. - Dynamisation du secteur culturel : "Wozo Vacances" stimule l'industrie culturelle et de divertissement en Côte d'Ivoire, contribuant ainsi à son développement économique. En somme, "Wozo Vacances" a non seulement révélé de nombreux talents artistiques mais a aussi joué un rôle crucial dans la promotion de la culture ivoirienne, l'éducation des jeunes, le renforcement de la cohésion sociale et le développement économique du pays.
