Title EN: Engagement dans un processus d’élaboration d’un statut pour l’artiste.
Goal: Promote Human Rights And Fundamental Freedoms
SDG: SDG 5 - Achieve gender equality and empower all women and girls,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels
Area of Monitoring: Artistic freedom
Cultural Domain: Performing Arts,Media Arts,Cinema and Audiovisual Arts,Music,Publishing,Visual Arts
Agency Implementation: le Ministère des Affaires Culturelles (MAC)
Main Feature: Les ICC sont les moteurs de développement économique et social. Ils se nourrissent à travers les talents créatifs dont le développement et le maintien nécessite la mise en place de politiques et de cadres réglementaires qui assurent des conditions de travail décentes, une rémunération équitable ainsi que l’accès à la formation pour les artistes et professionnels de la culture. En Tunisie la liberté artistique est garantie pour la constitution qui stipule dans son article 44 que « L’Etat encourage la créativité culturelle et soutient la culture nationale dans son originalité, sa diversité et son innovation ». L’article 37 dispose que « les libertés d’opinion, de pensées, d’expression, d’information et de publication sont garanties, aucun contrôle préalable ne peut être exercé sur ces libertés ». Par ailleurs la constitution garantit aussi la primauté des conventions internationales (dont la convention de 2005 pour la protection et la promotion de la diversité des expressions culturelles) sur le droit interne. En effet aux termes de l’article 74 de la constitution « les traités ratifiés par le président de la république et approuvés par l’assemblée des représentants des peuples (APR) ont une autorité supérieure à la loi et inférieure à la constitution ». Sauf que la garantie constitutionnelle des libertés artistiques ne peut être approchée de manière effective et efficace que dans le cadre d’une vision globale de la condition de l’artiste, créateur et professionnel de la culture (protection sociale et économique, mobilité et liberté de circulation, droit à un travail décent, à la rémunération des activités artistiques.). C’est dans le cadre  de cette optique et des efforts visant à améliorer la situation  de l’artiste et des professionnels des métiers artistiques pour qu’il puissent jouir pleinement de ces droits et libertés garantis par la constitution, que le Ministère des Affaires Culturelles a pris l’initiative de s’engager dans un processus d’élaboration d’une loi portant sur le statut de l’artiste et les métiers artistiques et ce, en conformité de la recommandation de l’Unesco de 1980 relative à la condition de l’artiste qui invite les états membres à améliorer la condition professionnelle, sociale et économique des artistes en mettant en œuvre des politiques et des mesures relatives à la sécurité sociale  , l’emploi, la fiscalité, la formation, la mobilité et la liberté d’expression, et plus largement, en synergie avec l’essence même  de la convention 2005 qui stipule dans son article 2 comme premier principe directeur que «  La diversité culturelle ne peut être protégée et promu que si les droits de l’homme et les libertés fondamentales telles que la liberté d’expression, d’information et de communication, ainsi que la possibilité pour les individus de choisir les expressions culturelles, sont garanties ».  Cette initiative est engagée par le MAC dans le cadre du programme ASCHBERG – UNESCO qui fournit une assistance technique et financière aux institutions gouvernementales et aux OSC pour réviser ou concevoir les cadres réglementaires et politiques qui renforcent la liberté artistique et qui, suite à son appel à projet annuel lancé en septembre 2021, a mobilisé plus de 600.000 dollars dans pour soutenir le statut de l’artiste et promouvoir la liberté artistique dans 12 Etats membres de l’Unesco dont la Tunisie, sélectionnés avec une priorité accordée à l’Afrique. Cette assistance couvre le renforcement de législations et politiques nationales, le renforcement des capacités, les efforts de suivi et les initiatives de plaidoyer en relation avec un large éventail de questions liées aux droits fondamentaux des artistes tels que le travail décent, la sécurité sociale, la liberté d’expression artistique ; la protection des droits d’auteurs et la sensibilisation du grand public à l’importance d’améliorer le statut de l’artiste.
Results: En s’appuyant  sur le guide méthodologique du programme ASCHBERG – UNESCO qui définit toutes les étapes nécessaires à la rédaction d’un texte de loi consacré aux artistes et aux professionnels des métiers artistiques reflétant l’importance de l’art et de la création et explicitant clairement leurs préoccupations et besoins  et proposant les solutions et les garanties efficaces  pour la pratique de leur activité en toute liberté et en toute dignité, le MAC a engagé un processus inclusif et participatif impliquant la quasi-totalité des parties prenantes (gouvernementales, organisations syndicales, la présidence du gouvernement, l ’ARP…) pour élaborer un projet de texte de loi portant sur le statut de l’artiste dont l’objectif et de «  régler le statut  juridique de l’artiste afin de garantir ses droits, définir ses devoirs et lui assurer la place qu’il mérite dans la société compte tenu des rôles importants qu’il joue dans le développement  de la vie culturelle, sociale et économique ».  Deux ateliers de travail sont organisés par le MAC respectivement au mois de Juillet et Septembre 2023 (en coordination entre des services chargés du MAC à savoir le service juridique et le point focal désigné pour suivre les projets au sein du bureau de la planification, des études de la programmation). L’objectif étant de réunir dans le cadre d’une approche inclusive et participative toutes les parties prenantes pour débattre dans le cadre de groupes de travail les différentes thématiques (droits sociaux- responsabilité fiscale, les questions en relation avec les accidents de travail et les maladies professionnelles..) et mettre l’accent sur la nécessité de clarifier un certain nombre de notions de base pour parvenir à un cadre juridique solide permettant de plaidoyer les droits de l’artiste et de consolider son rôle dans  la production d’un contenu culturel de qualité. Parmi les notions débattues : L’artiste professionnel, le professionnalisme et l’amateurisme, le contrat artistique, le contrat cadre, la situation de l’artiste étranger, l’intégrité dans le secteur artistique, les négociations sociales dans le secteur artistique, la représentativité syndicale. Le projet de loi résultant de ce processus participatif est débattu à plusieurs occasions est soumis aux services du conseiller juridique et législatif du gouvernement pour consultation tout en poursuivant le processus de concertation avec les autres départements impliqués (Ministère des finance, Ministère des Affaires sociales).
Financial Ressources: Financement et assistance technique dans le cadre du programme ASCHBERG – UNESCO pour les artistes et les professionnels de la culture (150 mille dollars).

Title EN: ENP – Eastern Partnership EU4Culture Programme
Goal: Integrate Culture In Sustainable Development Frameworks
SDG: SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: International cooperation for sustainable development
Cultural Domain: Design,Performing Arts,Media Arts,Cinema and Audiovisual Arts,Music,Publishing,Visual Arts
Agency Implementation: Goethe-Institut e.V. and its affiliated entity Goethe-Institut Georgien
Main Feature: EU4Culture targets the cultural and creative sector in the Eastern Partnership (EaP) countries, aiming to support the development of culture as an engine for growth and social development across the region.  EU4Culture places particular focus on non-capital cities and towns of the Eastern Partnership countries. The project assists cities in the EaP region to develop and implement a Cultural Development Strategy.  EU4Culture also supports the cities with capacity building activities related to strategy development, strategy sustainability, internationalisation, cultural enterprise and management, and cultural indicators and statistics.  A grant scheme for cultural projects, cross-innovation projects, festivals, as well as mobility scheme for artists and cultural professionals from EaP countries complement the project.
Results: EU4Culture Support to non-capital cities to develop and implement Cultural Development Strategies -	14 non-capital cities in Armenia, Azerbaijan, Georgia, Republic of Moldova and Ukraine elaborated Cultural Development Strategies. -	4 non-capital cities in Armenia, Azerbaijan, Georgia and Republic of Moldova received funding of up to €300,000 each to implement cultural strategies. -	In Ukraine, 3 regional cities Rivne, Vinnytsia and Odesa received funding of €100,000 each to implement strategies/projects aligned with emerging needs and existing situation. -	5 cities in Armenia, Georgia and the Republic of Moldova received funding of up to €30,000 implement selected actions based on the city Cultural Development Strategies EU4Culture Support to Cultural Organisations in Eastern Partnership Countries to implement Cultural and Cross-Innovation projects -	15 Cultural and Cross-Innovation Projects are being implemented in the regional cities in Armenia, Georgia, Republic of Moldova and Ukraine  EU4Culture Support to Individual Artists and Cultural Professionals from EaP countries -	In total 319 Artists and Cultural Professionals from Armenia, Azerbaijan, Georgia, Republic of Moldova and Ukraine received EU4Culture support for their international Mobility Projects. 196 (136 Female / 60 Male) Artists and Cultural Professionals already successfully completed their mobility projects. EU4Culture Support for Mobility Projects and Cultural and Cross-Innovation projects in favour of the civil society and citizens of the Republic of Belarus -	78 Artists & Cultural Professionals from Belarus received EU4Culture support to implement mobility projects. 61 (40 Female, 25 Male, 2 non-binary) Artists and Cultural Professionals already successfully completed their mobility projects. -	EU4Culture supported 28 Cultural and Cross-Innovation projects implemented by Civil Society Organisations from Belarus. EU4Culture Capacity-Building Support -	38 local experts from Armenia, Azerbaijan, Georgia, Republic of Moldova and Ukraine were trained as trainers in Cultural Development Strategy Elaboration, Interationalisation, Cultural Enterprise and Management and Cultural Indicators and Statistics. -	In total 146 Stakeholders (public and Private) Armenia, Azerbaijan, Georgia, Republic of Moldova and Ukraine, participated in EU4Culture capacity building and awareness raising events on strategy development and increased knowledge on the matter. -	In total 87 stakeholders (public and private) from Armenia, Georgia, the Republic of Moldova and Ukraine participated in training on internationalisation and increased their knowledge -	In total 97 stakeholders (public and private) from Armenia, Azerbaijan, Georgia, the Republic of Moldova and Ukraine participated in training on Cultural Enterprise and Management and increased their knowledge -	In total 62 stakeholders (public and private) from Armenia, Azerbaijan, Georgia, the Republic of Moldova and Ukraine participated in training on Cultural Indicators and Statistics and increased their knowledge EU4Culture Support for Regional Cooperation -	EU4Culture informally established the EU4Culture City Network. The Network brings together 14 selected cities from participating EaP countries, which received EU funding to prepare Culturel Development strategies. EU4Culture organises annual regional network conferences (3 regional conferences already organised). Envisioned results: o	Improved Cooperation between EaP countries regional cities  o	Popularisation of Cultural Assets of the cities and touristic potential among EaP countries o	Experience sharing, familiarisation and eventual implementation of EU best practices  o	Acknowledgment of common challenges
Financial Ressources: Aprox. USD 8.7 million [EUR 7.85 million]
Recommandations: Appreciation of the project opportunities by the beneficiaries is noted in the report. The report also makes key recommendations related to sustainability of Cultural Development Strategies by the cities, increased focus on cross-cutting issues, enhanced capacity-building for mobility grant applicants.

Title EN: Ensure continuity of local musical practices
Goal: Integrate Culture In Sustainable Development Frameworks
SDG: SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: International cooperation for sustainable development
Cultural Domain: Performing Arts,Media Arts,Cinema and Audiovisual Arts,Music,Publishing
Agency Implementation: ABAIM
Main Feature: Global network and collaboration Two UNESCO accredited NGOs, Finnish Folk Music Institute and ABAIM, Mauritius, alongside Sibelius Academy, Finland, and Echoes in the Valley (EitV), Nepal, share a common goal and focus on educational and artistic practices.  The project, which started in 2018 to run up to August 2024, enables a collaborative platform that enhances the participants' understanding of their local practices from a global perspective. Mirroring the artistic and educational practices in the three countries was intended to enhance the participant's understanding of the limitations, complexities and opportunities involved in music as means for cultural and social sustainability and contribute to developing practices in all three sites as well as global understandings. The project thus benefits not just our local surroundings but provides views on the approaches to intangible musical heritages globally through research and connectedness.  It moreover has a direct impact on showcasing and enhancing cultural diversity at an international level.  CONTENT AND ACTIVITIES Project description The project starts with the idea that continuity of the local musical practices can be notably supported by developing and enhancing the opportunities for the young generation to engage through new educational and artistic means.  Thus, the project offers a scenario where the local musical practices provide a starting point for educational and artistic innovations that have the potential for constructing a sustainable future and promoting the very idea of cultural diversity. The project works with and for the communities through a bottom-up approach. The three NGOsÂ´ involved in the project centre the activities on the traditional musical communities in their local environments. In the project, the communities, practitioners and students are involved in the planning and implementing of the activities through participating in online workshops and webinars. During the project period, 1.1.2023 - 1.8.2024, the project has achieved in organising and implementing: 1) Five online workshops with different approaches to the topic (artistic, archives, community, formal and non-formal music education). Workshops have been organized for the staff, students, and the tradition bearer communities involved in the four participating organizations  2)Two online webinars have been organized from two different standpoints: performing arts and music education. A third webinar is programmed in August and will address the theme of research. 3) Webinars are open to the public and include guest speakers. 3) An exchange programme for NGO workers, artists and researchers, each of the three countries have hosted a visit of two to three persons from another participant organization  4) One video postcard from each country that presents a journey of a musical piece from archives/traditional local context to contemporary video-recorded performance, with reflections on the artists are in preparation. The three video postcards will be later edited into a form of a minidocumentary and will be distributed through all the available means of the established network.  5) Research steered by Sibelius Academy researchers in close collaboration with practitioners from the other organisations is well underway.  The overall timeline  The project has started in June 2018 1.1.2023 â" and is expected to end by the end of August 2024. 31.8.2024.   Bimonthly online workshops or webinars have been organized. An opening meeting was held in January 2023. The Nepali participants have visited Kaustinen in July 2023, the Finnish participants have visited Mauritius in January 2024, and participants from Mauritius have visited Nepal in March 2024.  In August 2024, a final meeting of the project will be held. The activities will be executed as mentioned above. The research material is collected through the span of the activities, and the publication of the results will happen in 2024.
Results: Bimonthly online workshops or webinars have been organized. An opening meeting was held in January 2023.  The Nepali participants have visited Kaustinen in July 2023, the Finnish participants have visited Mauritius in January 2024, and participants from Mauritius have visited Nepal in March 2024. In August 2024, a final meeting of the project will be held.  The activities have been executed as mentioned above.  The research material is collected through the span of the activities, and the publication of the results will happen in 2024. In persons meetings took place in conducive conditions and environments in Finland, Mauritius and Nepal.    Fruitful exchange between practitioners was made possible for every participant to discover the value of cultural diversity and the local and community mechanisms through which people from the three countries have managed to live in harmony despite various types of adversity and mostly while relying of the richness of intercultural relations among themselves.  Discovering art forms and music genre has allowed for co-creation among the practitioners, including children who were central at Abaim in Mauritius.   Interesting meetings with State party bearers have occurred with promising results and advocacy was central at these meetings. The documentation of good practices is well under way and will serve for further actions.  The research component of the project is well underway and will be published by end of December 2024. The project has received good traditional media coverage and excellent social network media coverage.

Title EN: Ensuring Governance System for the Copyright And Neighbouring Rights
Goal: Promote Human Rights And Fundamental Freedoms
SDG: SDG 5 - Achieve gender equality and empower all women and girls,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels
Area of Monitoring: Artistic freedom
Agency Implementation: Ethiopian Music Sectors Union
Main Feature: The Ethiopian Music Sectors Union has made significant strides in enhancing the governance system for copyright and neighboring rights over the past four years. Key achievements include the creation of a comprehensive database for rights owners and users, integrating with the Ethiopian Copyright Management Organization (CMO), establishing fair royalty rates and legal endorsements, and developing software to streamline royalty collection and distribution.  Over the past four years, the Ethiopian Music Sectors Union has significantly advanced the copyright and neighboring rights governance system. The following summary details the key accomplishments and initiatives undertaken:  Mapping and Registration:  Objective: To ensure comprehensive management of intellectual property rights.  Actions Taken: A detailed mapping and registration process was established to identify and catalog rights owners and users/beneficiaries. This process involved creating a centralized database to track and manage all relevant information efficiently.  Integration with Ethiopian Copyright Management Organization (CMO):  Objective: To align with national standards and enhance copyright administration.  Actions Taken: The Union joined the Ethiopian Copyright Management Organization (CMO), facilitating collaboration and adherence to national copyright management practices. This membership supports the standardization and enforcement of copyright laws.  Royalty Rates and Legal Endorsements:  Objective: To establish fair compensation practices and support legal frameworks.  Actions Taken: The Union developed and set rates for royalties, ensuring that they reflect the value of the intellectual property. Additionally, legal instruments were endorsed to support these practices, providing a solid legal foundation for enforcement and compliance.  Development of Software for Royalty Management:  Objective: To streamline the collection and distribution of royalties.  Actions Taken: A specialized software was developed to automate and manage the collection and distribution of royalties. This software enhances efficiency, accuracy, and transparency in handling financial transactions related to intellectual property rights.
Results: The following are the key results delivered from the report on the governance system for copyright and neighboring rights:  Registered Music Works:  Overview: The initiative led to the comprehensive registration of various music works. This process involved cataloging and officially recording musical compositions, sound recordings, and other relevant works within a centralized database. The registration ensures that creators' rights are recognized and protected, facilitating proper management and enforcement of intellectual property rights.  Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) Between Copyright Society and Music Copyright Society:  Overview: An MoU was established between the general copyright society and the specific music copyright society. This agreement outlines the collaborative framework for managing and administering copyright and neighboring rights. It includes provisions for mutual support in licensing, royalty collection, and legal enforcement, enhancing coordination and efficiency in protecting the rights of music creators and stakeholders.  Milestones for Royalty Collection:  Overview: Significant milestones were achieved in the collection of royalties, including the implementation of new systems and processes. This includes the development and deployment of software designed to automate and streamline the collection and distribution of royalties. The milestones reflect improvements in transparency, accuracy, and efficiency in managing financial transactions related to intellectual property.

Title EN: Entrée, séjour et emploi d'artistes de pays tiers (hors UE/AELE). Élaboration d’un guide pour les artistes, les professionnelles et les professionnels de la culture, les organisatrices et les organisateurs ainsi que les collaboratrices et les collaborateu
Goal: Achieve A Balanced Flow Of Cultural Goods And Services And Increase The Mobility Of Artists And Cultural Professionals
SDG: SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 10 - Reduce inequality within and among countries,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Mobility of artists and cultural professionals
Cultural Domain: Design,Performing Arts,Media Arts,Cinema and Audiovisual Arts,Music,Publishing,Visual Arts
Agency Implementation: Office fédéral de la culture OFC, Secrétariat d’État aux Migrations SEM, Direction du développement et de la coopération DDC, Département fédéral des affaires étrangères DFAE - Section UNESCO, Commission suisse pour l’UNESCO, Pro Helvetia
Main Feature: La problématique de la mobilité des artistes, professionnelles et professionnels de la culture a été identifiée comme un enjeu important par la société civile lors de l’établissement du rapport périodique quadriennal 2020. Ce sujet a été repris comme l’un des défis identifiés en 2020 sur la mise en œuvre de la Convention, en particulier de son article 16, pour lequel des mesures étaient à prendre. La thématique précise des visas et permis de travail pour les artistes, professionnelles et professionnels de la culture a été traitée de longue date par la Coalition suisse pour la diversité culturelle. Cette dernière a réalisé et publié un Memento sur les visas et permis de travail pour les artistes provenant de pays tiers (hors UE/ AELE). Il a toutefois été constaté qu’un effort pour consolider et renforcer une base d’information claire et accessible sur la thématique des visas et permis de travail pour les artistes, les professionnelles et professionnels de la culture était nécessaire. Pour ce faire, un groupe de travail réunissant les autorités fédérales concernées (Office fédéral de la culture OFC, Secrétariat d’État aux Migrations SEM, Direction du développement et de la coopération DDC, Département fédéral des affaires étrangères DFAE - Section UNESCO, Commission suisse pour l’UNESCO, la fondation suisse pour la culture Pro Helvetia et la Coalition suisse pour la diversité culturelle) a été constitué en 2022. Il a eu pour missions de formuler des bases d’informations consolidées et accessibles pour les demandes de visas et de permis de travail à l’attention aussi bien des artistes, des professionnelles et professionnels de la culture, des organisatrices culturelles et organisateurs culturels en Suisse ainsi que des autorités suisses concernées. Ce groupe de travail a permis d’identifier les défis, les besoins, les cas, les bases légales pertinentes à intégrer dans une base d’information. Il a élaboré les lignes directrices et les textes nécessaires pour mettre en place un outil d’information en ligne.
Results: En mars 2024, le groupe de travail a réalisé les bases conceptuelles et textuelles d’un nouveau guide sur l’entrée, le séjour et l’emploi d'artistes de pays tiers (hors UE/AELE) pour les artistes, les professionnelles et les professionnels de la culture, les organisatrices et les organisateurs ainsi que les collaboratrices et les collaborateurs des autorités suisses. La mise en forme, la traduction et la diffusion de ce nouvel outil en ligne seront réalisées en cours d’année 2024.
Financial Ressources: Contribution « in kind » (effort humain non chiffré)

Title EN: Establishment of quotas to reduce gender gaps in the cultural sector, as well as affirmative actions to reduce inequalities between cultural agents of the indigenous population, AfroPeruvian peoples or those with some type of disability.
Goal: Promote Human Rights And Fundamental Freedoms
SDG: SDG 5 - Achieve gender equality and empower all women and girls,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels
Area of Monitoring: Gender equality
Cultural Domain: Performing Arts,Media Arts,Cinema and Audiovisual Arts,Music,Publishing,Visual Arts
Agency Implementation: General Directorate of Cultural Industries and Arts (Ministry of Culture)
Main Feature: The Ministry of Culture has established specific strategies to reduce gender gaps in the cultural sector, as well as affirmative actions to reduce inequalities between cultural agents of the indigenous population, Afro-Peruvian peoples or those with some type of disability.  As one of the measures to address the public problem, the Ministry of Culture, through the “Recovery Plan for Cultural Industries by 2030” (2022), establishes specific strategies to reduce gender gaps in the culture sector such as establish a minimum percentage of female beneficiaries. This is in line with the UNESCO publication “Gender & Creativity: progress on the edge of the precipice” (2021), which recommends that public institutions apply transformative cultural policies and measures that promote gender equality in the cultural sectors and access of women to cultural life, as well as guaranteeing gender equality in financing policies of cultural sectors. Based on this, starting in 2022, the Annual Economic Stimulus Plan for the Arts established a quota of at least 40% of the amount to be delivered for female beneficiaries and this goal was exceeded by reaching 56%.  On the other hand, in the Regulations of the Second Final Complementary Provision of Emergency Decree No. 022-2019, it is indicated that at least 40% of the beneficiaries of the Economic Stimuli for Culture must be from regions excluding Metropolitan Lima and Callao. In this sense, the Arts Directorate has been training cultural agents from the regions of the country, resulting in 61% of the applicants during 2023 being applicants from the regions, excluding Metropolitan Lima and Callao.
Results: The profile of beneficiaries of the Economic Stimulus for the Arts has changed compared to previous ones. On the one hand, until 2020, the percentage of female beneficiaries was comparable to that of men; however, by 2022 this percentage increased to 56%. On the other hand, while in 2018, beneficiaries from regions (excluding Lima and Callao) represented 31% of the total, this percentage has been increasing progressively, resulting in 66% of beneficiaries being from regions by 2023.

Title EN: Establishment of the Malawian Artists Welfare Fund
Goal: Promote Human Rights And Fundamental Freedoms
SDG: SDG 5 - Achieve gender equality and empower all women and girls,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels
Area of Monitoring: Artistic freedom
Cultural Domain: Design,Performing Arts,Media Arts,Cinema and Audiovisual Arts,Music,Publishing,Visual Arts
Agency Implementation: Department of Arts
Main Feature: The Malawian Artists Welfare Fund was established in October 2020 to mobilize finances and resources and direct them towards the following:  (a)	Assisting artists when sick and hospitalised or when facing terminal illness, (b)	Assisting bereaved families during bereavement of artists.  The Fund is a membership-based initiative and assist artists whose annual membership fee is paid up and current. Beneficiaries get assistance through their respective rights holder associations. Save as provided for above, rights holder associations also use the Artists Welfare Fund to assist veteran artists whose income earnings cannot cover the costs of their sickness or demise.  Currently there are 11 rights holders associations, which are artists associations registered with the Copyright Society of Malawi, namely: Book Publishers Association of Malawi; Filmmakers Association of Malawi; Journalists Union of Malawi; Malawi Union of Academic and Non fiction Authors ; Malawi Writers Union; Malawi Folk, Dance, Music, and Songs Society; Musicians Union of Malawi; National Theatre Association of Malawi; Poetry Association of Malawi; Photographers Association of Malawi and Visual Arts Association of Malawi.  The Fund works along the principle of supporting the artists' welfare to ensure they have enough time and resources to continue with their artistic activities.
Results: A number of artists have been assisted with hospital bills thereby allowing them a better opportunity to continue with their routine business of creating.
Financial Ressources: Start up of 9,000

Title EN: EveryDay8March – cultural education program
Goal: Promote Human Rights And Fundamental Freedoms
SDG: SDG 5 - Achieve gender equality and empower all women and girls,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels
Area of Monitoring: Gender equality
Cultural Domain: Design,Performing Arts,Media Arts,Cinema and Audiovisual Arts,Music,Publishing
Agency Implementation: City of Women, Association for the Promotion of Women in Culture
Main Feature: Inspired by feminist and queer pedagogy, our teaching materials, activities and participatory art processes are designed for young people aged 12+ who want to reflect on the ways in which gender inequality affects their lives and the lives of others, and who want to act against sexism, homophobia and other forms of discrimination. We also address teachers and youth workers who want to discuss the causes of gender inequality and the history of struggles for equality of women* and minorities (as well as their achievements) with young people. We introduce these themes via contemporary art practices, preferably in venues where these can be experienced.   Teaching materials for the International Women’s Day On 8 March, the City of Women annually prepares teaching materials for parents, youth workers and teachers who work with young people between the ages of fourteen and twenty. By structuring a 45-minute lesson entitled #8MarchEveryDay, we encourage them to address the social, political and economic causes for gender inequality, but also celebrate women’s achievements and learn about the long history of struggles for women’s rights. Since 2018, we have been designing the #EveryDay8March lesson as a quiz. It consists of a series of questions that assess the general knowledge of young people and expand their understanding of important historical and contemporary figures, organized struggles for equality, achieved women's rights, and areas where gender inequality remains or is becoming more pressing. The central goal of the lesson (45 minutes) is to encourage active discussion among young people. They can compete in groups in the quiz, and both the quiz and subsequent discussion are aimed at promoting their participation. In addition to the quiz questions, the material includes correct answers, explanations for the answers, and prompts that can be used to connect the discussion on individual questions to the material covered. Above all, it aims to deepen the discussion among young people on various aspects of gender (in)equality.  POWER – Who Needs Empowerment? Exploring Gender and Power Through/In Art   The POWER project offered young people creative and engaging ways to understand concepts related to social gender, to raise awareness of how gender is connected to power: how individuals still experience discrimination and oppression due to their sexual identity, to develop understanding, empathy, and solidarity with others who have different types of gender identities and sexual orientations, in order to challenge the oppression they face. Through a three-step process using informal and participatory methods based on art, we developed skills to communicate about gender-related inequalities and challenges, providing youth workers and leaders with a comprehensive toolkit to address issues of gender and power in a safe and appealing manner. Reflecting on gender inequality in the museumPower is unequally distributed among people in all societies: individuals have vary  Art Mediation workshops for Gender Empowerment  Art campaigns and toolkits for gender empowerment  Playbook on gender: Explore your powers through art   Professional conferences for educational workers The City of Women regularly organizes professional seminars aimed at educating and training teachers, as well as individuals involved in cultural and artistic education within youth centres, non-governmental organizations, associations, and similar entities. In this way, we convey knowledge that can be used through art to promote the recognition of gender inequalities within educational systems and society at large. Educating teaching professionals about gender-related topics is crucial for creating a more inclusive, fair, and supportive educational environment that respects and values the diverse identities and experiences of all students.  Manuals using various methods are available to create a safe space for addressing feminist themes, which can be utilized by professional educators in their work. We also engage youth in artistic production. Such examples are theatre production Everything is Alright and exhibition Corneous Stories.
Results: •	Higher visibility of women artists •	New teaching methodology and tools developed; •	Training and support to pedagogues and youth workers; •	Raised awareness among youth; •	Encouragement of youth for active citizens participation in discussions on gender equality and otger social questions related to genders; •	Diversification of career paths; •	Promotion of careers in cultural and creative sector among youth.

Title EN: Establishment of the Organization for European Programmes and Cultural Relations (OEPCR)
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture
SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Cultural and creative sectors
Agency Implementation: Deputy Ministry of Culture
Main Feature: The Organisation for European Programmes and Cultural Relations (OEPCR) was founded in 2020. The Organization aims to serve as the contact point for the two european funding programmes Creative Europe and “Citizens, Equality, Rights and Values” programme (CERV). OEPCR is also active in capacity building activities to foster and enhance european and international networking in the field of culture.   It also promotes innovation and International Networking, and participates in European initiatives and Networks such as the New European Bauhaus, European Union National Institutes for Culture (EUNIC) and others.   At the same time, the main purposes of its establishment are the maximization of the absorption of European resources for the fields of culture from the programs of the European Union through the continuous support, training and empowerment of the artists and the bodies of the contemporary creation in Cyprus.
Results: While between 2014 – 2020 the Cypriot absorption of EU funding under the Creative Europe Programme was 2 million euros, the absorption between 2021 - 2023 was increased to 3,2 million euros. In addition, the absorption of EU Funding under the CERV Programme was 4,3 million for the years 2021- 2023.
Financial Ressources: EU Funding: 214702 USD and National Funding: 322053 USD

Title EN: Establishment of the School of Arts, Communication and Design at the University of Malawi
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture
SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development

Agency Implementation: University of Malawi
Main Feature: The School of Arts, Communication and Design is among the five schools that have been established at the new University of Malawi, after the unbundling of the old University of Malawi which comprised of Chancellor College, Kamuzu College of Medicine, Kamuzu College of Nursing and the Polytechnic. The unbadling process commenced in 2017 and was completed in May 2021.   The University of Malawi School of Arts Communication and Designs envisions to place Malawian arts, communication and artistic design on the global map by the end of ten years. Housing Theatre and Drama, Music and Dance, Art and Design, Fashion and Design, Film and Photography, Media and Communication Studies, Entrepreneurship and Creative Industries, the school is bent to produce artists, art work, communicators, and entrepreneurs, in line with the nation’s development agenda, and the regional and continental needs in the disciplines that constitute it.   The School offers demand-driven and relevant programmes at Certificate, Diploma, Bachelor’s, Honours, Master’s and Doctoral studies level,
Results: Enrollment of students into the programmes at the new school is still in progress but the establishment of the school will definitely increase the number of learners in the cultural and creative programmes at tertiary level in the country.

Title EN: Establishment of The UAE Media Council
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture
SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Cultural and creative sectors
Agency Implementation: The UAE Media Council
Main Feature: In 2023, the UAE established a media regulatory body known as the UAE Media Council. This council was created to oversee and regulate the media landscape in the country. Its primary goals include enhancing media standards and fostering a responsible and ethical media environment. The council aims to support the growth of the media sector and promote innovation. The formation of the council is part of the UAE's broader efforts to modernize its regulatory frameworks and adapt to the evolving media landscape. The Council is affiliated to UAE Cabinet and aims to coordinate media efforts and strengthen cooperation between government media entities at the federal and local levels. The council is concerned in unifying media policies to highlight UAE identity. The Council will be suggesting legislations and standards necessary for regulating and licensing mass media and media activities, including media and online publishing, along with those operating in free zones. The new council will be supervising the implementation of these legislations and standards after being approved by the UAE Cabinet.  Also, the council will be oversee the media content within the UAE - including free zones, in addition to registering and accrediting media professionals and foreign media reporters in the country, including in free zones.
Results: The office has streamlined media governance, improved compliance, and supported the development of high-quality media content.

Title EN: Establishment, introduction and optimization of administration with the uniform digital platform e-KULTURA
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture
SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Digital environment
Agency Implementation: Ministry of Culture
Main Feature: The ultimate goal of the e-KULTURA project (January 1, 2021 to June 30, 2026) is to create a unified eCulture platform that connects and makes interoperable the following components:  - digitized and streamlined administrative procedures that artists and cultural professionals can use to apply for grants from the Ministry of Culture and manage their social rights, - a tool to collect, visualize and statistically process data from administrative procedures (including the above and other electronic sources), - artistic sub-portals (literature, film, performing arts, visual arts, etc.), each with its own database, news and events, - notifications of cultural events and cultural news, automatically merged from various existing specialized portals, but also allowing manual entry by cultural producers, - spatial representation of places where cultural producers are active on a global scale (interactive map), - a sub-portal for international cultural cooperation and promotion of Slovenian culture on the international stage: https://www.culture.si/en/Culture_of_Slovenia.
Results: The project is still in progress. So far, the Ministry of Culture has established a new Department for Digitialization in Culture, which, among other things, oversees this project. A system for electronic applications (e-application) has been set up. The Ministry has taken the first step in developing an artificial intelligence pilot program to extract cultural events from various sources and display them on the main platform (currently, such event listings are either manually entered or imported). The portal www.culture.si, which will be integrated into the platform, has been operational since 2010.

Title EN: Estonian Culture in the World
Goal: Achieve A Balanced Flow Of Cultural Goods And Services And Increase The Mobility Of Artists And Cultural Professionals
SDG: SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 10 - Reduce inequality within and among countries,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Mobility of artists and cultural professionals
Cultural Domain: Design,Performing Arts,Cinema and Audiovisual Arts,Music,Publishing,Visual Arts
Agency Implementation: Ministry of Culture
Main Feature: For Estonia, it is important that Estonian culture is visible and active at the international level, both in form of cultural exchange and co-operation as well as cultural export. One of the tasks of the Estonian Ministry of Culture is to promote the internationalization of Estonian culture, to develop cultural relations and diplomacy between countries facilitating this with different measures.    In this specific grant mechanism, the state provides money for international projects from the Estonian Culture in the World programme. This programme supports projects that promote the internationalisation and export of Estonian culture, the introduction of Estonia to the world through culture, and the creation of opportunities for Estonia’s creative people. The grant scheme supports music, literature, performing arts, film, visual arts, museums, folk culture, architecture, design and high-level cultural events related to Estonian communities abroad.   Support can be asked for participation in high-level cultural events important for Estonia and major international events with an Estonian focus, organization of high-level cultural projects, including concerts, performances, exhibitions, etc., organization of and participation in Estonian culture days and Estonian festivals abroad; participation in international networking events, residencies abroad, showcase festivals, and other events promoting the internationalization of Estonian culture. Legal persons registered in Estonia, state or local government agencies, and self-employed persons may apply for the support.   The maximum share of the grant in the eligible costs of the project is 80%. At least 20% of the eligible costs of the project must be covered by non-repayable or non-refundable grants from the state, local authorities or other European Union institutions or funds.
Results: The programme has helped various Estonian creative persons, cultural groups and creative enterprises enter the international stage. The grant mechanism has enabled activities and projects each year in ca 30-40 different countries.
Financial Ressources: The total sum for the period 2020-2023 is 2 330 000 USD

Title EN: EU Policy collaboration on artistic freedom
Goal: Promote Human Rights And Fundamental Freedoms
SDG: SDG 5 - Achieve gender equality and empower all women and girls,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels
Area of Monitoring: Artistic freedom
Cultural Domain: Design,Performing Arts,Media Arts,Cinema and Audiovisual Arts,Music,Publishing,Visual Arts
Agency Implementation: European Commission; Ministries of Culture EU Member States
Main Feature: As foreseen in the Council Work Plan for Culture 2019-2022, and upon the basis of a mandate approved by the Cultural Affairs Committee, a group of EU Member States’ experts, made up of Member States’ experts from the Ministries of Culture and of Employment/Social Affairs took up its work on the status and working conditions of artists and cultural and creative professionals. The group of EU Member States’ experts consisted of representatives of all 27 EU Member States and met between September 2021 and January 2023 working on a range of pertinent subjects: artist status and social security, fair practice, skills and life-long learning and artistic freedom. Their report was published on 4 July 2023 and included the following topics:  o	Status of the artist and social security,  o	Fair practice,  o	Skills and life-long learning and  o	Artistic freedom.  The report included recommendations for the EU Member States and the EU Institutions on how to strengthen freedom of artistic expression.  The website Creatives Unite (funded by the EU) has one section dedicated to the follow-up of the report, including the chapter on artistic freedom.   Moreover, the EU Work Plan for Culture 2023-2026 sets out priorities to address the main challenges facing the cultural and creative sectors today and corresponding actions to address them. The implementation involves the close cooperation between the Member States, the Commission and the Presidencies of the Council. Artistic freedom is one of the guiding principles, as well as one of the actions, under the priority “Artists and cultural professionals: empowering the cultural and creative sectors”. In this context,  under the Presidency of the EU Council of Sweden, two important milestones were reached: -	Council Conclusions on the issue of displaced/at risk artists. -	Presidency Conference on artistic freedom, focusing on artists, their working conditions, and the cultural and creative industries, (Umeå, Sweden, on 16-17 February 2023.)
Results: -	Open Method of Coordination expert group report on the status and working conditions of artists, including recommendations for the EU Member States and the EU Institutions on how to strengthen freedom of artistic expression -	Council Conclusions on the issue of displaced/at risk artists. -	A Presidency Conference on artistic freedom, focusing on artists, their working conditions, and the cultural and creative industries, took place in Umeå on 16-17 February 2023.
Financial Ressources: Ministries of Culture from the EU Member States

Title EN: European Capitals of Culture
Goal: Integrate Culture In Sustainable Development Frameworks
SDG: SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: National sustainable development policies and plans
Cultural Domain: Design,Performing Arts,Media Arts,Cinema and Audiovisual Arts,Music,Publishing,Visual Arts
Agency Implementation: European Commission
Main Feature: The European Capitals of Culture (ECOC) initiative is designed to:  - Highlight the richness and diversity of cultures in Europe  - Celebrate the cultural features Europeans share  - Increase European citizens' sense of belonging to a common cultural area  - Foster the contribution of culture to the development of cities. In addition to this, experience has shown that the event is an excellent opportunity for:  - Regenerating cities  - Raising the international profile of cities;  - Enhancing the image of cities in the eyes of their own inhabitants  - Breathing new life into a city's culture  - Boosting tourism.  The initiative was created in 1985 and has, to date, been awarded to more than 70 cities across the European Union (EU) and beyond.   Decision 445/2014/EU of the European Parliament and of the Council, which governs the European Capitals of Culture for the title-years 2020-2033, explicitly references the UNESCO 2005 Convention: https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=uriserv:OJ.L_.2014.132.01.0001.01.ENG
Results: There were no 2021 European Capitals of Culture, due to COVID-19. However, the 2020 European Capitals of Culture, Galway (Ireland) and Rijeka (Croatia) exceptionally held their title until April 2021.  The designated European Capitals of Culture during the reporting period have been:  2022 – Kaunas (Lithuania), Novi Sad (Serbia), Esch (Luxembourg) 2023 – Veszprém (Hungary), Timisoara (Romania) and Novi Sad (Serbia) 2024 – Bad Ischl –Salzkammergut (Austria), Bodø (Norway), Tartu (Estonia) 2025 – Chemnitz (Germany) and Nova Gorica (Slovenia) 2026 – Oulu (Finland) and Trencin (Slovakia) 2027 – Liepāja (Latvia) and Évora (Portugal) 2028 – Budweis (České Budějovice) (Czech Republic), Bourges (France) and Skopje (North Macedonia)
Financial Ressources: 1.5 million euros prize allocated to each city which was designated as European Capital of Culture
Recommandations: Each year until the title year 2019, the European Commission used to publish an ex-post evaluation report on the outcomes of the European Capitals of Culture of the previous year. For the Capitals post 2019, the cities themselves have the obligation to carry out their own evaluation and to send it to the Commission by the end of the year following that of the title.   These evaluations show that ECoCs have become laboratories of a strategic investment in culture, benefiting economies and communities as a whole. Cultural activity in ECoC title-holding cities increases, new audiences are reached, and the cities’ cultural operators acquire a more international outlook, become more ambitious and improve their skills and professionalism. Citizens become more aware of the richness and diversity of cultural expressions in Europe and of the common cultural elements we share as Europeans.   The Commission is also carrying out an evaluation of the current European Capital of Culture action (currently governed by Decision 445/2014/EU) in order to measure its impact (including in the longer run) and to reflect on its future.

Title EN: Eufonie International Festival of Central and Eastern European Music
Goal: Achieve A Balanced Flow Of Cultural Goods And Services And Increase The Mobility Of Artists And Cultural Professionals
SDG: SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 10 - Reduce inequality within and among countries,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Flow of cultural goods and services
Agency Implementation: National Centre for Culture Poland
Main Feature: The festival is held annually in Warsaw. It is a music festival referring to the tradition of the regional community of the majority of countries defined today as Central and Eastern Europe, stretching from the Balkans, through Romania and Austria, the Visegrad Group countries, Ukraine and Belarus, to the Baltic States, sometimes extended to Scandinavia. The area is a fascinating melting pot of clashing influences from East and West, brimming with cultural energy that has sometimes defined the identity of nations without their own states. Each year, the festival consists of more than a dozen artistic events, especially concerts performed by choirs, orchestras, smaller ensembles or soloists. Professional artists, mainly musicians, take part in the festival. Joint projects by artists from different countries are also often presented. Through its concerts and educational events, the festival raises awareness and respect for cultural diversity both among the local community and in a wider international context.  By inviting artists from different countries, including developing countries, the Euphonies strengthen international cooperation and solidarity, while supporting the cultural development of these countries.
Results: The Festival's audience in 2021-2023 was 15,420 live and 1,183,800 online, broadcast and transmission (internet, radio and TV). 44 cultural events were realized in the project in 2021-2023, with participation of 2,690 artists from 20 countries. The edition planned for 2020 did not take place due to the COVID-19 pandemic

Title EN: EU-Korea Protocol on Cultural Cooperation
Goal: Achieve A Balanced Flow Of Cultural Goods And Services And Increase The Mobility Of Artists And Cultural Professionals
SDG: SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 10 - Reduce inequality within and among countries,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Treaties and agreements
Cultural Domain: Design,Performing Arts,Media Arts,Cinema and Audiovisual Arts,Music,Publishing,Visual Arts
Agency Implementation: European Commission
Main Feature: The EU-Korea Protocol on Cultural Cooperation was concluded in 2009 within the framework of the EU-Korea Free Trade Agreement, and has been in full application since 13 December 2015.    The Protocol sets a framework within which the two Parties shall cooperate to facilitate exchange in cultural activities, goods and services, including in the audio-visual sector, and to improve the conditions governing such exchanges.    Under the Protocol, the EU and Korea have established a Committee on Cultural Cooperation to oversee its implementation. The Committee is composed of senior officials from within the administrations of each Party who have expertise and experience in cultural matters and practices.    Meetings are held once a year online, led by the EU and Korea alternately.    The main provision of the Protocol deals with audio-visual co-productions. The EU and Korea, in conformity with their respective legislation, have agreed to grant an entitlement for EU-Korea audio-visual co-productions to benefit from their respective schemes for the promotion of local/regional cultural content. This entitlement has been extended until 30 June 2026. The European Commission has promoted and disseminated information about the Protocol at professional events, including film festivals.
Results: During the reporting period the EU-Korea Cultural Cooperation Committee met annually each December, online.    Discussions encompassed the following topics:   •	Cultural Exchanges and Dialogue (Protocol, Article 2) •	Expanding Exchanges through Residency Programmes (Protocol, Article 4) •	Artists and other cultural professionals and practitioners (Protocol, Article 4) •	Audiovisual Co-productions (Protocol, Article 5) •	Performing Arts (Protocol, Article 8) •	Culture and Cities •	Effects of COVID on cultural and creative sectors •	Climate change and cultural heritage •	Digital transformation in the cultural sector •	Culture, health and well-being •	Culture and sustainable development •	Young Talent Architecture Award

Title EN: EUReKA project (European Resilience Knowledge Arena)
Goal: Integrate Culture In Sustainable Development Frameworks
SDG: SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: National sustainable development policies and plans
Cultural Domain: Design,Performing Arts,Media Arts,Cinema and Audiovisual Arts,Music,Publishing,Visual Arts
Agency Implementation: UNESCO Chair on Intersectoral Safety for Disaster Risk Reduction and Resilience,. SPRINT-Lab, University od Udine (Italy)
Main Feature: The UNESCO Chair in Intersectoral Safety for Disaster Risk Reduction and Resilience at the University of Udine is deeply committed to fostering resilience to disaster, for a sustainable development. This implies that Chair’s activities mainly fall under the Sustainable Development Goal 11 (Sustainable cities and communities). While the Chair's work primarily centers on technical and scientific aspects of resilience, it also recognizes the crucial role that cultural expression and diversity play in creating resilient communities. This understanding is evident in the EUReKA project, a three-year initiative promoted by the Chair. EUReKA (European Resilience Knowledge Arena) project serves as a platform for intergenerational dialogue, acknowledging the importance of shared knowledge and diverse perspectives in addressing complex challenges such as climate change, migration, and social inequalities. A cornerstone of the project is the "Knowledge Arena" where different actors play different roles. In particular, the Arena is a dynamic space where young people engage in meaningful conversations with local administrators currently working and former administrators, who supported the administrative and organizational activities that followed the reconstruction phase after the devastating Earthquakes in Friuli in 1976. This exchange of experiences and ideas fosters critical thinking, problem-solving skills, and a deeper understanding of the role that cultural memory and diversity play in shaping resilient communities. While EUReKA does not explicitly focus on cultural expression, it indirectly promotes the principles of the UNESCO 2005 Convention for the Protection and Promotion of the Diversity of Cultural Expressions. By encouraging open dialogue and the sharing of diverse perspectives, the project creates an environment where creativity flourishes and cultural exchange is valued. This, in turn, contributes to a more holistic understanding of resilience, recognizing that cultural expressions are not just valuable in their own right but also essential for building communities that can adapt and thrive in the face of adversity. Through EUReKA, the UNESCO Chair demonstrates its commitment to both the technical and cultural dimensions of resilience. By fostering intergenerational dialogue and embracing diverse perspectives, the project exemplifies the belief that resilience is not just about physical infrastructure and preparedness, but also about the cultural fabric that binds communities together and enables them to face challenges with creativity, adaptability, and a shared sense of purpose.
Results: While the EUReKA project is a three-year initiative, the first year has already yielded significant results, demonstrating the effectiveness of its approach to fostering resilience through intergenerational dialogue and cultural exchange. The most notable achievement is the successful implementation of the "Knowledge Arena", a dynamic platform that facilitated meaningful interactions between young people, local administrators, and individuals who experienced the 1976 Friuli earthquake. This unique exchange of knowledge and perspectives has fostered a deeper understanding of resilience from both historical and contemporary viewpoints. In addition to the Knowledge Arena, a comprehensive final report detailing the scientific outcomes of the intergenerational exchange has been produced. This report serves as a valuable resource, documenting the insights gained from the dialogue and highlighting the importance of cultural memory, diversity, and creative problem-solving in building resilient communities. The success of the first year of EUReKA underscores the value of intergenerational collaboration and the importance of recognizing cultural expression as an integral component of resilience. The project has not only generated valuable knowledge but has also created a sense of shared purpose and empowerment among participants. EUReKA aims to start bridging the gap between generations and fostering a deeper understanding of the past, for a more resilient future. The project's initial success also serves as a promising foundation for the remaining two years. Building on the momentum gained, EUReKA is poised to further explore the interconnectedness of resilience, creativity, and cultural diversity, ultimately contributing to a more sustainable and inclusive society.  The EUREKA project was not explicitly designed to implement the “2005 UNESCO Convention on the Protection and Promotion of the Diversity of Cultural Expressions”. However, the UNESCO Chair believes that the EUReKA project can contribute indirectly to the Convention's objectives and is therefore committed to continuing activities in a way that fosters intergenerational dialogue, with a particular emphasis on using creative and participative approaches to recognize and value diverse cultures, and integrate cultural understanding into strategies for strengthening resilience to disasters.

Title EN: European Creative Hubs Network
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture
SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Partnering with civil society
Agency Implementation: European Commission
Main Feature: The European Creative Hubs Network, co-funded by the EU, is a peer-led network with a mission to enhance the creative, economic, and social impact of hubs around Europe and neighbouring countries. As focal points for creative professionals and businesses, hubs offer the most effective way to support the growth and development of cultural and creative industries. The network consists of over 340 creative hubs in 13 sectors and in 50 countries. Among other activities, the network provides Peer to Peer Learning to facilitate innovative collaborations among creative hub managers, support for mobility and staff exchange between hubs, and knowledge sharing by allowing creative hubs to set up impactful workshops to spread and share specific knowhow and expertise.
Results: Among its activities of peer learning and exchanging of know-how and networking, a central achievement of the European Creative Hubs Network is the platform CreativesUnite http://creativesunite.eu.  The “Creatives Unite” platform, is a platform for and by the cultural and creative sectors. It has been set up with the help of the European Commission and the European Parliament Pilot project “FLIP (Finance, Learning, Innovation and Patenting for CCIs)”. The Creatives Unite platform offers a common space for all cultural and creative sectors in Europe and beyond (worldwide) to share their initiatives and actions.  The platform can be searched by Sector, Action and Area, including search by country. The platform has a “Contribute”-button, through which direct contributions can be made. The CreativesUnite platform offers specific online tools for the needs of cultural and creative professionals: (1) “So, you need money” fund-finder tool, (2) IPR tool, and (3) “This is How we work”, highlighting the results of the OMC Member States’ expert group on artists’ working conditions.  Creatives Unite also has a special feature on its landing page, highlighting cultural and creative sectors’ responses and initiatives linked to Ukraine, as well as a section on greening of cultural and creative sectors. There is also a specific section on the platform on “greening”.
Financial Ressources: (2019-2023 – aprox. USD 3.88 million [EUR3.5 million])   New phase started in May 2024 until September 2026 (Total budget: approx USD 1.44 million [EUR 1.3 million, (1.05m EU Co-financing)].
Recommandations: Creative FLIP submitted regular reports to the Commission with insights on user statistics. The most visited section of Creatives Unite is the ‘funding tool’. The Creative FLIP Pilot phase ran from 2019-2021. The project insights, milestones and final outputs are summarised in the Creative FLIP Impact Story: https://creativeflip.creativehubs.net/wp-content/uploads/2021/08/Creative_FLIP_Impact_Story_Design_FINAL_pages_new-1.pdf

Title EN: European Media Freedom Act
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture
SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Media diversity
Agency Implementation: EU Member State governments European Commission
Main Feature: The European Media Freedom Act puts in place a new set of rules to protect media pluralism and independence in the EU. The Act will ensure that media can operate more easily across borders in the EU internal market, without undue pressure and taking into account the digital transformation of the media space.  Among others, the European Media Freedom Act will:  -	Protect editorial independence -	Protect journalistic sources, including against the use of spyware -	Ensure the independent functioning of public service media -	Enhance transparency of media ownership -	Safeguard media against unjustified online content removal by very large online platforms -	Introduce a right of customisation of the media offer on devices and interfaces -	Guarantee transparency in state advertising for media service providers and online platforms -	Ensure Member States provide an assessment of the impact of key media market concentrations on media pluralism and editorial independence -	Boost transparency in audience measurement for media service providers and advertisers  A new independent European Board for Media Services, composed of representatives from the national media authorities or bodies and assisted by a Commission secretariat, will be set up. The Board will, among others, promote the effective and consistent application of the EU media law framework. It will replace the European Regulators Group for Audiovisual Media Services that was established under the Audiovisual Media Services Directive.
Results: The Act entered into force on 7 May 2024 and the new rules will, in principle, fully apply as of 8 August 2025.
