SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Partnering with civil society
Agency Implementation: Grotowski Institute
Main Feature: Network established to communicate and facilitate contacts between representatives of European Arthouses centers, theaters and performing arts Centers - LEPAC - Legacy of Performing Arts Centers. The idea of the network is to combine experiences and strengthen cooperation between people, teams and places that contributed to the paradigm shift in culture in the XX century and still care about participation in current discourse on this field. The idea of LEPAC was initiated in 2023 thanks to the cooperation of the Center for Documentation of the Art of Tadeusz Kantor CRICOTEKA, Pina Baush Zentrum and Marina Abramovic Institute by the invitation of the Jerzy Grotowski Institute, started building a network dedicated to the residencies of young artists.
Results: During short period since LEPAC was initiated, Grotowski Institute gathered the representative of European Arthouses centers, theaters and performing arts Centers, authors and publicists on a meeting discussion panels to present ideas and plans for future activities. The meeting was of a working, initiating nature, aimed at identifying the areas important to the representatives and the needs for which we are establishing LEPAC - connecting and facilitating contact and mobility opportunities for groups involved in the field of performing arts, students and young people.

Title EN: European Platforms for the promotion of emerging artists (Creative Europe)
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture
SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Partnering with civil society
Agency Implementation: European Commission
Main Feature: The European Platforms scheme, funded by the Creative Europe programme, offers action grants to organisations promoting European creators and artists, especially emerging talent, willing to engage at a European and transnational level. These organisations come together within a platform to showcase their common artistic vision and to help their members improve their audience development techniques.  The “European platforms for the promotion of emerging artists” scheme aims to increase the visibility and the circulation of European emerging artists and works outside their own borders; and to facilitate access to European works and artists coming from a diversity of countries for a large and diversified audience. Platforms must be composed of a coordinating entity and at least 11 members’ organisations registered in different participating countries. The grant requested per project cannot exceed EUR 2,800,000 in total.   The objectives are:  -	promotion of the mobility of creators and artists; -	promotion of emerging talent from other European countries;  -	stimulating a genuine Europe-wide programming of cultural and artistic activities;  -	contribution to audience development; and -	providing visibility to Europe’s values and different cultures.  During the period 2021-2023, 16 platforms have been supported during the reporting period, in fields as diverse as music, photography, architecture, circus, poetry, design and manufacture, dance.   Their definitions of emerging artists are as diverse as the sectors: some are young, in others age is not a barrier; some are leaving formal training, in others formal training is not a requirement. What all the alumni of the platforms share is talent, and what the platforms offer them is exposure at a European level.   The platforms use different mechanisms to promote emerging talent: they offer competitions, showcases, festivals along with coaching and mentoring by established artists and creators in the field.
Results: The 16 European Platforms supported during the period 2021-2023 have been:  -	Liveurope (music): initiative supporting concert venues in their efforts to promote up-and-coming European artists -	Magic Cartpets (performance): platform dedicated to emerging artists to start their magical journeys across Europe  -	Versopolis (performance/ literature):  European poetry platform that creates new opportunities for emerging European poets  -	European Media Art Platform (visual arts): platform specialised in Digital and Media Art, Bio Art and Robotic Art -	Circusnext (performance/ circus): platform supporting creation and diffusion to emerging contemporary circus authors -	Aerowaves (dance): platform creating cross-border performance opportunities for emerging choreographers -	FUTURES – European Photography Platform (photo) -	Distributed Design Platform (visual art/design): exchange and networking hub for the European maker movement -	FEDORA Platform (music/ dance): platform supporting innovation in opera and ballet -	European Festivals Fund for Emerging Artists (music/performing arts): platform developing the careers of emerging artists on an international level through festivals -	EENS Exchange (music): bring programming of emerging artists to music audiences -	LINA (architecture): network connecting cultural players with emerging practictioners and thinkers in architecture -	MERITA (music): platform increasing the visibility and circulation of professional young string quartets  -	SHAPE+ (music/audiovisual/visual arts): platform for emerging talents in innovative music and audiovisual art -	Theatre in Palm (theatre): platform for emerging theatre artists co-operation, career development and internationalisation -	UPBEAT (music): support to world music industry   The Platforms have brought a diversity of artists or works from underrepresented countries to a wider audience in other countries. Many are now mature with a strong brand identity and a robust grant distribution mechanism (using cascading grants).
Financial Ressources: Aprox. USD 35,8 million [EUR 32 million]
Recommandations: The current programme, which includes this action, is being evaluated.

Title EN: European Spaces of Culture
Goal: Integrate Culture In Sustainable Development Frameworks
SDG: SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: International cooperation for sustainable development
Cultural Domain: Design,Performing Arts,Media Arts,Cinema and Audiovisual Arts,Music,Publishing,Visual Arts
Agency Implementation: European Commission (Directorate General for Education, Culture, Youth and Sport)) EU National Institutes for Culture (EUNIC Global)
Main Feature: European Spaces of Culture started as a preparatory action proposed and funded by the European Parliament. The phase 1 of the action lasted from 2018-2021. Phase 2 and 3 were implemented in 2021-2023 and currently the project is supported by the Creative Europe Programme for the period 2023-2025. The project tests innovative collaboration models in cultural relations between European and local partner organisations in countries outside the EU. At the heart of the project lies a new spirit of dialogue, in which equality, mutual listening and learning represent the core values that help build trust and understanding between peoples.  By gathering policy recommendations, the project contributes to the implementation of the EU strategy for international cultural relations.
Results: Over the course of four rounds (2018-2025), the programme has resulted in 145 applications involving 91 countries, 571 local partners, 690 local EUNIC members (with 33 EUNIC headquarters represented out of 39), and 107 EU Delegations. With the available budgets, 33 projects have been awarded subgrants, in total involving 40 countries, 187 local partners, 158 local EUNIC members (from 21 EUNIC headquarters), and 33 EU Delegations. On average, this means 5 EUNIC members and 6 different local partners per project collaborating with each other and the local EU Delegation bringing cultural relations to life.
Financial Ressources: Aprox. USD 2.5 million [EUR 2.25 million] for the period 2021-2025

Title EN: Example of an individual measure at local level: free rental of art studios in Maribor
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture
SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Cultural and creative sectors
Agency Implementation: Municipality of Maribor
Main Feature: In 2022 and 2023, the City of Maribor offered artists and cultural workers the free use of artists' studios for a fixed period of three years to realise artistic activities in the fields of visual, audiovisual, performing arts, intermedia arts and design. A certain percentage of the studios were reserved for artists under the age of 35. It has rented 6 studios in 2022 and 4 studios in 2023.
Results: 14 artists applied for the 2022 and 2023 calls for artists' studios. A total of 10 artists were allocated studios. The following objectives were achieved with the free rental of artists' studios - Improve accessibility to cultural assets, - Promotion of creation in the local and Slovenian cultural area, - Increasing skills and mobility in the field of culture, - Participation of artists in various artistic fields in the local and national environment, - Promoting Slovenian culture and creativity on the national and international stage.

Title EN: Festival International de Théâtre de Guinée
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture
SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Cultural and creative sectors
Agency Implementation: Agence Culturelle Festi-Kaloum
Main Feature: Le théâtre est un élément vital d’une société dynamique. Il s’exprime dans la manière de raconter nos histoires, de fêter nos victoires, de rappeler notre passé, de nous divertir et d’imaginer notre avenir. En tant qu’expression créative, il aide à nous définir et à voir le monde à travers les yeux des autres.  Créée en 1994, l’Agence Culturelle Festi-Kaloum dans sa vision de promotion et de valorisation du Théâtre Africain a initié le Festival International de Théâtre de Guinée dans le but de relancer la pratique théâtrale en Guinée à travers des formations et des spectacles de qualité.   Le Festival International de Théâtre de Guinée se donne pour mission de créer un cadre de rencontres, d’échanges, de confrontations des pratiques artistiques dans le domaine du théâtre, de formation et de résidences artistiques pour permettre aux artistes de réaliser leurs œuvres et de les faire connaitre.  Ce festival est un facteur d’intégration, un espace de solidarité, de confiance harmonieuse et de paix sociale.  C’est un vivier de création, de diffusion, d’échange et de dialogue interculturel et un lieu d’émergence de nouveaux courants artistiques. Il a pour objectif général de promouvoir le théâtre guinéen en favorisant l’émergence d’une nouvelle génération d’artistes comédiens et dramaturges. De manière spécifique, il contribue à : -	œuvrer pour la promotion du théâtre en Guinée ; -	renforcer les capacités des comédiens et metteurs en scène en technique de jeu d’acteur et de mise en scène ; -	favoriser des échanges entre les professionnels des arts du spectacle ; -	favoriser le théâtre scolaire ; -	promouvoir des spectacles de percussions et de musiques traditionnelles. Dans la dynamique de promouvoir les compétences artistiques, de transfert des compétences et de donner un souffle à ce festival, un comité d’organisation composé d’une Direction du Festival, d’une Administration Générale, d’une Direction de communication, d’une Direction Technique, d’une Direction artistique est mis en place. Des commissions techniques ont été créées et placées sous l’autorité du comité d’organisation.  Le processus de sélection des troupes se déroule comme suit : lancement de l’appel à candidature ; présélection des troupes ; sélection des troupes. Pour atteindre ces objectifs, deux espaces ont été aménagés : -	un espace théâtre dédié aux spectacles de théâtre venant de la Guinée et de l’étranger ;  -	 un espace Percussion et musiques patrimoniales dédié aux groupes de percussions et de musiques traditionnelles de Guinée.
Results: Les résultats suivants ont été atteints en 2024 :   -	les capacités de 15 comédiens et metteurs en scène en technique de jeu d’acteur et de mise en scène ont été renforcées ; -	quatorze (14) spectacles de théâtre de qualité ont été diffusés ; -	six (6) spectacles de musiques patrimoniales ont été diffusés ; -	quatre (4) spectacles de théâtre scolaire ont été diffusés ;  -	une (1) rencontre entre les professionnels des arts du spectacle de la Guinée et de l’étranger (Sénégal, Mali, Côte d’Ivoire, Bénin, Togo, Mauritanie, Maroc, etc.) a été organisée; -	une (1) visite des sites touristiques a été organisée.

Title EN: Fostering reading culture in Ghana.
Goal: Integrate Culture In Sustainable Development Frameworks
SDG: SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: National sustainable development policies and plans
Agency Implementation: Ghana Publishers Association
Main Feature: The Ghana Publishers Association has encouraged its members to publish cultural materials (books) on different subjects matters. Books on environmental degradation, sanitation, health (COVID 19) and some unfriendly government policies. For example the association held a press conference in May 2024 to speak against imposition of VAT on books. The association organized educational programmes in some rural areas in the Ashanti Region in September 2023 to promote reading and literacy. Textbooks and supplementary reading materials were donated to the schools across the Ghana.
Results: Reading clubs were formed in schools. Mini libraries were also created in the various schools to help the pupils pick books and read on daily basis. Reading is being improved among the students through this initiative.

Title EN: Executive order No. 558-21 to put into effect the Patronage Law
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture
SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Cultural and creative sectors
Cultural Domain: Design,Performing Arts,Media Arts,Cinema and Audiovisual Arts,Music,Publishing,Visual Arts
Agency Implementation: Ministry of Culture and its newly established General Direction for Patronage
Main Feature: Although the Law No. 540-19 to promote and provide incentives for patronage in the Dominican Republic was signed into effect in 2019, it was dormant because it was lacking its application regulation. The Executive Order No. 558-21 approving said regulations was issued in 2021 by the Executive Branch, and so the National Council for Patronage was constituted, and the General Director appointed in a transparent process according to regulations. The office underwent the bureaucratic process required as a public institution, becoming operational in 2023. The patronage law facilitates financial support for artists, cultural projects, and institutions by providing tax incentives to donors. It encourages the development of the cultural sector by creating mechanisms for businesses and individuals to invest in cultural initiatives.
Results: The first 100 projects certified as Projects of national cultural interest in 2023. The 2024 call for applications is currently open. The certification allows the recipient to seek funding, both in the private sector and international cooperation entities.

Title EN: Festival Fronteira – Border Festival “Cultural Exchange in Strengthening Reconciliation"
Goal: Integrate Culture In Sustainable Development Frameworks
SDG: SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: National sustainable development policies and plans
Agency Implementation: Centro Nacional Chega (CNC, I.P)
Main Feature: National Center Chega, I.P. and the State Secretariat for Art and Culture, in partnership with the Indonesian Embassy in Dili, have launched the Border Festival on the theme of “Cultural Exchange in Strengthening Reconciliation”. The event aims to promote reconciliation between the people of Timor-Leste and Indonesia, especially those who are living in the border area. The event was held for first time in 2023, 23 years after Timor-Leste attained independence and separation from Indonesia. The Festival intends to:  a.	Promote a culture of dialogue between the new generations of the two countries through the joint production of historical and cultural content in art and literature, as well as promoting exchange in a space of joint collaboration in order to contribute to a positive balance in the historical narrative; b.	Promote reconciliation between the Timorese living in Indonesia and the Timorese living in Timor-Leste to maintain the bond of friendship in the future.  The first Border Festival was celebrated for four days, between 15 and 18 November 2023 in the Municipality of Bobonaro with the activities including production on mural paintings, conference and seminars on history and tradition of Timor island and cultural performances.
Results: The effect of such festival in peace building is yet to be gauged given it is a new initiative.  The festival is however expected to be an annual event and is expected to be an important case study on culture-based reconciliation.  The key actors in Timor Leste believes that culture and creative industries will be the effective entry points for peace building.

Title EN: Exemplary Regional Government Measures that Support the Mobility of Artists and Cultural Professionals
Goal: Achieve A Balanced Flow Of Cultural Goods And Services And Increase The Mobility Of Artists And Cultural Professionals
SDG: SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 10 - Reduce inequality within and among countries,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Flow of cultural goods and services
Agency Implementation: 1. Ministry of Education, Culture, Research, and Technology  2. Ministry of Tourism and Creative Economy/Tourism 3. Office of Culture, Provincial Government of Bali 4. Office of Tourism, Provincial Government of Maluku and others
Main Feature: In the past four years, exemplary regional government measures that support the mobility of artists and cultural professionals include: 1. Bali Arts Festival (Pesta Kesenian Bali, PKB); 2. Bali Jani Arts Festival (Festival Seni Bali Jani, FSBJ); 3. Spice Island Festival; 4. Central Java Cultural Arts Parade; 5. Isen Mulang Cultural Festival;  6. Cultural Performances;  7. Gandrung Sewu Festival;  8. Buen Festival;  9. Kiram Arts Festival; and  10. Riau Islands Local Culture Week.   PKB was reported in the 2020 QPR and is still being organized annually by Disbud Bali when this report was drafted. The festival was only not organized in 2020 due to the COVID-19 pandemic. In 2021, it was organized in a hybrid manner (in person and virtually), and since 2022, it has been back to normal.   Disbud Bali also initiated FSBJ as an annual arts festival to accommodate the activities and creativity of artists in exploring, preserving, and developing modern Balinese artistic and cultural values. It was first held in 2019, then in 2020, it was held virtually due to the COVID-19 pandemic, and in 2021, it was held in a hybrid manner. Starting in 2022, FSBJ has been held in person at the Bali Provincial Cultural Park. The series of activities of this festival include an animation film competition, poetry reading competition, modern theater, choir, and stand-up comedy.  The next program is the Spice Island Festival, an annual event held by Dispar Maluku to showcase Maluku's traditional art and culture while embracing modernity without ignoring the original values ​​of traditional arts and culture. Apart from focusing on arts and culture, the main objective of the Spice Island Festival is to provide education regarding the rich history of spices that attracted Europeans in the past. Located in one of the leading destinations and historical sites on Naira Island, the 2023 Spice Island Festival presented arts, culture, and musical performances. This festival explicitly targets youth while still prioritizing educational elements related to spices in Maluku with the hope that more young people will be interested in preserving spices and history in Maluku. This festival is supported by the Kharisma Event Nusantara program (see Goal 2, Policies and Measures that Support the Inward Mobility of Foreign Artists and Cultural Professionals to Indonesia).  Then, there is the Central Java Cultural Arts Parade, which aims to preserve and develop the culture of the districts and cities in Central Java. Disdikbud Jateng organizes the parade annually on August 19, which is the anniversary of the Central Java Province. In 2023, the event was held in Magelang with the specific objective of supporting Borobudur as a Super Priority Destination Program.  One program in Kalimantan, the Isen Mulang Cultural Festival (FBIM), which has been held by Disbudpar Kalteng since 1993, is aimed at promoting cultural attractions in Central Kalimantan, providing interesting spectacles for the community, as well as preserving traditional culture. This festival gathered representatives from 14 city/regency governments in Central Kalimantan. FBIM has an essential meaning for the people of Central Kalimantan as a symbol of "meeting," a place to show the creativity of local artists based on cultural practices that already exist and live in every aspect of the life of the Dayak people in Central Kalimantan. This festival presents various competitions, including a cultural carnival, tourism pageant, traditional arts, traditional games, traditional sports, and traditional cuisine/culinary from the Dayak community of Central Kalimantan. This festival is also one of the festivals supported by the Kharisma Event Nusantara program (see Goal 2, Policies and Measures that Support the Inward Mobility of Foreign Artists and Cultural Professionals to Indonesia).  Another program in West Nusa Tenggara (Nusa Tenggara Barat, NTB), the NTB Cultural Event is a series of cultural activities from, by, and for all educational units ranging from pre-schools to senior high schools, including both state and private educational institutions, in the province of NTB. This event, which Disdikbud NTB supports, is held annually to celebrate NTB's anniversary on December 17. The series of activities being organized over five days include cultural parades, cultural attractions, cultural dialogue, cultural awards, competitions related to culture (such as traditional medicine, folk games and traditional sports, art, historical traces of traditions, language, and oral traditions), and cultural exhibitions of students' work (such as culinary, batik, weaving, student-designed clothing, crafts, traditional technology, painting, crafts, etc.).   Next, there is the Gandrung Sewu Festival, an annual colossal Gandrung dance festival at Boom Beach, Banyuwangi Regency, East Java, set against the backdrop of the Bali Strait. First initiated in 2012, this festival was held to introduce Banyuwangi culture, especially Gandrung, to a broad audience. In its development, the festival, which received support from Disbudpar Jatim, has grown into an icon of Banyuwangi cultural tourism and is one part of the Banyuwangi Festival. This festival is also one of the festivals supported by the Kharisma Event Nusantara program (see Goal 2, Policies and Measures that Support the Inward Mobility of Foreign Artists and Cultural Professionals to Indonesia).  Then, there is the Buen Festival, an annual program organized by the Regency Government of North Penajam Paser, East Kalimantan Province, since 2016. This festival aims to introduce unique arts, culture, and customs to local and foreign tourists, exchange cultural knowledge with invited participating countries, and collaborate with domestic and international artists. With support from Disdikbud Kaltim, various activities are held during this festival, including culinary festivals, cultural parades, arts and culture festivals, traditional games, and rituals.   Meanwhile, the South Kalimantan Kiram Arts Festival is an event by Disdikbud Kalsel. The first event was held in 2018 under the name South Borneo Art Festival. The second was held on November 8-12, 2023, featuring various art performances and exhibitions, including dance, music, literature, theater, painting, workshops, and South Kalimantan authentic MSME products.  Lastly, Disbud Kepri held the Riau Islands Cultural Week for the first time on September 21-23, 2023, which coincided with the anniversary of the Riau Islands Province. This event displayed Malay culture, such as Malay poetry, Syair Gurindam 12, and Malay dances. It also featured cultural arts from ethnic Chinese in the form of Barongsai and Reog performances from Java as a form of intercultural harmony.   In general, exemplary regional government measures that support the mobility of artists and cultural professionals are aimed at contributing to achieving the following agenda(s) of the National Strategy for Culture: 1. Provide space for the diversity of cultural expressions and encourage cultural interaction to strengthen the inclusiveness of culture (Agenda 1); 2. Protect and develop values, expressions, and practices of traditional culture to enrich national culture (Agenda 2); and 3. Develop and utilize cultural resources to strengthen the position of Indonesia internationally (Agenda 3).
Results: PKB: In 2022 and 2023, this annual festival gathered around 500 international participants and was watched by more than 1 million visitors. In 2023, more than 1,600,000 people visited the 44th PKB.  Central Java Cultural Arts Parade: This annual event usually involves 1,750 artists and arts workers, with at least 50 people per delegation per city/regency. The delegation comprises dancers, choreographers, musicians, music arrangers, and others. Each performer was given 5 minutes to appear in front of the honorary stage.  Buen Festival: The various activities held involved around 500 local MSMEs.  Kiram Arts Festival: In 2018, 100 local artists and 20 international artists attended the festival. In 2023, the festival gathered local South Kalimantan artists from 13 regencies/cities and 14 Asian countries, namely Malaysia, Philippines, Cambodia, Thailand, Japan, Hong Kong, Taiwan, India, Zimbabwe, Ghana, Australia, New Caledonia, Zealand New, UK, Sweden, Italy, Germany, Colombia, and the Netherlands.  Riau Islands Cultural Week: The event, which involved 70 artists from neighboring countries, namely Malaysia and Singapore, was attended by around 5,000 spectators.
Financial Ressources: NTB Cultural Event:  In 2020, IDR 20,000,000 / 1.225,70 USD was allocated from the NTB Provincial Revenue and Expenditure Budget. However, funding has come from the School Principals' Work Deliberation (Musyawarah Kerja Kepala Sekolah) across the NTB Province since 2021. Title EN: General Public Participation, enjoyment & engagement with culture
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture
SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Cultural and creative sectors
Agency Implementation: Art Jameel Dubai  Alserkal Avenue The Cultural Foundation Salama Bint Hamdan Al Nahyan Foundation Louvre Abu Dhabi Manarat Al Saadiyat Abu Dhabi Department of Culture and Tourism Abu Dhabi Music and Arts Foundation Red Crescent Art Dubai
Main Feature: Many cultural events are regularly held in the UAE. These provide opportunities for artists and professionals to showcase their talents, products, and services; and also allow a wider engagement of the community with cultural ideas and platforms. Some of the notable cultural events and program held in the UAE include: Zayed Heritage Festival: Named in honor of the late Sheikh Zayed bin Sultan Al Nahyan, founding father of the United Arab Emirates, the annual Sheikh Zayed Heritage Festival celebrates the United Arab Emirates’ cultural inheritance, showcases the rich diversity of its traditions and enlightens visitors about the legacy of the nation’s founder. Visitors to the festival can experience Emirati heritage and culture through its arts, crafts, foods and customs. A central feature of the festival is the UAE Heritage District, which hosts exhibitions, events and popular markets reflecting traditional Emirati life. The World Heritage district reflects the architectural heritage, crafts, products and traditional arts of other countries. The festival also features camel races, falconry shows, and a variety of competitions. Mother of the Nation Festival: The annual event honors Her Highness Sheikha Fatima Bint Mubarak, the wife of the late Sheikh Zayed Bin Sultan Al Nahyan, the founding father of the UAE. She has been a pioneer in supporting women’s empowerment and rights in the UAE and the region. The festival creates an entertaining and interactive atmosphere that welcomes families and individuals from all walks of life and supports artistic and cultural performances. The festival includes a showcase of cultural businesses such as fashion, cultural products, and competitions.  Liwa Date Festival: The versatile date palm and the date fruit have played an important role in fulfilling the dietary needs of generations of desert communities, including those in the United Arab Emirates.  The fruit is highly nutritious, while the trunk, fronds and other parts of the tree were traditionally used in buildings, handicrafts and tools. The Liwa Date Festival highlights these and other important aspects of the date palm. Held in Abu Dhabi, the Liwa Date Festival is an annual event that introduces date producers to modern agricultural practices and facilitates the exchange of expertise on the best ways to produce the highest quality date. The festival also is one of Abu Dhabi’s most significant heritage events and tourist attractions that highlights the many ways dates have impacted the cultural, heritage and economic life of the country. It provides a great place for visitors to learn about dates and to sample the most popular date varieties grown in the UAE. The festival’s main event is the competition for the best date fruit. Emirati farms vie for the title of best date grower. It also includes lectures on date farming, poetry evenings, and an exhibition space for date farming equipment and date products. Alserkal Avenue Programs: Al Serkal Avenue in Dubai develops year-round programming dedicated to fostering arts and culture education and engagement. The annual program is thematically developed to focus on a particular issue, bringing artists and professionals from different fields together to examine a concept through talks, screenings, workshops and festivals. Abu Dhabi Classics: The Abu Dhabi Music and Arts Foundation annually brings classical and traditional music to Abu Dhabi, featuring world-class performers and orchestras from around the world. The program incorporates Abu Dhabi Classics, the Emirati Music Series, Umsiyat and the Bait Al Oud Concert Series. The events are held at leading venues across the emirate and include performances, talks, master classes and lectures from some of the most influential contemporary musicians from around the world. Abu Dhabi Art: Abu Dhabi Art is an annual event that expands beyond the notion of a traditional art fair, in placing strong emphasis on a diverse public engagement program, including art installations and exhibitions, talks and events that take place in different locations throughout the year. The culmination of this year-long program is the Abu Dhabi Art event in November, which provides an important sales platform for participating galleries whilst also offering these galleries an opportunity to showcase ambitious installations and site-specific works by their artists to an audience of over 20,000 visitors. Abu Dhabi International Book Fair: Abu Dhabi International Book Fair is a major annual initiative that seeks to develop the regional publishing industry and promote reading in Abu Dhabi and the UAE. It holds many talks, lectures, and cultural activities, and ensures the participation of notable thinkers and writers from around the world.  Abu Dhabi Culinary Season: Launched in 2019, the Abu Dhabi Culinary Season is an annual six-week foodie affair featuring consumer events, interactive dining experiences, and city-wide promotions from casual to fine dining, while hosting internationally acclaimed chefs and restaurants for pop-ups across the emirate. The Season was created to highlight the wide variety of culinary offerings in the UAE capital. Ataya Exhibition: Ataya (means ‘giving’ in Arabic) is, and it is an exhibition for charity organized by Emirates Red Crescent under the Patronage of Her Highness Sheikha Shamsa Bint Hamdan Bin Mohammed Al Nahyan. The annual Ataya Exhibition - since inception a short 5 years back – has quickly become a landmark in Abu Dhabi’s cultural calendar, where a wide range of fresh and distinct fashion wear, jewelry, home accessories and furniture is exhibited and sold. The exhibits are by talented designers and artists from the UAE and the region, with each being picked individually by the Higher Committee of the Exhibition. Ras Al Khaimah Fine Arts Festival: Established in 2013, the Ras Al Khaimah Fine Arts Festival is a non-profit initiative designed to showcase, in a community setting, the talent and work of local and international artists, photographers, and filmmakers. The festival initially began as a three-day event in 2013 and has grown to become a two-month festival that includes a month of programmed events and an eight-week visual arts exhibition. Since 2019, the festival was moved to be an outdoor exhibition in Al Jazira Al Hamra Heritage Village. Art Dubai: Art Dubai is one of the world’s leading international art fairs, presenting 90 galleries from more than 40 countries. Art Dubai, founded in 2007 and going into its 14th edition, offers a unique art fair proposition of commercial and non-profit cross-disciplinary platforms, and a commitment to cultivating a culture of discovery, education and thought leadership. Featuring three gallery sections (Contemporary, Modern, Bawwaba), the fair drives meaningful engagement with the rich cultural heritage and contemporary art practices of the region and extending to territories across what is known as “The Global South”, including the Middle East, South and Southeast Asia, the African continent, and Latin America. Art Dubai has been the launch pad and development platform of the successful careers of artists, curators and art professionals, and continues to celebrate art excellence through its extended fair programming, artist commissions and initiatives. Sharjah Architecture Triennial: Sharjah Architecture Triennial is the first major platform for architecture and urbanism in the Middle East, North and East Africa, and South and Southeast Asia. It serves as a space for critical reflection and supports research that situates the built environment within its complex social, economic, and cultural contexts. The Triennial invites architectural practitioners, students, scholars, practitioners, policy makers, and members of the public to enrich international discourses by engaging in them from a regional perspective.  Sharjah International book Fair (SIBF): Sharjah International Book Fair, launched in 1982, is one of the world’s largest international book fairs. The 11-day event runs over 400 intellectual, cultural and artistic activities every year, including writing workshops, poetry readings and book signings, and has established awards programs designed to encourage and promote the literary community.  Al Dhafra Festival: A cultural festival celebrating Bedouin traditions and heritage, including camel racing, traditional crafts, and folklore performances. Louvre Abu Dhabi Exhibitions: The Louvre Abu Dhabi, a major cultural institution, hosts various high-profile exhibitions that cover a range of art and historical periods.
Results: There are many cultural events held in the UAE and they have many visitors as the statistics below show: •	2024 edtion of Abu Dhabi Book Fair welcomed 231,168 visitors  and sold 160,152 books. it also featured 1,350 publishers from 90 countries,and more than 2,000 activities. •	Mother of the Nation Festival: This annual festival sees around 160,000 visitors over its 12-day run, celebrating Emirati culture and heritage with diverse activities and entertainment. •	Abu Dhabi Culinary Season: Attracts approximately 100,000 visitors each year during its six-week period, showcasing culinary arts and gastronomy. •	Abu Dhabi Art: This four-day art fair draws about 20,000 visitors and features around 40 galleries, highlighting contemporary art from local and international artists. •	The 16th edition of Art Dubai in 2023 welcomed well over 30,000 visitors to its Contemporary, Modern, Bawwaba and Digital sections. Altogether, more than 130 galleries from 43 countries participated in the fair. The 42nd edition of the Sharjah International Book Fair in 2023 received more than 2 million visitors and 2033 publishers from 109 countries, who displayed more than 1.5 million titles in various sectors of knowledge and culture. It also witnessed the organization of 1700 diverse events, in which more than 215 guests from 69 countries participated, in addition to 460 events within a rich cultural program presented by 127 participants from prominent Arab and foreign writers and artists from 33 countries.The data above demonstrate that the UAE has become a successful destination for cultural events.
Recommandations: There are many events held regularly in the UAE and there is more variety in the types of cultural events implemented in the country to ensure the engagement of different segments of society with the arts and culture.

Main Feature: The Export Support Service is a new helpline and online service where all UK businesses can get answers to practical questions about exporting to Europe. The service is a ‘one-stop shop’ and brings together UK government information, making it easier for exporters to access advice and support. British businesses exporting to Europe will now be able to access one-to-one advice via the new phone and online service. From queries around rules of origin, to guidance on recognising professional qualifications and entering new markets, the Export Support Service will provide a single point of contact. It will help exporters navigate a range of complex information simply and quickly.    The Export Support Service includes programmes such as the UK Export Academy, which aims to help businesses grow by giving them the confidence and knowledge to trade overseas.
Results: Over 18,000 businesses across the UK have already joined the UK Export Academy.

Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture

Agency Implementation: Sheikh Mohammed bin Rashid Al Maktoum Center for Cultural Understanding (SMCCU)
Main Feature: Since 2020, the SMCCU has continued its mission to promote cultural understanding and tolerance in the UAE under the theme "Open Doors, Open Minds." The Center offers a variety of programs aimed at educating both residents and visitors about the UAE's rich cultural heritage. These programs include traditional Emirati meals, guided tours of historical sites, and interactive sessions that allow participants to engage directly with Emirati culture. Recent initiatives include special events designed for specific groups such as children of determination (children with disabilities), breast cancer survivors, and the elderly, ensuring inclusivity and accessibility. The Center has also participated in significant events like the Arabian Travel Market and the Dubai Food Festival, highlighting its role in promoting cultural tourism and understanding.
Results: The SMCCU continues to expand its reach and impact. From 2020 onwards, the Center has hosted numerous cultural events and educational programs, attracting a diverse audience from all walks of life. The Center's efforts have been pivotal in fostering a deeper understanding and appreciation of Emirati culture among expatriates and visitors, contributing to the UAE's broader goals of cultural diversity and tolerance.

Title EN: Facilitating the study of artistic professions abroad
Goal: Achieve A Balanced Flow Of Cultural Goods And Services And Increase The Mobility Of Artists And Cultural Professionals
SDG: SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 10 - Reduce inequality within and among countries,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Mobility of artists and cultural professionals
Cultural Domain: Design,Performing Arts,Media Arts,Cinema and Audiovisual Arts,Music,Publishing,Visual Arts
Agency Implementation: Ministry of Culture
Main Feature: The Ministry of Culture implements two measures related to scholarships for artistic studies abroad: an annual call for applications for undergraduate studies in artistic professions abroad (financed from the general budget) and scholarships for specialized cultural professions for postgraduate studies abroad, as well as scholarships for training or studies abroad (financed by the European Social Fund, with five calls for applications between 2020 and 2023). Scholarships create the conditions for acquiring new knowledge and access to the arts, promote research and creativity, and foster international connections. They also contribute to a knowledge-based society that enriches the domestic creative sector and extends to the wider context of the European Union. In the long term, education can deepen knowledge and produce a well-educated workforce capable of passing on knowledge to future generations. A scholarship serves as additional income to cover the costs incurred during the course of study. It partially covers:  - tuition fees (often including materials, technical aids, theoretical knowledge acquisition, and practical learning);  - other study-related expenses abroad, such as monthly transit passes, health insurance subsidies, housing costs, food, books, clothing, recreational activities, and student visa fees.
Results: In 2020-2023, ten public calls for scholarships were issued: a total of 102 scholarships were awarded for undergraduate studies and 40 scholarships for postgraduate studies abroad.
Recommandations: The scholarship program for bachelor studies in artistic fields abroad will be continued within the existing financial framework. As part of the European Cohesion Policy Program in Slovenia for the period 2021-2027, the ESS scholarships for postgraduate studies in artistic fields abroad will also be continued. The scholarship program will be extended to studies outside the EU member states and will also include doctoral studies. The calls for applications for scholarships will continue in 2024, with a slight increase in the available funds and the amount of each scholarship.

Agency Implementation: PALAIS DE LA CULTURE BERNARD BINLIN-DADIE (ABIDJAN)
Main Feature: La politique de facilitation d’accès aux espaces et salles de spectacles au Palais de la Culture Bernard Binlin-Dadié vise à promouvoir l’accès des artistes et du public aux infrastructures culturelles. Cette initiative réduit les coûts de location des salles pour les artistes locaux et offre des subventions pour l'organisation d'événements culturels. Elle prévoit également des programmes de formation et de perfectionnement pour les artistes, ainsi que des partenariats avec des institutions culturelles locales et internationales pour favoriser les échanges artistiques et la diffusion des œuvres.
Results: La politique a permis d’augmenter significativement le nombre d'événements culturels organisés au Palais de la Culture. De nombreux artistes locaux ont pu bénéficier des infrastructures à un coût réduit, ce qui a stimulé la création et la diffusion des œuvres culturelles. Le public a également bénéficié d'un accès plus large à une variété d'événements culturels de qualité, renforçant ainsi l'attrait culturel de la région.
Recommandations: L'évaluation a montré que cette politique a grandement contribué à dynamiser la scène culturelle à Abidjan. Il est recommandé de continuer à soutenir les artistes locaux par des formations régulières et des opportunités de réseautage. D'autres recommandations incluent l'amélioration des infrastructures techniques des salles de spectacles pour répondre aux normes internationales et l'élargissement du programme pour inclure d'autres villes en Côte d'Ivoire.

Title EN: Fair Pay Reader
Goal: Promote Human Rights And Fundamental Freedoms
SDG: SDG 5 - Achieve gender equality and empower all women and girls,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels
Area of Monitoring: Artistic freedom
Cultural Domain: Design,Performing Arts,Media Arts,Cinema and Audiovisual Arts,Music,Publishing,Visual Arts
Agency Implementation: Kulturrat Österreich
Main Feature: The publication "Fair Pay - For fair conditions in the arts, culture and media" (Kulturrat Österreich, Sept. 2021) provides insights into working conditions in the arts and culture sector in Austria and is designed as a handbook with a practical part (including tools for calculating fair remuneration). For the Fair Pay Reader, the Kulturrat Österreich (Austrian Cultural Council) invited stakeholders to describe the main characteristics of work and remuneration in their respective sectors, as well as the tools and solutions developed so far to achieve fair and adequate remuneration. Each section is followed by a list of specific instruments, such as pay scales, collective agreements, calculators or recommended fees. The reader also covers copyright and contract law. Title EN: Factory platform by the Jordan National Gallery of Fine Arts
Goal: Integrate Culture In Sustainable Development Frameworks
SDG: SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: National sustainable development policies and plans
Cultural Domain: Design,Performing Arts,Media Arts,Cinema and Audiovisual Arts,Music,Publishing,Visual Arts
Agency Implementation: CSO NAME: The Jordan National Gallery of Fine Arts EMAIL: info@nationalgallery.org   PHONE: 00962 6 463 0128
Main Feature: Over the past 4 years the Jordan National Gallery of Fine Arts, continued through its Factory Platform for creation and contemporary thought to champion cultural and artistic diversity, co-learning and collaborative production within the realm of socially engaged art projects. Below is a general overview of Factory which continues to promote the cultural and creative sectors and the diversity of cultural expressions.  Factory Platform is a project launched by the Jordan National Gallery of Fine Arts (JNGFA) in 2018 to meet its goal to open up to the local community in all its aspects and involve them in the creative process, in addition to putting the Gallery on the map of international art.  The Platform is designed to give opportunities to youth to develop didactic strategies with the social network through fully promoting collaborative or participatory processes and projects in various fields of visual arts, music, theater, literature, contemporary dance and performing arts, through international open calls as well as invitations directed to certain projects across Factory’s: Emerging Art Projects, Art Residencies, Curatorial Projects, and Public Art Projects.  (1) THE EMERGING ART PROJECTS PROGRAM Through this program, Factory hosts projects in the process of development, generated from contemporary creation and innovation. This program supports projects and proposals that are in the process of investigation and require an impulse for their development, production and implementation. Program Objectives: - Improve experimentation and innovation in social, creative, artistic, social, urban, technological and environmental spheres. - Encourage the introduction of new formats and expository and didactic discourses in relation to the topics investigated. - Encouraging citizen participation in the fields of the creation of different disciplines. - Revalue research in different fields of creation, giving impetus and visibility to the projects and their creators.  (2) JORDAN ART RESIDENCIES AND STUDIOS PROGRAM (JARS) Through Factory under the umbrella of the JNGFA we provide the space and time for reflection, research, presentation and/or production to the selected residents. JARS allows people to explore their practice within the framework of another community; meeting new people, using new materials, experiencing life in a new location. JARS emphasizes the importance of interdisciplinary cultural exchange and immersion in another culture. Therefore, art projects that involve the local community through presentations, workshops or collaborations will be especially valued. The JNGFA is committed to exhibit the residents' works, as well as helping them to carry out scheduled meetings and workshops to disseminate their research. Program Objectives: - Improve experimentation and innovation in social, creative, artistic, urban, technological and environmental spheres. - Encourage artistic practice within the framework of another community; meeting new people, using new materials, experiencing life in a new location. - Encourage participation and collaboration with other cultures. - Revalue research in different fields of creation, discover artists and thinkers, and give visibility and publicity to their projects.  (3) THE CURATORIAL ART PROJECTS PROGRAM Through this open call, Factory will host curators who develop curatorial projects in any discipline linked to contemporary creative practices such as; drawing, painting, graphic, sculpture, photography, video art, installation, performance art, dance, music, theater, film, anime, architecture, design, urban planning, technology, social and environmental projects, etc. The curators are encouraged to give special attention to the following topics: The Jordan National Gallery's Permanent Collection; modern Jordanian art trends; social, environmental, gender issues, among others; experimentation and innovation in the field of artistic creation; expository discourses in relation to new technologies. Program Objectives: - Encourage research around the National Gallery's Permanent Collection. - Promote research in social, creative, artistic, urban, technological, environmental, etc. - Give international visibility to the contemporary artistic scenes of the Middle East. - Encourage the introduction of new formats and expository and didactic discourses in relation to the topics investigated. Revalue research in different fields of creation, giving impetus and visibility to the projects and their creators.  (4) PUBLIC ART PROJECTS The Public Art Projects is based on the conviction that the creative community builds bridges and demolishes walls and borders through an open call that takes place in public places in Jordan. The works will be designed to be placed in specific outdoor or indoor public locations and will be available for public interaction day and night during the exhibition period. Program Objectives: - Support new artistic expressions in the urban space. - Provoke a dialogue with the public, community interaction and exchange with the spatial surroundings. - Develop didactic that bring art closer to the citizen. - Stimulate citizen participation and re-evaluate public space as a place where art becomes available to interlocutors who will play an important role in building meanings and exploiting the spaces they usually pass by. - Focus on moral/social discourse, aesthetic discourse or both with the routine life of the city.
Results: Over the past four years, Factory Platform by JNGFA has supported five major projects across its four programs: The Laboratory of the Future through Factory’s Public Art Projects, Zajal Movement project through the Emerging Art Projects program, Midan Dance Performance, and two editions of the annual Digital Transmission Program through Factory’s Art Residencies. These projects have led to over 30 public events, engaging around 200 artists and more than 3500 audience members through live performances, artist talks, public art interventions, and exhibitions at JNGFA.  Outcomes: These initiatives have promoted the cultural and creative sectors and the diversity of cultural expressions in the following areas (with essential crossovers across the four 2005 convention goals): Information and Awareness: Conferences, debates, and other activities. Capacity Building: Training for artists and cultural professionals. Support for Creative Industries: Assistance to small or micro-enterprises, including micro-credit schemes and innovation labs. Digital Literacy and Creativity: Promotion of digital skills and content creation. Artistic and Media Activities: Initiatives promoting diverse cultural expressions. Manage or contribute to mobility funds for artists and cultural professionals (scholarships, travel grants, etc.) Manage infrastructure (arts residencies) and major cultural events (cultural seasons, festivals) promoting the diversity of cultural expressions and hosting a large number of foreign artists, notably from developing countries Facilitate participation in cultural life and access to diverse cultural facilities and expressions, notably addressing the needs of disadvantaged or vulnerable groups. Support women's full participation in cultural life Support the recognition and advancement of women as artists, cultural professionals and/or creative entrepreneurs  Key Projects: Laboratory of the Future: After the COVID-19 pandemic, Factory launched an open call through its Public Art Projects with the Goethe and French Institutes in Jordan titled "Laboratory of the Future." Nine cultural actors from various disciplines collaborated for four months, culminating in the "Remote Closeness" event in summer 2021. This event featured an art trail across Jordan, an exhibition at JNGFA, and a research residency, addressing environmental, urban, social, economic, and political issues. This project has also led to the formation of the artist collective "Remote Closeness." Emerging Art Projects Program: From fall 2021 to fall 2023, this program supported two initiatives in Amman: Zajal Movement: This project partnered with "Underground Amman," a Hip Hop culture initiative. It hosted monthly events featuring Hip Hop and graffiti shows, juried contests, artist talks, and discussions on sociocultural issues like diaspora and marginalization. The project concluded with an exhibition documenting the local Hip Hop scene's growth. Midan Amman Dance Lab: Hosted within Factory’s Art Residencies, this initiative provided resources and space for regular practice and monthly public performances at the Gallery, supporting emerging performers and helping establish the music group Sawwa7. Two major performances were directed by acclaimed choreographer Yoshiko Chuma. [Digital] Transmissions: Organized in collaboration with FutureEverything (UK) and the British Council (Jordan), this program offered a four-month remote residency for 12 artists from various disciplines. Mentored by professionals from Jordan and the UK, participants developed new digital art projects addressing critical social, cultural, and political themes.  These projects have significantly contributed to the cultural and creative sectors, fostering diverse cultural expressions and supporting artists through training, capacity building, innovation, and mobility initiatives.

Title EN: FESTIVAL DE CINEMA DES ECOLES D’ABIDJAN (FESCEA)
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture

Area of Monitoring: Cultural and creative sectors
Agency Implementation: Direction Régionale de la Culture et de la Francophonie d’Abidjan
Main Feature: Le cinéma a pris une place importante dans l’éducation secondaire et supérieure, menant à la création de filières dédiées dans divers établissements. La prolifération de festivals et compétitions de cinéma amateur, soutenue par des politiques culturelles, a révélé de nouveaux talents et idées, propulsant ainsi l'industrie cinématographique.  C’est dans ce contexte que la Direction Régionale de la Culture et de la Francophonie d'Abidjan, en collaboration avec Fidelio Ets, a lancé en 2017 le Festival de Cinéma des Écoles d’Abidjan (FESCEA). Ce festival vise à promouvoir le cinéma et l’audiovisuel dans la région. La première édition, qui a eu lieu à l’ONAC-CI, a présenté des films réalisés par plusieurs établissements scolaires d’Abidjan, marquant le début d'une aventure prometteuse.  La deuxième édition, en 2021, s’est tenue au groupe ETIC avec onze films en compétition. Plutôt que de distribuer des récompenses, cette édition s’est concentrée sur les projections et les échanges avec des figures importantes du cinéma ivoirien, ainsi que la remise de diplômes aux participants. Les projections ont permis aux élèves acteurs, techniciens et responsables de ces œuvres d’apprécier leur travail achevé.  En décembre 2022, la troisième édition s’est déroulée dans la commune de Koumassi, intégrée au festival local « J’AIME KOUMASSI ». Cette édition a proposé des master classes et des projections sur trois sites différents, abordant des thèmes tels que l’écriture de scénarios et le jeu d’acteur. Des experts renommés du cinéma ivoirien ont animé ces formations, attirant plus de 1500 participants par site et la présence d’autorités municipales et éducatives. Vingt-six films provenant de divers établissements ont été projetés, contribuant au succès de l’événement.  Forte du succès de cette édition, la commune de Koumassi a décidé d’accueillir à nouveau le festival. La quatrième édition a continué sur cette lancée avec des formations supplémentaires sur l’écriture de scénarios, le jeu d’acteur, et la gestion d’une équipe de tournage. Plus de 1000 élèves et étudiants ont bénéficié de l’expérience des formateurs, et la participation de figures notables du cinéma ivoirien comme Guy Kalou a enrichi les échanges. La soirée de projections a attiré plus de 5000 personnes, consolidant l’importance du festival dans la promotion du cinéma local.  À ce jour, les préparatifs pour la cinquième édition sont en cours, promettant de continuer à inspirer et former de nouveaux talents cinématographiques en Côte d’Ivoire.
Results: La créativité cinématographique est suscitée et encouragée chez les jeunes ; - Les multiples métiers du cinéma sont connus, aimés et adoptés ; - La sensibilité de la jeune génération est touchée afin de révéler le génie créatif ; - Les jeunes talents sont détectés et encouragés ; - Les populations de la commune sont édifiées à travers les projections ; - Les populations découvrent des corps de métiers différents des classiques ; - Les populations visionnent des films gratuitement.
Recommandations: C’est une belle activité qui mérite d’être suivie et accompagnée.  Il faut accompagner  avec  plus de moyens pour les récompenses afin d’encourager  la promotion de notre domaine d’activité en leur donnant des gadgets comme des appareils photos numériques, des cameras, des ordinateurs, des bourses pour des participations à des résidences d’écritures.  Elargir notre champ de communication afin de permettre une large participation des 13 communes et sous préfectures de la région d’Abidjan

Title EN: FESTIVAL INTERNATIONAL DE LA MODE ET DU RECYCLAGE (FIMORE)
Goal: Integrate Culture In Sustainable Development Frameworks
SDG: SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: National sustainable development policies and plans
Agency Implementation: FIMORE
Main Feature: Les progrès technologiques ont apporté à l’homme des avancées notables qui affectent directement sa qualité de vie, mais certains processus industriels ont causé différents problèmes liés à l’environnement qui le détériore et finissent par affecter la vie sur notre planète. D’où l’importance de considérer le recyclage comme une alternative pour minimiser les effets de certains processus industriels.  En Côte d’Ivoire où le phénomène de la prolifération des déchets plastiques est grandissant, l’Etat mène des actions en vue de sa réduction, via les Ministères concernés et les institutions étatiques. Les acteurs de la mode ne sont pas en reste.  Le recyclage dans la mode consiste à faire du neuf avec de l’ancien. Cette tendance écoresponsable séduit tant les créateurs que les acheteurs dans un contexte économique et politique où la préservation de l’environnement est de plus en plus mise en avant.  Le recyclage consiste à transformer un objet en matière première qui est alors utilisée pour produire de nouveaux produits. En matière de mode, il s’agit entre autres, soit à collecter de vieux vêtements, à les broyer pour les ramener à l’état de fibres textiles ou  à réutiliser les déchets de certains produits pour en fabriquer d’autres matériaux qui sont utilisables.  Selon une étude de l’UNICEF menée en 2014, on estime entre 40.000 et 100.000 tonnes de déchets plastiques qui sont produits par an en Côte d’Ivoire. Ce flux de déchets,  dont seulement 5 à 20% sont recyclés, et le reste étant jetés dans les rues, les dépôts sauvages ou brûlés à l’air libre, représente une menace sanitaire et environnementale. Au regard du constat ci-dessus, alarmant, à savoir la croissance de la quantité des déchets, qui devrait augmenter de 70% d’ici à 2050, le recyclage des déchets apparaît comme une solution. Il se présente comme un mode de production et de consommation qui consiste à réparer, réutiliser, remettre à neuf et recycler le plus longtemps possible les matériaux et produits existants. Dans le cadre de la mise en œuvre de cette mesure, dans l’industrie de la mode,  les acteurs du secteur, se proposent de  contribuer, dans une grande mesure, à améliorer la gestion des déchets, tout en luttant contre la pauvreté en créant un modèle générateur de nombreux emplois.
Results: Les résultats atteints par l'initiative sont:  -Le développement de la mode via le recyclage d’objets provenant des ordures ménagères, est un concept promu ;  -L’entreprenariat des jeunes et des femmes acteurs de mode, à la fabrication des objets recyclés, est effectif ; -Les techniques de recyclage des tissus et objets plastiques sont maitrisés par les acteurs ; -Le grand public découvre et s’approprie des créations issus  du recyclage des déchets, par les acteurs des ICC au plan local ; -Les autorités locales et les populations valorisent les ordures ménagères.

Il s'adresse aux cinéphiles, cinéastes et spécialistes en industrie cinématographique mondiale. Il s’étend, chaque année, sur cinq (05) jours entre cinéma, rencontres, formation et inspiration. Il comprend, en outre, une plateforme dédiée à la gloire du cinéma et au ralliement des cultures. Il s'agit également d'une occasion unique d'accéder aux marchés arabe, africain et international, et encourager ainsi de nouveaux talents en soutenant la coproduction et la distribution à travers le monde. La compétition oppose les meilleurs films nationaux et internationaux. Les films sélectionnés sont nominés aux grands festivals internationaux de films tels que le festival de Cannes, le festival de RED SEA, le Festival de Carthage, le Festival International du Film du Caire, etc. En outre, le programme comprend des projections de films, des master class, des ateliers de formation, ainsi que des colloques sur un ensemble de sujets dans le domaine de la cinématographique, des expositions artistiques et de nombreuses visites guidées autour des monuments et sites archéologiques «Imedghassen – Timgad», et ce pour stimuler le secteur du tourisme dans le pays. Les enfants ne sont pas en reste dans ce festival, il leur réserve un espace comprenant une compétition de courts métrages de leur réalisation et une projection de films à leur intention à travers de nombreuses daïras de la wilaya de Batna. En résumé, le Festival International Imedghassen se distingue non seulement par la qualité de ses projections, mais également par l’ampleur de son impact sur le cinéma et la culture.
Results: Le Festival International du Cinéma Imedghassen (IIFF), représente un événement culturel majeur dans la région des Aurès, a permis de réaliser les résultats suivants :  •	Faire du festival une manifestation cinématographique dans la région des Aurès, ce qui a permis de susciter l'intérêt des communautés nationale et internationale en stimulant collaboration et soutien entre (cinéastes, artistes, formateurs, stagiaires, presse, sponsors, festivals, ambassades, etc.) ; •	Promouvoir le patrimoine culturel et touristique de la région en mettant en valeur les sites archéologiques, tels que le tombeau royal numide « Imedghassen » datant de 400 ans avant J.-C, et la ville de Timgad, etc. ; •	Mise en valeur du site Imedghassen suite aux visites répétées des invités du festival qui les ont conduites au tombeau royal numide « Imedghassen » ;  •	Encourager les productions cinématographiques dans la région.
Recommandations: Il est recommandé de capitaliser les acquis des précédents festivals en procédant à un audit qui permettrait de diagnostiquer les éventuelles défaillances et les solutionner en vue des éditions futures

Title EN: Film in Georgia
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture
SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Cultural and creative sectors
Agency Implementation: LEPL Enterprise Georgia
Main Feature: In 2015, the Government of Georgia launched the "Film in Georgia" incentive programme to support the film industry. The programme offers a 20-25% cash rebate on qualified expenses for international and local production companies operating in Georgia. The eligible products for cash rebate include feature films, drama/series, mini-series (including pilots), animated films, documentary films, advertising video production, reality shows, and music videos. The "Film in Georgia" programme has been highly successful since its inception in 2016. Currently, 48 international projects are part of the portfolio, with 30 of them having received rebates. As of now, 200 000 000 Georgian Lari have been spent in Georgia, and 137 000 000 Georgian Lari have been qualified by authorized audit documents. Since 2020, 25 international projects have been registered, with qualified expenses totaling 52,000,000 Georgian Lari.   In line with its commitment to supporting the film industry, Enterprise Georgia offers the Business Universal Program, which subsidizes the loan interest rate by the national refinancing rate minus 5% for the entire loan term. This enables production companies to build or expand film studios, or purchase equipment through leasing, at a significantly reduced cost.   Enterprise Georgia also provides opportunities for the creative industry sector to strengthen its international connections by financing Georgian Pavilions and representations at major film markets and festivals such as the American Film Market, Berlinale, Annecy Animated Film Festival, Cannes International Film Festival, Beijing Film Market, Producers Guild of America Conferences, and more.   Since 2016, Enterprise Georgia has organized training sessions for Georgian film industry members to enhance their skills and align with international standards. The latest training program, conducted in May 2023, was attended by 21 Georgian film production companies and was led by a film producer Jeanette Milio. Moreover, Enterprise Georgia invites producers and location managers, especially from MPA member companies, to explore untapped filming locations in Georgia.
Results: From 2016 to 2024 (as of May, 2024), 48 projects were registered under the "Film in Georgia" program, with qualified expenses totaling over 137 million GEL. Since 2020, the "Film in Georgia" Cash Rebate program has been officially showcased at major film markets and festivals. Around 20 production companies have participated in various markets organized by "Enterprise Georgia," including the Cannes International Film Festival, European Film Market, American Film Market, MIFA, and London Focus. The agency successfully financed and organized official market screenings of Georgian movies at the Cannes International Film Festival.   Additionally, 21 Georgian film production companies received valuable training from film producer Jeanette Milio.  The agency has conducted 6 Familiarization tours since 2016 to promote Georgia as a favorable Eastern European filming destination. From 2020 to the present, three international producers have visited Georgia, with one of them already returning to Georgia with an American movie.
Financial Ressources: Approximately 2 000 000 USD per year
Recommandations: The program is operating successfully. Georgia has emerged as one of the leaders in attracting international production, and these accomplishments are evident in the statistics. To date, we have attracted 48 global projects with 137,000,000 GEL in qualified expenses.

Title EN: Financial support and benefits for entrepreneurs in the field of culture and art on the basis of public-private partnership
Goal: Integrate Culture In Sustainable Development Frameworks

Area of Monitoring: National sustainable development policies and plans
Cultural Domain: Design,Performing Arts,Media Arts,Cinema and Audiovisual Arts,Music,Publishing,Visual Arts
Agency Implementation: Ministry of culture of the Republic of Uzbekistan
Main Feature: The state selects partners based on a competition held by the Ministry of Culture. An agreement is concluded with private entrepreneurs for a certain period and monitoring of compliance with its terms is carried out. For agreements, depending on the form of partnership, terms range from 1 year to 30 years. During the term of the agreement, the repurposing of a non-state cultural and art institution is prohibited. It should be borne in mind that the following investment obligations may be imposed on the private partner, depending on the form of partnership: ˗	provision of benefits to categories of the population in need of social protection in the provision of cultural services; ˗	timely and high-quality implementation of construction, reconstruction, major repairs and equipment of cultural and art institutions; ˗	fulfillment of other obligations provided for in the public-private partnership agreement. A procedure is being introduced for allocating subsidies from the State Budget of the Republic of Uzbekistan to non-state cultural and art institutions created on the basis of public-private partnership conditions to cover part of their expenses based on the annual income and expenses of state cultural and art institutions. An account is being opened in the Fund for Financing State Development Programs of the Republic of Uzbekistan under the Cabinet of Ministers, in which funds will be accumulated to finance the development of non-state cultural and art institutions and activities to stimulate public-private partnerships. Non-state cultural and art institutions created on the basis of public-private partnership, for which the share of net revenue from the provision of services in the field of culture and art in the total volume of sales is at least 80% based on the results of the reporting (tax) period, are exempt: ˗	for the main type of activity from paying all types of taxes and mandatory contributions to state trust funds; ˗	for a period of 3 years from the date of conclusion of the agreement on public-private partnership from customs payments (except for customs clearance fees) for technical means and other equipment imported according to lists formed in the prescribed manner for their own needs.
Results: ˗	List of empty state-owned properties has been compiled, as well as non-functioning buildings and structures of state cultural and art institutions that are subject to reconstruction and major repairs; ˗	Land plots are determined annually that can be allocated for permanent use free of charge for the construction of buildings of non-state cultural and art institutions on the terms of public-private partnership; ˗	The allocation of land plots is ensured for the organization of a non-state cultural and art institution, as well as state registration of the right to a land plot; ˗	During the construction of non-state cultural and art institutions, they are provided at the expense of local budgets with the necessary external engineering and communication infrastructure (electricity, gas supply, water supply, sewerage, roads and others) and covering project costs.
Financial Ressources: USD 2,5 mln in 2023-2024
Recommandations: There have been positive results from this measure, which promotes more efficient use of state property, creates additional jobs, expands cultural infrastructure and increases the level of provision of services to the population in the field of art and culture.
