Title EN: Flow and internationalisation through the use of the maritime container. Teatro Container.
Goal: Achieve A Balanced Flow Of Cultural Goods And Services And Increase The Mobility Of Artists And Cultural Professionals
SDG: SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 10 - Reduce inequality within and among countries,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Mobility of artists and cultural professionals
Cultural Domain: Performing Arts,Cinema and Audiovisual Arts,Publishing,Visual Arts
Agency Implementation: Teatro Container Cultural Center.
Main Feature: Since its creation in 2008, the Teatro Container Cultural Center has transformed sea containers into mobile stages for the performing arts, promoting global collaboration and flow and empowering local communities. Over the years, this project has become a theatre for creativity, innovation and promotion of connection to the disipline. The Teatro Container Cultural Center has pioneeered in the innovative use of the sea containers as performance spaces.   Each container is converted into a canvas, a gallery or a stage, challenging the traditional theatre limits. This dynamic transformation is not only an architectural work, but also a testimony to creativity that seeks to transcend physical and cultural barriers for the performing arts. The Teatro Container creations programme stands out for its focus on multi-cultural collaboration.   Through festivals and biennials, it has united artists from all corners of the world, creating a cultural flow that not only nourishes the local audience with a global perspective, but also provides a platform so that international and local artists mutually inspire each other. The Teatro container goes beyond entertainment, it is an agent of social change through educational programmes and workshops. Through these, local talent has been nurtured,  empowering young artists to explore their creativity and find their voice in the arts world.   The impact of Teatro Container extends to the streets of the Valparaíso Region through community art projects, transforming public spaces into a stage for artistic expressions. Finally, we can consider this measure within the indicator on "policies and measures that support the outward and inward mobility of dynamic cultural and creative sectors" from the monitoring framework of the 2005 Convention.
Results: Since 2008, Teatro Container has abolished geographical and cultural barriers, taking the art from Valparaíso to European stages through diverse performing arts festivals. Its mission is to create a global movement where everyone, no matter their origin or condition, can share the theatre experience, a future where each maritime container, apart from carrying goods, also carries the theatre show, uniting people through shared histories and emotions.   Artists from all corners of the world have been welcomed, forming a global community united in admiration of the performing arts. Each performance is not only a show: it is an opening act, an invitation for all to be a part of something bigger.   Teatro Container imagines a world where, for every thousand containers, one carries something more than goods: it carries the wonder of a theatrical storytelling, it carries the sense of belonging to a common experience.

Area of Monitoring: Cultural and creative sectors
Agency Implementation: FONDS DE SOUTIEN A L'INDUSTRIE CINEMATOGRAPHIQUE DE COTE D'IVOIRE  ( FONSIC) OFFICE NATIONAL DU CINEMA DE CÖTE DIVOIRE (ONAC-CI)
Main Feature: Le projet" CLAP ACP /FONSIC  "vise à renforcer l'industrie cinématographique en Côte d'Ivoire et dans les pays ACP (Afrique, Caraïbes, Pacifique). Il offre un soutien financier et technique aux cinéastes pour la production et la diffusion de films, ainsi que pour des formations professionnelles. Le projet encourage la création de contenus culturels locaux et vise à améliorer la qualité et la compétitivité des productions cinématographiques dans la région. En effet face aux nombreuses sollicitations des cinéastes et à l’insuffisance des moyens de l’État, le Gouvernement ivoirien, à travers le Ministère en charge de la Culture, a jugé utile d’explorer de nouvelles pistes en vue d’accroître les moyens de production. Suite à l’appel à candidature de l’Union Européenne dans le cadre de son programme ACP-UE Culture lancé à l’endroit des Fonds nationaux africains afin d’héberger le fonds CLAP-ACP, la Côte d’Ivoire a été retenue. Sur un ensemble de pays africains, la Côte d’Ivoire a été éligible pour le dynamisme et le mode de fonctionnement de son Fonds national d’appui au cinéma, le Fonds de Soutien à l’Industrie Cinématographique (FONSIC). Réservé aux productions des pays du groupe Afrique, Caraïbe, Pacifique (ACP), ce Fonds est alloué par le Fonds Européen de Développement et le FONSIC. Ce programme est mené par le FONSIC en partenariat avec l’Organisation Internationale de la Francophonie (OIF). Essentiellement basé sur la coproduction entre cinéastes des États ACP, il vise à financer des productions et coproductions dans les catégories Long Métrage, Série et Documentaire. Le fonds CLAP-ACP/ FONSIC est un programme qui s’étendait sur 2 ans (2020 -2021) avec à la clé le financement de 18 films. il a été reconduit pour deux autres années  2022 - 2024/  Ce projet est ouvert à tous les cinéastes des états ACP. Aussi, les producteurs ivoiriens sont-ils au centre de ce projet par la mise en place d’une coproduction obligatoire. Il s’agit entre autres de : - mettre en relation un producteur ivoirien avec son ou ses homologues des autres Etats ACP ; - utiliser des comédiens ou techniciens ivoiriens ; - tourner tout ou une partie du film en Côte d’Ivoire. le programme "CLAP ACP FONSIC" est à sa deuxième phase et  mené toujours avec la collaboration de l'OIF , le FONSIC et l'Union Européenne.  Ces fonds  sont destinés à financer des coproductions de films et séries associant la Côte d’Ivoire à des pays de l’Organisation des Etats ACP à travers une sélection annuelle effectuée par la Commission Technique de Lecture de l’Office National du Cinéma de Côte d’Ivoire (ONAC-CI).
Results: Le projet a permis de financer plusieurs productions cinématographiques locales, d'organiser des ateliers de formation pour les professionnels du cinéma, et de créer des opportunités de collaboration entre les cinéastes de la région ACP. Les productions soutenues par le CLAP- ACP/FONSIC ont été diffusées dans divers festivals internationaux, augmentant ainsi la visibilité du cinéma africain sur la scène mondiale. plus de 18 films ont été financés
Financial Ressources: le Fonds CLAP ACP/ FONSIC 2 est doté d’environ 577 243 800FCFA SOIT 943 209 USD, dont 262 382 800F CFA SOIT 428 730 USD  alloués par le FONSIC et 314 859360 FCFA soit 514 476 USD alloués par le Fonds Européen de Développement).
Recommandations: L'évaluation a indiqué que le projet CLAP FONSIC ACP a significativement contribué au développement de l'industrie cinématographique locale. Les recommandations incluent l'augmentation des fonds disponibles pour soutenir un plus grand nombre de projets, l'élargissement des programmes de formation pour inclure plus de jeunes et de femmes, et le renforcement des réseaux de distribution pour assurer une plus large diffusion des films produits.

Title EN: Formar Cultura
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture
SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Cultural and creative sectors
Cultural Domain: Design,Performing Arts,Media Arts,Cinema and Audiovisual Arts,Music,Publishing,Visual Arts
Agency Implementation: Secretariat of Culture of Argentina
Main Feature: The program arose in 2020 in the context of the preventive and mandatory social isolation decreed by the government in response to the Covid-19 pandemic.  The objective of Formar Cultura is to contribute to the strengthening and professional development of cultural managers, creators and producers throughout the country by means of resources, materials and training, research, practice and professional exchange spaces, through the web platform formar.cultura.gob.ar.  Formar Cultura has different sections, in which you can find educational and didactic material, including: media library (didactic audiovisual content), classroom (virtual campus), community (section to learn about the profiles and careers of people registered on the platform), library (online archives), career radar (search engine for academic training offers related to cultural management), events (announcements of upcoming calls and training meetings) and diploma courses.  It should be noted that the teaching material was developed and edited by the National Secretariat of Culture together with universities, publishing houses and specialized centers, among others. In this way, the program seeks to contribute to professional training and updating through the development of contents and pedagogical resources that establish a free, accessible, federal and high quality space for cultural training.  In 2023, this program included training on the link between culture and the environment, which discussed the main environmental issues and aimed to provide tools and information to build new environmentally friendly practices in cultural spaces and therefore promote sustainability. The training also discussed the potential of the cultural sector as a transmitter of respect for the environment.
Results: At the beginning of 2024, the platform has 330,308 registered users: 54,260 and platform visits: 2,362,972.  In relation to its results, since its inception Formar Cultura has achieved: 1) Promote the dissemination of a wide variety of content through MEDIATECA, a repository of more than 180 audiovisual materials. These address various theoretical and practical areas in cultural management, including interviews, courses, seminars and talks on topics such as cultural policies, communication and digital culture, community culture, audience management and project development, among others. All carried out by cultural workers reflecting cultural diversity and the federalist approach.  2) To make available to users a complete library with more than 40 titles available, covering a wide selection of reading materials related to the cultural field. These resources come from both the National Ministry of Culture and other state agencies, private and independent partners. The library serves as a central point that brings together and facilitates access to outreach materials and specialized bibliography, while strengthening connections between professionals, managers and creators from all over the country.  3) Create and promote 10 self-guided courses, an asynchronous, open-access, self managed training model that addresses a wide variety of topics.  4) Form and consolidate a Career Radar, which includes more than 45 educational offers for professional development promoted by institutions and houses of study throughout the country.  5) Conduct face-to-face training activities, generating spaces for horizontal exchange for the construction of knowledge.  6) Design and promote content related to the planning and development of cultural projects, with a focus on the following cross-cutting themes: sustainability and environment, technology and digital culture, cultural management tools and strategies, culture and consumption, globalization and localization, identity and migration, education and culture, and culture and tourism, among others.

Title EN: FORMATION CINEMATOGRAPHIQUE PERSONNALISEE
Goal: Integrate Culture In Sustainable Development Frameworks
SDG: SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: National sustainable development policies and plans
Agency Implementation: ONG Inter Palm Lumière (IPL)
Main Feature: L’ONG Inter Palm Lumière (IPL) promeut l’éducation et les droits de l’enfant via le cinéma, le théâtre et le sport. Elle offre des formations en cinéma adaptées à des individus et groupes, répondant aux aspirations des jeunes passionnés du 7ème art souvent exclus des formations classiques. Ces jeunes, malgré le manque de moyens, s’achètent des caméras bon marché ou utilisent leurs téléphones pour créer des vidéos, couvrant événements comme mariages et baptêmes, et même produisant des films de fiction. Ils improvisent souvent leurs productions, ignorant les règles techniques du montage et de la réalisation. L'ONG IPL reconnaît cette passion et propose des formations de trois à quatre mois, flexibles et adaptées aux disponibilités des participants. Les cours, théoriques et pratiques, couvrent l’écriture de scénarios, la réalisation, le cadrage, le montage vidéo et le jeu d’acteur. Les participants, travaillant en équipe, réalisent un film en fin de formation, attestant de leurs compétences acquises. Un tronc commun d’un mois initie tous les apprenants aux bases du cinéma, avant qu’ils ne se spécialisent dans des domaines spécifiques durant les trois mois restants.  Une particularité de cette formation est l’apprentissage du lexique cinématographique, crucial pour comprendre les instructions sur un plateau de tournage. La formation théorique et pratique est encadrée par un formateur dédié, permettant aux participants de concrétiser leurs apprentissages en réalisant un film de 3 à 26 minutes en fin de cycle. L'ONG IPL a déjà réalisé de nombreuses formations, dont une notable avec la Communauté Face Life Channel à Bonoua, où 120 membres ont suivi le programme de formation cinématographique personnalisée avec succès.
Results: Les résultats atteints jusqu’à présent grâce à la mise en œuvre de la FORMATION CINEMATOGRAPHIQUE PERSONNALISEE sont multiples:  -Création d’emplois et délinquance juvénile. Grâce à la formation cinématographique personnalisée, bon nombre de jeunes ont pu acquérir des compétences et éviter la rue. Ils ont intégré des équipes de tournage. Sur toute la chaine de création d’une œuvre cinématographique, ils se définissent compétents: scénaristes, réalisateurs, monteurs, cadreurs, acteurs, ils sont déterminés à faire au mieux leur travail. Aussi, cela peut s’interpréter comme, leur rêve s’est concrétisé grâce à l’ONG IPL qui a initié et inclus la FORMATION CINEMATOGRAPHIQUE PERSONNALISEE dans son programme d’activité. Ces jeunes gens participent au développement socio-culturel et économique dans leur milieu de vie. Ils produisent des œuvres de qualité. Des scénarios bien ficelés, des intrigues bien montés, des marches dramatiques dans la norme, en un mot, une narration cohérente. Sur les plateaux de tournage, ils travaillent en professionnel. Ayant combiné la théorie et la pratique,  - La FORMATION CINEMATOGRAPHIQUE PERSONNALISEE initiée par l’’ONG IPL a permis à des personnes bien âge d’être initiées à l’art cinématographique. Des personnes qui ne pouvaient plus croire à leur rencontre avec le cinéma dans sa création. Des mamans et papa ont pu comprendre que ce qu’ils voyaient sur les écrans n’étaient des mises en scènes.  Pendant l’expérience du centre d’incubation de Bonoua avec la communauté FACE LIFE CHANNEL, une personne vivant avec un  handicap a pu bénéficier de la FORMATION CINEMATOGRAPHIQUE PERSONNALISEE. elle  a reçu la formation de montage vidéo. Pour son état et  a fait la post-production. L’ONG IPL, pour ce programme de La FORMATION CINEMATOGRAPHIQUE PERSONNALISEE, a aidé bon nombre de jeunes à vivre leur rêve.

Title EN: FORMATION DES JEUNES  (HOMMES ET FEMMES ) AUX METIERS DE LA MODE  ET DE L'ARTISANAT

Main Feature: L'ONG EWOUKA a pour vision de créer une corporation forte des créateurs. L’initiative de l’ONG EWOUKA se matérialise  comme suit :  -Des acteurs de mode sont sensibilisés périodiquement sur la nécessité de se professionnaliser. Cette initiative a orienté les artisans de différents secteurs : couturiers, commerçants, ferronniers, ferrailleurs, mécaniciens, blanchisseurs, etc.) dans un processus d’identification et de création formelle de petites entreprises artisanales et culturelles, afin de sortir du cadre informel et d’accroitre leur potentiel.  -Des acteurs de mode et culturels sont constitués en groupements ou fédérations (couturiers, tisserands, acteurs culturels, etc.) en vue de constituer une base de données quantitative et qualitative, permettant aux autorités compétentes et institutionnelles de tutelle, d’avoir accès à un instrument très important et qui leur sera utile dans le cadre de l’élaboration de politiques décisionnelles sur mesure adapté aux artisans de mode et professionnels de la culture.  -Création de concours du meilleur styliste ou couturier à l’intérieur du pays pour susciter l’engouement chez les jeunes au métier de la couture.   -Collecte des fonds durant la période de COVID-19 pour soutenir les activités des membres de l’organisation et des femmes en situation de précarité avancée dans les différentes communes du district d’Abidjan. Cette mesure de courte durée menée par l’organisation en réponse à l’épidémie du COVID ayant occasionné un arrêt considérable de bon nombre d’activités en Côte d’Ivoire a permis d’appuyer quelques femmes membres de l’organisation et d’autres femmes non membres de l’organisation dans le district d’Abidjan, en leur apportant une subvention modeste dans un élan de solidarité.
Results: Les résultats atteints sont les suivants:  Des acteurs de mode professionnels ayant quitté le milieu informel : dans les différentes villes de l’intérieur ont permis à la jeunesse rurale d’apprendre un métier noble et de trouver un emploi auprès des acteurs déjà en activité et ayant besoin de main d’œuvre   -Des acteurs de mode regroupés et unis qui sont force de proposition pour le ministère et le gouvernement dans l’orientation des politiques culturelles : le processus d’identification pour le regroupement est toujours en cours au sein de chaque localité pour la prise en compte d’un maximum d’acteurs.  -Augmentation du taux d’employabilité des jeunes à la couture et contribution des actions de l’organisation à la baisse du chômage et de l’exode rural. Ces jeunes ont pour certains, réussi à obtenir de leur famille un soutien à l’installation de leur petit atelier de couture, et pour d’autres, obtenu un emploi temporaire chez des couturiers déjà en activité  -L’ONG a formé plus de 100 jeunes des villes de Bouaké, Daoukro, Ouellé , M’bahiakro , Bocanda  qui ont bénéficié de savoir-faire afin de se mettre à leur propre compte. Cette mesure a mis l’accent sur la réduction du taux de chômage en milieu rural et la lutte contre l’exode rural.

Title EN: Forum des Arts Visuels
Goal: Promote Human Rights And Fundamental Freedoms
SDG: SDG 5 - Achieve gender equality and empower all women and girls,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels
Area of Monitoring: Artistic freedom
Agency Implementation: Visarte Vaud
Main Feature: Visarte Vaud se donne pour tâches de faire progresser la reconnaissance de la profession et la sécurité sociale de ses membres, de défendre leurs droits, d’encourager la solidarité entre les professionnelles et professionnels, d’aider les membres en matière juridique, financière et sociale, de traiter des questions pertinentes et de les diffuser sur diverses plateformes. Elle est impliquée dans le développement de stratégies culturelles et leur mise en application concrète.  Le Forum des Arts Visuels (29 et 30 septembre 2023) est issu du programme « projet de transformation » proposé dans les mesures COVID-19, il a bénéficié du soutien du Canton de Vaud. Suite aux interviews d’artistes et aux focus groups réalisés en 2022 dans le cadre de l’enquête sur le statut des artistes du canton de Vaud, Visarte Vaud a décidé de créer, en 2023, un Forum des Arts Visuels pour fédérer les divers actrices et acteurs du monde des arts visuels.  Le Forum des Arts Visuels a été un espace de travail, de communication, d’information et de partage, entre toutes les parties prenantes du monde des arts visuels : les professionnelles et professionnels de l'art (artistes, curatrices et curateurs, scénographes, techniciennes et techniciens, etc.), les responsables des institutions muséales, des institutions formatrices, la recherche académique, les responsables du monde politique, le public, etc. Le but était de travailler ensemble, et de manière bienveillante, sur la porosité des différents territoires concernés.
Results: Le Forum des Arts Visuels a constitué un moment décisif pour la progression et les changements attendus concernant les différentes problématiques que l’enquête de 2022 a mis en évidence. Cet évènement a été, pour de beaucoup de travailleuses et travailleurs de l'art indépendantes et indépendants ou intermittentes et intermittents, un moment inédit de rencontres, d'échanges ainsi que d'acquisition/transmission de compétences/connaissances/réseaux. Ce moment a favorisé un sentiment de cohésion, de confiance, de sécurité́ et de pouvoir d'agir au sein d'une population habituée plutôt à des sentiments d'incertitude, de solitude et d'insécurité́. Concernant les intervenantes et intervenants qui représentaient les institutions d'exposition et de formation ainsi que les pouvoirs publics et les bailleurs de fonds, celles-ci et ceux-ci  en prenant part activement au Forum, et de par le contenu de leurs interventions  ont répondu positivement et de manière engagée à l'appel qui leur avait été fait, et qui peut être résumé par le titre du Forum : Fédération, soutien et reconnaissance au sein du monde des arts visuels contemporains. Finalement, le grand public (ou public non spécialisé) a également formulé sa reconnaissance et ses félicitations à l'issue de sa participation à la rencontre. Il semblerait que celle-ci l'ait aidé à clarifier ses représentations sur le monde des arts visuels.

Main Feature: Le Forum International des Radios Services et Télévisions (FIRST) est une initiative visant à mobiliser et réunir les consommateurs des médias et les opérateurs économiques. Cet événement, organisé par l'Association Internationale des Professionnels des Médias et de la Culture (AIPMC), met en avant le rôle crucial des médias comme vecteurs d’information, d’éducation et de divertissement. Les activités de la FIRST comprennent des conférences, des séances de formation, des émissions publiques, des animations, des concerts, un salon des médias, et des jeux. Le point culminant de l'événement est les "FIRST Awards", une cérémonie de gala avec des distinctions pour les acteurs des médias et de la communication.    Les objectifs principaux sont d'apporter une valeur ajoutée au paysage de la communication en Afrique, de promouvoir les programmes audiovisuels, de rapprocher les consommateurs des producteurs, et de professionnaliser les services de radios et télévisions. Les résultats attendus incluent la création d'un espace de diffusion et de promotion, la consolidation des relations entre radios et télévisions, et la mise en réseau des programmes audiovisuels.    Le Forum FIRST, prévu du 11 au 15 Novembre 2024 au Palais de la Culture, prévoit une participation massive avec plus de 2000 visiteurs quotidiens. L'événement est soutenu par divers partenaires institutionnels et privés, y compris des ministères et des organisations internationales.
Results: Jusqu'à présent, le Forum FIRST a réussi à créer un espace de diffusion et de promotion pour les programmes audiovisuels, offrant des opportunités d'affaires pour les entreprises de fabrication d'équipements audiovisuels.  Il a également facilité le rapprochement et la consolidation des relations entre les radios et les télévisions, promu la professionnalisation des acteurs des médias, et favorisé la découverte de nouveaux matériels techniques. Des conventions de partenariat au niveau national et international ont été signées, et une plateforme d'échanges commerciaux pour les médias a été créée.  Le public a pu découvrir les techniques de production et de réalisation des émissions radio et télé, ce qui a suscité une émulation entre auditeurs, téléspectateurs, et animateurs.  Les opérateurs économiques ont bénéficié d'offres promotionnelles pour la diffusion de leurs spots publicitaires.

Title EN: Fostering television content producion. CNTV Fund.
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture
SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Media diversity
Agency Implementation: National Television Council (CNTV).
Main Feature: The CNTV Fund is a public contest through which the Chilean National Television Council assigns resources for total or partial funding of television series productions for free-to-air transmission, which are of high quality and therefore a contribution to diverse audiences.   The mangamente of the CNTV Fund is regulated by the contest conditions, whose amount is designated annually through the Budget Law. It is an annual contest and independent producers and television operators can apply with different projects, which enables fostering of pluralist audiovisual creation, and promoting diversity of cultural expressions with this public policy.   Currently, there are eight contest categories in which projects can be presented, which receive specific topics and audiences. The categories are: fiction, non-fiction, historical, regional, local or local community series, child audiences between 3 and 6 years of age, child audiences between 7 and 12 years of age, and new seasons. According to the average in recent years, between 18 and 22 projects benefit annually.   Once awarded, the projects have two years in order to be broadcast on free-to-air television, which can be on national, regional, local or local community channels. This public policy is enforced since 1993, and during this period has contributed to total or partial funding of more than 450 television series and television films.
Results: Since its beginnings, the CNTV Fund has awarded around 400 productions, from different television genres, stimulating the funding of productions that tend towards diversity in television content â"especially of an artistic and cultural type- and that reflect the pluralist nature of society.   This measure stands out for the the impact on the audiences of various highly-acclaimed productions in Chile, such as the series "Los 80", "31 Minutes" or "El Reemplazante", and its international recognition, with two Emmy awards ("The Suspended Mourning" and "What is your Dream?") and the Oscar nomination in the "best documentary" category in 2021 for "The Mole Agent".   To put into perspective the implications of the CNTV Fund programming, within the entire schedule of free-to-air television channels in Chile, 2021 should be taken as an example when it represented less than 1% of the general programming, which is in the order of 182 hour total for the year. Even though the figure regarding the programming total is marginal, it is within the range for the type of offering since the last decade (always below 1%).   However, if the presence of the CNTV Fund programming is narrowed down to the time slots and is compared to the remaining offering, the profile of a different kind of television proposition emerges, high-quality in terms of craft and production values, and also in terms of the format and mainly socio-historical and cultral content. In turn, the constant presence of CNTV in the last decade on free-to-air television should be noted. Between 2019 and 2020, the CNTV Fund hours of programming increased by 76%, mainly a product of the daily transmission of all of the seasons of the "Los 80" series on Chile's Canal 13.
Recommandations: The last evaluation of the CNTV Fund, undertaken in 2019, identified diverse results and considerations. The following highlights some of them. A suggestion was made to establish the current position of television, in terms of cultural and public dissemination in comparison to other emerging platforms; a recommendation was made to co-ordinate with the audiovisual industry in order to create unified platforms, specifically in collaboration with MINCAP, with the aim of optimising the distribution of audiovisual works.   In terms of financial areas, the recommendation was to conduct research around the coststructure in the audiovisual industry, focusing on the production of television series, in order to establish an adecuate model in terms of the realtionship between cost and quality and to update the cost models.   Lastly, regarding public policies, establishing institutional strategies and innovating business models in collaboration with other actors from the industry was proposed, in order to face current challenges, such as the television crisis and the proliferation of new platforms, within the scope of the Council of Audiovisual and Art.

Title EN: Framework for collaboration between civil society and public sector in the cultural field
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture
SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Partnering with civil society
Agency Implementation: Ideell kulturallians
Main Feature: Ideell kulturallians is an umbrella organisation for civil society’s national organisations in the field of culture. In collaboration with our 21 member organisations, we work to coordinate common issues, support members, pursue debate, spread knowledge and influence the public sector and society at large. All to improve our conditions and strengthen Sweden’s cultural life with a diversity of cultural expressions.  Ideell kulturallians operates in three strategic areas •	Knowledge and analysis •	Policy and advocacy •	Networking and co-operation  Representatives of the member organizations meet regularly to provide their perspectives on current cultural policies issues. Anchored in the member organizations, Ideell kulturallians has built up an expertise in the conditions, challenges and possibilities of the civil society’s cultural sector.  Cultural Cooperation Model Kultursamverkansmodellen (The Cultural Cooperation model) was introduced in 2012 and means that regions allocate state grants to the cultural sector within their region. As part of the process, the regions, in cooperation with the region's municipalities, develop new regional cultural plans every three or four years. In the process of creating new cultural plans, the regions are also required by the regulation on cultural cooperation to consult with representatives of professional cultural creators and civil society organizations. This means that Ideell kulturallians is invitet to contribute to the regional cultural policy work in the regions where it is time to develop a new cultural plan each year. Ideell kulturallians does this through contacts with local and regional civil society organizations in the regions, by participating in the region's consultation meetings, and by submitting a written statement on the draft version of the cultural plan.  Government Investigations Ideell kulturallians has contributed its knowledge and analysis as experts in two government investigations during the period. The executive director of Ideell kulturallians, participated in Återstartsutredningen (The Restart Investigation) in 2021, which examined the effects of the pandemic and proposed measures for the restart of cultural life after the pandemic. The executive director of Ideell kulturallians then participated as an expert in Kultursamverkansutredningen (The Cultural Cooperation Model Investigation) in 2023.  Ideell kulturallians has also submitted statements on several government investigations in the cultural sector, including Återstartsutredningen and Kultursamverkansutredningen.  Education for Politicians and Public Officials It is essential that politicians and public officials have knowledge of the extensive and multifaceted non-profit cultural sector. Therefore, Ideell kulturallians has developed a training program for politicians and public officials at the municipal and regional levels, which provides basic knowledge of the non-profit cultural sector. The training includes lectures and workshops lasting two to three hours and can be conducted both digitally and physically.  Advocacy and Debate Ideell kulturallians also uses its expertise in civil society and culture through ongoing work in advocacy and influence. This is done through opinion pieces, statements in our own media (website, newsletter, social media), and panel discussions. The need to express our perspective on cultural policy has increased as civil society's cultural organisations are facing severe challenges. The pandemic hit the local community life hard. The activities are fragile as they rely largely on voluntary engagement, and the pandemic shattered both the economic conditions and broke down relationships and people's habits. It takes time to rebuild structures to bring back organizers, practitioners, and audiences.  After the pandemic, the difficult economic situation with high inflation has worsened the situation further.  Sweden has long had a positive attitude towards civil society from the public sector. Civil society policy was established in 2009 in a proposition adopted by the Swedish Parliament. It outlines six fundamental principles guiding the relationship between the public sector and civil society. These are Independence and Autonomy, Dialogue, Quality, Long-term Perspective, Transparency and Insight, and Diversity. However, in recent years, Ideell kulturallians has noted a tendency to move away from these principles towards greater control and stricter governance, as well as a drastic cut in financial allocations to civil society organizations.  The concern for the future is therefore very great. In the autumn of 2023, the government presented a very tight budget that will have far-reaching consequences for cultural diversity. The allocation to national organizations of ethnic associations, including one of Ideell kulturallians member organizations, was completely withdrawn. The grants to the educational associations (studieförbunden) are to be cut by a third over a three-year period. This will hit hard as the educational associations themselves organize thousands of cultural programs every year and are also an important partner for local cultural associations. Additionally, the allocation to national civil society organisations has been reduced. The impact of the reduction in allocation is intensified by inflation.
Results: By continuously incorporating the perspectives of civil society in the process of developing new regional cultural plans, the cultural plans of today highlight a broader spectrum of culture. It has made visible that the civil society contributes to a cultural ecosystem where professional cultural creators, the public sector, and civil society play various important roles. We know that civil society commissions professional cultural creators and provides them with opportunities to meet their audience through concerts, theatre performances, exhibitions, author talks, and more. The diverse local cultural activities are enriching the regional cultural plans. Furthermore, civil society organizations contribute to children and young people participating in cultural life, which is crucial both for future cultural practitioners and for future audiences.  The responses that Ideell kulturallians has submitted to government investigations ensure that our perspectives are considered in ongoing processes.  The training program has been successfully conducted in eight regions during a pilot phase and will continue to be offered within our operations.  The seriousness with which our opinion pieces on the development of cultural policy are taken is also evident in the interest they generate and, for example, in the high participation in our programs at the cultural policy event “Folk och Kultur”.

Title EN: Further increasing the role and significance of the sphere of culture and art in the life of society
Goal: Integrate Culture In Sustainable Development Frameworks

Agency Implementation: Ministry of Culture of the Republic of Uzbekistan
Main Feature: In recent years, the Republic of Uzbekistan has implemented systemic measures aimed at further developing national culture, creating a new history of new Uzbekistan, preserving and promoting the pearls of tangible and intangible cultural heritage, further popularizing oral folk art and amateur art, ensuring the active integration of our country into the world cultural space, as well as innovative development of the sphere of culture and art. At the same time, there was no comprehensive system for implementing the Concept, introducing modern information and communication technologies into this area, training highly qualified personnel, searching for and supporting talented young creative figures, providing educational institutions with music textbooks, collections of notes, and educational literature. Increasing the level of provision of cultural recreation services to the population, especially citizens living in remote areas of the republic, and establishing for this purpose on an ongoing basis the activities of theaters, museums, traveling circuses and zoos in all regions of the republic remains an urgent task. In order to effectively implement the above tasks, accelerate the continuation of reforms in the field of culture and art, further improve the activities of cultural bodies and institutions, as well as ensure the implementation of the Action Strategy for five priority areas of development of the Republic of Uzbekistan, a Program of additional measures for the further development of the sphere of culture and art in the Republic of Uzbekistan in 2020 – 2021, Target indicators for the implementation of the Concept for the further development of national culture in the Republic of Uzbekistan in 2021 – 2025.
Results: ˗	Licensing of concert and entertainment activities has been introduced, maintaining the state register of licensees, entering information about their activities and achievements is carried out through the Unified online portal of participants in concert and entertainment activities; ˗	Fees collected for issuing a one-time permit to hold a concert and entertainment event have been cancelled; ˗	Mass cultural, concert and entertainment events organized at the initiative of government bodies and organizations are held on the basis of annually approved calendar plans for mass cultural, concert and entertainment events. Documents providing for the holding of government events not provided for in calendar plans indicate customers and sources of financing for services for organizing these events. All services provided by persons carrying out concert and entertainment activities commissioned by state bodies and other organizations are provided on the basis of written and paid contracts, with the exception of obligations arising from employment contracts concluded with employees of state institutions carrying out concert and entertainment activities. It is not allowed to attract creative figures and performers to state and other events on a voluntary basis; ˗	A procedure has been introduced for providing a 50 percent discount on rent for concert programs held in concert organizations, palaces of culture, and other institutions of the system of government bodies and organizations on the basis of full live performance; ˗	The Chamber for the protection of copyrights of artists, creative figures and performers has been created; ˗	Staging and performance of dramatic, musical and musical-dramatic works acquired by the Ministry of Culture and intended for public performance also in private theaters are permitted. At the same time, payment of royalties for production and performance in private theaters is made within the framework of funds allocated annually from the state budget of the Republic of Uzbekistan. ˗	The creation and constant operation of traveling circuses (shapito-circuses, groups of tightrope walkers) and zoos in each region have been ensured. It has been established that it is not necessary to obtain permission to hold a mass event and other permitting documents for entertainment events held by traveling circuses (shapito-circuses, groups of tightrope walkers), while the organizers of the event notify the internal affairs authorities in writing at least 10 days in advance about the location and the time of their implementation. The internal affairs bodies, the National Guard and the Ministry of Emergency Situations ensure public order and fire safety at entertainment events held by traveling circuses (shapito-circuses, groups of tightrope walkers) without charging a fee. For events held by traveling circuses (shapito-circuses, groups of tightrope walkers) in cultural and recreational parks and sports facilities of the system of government bodies and organizations, as well as in squares and other open spaces, rent and other types of payments are not charged; ˗	Activities for the preservation and use of objects of intangible cultural heritage (dorboz, askia and lapar) are included in the List of types of activities (services, works) for which temporary labor certificates are issued to self-employed citizens (with the exception of persons operating in the structure of cultural centers), on their income received from this activity is not subject to income tax levied on individuals; ˗	National Institute of Musical Art named after Yunus Rajabi has been established on the basis of the “Uzbek art of maqom” faculty of the State Conservatory of Uzbekistan and the corresponding areas of education and specialties of the Uzbek State Institute of Arts and Culture, a basic higher educational institution for training personnel in the areas of “the art of performing maqom”, “the art of bakhshi” and “katta ashula”;  ˗	Republican specialized music academic lyceums named after V.Uspensky and R.Glier were transformed into republican specialized music schools named after V.Uspensky and R.Glier, respectively, with the benefits established for boarding schools extended to them; ˗	In state museums, the first Sunday of every month is declared an “open day” and citizens are allowed free access to state museums to see museum objects and museum collections; ˗	Measures have been taken to create local history museums in each district and city in the form of branches of state museums of history and culture with their inclusion in the list of museums, branches and departments of museums financed by the State budget of the Republic of Uzbekistan; ˗	The basic salaries of museum workers with an academic degree have been increased. ˗	Ensured that the positive experience of creating “clubs of friends” of advanced creative organizations will be extended to the museum sphere; ˗	April 15 was declared the Day of Workers of Culture and Art.

Results: The recent G20 Culture Ministers Meeting Outcome reaffirmed the role of culture as an enabler and driver for sustainable development, contributing directly and indirectly to the implementation of the Sustainable Development Goals. The meeting encouraged the integration of culture as a specific goal in its own right in the development agenda. The meeting reiterating concerns about the growing, multifaceted impact of climate change on the conservation and safeguarding of cultural and natural heritage. It also reaffirmed the strong conviction that culture, across its different components – including intangible and tangible cultural heritage, creativity, local communities as well as Indigenous Peoples languages and knowledge systems – offers great potential to contribute meaningfully to climate change mitigation and adaptation.

Title EN: Ibero-American Cooperation Programs
Goal: Achieve A Balanced Flow Of Cultural Goods And Services And Increase The Mobility Of Artists And Cultural Professionals

Area of Monitoring: Flow of cultural goods and services
Agency Implementation: DGArtes - Directorate General for the Arts
Main Feature: The DGARTES participates in the following Ibero-American Cooperation programs:  IBERCENA (since 2019) - It is an Ibero-American Cooperation Program for the Performing Arts, involving 17 countries that pay an annual fee to create an economic fund available to performing arts professionals residing in the member countries of the program. Portugal's membership in this program involves the payment of an annual fee and the presence of a representative at the Intergovernmental Council meetings, which is currently ensured by the Director-General of the Arts.  IBERMUSICAS (since 2020) - It is an Ibero-American Cooperation Program aimed at promoting the presence and knowledge of Ibero-American musical diversity, stimulating the formation of new audiences in the region, and expanding the job market for professionals in the sector. It consists of 15 countries that pay an annual fee to create an economic fund available to professionals residing in the member countries of the program.  IBERORQUESTAS JUVENIS (since 2023) - It is a technical and financial cooperation program that aims to encourage and support the implementation of musical practice among children, adolescents, and young people, contributing to the realization of cross-cutting initiatives in the Ibero-American Cultural Space countries. It is composed of 15 member countries. Portugal joined this program in 2023.  Ibero-American Dance Platform (PID) (informal) (since 2023) - In February 2023, Portugal joined the Ibero-American Dance Platform, an integration and coordination body of public institutions with the mission of managing alliances and projects for regional inclusion and network work in the field of Dance. The formal recognition of membership in PID took place in 2018, during the XIX Ibero-American Conference of Ministers of Culture in Antigua, Guatemala, where its work in enriching and valuing Dance was acknowledged, urging SEGIB to enhance its work through the IBERCENA Program.
Results: IBERCENA has made substantial strides in promoting cultural exchange and collaboration. Since 2019, Portugal has committed €375,000 annually to support IBERCENA, facilitating 68 artistic projects over four years. This funding has enabled Portuguese artists and cultural professionals to collaborate with counterparts from 12 Ibero-American countries, as well as nations across Europe, Asia, and Africa. The program has facilitated 30 international co-productions and 40 artistic residencies, fostering mutual understanding and enhancing cultural dialogue on a global scale.  IBERMÚSICAS has significantly contributed to the promotion of Ibero-American music diversity. From 2021 to 2023, Portugal allocated €252,000 to IBERMÚSICAS, supporting a wide range of projects including concert tours, programming, residencies, and professional training. Portuguese artists reached over 50,000 attendees through 30 concerts and cultural events across Ibero-America during this period. Over 150 scholarships were awarded to musicians and music professionals, enhancing their skills and fostering long-term collaborations between Portugal and other member countries.  IBERORQUESTRAS JUVENIS marks a promising initiative for Portugal, with participation scheduled to commence in 2024. The program aims to allocate €80,000 annually to engage 500 young musicians annually in Portugal. It seeks to promote social inclusion and cultural diversity through music education, fostering partnerships with youth orchestras across Ibero-America. By exchanging best practices and promoting intercultural dialogue, IBERORQUESTRAS JUVENIS aims to empower young musicians and cultivate a vibrant orchestral music community in Portugal and beyond.  These programs illustrate Portugal's commitment to enhancing cultural cooperation and promoting artistic excellence across Ibero-America. Through IBERCENA, IBERMÚSICAS, and IBERORQUESTRAS JUVENIS, Portugal continues to foster meaningful cultural exchanges, strengthen international partnerships, and enrich the cultural landscape both domestically and internationally.  Besides the specific Ibero-American cooperation programs such as IBERCENA, IBERMÚSICAS, and IBERORQUESTRAS JUVENIS, Portugal is preparing an innovative measure to strengthen cultural ties within the Community of Portuguese-Speaking Countries (CPLP). This new initiative, named "Journeys through Language," aims to promote linguistic and cultural diversity through educational and cultural projects that highlight Portuguese language as a unifying element.

Main Feature: Pour tenir compte des dernières évolutions du marché avec la montée en puissance des éditeurs de services de média audiovisuels en ligne, dont les plus gros acteurs sont principalement établis à l’étranger, l’écosystème audiovisuel français a connu un certain nombre d’adaptations de son cadre législatif et règlementaire.  L’adoption du décret 22 juin 2021 relatif aux « services de médias audiovisuels à la demande » (SMAD) en application de la directive européenne sur les services de médias audiovisuels a permis d’étendre le champ des obligations d’investissement directes à la production cinématographique et audiovisuelle, jusqu’alors seulement imposées aux services de médias audiovisuels français, à ceux établis à l’étranger mais dont l’offre de services vise le territoire français.  La loi de finances rectificative pour 2013 a également étendu le champ des obligations d’investissement indirects à ces mêmes services qui doivent contribuer à la taxe sur la vidéo physique et en ligne assise sur leur chiffre d’affaires (à un taux de 5,5%).  Ces acteurs sont également soumis à la chronologie des médias.  Dans le contexte de l’intégration de ces services dans le champ des obligations précitées, le cadre juridique a également évolué afin qu’ils puissent bénéficier de plusieurs dispositifs nationaux, les œuvres audiovisuelles qu’ils financent bénéficiant désormais des aides en faveur de la production du CNC.

IAC´s representative council is appointed by IAC founding organisations. Each party nominates one representative in the council, except The Association of Icelandic Visual Artists, which nominates five representatives. The Center facilitates professional partnerships, visitor programs and international artist collaborations. The Center serves as an information hub for curators, press, artists and art institutions. These are primarily intended to ease the mobility of artists and may cover costs of traveling, accommodation and other general travel related expenses. In order to receive a Travel Grant allocation an artist must have a confirmed offer to exhibit their artwork at an art institution, gallery, publisher or similar for the same year that the Grant covers. Travel grants are allocated three times a year. The Artists House Bethanien has signed an agreement with the Icelandic Art Center regarding residencies for Icelandic artists in Berlin. This provides artists with a private studio and access to workshops and libraries, with the option of living in the studio.

Main Feature: The policy provides a productive incentive to all the cultural sectors that make up the MICA. The budget granted is earmarked for the circulation and marketing of goods and services of Argentine cultural industries, both in the domestic and foreign markets, and for participation in fairs, festivals and other markets. On the other hand, MICA Incuba, an incubation program aimed at promoting SMEs and MSMEs in the cultural industries, handicrafts and the management of cultural spaces through follow-up, advice, training and support, was developed. Among the incubation lines are: Entrepreneurial development - aimed at one-person or collective projects, with or without formalization that seek to design and implement a business plan, design and/or improve their communication and marketing strategy; SME development - aimed at micro, small or medium-sized companies and with the objective of consolidating a business model, develop new business units, improve their digital marketing strategy and/or diversify markets; and Internationalization - aimed at SMEs with export potential or that export on an eventual basis, which seeks to start/consolidate the export of goods and services, follow up on post MICA 2022 opportunities. MICA INCUBA's training activities were designed and implemented in conjunction with institutional partners such as the Empretec Foundation and the Argentine Investment Agency. They were aimed at providing participants with content related to various key topics for business development. In addition to the training sessions, individual counseling and mentoring were provided.  During the year 2021, the launching ceremony of the MICA Digital Platform was held, which was developed by the then Ministry of Culture of the Nation, together with Empresa Argentina de Soluciones Satelitales (ARSAT S.A.). The platform is an innovative tool that allows continuous training and the generation of links between the different actors of the Cultural Industries both nationally and internationally, maintaining a business relationship that culminates in a business round for the internationalization of new cultural goods and services. The platform functions as a virtual window of international scope in which Argentine cultural products and services are exhibited, thus allowing MICA to be taken to the world. The quality and artistic diversity of our cultural actors have turned us into an export market, ready to conquer new markets.  The MICA website promotes the participation of professionals and companies associated with the following sectors: Video Games, Visual Arts, Publishing, Design, Audiovisual, Circus, Theater, Dance, Tango, Folklore, Hip-Hop, Children, Music, Academic Music, Crafts and Gastronomy. At the beginning of 2024, the platform has 23,300 registered users and 6,600 published portfolios. It also has a catalog of 7,000 exhibited cultural products and services.  It should be noted that MICA has held 8 editions: 2011, 2013, 2015, 2017, 2019, 2019, 2021, 2022 and 2023.  Cultural industries have an enormous participation in provincial economies. For this reason, the MICA Nodes have been implemented with the purpose of revaluing, reactivating and strengthening regional cultural economies for their subsequent internationalization. Between the months of November and December 2021, sectoral meetings, talks, workshops and rounds of linkages were held in conjunction with provincial and municipal governments. The main themes of these activities were: Financial Inclusion, Digital Inclusion and tools for the internationalization of cultural products and services.

Area of Monitoring: Cultural and creative sectors
Agency Implementation: Slovenian Film Center
Main Feature: The Republic of Slovenia encourages investments in Slovenian audiovisual production by foreign production companies cooperating with Slovenian producers. These incentives take the form of financial reimbursement of up to 25% of the justified costs of culturally qualified investments in audiovisual production on the territory of Slovenia. Eligible production formats include feature films, documentaries, TV dramas and animation. However, the incentive does not apply to commercials, reality TV, game shows or soap operas.  The incentives are specifically designed for foreign producers (or executive producers) from the EU, the EEA, partner countries of the EU or third countries. To be eligible, their projects must meet certain economic and cultural requirements. In addition, part of the production, post-production and related services must take place in Slovenia. The criteria also take into account the Slovenian cultural significance of the film, the use of production and post-production capacities in Slovenia and the cooperation with Slovenian film and audiovisual professionals. As this measure has a significant impact on the development of the industry, it also promotes Slovenia's natural and cultural heritage.
Results: Spending on foreign productions on the territory of the Republic of Slovenia is increasing, which proves that Slovenia is becoming an attractive film location for foreign production companies. In addition, the share of Slovenian cultural content (e.g. themes or content derived from Slovenian or European culture, history, mythology or religion; projects based on people who are part of Slovenian or European culture, history, mythology or religion; visual representations in films or audiovisual works that show or promote the Republic of Slovenia) is also increasing. The rate of 56% in 2020 has increased to 81% in 2022. The financial reimbursement measure also has a direct economic impact on the local economy (hospitality, accommodation, transportation) and on Slovenian tourism, as it promotes the locations where the film was shot.

Title EN: Inclusion in the National Development Plan of goals, policies, programs and projects for the development of the cultural sector.
Goal: Integrate Culture In Sustainable Development Frameworks
SDG: SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: National sustainable development policies and plans
Agency Implementation: Ministerio de Cultura y Patrimonio
Main Feature: Article 280 of the Constitution of the Republic of Ecuador states that "The National Development Plan is the instrument to which public policies, programs and projects shall be subject; the programming and execution of the State budget; and the investment and allocation of public resources; and to coordinate the exclusive competencies between the central State and the decentralized autonomous governments. Its observance shall be mandatory for the public sector and indicative for the other sectors". It was for this reason that from the National Development Plan 2009-2013, aspects related to cultural diversities were included. Objective 7 of that Plan (Build and strengthen public, intercultural and common meeting spaces), established in policy 7.4 (Democratize the supply and diverse cultural expressions, ensuring free circulation, recognition and respect for multiple social identities), as Goal 7.4.1, "Increase by 40% the weekly time devoted to culture until 2013." In the following National Development Plan 2013-2017, objective 5 (Build common meeting spaces and strengthen national identity, diverse identities, plurinationality and interculturality) established two policies: 5.3. Encourage the processes of cultural creation in all its forms, languages and expressions, both by individuals and diverse collectivities; 5.4. Promote cultural and creative industries and enterprises, as well as their contribution to the transformation of the productive matrix. The goals focused on increasing audiovisual production (5.4), its circulation in national theaters (5.5), and reversing citizen participation in cultural activities, which, according to the diagnosis, had decreased (5.2). The National Development Plan 2017-2021, within Objective 2 (Affirm interculturality and plurinationality, revaluing diverse identities), establishes the following two goals for the cultural field: Goal 2.3: Increase the percentage of people aged 15 and over who carry out cultural activities from 3.9% to 5% by 2021; Goal 2.4: Increase the contribution of cultural activities to the gross domestic product from 2.4% to 3.5% by 2021; Goal 2.5: Increase the contribution of cultural activities to the gross domestic product from 2.4% to 3.5% by 2021. The National Development Plan 2021-2025, Objective 2 (Increase the creation, production and circulation of artistic and cultural goods and services), establishes two specific intervention indicators for the PEI: Percentage of people employed monthly in artistic and cultural activities; and, Percentage contribution of cultural activities to the Gross Domestic Product GDP. The National Development Plan 2024-2025, within the Social Axis, Objective 2, policy 2. 7 (Promote artistic creation and cultural industries), establishes two goals: Increase the number of artistic and cultural works, projects and productions with presence in international spaces financed with non-refundable funds from the international mobility call from 109 in 2023 to 132 in 2025; and, Increase the amount of private investment destined to the artistic and cultural and heritage sector, through cultural tax incentives from 3.6 million in 2023 to 4 million in 2025.  Seen in this perspective, the Development Plans have outlined cultural policies that have gone beyond guaranteeing access to cultural rights and their symbolic-productive components, with the purpose of emphasizing economic-productive aspects of the cultural area, related to the increase in employment and the contribution to the GDP.
Results: In terms of employment, the indicator has evolved as follows:  This indicator is calculated with the Directory of Companies and Establishments DIIE of the National Institute of Statistics and Census - INEC. Methodologically, the justification of the goal to be achieved is identified by quantifying those persons with social security in artistic and cultural activities (ISIC 4) registered by the companies and establishments in the directory.  In order to define the ISICs dedicated to cultural activities, the methodology for the construction of the Ecuadorian Culture Satellite Account was taken into account, which is subject to the general definitions of the Andrés Bello Agreement.  Once the persons employed in these cultural activities have been identified, the numerator of the indicator is constructed: the sum of persons employed monthly in activities defined as cultural (ISIC 4).  The denominator corresponds to the sum of persons employed monthly.  The bases of the Directory of Companies and Establishments have a lag of one year, i.e. in October 2023 the data for 2022 was published, therefore, for the base year of the indicator a projection has been taken.  Given the delay in the reporting of information maintained by INEC, for the calculation of the year 2019, the information is calculated with the data published in 2020. In this sense, the calculation of 2020 (base year of the indicator) corresponds to an estimate, which could vary the data series in terms of the goals established for the following fiscal years. In keeping a base year as a projection, given the context of the pandemic, 2020 is considered an atypical year, i.e., it must be taken into account that the economy first establishes a recovery stage, which could vary the projections that have been estimated. In addition, methodological improvements could be included in the measurement, which is why the data series reported by the Ministry of Culture and Heritage could vary.  The following is the projection table for reaching the goal of the indicator that is the subject of this report, as follows:   2020 (base year): The indicator target for this year is 5.19%. 2021: The indicator target is increased to 5.34%. 2022: The indicator target increases to 5.50%. 2023: Indicator target increases to 5.66%. 2024: Indicator target increases to 5.83%. 2025: The indicator target reaches 6.00%.  In summary, there is a gradual increase in the indicator target each year, from 5.19% in 2020 to 6.00% in 2025. Defined the Indicator that measures the percentage of people employed monthly in artistic and cultural activities over the total number of people with monthly employment registered in the Directory of Companies and Establishment, whose ISIC corresponds to the digit 4.  In such sense, the methodological structure that technically supports the definition of the indicator to be considered within the National Development Plan 2021-2025, is formalized through official letter No. MCYP-MCYP-2021-0608-O, establishing the following chronological or historical series:  2021: Registered employment in the cultural sector: 146,449 National registered employment: 2,785,596 Percentage: 5.31%.  2022: Registered employment in the cultural sector: 152,202 National registered employment: 2,875,195 Percentage: 5.29 Trend Analysis:  Decline in percentage of cultural employment: From 2013 to 2022, there is a general downward trend in the percentage that cultural employment represents of total national employment, from 7.31% in 2013 to 5.29% in 2022. Decrease in absolute numbers of cultural employment: A decrease in absolute numbers of registered employment in the cultural sector is also seen, with a peak of 213,222 in 2014 and a low of 146,449 in 2021. Variability in national employment: national registered employment shows variability, with a peak of 3,012,114 in 2015 and fluctuations in subsequent years. This analysis suggests a reduction in both relative and absolute terms of employment in the cultural sector over the period, which could be related to economic factors, changes in cultural policies, or variations in the demand for cultural activities.  From the aforementioned, the base of the goal, as mentioned, is the year 2022 with 5.29%, which should reach the goal of 6.00% by 2025, according to the detail of "increasing the percentage of people employed monthly in artistic and cultural activities". As for the percentage contribution to GDP, the indicator has evolved as follows: The Central Bank of Ecuador established in 2007 the last methodological update of measurement, so evidently all data reported by the governing body of Culture and Heritage will have significant variations.  In addition, the ECB publishes definitive figures with a two-year lag and semi-definitive figures with a one-year lag, on the production of the cultural sectors (numerator) contained in the Supply-Utilization Tables. The same applies to the value of total GDP (denominator).  In other words, in 2021, the Ministry of Culture will report the definitive data for 2018 and semi-definitive data for 2019, and so on for the following years.   In this sense, this report contains the data provided by the Information Directorate of the National Culture System that correspond to the year 2020, due to the projection methodology, since this body does not analyze all the sources, such as those that correspond to the Sectorial Council to which the governing body of culture belongs.   However, the record contained in the SIIC's Strategic Indicators Matrix maintains information that is subject to the Government's term and coincides with the National Development Plan, hence the percentage of compliance with Goal 2.4.1. 1 Increase from 1.49% to 1.80% the contribution of cultural activities in the Gross Domestic Product, which corresponds to objective 2.4 of the National Development Plan "Creating Opportunities 2021-2025".   Year-by-year data are detailed below: Targets: 2021: 1,55% 2022: 1,61% 2023: 1,67% 2024: 1,73% 2025: 1,80% Results* (Two-year lag): 2021: 1,49% 2022: 0,00% 2023: 0,00% 2024: 0,00% 2025: 0,00%  This means that the result of the 2021 target will have to be analyzed through the fulfillment of the actions that determine the achievement of this result during fiscal year 2023.  For now, the administrative record shows the result projected by the analysis formulated by the DISNC for the 2020 target, due to the two years of delay in the ECB information; thus  Administrative record of the SIIC year 2020 From the two preceding tables it can be evidenced that the actual percentage of official source of the BCE until fiscal year 2020 in relation to the methodological projection formulated by the team of the Information Directorate of the National System of Culture, housed in the Integral System of Cultural Information, the goal has decreased: with actual data from 2017 from 1.9% to 1.7%; and with projection to 2021 reaching 1.5%.  From that year onwards it increases again until reaching 1.80% by 2025.   2017 a 2018: The value of the indicator remains constant at 1.9%. This indicates stability in the indicator during this period. 2018 a 2019: The indicator value decreases from 1.9% to 1.8%. This represents a decrease of 0.1%, suggesting a worsening in the metric measured by the indicator. 2019 a 2020: The indicator value continues to decrease from 1.8% to 1.7%. This represents another 0.1% reduction, continuing the negative trend.
Recommandations: In relation to the data provided by the Central Bank of Ecuador, regarding the measurement of results of the goals referred to the indicator of contribution of cultural activities to the Gross Domestic Product, it publishes definitive figures with a two-year delay and semi-definitive figures with a one-year delay. -Regarding the employment indicator, a high percentage of workers in the cultural sector do not have employment contracts; the sector's income is established through the sale of goods or access to services through civil contracts. -The Ministry of Culture and Heritage is active for the Subsystem of Arts and Innovation, allocations from the Fund for the Promotion of Arts and Cultural Incentives, so that the cultural sector can execute its artistic and cultural proposals and, through these activities, promote the labor management of the sector. -We worked on the internationalization of the artistic sector with actions such as: participation in international fairs, placement of products in international spaces, promoting the international mobility of the sector. -Cultural incentives were promoted to encourage private enterprise to invest in the cultural sector, promoting job opportunities for arts workers. -The cultural incentives were implemented to promote the work of the cultural sector in the national territory, providing financing for the sustainability of the activities of collectives, organizations and groups.

Main Feature: Around 30% of residents of the city of Innsbruck (capital city of the Federal State of Tyrol) are non-Austrian citizens, thus making the city a place of living for people of different backgrounds. However, the diversity of the city’s population is not (sufficiently) reflected in the cultural activities, projects and initiatives of Innsbruck. A substantial part of the population seems to be invisible in the city’s cultural life. Also, the city’s cultural funding statistics show that most public funds are allocated to actors and initiatives representing the majority population. Cultural funding for marginalized groups of society tends to be an exception.  Against this backdrop, TKI Tiroler Kulturinitiativen und die Initiative Minderheiten Tirol have started the project “Inclusive Cultural Funding for Innsbruck” that aims at identifying structural exclusion mechanisms in cultural funding and developing solutions for a more inclusive and diverse allocation of fundings.
