Title EN: INITIATION A L' ART DE LA MARIONETTE
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture
SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Cultural and creative sectors
Agency Implementation: Académie Ivoire Marionnette
Main Feature: L'Académie Ivoire Marionnette, située en Côte d'Ivoire, offre une formation exceptionnelle dans l'art de la marionnette, attirant ainsi des jeunes talents de tout le pays et même au-delà. Ce programme de formation n'est pas seulement un cours de manipulation de marionnettes ; il s'agit d'une immersion profonde dans un monde où l'art rencontre la tradition, l'innovation et l'expression personnelle. Avec une approche holistique et interdisciplinaire, l'académie prépare les étudiants à devenir des marionnettistes accomplis, capables de captiver les publics avec leurs créations animées et narratives. En ce qui concerne l'approche interdisciplinaire et intégrative, il faut noter qu'au cœur de la formation à l'Académie Ivoire Marionnette se trouve l'approche interdisciplinaire, qui sert de fondation à l'apprentissage. Les étudiants explorent une variété de disciplines artistiques qui enrichissent leur pratique marionnettique.  Le théâtre, élément central, aide à comprendre la narration et le jeu d'acteur, essentiels pour donner vie à des personnages inanimés.  La danse apporte une compréhension du mouvement et de la chorégraphie, crucial pour la fluidité des manipulations.  La musique, intégrée dans le curriculum, offre aux étudiants les outils pour composer ou choisir les accompagnements sonores qui renforcent l'impact émotionnel de leurs spectacles.  Les arts plastiques, quant à eux, sont fondamentaux pour la conception et la création des marionnettes elles-mêmes, permettant aux étudiants de réaliser des créations uniques qui reflètent leur identité artistique.  En matière de développement de compétences spécifiques, l'académie met un point d'honneur à enseigner des compétences spécifiques à la marionnette, telles que la manipulation, la fabrication et la mise en scène. Les étudiants apprennent différentes techniques de manipulation, allant des marionnettes à fils traditionnelles aux formes plus modernes comme les marionnettes géantes ou animatroniques. La fabrication de marionnettes comprend l'apprentissage des matériaux, des méthodes de construction et des finitions artistiques. Quant à la mise en scène, elle englobe la direction artistique de spectacles complets, intégrant scénographie, lumière et son, pour créer des expériences théâtrales captivantes. Concernant la collaboration et projets collectifs, La collaboration est fortement encouragée à l'Académie Ivoire Marionnette. Les étudiants travaillent souvent en groupes pour concevoir et réaliser des projets, ce qui leur apprend à combiner leurs compétences, à partager des idées et à gérer des projets d'envergure. Ces projets collectifs peuvent inclure des spectacles pour des festivals, des représentations communautaires, ou des productions spéciales pour des événements locaux et internationaux, donnant aux étudiants une exposition précieuse et des retours pratiques sur leur travail. Pour ce qui est relatif à l'impact culturel et social, la formation à l'Académie Ivoire Marionnette n'est pas seulement une question de développement de compétences individuelles ; elle a également un impact profond sur le plan culturel et social. En formant une nouvelle génération de marionnettistes, l'académie contribue à la préservation et à l'innovation dans l'art de la marionnette en Côte d'Ivoire. Elle offre une plateforme pour que les traditions orales et les récits culturels soient transmis et renouvelés, tout en fournissant aux jeunes des perspectives professionnelles dans le domaine artistique. De plus, en incluant activement les femmes et les personnes issues de milieux défavorisés, l'académie joue un rôle clé dans la promotion de l'égalité des chances et de l'inclusion. L'Académie Ivoire Marionnette est donc bien plus qu'un simple centre de formation , elle est un creuset de créativité et d'innovation où les jeunes talents peuvent se développer en artistes complets, prêts à enrichir le patrimoine culturel de la Côte d'Ivoire et à présenter leur art sur la scène mondiale.
Results: Depuis son inauguration, l'Académie Ivoire Marionnette a joué un rôle pionnier dans la revitalisation de l'art traditionnel de la marionnette en Côte d'Ivoire, tout en intégrant des aspects innovants et modernes dans sa formation. L'initiative de former les jeunes, en particulier ceux des régions défavorisées et les femmes, a porté ses fruits de manière impressionnante, transformant non seulement la scène artistique mais aussi les vies de ceux qui y participent. La formation à l'Académie Ivoire Marionnette est devenue une véritable aubaine pour les jeunes issus de milieux ruraux et économiquement défavorisés. En leur offrant des compétences non seulement dans l'art de la manipulation de marionnettes mais aussi dans la fabrication et la mise en scène, l'Académie a ouvert de nouvelles avenues pour leur expression artistique et leur épanouissement personnel. Cette formation va au-delà de l'acquisition de compétences techniques; elle encourage également la confiance en soi, la créativité et le travail d'équipe, compétences essentielles dans tout milieu professionnel. La marionnette est valorisée par l'Académie comme un puissant outil de communication et d'éducation : les jeunes formés deviennent des ambassadeurs de leur culture et de leur histoire. L'inclusion des femmes dans ce programme a été particulièrement transformative. En brisant les barrières traditionnelles qui limitent souvent l'accès des femmes aux arts dans les régions rurales, l'Académie a non seulement favorisé l'égalité des genres mais a aussi enrichi l'art de la marionnette lui-même. Les perspectives et les récits féminins apportent une nouvelle profondeur à l'art, permettant des créations plus diversifiées et inclusives. Ces efforts ont contribué à un changement de perception, où les femmes sont désormais vues comme des créatrices et des artistes à part entière. L'impact social de cette mesure est palpable. En transformant les jeunes et les femmes en acteurs de changement à travers l'art de la marionnette, l'Académie Ivoire Marionnette contribue à la construction d'une société plus inclusive et créative. Les compétences acquises par les participants les préparent à des carrières dans divers secteurs artistiques et culturels, créant ainsi des opportunités économiques et favorisant le développement local.  L'Académie Ivoire Marionnette est bien plus qu'un simple centre de formation, c'est un catalyseur de transformation sociale et culturelle, un lieu où l'art de la marionnette est non seulement préservé mais aussi renouvelé, enrichissant ainsi le tissu culturel de la Côte d'Ivoire.

Main Feature: Le guichet unique « Initiative Fin Culture » est un programme qui est exécuté par l’Agence Emploi Jeunes (AEJ) et le Ministère de la Culture et de la Francophonie (MCF) en lien avec le Partenaire financier Birimian. De façon générale, il vise à soutenir les acteurs du secteur culturel par le financement de leurs projets à hauteur de 20.000.000 FCFA.  En effet, ce guichet a pour cibles, les entreprises du secteur de la culture (mode et design, arts du spectacle, arts plastiques et visuels, livre, cinéma/audiovisuel) dirigées par un jeune ou collectif de jeunes caractérisés par les critères suivants : -Être de nationalité ivoirienne ; -Être âgé(e) de 18 à 55 ans au 31 décembre de l’année de dépôt du dossier (pour les entreprises dirigées par un collectif de jeunes, le demandeur principal est tenu de respecter le critère d’âge) ;  -Résider en Côte d’ivoire ; -Avoir une activité ou un projet de développement d’activité correspondant à un besoin réel ; -Avoir un besoin de financement n’excédant pas les fourchettes indiquées ; -Justifier d’une qualification et/ou expérience pertinente dans le secteur d’activité indiqué ; -Présenter un dossier complet (Voir Etape 1 : Soumission des plans d’affaires). En ce qui concerne le processus de soumission, les jeunes/entreprises devront obligatoirement disposer d’un numéro AEJ donc s’inscrire sur la plateforme de l’Agence (www.agenceemploijeunes.ci). A l’issue de cette identification, le promoteur pourra se présenter sur la plateforme dédiée aux guichets de financement (https://projets.agenceemploijeunes.ci/ ) afin d’y soumettre son plan d’affaires ainsi qu’un ensemble de pièces jointes permettant de faciliter la prise en charge de sa demande. Il s’agit notamment, la copie de sa pièce d’identité (CNI, Attestation d’Identité ou Passeport) ; le registre de commerce de l’entreprise (pour les projets en développement) et sa Déclaration Fiscale d’Existence (pour les projets en développement). Le promoteur pourra également bénéficier de l’appui et des orientations du Ministère de la Culture et de la Francophonie impliqués dans la présente initiative. En effet, la Direction du Partenariat et des Relations Extérieures qui est le point focal du Ministère de la Culture et de la Francophonie à la possibilité de visualiser les dossiers soumis et en cours de traitement par les équipes de l’Agence Emploi Jeunes afin de faciliter le suivi. Notons que le programme couvre l’ensemble du territoire.
Results: -Création d'emploi  afin de contribuer à la réduction du chômage des jeunes. -Autonomisation des jeune pour une jeunesse active et responsable pour promouvoir le leadership. - Insertion des jeunes dans le tissu économique pour développer leur estime de soit.

Agency Implementation: Initiative Urheberrecht Österreich
Main Feature: The Austrian Copyright Initiative is a coalition of Austrian artists' organizations (authors and performers) that aims at improving copyright as well as collecting society legislation in Austria. It is a cross-sectoral platform and lobby group for all artists and cultural workers in Austria.  The initiative especially focuses on strengthening the typically weaker negotiating position of artists vis-à-vis their contractual partners (publishers, labels, film producers, broadcasters, other users) and improving the economic situation of artists in Austria (focuses on questions of adequate remuneration, fair contracts for artists and cultural workers). It was created to institutionalize, professionalize, and ensure the continuity of the representation of interests, in particular with regard to copyright, ancillary copyright, and collecting society legislations.  The initiative is financed through the social and cultural institutions (SKE) of the Austrian Collecting Societies AKM, Bildrecht, Literar Mechana, LSG Interpreten/OESTIG und VdFS - Verwertungsgesellschaft der Filmschaffenden.  Name(s) of partners engaged in the implementation of the policy/measure: AAC - Verband österreichischer Kameraleute, ADA - Austrian Directors' Association, AEA - Österreichischer Verband Filmschnitt, art-bv Berufsvereinigung der Bildenden Künstler Österreichs, Austrian Composters Association/Vereinigung Österreichischer Komponistinnen und Komponisten, Dachverband der Österreichischen Filmschaffenden, Design Austria, Drehbuchverband Austria, IG Autorinnen Autoren, IG Übersetzerinnen Übersetzer, Künstlerhaus Vereinigung, MICA - Music Austria, Musiker-Komponisten- Autoren Gilde, Österreichischer Musikrat (ÖMR), Verband Filmregie Österreich, VÖF - Verband österreichischer Filmausstatter:innen, VÖFS - Verband österreichischer Filmschauspieler:innen, VOICE Sprecherverband, Younion/Sektion Film, Bildrecht, LSG Interpreten/ÖSTIG and VdFS - Verwertungsgesellschaft der Filmschaffenden.
Results: The Austrian Copyright Initiative has been actively involved in the process of amending the Austrian Copyright Act (2021), and the Initiative's proposals have been taken into account in the final version of the Copyright Act.

Title EN: INTERNATIONAL ARTICULATION FROM AND FOR THE CULTURES OF THE MUNICIPAL AUTONOMOUS GOVERNMENT OF LA PAZ
Goal: Integrate Culture In Sustainable Development Frameworks
SDG: SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: International cooperation for sustainable development
Cultural Domain: Design,Performing Arts,Media Arts,Cinema and Audiovisual Arts,Music,Publishing,Visual Arts
Agency Implementation: Municipal Autonomous Government of La Paz/Secretariat of Culture and Tourism
Main Feature: The International Articulation of the Autonomous Municipal Government of La Paz is a strategic program aimed at energizing the relationship of the municipality with international organizations, agencies and networks for the promotion of cultures, promoting artistic-cultural mobility and circulation in addition to collaborative networking, positioning cultural development as the fourth pillar of sustainable development and deepening people's diplomacy.  Among the main actions carried out, the following can be highlighted:  -	Relations with the Diplomatic Corps and International Cooperation based in La Paz. Links and joint actions were established with the International Cooperation based in La Paz, mainly with member countries of the European Union such as Germany, Spain, France, Italy, Holland and which make up the Latin American Group of Cultures (GRULAC), as well as with the Cultural Centers of Gohet Institut, Alliance Française, Cultural Center of Spain in La Paz and the Cultural Center of Brazil, France (Alliance Française) and Dante Alighieri Cultural Center.  -	Consolidation of the Cultural Integration Group-GIC was supported, which was established by the previous administration at the initiative of cultural managers as a space for coordination and joint work between the GAMLP, the diplomatic corps and cultural managers for the strengthening and support of the Cultural Program of the Municipality through regular meetings and the development of joint agendas. The GIC is mainly made up of representatives of Latin American countries, various members of the European Union with a presence in Bolivia, the Embassies of Switzerland, Japan and the People's Republic of China, as well as international cultural institutions based in the city and the main international artistic festivals of the municipality.  -	Bilateral relations with local governments around the world: During this period, especially before the pandemic, relations and joint bilateral work were managed with different local governments in sister countries, often based on pre-existing twinning agreements with the municipality of La Paz, giving priority to relations with municipalities in southern Peru, northern Chile and northern Argentina due to socio-cultural affinities.  -	This program mainly focused on generating agendas for relationships, exchange, technical assistance, actions and joint learning, highlighting the links achieved with the local governments of Arica -Chile, Buenos Aires-Argentina, Arequipa- Peru, Bogotá -Colombia, Bonn -Germany, Córdoba-Argentina, - Santa Fé- Argentina, Canelones - Uruguay, Concepción- Chile, Madrid - Spain, Montevideo - Uruguay and Peñalolen- Chile.  -	Proactive participation of the Municipal Autonomous Government of La Paz in international cultural networks Significant efforts were made in the proactive participation and relationship of the La Paz Government in international cultural networks and organizations, at the local government level and at the state level, but also at the sectoral level, with the aim of promoting the exchange of experiences, the development of regional cultural agendas and the promotion of good cultural practices in the municipality.  -	United Cities and Local Governments – UCLG : During this period, La Paz had an intense activity of coordination and mutual collaboration with UCLG, mainly in relation to the promotion of cultural development as the Fourth Pillar of Sustainable Development in the region, participating in the Pilot Cities Program and becoming a strategic ally and named in 2020 as “Leading City of Agenda 21 for Culture”. The Commission participated in various spaces for articulation and discussion of the Culture Committee, such as Culture Summits, regional meetings and international seminars, in addition to the fact that this Committee contributed with speakers to various international face-to-face and virtual seminars organized by the Government of La Paz. In turn, in the city of La Paz, the Meeting of Cultural Capitals of the World was organized in 2018 with the support of UCLG and UCCI, in which the mechanisms for selecting cultural awards according to their continent were analyzed, with the perspective of unifying criteria and enhancing the visibility of good practices, programs and policies of the creditors of the awards as cultural capitals in different regions.  -	Union of Capital Cities of Ibero-America – UCCI: The city actively participated in the Union of Capital Cities of Ibero-America – UCCI, becoming co-president with Madrid for the period 2016-2018. Specifically, in relation to the cultural field, it carried out various tasks of coordination, advice, strengthening and promotion of the Sectoral Committee on Culture, being nominated in 2025 for the fourth time as the Ibero-American Capital of Cultures. To give some examples, it participated in the process of preparing and selecting candidates for 2020-2021 for the Ibero-American Capital of Cultures award and in various international forums and coordination bodies organized by the UCCI, for example, with the Organization of Ibero-American States (OIAS) in 2019. In turn, it actively participated in the annual meetings of the Sectoral Committee on Culture.  -	Mercociudades Network: Proactive participation in the Mercociudades Network was intensified, specifically in its Thematic Unit of Cultures- (UTC), coordinating it for three administrations. In this sense, the Municipal Autonomous Government of La Paz, mainly through the MSC: 1) participated in different Thematic Unit of Cultures (UTC), meetings and in coordination and planning spaces of the Technical Secretariat of the network, 2) collaboratively organized seminars and international meetings of the network, many of which took place in other cities of Mercosur, 3) managed the incorporation of new members, especially from municipalities in Bolivia, 4) developed specific technical assistance activities and collaborative work with local governments that are members of the network, and 5) contributed to the planning and monitoring of the Thematic Unit of Cultures (UTC), agenda from 2017 to 2020.  Participation in meetings and encounters in different regions of the world to promote the city of La Paz and to publicize the most important results of municipal cultural management, arranging presentations and exhibitions of our most representative events in different cities of Latin America.  The municipality managed the promotion and strengthening of the participation of cultural workers in programs, spaces, festivals, cultural corridors and networks at an international level, such as: Latin American Movement of Community Living Culture, Latin American Network of Museum Pedagogy, Latin American Network of Film Commissions, Ibero-American Network of Heritage Cemeteries, IberCultura Viva Network and network festivals, among others.
Results: -	Proactive international presence and participation of the Municipality of La Paz in different spaces of coordination and colorful work in the cultural field. -	Positioning of the Municipality of La Paz in terms of public cultural management through its participation in meetings and encounters in different regions of the world to promote the city of La Paz and publicize the most important results of municipal cultural management, managing presentations and exhibitions of our most representative events in different cities of Latin America. -	More than 12 diplomatic and international cooperation representations in Bolivia actively participated in the Municipality's Cultural Program. -	Joint statements at regional level on the importance of cultures as the Fourth Pillar of Sustainable Development. -	The generation of specific experiences of circulation and cultural exchange between member cities of the Networks in which they participate or have some type of twinning. -	Identifying good practices in South American cities. -	The naming of La Paz as the Ibero-American Capital of Cultures on four occasions, which constitutes an opportunity to make visible the importance of the Cultural Ecosystem in comprehensive development. -	La Paz was designated as a “Leading City of Agenda 21 for Culture” in 2021. -	In 2023, AMGLP won the UCLG – Mexico City Culture 21 International Award with the project of the Traditional Medicine Information and Guidance Centers “Qullañ Uta” which aims to influence the quality of the intercultural health system of the Municipality of La Paz, promoting the incorporation of knowledge, know-how and practices of traditional medicine in the population of the Municipality. The project is part of the planning of cultural policies, which aim to interweave cultures with the care of life. -	In relation to the coordination of the Thematic Unit of Cultures (UTC),  by the Government of La Paz, the following can be highlighted: joint statements at a regional level on the importance of cultures as the Fourth Pillar of Sustainable Development, the generation of specific experiences of cultural circulation and exchange between member cities, the identification of good practices in South American cities, the formation of national networks of local governments in Brazil, Peru, Argentina and Bolivia and the creation of a database of the main festivities and festivals in each city. In turn, based on the leadership of La Paz, within the framework of the TUC (UTC), the creation of the “Cultural Capital of Mercociudades” award and the “Declaration of mayors for cultural circulation and mobility in the cities of the region” were proposed, proposals that are expected to be implemented in the coming years.
Financial Ressources: DOES NOT INCLUDE BUDGET
Recommandations: The GAMLP's international articulation policy has provided a series of benefits to municipal cultural management.  Firstly, to the extent that it has allowed the Governement of La Paz and the work it does in cultures to be positioned in different international spaces.  Secondly, it generates the possibility of generating an exchange of experiences and knowledge, reciprocal technical assistance with other municipal administrations, artistic mobility and circulation of cultural goods. Added to this is the fact that it makes it possible to broaden the vision of public cultural management by learning about and dialoguing with other experiences and contributing to regional integration. It is essential to continue, deepen and expand proactive participation in international spaces, especially regional, of cooperation, coordination, technical assistance and visibility of successful experiences, both at the State level (Mercosur, Organization of Ibero-American States, Bolivarian Alliance for the Peoples of Our America (ALBA), and UNESCO, local government level (Culture Commission of the Union of Ibero-American Capital Cities (UCCI), Thematic Unit of Culture of the MERCOCIUDADES Network, Culture Commission of Cities and Local Governments United UCLG and others), as well as at the sectoral level (Latin American Network of Film Commissions, Network of Heritage Cemeteries, Ibero-American Network of Living Cultures, IberCultura Viva Network, among others). At the same time, it is necessary for the State to take greater steps to provide international funding to enable the development of co-production projects by workers from national cultures with those from other countries, as is the case of Iberescena and Ibermedia.

Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture
SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Cultural and creative sectors
Cultural Domain: Design,Performing Arts,Media Arts,Cinema and Audiovisual Arts,Music,Publishing,Visual Arts
Agency Implementation: Ministry of Culture and Sport
Main Feature: As part of the cultural cooperation agreement between China and Ethiopia for the period 2024-2026, significant efforts have been made to enhance capacity building within Ethiopia's cultural sector. This initiative includes two key training programs funded by the Chinese government aimed at advancing the skills and knowledge of professionals in the creative arts industry. Key Details: Agreement Overview: The capacity building program is part of a broader cultural cooperation agreement between China and Ethiopia, covering the years 2024-2026. The objective is to strengthen Ethiopia's cultural sector through targeted training and development.  Training Programs: Training on Digital Culture Industry Cultivation: Location: Beijing, China Dates: June 19 to July 2, 2024 Focus: This training program is designed to enhance skills in digital culture industry management and innovation, equipping participants with knowledge on integrating digital technologies into cultural practices.  Training on Cultural Creative Industry: Location: Jinhua City, China Dates: June 14 to June 27, 2024 Focus: This program targets the development of cultural creative industries, including strategies for promoting and managing cultural creative enterprises.  Impact: These training programs are expected to significantly bolster the capabilities of Ethiopian cultural professionals, fostering growth and innovation within the country's creative arts sector.  Future Outlook: The ongoing collaboration between China and Ethiopia is set to continue impacting the cultural sector positively, with further initiatives planned for subsequent years.
Results: The capacity-building initiative aimed at enhancing the creative art sector in Ethiopia has significantly benefited from practical exposure to digital culture strategies. This exposure has been facilitated through peer-to-peer learning opportunities, drawing on the successful experiences of the Chinese government and private sector in digitizing their creative industry. Key Highlights: Practical Exposure: The initiative provided Ethiopian professionals with hands-on experience in the field of digital culture. This exposure allowed them to observe and engage with advanced practices and technologies employed in the Chinese creative industry.  Peer-to-Peer Learning: Learning opportunities were structured to enable Ethiopian participants to gain insights from their Chinese counterparts. This included understanding how China has effectively integrated digital tools and platforms into its creative sectors. The focus was on replicating successful digital strategies and innovations that have been effective in China, thus fostering a knowledge exchange that enhances Ethiopia's digital cultural landscape.  Successful Practices from China: The Chinese government's and private sector's efforts in digitizing their creative industries served as a model. Key practices included leveraging digital platforms for content distribution, utilizing data analytics for audience engagement, and adopting cutting-edge technologies to enhance creative production and management.  Impact: The practical exposure and peer learning have equipped Ethiopian cultural professionals with valuable skills and knowledge. This is expected to drive digital transformation within Ethiopia's creative sector, fostering innovation and expanding digital presence.

Results: 2020 - 2021 PROJECT: Fostering cultural entrepreneurship in Cuenca (Fostering cultural entrepreneurship in Cuenca) https://www.cceazuay.gob.ec/  The Casa de la Cultura Ecuatoriana Núcleo del Azuay, a public institution in charge of promoting the cultural sector in the province of Azuay proposes to: (1) Consolidate the support ecosystem for the promotion of a cultural entrepreneurship program in Cuenca; (2) Establish a Cultural Entrepreneurship Incubator; (3) Strengthen the capacities of 30 cultural entrepreneurs in Cuenca; (4) Provide 10 cultural entrepreneurs with access to seed funding and credit and support for market access.  How does this project contribute to the implementation of the 2005 Convention? Expand the participation of previously excluded regions and social groups in the creation, production and distribution of cultural goods and services -The establishment of a permanent cultural entrepreneurship incubator will establish the necessary conditions for the development of cultural businesses in Cuenca, contributing to the creation of employment opportunities and income generation.  Strengthen public cultural institutions that are essential for the development of cultural industries - The project will strengthen the institution's capacity to support entrepreneurship in Cuenca through the establishment of a permanent cultural entrepreneurship incubator at the Casa de la Cultura Ecuatoriana Núcleo del Azuay, as well as through the consolidation of an ecosystem to support the cultural entrepreneurship program.  Strengthen financing mechanisms and market development for cultural goods and services: the project will promote public and private collaboration to support the financing and creation of markets for cultural entrepreneurship. Through the consolidation of an ecosystem to support the cultural entrepreneurship program, cultural entrepreneurs will have access to credit with preferential conditions to finance their ventures. In addition, access to markets will be promoted through collaboration with potential investors, professionals and commercial agents.  Main activities:  Establishment of a network of public and private institutions to provide training, access to financing and access to markets for local cultural enterprises.  Formation of a local inter-institutional working group to follow up on the implementation of the cultural entrepreneurship program.  Creation of an incubator to promote cultural entrepreneurship. Development of a website to promote cultural entrepreneurship, including a news portal, a digital portfolio of participating companies and training materials. Development of a training methodology for cultural entrepreneurship.  *(Including Ecuador, presented by FIACINE, Colombia) 2022 - 2023 PROJECT: SOMOS DIVERSAS: Empowering women audiovisual professionals from vulnerable groups in seven Latin American countries. https://www.fiacine.com/somos-diversas  The Ibero-American Federation of Film Arts and Sciences Academies (FIACINE), a non-profit organization that brings together film, arts and sciences academies in the region, aims to: 1) identify groups of women belonging to vulnerable groups working in the audiovisual industry in 7 Latin American countries; 2) identify the employment and training situation of women belonging to the target groups; 3) generate a mapping report of the audiovisual sector, focused on the identified groups, including recommendations for the development of public policies; 4) create a space for networking among the identified minority groups.  How does this project contribute to the implementation of the 2005 Convention?  Strengthens job creation and entrepreneurship measures: the project empowers minority groups by equipping them with entrepreneurial skills.  Supports women artists and cultural professionals: through its various activities, the project creates and strengthens networks among women and supports them as artists and professionals. Main activities:  Identify people from vulnerable groups through a virtual census.  Collect census information and develop a database of groups belonging to vulnerable groups.  Conduct a study on the employment and training needs of the target groups through surveys.  Design and implement virtual workshops on entrepreneurship in the audiovisual sector.  Formulate recommendations for the development of public policy actions and strategies.  Publish a SOMOS DIVERSOS report with the mapping and analysis of the information gathered throughout the project, as well as recommendations for the development of public policy strategies.  Organize the SOMOS DIVERSOS forum as a space for networking among the identified minority groups.

Agency Implementation: Corporación Academia de las Artes Cinematográficas de Chile, National Union of Artists (UNA).
Main Feature: Founded in 2018, the Chilean Film Academy is a non-profit, autonomous and independent, private institution that represents many roles from the film industry in Chile. Among others, its goals are to promote the creation of audiovisual and cinematographic arts, to value cinema as an essential component of the Chilean cultural diversity, and to motivate and strengthen the industry through the exchange of ideas and knowledge between the professionals and technicians of the audiovisual arts in Chile.   Since 2020, the Film Academy has been responsible for selecting the films that represent Chile at international awards such as the Oscars, Goyas, Ariels, by vote of its members. An entity that brings together diverse professionals from the audiovisual industry and that acts as a advocate of Chilean cinema and a selection body for films that represent Chile in international award circuits.   Among its members there are producers, directors of photography, makeup directors, animators, screenwriters, directors, costumers, actors and actresses, among other agents in the Chilean audiovisual sector. With regard to the monitoring framework of the 2005 Convention, the Chilean Film Academy, through its actions, reports on the "information systems that evaluate international flows of cultural goods and services" indicator.
Results: The main result of this policy is to select representative Chilean audiovisual productions for various international events, through a selection validated by a large number of professionals from the Chilean film industry. Regarding association, the Chilean Film Academy has increased its membership by 100% between 2021 and 2023.   Regarding the gender gaps, there is evidence of a narrowing in the gap from 70% men and 30% women in 2021 to 63% men and 37% women in 2023. In terms of international association, the Chilean Film Academy is part of the Ibero-American Federation of Motion Pictures, Arts and Sciences Academies (FIACINE), where projects such as "We are diverse" have been launched, cofunded by UNESCO, and currently in underway in seven countries, among them Chile.   Finally, the Chilean Film Academy was elected to the first vice presidency of FIACINE, taking an active role in this association. New partnerships with Latin American sister academies for participating in their film awards: ColibrÃ­ Awards from Ecuador, Macondo Awards from Colombia and the Grand Prize of Brazilian Cinema.
Recommandations: Regarding the Chilean Film Academy's years of operation and the implementation of its actions, greater legitimacy has been achieved in the slection of films for their participation in international awards. Moreover, the interest for associative participation has grown among film arts and industry professionals and creators. In addition, the positioning of Chilean film and its creators has strengthened on a national and international level.   A sense of belonging and value of cinema as a fundamental tool for the creation of the country's cultural heritage. Lastly, in relation to certain recommendations, the national film awards should be implemented again, which have been suspended and are vital for validation and recognition of the audiovisual arts and its various roles. Lastly, the Chilean Film Academy generates projects and obtains financing to promote film as an essential component of our memory and culture among children and youth.

These actions aim to leverage partnerships with different festivals and markets to enhance the international visibility and positioning of Dominican film agents and projects.

Title EN: Investing in creative development, exploiting the economic aspects of creativity, and protecting copyrights.
Goal: Promote Human Rights And Fundamental Freedoms
SDG: SDG 5 - Achieve gender equality and empower all women and girls,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels

Cultural Domain: Design,Performing Arts,Media Arts,Cinema and Audiovisual Arts,Music,Publishing,Visual Arts
Agency Implementation: Viet Nam Creativity and Copyright Association
Main Feature: The Viet Nam Creativity and Copyright Association (the Association) was established under Decision No. 404/QD-BNV dated March 19, 2021, by the Minister of Home Affairs, under the state management of the Ministry of Home Affairs and the management of relevant ministries and agencies related to the activities of the Association. The Association operates in accordance with the charter approved by the Minister of Home Affairs in Decision No. 790/QD-BNV dated July 5, 2021. The Association has legal status, a seal, and a separate account. It operates nationwide in the field of creativity and copyright for literary and artistic works as prescribed by law. The Association carries out the following main tasks: “Organizing activities in the field of creativity and copyright for literary and artistic works in accordance with laws and regulations; copyright protection measures for literary and artistic works as prescribed by laws and regulations; participating in and proposing to competent authorities policies related to the field of the Association's activities as in compliance with laws and regulations; disseminating and fostering knowledge; cooperating in exchange of information and communication on creative development and copyright for literary and artistic works as prescribed by laws and regulations; connecting creative development and copyright protection for literary and artistic works; organizing conferences, seminars, fairs, exhibitions, and other activities appropriate to the scope of activities, principles, objectives in accordance with laws and regulations; publishing documents, media publications, electronic information pages to support the development of creativity and copyright protection for literary and artistic works in accordance with the principles, objectives of the Association, laws and  regulations; strengthening international cooperation in the field of creativity and copyright for literary and artistic works as prescribed by laws and regulations and other tasks when requested by competent authorities.” Regarding organizational structure, the Association has an Inspection Board, a Membership Board, an Office, and an International Cooperation Board.
Results: The Association has participated in activities such as:  (i) Consulting, proposing, contributing to finalizing mechanisms and policies, including legal provisions on copyright, related rights (Law on Amending and Supplementing a number of articles of Intellectual Property Law, Decrees, Circulars) and policies for the development of cultural and creative industries; (ii) Organizing communication, including raising awareness of the development of creative industries and copyright protection through forums, conferences, seminars, training courses in fields such as publishing, libraries, journalism, film, etc., on television, and at the Academy of Journalism and Communication and University of Social Sciences and Humanities (through training courses for students);  (iii) International cooperation, including signing cooperation agreements with the Representative Office of the Korean Copyright Commission in Hanoi, Viet Nam and attending the 45th Session of Standing Committee on Copyright and Related Rights (from 16 to 19 April, 2024) of the World Intellectual Property Organization in Geneva, Switzerland. The Association currently has 112 members. Up to now, the Association has developed a project to submit to competent authorities for permission to establish six legal entities, each with its own legal status, seal, and separate account. These entities include the Viet Nam Creative Technology and Copyright Center (VCTCC), the Viet Nam Center for Expertise and Certification of Digital Copyright (CECDC), the Viet Nam Center for Creativity Investment and Exploitation of Digital Copyright (VCCDC), the Viet Nam Copyright and Mind Map Creative Development Research Institute (VCMCI), and the Digital Copyright and Creative Economy Institute (DCEI).   The Association has signed cooperation agreements with related domestic and international organizations such as the Korean Copyright Commission in Viet Nam (KCC), the National Political Publishing House, the Viet Nam Blockchain Association, the Viet Nam Consumers Ceramics Association, the Viet Nam Reproduction Rights Organization, the Viet Nam Association of Administrative Sciences, and Viet Nam Digital Communications Association.

SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Digital environment
Agency Implementation: « Le Centre International de Tunis pour l’Economie Culturelle Numérique » (TICDCE) (Un Etablissement public à caractère non administrative sous tutelle du Ministère des Affaires Culturelles )
Main Feature: La création du TICDCE s’inscrit dans le cadre d’une vision du Ministère des affaires culturelles (MAC) qui préconise la culture comme vecteur de développement économique promoteur, générateur d’emplois. Cette structure crée en vertu du décret gouvernemental n°2019-1062 du 04 novembre 2019  est une initiative du MAC qui vient appuyer les politiques et les orientations stratégiques de l’état en terme de développement culturel par le biais des supports numériques et de ’innovation. Les missions du centre tournent principalement autour de 03 grands axes : •	Le développement de l’économie culturelle à travers les opportunités qu’offrent les nouvelles technologies ; •	La promotion et la valorisation de la culture tunisienne dans sa diversité par sa digitalisation ; •	Faire de l’économie culturelle numérique un choix économique incontournable qui s’impose au même titre que l’innovation technologique ; Afin de bien s’acquitter de ses missions, le centre est doté de moyens et de logistique de pointe mis à disposition des jeunes porteurs de projets innovants : •	Un co-working space avec une capacité d’accueil de 30 co-workers ; •	Un studio d’enregistrement vidéo ; •	Un studio Son et post-production •	Un Hub-room équipée de matériel de projection interactif ; Situé au cœur de la Cité de la culture, le centre représente un cadre approprié pour la conception, l’innovation et la créativité dans le domaine culturel. Il offre une plateforme innovante dédiée à la création, la production, la diffusion  et la démocratisation de l’œuvre culturelle ce qui répond parfaitement aux objectifs de la convention notamment la réaffirmation du lien de complémentarité entre les aspects économiques et culturels du développement et cadre aussi avec les différents maillons de la chaine des valeurs qu’elle véhicule à savoir la création-la production-la distribution et la jouissance/participation.  La mesure cible en premier lieu les jeunes porteurs de projets, en quête de reconnaissance et qui souhaitent intégrer le milieu compétitif des industries culturelles et créatives dans ses expressions diverses (cinéma-livre-arts visuels-jeux vidéo-design..) ainsi que les petites et moyennes entreprises (PME) émergentes œuvrant dans le domaine de l’innovation numérique et ce, en leur fournissant à la fois un laboratoire de recherche, d’accompagnement et de documentation, un centre de formation et un incubateur de réflexion et d’échange.  Les principales caractéristiques de la politique de transformation numérique des industries culturelles et créatives   comme levier de croissance économique, d’innovation sociale et de promotion de la diversité culturelle véhiculée par le TICDCE sont décrites par la Stratégie du (MAC): « Stratégie de la Culture à l’horizon 2035 ». Ces caractéristiques peuvent être résumés comme suit selon les axes de priorité de la stratégie : 1-	Démocratiser l’accès à la culture et l’exposition aux produits culturels pour toutes et tous (Promotion de la diversité culturelle) et ce, à travers les activités suivantes :  •	 Enrichir l’offre culturelle Tunisienne en face de la surabondance d’une offre maitrisée par des acteurs externes (les GAFA) (encourager fiscalement et financièrement le contenu Tunisien) d’où accroitre la visibilité des cultures marginalisées ou peu présentées à travers les plateformes numériques. Des œuvres de niche peuvent trouver leur public sans les contraintes des circuits de distribution traditionnels. •	Réduire la « fracture numérique ». (70% des Tunisiens ont accès à internet) il est donc nécessaire de compléter la couverture numérique pour permettre à chacun d’avoir accès à l’offre culturelle •	L’évaluation des offres devra être décalée de la programmation vers la consommation effective : les entreprises vertueuses, à l’ère de la surabondance, sont moins celles qui présentent une variété d’œuvres que celles qui donnent lieu à une consommation effective d’une variété d’œuvres numériques. •	Encourager les contenus culturels destinés pour les handicapés (créer des faveurs dans la valorisation) 2-	Dynamiser et soutenir l’offre culturelle et le capital humain créatifs : Face à une problématique liée au fait que les études faites par le MAC  ont montré une carence identifiée dans le manque d’aptitudes managériales et entrepreneuriales et des difficultés à adopter les nouvelles technologies, des actions ont été mises en œuvre tels que : •	Le Développement des compétences managériales pour moderniser les pratiques et renforcer les institutions et la professionnalisation du système des ICC en Tunisie. •	La Valorisation des métiers sensibles (livre, théâtre,,,,) •	Mettre en place des résidences mixtes, des cohortes, l’incubation des groupes multi professionnels et favoriser l’échange multidisciplinaire et l’entrepreneuriat créatif et l’intelligence collective via le numérique. •	Développer les Portail des professions artistiques et culturelles (numérisation des cartes professionnelles, formations, résidences,  ..) •	S’engager sur une formation professionnelle et académique adaptée aux besoins du marché (coopérer avec le Ministère de l’enseignement supérieur pour installer le 1er Master en management culturel en Tunisie)  3-	Soutenir les modèles économiques et de financements culturels et créatifs : cet axe répond à une problématique qui concerne la difficulté d’accès au financement en raison notamment du caractère jugé « risqué » des ICC. (notamment pour les contenus numériques). En fait, Le système actuel d’aides et de subventions publiques souffre de plusieurs lacunes surtout en ce qui concerne la création digitale. Pour cela plusieurs actions ont été prise à travers le TICDCE pour faire face à ces carences tels que : •	Participer à évaluer  le Fonds De Garantie Des Industries Culturelles (FGIC) afin de le réactiver •	Encourager l’émergence d'incubateurs dédiés à la création numérique •	Promouvoir la diffusion numérique privé du livre (e-book et audio-book) •	Elargir le champ d’octroi des subventions vers les nouveaux ICC numériques (jeux vidéo, ar, xr,…) •	Faciliter l’accès au marché (le crowedfunding, l’achat innovant, …) 4-	Accompagner les transitions territoriales et phygitale et une nouvelle génération d’établissements publics :  Une constatation de faible programmation concernant les établissements culturels a été faite et qui ne répond pas aux attentes du grand public malgré l' infrastructure (salles de cinéma, sites historiques, …) importante mais inadaptée/obsolète ne permettant pas de satisfaire les attentes des créateurs et du grand public.  Une solution a été adoptée qui concerne la création et l’Installation des créatifs hub à travers le redéploiement des établissements déjà existants. Dans ce contexte le TICDCE a créé le projet « Makan » espace d’innovation et d’intelligence collective dans l’espace « Fadhel ben Achour" à la Marsa (un banlieue de la capital Tunis) . Plusieurs autres hubs créatifs sont envisagés La transformation numérique des industries culturelles et créatives est un phénomène puissant qui agit comme un levier de croissance économique, stimule l’innovation sociale et promeut la diversité culturelle. Elle redéfinit les modèles économiques, démocratise l’accès à la culture et ouvre de nouvelles perspectives pour la création et la diffusion des œuvres culturelles. Cette transformation nécessite toutefois une adaptation continue des acteurs des ICC et une réflexion sur les enjeux éthiques et économiques qui en découlent.
Results: -	Accompagnement de 45 startups (entre 2019 et 2023). 15 startups ont été labélisées et sont actives sur le marché. Et ce dans le cadre de l’activité de « Innovation startuplab », un programme du TICDCE. -	Accompagnement et formation de 235 acteurs culturels dans les régions dans le domaine de l’entrepreneuriat créatif en 2023 dont 51% des femmes et 49% hommes, et l’élaboration d’un rapport sur la cartographie culturelle https://vu.fr/StHgf  et un guide de l’entrepreneuriat créatif https://vu.fr/zAncO.  -	L’aménagement et la mise en activité du hub créatif mobile « Madad » en 2023 et qui a fait 10 workshops dans 10 régions avec 70 participants en moyenne de chaque région.  -	La conception l’installation du projet « Makan » à la Marsa (une banlieue de la Capitale) en 2023. C’est un projet qui abrite 5 hubs créatifs (le design, l’IA, le Podcast, la calligraphie arabe et un studio XR) des coworking space et un musée des contenus numériques. L’idée de ce projet tourne autour de l’intelligence collective. -	Développement d’une plateforme numérique pour les livres audio et livres numériques et IA www.ekotbia.tn  en 2023. Recommandations: -	L’industrie culturelle créative en Tunisie a remarquablement évolué -	Une prise de conscience générale sur l’importance du domaine des ICC a été remarquée surtout à partir de 2022. -	Un besoin d’adaptation du cadre législatif et réglementaire avec cette nouvelle réalité s'impose.

Title EN: Kan Yama Kan
Goal: Integrate Culture In Sustainable Development Frameworks
SDG: SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: International cooperation for sustainable development
Agency Implementation: UAE Board on Books for Young People
Main Feature: The "Kan Yama Kan" initiative by the UAE Board on Books for Young People (UAEBBY) is designed to promote reading and cultural exchange among children, especially in underserved communities. The program collects and distributes Arabic children's books to various regions, fostering a love for reading and enhancing cultural awareness. It also aims to support libraries and educational institutions worldwide. The initiative embodies the UAE's commitment to humanitarian and cultural giving, reflecting the nation's vision of spreading knowledge and literacy.
Results: Since its launch, "Kan Yama Kan" has successfully distributed thousands of books to children in various countries, significantly impacting their access to literature and education. This has helped inspire young readers, foster cross-cultural understanding, and promote the Arabic language and literature globally. The program's emphasis on literacy has also contributed to educational development in underserved communities, aligning with global educational goals.

Title EN: Kanz Al Jeel Award
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture
SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Cultural and creative sectors
Agency Implementation: Abu Dhabi Arabic Language Centre. Department of Culture and Tourism - Abu Dhabi.
Main Feature: Kanz Al Jeel Award was launched by the Abu Dhabi Arabic Language Centre (ALC), part of the Department of Culture and Tourism - Abu Dhabi (DCT Abu Dhabi), to honor Traditional poetry pieces, folklore studies, and research by scholars and creators whose works represent the heritage of Traditional poetry and its inherent values. The Award draws its name from one of the late Sheikh Zayed’s renowned works underlining his great legacy in the world of poetry and creativity. The Award also aims to promote creativity and critical thinking to create a poetic, critical, and artistic movement that will make Sheikh Zayed’s creative experience a focal point for new forms of creativity. The late Sheikh Zayed bin Sultan Al Nahyan, the UAE’s Founding Father, was a great leader who united a nation, shaped the UAE identity, and built a society that believes in tolerance and has accomplished major transformations. Sheikh Zayed laid the foundations for a unique ecosystem for poetry that reflects the depth of his relationship with Arabic and Traditional poetic heritage on one hand, and his ability to shape his unique aesthetic perspective on another. The Award embraces Sheikh Zayed’s poetic journey and serves as a catalyst for novel artworks that celebrates its aesthetic value and ingenuity, once again highlighting the greater values of truthfulness, goodness, and beauty. The Kanz Al Jeel Award features six different categories, including the Poetry Matching Award, which is granted to the poem that most closely matches one of Sheikh Zayed’s poems in meter, rhyme, and subject. The poem should have an equal number of lines and imitate the language, figures of speech, and rhythm of the original poem. The Poetic Publications Award recognizes Traditional poetry books that are authentic in both form and content and constitute a notable addition to this poetic field. The Arts Award celebrates works of art that use visual tools to read, perform, and embody Sheikh Zayed’s poetry and Traditional poetry in general. These include Arabic calligraphy, plastic art, short films, or singing, which engages vocal talents and musical instruments, and Arabic poetry at large. The Studies and Research Award is granted to research studies published on Traditional poetry that address this poetry’s methods, content, and lexicon in a scientific manner. The Translation Award is granted to works and studies translated from Arabic, and to collections of poems translated from Arabic to other languages, whether printed or handwritten. (Copyrights of handwritten works go to the Award). The Creative Personality Award celebrates the winning work that made outstanding and effective creative contributions to Traditional poetry and affiliated studies, as well as to music, singing, drawing, and Arabic calligraphy.
Results: In 2023, the award saw a significant increase, with 264 entries from 27 countries, including 17 Arab nations and 10 others globally. This growth highlights a heightened global interest in Traditional poetry and underscores the award's role in fostering cultural exchange and enhancing its prestige. The increased submissions for the Kanz Al Jeel Award indicate a growing global interest in Traditional poetry, highlighting its universal appeal beyond traditional boundaries. The diverse international participation demonstrates the award's effectiveness in fostering cultural exchange, attracting scholars, poets, and artists from various backgrounds. This enriches the dialogue around Traditional poetry and enhances its appreciation worldwide. The rising prestige of the award is evident from the growing recognition in the global literary and cultural community. This elevates Traditional poetry's status internationally, contributing to its preservation and promotion. By expanding its reach, the award celebrates artistic and scholarly achievements while revitalizing this unique cultural heritage.
Recommandations: The Kanz Al Jeel Award, launched by the Abu Dhabi Arabic Language Centre, successfully promotes Traditional poetry and celebrates cultural heritage.

Title EN: PLURINATIONAL SKILLS CERTIFICATION SYSTEM
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture
SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Cultural and creative sectors
Cultural Domain: Design,Performing Arts,Media Arts,Cinema and Audiovisual Arts,Music,Publishing,Visual Arts
Agency Implementation: MINISTRY OF EDUCATION
Main Feature: The Program called Sistema Plurinacional de Certificación de Competencias en Bolivia – SPCC (Plurinational Skills Certification System), was implemented within the framework of the National Development Plan “Bolivia digna, soberana, Productiva y democrática para Vivir bien” (Dignified, sovereign, Productive and democratic Bolivia to Live Well) and seeks to legitimize, through a certification process, the competencies, knowledge, and skills acquired empirically by young people and adults under the criteria of productivity, recovery of cultural knowledge.  The main objective of the SPCC is the formal recognition of the skills and knowledge acquired by people throughout their lives, regardless of their formal educational context, due to the need to certify the labor competencies of Bolivians. This system responds to the demand of workers seeking to validate their knowledge and skills acquired in practice, promoting social equity, inclusion and the decolonization of education; seeking to contribute to sustainably improving the living conditions of individuals, families and communities, increasing their opportunities to access the world of work, dynamizing their social and productive systems, with a valid recognition in the name of the Plurinational State of Bolivia. The technical standard consists of specifications that define the competencies, skills and knowledge required to perform various occupations effectively. These are essential for the certification process, as they establish clear and measurable criteria that applicants must meet to be evaluated and certified. All standards are built at the request of the occupational sector.  In this process, the competencies and sub-competencies, skills, knowledge and aptitudes that people have developed throughout their lives are identified. This activity also establishes the years of experience required by the applicant to access certification. After the standard is developed, it is validated. Each occupational standard is developed and validated by the same actors of each occupation in a participatory manner. The following technical standards have been achieved in the cultural field:   1. Photographer and/or filmmaker 2. Industrial Weaving and Spinning 3. Charango performer 4. Leather goods 5. Social Community Radio Communicator 6. Band Musician 7. Worker in the Transformation of Quarry Stone 8. Graphic Arts Worker 9. Technician of the Occupational Sector of Heritage Property Restorer 10. Producer Owner Goldsmith in Filigree and/or Carving Techniques, Embossing Chiseling 11. Producer/Owner in Artisan Manufacturing of Felt Hats 12. Producer/Owner in the Making of Paceña and/or Cochabambina Polleras 13. Producer/Owner in the Making of Chuquisaqueña, Potosina and/or Tarijeña Polleras 14. Producer in Handmade Weaving 15. Radio Journalist Technician 16. Goldsmith Technician 17. Radio Station Operator Technician 18. Photojournalist Technician 19. Cameraman Technician Director 20. Artist Technician in Recreation and Animation 21. Artisan Technician of Ornamental Wooden Pieces 22. Ceramic Pieces Artisan Technician 23. Occupational Sector Technician: Performing Arts – Theater 24. Performing Arts Technician - Bolivian Folk Dance
Results: The SPCC (Plurinational Skills Certification System) has had a significant impact on the lives of Bolivian workers, particularly those in the cultural sectors, because it has managed to advance the professionalization of cultural workers, improving their employability so they can access better job opportunities and at the same time contribute to strengthening cultural identity recognizing ancestral know-how knowledge.  The program contributes greatly to the valorization of Bolivian culture and traditions. This year, 22,946 people have benefited, of whom 1,875 are from the cultural and creative industries sectors.
Financial Ressources: $us. 5,000 (annually)

Title EN: Khorfakkan Theatre Festival 2024
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture
SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Cultural and creative sectors
Agency Implementation: Sharjah Department of Culture
Main Feature: The prestigious event attracted both local and international theatre groups, with the aim of promoting cultural exchange, artistic expression and community engagement. Attendees enjoyed a variety of performances, workshops and interactive activities. From engaging theatre performances to educational workshops, the festival offered a rich tapestry of artistic and cultural experiences. A highlight of the festival was the opening show, a display featuring creatively decorated vehicles, mechanical and acrobatic stunts and performances by various artistic and cultural groups, setting a lively and festive tone. Traditional Emirati arts, such as Al Ayala, were showcased alongside international heritage performances, reflecting the UAE’s commitment to cultural diversity. The festival also emphasized community participation through interactive mask-making, decoration and costume competitions, which fostered creativity and engagement among attendees. Educational activities, including school theatre performances and workshops, played a crucial role in promoting cultural education and youth engagement. With advanced audio-visual facilities, the festival grounds were well-equipped to support high-quality performances and shows, contributing to an immersive and enjoyable experience for all. By promoting cultural exchange and artistic collaboration, the Khorfakkan Theatre Festival has greatly enhanced Sharjah’s cultural vibrancy. It celebrates traditional and contemporary arts, fosters community bonds, and contributes to the UAE’s dynamic cultural landscape.
Results: The Department of Culture's Theatre Department hosted a phenomenal 9th edition of the Khorfakkan Theatre Festival, drawing thousands of attendees to Khorfakkan Park. The festival was an a affirmation of cultural diversity and artistic expression. An international artistic march kicked off the event, featuring vibrant groups from the UAE, Egypt, Oman, India, South Africa, and more. This showcased the festival's commitment to global cultural exchange. Khorfakkan Park became a hub of creativity. Attendees enjoyed a diverse lineup of theatrical performances, including short plays, captivating scout productions, and engaging children's shows. The festival fostered a love for the arts with workshops and competitions. The 9th Khorfakkan Theatre Festival successfully united communities through the power of theatre and artistic expression.
Recommandations: To build on the success of the Khorfakkan Festival and further enhance cultural diversity, it is recommended to introduce more collaborative projects between local and international artists. This can include joint performances, workshops, and cultural exchange programs that foster deeper understanding and appreciation of different cultural traditions. Expanding the festival's outreach to include more diverse communities within the UAE and inviting performers from a broader range of countries can also enrich the festival's offerings. Implementing educational initiatives, such as cultural heritage tours and interactive sessions with artists, can engage younger audiences and promote cultural literacy. Additionally, leveraging digital platforms to livestream events and share festival highlights can extend its reach to a global audience, increasing visibility and participation. By continuously evolving and embracing new cultural elements, the Khorfakkan Festival can further establish itself as a vibrant celebration of cultural diversity and community spirit in Sharjah.

Title EN: Kids' TV Writing Incubator
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture
SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Cultural and creative sectors
Agency Implementation: CSO NAME: BIPOC TV & Film   _______________    BIPOC TV & Film is a member of the Coalition for the Diversity of Cultural Expressions (CDCE) EMAIL: coalition@cdec-cdce.org PHONE: (+1) 514-277-2666
Main Feature: [2018-2023] The Kids’ TV Writing Incubator is a 6-month intensive program designed for emerging to mid-level Black, indigenous, and people of color (BIPOC) screenwriters as they develop a pilot script for kids’ TV (preschool, ages 6-9, tween or Young Adults). Participants are also introduced to other industry professionals to build and enhance their networks as they launch their writing careers in Children’s TV.  The program is designed to give participants an in-depth overview of the business and craft of writing for children’s TV. It covers story structure, standards and practices, buyers and genres, demographics, live action vs. animation, pitching, how to take a meeting, general industry etiquette, and introduce participants to network executives and kids’ content producers from Canada and the United States. By the end of the program, each writer will have a completed and polished spec script and an original pilot script in their portfolio.  Led by award-winning writer John May (The Magic School Bus, Sesame Street, 16 Hudson) and Nathalie Younglai (Dino Dana, 16 Hudson, The Magic School Bus Rides Again), participants get to experience real-world writing deadlines to prepare them for working in the kids’ TV industry.  For the 2020-2023 editions, 5 writers were selected annually for internship placements at Wildbrain in Toronto.
Results: BIPOC TV and FILM focus is on expanding networks (domestically and internationally) for Canadian Indigenous, Black and racialized creators and media professionals and building their capacity creatively and entrepreneurially. The programming will continue to develop opportunities for business and market success and develop creative talent to facilitate a diverse and highly skilled workforce.

Title EN: L’INTEGRATION DE LA ZONE DE LIBRE-ÉCHANGE CONTINENTALE AFRICAINE
Goal: Achieve A Balanced Flow Of Cultural Goods And Services And Increase The Mobility Of Artists And Cultural Professionals
SDG: SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 10 - Reduce inequality within and among countries,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Treaties and agreements
Cultural Domain: Design,Media Arts,Cinema and Audiovisual Arts,Music,Publishing,Visual Arts
Agency Implementation: Ministère du Commerce et de l’Industrie.
Main Feature: Depuis le 21 mars 2018 à Kigali, Il est créé en Afrique une Zone de libre-échange continentale africaine, ci-après dénommée « ZLECAF ». Dans l’un de ses objectifs généraux, la ZLECAF vise à   promouvoir le développement industriel à travers la diversification et le développement des chaînes de valeurs régionales, le développement de l’agriculture et la sécurité alimentaire. Aux fins de la réalisation des objectifs énoncés à l’article 3, les États parties s’engagent entre autres à :  éliminer progressivement les barrières tarifaires et non-tarifaires au commerce des marchandises, libéraliser progressivement le commerce des services, coopérer en matière d’investissement, de droits de propriété intellectuelle et de politique de concurrence, coopérer dans tous les domaines liés au commerce.
Results: La République Centrafricaine est devenue Etat partie à cet Accord en Septembre 2020. En prélude au Salon National des Femmes Entrepreneurs de Centrafrique qui a eu lieu du 4 au 9 mars 2024, la FAFECA (Fédération des Associations des Femmes Entrepreneuses de Centrafrique) a organisé une formation pour outiller ses membres sur la ZLECAF afin qu’elles soient capables de gérer leurs produits sur les marchés. L’objectif de cette formation est d’apprendre à ces femmes entrepreneures la création des marchés uniques et la libre circulation des biens et des personnes sur le continent africain. Un échange fructueux a eu lieu entre les participantes et les experts  comme Cyriaque Guenefio, chargé de mission en matière de l’industrie, point focal national pour le suivi de l’accord de la ZLECAF en RCA et formateur a dit plus : « Cette formation s’inscrit dans le cadre de l’appropriation de l’accord de la ZLECAF. La place de la femme entrepreneure dans les accords du moins importants à partir du moment qu’on est en train de négocier le protocole sur le commerce des femmes et des jeunes. La ZLECAF est un accord qui de manière globale parle de libre circulation des biens et des personnes sur le continent africain et la création de marché unique. Cela est profitable pour la RCA, à partir du moment où nous faisons partie des états signataires et nous avons ratifié cet accord, cela nous sera profitable à partir du moment où si nous nous engageons à mettre en œuvre les outils et les mécanismes des dispositions qui sont contenus, si la Centrafrique ne se prépare pas à vendre ses produits à l’extérieur, elle sera inondée par des produits d’ailleurs.
