Title EN: National and Local Cultural and Creative Industries Strategies
Goal: Integrate Culture In Sustainable Development Frameworks
SDG: SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: National sustainable development policies and plans
Agency Implementation: Ministry of Culture. Department of Culture and Tourism Abu Dhabi. Dubai Culture and Arts Authority.
Main Feature: Many countries have crafted Cultural and Creative Strategies to harness the economic potential of this dynamic sector. By investing in culture, nations can generate jobs and stimulate business growth. With strategic planning, the cultural sector can significantly boost domestic economies and enhance the quality of life for individuals. The UAE has learned from successful examples, and the Ministry of Culture has introduced the concept in the UAE. Below is a highlight of efforts at the federal and local governments to develop strategies to strengthen and nurture the cultural and creative industries (CCI): o	National Strategy for the Cultural and Creative Industries: The National Strategy for the Cultural and Creative Industries aims to promote the growth of the cultural and creative industries sector and increase its contribution to 5 per cent of the national GDP by 2031. It also seeks to strengthen the UAE’s position on the global cultural and creativity map and inspire creative thinking and attract cultural talents and creative entrepreneurs from around the world amongst others. Launched in 2021, the UAE’s National Strategy for the Cultural and Creative Industries aims to promote the growth of the cultural and creative industries’ sector and increase its contribution to 5 per cent of the national GDP by 2031. It also seeks to: •	strengthen the UAE’s position on the global cultural and creativity map •	inspire creative thinking and attract cultural talents and creative entrepreneurs from around the world •	double the number of enterprises operating in the sector •	create new jobs in the creative industries •	raise the average income of those employed in this field •	attract freelancers and creative start-ups to set up, live and work in the UAE.  To achieve these objectives, it focuses on 40 initiatives covering three main segments: •	talents and creatives •	professionals and business environment •	enabling the business environment.  The strategy is based on partnerships between the public and private sectors to implement comprehensive programs. It will enhance the UAE’s position as a global destination for a knowledge-economy based on creativity, innovation, talent and technology. •	Abu Dhabi Culture and Creative Industries Strategy – 2020 – 2024: In 2019, Abu Dhabi developed a 5-year culture and creative industries strategy 2020-2024, working in collaboration with key sector partners. The Strategy seeks to strengthen Abu Dhabi’s position as a globally recognized center of creative talent and a leading regional producer and exporter of creative and cultural content. Five strategic pillars provide a framework for initiatives to be implemented over the term of the Strategy, which include: Governance, Talent, Innovation, Business Development, and Place. The Strategy will be implemented by the Government of Abu Dhabi and by sector partners. The vision is to position CCI as a critical contributor to live ability and vitality in the community, and to economic development and diversification, including job creation.  Dubai Creative Economy Strategy: The Dubai Creative Economy Strategy aims to double the contribution of the creative industries to the GDP of Dubai from 2.6 per cent in 2020 to 5 per cent by 2025. It also seeks to more than double the number of Dubai-based creative companies from 8,300 in 2020 to 15,000 by 2025, and more than double the number of creators based in the emirate, from 70,000 in 2020 to 140,000 by 2025. The Dubai Creative Economy Strategy aims to transform the emirate Dubai into an international destination for creativity and the capital of creative economy by 2025. The Dubai Creative Economy Strategy aims to double the contribution of the creative industries to the GDP of Dubai from 2.6 per cent in 2020 to 5 per cent by 2025. It also seeks to more than double the number of Dubai-based creative companies from 8,300 in 2020 to 15,000 by 2025, and more than double the number of creators based in the emirate, from 70,000 in 2020 to 140,000 by 2025. Under the strategy, creativity covers several fields which include: o	publishing o	writing o	print and audio-visual media such as cinema, music and video o	artistic and cultural industries o	cultural heritage museums o	historical sites o	archives o	major cultural events o	libraries o	software and videogame industry.  It also includes design in all of its many variations, whether related to fashion, gaming, software, or architecture. Measures to achieve the objectives of the strategy To achieve the objectives of creative economy, Dubai will: o	roll out the requisite legislative, investment and technical framework to support the creative community in Dubai o	provide flexible packages, incentives and advanced creative incubators to maintain pace with the rapid technological developments o	provide a suitable and stimulating climate for creatives to generate added economic value, by integrating creativity with capital investment opportunities with distinguished returns. Dubai will also contribute significantly to diversifying and accelerating an economy based on knowledge, innovation and creativity.
Results: The UAE has achieved significant results through its cultural and creative industries strategies, reflecting a commitment to economic diversification and enhancing its global profile. The cultural and creative sectors have become increasingly vital to the UAE's GDP, driven by initiatives like the Dubai Design District (d3) and Abu Dhabi's Cultural Foundation, which have attracted international talent and investment. Major cultural institutions, such as the Louvre Abu Dhabi and the upcoming Guggenheim Abu Dhabi, alongside various museums and galleries, have been established, contributing to a vibrant creative ecosystem that also boosts tourism and provides platforms for artists from around the world.  In addition to fostering a creative economy, the UAE's government has introduced policies to support this sector, exemplified by Dubai's designation as a UNESCO City of Design. This recognition highlights the country's commitment to a design-driven economy and community. The UAE also uses its cultural investments as a tool for soft power, strengthening international diplomatic relationships and enhancing its global image through cultural exchange programs and partnerships with global cultural institutions.
Recommandations: As the UAE's cultural and creative industries strategies are still in progress, several key conclusions and recommendations can guide their continued development and success. First, ongoing investment in cultural infrastructure is crucial, including expanding museums, galleries, and creative hubs. Encouraging public-private partnerships can enhance resource pooling and expertise. Supporting local talent remains a priority; expanding funding opportunities, training programs, and platforms for international exposure, as well as developing mentorship programs, will benefit emerging artists.

Title EN: Koulukino´s online service for film educatio
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture
SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Digital environment
Agency Implementation: School Cinema Association -Koulukino Association
Main Feature: The Koulukino Association generates educational learning materials related to both big-screen films and Finnish short and documentary films featured on the Koulukino VOD platform. These materials cater to all educational levels, from early childhood education and preschool to upper secondary education. The film-related learning materials are available on the Koulukino website, free of charge for non-commercial use. The purpose of these learning materials is to enhance film literacy as well as broader digital literacy.   The Koulukino website, which contains approximately 800 pedagogical materials, serves as a comprehensive online service and a learning environment in itself. The methods of processing the films vary considerably depending on the target group and the themes of the learning material. For example, the films and the learning materials could be used as a tool for practising information retrieval, or for developing group work or emotional skills. Starting point is film is a brilliant pedagogical tool. It provides various topics for discussion, introduces foreign cultures, offers the watcher powerful experiences and the chance to identify with the characters, and enhances one’s understanding of oneself and the surrounding world.  The films covered at the website are picked so that the service would include as wide variety of film culture as possible.
Results: Koulukino´s pedagogical film literacy materials are widely used in Finnish schools. During the period 2020-2023 materials have covered for example human rights education, global education and environmental education integrated with film literacy.

Title EN: La Bibliobici de Arequipa
Goal: Integrate Culture In Sustainable Development Frameworks
SDG: SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: National sustainable development policies and plans
Agency Implementation: Organized civil society linked to books and reading
Main Feature: The Bibliobici de Arequipa is a communal and itinerant library that has been touring the city's public spaces since 2017. It is constituted as a non-profit association, is directed by two reading mediators who in turn fulfill the functions of librarians, is supported by civil society and is self-managed thanks to the collaboration of citizens. Its purpose is to generate a meeting space where people can approach reading and promote ties between members of the community based on books. All this with the purpose of promoting reading as a sociocultural activity, promoting access to books and reading in a democratic way and strengthening the importance of the library in the community by developing lifelong learning, claiming their cultural rights and their rights to information and knowledge. The community that attends is made up of children and adolescents who participate mostly accompanied by their caregivers. Young people (high school or university students) who are interested in reading and writing and who do not have the resources to access their own books also attend. Some attendees are migrants or belong to other provinces in the region. Recently, the attendance of neurodiverse audiences has increased. The Bibliobici does not have its own premises or space and its itinerant nature allows it to adapt to different spaces for the benefit of the community, offering the following services: Loan of books in the "room" and at home, thematic exhibitions, reference service, reading circles, reading mediation sessions for the community (virtual and face-to-face), cultural walks,  practice of traditional games, reading mediation and training workshops for teachers and families, writing workshops and creation of cartonero books and cartonera publishing house.
Results: The activities and services offered by the library in an unconventional space have made it possible to create a place for children, adolescents and adults to approach reading freely. In turn, this has allowed them to change their vision of reading and understand it as a voluntary, community-based, and unschooled practice. The continuity of the activities and services offered have generated that the members of the library attend assiduously  In addition, there has been an appropriation of writing practices by users, which has allowed them to become authors and has led the library to create its own cardboard publishing house. Likewise, access to relevant, diverse and literary quality texts (bibliodiverse) allows different types of users to find readings that arouse their interest and connect with their particular trajectories and contexts.  The Biblio bice is a project that has been sustainable since 2017, and has been recognized by citizens, and by the Ministry of Culture, being a beneficiary of economic stimuli for culture on 3 occasions: 1.	Year 2018: "La Bibliobici de Arequipa: free and itinerant library",  2.	2021: "Reading communities" in which the project was presented as a natural person in the name of one of the associates, 3.	2023 was the project "Cartonera Words". In addition, she was a beneficiary of the 2021 Cultural Management Competitive Funds organized by the Provincial Municipality of Arequipa with the project: "Itinerant myths and legends"

Title EN: Le Plan sectoriel de l’éducation nationale
Goal: Integrate Culture In Sustainable Development Frameworks
SDG: SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: National sustainable development policies and plans
Agency Implementation: Ministère de l’Education Nationale
Main Feature: Le Plan sectoriel de l’éducation 2020-2029 de la République centrafricaine introduit l’enseignement en langue sango au cycle primaire.   La République Centrafricaine se distingue de la plupart des autres pays d'Afrique subsaharienne par l'utilisation quasi-généralisée d'une langue vernaculaire nationale, le sango (voir §I.5.3), ce qui faciliterait grandement l’enseignement en langue nationale. Le Ministère a déjà pris un arrêté pour autoriser une expérimentation de l’utilisation du sango comme langue d’enseignement. L’Institut National de la Recherche et de l’Animation Pédagogique est chargé d'élaborer les documents pédagogiques nécessaires et vient de mettre en place un groupe de travail pour l'enseignement en sango, auquel participe l’ONG Siriri. Celle-ci a acquis, depuis 2015, de l’expérience dans l’enseignement en sango dans des écoles de deux préfectures de l’ouest du pays.  L’introduction de l’enseignement dans la langue vernaculaire du pays lors des premières années du cycle primaire doit se faire en fonction de l’objectif premier d’améliorer l’apprentissage de la lecture et de l’écriture par les enfants. Aussi, le sango qui sera utilisé comme langue d’enseignement doit être celui qui est compris et accessible au plus grand nombre. Un effet secondaire de l’enseignement en sango sera de promouvoir et diffuser une langue vraiment commune à l’ensemble des centrafricains (un sango unifié). Il sera donc possible, dans un second temps, d’introduire progressivement des variations dans la langue pour progresser vers le sango académique. Le Plan prévoit également de développer une politique des manuels scolaires et du livre. Un objectif de cette politique sera de doter chaque élève d’un nombre suffisant de manuels pour les disciplines fondamentales (lecture, mathématiques, sciences), en fonction des priorités d’enseignement. À cette fin, des ratios élèves/manuel devront être fixés pour chaque niveau scolaire ; ces ratios nationaux devraient conduire à l’élimination des inégalités entre les régions. Notons que ces objectifs ne pourront être atteints que si les coûts unitaires des manuels sont drastiquement revus à la baisse. Enfin, la politique nationale du livre doit prévoir de (i) mettre en place et équiper des bibliothèques scolaires dans les établissements des cycles primaire et secondaire ; (ii) développer et mettre à la disposition des élèves des livres destinés à renforcer les capacités de lecture. Lors de la première année du cycle Fondamental 1, par exemple, chaque élève devrait avoir accès à des séries de livres de lecture nivelés, c’est-à-dire gradués par niveaux d’acquisition de l’apprentissage de la lecture, avec d’abord un vocabulaire simple puis l’introduction d’une plus grande richesse lexicale, pour permettre aux élèves de développer progressivement leurs compétences.  Dans ce document stratégique, on note la promotion de la recherche scientifique et l’innovation technologique. Selon la Stratégie de la Science, Technologie et Innovation pour l’Afrique pour 2024 (STI), « L’Agenda [2063 de l’Union Africaine] souligne […] que la croissance soutenue, la compétitivité et la mutation économique de l’Afrique nécessiteront des investissements durables dans les nouvelles technologies et des innovations continues dans les domaines tels que l’agriculture, les énergies propres, l’éducation et la santé ».  Il est également précisé dans la stratégie STI pour l’Afrique que « se préparer à appuyer l’innovation et à faciliter les activités économiques nécessite des infrastructures à l’égard de l’accès à l’internet à large bande, des services élémentaires de télécommunication, l’approvisionnement fiable en électricité, en eau, de bons réseaux de transport, des équipements de laboratoire et des systèmes fiscaux harmonisés afin de soutenir l’innovation dans le secteur privé » . Toutes ces infrastructures sont en nombre insuffisant en RCA. Il est donc nécessaire d’adopter une stratégie très pragmatique et adaptée au contexte centrafricain pour la recherche scientifique et l’innovation technologique. Celle-ci devra passer par le développement de partenariat stratégiques avec les universités internationales, dont celles du continent africain. En effet, « les sciences sont le fruit d’une entreprise internationale, et la collaboration en matière de recherche est un facteur important de réussite » ( Stratégie de la Science, Technologie et Innovation pour l’Afrique pour 2024 (p.18)).La Politique Nationale de la Recherche Scientifique et de l’Innovation Technologique (PNRSIT, 2020-2030) de la République centrafricaine recommande : (i) la mise en place d’un Conseil National de la Recherche Scientifique et de l’Innovation Technologique (CNRSIT) afin de renforcer la coordination des activités de recherche, et (ii) le développement des partenariats bilatéraux pour favoriser l’introduction de nouvelles technologies. Il est ajouté ici que, pour promouvoir la recherche scientifique et l’innovation technologique, une étude devrait être menée pour évaluer les besoins nationaux de transfert de technologies dans tous les secteurs porteurs de l’économie. Cette évaluation permettrait de faire des préconisations sur les programmes de recherche crédibles et viables qui devraient être développés pour répondre aux besoins prioritaires de la RCA. En effet, cette politique permettra de créer en République Centrafricaine un environnement encourageant les individus et les groupes sociaux non seulement à créer, produire, diffuser et distribuer leurs propres expressions culturelles et à y avoir accès, en tenant dûment compte des conditions et besoins particuliers des femmes, ainsi que de divers groupes sociaux, y compris les personnes appartenant aux minorités et les peuples autochtones, mais aussi, à avoir accès aux diverses expressions culturelles provenant de notre territoire ainsi que des autres pays du monde.
Results: Chaque année scolaire, le Ministère organise une semaine culturelle. Mais les domaines de création dans le secteur de la culture ne sont pas encore entrés dans la mise en œuvre de cette politique.

Title EN: la décentralisation et la démocratisation de l’offre des espaces culturels
Goal: Integrate Culture In Sustainable Development Frameworks
SDG: SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: National sustainable development policies and plans
Agency Implementation: Kota Guira et La Tomie
Main Feature: Selon l’article 27 de la Déclaration universelle des droit de l’homme, « toute personne a le droit de prendre part librement à la vie culturelle de la communauté, de jouir des arts et de participer au progrès scientifique et aux biens qui en résultent ». La protection et la promotion de la culture est un impératif des droits humains. Le droit de participer à la vie culturelle garantit à chacun le droit d’accéder à la culture, au patrimoine culturel et aux expressions culturelles, d’y participer et d’en jouir. La pleine réalisation de ce droit dépend de mesures concrètes pour la conservation, le développement et la diffusion de la culture.   La gouvernance nationale ou locale requiert une responsabilité conjointe des citoyens, de la société civile, du secteur privé et du Gouvernement. La participation des citoyens à la vie culturelle peut renvoyer à la fois aux pratiques culturelles, aux pratiques artistiques, à la fréquentation des équipements culturels, à la concertation autour des politiques culturelles.  C’est dans cet ordre d’idée que deux opérateurs Culturels ont créé respectivement deux Centres Culturels en dehors de la Capitale Bangui. Il s’agit du centre socioculturel la Tomie et Kota Guira qui sont situés à Sibut dans la préfecture de la Kemo.
Results: Ces deux centres aujourd’hui contribuent à l’intérieur du pays  à la promotion et à la dynamisation des activités artistiques et culturelles pour le développement des communautés, en mettant à leur disposition des structures d’accès aux œuvres littéraires et artistiques, en s’appuyant sur les ressources sociales et les valeurs culturelles du terroir pour restaurer  et intégrer les communautés, en assurant la production et ou la coproduction des spectacles et en accueillant des artistes en résidence de création.

Title EN: La fabrique des résidences

SDG: SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 10 - Reduce inequality within and among countries,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development

Cultural Domain: Performing Arts,Media Arts,Cinema and Audiovisual Arts,Music,Publishing,Visual Arts

Main Feature: Le dispositif La Fabrique des résidences s’adresse à tous les postes du réseau, Instituts français, Alliances Françaises et centres binationaux, quelle que soit leur géographie. Il a pour objectif d’accompagner le réseau culturel de la conception jusqu’à la mise en œuvre de nouveaux programmes de résidences pérennes, ou sur une phase d’évolution d’un programme existant.
Results: Depuis sa création en 2018 et à travers 5 éditions, La Fabrique des résidences a permis de développer 30 programmes de résidences dans 24 pays et a ainsi offert l’opportunité à 145 artistes d’en bénéficier.
Financial Ressources: 261 000 USD par an.
Recommandations: L’appel à projets a été repensé en 2023 dans une perspective de financement pluriannuel sur trois ans pour permettre aux postes : •	De développer un ensemble de bonnes pratiques autour de l’accueil en résidence d’artistes, de créateurs ou de créatrices ; •	De structurer leur programme de résidence dans le temps et sur leur territoire ; •	De mettre en œuvre une dynamique de développement et une construction partenariale au service de la pérennisation du programme de résidence ; •	De rejoindre à moyen terme un réseau de résidences au sein du réseau diplomatique où seront partagées expériences, compétences et actions de communication.

Title EN: LA PAZ INTERNATIONAL THEATER FESTIVAL – FITAZ “THEATRE FOR PEACE IN THE WORLD”
Goal: Achieve A Balanced Flow Of Cultural Goods And Services And Increase The Mobility Of Artists And Cultural Professionals
SDG: SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 10 - Reduce inequality within and among countries,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Flow of cultural goods and services
Agency Implementation: FITAZ, Grito Theater (Carmen Guillén Ortúzar), Casa Grito (Mariel Camacho Ovando)
Main Feature: The La Paz International Theatre Festival – FITAZ is one of the most important biennial events in Bolivia, with 25 years of experience, it brings together national and international theatre companies, prioritising the quality of the shows to offer a programme in line with the diversity of audiences in the city of La Paz. The various editions have seen the participation of national and international works aimed at adult audiences, children and adolescents; both works for theatres and works for the street and for non-conventional spaces. FITAZ was named Intangible Cultural Heritage of the Municipality of La Paz by the Autonomous Municipal Government of La Paz in 2018, and in 2022 its social and cultural contribution was recognized by the Senate of the Plurinational State of Bolivia. In the 2024 edition, the festival was one of the projects benefiting from the Ibero-American Performing Arts Aid Fund IBERESCENA. The countries that have participated in FITAZ in its 25 years of existence, in addition to Bolivia, are: Germany, Argentina, Australia, Brazil, Chile, Costa Rica, Cuba, Congo, Colombia, Denmark, Ecuador, Egypt, El Salvador, Spain, Slovenia, United States, France, Italy, India, Indonesia, Japan, Malaysia, Mexico, Nicaragua, Netherlands, Paraguay, Peru, Portugal, Sweden, Switzerland, Taiwan, Uruguay and Venezuela. FITAZ opened its first version on March 17, 1999, at the Municipal Theater of La Paz, becoming the first International Theater Festival of La Paz, FITAZ. The first in the city and the second in the country.
Results: In the 25 years of history of the festival since 1999, 14 editions have been held (biannually), with the participation of 33 countries plus Bolivia over these years. More than 560 plays have been presented (162 international, 262 national and more than 138 training events and complementary to the theatre performances). More than 30 different spaces have been used for theatre performances (municipal, state, independent, self-managed, alternative stages, district houses, squares) The festival also has a qualitative aspect, becoming a platform that promotes the visibility of national and international theatrical proposals. It is a meeting place for diverse audiences with the works, their themes and aesthetics, which generates greater access and participation of diverse audiences with the performing arts, as well as creating conditions for performing artists to share their work. It also links objectives in relation to artistic exchanges, international circulation and collaborative and co-production articulation. Each edition generates significant economic activity, as it demands the provision of inputs and services in different sectors linked, for example, to the hotel, gastronomy, tourism, technical services, artistic services, transportation, among others. However, we believe that the fundamental value of FITAZ is based on the opportunity it represents (for its managers and artists) to influence the daily lives of people who come to this festival as an audience, thus contributing to promoting their access and participation in cultural and artistic life, to that extent and from a comprehensive perspective, to improve their quality of life. But also, the opportunity for audiences to encounter diverse theatrical languages from Latin America and the world, to enter dialogue with artistic proposals from other symbolic territories, to broaden their own frameworks of interpretation, meanings and senses, also fundamental to promote inter-territorial and intercultural dialogue, the basis for coexistence and sustainable development. For this reason, we firmly believe that holding this festival is not only a necessity, but rather a social, cultural and political responsibility. In recent editions, more than 40 activities have been held, including presentations in theatres, neighbourhoods, cultural spaces, information activities and discussions, involving more than a hundred artists and nearly 10,000 people directly involved in each edition of the event.

Title EN: La prise en compte de la culture dans la décentralisation
Goal: Integrate Culture In Sustainable Development Frameworks
SDG: SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: National sustainable development policies and plans
Cultural Domain: Design,Performing Arts,Media Arts,Cinema and Audiovisual Arts,Music,Publishing,Visual Arts
Agency Implementation: Bureau de Stratégie et de Développement (BSD) du Ministère de la Culture, du Tourisme et de l’Artisanat
Main Feature: La décentralisation en République de Guinée est régie par la loi ordinaire l/2017/040/AN du 24 février 2017, portant code révisé des collectivités locales.  La mise en œuvre de cette loi a conduit à l’organisation intégrale du territoire en Régions, Communes urbaines et Communes Rurales. Pour le bon fonctionnement des collectivités territoriales, l’Etat, de façon progressive, a transféré des compétences et des ressources dans plusieurs domaines dont celui de la culture.  Dans le secteur de la culture, la décentralisation a été marquée par un transfert de compétences et de ressources de l’Etat aux Collectivités territoriales à travers le décret D/2017/197/PRG/SGG du 28 juillet 2017. Des services de la culture ont été mis en place dans les différentes régions et préfectures de Guinée, bénéficiant d’une subvention annuelle de 431 000 USD.  Malgré les efforts consentis par les acteurs, les faiblesses de la décentralisation ont été relevées dans le processus de l’application du décret à travers l’état des lieux qui a été réalisé en 2020. Dans le secteur de la culture, les faiblesses suivantes ont été constatées, notamment :   -	la faible appropriation et prise en charge des compétences transférées par les élus locaux ;  -	la faible allocation budgétaire dans les plans communaux et régionaux ; -	la méconnaissance des potentialités culturelles locales destinées au développement des arts et de la culture ; -	le faible soutien des partenaires locaux aux activités culturelles initiées au niveau local ;  -	les difficultés de gestion des ressources transférées telles que la construction des infrastructures artistiques et culturelles ; -	l’insuffisance des ressources humaines et matérielles pour la mise en œuvre des activités artistiques et culturelles ; -	la faiblesse de la créativité entrepreneuriale au niveau local.  Au regard de ces faiblesses constatées, il est important de renforcer les capacités des collectivités territoriales pour une meilleure prise en compte de la culture dans leurs programmes de développement local et d’investissement pour matérialiser l’effectivité des compétences transférées et cela s’ajoute une gestion efficace des ressources transférées dans le domaine de la construction des infrastructures culturelles. A cet effet, l’Etat a mis en place un Fonds national de développement local (FNDL) et un Fonds de Développement Local (FODEL) consacrés au développement socio-économique et culturel des collectivités locales pour la période 2020-2024.  Les résultats attendus dans la mise en place de ces fonds est de prendre en compte dans les planifications communales et régionales les besoins et les préoccupations des arts et de la culture pour un développement harmonieux.
Results: La mise en œuvre de cette mesure a permis d’atteindre, sur la période de 2020 à 2024, les résultats suivants :  sur le plan institutionnel :  -	les secteurs culturels et créatifs sont pris en compte dans les plans de développement local et d’investissement de la majorité des communes urbaines et rurales de la République de Guinée au nombre de 370 ; -	les secteurs culturels et créatifs sont pris en compte dans les nouveaux plans régionaux de développement (2020-2024) de toutes les régions des collectivités territoriales ;  -	des services préfectoraux et régionaux de la Culture, du Tourisme et de l’Artisanat sont mis en place depuis 2022 ; -	des réseaux des faitières (OSC Culturelle) sont mis en place dans la plupart des communes urbaines et rurales. Sur les plans technique et financier : -	l’existence d’une ligne budgétaire destinée aux activités artistiques et culturelles des collectivités locales depuis 2022.  Sur le plan infrastructurel et celui des ressources humaines : -	les ressources financières pour la réalisation des infrastructures artistiques et culturelles sont transférées aux collectivités conformément au plan d’investissement ; -	deux (2) salles de cinéma sont en cours de réalisation au Km 36 et à Dubréka ; -	les capacités des acteurs pour la mise en œuvre des activités artistiques et culturelles sont renforcées grâce à des sessions de formation et de mise à niveau ; -	au niveau local, le développement de l’entrepreneurial a rehaussé l’implication des faitières (OSC Culturelles).
Financial Ressources: Le Fonds de Développement Local (FODEL) est alimenté par 1% du chiffre d’affaires des exploitants d’or et du diamant et 0,5 % du chiffre d’affaires des exploitants des autres substances minières dont la bauxite et le fer. Quant au Fonds national de développement local (FNDL), il est alimenté par 15% des revenus miniers collectés (précisément sur 6 taxes et redevances).

Title EN: Policies and Measures that Support the Development of the Publishing Industry
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture
SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Cultural and creative sectors
Agency Implementation: 1. Ministry of Education, Culture, Research, and Technology  2 . Ministry of Finance National Library of Indonesia  3. Provincial Government of DKI Jakarta
Main Feature: In the past four years, policies and measures that support the development of the publishing industry include:  1. Law 3 of 2017 on the Bookkeeping System (Law on Bookkeeping);  2. Draft Law on Amendments to Law 3 of 2017 the Bookkeeping System (Draft Law on Bookkeeping);  3. Government Regulation 75 of 2019 on the Implementation Regulation of Law 3 of 2017 on the Bookkeeping System (GR on Bookkeeping Implementation);   4. Government Regulation 49 of 2022 on Value Added Tax Exempted and Value Added Tax or Value Added Tax and Sales Tax on Luxury Goods Not Charged on the Import and/or Delivery of Certain Taxable Goods and/or Delivery of Certain Taxable Services and/or Utilization of Certain Taxable Services from Outside the Customs;   5. Minister of Finance Regulation 5/PMK.010/2020 of 2020 on General Textbooks, Holy Books, and Religious Textbooks whose Import and/or Delivery are Exempt from Value Added Taxes;  6. Ubud Writers and Readers Festival (UWRF);   7. Makassar International Writers Festival (MIWF);   8. Indonesia International Book Fair (IIBF);   9. Jakarta International Literary Festival (JILF);   10. Participation in the 2022 London Book Fair;  11.Hosting of the 33rd International Publishers Congress;  12.National Library digital services; and  13. Indonesian Bookkeeping Information System (Sistem Informasi Perbukuan Indonesia, SIBI).  Several policies and measures reported in the 2020 QPR, namely: (1) Law on Bookkeeping, (2) UWRF, (3) MIWF, (4) IIBF, (5) JILF, (6) participation in the London Book Fair, and (7) National Library digital services, are still valid/ongoing at the time this report was drafted, although activities were hampered or temporarily stopped due to the COVID-19 pandemic. Regarding the Law on Bookkeeping, stakeholders have identified a real need from the field to update this Law so that it is more responsive to current developments and all its challenges and opportunities. Even though the Draft Law on Bookkeeping has been registered with the National Legislation Program, it is not yet a priority for completion in 2024.  In recent developments since the COVID-19 pandemic, UWRF has been held annually. In 2021, UWRF took place from 8-17 October, thanks to a collaboration with Writing Western Australia. The festival's theme was taken from the Hindu-Balinese philosophy “Mulat Sarira,” which means self-reflection. In 2022, UWRF was held on 27–30 October with the theme "Memayu Hayuning Bawana" from an ancient Javanese philosophy, which means the principles used to care for, protect, and beautify the universe. Meanwhile, to mark its 20th-anniversary celebration in 2023, UWRF was held on October 18-22 with the theme "Atita, Wartamana, Anagata: Past, Present, Future."  On the other hand, in 2020-2021, MIWF continued to hold regular discussions by presenting national and local writers through virtual spaces to actively build networks with the theme "MIWF Memory Project." Monthly activities held by MIWF started in July 2020, inviting various parties to work together to create a meeting and discussion space amidst various limitations. In collaboration with Indonesia Tera and Patjarmerah, in October 2020, the MIWF Memory Project presented book discussions from young writers from Eastern Indonesia. MIWF began to run normally, starting June 23-26, 2022.  For IIBF, activities continued to be held during the pandemic, although in 2020, it was held virtually for ten days, and in 2021-2022, it was held on a hybrid basis in collaboration with market workshops. In 2023, the Indonesian Publishers Association (Ikatan Penerbit Indonesia, IKAPI) held the 43rd IIBF from September 27 to October 1 with the theme "It's Time to Read!" The 2023 IIBF was held offline with guests of honor from Korea. Various events such as discussions, book launches, author meetings, literacy tours, and cosplay enliven IIBF. The Indonesia Rights Fair, a side event for copyright transactions, was held for three days (27-29 September 2023).   Then, JILF, which only started in 2019, had to go on hiatus for two years from 2020 to 2021. As a place to introduce and increase collaboration between writers and publishers from within and outside the country, especially from countries in the Southern Hemisphere, JILF was only held again on 22-26 October 2022 at Taman Ismail Marzuki. As for the London Book Fair, participation only began to be facilitated again on April 5-7, 2022.  Meanwhile, besides the Indonesia Onesearch website, the National Library digital services are now also available through a special iPusnas application. Books in the iPusnas catalog are slightly different from the collections in the national library catalog. Books on iPusnas tend to be general reading books such as novels, comics, and self-motivation. Meanwhile, in Indonesia Onesearch, we can find other collections besides books, such as maps, and we can even watch films. iPusnas itself is designed with social media features that interest young users, such as following, chatting, rating, sharing reading book recommendations, and bookshelf features.  One policy that has not been reported in the 2020 QPR is GR on Bookkeeping Implementation. This GR is used as a measure and criterion for obtaining manuscripts and publishing books to produce quality books. With this GR, there is a professional certification program for bookkeeping professionals whose provision is tailored to their respective fields of expertise and professional bookkeeping organizations. This GR also regulates that the mentoring and capacity building of bookkeepers needs to be carried out on an ongoing basis by professional organizations, the Central Government, and regional governments.  Another policy that can be reported is Government Regulation 49 of 2022 on Value Added Tax Exempted and Value Added Tax or Value Added Tax and Sales Tax on Luxury Goods Not Charged on the Import and/or Delivery of Certain Taxable Goods and/or Delivery of Certain Taxable Services and/or Utilization of Certain Taxable Services from Outside the Customs (see Goal 2, Policies that Support a Balanced Flow of International Cultural Goods and Services). Part of the regulation that is relevant to the development of the publishing industry is the exemption of general textbooks, including educational books and general books containing elements of arts and culture education, from the imposition of value-added tax. More technical regulations are further stipulated in Minister of Finance Regulation 5/PMK.010/2020 of 2020 on General Textbooks, Holy Books, and Religious Textbooks whose Import and/or Delivery are Exempt from Value Added Taxes.  As for measures, one of the newest is hosting the 33rd International Publishers Congress on 10-12 November 2022 in Jakarta. This congress presented discussion sessions on "Books for Children: Future-proofing Tomorrow's Readers" and "Transformation: Future of Creative Industry & Content Development." This congress is a joint work between the Provincial Government of DKI Jakarta through the Office of Tourism and Creative Economy with the International Publishers Association (IPA), IKAPI, the Jakarta Book City Committee, and the Jakarta Experience Board (JXB).  The final reportable measure is SIBI. SIBI is a Kemendikbudristek website under the management of the Book Center, which started in 2021 and opened access to the public, especially students, teachers, and parents, to books from PAUD to upper secondary level that have passed the Book Center assessment. The three categories of books available are (1) Merdeka Curriculum textbooks (published in 2021), (2) 2013 Curriculum textbooks (published in 2013), and (3) non-text books (complementary learning books), including arts and culture textbooks and literary works. The entire collection is available in electronic form, while some are also available in audio and/or interactive form. Besides being based on grade level, book selection is also available for seven levels of reading proficiency, from Early Readers (A) to Advanced Readers (E).  In general, policies and measures that support the development of the publishing industry are aimed at contributing to achieving the following agenda(s) of the National Strategy for Culture:  1. Provide space for the diversity of cultural expressions and encourage cultural interaction to strengthen the inclusiveness of culture (Agenda 1);  2. Develop and utilize cultural resources to strengthen the position of Indonesia internationally (Agenda 3);  3. Utilize objects of culture advancement to improve people’s welfare (Agenda 4);  4. Institutional reform and culture budgeting to support the culture advancement agenda (Agenda 6); and  5.Strengthen the role of the government as a facilitator of culture advancement (Agenda 7).
Results: UWRF: 1. In 2021, 130 speakers attended offline in Ubud, as well as many others online. 2. In 2023, it featured more than 200 speakers and attracted more than 15,000 visitors.  2020 MIWF: Received the International Excellence Award for the best literary festival in 2020 from the London Book Fair.  IIBF: 1. In 2020, there were 175 participant booths, both for selling physical books, transacting copyrights, and exhibiting programs and activities. A total of 150 performers participated in the activity as resource persons, including writers, designers, book activists, writers, librarians, and teachers. Meanwhile, the number of events reached 79 activities. 2. Successfully sold more book titles through the Indonesia Book Partnership program, from 42 book titles in 2019 increasing to 60 book titles in 2023. 3. The number of overseas participants had also increased, from only 6-7 participants in 2020-2022 to 15 participants from 15 foreign countries in 2023. 4. In 2023, more than 60 publishers/literary agencies from 15 countries attended the Indonesia Rights Fair.  2022 JILF: Presenting 25 authors, 11 communities, and 41 program events such as discussions, book markets, work readings, children's stories, coffee shops, exhibitions, theater performances, and music.  Participation in the 2022 London Book Fair: Participation from 10 co-exhibitors from Indonesia was facilitated, namely eight publishers (Mizan Pustaka, Gagas Media, Gramedia International, Kanisius, Afterhours Book, re:ON Comics, Pustaka Obor Indonesia Foundation, and Zikrul Bestari) and two literacy bodies (Borobudur Agency and Literasia Creativa). The Indonesian contingent brought around 260 book titles, which were divided into four large categories, namely children's books, fiction, non-fiction, and comics.  National Library digital services: In 2024, Indonesia Onesearch will have more than 12.7 million entries from 3,316 institutions, 4,542 libraries, and 12,092 repositories, up more than 3 million entries from 2020.  SIBI: When drafting this report, it was recorded that 2,039 books were available, 4,927,068 books were read, and 1,532,878 books were downloaded.
Financial Ressources: MIWF:  In 2022, funds from the Central Government amounted to IDR 130,000,000./ 7.968,18 USD In 2023, funds from the Central Government amounted to IDR 134,000,000, / 8.213,35 USD and from the regional government, IDR 10,000,000. / 612.94 USD

Title EN: Largo Residências
Goal: Integrate Culture In Sustainable Development Frameworks
SDG: SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: National sustainable development policies and plans
Cultural Domain: Design,Performing Arts,Media Arts,Cinema and Audiovisual Arts,Music,Publishing,Visual Arts
Agency Implementation: SOU LARGO, crl
Main Feature: LARGO Residências aims to contribute to local development, through the concretization of cultural activities and social businesses, boosters in artistic creation and stimulation, as well as boosters for community involvement and integration. This is done in a continuity and growth logic, so that they allow for the assurance of their own simultaneous sustainability. In 2011, it was situated in Largo do Intendente (Lisbon), where it developed its cultural activities of social inclusion and local development. The main goal is to promote culture, creativity and knowledge as decisive factors for success and sustainability of the processes of social and urbanistic regeneration. By providing conditions for research and creation to artists that want to reside here, the focus of this project is to sustain a building ready to take in and produce works from particularly distinct artistic areas - generally, from the cultural and creative sector. The focus is also to receive research projects and academic work from fields as diverse as anthropology, sociology, psychology or architecture. In this scenario, the technical and production means necessary are assured, as well as specialised knowledge, which will allow the successful monitoring and execution of each project. The creative basis of each proposal needs to include at least one of the following inspiring and critical points: the physical and humane property of the neighbourhood. The social and economic sustainability in LARGO Residências resides in an economic ecosystem, supported by three social businesses: the residencies, the cafe and the store. These constitute complementary pieces of the same building, where artists coexist - resident or not - and are involved in the creative side of the project, and visitors who are, initially, just passing, later deciding to stay because they recognise themselves in LARGO’s philosophy. This allows for unique and enriching experience and trade, in a format that allows for the sustainability of this project as a whole: the social businesses sustain the cultural and social activities of the collective. Currently, the collective constitutes the fundamental bridge between the cultural events that take place in its quarters, the artists with whom it establishes collaborations of various natures and the community in which it is inserted. In this way, LARGO contributes to the process of urban and social regeneration, in a conversation and contemplation dynamic, aware of the developments observed in the aforementioned geographic environment. The cultural activity taking place in Largo Residências intends, in a maximal inclusion approach, to cross old and new residents, both national and foreign, attracting new audiences to whom it is interesting and important to show how these cosmopolitan cities live and breathe, in a profound and fast transformation. Since October 2022 the old and vacant GNR (Portuguese national gendarmerie force) barracks was adopted to implement this project and convert it in a place for citizenship, culture and inclusion. This was made possible thanks to an initial coordination with civil society and the state. After having to leave this new space, after consultation with the government and the social sector this initiative continues to revitalize and create a new cultural and community center (Jardins do Bombarda).
Results: LARGO aimed to have a social, cultural, local and environmental impact. After almost 13 years of activity there were more than 900 events and education programs organized with socio-cultural partners and more than 40.000 visitors. The permanent space housed 40 different socio-cultural projects (both group and individual projects) involving 190 workers. More than 4500 artists and cultural workers (local, national and international) were engaged, more than 4000 community participants, more than 2000 cultural activities (creation, programming, education and investigation) and 60 case study lectures/talks were organized. Furthermore, the Largo, crl reports that in terms of employment they have generated 49 work contracts, 67 service providers, 64 temporary internships/supported employment and 1,000 one-off service providers. In total the activity generated 1.414.868 USD (1.300.000 €) turnover for the resident cultural entities. The project has been widely recognized and got different awards.
Recommandations: The inclusion of citizens in vulnerable conditions (people experiencing homelessness or refugees); integration and giving voice to groups of activists for different causes (climate, gender, etc), local development and engagement with neighbors and social partners (creating a safe, democratic, intergenerational and multicultural place).

Cet établissemnt a formé depuis sa création jusqu’à 1999, plus de cinq cent (500) Cadres moyens recrutés à base du Brevet d’Etude du Premier Cycle (BEPC) comme diplôme d’entrée dans les différents domaines du secteur des arts et de la culture : arts appliqués, arts dramatiques, arts audiovisuels, muséographie, etc.  C’est en 2011 que le Département en charge des Arts et de la Culture a revu le programme de formation de l’Ecole, en inscrivant dans le système de Licence –Master- Doctorat (LMD) en partenariat avec l’Université de Bangui. Title EN: Lausanne Méditerranées
Goal: Achieve A Balanced Flow Of Cultural Goods And Services And Increase The Mobility Of Artists And Cultural Professionals
SDG: SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 10 - Reduce inequality within and among countries,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Mobility of artists and cultural professionals
Cultural Domain: Performing Arts,Cinema and Audiovisual Arts,Music,Visual Arts
Agency Implementation: Ville de Lausanne
Main Feature: Lausanne Méditerranées présente différents aspects du monde méditerranéen aux Lausannoises et Lausannois et permet de mieux faire connaître les personnes et populations issues de pays méditerranéens présentes à Lausanne. Les premières éditions ont permis d’explorer le Maghreb (2017), la Grèce (2018), l’Albanie (2019) et le Liban (2023). Dès 2023, la participation culturelle est désormais placée au cœur de l'événement avec pour objectifs d’étendre son action en termes de territoires, de publics, de partenaires, de programmation et de gouvernance.   Un groupe de référence est constitué pour la mise en œuvre des différents temps de Lausanne Méditerranées. Il regroupe les associations du pays à l’honneur, des personnes relais, des partenaires culturels ainsi que des personnes originaires du pays à l’honneur vivant à Lausanne. Plusieurs services de la Ville de Lausanne sont également réunis dans le cadre d’un comité de pilotage : le Secrétariat municipal, le Service de la culture et le Bureau lausannois pour les immigrés. De 2023 à 2025, Lausanne Méditerranées est soutenu par le crédit de la Confédération destiné à l’intégration, dans le cadre de son programme « Nouveau Nous ».  Porté par la Ville de Lausanne depuis 2016, Lausanne Méditerranées est un focus culturel qui promeut la diversité et l'interculturalité. Organisée à l’automne, cette manifestation vise non seulement à marquer l’engagement de la Ville de Lausanne et ses liens internationaux, mais aussi à ouvrir un espace de partage avec les personnes et populations issues de la migration présentes à Lausanne. Lausanne Méditerranées est pensé comme un geste d’ouverture au monde, à la culture contemporaine des pays mis à l’honneur, ainsi qu’à l’interculturalité qui se tisse à Lausanne. Ce rendez-vous vise à promouvoir la diversité et le dialogue à travers une programmation intégrant spectacles, projections, concerts, performances, expositions, débats, conférences, rencontres, ateliers, marché et découvertes culinaires. Il se décline autour de trois axes : socio-politique, culturel et interculturel.
Results: Le projet est pensé tel un laboratoire qui s’implante dans le paysage lausannois des événements de la rentrée culturelle à l'automne.   Pour sa 4ème édition de Lausanne Méditerranées – qui s’est tenue du 30 septembre au 8 octobre 2023 (précédée d’un prologue depuis mi-septembre) – l’ambition a été d’associer plus intensément les communautés locales pour concevoir et programmer avec elles ce focus, valorisant le métissage créé par le double apport « ici » et « là-bas » et mettant ainsi en valeur les aspects de leur culture d'origine.  L'accent porté sur la participation culturelle a permis de réunir et de fédérer des personnes et des populations issues du Liban, ainsi que le plus grand nombre autour d’une programmation à la fois rassembleuse et ouverte.  L’événement a ainsi pu offrir de nouveaux terrains d’expression. Près de 3000 personnes ont pris part à l’une des 40 propositions (spectacles, concerts, ateliers, conférences, etc.) pour faire de cette semaine d’échange et de culture un véritable rendez-vous automnal tourné vers la Méditerranée.  En valorisant le processus autant que le résultat, l'objectif a été d’offrir une place à toute initiative, d’inclure et d’associer le plus grand nombre à la démarche. Co-construire, favoriser l’échange, faire dialoguer les cultures, stimuler le vivre ensemble, susciter de nouvelles synergies et garder une trace, sont autant d’objectifs poursuivis par Lausanne Méditerranées.

Title EN: Law on Cinema of Viet Nam 2022 (Law No. 05/2022/QH15 issued by the National Assembly on June 15, 2022)
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture
SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Cultural and creative sectors
Agency Implementation: Vietnamese agencies, organizations, and individuals participating in cinematographic activities in Viet Nam and abroad; foreign organizations and individuals participating in cinematographic activities in Vietnam; state management agencies; others
Main Feature: The Cinema Law 2022 inherits, amends, and supplements 32 articles and introduces 18 new articles compared to the previous Cinema Law. This law stipulates cinematographic activities, the rights, obligations, and responsibilities of agencies, organizations, and individuals participating in cinematographic activities, and the state management of cinematography. This law is applied to: (i) Vietnamese agencies, organizations, and individuals participating in cinematographic activities in Viet Nam and abroad; (ii) Foreign organizations and individuals participating in cinematographic activities in Viet Nam; and (iii) State management agencies in charge of cinematography; agencies, organizations, and individuals involved in cinematographic activities.  The Cinema Law 2022 comes into effect on January 1, 2023, with the aim of creating a groundbreaking legal framework with a long-term vision to develop cinematography into a true cultural industry and an economic sector in Viet Nam. Two significant amendments to the Cinematography Law 2022 include regulations on film dissemination on the Internet and the decentralization process, which involves assigning local authorities to establish a Film Appraisal and Rating Board. Specifically, the amendments include: - Managing the dissemination of films on the internet, implementing the necessary technical measures, and providing guidance to ensure that parents or guardians can effectively control and manage children's film viewing, thereby ensuring that children watch age-appropriate films online. - Stipulating the issuance of Film Classification Licenses, film appraisal, and classification: The law delegates authority to the provincial People's Committees to issue Film Classification Licenses, provided they comply with the regulations set forth by the Ministry of Culture, Sports, and Tourism. - Stipulating that films must be classified by content to ensure they are suitable for viewers of different ages. Additionally, a new classification category, "Type K," has been introduced: films that may be viewed by audiences under 13 years of age, provided they are accompanied by a parent or guardian.
Financial Ressources: State budget; income from services stipulated by regulations; sponsorship, aid, donations, and contributions from domestic and foreign organizations and individuals in accordance with the law; and other legitimate sources of revenue.

Title EN: Law on equal status and equal rights of the sexes
Goal: Promote Human Rights And Fundamental Freedoms
SDG: SDG 5 - Achieve gender equality and empower all women and girls,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels
Area of Monitoring: Gender equality
Cultural Domain: Design,Performing Arts,Media Arts,Cinema and Audiovisual Arts,Music,Publishing,Visual Arts
Agency Implementation: The Prime Ministers Ministry
Main Feature: The Law on equal status and equal rights of the sexes  entered into force on January 6, 2021. The aim of this law is to prevent discrimination based on gender and to establish and maintain equality and equal opportunities for the sexes in all areas of society. All people should have equal opportunities to enjoy their own energy and develop their talents, regardless of gender. Gender in this law refers to women, men and people with gender neutral registration in the national register, unless otherwise specifically stated . This goal shall be achieved by:     a. observe equality considerations and work towards the integration of gender and equality considerations in policy making and decisions in all areas of society,     b. work towards equal influence of women and men in society,     c. especially improve the position of women and increase their potential in society,     d. work against wage inequality and other discrimination based on gender in the labor market, i.a. by ensuring that companies and organizations meet the conditions of equal pay certification or equal pay confirmation,     e. enable everyone, regardless of gender, to balance family and professional life,     f. promote education on equality issues,     g. analyze statistical information by gender,     h. promote research in gender and equality studies,     i. work against gender-based violence, gender-based harassment and sexual harassment,     j. change traditional gender images and work against negative stereotypes about the roles of women and men,     k. promote that jobs are not classified into separate women's and men's jobs,     l. pay special attention to the status of people with gender-neutral registration in the national register,     m. work against multiple discrimination.
Results: At least once a year, a consultation forum on gender equality, the Equality Council, shall be convened, with representatives from the labor market, the academic community and organizations working on gender equality according to this law. The role of the consultation forum is to advise the Minister of Equality in professional policy-making in matters related to gender equality, and the minister shall meet once a year with the consultation forum. The consultation forum on equality issues, the Equality Council, submits minutes of its meetings to the minister. A summary of the meeting minutes of the consultation forum shall be published as attachments with the minister's report, which is published once per election period, cf. Article 12 Act on the Administration of Equality Matters. The ministry in charge of equality matters administers the consultation forum on equality issues, including advertising the consultation forum and giving parties the opportunity to request participation. Other tasks of the consultation forum are determined by the ministry as appropriate. The costs of the activities of the consultation forum are paid from the treasury. The Minister of Equality is authorized to award a special recognition of equality annually to the person, company, institution or organization that has excelled or made a mark in the field of equality. The ministry can request nominations, including from the consultation forum on equality issues, and is authorized to appoint a special selection committee to choose from the submitted nominations.  Article 25 Equality Congress.  The Minister shall convene an equality forum every two years, where gender equality shall be discussed. The ministry dealing with equality issues must ensure that the discussions of the parliament are compiled and handed over to the minister. The minister decides the program of the assembly each time. The assembly is open to everyone, but the ministry dealing with equality issues must invite members of parliament, representatives of state and local government institutions, including equality representatives, as well as representatives of the labor market and non-governmental organizations that have equality issues on their agenda. Sitting in the parliament is unpaid, but other necessary costs of the parliament are paid from the treasury according to the decision of the minister.  Article 26 Parliamentary resolution on implementation plan in gender equality issues.  Every four years, the Minister shall submit to Alþingi a proposal for a parliamentary resolution on an implementation plan for gender equality issues for four years at a time after receiving proposals from individual ministries and after consultation with the Office for Equality. Moreover, the discussions of the equality forum shall be taken into account, cf. Article 25 An implementation plan in gender equality matters shall include a project intended to ensure equal status and equal rights of the sexes in Icelandic society, cf. Article 1 Responsibility for the projects and their estimated costs must be specified in the implementation plan, together with how the success of the actions will be evaluated. Report on the status and development of equality issues, cf. Article 12 Act on the Administration of Equality Matters, shall be accompanied by a proposal for a parliamentary resolution on an implementation plan in gender equality matters.  Article 27 Equality representatives.  Every ministry must have an equality representative who has expertise in gender equality. The equality representative deals with and supervises equality work in the relevant ministry and its institutions, among which he must work on the integration of gender and equality perspectives in the ministry's issue area. The equality representative shall annually send the Equality Office a report on the status and development of gender equality issues in the relevant ministry's field of affairs.  Article 28 Participation in committees, councils and boards in the public sector.  When appointing to committees, councils and boards on behalf of the state and municipalities, it must be ensured that the ratio of women and men is as equal as possible and not less than 40% when there are more than three representatives. This also applies to boards of public limited companies and companies of which the state or municipality is the main owner. When nominating to committees, councils and boards on behalf of the state and municipalities, both men and women must be nominated. However, the nominating party is permitted to deviate from it when objective reasons lead to this not being possible. The nominator must then explain the reasons for this. The appointing party is permitted to deviate from the provisions of paragraph 1. if the exemption authority of paragraph 2. applies. This provision does not prevent the nomination and appointment of people with gender-neutral registration in the national register to committees, councils and boards in the public sector. This also applies to boards of public limited companies and companies of which the state or municipality is the main owner. However, the percentage of women must never be less than 40%.  Article 29 Analysis of statistical information.  In official statistics on individuals and in interviews and opinion polls, a distinction must be made between genders when collecting data, processing it and publishing information, unless special reasons, such as privacy interests, militate against it. Public bodies must also strive to differentiate between genders during all statistical processing, unless special reasons, such as privacy interests, militate against this.  Article 30 Integration of gender and equality perspectives.  The integration of gender and equality considerations must be taken into account in all policy making and planning carried out by ministries and public institutions operating in their field. The same applies to all decision-making within ministries and institutions, as applicable.

Main Feature: 'The "Let's Talk Art" initiative, launched by the Cultural Office of Her Highness Sheikha Manal bint Mohammed bin Rashid Al Maktoum, is a multifaceted program designed to promote art appreciation and cultural dialogue within the UAE. The initiative features interactive workshops, panel discussions, and exhibitions, with a particular focus on various art forms and techniques. One of the standout events focused on mural painting, bringing together renowned artists to lead hands-on sessions for participants. This event not only showcased the creative process behind mural art but also allowed participants to engage directly with artists, fostering a deeper understanding and appreciation of this art form. The program aims to bridge the gap between artists and the community, encouraging artistic expression and education.
Results: Since its inception, "Let's Talk Art" has successfully engaged a diverse audience, including artists, art enthusiasts, and members of the public. The initiative has significantly raised the profile of mural art in the UAE, providing artists with a prominent platform to display their work and interact with the community. Workshops and discussions have enhanced participants' understanding of artistic techniques and processes, contributing to the cultural and artistic development of the region. Moreover, the program has played a crucial role in fostering community spirit by bringing people together through shared artistic experiences. The increased visibility and appreciation of mural art have also encouraged more public art projects, enriching the cultural landscape of the UAE.

Establishing collaborations with international artists and art institutions could introduce new perspectives and elevate the program's profile globally. Additionally, implementing long-term community art projects, such as collaborative murals, could create lasting cultural landmarks and foster continuous community engagement.

Area of Monitoring: Cultural and creative sectors
Agency Implementation: MY World México
Main Feature: The Letter of the City of San Luis Potosí for Cultural Rights, agreed on the basis of the UNESCO San Luis initiative, is a commitment to the future in favour of the co-design and participatory construction of a new local regulation in terms of development and Cultural Rights, which takes as its starting point the international, national and state instruments of culture and Human Rights. The Letter has as its initial starting point the acceptance of the capital of the State of San Luis Potosí as a member of the IberCultura Viva Network of Cities and Local Governments of the Ibero-American General Secretariat, and has been developed in coordination with the UNESCO Offices in Mexico, the United Nations Action Campaign for Sustainable Development My World and under the strict observance of the State Commission of Human Rights of San Luis Potosí.  The Letter is a binding instrument, of local elaboration and international anchorage, which recognises the need and convenience of broadly integrating cultural governance, through the active participation of society, in the development of municipal regulations in the field of culture. Its main function is to recognise, protect and guarantee the full enjoyment of cultural rights for all inhabitants, visitors and people in transit in the capital city of Potosí.  Based on the Charter of the City for Cultural Rights, the City Council of San Luis Potosí (2018-2024) approves the Municipal Regulation of Culture and Cultural Rights.
Results: The Municipal Regulation remains in force and binding. The Citizen Council established in the Regulation was formed and operates, as well as the Thematic Cabinet for Cultural Mainstreaming, a collegiate and articulation space of the executive branch, which aims to ensure the incorporation of the cultural rights perspective and the cultural dimension of human rights in the totality of local public policy.  By mid-2022, it was recognised as one of the 50 Best Actions worldwide in favour of cultural rights in the context of the health crisis by the UCLG Committee on Culture; it was highlighted in the Biannual Report of Results of the UNESCO Office in Mexico for the period 2020-2021, in the Annual Report of Activities 2021 of the CEDH and in the book "ResiliArt100", UNESCO's preparatory publication for the World Conference on Cultural Policies and Sustainable Development, Mondiacult 2022. It is considered as a Good Practice by the UN MY World Campaign and by the IberCultura Viva Programme, directly inspiring Niterói, Rio de Janeiro, Brazil and Concepción, Chile, in the promotion and enactment of their respective declarations.

Parmi ces textes, figure le décret exécutif n° 06-218 fixant les conditions et modalités d'exercice de l'activité de promoteur de spectacles culturels.  Ce décret exécutif a pour objectif de se conformer à la politique culturelle nationale visant à générer des revenus, afin d’impliquer le secteur de la culture et des arts dans la dynamique économique nationale, en y intégrant des dispositions qui consistent à définir les conditions et modalités d’attribution de l’autorisation d’exercice de l’activité de promoteur de spectacles culturels et artistiques, opération de remise dont la gestion a été confiée à la Direction de l’Organisation de la Diffusion du Produit Culturel et Artistique (DODPCA). Le texte définit, avec précision et dans le détail, la qualité de promoteur de spectacles culturels, ainsi que toute personne physique ou morale concernée par l’organisation de prestations culturelles dans un cadre professionnel, précisant que l’exercice de cette activité est soumis à une licence préalable, délivrée par la Ministre chargée de la culture et des arts, ou par le directeur de la culture au niveau local. La durée de validité de cette licence n’excède pas trois (03) années renouvelables. Pour ce faire, un dossier est déposé auprès des services de la Direction de l’Organisation de la Diffusion du Produit Culturel et Artistique (DODPCA) qui devra comporter un document établissant la spécialisation de l’intéressé dans le domaine artistique. A rappeler que pour tout renouvellement, le dépôt du document doit se faire six (06) mois avant sa date d’expiration. Les activités culturelles et artistiques sont organisées conformément au cahier des charges annexé au décret exécutif susmentionné, sur lequel cahier des charges l’objet et le lieu de chaque activité culturelle devront être indiqués, et organisées dans des régions disposant d’espaces culturels adéquats et appropriés, dotés de capacités d’accueil suffisantes et d’installations de service appropriées et correspondant à la nature des activités projetées.
