Title EN: Meeting of Ministers of Culture of the Group of 77 and China, held on May 4, 2023 in Havana.
Goal: Integrate Culture In Sustainable Development Frameworks
SDG: SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: International cooperation for sustainable development
Cultural Domain: Design,Performing Arts,Media Arts,Cinema and Audiovisual Arts,Music,Publishing,Visual Arts
Agency Implementation: Ministry of Culture
Main Feature: The multilateral forum was developed within the framework of the Cuban pro-tempore presidency of the G77 during 2023. Taking as a background the reflections emanating from the World Conference on Cultural Policies (MONDIACULT 2022), it promoted dialogue and reflection on the development of the culture and the promotion of mechanisms and alternatives for South-South cooperation of the nations that make up the G77 and China in the cultural field. Three thematic axes were addressed: - I. Culture as a global public good. South-South cooperation mechanisms and alternatives for sustainable development. - II. The social and economic dimension of culture. The role of creative economies and cultural industries in developing countries. Models and alternatives. - III. Comprehensive Management of Cultural Heritage. Cultural-heritage tourism and its contribution to sustainable development in developing countries. Exchange of good practices and capacity building. As a result of the debate, 41 interventions took place, of which 25 were in person and 16 virtual. The main ideas expressed in the interventions were related to: - The commitment to strengthen South-South cooperation mechanisms and alternatives. - The importance of sharing good practices in the cultural sector and the support of governments through cultural policies aimed at safeguarding tangible and intangible assets and their legacy to future generations. - Tourism-culture relationship as a valid mechanism for sustainable local development, generation of sources of employment and equitable remuneration. - Prevention and fight against illicit trafficking of cultural property and their restitution to their original territories. - Promotion of inclusive public policies that respect the identity and multiculturalism of peoples - Professionalization and development of human capital working in the sector. - Reaffirmation of the value of culture as a global public good. - Post-Agenda 2030 inclusion of Sustainable Development Goal no. 18.
Results: The meeting was successful and enriching. The essence and content of the interventions highlighted the common challenges faced by Southern countries, related to the existing disparity between developed and developing countries. The representatives of the group supported solidarity, unity, joint mechanisms and initiatives of International Cooperation in all its dimensions and the exchange of good practices as the way forward to promote the development of our nations and achieve common objectives. traced. Cuba's leadership in the defense of culture and Heritage was recognized, as well as the importance, support and accompaniment that the highest leadership of the Cuban government provides to these issues. Within the framework of the meeting, 13 bilateral meetings were held with representatives of other countries. Of them, nine were ministers of culture and four were with companies, institutions and artistic teaching centers in our country. Three cultural cooperation agreements were signed with the ministries of culture of Algeria, Palestine and Bolivia.

Main Feature: Both organisations (The Council of Creative Unions of Latvia and Association of Non-governmentalOrganizations of Contemporary Culture) are members of National Council for Culture and implementsvery active participation. The Latvian National Council of Culture was established in 2009, its operationwas renewed at the beginning of 2014. It is a public consultative institution of the Ministry of Culture oncultural sectors and cultural policy, the aim of which is to promote balanced development of cultural andcultural heritage sectors in the interests of the whole society. The tasks of the National Council ofCulture are: 1. to evaluate and forecast cultural perspectives in the context of cultural policy andnational development and to provide the Ministry of Culture and the Minister of Culture with reasonedproposals; 2. to co-operate with the Minister of Culture, structural units and institutions of the Ministry ofCulture in the development of sectoral strategies and policies, determination of priorities, developmentof budget and investment policy and evaluation of draft legal acts; 3. to maintain links with the cultural,cultural heritage sectors and cross-sectoral sectors, discuss issues relevant to them and makeproposals for solutions; 4. to coordinate the opinions of state institutions and various interest groups inthe field of culture on issues of cultural policy; 5. to represent the interests of culture, cultural heritagesectors and related inter-sectors in the context of the formation and development of state policy bydelegating representatives to negotiations with state and local government institutions; 6. to maintain adiscussion in society about the role of culture in the development of society and the state; 7. to evaluatethe applications of the applicants for the Award of Excellence in Culture and to submit proposals to theMinister of Culture regarding the candidates for the award; 8. to nominate a representative from amongits members in the institutions (for example, in the council of the State Culture Capital Fund), in whichthe council must be represented The Council of the Creative Unions of Latvia (CCUL) was founded in1988 at the Plenary Meeting of Writers Union as Culture Council of Creative Unions. SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development

Agency Implementation: Selam Ethiopia
Main Feature: Selam talks  Following its research works on different topics Selam has organized different discussion sessions with artists, stakeholders, and concerned bodies from different sectors to discuss on findings of the research and obtain feedback from the participants. To this end, Selam has organized three Selam talks inviting panelists from across the country and abroad to discuss various issues in Ethiopia. The series consisted of three sessions held on November 22, 2022, December 16, 2022, and February 22, 2023. The first session on November 22, 2022, focused on the role of art and culture in the peacebuilding process in Ethiopia. The panel discussion included insights from artists, cultural experts, peace actors, and institutions. The panelists discussed the challenges, opportunities, and best practices of the arts and culture sector in peacebuilding in Ethiopia. The event was held at the Embassy of Sweden in Addis Ababa, and attendees engaged in a lively conversation about the potential for art and culture to contribute to peacebuilding in Ethiopia. The discussion was led by panelists including Mrs. Asma Redi, CEO of the Nation Building Ministry of Peace, Agegnehu Adane Dilnesahu, Director of the Alle School of Fine Arts and Design of Addis Ababa University, Yared Shumete, a filmmaker, and Mahlet Solomon, a theatre/ film director, scriptwriter, actress, and producer. The discussion was moderated by Samuel Tefera (PhD), an assistant professor at the Centre for African and Asian Studies. The second session, titled “Human Rights and Democracy at a Glance of Art and Culture,” took place on December 16, 2022. The panel discussion focused on how art and cultural activities can play a vital role in promoting human rights and democracy. The talk was led by panelists, including Tigist Alemayehu Gion, a lecturer at Addis Ababa University’s School of Theater Arts; Hanna Andargachew, Partnership Director; and researcher Samuel Tefera (PhD), an assistant professor at the Centre for African and Asian Studies. The event was moderated by Metasebia Dereje, a news editor, anchor, and morning show host. During the panel discussion, the panelists explored how events such as music festivals, documentary films, and art exhibitions can raise awareness about oppression, support resistance, and promote human rights and democracy. They also discussed the challenges of promoting human rights and democracy through art and culture in Ethiopia, given the country’s political context. The event was held at the Embassy of Sweden in Addis Ababa and was attended by professionals from various fields, including arts, education, and human rights. The event saw the participation of 47 attendees and received wider media coverage from Fana TV, Ethiopian Reporter, Awash Radio, Walta TV, Ethiopian Broadcasting Corporation, Addis Media Network, Ahadu Radio, Arts TV, and Adis Maleda Newspaper. The third episode of Selam Talks was held on February 22, 2023, at the Embassy of Sweden. The topic of discussion was “The Status of Artistic Freedom in Ethiopia,” based on a research study conducted under a similar topic. The research study revealed that while the overall practice of artistic freedom in Ethiopia is promising, financial constraints, limited human capacity, lack of equipment and facilities, lack of recognition from the government, and insecurity are the top five challenges for artistic freedom in the country. The study also indicated that most artists in the sector work on an amateur basis and have no direct and relevant educational background, which could affect artistic freedom. The findings revealed a high level of commitment from artists, the readiness of the government to support art industries, a large user base for art’s outputs, and the expansion of social media platforms to disseminate artwork. However, attendees at the panel discussion cited constraints not only from the government but also from society and religion as limitations to practicing artistic freedom. Tribalism and a lack of art education by qualified professionals were also mentioned as factors that affect the arts.  In terms of circus arts, a significant gender imbalance was noted, and artistic freedom should also be seen from a gender perspective. Copyright was identified as one of the biggest challenges in the music industry. The lack of financial resources to do artistic work and the absence of financial benefits for artists were also repeatedly mentioned as the biggest challenges in the arts sector. During the panel discussion, the panelists, including Henok Ayele, a filmmaker; Yikuno Amlak Mezgebu, the Director General for National Archives and Library of Ethiopia and a Lecturer at Addis Ababa University, Ethiopian Language and Literature; Dawit Tesfaye, a filmmaker, producer, director, screenplay writer, and songwriter; Sosina Wogayehu, a circus professional, CEO of Ethio Circus Entertainment, President of the Addis Ababa Gymnastics Federation, Board Member of the Addis Ababa Diaspora Association, and International Jury Member; and Dr. Mesenbet Asefa, a lawyer, presented their views and opinions on the topic and engaged in a dialogue with other panelists and the audience. Approximately 50 people from various sectors, including the arts, government officials, professional associations, media, and other bodies, attended the panel discussion. The event received media coverage from Balageru TV and Reporter Amharic and English newspapers.
Results: Critical issues in the Ethiopian Arts and Culture sector got attention from decision-makers  Through research-based inputs, awareness has been raised on various issues.

Title EN: MétaMusique
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture
SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Digital environment
Agency Implementation: MétaMusique is a member of the Coalition for the Diversity of Cultural Expressions (CDEC)
Main Feature: MétaMusique initiative is a guide designed by the NPO of the same name founded in 2020, to help rights holders in the musical value chain index their content using metadata. It aims to establish a common metadata model for all music content, offering detailed instructions on how to use and apply it effectively.  This guide includes a reference work that defines the metadata fields included in MetaMusic, highlighting those that are mandatory, recommended or specific to certain stakeholders. Thus, this initiative promotes better discoverability of content, and therefore a better diversity of discoverable musical content, by equipping and enabling artists with the help of educational content. When works or sound recordings are poorly indexed, it hampers the ability of collectives to pay rights holders their due royalties and reduces the discoverability of musical content. Adopting comprehensive, standardized indexing practices is crucial to ensuring the existence of digital content and is an essential prerequisite to any go-to-market strategy. In addition, this makes it possible to distinguish professional content from amateur content. This initiative therefore contributes to promoting the Quebec music industry as a whole by promoting standardized indexing practices. MétaMusique is the result of the desire of the Quebec music community to have a professional collective tool aimed at improving the quality of metadata describing local musical content. Its objective is twofold: to allow all rights holders linked to a musical project to receive the royalties due to them and to activate the discoverability of Quebec music on digital and traditional platforms. This initiative has a second component still under development: a tool for capturing and distributing musical metadata which will further facilitate the referencing process and thus promote the influence of Quebec musical artists in the international ecosystem.
Results: In its current version, the MétaMusique initiative already has a certain notoriety, attracting more than 42,000 visits to its web page to date. This strong attendance demonstrates the commitment and interest of the Quebec musical community in this innovative initiative. By providing a detailed guide on the indexing of musical content and facilitating the referencing process through consistent and complete metadata, MétaMusique has enabled artists and rights holders to better manage their copyright and promote their music on the different platforms, thus helping to strengthen the Quebec music industry as a whole.

Title EN: MOVING FROM CENSORSHIP TO ARTS PROMOTION PROGRAM
Goal: Promote Human Rights And Fundamental Freedoms
SDG: SDG 5 - Achieve gender equality and empower all women and girls,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels
Area of Monitoring: Artistic freedom
Agency Implementation: National Arts Council
Main Feature: This is a new philosophy of the National Arts Council aimed at restoring the Council's primary role of promoting and developing the arts in the country, moving away from the concept of controlling and censoring artistic works.   The philosophy carries the vision of empowering artists to work freely and to uphold their fundamental rights, such as freedom of expression, speech, and cultural sharing. Through this philosophy, the National Arts Council (BASATA) launched the Ethics Guide on November, 2023, to providing artists with this guide to create, sing, and perform their artistic works while adhering to Tanzanian ethical principles and procedures without interference from the National Arts Council or any other artistic authority.  Additionally, through this philosophy, the Council has improved its regulations to align with the pace of the digital world, particularly Regulation 25. Currently, the Council reviews artistic works by categorizing (grading) them based on the messages they convey, their content, and their target audience. These categories are determined by considering the age and specific areas where these songs/artistic works should or deserve to be heard.  Moreover, the Artists have the right to establish unions and associations, and to make autonomous decisions regarding their work and activities without interference. The council provides advisory services, funding, and training to enable artists to perform their work professionally and secure their fundamental rights. Moreover, the council advocates for the economic rights of artists and offers opportunities for participating in national and international festivals and events through its Legal Department and the Department of Arts Promotion and Development.
Results: The number of songs/artworks to be banned has decreased. The number of cases involving artists being banned has also decreased. The Council has created many opportunities and initiated including numerous programs aimed at empowering and promoting the arts in the country. Complaints from artists and art stakeholders to the Council have decreased, and the Council has become a friendly and close advisor to artists and cultural stakeholders.
Recommandations: There is a need to provide more education and training to artists and cultural stakeholders to observes Ethics issues in their artistic works, as well as adhere to the regulations set forth by the National Arts Council. These efforts aim to promote and develop the culture and creative industry and improve services related to freedom of expression and fundamental freedoms for artists and cultural stakeholders in Tanzania.

Main Feature: On May 3, 2023 The Parliament, Alþingi,  approved the Ministry of Culture and Business Affairs  parlimentary resolution on music, the first comprehensive policy on the matter in Iceland. The music policy was approved as a parliamentary resolution on May 3, 2023. The strategy contains the vision and goals of music until the year 2030 as well as actions that have been formulated as part of achieving the set goals. The action plan of the policy will be in two parts. The first part, which is presented here, is valid for the years 2023−2026, and later an action plan will be formulated that will be valid for the years 2027−2030. The foundation for a music policy was laid with the report of a working group on the Music Center from 2021. The working group submitted a report in the spring of 2021, which included, among other things, a draft of a music policy and a plan for a new music fund.  On the basis of that report, work was done on further shaping music policy with the involvement of stakeholders, including the Iceland Symphony Orchestra, the Icelandic Music Export Office, the National Broadcasting Company, the Icelandic Music Center, STEFS, the Association of Icelandic Musicians, the Association of Icelandic Musicians, the City of Music Reykjavík, the Iceland Academy of the Arts, the Association of Composers and Lyricists, The Composers' Association, Harpa and other organizations related to culture and the arts. The methodology of strategic planning by the Council of Ministers was considered, where an assessment of the current situation is made, a future vision is presented and subsequently the best way to achieve it is chosen.  Music education is an integral part of a musical environment, and therefore the education part of the policy was developed in good cooperation with the Ministry of Education and Children's Affairs and the Ministry of Universities, Industry and Innovation.  A draft of the policy was published in the summer of 2022 in the government's Consultation Portal, where comments on content, priorities and actions were called for, thereby providing an opportunity for an even wider consultation. A number of suggestions were received which were taken into account during the final processing of the policy. In particular, there were many comments related to the educational part of the policy, where a clearer vision was called for in matters of music education. As a result, work began in the Ministry of Education and Children's Affairs, where it was concluded that it was time to start a complete revision of the main curriculum of music schools   The legislation aims to establish a new music policy for 2030 by strengthening the environment for the creation and performance of music in Iceland, establishing a comprehensive framework for music-related issues, and creating favourable conditions for its creation, promotion, and performance.  The bill is seen as especially important given the role that music has historically played in Icelandic culture and the promotion of Iceland abroad.  A key achievement of the bill is the creation of a new centre for music, to be established later this year, and is intended to support all kinds of music activities and export projects for all music genres. In addition, the centre will manage the registration, administration and distribution of Icelandic music.  New sources of funding will also become available under the law, which merges the current Music Fund, the Sound Recording Fund and the Icelandic Music Export Fund. The role of the new fund will be to promote Icelandic music, sound recording and development work in the Icelandic music industry. The fund will promote  Icelandic musicians and their work, both in Iceland and abroad.  The legislation is the result of a 2021 working group which identified both the central importance of music to the Icelandic economy and also the lack of a comprehensive government policy for music funding and education. The working group was composed of individuals within the Icelandic music industry, staff at the University of Iceland, and also representatives from the Ministry of Education and Children’s Affairs. Key among the recommendations of the working group were the need to establish a Music Center and to merge several existing funds, which were shown to overlap in several responsibilities.  The new policy identifies music as not just one among many of Iceland’s exports, but instead as a cornerstone of Icelandic education, tourism, and commerce. Given its central importance, the new legislation hopes to shape music policy in Iceland through 2030 in a way that has already been done in other cultural fields. In addition to the new, streamlined structure for funding, the new bill hopes to increase total funding for music in Iceland.  The new policy will consist of two separate action plans, one valid through 2026, and the other until 2030. As of now, only the action plan for the years 2023 – 2026 has been published.
Results: The establishment of the  new Iceland Music Office to support all kinds of music activities and export projects for all music genres. In addition, the centre will manage the registration, administration and distribution of Icelandic music and a more powerful Music Fund.

Title EN: Mise en œuvre de la Politique Nationale du Genre Révisée en République de Guinée
Goal: Promote Human Rights And Fundamental Freedoms
SDG: SDG 5 - Achieve gender equality and empower all women and girls,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels
Area of Monitoring: Gender equality
Cultural Domain: Design,Performing Arts,Media Arts,Cinema and Audiovisual Arts,Music,Publishing,Visual Arts
Agency Implementation: Ministère de la Promotion Féminine, de l’Enfance et des Personnes Vulnérables
Main Feature: Depuis son accession à l’indépendance (2 octobre 1958), la République de Guinée a toujours adhéré aux idéaux prônés par les Nations Unies, notamment celui de l’égalité entre les hommes et les femmes. Cet engagement politique et social a été pris dans l’optique de garantir et renforcer un fondement idéal et indispensable à l’édification d’une société bâtie sur l’égalité de chance et la justice sociale. Dans cette perspective, le Gouvernement de la 3ème République a initié et adopté dès l’année 2011 la première Politique Nationale Genre. Cette politique a été la pierre angulaire de l’élaboration des volets de différents programmes, Plans et politiques du Gouvernement. Tels que : (i) le Programme National de Réforme et de la Modernisation de l’Administration Publique adopté et mis en œuvre à partir de 2012, en son volet Rajeunissement et Féminisation de l’Administration Publique ; (ii) le Plan National de Développement Economique et Social 2016-2020 en son volet épanouissement social, politique et culturel des femmes en prenant en compte sa vision de « bâtir une société débarrassée de toutes les formes d’inégalités et d’iniquité, qui garantit à tous (hommes et femmes, filles et garçons) la réalisation de leur potentiel pour leur plein épanouissement » ; (iii) la Politique Nationale de Protection sociale 2016-2021 qui elle-même est entièrement bâtie sur les principes d’équité, d’égalité de genre et de respect des droits humains. Cette logique s’inscrit dans la tendance globale dans la mesure où au niveau sous régional, régional et international des avancées majeures relatives à la réduction des inégalités ont été enregistrées. A titre d’illustration, en 2015, la CEDEAO et l’Union Africaine ont adopté respectivement l’Acte Additionnel sur l’Egalité entre les Sexes et l’Agenda 2063 visant à générer une Afrique débarrassée de toutes les formes de discrimination fondée sur le sexe, ainsi que la Communauté Internationale, les Objectifs pour le Développement Durable (ODD) à l’horizon 2030. C’est dans ce contexte que le Gouvernement guinéen, avec l’appui du PNUD, a initié à travers le Ministère de l’Action Sociale, de la Promotion Féminine et de l’Enfance d’alors, la révision et l’alignement de la Politique Nationale Genre sur les priorités mondiales afin qu’elle serve de cadre d’actions pour l’élimination des disparités sociales, économiques, culturelles, juridiques et politiques dans notre pays. En effet, le processus de sa révision a privilégié l’approche de la participation impliquant tous les acteurs de la promotion du genre de l’Administration Publique, des Institutions Républicaines, du Secteur Privé, de la Société Civile, du Syndicat, du Système des Nations Unies, des ONG Nationales et Internationales, qui a permis de dégager un consensus national autour de ce document validé en Mai 2017 à Kindia lors d’un atelier national. La Politique Nationale du Genre Révisée a permis de mettre en place : a- Les organes de coordination et d’orientation : - Le Conseil national pour la promotion du genre (CONAPG) ; - le conseil régional pour la promotion du genre (COREPG) ; - le Conseil préfectoral et communal pour la promotion du genre (COPPG/ COCPG). b- Les organes permanents de coordination - le Secrétariat permanent du Conseil national pour la promotion du genre ; - les services genre et équité des ministères ; - les services genre et équité régionaux pour la promotion du Genre. c- Un système de suivi-évaluation qui intègre l’aspect genre pour faciliter la convergence vers les objectifs visés d- La création du Fonds National de Promotion du genre alimenté par le Budget National de Développement et l’apport des partenaires techniques et financiers.
Results: Les résultats suivants ont été atteints : - Création des services équités et genre dans les différents départements ministériels en 2012 ; - De 2012 à 2016, 1 102 jeunes cadres guinéens dont 600 femmes ont été recrutés et formés par le projet rajeunir et féminiser l’administration guinéenne ; - La prise en compte des femmes dans les décrets de nomination aux postes ministériels a augmenté de 5 à 35% depuis 2016 ; - l’évolution du nombre de femmes travaillant dans l’administration culturelle passant de 15% en 2016 à 20% en 2017 dont 30% des femmes occupent des postes de responsabilité ; - l’évolution du nombre de femmes dans les métiers de l’art (théâtre, cinéma, photographie, peinture, …) passant de 10% en 2016 à 35% en 2022.

Title EN: Mise en œuvre de la Stratégie Nationale Genre 2020-2024
Goal: Promote Human Rights And Fundamental Freedoms
SDG: SDG 5 - Achieve gender equality and empower all women and girls,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels
Area of Monitoring: Gender equality
Agency Implementation: Ministère de la Solidarité, de l’Action Humanitaire, de la Réconciliation Nationale, du Genre et de la Famille (MSAHRNGF)
Main Feature: Le Burkina Faso dans sa volonté d’internaliser la prise en compte du genre dans tous les domaines en vue d’une réduction des inégalités et des disparités entre les hommes et les femmes, s’est doté d’une Politique Nationale Genre (PNG) qui a certes permis d’engranger des résultats mais des défis demeurent.    Dans l’optique de consolider les acquis de la PNG et de relever les défis le gouvernement du Burkina Faso a élaboré, avec l’appui de ses partenaires au développement, la Stratégie Nationale Genre (SNG) 2020-2024.   La SNG a pour vision de « bâtir une société d’égalité et d’équité entre hommes et femmes, qui assure à l’ensemble des citoyens et citoyennes, les sécurités essentielles pour leur épanouissement social, culturel, politique et économique ». Elle est bâtie autour de cinq grands axes d’intervention.     Son objectif général est de « favoriser l’instauration de l’égalité entre les sexes et de l’autonomisation des femmes et des filles au Burkina Faso grâce à la mise en œuvre d’actions concrètes à tous les niveaux (central, local, communautaire), par les différents acteurs dans les secteurs et domaines prioritaires du développement national ».   Les effets attendus de la mise en œuvre du plan d’actions en matière de promotion culturelle sont entre autres :   les mesures incitatives favorables au développement de l’entrepreneuriat féminin sont appliquées ;   les femmes et les jeunes filles ont davantage accès à l’énergie, aux nouvelles technologies adaptées de production, de transformation et de communication ;   les capacités des femmes et des jeunes filles à défendre leurs droits fondamentaux sont renforcées
Results: Plusieurs résultats ont été engrangés dans le domaine de la culture grâce à la mise en œuvre de cette politique. Il s’agit de :   la visibilité des femmes réalisatrices : il s’est agi de l’organisation d’une projection de film de femmes réalisatrices exemplaires ;   le renforcement des capacités techniques et matérielles des actrices culturelles : à ce niveau, 27 membres des coopératives et associations féminines ont bénéficié d’une formation en métiers tels que le tissage, la savonnerie et la transformation de Produits Forestiers Non Ligneux (PFNL). Elles ont également été équipées en matériels de travail. Aussi, 80 jeunes filles ont bénéficié d’une formation professionnelle dans les filières de la restauration, la santé et l’artisanat. Des kits d’installation leur ont été octroyés à l’issue de la formation ;   la construction d’infrastructures : un atelier a été construit au profit des femmes tisserandes. Aussi, une unité de production des Produits Forestiers Non Ligneux a été construite avec équipement d’une vitrine d’exposition de ces produits.

Agency Implementation: Agence de développement des arts et de la culture (ADAC)
Main Feature: L'Agence de développement des arts et de la culture (ADAC) est une agence gouvernementale sous tutelle du ministère en charge de la Culture du Bénin. Elle est créée par le décret n°2024-899 du 17 avril 2024 portant approbation des statuts modifiés. Elle a pour mission de promouvoir l'économie culturelle et artistique dans les disciplines des arts visuels, du cinéma, des arts de la scène, du livre et de la lecture.  En matière de soutien et d’appui technique et financier aux artistes, l’ADAC est chargée de :  -	Accompagner l’opérationnalisation de la politique de l'État en matière d’industries culturelles et créatives ; -	Accompagner la programmation culturelle et artistique et sa promotion par toutes voies utiles ;  -	Accompagner des projets culturels et artistiques répondant à l’intérêt général sur l'ensemble du territoire national en contribuant à la structuration et à l’animation d’un réseau vivant d’institutions et d’évènements culturels destinés à promouvoir la création contemporaine et le patrimoine culturel artistique notamment les centres culturels, les écoles d’art, les compagnies artistiques et les lieux de diffusion ; -	Soutenir les professionnels des arts et de la culture par l’incitation à la recherche et à la production et par l’accompagnement technique et ou financier et établir des collaborations avec les galeristes, les éditeurs et les maisons de production ; -	Appuyer financièrement la promotion du patrimoine et des industries culturelles et créatives, à travers la valorisation des potentialités et l'accompagnement des promoteurs de projets culturels ; -	Soutenir le financement des actions et activités de production et de diffusion des œuvres artistiques et culturelles ;  -	Appuyer et accompagner l’entreprenariat culturel ;  -	Mettre en place un mécanisme permanent de renforcement des capacités et d’encadrement des artistes et des acteurs culturels dans leurs disciplines respectives ;  -	Mettre en œuvre la fonction d’observatoire et de centre de ressources professionnel pour les métiers de la culture et des arts ; -	Garantir la veille stratégique sur l’environnement juridique du droit d’auteur et de l’économie de la création ; -	Œuvrer pour la dynamisation des systèmes d’information dans le secteur de la culture et des arts ; -	Assurer un rôle d'expertise et de conseil auprès des créateurs, entrepreneurs et opérateurs culturels de l’écosystème en encourageant la création artistique, en proposant et en accompagnant des projets d’action culturelle aux échelles nationale et internationale. En matière de production et de promotion artistique et culturelle, de -	Développer la chaîne des valeurs des industries culturelles et artistiques ; -	Favoriser un écosystème des arts et de la culture dynamique et inclusif en veillant à la détection et à la mise en valeur de nouveaux professionnels des arts et de la culture ; -	Élaborer et actualiser l’agenda des événements culturels nationaux en vue d’accompagner leur organisation sur les territoires et leur promotion au niveau international ; -	Animer les réseaux de création, de production et de diffusion artistique et culturelle ; -	Mettre en œuvre des actions structurantes de promotion des industries de l’écran en lien avec les structures concernées ; -	Concevoir, élaborer et initier des activités de promotion du livre aux plans national et international en lien avec les structures concernées ; -	Promouvoir la création et l’édition littéraires en langues nationales ;  -	Promouvoir l'éducation artistique et culturelle en milieu scolaire et universitaire en liaison avec les structures concernées. En matière de coopération internationale et de développement partenarial, de -	Contribuer à révéler les artistes et acteurs culturels à travers notamment la proposition d’organisation de festivals, d’expositions et d’ateliers de sensibilisation ouverts au grand public ;  -	Mener des actions visant à positionner le Bénin dans le circuit international de circulation, d’exposition, de représentation des créations artistiques et culturelles en lien avec les structures concernées ; -	Accompagner la mobilité des artistes et acteurs culturels ainsi que la circulation de leurs œuvres à l’échelle régionale et internationale ; -	Développer des partenariats aux plans national et international avec des institutions ou organismes intervenant dans la culture et les arts ; -	Initier et/ou développer des réseaux de mécénat pour l’appui des projets culturels et artistiques structurants.
Results: -	Accompagnement de la promotion artistique et culturelle ;  -	Promotion de la circulation des œuvres à l’échelle internationale (Nouvelle structure. A évaluer dans le cadre du prochain RPQ)

Title EN: Mise en place d'un programme national d'éducation artistique intitulé "L'éducation artistique et esthétique, levier du développement culturel"
Goal: Integrate Culture In Sustainable Development Frameworks
SDG: SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development

Agency Implementation: Département de la Culture
Main Feature: Le  programme national d'éducation artistique intitulé "L'éducation artistique et esthétique, levier du développement culturel"  englobe tous les domaines de la création artistique, y compris la musique et la chorégraphie, et propose des ateliers de sensibilisation et de formation pour les enfants et les jeunes. Ces ateliers seront organisés tout au long de l'année dans les différents centres culturels du pays.
Results: Depuis la mise en œuvre du programme national d'éducation artistique intitulé "L'éducation artistique et esthétique, levier du développement culturel", plusieurs résultats significatifs ont été atteints. Les ateliers de sensibilisation et de formation, organisés tout au long de l'année dans divers centres culturels du pays, ont permis une meilleure accessibilité à l'éducation artistique pour les enfants et les jeunes. En conséquence, il y a eu une augmentation notable de la participation aux activités artistiques, avec de plus en plus de jeunes impliqués dans des disciplines telles que la musique et la chorégraphie.  Les retours des participants indiquent un développement accru de leurs compétences artistiques et une sensibilisation renforcée à l'importance de la culture et des arts dans leur éducation. De plus, ces ateliers ont favorisé la découverte de nouveaux talents et la création de liens entre les jeunes artistes et les professionnels du secteur. Enfin, en célébrant des événements comme la journée nationale de la musique avec des activités et des spectacles, le programme a contribué à dynamiser la vie culturelle locale et à promouvoir l'art comme un vecteur essentiel de développement culturel et social.

Main Feature: Le ministère de la Culture au Maroc a lancé la plateforme en ligne daam.minculture.ma pour la soumission et le traitement des projets culturels sollicitant un soutien financier. Cette initiative s'inscrit dans un effort plus large de numérisation des processus administratifs, visant à accroître la transparence, l'efficacité et l'accessibilité des financements culturels. La plateforme daam.minculture.ma permet aux artistes et aux organisations culturelles de soumettre leurs projets directement en ligne, simplifiant ainsi le processus de dépôt des dossiers et éliminant la nécessité de déplacements physiques. Les instructions claires et les formulaires standardisés fournis par la plateforme facilitent le montage des projets culturels et artistiques pour les porteurs de projets et le traitement pour le comité d’étude de dossiers. Une fois soumis, les projets sont évalués par des comités indépendants d'experts, choisis pour leur expertise dans le domaine culturel. La gestion centralisée et transparente des demandes via la plateforme permet un suivi en temps réel du statut des dossiers. Les décisions concernant l’attribution des financements sont également communiquées via la plateforme, garantissant une transparence totale et une traçabilité des décisions. Les candidats peuvent accéder à des retours d'information sur leur demande, ce qui contribue à un processus d'amélioration continue. Cette initiative a un impact significatif sur la liberté artistique au Maroc. En facilitant l'accès équitable aux financements et en garantissant un processus de sélection transparent et impartial, daam.minculture.ma permet aux artistes de se concentrer davantage sur leur création artistique plutôt que sur des démarches administratives complexes. De plus, la transparence accrue et la possibilité de recevoir des retours d'information renforcent la confiance des artistes dans le système de soutien culturel, encourageant ainsi une plus grande diversité et innovation dans le domaine artistique. En fin de compte, cette initiative contribue à créer un environnement où la liberté artistique est mieux protégée et soutenue.
Results: Depuis la mise en œuvre de la plateforme en ligne daam.minculture.gov.ma par le ministère de la Culture au Maroc, plusieurs résultats notables ont été atteints. La numérisation des processus de demande de financement a considérablement amélioré l'efficacité et la transparence dans l'attribution des soutiens financiers aux projets culturels.  Premièrement, le nombre de demandes de financement a augmenté, indiquant que plus d'artistes et d'organisations culturelles sont désormais en mesure de participer au processus de soutien grâce à l'accessibilité en ligne. La simplification des démarches administratives a permis une participation plus large et diversifiée, incluant des artistes de régions éloignées ou moins desservies.  Deuxièmement, la transparence du processus d'évaluation et de décision s'est accrue. Les comités indépendants d'experts qui évaluent les projets garantissent une sélection impartiale, et la communication des résultats via la plateforme assure une traçabilité complète des décisions. Cette transparence a renforcé la confiance des artistes dans le système de soutien culturel.  Troisièmement, la plateforme a facilité un suivi en temps réel des projets soumis, permettant aux artistes de recevoir des mises à jour sur le statut de leurs demandes et d'accéder à des retours d'information. Cela a non seulement amélioré l'expérience des utilisateurs, mais a également contribué à un processus d'amélioration continue.  Enfin, la plateforme daam.minculture.gov.ma a encouragé une plus grande diversité et innovation dans le secteur artistique marocain. En offrant un accès équitable aux financements, elle a permis à des projets variés et novateurs de voir le jour, enrichissant ainsi la scène culturelle marocaine.  En somme, la mise en œuvre de daam.minculture.gov.ma a non seulement rationalisé et rendu plus transparent le processus de financement culturel, mais a également renforcé la confiance des artistes et stimulé la diversité et l'innovation dans le secteur artistique.

Title EN: Mobilité des artistes et des professionnels de la culture
Goal: Achieve A Balanced Flow Of Cultural Goods And Services And Increase The Mobility Of Artists And Cultural Professionals
SDG: SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 10 - Reduce inequality within and among countries,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development

Cultural Domain: Design,Performing Arts,Cinema and Audiovisual Arts,Music,Publishing,Visual Arts
Agency Implementation: Agence Algérienne pour le Rayonnement Culturel (AARC)
Main Feature: Créée en 2005, l'Agence Algérienne pour le Rayonnement Culturel (AARC) est un opérateur culturel à part entière, disposant, depuis 2008, du statut d'entreprise et assure, pour le compte de l'État, un service public. L’AARC organise des évènements et apporte son soutien à des projets d’artistes, d’institutions ou d’associations culturelles, tant pour la création que pour la promotion et la diffusion. Elle encourage notamment les productions contemporaines de créateurs et auteurs algériens, tant sur le territoire national qu’en dehors. Elle a, depuis 2008, pour siège la villa Abd-el-Tif (ou Dar Abd-el-Tif), classée monument historique. L'AARC dispose aussi d'un centre de documentation abrité par le Centre des Arts de Riadh-El-Feth et dédié, en priorité, aux artistes, étudiants et journalistes s’intéressant au domaine culturel. Cet espace de travail et d'information fournit une documentation spécialisée sur différentes disciplines de l'art et de la culture. Elle a pour missions : Diffuser la culture algérienne dans le monde : l'AARC organise et Co-organise des manifestations culturelles à l'étranger pour promouvoir les œuvres et les artistes algériens toutes disciplines confondues, elle s’attèle à faire connaître les expressions contemporaines nées dans le pays ou parmi la communauté algérienne installée à l’étranger. Elle participe de manière régulière à de nombreux évènements internationaux tels que : Festival de Cannes, Abu Dhabi Film Festival, Festival du Monde Arabe de Montréal, Festival de la BD d'Angoulême Mapping Subjectivity au MoMa de New York, Biennale de Dakar, Journée Mondiale du jazz, , exposition et spectacles à l'IMA, etc.  Accueillir les œuvres du monde en Algérie : l'AARC accueille, dans la capitale et dans d'autres villes du pays, des projections, spectacles, concerts et expositions. L’Agence entretient des relations d’échange et de partenariat avec des institutions publiques et des acteurs des industries culturelles dans le monde. Accompagner la coproduction, le soutien et la promotion : en tant qu'acteur culturel, l'Agence agit en amont, en apportant son soutien à la création et à la production d'œuvres culturelles diverses. Ce volet se traduit entre autres par un rôle actif de coproducteur, notamment dans le cinéma où elle participe au développement de la production nationale.
Results: En 2020 : •	Participation de l’artiste Mehdi Laifaoui au festival « Sauti Za Buzara »  Zanzibar/Tanzanie ; •	Aide à la mobilité au profit du groupe Tikoubaouine, participation à un concert de musique en France ; •	Spectacle musical animé par Salim Chaoui et Arezki Ameziane, journée de la terre à Lille ; •	Participation de la troupe théâtrale (Jeunesse el Djar) à la 5ème édition du Festival International de Charm-el-Cheikh en Egypte. En 2021 : •	Participation de l’artiste Asma Alla au festival «Al-Andalus» à Montpellier ; •	Participation au Festival Panafricain à Acra- Ghana (en virtuel) captation du spectacle de musique ;   •	Participation à l’évènement Dubaï Expo du Groupe El Dey et la chanteuse Nacima Ait Ami. En 2022 : •	Aide à la mobilité au profit des artistes algériens ;  •	Participation du groupe Iwel et Tikoubaouine à Dubaï Expo ;  •	Participation au Salon International du Livre du Caire Egypte  •	Participation au Salon International du Livre à Masquât Oman ; •	Participation au festival de Babel en Roumanie ;  •	Participation de Lila Borsali et de Hakim SALHI au festival «IRBID» en Jordanie ; •	Participation à la semaine culturelle de Bruxelles exposition d’œuvres d’art ;  •	Participation de la troupe « El Kheima » au festival de Zagreb ;  •	Célébration de la journée internationale du Jazz/Artistes étrangers ; •	Master class avec le réalisateur français Fabien Gorgeat ; •	Participation à la 14ème Biennale de Dakar – Sénégal ; •	Soutien à la participation algérienne à la Fashion week de Milan ; •	Participation à la Foire Internationale d’Art Contemporain à Dubaï. En 2023 : •	Aide à la mobilité du styliste Kerzabi à la fashion week de Milan ; •	Résidence et exposition de l'artiste Denis Martinez : "Acte de vie " à Dar Abd-el-Tif à Alger.
Recommandations: Il est fortement souhaitable de multiplier les axes des échanges culturels internationaux, afin de stimuler le dialogue interculturel sous toutes ses formes.

Title EN: Mobility programmes (since 2022): "Culture in the Regions – Mobility of Museum Collections" "Culture in the Regions – Mobility of Performing Arts"
Goal: Integrate Culture In Sustainable Development Frameworks
SDG: SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: National sustainable development policies and plans
Agency Implementation: Ministry of Culture of the Republic of Lithuania, Lithuanian Council for Culture
Main Feature: Since 2022 under the initiative of the Ministry of Culture two mobility actions “Culture in the Regions – Mobility of Museum Collections“ and “Culture in the Regions - Mobility of Performing Arts“ have been implemented.   The actions are implemented under the Progress Measure No. 08-001-04-01-01 "Increasing access to high artistic value, diverse and inclusive cultural content".   The aim of initiative “Culture in the Regions – Mobility of Museum Collections“ is to make museum exhibitions of high artistic value at national or international level accessible to the inhabitants of the regions by promoting the accessibility of such services throughout the territory of the country to different groups of the population, while at the same time contributing to the development of the professional and special skills of the staff of municipal museums.  The aim of the initiative “Culture in the Regions - Mobility of Performing Arts“ is to reduce disparities in access to culture in regions and to provide opportunities to see high artistic value performing arts works.   The initiative enables the development of performing arts works specifically for the regions: small-scale but high artistic quality works that are adapted to the stages of cultural centres and do not require special equipment and techniques. Target group: inhabitants of regions of the Republic of Lithuania where cultural services are less accessible.
Results: In 2022–2024, in total 44 museum collections mobility projects were funded: Lithuanian Council for Culture provided partial funding for the implementation of 39 museum collection mobility projects, Ministry of Culture of the Republic of Lithuania funded 5 museum collections mobility projects of the state museums. These projects have resulted in 40 traveling exhibitions in more than 63 cities and towns across Lithuania.  Meanwhile, in 2022–2024 under the action "Culture in the Regions – Mobility of Performing Arts", the Ministry of Culture of the Republic of Lithuania allocated support to 44 projects implemented by national and state theatres and concert venues.  In 2022–2023, more than 300 public performances, concerts and educational programmes were presented in 10 districts (regions) of Lithuania (Panevėžys, Šiauliai, Utena, Alytus, Ukmergė, Tauragė, Telšiai, Mažeikiai, Biržai and Rokiškis) reaching more than 66 700  visitors. These specific districts (regions) were chosen based on the results of the survey "Participation in Culture and Satisfaction with Cultural Services in Lithuania", published in 2021, and commissioned by the Lithuanian Council for Culture For more detail: Participation-in-culture-and-satisfaction-with-cultural-services-in-2020-Lithuania-Summary.pdf (kulturostyrimai.lt).  The survey showed that in these counties either the proportion of local residents willing to participate themselves in cultural artistic activities and/or satisfaction with the accessibility of cultural services is significantly lower, or, in contrast, the number of people willing to get involved in cultural activities is higher in comparison with the rest of the population.
Financial Ressources: Funds allocated for initiative “Culture in the Regions – Mobility of Performing Arts" –  approx. USD 773 000  (EUR 700 000). Duration: 2022– 2024.  Funds allocated for initiative “Culture in the Regions – Mobility of Museum Collections" –approx. EUR 828 200 (EUR 750 000). Duration: 2022– 2024.

Title EN: Modernisation des services culturels et de la promotion de l'accès à la culture pour tous
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture
SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Digital environment
Agency Implementation: Ministère de la Jeunesse, de la Culture et de la Communication – Département de la culture
Main Feature: Le ministère de la Jeunesse, de la Culture et de la Communication – Département de la culture, dans ses efforts continus pour renforcer et développer les industries culturelles numériques, a lancé une nouvelle bibliothèque en ligne permettant de télécharger et lire 328.480 livres électroniques couvrant divers domaines du savoir. Cette initiative vise à offrir des contenus numériques constamment renouvelés pour répondre aux besoins des lecteurs, promouvoir la lecture, et démocratiser l'accès aux livres. Le ministère entend ainsi étoffer le catalogue des bibliothèques publiques, étendre l'accès à cette bibliothèque numérique à un maximum de bibliothèques, et fournir environ 9.979 comptes aux adhérents pour un accès gratuit et immédiat aux livres. La plateforme se distingue par une riche collection de contenu numérique en langue arabe, avec plus de 20.600 titres, reflétant les efforts des maisons d'édition marocaines et arabes pour s'adapter à l'évolution technologique et promouvoir les œuvres des auteurs marocains à une échelle géographique étendue. De plus, elle propose un programme culturel prometteur avec 141.500 livres en français, 58.400 en anglais, et 8.000 titres dans d'autres langues étrangères. En tout, la bibliothèque offre un accès à plus de 100.000 titres de productions littéraires marocaines et internationales, y compris environ 60.000 livres destinés aux enfants et aux jeunes adultes, visant à satisfaire leur curiosité culturelle et stimuler leur imagination.
Results: Le lancement de la bibliothèque numérique par le ministère de la Jeunesse, de la Culture et de la Communication vise plusieurs résultats importants: étoffer le catalogue des bibliothèques publiques, étendre l'accès aux ressources numériques à un large public, et fournir près de 10.000 comptes d'accès gratuits permettant le téléchargement instantané de livres. Cette initiative contribue à la démocratisation de l'accès à la lecture, à la promotion de la diversité culturelle, et au soutien de la création littéraire marocaine.  Cette action est étroitement liée aux objectifs de la Convention de 2005 de l'UNESCO sur la protection et la promotion de la diversité des expressions culturelles. En offrant une vaste collection de livres électroniques dans différentes langues, y compris plus de 20.600 titres en arabe et une importante sélection d'ouvrages en français, anglais et autres langues, la bibliothèque numérique soutient la diversité culturelle et linguistique. Elle permet également de diffuser largement les œuvres des auteurs marocains, contribuant ainsi à la promotion de la création locale et à l'enrichissement du patrimoine culturel mondial.  En outre, cette initiative répond à l'objectif de la Convention de renforcer les capacités des institutions culturelles et de favoriser un accès équitable à une grande variété de contenus culturels. En fournissant des ressources numériques accessibles à tous, le ministère facilite l'inclusion culturelle et l'accès à l'information, des principes clés de la Convention de 2005. Par cette action, le ministère non seulement modernise les services bibliothécaires mais aussi encourage la diversité des expressions culturelles, soutenant ainsi les objectifs globaux de l'UNESCO en matière de culture et de développement durable.

Title EN: Mondes nouveaux
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture
SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Cultural and creative sectors
Cultural Domain: Design,Performing Arts,Media Arts,Cinema and Audiovisual Arts,Music,Publishing,Visual Arts
Agency Implementation: Ministère de la Culture
Main Feature: La création artistique a été particulièrement affectée par la crise sanitaire. Pour soutenir le secteur, le Gouvernement a souhaité, dans le cadre du volet culture de France Relance, consacrer 30 millions d’euros à un programme de soutien novateur à la conception et à la réalisation de projets artistiques. Dans un format sans précédent, toute créatrice et créateur aura pu soumettre un projet pour être ensuite soutenu dans son élaboration et accompagné dans sa réalisation.  Au cours de l’année 2022, partout en France et notamment dans les Outre-mer, 430 artistes ont conçu et présenté une œuvre originale. Toutes les disciplines étaient représentées - arts visuels, musique, écritures, spectacle vivant, design et arts appliqués - dont certaines croisées dans le cadre de projets portés par des collectifs.   Plus de 3000 projets ont été soumis au comité artistique que préside Bernard Blistène, ancien directeur du Musée national d'art moderne au Centre Pompidou. C’est en portant une attention particulière à la jeunesse, 60% des artistes ayant moins de 40 ans, et à l’hybridation des pratiques, avec 85 collectifs, que les projets ont été sélectionnés. « Mondes nouveaux » offre à des créateurs et créatrices, en devenir ou déjà reconnus, l’opportunité de révéler toute leur énergie et leur vitalité.  Différemment de la logique de commande artistique, « Mondes nouveaux » propose à l’ensemble des artistes sélectionnés d’exprimer leurs désirs sans critère imposé, de bénéficier d’une allocation de recherche pour cadrer leur projet, de recevoir l’accompagnement du comité artistique et de rester propriétaire de leur œuvre. Le programme documentera tout au long des prochains mois le public sur le processus de création et de conception de chaque œuvre. « Mondes nouveaux » bénéficie d’un budget de 30 millions d’euros dans le cadre du plan France relance du Gouvernement.  Face au succès du dispositif, le ministère de la Culture a annoncé en octobre 2022 la reconduction de Mondes Nouveaux pour une période de trois ans à raison d’un budget de dix millions par an sur trois ans, de 2023 à 2025.
Results: Plus de 3000 projets ont été soumis au comité artistique lors du lancement du premier appel à manifestation d’intérêt, pour 264 projets retenus.
Financial Ressources: 30 millions d’euros (2023-2025)

Title EN: Mongolia-Korea joint residency exchange program
Goal: Achieve A Balanced Flow Of Cultural Goods And Services And Increase The Mobility Of Artists And Cultural Professionals
SDG: SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 10 - Reduce inequality within and among countries,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Mobility of artists and cultural professionals
Agency Implementation: Art Council of Mongolia
Main Feature: The Arts Council of Mongolia (ACM) and the Art Council of Korea (AAC) organized the Mongolia-Korea joint residency exchange program in Terelj and Ulaanbaatar from June 12-22, 2024, as part of the 12th year of the "Motion Mongolia" contemporary dance festival. To provide space for young Mongolian artists to create new works and enhance international cooperation, ACM has annually organized the "Time and Space" workshop since 2008, focusing on visual arts and music. Starting in 2024, the program expanded into dance art for the first time, supporting collaboration between Mongolian and Korean dancers. This initiative provided an opportunity for exchange of experiences and joint creation of new modern dance works. In this program, 5 dancers from the Ulaanbaatar Theater and 6 artists from the Korean "Müden" troupe participated. They immersed themselves in the picturesque landscapes of Gorkhi-Terelj, improvised directly, drew inspiration from nature, and collaboratively developed new creative works in the realm of modern dance.
Results: As a result of the program, Mongolian and Korean artists collaboratively created a new contemporary dance work. The performance was held on the stage of the Ulaanbaatar Theater and was attended by more than 400 people.

Title EN: Multiple Programmes in the Field of Visual Art
Goal: Promote Human Rights And Fundamental Freedoms
SDG: SDG 5 - Achieve gender equality and empower all women and girls,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels
Area of Monitoring: Gender equality
Agency Implementation: Ministry of Culture
Main Feature: Lalit Kala Akademi (National Academy of Art), New Delhi was inaugurated on 5th August 1954 by the then Minister for Education, Maulana Abul Kalam Azad and was registered under the Societies Registration Act 1860, on 11th March 1957. In pursuance of the objectives set out in the Constitution, the organisation functions through its General Council, Executive Board and other Committees.  Lalit Kala Akademi, the youngest of the three Akademies founded by Govt. of India, establishes to direct its focus on activities in the field of Visual Arts. In his inaugural speech Maulana Abul Kalam Azad had stated “The Akademi must work to preserve the glorious traditions of the past and enrich them by the work of our modern artists”. Akademi has preserved and documented a permanent collection of the highest order that reflects the vitality, complexity and unfolding patterns of contemporary, modern, folk and tribal art in India. Lalit Kala Akademi New Delhi along with its Regional Centres situated at Chennai, Lucknow, Kolkata, Bhubaneswar, Garhi (New Delhi) and sub-centres at Shimla, Ahmedabad, Agartala, Patna presents exhibitions workshops, camps lectures, retrospectives shows and many other art activities of unparalleled significance.
Results: The measures promote Human Rights and Fundamental Freedom Policies, and several measures have been adopted to support the recognition and advancement of women as artists, cultural professionals or creative entrepreneurs. The Akademi organises various programmes especially designed for women artists that ensure women participation with equal share of monetary benefits.

During 2022 it was, at the same time, a uniting point with the MINEDUC reading and writing strategy; each establishment that received musical performances could also express emotions and thoughts on the “wall of words”, publishing opinions, feelings and evocations produced by the musical stimulus.  Fifty establishments were included, with 50 performances and 3 macro-zone conferences. In 2023, a pedagogical variable has been introduced aimedat diversifying art experiences, promoting not only musical appreciation, but complementing it with the historical moment of the times when it was composed, relating it with lyrics and literature from the past and visual arts representing that generation.
Results: Regarding quantitative data that show results following the measure implementation, it is worth mentioning that performances were held in 50 educational establishments in 2022. These performances were presented by string, brass or woodwind chamber groups, quartets or quintets. In relation to the educational workshops, four were held in the orchestral area: (1) instrumental pedagogical workshop, (2) lutherie workshop, (3) orchestra conducting workshop and (4) orchestra cultural management workshop.  During the same year, three macro-zone conferences were held, covering the entire national territory: (1) School orchestra conference in the northern macro-zone, (2) School orchestra conference in the central macro-zone and (3) School orchestra conference in the southern macro-zone.  Finally, and as general information for the year 2023, 540 artistic workshops were held in all the regions of the country, where the Metropolitan Region stands out with 50 workshops, Valparaíso region with 48 and Biobío region with 48.
Recommandations: In 2022, a qualitative satisfaction survey was conducted, in which various favourable testimonials from teachers, directors and students were expressed. Regarding general conclusions, we can sustain that the measure promotes the participation of children and youth in the arts and culture through actions in educational establishments.   At the same time, they not only live the art experience but are also involved in the creative process, awakening future interest in art practices, in this case in performing on musical and orchestral instruments. Title EN: Music Decent Work
Goal: Integrate Culture In Sustainable Development Frameworks
SDG: SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: National sustainable development policies and plans
Agency Implementation: Music Crossroads Academy Zimbabwe  & Nhimbe Trust
Main Feature: Nhimbe Trust and Music Crossroads collaborated to monitor all aspects of decent work by reporting developments, inspiring related sector dialogue and informing national policy-making on decent work. This was aimed at improving the state of music decent work rights through the operationalisation of global normative frameworks that ensure inclusive and equal treatment, protection of fundamental freedoms and the realisation of sustainable livelihoods.   The initiative had three overarching goals:  a)	Improved governance of access to the labour market and decent work for musicians   b)	Strengthened protection measures and decent working conditions for musicians and cultural and creative professionals through enhancing social protection mechanisms, improving working conditions and identifying and mitigating against violations of the fundamental principles and rights at work  c)	Increased opportunities for jobs, income and livelihoods for musicians and cultural and creative professionals, as well as for host communities
Results: Information collected through research, interviews with musicians and industry experts has culminated into training modules on music decent work. Music business master-classes have been hosted to date, focusing on the capacitation of all professionals in the music value chain in areas of:  •	Sustainability  •	Decent work in conditions of informality  •	The domestication and localisation of ILO decent work elements and indicators  What has emerged through research and trainings is that there is lack of trust in mainstream social protection and health systems, due to a volatile national economy that makes such systems susceptible to gradual or immediate collapse, leaving music professionals in a more vulnerable state without gains of social protection investment. Alternative forms of social protection developed through knowledge from decent work trainings and mentorship have included money clubs, investments in sustainable income generation projects that guarantee dignified retirement, as well as medical aid cooperatives.

Main Feature: Music Hubs are partnerships that support, deliver and enable access to music education for children and young people within a local area. The Music Hub programme supports a network of 43 Hub partnerships which cover every area of England. Music Hubs are co-ordinated by a Hub Lead Organisation and can include schools, local authorities, community groups, music organisations, industry and more.    Music Hubs play a critical role in supporting the vision of the National Plan for Music Education, that all children and young people should be able to learn to sing, play and instrument and create music together, and have the opportunity to progress their musical interests and potential, including into a professional creative career. They achieve this through programmes and activity that support schools and other education settings to deliver high-quality music education, supports young people to further develop their musical interests and talent including into employment and supports all children and young people to engage with a range of musical opportunities in and out of school.
Results: Arts Council England is investing over £101 million in new Music Hub Lead organisations on behalf of the Department for Education. They provide more than £76m to coordinate music education in every local area, and as well as an additional £25m to invest in new musical instruments, equipment and technology, including instruments for children and young people with special education needs or disabilities.
Recommandations: The programme was evaluated in 2023. Below are the key themes of the findings:  -More strategic collaboration across wider geographies could be beneficial for the experience of children and young people. It could also enable consistent monitoring and evaluation, provide better access to training and networking for the music education workforce, and support fundraising and income generation  -The number of Hubs is considered to be less important than the appropriateness and quality of the new geographies, and how they will respond to the needs of children and young people   -A new structure should seek to respond to local contexts, existing alliances and ways of working, and build on positive and impactful sector developments. Main Feature: The National Council for Culture has the task of acting as an advisory body and providing expert opinions and recommendations on cultural policy and strategy. Its main task is to advise the government and other relevant institutions on matters of cultural development, preservation and promotion. The council consists of 7 members, including prominent cultural figures, experts and representatives of various cultural disciplines, who are appointed by the government and selected on the basis of their knowledge and experience in the field of arts and culture. The members of the council have a term of office of five years. The council operates independently, with the Ministry of Culture providing administrative and technical support and funding for its activities. The main tasks of the National Council for Culture include assessing the impact of cultural policy on cultural development, issuing opinions on the national cultural program and the annual reports on its implementation, reviewing proposed legislation and other regulations in the cultural sector and developing initiatives and proposals to solve specific problems in the cultural sector. It can also initiate research and studies on specific cultural issues and thus contribute to the development of evidence-based policy. Overall, the National Council for Culture is an important independent body that represents civil society, as well as specific cultural sectors and their interests, and plays an important role in promoting dialog between cultural institutions, policy makers and the public.
Results: Between 2019 and 2024, the National Council for Culture held 30 meetings. During this time, the council made numerous recommendations to the Ministry of Culture, seeking to clarify the ministry's legislative and administrative activities and enabling legislators to better align their work with the expectations of civil society, professional organizations, and representatives of the various arts sectors. As an oversight mechanism and a platform for discussion between the government and the cultural sector, the Council provided a valuable public forum open to the public and journalists, allowing for transparency and broader dialogue. As part of its activities, the council also commissioned two studies. The first, carried out in 2021, was a comparative analysis of peer evaluation of cultural programs and projects funded from the state budget, with suggestions for improvements in this area in Slovenia. The second study, which began in 2022 and continued in 2023, was an international comparative analysis of European models for evaluating publicly funded cultural programs and projects. These studies now serve as comprehensive resources for the Ministry of Culture to conduct its affairs in this regard.
