Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture
SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Digital environment
Agency Implementation: Ministère de la Jeunesse, de la Culture et de la Communication
Main Feature: La plateforme numérique www.culture.ma, dont l'objectif principal est la valorisation et la promotion du patrimoine marocain, des livres et des festivals culturels, donne accès à des contenus marocains dans les domaines du livre, du patrimoine et de la musique. Elle contribue au processus d'inventaire du patrimoine matériel et immatériel marocain et à sa présentation à travers des photos, des capsules, des vidéos et un aperçu de chacun de ses éléments. Il s'agit également de faire connaître les festivals culturels nationaux et les livres disponibles, indique un communiqué du ministère.  La plateforme www.culture.ma revêt une grande importance, car elle favorise l'accès à la culture et la publication de contenus multimédias dans les domaines des arts, du livre et du patrimoine. Cela se fait à travers plusieurs vidéos documentant les festivals culturels, les salons du livre et le patrimoine culturel matériel et immatériel, souligne la même source. Elle constitue une bibliothèque virtuelle mise à la disposition du grand public, permettant de présenter et de documenter les grands événements culturels, valoriser les énergies artistiques, promouvoir les œuvres littéraires et préserver le patrimoine culturel marocain, ajoute le ministère.  En outre, cette plateforme permet de partager les différentes activités du secteur de la culture, conformément à la même démarche inhérente à la réalisation des objectifs de protection et de valorisation du patrimoine culturel marocain, indique-t-on.  Les données de la plateforme sont régulièrement mises à jour et enrichies par de nouveaux contenus, et ce afin que chaque visite sur la plateforme soit une expérience interactive, avec la possibilité de découvrir de nouvelles vidéos sur le patrimoine culturel, les écrivains et les arts.

Title EN: ORIGEN: Amplificando la voz de los cineastas indígenas
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture

Area of Monitoring: Media diversity
Agency Implementation: National Institute of Indigenous Affairs (INAI), Ministry of Justice.
Main Feature: The National Institute of Indigenous Affairs (INAI), the national agency responsible for respecting the rights of indigenous peoples, proposed to create new opportunities for Argentine indigenous filmmakers. It expanded participation in the creation, production and distribution of cultural goods. The project enabled young people from the Wichi, Mbyá Guaraní, Huarpe, Kolla and Qom indigenous communities to participate in the creation and production of films. In addition, the project promoted their creations through a digital platform developed specifically for the dissemination of indigenous audiovisual productions, and also through a collective exhibition.  It introduced measures to promote fair access to cultural goods. The project worked with a group of young people ensuring gender equality, promoting the equal participation of indigenous women and training communities on women's rights. The documentaries produced were promoted by the National Institute of Cinema and Audiovisual Arts (INCAA) and on a virtual platform to maximize opportunities for visibility and exposure.
Results: A network of indigenous filmmakers will be fully operational after the end of the project. This network will be permanently linked to the Culture area of the National Institute of Indigenous Affairs through regular meetings, where difficulties will be monitored and discussed. In addition, the National Institute of Indigenous Affairs and other agencies of the Argentinean National State will attend to and resolve any issues that may arise after the completion of the project.  The development of an ORIGEN Network will be encouraged through constant communication with the aforementioned groups, coordinated by INAI's Culture area and the National Institute of Cinema and Audiovisual Arts. Follow up meetings will be held in addition to an annual national meeting where the groups involved can continue to work together.  ORIGEN will keep in touch with those who participate in the workshops and will conduct a survey to analyze whether the participants have been able to add to their skill set. In addition, once the training stage is over, the team of trainers will be available for remote consultation. All agencies involved in ORIGEN intend to publicize the films through different distribution channels, such as festivals, forums and summits where both indigenous and non-indigenous films are disseminated. This will allow the event organizers to make contact with other filmmaking groups around the world, offering these entrepreneurs the opportunity to obtain new resources so that they can continue working, either with national or international funding. For example, INAI's culture team is currently in contact and working with the Mexican community film project ‘Ambulante’, which trains filmmakers and distributes their films throughout Mexico. INAI hopes to continue to cultivate these relationships, as well as develop new ones, so that the indigenous filmmakers trained in the framework of the ORIGEN project can continue to advance their work in the medium and long term.
Financial Ressources: IFCD contribution 83 118.00 USD Contribution of the Institute 94,300 USD

Title EN: Obligations d’investissement direct dans la production cinématographique et audiovisuelle
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture
SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Cultural and creative sectors
Agency Implementation: Autorité de régulation de la communication audiovisuelle et numérique (ARCOM)
Main Feature: Le financement de la création cinématographique et audiovisuelle en France repose sur un principe selon lequel ceux qui tirent un bénéfice des œuvres doivent participer au financement de leur création (« l’aval finance l’amont »). Deux mesures servent cet objectif, les obligations d’investissement direct dans la production et les contributions fiscales (voir mesure 2).  Prises notamment en lien avec l’article 13(2) de la directive SMA, les obligations d’investissement direct s’imposent aux diffuseurs linéaires et non linéaires, des secteurs publics et privés, établis en France et ceux établis à l’étranger dont l’offre de services est dirigée vers le territoire français. Ces obligations se traduisent comme suit :  •	Sur le plan quantitatif, les plus gros diffuseurs, principalement ceux dont le chiffre d’affaires annuel net réalisé en France dépasse 5 millions d’euros, doivent investir, selon le cas, un pourcentage compris entre 20 et 25% de ce CA réalisé au cours de l’année précédente en faveur de la production d’œuvres européennes.  •	Sur le plan qualitatif, et pour tous les diffuseurs, ces investissements font l’objet de sous-quotas divers, qui dans la plus grande partie des cas sont les suivants : 85 % de ces investissements doivent être versés au soutien des œuvres d’expression originales françaises (EOF), 75 % en faveur des œuvres cinématographiques indépendantes et 66 % pour les œuvres audiovisuelles indépendantes.
Financial Ressources: 1,7 milliards de dollars par an
Recommandations: La mise en œuvre de cette politique est évaluée chaque année dans le bilan de financement de la production de l’ARCOM dont voici les principales données pour 2022 :  1.	Obligations de contribution globale en faveur de la production audiovisuelle et cinématographique :  •	Le montant total généré a permis de financer la production audiovisuelle à hauteur de 1,25 milliards de dollars (1,167 Mds€) et la production cinématographique à hauteur de 443 millions de dollars (415 M€), soit un montant global de 1,693 milliards de dollars (1,58 mds€). Ce chiffre est en progression de plus de 12 % par rapport à l’année précédente.  •	La contribution des services de télévision est prépondérante et représente 80 % de la contribution globale soit un montant à hauteur de 1,33 milliards de dollars (1,237 Mds€).  •	Les services de médias audiovisuels (SMAD) contribuent de manière accrue avec une contribution qui se chiffre à 370 millions de dollars (345,3 M€) soit le double par rapport à 2021 et représentant 21 % de la contribution globale.  2.	Obligations de contribution en faveur de la production audiovisuelle : une forte croissance des investissements des SMAD en faveur de la production audiovisuelle est constatée puisqu’elle représente désormais 25 % de la contribution totale. Cette augmentation est due à l’apport des services de vidéo à la demande (SVAD) étrangers en lien avec l’application du décret SMAD dont la contribution a doublé par rapport à l’année précédente avec un montant de 307,22 millions de dollars (286,8 M€).  3.	Obligations de contribution en faveur de la production cinématographique : Les services de télévision assurent la très grande majorité de la contribution totale en faveur de la production cinématographique à hauteur de 382,41 millions de dollars (357 M€) soit 86 % du montant total.

Title EN: Online News Act
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture
SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Media diversity
Agency Implementation: Canadian Heritage
Main Feature: The Online News Act aims to ensure that dominant online platforms compensate news businesses when their content is made available on these platforms’ services, by creating a bargaining framework for fair deals between the two. The intent of the regulations is to provide platforms the opportunity to reach fair commercial agreements with news businesses, including the possibility of a single agreement with a group of news businesses, and thereby contribute to the overall sustainability of the Canadian news marketplace.
Results: The Online News Act received Royal Assent on June 22, 2023. The Online News Act Application and Exemption Regulations have been published in late December 2023 Since the framework has just been introduced, bargaining has not yet begun; platforms subject to the Act are now preparing to launch the processes through which they will negotiate with news businesses. The CRTC has launched public consultations to gather the views of Canadians and interested parties on the regulatory framework which is intended be implemented post fall 2024.  This initiative is at the heart of Canada's efforts to ensure fair remuneration for artists, authors, and journalists in the online environment. Media diversity is an essential element for the flourishing of cultural expressions within Canadian society, in accordance with the preamble to the Convention.   The CRTC is in the process of launching its own consultation process in connection with its regulations where it will further define:  •	The mandatory bargaining process; •	The code of conduct to support fairness and transparency; •	The rules on undue preference or discrimination; •	The eligibility of news businesses to participate in the framework.

Title EN: Ontario Creates’ Diversity Enhancement Fund
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture
SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Cultural and creative sectors
Agency Implementation: Ontario Creates (an agency of the Ontario Ministry of Tourism, Culture and Sport)
Main Feature: The Diversity Enhancement Fund is a yearly program that offers enhancements to financial support provided through Ontario Creates’ Film Fund, Industry Development Program, and Music Investment Fund.   The Diversity Enhancement Fund is delivered through three core investment areas: 1.	Film Fund Diversity Enhancement for films with diverse key creatives, voice and story;  2.	Industry Development Program towards initiatives that support diverse workforce development and increased inclusion in industry mentorship and professional development opportunities; and, 3.	Music Investment Fund providing additional support to companies and organizations demonstrating tangible, measurable efforts to support and increase diversity in staffing (including executive positions), roster and mentorship/training/professional development activities.  The enhancement provides dedicated funding for projects that meet the provincial definition of diversity, encompassing: ancestry, culture, ethnicity, gender identity and expression, language, physical and intellectual ability, race, religion, sex, sexual orientation and socio-economic status.   The Film Fund is intended to increase the level of domestic feature film production in Ontario. It provides support to Ontario’s producers for feature film projects with development and production financing. To reduce barriers to entry, the diversity enhancement was designed with lower entry thresholds for Film Fund applicants, to allow funding levels above the normal program caps, and with modified evaluation criteria to reflect the diverse elements of projects applying.  The Industry Development Program provides targeted financial and strategic support to Ontario’s established trade and event organizations to offer initiatives, events, and activities with long-term impacts on growth and sustainability in the book, magazine, film, television, and interactive digital media (IDM) sectors.   The Music Investment Fund is aimed at strengthening and stimulating growth in Ontario’s music companies. Ontario Creates offers financial support to drive activity and investment and to support Ontario’s music companies and organizations in expanding their economic and cultural footprints within Canada and around the world.
Results: Film Fund Diversity Enhancement – Number of Successful Applicants 2020-21 : Not available 2021-22 : 41 [12 productions, 29 developments] 2022-23 : Not available  Industry Development Program Diversity Enhancement – Number of Successful Applicants 2020-21 : Not available 2021-22 : 25 2022-23 : Not available  Music Investment Fund Diversity Enhancement – Number of Successful Applicants  2020-21 : Not available 2021-22 : 89 [38 music creations,  15 music industry initiatives, 15 global market developments, 21 live music] 2022-23 : Not available  Recent results of the Diversity Enhancement Fund include:  •	In 2021-22, the Film Fund Diversity Enhancement provided an additional CAD 1.43 million to diverse films. 53% of Film Fund supported films received Diversity Enhancement, including 3 Indigenous projects and 14 from people of colour. •	In 2021-22, Ontario Creates partnered with the Indigenous Screen Office to support ongoing on-set mentorship and training initiatives for Indigenous crews, specifically on the sets of the film Rosie and Cafe Daughter, which were also supported by the Film Fund.  •	In 2021-22, the Industry Development Program Diversity Enhancement assisted 25 initiatives across sectors including the International Film Festival of South Asia Bright Lights program, the Ontario Book Publishers Organization’s diverse intern program, the IDM Fund Future training programs (including one program targeted to Black content creators), and the Inside Out Festival’s International Financing Forum. •	The Industry Development Program supported a series of reports from the Black Screen Office entitled Being Seen: Directives for creating authentic and inclusive content, with chapters focused on various underrepresented communities: people of colour, people with disabilities, 2SLGBTQIA+, Black communities and a report specific to children’s media. The project aims to provide guidelines and strategies to those in the film, TV and IDM industries to help them commission and create more authentic content. •	Ontario Creates partnered with ADVANCE – Canada’s Black Music Business collective, to offer a cross-sector anti-racism training to Ontario companies. The first session in a three-part series was a 101 on Diversity, Equity and Inclusion with attendance from nearly 80 stakeholders across all sectors.
Financial Ressources: •	CAD 2.15 million in 2022-23 for the Diversity Enhancement, AcceleratiON: Black and Indigenous Entrepreneurship, and other strategic, time-limited initiatives (USD 1,561,330 as of April 2024). •	CAD 1.775 million in 2023-24 for the Diversity Enhancement and AcceleratiON: Black and Indigenous Entrepreneurship programs (USD 1,288,470 as of April 2024).
Recommandations: •	Ontario Creates has observed significant benefits from supporting diverse projects, including critical acclaim, workforce development and box office success. •	The additional investment has been highly successful in allowing the agency to reduce the barriers to entry and to support a greater number of important projects and initiatives than would have been possible under traditional selection systems.

These initiatives pave the way for qualified artists to become part of Qatar's story and history by engaging in the States cultural and artistic scene through their artworks.
Results: Qatar Museums Authority (QMA) has launched several initiatives related to its annual open public art calls for artistic intervention and participation in cultural life. These initiatives primarily include:  1.	Public Art Annual Intervention Open Call for Artists: Through this initiative, Qatar Museums encourages resident artists to propose public art projects that contribute to improving the quality of life in cities. Title EN: Open public libraries
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture
SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Cultural and creative sectors
Agency Implementation: Educab Romania,CRIDL,: Asociatia Comunitatile Viitorului
Main Feature: In alignment with the UNESCO 2005 Convention for the Protection and Promotion of the Diversity of Cultural Expressions, EDUCAB Romania has been instrumental in transforming libraries in small communities into inclusive cultural hubs. Rooted in the Convention’s principles, EDUCAB's mission supports libraries in opening their doors to everyone, fostering inclusive and culturally rich environments.  EDUCAB Romania uses strategies such as organizing meetings with ambassadors and decision-makers to plan and strategize support for libraries. By engaging influential figures and policymakers, EDUCAB invest energy so that public libraries receive the necessary backing to become vibrant centers of cultural exchange and learning.  EDUCAB Romania has significantly contributed through advocacy for the "Funding Libraries to Become Digital Skills Development Hubs" program from the National Recovery and Resilience Plan (PNRR), Pillar II, Component 7, Digital Transformation, Operation D: Digital Competencies, Human Capital, and Internet Use, approved by OMCID no. 21301/30.10.2023. This funding aims to equip libraries with the necessary technology and resources to function as digital hubs, providing community members with access to education and skill-building opportunities. This initiative further strengthens libraries' roles in digital literacy and community development.  Through Dare to care, project co-founded by the Erasmus+ Programme of the European Union, EducaB partner to reinforced and upgraded youth group methodology on building healthy relationships in rural and small urban communities of Romania, through the public libraries network.  In partnership with the Communities of the Future Association, New Horizons Association, and others, EDUCAB Romania has supported the development of services for Ukrainian refugees in Romanian public libraries. These initiative underscores the importance of providing access to cultural expressions for all, including underserved teenagers and marginalized and displaced populations. By integrating services for youth, refugees and other populations, libraries promote intercultural dialogue and understanding, aligning with the UNESCO Convention.  Transforming libraries involves making physical spaces more welcoming and functional for community activities. The International Organization for Migration (IOM) has supported these transformations, helping to redesign library spaces to be more open and accessible, facilitating greater community engagement and support. These physical changes are crucial in making libraries true community hubs where cultural expressions can be shared and celebrated.  Over the past four years, EDUCAB Romania has facilitated numerous cultural and informational events for underserved communities. These events range from theater and movie nights to digital literacy workshops and job skills training sessions. By providing a platform for diverse cultural activities, libraries supported by EDUCAB have become essential venues for cultural expression and community building.   The UNESCO 2005 Convention highlights the role of cultural policies in promoting diversity. EDUCAB Romania's efforts reflect this by advocating for policies that support the transformation of libraries into inclusive spaces. By doing so, they ensure that libraries continue to serve as dynamic cultural hubs that meet the evolving needs of their communities.  The initiatives to support Ukrainian refugees exemplify how libraries can respond to contemporary challenges. By offering tailored services and programs, libraries provide essential resources and support for refugees, fostering a sense of belonging and community. This adaptability ensures that libraries remain relevant and valuable cultural institutions.  Support from organizations like IOM has been crucial in these efforts. By assisting in the redesign of library spaces, IOM helps create functional, inviting, and accessible environments. These improvements enable libraries to host a wide range of events and activities, further enhancing their role as cultural hubs.  EDUCAB Romania’s efforts in transforming libraries align closely with the UNESCO 2005 Convention. By opening libraries to all community members, fostering partnerships, and transforming physical spaces, EDUCAB ensures that libraries serve as vibrant centers of cultural expression and community engagement. This initiative promotes cultural diversity and supports the social and cultural development of small communities, making libraries indispensable assets in Romania's cultural landscape.
Results: EDUCAB Romania has been actively transforming libraries into inclusive cultural hubs. Some of the results from the past four years are listed below.  The "Dare to Care" program has successfully implemented the Re-Group methodology in 14 public libraries across Romania, reaching over 150 teenagers. This ongoing process focuses on training librarians to work with youth groups, fostering engagement and cultural activities.  With the support of the International Organization for Migration (IOM), five public libraries have been refurbished to create more welcoming and functional spaces. These improvements are vital for facilitating community engagement and providing a conducive environment for cultural exchange.  Furthermore, seven public libraries now provide recurring services specifically designed for Ukrainian communities. These services include access to educational resources, cultural activities, and support networks, highlighting the libraries' role in promoting intercultural dialogue and understanding.  Additionally, over 100 libraries in Romania, supported by EDUCAB, offer recurring cultural events in their communities. Organizing movie nights or workshops, these public libraries  are providing a platform for diverse cultural activities and have become essential venues for cultural expression and community building.  EDUCAB Romania's comprehensive efforts, from refurbishing libraries and implementing the Re-Group methodology to supporting Ukrainian communities and promoting cultural events, demonstrate their commitment to enhancing the role of libraries as vibrant centers of cultural expression and learning. Through these initiatives, EDUCAB ensures that libraries remain relevant and valuable cultural institutions, fostering cultural diversity and community engagement.

Title EN: Organize CCI summit Ethiopia
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture
SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Partnering with civil society
Agency Implementation: Selam Ethiopia
Main Feature: CCI Summit Ethiopia  Selam Ethiopia organized the inaugural CCI Summit Ethiopia on April 8th and 9th, 2024, at Addis Ababa University's main campus in Ras Mekonnen Hall. The summit focused primarily on the Ethiopian music and film industries from a business perspective. Over two consecutive days, the event featured six presentations, followed by panel discussions and talks, as well as three pitches. A total of 28 professionals from Ethiopia, Sweden, and Rwanda participated as speakers, panelists, or moderators. The summit drew an audience of more than 134 individuals from diverse sectors, demonstrating high interest. Additionally, it gained significant media coverage which helped raise public awareness of the importance of the CCIs within the broader agenda for job creation and economic growth.  The CCI Summit Ethiopia inspired stakeholders such as the Addis Ababa Culture, Arts and Tourism Bureau, Addis Ababa University Institute of Ethiopian Studies, and the British Council to express their interest in future collaboration with Selam.  Business startups in the industry had the opportunity to present pitches, leading to one gaming sector company, one in the music sector, and one in the film industry receiving support from the Ministry of Labour and Skills. The summit fostered extensive networking and collaboration opportunities at national, regional, and international levels among participants, presenters, pitch session participants, and panelists.   It also paved the way for new initiatives for Selam and its partners; for instance, Selam, the Ethiopian Intellectual Property Authority, and CISAC (The International Societies of Authors and Composers) agreed to work together on copyright issues in Ethiopia, and Selam and AYO (Renowned Swedish and US-based publishing company) discussed strengthening their partnership in publishing. The sessions facilitated significant knowledge transfer and experience sharing among panelists, participants, and researchers.  Additionally, the summit showcased the untapped and vast business potential of the Ethiopian film and music sectors to investors and other stakeholders. As a pilot project, Selam implemented an entrance fee for participants through online applications, attracting 10 paid attendees and demonstrating high interest from various stakeholders and professionals.  Overall, the summit successfully achieved its objectives for the year. Firstly, it established the groundwork for the annual CCI summit in Ethiopia. Secondly, it facilitated extensive networking, experience sharing, and knowledge transfer among professionals in the sector at national, regional, and international levels. Lastly, it underscored the substantial potential of the Ethiopian music and film industries for economic development and job creation.
Results: As the first time event it successfully highlighted key issues and it raised lots of interest for the next events.  Networking and experience sharing are facilitated at national, regional, and international levels.

Title EN: ORGANISATION DE CAFES LITTERAIRES
Goal: Integrate Culture In Sustainable Development Frameworks
SDG: SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: National sustainable development policies and plans
Agency Implementation: Direction Régionale de la Culture et de la Francophonie d’Abidjan.
Main Feature: Dans l’esprit de la politique d’inclusion de la culture aux cadres du développement durable, les secteurs culturels et créatifs connaissent des essors divers. Contrairement au domaine musical et cinématographique dont le dynamisme est apparent, le domaine littéraire ne l’est pas et semble vraiment en souffrance.  En effet, aujourd’hui les jeunes préfèrent de loin l’image et le son via la technologie de l’androïd et de l’internet, par rapport au livre.  Cela impacte gravement et négativement leur niveau de langue ainsi que leur ouverture d’esprit devant concourir à leur développement personnel. Le secteur littéraire qui est un grand vivier d’emplois pouvant absorber nombre d’intelligences capable d’animer la chaine du livre est méconnu et mérite qu’on s’y intéresse davantage. C’est la raison qui fonde cette politique que nous avons instituée pour mener en amont, à partir du système de formation, l’élève de façon dynamique et attractive vers le monde littéraire et culturel en développant ses compétences artistiques et culturelles. L’aspect concret de cette politique, précisément en son volet promotion et valorisation du livre et de la lecture en région, en se rapprochant des populations, est intitulé « le café Littéraire ». Cette politique à travers cet angle dénommé « café littéraire », offre un espace convivial où les passionnés de littérature peuvent se réunir pour discuter de leurs lectures, partager des idées et découvrir de nouveaux auteurs, l’objectif étant de faire découvrir ce domaine passionnant à tout amateur potentiel. Cela favorise également la création de liens sociaux et le développement d’une communauté avertie autour de la littérature. Cette politique permet de renforcer l’intérêt et l’engagement du lecteur dans l’échange et la controverse. Il place l’élève dans une forme de lecture engageante qui cherche à développer l’implication éthique et sensible du lecteur dans sa transformation profonde de son rapport au monde, de même que dans son rapport à soi et aux autres. Au cours du café littéraire, chaque élève est en effet amené à interroger l’auteur en mobilisant ou en remobilisant des compétences littéraires et en mettant à l’épreuve ses croyances. Dans un contexte de plus en plus numérique, « le café littéraire » offre un refuge pour la conversation intellectuelle et la créativité. Il encourage les échanges d'idées, la découverte de nouvelles œuvres littéraires et la création de liens sociaux entre les amateurs de littérature, contribue à la revitalisation des quartiers en tant que points de rencontre culturels, favorisant ainsi le dynamisme économique local.   Une autre caractéristique importante de cette politique, est qu’elle créé un cadre d’expression littéraire, d’initiation à l’écriture et à la pratique littéraire qui vise à susciter la graine de l’écriture dans toutes ses tendances chez les apprenants par des concours d’écriture. Elle est véritablement une étape préparatoire à la formation à l’écriture. Elle offre un cadre d’échanges privilégié entre les élèves, les enseignants et les auteurs en favorisant la création littéraire et artistique par l’accent mis sur la collaboration entre les écrivains, éditeurs et élèves et par l’incitation des partenariats entre les différentes maisons d’édition et les imprimeurs.  La caractéristique suivante de cette politique est qu’elle créé un véritable cadre de consolidation du circuit littéraire pour assurer la création de ressources financières. Cela à coup sûr permettra de redynamiser les maillons de la chaine du livre, et encouragera la commercialisation des ouvrages ou produits littéraires par les libraires sur le site de l’activité. Pour être concret, un espace de distribution et de vente est toujours dédié pour la promotion du livre sur les sites du « CAFE LITTERAIRE ».  En somme, les « CAFE LITTERAIRES » sont des lieux essentiels pour promouvoir le livre, pour nourrir l'esprit et renforcer le tissu social.    Créé en 2018 de la volonté du Ministère de la Culture et de la Francophonie à travers ses Directions Régionales, le « CAFE LITTERAIRE » sillonne les établissements primaires et secondaires afin d’initier les pratiques culturelles en milieu scolaire. L’enjeu majeur de cette activité étant de familiariser l’élève avec l’univers du livre et d’installer dans le temps des habitudes et des repères par rapport à des pratiques qui lui sont étrangères. L’éducation doit développer chez le jeune le goût de créer, d’exercer des activités culturelles et artistiques. Créer une situation de pédagogie innovante par le biais des médiations culturelles.  La première édition du Café Littéraire a eu lieu le 30 Mars 2018 à Yopougon Andokoi et a tenu toutes ses promesses avec plus de 300 participants. La deuxième édition en 2019 à Koumassi n’a pas puis se tenir en la faveur du Covid19. Le « CAFE LITTERAIRE » a pu reprendre de plus belle en Novembre 2021 au Lycée Moderne Simone Ehivet GBAGBO et a tenu aussi toutes ses promesses avec la présence d’au moins 400 participants. Cette édition a atteint son paroxysme avec le sponsoring de certaines structures ayant compris la nécessité de soutenir cette politique, en offrant des gadgets aux participants. Le jeudi 07 Avril 2022, la direction Lycée Moderne Alassane Ouattara pour la quatrième édition du « CAFE LITTERAIRE » connaitra également un engouement de taille avec la maison d’Edition Valesse qui l’a accompagné en plus de la distribution de gadgets par deux structures qui ont accepté de le sponsoriser. Une cinquième édition du « CAFE LITTERAIRE » a connu a connu le même succès à Yopougon encore, en étant meublé bien sûr d’autres aspects de la création culturelle et artistique telles les prestations artistiques pour donner un aspect festif à l’activité.
Results: -  Existence dans les écoles de clubs de pratique littéraire par les élèves et les encadreurs ;   - Existence d’un espace de rencontre et d’échanges entre les écrivains, les élèves et les enseignants ;  -  Existence des Clubs de lecture dans les établissements.
Financial Ressources: 523.40 USD par séance de "Café Littéraires"
Recommandations: Le "café littéraire" joue un rôle fondamental dans la promotion de la lecture. C’est une activité qui mérite d’être suivi et encouragée.  -Subventionner cette politique pour la consolider ; -Continuer de faire la promotion de cette politique ; -Etendre cette politique à un terrain plus large comprenant les grandes écoles, universités…

Since 2010, the Ministry for Pacific Peoples has been supporting Pacific Language Weeks, promoting and raising awareness of the diversity of our Pacific languages. Each year, the Ministry works closely with Pacific communities to maintain and promote indigenous languages across the country, encouraging their use in our daily lives to help them thrive.  The Strategy is founded on the vision that “Thriving Pacific languages build a prosperous Aotearoa” and its three key objectives are to:  •	recognise the value of Pacific languages in Aotearoa •	strengthen pathways and resources for learning, and learning in, Pacific languages •	create environments for Pacific languages to be used more often and in more spaces.  The Strategy is implemented through a Pacific Languages Government Action Plan and ethnic-specific Community Language Action Plans.  Pacific languages play an important role in strengthening Pacific peoples’ sense of identity and belonging. This, in turn, increases confidence, educational outcomes, employability and the ability to make strong contributions to their communities, to New Zealand and the Pacific region.  Notably, the New Zealand government plays a key role in protecting and maintaining the Tokelau, Niuean, and Cook Island languages (realm countries) which are classified as endangered by the United Nations. These populations predominantly reside in New Zealand and are New Zealand citizens. This work helps profile the Ministry in the wider Pacific region as a trusted supporter of Pacific languages and culture, ultimately strengthening our bilateral relationships.  Pacific Language Weeks The Ministry’s 11 Pacific Language Weeks (running from May until November 2024) celebrate regional unity, contribute to New Zealand culture and our long-standing links with the Pacific. The Ministry will continue to work collaboratively with Pacific nations, sharing information and resources to support language revitalisation and maintenance in the region, recognising the diversity between and within Pacific indigenous values and priorities. These 11 Pacific Language Weeks raise awareness around the value and use of Pacific languages in Aotearoa. Language weeks include Rotuma, Samoa, Kiribati, Cook Islands, Tongan, Tuvaluan, Fijian, Niuean, Tokelau, Tok Pisin (Papua New Guinea), and Solomon Islands Pijin. Funding for Pacific language classes The Ministry funds the Centre for Pacific Languages to deliver language classes for 9 Pacific languages: Tokelau, Niue, Cook Islands, Samoan, Tongan, Tuvaluan, Kiribati, Fijian, and Rotuman. Pacific languages community fund This is funding to support community Pacific language initiatives to support Pacific language use and learning, and creation of resources.
Results: A Leo Moana o Aotearoa project was launched by the Ministry alongside the Pacific Languages Strategy in 2022. The research project involved both a national survey as well as talanoa with Pacific communities from nine Pacific groups across Aotearoa (Tokelau, Niue, Cook Islands, Samoa, Tonga, Tuvalu, Fiji, Rotuma, and Kiribati) to gain an in-depth understanding of the use and valuing of Pacific languages by Pacific people in Aotearoa. The aim of the project was to provide baseline data and a better understanding of the current state of Pacific languages in Aotearoa and support the revitalisation, maintenance and sustainability of Pacific languages in Aotearoa.   This project will be repeated every four years to monitor progress of the Pacific Languages Strategy, and to help to determine where to direct new investment in Pacific languages. The key findings from the 2022 report (https://www.mpp.govt.nz/assets/Reports/Leo-Moana/Leo-Moana-Survey-Report-Web2.1.pdf) indicate that: •	Pacific languages are valued highly by Pacific people. Pacific languages are an important part of New Zealand’s national identity.  •	There is unmet demand for Pacific language education – both the learning of Pacific languages in education, as well as Pacific bilingual and immersion schooling. •	There is a clear and significant break in intergenerational transmission of Pacific languages across all language groups. The rates of transmission of languages from adults to school-aged children are extremely low. This threatens the continuity of Pacific languages. •	There is an increasing number of Pacific people, particularly young people, who speak English as a first language. •	The emerging domains of media and technology, sport and recreation, and the workplace as spaces where more Pacific languages are being used, are significant.
Financial Ressources: Budget 2023 provided $13.3 million NZD/ $ 8.1 million USD over four years to implement the Pacific Languages Strategy, which includes: •	$9.2 million NZD/ $5.6 million USD for Pacific media entities to deliver Pacific language programming in innovative and sustainable ways. •	$4.1 million NZD/ $2.5 million USD for an online resource hub and public information campaign to create a new platform for Pacific language learners and speakers, with better access to resources to support their learning journey. https://www.beehive.govt.nz/release/budget-2023-invests-pacific-wellbeing-and-prosperity

Title EN: Participation à la mise en oeuvre de la Déclaration de Marrakech 2020 pour la lutte contre la violence faite aux femmes
Goal: Promote Human Rights And Fundamental Freedoms
SDG: SDG 5 - Achieve gender equality and empower all women and girls,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels
Area of Monitoring: Gender equality
Cultural Domain: Design,Performing Arts,Media Arts,Cinema and Audiovisual Arts,Music,Publishing,Visual Arts
Agency Implementation: Ministère de la Jeunesse, de la Culture et de la Communication-Département de la Culture
Main Feature: Les femmes constituent un élément clé de l'équation sociale basée sur le genre. Elles constituent un enjeu politique, économique et culturel, ce qui en fait une préoccupation juridique en matière de droits de l'homme et de développement dans de nombreux secteurs gouvernementaux, organisations et comités régionaux et internationaux. La Déclaration de Marrakech sur l'élimination de la violence à l'égard des femmes rassemble les efforts de nombreux acteurs aux niveaux national, régional et local pour améliorer la situation des femmes marocaines, leur permettre d'exercer pleinement leurs droits dans tous les domaines et œuvrer à l'amélioration de leur image.  Dans le cadre des engagements du ministère de la Jeunesse, de la Culture et de la Communication, secteur de la Culture, liés à la Déclaration de Marrakech, le ministère, en collaboration avec ses directions régionales et ses institutions culturelles, prend une série de mesures pour sensibiliser à l'importance des femmes, lutter contre toutes les formes de violence à leur égard et combattre les stéréotypes et les perceptions négatives les concernant. Voici les actions mises en œuvre :  Formulation d'un programme pour le secteur de la culture afin de mettre en œuvre la Déclaration de Marrakech 2020 en coordination avec l'Union nationale des femmes marocaines (19 janvier 2021) et émission d'un mémorandum aux directeurs régionaux pour son application. Transfert d'une contribution financière de 500 000 dirhams à l'Union nationale des femmes marocaines pour l'année 2021, dans le cadre de l'accord conclu avec le ministère de la Jeunesse, de la Culture et de la Communication, secteur de la Culture, pour une période de trois ans. Participation à l'élaboration du projet de stratégie nationale de lutte contre la violence à l'égard des femmes et des filles 2020-2030 sous la tutelle du ministère de la Solidarité, du Développement social, de l'Égalité et de la Famille, avec d'autres secteurs, à travers une série d'actions et d'engagements. Participation au colloque international consacré à la présentation du guide de référence "Pour des espaces publics urbains accessibles aux femmes et aux filles" organisé par le ministère de la Préparation territoriale, de l'Urbanisation, du Logement et de la Politique de la ville en partenariat avec ONU Femmes, le 8 mars 2021. Participation à la réunion consultative nationale sur les résultats et les défis de la mise en œuvre de la Déclaration et du Programme d'action de Pékin, sur le thème : "Promouvoir un environnement favorable et durable pour l'autonomisation économique des femmes et des filles", le mardi 8 juin 2021. Organisation de quatre ateliers artistiques (atelier d'art, atelier de gravure, atelier de bandes dessinées, atelier de cinéma d'animation) par l'Institut National des Beaux-Arts, en collaboration avec l'Union de l'Action Féminine, section Martil, dans le cadre du projet "Marché de la Femme". Une série d'œuvres d'art réalisées par les étudiants de l'institut (11 femmes, 6 hommes) sous la supervision académique et technique des professeurs de l'institut. Création d'un guide pour l'exposition "Musawah" par l'Institut National des Beaux-Arts et la direction régionale de Tanger-Tétouan Al Hoceima, présentant les œuvres d'art des étudiants de l'institut réalisées dans le cadre du projet "Marché de la Femme", en coopération avec des associations de la société civile à Tétouan. Organisation d'ateliers de sensibilisation basés sur la technique théâtrale "théâtre forum" par l'Institut supérieur d'art dramatique et d'animation culturelle, sous la supervision des diplômés de l'Institut et l'orientation de leurs professeurs, où des événements simulant la réalité sont présentés sous forme théâtrale pour interagir avec le public. Organisation d'ateliers artistiques dans plusieurs centres culturels appartenant au secteur de la culture, avec la participation d'artistes, de poètes et d'intellectuels locaux, pour promouvoir les valeurs et corriger les idées fausses concernant les femmes et leur rôle dans la société. Organisation de réunions intellectuelles et de lectures de poèmes de femmes à distance par les directions régionales et les centres culturels. Célébration annuelle de la Journée internationale de la femme dans toutes les directions régionales de la culture et les institutions et espaces culturels appartenant au secteur de la culture, pour promouvoir le rôle des femmes dans la réalité culturelle et reconnaître leurs contributions en tant qu'actrices clés du mouvement culturel et intellectuel au sein de la société. Promotion des réalisations créatives, intellectuelles et culturelles des femmes en présentant leurs publications littéraires lors des foires du livre régionales ou des festivals et événements culturels et artistiques organisés régulièrement par le ministère. Mise en valeur du dynamisme culturel de certaines associations féminines œuvrant dans le domaine de la culture, des arts et du patrimoine culturel, et soutien à leurs activités culturelles et artistiques. Conclusion d'accords de partenariat et de coopération avec des comités régionaux, des ONG et des acteurs de la société civile pour promouvoir les droits et libertés des femmes et les sensibiliser à leur rôle de pionnières dans divers domaines. Organisation d'expositions formatives qui mettent en valeur les compétences des femmes et abordent les problèmes et les formes de violence dont elles sont victimes. Augmentation du pourcentage de participation des femmes à tous les événements et festivals culturels et artistiques organisés par le ministère, avec des segments dédiés aux femmes créatrices sur la scène culturelle pour stimuler les talents féminins.
Results: La mise en œuvre des politiques et mesures visant à promouvoir les droits et le rôle des femmes dans la société marocaine a abouti à des résultats significatifs et diversifiés. Depuis l'adoption de la Déclaration de Marrakech sur l'élimination de la violence à l'égard des femmes, plusieurs avancées tangibles ont été observées grâce à l'engagement continu du ministère de la Jeunesse, de la Culture et de la Communication, secteur de la Culture, en collaboration avec ses partenaires locaux et internationaux.  Premièrement, sur le plan de la sensibilisation et de l'éducation, la formulation d'un programme dédié a permis d'accroître la conscientisation quant à l'importance des droits des femmes et à la nécessité de lutter contre toutes les formes de violence à leur encontre. Des ateliers artistiques et des événements culturels ont été organisés à travers le pays, mobilisant des artistes, des intellectuels et des communautés locales pour promouvoir une image positive des femmes et déconstruire les stéréotypes négatifs.  Deuxièmement, sur le plan institutionnel, des partenariats stratégiques ont été établis avec des organisations de la société civile, des ONG et d'autres acteurs régionaux pour renforcer les politiques de protection des droits des femmes. La création d'un guide pour l'exposition "Musawah" et la participation à des colloques internationaux ont permis d'intégrer les perspectives féminines dans les politiques nationales et internationales de lutte contre la violence de genre.  Troisièmement, sur le plan économique et social, des initiatives spécifiques ont été mises en place pour promouvoir l'autonomisation économique des femmes à travers des programmes d'entrepreneuriat et de formation professionnelle. Cette approche vise à réduire les disparités économiques entre les genres et à renforcer la participation des femmes dans le développement économique du pays.  En outre, la célébration annuelle de la Journée internationale de la femme dans toutes les régions du Maroc a renforcé la visibilité et la reconnaissance des contributions des femmes dans le domaine culturel et intellectuel. Ces événements ont également servi de plateforme pour honorer les réalisations créatives et intellectuelles des femmes à travers des expositions littéraires, des performances artistiques et des forums de discussion.  Enfin, la politique mise en œuvre a également eu un impact sur la législation et les politiques publiques, contribuant à l'élaboration de la stratégie nationale de lutte contre la violence à l'égard des femmes et des filles 2020-2030. Cette stratégie guide les efforts gouvernementaux pour renforcer la protection juridique des femmes et améliorer l'accès à la justice pour les victimes de violence.  En résumé, la mise en œuvre proactive des politiques et mesures par le ministère de la Jeunesse, de la Culture et de la Communication a non seulement renforcé la position des femmes dans la société marocaine, mais a également jeté les bases d'une transformation culturelle et sociale plus inclusive. Ces efforts continus sont essentiels pour assurer que les droits des femmes soient pleinement respectés et que leur potentiel soit pleinement réalisé dans tous les aspects de la vie publique et privée au Maroc.

Title EN: PARTICIPATIONS AUX SOMMETS DE LA FRANCOPHONIE
Goal: Integrate Culture In Sustainable Development Frameworks
SDG: SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: International cooperation for sustainable development
Cultural Domain: Design,Performing Arts,Media Arts,Cinema and Audiovisual Arts,Music,Publishing,Visual Arts
Agency Implementation: Commission Nationale de la Francophonie (CNF)
Main Feature: Le Sommet de la Francophonie est une rencontre biennale des chefs d'État et de gouvernement des pays ayant le français en partage. Ce sommet vise à renforcer les liens de coopération entre les pays francophones et à promouvoir la langue française ainsi que les valeurs communes de démocratie, de droits de l’homme, et de développement durable. Les discussions portent sur des thèmes variés tels que l’éducation, la culture, l’économie, et les enjeux géopolitiques. Le sommet se termine généralement par l’adoption de déclarations et de résolutions visant à promouvoir la solidarité et la coopération au sein de la Francophonie. la Côte d'Ivoire participe régulièrement aux sommets de la Francophonie.
Results: Les résultats atteints sont :  -Renforcer la coopération politique, économique et culturelle entre les pays membres. - Promouvoir les droits de l’homme, la démocratie et la diversité culturelle. - Encourager le développement de programmes éducatifs et culturels. - Mobiliser des ressources pour des initiatives en faveur du développement durable. - Mettre en avant des solutions communes aux défis globaux, notamment en matière de climat et de sécurité.
Recommandations: L'évaluation a montré que le Sommet de la Francophonie joue un rôle indéniable dans la promotion de la coopération et de la solidarité entre les pays francophones. Les recommandations principales sont:   -Continuer à soutenir les initiatives de promotion de la langue française et de la diversité culturelle. -Renforcer les mécanismes de suivi et d'évaluation des décisions prises lors des sommets. - Encourager une participation plus active de la société civile et des jeunes dans les processus décisionnels. - Développer des partenariats plus étroits avec le secteur privé pour soutenir les projets de développement durable. Améliorer la communication et la visibilité des actions entreprises dans le cadre de la Francophonie.

Title EN: Performer avec les médias numériques - Formes d'interaction hybrides dans le jeu (théâtral) des jeunes
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture

Main Feature: Ce projet a la volonté d’initier les jeunes à une nouvelle forme de participation culturelle à l'ère numérique. Il s’agit de développer et d’expérimenter des formes d'expression théâtrales hybrides avec de jeunes clubs de théâtre. Les formats de jeux, qui sont devenus depuis longtemps une forme d'art à part entière, seront associés aux moyens des arts de la scène pour créer de nouvelles formes de jeu interactives. Les formes d'expression culturelles traditionnelles doivent être associées aux nouvelles technologies et permettre aux jeunes de faire leurs propres recherches dans un espace protégé. Grâce à la réalité augmentée, mixte et virtuelle, à l'interactivité en temps réel, à l'utilisation d'applications existantes, aux flux en direct, aux votes en ligne, aux projets immersifs, etc., elles et ils expérimentent le théâtre et le jeu sous forme hybride. Area of Monitoring: Partnering with civil society
Agency Implementation: Kenya Cultural Centre
Main Feature: Kenya Cultural Centre incorporating the Kenya National Theatre (KCC-NT) has partnered with Ignite Culture: ACP-EU Culture Programme (Eastern Africa) to implement the Poetry Theatre Development Project. The primary objective of the project is to provide emerging and existing artists with an opportunity to train, develop, nurture, and hone their poetry skills in a peer development mechanism for social-economic stability. KCC-NT runs a program called Poetry After Lunch (PAL). PAL is a national talent development platform that includes artists in different counties in Kenya. The main aim of PAL is to discover, mentor, and network artists for better placement in the creative industry. Currently, PAL national platform is in Nairobi with ten satellites in ten counties i.e. Lodwar, Narok, Kisumu, Embu, Meru, Busia, Nakuru, Kilifi, Kakamega, and Mombasa. Poetry Theatre Development Project is targeting PAL artists among other poets in the 11 counties. Most poets in these platforms write and perform short poetic pieces but lack adequate skills to write and perform long pieces and integrate them with other art disciplines to produce ticketed shows (full poetic theatre) that would enable them to earn a living from their art and positively impact the society. Accordingly, there is a need to enhance their artistic skills in writing, performing, entrepreneurial, and personal branding skills. This project is supported by a grant from Ignite Culture: ACP-EU Culture Programme (Eastern Africa). This fund is being implemented by HEVA Fund, in partnership with the British Council Kenya with the financial contribution of the European Union, and with further support from the Organisation of ACP (African, Caribbean and Pacific) States. It is part of the global ACP-EU Culture Programme. The project activities include training needs assessment, curriculum development, auditions and artist selection, and training and mentorship for the selected artists.
Results: Enhanced artistic skills, entrepreneurial capabilities, and personal branding of poets in Kenya, providing structured pathway for artists to develop sustainable careers in the creative industry while positively impacting their communities through arts and culture.

Title EN: Performing arts training in the education cycle. Theater in Education.
Goal: Integrate Culture In Sustainable Development Frameworks

Area of Monitoring: National sustainable development policies and plans
Agency Implementation: Teatro a Mil International Festival Foundation (FITAM).
Main Feature: Theater in Education is a programme of the Teatro a Mil International Foundation (FITAM), that has taken place since 2016 in a variety of public shools in the Metropolitan Region of Chile for the performing arts subject within the school full-day education curriculum for primary education, with the aim of contributing to integral development and strengthen cultural involvement of children and youth.  To date, since its launch, more than 2,000 students, 100 classes, from 21 schools in 7 communes of this region have participated in the experience. The measure is carried out in schools, within medium and medium-low performance categories and in areas with high levels of social vulnerability. This year (2023) Theatre in Eucation is being implemented over 12 courses, for the first and second primary cycle, in public schools of the Lampa and La Granja communes.  The specific programme goals are focused on: enhancing creative capacities and expressive skills of children and youth, through dramatic play and artistic experimentation of stage language; developing social-emotional skills that favour good treatment among peers and contribute to the school's social climate through dramatic play and collective participation in creative processes; transferring fun and active methodologies, from theatrical pedagogy, to teachers of the school community, through the creation of co-teaching in the performing arts subject; and contributing to the cultural participation of children and youth and their educational communities in creation and pleasure of art experiences related to the performing arts.  In addition to these goals, pedagogical practices include a rights-based approach and a gender perspective.
Results: To date, since its launch, more than 2,000 students have participated in the experience, 100 courses from 21 schools in 7 districts of the Metropolitan Region of Chile. All these students have been to a theatre on pedagogical excursions at least once, each of the 100 classes, of the first and second primary cycle, have had at least 50 pedagogical hours of performing arts classes annually within their school full-day schedule and have reached the end with a theatre show that they could perform in front of the school community.  Given that the performing arts are not part of the national primary education curriculum, like the visual or music arts are, the impact of the measure has achieved the consolidation of a curriculum proposal par excellence, with an interdisciplinary work methodology that is in line with institutional frameworks, contributing to the development of the Sustainable Development Goals, the National Policy on Culture and the recommendations from the Foro de Educación Artística (Arts Education Forum), proposing an innovation to the school curriculum and to the public policies on education, exploring a feasable model for implementation in schools.  Its sustained development has provided evidence and important lessons regardingthe opportunities that theatre offers in early socialisation by adding it in school, expanding creative, communicative and social-emotional skills that have an impact on learning, cultural capital and school coexistence.  Its implementation promotes cultural participation of students from public schools, with reduced access to artistic experiences related to the performing arts, thus constributing to the promotion and assurance of guaranteed cultural rights by the Organization of Ibero-American States (OEI) and the United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organisation (UNESCO).
Recommandations: During 2022, evaluation questionnaires were given to students, obtaining a sample of 243 responses. Based on this, the following results are obtained, in relation to the recognition of the effects of this measure on creative and social-emotional skills.   Ot those studients, 85% sustain that the class helped them learn how to regulate their energy and behavior, 80% rated their experience in the subject with an outstanding grade (7.0), 89% believed that the classes were a space to create, where they could develop their imagination and 87%  affirmed that the subject helped them to get to know and value themselves more.   On the other hand, interviews and focus groups with co-teachers were conducted, where the following testimonies from the studens, on learning about overcoming shame, personality development and teamwork, stand out: âI learned to value myself, to get rid of my fear of being in front of many people and to be a little more empatheticâ, âto be able to express my ideas, to learn new things, I worked in a team with people I never imaginedâ.

Title EN: Policies that Support a Balanced Flow of International Cultural Goods and Services
Goal: Achieve A Balanced Flow Of Cultural Goods And Services And Increase The Mobility Of Artists And Cultural Professionals
SDG: SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 10 - Reduce inequality within and among countries,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Flow of cultural goods and services
Cultural Domain: Design,Performing Arts,Media Arts,Cinema and Audiovisual Arts,Music
Agency Implementation: 1. Ministry of Finance (Kementerian Keuangan, Kemenkeu)  2. Ministry of Trade (Kementerian Perdagangan, Kemendag)
Main Feature: In the past four years, policies that support a balanced flow of international cultural goods and services include:  1. Law 24 of 2000 on International Agreements (Law on International Agreements);  2. Law 7 of 2014 on Trade (Law on Trade);  3. Law 6 of 2023 on the Stipulation of Government Regulation in Lieu of Law 2 of 2022 on Job Creation into Law (Law on Job Creation);   4. Draft Law on Amendments to Law 24 of 2000 on International Agreements (Draft Law on International Agreements);  5. Draft Law on Amendments to Law 7 of 2014 on Trade (Draft Law on Trade);  6. Government Regulation 80 of 2019 on Trades through Electronic Systems (Perdagangan melalui Sistem Elektronik) (GR on PMSE);  7. Government Regulation 49 of 2022 on Value-Added Tax Exempted and Value-Added Tax or Value-Added Tax and Sales Tax on Luxury Goods Not Charged on the Import and/or Delivery of Certain Taxable Goods and/or Delivery of Certain Taxable Services and/or Utilization of Certain Taxable Services from Outside the Customs;  8. Minister of Finance Regulation 90/PMK.04/2012 on Exemption from Import Duty on Imports of Goods for Museums, Zoos, and Other Similar Places Open to the Public, as well as Goods for Nature Conservation;  9. Minister of Finance Regulation 223/PMK.011/2014 on Criteria for Educational Services that are Not Subject to Value-Added Tax;  10. Minister of Finance Regulation 228/PMK.04/2014 on Temporary Imports using a Carnet or Exports that are Intended to be Reimported within a Certain Time Period using a Carnet;  11. Minister of Finance Regulation 32/PMK.010/2019 on Limitations on Activities and Types of Taxable Services whose Exports Are Subject to Value-Added Tax;  12. Minister of Finance Regulation 5/PMK.010/2020 of 2020 on General Textbooks, Holy Books, and Religious Textbooks whose Import and/or Delivery are Exempt from Value-Added Taxes;   13. Minister of Finance Regulation 115/PMK.03/2021 on Procedures for Providing Facilities to be Exempted from the Imposition of Value-Added Tax on the Import and/or Delivery of Certain Strategic Taxable Goods, Procedures for Payment of Value-Added Tax on Certain Strategic Taxable Goods that Have Been Exempted from the Imposition of Value-Added Tax Used are Not in Accordance with Original or Transferred Purpose, and Imposition of Sanctions for Late Payment of Value-Added Tax; and  14. Minister of Finance Regulation 70/PMK.03/2022 on Criteria and/or Details of Food and Beverages, Arts and Entertainment Services, Hospitality Services, Parking Space Provision Services, and Catering Services, which are Not Subject to Value-Added Tax.  Several policies reported in the 2020 QPR, namely: (1) Minister of Finance Regulation 228/PMK.04/2014 on Temporary Imports using a Carnet or Exports that are Intended to be Reimported within a Certain Time Period using a Carnet; and (2) Minister of Finance Regulation 32/PMK.010/2019 on Limitations on Activities and Types of Taxable Services whose Exports Are Subject to Value-Added Tax, are still valid at the time of drafting this report. Meanwhile, the Minister of Finance Regulation 158/PMK.010/2015 on Criteria for Arts and Entertainment Services that are Not Subject to Value-Added Tax has been replaced with the Minister of Finance Regulation 70/PMK.03/2022 on Criteria and/or Details of Food and Beverages, Arts and Entertainment Services, Hospitality Services, Parking Space Provision Services, and Catering Services, which are Not Subject to Value-Added Tax.  This value-added tax policy is one of the most essential instruments in supporting the balance of the international flow of goods and services, including arts and culture. To simplify regulations and adjust arrangements in providing convenience in the field of value-added tax and sales tax on luxury goods, Government Regulation 49 of 2022 on Value-Added Tax Exempted and Value-Added Tax or Value-Added Tax and Sales Tax on Luxury Goods Not Charged on the Import and/or Delivery of Certain Taxable Goods and/or Delivery of Certain Taxable Services and/or Utilization of Certain Taxable Services from Outside the Customs. Several parts of the regulations in the GR that are relevant to the Convention include exemptions for (1) general textbooks, including educational books and general books that contain elements of arts and culture education; (2) raw materials for silver crafts in the form of silver granules and/or silver bars; (3) raw untanned hides and skins; (4) goods for museums and other similar places open to the public which are granted exemption from import duty; and (5) formal and non-formal education services, from the imposition of value-added tax.  For more technical regulations, several Minister of Finance Regulations have existed or have just been issued in the past four years, as follows. 1. The Minister of Finance Regulation 90/PMK.04/2012 on Exemption from Import Duty on Imports of Goods for Museums, Zoos, and Other Similar Places Open to the Public, as well as Goods for Nature Conservation, regulates the exemption from value-added tax for goods for museum purposes and other similar places.  2. The Minister of Finance Regulation 223/PMK.011/2014 on Criteria for Educational Services that are Not Subject to Value-Added Tax regulates the exemption from value-added tax for formal and non-formal education services.  3. The Minister of Finance Regulation 5/PMK.010/2020 of 2020 on General Textbooks, Holy Books, and Religious Textbooks whose Import and/or Delivery are Exempt from Value-Added Taxes regulates the exemption from value-added tax for general textbooks.  4. The Minister of Finance Regulation 115/PMK.03/2021 on Procedures for Providing Facilities to be Exempted from the Imposition of Value-Added Tax on the Import and/or Delivery of Certain Strategic Taxable Goods, Procedures for Payment of Value-Added Tax on Certain Strategic Taxable Goods that Have Been Exempted from the Imposition of Value-Added Tax Used are Not in Accordance with Original or Transferred Purpose, and Imposition of Sanctions for Late Payment of Value-Added Tax regulates the exemption from value-added tax for raw materials for silver crafts in the form of granular silver and/or silver bullion as well as untanned raw hides and skins.  Furthermore, there are several other Minister of Finance Regulations which also regulate tax exemptions, such as (1) the Minister of Finance Regulation 228/PMK.04/2014 on Temporary Imports using a Carnet or Exports that are Intended to be Reimported within a Certain Time Period using a Carnet; (2) the Minister of Finance Regulation 32/PMK.010/2019 on Limitations on Activities and Types of Taxable Services whose Exports Are Subject to Value-Added Tax; and (3) the Minister of Finance Regulation 70/PMK.03/2022 on Criteria and/or Details of Food and Beverages, Arts and Entertainment Services, Hospitality Services, Parking Space Provision Services, and Catering Services, which are Not Subject to Value-Added Taxes.  Balance in the flow of international arts and culture services can also be achieved through the implementation of the Law on International Agreements, the Law on Trade, and the Law on Job Creation (see Goal 1, Policies and Measures that Encourage Job Creation and Entrepreneurship in Culture and Creative Economy Sectors), especially regarding trade in arts and cultural goods and the use of foreign film personnel. As regulated in the Law on International Agreements, the international cooperation that Indonesia participates in is guided by national interests and based on the principles of equality and mutual benefit, taking into account both applicable national and international laws. Furthermore, the Law on Trade states that one of the trade objectives is to increase trade in creative economy-based products. The matters directed in these two laws support the creation of a balanced flow of international arts and cultural services.  The implementation of GR on PMSE can also balance the flow of international arts and cultural goods. In this GR, the Central Government determines a positive list of imported goods that can be imported directly via electronic system trading (e-commerce). The types of imported goods allowed to be sold via e-commerce are books, films, software, and music at below USD 100. Thus, other commodities can only be imported directly via e-commerce if the price exceeds USD 100.  In recent developments, stakeholders have identified a real need to update the Law on International Agreements and the Law on Trade to be more responsive to current developments and all its challenges and opportunities. Although the Draft Law on International Agreements and Draft Law on Trade have been registered with the National Legislation Program, they are not yet a priority for completion in 2024.  In general, policies that support a balanced flow of international cultural goods and services are aimed at contributing to achieving the following agenda(s) of the National Strategy for Culture:  1. Provide space for the diversity of cultural expressions and encourage cultural interaction to strengthen the inclusiveness of culture (Agenda 1);  2. Develop and utilize cultural resources to strengthen the position of Indonesia internationally (Agenda 3); and  3. Strengthen the role of the government as a facilitator of culture advancement (Agenda 7).

Title EN: Pilot Project for the Implemention of the UNESCO Culture|2030 Indicators in Viet Nam and the City of Hue
Goal: Integrate Culture In Sustainable Development Frameworks
SDG: SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: International cooperation for sustainable development
Cultural Domain: Design,Performing Arts,Media Arts,Cinema and Audiovisual Arts,Music,Publishing,Visual Arts
Agency Implementation: Vietnam National Institute of Culture and Arts Studies (Ministry of Culture, Sports and Tourism); International Cooperation Department (Ministry of Culture, Sports and Tourism)
Main Feature: The pilot implementation of the Culture|2030 Indicators is part of a long-term plan spearheaded by UNESCO to develop a comprehensive system of tools for measuring and monitoring the contributions of culture in achieving the Sustainable Development Goals of the 2030 Agenda. In Viet Nam, pursuant to the agreement signed between UNESCO and the Ministry of Culture, Sports, and Tourism, the project has been executed at both national and local levels (specifically in the city of Hue) from October 2021 to June 2022. The Culture|2030 Indicators comprise 22 indicators categorized into 4 groups that encompass the most critical aspects of sustainable development, spanning from environmental to economic and social dimensions. This instrument serves to evaluate the role of culture both as an independent domain and as a cross-cutting element in various other sectors.
Results: Through systematically collected and analyzed data, the Culture|2030 Indicators facilitate a comprehensive and objective assessment of the scale and degree of development within Viet Nam's cultural sector. This includes various dimensions such as the contribution of culture to GDP, the commercial value of cultural goods and services, the number of individuals employed in the cultural sector, and the number of cultural enterprises. These findings also play a crucial role in monitoring the implementation of the 2030 Agenda both nationally and in the city of Hue. Moreover, being one of the first 12 countries to implement UNESCO's Culture|2030 Indicators provides Viet Nam with the opportunity to review its cultural statistics system, apply advanced statistical methods developed by international experts, enhance the capabilities of domestic specialists, and raise awareness regarding the significance of culture in sustainable development.
Recommandations: The outcomes of the project have received approval from the lead agency, the Ministry of Culture, Sports, and Tourism, along with the agencies providing data at both the national and local levels. The national and local project reports have been integrated into UNESCO's online database. Drawing on the theoretical foundation and methodology of the Culture|2030 Indicators, and the insights gained from the project's implementation, the Ministry of Culture, Sports, and Tourism has been systematically developing and enhancing Viet Nam's national indicators. These indicators aim to measure the contributions of culture and furnish solid evidence for policy-making, strategic planning, and practical development programs. In October 2023, the Ministry of Culture, Sports, and Tourism issued Decision No. 2974/QĐ-BVHTTDL, approving the Plan for the Development of National Cultural Indicators for Sustainable Development. This initiative has been executed over the period of 2023-2024, led by the Viet Nam National Institute of Culture and Arts Studies, with the participation and coordination of various agencies and units both within and outside the Ministry.

Area of Monitoring: Cultural and creative sectors
Cultural Domain: Design,Media Arts,Cinema and Audiovisual Arts,Music,Publishing,Visual Arts
Agency Implementation: Bissap Lab   Xácara Culture
Main Feature: Under the leadership of the organisations Bissap Lab and Xacara Culture, a pilot online training workshop on the 2005 UNESCO Convention took place in November 2023, with the aim of socialising its principles and contents, practical guidelines, monitoring framework and participation mechanisms with members of civil organisations active in the Mexican civic space, in order to strengthen their involvement in filling out the official forms that are directly linked to the accountability actions on this international treaty. The workshop was piloted in webinar format through the Zoom videoconferencing platform and with the use of two additional virtual interaction tools: 1) Breaking Rooms, to stimulate reflection and conversation among attendees, and 2) the Kahoot! platform to reinforce the knowledge transmitted throughout the session through a game and trivia dynamic related to the 2005 Convention. The participation of groups from various parts of the country was achieved, with whom we sought more specifically:  - To be aware of the tool in general terms and its potential benefits, above all, for influencing decision-making processes and the design-monitoring of cultural policies.  - To imagine creative ways of interacting with and taking advantage of the Convention in their different domains of work, i.e. without adding layers of complexity and difficulties to their daily work.  - To identify the guidelines and tools of the CSO Forms, to take ownership of them and, in turn, to disseminate them among their peers, to enrich the perspectives of the Quadrennial Periodic Report to be integrated in 2024. Finally, the official tool provided by UNESCO was presented, with which organisations can make known the measures and projects they promote to contribute to the protection and promotion of the diversity of cultural expressions. The presentation represented a sequential guide of the questions that would be found throughout the questionnaire, recommendations on how to best approach it, who can answer it, official languages and assistance for translation, channels for sending it to UNESCO and how to submit it for subsequent consideration by the State Party in the Quadrennial Periodic Report
Results: Creation of a Recommendations Report (Discussion Paper), based on the findings of the workshop and the weightings elaborated by the Bissap Lab and Xácara Culture teams.  Elaboration of a self-assessment guide to measure the openness or obstruction of the Mexican Civic Space to protect and promote the diversity of cultural expressions.
