Title EN: Residency Programs
Goal: Achieve A Balanced Flow Of Cultural Goods And Services And Increase The Mobility Of Artists And Cultural Professionals
SDG: SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 10 - Reduce inequality within and among countries,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Mobility of artists and cultural professionals
Agency Implementation: Art Jameel Dubai Warehouse 421 Alserkal Arts Foundation Abu Dhabi Department of Culture and Tourism The Cultural Foundation Abu Dhabi Art Hub
Main Feature: Various institutions in the UAE have offered and continue to offer cultural residency programs to support the arts, culture, and ensure cultural diversity in the UAE. Some of the existing residency programs in the UAE include: 421 Homebound Residency Program: The program is delivered by 421 and aims to support creative practitioners in the region in producing new work and exploring digital forms of community engagement in their practices while socially isolating. The residency program offers residents a production budget that can go up to AED 20,000 to spend on equipment and materials for the realization of their projects in their own spaces. The Program is open to all creative practitioners, including but not limited to Visual Arts and Curation, Design and Technology, Literary Arts, Music, Culinary Arts, Theatre and Performance, in the Middle East, North Africa and South Asia region. Art Residency: The educational platforms at the Cultural Foundation include Art Residency. The six-month residency provides professional artists with a platform to hone and advance their art practice. Cultural Foundation provides dedicated studio space, specialized resources, and access to its facilities. The residency program also provides participants with opportunities to produce, and exhibit works within the Cultural Foundation, strengthening their presence in the local art scene. Artist Residency Grants: The Al Qasimi Foundation's Artist Residency Grants provide opportunities for visiting local and international artists to produce new works and engage in cultural exchange with the Ras Al Khaimah community. Visiting artists are encouraged to draw inspiration from the Emirates as they work on personal projects and to share their talent with the local community by leading art workshops and classes. Applications are welcome from all nationalities and artistic media for residencies lasting 6-12 months. Artists are based in the Al Qasimi Foundation’s Studio & Gallery during their residencies, culminating in an exhibition and the potential to engage the community in developing a public art installation. Residency Programme: The Sharjah Art Foundation Residency Programme offers visiting artists and art practitioners a dedicated outpost in Sharjah, not only as a place of rest, reflection and exploration, but also as a unique point of departure for those who are reassessing their relationship with the Emirates and the region at large. Residencies are offered by invitation or through a call for applications. While the specific aims of the residency may vary, we look for proposals that reflect, in a broad sense, an interest and engagement with the regional context. This could simply be the desire for a new cultural experience that might later impact an artist’s work, or it may result in art that is a direct response to this experience or perhaps even a site-specific project. With this programme we aim to promote the possibilities of exchange between artists, the local community and the broader cultural landscape. The Writers' Retreat: The Writers' Retreat, a distinguished initiative presented by the Ministry of Culture in collaboration with Kalimat Group, offers a unique opportunity to draw inspiration from industry professionals and connect with fellow writers. it is a seven-night, eight-day experience designed to transform the writing practice. The retreat features a series of meticulously curated workshops, masterclasses, and seminars led by acclaimed authors and literary experts. Participants will have the chance to broaden their horizons and enhance their writing skills through comprehensive sessions covering all facets of the creative process. With personalized feedback and expert guidance, attendees can expect to see their talents flourish in unprecedented ways. Art Jameel Commissions: Art Jameel Center has a longstanding interest in commissioning artists to make new works, often for the public realm, as well as in media or situations that further their ongoing artistic practice.  Al Serkal Residency: Alserkal Residency is provided by Al Serkal Arts Foundation and was created as a platform for artistic and discursive exchange, seeking to support cultural practitioners as they realize projects pertinent to their respective practices. The program is designed to be immersive and engage the local interdisciplinary community through a series of public events and conversations. It focuses on research-based and socially engaged practices.
Recommandations: Art residency programs in the UAE have made significant contributions to the artistic community, enhancing both individual careers and the broader cultural landscape. These programs offer essential support for artists by providing dedicated time, space, and resources, which are crucial for their creative development. They also play a key role in fostering cultural exchange by bringing together artists from diverse backgrounds, enriching the local art scene, and facilitating cross-cultural dialogue. Additionally, these residencies engage the local community through workshops, exhibitions, and public talks, helping to deepen public appreciation for contemporary art.

Title EN: Programme for the Support of Cultural and Artistic Festivals (PROFEST)
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture
SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Cultural and creative sectors
Agency Implementation: Directorate General for Cultural Promotion and Festivals , Ministry of Culture
Main Feature: The Ministry of Culture of the Government of Mexico, through the General Directorate for Cultural Promotion and Festivals (DGPFC) oversees the Support Programme for Cultural and Artistic Festivals (PROFEST). This initiative aims to promote, preserve, and enhance Mexico's artistic and cultural heritage.   PROFEST provides co-investment support to festivals encompassing performing arts, visual arts, film, design, literature, and food culture. These festivals are organized by municipalities, municipal cultural institutions, state public universities, and non-profit civil society organizations. The primary objective is to ensure widespread access to cultural experiences for the population, thereby promoting the fundamental right to culture.
Results: The annual call of this program significantly enhances the cultural and artistic landscape nationwide. It promotes broad access to culture for all citizens by fostering the organization and professionalization of cultural and artistic festivals. Moreover, it plays a pivotal role in revitalizing the artistic sector post the COVID-19 pandemic, prompting festivals to adopt hybrid formats from 2020 onwards to engage the public with artistic projects.  Between 2021 and 2022, the program supported 358 festivals, enabling the realization of 9,624 activities. These events attracted an audience totaling 10,087,094 individuals and involved 46,444 artistic groups across all 32 states of the country.

Title EN: Programme National Le théâtre en mouvement
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture
SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Cultural and creative sectors
Agency Implementation: Ministère de la Jeunesse, de la Culture et de la Communication-Département de la Culture
Main Feature: L’initiative du théâtre move a pour objectif de promouvoir et de développer les industries culturelles et créatives nationales. Ce programme vise à atténuer les répercussions de la crise sur le secteur de théâtre. Via ce grand chantier en partenariat avec la Société nationale de radiodiffusion et de télévision, le Département de la Culture vise  également à rapprocher le théâtre du grand public et à mettre en lumière le rôle de la culture, notamment dans un contexte de crise. Dans ce cadre, 60 pièces de théâtre sont filmées et diffusées sur les chaînes de la SNRT et sur la plateforme numérique du département de la culture. Les droits de diffusion de ces pièces de théâtre sont achetés moyennant des montants allant de 15.000 à 20.000 euros. Une commission conjointe regroupant des représentants des deux institutions et des professionnels du secteur sera ainsi mise en place afin de choisir les productions théâtrales qui seront filmées et diffusées dans le cadre de cette initiative. En ce qui concerne les critères d’éligibilité, ce programme est par ailleurs destiné aux troupes marocaines professionnelles, organisées sous forme d’associations ou sociétés. Sont éligibles en fait les productions théâtrales produites entre 2016-2021 et prêtes pour le tournage.
Results: •  Rapprochement du théâtre avec le grand public : En filmant et diffusant 60 pièces de théâtre sur les chaînes de la SNRT et sur la plateforme numérique du Département de la Culture, l'initiative a permis de rendre le théâtre plus accessible au grand public, élargissant ainsi l'audience et suscitant un intérêt renouvelé pour cet art. •  Soutien financier aux troupes théâtrales : Les droits de diffusion des pièces de théâtre ont été achetés pour des montants allant de 15.000 à 20.000 euros, offrant ainsi un soutien financier significatif aux troupes marocaines professionnelles. Cela a aidé les troupes à surmonter les difficultés économiques engendrées par la crise. •  Valorisation des productions nationales : En choisissant des productions théâtrales produites entre 2016 et 2021, l’initiative a mis en lumière la diversité et la richesse des créations théâtrales marocaines, tout en valorisant le travail des artistes locaux. •  Mise en avant du rôle de la culture en période de crise : En mettant en lumière le rôle crucial de la culture, notamment en période de crise, l’initiative a souligné l’importance des arts dans le soutien moral et psychologique des populations, ainsi que dans la préservation du patrimoine culturel.
Recommandations: Accessibilité accrue au théâtre : L'initiative a réussi à rapprocher le théâtre du grand public grâce à la diffusion télévisuelle et en ligne, augmentant ainsi la visibilité et l'accessibilité de cet art. Valorisation des productions locales : La mise en lumière des productions théâtrales marocaines a démontré la richesse et la diversité du théâtre national, renforçant l'identité culturelle et artistique du pays. Rôle crucial de la culture en temps de crise : L'initiative a mis en évidence l'importance de la culture comme facteur de résilience et de soutien moral pour la population en période de crise.

Title EN: PROMOTING INTELLECTUAL PRODUCTION AND READING THROUGH PUBLISHING ACTIVITIES, PRODUCTION AND DISTRIBUTION IN BOLIVIA
Goal: Achieve A Balanced Flow Of Cultural Goods And Services And Increase The Mobility Of Artists And Cultural Professionals
SDG: SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 10 - Reduce inequality within and among countries,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Flow of cultural goods and services
Agency Implementation: EDITORIAL DEL ESTADO PLURINACIONAL DE BOLIVIA (PUBLISHING COMPANY OF THE PLURINATIONAL STATE OF BOLIVIA )
Main Feature: The PUBLISHING COMPANY OF THE PLURINATIONAL STATE OF BOLIVIA  focuses on the democratization of the people's access to knowledge through three main axes:  •	Promotion of literary production by national and international authors •	Production and publication of works at low cost •	Promotion of reading through the dissemination of the Popular Library through participation in both national and international fairs, and through the mobile library Pankanak qïpiri , which takes books to places where book fairs do not reach or where there are limitations regarding access to libraries in rural educational units and peri-urban areas.
Results: From 2021 to August 2024, the following was achieved: 1.	Establish the "Biblioteca Popular" (Popular Library) to promote reading by means of the dissemination and distribution, at affordable prices for the people, of more than 310 titles. More than 70 titles were published under this publishing imprint, as a result of the promotion of literary production by national and international authors.  Every year, the Popular Library collection is made known and distributed in more than 16 book fairs, both national and international (Colombia, Cuba, Mexico, Venezuela and Peru), and in peri-urban and rural areas through the mobile library "Pankanak qïpiri" , which takes books to places where book fairs cannot reach. 2.	Permanent national call "Cuentos Mágicos" (Magical Tales) to strengthen the capacity, creativity, imagination, girls and boys at the primary education level, as well as to encourage their level of expression through letters. This measure was implemented in 2023 as a result of the collaboration between the Publishing Company of the Plurinational State of Bolivia and the primary level educational units, within the framework of the Interinstitutional Cooperation Agreement signed with the Ministry of Education, to motivate students to write. The 20 titles of Magic Tales were edited and printed by the EEPB, disseminated and distributed through the Popular Library in the editorial line "Construyendo Utopías", the sale price is Bs. 1 ($us. 0.15 aprox.) so that the same boys and girls have access to these works. For the Bicentennial of the Plurinational State of Bolivia, it is intended to edit, produce and publish 200 Titles. 3.	Permanent national call "Rescatando la memoria de nuestras abuelas y abuelos" (Rescuing the memory of our grandmothers and grandfathers) to strengthen the investigative capacity of young people who, through the interview tool, seek information to preserve the stories of oral tradition, which allows valuing the wisdom and experience of the elderly. With this, we strengthen intergenerational relationships. This measure was implemented in 2024 as a result of the collaboration between the Publishing Company of the Plurinational State of Bolivia and secondary school units, within the framework of the Interinstitutional Cooperation Agreement signed with the Ministry of Education, to motivate students to write.  The 6 titles were published by the EEPB, disseminated and distributed through the Popular Library in the editorial line "Lecturas para Caminar", at a price of Bs. 5 ($us. 0.72 aprox). 4.	Since 2023, the Publishing Company has initiated annual calls for literary writing to preserve the memory of important events in the history of Bolivia, as well as to offer a voice to people from specific sectors. To this end, the Publishing Company signed an agreement with the ALBOR Art and Culture Center, which is dedicated to the psychosocial development of children and young people through art, to carry out “Trinchera” literary writing contests to preserve historical and collective memory, generate spaces for reflection and strengthen the critical thinking of young people.  Also, it signed an agreement with the General Directorate of the Penitentiary Regime and the General Directorate of Post-Literacy to promote the writing of people deprived of liberty through the literary contests “Cuentos con Ajayu ” to give voice to people deprived of liberty. The State Publishing Company edits and prints the winning titles, also disseminated and distributed through the Popular Library. 5.	Since Bolivia is a Plurinational State that recognizes 36 indigenous, native and peasant nations in its Political Constitution, the State Publishing Company, as part of the central government, takes on the challenge of strengthening these peoples through the production of bibliography in native languages. In this sense, the translation, publication and distribution of The Little Prince was achieved in 3 native languages: Warawar Wawa (in Aymara), Mburuvicharai (in Guaraní) and Apu Wawa (in Quechua). Each book includes a QR code for each chapter that allows access via technology to the audio of the story in the native language, thus making it easier to know the pronunciation of the words translated into that language.
Financial Ressources: $us. 133,500.00 (Annually)

Title EN: Project "Supporting cooperatives with women participating in management, creating jobs for female workers until 2030" (according to Decision No. 01/QD-TTg dated January 3, 2023 of the Prime Minister)
Goal: Promote Human Rights And Fundamental Freedoms

Area of Monitoring: Gender equality
Cultural Domain: Design,Performing Arts,Media Arts,Cinema and Audiovisual Arts,Music,Publishing,Visual Arts
Agency Implementation: Ministry of Culture, Sports and Tourism; Ministry of Finance; National Committee of Viet Nam Union of Literature and Arts Associations; Viet Nam Journalists' Association; provincial and municipal People's Committees.
Main Feature: The program’s objectives include:  a) To invest and support authors, groups of authors, and creative activities in the fields of literature, arts (fine arts, music, theater, cinema, architecture, photography, dance, folk art, art of ethnic minorities) and journalistic activities at the Central level and local Literature and Arts Associations to create more works and projects of high ideological and artistic value, rich and diverse in form and expression, creating aesthetic orientation value and shaping personality, ethics, and lifestyle, contributing to the comprehensive development of Vietnamese people; focusing mainly on topics of current societal interest.  b) To support the creation of high-quality journalistic works at the local level, with a priority focus on major topics.  c) To provide support in-depth creativity for authors and groups of authors who have made significant contributions to literature, arts, and journalism, who possess extensive life experience but have not yet received investment to create more high-quality works and projects; to support training, professional development, and nurturing of young talents to build and develop a team of artists, journalists, and reporters in a comprehensive manner, both in terms of quantity and quality; to uphold civic responsibility and social activism; to accompany the nation strongly; to align with the interests of the interests of the nation; to constantly continually foster innovative thinking and enhance professional skills.  The program’s beneficiaries include:  a) Authors, groups of authors, the creation of literary, artistic, and journalistic works at the central level supported through the Central specialized Literature and Arts Associations, the National Committee of Viet Nam Union of Literature and Arts Associations, and the Viet Nam Journalists' Association.  b) Authors, groups of authors, the creation of literary and artistic works for localities supported through local Literature and Arts Associations and the National Committee of Viet Nam Union of Literature and Arts Associations.  c) Authors, groups of authors, and the creation of high-quality journalistic works at the local level, supported by local Journalists' Associations and the Viet Nam Journalists' Association.
Financial Ressources: The total estimated budget for implementing the program to support the creation of works and projects in literature, art, and journalism at the central level and local literary and art associations, as well as to support high-quality journalistic works in local journalist associations for the 2021 - 2025 period, is 14 million USD
Recommandations: On March 18, 2024, in Ho Chi Minh City, the Viet Nam Journalists’ Association held a 3-year Review Conference on the implementation of Prime Minister's Decision No. 558/QD-TTg for the period of 2021–2023. The report at the conference indicated that the provincial and municipal journalist associations, the affiliated journalist groups, and the central and local journalist associations have generally implemented Decision No. 558/QĐ-TTg effectively.  Specifically, from 2021 to 2023, the state budget allocated 27.7 billion VND to support the creation of high-quality journalistic works by local journalist associations nationwide, with over 25.6 billion VND implemented and settled. This funding has directly supported over 4,000 authors, resulting in more than 4,260 high-quality journalistic works in various forms. Additionally, more than 11.4 billion VND was allocated to support the creation of high-quality journalistic works at the central level, with over 10.1 billion VND implemented and settled. This funding has supported nearly 4,000 authors, resulting in 3,875 high-quality journalistic works across various forms and organizing professional activities to enhance the quality of journalistic works.

Title EN: Project Grant for Internationalisation
Goal: Achieve A Balanced Flow Of Cultural Goods And Services And Increase The Mobility Of Artists And Cultural Professionals
SDG: SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 10 - Reduce inequality within and among countries,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Mobility of artists and cultural professionals
Agency Implementation: Swedish Arts Council
Main Feature: The project grant designated for internationalisation aims to strengthen the intermediary sector by supporting promotional efforts within visual arts, design, crafts, literature, drama, performing arts, and music. The grant is available to intermediaries operating in Sweden who represent and present professional practitioners and their works.  In this context, intermediaries refer to professionals active in Sweden who represent and showcase professional practitioners and their works. The grant aims to facilitate activities that promote networking, collaboration, and connections with international partners. The project’s goal should be future exchanges and/or collaborations, as well as creating employment opportunities for artistic practitioners.   The grant can be applied for activities that promote the internationalisation of cultural life and lead to networking and collaboration with international partners. In this context, promoting the internationalisation of cultural life means participating in strategically selected events such as fairs, biennials, or other meeting places, where artistic practitioners active in Sweden can represent and showcase their work within visual arts, design, crafts, literature, drama, performing arts, and music. It can also include facilitating for international actors to participate in selected events in Sweden. The annual budget is approx. 2 million SEK (188 500 USD). The regular funding schemes of both the Swedish Arts Council and Swedish Arts Grants Committee can also be used for international exchange, both for inward and outward travel and exchanges, but the Swedish Arts Council also saw the need for earmarked funding for these particular aspects of international exchange and cooperation.  This funding scheme was created after a previous temporary project had concluded, which was seen to be successful (and was mentioned in Sweden’s QPR from 2020). During the years 2016-2018 the Swedish Arts Council and the Swedish Agency for Economic and Regional Growth in collaboration ran a project funding grants for cultural exports. The purpose of the grant was to promote the internationalisation of intermediary actors (including agents and producers, along with galleries and publishers) that at the time fell outside the scope of the Swedish Arts Council’s regular grants scheme. The Swedish Arts Council administered a total of 1 million SEK (94 250 USD) per year over three years, provided by the Swedish Agency for Economic and Regional Growth. There was a very large number of applications, and external follow-up showed that the project was successful.
Results: The Swedish Arts Council has received many applications from the sector and the interest for this earmarked funding is considered to remain high. The results are still difficult to assess since the projects have not yet been fully accounted for (the funding scheme was set up in 2023). The Swedish Arts Council assesses that there is a continued significant need for funding in order to support initiatives aimed at the internationalisation of the cultural sector and cultural exports that can contribute to increased work opportunities and collaboration areas, and thereby increased revenue possibilities for Swedish cultural actors and artists.
Financial Ressources: 188 500 USD (2 million SEK) per year

Title EN: Promotion of Swedish music, film and literature (ongoing measure)
Goal: Achieve A Balanced Flow Of Cultural Goods And Services And Increase The Mobility Of Artists And Cultural Professionals
SDG: SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 10 - Reduce inequality within and among countries,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Flow of cultural goods and services
Agency Implementation: Swedish Arts Council, Swedish Film Institute, Export Music Sweden
Main Feature: Music: Export Music Sweden (ExMS) is an organisation receiving public funding (public funding from the Swedish Arts Council, Arts Grants Committee, the Foreign Office and financing from copyright organisations) to promote Swedish music abroad.  Export Music Sweden’s focus and long-term goals are increased revenues for Sweden’s entire music export and supporting all of Sweden’s music genres. Export Music Sweden operates with four main focus areas: education, networking and trade shows, data collection and presentation of data, as well as support and grants. ExMS provides greater international exposure for Swedish music at music fairs and festivals around the world. They organise seminars for the Swedish music industry to share knowledge about music export at all levels and regularly meet with professional musicians to offer personalized advice and expert assistance on export. Also, they periodically arrange trade missions to various focus areas, where productive business visits are combined with relevant fairs, festivals, and individual meetings.   Film: Swedish Film Institute assists new Swedish films with presence and visibility at film festivals, film markets and other film-related events abroad. They work closely with producers and sales agents to ensure that Swedish films truly reach international audiences and to increase the export of Swedish cinema. The Swedish Film Institute is part of the two international networks Scandinavian Films and EFP– European Film Promotion. A guide of international film festivals is produced for Swedish film producers and a catalogue is produced presenting Swedish film and film makers. Grants are awarded to launch and distribute films at various festivals, markets, and other cultural and commercial events.  Literature: The Swedish Arts Council is the authority with responsibility for promoting Swedish literature in translation. Through Swedish Literature Exchange (SLE) they coordinate a number of efforts within the field. SLE awards grants every year to translations and literature events, participate in international networks and book fairs, and arrange visitor programmes in Sweden for foreign publishing houses and translators. They perform active work to strengthen the translators, through grants, workshops, and conferences. SLE arranges special conferences for translators, visitor programmes for foreign publishers, and participate in the larger international book fairs. In Frankfurt, they coordinate the Swedish collective stand for Swedish publishers, organisations and agencies. In London they coordinate, in cooperation with Nordic colleagues, a Nordic collective stand for Nordic publishing houses and agencies. In addition, SLE offers information on Swedish literature in our publications on different themes.  There are grants for translators of Swedish literature that promote international exchange and skill improvement activities among translators of Swedish literature and drama. About VMIN - Vietnam Music Industry Network: VMIN is an online community platform aimed at supporting members of the music business in Vietnam to learn, connect, collaborate, and develop together. With a mission to facilitate career opportunities in the music business and promote sustainable development in Vietnam's music industry, VMIN has progressively contributed positive values to the Vietnamese music business community. Since 2021, the Vietnam Music Week (VMW) has successfully completed three editions, attracting significant participation from audiences and industry partners within Vietnam's music sector and internationally. The program targets current and future Vietnamese industry leaders who possess a mindset for continuous learning and professional growth to advance their careers in music business, actively contributing to the development of Vietnam's music industry community. VMW Vietnam Music Week has also effectively connected individuals, companies, and organizations within and beyond Vietnam's music industry. Several prominent companies and organizations have participated as speakers over the past three years include: - Domestic: C Mazor Entertainment & Media, Double U, Hanoi Rock City, JB Art, Lava Digital Group - Digital Media Solution, MCMA, Pencil Group - never run out of ink, ST.319 Entertainment, The First Management, TRUM., Monsoon Music Festival, VCPMC, W Media and Ent, Hot Panda Media, Cổng Trời, LCV, EMVN, Tuniver, Billboard Vietnam, Show Service, WOW Media/The Bros, Believe Vietnam, Universal Music Vietnam, Vietfest, Warner Chappell Music Vietnam, YouTube Vietnam, Yamaha Music Vietnam, etc. - International: Gig Life Pro, Monstercat, Fungjai, MusicDish, catsound., Third Culture Entertainment, Steady State Records, Jade Music Festival, Inter Idoru Artist Management, Australia Arts Council, The Mumbai Assembly, EARS, Godset, Durham College, Small World Music, Global Toronto, etc. - Artists: Thắng Ngọt, Kai Đinh, JB Lê Phương, etc. Furthermore, VMW Vietnam Music Week has received positive feedback regarding its impactful contributions to the community annually, such as: - Addressing human resource challenges within Vietnam's music industry: Many participants have found suitable career opportunities at music companies and organizations, helping them solve personnel issues with knowledgeable and professionally qualified individuals within the industry; - Creating opportunities for new collaborations post-event, such as music production partnerships, co-composition, and co-organization of new live music events, etc.; - Promoting Vietnamese artists and music experts by inviting them to perform at VMW in local and international music programs and participating in local and international music seminar programs.

Title EN: Promoting culture as a driver for economy in regional cities EU4Culture project in Armenia
Goal: Integrate Culture In Sustainable Development Frameworks

Main Feature: EU4Culture assists cities in the Eastern Partnership (EaP) region in developing and implementing their Cultural Development Strategies following the approach of the European Capitals of Culture model. The objective is to increase the role of Culture as an engine for economic development in these cities.  14 regional cities have been selected through a competitive process to receive support in formulating their Cultural Development Strategies. In Armenia, the cities of Charentsavan, Ijevan, and Sevan were selected and awarded a grant of € 30,000 to develop their Cultural Development Strategies. These cities are brought together to exchange knowledge and explore pathways for collaboration. Three Regional Network Conferences and the Strategy Empowerment Conference have provided them with platforms for sharing experiences and finding new connections. Further to a competitive selection process among the Armenian cities, Ijevan was awarded a grant of up to €300,000 to implement its cultural strategy from September 2022 to August 2024. The cities of Charentsavan and Sevan are members of the Regional Cities Network and benefit from capacity-building support. Since late 2022, these cities have been implementing their Cultural Strategies with their budgets. In early 2024, each city was awarded an EU grant of 30,000 euros to implement part of their strategies.  In Armenia, to further support the regional cities and local creative and cultural sector in implementing their Cultural Development Strategies, three cultural and cross-innovation projects were selected and received a total of 55,000 euros.  Moreover, EU4Culture has offered an opportunity to 60 individual Armenian artists and cultural professionals to travel abroad, in the EU and EaP countries. These mobility projects have enabled participants to build new partnerships and collaboration models, as well as broaden their professional networks. With newfound knowledge and experiences acquired during their travels, along with support from new partners in the EU and EaP countries, artists and cultural professionals from Armenia are actively enhancing the cultural and creative landscape of the country. The winning cities and towns are supported through regular Capacity Building activities in the fields of Internationalization, Cultural Enterprise and Management, and Cultural Indicators and Statistics.
Results: Ijevan Cultural Development Strategy Highlights The overall objective of the cultural strategy is to build a strong and collaborative cultural sector in the multi-settlement community of Ijevan. Local civil society, NGOs, and representatives from cultural and creative sectors contributed to the formulation of this objective. Ijevan identified three main directions for its Cultural Strategy: Cultural Sector Management, Activated Cultural and Economic Life and Collaborative and Culture-Led Economic Development.  -	1st Direction: Cultural Sector Management o	Ijevan developed an electronic database of culture and a Geographic Information System-based digital platform highlighting the municipality’s cultural assets and their locations.  o	The city supported cultural professionals and artists with two study visits to cultural festivals in the region, three joint initiatives with peer communities, and four professional exchanges, as a result of which the local creative sector representatives gained knowledge and expanded their network.  -	2nd Strategic Direction: Active Cultural and Economic Life o	Ijevan trained 120 representatives of the local private sector, CSOs, cultural and creative industries, thus improving their skills, knowledge, and networks and making them more competitive on national and international markets.  o	120 individuals took part in the city’s “Idea Harvest” forum, which is based on the principle of “thinking outside box” where they generated 17 concepts on creative cultural development. o	Ijevan provided businesses, CSOs and individuals with six grants as part of the city’s Cultural Development Strategy. The municipality awarded three Heritage Grants to support the preservation and advancement of the local cultural heritage.  -	3rd Strategic Direction: Collaborative and Culture-Led Economic Development o	The city organised a Community Festival, where representatives of 19 settlements participated. The event, which aimed at showcasing the local cultural heritage and benefitted 160 businesses, was attended by more than 3,000 people. The purpose of the Community Festival is to catalyse tourism, economic activity, and collaborative, culture-led development.  The Cultural Development Strategies in the Cities of Charentsavan and Sevan -	Charentsavan will enhance the capacities of municipality’s culture department, specialists from the local educational institutions, and artists with a training module. The city will also work with the Charentsavan Music School named after Aram Khachatryan to pioneer a six-week music program for 450 preschool children. As a culmination of the program, they will take part in the local open-air concert on 1 June – International Children’s Day. The purpose of Charentsavan’s series of activities is to enhance the cultural and creative industry sector in the Charentsavan community.  -	Sevan will celebrate its rich cultural heritage by mapping its cultural assets, developing a cultural database with the information collected, and launching a public campaign promoting the platform.  Support to Cultural and Cross-Innovation Projects 	“Art Summer Camp” (from April until June 2024): the main objective of the project is to organise an art camp in June 2024 for approximately 40 children studying in music and art schools in Charentsavan and Ijevan communities. o	Implemented by: Children’s Music School Named after Aram Khachatryan 	“Sevan Art Hub” (from December 2023 until May 2024): The project aims to establish an educational space dedicated to artistic experience, art history, and art education. o	Implemented by: Armenian Centre for Contemporary Experimental Art  	“EUDigitLab “(from December 2023 until July 2024): the project develops a tech-learning lab where young people can have the opportunity to learn essential skills in all aspects of product development including graphic design, modelling, texturing, editing, and animation. o	Implemented by: Tavush Innovation Centre; Union of Advanced Technology Enterprises; CO-WO; Enterprise Incubator Foundation; Saqanima  Mobility Grants Scheme Currently, 45 Mobilities (34 women and 11 men) have been completed. Italy (29%), Germany (18%), France (12%) and Spain (9%) are the top four destinations of the mobility grantees from Armenia. The most represented sectors among the participants are cultural education (18%); music and performance (31%); fine arts, crafts (26%), and film and video (15%).
Financial Ressources: The Program budget: 7,850,000€
Recommandations: Animation of cultural life of the cities is a good mechanism against brain drain. With examples of artists returning from the capital to the regional city. The animation of cultural life also aims to promote cultural assets – it contributes to an increase in tourism and creates jobs. The EU4Culture project has also been assessed as a mechanism that strengthens ties between public and private sectors, enhances participatory dialogue, strengthens the Regional Network and cooperation and EaP cities, while also supporting the inventorisation of local tangible and intangible cultural assets, which will be used for GIS mapping.  The measure will be fully evaluated retroactively by 2024, by the European Commission.

Agency Implementation: Ministry of Culture
Main Feature: In 2023, the Government of the Republic of Slovenia included the "Green Transition in Culture" project in the Decree on the Use of Funds from the Climate Change Fund for 2023–2026. The Climate Change Fund is a special budget fund managed by the Ministry of Environment, Climate and Energy and financed by the sale of emission allowances. It is used to finance measures to mitigate and adapt to climate change. The Ministry of Culture is implementing the "Green Transition in Culture" project in the form of a public call announced in 2024. It will support the adoption of green practices and promote the development of innovative green approaches in the cultural sector. This will enable changes in the management of organizations, venues and cultural events and raise public awareness of the importance of the green transition. The aim of the call for proposals is to reduce the carbon footprint directly linked to the activities of organizations in the cultural sector or cultural events and activities, to raise awareness of environmental issues and to promote sustainable values through cultural expressions. The call for proposals will help improve the Republic of Slovenia's resilience to climate change, while enabling it to meet its climate neutrality commitments more successfully and quickly. The call follows the European and Slovenian guidelines in this area. Strand A is intended for the co-financing of pilot projects for the green transition in culture. This includes the implementation of pilot activities to reduce the carbon footprint of cultural institutions, the development of management models for environmentally neutral cultural institutions, advisory and information activities on the green transition for cultural institutions, raising public awareness and training stakeholders to implement green practices in culture, the use of new technologies for the green transition in culture and the development of solutions for sustainable mobility when attending cultural events. Strand B will finance  projects that improve the climate neutrality and environmental sustainability of existing multi-day cultural events or program cycles. The beneficiaries of the call for proposals are public institutions and non-governmental organizations in the field of culture.
Results: The first results of the measure will be available in 2025.

In 2023, guides, tour operators, employees of accommodation facilities, and other sector representatives completed a diverse range of training courses. These courses, designed to enhance professional skills and knowledge, covered a wide array of topics, ensuring a comprehensive and well-rounded development for our industry representatives. ·         Family hotel management ·         Social media management ·         Rural tourism and features of tourist services in rural areas ·         Digital Marketing ·         Hygiene and food safety ·         Inclusive tourism products and services for people with disabilities ·         First aid ·         International sommelier courses ·         Eco-gastronomic tourism training course ·         Marking and maintenance of footpaths GNTA establishes necessary contacts and cooperates with foreign tourism industries to promote Georgia's tourism potential in international markets. It plans invitations and hosts foreign journalists, bloggers, tour operators, and other representatives from related fields in Georgia. During their visits, the bloggers, tour operators, and other representatives can visit Georgia's cultural heritage sites.
Results: In 2023, GNTA supported up to 50 (some of them participated in more than one tourism exhibition) companies from the private tourism sector in 13 international tourism exhibitions. From 2020 to 2021, some of the exhibitions were cancelled due to the pandemic to prevent the risks of spreading the new coronavirus, COVID-19.   In 2020-2024, GNTA retrained up to 9,000 individuals in or seeking employment within the tourism industry.  In 2020-2024, 229 press and familiarization trips were planned and executed, with the participation of up to 1657 individuals. These trips offered participants the opportunity to visit and acquaint themselves with a wide range of historical monuments and cultural heritage sites across different regions of Georgia, as well as intangible cultural aspects, like traditions, Georgian cuisine, wine, and polyphonic singing.
Financial Ressources: Approximately 143 000 USD per year (approximately 400,000 Gel)
Recommandations: The goals and objectives of the GNTA are the formation and implementation of the Georgian tourism development state policy, promotion of sustainable tourism development, promotion of high export income growth and job creation in the country based on the tourism development, attraction of the foreign tourists to Georgia and development of the domestic tourism as well, promotion of human resources development in the field of tourism destinations, infrastructure and tourism. All marketing activities implemented by GNTA promote sustainable tourism development.  In 2023, Georgia reported a total income of USD 4,1 billion, reflecting a remarkable 26.2% growth compared to 2019. We are herewith delighted to witness the dynamics of the substantial recovery in the number of international visitors to the country. Namely, in 2023, the recovery rate of international traveler trips reached 75.6% (7,072,220 international traveler trips total), and the recovery of tourist trips equaled 91.9% (4,669,467 tourist trips total). Furthermore, in the I Quarter of 2024, the recovery rate of international traveler trips reached 80.4% (1,300,551 international traveler trips in total), and the growth of tourist trips was 6.4% (938,644 tourist trips totaled).  At the same time, revenue from tourism amounted to $807,674,030, a 39.6% increase compared to the 2019 data. More than that, during the first quarter of 2024, we witnessed a remarkable rate of growth of international visitors from the EU member states and GB compared with the 2019 data, representing 44.4% growth.

Title EN: Promotion and dissemination of theatre arts in the country and across the globe
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture
SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Cultural and creative sectors
Agency Implementation: NATIONAL SCHOOL OF DRAMA
Main Feature: The National School of Drama is one of the foremost theatre training institutions in the world and the only one of its kind in India. It was set up by the Sangeet Natak Akademi as one of its constituent units in 1959. In 1975, it became an independent entity and was registered as an autonomous organization under the Societies Registration Act XXI of 1860, fully financed by the Ministry of Culture, Government of India. Training in the School is highly intensive and is based on a thorough, comprehensive, carefully planned syllabus which covers every aspect of theatre and in which theory is related to practice. As a part of their training, students are required to produce plays which are then performed before the public. The syllabus takes into account the methods of great theatre personalities who have shaped contemporary theatre in all its variety. The systematic study and practical performing experience of Sanskrit drama, modern Indian drama, traditional Indian theatre forms, Asian drama and western dramatic protocols give the students a solid grounding and a wide perspective in the art of theatre. Besides its 3-year training programme, the School has also explored new vistas in the areas of children’s theatre and decentralization of theatre training through workshops under the Extension Programme. The School has two performing wings – the Repertory Company and Theatre-in-Education Company.  The Repertory Company was started in 1964 with four artistes – Shri Ramamurthy, Ms. Meena Williams, Ms. Sudha Shivpuri and Shri Om Shivpuri – with the objective of providing a platform where graduates of the School could perform plays professionally. Over the years it has presented works of various playwrights and directors who have been associated with it and has evolved into one of NSD’s major institutions, working on contemporary and modern plays as well as introducing experimental work on a regular basis. In addition to doing productions, it organizes its own Festival, where past and new productions are introduced and staged each summer. NSD’s Repertory Company also tours and performs extensively in India and abroad. The second performing wing the ‘Theatre-In-Education Company’ (Sanskar Rang Toli) was established in October 16, 1989, and is one of the most important theatre education resource centres in the country. It consists of a group of actor-teachers working with and performing for children. The major focus of the TIE Company is to perform creative, curriculum-based and participatory plays in schools, specially designed and prepared for children of different age groups. The major thrust of the plays is to create an atmosphere that encourages children to raise questions, take decisions and make choices with an awareness of themselves within the larger social context. The TIE Company has done more than 800 performances of 26 plays in Delhi and other parts of the country. More than 5.5 lakhs children, apart from college students, teachers, parents and theatre lovers, have witnessed these plays. In addition to these two wings, the School also has an active Extension Programme, a publication section and a literary forum named ‘Shruti’. The Extension Programme, under which NSD faculty and alumni conduct workshops in various parts of the country, was launched in 1978 and since then has conducted workshops and programmes for adults and children across the country and in Nepal, Sikkim, Ladakh and Bhutan as well. The ‘Traditional Theatre Project’ initiated in 1980, has facilitated creative interaction between traditional and contemporary theatre artists on a regular basis. Along with an introduction to theatre, these workshops also seek to develop personality and expand the emotional horizons of the participants. The Publication Unit of the National School of Drama is responsible for publishing text books on theatre, arranging for the translation of important books on theatre from English into Hindi and bringing out other important books on theatre. The unit’s first major publication titled Rang Yatra which chronicled 25 years history of the NSD Repertory Company from 1964 onwards, came out in 1990. Besides its regular publications, until 2010 the unit has brought out 82 publications on drama and related subjects. Bharat Rang Mahotsav: BRM is the largest international theatre festival in the world, attracting plays from across India and the world for the past 25 years. The festival involves every possible form of theatre from Folk and classical to contemporary Theatre. The festival has showcased near about 2000 Plays witnessed by Lakhs of Audience.   05 Regional Training Centre- ·   	Gangtok (Estd. 2012) ·   	Agartala (Estd. 2012) ·   	Bengaluru (Estd. 2015) ·   	Varanasi (Estd. 2018) ·   	Srinagar (Estd. 2021) As part of its mandate to strengthen education and training in theatre NSD regularly organizes and takes part in exchange programs for its students and faculty, both nationally and internationally. NSD has organized 52 Summer Theatre Workshops for Children including down-trodden sections of the Society in the month of June-July, 2024. NSD is also planning to host 17th APB Theatre Schools Festival at NSD in August, 2024.
Results: National School of Drama has imparted rigorous training to about 1200 young graduates. These NSD Alumni have contributed immensely in the development and promotion of the cultural landscape in India and abroad. They have influenced millions through their work. Each year NSD imparts short-term training to about 2000-3000 enthusiastic theatre practitioners and school children. NSD also organizes various festivals with more than 3000 artists participating every year and provides qualitative entertainment to the thousands of people. NSD has also played a pioneering role in collaborating with various institutions in the world through exchange of experts, ideas knowledge and tradition.  NSD students participated in GITIS Fest which was held in Moscow, Russia in the month of November, 2023 and also performed a play in traditional style in the GITIS Fest. In the month of April, 2024, NSD Students also participated in the GITIS Fest and performed Therukoothu was also held in Moscow, Russia. NSD also participated in the 7th Asian Theatre School Festival which was held in Beijing, China. A solo performance was performed by NSD in Mauritius on the occasion of World Hindi Day in the month of January, 2024.

An important part of the Cultural Bazaar is also the national interdepartmental professional training of professionals from the fields of education, culture, health, social affairs, the environment and the general professional public. The Cultural Bazaar is also responsible for the development of a national network for cultural and artistic education made up of coordinators from educational institutions, cultural institutions and local communities. The objectives pursued by the Cultural Bazaar are: To connect educational institutions, cultural institutions, artists and other stakeholders in the implementation and ensure accessibility to quality cultural and artistic education, both in formal and non-formal education, and to support accessibility to quality projects prepared by cultural institutions and artists from all fields of culture and arts for different target groups. Each year, cross-departmental training courses cover topics that correspond to the various objectives of the 2005 Convention. In 2020, the main theme was "Equality in Diversity"," in 2021 "Art-Science-Technology-Education: Thinking about the future today'," in 2022 'Culture and the arts - the well-being of society and the individual' and in 2023 'Creativity for sustainable development'. Each year, with 40 programme items, the Culture Bazaar helps to raise awareness of culture and art among the general public, raise awareness of their important role in various social, sustainability and health issues and raise awareness of how culture and art contribute to our quality of life.
Results: The results of the project are:  - better information about quality professional cultural offers for children and youth,  - additional skills for professionals,  - increased cooperation and partnership between schools and kindergartens and cultural institutions/artists,  - more, more diverse and higher quality offers by cultural institutions,  - improved accessibility to cultural and arts education programs.

Title EN: Promotion of Media Education and good medialiteracy
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture
SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Cultural and creative sectors
Agency Implementation: Ministry of Education and Culture & National Audiovisual Institute KAVI
Main Feature: KAVI coordinates the implementation of Finnish national media education and media literacy policy. In Finland, KAVI operates mainly on the national level, but also reinforces regional media education. This is done, for example, by supporting regional and local organizations in strategic media education planning.   KAVI develops and promotes media education practices, operational models, and pedagogies. We support the media education awareness and competencies of educators, for example, by maintaining an online Media Literacy School. The site provides information on media education, media literacy and media culture as well as a wealth of teaching and learning resources.  KAVI conducts development projects. For more than 10 years, KAVI has coordinated the Finnish Safer Internet Centre (FISIC) projects. FISIC is co-funded by the European Commission and implemented in cooperation with two non-governmental organisations, the Mannerheim League for Child Welfare and Save the Children Finland. FISIC is a wide-ranging action aiming to promote media literacy, media education and safer media environment for children. FISIC implements the European BIK+ strategy.   Between 2020 and 2023 KAVI has been coordinating the national New Literacies development program in cooperation with the Ministry of Education and Culture and the Finnish National Agency for Education. New Literacies aimed to strengthen the media literacy, ICT competence and programming skills of children and young people in early childhood, pre-primary and basic education. With more than 10 million euros funding for its implementation in municipalities, the program has been the biggest single investment in media education in Finland.
Results: Finland was one of the first countries in the world to have a media education strategy. The latest policy guidelines were published in 2019.  Through this long term systematic, comprehensive work Finland is one of the leading countries in media literacy.

Title EN: Promotion of Slovenian culture by Slovenian embassies and Slovenian cultural centers abroad
Goal: Achieve A Balanced Flow Of Cultural Goods And Services And Increase The Mobility Of Artists And Cultural Professionals

Agency Implementation: Ministry of Culture Ministry of Foreign and European Affairs
Main Feature: In 2011, the first Slovenian Cultural Information Centre (SKICA) was founded to promote Slovenian culture and art and to network Slovenians in Vienna and, more broadly, in Austria. 5 years later, the second Slovenian cultural centre was founded in Berlin, Germany. Both centres serve as advisory and organisational institutions for the presentation of Slovenian art in partnership with important institutions in Vienna and Berlin and other relevant actors of the cultural scene in Austria and Germany. Both centres are funded and managed by the Ministry of Culture as well as the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, which is a great practise of inter-ministerial cooperation. The Cultural Fund serves to co-finance cultural projects carried out within the framework of the diplomatic-consular representations of the Republic of Slovenia abroad, with the Ministry of Culture and the Ministry of Foreign Affairs each providing half of the funds. These are projects initiated by a diplomatic-consular mission of the Republic of Slovenia abroad on the basis of an invitation or initiative of the organiser abroad. The objectives of co-financing projects are the presentation of outstanding Slovenian cultural achievements on the international stage, timely and flexible response to quality initiatives from abroad, promotion of intercultural dialogue and continuous inter-ministerial cooperation in supporting Slovenian cultural excellence in international reference locations. The eligibility of the proposed cultural projects is determined on the basis of the rules adopted by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and the Ministry of Culture.
Results: The Slovenian Cultural Centres bring together Slovenian and Austrian/German cultural institutions and artists and work closely with them. They promote sustainable alliances between institutions and their co-productions, support creative thinking and present and promote Slovenian art of the highest quality in Austria/Germany. They promote international cooperation and the mobility of Slovenian artists and support intercultural dialogue, innovation and diversity.
Recommandations: Both centres and their work were assessed as extremely positive by the expert commission for international cooperation and promotion of the Ministry of Culture, with only a few comments on the lack of personnel, which could be improved. There is no systematic evaluation of the Cultural Fund yet, but one is being planned. In principle, the response is always very positive.

Title EN: Quebec’s Support for the International Solidarity Center of Saguenay-Lac-Saint-Jean
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture
SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Partnering with civil society
Cultural Domain: Performing Arts,Cinema and Audiovisual Arts,Visual Arts
Agency Implementation: Ministry of International Relations and La Francophonie
Main Feature: New Quebec without borders is an international solidarity program aimed at Quebec international cooperation organizations. It contributes to the international effort to combat poverty and social exclusion, from a perspective of sustainable development, human rights, including equality between women and men, and women's empowerment.  The specific objectives of the program are: -	Facilitate the implementation of initiatives to improve the living conditions of populations located primarily in French-speaking Africa, Latin America and the Antilles; -	Contribute to the development of global citizenship education (GCE) actions across the regions of Quebec; -	Promote and consolidate the expertise of international cooperation organizations (OIC) and that of their local partners; -	Promote the creation and maintenance of partnerships by encouraging the contribution of women and the organizations that represent them; -	Promote the introduction to international solidarity, particularly among young people, as part of the experiences of Quebec without Borders Volunteers; -	Contribute to the next generation of international solidarity, ensuring that this succession reflects diversity and inclusion.  As part of Part 1 of the NQSF program, support for the global mission, the government of Quebec financially supports the International Solidarity Center of Saguenay-Lac-Saint-Jean (CSI – SLSJ). This funding allows the CSI-SLSJ to carry out a project in Ecuador in the cultural sector.  The partnership between CSI-SLSJ and Fundación Arte Nativo supports the production of theater works, dance, and short films in the community of La Moya.
Results: For the year 2022-2023, the partnership between the Fundación Arte Nativo and the CSI-SLSJ has notably enabled the creation of artistic products for community tourism, the staging of a play “Las Hieleras del Chimborazo ” by children and teenagers from La Moya and the production of the short fiction video “Yanda Yana / The guardian of the forest ".  These cultural productions highlight the important contribution of women in the history of their community and express their desire to protect the environment.  Overall, this project strengthened the self-determination of women and girls in the Indigenous community of the Chimborazo region. Mainly, these efforts have led to an improvement in relations between men and women so that they are more respectful and inclusive. The number of targeted beneficiaries was 927 people (women, men, and children), or 348 families.  Kichwa women from the province of Cotacachi -Imbabura (Cotachis) and the province of La Moya-Chimborazo (Puruhaes) was facilitated by the partner Arte Nativo. This meeting made possible dialogue and the exchange of ancestral Andean knowledge, illustrating the gastronomic, musical, clothing, linguistic, artisanal diversity, and indigenous ancestral medicine of the communities.  This meeting was held on the territory of the Municipality of La Moya. Women were also made aware of midwifery practices Contacachi, women of wisdom who maintain ancestral traditional medicine. The women were further able to discuss the funeral rites of Indigenous Peoples through a performance. This meeting was a period of rich intercultural exchange for Indigenous women.
Financial Ressources: The financial resources allocated for carrying out the activities presented above are approximately CAD 10,000 in 2022-2023, for an approximate USD 7,341.  This is an estimate (in canadian dollars) based on the CSI-SLSJ financial report for 2022-2023.
Recommandations: The results are generally positive, minor modifications are proposed to facilitate the management of the program and maximize its impact.

Title EN: Promouvoir les Arts Plastiques et Visuels en Côte d’Ivoire
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture
SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Cultural and creative sectors
Agency Implementation: MINISTERE EN CHARGE DE LA CULTURE / Direction de la Promotion des Arts Plastiques et Visuels
Main Feature: La Direction de la Promotion des Arts Plastiques et Visuels  a pour mission de : promouvoir et vulgariser les œuvres plastiques, d’art photographique, de la sculpture et des autres arts assimilés ; susciter et  coordonner l’organisation des expositions ; délivrer des agréments et autorisations aux personnes physiques ou morales intervenant dans le domaine des Arts Plastiques et Visuels ; veiller à la mise en œuvre de la politique nationale en matière de promotion et de développement des Arts Plastiques et Visuels ; professionnaliser les métiers des Arts Plastiques et Visuels par la formation et l’organisation des acteurs du secteur. A cet effet, pendant la CAN 2023 organisée par Côte d’Ivoire, plusieurs activités ont été menées afin de promouvoir nos Arts. Il s’agit d’Abidjan Art Week. A travers cette activité en partenariat avec douze (12) galeries et le ministère du tourisme ; plus de 70 personnes ont pu découvrir le travail de jeunes artistes plasticiens. Cette activité a vu la participation du Ministère de la Culture et de la Francophonie avec la présence de Madame la Ministre à chaque étape. La Politique favorise à la fois les jeunes et les seniors car l'objectif  est de favoriser des créations artistiques dans tous les domaines des Arts Plastiques et Visuels. Plusieurs partenaires  sont d’un apport indéniable  au secteur des Arts plastiques. Ainsi, la Fondation DONWAHI œuvre à la promotion des artistes contemporains africains à travers l’organisation de plusieurs expositions à la fois en Côte d’Ivoire ainsi qu’à l’étranger.   L’Institut Français d’Abidjan également contribue à l’accompagnement des Artistes à travers à la mise à disposition de son espace pour l’organisation de plusieurs expositions.  L’école en charge des  Beaux-Arts d’Abidjan l’ESAPAD de l’INSAAC participe à l’organisation de conférence, de panel avec les étudiants, les artistes ainsi que les enseignants au tour de l’histoire de l’Art Africain ; le marché de l’Art contemporain et les jurys d’exposition de fin d’année.  Les associations du secteur, les artistes et les faitières  contribuent à à la promotion de ce secteur également par des conseils, et l’accompagnement des acteurs du secteur afin de faciliter leur professionnalisation.
Results: Au niveau de la  formation, grâce à cette  politique les jeunes artistes plasticiens sont formés et accompagnés régulièrement à travers des conférences, des panels et des débats sur le marché de l’art contemporain mais aussi sur l’histoire de l’art africain. L’accompagnement technique et financier des jeunes artistes à travers l’organisation de plusieurs concours de peinture organisés par les entreprises en Côte d’ivoire afin de booster la dynamique de création des jeunes artistes.
Financial Ressources: Les ressources financières allouées pour l’accompagnement des artistes du secteur des Arts Plastiques et Visuels peuvent être évalué à 150.000 Dollars en 2023.
Recommandations: Les principales conclusions sont les suivantes : Un manque de cohérence dans la déclinaison du programme national de développement de la culture et la feuille de route du ministère en charge de la culture pour ce qui est du secteur des arts plastique et visuels. Title EN: Protection et préservation de la diversité culturelle dans le cadre des négociations
Goal: Achieve A Balanced Flow Of Cultural Goods And Services And Increase The Mobility Of Artists And Cultural Professionals
SDG: SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 10 - Reduce inequality within and among countries,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Treaties and agreements
Agency Implementation: Ministère de la Culture
Main Feature: En conformité avec la position constante défendue depuis l’accord général sur le commerce des services (AGCS) de 1994, la Commission européenne a reçu de la part des Etats membres de l’Union européenne le mandat d’exclure les services audiovisuels de la négociation des accords de libre-échange et de commerce négociés durant ces 4 dernières années et en cours de négociation ou de modernisation (Royaume-Uni, Inde, Thaïlande, Indonésie, Philippines, Australie, Nouvelle Zélande, Mercosur, Mexique, Chili, Singapour, Corée, Japon). Cette exclusion fait également partie du mandat donné à la Commission dans le cadre des négociations plurilatérales en cours à l’OMC sur le commerce numérique. A cet égard, la notion de produit numérique utilisée par certains pays ne correspond à aucune nomenclature habituellement utilisée, cette notion floue ne permet pas de garantir l’exclusion des services audiovisuels. La France a soutenu cette approche européenne de la coopération culturelle avec les pays tiers, fondée sur l’autonomie des négociations commerciales et culturelles en raison de la nature spécifique des biens et services culturels telle que consacrée par la Convention de l’UNESCO, dans un objectif de promotion de la diversité culturelle. Le ministère de la Culture français s'est également engagé dans le processus de rédaction et de publication d'une charte pour la culture équitable, aux côtés de la Commission allemande pour l'Unesco et d'autres partenaires européens et internationaux.
Results: L’UE et ses Etats membres conservent leur capacité de réguler et soutenir le secteur audiovisuel afin de protéger la diversité culturelle et adapter leurs politiques aux évolutions technologiques. En ce sens la révision de la directive services de médias audiovisuels (SMA) a permis d’étendre son champ d’application aux fournisseurs de plateformes de partage de vidéos, acteurs incontournables de la diffusion de contenus audiovisuels, en permettant notamment aux Etats membres de leur imposer une obligation de promotion des œuvres européennes sur leurs catalogues, et à titre optionnel de les soumettre à des obligations de contributions financières à la production européenne et locale. La plupart des Etats membres de l’UE dont la France se sont saisis de cette possibilité en mettant en œuvre de telles obligations.
Recommandations: La France, aux côtés de l’Union européenne, met à profit la dynamique créée par l’entrée en vigueur de la Convention de l’UNESCO sur la protection et la promotion de la diversité des expressions culturelles lors de négociations de cadres spécifiques de coopération culturelle. Plus largement, cette exclusion du champ de la libéralisation des échanges permet de garantir la préservation de la capacité de l’Union et de ses Etats membres de développer et de mettre en œuvre des politiques de soutien et de régulation du secteur audiovisuel qui visent à protéger la diversité des expressions culturelles. Cette exclusion s’applique conformément au principe de neutralité technologique ce qui signifie qu’elle s’applique à l’ensemble des services audiovisuels étant entendu que ces derniers ne changent pas de nature en fonction de leur mode de diffusion.

Agency Implementation: Immigration agency of Mongolia
Main Feature: This law establishes the legal status of foreigners and regulates matters pertaining to their entry, exit, transit, and residence in Mongolia. It governs the issuance of Mongolian visas and visa permits to foreigners and stateless persons, procedures for extending visas for their stay in the country, as well as the cancellation of visas issued to foreigners and stateless persons.
Results: As of 2024, Mongolian citizens can  visa-free travel to 29 countries for stays ranging from 14 to 90 days with all types of passports. Diplomatic and official passport holders can travel visa-free to 65 countries for similar durations. For multiple-entry visas valid between 3 to 10 years, discounted arrangements are available for travel to the USA, Canada, Japan, Switzerland, and the UK. Egypt, Indonesia, and Kenya provide visas on arrival to Mongolian citizens at their border crossings. Conversely, Mongolia issues "tourist" entry visas valid for up to 30 days to foreigners arriving at its international borders. Under Resolution No. 01 of 2023 by the Government of Mongolia, citizens from 35 countries can stay visa-free in Mongolia for up to 30 days until December 31, 2025. Additionally, "K4" visas are specifically designated for foreign nationals participating in cultural and sports events, artistic competitions, and film production in Mongolia. These visas can be obtained electronically through the responsible state administrative body handling foreign citizens' affairs, with processing typically completed within 2 days. Since its inception, a total of 1490 "K4" visas have been issued, although specific figures for artists were not provided.
