Agency Implementation: Provincial Departments of Arts and Culture in partnership with Community Arts Centres and Community Arts Organisations.
Main Feature: Community Arts Centres have been in existence since 1948 and became the only available venues where young black students could learn creative skills in disciplines of music, drama, dance, and fine art which are absent from most black schools. The Community Arts Centres played a very important role in shaping the black art or African Art in South Africa in all its various forms. It was in the arts centres where it was commonly called informal arts training institutions, aspiring black artists receive their training from either missionaries, colonialists, or artists. The following are the main objectives of the Provincial Community Arts Centers: •	Promoting access to and participation in arts and culture for all South Africans at the most local level. •	Promoting the development of local cultural identities and associated arts and cultural practices in the face of the culturally ‘flattening’ effects of globalization. •	Promoting the role of Community Arts and Culture Centres in social and economic development, especially regarding education and training, tourism and small business development. •	Promoting greater connection and co-operation between the functions of different spheres of Government as they pertain to culture. •	Promoting greater connection and co-operation between Community Arts and Culture Centres and Programmes and other related forms of local service delivery infrastructure (e.g. multi-purpose community centres, science centres, public museums and galleries, libraries and so on).
Results: The policy supported programmes and kept centres operational and serve communities, create jobs, training, cultural development, arts education and training, audience development. Achievements from 2018 to 2024 supported the implementation of Districts Arts Programmes in all 9 provinces through Provincial CACs Associations, Centres of Excellence and individual Centres.  A total of 150 arts projects and training programmes were funded.   In the 2019/2020 financial year a budget of R14 935 300.00 supported the DSAC strategic programme of Provincial Community Arts Development Programmes in seven (7) provinces in collaboration with the Associations of CACs. Research on “Towards a Re-defined Approach and Mandate for Community Arts Centre Ecosystem Development in South Africa was also conducted”.   In 2020/2021 financial year the Department (DSAC) appointed Sibikwa Arts Centres to develop and implement the Arts, Culture and Heritage Development Programmes in collaboration with community arts centres and community arts organizations in four (4) Provinces, i.e. Free State, Mpumalanga, Northern Cape, and Limpopo. The total budget for the project was R23 673 153.   Furthermore, in 2021/2022 the DSAC Supported the implementation of 150 projects through the Provincial Community Arts centre programmes, the total budget of R 22,450,000.00 was spent in this regard.  Between 2022 and 2023 the various MOUs were signed by the nine (9) provinces with their implementing agencies to continue the implementation of Provincial Community Arts Cetres Programmes. In the year under review, the total budget of R27 974 000 was set aside to support 154 projects on community arts centres.   In 2023/2024234 projects were supported in the implementation of Provincial Community Arts Development Programmes with a total budget of R28 686 000.  For 2025 it is estimated that 215 projects will be supported with an estimated budget of R28 386 000 for the Provincial CACs Programme.

Title EN: PRR - Recovery and Resilience Plan - RE - C04-i01: Cultural Networks and Digital Transition
Goal: Integrate Culture In Sustainable Development Frameworks
SDG: SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: National sustainable development policies and plans
Agency Implementation: GEPAC - Cultural Strategy, Planning and Assessment Bureau-Ministry of Culture
Main Feature: In the context of the COVID-19 pandemic the European Union decided to create a mechanism to address the difficulties created by the pandemic called the Next Generation EU. This was an instrument designed to help Europe recover economically and socially. To finance it, the Recovery and Resilience Facility was created, under which the Portuguese PRR (Plano de Recuperação e Resiliência) is included. Each member-state had to present its PRR, which meant a plan with the projects deemed essential for its recovery. The plan presented by Portugal was approved on July 13, 2021, along with 11 other PRRs, and it was decided that one of the areas to support would be Culture under the umbrella of the Resilience component. The main goal was to act on cultural networks and digital transition, including the modernization of public cultural facilities and the digitization of artworks and cultural heritage. They include ongoing projects in the areas of Digitization of Collection Records; the creation of online mobile libraries, information systems and integrated catalogs for at least 239 public libraries; the Installation of WiFi coverage in 50 museums, palaces and monuments; the Acquisition of digital and video projection equipment for 155 public cinema theaters and contemporary art centers; the technological modernization and maintenance of public laboratories (for restauration and conservation of important projects; the technological modernization of the National Moving Image Archive (ANIM); the installation of the National Sound Archive. Another area of support was the Digitization and virtualization of collections: of public library collections (20,000,000 images); the digitization and virtualization of national archive collections (19,50,000 documents); digitization of 59,500 public museum records; creation of virtual visits to museums; the digitization of 1,000 films (Cinematheque); the digitization and making available to the public 45,000 hours of audiovisual material from the archives of the country's historical providers of social communication and television broadcasting services. Finally, the plan aimed to support the internationalization, modernization and digital transition of books and authors: support for the translation and publication of books into foreign languages; support for the translation and editing of literary works, including audiobooks and digital books; support for the modernization and digital transition of bookstores for the purpose of acquiring equipment and technology.
Results: The plan intends the economic and social recovery of Portugal mitigating the natural impacts of the pandemic. It aimed for the modernization of the technological infrastructure of cultural facilities. The plan is still being implemented. Some results are nonetheless already visible. Two examples are: on the one hand, the creation of Intermunicipality Library networks, the renewal of IT equipment in different libraries across the country (and its autonomous regions) and the creation or improvement of catalogue aggregator services for the Library Networks. On the other hand, in 2024 there were at least 465 videos and films digitized and partially put available for public consultation by the Cinematheque. One of the objectives of component 4 (Culture) of the PRR has been achieved, which involves valuing the arts, heritage and culture as elements of affirming identity, social and territorial cohesion and increasing economic competitiveness.

Title EN: Public community centres - Bulgarian cultural and educational associations
Goal: Integrate Culture In Sustainable Development Frameworks
SDG: SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: National sustainable development policies and plans
Agency Implementation: Ministry of Culture
Main Feature: Community centres hold a special place in the country's ongoing cultural policy for culture development at national, regional and local levels. They serve as an established factor for developing a civil society mindset in Bulgaria, including, inter alia, by applying the principles of tolerance and respect for cultural expression of all communities in the country and beyond. As of 2023, there are 3,700 Community centres registered in Bulgaria, in small, medium and big villages, towns and cities. They are displaced equally in the whole territory of the country. According to the provisions of the Public Community Centres Act, they are traditional self-governing Bulgarian cultural and educational associations established in settlements nationwide, which also perform state cultural and educational tasks. All individuals, regardless of their age and gender, political and religious beliefs and ethnic self-awareness, may participate in their activities. In addition to general cultural and educational tasks, they are also called upon to help preserve the customs and traditions of the Bulgarian nation in its vast diversity. Community centres enable equal representation of different ethnic and religious communities, as well as people of different genders and faiths. Thus, community centres become an expression of the cultural-ethnic identity for the people who establish them. This is where different elements of cultural expression continuity and diversity can be noticed most distinctly. Community centres themselves have become initiators and organisers of numerous festivals and cultural events of a diverse nature and format, in which the country's various ethnic communities display their traditional culture preserved over the years. Indicatively, the country's community centres are becoming a vivid expression hub for concepts set forth in the series of international regulations adopted in recent years, which were also ratified by Bulgaria. Since the dawn of their creation, Bulgarian community centres, by their very nature, have applied the basic principles of these documents in terms of preserving and promoting cultural expression diversity, as well as enabling different cultures to flourish and engage in mutually enriching free interaction.
Results: With its sustainable development programs and policies, the Ministry of Culture creates real prerequisites for establishing the existing and introducing new cultural and educational activities in community centres. The Ministry's priorities are activities aimed at children and young people, intangible cultural heritage protection, non-professional art development, cultural integration of ethnic communities, disabled people, active ageing, equal involvement of women and men in cultural life, etc.  The Ministry supports the community centres’ budget by allocating additional subsidised units. The allocation was made in compliance with the Regulations for allocating budget resources for additional subsidised units to public community centres per region, municipality, settlement, and per community centre.

Title EN: Publication “Unterstützung für geflüchtete ukrainische Kulturmachende”, presenting findings and recommendations of an interview project on support for refugee cultural professionals from Ukraine (2023)
Goal: Promote Human Rights And Fundamental Freedoms
SDG: SDG 5 - Achieve gender equality and empower all women and girls,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels
Area of Monitoring: Artistic freedom
Cultural Domain: Design,Performing Arts,Media Arts,Cinema and Audiovisual Arts,Music,Publishing,Visual Arts
Agency Implementation: German Commission for UNESCO, national point of contact for the 2005 UNESCO Convention
Main Feature: *Cultural domain covered by the policy/measure: Cultural and creative sectors  Main aims: Gaining insights into the help made available for refugee cultural professionals in Germany, identifying the main challenges and success factors, and making proposals for medium- and long-term prospects and structures for refugee cultural professionals  Target groups: (Culture) policy-makers, cultural institutions of all types, civil society in Germany   Expected results: - Providing an overview of the situation and challenges facing refugee cultural professionals from Ukraine in Germany and the cultural institutions welcoming/supporting them; - Helping to improve the situation of refugee cultural professionals in Germany; - Contributing to the implementation of the 2005 UNESCO Convention
Results: - 40 interviews conducted with Ukrainian cultural professionals and German cultural institutions; results analysed and published in a booklet; - Key conditions for success, challenges and the steps necessary to optimise emergency support programmes for cultural professionals in Germany identified in that publication; - Five recommendations for action formulated (see above); - Findings presented in the context of an online event and shared with partners nationally and internationally; - Dialogue established with other European points of contact for the 2005 UNESCO Convention about the situation of Ukrainian cultural professionals in Europe
Financial Ressources: approx. EUR 3,000 (plus staffing costs from the institutional budget)
Recommandations: There was no evaluation of the publication itself; the publication is a critical review.  The publication is based on an analysis of qualitative interviews with Ukrainian cultural professionals and German cultural institutions. Five recommendations were derived from the findings: (1) foster connections and partnerships among cultural institutions offering help and among refugee cultural professionals as well as between institutions and refugees, (2) finance assistance programmes for the long term and make them more permanent, (3) simplify and improve the flexibility of bureaucratic procedures at all levels for all involved, (4) make information easier to find and (5) expand psychological and linguistic support for refugee cultural professionals.

Main Feature: The Cultural Diversity Observatory is a non-governmental organization whose central objectives are to produce and disseminate qualified information, develop research that generates critical knowledge, carry out training processes and provide consultancy in the interdisciplinary field of protection and promotion of cultural diversity and its interfaces with cultural policies, cultural management, mediation processes, memory and heritage, education, health, environment, etc. To this end, the Observatory develops training, research, information dissemination and consultancy projects and actions. In addition, two types of publication are carried out: books and a Bulletin that has already had 101 editions. In the reported period (2020-2023), the Observatory published the book « Diversity, sustainability and policies: the Brazilian National Culture Plan and the Cultural Diversity Convention », by José Márcio Barros and Giselle Dupin ( Orgs .). This publication was the result of a partnership between the Observatory, the Center for Research and Training of the Social Service of Commerce - SESC São Paulo and the UNESCO Representation in Brazil, which made it possible to hold a virtual seminar (in the midst of the Covid-19 pandemic). 19). The seminar brought together 11 Brazilian researchers to analyze the relationships between cultural policies, diversity and sustainability, based on a time reference situated between the 15 years of the 2005 UNESCO Convention and the 10 years of the Brazilian National Culture Plan. The speakers' contributions were gathered in the publication discussed here, with 10 articles: Section I - Cultural Diversity and Sustainable Development •	Rethinking cultural diversity , by Giuliana Kauark •	Culture as Sustainable Development: the urgency of public policies for Brazilian cultural biodiversity , by Cláudia Leitão •	Culture, diversity and the Sustainable Development Goals , by Giselle Dupin and José Márcio Barros •	The definition of culture indicators in the context of local monitoring of the SDG Agenda: challenges and perspectives based on the Belo Horizonte experience , by Rodrigo Nunes Ferreira •	Cultural diversity and sustainable development: introduction to a debate , by José Rogério Lopes Section II - The 10 years of Brazil's National Culture Plan •	A decade of the National Culture Plan – what have we learned? , by Rosimeri Carvalho da Silva •	National Culture Plan: from unanimous emergence to melancholic sunset , by Francisco Humberto Cunha Filho •	National Culture Plan and the next 10 years , by Antonio Albino Canelas Rubim •	National Culture Plan: what about the next ten years? A reflection based on concepts from Political Discourse Theory , by Ernesto Laclau, Chantal Mouffe , and Eloise Helena Livramento Dellagnelo •	A new culture for the National Culture Plan , by Guilherme Varella As for the Cultural Diversity Observatory Bulletin, it has the contribution of researchers from the institution and external specialist collaborators, and regularly brings reflections on current issues in the country and the world, from the perspective of protecting and promoting cultural diversity. In the period from 2020 to 2023, 13 editions of the Bulletin were published.
Results: The book « Diversity, sustainability and policies: the Brazilian National Culture Plan and the Cultural Diversity Convention » was well received by the public and is available for free access in virtual format at:   The consolidation of the publication of the Cultural Diversity Observatory Bulletin has made it a reference for content on topics related to diversity. The subdivision of editions by specific themes meant that they had more concrete results in the sense of guiding those looking for references to promote diversity for issues in their daily management. Results: The MCC supports various initiatives to contribute to the vitality of Indigenous cultures, languages, and media. In 2022-2023, the total amount paid was CAD 4.6 million. In addition to the renewal of a three-year cultural development agreement, 8 agreements were enhanced for Indigenous languages. The Ministry also contributed to the hiring of 27 indigenous cultural development officers and supported 30 projects affecting indigenous languages, media and youth, as well as 20 local indigenous radio stations and 3 communications companies. Title EN: Quebec’s Support to Gender Parity in the Audiovisual Sector

Area of Monitoring: Gender equality
Agency Implementation: Cultural Business Development Corporation (SODEC)
Main Feature: "In terms of parity in the audiovisual sector, SODEC continues to encourage the submission of projects written or produced by a female screenwriter or director in its production assistance program Part 1 Selective assistance for the production of feature-length fiction films and Part 2 Selective assistance for the production of short films and short-format narrative digital projects by including the following special conditions to authorize the submission of more than one project:  • Part 1: If the same company, including related companies, submits more than one featurelength fiction film project per submission, at least half of the projects must be written or directed by a female screenwriter or director. In the case of an odd number of projects submitted, beyond two projects, the majority of projects must be projects scripted or directed by women.  • Part 2: If the same company, including related companies, submits more than one project per submission, at least half of the projects must be written or directed by a female screenwriter or director in the case of a cinematographic work, and carried by a designer in the case of a digital work. In the case of an odd number of projects submitted, beyond two projects, the majority of projects must be projects scripted or directed by women."
Results: "Every year, Realizers Equitables compiles figures from different institutions in order to analyze the place of women on screens and ensure that political will is transformed into concrete results.  For SODEC, • In 2020-2021: 48% of projects were accepted with a female director and 50.9% of budgets were granted to projects with a female director • In 2021-2022: 62% of projects were accepted with a female director and 63% of budgets were granted to projects with a female director • In 2022-2023: 47.37% of projects were accepted with female director"
Recommandations: "Among the main conclusions, several observations demonstrate that the number of films directed by Indigenous and diverse women remains insufficient. The more detailed the figures are on the presence of women in the different programs, the clearer we will have a picture of the situation. By having public data from all institutions, it will be possible to establish and target action strategies leading to concrete results.  For cinema written and directed by women to flourish in an autonomous and sustainable manner, parity must be integrated at every stage, from creation to production, including marketing."

Title EN: Social inclusion through the performing arts. Encuentro Festival Teatro Latinoamericano.
Goal: Integrate Culture In Sustainable Development Frameworks
SDG: SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: National sustainable development policies and plans
Agency Implementation: Fundación Calibrarte.
Main Feature: The Encuentro Festival Teatro Latinoamericano is a far reaching artistic and cultural event that takes place in the La Granja commune (where IFCD "Ciudad Sur" is implemented), in the south area of Santiago city, in Chile. Its goal is to foster theatre culture, social integration and inclusion through performing art, providing open and free access to high quality theatre presentations by both national and international professional theatre  groups.   This festival takes diverse actions for its implementation, making a personalised selective call, oriented towards professional theatre groups with a long history in their coutries of origin. During ten days, the festival offers around fifty evening itinerant performing arts presentations in public spaces and community centres around La Granja and other communes in the Metropolitan Region.   Regarding access, the festival is free and without discrimination, eliminating any type of social, sexual, gender, economic, educational, ethnic or disability exclusion. Apart from the theatre functions, the festival organises discussion groups and workshops for the flow of experiences among the participating groups, with the aim of establishing ties that favour artistic, social and cultural development.   At the same time, it organises workshops and seminars aimed at the general community population and spectators, with the purpose of fostering insertion, inclusion, education and educating multiple age-group audiences in the cultural theatrearea. Lastly, we can include this measure in the indicator on "measures that strengthen the skills and capacities of civil society" from the monitoring framework of the 2005 Convention.
Results: The Encuentro has fostered inclusion of and sensibilisation to the arts and cultre among Chilean families through the participation of more than 6,000 people from different age groups, be they audiences or creative agents. Furthermore, it has created a multi-institute support network for social organisations and families, as well as a type of a local and Latin American theatre network for prefessionals of the performing arts.   The continuity of the programme has allowed the implementation of the festival, psychosocial support for the participating community and Latin American theatre professional flows. Lastly, the goal of adding cultural value to the community and their territories, has been a driving force for the Festival.

Main Feature: la Rencontre Nationale sur les Mécanismes d’Investissement dans le Domaine de l'Industrie Cinématographique qui s’est déroulée le mardi 13 février 2024 au Palais de la Culture  «Moufdi Zakaria » à Alger, avec la participation de l’Agence Algérienne de Promotion de l'Investissement (AAPI), a permis de réunir un ensemble de partenaires et d’acteurs intervenant dans les domaines respectifs du cinéma et de l’investissement.  Le secteur de la culture et des arts avait pris l'initiative d'accueillir et d'accompagner plusieurs porteurs de projets d'investissement dans le domaine de l'industrie cinématographique, ajoutant que de nombreuses rencontres similaires ont été organisées avec des cadres de l'AAPI pour examiner les différents mécanismes d'octroi d'assiettes foncières destinées à la réalisation de projets d'investissement dans le domaine du cinéma, outre les avantages et incitations octroyés par l'Agence. Le secteur s’attèle actuellement avec le Ministère des Finances, à travers des Comités interministériels, à : •	Procéder à la révision des mécanismes de financement et d'appui à la production cinématographique ; •	Procéder à l'exploitation des salles de cinéma par les opérateurs privés ; •	Garantir des facilitations fiscales et incitations bancaires pour l'investissement ; •	Faire connaitre, parmi les professionnels du cinéma, l’accompagnement et le soutien que l’Agence offrirait aux investisseurs privés ;  •	Explorer des mécanismes d'investissement en cinématographie dans le cadre des efforts consentis précédemment en la matière ; •	Ouvrir un débat avec les experts et les spécialistes. Cette rencontre  a vu la présentation, par deux chefs d'études relevant de l'AAPI, de deux interventions sur le système d'incitation dans le cadre de la loi sur l'investissement, ainsi que sur les conditions et modalités d'octroi du foncier économique relevant des domaines de l'Etat, destinés à la réalisation de projets d'investissement, outre une troisième intervention sur les mécanismes de financement bancaire des projets d'investissement dans le domaine du cinéma, présentée par le commissaire général de l'ABEF. A cette occasion, des projets cinématographiques réussis, ayant bénéficié d'un soutien technique, artistique et financier du Ministère de la Culture et des Arts, ont été présentés, dont le multiplex cinématographique "TMV" à Alger, le complexe  cinématographique "Ciné Gold" à Oran, ainsi qu'un autre complexe cinématographique à Oran du groupe hôtelier "AZ".
Results: Un accord-cadre est en phase de préparation avec l'Association Professionnelle des Banques et Etablissements Financiers (ABEF) comprenant une série de propositions visant à : •	lever les obstacles aux porteurs de projets, •	accorder des prêts bancaires à taux d'intérêt bonifiés aux investisseurs et aux producteurs dans les domaines liés au secteur cinématographique et culturel en général, •	mettre en évidence l'accompagnement et le soutien que l’AAPI peut assurer aux investisseurs dans ce domaine, tels que « les avantages fiscaux et parafiscaux offerts par la nouvelle loi sur l'investissement, ainsi que l'accès au foncier économique pour la réalisation de ces projets », •	Inciter au rapprochement de l’agence à travers l’adhésion à la plateforme numérique de l'investisseur, plateforme qui permet aux investisseurs de consulter la disponibilité du foncier à l'échelle nationale ; •	sensibiliser quant aux réformes initiées par l'Algérie dans le souci de diversifier son économie, à travers, entre autres l'industrie cinématographique considérée comme source de diversification des revenues. .       l'Agence a enregistré 06 demande  d'investisseurs  dans les domaines liés au secteur de l’industrie cinématographique et culturelle en général.

Title EN: Realization  of the 2nd Edition of the Brazilian Creative Industries Market – MICBR 2021
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture
SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Cultural and creative sectors
Cultural Domain: Design,Performing Arts,Media Arts,Cinema and Audiovisual Arts,Music,Publishing
Agency Implementation: Special Secretariat for Culture (current Ministry of Culture; in 2021, linked to the Ministry of Tourism)
Main Feature: MICBR is a business event that brings together entrepreneurs from the cultural and creative sectors in Brazil and other countries. Between the 17th and 19th of November 2021, the then Special Secretariat for Culture (currently the Ministry of Culture), linked to the Ministry of Tourism, held the second edition of the MICBR, in partnership with the Organization of Ibero-American States for Education , Science and Culture (OEI). The edition took place in virtual mode, in view of the pandemic declared due to Covid-19. In this sense, MICBR 2021 aimed to expand business relationships and the expectation of concluding commercial contracts, as well as strengthening the production chains of the creative economy in Brazil. The program included training and training activities and business activities, mainly business rounds and cross pitchings . The program for the second edition of MICBR - held entirely virtually - was made up of spaces for exchanging professional contacts (networking) carried out on the event platform via spatial chat ; opportunities to present products and services ( pitchings ) by selected entrepreneurs; training activities for entrepreneurs workshops; activities open to the general public lectures and master conferences.
Results: Event numbers: » More than 700 business rounds held between entrepreneurs selected via public notice and national and international buyers; » Participation of 1,016 registrants in activities carried out over three days of online event; » 235 participating companies, with 120 specialized buyers and 115 entrepreneurs selected through a Public Selection Notice; » 3 master lectures; » 30 speakers; » 235 crossed pitchings ; » US$535,664.943 (R$ 2,714,000.00) in deals closed 6 months after the event.  Participants had an increase of at least 1 to 3 contracts concluded after the event. Furthermore, the participating public signaled greater security, especially in relation to information about possible obstacles to expanding business and how to seek international partners, relevant knowledge for the national and international promotion of their ventures. They also showed, to a lesser extent, greater knowledge regarding the processes necessary to expand their business, the notion of the main markets where they can buy/sell products or services and how to seek national partners for this. Furthermore, they indicated greater confidence in seeing their international contacts as potential business partners. was carried out, through a partnership with the Center for Studies in Creative Economy and Culture of the Federal University of Rio Grande do Sul, to monitor and evaluate the activities carried out within the scope of MicBR 2021. Three evaluation strategies were used: processes, results and economic impact. The research revealed that: • After holding MICBR 2021, there was a considerable increase (17%) in the percentage of entrepreneurs with a number of 1 to 20 international contacts. This increase is in line with the 16% decrease in the percentage of respondents who stated that they did not have any international contacts in their networks. This indicates that there has been an expansion of international networks for entrepreneurs who still have no contact abroad. • There was an increase in the percentage of respondents who stated that they had carried out 1 to 3 businesses, in the sectors: Design, Fashion, Performing Arts and Audiovisual & Animation. The increase in the percentage of respondents who said they had completed 4 to 7 can be seen in the Performing Arts, Crafts, Electronic Games and Music sectors, with emphasis on the last two. After the event, cultural agents responded to the survey regarding the knowledge needed to expand their businesses: • The participating public signaled greater confidence, mainly in relation to information about possible obstacles to expanding business and how to seek international partners, relevant knowledge for the national and international promotion of their ventures. • They also showed, to a lesser extent, greater knowledge regarding the processes necessary to expand their business, the notion of the main markets where they can buy/sell products or services and how to seek national partners for this. The Covid-19 pandemic has affected the creative sectors in different ways: • Performing Arts, Audiovisual & animation, Editorial, Fashion and Music indicated having suffered a greater impact. • Electronic Games and Design indicated a less intense impact. • 68% of respondents reported that they found opportunities to develop their business in the context of the pandemic.
Financial Ressources: US$29,605.6527 (R$150,000.00) invested in research into the results of the event.

Title EN: RECOVERY PLAN OF CULTURAL INDUSTRIES AND ARTS BY 2030
Goal: Integrate Culture In Sustainable Development Frameworks
SDG: SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: National sustainable development policies and plans
Cultural Domain: Design,Performing Arts,Media Arts,Cinema and Audiovisual Arts,Music,Publishing,Visual Arts
Agency Implementation: General Directorate of Cultural Industries and Arts (Ministry of Culture)
Main Feature: The Recovery Plan for the cultural industries and arts by 2030, approved with Ministerial Resolution No. 000086-2022-DM/MC (March 28, 2022), is a management instrument of the Ministry of Culture, whose general objective is to reactivate and develop cultural industries and arts after the impact of COVID-19; contributing to solving the public problem, recognized in the National Culture Policy (PNC), of the “Limited exercise of the cultural rights of the population.” To this end, 5 strategic objectives, 16 activities and 92 tasks have been established:  -	OE 1. Incrementar la participación de la población en las expresiones de las artes y las industrias culturales. A1.1. Impulsar la reactivación de las actividades artístico- culturales que promuevan el acceso de la población. A1.2. Implementar espacios físicos y virtuales de contenido artístico y cultural para el acceso de la población. A1.3.  Fortalecer las capacidades de docentes y mediadores/as para facilitar el acceso a la cultura. -	OE 2. Impulsar el empleo en las industrias culturales y las artes. A2.1. Implementar medidas de financiamiento para proyectos vinculados a las industrias culturales y artes A2.2.  Implementar medidas que impulsen el desarrollo de mercados culturales A2.3. Fortalecer las capacidades de lo/as trabajadores/as de las artes e industrias culturales para la mejora de sus condiciones laborales.    -	OE 3. Strenghten the capacities of cultural agents for the development of cultural and art industries. A3.1.  Develop training addressed to cultural agents related to management of cultural and art industries. A3.2. Develop training addressed to cultural agents with the purpose to promote the Access to culture by the population. A3.3.  Develop training addressed to cultural agents with the purpose to strenghten artistic education.  -	OE 4. Guarantee cultural governance sustainability in cultural industries and the arts. A4.1.  Generate spaces for articulation with public and private organizations to promote the reactivation of the arts and cultural industries A4.2. Promote studies and information management regarding cultural industries and the arts. A4.3. Creation of regulations and guidelines aimed at promoting the reactivation of cultural industries and the arts. -	OE 5. Strenghten development of cultural policies in subnational governments. A5.1. Promote in subnational governments, the development of policies that promote the use of cultural spaces in their jurisdictions. A5.2. Promote the execution of measures and actions by subnational governments for strenghtening institutionality in cultural matter. A5.3.  Develop training actions on cultural public management for servers of subnational governments.  For the preparation of the Recovery Plan, there was technical assistance from UNESCO and the cooperation of the Swedish government. From the beginning, the process of building the Plan was conceived to be participatory, which is how 59 participation spaces were implemented at the national level (including 3 tables in native languages and one table in sign language), in which 1,278 agents participated and cultural, public servants and citizens, receiving 1913 contributions that were finally made visible and incorporated into the Recovery Plan. This process included the formation of a Consultative Committee made up of representative cultural agents, academia, and the public sector, who accompanied each of the phases that were part of the design, approval, and socialization of the document.
Results: - 5 objectives were established, with 16 activities and 92 tasks aimed at promoting cultural industries and arts. - Actions defined as priority have an approved budget. - The institutional objectives of the DGIA are aimed at the reactivation and development of the sector. - Thought and conceived, having the citizen as the center. - Specifically, for OE2 and OE3, specific strategies are established to reduce gender gaps in the cultural sector, as well as affirmative actions to reduce inequalities between cultural agents of the indigenous population, Afro-Peruvian peoples or those with some type of disability. - Socialization campaigns were developed at the national level with different agents of the cultural sector, public servants and private institutions with the purpose of getting more actors to contribute to the achievement of the plan. -Among the main goals achieved are: the creation of RENTOCA, the preparation of manuals to guide public management, the incorporation and increase of gender and intercultural quotas in the different services and incentives provided by the Ministry of Culture. Likewise, the study of information on the cultural and arts industries has been promoted, training has been developed that promotes the reduction of gaps in the sector, among others.

Title EN: Regional Symposium, Exhibition, and Festival
Goal: Achieve A Balanced Flow Of Cultural Goods And Services And Increase The Mobility Of Artists And Cultural Professionals
SDG: SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 10 - Reduce inequality within and among countries,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Flow of cultural goods and services
Cultural Domain: Performing Arts,Cinema and Audiovisual Arts,Music,Visual Arts
Agency Implementation: Ministry of Culture and Sport
Main Feature: Overview In June 2022, Addis Ababa hosted the East African Art and Culture Festival, a regional event that showcased a diverse array of artistic and cultural expressions. The festival featured several key components:  1. Film Festival: Celebrating the vibrant film industry in East Africa, this segment showcased regional films, highlighting various genres and storytelling techniques.  2. Craft Exhibition: An exhibition of traditional and contemporary crafts from across East Africa, providing a platform for artisans to display their work.  3. Music Festival: Featuring performances from renowned and emerging artists, this festival celebrates the rich musical heritage of the region.  4. Symposium: A crucial part of the festival, the symposium focused on the contributions of culture and art to the national economy, sustainable development, peace, and national identity. Professionals presented papers and engaged in discussions on these themes.  5. Visual Art Exhibition: Displaying visual arts from across the region, this exhibition included paintings, sculptures, and other art forms, emphasizing the region’s artistic diversity.  Regional Conferences Organized annually by the Ministry of Culture and Sport, these conferences are dedicated to discussing the impact of culture and art on various aspects of national development. The 2022 symposium brought together stakeholders from Kenya, Sudan, and Tanzania, providing a platform for cross-border dialogue and collaboration.  Key Outcomes Enhanced regional cultural exchange and cooperation. Increased visibility for East African artists and cultural practitioners. Facilitated discussions on the role of culture in fostering economic growth and sustainable development. This festival underscored the importance of art and culture in strengthening regional ties and promoting shared values.
Results: Enhanced Integration through Art and Culture: Symposiums and workshops facilitated dialogue and consensus-building among stakeholders, leading to the development of strategies to integrate art and culture more effectively into regional and national frameworks. These platforms allow for the sharing of best practices and innovative approaches to cultural integration.  Advocacy for Economic and Social Contributions: The events underscored the significant role of culture and art in contributing to the national economy and social development. Through presentations and discussions, the value of cultural industries in job creation, GDP growth, and social cohesion was highlighted, advocating for increased support and investment in these sectors.  Strengthened Participation and Solidarity: The symposiums and workshops fostered greater participation and solidarity among people in the region and key stakeholders in the cultural and creative industries. By bringing together diverse groups, these events reinforced collaboration and mutual support, enhancing regional unity and collective action in the cultural sector.  These achievements reflect the success of the events in advancing the integration of culture into broader economic and social policies, while also building a stronger network of cultural practitioners and advocates.
Recommandations: Conclusion   Cultural and regional festivals, along with symposiums, play a crucial role in enhancing regional integration and advancing the development of culture and creative industries. These events create platforms for the equitable exchange of cultural goods and services, as well as promoting artistic mobility. They also advocate for leveraging the potential of cultural and creative industries to foster social and economic development. Recommendation To further strengthen regional integration and support the development of the cultural and creative sectors, it is recommended that culture and art festivals and symposiums continue. These events should focus on: 1. Strengthening Regional Integration: Facilitate collaboration and unity across regions. 2. Policy Advocacy: Promote policies that support the cultural and creative industries. 3. Artistic Mobility: Enhance opportunities for artists to travel and exchange ideas. 4. Fair Flow of Cultural Goods and Services: Ensure equitable distribution and accessibility.  Continued support and development of these initiatives will contribute significantly to the growth and sustainability of the cultural sector.

Title EN: Régulation de l’audiovisuel et de la communication au Bénin
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture
SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Media diversity
Agency Implementation: La Haute Autorité de l'audiovisuel et de la communication (HAAC)
Main Feature: L’audiovisuel et la communication sont deux secteurs importants pour toute société. En effet, transmettre des messages, raconter des histoires, informer ou exprimer des idées à travers une combinaison puissante de l'image et du son dans un monde globalisé relèvent de ce que certains appellent le 4ème pouvoir, est encadré par la Constitution qui y a consacré une institution : la Haute Autorité de l’Audiovisuel et de la communication (HAAC).  •	garantir et assurer la liberté et la protection de la presse ainsi que tous les moyens de communication de masse dans le respect de la loi ; •	veiller au respect de la déontologie en matière d’information et à l’accès équitable des partis politiques, des associations et des citoyens aux moyens officiels d’information et de communication ; •	garantir l’utilisation équitable et appropriée des organismes publics de presse et de communication audiovisuelle par les institutions de la République, chacune en fonction de ses missions constitutionnelles et d’assurer le cas échéant les arbitrages nécessaires. •	Veiller à la qualité et à la diversité des programmes, au développement de la production et de la création audiovisuelle nationale, ainsi qu’à la mise en valeur du patrimoine culturel national et universel.  •	Proposer à la nomination par le Chef de l’État en conseil des ministres, les directeurs des organes de presse publique et garantit l’autonomie et l’impartialité des moyens publics d’information et de communication ; •	Délivrer les autorisations d’usage de fréquence pour la radiodiffusion sonore, la télévision par voie hertzienne terrestre ou par satellite, •	déterminer dans le respect des principes de l’égalité de traitement et d’accès aux médias officiels, les conditions des prestations audiovisuelles des partis politiques, des associations et ces citoyens et à en contrôler la mise en œuvre.
Results: -	En 2021, la Haute Autorité de l’Audiovisuel et de la Communication (HAAC), régulateur béninois des médias, a lancé un processus d’accréditation pour les entreprises de presse en ligne. 59 médias avaient alors été sélectionnés puis mis en observation. Après plusieurs vérifications, 46 médias ont été officiellement reconnus. Parmi ceux-ci, on compte 26 web TV, 16 sites d’information et 4 radios en ligne. -	Délivrance de carte de presse, qui permet au journaliste professionnel de prouver son activité, d'accéder plus facilement à des lieux qui lui servent à obtenir des informations (salles de presse, bureaux officiels, musées, etc.) et de faire valoir son droit à la protection sociale prévue par le statut de journaliste professionnel créé par la Loi n° 2015-07 portant code de l’information et de la communication en République du Bénin. Selon la décision n° 24 -023/ HAAC du 21 mars 2024, il y a 184 journalistes accrédités au Bénin. (Source : HAAC, 2024)

Title EN: Regulation of audio-visual media sector
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture
SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Media diversity
Agency Implementation: National Assembly of the Republic of Armenia and interested state bodies
Main Feature: The Law of the Republic of Armenia "On Audio-visual Media" adopted by the National Assembly of the Republic of Armenia on July 16, 2020 (amendments to the “Law on Audio-visual Media" in 2022, 2023, 2024), which aims at ensuring everyone's right to receive reliable information, the right for editorial independence and the right to freedom of expression of opinion, independence of the body regulating audio-visual media sector, independence of the body ensuring management of activities of public audio-visual media services and carrying out control, diversity of audio-visual programmes and protection and development of audio-visual information area. Legal framework to support self-regulation measures. Government of the Republic of Armenia has outlined a series of initiatives in its 2021-2026 action plan. These endeavors are directed towards fostering a more participatory approach to the formulation of new legislation on mass media. The main aim of this initiative is to establish a legal framework for the self-regulation system. It aims to guarantee accuracy, objectivity, and diversity in the information shared with the public. The initiative also strives to boost the social responsibility of journalists, reduce the disinformation or offensive content, uphold professional ethics, and foster the establishment of professional integrity. The Ministry of Justice held several meetings with media representatives to discuss the primary aspects of the media self-regulation concept. Moreover, on April 19 of 2022, a memorandum of tripartite cooperation was signed involving the Ministry of Justice, the Standing Committee on Science, Education, Culture, Diaspora, Youth, and Sport of the National Assembly, and the Freedom of Speech Protection Committee representing the journalist community. The memorandum focuses on collaboratively shaping and endorsing a comprehensive policy for the information sphere and media development. It also encompasses the reform concept for legislation governing mass media activities and the drafting of new legal acts stemming from this concept.  In spring 2022 a Media Sector Needs Assessment Report (Technical Paper) was delivered to authorities in Armenia; and discussed in September 2022 through a large forum/conference involving media stakeholders in the country and the international community in the country. Following the recommendations contained in the Technical Paper, a Draft Concept Note, the Institutional Strengthening of the Mass Media Self (co)-Regulation System was developed by the Ministry of Justice of Armenia.  In December 2022, the Ministry of Justice requested the Council of Europe to conduct an expert review of the newly developed Concept Note for legislation governing mass media activities. Taking into consideration the expert opinion presented by the Council of Europe's experts, discussions have been organized with the participation of representatives from mass media, non-governmental organizations and the Parliament. These discussions led to the development of a comprehensive package of legislative drafts which were submitted for public discussion on November 29, 2023. The package of legislative drafts entails the redefinition of mass media and the establishment of a legal framework to support self-regulation measures. Moreover, the package of legislative drafts aims to introduce regulations that providing legislative recognition and state-guaranteed privileges to those media outlets, which adhere to a well-functioning self-regulatory system in Armenia․ As the ultimate goal, it was proposed to have a completely independent journalistic body from the state - the Media Council, in which the state will not participate and which will unite all the media and their self-regulation mechanisms as a collective structure. The package of legislative drafts is currently in the discussion phase, and there are plans for further improvements.
Results: As a result of the implementation of the policy in the field of audio-visual media, the quality of audio-visual products of public broadcasters has been improved, a favorable and prospective legal framework and an equal competitive environment in the media sector have been created, which should contribute to the increase of quality journalism, media literacy, exclude hate speech, ensure effective media management, transparency of the ownership rights in the media sector.
Financial Ressources: every year 87500,0
Recommandations: The new law governing the sector makes it possible to regulate all types of audiovisual communications that are under the responsibility of editorial staff of the service provider, distributors and those making audio-visual products available to users.

Title EN: REGULATION OF TICKET EXPENSES AND TRAVEL ALLOWANCES FOR ARTISTS PRODUCING BOLIVIAN CULTURAL GOODS, WHO REPRESENT THE COUNTRY IN INTERNATIONAL OFFICIAL EVENTS
Goal: Achieve A Balanced Flow Of Cultural Goods And Services And Increase The Mobility Of Artists And Cultural Professionals
SDG: SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 10 - Reduce inequality within and among countries,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Mobility of artists and cultural professionals
Cultural Domain: Design,Performing Arts,Media Arts,Cinema and Audiovisual Arts,Music,Publishing,Visual Arts
Agency Implementation: MINISTERIO DE CULTURAS, DESCOLONIZACIÓN Y DESPATRIARCALIZACIÓN (MINISTRY OF CULTURES, DECOLONIZATION AND DEPATRIARCHALIZATION)
Main Feature: Within the framework of paragraph VIII of article 21 of Law No. 1267 of December 20, 2019, incorporated by the First Additional Provision of Law No. 1493 of December 17, 2022, of the General State Budget for 2023, it establishes that: "VIII. The Ministry of Cultures, Decolonization and Depatriarchalization is authorized to cover, within its institutional budget, the cost of tickets and travel expenses of Bolivian Artists Producers of Cultural Goods, who represent the country in international official events. It becomes effective with the validity of the regulations approved by Bi-ministerial Resolution No. 19 dated August 4, 2023, issued by the Ministries of Cultures, Decolonization and Depatriarchalization and of Economy and Public Finance. The purpose of the Regulation is to establish the procedure, requirements and responsibilities for the allocation of tickets and travel expenses for Artists Producing Bolivian Cultural Assets, who represent the country in official international events, and who must meet the established requirements to access them. The expenses for tickets and travel expenses are included in the Annual Operating Plan and programmed in the budget of the Ministry of Culture, Decolonization and Depatriarchalization.  The granting of tickets and/or travel expenses to Artists Producing Bolivian Cultural Assets, who represent the country in official international events, is authorized by Ministerial Resolution of the Highest Executive Authority of the Ministry of Culture, Decolonization and Depatriarchalization.
Results: Through this measure, the Ministry of Culture, Decolonization and Depatriarchalization has promoted the participation of Bolivian artists and artisans in international fairs and events such as: Ruraq Maki Fair in Lima, Peru, where 6 artisans from the eastern, valleys and highland regions participated. II International Children's Cultural Forum in Moscow, Russia, with the participation of Bolivian child artists. International Book Fairs in Mexico and Havana, Cuba. Representation at the Venice Biennale  This has allowed Bolivian creators to showcase their work to new audiences and markets, expanding the visibility of the country's cultural expressions and learning from the experiences of other countries. This contributes to the development of more effective policies and programs for the sector. In this first year of operation, the measure has benefited approximately 20 producers of Cultural Assets.
Financial Ressources: $us. 80,000 (Annually)

Title EN: Renforcement de la mobilité entrante des artistes en République de Guinée
Goal: Achieve A Balanced Flow Of Cultural Goods And Services And Increase The Mobility Of Artists And Cultural Professionals
SDG: SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 10 - Reduce inequality within and among countries,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Mobility of artists and cultural professionals
Cultural Domain: Design,Performing Arts,Media Arts,Cinema and Audiovisual Arts,Music,Publishing,Visual Arts
Agency Implementation: Ministère de la Culture, du Tourisme et de l’Artisanat
Main Feature: Des évènements artistiques et culturels de dimension internationale suscitant un intérêt auprès des artistes et des professionnels guinéens non résident et les étrangers sont organisés en République de Guinée. Malgré ce foisonnement, leur participation est limitée pour des raisons organisationnelles et financières.  Pour conférer à ces évènements le succès escompté à travers la participation des artistes internationaux, l’Etat guinéen et les partenaires techniques et financiers accompagnent les organisateurs en leur facilitant l’obtention de visas et d’accréditations, la prise en charge partielle ou totale du séjour des artistes et professionnels. Selon les filières et les disciplines artistiques, il existe une diversité de manifestations artistiques et culturelles à dimension internationale comme le Festival National des Arts et de la Culture, le Festival International du Théâtre de Guinée, le Festival International du Djembé, le Festival D’mba, le Festival des Arts de Dubréka, de Koundara, de Faranah, le Festival International de Grillades, le Salon International du Textile Africain, le Salon International du Livre et de la Lecture, la Semaine de fraternité et de l’amitié (SAFRA), la Mamaya de Kankan, le Doundounba de Kouroussa, les dédicaces des artistes, etc. A chaque édition, ces évènements mobilisent un grand nombre d’artistes et de professionnels de la culture et des arts à travers le monde. L’objectif principal de cette mesure est de contribuer à l’accroissement de la mobilité entrante des artistes et professionnels de la culture en République de Guinée. Il s’agit :  -	d’encourager et de faciliter la participation des artistes et professionnels de la culture d’autres pays à des évènements artistiques et culturels en République de Guinée ;  -	de favoriser les contacts, les échanges et le partage d’expériences autour des projets culturels et  -	de renforcer les capacités institutionnelles, techniques et opérationnelles des artistes et professionnels de la culture.  Les résultats attendus de l’organisation de ces manifestations sont :  -	organiser des rencontres professionnelles à l’occasion des événements artistiques et culturels ;  -	accroître le nombre d’artistes et de professionnels participant aux événements artistiques et culturels.
Results: L’organisation régulière de ces manifestations artistiques et culturelles a permis à plusieurs artistes et professionnels de la culture de venir en Guinée. Par exemple : -	1 500 artistes et professionnels (dont 820 étrangers) de 42 pays (y compris la République de Guinée) ont été accrédités lors de la 1ère édition du Salon International du Textile Africain (SITA), en 2023 ; -	100 personnalités venues de différents horizons (des directeurs de cinématographie, des jurés, des réalisateurs et des personnes ressources) ont été invités et pris en charge : le transport aller-retour, la restauration et l’hébergement à la 9ème édition du Festival de la Création Cinématographique de Guinée (FECCIG) (Août 2022) et au Festival de Film Espoir (FIFE) (22 au 25 novembre 2024) ;  -	350 artistes et professionnels du théâtre, venus de la Côte d’Ivoire, du Sénégal, du Mali, du Cameroun, du Gabon, du Congo, de la France, du Tchad, ont pris part au Festival International du Théâtre de Guinée et au Festival des Arts de Dubréka en 2023 ; -	80 visiteurs et acheteurs professionnels, 600 journalistes et 420 exposants de 8 pays d’Afrique, d’Asie et d’Europe, ont pris part aux différentes éditions des foires et salons artisanaux en 2020, 2021, 2022 et 2023.

Title EN: Second Austrian Film Gender Report
Goal: Promote Human Rights And Fundamental Freedoms
SDG: SDG 5 - Achieve gender equality and empower all women and girls,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels
Area of Monitoring: Gender equality
Agency Implementation: Austrian Film Institute
Main Feature: Following the publication of the First Austrian Film Gender Report in 2018, the Second Austrian Film Gender Report was published in 2021. The report presents solid data on gender (in-)equality in the Austrian film sector. Through comparison with the previous report, developments and progress can be shown. The reports are important means for the evaluation of the effectiveness of measures already implemented to promote gender equality (Gender Incentives, Gender Budgeting) and support the development of new measures and initiatives.  By drawing on internationally standardized analysis frameworks (such as the “Swedish Model”) the report allows for a comparison of the data beyond the national framework. The fundamental aim of the report is to raise awareness for gender inequalities and to contribute to the achievement of a more balanced film sector.  Part A of the Second Film Gender Report presents a quantitative analysis of the film and television projects funded by the largest Austrian subsidizers in the time period 2017 to 2019. The report shows that women were underrepresented in both cinema and television funding. When the Swedish Model is applied for compiling data from all areas of funding, women received less than one-third (28%) of the funding approved for cinema projects. In television, less than one-fifth (18%) of funding was allocated to women. In the areas of cinema and TV together, solely one-fourth (25%) of funding went to women. At the same time, it can be shown that the share of funding allocated to women has risen since the last report. Compared to 2012 to 2016, the number of women in cinema script development as calculated with the Swedish Model increased by nearly 8% and almost 12% in cinema project development. Of all areas, the increase in that of production, which received the most funding by far, was the lowest. Part B of the report quantitatively analyses all Austrian fiction films that were released to cinemas between 2012 and 2019. Furthermore, the content of 12 films from this sample underwent qualitative analysis. The qualitative analysis of 12 fiction films chosen in light of the percentages of males and females in the core crews took a look at the extent to which their portrayals were characterized by gender equality, the absence of sexism, representation of diversity and a lack of discrimination. Films with positive results in all four of these categories were deemed in the analysis to be “inclusive.” Among other things, the analysis shows a correlation between the gender ratio of the crew and the onscreen portrayals: While all female-driven films were “inclusive” in all four areas, none of the male-driven films were.  Part C of the report focuses on data relating to the film funding provided by the Austrian Film Institute from 2017 to 2019. The data show that women received less than one-third of all approved moneys. This imbalance could be observed in applications: Less than one-third of all funding was applied for by female members of the core crew. The report also provides data on the Austrian Film Institutes supervisory board and project commission and shows that the percentage of women in the Supervisory Board rose from 17% in 2012 to 50% in 2019. The Project Commission consisted of approximately equal numbers of women (56%) and men. An English version (shortened) of the report is available online (s. above).

Title EN: Renforcement de la protection de la propriété littéraire et artistique au Bénin par la relecture des statuts du bureau de gestion du droit d’auteur
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture
SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Cultural and creative sectors
Cultural Domain: Design,Performing Arts,Media Arts,Cinema and Audiovisual Arts,Music,Publishing,Visual Arts
Agency Implementation: Bureau Béninois du Droit d'Auteur et des Droits Voisins (BUBEDRA)
Main Feature: Le droit d'auteur a toujours été et doit toujours être, y compris à l'heure du numérique, favorable au créateur et à l'utilisateur. Depuis quelques années, les moyens de production, de diffusion et de consommation des œuvres artistiques et culturelles ont considérablement évolué avec l’apparition de nouveaux outils et supports. Ceci a engendré un nouveau modèle économique et surtout une évasion de ressources pour le créateur. En plus de la reconnaissance des droits voisins, la prise en compte de la dématérialisation de la production et de la consommation a conduit le Gouvernement du Bénin à inscrire au titre de ses réformes, la relecture des statuts du Bureau Béninois du Droit d’Auteur et des droits voisins pour une meilleure protection des créateurs, de leurs ayants droits et de la création. Il s’agit d’assurer la digitalisation de la gestion des droits, la protection des œuvres et la perception des redevances de droit d'auteur pour les exploitations numériques des œuvres des titulaires de droit. A travers cette mesure, l’État entend :   •	Protéger et défendre sur le territoire national et à l'étranger des intérêts professionnels et patrimoniaux des auteurs d’œuvres littéraires et artistiques ressortissants de la République du Bénin ou de leurs ayants droit ; •	Protéger et défendre sur le territoire national et à l'étranger des intérêts professionnels et patrimoniaux des titulaires de droits voisins que sont les interprètes ou exécutants, les producteurs de phonogrammes ressortissants béninois et leurs ayants droit ; •	Protéger et défendre sur le territoire national et à l'étranger des intérêts professionnels et patrimoniaux des organismes de radiodiffusion ou de télévision dont le siège social se trouve au Bénin ; •	Contribuer à la promotion de la créativité artistique et culturelle nationale par tous moyens appropriés relevant de sa compétence. •	Mettre en place une plateforme électronique web et mobile fonctionnant sur terminaux Android (tablettes, smartphones, etc.) avec pour objectif principal, la dématérialisation du processus de collecte et la sécurisation des redevances de droits d’auteur. •	Disposer d’une interface d’enregistrement et de suivi des paiements de redevances de droit d’auteur ;   •	Couvrir à court terme l’ensemble du territoire national ;  •	Constituer une base de données centralisée des redevables (statistiques, estimation des recettes) ;  •	cartographier les usagers (recensement, identifications unique et localisation GPS), retracer automatiquement chaque perception reçue.  •	Doter les redevables du BUBEDRA d’un Menu USSD à travers les Opérateurs de Téléphonie Mobile (MTN, MOOV, SBIN). Ce menu leur permet de payer via mobile money directement leur redevance partout sur l’étendue du territoire Béninois. Cette démarche vise également à sécuriser les fonds. Cette réforme est prévue au PAG 2021-2026 et sa mise en œuvre a démarré.
