Title EN: Support for amateur culture (Republic of Slovenia Public Fund for Cultural Activities)
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture
SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Cultural and creative sectors
Agency Implementation: Javni sklad Republike Slovenije za kulturne dejavnosti (Republic of Slovenia Public Fund for Cultural Activities)
Main Feature: The key to the work of Republic of Slovenia Public Fund for Cultural Activities is its cultural network of 59 regional branches, which cover the entire Slovenian territory as well as neighbouring countries and the international level and provide access to important cultural and artistic achievements in the Slovenian cultural space and beyond. Each year, the fund issues several public calls for proposals to support the activities of amateur cultural associations active in various fields (choir, instrumental music, theatre, puppetry, folklore, film, dance, literature, visual arts, intermedia) as well as associations active in the field of various ethnic minorities and immigrants in the Republic of Slovenia. By financially supporting the activities of amateur cultural associations, the state aims to promote the growth of creativity and the development of quality projects that are important for general cultural development in Slovenia and abroad. The financial support of the state also enables the organisation of a variety of cultural events and the development of quality cultural education programmes. Through the annual public call for proposals, which targets the activities of various ethnic minorities and immigrant communities in Slovenia, the state aims to encourage the creativity of their members and contribute to the preservation of their cultural identity. Through the call for proposals, the state supports high-quality projects that are important for the cultural development of members of ethnic minorities and immigrants and promotes the presentation of ethnic minority and immigrant culture in a broader environment. Through a special call for proposals, the fund also co-finances the provision of the most necessary premises and equipment for the development of amateur and professional non-governmental organisations. In addition to the public fund, amateur culture is also supported by local authorities, but most activities are based on the voluntary work and commitment of the amateur culture creators themselves.
Results: Funding cultural activities of amateurs facilitates personal growth and cultural integration, promotes cultural education and lifelong learning programmes, and strengthens competencies, skills and abilities. The public fund supports the activities of local cultural associations and organisations through public tenders. Both are important pillars of cultural creation at local level and beyond. The activities of amateur cultural associations lead to numerous events. Between 2020 and 2023, more than 4,300 events with a total of almost 600,000 visitors were organised through the public fund and its branches.
Recommandations: The effectiveness of the measures is regularly evaluated as part of the public fund's annual report. The co-financing of cultural events and the activities of cultural associations is one of the most important mechanisms for maintaining and strengthening the amateur cultural network throughout Slovenia and for networking with Slovenian associations operating abroad. The annual report also shows that amateur culture - especially choirs, folklore and theatre activities - operates successfully, that the public fund, through its mechanisms, ensures equal conditions for all amateur culture creators and at the same time tries to take into account the specifics of the place and time. This is made possible both by territorial access through the branches and by a uniform working system and guidelines established by the professional programme service. All this contributes to the strengthening, quality, diversity and development of amateur culture in Slovenia.

Title EN: Support for books and publishing (The Slovenian Book Agency)
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture
SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Cultural and creative sectors
Agency Implementation: Javna agencija za knjigo RS (Slovenian Book Agency)
Main Feature: The basic task of the Slovenian Book Agency is to find system solutions for long-term and stable support of the Slovenian publishing industry, especially for the promotion of original creativity and the preservation of the Slovenian language and terminology in translated works. One of the priority tasks of the public agency is also to promote reading culture and strengthen the role of the creative, literate Slovenian language, especially in the form of support for the promotion of reading and the purchase of books at the national level, as well as support for the improvement of the bookselling network, which should ensure the availability of books throughout the Slovenian cultural space. To achieve these goals, the public agency conducts public tenders every year. At the end of 2023, the agency announced three four-year program calls for the period 2024-2027 (book programs, international cooperation programs, literary events and reading culture programs). In 2023, all four-year programs from the 2020-2023 period and the first year of the three-year call for journals 2023-2025 were implemented. In 2023, co-financing was also implemented as part of a three-year call to support ambitious multi-annual projects for the period 2022-2024. Already in 2016, the agency launched two-year calls for projects, the fourth two-year call for projects took place in 2022-2023, in the areas of co-financing projects in the fields of book publishing, international cooperation, literary events and reading culture (two-year contracts for the period 2022-2023 ). In 2023, the agency also carried out the second year of a two-year call for proposals for the co-financing of bookshops for the period 2022-2023 (two-year contracts). A special call to support online media in the field of literature was also launched in 2023. With four-, three- and two-year co-funding periods, the agency created the conditions for longer-term planning of cultural programs and projects and more stable operations that allow the development of programs and projects of book and magazine publishers, festival organizers, actors in the field of reading culture and in the field of international cooperation for the next two, three or four years. It is also worth mentioning the annual public call for the selection of cultural projects in the field of translations into foreign languages, which aims to promote the translation of the first edition of high-quality and recognized Slovenian works into foreign languages, authors and their works at home and abroad, as well as support for translators from Slovenian into foreign languages. Also important is the public call through which the agency finances the cultural project "Growing up with a book", which encourages young people to read quality Slovenian fiction and humanistic and popular science works for young people and to visit public libraries. The project also promotes awareness of top Slovenian authors in the field of fiction and humanistic and popular science works for young people and motivates publishers to include more contemporary Slovenian titles for young people in their publishing programs. At the same time, other public calls should also be emphasized, including certainly the public call for the selection of recipients of scholarships for creativity and the public call for the awarding of working scholarships to literary critics, writers and translators from Slovene into foreign languages.
Results: The Slovenian Book Agency aims to support the publication of high-quality books and magazines and projects in the field of fiction and the humanities, to create conditions for the creativity of authors and to ensure a high level of accessibility to high-quality books and magazines. In addition, the agency also aims to develop electronic publishing, i.e. the availability of electronic books and audio books as well as online media in the narrower field of literature and literary criticism. Such support is particularly important in countries with a limited number of speakers and a limited number of buyers of book products, which is certainly the case in Slovenia with its two million inhabitants. State support enables stable publishing activity, which is essential for the publication of Slovenian books, magazines and other publications in the Slovenian language. Significant results are also achieved in the area of reading culture development, where the agency contributes with its public calls mechanisms to strengthen the development of reading culture among various target groups, create lifelong reading habits and make quality and high-profile literary events in the field of fiction and the humanities easily accessible, promoting Slovenian authors and creativity in the field of fiction and the humanities.
Recommandations: The evaluation is carried out regularly, annually, as well as over a longer period when strategic documents are adopted in the field of books. In addition, the agency also funds a longitudinal study, Books and Readers, which looks at reading culture and book buying and suggests measures to improve the situation of books and reading culture. Co-financing in the book sector is essential for maintaining the stability of the Slovenian publishing industry, but also for its development. It enables publishers to publish quality titles that may be less marketable or whose costs would be so high without financial support that the books would be inaccessible to a wider readership.

Title EN: Support for diaspora artists
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture
SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Cultural and creative sectors
Agency Implementation: Office of the High Commissioner for Diaspora Affairs of the Republic of Armenia,  Ministry of Education, Science, Culture and Sport
Main Feature: The main feature of implementation of the policy is the preservation of the Armenian identity; identification of the potential of the Diaspora and use of that potential in the processes in Armenia; preparation of community figures; implementation of cultural programmes in Armenia and the Diaspora; training courses and presentation of the activities of Armenian artists under the influence of different cultural environments. The following events have been held in order to achieve the aforementioned goals:  -	“iGorts” program Since 2020, the Office of the High Commisioner for Diaspora Affairs has been implementing the “iGorts” program, the purpose of which is to involve professionals with a master’s degree from top universities in the world for one year to work in various bodies of the state administration system of the Republic of Armenia and other government structures. During this period, more than 200 people from 30 countries have participated in the program. There are nine iGorts fellows working in cultural institutions. -	“Step Toward Home” program The educational program “Step toward Home” has been held since 2008 for Armenian boys and girls from Diaspora aged 13 to 18 years. During this period, 1622 Armenians from the Diaspora from 25 countries have participated in the program. Within the framework of the program, singing, dancing, embroidery lessons, meeting with cultural figures, and visits to various cultural institutions in Armenia are organized for participants.  -	“Training for Diaspora Armenian Youth Leaders” program The program “Retraining of Youth Leaders of the Diaspora” has been since 2021. The aim is to retrain youth from the Armenian Diaspora active in their communities between the ages of 20 and 35, within which participants have the opportunity to meet with representatives of formal and non-formal education, get acquainted with their programs, and spread information in their communities. During this period, about 60 youth from 36 countries have participated in the program. -	“Mapping the Professional Potential of the Diaspora” program The program “Mapping the Professional Potential of the Diaspora” also collects data from famous figures and cultural groups in the cultural sphere.  During this period have been continued the program “Training Course for National Dance Instructors and Choirmasters”.  In 2023, as part of the 120th anniversary of Aram Khachatryan, concert programs of the Aram Khachaturian Trio, state orchestras of Armenia, ballet performances, many exhibitions and more were organized in a number of countries (Argentina, Urugway, USA, Italy, Greece, France, Germany, China, Belgium, Russia, Kazakhstan, etc).  Diaspora dance groups, performing musicians, composers, conductors, other artists performed in Armenia. -		“Hayahavaq” project  Artists of Armenian origin perform in Armenia within the framework of the “Hayahavaq” project of the National Chamber Music Center realized and supported by the Ministry of Education and Culture of the Republic of Armenia. As part of the project, in 2020-2023, conductors Misak Baghputaryan (Syria), Nurhan Arman (Canada), Luc Baghdasaryan (Switzerland), Karo Avesyan (Lebanon) and Petros Shetilyan (USA), Hmayak Durgaryan (Spain), Ruben Ghazaryan (Germany), Hayk Davtyan (France) performed in Yerevan. In 2022, with the joint concert programs have been performed tenor and conductor Sipan Olah (Great Britain), Hakob Jake Muratyan, (Great Britain), composer David Halajyan (Switzerland), bariton Adam Baro and soprano Anna Kasyan (France). Theater and dance performances are created in cooperation with Armenian theater directors, who lives in Diaspora. In particular, as a result of cooperation with Sate Artre Company, new performances were staged in the state theaters of Vanadzor, Gyumri, and Goris. The dance performance dedicated to the 100th anniversary of Sergey Parajanov was staged with one of the state dance groups. It is planned to prepare a performance dedicated to Misak Manushyan.
Results: Tangible results have been recorded and particularly concern the professional training courses for cultural figures, heads and members of cultural groups of the Diaspora in Armenia and the Diaspora; awareness-raising of their activities in the homeland; support provided to educational and cultural institutions; revitalisation of cultural life in communities of the Diaspora and the operation of informational and cognitive websites presenting various sectors of Armenian culture.
Recommandations: Presenting themselves alongside the best artists and field representatives of the world on reputable international platforms gives the representatives of the Armenian Diaspora the opportunity to present the traditions of not only Armenian culture, but also the cultures of their respective countries of residence, bringing the best practices to not only Armenia, but also their respective places of residence. Over the years, they have presented Armenian culture at international biennials and musical competitions, and initiated the implementation of joint theater and dance performances with other countries, with the participation of artists and theater and concert organizations of Armenia.

Likewise, with the sustained presence of Colombian music agents over the last 10 years at Womex, they have benefited from artist tours, copyright sales, co-productions, co-creations, artistic residencies, and international businesses. Title EN: Support for the artistic community in Mozambique 2021-2023

Main Feature: Within its programming, the Estúdios Vitor Córdon—a creative platform under OPART, dedicated to supporting the independent artistic community—prioritizes proximity, intercultural dialogue, and artistic versatility. It serves as a space for practice, research, experimentation, creation, and thought, promoting diverse perspectives and fostering peer communication.  In collaboration with the Portuguese Cultural Center in Maputo, Estúdios Vitor Córdon (EVC) have developed initiatives aimed at internationalizing artists from Portuguese-speaking African countries. This programming began in 2021 and continued through the end of 2023.  Itinerários Project (2021/2023): This initiative incentivizes artistic creation, specifically targeting Mozambican creators in dance. The project aims to establish a network between Mozambique, Portugal, and other European partners to promote internationalization. The second edition included residencies in Barcelona and Lisbon, with public presentations of outcomes in each residency location, including Maputo during the Dance Week (2022) and Kinani Festival (2021 and 2023). The program repeated in 2023 following the same format.  Uma Coleção Para Amanhã | 2nd Edition, 2022: A monthly conversation program streamed on EVC's YouTube channel, Camões delegation in Maputo, and other associated institutions across Portuguese-speaking African countries. The program featured 10 artists and promoters in dance, addressing essential topics for facilitating movement and exchange of people and works between Mozambique and Europe.  Training, 2022: A workshop in Maputo with Portuguese choreographer Victor Hugo Pontes, involving an intensive week of work preparing for a new creation commissioned for 2023.  Creation, 2023: Production of a dance performance choreographed by Victor Hugo Pontes, featuring dancers from Mozambique and Portugal. The show premiered in 2023 at the Teatro Nacional de São João in Porto, followed by tours in Portugal and Maputo (2023/24) as part of the Kinani Festival 2023.  These initiatives underline EVC's commitment to enhancing artistic exchange, collaboration, and cultural development between Mozambique, Portugal, and the broader European and Lusophone African contexts.
Results: The initiatives within the three-year programming cycle are designed in an evolutionary and interconnected manner, enhancing collaboration and achieving their goals progressively. The purpose is to develop a programming framework that extends beyond this temporal period, fostering sustained growth and continued achievement of objectives.
Financial Ressources: Without information

Main Feature: The Ministry of Culture has published an annual call for proposals for the co-financing of media content programmes from 2020 to 2023 to support the media in the production and dissemination of programmes relevant to the public interest in the media sector. With the selection of projects, the Ministry aims to ensure the exercise of the right to public information and the right to information and to contribute to media pluralism and diversity or the diversity of programme content. Supporting a variety of media or programmes of special interest (local, regional, student and non-profit radio and television programmes) ensures a greater proportion of local programming and the provision of high-quality media content of public interest that is not covered by the national media but is a valuable source of information for the local population. This ensures access to information and the right to information for all, regardless of where they live. Programmes of special interest are also funded for various ethnic communities (including two indigenous communities - Italians and Hungarians, but also Roma and members of the nations of the former Yugoslavia) and for Slovenes living in neighbouring countries.
Results: Among other things, the Ministry of Culture provided funding for informative media programmes that deal with the problems of ethnic communities, inform about the situation of the communities or report on current events in the life of the community. As part of the regular annual public call for proposals for the co-financing of media programmes, the following projects, among others, received financial support: The Radio Student Institute provides regular information on individuals and organisations from both the former Yugoslavia and Slovenia as part of the Urban Student Media and Education Platform project, and also acts as a bridge between cultural, political, scientific and other developments in Slovenia and the former Yugoslavia. Title EN: Supporting production, distribution and access to diverse content for social minorities
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture
SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Media diversity
Agency Implementation: RTV Slovenija
Main Feature: The Slovenian Radio and Television Act requires RTV Slovenia to create, produce, archive and broadcast the following programs, among others - a radio and television program for the autochthonous Italian and Hungarian ethnic groups and a radio and television program for the Roma ethnic group; - radio and television programs for Slovenian national minorities in neighboring countries and for Slovenian emigrants abroad. In addition, RTV Slovenia is legally obliged to provide services to other social minorities, such as - providing quality in-house productions for children, youth and the elderly, - paying special attention to people with disabilities and appropriate content, - paying special attention to the problems and needs of children, families and groups of people with disabilities who, due to their special circumstances, are more sensitive to social events, - pays special attention to the situation and activities of registered religious communities, - ensures the production and broadcasting of Slovenian audiovisual works and audiovisual works by independent producers. With regard to the care for minorities, the law provides for the activity of special program committees at RTV Slovenia: - Program Committee for the Italian Nationality Program, - Program committee for the program of Hungarian nationality, - Program Committee for the Issue of Program Content for People with Disabilities. National minorities and people with disabilities have their own representatives in the above-mentioned committees. The committees discuss the implementation of the program concept with regard to content concerning their area, comments and suggestions from viewers or listeners, and take initiatives with the RTV authorities to solve problems in their respective areas. The law also obliges RTV Slovenia to provide program content for the blind and visually impaired, as well as the deaf and deaf-blind, using adapted technology. For this purpose, viewers are provided with various technologies - audio description, captioning, sign language and automatic captioning. The programs equipped with these technologies are also accessible to viewers through the web portal https://www.rtvslo.si/dostopno/. In addition, RTV Slovenia has set up a news portal www.rtvslo.si/enostavno, which offers news in an easy-to-read format
Results: The annual reports of RTV Slovenia (https://www.rtvslo.si/rtv/kdo-smo/zakoni-predpisi-in-dokumenti/letni-nacrti-in-porocila/471839) show that an integral part of the daily programming in the areas of news, children and youth, sport, education and film is content or entire programs that deal with topics and issues of social minorities, are written in minority languages or provide various access services.

Main Feature: Following the public health emergency that occurred in Chile and the world, the State of Chile, facing repercussions of that the pandemic on the cultural sector, decides to present a benefit to cultural workers as part of the Plan Chile Apoya.   Following a participatory process with diverse trade organisations from the arts sector, it was decided that the benefit would be presented to those who are in the 40% to 80% range of the Registro Social de Hogares (Chilean Social Registry of Households), compliying first with a gender and then a territorial approach. Es decir, el aporte en primer término es para jefas de hogares con hijos, hijas o personas dependientes.  This benefit aided, with up to 450 thousand Chilean peasos (USD 487.50), cultural workers whose income was affected by the public health emergency, which meant a direct payment of $ 14,780 million (USD 15,991,909) destined towards the recovery of the Chilean arts and culture sector. For the presentation of the benefit, gender, parenthood, descentralisation and vulnerability criteria were defined.   Therefore, the prioritised recipients of the benefit were: (a) members of female-headed households, single-parent and with dependants, (b) members of male-headed households, single-parent and with dependants, c) members of female-headed households (non single-parent) with dependants, c) members of male-headed households (non single-parent) with dependants.   In case of two or more applicants that fulfil the same criteria to access the benefit, the benefit was prioritised for the woman applicant, and in the case of persons of the same sex, to the older person within the applicants. Afterwards, with the remaining resources, a second application round opened, maintaining  the same priority and priority criteria.   Finally, in line with the monitoring framework of the 2005 Convention, this benefit reports on the indicator on "policies and measures that support the outward and inward mobility of dynamic communication and creative sectors".
Results: During 2022, the Ministry of Cultures, Arts and Heritage designed and carried out the presentation of the benefit to cultural workers. The Decree N° 27 of 2022 defined the mechanisms for application and presentation of the benefit.   This benefit, with the sole sum of 450 thousand pesos (approx. USD 515) to 32,841 beneficiaries, was presented following the implementation of two application rounds: the first during May and June, and the second during October and November.   In order to define the benefit selection criteria, the Ministry of Labor, together with the Social Policy Division of the Undersecretariat of Social Evaluation, part of the Ministry of Social Development and Family Ministry, worked on aspects that considered a gender, caregiving and territorial approach.   Of the all the beneficiaries, 36% correspond to the Metropolitan Region, while the rest is distributed in the rest of the country's regions, and 24.9% corresponds to the performing arts. The sub-sectors with the highest percentage of beneficiaries were crafts (23.7%) and music (21.6%). Regarding the gender distribution, 16,377 people declared being of female gender, 14,723 male gender, 590 non-binary gender and 101 transgender.   The remaining universe was distributed between the categories "I do not know", "others" and "rather not answer".

Title EN: Survey on Media Literacy Level in Lithuania
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture
SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Cultural and creative sectors
Agency Implementation: Ministry of Culture of the Republic of Lithuania
Main Feature: In 2017 the Ministry of Culture started measuring the media literacy level of the population. The aim of this survey was to identify and assess the ability of the Lithuanian population to use the media, to critically evaluate the information presented in the media and their communication skills. A separate part of the questionnaire was designed to investigate how the population perceives the Lithuanian media, and the information disseminated in them. A second periodic survey was conducted in 2021, and the results are published and can be compared with the 2017 data.
Results: The second survey showed that the use of information and communication tools by the Lithuanian population over four years has increased, with the Internet becoming more important than television, and social networks almost on a par with news portals. During this period, trust in all media channels has decreased and the population has become much more sensitive to inaccuracies or misinformation.  The survey revealed that the COVID-19 pandemic and the associated constraints have given impetus to increased use of online media, as well as to an increase in the consumption of digital communication and services.  In everyday life, the Internet is used in almost every area, from leisure activities to the use of services provided by public authorities, which has also increased in the last period. The Lithuanian population has a good grasp of the basic technical principles of safe online behaviour: most of the Internet users have an anti-virus programme installed, which is the most popular form of protection, use their email address responsibly, and take some additional security precautions when visiting new websites. Moreover, the survey showed that the number of Lithuanians who understand that online content can lead to legal liability has increased significantly.  Despite the growing importance of the Internet, traditional media, television and radio are still seen as important sources of information, especially by senior people.  When consuming the media, the population is quite critical of the information it receives, with a higher proportion of participants noting differences in the presentation of facts in different sources of information. It is likely that recent educational activities have strengthened media consumers' critical evaluation skills. Fake news is increasingly being highlighted by the survey participants, and the media is perceived by a larger part as a tool for influence.  The overall level of media literacy of the Lithuanian population was predicted to increase every three years since the 2017 survey (then at 37.9%), as follows: 39% in 2020 and 41.3% in 2023. However, the survey conducted in 2020 exceeded this prediction and revealed a much more positive change – 48.7%.   The third periodic survey is planned for 2024.
Financial Ressources: Approx. USD 23 428
Recommandations: The surveys are a useful tool to see changes and trends in media. The results are used for shaping policy in the field of media.

Title EN: SWISS CULTURE SUPPORT FUND
Goal: Integrate Culture In Sustainable Development Frameworks
SDG: SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: National sustainable development policies and plans
Agency Implementation: SOLIDAR SUIZA BOLIVIA  EMAIL: solidar@solidar-suiza.org.bo PHONE: 2-2114190
Main Feature: The FSAC project, which ran from 2014 to 2023 (in 3 phases), was characterized by: -	Promote the approach of culture linked to development: assuming culture as an instrument of social transformation. In this sense, participatory spaces for reflection and dialogue were generated based on art, connected with human rights and central issues of quality of life (example: the fight against violence against women). -	Promote cultural democratization and intercultural dialogue: cultural democratization not only means the coverage and support of cultural projects throughout the country, but also to bridge the social gaps that exist between rural and urban areas. That is why, considering that support for cultural actions is concentrated mainly in urban areas, priority was given in the calls for proposals from rural and peri-urban areas, to provide opportunities for cultural initiatives that do not have the support of either the State or the private sector. -	Contribute to the debate on the institutionality of cultural public policies: Within the framework of sustainability, it was considered important to strengthen the processes of building public policies in favor of culture (which were beginning to be built in Bolivia since 2018), spaces in which they initially invited people to share the experience of the Swiss Fund for Support to Culture as an inspiring practice. -	Contribute to the capacity building of artists and cultural managers: The artists and cultural managers responsible for cultural projects and other invited artists and managers participated in capacity building spaces, thus contributing to better project management and the exchange of experiences. -	Generate intra and intercultural dialogues, through artistic-cultural projects by artists and/or cultural groups, reinforcing democratic values and their resilient attitude, to strengthen the construction of a culture of peace and social cohesion, in and between rural and peri-urban areas.  For all the work carried out, the FSAC adopted the following approaches: -	Culture - arts as a right: Recognizing culture and the arts as spaces for the exercise of rights, for encounters between diverse people, for transformation and construction of content and behavior, for daily creation; therefore, democratic access to these spaces is understood as a right for all. -	Culture – arts as a space for strengthening cultural identities: There is no society without culture. Collective identity is the sense of belonging of individuals, who throughout their lives internalize cultural representations, norms, values, beliefs and symbols that make them members of a community and generate a feeling of pride and belonging. Language, arts, textiles, monuments and others make up the cultural heritage of a social group, a community, a country. Hence the importance of rescuing cultural heritage to strengthen collective identity (local, regional and national) , culture and enable intercultural dialogue. -	Culture - arts as a process of social cohesion and inclusion: Culture and the arts constitute a factor of cohesion and peacebuilding, to the extent that they are supported by spaces for intra- and intercultural dialogue, plural participation, the promotion of values such as respect and acceptance of others, and co-responsibility in the construction of new social fabrics. -	Culture - arts as a space to broaden and deepen democratic culture: Culture and the arts promote responsible participation, with rights and responsibilities. A democratic culture is based on the exercise of citizenship, on diverse, plural participation, conscious of its rights and responsibilities. This is the starting point for any conflict management process. -	Culture - arts as a space to improve prospects: Culture and the arts create spaces to redraw, influence and guide towards the opening of new visions of the future - social and individual -, particularly for young people.
Results: During the last phase (2020-2023) of the Swiss Fund for Support to Culture (FSAC), three strategic lines of action were implemented through competitive funds: the Fund for Support to the Democratization of Culture and the Arts (FADCA), the Fund for Support to Intercultural Dialogue (FADI) and the Fund for Cultural Heritage Rescue Initiatives. These funds generated a positive impact in the cultural sphere of Bolivia.  The FSAC directly involved more than 12,000 people, while the indirect reach exceeded 88,000 people. The initiative supported the work of 250 artists and representatives of cultural groups (63% women and 37% men) who promoted spaces for intra- and intercultural dialogue, especially in rural and peri-urban areas, contributing to democratic values and a resilient attitude in their communities.  In total, FSAC supported 72 initiatives, with a priority on the inclusion of rural and peri-urban areas. Of these projects, 60% addressed themes such as democratic values, resilience, culture of peace, intercultural dialogue and social cohesion, thus strengthening the social and cultural fabric. In addition, 60% of the projects promoted gender equity and equality, including women's rights and questioning power relations in their content and approach.  In terms of sustainability, 46% of the projects have operational strategies for their continuity, and 42% have obtained state or private support that favors their long-term sustainability. Likewise, 46% of the initiatives adopted good practices in cultural impact and cultural business models, contributing to their viability and durability over time.  The FSAC has been a key driver in democratising culture and strengthening intercultural dialogue in Bolivia, promoting access to arts and culture in underprivileged communities and ensuring that supported projects can continue to generate impact.

The circuses group gives daily practices for their members which enable the artiste’s competent and healthy citizens physically and psychologically.  Since the last 20 years, the international demand for circus art in Ethiopia has been increasing, and the circus groups have realized this demand and are providing international standard circus training for their 7,750 members, females 3,274, and males 4,486. The circus artists signed contracts with international circus festival organizers, circus companies, ship entertainment agencies, and theater houses and presented their works. Their works have been performed at 15 international festivals, 30 international circus companies, 6 entertainment cruise ships, and more than 20 theater houses in Africa, Europe, North America, Australia, Asia, America, and the Caribbean Island counties. Main Feature: TELARTES is a platform for the articulation of the Bolivian cultural sector, created in 2012 with the aim of strengthening the dispersed scenario through the development of capacities for articulation, collaboration, exchange and, fundamentally, influence on public policy. It is characterized by being an open, inclusive and independent movement to contribute socially to Living Well through cultures and the arts, to support the strengthening of the cultural sector at all its levels and expressions, cultural rights, participatory democracy and social cohesion; developing networking tools (articulation and collaboration) in permanent dialogue with the State as well as with cultural actors of civil society and in alliance with similar processes on the continent and globally. Its actions are developed along four axes: Incidence, Cultural Circulation, Training-Research and Sustainability; under an organic articulation matrix that is periodically renewed, deploying local responsibilities and action axes. Its work was mainly carried out by a coordination team at the head of the management group, with the operational work of a technical coordination. From an initial group of 7 organizations, in its second year of implementation (2013) it was able to form a national work team of 20 members with the capacity to convene more than 200 cultural organizations and activists from the country, in a Network Culture Meeting that year. This fact allowed the development of a common agenda with the Ministry of Culture and Tourism, in which the following topics are established: Cultural Legislation, Citizen Participation, Cultural Circulation, Satellite Account, Cultural Communication, Network Culture and Community Living Culture. In this task, TELARTES and the Ministry of Culture and Tourism, focusing primarily on legislative issues, have agreed on the Draft Framework Law on Cultures, validated at the first Congress convened by civil society called “Culturas en movimiento" (Cultures in Motion) held in October 2015 and presented to the Plurinational Legislative Assembly (Congress of the country). At the same time, other legislative proposals were worked on, such as the one on the Artist and the one on Cultural Spaces; contributing in turn to the promotion of the Bolivian Film and Audiovisual Law, already proposed by the organized film and audiovisual sector of Bolivia, the one on Cultural Spaces, and the initiatives of the Law of the Artist were promoted. At the municipal level, it worked actively throughout the process, until its promulgation, with the Municipal Autonomous Law of Cultures of La Paz, Bolivia. TELARTES, through its other components, developed communication tools that include intensive work through social networks, the use of social technology tools, as well as training workshops and the development of communication teams. Additionally, it has worked in the areas of Collaborative Economy and Cultural Circulation, developing the management of Festivales en Red, Grito Rock, Hospeda Cultura and other initiatives linked to the platforms of Cultura de Red and Cultura Viva Comunitaria (this one, until a first phase). In research, matrices have been developed to survey significant cultural experiences, the action of recording artists and mapping cultural spaces has been deployed. It has developed training proposals in different areas: impact of cultural policies, cultural management, cultural articulation, cultural promotion and diversity, online communication and digital culture, creative economy, among others. The project developed mainly actions linked to legislative support: a large part of its energy was focused on promoting the Framework Law on Cultures, whose work was promoted by the Ministry of Culture and Tourism, being the first time that the ministry socialized a legislative project agreed upon in its drafting with civil society bodies. It also deployed actions linked to strengthening cultural circulation, communication development and the organization of the network. In 2016, because of the II Congress “Cultures in Motion”, essential postulates were established for the construction of legislative frameworks. Following the inability to obtain refinancing at the beginning of 2017, the impetus for its management was extended through voluntary action, developing local advocacy actions in the cities of La Paz, Sucre and Cochabamba, where actions were mainly promoted to influence cultural policies and legislative regulations. With a particular effort by members of the coordinating team, its drive was deployed until the end of 2019, holding a weekly opinion column in the newspaper Opinión (Cochabamba, national circulation), and extending its coordination, communication and representation activities, until today, with an increasingly diminished participation and the maintenance of the coordination of a core of trust. Social events, both the transition of government combined with the confinement due to the COVID-19 pandemic, have been catalysts for the weakening of the network's organization.
Results: -	During its administration has deployed the vanguard in open and free communication mechanisms, forms and devices, developing dissemination and training actions in collaborative applications and training in digital and network communication regarding the safeguarding of alternative forms of intellectual property protection. It has also had a predominant media presence and coverage; between 2017 and 2019 has published a weekly opinion column in the national circulation newspaper Opinión. -	It has held two congresses of national character and presence to discuss issues related to cultural management in the country, called "Cultures in Movement", legitimate and representative of the sector, in both it has developed a framework of specific proposals for the sector. -	Thanks to its face-to-face meetings and its articulation with national and international network platforms, it has strengthened the circulation and development of specific cultural and artistic management platforms: Danzénica, Festival Abril en Tarija, Grito Rock, Festivales en red, Circula Cultura, Hospeda Cultura, Bolivia Lab, among others. -	It has been the main platform for legislative promotion and influence on cultural rights in its actions: -	Drafting and joint review with the Ministry of Culture and Tourism of the Framework Law on Cultures, which was disseminated by government bodies and discussed at the two national congresses “Cultures in Motion” (2016 and 2017). -	Support for the Film Law, enacted at the national level. -	Development of legislative proposals for the Law on Cultural Spaces and the Law on Artists, at the national level. -	Coordination and support in the proposal and promulgation of laws and/or legislative regulations at the municipal level in the municipalities of La Paz, Oruro, Sucre and Cochabamba. -	Development of "El Espaciario": Mapping of non-state cultural spaces, developing in 2016, a registry of 131 spaces in 33 cities of the country, from all its departments. Obtaining a publication that collects the information of each of the spaces, including a cataloging and a survey of the plans of its main rooms. -	It has promoted the articulation of festivals at a national level , achieving two “Festivals in Network” meetings bringing together cultural managers and producers from Bolivia. -	Has developed mechanisms for collecting information and systematizing cultural experiences . -	It has fostered open and inclusive training spaces on the topics of its organization: cultural management, sustainability-creative economy, open communication, cultural circulation, incidence and others.

Title EN: Tandem Diversité
Goal: Integrate Culture In Sustainable Development Frameworks
SDG: SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: National sustainable development policies and plans
Cultural Domain: Design,Performing Arts,Media Arts,Cinema and Audiovisual Arts,Music,Publishing,Visual Arts
Agency Implementation: Pro Helvetia
Main Feature: Avec le programme « Tandem Diversité », la fondation Pro Helvetia soutient depuis 2022 des institutions culturelles dans leur processus interne en faveur de la promotion de la diversité. Les institutions sélectionnées participent à un atelier de deux jours où elles apprennent les bases du développement organisationnel axé sur la diversité et réfléchissent à leur organisation. Elles peuvent demander ensuite un soutien financier pour lancer et mettre en œuvre un processus de diversité à long terme avec des coaches spécialisées et des coachs spécialisés dans différents aspects de la diversité (genre, migration, orientation sexuelle, handicap etc.).
Results: En 2022, 12 institutions issues de disciplines artistiques diverses (musées, musique, théâtre, danse) ont participé à l’atelier de deux jours. Sept d’entre elles ont ensuite reçu un soutien financier pour un accompagnement individualisé de la mise en œuvre de leur processus de diversité. En 2023, ce sont 16 institutions culturelles qui ont participé à l’atelier de 2 jours. L’offre rencontre un écho très positif auprès des institutions culturelles qui sont de plus en plus sensibilisées à l’importance de la promotion de la diversité.
Financial Ressources: 489 418 USD pour les montants financiers alloués et 141 412 USD pour l’organisation des ateliers (sans compter les ressources humaines de Pro Helvetia)
Recommandations: L'évaluation qualitative a permis de formuler les conclusions suivantes :  1. L'atelier, qui est au cœur de l'appel d'offres, permet la mise en réseau et donne à toutes les organisations participantes les connaissances de bases communes et l’impulsion pour développer des processus de diversité.  2. Le développement et l'intégration de critères de qualité pour les processus de diversité sont particulièrement importants pour l'évaluation des processus qui bénéficient d’un soutien.  3. La vision à long terme du processus doit être prise en compte dans la conception du soutien des processus et dans leurs suivis. Cela signifie que, même après un processus de diversité, des ressources doivent être mises à disposition pour un soutien de longue durée (par exemple avec un poste d'agente ou d’agent de la diversité et/ou un budget pour la diversité).  4. La mise en réseau des organisations engagées dans un processus de diversité est essentielle. À l'avenir, le réseau continuera à se développer et, par conséquent, le besoin d'échange aussi. Cette mise en réseau peut aussi se faire à bas seuil, par exemple par des formats en ligne ou sous forme de « table ronde ». Il est important que les organisations puissent échanger dans un cadre confidentiel sur des sujets sensibles tels que la politique du personnel.  5. La coordination entre les organismes de financement est cruciale pour l'impact à long terme des processus. À plus long terme, un changement structurel profond n'est possible que si davantage de ressources peuvent être engagées ou si des mandats politiques clairs sont donnés, si, par exemple, la diversité est prise en compte dans les accords de prestations entre les organisations culturelles, les villes et les cantons, et si elle est encouragée en conséquence.

Main Feature: Tax incentive for Orange Economy companies (technological value-added industries and creative activities), where the income that came from their corporate purpose was exempt for a period of seven or five years, depending on the date on which they applied. (Law 2010 of 2019, art. 91, with some modifications raised in articles 44 and partially 65 of Law 2155 of 2021.) This program was implemented from 2020 to 2022.                  It was aimed at legal entities (companies) incorporated before June 30, 2022, which were taxpayers of income tax and complementary to the ordinary regime (Responsibility 05- Income tax and complementary. Ordinary regime expressed in the RUT, in Sanish), with a postal address within Colombian territory and whose corporate purpose was exclusively the development of technological value-added industries and/or creative activities.                  The requirements to access this incentive were:                  1. Be a legal entity and begin the development of activities before June 30, 2022.                  2. The corporate purpose must be exclusive to the development of technological value-added industries and/or creative activities and all economic activities registered by the RUT and the Single Business Registry RUES, in Spanishm must be framed within 27 economic activities (International Uniform Industrial Classification of all economic activities Revision 4 adapted for Colombia ISIC Rev. 4 A.C. for codes 3210, 5811, 5820, 5911, 5912, 5913, 5914, 5920, 6010, 6020, 6201,6202, 7111, 7112, 7220, 7410, 7420, 9001, 9002, 9003, 9004, 9005, 9006, 9007, 9008, 9101, 9102. For more information: https://www.dane.gov.co/files/sen/nomenclatura/ciiu/CIIU_Rev_4_AC2020.pdf           and activities related to cultural tourism, as well as activities related to sports, recreation, and leisure.                   3. The gross annual income could not be greater than 80,000 UVT, that is, income with a cut-off date of December 31 of the year immediately prior to the presentation of the project (for companies created in 2021 and previous years) or with a cut-off date of the previous month of presentation of the project (for companies created in 2022) must be less than COP$3,040,320,000 (COP$38,004 = 1 UVT in 2022). Except for the case of companies whose main economic activity was framed in the ISIC code 5911, whose annual gross income could be greater than 80,000 UVT.                   4. They should generate new jobs directly related to technological value-added industries and creative activities. These had to be permanent, taking into account the amount of gross annual income. It should be noted that for those companies whose exclusive corporate purpose corresponded to activities framed within the Classification of Economic Activities ISIC 5911, they had to prove the direct hiring through an employment contract and during the time that production lasted, of the number of employees according to the table that was about article 235-2. When the gross tax revenue value exceeded eighty thousand (80,000) tax value units (UVT), for every twenty thousand (20,000) tax value units (UVT) of additional gross tax revenue they had to hire one (1) additional employee.                  Regulations: On December 27, 2019, Law 2010 of 2019 (Economic Growth Law) is issued, whose article 91 modifies article 235-2 of the Tax Statute, regulated under Decree 286 of February 26, 2020, modified by Decree 1843 of December 24, 2021, after the approval of Law 2155 of 2021 (Social Investment Law) by the Colombian government. Finally repealed by article 96 of Law 2277 of 2022."
Results: In total, 1,482 companies in the Cultural and Creative sector benefited.

Culture plans (regional or local, depending on the case) are a public planning tool, built in a participatory manner, that allows designing the cultural development strategy of a territory. Main Feature: Objective: For industry stakeholders to have access to current research to support strategic, informed decisions about the production, marketing and distribution of their content, as well as building talent capacity, and implementing best industry practices.    Business Intelligence Funding: Telefilm conducts, finances and communicates market intelligence, data and research for the industry, policy makers, and general public. By providing access to these insights, they help to address gaps and challenges, and bring forth best practices.   Telefilm commissions research, as well as finances industry-partner research, on key issues in the AV industry ecosystem, that include, but is not limited to audience engagement challenges; insights on equity, diversity and inclusion and cultural policy issues; sustainability and environmental issues.   	Industry Partners apply for research financing on relevant issues. Telefilm can be either the sole funder, or one of a combination of funders to support the research mandate presented by the partner. 	Telefilm can and does commission industry research from recognized research experts.  Promotion and Sharing of Research:  	Most research, if standards met, is posted on the website. 	Research is promoted on social platforms, and via event activations in partnership with the industry (e.g. panels at Festivals).  Although Business Intelligence is not specifically targeted to the young, recent research has focused on young Canadians: e.g. The Power of Canadian Film: Youth Film Consumption and Engagement.
Results: There are no specific measurable outcomes to share at this time. Telefilm has just started track downloads, attendance at panels, and traction on social media.
Financial Ressources: The annual allocation varies from USD 110,000 - USD 150,000.
Recommandations: Based on feedback from the industry via consultations/one-on-one meetings, conferences, panels, workshops, industry surveys, and other - quality research is valued and helps inform decision-making, and industry conversations on collective issues and challenges.   Examples of Issues and Challenges:  -	Telefilm’s Industry Surveys on Sustainability (2 iterations completed) have highlighted the industry’s needs on this priority (e.g. they want more training and education) andindicated the perceived obstacles for sustainable production (i.e. need for additional resources). The report also highlights current sustainable production practices. -	Challenges and opportunities for audience engagement with feature film: Telefilm commissioned an extensive survey (2000+) called Canadian Movie-Consumption presented at Prime Time 2024. Based on feedback, this has already proved valuable to exhibitors and distributors with plenty of lessons learned which can be applied by independent exhibitors immediately, through better understanding audience types, thinking strategically about how audiences make a decision to see a film, the kinds of films that motivate people to leave the comfort of their home, and more. -	The increasing challenges facing documentary filmmakers in Canada: A multi-partner report was supported that investigated key issues, challenges for the documentary genre “Getting Real 7” which looks at the economic impact of documentary production from 2016-2017 to 2020-2021, as well as trends in production, budgets and financing, and audiences. One of the most referenced research supported is PROFILE, which is a valued source that assesses health of the industry.

Title EN: Telefilm’s new General Admission Festivals Program, Medium to Large Scale Festivals Program, Promotion – Industry Initiatives Stream
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture
SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Cultural and creative sectors
Agency Implementation: Telefilm Canada
Main Feature: In 2023, Telefilm updated their programs aimed at supporting the industry by creating the General Admission Festivals Program, Medium to Large Scale Festivals Program, Promotion – Industry Initiatives Stream to better promote the Diversity of Cultural Expressions across the country.    The Promotion Program Funding provides support for Canadian film festivals that are aimed at the general public under two funding programs (General Admission Festivals Program which provides streamlined funding for small and/or emerging film festivals, and Medium to Large-Scale Festivals Program which finances long-established medium to large-scale festivals) and industry activities that stimulate demand for Canadian content as well as career development opportunities (through the Promotion Program – Industry Initiatives Stream, supporting activities including national award ceremonies, alternative distribution networks, conferences, and training activities).    Specific considerations are included in the evaluation of festivals and activities on their support by ensuring that there is strong representation regionally and from diverse backgrounds involved not only from a presentation or mandate point of view, but also from program design and staffing, as well as ensuring advance sustainable practices and environmental responsibility. These three programs are an evolution from the previous Promotion Program which supported these activities under one umbrella and has allowed for further emphasis of support in the promotion and protection of the diversity of cultural expressions. For example, access to higher levels of funding in the General Admission Festivals Program is reserved for festivals that have an underrepresented mandate or are regionally located. As well, the Medium to Large-Scale Festivals Program includes scoring based on the applicant’s dedication to serving underrepresented voices and accessibility measures.
Results: At the launch of the new programs in 2023, a target of 101 Canadian film festivals and training activities that have a local/regional impact and/or an underrepresented targeted mandate was set. As of January 26, 2024, this target has already been exceeded with a total of 117 Canadian film festivals and training activities supported.
Financial Ressources: Program Funding: USD 5.77 million
Recommandations: While the modernized programs have just recently been introduced, preliminary evaluation of these programs have shown that the added transparency and access has allowed festivals to access Telefilm support and potentially obtain higher levels of support as evaluated to their current operations. In the second year of these programs, Telefilm has been able to bring adjustments to reflect the changing needs of the industry, and to review its impact. Evaluation processes are also very rigid with strict criteria to ensure fairness, while ensuring that regional and underrepresented-mandated festivals are not negatively impacted.

Based on a challenge launched to artists of several languages to musically and performatively think about a specific territory developed five programming moments that implemented new ways of relating to the natural, human and historical heritage of the Island. At the base, a proposed trail is activated with site-specific musical creations, multimedia installations and performative acts. At the end, a cycle of talks and other discussion actions sought to provide a framework for the exchange proposed by the artistic residencies.
Results: Access and support to/for contemporary arts in low-density municipalities through, inter alia: programming of artistic productions, involvement of residents in creative processes and audience development activities. During Terra Incógnita’s lifetime multiple sound trails were created, mapping out the Island of S. Miguel through the lens of contemporary arts and the collaborative artistic work developed in site-specific artistic residencies. Within the project several relationships and forms of cooperation were explored - at local, national, and international levels -, in a variety of ways: through artistic dialogue, institutional cooperation or by attracting new audiences through its interest in technology, art, and nature. The international partnerships established within the scope of the project, contributed, inter alia, to the mobility of a multitude of artists and cultural professionals. The project placed the exchange of knowledge, collaboration, experimentation, and active participation as its key principles, to take thew island as a site for contemporary artistic creation processes, enhancing repertoires and platforms for continuity, visibility, and career expansion in the local cultural ecosystem. Terra Incognita takes place in a digital environment too, inter alias launched a mobile app in which the existing artistic creations/musical trails were compiled, as other paths unveiled over time can be - thus creating a living and mutable archive, inhabited by its user's interactions, and bringing the human closer to the natural, while simultaneously creating a cultural product of touristic value.

Title EN: Territorial equity for communities. Strengthening regional cultural identity programme.
Goal: Promote Human Rights And Fundamental Freedoms
SDG: SDG 5 - Achieve gender equality and empower all women and girls,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels
Area of Monitoring: Artistic freedom
Agency Implementation: Ministry of Cultures, Arts and Heritage – Undersecretariat of Cultures and Arts.
Main Feature: The Strengthening Regional Cultural Identity programme (FICR) has a mission to contribute to the decentralisation of culture and the arts, to territorial equity and to broaden access to artistic and cultural goods and services, especially catering to territories with less opportunities for artistic and cultural participation, geographically isolated, as well as with an emphasis on communes other than Chile's regional capitals.   Its purpose is to broaden access to artistic and cultural goods and services in communes other than Chile's regional capitals, creating opportunities for artistic and cultural participation and to contribute to strengthening the identity of the territories and the communities that live there. For that, a series of cultural initiatives with a regional identity takes place, that come into being through cultural projects, meetings and exchanges, local and regional projects. Regarding this  measure, we highlight the following projects and/or initiatives:  (1) gathering of indigenous practitioners, a space whose goal is to recognise, revitalise, exchange and transmit cultural practices related to crafts and gastronomy par excellence, which is a fundamental part of the identity of the territories and the communities that live in the northern macro-zone of Chile, contributing a valuable testament of who we are.  (2) initiative "Alta Seguridad" ("High Security") residency in a prison complex, an arts residency in the prison complex of the Quillota commune, Valparaíso Region. It consists of theatre work with female inmates and its aim is to address theatrical processes with persons deprived of liberty, with an emphasis on a rights and gender approach.   (3) “Corredorbiobío” - a community of cultural spaces whose goal is to guarantee access to quality cultural properties for the public, by forming a collaborative working community, that gradually involves public infrastructure whose role is based on the right to culture, generating training opportunities that strengthen management and promoting the circulation of regional artistic creation in these spaces.   Finally, in line with the framework of the 2005 Convention, this measure falls within the indicator on "policies and measures that promote and protect  freedoms of creation and expression and participation in cultural life".
Results: Regarding the gathering of indigenous practitioners, during a period of 16 years it has been fostered as a meeting point for diverse indigenous communities (Aymara, Quechua, Licanantay, Diaguita and Coya); for exchange, training, reflection and discussion on wisdom, knowledge, practice and concerns specific to the communities and nations that are part of the northern macro-zone, in order to revitilise, protect, echange and disseminate their living practices.   It is a macro-zonal platform, since it integrates communities from the Arica and Parinacota, Tarapacá, Antofagasta, Atacama and Coquimbo regions. It is a space where diverse working formats converge: more intimate discussion spaces, training and exchange on interest-based or current topics (music, dance, gastronomy, envornmental and political topics); a showcase of expressions and expressive practices and a fair for the sale of ther artisan creations. "Alta seguridad" residency initiative in a prison complex.  This project derives from an initiative created in 1997, developing its methodology with persons deprived of liberty in Valparaíso. Since 2014, approximately 50 persons deprived of liberty participated in these residencies, creating 4 to 5 theatre performances presented to cultural authorities, the Chilean Gendarmerie, fellow prisoners and families. With it, intersectoral   alliances have been established between Culture, Justice and Public Security, resulting in – for example- community intervention projects; workshops promoting reading and writing for women deprived of liberty.   With the passage of time, and with the aim of decentralising this initiative, in 2020 it is transferred to the Centro de Detención Preventiva (CDP) remand  centre in Quillota in order to work with women (cis and diversities) with the aim of including this population in the socio-cultural activities and combat marginalisation and societal stigmatisation they have suffered. In 2021 breastfeeding women are included.   Corredorbiobío, community of Cultural Spaces. Reactivation of in-person programming and activities, artistic and cultural circulation and team-building activities for cultual infrastructure. The project is linked to the Incubadora Corredorbiobío. A working group has been established between Corredorbiobío, GORE (regional government) and FICR (regional identity programme) of the Biobío Regional Ministerial Service of Cultures, which has  enabled a great management capacity and raising regional funding.   Resources have increased exponentially with the aim of incorporating new infrastructure without affecting or reducing the resources they already have. The work of the technical working group has been fostered between Corredorbiobío, regional government (GORE) and the regional identity programme (FICR) of the Biobío Regional Ministerial Service of Cultures. Cultural spaces that are part of Incubadora Corredorbiobío have been incorporated into the project.

Title EN: The 2021-2023 National Strategy for preventing and combating anti-Semitism, xenophobia, radicalization and hate speech
Goal: Integrate Culture In Sustainable Development Frameworks
SDG: SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: National sustainable development policies and plans
Cultural Domain: Design,Performing Arts,Media Arts,Cinema and Audiovisual Arts,Music,Publishing,Visual Arts
Agency Implementation: Ministry of Foreign Affairs
Main Feature: The Strategy is structured around three general goals, 12 specific goals, and 36 key actions, pursuing the prevention of the replication in Romania of the negative developments registered in this respect in other countries, ensuring the instruments necessary to sanction the deeds associated with antisemitism, xenophobia, radicalization, and hate speech, as well as the correlation of the sectoral efforts dedicated to preventing the aforementioned. The main objectives were: - to prevent anti-Semitism and xenophobia; - to combat radicalization (identify and address the root causes of radicalization and implement programs to prevent it); - to counter hate speech: reduce its presence, particularly online, and promote respectful and inclusive discourse; - to promote education and awareness; - to support victims of hate crimes and discrimination. The Ministry of Culture and its subordinate institutions, such as the Administration of the National Cultural Fund, Romanian Film Centre, the National Village Museum "Dimitrie Gusti", the National Museum of the Romanian Peasant, the "George Apostu" Culture Centre, etc., finances cultural projects on the history, language, culture and life of Jews and Roma minorities, which contribute to the achievement of the objectives contained in the National Strategy for preventing and combating anti-Semitism, xenophobia, radicalisation and hate speech for the period 2021-2023 as well as projects concerning the implementation of the Romanian Government Strategy for the inclusion of Romanian citizens belonging to the Roma minority for the period 2022-2027.
Results: The assessment at the end of the implementation cycle shows that most of the actions corresponded to the commitments assumed by the responsible institutions, despite the challenges that arose amid the difficulty of identifying funding sources, allocated resources, or bureaucratic impediments.  From a quantitative perspective, significant progress has been made so that, compared to the 36 key actions included in the Action Plan, the degree of implementation is 78%, with 28 key actions implemented and 8 key actions only partially implemented.  It should also be noted that several actions had immediate effects and concrete outcomes following implementation, nevertheless, most of them will produce visible effects in society in a wider time horizon.  The Government of Romania remains firmly committed to the objectives of combating anti-Semitism, xenophobia, radicalization, and hate speech, preserving the memory of the Holocaust, and supporting education and research about the Holocaust.

Title EN: The Act of 28 May 2021 no. 49 on Collective Management of Copyright, etc.
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture
SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Cultural and creative sectors
Agency Implementation: Norwegian Ministry of Culture and Equality
Main Feature: The Act on Collective Management of Copyright, etc. is based on a proposal (Prop. 53 L (2020-2021)) by the Norwegian Ministry of Culture: https://www.regjeringen.no/no/dokumenter/prop.-53-l-20202021/id2786562/ (in Norwegian). The Act regulates how collective management organizations should handle copyright and related rights on behalf of rightsholders. The purpose of the Act is to safeguard the right of self-determination of holders of copyright and related rights, to promote the functioning of copyright markets and to ensure the responsible, efficient and transparent collective management of copyright and related rights with respect to both right holders and users.  The rules aim to lay down requirements applicable to collective management organizations, in order to ensure a high standard of governance, financial management, transparency and reporting. The Act also imposes requirements regarding accountability in managing royalty payments and members’ right to participate in the decision-making process. Additionally, the Act facilitates multi-territorial licensing of music rights, especially for new online services.   The Act on Collective Management of Copyright, etc. is a transposition of the EU Directive on collective management of copyright and related rights and multi-territorial licensing of rights in musical works for online use in the internal market (2014/26/EU).
Results: The purpose of this Act is to ensure responsible, effective, and transparent collective management of copyright and related rights for both rightsholders and users. It also aims to safeguard rightsholders’ freedom of choice in collective rights management.

Title EN: The Icelandic Film Centre
Goal: Achieve A Balanced Flow Of Cultural Goods And Services And Increase The Mobility Of Artists And Cultural Professionals
SDG: SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 10 - Reduce inequality within and among countries,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Flow of cultural goods and services
Agency Implementation: The Ministry of culture and Business Affairs The Icelandic Film Centre
Main Feature: The Icelandic Film Centre operates in accordance with the Film Act no. 137/2001. The Film Centre’s main goal is to oversee the Icelandic Film Museum, the Icelandic Film Council and Icelandic Film Fund.  The Icelandic film and television production sector has seen incredibly rapid recent growth. With a number of large productions occurring within the country, Iceland has become a hotspot for international filmmaking. As such, the Film Centre’s role has grown in importance over the course of the last years. The Film Centre provides incentive to foreign production firms to produce films in Iceland via a reimbursement of up to 35% of production costs that occur within the country.  Projects must fulfill certain cultural and production criteria in order to receive a letter of intent for reimbursement. The Film Centre also plays a pivotal role in Icelandic filmmaking through management of the Film Fund, which provides financial support for films at various stages of production. These may be for example grants for screenwriting, project development, production, post-production and promotional purposes.
Results: The Icelandic Film Centre has played a crucial role in supporting the rapid development of the Icelandic film industry in recent years. The fiscal support provided by the funds and measures that the Icelandic Film Centre manages has given Icelandic filmmakers the opportunity to create culturally relevant and meaningful content to enhance the local culture. In 1999, the Act on Temporary Reimbursements for Film Production in Iceland no. 43/1999 was passed in Parliament. This authorized the State Treasury to reimburse filmmakers for partial production costs incurred within the country. Since the Act was passed it has attracted numerous sizeable international projects that provide individuals with employment, fuel the economy and expand the cultural landscape.
Financial Ressources: In 2024 123.054 USD was allocated to the Icelandic Film Centre (153.300.000 ISK)

Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture
SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
