Cultural Domain: Design,Performing Arts,Media Arts,Cinema and Audiovisual Arts,Music,Publishing,Visual Arts
Agency Implementation: The Council of Ministers of the Republic of Belarus
Main Feature: According to the Ministry of Justice, in Belarus, as of January 1, 2023, there are 2,544 public associations (213 international, 668 republican and 1,663 local) and 45,706 organizational structures of public associations, 44 unions (associations) of public associations, as well as 7 republican state-public associations. On February 14, 2023, the Law N250-Z "On Public Associations" was adopted. This Law defines the concept of civil society in the Republic of Belarus, establishes the legal and organizational basis for interaction between state bodies (organizations) and civil society in order to ensure the consolidation of the efforts of the individual, society and the state to implement the national interests of the Republic of Belarus. Cultural and educational institutions make around one third of all the registered public associations and companies. According to the Law ‘On Public Associations’, the state cooperates with and provides support to non-governmental organizations in several ways: participation of civil society entities in the work of collegial formations of government bodies, public advisory councils, meetings of localexecutive and administrative bodies at their invitation; provision by government bodies (organizations) of assistance in the implementation of activities of civil society entities; participation of civil society entities in the formation and implementation of state policy; submission by civil society entities to rule-making bodies of proposals on improving legislative acts; participation of civil society entities in the preparation and public discussion of draft regulatory legal acts; implementation of public control; formation and implementation of state social procurement. Title EN: The Digital Plan for Irish
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture
SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Digital environment
Agency Implementation: Department of Tourism, Culture, Arts, Gaeltacht, Sport and Media
Main Feature: The Digital Plan for Irish was published in December 2022. The objective of this plan is to enable the Irish-language community to build and revitalise the language by establishing and developing a vibrant Irish-language technology sector, enabling this community to take up new opportunities to participate fully in modern day society. The digital revolution, described as a “digital timebomb” facing lesser-used language speakers, is feeding the globalisation of Anglocentric culture, fuelling the processes whereby minority languages are being lost at an unprecedented rate. However, this same digital technology offers unique opportunities to counteract this trend of language attrition to help document, preserve, maintain and revitalise endangered languages and dialects. Precisely because it pervades every aspect of our lives, embedding Irish in technology facilitates its use in multiple domains of activity and harnesses the opportunities for the language to be part of this new digital age. In bringing the language into the digital age, this Plan aims to seamlessly marry our heritage with modern Ireland, retaining our identity in an increasingly homogenised world culture. Examples of some of the digital programmes supported under this plan are outlined below.  The Clár TechSpace project is a national project that aims to impact the lives of young people by becoming Ireland’s leading creative technology network for outcome focused youth development through the medium of Irish.  TechSpace is a national network of digital media spaces in youth centres and schools. The network helps young people to create digital and technological material as they engage in activities such as digital film, web design, mobile app development and robotics, among others.  Under the direction of trained instructors and mentors, young people can enhance their computer competency, while improving their self-confidence and social skills, all through the medium of Irish.  Funding of €632,538 was provided in 2023 to continue with the expansion of the programme nationwide and also to hold the annual Tech Féile- a festival which celebrates the creativity of young people through Irish.  https://kinia.ie/clar-techspace/   A variety of schemes to support Irish language technology initiatives are being progressed and developed, including the development of machine translation systems by Dublin City University (DCU) and Trinity College Dublin (TCD). Examples of this work include the text to speech synthesis project Abair.ie (https://www.abair.ie/en). ABAIR's main objective is that spoken Irish will be at the heart of digital life, and ABAIR helps to achieve this aim by providing a range of speech technologies that are of an international standard. Digitisation projects in DCU including the LEX programme for the provision of terminology for EU institutions and other projects include Logainm.ie, Ainm.ie, Dúchas.ie. https://www.abair.ie/en  The Irish Folklore Commission Collection is inscribed on the UNESCO Memory of the World Register. The Collection was assembled in the years 1935-1970 and forms the core archival material held in the National Folklore Collection UCD (University College Dublin). The collection compromises varied documentary formats which include audio, visual, manuscript and rare printed materials, spanning all aspects of human endeavor and traditional knowledge, from material culture to oral literature, language and artistic expression. Much of the material has been digitised by Fiontar DCU with funding from the Department of Tourism, Culture, Arts, Gaeltacht, Sport and Media and is freely available at www.duchas.ie .  Financial supports are also provided to DCU for work on it’s eStór project which works to identify bilingual materials for the eStór platform for the benefit of Irish input on the European Commission's eTranslation machine. Through the platform language resources are collected, prepared and shared amongst public institutions and translation centres. https://estor.ie/   ‘Foclóir Stairiúil na Gaeilge’ – an initiative of the Royal Irish Academy – is funded by the Department of Tourism, Culture, Arts, Gaeltacht, Sport and Media and is one of the most ambitious linguistic research projects to be ever undertaken in Europe with over 90 million words already compiled and digitised, and freely accessible.  Its primary objective is to establish an historical dictionary of Modern Irish (1600-2000) which will show the evolution of the language in the given period. It will be based on digitised corpora to include printed texts, texts from manuscripts and material from other sources.  https://www.ria.ie/research-projects/focloir-stairiuil-na-gaeilge/eolas-ginearalta   Other Irish-language media and broadcasting supports include; •	The Irish Government has continued to increase its investment in Irish language broadcasting. Exchequer support for TG4 increased by €4.8m in Budget 2024 which represents a total increase of almost €20 million since 2019.  •	An additional €2m Exchequer allocation was made to Coimisiún na Meán to enable a funding round of the Sound and Vision Scheme to support the production of culturally valuable broadcast content, including content in the Irish language focused on the voice of immigrant and new Irish Communities. This round of funding (Round 54) will open on 27th June 2024 for broadcasters and independent producers. •	Alongside the New Decade New Approach Agreement, €1.2m per annum is being provided over the period 2021-2023 for the promotion of Irish Language in Northern Ireland.  This has been extended for 2024, with €1m was made available for the Irish Language Broadcasting Fund in Northern Ireland for content creation, with €100k provided to both RTÉ and TG4 to further support the promotion of Irish language broadcasting in Northern Ireland. •	€3.3 million of exchequer funding was provided in Budget 2023 to support the development and launch of Cúla4, a new Irish language television service for children and young people. The new channel launched in September 2023.
Results: Clár TechSpace makes the connection between the language and technology from an early age.  To date 20,500 Educators have been Upskilled with 368,000 Young People involved with Kinia’s programme.  Abair project ensures the Irish language will be catered for in the area of text-to-speech technologies.  The Digitisation projects (Lex, Logainm, Ainm.ie, Dúchas.ie) provide an online repository of terminology, placenames, names and old photos and documents in a digital corpus.  eStór: Ensuring the Irish Language translators in the EU have a corpus of terminology and that the language can be used in the EU.  ‘Foclóir Stairiúil na Gaeilge’: Over 90 million words have be digitised to date ensuring they will not be lost.
Financial Ressources: Clár Techspace: €2,243,466 (approx. $ 2,243,466 USD) has been awarded to Kinia for Clár Techspace between 2020 and 2023.  Abair: €2,017,470 (approx. $2,017,470 USD) between 2021 to date.  The Digitisation projects (Lex, Logainm, Ainm.ie, Dúchas.ie): Over €3.5 million (approx. $3,803,450 USD) since 2020 has been awarded for these projects.  eStór: €845,426 (approx. $918,724.43 USD) awarded since 2021.  ‘Foclóir Stairiúil na Gaeilge’: €920,183 (approx. $920,183 USD) since 2020.
Recommandations: Clár TechSpace: This project is vital in ensuring that Irish speakers are involved in the world of technology from a young age to ensure the language stays relevant in the digital age.  Abair: This project is vital in ensuring that text to speech technologies can be catered for in the Irish language.  The Digitisation projects (Lex, Logainm, Ainm.ie, Dúchas.ie): These digitisation projects are extremely valuable in ensuring that important historical and cultural documents are not lost and can be accessed and enjoyed by many worldwide for years to come.  eStór: By giving digital support to the language in this way, Irish will have the same opportunities as other languages in the EU. The EU’s eTranslation system has benefitted from the translations made available through the project and the output of Irish translations has improved as a result.  ‘Foclóir Stairiúil na Gaeilge’: This project is addressing the major gap in the vocabulary of Irish, as a contemporary European language, that there is no authoritative historical dictionary available for it.

Area of Monitoring: Media diversity
Agency Implementation: Council of Ministers
Main Feature: Under Law No. (13) of 2019, dated May 30, 2019, the "Media City" was established (Annex No. (13)). This institution aims to enhance media diversity. For the purposes of this periodic report, the focus should primarily be on the following objectives of Media City:  -	Granting licenses, permits, and approvals to individuals, companies, and other entities wishing to operate in Media City, including licenses for television and radio broadcasting, and publishing and distribution licenses for newspapers, magazines, and books for licensed companies. -	Conducting research and consultations related to laws and regulations for organizing and promoting media and scientific research. -	Providing administrative, logistical, and technical services to licensed companies of all kinds operating in Media City. -Establishing business incubators to support initiatives in digital and technological media. -Creating an investment fund in the media sector. -Creating an investment fund in the film and television production sector. The State's goal through this measure is to create a free zone that complements local media and serves as an effective mechanism to support the media industry. It aims to attract global media, technological companies, and research and training institutions in the media and digital media fields, especially international content producers. Additionally, it seeks to provide the necessary services for the operation of selected media institutions according to specific criteria. It aims to offer opportunities for innovative and creative media to thrive in the state through various mechanisms. These mechanisms include establishing business incubators to support initiatives in digital and technological media. Another mechanism is creating an investment fund in the media sector. It also involves creating an investment fund in the film and television production sector.
Results: Since its establishment in 2019, Media City has achieved interesting results. Some of these results extend beyond the scope of this periodic report, such as the success of launching four editions of the Qatar Economic Forum. Additionally, there have been significant achievements in signing several influential memoranda in the media field. Notably, there were agreements signed with Bloomberg Media Group in 2023. However, some of the most important achievements related directly to the scope of this report include:  -	Participation in Web Summit Qatar 2024 by sponsoring the Media Village at the summit, providing a dynamic platform for communication and collaboration among journalists, media outlets, and industry specialists. Also, participating in the Invest Qatar pioneering 'Startup Qatar' initiative aimed at connecting summit participants with key stakeholders and providing a comprehensive digital platform to meet all business needs in one place. -	Launching a workshop in May 2023 to enhance the media environment in the country and promote digital transformation. The workshop aimed at strengthening cooperation with various relevant government entities. It was held in partnership with Amazon Web Services. Amazon Web Services provides on-demand cloud computing platforms and APIs. -	Organizing a training camp in Lyon, France, in February 2023 for Media City's team in collaboration with the EuroNews network, covering various fields related to digital media and content production. -	The success of Media City and Group ONE Holdings in 2022 in signing a Memorandum of Understanding to establish and develop a long-term strategic partnership to produce and develop a wide range of content in the State of Qatar through various media channels. This partnership was highlighted during the filming of the second season of the reality TV series " The Apprentice: One Championship Edition," which is broadcasted by Netflix in over 150 countries.

Main Feature: The first Ethiopian Circus Festival is a celebration of talent, culture, and community in Ethiopia. The Circus Festival was organized in Addis Abeba Ethiopia from May 5 to 7, 2023.  The objective of the festival was catalysts for growth: Leverage circus art to drive economic development, strengthen social cohesion, and preserve cultural traditions. The festival created the opportunity for the Circus Companies and artists to meet with different producers and promoters to sell their productions in the international market, strengthen their partnerships, and show their different circus acts to the Ethiopian community. This helped different circuses from 10 regions to share their best experiences among themselves. Panel discussions and knowledge transfer and exchange programs are conducted at the same time. Four panelists from Addis Abeba University, the Ministry of Culture and Sport, an economy expert from the Plan Ministry, and a Social Enterprise consultant presented their papers on the topics of Ethiopian circus art and artist on the international stage and the contribution of the establishment of ENCAC for the development of the circus art in Ethiopia, the power of circus art to address different social issues, circus art contribution in the economic and social development in Ethiopia and the Ethiopian government perception about circus art and future direction. 42 Delegates from the circus sector (managers, trainers, artists, and directors), 7 embassy culture sector representatives, 10 Local NGO delegates, Culture and sport ministry minister's and sector leaders attended the panel. The festival was organized together with Flawless Event with the partnership of FDRE Ministry Culture and Sport. Universoul Circus, St. George beer, and Lolichips sponsored the festival. Kana TV was the Media partner.   The specific objectives of the festival are: • To show the level of the Ethiopian circus development and potential to the nation as well as the international stakeholders.  • Creating an equal job opportunity platform for the artists to promote their talent to the global market. • To build strong and positive relationships among Ethiopian circus companies and organizations. • To set circus art as a preferred form of entertainment in Ethiopia. • Inform policymaking in order to consider and mainstream circus arts during decision-making at the national, regional, and woreda levels. • Show the relevance of the circus in the process of economic, social, political, and cultural well-being of the community. • Rebuild the social capital of our people through exchanging best practices among participants
Results: The Festival  10 regions, Addis Abeba and Dire Dawa city administrations, Tigiray, Amhara, Oromiya, Southwest Ethiopia, South Ethiopia, Sidama, Afar, and Central Ethiopia regions circuses have got a chance to present their works. 120 Circus artists presented their talents 45 group artists presented their work 5000 families entertained Created job opportunities for 43 circus artists on the spot for a year – 4-year contract at the international circus companies.  32 awards given to the winners 1.5 million social media reached  News coverage in 9 mainstreaming channels and pre and post-festival broadcasting on KANA TV.  5 billboards displayed in the main squares of Addis Ababa city.  The festival was promoted and advertised in the city through pared shows and speaker announcements and reached the community at large. Title EN: The Fund for the Support of Culture and Art of the President of the Republic of Belarus

Main Feature: The Fund for the Support of Culture and Art of the President of the Republic of Belarus was established on April 15, 1998. by Decree of the President of the Republic of Belarus No. 211 acts on the basis of Decree of the President of the Republic of Belarus dated December 13, 2004 No. 601 "On some issues of the activity of the Fund for the Support of Culture and Art of the President of the Republic of Belarus ". It is aimed at financing culture and art, creating favorable conditions for the creative development of a person, social support for cultural and art workers, preservation of the historical heritage and cultural traditions of the Belarusian people. The resources are received by the fund from the republican budget, charitable contributions of the Belarusian and foreign citizens, companies, enterprises, foundations, and other legal entities. The Fund’s resources are managed by the Fund’s Council, which is formed from the leading cultural and art workers, representatives of the Presidential Administration of the Republic of Belarus, the Council of Ministers of the Republic of Belarus, ministries concerned, and other republican government bodies, creative unions and public associations. The Fund’s Council, on the basis of proposals received from companies, institutions, creative unions, and various public associations, makes decisions on the allocation of funds for: • payment of fees and grants for the creation of works of culture and art; • acquisition of tools and materials for classes to improve skills and the implementation of creative activities; • internships for cultural and art workers, the implementation of creative projects in Belarus and abroad; • ensuring the participation of creators in competitions, exhibitions, festivals, symposiums and other events in the field of culture and art; • organization of festivals, concerts, exhibitions, publications, and creation of stage works, works of fine art, other events to identify and promote talents and works; • assistance in organizing advanced training, improving the professional skills of creative workers; • single time payment of financial aid to cultural and art workers; • other goals related to the preservation of historical and cultural values. Every year, the fund sponsors the awards of the President of the Republic of Belarus ‘For Spiritual Revival’ and special prizes to cultural and art workers The activities of the Presidential Fund for Support of Culture and Arts are one of the avenues of according targeted assistance to the national culture development by the state.
Results: The Fund provides the sustainable funding for programs to support culture and art, the mobility of artists, formal and non-formal education in the field of culture, pay scholarships and bonuses to cultural and art workers, which in general allows organizing the sequence and continuity of the cultural development process and its promotion at the national and international levels. Part of the funds goes to support the projects of non-governmental organizations in the field of culture and art.

Title EN: The Hong Kong SAR fosters cultural exchange by collaborating with various cultural organisations and institutions from overseas
Goal: Achieve A Balanced Flow Of Cultural Goods And Services And Increase The Mobility Of Artists And Cultural Professionals
SDG: SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 10 - Reduce inequality within and among countries,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Mobility of artists and cultural professionals
Cultural Domain: Design,Performing Arts,Media Arts,Cinema and Audiovisual Arts,Music,Publishing,Visual Arts
Agency Implementation: Cultural, Sports and Tourism Bureau (CSTB) and Leisure and Cultural Services Department (LCSD) of The Hong Kong SAR Government
Main Feature: The LCSD endeavours to foster cultural exchange by collaborating with various cultural organisations and institutions from overseas with a view to promoting Hong Kong’s cosmopolitan image by showcasing distinguished local artists and arts groups outside Hong Kong while bringing high quality visiting programmes to Hong Kong.  As announced by the Chief Executive in the 2021 Policy Address, the Hong Kong SAR Government pledged to strengthen connections with overseas arts and cultural organisations and enhance cultural exchange and co-operation with the Mainland. These efforts aim to realise the strategic positioning of Hong Kong as an East-meets-West Center for International Cultural Exchange, in line with the objectives outlined in the 14th Five-Year Plan.  The 2023-24 Budget has allocated funding for hosting the 4th Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Greater Bay Area (GBA) Culture and Arts Festival in Hong Kong. The festival aims to coordinate and organise high-quality cultural and arts activities within the GBA, facilitate cultural exchange and long-term development, enhance the cultural image of the GBA, and fully implement the Outline Development Plan for the Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Greater Bay Area, which aims to “Jointly Develop a Cultured Bay Area”.  Since 2019, the LCSD has been organising “Hong Kong Week” in the Mainland cities to showcase local arts groups and artists in different regions. In 2023, for the first time in an overseas city, the “Hong Kong Week” was held in Bangkok. The next “Hong Kong Week” is planned to be held in Seoul in 2025.  The LCSD will continue to deepen the cultural exchange work to support and promote the participation of local arts groups and artists in annual festival programmes, thereby enhancing the cultural brand of Hong Kong. Furthermore, there will be strengthened cooperation with municipal governments, performance venues, and cultural institutions in the GBA to organise festive events and co-commission new productions. Additionally, various programmes and activities will be organised to promote cultural exchange and training among art practitioners. Various collaboration models are also actively being explored to maximise resources and support the long-term development of local artists and arts groups in the area.  With a view to attracting arts and cultural talents to Hong Kong, the Government has included the professionals of arts promoters, conservators for movable cultural heritage, creative industries professionals in publishing, creative industries professionals in film, performing arts professionals in arts technology, creative industries professionals in music; and creative industries professionals in digital entertainment under the Talent List.  In addition, the arts and culture sector and creative industries sectors have been included as designated sectors under the “Pilot Scheme on Immigration Facilitation for Visitors Participating in Short-term Activities in Designated Sectors”, allowing more non-local arts and cultural talents to participate in specified short-term activities as visitors, without the need to apply for employment visas/entry permits.
Results: (i)	Recurrent provision for cultural exchanges  Following the easing of travel restrictions of different overseas countries and resumption of normal travel between Hong Kong and Mainland, local arts groups/artists have been actively participating in the cultural exchange activities outside Hong Kong since the second half of 2022. The funding supported over 200 performances, exhibition and arts and cultural exchange activities conducted in the Mainland and overseas in 2022-23 and 2023-24, spanning across Germany, Italy, United Kingdom, Canada, Thailand, Malaysia, Singapore, Australia, Japan, Korea and various Mainland cities.    LCSD organised “Hong Kong Week” in Guangzhou, Wuhan, and Bangkok. The “Hong Kong Week” held in Bangkok in 2023 was the first overseas “Hong Kong Week”, attracting audience over 781,000 in 62 activities.    (ii)	Dedicated funding to support the awardees of the CNAF in Hong Kong  From 2022 to 2024, 31 Hong Kong arts projects have been selected by the CNAF.  The CSTB has approved dedicated funding for 14 projects selected in 2022 and 2023. Some of them have been successfully held in 2023 and Q1 2024, spanning across Canada, Greece, Bulgaria, Serbia, Romania, and Macao. Other funded projects will continue to showcase in Mainland and overseas from 2024 to 2025, promoting the inheritance and innovation of Chinese culture and facilitating international cultural exchanges.  (iii)	Dedicated funding to promote cultural exchanges in the GBA  During the five years from 2018-19 to 2022-23, LCSD collaborated with major venue operators in the GBA and supported 54 online and offline productions, and staging a total of 141 touring performances and exchange activities in GBA cities, covering different art forms such as Chinese and western music, jazz, dance, drama, Cantonese opera and family entertainment etc.  The productions attracted over 60 000 admissions, and over 6.68 million views online.  In 2023-24, LCSD supported 24 productions, staging over 100 touring performance and exchange activities and covering different art forms.  The production attracted over 400 000 audiences.
Financial Ressources: Funding of around 6.4 million USD was set aside annually for strengthening collaboration with government authorities and cultural organisations of Mainland provinces and municipalities as well as overseas, and supporting our arts groups and artists to perform and stage exhibitions outside Hong Kong. In 2023-24, funding of around 1.3million USD was set aside annually to support local outstanding arts projects recognised by the CNAF to conduct cultural exchanges outside Hong Kong. The Government allocated a sum of around 18.5 million USD to LCSD from 2018-19 to 2022-23 to support local artists/arts groups to conduct touring performances and exchange activities in the GBA.
Recommandations: Feedback from artists and groups have been collected. The measures were effective in fostering cultural exchange and promoting Hong Kong’s cosmopolitan image.

Title EN: The International Cities of Refuge Network – ICORN
Goal: Promote Human Rights And Fundamental Freedoms
SDG: SDG 5 - Achieve gender equality and empower all women and girls,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels
Area of Monitoring: Artistic freedom
Agency Implementation: Municipality of Ljubljana
Main Feature: ICORN is an international network of cities and regions that promote freedom of expression and offer refuge to persecuted artists who are under pressure in their own countries for their work and views. It was founded in 1994 at the suggestion of Salman Rushdie and Ljubljana joined the network in 2011. Poets, writers, journalists, bloggers, illustrators, cartoonists, translators and, since the ICORN General Assembly in Ljubljana in 2014, visual artists, directors and musicians also find refuge. The city of Ljubljana, together with the Slovenian PEN Centre and the international network, offers a safe haven for persecuted artists. After their arrival in Ljubljana, they ensure that the persecuted artists are accommodated in one of the city's facilities for a period of two years, receive a stipend for basic living expenses and are covered by health insurance during their stay in Slovenia. In addition, the municipality and literary organisations will enable the persecuted author to actively participate in cultural life in Ljubljana and beyond. Prior to the arrival of the persecuted artist, the Ministry of the Interior conducts a procedure for issuing a temporary residence permit in Slovenia on the basis of the Aliens Act. The decisive factor in this procedure is the opinion of the Ministry of Culture on the interest of the Republic of Slovenia in issuing the temporary residence permit, which is subsequently confirmed by the Government of the Republic of Slovenia. The Ministry of Culture bases its opinion on the creative work of the persecuted writer, focusing on his active commitment to fundamental human rights, which jeopardises his life in his home country. In this way, Slovenia is making a clear commitment to respecting democracy and human rights and drawing attention to the fact that there are parts of the world where systematic human rights violations still take place.
Results: With this initiative, since the Municipality of Ljubljana joined the ICORN network in 2011, Slovenia has granted refuge to six people - from writers to journalists to bloggers - whose lives were threatened in their home countries because of their creative work and active advocacy for the violation of fundamental human rights and freedoms. Together with the Slovenian state, the Municipality of Ljubljana has ensured that partners of persecuted artists can also find refuge in Slovenia if they are threatened with retaliation in their home countries. This initiative is important not only for the protection of the lives and freedom of persecuted artists who dare to draw attention to the violation of basic human rights and freedoms in their home countries, but also for the active engagement of these individuals after their arrival in Slovenia. These persecuted artists have various performances here in the capital and throughout Slovenia, which significantly contribute to raising awareness of the importance of protecting and respecting basic human rights, especially the right to freedom of expression and creativity. They can also sensitize the international community to the situation in their home countries and the consequences that undemocratic systems and leaders have on the lives of individuals and communities.
Recommandations: The relevance of the intake is regularly assessed during the implementation of the measure itself. It is repeatedly confirmed that the decision to include Ljubljana in the network was the right one. In addition, the implementation of the measure is one of the examples of good practice in cooperation between the municipality and the state.

Title EN: The International Guiding Principles on Diversity of Content Online
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture
SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Digital environment
Agency Implementation: Department of Canadian Heritage
Main Feature: The Guiding Principles are a norm-setting document that aims to guide actions and measures that foster greater exposure to diverse cultural content, information, and news online. They are not legally binding and complement existing domestic and international obligations such as the UNESCO Convention.  The primary aim of this international group of like-minded countries is to establish broad and common principles that promote the objectives of the Convention in an environment where competing and contradictory principles may emerge from cooperation among different cultures.  The Guide covers four themes deemed essential to the promotion of diversity of content online:  1.	Creation, access and discoverability of diverse content online; 2.	Fair remuneration and economic viability of content creators; 3.	Promotion of diverse, pluralistic sources of news and information as well as resilience against disinformation and misinformation; 4.	Transparency of the impacts of algorithmic treatments of online content.
Results: The Guiding Principles were developed in a multi-stakeholder working group that consisted of officials from governments, as well as representatives from industry and civil society organizations. The Guiding Principles were published in June 2021 on the Government of Canada website.  The exposure to diverse content should contribute to a healthier public discourse, greater social inclusion within society, bolster resilience to disinformation and misinformation, and increase citizens’ ability to participate in democratic processes.
Financial Ressources: A total of USD 2.75 million (2019 dollars) across 4 years were committed to the initiative.

Area of Monitoring: Cultural and creative sectors
Agency Implementation: State Department for Culture, The Arts and Heritage
Main Feature: The Kenya Music and Cultural Festival is an annual festival that brings together all the communities in the republic of Kenya to celebrate the diversity of their cultural expressions.  The festival, held annually, brings together all communities in Kenya showcasing the diversity of the Kenyan cultural expressions including music, dance, drama, chants, oral traditions, artifacts, crafts, traditional foods and indigenous practices. It is held for 8 days in the last week of November and the first week of December.The National festival is a culmination of community festivals held at the County level. Every year, the festival experiences growth as more art forms and wider range of participants seek to take part. The festival provides a platform for all communities to showcase excellence in various art forms and is specifically tailored for groups that are outside of the schools programme such as community cultural troupes, out of school youth troupes, church groups, institutional performing and visual arts groups among others. Whereas the festival takes a competitive angle where winners are awarded, the main focus of the festival is the preservation of Kenyan Cultural expressions and providing a platform where this knowledge can be shared among generations. The Kenya Music and Cultural Festival is organized by the Department of Culture with the support of the Festival National Organizing committee and County Governments. The membership of the National committee is drawn from experts in the different genres of cultural expressions including music, drama, theatre, film and visual arts and come from both professional organizations and the communities. Preparation for the annual festival begins with the writing of a syllabus for the festival. The syllabus stipulates the organization of the festival in terms of the content and context. The syllabus is prepared in a participatory workshop where communities, County Governments, the National committee and the Department of Culture are represented. The syllabus is then disseminated to trainers of community groups and County officials in a capacity building workshop. It is from this workshop that county officials and community trainers get materials with which they prepare their teams for participation in the National Festival.A county level festival is conducted in every County from which a team to participate in the National Festival is selected. A programme for performances and exhibitions drawn from all participating counties is then developed and is implemented at the National Festival. Participation is open to all community art and culture troupes as well as art groups in  Technical and Vocational Training Institutes(TVETS), Parastatals, clubs, Ministries, Departments and state Agencies.  The Festival celebrates the communities in Music, dance, poetry, Drama and film. An exhibition of fine arts, artifacts and fashion as well as community food ways is also curated.
Results: About 10,000 participants from an average of 25 Counties get an opportunity to showcase and enjoy their cultural expressions every year Enhanced participation in cultural life Avenue for continuity of Cultural Expressions

In the implementation of this law, equality must be respected and special attention must be paid to the equal status of the sexes. The minister is in charge of issues related to music according to this law.  Music Center and Music Council. Article 3: Role and main tasks. The fund shall promote the promotion of Icelandic musicians and their compositions in Iceland and abroad. The income of the music fund is:     a. contribution from the treasury as determined in the budget,     b. other contributions. This includes about 90 exhibition rooms, as well as a library and activity and event rooms for the public, and office space and facilities for conservation, digitization and storage of the collection. The collections include older and modern art, contemporary art, architecture and design.
Results: The new National Museum is able to showcase both Norwegian and international arts and craft at a whole new level, both in terms of security, but also in terms of available space. The new Light Hall, which is the new museum's space for temporary exhibitions, has a floor space of 2400 square metres, and a floor to ceiling height of seven metres. This Hall will be able to accommodate exhibitions on a scale not previously possible in Norway, both from Norwegian art and international collaborations. The Museum was visited by 1.5 million people in its first year, about three times as many visitors than before the new build.

Title EN: The State Strategy for Civic Equality and Integration 2021-2030
Goal: Integrate Culture In Sustainable Development Frameworks
SDG: SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: National sustainable development policies and plans
Cultural Domain: Design,Performing Arts,Media Arts,Cinema and Audiovisual Arts,Music,Publishing,Visual Arts
Agency Implementation: Office of the State Minister of Georgia for Reconciliation and Civic Equality
Main Feature: The State Strategy for Civic Equality and Integration 2021-2030 was approved by the decree of the Government of Georgia on July 13, 2021, with the coordination of the Office of the State Minister of Georgia for Reconciliation and Civic Equality. The Strategy identifies the country's long-term priorities and objectives, aiming to develop a multi-sector policy that will facilitate the protection of ethnic minority rights, including their cultural rights.  The State Strategy for 2021-2030 is the second strategic document on civic equality and integration, based on the results and final assessments of the 2015-2020 Strategy. The document aims to strengthen democracy and the rule of law, which implies equality of each citizen by and before the law, and to strengthen a tolerant and inclusive environment where cultural diversity and equality are ensured.  The State Strategy defines five priority directions: state language to support integration, access to quality education, equality, civic and political participation, social and economic integration, and intercultural dialogue. The objectives within the framework of the intercultural dialogue direction were defined to support further deepening positive communication between various ethnic groups and overcoming the barriers that still exist. The State puts efforts into strengthening intercultural dialogue and multi-ethnic cooperation; it supports the preservation of cultural traditions of ethnic minorities and their development and rapprochement with modern cultural achievements. Regular joint sports and culture activities organized in the framework of the Strategy's annual action plans help bring various ethnic groups and majority representatives together to share values, knowledge, and experiences and strengthen self-expression and tolerance, integration and harmonious coexistence.  To protect and promote cultural heritage, the State ensures inventory and registration of ethnic minorities' tangible and intangible cultural heritage, conservation and restoration of cultural monuments, and funding of theatres, museums, libraries and cultural events. In order to strengthen dialogue and solidarity between ethnic groups, the development of necessary infrastructure is supported. The objective of protection and development of cultural identities also encompasses the following activities: •	Promotion of literature, folklore, and music •	Financial assistance for Armenian, Azerbaijani and Russian theatres and museums •	Cultural events, including exhibitions and publications  The primary tool for implementing the Strategy is the Annual Action Plans designed by sector-specific agencies.  Line ministries and international partner organizations, including the UN Association of Georgia, Center for Civic Integration and Inter-ethnic Relations, Human Rights Education and Monitoring Center, the Council of Europe, the OSCE High Commissioner on National Minorities, and others, were invited to contribute their expertise in the field. They were asked to conduct a comprehensive situation analysis, identify challenges, and present their visions of profile-specific activities. The insights, documents, and proposals they provided were instrumental in developing the Strategy.
Results: Assessments will occur in 2024 and 2027, with the final evaluation planned for the end of the ten-year implementation period in 2030.
Financial Ressources: The major tool for the implementation of the Strategy is the Annual Action Plans designed by sector-specific agencies. In order to reach the overall objectives defined in the Strategy, the respective allocations are envisaged within the budgets of the implementing institutions.

Title EN: The Reading for Enjoyment Strategy

Area of Monitoring: National sustainable development policies and plans
Agency Implementation: Norwegian Ministry of Culture and Equality
Main Feature: The Norwegian population, especially children and young people, are reading less than before. The Government aims to reverse this trend by promoting reading for enjoyment through a new strategy. The Strategy aims to create a reading culture. It is recognised that reading not only provides enriching experiences, but is crucial for acquiring knowledge, expressing ourselves, participating in society, and developing a critical sense. Reading is a fundamental skill that is crucial for the freedom of speech. The Government will, among other things, strengthen school libraries with staff resources and books, develop capacity-building measures for teachers, increase the support to reading projects and support the production and distribution of cartoons. The Strategy was launched on 29 May 2024.
Results: The white paper was approved by the Norwegian Parliament on 19 March 2024 and the measures have therefore not yet been implemented.

Title EN: The Stories of Us*
Goal: Promote Human Rights And Fundamental Freedoms
SDG: SDG 5 - Achieve gender equality and empower all women and girls,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels
Area of Monitoring: Gender equality
Agency Implementation: Be You Network
Main Feature: En Suisse en 2020, de nombreuses et de nombreux jeunes LGBTIQ+ partagent encore un parcours similaire. Celui d’être seules et seuls dans la découverte de soi, souvent obligées et obligés de faire preuve de courage pour comprendre, accepter et partager leur identité, que la société considère encore « hors-norme ». The Stories of Us* souhaite contribuer à changer notre narratif commun pour inclure des parcours de vie LGBTIQ+, pallier au manque de représentation et améliorer le sentiment d’inclusion des jeunes LGBTIQ+. À travers 12 podcasts, le projet partagera les histoires de « coming-in » et de « coming-out » de jeunes de 9 orientations sexuelles et identités de genres minoritaires, dans le but de diffuser des vécus instigateurs d’espoirs pour la nouvelle génération LGBTIQ+. Des événements participatifs seront également organisés pour les jeunes dans 4 cantons romands (GE, VD, VS, FR), en partenariat avec les associations LGBTIQ+ locales, afin de permettre l’échange entre jeunes et le soutien entre pairs. The Stories of Us* a bénéficié du soutien financier de l’Office fédéral des assurance sociales OFAS pour un projet encourageant la participation, selon l’art. 8, al. 1, let. b de la loi sur l’encouragement de l’enfance et de la jeunesse LEEJ.
Recommandations: Un rapport final a été transmis, il est prévu que Be You Network continue de publier des podcasts.

Title EN: The Strategy for Language-Based Arts
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture
SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Cultural and creative sectors
Agency Implementation: Department of Tourism, Culture, Arts, Gaeltacht, Sport and Media
Main Feature: The Strategy for the Language-Based Arts and the related action plan was published in March 2024. Despite being an official language of Ireland, the Irish-language (Gaeilge) is a first language of only about 2% of the population, primarily living in Gaeltacht regions. Protection and promotion of Irish-language based arts is therefore necessary to safeguard these practices and maintain diversity of culture on the island.   The Strategy lays out strategic ways to promote and strengthen the Irish language-based arts in the wider public but also to include them in the education system and the early-years sector in partnership with various departments and institutions.  The main aims of the strategy are: •	ensuring better coordination and collaboration in the development of the Gaeltacht (the regions in Ireland in which the Irish language is, or was until recently, the primary spoken language of the majority of the community) and Irish-language arts;  •	further strengthening the relationships among the interested parties; •	increasing and promoting the profile of Gaeltacht and Irish-language arts nationally and internationally; •	finding opportunities to provide more support for the Gaeltacht and Irish-language arts and to further develop them.  Along with the strategy, a significant funding package was announced for An Taidhbhearc Theatre (the National Irish Language Theatre of Ireland) and Oireachtas na Gaeilge (the organisation responsible for the annual arts festival of Irish Culture) in order to complete a significant portion of the goals set out in this plan. This significant investment in this sector will boost language-based arts in the years to come.  The increase in funding awarded to An Taibhdhearc theatre (https://www.antaibhdhearc.com/) is €5.78 million over the next 4 years. This funding will allow An Taibhdhearc to recruit a team of trained theatre professionals enabling the theatre to fulfill its’ role as a National Theatre for the Irish Language.  An tOireachtas - National Action Plan: One of the other major activities planned as part of the Strategy for the Language-based Arts is to establish a structure under which comprehensive support will be given to the development of the Language-based Arts in areas outside the Gaeltacht, where Irish is not commonly spoken as a first language. It is recognized that there is a need for more support from the language-based arts across the country and from Irish language drama in particular. The Department has agreed a funding package of more than €4 million for An tOireachtas over 4 years for an action plan in this area that will benefit from the experience and expertise of the Oireachtas na Gaeilge in order to achieve the goals of the strategy that falls under its remit. https://www.antoireachtas.ie/)    As well as the measures outlined in the strategy, the Scéimeana Tacaíochta Gaeilge scheme supports other organisations and programmes which work to promote the Irish Language, including;  Conradh na Gaeilge is a social and cultural organisation which promotes the Irish language in Ireland and worldwide. Conradh na Gaeilge’s ‘Ciste Spreagtha’ (https://cnag.ie/en/get-involved/take-part/ciste-spreagtha-support-fund.html) is a support fund linked to Seachtain na Gaeilge (Irish Language Week) (https://snag.ie/en/)   The aim of the fund is to encourage community groups inside and outside the Gaeltacht regions to organise community events that promote the Irish language during Seachtain na Gaeilge.   The Céad Míle Fáilte campaign in attracting people from different backgrounds who are now living in Ireland to learn Irish. The campaign focuses on the benefit that new Irish communities can derive from the Irish language - in relation to the importance of the language, the additional opportunities associated with it and in terms of integration into Irish society as a whole. The purpose of the campaign is to encourage the new Irish communities in Ireland to learn and use the Irish language as a way to build a stronger Irish cultural identity for themselves. This is achieved through providing a series of language classes and workshops of special interest to groups of new Irish people around the country and by providing them with language resources to help them learn and use the language. Gaeltacht scholarships are awarded to some of the participants so that they can attend a Gaeltacht course. https://www.gov.ie/en/press-release/ffa90-minister-thomas-byrne-launches-conradh-na-gaeilges-cead-mile-failte-initiative-in-dublin-today/   The Irish Language programme by Fighting Words (a civil society organisation which offers teaching and mentoring in all forms of creative writing for children, young people and adults). Fighting Words aims to help young people from all backgrounds develop the gift of writing. https://www.fightingwords.ie/what-we-do/fighting-words-na-gaeilge   The St. Patrick's Day festival is globally recognised as Ireland's major annual cultural festival. The Government supports the Irish language stream of the Festival since 2020 to ensure that the Irish language plays a central role in this important festival. The Government funding gives the organizers of the Festival the opportunity to hold various Irish cultural and artistic events during the Festival which are suitable for people of all ages, and for all levels of Irish. https://stpatricksfestival.ie/    The Official Languages (Amendment) Act 2021 was signed by the President of Ireland on 22 December. Additionally, Gaeilge became a full working language of the EU on 31 December 2021. https://www.gov.ie/en/press-release/68efe-increase-in-advertising-through-irish-establishment-of-the-irish-language-services-advisory-committee-agreement-of-a-research-contract-for-the-national-plan-see-what-else-was-achieved-under-the-official-languages-amendment-act-2021-in-the-last-year/   https://www.gov.ie/en/press-release/e3150-the-irish-language-gains-full-official-and-working-status-in-the-european-union/
Results: The Strategy for Language-Based Arts was adopted in March 2024, results will be monitored on an ongoing basis.  Conradh na Gaeilge’s ‘Ciste Spreagtha’:  Over 400 Irish Language events organised in local Communities all over Ireland since its inception in 2022 with more to be organised before the end of the year  ‘Céad Míle Fáilte’: The Department of Tourism, Culture, Arts, Gaeltacht, Sport and Media begun funding this project in late 2023.  Fighting Words: Fighting words has provided creative writing workshops through Irish to hundreds of children in schools outside of Irish speaking areas since the Department of Tourism, Culture, Arts, Gaeltacht, Sport and Media began funding this project in 2022  St. Patrick's Day festival: St Patrick’s Day is Irelands biggest National Festival and Holiday. The funding for an Irish Language Strand of this event ensures that the language remains centre stage in the celebrations.
Financial Ressources: The Strategy for Language-Based Arts:  €9,865,963.47 (approx. $10,721,342.50 USD) has been agreed to date with the two organisations mentioned above - An Taibhdhearc and An Oireachtas.  Conradh na Gaeilge’s ‘Ciste Spreagtha’:  €550,000 (approx. $597,685 USD) since its’ inception in 2022.  Céad Míle Fáilte’: €29,2032 (approx. $317,351.17 USD) for 2023 and 2024.  Fighting Words: €305,000 (approx. $331,443.50 USD) since its inception in 2022.  St. Patrick's Day festival (Irish Language Strand): €190,000 (approx. $206,473 USD) since 2020.
Recommandations: Conradh na Gaeilge’s ‘Ciste Spreagtha’: This project gives people of all ages, in local communities all over Ireland a chance to engage with the language at a level they are comfortable with. It normalises the language and integrates in into local communities which may not have many opportunities to interact with the language socially otherwise.  Céad Míle Fáilte’: Not evaluated to date.  Fighting Words: Evaluation due in 2025 (end of the current grant agreement).  St. Patrick's Day festival: This initiative exposes the thousands of people both Irish and from oversees who descend on Dublin for the festivities to the Irish Language in a celebratory and positive way.

Title EN: The Strategy of the National Commission on Sustainable Development 2022–2030 : A prosperous and globally responsible Finland that protects the carrying capacity of nature
Goal: Integrate Culture In Sustainable Development Frameworks
SDG: SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: National sustainable development policies and plans
Agency Implementation: Prime Minister's Office
Main Feature: The Strategy of the National Commission on Sustainable Development 2022-2030 is a key guiding document for the implementation of Agenda 2030 in Finland. Culture has been integrated into the strategy, and awareness of the potential of culture to support the achievement of several SDGs can generally be said to be on the rise. The composition of the National Commission, appointed for 2024-2027, also reflects the integration of culture with the appointment of representatives from Arts Promotion Centre and Kulta ry (central organization for support and producer associations operating in the Finnish arts and culture industry).     The strategy features six areas of change, one of which encompasses the potential of arts, culture and cultural heritage in expediting the sustainability transformation. The Strategy also pays attention to cultural participation. The strategy is intended to be a strategy for the whole of Finland: i.e. public and private sector and the civil society alike. The Ministry of Education and Culture participates in its implementation as part of the Government.    Finland’s most recent VNR (2020) references certain strategic documents, i.e. the Ministry of Education and Culture’s sustainable development policy and EU Resolution of the Council on the Cultural Dimension of Sustainable Development. The latter was prepared and adopted in 2019 during Finland’s Presidency of the Council of the European Union.

Title EN: The Strategy of the Romanian Cultural Institute 2022- 2026
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture
SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development

Agency Implementation: Romanian Cultural Institute
Main Feature: The Strategy of the Romanian Cultural Institute 2022- 2026 is in line with the objectives of the 2005 Convention. It also has a key role in supporting sustainable systems of governance for culture, at all levels: international, national, regional, and local.   Out of the nine objectives of the Convention, the Strategy places a particular emphasis on:  -Encouraging the dialogue between cultures for facilitating more ample and balanced cultural exchanges in the world, which benefit intercultural aspects -Promoting interculturality for developing cultural interactions which are meant to build bridges between nations -Promoting respect for cultural diversity and the awareness of its value on a local, national and international level.  It also has a key role in integrating culture in sustainable development projects, supporting gender equality,  artistic freedom and freedom of speech.    The Romanian Cultural Institute works in cooperation with a wide range of national governmental institutions (Romanian Ministry of Foreign Affairs, the Romanian Ministry of Culture, The Ministry of Education, the Department of the Romanians abroad), universities and national civil society organisations.  At the same time, the Romanian Cultural Institute implements several projects as a partner in  European projects co-funded by the European Commission (Horizon Europe, Creative Europe etc).

Recommandations: The implementation of the Strategy is evaluated on an annual basis, including through activity reports, that demonstrate that all the objectives related to the implementation of the Convention are accomplished. Title EN: The Sultan Bin Ali Al Owais Cultural Award
Goal: Achieve A Balanced Flow Of Cultural Goods And Services And Increase The Mobility Of Artists And Cultural Professionals
SDG: SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 10 - Reduce inequality within and among countries,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Flow of cultural goods and services
Agency Implementation: Sultan Bin Ali Al Owais Cultural Foundation
Main Feature: The Sultan Bin Ali Al Owais Cultural Award is presented every two years to a group of outstanding Arab writers and intellectuals for their poetry, stories, novels, plays, criticism and literary studies, and futuristic and humanitarian studies. The only condition is that their work must reflect Arab thought, portray the aspirations of the Arab people, and influence scholarly, literary, and cultural life. The award can be presented to nominees for one or more outstanding works that have had a deep impact on Arab cultural life. The Sultan Bin Ali Al Owais Cultural Award aims to honor, encourage, and support Arab scholars, litterateurs, and intellectuals so they can play their role in the cultural, intellectual, and scientific development of the Arab homeland. The award is given to one poet and may be shared between two poets. The award is given to a winner in one of the three genres of story, novel, and play, and may be shared between two winners from one or two genres. The award is given to a winner in criticism or literary studies and may be shared between two winners from one or two genres. The award is given to a winner in futuristic or humanitarian studies and may be shared between two winners from one or two genres.
Results: Since its inception, the Sultan Bin Ali Al Owais Cultural Award has recognized 101 Arab writers and thinkers and five cultural institutions for their contributions to poetry, stories, novels, plays, criticism, literary studies, and futuristic and humanitarian studies. This has significantly promoted Arab thought and intellectual excellence. With over 270 diverse judges and consultants involved, the award maintains its independence and impartiality, making decisions based solely on creative merit. Each award, valued at $120,000, provides substantial financial support, enabling recipients to continue their impactful work. The award has elevated the global profile of Arab writers and thinkers, fostering greater appreciation of Arab culture. It has encouraged diverse creative expressions and upheld high standards, inspiring intellectual and cultural growth. Recognition of cultural institutions has strengthened their roles within the cultural ecosystem, while the award has facilitated intellectual dialogue and exchange among Arab scholars and intellectuals. Overall, the Sultan Bin Ali Al Owais Cultural Award has profoundly impacted the cultural and intellectual development of the Arab world.

Title EN: The Swedish-Icelandic Collaboration Fund
Goal: Achieve A Balanced Flow Of Cultural Goods And Services And Increase The Mobility Of Artists And Cultural Professionals
SDG: SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 10 - Reduce inequality within and among countries,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Mobility of artists and cultural professionals
Agency Implementation: The Swedish-Icelandic Collaboration Fund
Main Feature: The Swedish-Icelandic Collaboration Fund was established in 1995 following a gift from the Swedish government on the 50th anniversary of the republic of Iceland in 1994. This present to the nation was a monetary sum to be used to support the two nations’ cultural exchanges and laid the foundation for the Fund. The Fund’s aim is to promote Swedish-Icelandic cooperation and mutual cultural exchanges. Grants are allocated from the Fund for various cooperative projects, such as in the fields of science; social work; educational matters; and cultural matters. Funding is provided to individual projects of different types, though for the last few years the Fund has only allocated travel grants. Allocations are decided by the board of the Fund, which is made up of three individuals from each country.
Results: The Swedish-Icelandic Collaboration Fund has provided a solid foundation for collaboration and shared cultural expressions between the two nations. Through the Fund, collaborative projects between the two nations have become more accessible and the free flow of artists and ideas between the two countries is further supported. Ultimately it supports artists in their ability to work and enable communications within a larger cultural setting, leading to a richer overall cultural environment for both nations, leading to potential enrichment in other facets of society.

Title EN: The World Conference on Culture and Arts Education 2024
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture

Area of Monitoring: Cultural and creative sectors
Agency Implementation: Department of Culture and Tourism – Abu Dhabi. Ministry of Culture.
Main Feature: The World Conference on Arts and Culture Education, held in Abu Dhabi from 13 to 15 February 2024, is an international gathering organized by UNESCO and hosted by the United Arab Emirates. The conference brought together over 90 ministers of education and culture, along with policymakers, UN agencies and other stakeholders from around the world. The primary objective was to discuss and develop a global framework for arts and culture education, building on previous UNESCO initiatives such as the 2006 Lisbon Conference and the 2010 Seoul Agenda. The updated framework for arts and culture education Key features of the conference include: • Adoption of the global framework: The event aimed to adopt a comprehensive framework for integrating arts and culture education into national education systems around the world. This includes promoting equitable access to arts and culture education, enhancing lifelong learning, and leveraging digital technologies and artificial intelligence in arts education. • Thematic discussions: The conference included sessions on various topics, such as institutionalizing arts and culture education systems, partnerships and financing, and monitoring and researching data on cultural education. • Cultural exchange and performances: Alongside the conference, there were exhibitions, performances and interactive sessions showcasing the UAE’s cultural heritage and promoting intercultural dialogue.
Results: The Adoption of the Art and Culture Education framework.

Title EN: THEATER - grant programme
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture
SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Cultural and creative sectors
Agency Implementation: Ministry of Culture and National Heritage
Main Feature: The strategic goal of the program is to support the most valuable phenomena and trends in contemporary theatre. The program aims to support initiatives that cultivate tradition and reference the most outstanding achievements of dramatic theatre, as well as projects focused on creating new values, often engaging in critical discourse on contemporary reality and exploring original means of artistic expression.  The program's tasks include supporting comprehensive projects, both those implemented outside the standard frameworks of the applicants' current activities and those fitting into a consistently implemented development plan that significantly elevates the level of these activities. The primary goal of the program is to support non-commercial endeavours. Due to the nationwide scope of the program, an important goal is to highlight the most valuable projects carried out outside the largest cultural and economic centres of Poland, in regions with limited access to cultural goods. However, this goal does not imply the conduct of ad hoc or interventionist activities but rather support for initiatives with their own, original formula of participation in culture, which, due to their innovativeness, can be a source of inspiration also from a national perspective.  Endeavours that achieve the fundamental goals of the program should showcase the full spectrum of stage creativity, creating a distinctive showcase of contemporary Polish culture.
Results: Program of the Minister of Culture and National Heritage “Theatre”  [for the year 2020 the name of the program was: “Theatre and Dance” and it covered both fields of artistic activity] Number of funded projects: 456 Amount of funds allocated for subsidies: 47,778,786.70 PLN
Recommandations: The main conclusion concerning the program, is the importance of that multimedia activities, and digital space in the implementation of projects. Therefore projects carried out entirely online are permitted since 2020. These activities present and popularize achievements in the fields of theatre and other performing arts in the following forms: -	Creative and educational activities, including workshops, webinars, e-learning courses, video blogs, and podcasts conducted online, aimed at enhancing the cultural competencies of the task's recipients or transmitting unique knowledge and skills. -	Competitions, short audiovisual forms made available on the Internet, concerts, performances, readings, recitals, meetings with creators/artists. -	Making recordings of the aforementioned cultural events available. -	Providing and reusing digital audiovisual resources, creating websites or applications that popularize digital resources, developing and modernizing websites, online games, and mobile applications.  Since 2020, these activities have been promoted with the possibility of obtaining up to 100% funding from the budget of the Ministry of Culture and National Heritage. The change that occurred in this way is a consequence of the situation related to the pandemic, but at the same time it carries implications that align with the EU's goals related to digital transformation as one of the key elements of the Union's economic development and strategic autonomy. Through the implementation of online projects, new competencies are being developed in the art market, both among recipients and applicants.
