Title EN: Timișoara 2023 - European Capital of Culture
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture
SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Cultural and creative sectors
Agency Implementation: Centre of Projects of Timisoara City Council, Centre For Culture and Arts of Timiș County Council and  Association Timișoara 2023 European Capital of Culture.
Main Feature: Following the Decision no. 445/2014/EU of the European Parliament and the Council and the Decision 2229/2020, which regulates the European Capitals of Culture action for the years 2020-2033, and the competition organized by the Ministry of Culture, Timisoara was nominated European Capital of Culture (ECOC) in 2021, by Order of the Minister of Culture no. 3867 of 25.10.2016.  Due to the sanitary crisis generated by the COVID-19 pandemic, the holding of the title for the cities declared European Capitals of Culture in 2021 was postponed to 2023. In this regard, the Decision (EU) No 2229/2020 of the European Parliament and of the Council of December 23, 2020, published in the Official Journal of the European Union, was issued. The Government of Romania, through the Ministry of Culture, financially supported the implementation of the Program "Timisoara - European Capital of Culture in 2023", with multiannual funding, assumed in the city bid-book. "Timisoara - European Capital of Culture in 2023" was a national program of strategic importance and that generated substantial benefits in the cultural, social and economic fields, both during the year of winning the title and afterwards.
Results: Timișoara 2023 came with a challenge: the ECOC slogan “Light up the city through you!” meant to light up the city together with its citizens bright curiosity, love of art and respect for diversity, determination to step forward and take a stand for shared European values. Within the ECOC 2023 Program, the main focus is the promotion of Timișoara's European journey, through which the city offers European and international partners the opportunity to present its culture as part of our common European heritage. The Banat region has been a cultural melting pot over the centuries, being the place that currently hosts over 30 cultural communities, among which are Romanians, Roma, Germans, Hungarians, Serbs, Croatians, Italians, Romanians, Spanish and Bulgarians. This cultural palette represents the added value of the city, as it established the emergence of public entities dedicated especially to European citizens settled in Timişoara. The capital of the historical province of Banat, Timişoara is the seat of Timiş county and the cultural and economic center of the western part of Romania. With a population of 306,500, the city crossed by the Bega River has long maintained its reputation as a western, cross-border, young and entrepreneurial city. The ECOC Timisoara2023 program benefits from broad and consistent political support, as well as sustainable commitment from local, regional and national authorities. In the period 2019-2024, the Ministry of Culture coordinated the amendment of the national legislation, so that the legal and budgetary framework necessary for the implementation of the ECOC National Program would be ensured in due time. I.	The ECOC Cultural Program was built in the balance between the specific subjects of the program and the diversity of cultural interventions based on the following ten criteria: 	artistic and interdisciplinary excellence, which shows originality and/or quality. Proposals must creatively combine different artistic forms, but also combine arts and culture with other sectors (social, educational and economic). The combination of traditional art forms with new, innovative and experimental cultural expressions will be encouraged; 	European dimension, highlighting the wealth of cultural diversity in Europe. A wide range of possibilities will be encouraged, from creative exchanges to sustainable partnerships and co-productions between existing initiatives such as festivals and new partners; 	audience development: projects will address one or more levels of public engagement, participation and information: to inspire self-expression, to receive user-generated cultural content, encourage co-creation or engage and train volunteers. Proposals are encouraged to include vulnerable groups and/or address social issues; 	cooperation between the established cultural institutions and emerging independent groups and artists, local or international; 	contribution to the openness and accessibility of the city, integrating neglected dimensions; 	promoting heritage and new technological encounters: in accordance with the programs of the European Digital Agenda, projects will promote open and collective cultural content platforms, and offer citizens the opportunity to acquire advanced skills for content production, access and circulation; 	culture as an engine of development and innovation: the projects will promote new forms of cultural and creative entrepreneurship, the creation of new employment opportunities in the CCI sector and the contribution to the transformation of Timisoara and Banat into a centre of cultural creativity; 	encouraging the educational component through the active involvement of schools and promoting cooperation with educational institutions from different European countries.  	the development of the tourism sector, the locations of the events will be spread equally in the city and in the surroundings, covering the entire region; 	long-lasting heritage, in accordance with the city's cultural strategy, will be evaluated in terms of sustainable cultural, social and economic impact.  II.	The results of the ECOC Cultural Program in numbers: The current main production of the Timisoara2023 Program corresponds to a number of more than 2000 cultural events, such as: 	350 concerts; 	300 art exhibitions; 	130 festivals; 	120 film screenings; 	350 dance and theatre performances; 	300 artistic workshops and cultural mediation; 	80 specialized conferences; 	over 400 national and international press articles and radio/TV/online broadcasts launched so far about the Timisoara 2023 program; 	more than 300 national and international press materials are planned to be released by the end of 2023, including the closing event in December 2023; 	the involvement of over 5000 artists, cultural managers and other cultural professionals and 2500 volunteers at cultural events; 	over 700,000 tourists who visited Timişoara in 2023; 	over 20 cultural infrastructure objectives refurbished: cinemas, theatres, museums, cultural and multifunctional centres and spaces. III.	The Heritage of the ECOC Cultural Program: One of the most important legacies of the TM2023 Program is that it should increase sensitivity to the European diversity. The legacy the city has already witnessed throughout 2023 is the transformative power that culture can bring to people's everyday lives. The "journey" through the year 2023 is mapped with the intention of awakening a change in the city and in the region, in order to create conditions for a sustainable transformation. The legacy of TM2023 will constitute a significant contribution to European cultural development, but also a decisive moment for the city of Timișoara, which entered the great family of European cultural capitals. Last but not least, the cultural heritage of the Program will provide a more competitive cultural and creative scene with international partners and the ability to engage in European networks, viable legal solutions for sponsorships, transparent funding of the independent cultural sector and well-developed regional strategies. Citizens are encouraged to reclaim neglected neighbourhoods. The public development strategy will also increase critical thinking and participation in the cultural life of the city. These are the expected results that make all the efforts of the community worth it - to leave Timisoara to the next generation, in a better shape than the one in which it was found. The bright light of hope and community will be lit up, while recovering and giving a contemporary meaning to the "spirit of Timișoara".
Financial Ressources: The Government multiannual contribution at the ECOC Program Tm2023 raises at the total secured value of 36 million USD, comprising 11 million USD for the Cultural Program and 25 million USD for the Infrastructure Program. Main Feature: *Cultural domains covered by the policy/measure: Cultural and creative   Main aims: Making processed information available to creative and cultural professionals on inward and outward mobility and advising them on administrative and organisational matters arising in cross-border work which pertain to artistic, curatorial and organisational practice  Target groups: Artists and cultural professionals living in Germany who are planning and implementing international projects, representatives of cultural institutions or groups in Germany who are working with artists from other countries, artists and cultural professionals from other countries who are working temporarily in Germany or wish to do so, and artists from non-EU countries who wish to establish themselves in Germany      Expected results: •	Processing some 1000 requests for advice each year •	Organising and conducting about 10 workshops and networking events and 10 to 15 workshops for external organisations
Results: New in the 2020-2023 reporting period (Information on the previous funding period of this measure can be found in the third periodic report.): •	Touring Artists portal expanded to include information on entry and residence regulations, on social insurance in the international context, on tax deduction at source and on drawing welfare benefits in Germany for artists who have fled Ukraine •	Information portal relaunched, one new feature being a step-by-step guide providing tailored answers to questions regarding international art projects •	Brexit Infopoint service tool developed to alleviate new obstacles to German-British collaboration resulting from Brexit •	More European Mobility Information Points (MIPs) created to intensify information exchanges and experience-sharing within the framework of the On the Move organisation  •	Between 150,000 and 200,000 hits recorded on the website in 2023

Recommandations: There has been NO evaluation, BUT a user survey was conducted in 2021, consultations are normally documented, statistics are compiled and website use is analysed.          The user survey yielded the following findings: particularly with regard to taxation and social insurance in the international context as well as matters concerning visas and residence law, the provision of information and advice significantly facilitated international cultural activity. The Touring Artists services provide an important point of contact, especially for smaller groups and ensembles. Consultations enable them to establish themselves more quickly in the German cultural sector, and their careers often develop an international scope within one to two years.

Main Feature: The Touring Ventures programme aims to support broader, cost-effective opportunities for the nation’s cultural output to be viewed, participated in and enjoyed within South Africa and abroad. The objectives are:  •	To increase the audience and exposure that each production receives which will in turn increase jobs created, livelihoods supported, and income generated through the events.  •	To enhance the social cohesion in the country by promoting diversity of content and audiences in the specific the location of the project.  •	To increase the up-skilling opportunities for creative practitioners and communities.  •	To support the national, provincial and local government, cultural institutions, cultural agencies, arts groupings and individual arts practitioners in a reciprocal and sustainable approach to touring.  •	The development of new audiences for existing work development  •	Creating market access through annual programmes aimed at the development and promotion of young artists.
Results: The achievement is based on the projects that have been assisted to travel annually through the MGE Open Call and those that receive invitation and are approved by the department to travel referred to as Unsolicited Touring Ventures.  The MGE Open Call will have more/less the following outputs: In 2024-25, 24 projects approved In 2023-24, 19 projects approved In 2022-23, projects were rolled over In 2021-22, 50 Projects approved In 2019-20, 20 Projects approved 2018-19, 32 Projects approved 2017-18, 78 Projects approved Unsolicited Touring Ventures also have a number of projects for the years that have adjudication and budgets allocation.
Recommandations: The main conclusion was:  The study, based on the preliminary analysis of the desktop and documentary analysis components of selected MGE work streams, reveals that there remains a high reliance on public sector funding which includes DSAC and other national as well as provincial and local government departments. Thus, the economic/ financial sustainability of the MGE strategy is likely to be challenging, and new approaches and funding models should be considered as proposed in this research. The MGE strategy contributes substantially to social sustainability, including social cohesion, job creation, audience exposure and training. However, some need to be assisted to improve audience development and job creation. Additionally, more attention needs to be paid to environmental sustainability considerations.   The recommendations highlighted the following:  -Policy Changes -Improved Knowledge Data Management  -Training and Capacity Development  -Funding Framework

Title EN: Training programme in dance and choreography as promoting mobility of artists
Goal: Achieve A Balanced Flow Of Cultural Goods And Services And Increase The Mobility Of Artists And Cultural Professionals
SDG: SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 10 - Reduce inequality within and among countries,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Mobility of artists and cultural professionals
Agency Implementation: Association Danse Esprit Ravanne
Main Feature: Achieving a balanced flow of cultural goods and services and promoting the mobility of cultural professionals has been our mission for years.  Initially, through our dance school and company and more recently via the Artistic Association "Danse Esprit Ravanne', we have established comprehensive training programs in dance, choreography and music.  These programs have consistently been delivered professionally across various occasions and services.  We provide dance entertainment for specific tourism venues such as in hotels, allowing a cosmopolitan audience to discover Mauritian culture through its cultural diversity, showcasing multi ethnic dances and music.  In doing so, we support other artists - musicians who create original instruments highly appreciated by tourists and now exported abroad as artistic goods.  The same venues have hosted newly organised events, such as luxurious weddings, where dance shows are in high demand.  These group dance performances naturally attract international interest.  Additionally, we participate in other local and international events - conferences, product launches and business presentations - where dance performances play an essential role in entertainment and association.  In recent years, the expanding film industry in Mauritius has significantly increased the demand for dancers, choreographers and dance performances, both as featured acts and as support for acting.  Simultaneously, there has been a growing interest in dance creation.  Our training, information dissemination and awareness-raising efforts have encouraged performers from various dance styles to engage into dance creation.  This has opened doors to international opportunities such as invitations to festivals, biennales and other dance events.  We have successfully invited professional dancers and choreographers to conduct training, workshops and performances, fostering artistic collaborations and building bridges between Mauritius and the international community.  Our ongoing collaboration with new choreographers includes training and preparing them for new opportunities, enabling them to participate in dance events abroad and welcoming international dance artists.  This artistic collaboration encompasses multidisciplinary artists - musicians, visual artists and singers - who continuously participate both locally and internationally.  This large and diverse artistic platform exemplifies our commitment to cultural exchange and professional mobility.
Results: Our initial efforts led to the establishment of our first professional structure, complete with a dedicated team for logistics, administration and technical support. This foundation laid the groundwork for our economic stability, beginning with an office staffed with adequate personnel and a budget covering all expenses, including salaries and operational costs. We have developed suitable and well-equipped dance spaces, including a professional dance school that offers training to children, youth, adults and underprivileged children.  Our ongoing training programs have produced semi-professional dancers and choreographers, representing a new generation of dance artists. Our achievements have attracted media interest, resulting in press articles and various television appearances.  This exposure has drawn other partners to our dance activities, leading to increased funding and sponsorships. This marked the beginning of our mobility.  We have travelled to dance events to showcase our work, attend other performances and workshops and establish our initial network.  This international exposure facilitated valuable contacts, communication, learning opportunities and visibility on the global stage. Our progress has been tangible, with ongoing dance research and continuous invitations to festivals, workshops, training sessions and other dance events.  This has contributed to the development of a dance archive and a distinctive dance identity. Continuous artistic exchanges between us and international artists have led to numerous dance events in Mauritius, culminating in the creation of the first international dance festival in Mauritius, SAGAM.  This festival consistently invites international dance artists from various countries and styles, including France, Greece, India, different parts of Africa, Reunion Island, Rodrigues Island and Seychelles.  This event has attracted a diverse audience, both local and international, reflecting the multi-ethnic nature of Mauritius.  The festival features a variety of dance styles, including, Indian, afro, hip-hop and more showcasing cultural diversity through dance.  Our goal is to maintain and promote this unique dance identity, rooted in our insular and multi-ethnic heritage and to continue nurturing these essences through our work.

Title EN: WIPO Copyright Treaty (WCT) and WIPO performances and Phonograms Treaty (WPPT) – “Also known as the “Internet Treaties”
Goal: Achieve A Balanced Flow Of Cultural Goods And Services And Increase The Mobility Of Artists And Cultural Professionals
SDG: SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 10 - Reduce inequality within and among countries,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Treaties and agreements
Cultural Domain: Design,Performing Arts,Media Arts,Cinema and Audiovisual Arts,Music,Publishing,Visual Arts
Agency Implementation: Copyright Office of Tanzania
Main Feature: The WIPO Copyright Treaty (WCT) is a special agreement under the Berne Convention which deals with the protection of works and the rights of their authors in the digital environment. In addition to the rights recognized by the Berne Convention, they are granted certain economic rights. The WIPO Copyright Treaty was adopted in Geneva on 20th December, 1996, desiring to develop and maintain the protection of the rights of authors in their literary and artistic works in a manner as effective and uniform as possible. The WIPO Performances and Phonograms Treaty (WPPT) deals with the rights of two kinds of beneficiaries, particularly in the digital environment: (i) performers (actors, singers, musicians, etc.); and (ii) producers of phonograms (persons or legal entities that take the initiative and have the responsibility for the fixation of sounds). These rights are addressed in the same instrument, because most of the rights granted by the Treaty to performers are rights connected to their fixed, purely aural performances (which are the subject matter of phonograms).The Treaty provides that performers and producers of phonograms have the right to a single equitable remuneration for the direct or indirect use of phonograms, published for commercial purposes, broadcasting or communication to the public. The WCT and the WPPT entered into force on March 6, 2002, and May 20, 2002, respectively. Each treaty had to be ratified or acceded to by 30 countries before it entered into force. The countries which have adhered to the treaties come from all regions of the world, and include both developing and developed countries. The purpose of the two new WIPO treaties is to update and improve the protection of the already existing copyright and related rights treaties. The WCT and WPPT provide responses to the challenges of the new digital technologies. Both treaties require countries to provide a framework of basic rights, allowing creators to control and/or be compensated for the various ways in which their creations are used and enjoyed by others. Most important at the beginning of the new millennium, the treaties ensure that the owners of those rights will continue to be adequately and effectively protected when their works are disseminated through new technologies and communications systems such as the Internet. The treaties thus clarify, first, that the traditional right of reproduction continues to apply in the digital environment, including to the storage of material in digital form in an electronic medium. Second, they clarify that the owners of rights can control whether and how their creations are made available online to individual consumers at a time and a place chosen by the consumer, e.g., at home via the Internet.
Results: The responsible entities had already discussed the protocols/Treaties, waiting to conduct a meeting with stakeholders to have their views then it will be submitted to the ministerial level.  Following all necessary procedures, the treaties will be signed in our nation.

Title EN: Visual arts, music, audiovisual arts and books Sectoral assesment of gender gaps, barriers and inequalities.

Agency Implementation: Ministry of Cultures, Arts and Heritage.
Main Feature: Between 2019 and 2022, from within MINCAP, studies are carried out through a public bid, for the analysis of four cultural fields (visual arts, music, audiovisual arts and books) with the goal of having a diagnosis of gender gaps and barriers in different sectors, and to identify courses of action for a better incorporate a gender approach within institutional activities of the Undersecretariat of Cultures and Arts. These studies are:  (a) “Women artists in the visual arts sphere: gender gaps, barriers and inequalities in the Chilean artistic sector” (free translation) (Isónoma, 2019)  (b) “Women in the music sphere: gender barriers and gaps in the Chilean artistic sector” (free translation) (CPO, 2020),  (c) “Women in the audiovisual sphere: gaps and barriers in the Chilean artistic sector” (free translation) (CPO, 2021) and (d) “Women in the book sphere: gender barriers and gaps' (free translation) (CPO, 2022)43.  With this measure, a gender perspective is sought for integration in MINCAP's institutional activities, through the dignosis and dissemination of statistics, analysis and guidelines with a focus on gender for the design of strategies and actions which help eliminate gaps, barriers and inequalities in the sector. Specifically, the measure contributes to:  (a) Raising awareness of accurate and official data on gaps between women and men regarding the access to, use of, control of and involvement in the distribution of resources, services, opportunities and benefits, as well as the exercise of ther rights and freedoms, as a fundamental basis for the design, implementation and monitoring of public policy.  (b) Generating a system of institutional information that facilitates information on the state and performance of the cultural sector, in a way that both civil servants as wall as the public and the artistic community in general (guilds, collectives, unions, associations) can grow their plans of action and create internal policies that contribute to eliminating gender inequalities, gaps and barriers present in the sector.  (c) Providing knowledge and recommendations for incorporating measures in order to imporve the standard of living and work for women on the decent cultural work agenda and the legislation bill regarding the cultural worker statute.  (d) Providing knowledge and guidelines of civil servants in the Service for mainstreaming of the gender approach in internal and external management, specifically in order to help with reducing obstacles and improving work and personal conditions of female workers in the sector.
Results: Identifying and characterising gender barriers and inequalities in cultural participation of women artists in the fields of visual arts, audiovisual arts, music and books, as far as their sepcific fields of pursuit, allowed determening areas where gender inequalities and barriers to equality exist and the having data in order to gauge its nature and magnitude.  Recommendations have been prepared based on these discoveries, aimed at reducing the identified gender gaps, and establishing, with clarity, measures which the Undersecretariat of Cultures and Arts can adopt in order to promote gender equality, taking into consideration the Sustainable Development Goals on the matter. Some of these recommendations are:  (a) To support the dissemination of the artistic work of women, through specific measures that promote equal participation of women within dissemination, distribution and mobility opportunities.  (b) To include in the Book Fund, specifically in the mobility category, care of children as a measure of support for mothers dedicated to book field.  (c) To give more public coverage to awards given to women, as well as to create specific categories within the national awards, oriented towards women, be they for works or career.  (d) Public awareness campaigns on gender gaps, inequalities and barriers.  (e) to consider childcare within the items funded by FONDART, in a way that if the artist's project has been selected and they have children, they can count on a sum for childcare, guaranteeing their work space.  (f) Development of mentorship opportunities for women artists.  (g) To raise awareness regarding the bill on salary equality.  (h) Inclusion with a gender approach in criticism.  (I) To strengthen the role of exhibition spaces, such as museums and galleries, and specially those that obtain public funding, which should take an active and key role in reducing gender inequalities, gaps and barriers. For that, the recommendation is for those spaces to carry out, at the very least, the following activities:  (j) To offer training (in the form of courses, seminars, etc) around art by women and feminist art.  (k) To connect with artist associations and collectives, generating alliances in order to diversify the scene and generate more spaces for production by women. Title EN: Working and Living Conditions of Artists in Northern Ireland Report
Goal: Promote Human Rights And Fundamental Freedoms
SDG: SDG 5 - Achieve gender equality and empower all women and girls,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels
Area of Monitoring: Artistic freedom
Agency Implementation: Arts Council of Northern Ireland
Main Feature: The Arts Council of Northern Ireland (ACNI) commissioned Perspective Economics to conduct a comprehensive study on the working and living conditions of artists in Northern Ireland.     The study involved participatory research through an online survey, which gathered 481 responses from a diverse range of artists across various demographics, career stages, and artistic disciplines. The research develops an enhanced evidence base to help understand the key challenges and barriers facing artists, advocate for artists, and consider new ways of supporting the sector. The research builds a detailed, up-to-date estimate of income and working conditions across the entire arts sector, capturing the breadth of artist experiences and the unique challenges they face. It also explores artist views on the availability and impact of existing support and gathers insights on new forms of support they would welcome.
Results: The study involved participatory research through an online survey, which gathered 481 responses from a diverse range of artists across various demographics, career stages, and artistic disciplines. The research develops an enhanced evidence base to help understand the key challenges and barriers facing artists, advocate for artists, and consider new ways of supporting the sector. The research builds a detailed, up-to-date estimate of income and working conditions across the entire arts sector, capturing the breadth of artist experiences and the unique challenges they face. It also explores artist views on the availability and impact of existing support and gathers insights on new forms of support they would welcome.
Recommandations: The report has highlighted the following conclusions and/or recommendations:      Policymakers should set out a clear strategy for measuring and increasing audiences, growing the sector, and recognising the relational and distributional impacts of supporting the whole arts ecosystem on a long-term basis.    Throughout this research, artists have highlighted the positive impact that individual and organisational grants can have upon growing their careers and providing support through challenging times. There is also a recognition that demand is significantly higher than the volume of grants available to artists, and this can be challenging for artists that may seek additional support to record or write new material or commission new pieces of work.     There is a need for policy to consider, for example: increasing public investment in the arts, supporting local artists access wider local, national, and international funding schemes, unlocking additional private investment, and/or streamlining the funding process and accounting for the differences in applying for funding to different types of artists.     It is important to explore novel mechanisms and advocacy for the arts at various levels. This could include: the role of an arts champion as an advocate for the arts, exploring a basic income scheme for artists, and/or alternative funding models.     Within this survey research, artists frequently cited that access to affordable studio or performance space was a key barrier. This suggests policy interventions to help with: providing artists with access to affordable studio or performance space to allow them to create, sell and perform their work and/or providing artists with support for exhibitions, fairs, and events to showcase their work.    Growing the sector and supporting access to commercial opportunities is vital to supporting artists. However, the research also highlights a need for policy to consider how to best provide artists with opportunities to innovate and risk-take. Policy interventions should aim to create an environment that supports risk-taking and innovation by providing funding, resources, and platforms for artists to explore new creative avenues. This can involve investing in research and development grants, supporting the creation of experimental works, and promoting collaborations between artists and professionals from other disciplines.     Further, providing training and learning opportunities to develop artist talent and prepare them for the professional landscape is also highly important. The report highlights the importance of providing diverse training and learning opportunities to develop artist talent and provide them with the tools needed for the professional landscape.

Title EN: Guidelines on cultural ethics (1) & A follow-up study 2022 on harassment and other inappropriate treatment in the film and theatre industry (2)
Goal: Promote Human Rights And Fundamental Freedoms
SDG: SDG 5 - Achieve gender equality and empower all women and girls,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels
Area of Monitoring: Gender equality
Agency Implementation: Ministry of Education and Culture   Forum Artis
Main Feature: a) In 2021, the Ministry of Education and Culture commissioned the organisation representing the arts and culture sector - Forum Artis - to draw up guidelines on cultural ethics in cooperation with actors in the sector. The assignment was based on problems in the sector related to, for example, gender equality and sexual harassment. The pilot version of the guidelines launched 31 December 2022.      Since the newly formulated ethical guidelines are the first of it’s kind, it was introduced as a pilot version. Forum Artis expresses its readiness to gather experiences with the guidelines, test their applicability, and compile any potential need for changes as a basis for further development.   In 2023, Forum Artis conducted a survey on its website, where individuals who have experienced misconduct could anonymously report ongoing or up to two years old (since 2021) issues related to harassment or other unethical conduct. The cases are compiled and analyzed to gain a better understanding of the types of ethical problems.      b )The Ministry of Education and Culture commissioned a report from Jaana Paanetoja, LL. D., in 2018 on sexual harassment and inappropriate treatment in the film and theatre industries. Changes were then implemented in these industries over the course of four years. For this reason, a further study was deemed necessary in 2022 to examine what improvements have been made and in which areas attention should be placed in the future.    Based on the responses to a questionnaire drawn up by Mitro Kaurinkoski, it transpired that both sexual harassment and inappropriate treatment have been taken seriously and that changes are in progress, but the pace is slow. The parties have drawn up guidelines, recruited harassment contact persons for film and theatre productions, and the issue has been integrated into the education and training in the industries. However, the responses in the report show that problems still exist and much remains to be done.    One common denominator in the industries is that employment relationships are often atypical, which easily exposes employees to wrong kinds of power positions and puts employees in a vulnerable position. Lack of resources, both time and money, is also considered to increase the risk of inappropriate treatment. The report also highlighted the importance of establishing a body to address ethical issues in the cultural sector and the need to set up an anonymous reporting channel. These would help small operators in particular. It is important to continue discussion and monitoring.
Results: A) The guidelines on cultural ethics have sparked a lot of discussion about practices and inappropriate treatment in the arts and culture sector. Since the website has only been open and data has been collected for about a year, the collected data has not yet been analyzed.      B) The audiovisual sector has launched several surveys and actions in order to tackle this large problem. Though problems still remain, the situation is brighter than it was five years ago.

Area of Monitoring: Media diversity
Agency Implementation: Te Puni Kōkiri Ministry of Māori Development
Main Feature: Describe the main features of the policy/measure: Māori media plays a vital role in providing broad public exposure to Māori language and culture and supporting people’s ability to speak te reo Māori.  The New Zealand Government supports a range of Māori media entities with the primary purpose of protecting, promoting and revitalising te reo Māori me ngā tikanga Māori:  Te Māngai Pāho Te Māngai Pāho is a Crown entity that was established by part 4A 41 of the Broadcasting Act under the Broadcasting Amendment Act 1993. Te Māngai Pāho is responsible for the promotion of Māori language and Māori culture and does this primarily by disbursing funds to promote Māori language and culture through television, iwi radio, music and other media.   Whakaata Māori Whakaata Māori was established by the Māori Television Service (Te Aratuku Whakaata Irirangi Māori) Act 2003. It is a statutory entity that provides a multichannel television service, including a dedicated Te Reo channel, an online presence, in te reo Māori and English in order to promote te reo Māori me ngā tikanga Māori and enrich New Zealand society.  Iwi radio stations There are currently 27 iwi radio stations broadcasting on 68 frequencies specifically reserved for the promotion of Māori language and culture. 21 of these stations receive government funding, and 20 of those stations are represented by a national representative body, Te Whakaruruhau o Ngā Reo Irirangi Māori (charitable trust) which formed in 1991.  Government funding  Government funding strengthens the Māori media sector to ensure its sustainability and provides content that reflects Māori language, culture, stories, and perspectives to support te reo Māori revitalisation and a shared national identity. Funding also supports growing the capacity and capability of the Māori media workforce, the operational functions of the Māori media sector and delivery across a range of platforms. Government funding for the Māori media sector through Vote Māori Development is distributed to Te Māngai Pāho (content funding) and Whakaata Māori (operational support but moving to also receiving direct content funding). In August 2022, the Government agreed a suite of actions to strengthen the Māori media sector, including time-limited additional funding of $NZD40 million in Budget 2022 and $NZD51 million in Budget 2023.
Results: In 2022/23 funding resulted in: •	$NZD85,259 worth of funding to Te Māngai Pāho to enable diverse content, including Māori music and Māori radio.  •	1242.30 hours of Māori content produced through Whakaata Māori, aimed at achieving the goal to reach for the vitality of te reo Māori. In 2022/23, Te Māngai Pāho funded innovative content such as supporting the Celebrate Matariki broadcast alongside New Zealand On Air, which was available on Whakaata Māori and Māori+, as well as free to air television channels (TVNZ One and TVNZ+, THREE, Pasifika TV, Prime), radio stations (Radio NZ, Iwi Radio), and other information channels (Stuff, and the national Matariki website). Over 2022/23, Whakaata Māori achievements in content production included the live broadcast of significant Māori events such as the 2023 Waka Ama National Sprint Championships, Waitangi Day celebrations, Te Matatini Herenga Waka Herenga Tangata Festival, and a Cyclone Gabrielle Relief Concert.

Title EN: Grant of support for creative work
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture
SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Partnering with civil society
Cultural Domain: Design,Performing Arts,Media Arts,Cinema and Audiovisual Arts,Music,Publishing,Visual Arts
Agency Implementation: Ministry of Culture
Main Feature: The aim of the measure is to support cultural creativity and the development of the fine arts at a professional level, and to improve the conditions necessary for the creative activities of creative persons through creative associations and to create relevant guarantees.   The measure is based on the Creative Persons and Artistic Associations Act. Under the Act, freelance creative persons who are engaged in creative activities as authors or performers and whose creative activities result in a specific work - the subject of copyright - can apply for creative support.   The measure is funded from the state budget, but its distribution is organised by the artistic associations. An artistic association is a non-profit organisation the purpose of which is to promote one artistic field and support the creative activities of its member creators. There are 17 recognised artistic associations in Estonia, covering the creative fields of architecture, audiovisual art, design, performing arts, sound art, literature, visual arts and stenography etc.   The artistic association’s grant is paid once a year to recognised artistic associations on the basis of the number of members. The artistic association will use the grant to pay grants to its members, where possible, bursaries for creative activities and related training and to cover the costs of organising related activities. An artist is eligible if she/he has been engaged in creative work for at least the last three years and her/his works have been published or have been made available to the public during that period.   A freelance artist can apply for a grant in two ways: members of an artistic association apply to their association; freelance artists who do not belong to any association, apply to the Ministry of Culture.
Results: As social and employment policies tend to be reactive in the cultural sector, it is important for freelancers in the cultural sector to increasingly provide grants to support creative activities. In 2020 in particular, creative support was vitally necessary for freelancers and helped to compensate for the lack of work because of pandemics. The grant has strengthened the message to society that creative work by freelance artists should be considered as an activity equivalent to work and this work is as important as anyone else’s.
Financial Ressources: For the period 2020-2023 the total sum was 11 766 883 USD, including extra support for mitigating the impact of COVID-19.-19
Recommandations: Policy recommendation: Expand the range of activities that may be supported with a grant of support for creative work. Art forms and their importance are constantly changing and emerging. Naming more general fields of activity instead of individual activities makes it possible to treat creative areas more equally and to keep pace with the emergence of new art forms.   Policy recommendation: Ensure that current and new grants and scholarships provided by the Ministry of Culture, the Cultural Endowment and other institutions would always cover the social tax paid on them. By paying the social tax, it is ensured that the recipient also receives - health insurance, pension qualifying period, parental benefit. Depending on the nature of the specific benefit, consideration should also be given to taking into account unemployment insurance premiums for seniority in office in the event of unemployment.

Title EN: Helvetiarockt : Diversity Roadmap – « Violences sexualisées »
Goal: Promote Human Rights And Fundamental Freedoms
SDG: SDG 5 - Achieve gender equality and empower all women and girls,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels
Area of Monitoring: Artistic freedom
Agency Implementation: Helvetiarockt
Main Feature: La Feuille de route pour la diversité fournit de bonnes raisons, des recommandations simples et des mesures réalisables pour créer des espaces préservés de toute discrimination. Elle a été lancée en 2019 par Helvetiarockt avec le soutien de PETZI (Fédération suisse des clubs et des festivals de musiques actuelles). Elle est traduite en trois langues (français, italien et anglais) et elle est accessible sous forme numérique sur un site web accessible à toutes et tous sous www.diversityroadmap.org.  L’objectif est que la branche musicale reste vigilante et s'oppose fermement à toute discrimination, qu’elle adopte une approche respectueuse et implique le plus grand nombre possible de personnes. En collaboration avec les partenaires, Helvetiarockt formule régulièrement de nouveaux conseils et de nouvelles suggestions sur la manière d’organiser des manifestations, de proposer des programmes, d’améliorer la communication et de rendre les structures moins discriminatoires et plus respectueuses de la diversité.  Depuis 2022, Helvetiarockt agit sur le thème prioritaire des violences sexualisées dans le cadre de la Feuille de route pour la diversité. Un avant-projet, soutenu par le Bureau fédéral de l'égalité entre femmes et hommes (BFEG), a permis d’élaborer les bases pour la prévention et l'intervention contre la violence sexualisée dans les clubs et les festivals et de les préparer pour le public cible. Des représentantes et représentants de clubs et de festivals ont été questionnées et questionnés dans le cadre d'enquêtes quantitatives et qualitatives sur les mesures, les bonnes pratiques et les obstacles à leur mise en œuvre. Helvetiarockt voulait notamment savoir de quel soutien les représentantes et les représentants avaient besoin pour la mise en œuvre des mesures. Les résultats de ces enquêtes sont publiés sous forme d’un rapport sur https://diversityroadmap.org/sexualisierte-gewalt.  En conclusion, les clubs et festivals impliqués sont déjà sensibilisés au thème des violences sexualisées, mais se trouvent à différents stades de la mise en œuvre de mesures appropriées. Il manque des offres de formation à grande échelle. Les bases et le matériel, tels que les guides et les modèles, ne sont souvent pas adaptés pour les clubs et festivals ainsi qu'à leurs collaboratrices et collaborateurs, et à leur public (en majorité de jeunes adultes). Le grand défi consiste à impliquer tous les secteurs d'un club ou d'un festival (collaboratrices et collaborateurs, bénévoles ainsi que prestataires de services externes) dans un processus et à ancrer durablement les mesures.
Results: L'objectif était de créer un outil de sensibilisation et de réflexion pour le secteur de la musique. Cet objectif a été atteint grâce à la Feuille de route pour la diversité. Les initiatrices et initiateurs ont été invitées et invités à présenter la Feuille de route de la diversité dans des lieux très divers : festivals, centres culturels et Hautes écoles.   D'autres institutions et d'autres secteurs utilisent également la Feuille de route pour la diversité. L'organisation européenne Live DMA, un réseau de clubs et de festivals de musique en Europe, a également pris connaissance de la Feuille de route pour la diversité et l'a traduite en anglais. Depuis son lancement, la Feuille de route est perçue et diffusée tant au niveau national qu'international. Live DMA est également en train de traduire le rapport « Pas seulement des affiches dans les toilettes – rapport sur les violences sexualisées dans les clubs et les festivals en Suisse ». Le site web www.diversityroadmap.org a été traduit en quatre langues et il est accessible à toutes et à tous. Son contenu a été élargi et complété par les textes de sensibilisation et de prévention « Le genre est une galaxie » et « Violences sexualisées ».

The development of Swedish cultural life is dependent on international collaborations and influences from abroad. All government agencies and institutions that allocate funding to artists have international and intercultural perspectives as an integral part of their tasks.   There are numerous funding schemes for international cultural exchange for artists and independent groups based in Sweden.   -  Residencies for Swedish artists abroad (visual arts, dance, music etc.) for example in Addis Abeba, Austin, Bangalore, Berlin, Jingdezhen, Johannesburg, London, New York, Paris, Riga, Tokyo and Warsaw. They are administered by the Swedish Arts Grants Committee.   -  Support for art projects abroad, travel grants, touring, research trips and international co-operation etc., administered by the Swedish Arts Grants Committee, the Swedish Arts Council, the Swedish Performing Arts Agency and the Swedish Authors’ Fund.  -	Support from the Swedish Film Institute to launch and distribute Swedish films at festivals, markets and other cultural and commercial events.
Results: The opportunity for Swedish artists to be part of an international exchange and to have the opportunity to exhibit their art on an international arena is important for the artistic development, for a vital cultural life and increased opportunities for work for artists. The international context is increasingly important, as artists often need an international labour market to be professionally active. In 2023 the level of international activity had returned to the same levels as before the pandemic.  Europe and the Nordic countries dominated the geographical distribution of the Swedish Arts Grants Committee´s grants for international travel and exchange in 2023, but all continents were represented.  As for the grants of the Swedish Arts Council similar data is not available.  During the period 2020 – 2023 the Swedish Arts Council has initiated two new funding schemes, one to co-fund initiatives within the EU Creative Europe programme and one specific funding scheme to promote the internationalization of cultural sector.

Title EN: Here We Are

Area of Monitoring: National sustainable development policies and plans

Main Feature: Here We Are est un programme de recherche participative pratique développée avec et pour les artistes ayant récemment immigré en Suisse. Here We Are propose des activités, des initiatives, des services et des possibilités de financement sur mesure pour soutenir ces artistes dans la poursuite de leur carrière artistique en Suisse.  Here We Are donne des moyens d'action aux artistes ayant une expérience de la migration et œuvre pour leur inclusion. Le terme d'expérience migratoire désigne les migrantes et migrants de première génération qui ont généralement investi dans leurs études et leur pratique artistique dans leur pays d'origine avant de poursuivre leur carrière en Suisse. L'inclusion de nouveaux artistes dans la scène culturelle suisse n'accroît pas seulement sa diversité culturelle, mais renforce la cohésion sociale.  Les questions qui motivent Here We Are sont : •	Comment fonctionne le paysage artistique et culturel suisse ? •	Qui sont les protagonistes ? •	Comment fonctionnent les mécanismes de financement dans le domaine des arts et de la culture en Suisse ? •	À quels organismes de financement puis-je m'adresser ? •	Comment puis-je entrer en contact avec mes pairs ? •	Quelles sont les possibilités de formation ? •	Qui représente mes intérêts ? •	Où et comment puis-je partager et promouvoir mon travail ? •	Comment puis-je identifier et accéder aux ressources dont j'ai besoin ? •	Quel est mon statut juridique en tant qu'artiste en Suisse ? •	À quoi doit ressembler une demande de financement et/ou mon portfolio ?  Here We Are place des artistes de différentes disciplines, ayant vécu l'expérience de la migration, au centre de sa méthodologie. Le programme n'est pas conçu pour, mais plutôt avec des artistes qui ont émigré et vivent désormais en Suisse. Here We Are suit un processus participatif basé sur trois modules, qui reposent eux-mêmes sur des ateliers ciblés et mesurés.
Results: Les artistes sont introduits dans une nouvelle communauté de soutien. Elles et ils ont rencontré des pairs, des collaboratrices et collaborateurs et des mentors. Elles et ils ont acquis de nouvelles compétences, des idées et la confiance nécessaire pour parler de leur pratique et poursuivre un nouveau travail. Elles et ils ont acquis une meilleure compréhension de l'écosystème culturel suisse et sont désormais reconnus par un plus grand nombre d'institutions culturelles. Elles et ils ont développé de nouvelles relations et des projets de collaboration. Elles et ils ont une présence numérique et publique plus forte (voir : https://www.artlink.ch/directory) et sont mieux représentées et représentés dans la programmation des institutions culturelles suisses. Elles et ils produisent des œuvres innovantes et percutantes et sont reconnus pour cela. En conséquence, elles et ils ont amélioré leurs moyens de subsistance grâce à de nouvelles opportunités.

Main Feature: The Urusaro International Women Film Festival, like any successful film festival, can be measured and evaluated through various features to assess its effectiveness and impact. Here are the key features of the measure for the festival: Attendance and Participation: The festival's success can be measured by the number of attendees, including filmmakers, industry professionals, and general audiences, as well as the diversity and engagement levels of these participants. Film Submissions and Screenings: Evaluating the quantity and quality of film submissions, the variety of genres and cultural backgrounds represented, and audience turnout and reception at screenings provides insight into the festival's reach and impact. Media Coverage and Publicity: The extent and quality of media coverage, social media engagement, and overall publicity efforts are crucial for assessing the festival's visibility and public awareness. Impact on Filmmakers: The festival's influence on the careers of participating filmmakers, including new projects, awards, networking outcomes, and feedback on the support provided, indicates its effectiveness in advancing women's roles in cinema. Workshops and Educational Programs: The number and variety of educational activities, along with participant feedback and their impact on skill development, measure the festival's contribution to filmmaker education and professional growth. Economic Impact: Revenue from ticket sales, sponsorships, and the economic benefits to the local community, including hospitality and tourism, highlight the festival's financial impact. Cultural and Social Impact: The festival's influence on perceptions of women in cinema, contributions to cultural exchange, and engagement with social issues reflect its broader cultural and societal impact. Awards and Recognition: The number and significance of awards given, their impact on recipients, and the festival's recognition in the film community showcase its role in promoting excellence and gaining prestige. Festival Growth and Development: Year-on-year growth in size, scope, and influence, along with innovations, improvements, and strategic partnerships, indicate the festival's development and long-term sustainability.
Results: Since its establishment in 2015, the Urusaro International Women Film Festival has made significant strides in promoting gender equality and supporting women filmmakers. Here are some of its main achievements: Increased Participation and Diversity: The festival has seen a steady increase in the number of film submissions and attendees from diverse cultural and professional backgrounds,up to date we have received 415 films highlighting its growing international reach and inclusivity from just Africa to America, Asia and beyond. Prominent Platform for Women Filmmakers: Urusaro IWFF has become a significant platform for women filmmakers to showcase their work, gaining recognition and visibility in the global film industry. This has led to career advancements for many participants.    Influential Educational Programs: The festival has conducted numerous workshops, seminars, and panel discussions, contributing to the professional development and skill enhancement of emerging women filmmakers. Enhanced Media Coverage: The festival has attracted substantial media coverage, both locally and internationally, raising awareness about gender disparities in cinema and promoting the work of women filmmakers. Successful Networking Opportunities: Urusaro IWFF has facilitated networking and collaboration opportunities for filmmakers, industry professionals, and other stakeholders, fostering partnerships and mentorship relationships. Recognition and Awards: The festival has awarded numerous films and filmmakers, boosting their profiles and helping them secure further opportunities in the industry. as of this year 2024 in June, we have awarded 11 outstanding films in the 8th edition of Urusaro International Women Film Festival Economic and Cultural Impact: The festival has positively impacted the local economy through tourism and related activities. It has also contributed to cultural exchange and understanding by showcasing diverse narratives. Advocacy for Gender Equality: Urusaro has been a vocal advocate for gender equality in the film industry, influencing discussions and policies aimed at supporting women’s participation and leadership in cinema.

Title EN: UK-Japan Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement (CEPA)
Goal: Achieve A Balanced Flow Of Cultural Goods And Services And Increase The Mobility Of Artists And Cultural Professionals
SDG: SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 10 - Reduce inequality within and among countries,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Treaties and agreements
Agency Implementation: Department for Business and Trade
Main Feature: The UK-Japan Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement came into force on 1 January 2021. Some features of the agreement pertinent to the cultural and creative sectors include:   1. Intellectual Property Rights - The UK-Japan CEPA strengthens commitments to promoting the best standards of practice of collective management organisations. Regarding fair remuneration for the music industry, we have secured a commitment to discuss with Japan the right to remuneration of performers and producers of phonograms (any sound recording) when phonograms published for commercial purposes are used for broadcasting or for any communication to the public. We have secured text that ensures legal protection and remedies against the circumvention of technological protection measures and also on rights management information.  The agreement also includes provisions to tackle online infringement of intellectual property rights, such as film and music piracy. These include provisions on access to justice, enforcement in the digital environmental and public awareness measures in respect of websites registered outside of the territories of Japan and the UK, and criminal remedies for certain IP rights infringement. For example, encouraging the use of voluntary initiatives to tackle infringement and awareness-raising among the public.  On designs, the UK locked in revisions to Japan’s design law which allows for multiple designs in one application. This means, for instance, a fashion designer who has recently designed a new product line of trainers can file for design right protection for these new products in one go instead of previously having to send the applications separately, which is more time consuming and costly.  2. Goods - CEPA makes it easier for UK clothing producers to export to Japan under reduced tariffs. In particular, we have introduced rules which allow clothing producers to undergo a single process in the UK, and then export to Japan under tariff preference, as long as 50% of the inputs are sourced domestically.   The UK has negotiated customs provisions that minimise costs and administrative burdens, meaning Japanese consumers can get more of the British products they enjoy, and UK companies benefit through simpler and more predictable customs procedures.  3. Business Mobility - CEPA contains provisions on temporary movement of highly skilled professionals, including for architects and advertising professionals.  4. Small and Midsized Enterprises - The UK also secured a dedicated SME chapter that ensures that UK SMES are provided with tools and resources necessary to seize the opportunities of exporting to Japan. This includes securing a commitment to make information on doing business in Japan available to UK SMEs.

Title EN: Un mécanisme d’aide sociale circonstancielle de soutien aux artistes en difficulté.
Goal: Promote Human Rights And Fundamental Freedoms
SDG: SDG 5 - Achieve gender equality and empower all women and girls,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels
Area of Monitoring: Artistic freedom
Cultural Domain: Design,Performing Arts,Media Arts,Cinema and Audiovisual Arts,Music,Publishing,Visual Arts
Agency Implementation: Le Ministère des Affaires Culturelles via une convention de partenariat avec l’organisme tunisien des droits d’auteurs et droits voisins- OTDAV (établissement public non administratif (EPNA)
Main Feature: En l’absence d’un cadre juridique (loi) qui réglemente les aspects relatifs aux droits sociaux et économiques en relation avec les artistes et professionnels de la culture, et dans le cadre des efforts déployés par le Ministère des Affaires Culturelles pour faire face à la situation assez précaire de certains d’entre eux sur le plan social, professionnel et économique, un mécanisme d’aide sociale circonstancielle/(ponctuelle) est mis en place pour soutenir les artistes en difficulté et répondre à des situations d’urgence (en relation avec l’état de santé, des situations familiales précaires..). En effet, les raisons de cette précarité bien qu’elles méritent d’être analysées se manière approfondie, sont surtout liées au fait que dans le secteur culturel, les acteurs sont plus dans l’informel, sans adhésion à la sécurité sociale ni à l’organisme des droits d’auteurs et droits voisins ni même à la mutuelle des artistes.
Results: Au titre des années 2022-2023, le Ministère des Affaires Culturelles via l’organisme tunisien des droits d’auteurs et droits voisins (OTDAV) à travers la signature d’une convention de partenariat fixant les modalités de mise en œuvre de ce mécanisme d’aide au profit des artistes en difficulté, a contribué à faire bénéficier 2021 artiste et professionnel du secteur culturel du mécanisme d’aide circonstancielle pour un montant de 2.5 Millions de dinars.  Année	                                            Nbre de bénéficiaire	                                       Budget alloué  2022	                                                        1092	                                                 1,2 Millions de dinars 2023	                                                         929	                                                 1,3 Millions de dinars
Financial Ressources: En 2024 le Ministère des Affaires Culturelles a augmenté le montant du budget annuel alloué au titre des aides circonstancielles à 1,4 millions de dinars.
Recommandations: Le mécanisme d’aide circonstancielle est conçu pour gérer des situations exceptionnelles à caractère ponctuel. Pour que l’exception ne se transforme pas en principe ou en droit acquis, la mise en place de réformes structurelles sur le moyen et le long terme s’avère incontournable.  D’ailleurs et pour encourager les artistes bénéficiant de ce mécanisme à passer au secteur formel, le Ministère des Affaires Culturelles conditionne l’octroi des deuxième et troisièmes tranches d’aide à une adhésion à la mutuelle des artistes et à l’organisme des droits d’auteur et des droits voisins (OTDAV). La mise en place d’une loi qui réglemente la situation sociale et économique des artistes est nécessaire et la crise sanitaire CIVID-19 a mis exergue les lacunes et les défaillances du système de gouvernance de la scène culturelle et artistique.
