Title EN: Une diplomatie culturelle fondée sur le développement des échanges internationaux et la promotion de la mobilité des artistes
Goal: Achieve A Balanced Flow Of Cultural Goods And Services And Increase The Mobility Of Artists And Cultural Professionals
SDG: SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 10 - Reduce inequality within and among countries,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Mobility of artists and cultural professionals
Cultural Domain: Design,Performing Arts,Media Arts,Cinema and Audiovisual Arts,Music,Publishing,Visual Arts
Agency Implementation: Le Ministères des affaires culturelles (MAC) à travers la Direction de la Coopération Internationale et des relations étrangères (DCI)
Main Feature: La stratégie du Ministère des Affaires Culturelles (MAC) en matière de diplomatie culturelle est fondée sur deux objectifs clés : -	Favoriser le dialogue entre les cultures et promouvoir la diversité culturelle -	Promouvoir davantage l’image de la Tunisie à travers la culture et ce, en soutenant la création, la production et la diffusion de produits culturels à la fois diversifiés et ancrés dans l’identité nationale mais aussi adaptés aux attentes du public étranger. Ces deux objectifs clés se déclinent en actions mises en œuvre par le MAC notamment la Direction de la Coopération Internationale (DCI) qui travaille en étroite coordination avec les différentes directions artistiques sectorielles (cinéma, théâtre, arts plastiques, musique et danse …) et les institutions et organismes de référence sous tutelle du MAC notamment : •	Le centre national du cinéma et de l'image (CNCI),  •	Le centre international de Tunis pour l'économie culturelle numérique (TICDCE),  •	La bibliothèque nationale de Tunis (BNT),  •	Le centre des musiques arabes et méditerranéennes (CMAM),  •	Le musée d'art moderne et contemporain (MACAM), •	Le centre national de la marionnette (CNM) •	Le théâtre national de Tunis (TNT) •	Le théâtre de l'opéra de Tunis (TOT) •	L'agence de mise en valeur du patrimoine et de promotion culturelle (AMVPPC).. L'objectif étant de parvenir à : -	Promouvoir la diversité des expressions culturelles, -	Encourager l’échange d’expériences et d’expertise dans les différents domaines artistiques, -	Favoriser la mobilité des artistes, professionnels de la culture ainsi que les créateurs et acteurs culturels porteurs de projets innovants, -	 Contribuer à développer davantage les liens de coopération (sud – sud et nord –sud) et le réseautage entre professionnels et praticien.(nes) de la culture tunisien.(nes) et leurs homologues étrangers dans un esprit de dialogue et d’enrichissement mutuel. -	Favoriser de nouvelles perspectives de coopération au profit des artistes et professionnels de la culture à travers notamment les possibilités de coproduction, d’entrepreneuriat culturel et d’initiatives indépendantes. La mise en œuvre de ces objectifs stratégiques, qui cadrent parfaitement avec les objectifs de la convention 2005 (article 1 «stimuler l’interculturalité afin de développer l’interaction culturelle dans l’esprit de bâtir des passerelles entre les peuples»), pour le développement des échanges internationaux et la promotion de la mobilité artistique se manifeste notamment à travers : •	L’appui aux artistes, créateurs et professionnels de la culture tunisiens pour prendre part aux différentes manifestations culturelles à l’étranger (expositions, foires, festivals, symposiums et conférences …) couvrant la quasi-totalité des disciplines artistiques (arts dramatiques, audiovisuels, arts numériques, arts plastiques, livre et littérature, arts de la scène, musique et danse…) et ce, à travers la prise en charge par le MAC des frais afférents à ces participations (transport international et/ou hébergement et/ou acheminement des œuvres) en fonction de la demande des artistes. A cet égard et dans le but d’assurer une meilleure gouvernance de ce mécanisme d’appui à la mobilité des artistes tunisien.(nes), notamment en termes de transparence dans l’attribution des financements publics, un comité chargé d’examiner les demandes de subventions des participations culturelles à l’étranger, est créé au sein du MAC (arrêté ministériel en date du 08 Janvier 2024). Parmi ses attributions l’élaboration d’un manuel de procédures pour améliorer la gouvernance de ce mécanisme d’appui à la mobilité artistique (en cours d’élaboration). •	Par ailleurs et toujours dans le cadre de sa politique de promotion des échanges et de la mobilité artistique en application des programmes et accords bilatéraux de coopération culturelle conclus avec plusieurs pays, le MAC organise et accueille des activités culturelles diversifiées afin de promouvoir la culture tunisienne et offrir aux artistes un cadre propice pour nouer des contacts avec leurs homologues étrangers dans le but d’une éventuelle collaboration sous forme de coproductions, projets et partenariats culturels, résidences artistiques, ateliers de formations…). •	Outre ces actions d’appui aux artistes et d’échange dans le cadre de la coopération bilatérale (Nord–Sud et Sud-Sud), un programme annuel d’échange culturel international est mis en place par le MAC à travers lequel la Tunisie accueille des troupes artistiques diversifiées en provenance de plusieurs pays pour se produire dans le cadre des festivals internationaux (festival international de Carthage, Hammamet, El Jem …) mais aussi et surtout dans le cadre des festivals organisés dans les différentes régions du pays par le biais d’une programmation élaborée de manière collégiale (DCI, bureau des affaires régionales (BAR), les commissariats régionaux aux affaires culturelles (CRAC)..…). cette programmation prend en considération le principe de discrimination positive au profit des régions les plus défavorisées de l’intérieur du pays et la nature du public cible (notamment les jeunes et les femmes dans les régions défavorisées selon les critères de développement).  •	Cette dynamique d’échange et de coopération est fondée sur un maillage institutionnel assez important et une infrastructure culturelle qui couvre pratiquement tout le territoire national avec plus de 700 institutions culturelles selon le rapport  du MAC pour l’année 2021(des CRAC, des maisons de culture, des clubs culturels, un réseau de bibliothèques publiques, des Centres d’Arts Dramatiques, des sociétés de production …) sans oublier aussi la plateforme de diffusion des produits culturels dont dispose la Tunisie qui totalise presque 300 festivals en plus des grandes manifestations culturelles qu’organise le Ministère des Affaires Culturelles (journées cinématographiques de Carthage-JCC, journées théâtrales de Carthage- JTC, journées musicales de Carthage- JMC, Foire internationale du livre de Tunis- FILT..) •	Et afin de faciliter la mobilité des artistes et professionnels de la culture qui participent à ces manifestations, le Ministère des Affaires Culturelles (à travers la DCI) entreprend les démarches nécessaires pour faciliter l’obtention du visa d’entrée sur le territoire tunisien et vice versa en coordination avec le Ministère des Affaires Etrangères (MAE), le Ministère de l’Intérieur et les représentations diplomatiques tunisiennes à l’étranger.
Results: Les manifestations culturelles constituent une plateforme qui favorise la mobilité artistique : quelques chiffres (2022-2023) -	Le festival international de Carthage (en 2022 on note l’octroi de 131 visas d’entrée sur le territoire tunisien et 107 visas en 2023) -	La foire internationale du livre de Tunis (en 2023 on note l’octroi de 251 visas d’entrée sur le territoire tunisien et 194 en 2024) -	Le festival international de Hammamet (54 visa) -	Les Journées théâtrales de Carthage (136 visa d’entrée en 2023) Dans le cadre du programme d’échange culturel international pour l’année 2023 : -	10 troupes artistiques accueillies provenant de 10 pays arabes, asiatiques et européens -	45 spectacles organisés couvrant 44 festivals dans 23 gouvernorats
Recommandations: On ne peut pas parler d’une évaluation dans sa définition stricte (dresser de manière ex post le bilan de la politique en se basant sur des indicateurs qualitatifs et quantitatifs bien déterminés pour mesurer les résultats atteints par rapport aux objectifs fixés. Cependant, une évaluation concomitante est assurée par le MAC à travers des réunions périodiques de suivi et des comités de pilotage qui constituent un cadre de réflexion sur l’impact de la mesure en termes de résultats, défis et difficultés de mise  en œuvre. Les principales recommandations sont: •	L’institutionnalisation de de diplomatie culturelle est un facteur essentiel pour améliorer l’image du pays et assurer son rayonnement à l’échelle régionale et internationale. •	La création de synergies interdépartementales (MAC, MAE, tourisme, ..) est fortement sollicitée pour développer une vision une diplomatie culturelle cohérente et intégrée. •	Focaliser les actions d’échange et de promotion de la culture tunisienne autour un Label qui met en exergue les spécificités de l’identité nationale tout en prenant en compte la nécessité de s’ouvrir sur les autres cultures dans un esprit d’échange, de complémentarité et d’interculturalité.

Title EN: Une vision stratégique du développement fondé sur l’inclusivité, l’équité et la durabilité.
Goal: Integrate Culture In Sustainable Development Frameworks
SDG: SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: National sustainable development policies and plans
Cultural Domain: Design,Performing Arts,Media Arts,Cinema and Audiovisual Arts,Music,Publishing,Visual Arts
Agency Implementation: Le Ministère de l'économie et de la planification (MEP)
Main Feature: L’année 2023 a été marquée par l’élaboration du nouveau plan de développement 2023-2025 conçu par le Ministère de l’Economie et de la Planification (MEP) en étroite collaboration avec tous les ministères et les structures publiques au niveau central et régional et avec la participation de représentants d’organisations nationales, d’organismes de la société civile et d’experts sectoriels. Ce plan constitue une référence essentielle en matière de développement puisqu’il définit les choix stratégiques et les mécanismes de fonctionnement à adopter pour répondre aux aspirations (économiques, sociales et culturelles) des citoyens. Sa conception a tenu compte des mutations nationales et mondiales qui se dessinent à l’horizon 2035 afin d’intégrer les risques et les opportunités qui en découlent.  Résultant d’un processus participatif (36 comités sectorielles, 24 comités régionales ainsi qu’une consultation nationale) incluant, pour une meilleure appropriation, partenaires institutionnels, acteurs de la société civile et acteurs privés, le plan de développement 2023-2025 ainsi que la note d’orientations stratégiques « vision Tunisie 2035 » définissent une nouvelle vision stratégique du développement fondée sur l’inclusivité, l’équité et la durabilité. Ceci cadre parfaitement avec le principe de développement durable que véhicule la convention de 2005 en vertu duquel « la diversité culturelle est une grande richesse pour les individus et les sociétés. La protection, la promotion et le maintien de la diversité culturelle est une condition essentielle pour un développement durable au bénéfice des générations présentes et futures ». Dans ce même cadre, l’article premier souligne, parmi les objectifs de la convention, « l’importance du lien entre culture et développement pour tous les pays en particulier les pays en développement et d’encourager les actions menées aux plans national et international pour que soit reconnue la véritable valeur de ce lien ». Tout en présentant la culture comme vecteur de développement durable et inclusif, facteur de cohésion sociale et source potentielle de génération de revenus et d’emplois, les deux documents de référence (le plan 2023-2025 et la note d’orientation 2035) prônent une culture de proximité axée sur le citoyen placé au cœur de l’action culturelle, la diversification des mécanismes de financement de la culture et des projets culturels, la promotion des industries culturelles et créatives (ICC), l’encouragement de la créativité et l’entreprenariat culturel dans les secteurs innovants à forte valeur ajoutée. Outre ces objectifs, les documents stratégiques orientent les efforts vers le renforcement de la contribution de la culture dans le développement notamment à travers l’adaptation du secteur culturel aux mutations accélérées dans le domaine des nouvelles technologies de l’information et de la communication (NTIC). Ainsi le secteur culturel requiert une importance particulière comme moyen de développement et de changement social. Il est considéré parmi les secteurs stratégiques pouvant contribuer au développement économique et socio-culturel.   Par ailleurs, le Ministère de l’Economie et de la Planification (MEP) et dans le cadre du programme national des réformes et du Plan de développement 2023-2025, a lancé une stratégie nationale pour l’amélioration du climat des affaires (2023-2025), élaborée selon une approche participative regroupant les secteurs public et privé sous  forme de dialogue public privé (DPP) réunissant plus de 175 participants représentant le secteur public (ministères et structures étatiques) et privé (chambres mixtes, Union Tunisienne de l'industrie, du commerce et de l'artisanat -UTICA, Institut arabe des chefs d’entreprise, Centre des jeunes dirigeants d’entreprise, Ordre des experts-comptables de Tunisie, Ordre des architectes de Tunisie…).  L’objectif étant de fédérer tous les efforts nationaux publics et privés afin d’améliorer durablement le climat des affaires et son attractivité vis-à-vis des investisseurs et de disposer d’une feuille de route qui identifie les contraintes rencontrées par les acteurs économiques et de proposer des mesures et des réformes structurantes qui permettront de surmonter les obstacles persistants, en se référant aux différentes stratégies nationales et sectorielles et au benchmark international. 229 mesures, 13 thématiques et 34 axes, réparties en trois vagues d’implémentation (2022-2025) et ciblant 94 objectifs ont été identifiées.
Results: Le cadre d’orientation stratégique élaboré suivant une démarche participative regroupant les propositions de 36 comités sectorielles (avec 8757 participants) et 24 comités régionales (11770 participants) dont 33% des femmes, a servi de référence pour le Ministère des Affaires Culturelles (MAC) pour définir ses objectifs et fixer ses priorités qui s’inscrivent pleinement dans le plan national des réformes: •	La promotion des industries culturelles et créatives comme étant un levier de développement global et durable et un véritable stimulant pour l’investissement •	Une infrastructure et des contenus culturels plus développée plus attractifs  •	La gestion efficace des éléments du patrimoine national, par sa préservation, sa valorisation et sa sauvegarde •	La culture comme facteur d’inclusion économique et sociale   •	Un cadre juridique fondateur d’un secteur culturel assez structuré et développé. •	Une diplomatie culturelle en faveur du rayonnement de la culture tunisienne à l’échelle régionale et internationale.

Title EN: UNESCO ASP Network Denmark
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture
SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Cultural and creative sectors
Agency Implementation: UNESCO ASP Network Denmark
Main Feature: The Danish UNESCO ASP network has contributed to Goal 1 through three main points 1) Strategic partnerships 2) Creation of a youth ambassador corps 3) Expansion of the network and ongoing activities 1. Strategic partnerships The Danish asp network has worked with SDG 4- Quality education in relation to the other world goals, as education can provide knowledge, action and motivation to work for sustainable development. Within the cultural area, we will highlight the network's work in seeking strategic partnerships that have had to influence the Danish politicians and especially the Minister of Education and also give the schools tools to work with sustainable development in education.  We have done this by participating in the Danish partnership Education for sustainable development (UBU), which brings together 80 actors around the education's contribution to young people's competencies and belief in sustainable development within all parts of the school and within all subjects - including the cultural and creative subjects. In the partnership, recommendations have been developed for the minister about how the politicians can support the schools, but also what the schools and stakeholders can do themselves. The Danish ASP network has also been the initiator of a partnership across Oman, Croatia and Denmark, which works to promote education within intangible cultural heritage. Another example is the Networks collaborates with museums, e.g. the Moesgård museum, which has developed teaching tools about intangible cultural heritage, which should promote mutual understanding across countries and cultures, by creating insight into each other's traditions and way of life. 2. The Danish UNESCO Youth Ambassador team ASP Denmark has established a team of 16 young people who are ambassadors for UNESCO and the World Goals. The aim was to: - To give students and young people a voice in UNESCO - To facilitate young-to-young learning - To enhance students' commitment & awareness of UNESCO values The youth ambassadors provide input and presentations within topics related to UNESCO (values) and the SDG. They get a course to start with, where they develop into the role of ambassador, and we help and support them along the way. They provide inspiration for the everyday teaching (not responsible for curriculums) and then they create Creating dialogue, reflection and debate among students and in school community. They have, among other things, made a workshop for young people from 24 different countries about In the workshop, which the youth ambassadors facilitated that the participants worked with various youth themes: social media, role models, music and expression in the form of style and fashion. Here the participants made collages about the four themes and collaborated across national borders. The participants got an insight into different nationalities and cultures. And we, the students, experienced the importance of diversity across national borders. We have also facilitated the young people making a UNESCO song in collaboration with rap musicians. The aim of the song was to give the young people a voice and emphasize that all young people have the right to be heard and to express themselves "claim your voice". The young people have developed in the process and inspired other young people. 3. A larger network and more activities for schools The Danish ASP network has grown from about 60 schools in 2020 to 88 schools in 2024. In the network, we bring schools together in projects, for conferences, workshops, where they can develop creative approaches to include sustainability in teaching - both in collaboration with local and global actors. Most recently, we have worked with future literacy, which to that extent opens the possibility of including art and culture when you have to talk about and express your ideas about the future. We hold an annual meeting every year, where all 88 schools participate and where we bring art and culture to the fore as a form of expression, both through singing together and through workshops.
Results: This is the results of the initiatives: 1. Strategic partnerships contribute to disseminating knowledge and the range of teaching materials with the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) and UNESCO as the starting point. The strong strategic partnerships have led to partners such as museums approaching us themselves and wanting to develop materials and convey them to our UNESCO schools. New collaborations are emerging continuously. Right now, there is a collaboration in progress with music festivals and sustainability. In Denmark, there are music festivals in many cities across the country, and they can engage their local educational institutions to address UNESCO's values through activities at the festivals. UNESCO's brand and targeted activities have led more schools to apply to participate in the UNESCO Associated Schools Project Network (ASPnet). The result of our efforts is that we have engaged more schools in UNESCO's values. This means that the Danish UNESCO ASPnet, with 88 schools, potentially can reach over 13,000 teachers and 100,000 students. The great strength is that we reach the teachers with our initiatives. Teachers are a difficult group to reach in Danish educational institutions because they often don't have time to participate. 2. The Youth Ambassador Corps has provided knowledge on how young people can motivate others to engage and express themselves. The establishment of the youth ambassador team has meant that we have gotten the team to engage other young people in UNESCO's values. Several of them say they have missed a youth community for others interested in art and culture, and they have found it here. Peer-to-peer communication works when young people are equipped to conduct workshops and ask good questions that create dialogue about UNESCO's values and the SDGs. In Denmark, many young people are tired of the SDGs because they have heard about them in the traditional form of education or as a theme day. When it is the youth ambassadors who are engaged to talk about them, it becomes a motivating alternative and something that creates receptiveness and motivation to work with values such as UNESCO's and the SDGs at their own school.

Title EN: Utanzania ni Nini? Project
Goal: Integrate Culture In Sustainable Development Frameworks
SDG: SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: National sustainable development policies and plans
Agency Implementation: Ona Stories
Main Feature: The "Utanzania ni Nini?" project is an innovative and comprehensive journalistic endeavor undertaken by OnaStories to explore and articulate the unique concept of "Tanzanianness" — the distinct national identity that sets Tanzania apart from other geopolitical and sociocultural identities. Despite being home to over 120 different tribes, Tanzania has successfully fostered a cohesive national culture over the past six decades. This project represents the first in-depth exploration of what constitutes Tanzanian culture, presenting its findings through a variety of multimedia formats, including articles, videos, illustrations, and photographs, all compiled on a dedicated website.  1. Continuous Exploration: "Utanzania" is a continuous project, reflecting the evolving nature of cultural identity. As Tanzania’s socio-cultural landscape changes, the project adapts and expands, providing ongoing insights and updates. This continuous approach ensures that the exploration of Tanzanian culture remains relevant and comprehensive. 2. Multimedia Storytelling: The use of multimedia storytelling is a hallmark of the "Utanzania" project. Each theme is explored through a combination of written articles, visual illustrations, engaging videos, and evocative photographs. This combination of media formats helps to convey the multifaceted nature of Tanzanian culture and makes the content more engaging and relatable to a wide audience. 3. Advanced Technological Integration: The project experiments with and utilizes advanced multimedia formats and technologies such as virtual reality (VR), augmented reality (AR), mixed reality (MR), and artificial intelligence (AI). These cutting-edge technologies provide immersive experiences, allowing users to explore Tanzanian culture in innovative and engaging ways. This technological integration not only enhances the storytelling but also attracts a tech-savvy audience interested in new media. 4. Dedicated Website: All the content produced for the "Utanzania" project is gathered together on a dedicated website. This centralized platform allows users to easily access and navigate through the different themes and media formats. The website serves as a comprehensive repository of information and a vibrant digital space for exploring Tanzanian culture. 5. Thematic Focus: The first phase of the "Utanzania" project began with three central themes pivotal to understanding Tanzanian culture: clothing, music, and language. ●	Clothing: The project examines the Tanzanian power suit, particularly focusing on the Kaunda suit and its influence on Tanzanian politics over the decades. This theme explores how clothing has not only been a marker of cultural identity but also a symbol of political power and social change in Tanzania. ●	Music: Singeli music, a popular genre in Tanzania, serves as a lens through which the project explores the interplay between popular culture and socioeconomics. This theme highlights how music reflects and influences the daily lives, struggles, and aspirations of Tanzanians, making it a vital component of the national identity. ●	Language: Kiswahili, Tanzania's national language, is central to the country's group identity formation. The project investigates the rise and continued prominence of Kiswahili, analyzing how language use has contributed to national cohesion and cultural expression. This theme underscores the importance of a common language in unifying diverse ethnic groups and fostering a shared sense of identity.
Results: Temporary Job Creation: The project has created employment opportunities for local creatives, including writers, photographers, videographers, illustrators, and technicians, contributing to the local economy and empowering these individuals to produce high-quality multimedia content. Multimedia Content: The first phase, focusing on clothing, music, and language, has produced extensive articles, videos, and illustrations. This content explores the significance of the Kaunda suit, the socio-economic impact of Singeli music, and the rise and influence of Kiswahili. Exhibitions: Over 1,000 Tanzanians and international visitors have attended exhibitions showcasing this content, providing immersive cultural experiences. Partnerships: Collaborations with cultural agencies have facilitated continued exhibitions, extending the project's reach and impact. National Pride: The project has fostered a sense of national pride and loyalty by highlighting unique aspects of Tanzanian culture, reinforcing a collective national identity. Cultural Awareness: By raising awareness of Tanzania's diverse cultures, the project educates a broad audience and aids in preserving these cultural practices for future generation.

Title EN: Unique Registry of Artisans of Colombia - RUAC
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture
SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Cultural and creative sectors
Agency Implementation: Artesanías de Colombia S.A-BIC-
Main Feature: The Unique Registry of Artisans of Colombia (RUAC), established within the framework of Law 2184 of 2022, aims to obtain and provide updated strategic statistical information on the artisan population in Colombia, including its number, location and basic characteristics. This valuable set of data will enable Artesanías de Colombia S.A.-BIC and the National Government to make informed decisions that improve the living conditions and well-being of artisans. This Law complements Law 36 of 1984, which regulates the "ARTISAN PROFESSION".                   The Unique Registry of Artisans of Colombia (RUAC) is a fundamental tool in the identification and recognition of the talented artisans who constitute our country's rich artisan tradition. This registry not only promotes and preserves traditional arts and crafts, but also provides opportunities and visibility to those whose manual work enriches Colombia's cultural and economic heritage.                  Certification as an artisan at the RUAC is an official recognition of the mastery and skills of artisans, confirming the authenticity and quality of their creations. Moreover, it opens doors to market opportunities and institutional support.
Results: After a year of hard work by the technical team formed at the entity, the RUAC has all the instruments built in the design phase. Under this line of work, the entity, complying with the statistical protocols, is carrying out the Pilot Test of all the designed processes, which were applied to all the artisans who presented their products in the context of Expoartesanías 2023. This exercise allowed us to make the adjustments with technical relevance of the designs carried out to ensure an implementation with all the quality parameters required by a Continuous Registry such as the RUAC, whose data will allow the construction of strategic indicators to be used as a baseline for the formulation, monitoring, and evaluation of sectoral public policies within the framework of the Mission of Artesanías de Colombia S.A.–BIC.                  According to the goal for 2023, corresponding to the execution of PHASE I: Conceptual and Methodological Design, there is a thematic, statistical, and operational design.

Title EN: UNITED NATIONS FRAMEWORK FOR SUSTAINABLE DEVELOPMENT IN URUGUAY.
Goal: Integrate Culture In Sustainable Development Frameworks
SDG: SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: National sustainable development policies and plans
Agency Implementation: NACIONES UNIDAS URUGUAY
Main Feature: On December 21, 2020, the United Nations Cooperation Framework for Sustainable Development in Uruguay 2021-2025. This document reflected the agreements reached between the Government of Uruguay and the United Nations System in Uruguay in relation to the cooperation that the latter would provide to the country in the period defined in the transition towards achieving full implementation of the 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development. In addition to the technical analyzes and political dialogue between national authorities and the United Nations System in Uruguay, this strategic framework incorporated the results of consultations with civil society actors, academic institutions and private sector organizations. The analysis of the country's main development challenges within the framework of the 2030 Agenda and the priorities defined in the Government's planning for the period considered led to the definition of four strategic priorities, number 1 being “an economy that innovates, that generates employment and guarantees the sustainability of development.” One of the results defined to achieve this objective at the end of the period is to have “consolidated the economic recovery based on the generation of quality employment, decent work and the promotion of the entrepreneurial capacity of the private sector, particularly small businesses.” and medium-sized businesses, increasing the participation of women in the economy.” Among the conditions and assumptions for Uruguay to advance towards this result, the generation, in the first years of the cooperation cycle, of an economic scenario that stimulated the development of entrepreneurship and the creation of quality jobs, significantly increasing participation of women and young people in the labor market, for which the fundamental role that creative industries could play is made explicit, making reference to the weight of cultural activity in the Gross Domestic Product (GDP) and the number of people it employs, appealing to sources such as the Uruguayan Culture Satellite Account published in 2012 and estimates from the Uruguay XXI agency based on the 2016 Continuous Household Survey of the National Institute of Statistics (INE).

Area of Monitoring: Partnering with civil society
Agency Implementation: International Federation of Coalitions for Cultural Diversity (IFCCD), Creativity and Culture Glocal, The U40 network EMAIL
Main Feature: The Training entitled UNESCO Convention 2005: A tool for the Latin American cultural sector took place online from November 6 to 28, 2020. The program was developed by the International Federation of Coalitions for Cultural Diversity (IFCCD), the Creatividad y Cultura Glocal association and the U40 network, in partnership with the German Commission for UNESCO and the Chilean and Paraguayan coalitions for cultural diversity. In total, eight two-hour sessions were offered, in Spanish: •	Session 1 : Essential concepts: Diversity of cultural expressions, cultural policies, culture and sustainable development." •	Session 2 : Cultural rights: International agreements, human rights, gender equality, indigenous peoples." •	Session 3 : The 2005 UNESCO Convention: History, content, recent developments, challenges." •	Session 4 : The Convention, the performing arts and the cultural and creative industries: References to the Convention in different sectors." •	Session 5 : Culture and Free Trade Agreements: Cultural exception clauses/reservations, preferential treatment, digital trade, intellectual property, most favored nation." •	Session 6 : Cultural diversity in the digital context: Opportunities, adaptation of laws, artificial intelligence. •	Session 7 : Civil society and the Convention: The experience of national coalitions of the IFCCD and other networks." •	Session 8 : Challenges and choices for the future in Latin America in the context of a global crisis.
Results: The training made it possible to: •	Reach people who were working, sometimes without knowing it, to implement the 2005 UNESCO Convention in their region; •	Increase knowledge of the tools available to defend and promote Latin American cultural expressions and their diversity; •	Mobilize cultural networks in Latin America; •	Provide opportunities for participating individuals to expand these networks nationally and regionally; •	Increase the visibility and reach of the IFCCD in Latin America; •	Bring the Convention closer to professionals from the public, private or civil society sectors who already work or wish to work in the cultural sector.

Agency Implementation: Coalition for the Diversity of Cultural Expressions ( CDCE ), International Federation of Coalitions for Cultural Diversity ( IFCCD )
Main Feature: The Program – Digital environment and artificial intelligence (AI) aims to monitor, popularize, consult and advocate on the subject.  As a reminder, already in 2018, the CDCE presented an initial reflection on AI so that discussions concerning its development and applications better integrate cultural issues in general, and those of the diversity of cultural expressions in particular. | W  List of activities carried out under this program (non-exhaustive): [2020 – 2023] The CDCE, its members and its partners have doubled their efforts to deepen the reflection, and to contribute to the development of legislation and policies relating to AI which are in line with the implementation of the 2005 Convention. The following initiatives in particular have contributed to its unfolding: [December 2020] Based on the work of the Center for Studies on Integration and Globalization (CEIM), as well as other studies and reports, the CDCE has developed the guide entitled “ The challenge of discoverability. The urgency of acting to defend the diversity of cultural expressions .” The latter analyzes the role played by different actors in terms of discoverability (what online services have changed, the strategies developed by cultural circles and the position of governments).  [February 2021] The guide was presented during a free online webinar, accessible in French and English, entitled “ Where are we on the discoverability of cultural content in the digital environment in 2021? ". This webinar was organized with the participation of the Ministry of Culture and Communications of Quebec, the UNESCO Chair on the Diversity of Cultural Expressions, the University of Quebec in Montreal (UQAM), and the International Organization of La Francophonie (OIF).  [September 2021] Brief from the CDCE as part of the Consultation on a modern copyright framework for artificial intelligence and the Internet of Things led by ISDE. | W [January 2022] International conference on legislative reforms to protect and promote the diversity of cultural expressions in the digital environment : The event was organized by the CDCE, in collaboration with the UNESCO chair on the diversity of cultural expressions and in partnership with the International Federation of Coalitions for Cultural Diversity (IFCCD). This day of conferences in virtual format brought together nearly 23 panelists. W | YouTube – FRA | YouTube ENG | YouTube – ESP [September 2023] Comments from the CDCE as part of the consultations of the Department of Science Innovation and Economic Development of Canada on the development of a Canadian code of practice for generative artificial intelligence systems. | W [2023] The CDCE has also organized and participated in a number of public awareness and community mobilization and reflection initiatives on the subject of AI – including: -	[September 2023] The CDCE has entered into a partnership with ALL IN which, with its 1,400 participants, describes itself as “the largest artificial intelligence event in Canada”, making it possible to give culture a place in this major event.  -	[November 2023] CDCE lunchtime conferences as part of the consultations of Industry Science and Economic Development and Canadian Heritage, dealing with copyright in the era of generative artificial intelligence.
Results: [2020 – 2023] All of the activities carried out under the Program – Digital Environment and Artificial Intelligence (AI) have enabled the cultural sector to clearly present its positions and the CDCE to put forward requests with consensus among its members.  [January 2022] International conference on legislative reforms to protect and promote the diversity of cultural expressions in the digital environment : More than a hundred people attended the conference live, and the videos generated 619 views in three languages on the CDCE YouTube channel after the event. This day of conferences allowed experts from Asia-Pacific, Europe, Africa and the Americas to discuss the crucial issues of the implementation in the digital environment of the UNESCO Convention on the protection and promotion of the diversity of cultural expressions of 2005.   [February 2021] [Webinar, free, accessible in French and English, entitled “ Where are we on the discoverability of cultural content in the digital environment in 2021? » – Presentation of the CDCE guide entitled “ The challenge of discoverability . The urgency of acting to defend the diversity of cultural expressions .”] In total, 181 people connected with an average participation oscillating between 130 and 150 throughout the webinar.  [September 2023] [ ALL IN ] Alongside the ten experts who spoke during the panels reserved for culture, within this event, the CDCE contributed to facilitating the discussion and the search for avenues and solutions around the following questions, among others: Could art direct the development of AI towards more ethical paths? Can it help resolve the bias problems intrinsic to current systems? How can we encourage a richer dialogue between artists, cultural entrepreneurs and the technological sector, not only to strengthen the power of these cultural actors to act, but also to nourish research and development in AI? 25 members of the CDCE were able to attend this event in person.

Title EN: Program – International Affairs
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture
SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Partnering with civil society
Agency Implementation: Coalition for the Diversity of Cultural Expressions ( CDCE ), International Federation of Coalitions for Cultural Diversity ( IFCCD )
Main Feature: International Affairs Program aims to promote networking, consultation and the contribution of civil society on the national, regional and international levels to UN decision-making processes.  The Coalition for the Diversity of Cultural Expressions (CDCE ) team serves as the Secretariat of the International Federation of Coalitions for Cultural Diversity ( IFCCD ). The IFCCD is an NGO in official partnership (association status) with UNESCO . It is the result of a significant mobilization of civil society in favor of the adoption and then the ratification of the Convention. Under the aegis of the IFCCD, including with the financial support of the Ministry of Culture and Communications ( MCC ) of Quebec and the Department of Canadian Heritage ( PCH ) of Canada, the members of management and representatives members of the CDCE and the IFCCD participate and contribute, on a regular basis, to the work of the governance bodies for the implementation of the Convention. Under the aegis of the IFCCD, the CDCE took part in the following meetings, for example: •	[2020 – 2023] The 13th,14th,15th, and 16th ordinary sessions of the Intergovernmental Committee for the Protection and Promotion of the Diversity of Cultural Expressions (IGC). •	[June 2021 and 2023] 3rd and 4th Civil Society Forum organized at UNESCO ahead of the 8th and 9th ordinary sessions of the Conference of the Parties to the Convention (CoP), respectively. The IFCCD was also part of the group of NGOs responsible for organizing the 4th Forum. •	[May 2022] UNESCO organized a ResiliArt debate (the second of its kind) in partnership with the IFCCD. ResiliArt is a global movement consisting of a series of virtual debates with key artists and professionals in the sector, the aim of which was to raise awareness of the considerable impact of the containment measures caused by the pandemic on the culture sector. •	[September 2022] The IFCCD and the CDCE took part in MONDIACULT 2022 , UNESCO's global conference on cultural policies and sustainable development, during which 150 States adopted a historic declaration for culture. •	[March 2023] The IFCCD supported the financing and the search for financing for the organization of a gathering of African coalitions which took place in Niamey, Niger, from March 14 to 16, 2023. The event was thus able to benefit from the support of the OIF and the German UNESCO Commission. In addition, virtually, the Secretary General and the President of the IFCCD delivered speeches.  The president of the IFCCD sits on a group of discoverability experts set up by the OIF.
Results: The activities of the IFCCD and its status as an official Partner of UNESCO reflect on the CDCE, enrich the analysis of members with an international dimension, provide a useful network of contacts, provide the opportunity to learn from experiences carried out elsewhere, as to assert those which are carried out in Canada.  The declaration resulting from MONDIACULT 2022, which uniquely recognizes culture as a global public good, echoes several requests put forward by the Federation, calling in particular to “integrate culture as a specific objective in its own right in the next United Nations Sustainable Development Goals" and "substantial regulation of the digital sector, in particular large platforms, for the benefit of online cultural diversity, the intellectual property of artists and equitable access for all to the contents”. IFCCD  The leadership and participation of the CDCE, alongside other members of the IFCCD in the statutory meetings of the governance bodies of the Convention, made possible thanks to the support granted to this end by the governments of Quebec and Canada, promote and contribute to strengthen in particular: •	Consultation and coordination of the contribution of civil society in the implementation of the Convention; •	The bilateral and multilateral dialogue between civil society and the Parties to the Convention and between civil society and the Secretariat of the Convention within UNESCO on this subject; •	Support from the Parties and the Convention Secretariat for civil society initiatives.  The medium and long-term impact of these consultations, contributions and dialogues can be assessed, among other things, according to the degree of effective consideration of civil society proposals in the decision-making processes of the Parties. During the period 2020 – 2023, the point of view of civil society was taken into consideration during several legislative processes and public consultations.  The IFCCD, the CDCE and their respective members work to ensure monitoring and follow-up of these proposals as well as the continuous improvement of the processes to do so.

Development and structuring of 26 municipal competitions, supported by “Law No. 1023, on competitive activities”, of August 27, 2021, focused on the following areas of Artistic Cultural expression: Literary Arts, Performing Arts, Plastic Arts – Visual Arts, Musical Arts, Audiovisual Arts, Crafts and Popular Arts, Cultural Management These competitions generate various mechanisms to promote and encourage the creation of artistic and cultural expressions, articulating the emergence of new talents and the consolidation of artistic creators already established in the field. Results: In the last 5 years, more than $us. 750,000 were invested in the implementation of the Municipal Competitions of Cochabamba. In 2023 alone, the participation of more than 2,000 local and national creative artists was achieved. This represents an important advance in artistic and cultural production in our environment, promoting both creation and consumption.

Recommandations: Conclusions: The resources invested by the GAMC in the Municipal Competitions are insufficient considering the exponential growth of the cultural artistic sector at the local level. A constant restructuring of competitions and calls for proposals is required to adapt them to the corresponding context. Recommendations: Coordinate efforts between GAMC and international cooperation institutions, non-governmental organizations and private companies. Creation of articulated platforms between the public sector and specialized actors and institutions, for the review and reformulation of competitions, their respective calls and supporting regulations. Manage intersectoral mechanisms that allow organic interaction between national and local regulations. Development of public structures that allow periodic meetings between the three levels of government: Ministerial, Departmental and Municipal. Reorganization of the organizational chart of the Secretariat in charge of Cultural Work in the Municipality of Cochabamba. Diversification of staff recruitment mechanisms, specialization of permanent staff and transformation of Units – Divisions – Departments – Directorates and Secretariat, according to local context studies.

Results: Three editions of the program were held with free admission in the cities of:   1) Posadas, capital of the province of Misiones, where the cultural network of the border between the province of Formosa and Paraguay was vindicated. Main Feature: The program seeks to contribute to the professionalization of cultural workers who develop their activities at different levels of the Public Administration and the university environment. It is composed of different complementary instances, in alliance with public cultural areas and agencies throughout the country, incorporating the diversity of experiences and regional and local particularities.  Likewise, the program's actions seek to deepen institutional linkages, articulation among public cultural managers and specialization in aspects of public cultural management.  Among its general objectives are:  1. To contribute to the professionalization of cultural workers at the various levels of the federal public administration in cultural matters.  2. To foster a critical and reflexive view, pondering the political dimension within the management of public culture.  In 2020, in the context of preventive and mandatory social isolation due to the Covid 19 pandemic, this training in Public Cultural Management was redesigned. Thus, it was edited in a virtual format, with new modules and contents, thinking of an introductory training path that provides basic management, communication and accessibility tools. This format made it possible to deliver the course simultaneously throughout the country, distributed in six regions (NOA, NEA, Patagonia, Cuyo, Buenos Aires) and with a total of 24 hours of synchronous courses over 12 weeks.
Results: Between 2020 and 2023, six cohorts were delivered in each region and more than 1,000 public cultural managers were certified.  Relevant actions include: In 2023, the following courses were given: Course on Public Cultural Management; Seminar on Cultural Audiences and Communities; Seminar on Cultural Rights; Specialization in public cultural policies on The Homeland of Childhood; University extension course on Territorial Mapping for the Construction of Situated Local Policies (in conjunction with the Latin American Faculty of Social Sciences).  The classes and theoretical/practical meetings resulted in a publication called: La Patria de la Infancia (2023), which seeks to contribute to the creation of the field of State Policies for and from children. It responds to the need to promote training and the exchange of knowledge of non-traditional forms of training and, above all, the articulation and systematization of the knowledge produced in each territory. Title EN: Programa Puntos de Cultura
Goal: Integrate Culture In Sustainable Development Frameworks
SDG: SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: National sustainable development policies and plans
Cultural Domain: Design,Performing Arts,Media Arts,Cinema and Audiovisual Arts,Music,Publishing,Visual Arts
Agency Implementation: Secretariat of Culture
Main Feature: The objective of the Puntos de Cultura program is to "promote inclusion and access to culture for the population, respecting the cultural diversity of the country, by strengthening social organizations and indigenous communities, which through their territorial intervention promote social inclusion, local identity, citizen participation and regional development through art and culture. This policy constitutes, therefore , a state action aimed at the democratization of access to and production of cultural goods, as tools that favor social inclusion, the construction of citizenship and the revaluation of local identity (Resolution No. 2641/2011).   Strategic objectives of the program:   1. Improve opportunities for the development and dissemination of cultural diversity and grassroots cultures.   2. To expand the possibilities of access to culture and the effective exercise of cultural, social, economic and political rights.   3. To broaden the federal and territorial scope of cultural policies.   4. Incorporate grassroots organizations without the financial or institutional capacity to meet program eligibility requirements.   5. To favor access by social organizations and indigenous communities to economic and material resources to guarantee the sustainability of their cultural projects. 6. Facilitate the access of social organizations and indigenous communities to dissemination channels.   7. To create channels for the exchange and dissemination of the productions made.   8. Strengthen the institutional and organizational capacity of social organizations and indigenous communities.   9. Ensure access of social organizations and indigenous communities to training, capacity building and technical assistance for project formulation.   10. Promote the articulation and exchange of knowledge and experiences of community culture.   The program calls for proposals, after which it provides assistance to different community cultural organizations in the country, with or without legal status, that develop artistic and cultural initiatives and promote social inclusion, local identity and citizen participation.
Results: Direct assistance to community cultural organizations, most of them located outside the large urban centers, to enable them to maintain their artistic and cultural activities. Likewise, the program's orientation was directed towards the consolidation and constitution of networks, which resulted in one of its most significant strengths.
Financial Ressources: $663,877,042 (equivalent to US$1,368,820) for the period 2020-2023
Recommandations: The evaluation of the program covered the years 2011 and 2021 inclusive. It assessed that 1836 community culture organizations from all over the country were beneficiaries of the Puntos de Cultura program between 2011 and 2021.  Sixty-four percent of them joined the program from 2020 to 2021. In turn, 60% of the organizations were located outside the capital cities.   The most frequent activities of these organizations are: artistic creation and training, solidarity activities (soup kitchens and/or canteens), communication, and the creation and development of new products and services.  community, sports activities and popular education. And 6 out of 10 organizations carry out activities for youth.   697 of the organizations registered in the Federal Registry of Culture platform operated in cultural spaces. Of these 697, 73% had Internet access and 62% carried out awareness-raising activities for the prevention of gender violence.   The most frequent type of relationship between the organizations and the spaces in which they operated was the commodatum. Half of the spaces in Buenos Aires City were rented.   In Buenos Aires, the Central and NEA regions, the most frequent type of relationship was the assignment or gratuitous bailment; while most of the organizations in Patagonia, NOA and the Cuyo region were owners of the spaces where they operated.   At the time of the evaluation, the Federal Registry of Culture had 53 indigenous community cultural organizations, more than half of which were located in the NOA region.   Finally, according to the data provided by the Federal Culture Registry as of November 2022, some of the impacts generated by the Puntos de Cultura program in its ten years of implementation can be mentioned:   ● Strengthened the approach of organizations through their cultural projects, promoting a federal and decentralized public policy.  ● Empowered indigenous organizations and communities with a track record: more than 1,000 organizations are at least 5 years old; and 548 have been in existence for more than 10 years.  ● It recognized the organizations in their role as community articulators and promoters of social containment, with subsidies such as the Extraordinary Reinforcement in the year 2021, within the framework of the health emergency.  ● Promoted community projects in more than 600 cultural spaces, of which 257 of the cultural spaces are located in poor neighborhoods and most of them have existed for more than 10 years (30% had computers for public use and 65% had Internet access).   In the 2020-2023 period, the program awarded grants for $663,877,042 to more than 1,300 community cultural organizations for the promotion and strengthening of projects.  community cultural events.

Title EN: Prevention of sexual harassment and sexual violence at the workplace in culture
Goal: Promote Human Rights And Fundamental Freedoms
SDG: SDG 5 - Achieve gender equality and empower all women and girls,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels
Area of Monitoring: Gender equality
Cultural Domain: Design,Performing Arts,Media Arts,Cinema and Audiovisual Arts,Music,Publishing,Visual Arts
Agency Implementation: Ministry of Culture
Main Feature: The Ministry of Culture, together with the City of Women – Association for the Promotion of Women in Culture, organized a public expert conference on the prevention of sexual harassment and sexual violence in the workplace in the cultural sector. The conference discussed examples of good practice presented by Katie Kheriji-Watts, Head of Research and Publications at On The Move (Belgium), Ulrike Kuner, Chair of the Board, and Dr. Marion Guerrero, Director of the organization vera* Vertrauensstelle gegen Belästigung und Gewalt in Kunst, Kultur und Sport (Austria), and Dr. Ksenija Vidmar Horvat, Vice-Rector for Academic and Student Affairs at the University of Ljubljana (Slovenia). The second part of the conference was dedicated to the presentation of the plan for the first survey on sexual harassment and sexual violence at the workplace in culture in Slovenia, which was carried out by the Ministry of Culture the following year and will serve as a basis for the development of appropriate measures in the future.
Results: In 2023, the Ministry of Culture conducted a survey on sexual harassment and sexual violence in the workplace in the cultural sector. The online questionnaire included questions on the following topics:  - socio-demographic characteristics,  - specific characteristics of working in the cultural sector,  - experience of 28 forms of sexual harassment (verbal, non-verbal, physical and sexual coercion) in the workplace, including frequency of sexual harassment, gender and position of the perpetrator, location of the harassment and presence of witnesses,  - consequences of sexual harassment for the target,  - possible disclosure and reporting of sexual harassment and the outcome of the report,  - measures that respondents believe are necessary to prevent and adequately address sexual harassment. The Ministry received 564 valid questionnaires, which were included in the analysis that will be presented in the report, which is currently being prepared.

Agency Implementation: Ministry of cultures, arts and heritage (mincap), through the department of education and training in arts and culture, dependent of the undersecretariat for cultures and arts.
Main Feature: The cecrea program seeks to resolve inequality in access to the creation and development of cultural expressions of boys, girls and young people between 7 and 19 years old in the country. for which it implements four components: 1) infrastructure/habilitation and/or remodeling and maintenance of the centers, to provide physical spaces where to develop cultural projects and activities; 2) programming of the centers, to provide permanent artistic and cultural content to the targeted population that will lead the artistic and cultural experiences of the centers; 3) technical and methodological assistance, to allow the beneficiaries to access didactic and training material in the areas of interest, supporting and strengthening their creation processes; 4) activities of associativity and exchange, to strengthen both the individual and collective expressions of children and young participants as well as their own artistic developments. the program is implemented in the regions: arica and parinacota, tarapaca, atacama, coquimbo, valparaiso, libertador general bernardo o'higgins, biobio, la araucania, los rios, los lagos; and, aysen. citizen participation in the cultural sphere involves the state both in recognizing rights in the field of culture, and in favoring the strengthening of the relationship between the state and citizens, integrating them in the design, implementation and evaluation of public policies. cultural. thus, the cecrea program is an "opportunity for the development of creative capacities in a space of collaboration and mutual learning" (cecrea educational model), whose purpose is to promote, facilitate and develop the right to imagine and create of children and adolescents. young people through creative learning processes that converge in the arts, sciences, technologies and sustainability. the convention on the rights of the child (1989) is relevant for the cecrea model, since it allows for the articulation of a new way of seeing and relating to children both at the individual, group and social level in an institutionalized way, since it changes its normative figure, going from being an "object" of protection to becoming a "titular subject" of rights to exercise. it establishes four general principles, non-discrimination (art. 2), the best interests of the child (art. 3), the right to life, survival and development (art. 6) and the right to express their opinion and that it is duly taken into account (art. 12). the spaces for citizen participation of chilendren and adolescents must tend to consolidate democracy, it is in the local space where they develop a large part of their social and affective action (family, school, neighborhood), being a place of bonding by excellence. in this line, the cecrea program is responsible for being an effective and concrete response to a space for children's participation from the local level, with real and effective incidence of children and youth, articulated with a national policy.
Results: The cecrea program has wide coverage at the national level, is present in 14 of the 16 regions of the country. also, by this time, 3 cecrea own infrastructures have been inaugurated in la ligua, valdivia and castro.

Area of Monitoring: National sustainable development policies and plans,Digital environment
Agency Implementation: Ministry of cultures, arts and heritage (mincap).
Main Feature: At the beginning of may 2019, the digital platform "choose culture" was officially launched, which aims to deliver all the artistic, cultural and heritage offer and programming throughout the country. its objective is to use the potential that technology provides to promote cultural development, that is one of the strategies in which mincap has made great progress. at the beginning of this month, "choose culture" was launched, a new collaborative cultural platform that brings together the country's artistic, cultural and heritage programming and that allows access to virtual cultural content from more than 350 cultural institutions and organizations nationwide. it has a complete billboard of cultural events from all regions, as well as multimedia material that allows access to various institutions and cultural spaces around the world, virtual tours of museums, online art collections, photo galleries, documentaries and mobile applications. the platform seeks to democratize culture by taking it to all homes, making the barriers that often prevent citizens from learning about the works of our talented creators disappear. it is a first step to a digitization of the national billboard. during its first year of operation (2019), choose culture continued to evolve with more and better tools on its platform, until it reached the creation of a mobile application that brings together a large part of the cultural, artistic and heritage offer that takes place in our country.
Results: As a way to facilitate and encourage access and cultural participation during the health emergency, the mincap made the cultural and heritage guide of chile, a monthly publication of the platform that brings together initiatives and activities promoted by the institution. available for downloading at www.cultura.gob.cl and www.eligecultura.cl.the guide is an invitation to discover, explore, and share culture, the arts and heritage remotely from mobile devices or computers with internet connection, accounting for the diverse and wide range of activities that take place in the 16 regions of the country. the document includes virtual tours and galleries that will allow citizens to visit some of the main museums in chile without leaving their homes, in addition to finding direct accesses to the digital public library, a platform for the loan of books and texts aimed at all kinds of public that has 60,000 books and 15,000 titles, and memoria chilean, a digital resource center on the history and culture of chile. the audiovisual world is also present in this edition through plan f, a series of short documentaries that presents multiple cultural projects and winning artistic works from the national fund for cultural development and the arts (fondart); and ondamedia.cl, a platform that has audiovisual content available for free, which includes the most awarded works of national cinema; short films and conferences on science and humanities. as a way of bringing national talent to chilean homes, the guide includes content from the rock and popular music schools, the chilean chamber orchestra and the bafona national folkloric ballet, which share valuable historical records with the public. of recitals and presentations, they have made throughout chile. the document also offers direct access to "chile for children", a project that seeks to bring the bibliographic heritage closer to children, and to "monumenteando", an activity of the council of national monuments that invites them to build, at home, the various national monuments present throughout the entire country. in the training section, two initiatives stand out: virtual classroom, which offers online training to develop skills to function in daily social, work and entrepreneurial life, and young programmers, a program that seeks to encourage the learning of programming in a virtual way, so everyone in chile - from the age of 8 onwards - is introduced to the language of codes and programming, going from being users to potential creators.

Title EN: "cinemachile, a sectoral brand for the international promotion of chilean audiovisual”.
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture,Integrate Culture In Sustainable Development Frameworks
SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development

Main Feature: Cinemachile is the public-private agency responsible for the promotion and dissemination of chilean audiovisual production throughout the world. it was created in 2009 by the association of film and television producers of chile (apct) and prochile, under the program “marcas sectoriales”. it is an active office that facilitates the export and internationalization of cinema, and all audiovisual production formats, both for companies consolidated in the foreign circuit, and for those that have just opened their way abroad. its objectives are as follows: facilitate the positioning of our productions in class a festivals, which increase the commercialization value of our products in the international market, as well as facilitate that productions in serial, virtual or animated formats, participate of the most important meetings of the field at an international level, develop a strategic and commercial marketing that makes the offer of national cinema, and television attractive in the foreign market, contribute to the professionalization of the sector and, maintain constant interaction with the actors of the national, and international audiovisual industry, including the media specialized in the film and tv industry at a global level.  at the same time, it develops the following actions: promote chilean films (fiction, documentary, animation, virtual reality), and their various formats, in international festivals and markets (or industry spaces) that cinemachile attends, from its participation in competitions up to market instances; promote television productions (fiction, documentary, animation, virtual reality), and their various formats, in the international markets (or industry meetings) that cinemachile attends; maintains contact and creates ties between the national and global audiovisual industry with special emphasis on buyers, producers, programmers, distributors and the press; facilitates the presence of national delegations that attend each festival, and market in which cinemachile participates, making available to chilean professionals diffusion spaces for their work (web platform, social networks, promotional pieces, events, among others); it disseminates the work (news) and the achievements of chilean cinema and tv in specialized press media; generates business agendas and commercial networks, both in individual meetings and in events of great international scope; produces annual publications such as the international film catalog and the international television catalog, to facilitate the work of international intermediary agents and prestigious festivals and; organizes and conducts seminars and talks aimed at the chilean audiovisual industry, which are the result of the experience of both cinemachile and that of national professionals who participate in foreign markets and festivals, materializing knowledge and work through these academic activities, always with a focus on training for the international market.
Results: After 10 years since its creation, cinemachile has international positioning strategies for the audiovisual sector, which go beyond the members of the association of film, and television producers (apct). the indirect beneficiaries of the cinemachile sector brand correspond to all associations of companies or professionals in the audiovisual sector, as well as independent professionals who aspire to export and/or access the international circuit. all of them benefit, or could benefit, from the networks of contacts and expertise developed by the sectorial brand, as well as from the participation in activities and events organized by cinemachile, their inclusion in the international catalogs (film or tv) that are published annually, and other graphic promotional pieces (presskit in international markets and festivals), dissemination of their contents on our communication platforms, among other actions that benefit (and have benefited in the past) across the sector, without necessarily belonging to the applicant association, and co-financier of cinemachile.  the foregoing, especially because within the apct there are companies dedicated to the production of products from all subsectors (animation, documentary, fiction, television) with which all the actions that this project contemplates imply an indirect benefit for members of other associations specific to those areas or genres (such as adoc or animachi) or diverse, such as apct and api (which produce all kinds of productions, of all genres and formats). in addition, adg partners are among our indirect beneficiaries, as well as chileactores, and sidarte partners, which are joined by independent professionals from the sector, and also audiovisual career students.
