Title EN: «kulturportier» kollektiv frei_raum
Goal: Integrate Culture In Sustainable Development Frameworks
SDG: SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: National sustainable development policies and plans,National sustainable development policies and plans
Agency Implementation: Die heitere fahne (info@dieheiterefahne.ch)
Main Feature: Frei_raum – inklusive kultur est un collectif de personnes engagees organisant des manifestations culturelles a berne qui ont, outre l’art et la culture presentes, toujours une dimension sociale, integrative et inclusive. le collectif vise a integrer une grande diversite de personnes a son offre culturelle et organise des mediations artistiques, culturelles et socialement engagees dans le cadre de manifestations culturelles prenant des formes innovantes. le collectif est actif a « heitere fahne » (www.dieheiterefahne.ch), dans un ancien restaurant pres de berne, qui est gere depuis six ans comme un centre culturel et un restaurant ouvert a tous.  le collectif organise divers projets culturels inclusifs concrets, par exemple des soirees culturelles inclusives, ou l'inclusion est integree dans la programmation, ou des offres de mediation et d'education, avec des ateliers de theatre permettant aux personnes en situation de handicap ou non de s’exercer et d’experimenter ensemble.  depuis 2016, le projet « kulturportier » (le portier culturel) est mis en oeuvre comme une « ouverture de porte » a la participation a la vie culturelle. le kulturportier facilite la participation autonome et independante de personnes en situation d’handicap a la programmation de « heitere fahne ». pour permettre ces actions participatives, une personne formee professionnellement (le kulturportier) est presente une fois par mois a « heitere fahne » depuis 2016 durant les evenements culturels (concerts, representations, lectures publiques, expositions, marche de noel) afin d’accompagner et soutenir les personnes en situation d’handicap. le kulturportier offre autant de soutien que necessaire. les 12 evenements annuels accompagnes par le kulturportier sont identifies par le label «freaks+stars » sur le site internet de « heitere fahne » et communiques a toutes les institutions de la region bernoise susceptibles d’etre interessees.
Results: Des personnes en situation de handicap ou non, des personnes ayant des problemes psychiques, des personnes issues de la migration, des enfants, des jeunes et des jeunes de coeur, en quete de sens et des idealistes courageux vivent et creent ensemble un programme culturel complet a « heitere fahne » et aussi en dehors de celui-ci, a berne et dans les environs. « heitere fahne » est un espace experimental pour la participation culturelle, l'inclusion active et le travail social innovant, tant pour l'equipe operationnelle inclusive – qui se compose d'environ 30 personnes – que pour de nombreux benevoles, artistes et visiteurs. la diversite et l'inclusion sont ici une evidence, tout comme la negociation et l'exploration constantes des possibles. l'attribution du label « kultur inklusiv » en 2016 et du prix de la culture du canton de berne (ete 2018) sont un signe de l'appreciation du public pour le travail du collectif et une incitation a poursuivre sur la voie empruntee avec engagement et ingeniosite.

Title EN: “cultura viva” national policy
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture,Integrate Culture In Sustainable Development Frameworks
SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: National sustainable development policies and plans,Partnering with civil society,National sustainable development policies and plans,National sustainable development policies and plans
Agency Implementation: Special secretariat for culture
Main Feature: The national policy "cultura viva" is a state policy managed by the national secretariat for creative economy and cultural diversity of the special secretariat for culture, in partnership with state and municipalities governments, as well as other civil society institutions (private institutions for-profit and cultural collectives) that articulate, train and foster cultural actions carried out in their communities, and come to be considered culture points or big culture points (when they articulate several points). this policy is based on community culture and manifests itself in different artistic and cultural languages and expressions. its origin dates back to the federal constitution of 1988, which establishes the duty of the state (public power of all spheres) to guarantee the citizen the full exercise of cultural rights and access to sources of national culture, in addition to fostering, valuing, and encouraging production, dissemination, and circulation of knowledge, universal access to cultural goods and services and cooperation between federated entities, public and private agents active in the cultural area, among others (cf / 88, art. 216-a, § 1, items i to iv). and so, as a result of the development of the former cultura viva program, created in 2004 by the then ministry of culture, the cultura viva state policy was instituted, following the publication of law no. 13.018, of 07/22/2014, regulated in 2016. it is the first community-based policy of the national culture system and prioritizes people, groups, communities, and populations that are in a situation of social vulnerability, with reduced access to the means of production, registration, enjoyment, and diffusion of their culture. implementation measures at the national level are carried out through public notices and tenders launched by the union, states, federal district and municipalities for actions to valorize community-based culture, such as: financial support to cultural agents, culture points and big culture points, cultural exchange, cultural education/training, mapping/georeferencing, and monitoring, among others.
Results: Until 2018, 3,602 cultural entities and collectives, located in all 26 states and the federal district, and in more than 1,200 municipalities in the country, were recognized as points of culture and mapped, under the "cultura viva" national policy. in the 2016-2019 period, procedural and documentary improvement actions were implemented, based on ex post evaluations of public policy, such as: (i) implementation of the cultura viva network platform (2016), with the objective of registering, monitoring, mapping/georeferencing the culture points and big culture points, and the cultura viva network; (ii) definition of standardized documents for work plans for interfederative partnerships (agreements) and partnerships with points and big culture points (terms of cultural commitment), with document review and annual update (2016-2020), in order to achieve greater success in planning and efficiency in the execution and accountability of cultural projects and partnerships of the national policy; (iii) renegotiation of inter-federative partnerships of the cultura viva policy, following the publication of ordinance minc no. 31, of 12/11/2018, to effectively make the agreements signed for the execution of networks of culture points feasible; (iv) a study carried out by the getulio vargas foundation on the "cultura viva" national policy and its actions as a state public policy (2018-2019), aiming to promote governance, to monitor, and to propose improvements; (v) allocation of public resources in the plurianual plan (ppa), which establishes the guidelines, goals and targets of the federal government budget for the period 2016-2019, improving the budgetary and financial planning of the policy.
Recommandations: According to the governance, monitoring and proposition for improvements of the cultura viva policy (culture points and big points) report, organized by the getulio vargas foundation (2018): “after the study, it was evident that the continuity of the existence of the culture points it is a sine qua non condition for strengthening cultural experiences, knowledge, and practices, democratizing access to goods and services, among other praxis. the partnerships format, however, must be redesigned, especially concerning accountability, to adapt to the reality of the culture points.” in turn, the monitoring report of the cultura viva national policy, organized by the secretariat of cultural diversity (2019), points out that: (i) the work plan for partnerships with federated entities and civil society organizations was standardized, aiming at better efficiency and good use of public resources by partners; (ii) the regional distribution of the funded partnership instruments is not equal, with greater concentration in the southeast and northeast regions. currently, to reduce this regional difference, the management's priority is to apply regionalization criteria in the public notices, in compliance with the principle of isonomy; (iii) the type of instrument used and the actions contemplated must consider that the culture points network agreements (partnership with federated entities) have their selection and financial support directed to culture points, which execute the cultural commitment term for carrying out cultural projects in the local/regional community; (iv) the public benefit from the actions of the culture points, as well as the segments contemplated in the cultural area, may be better defined when the public consultation with local/regional communities, scheduled for 2020, is carried out.

Main Feature: On 09/28/19, within the framework of the celebration of the national day of visual arts, the unions of that discipline grouped in the national union of artists (una), summoned artists and workers of the visual arts to form a work platform and reflection to improve its legislative and institutional conditions. great artists responded to the call, all of them pledged to work together for the dignity of their sector, which, unlike others such as music, cinema, books and -recently- the performing arts, does not have a development council, nor a fund, nor legislation that promotes it. in addition, the intellectual property law that protects the visual arts in chile dates from 1970.
Results: In november 2019, the bill on the intellectual property rights of artists, authors and performers of fixed image visual works, known as the “balmes law”, in homage to the chilean painter jose balmes, national plastic arts prize (1999). hand in hand with the so-called "visual arts platform", the national union of artists (a group made up of collective management entities and unions such as creaimagen, adg and apech, among others) made a call to strengthen the creation  of a legal framework that guarantees certain rights and provides adequate protection to visual artists. among the notable provisions of this project are the clarification of the basis for calculating the participation right, the application of the term of protection granted by law 17.336 to authors and their heirs and the application of these rights to foreign authors according to the principle of reciprocity.  the legislative processing of the balmes bill whose bulletin is 13098-24 can be followed at:  https://www.senado.cl/appsenado/templates/tramitacion/index.php

Title EN: “la independiente” peruvian publishers fair
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture,Integrate Culture In Sustainable Development Frameworks
SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: National sustainable development policies and plans,Partnering with civil society
Agency Implementation: Ministry of culture
Main Feature: La independiente was born in 2017 as an exhibition, trade, and meeting space for the promotion of peruvian publishing work, the productive exchange of ideas, management models and good publishing practices, and the dynamization of a wide offer of peruvian content that highlights the diversity of the publishing sector. this initiative also aims to encourage reading habits, make visible the literary and artistic production of peruvian authors, promote the development of publishers' catalogs, contribute to the professionalization of the book ecosystem agents and foster improved communication between participating providers and publishers. this fair is organized by the ministry of culture and has the support of the independent publishers association of peru (eip), a non-profit association the mission of which is to integrate and represent the interests of peruvian independent publishers. this association represents a broad spectrum of the national production and is exclusively made up of publishers (legal entities) that publish and promote, with special emphasis, the works of peruvian authors under the guidelines established to strengthen bibliodiversity. la independiente strengthens the capacities of civil society organizations through joint work with the public sector.
Results: The third edition of "la independiente" peruvian publishers fair, which took place in april 2019 in the kuelap room of the ministry of culture, included 42 publishers from 13 regions of the country: ancash, arequipa, cusco, huanuco, junin, la libertad, lambayeque, lima, loreto, moquegua, piura, puno and san martin. this edition had more than 80 programmed activities. over 40 book presentations stood out, addressing topics such as interculturality, illustration, gender, children and juvenile literature, horror, short story, novel, poetry, essay, testimony and digital books. additionally, poetry recitals, expert round tables, book signings and four activities for children were conducted. also, seven workshops took place within the program for the general public, touching on themes such as literary creation, physical and digital books publishing, picture books, among others. conecta editorial aimed to promote the strengthening of the publishing sector agents. in october 2017, an edition of la independiente fair took place in juliaca, in the atrium of the mother church of santa catalina. the publishing group "hijos de la lluvia" was the entity in charge of organizing this fair, which also received the support of the decentralized directorate of culture of puno. within the framework of the aforementioned fair, the first national assembly of publishers was conducted, where 18 publishers from all over peru participated, promoting association. la independiente at lima international book fair (fil lima)  likewise, the participation of la independiente in the lima international book fair expanded during 2018 and 2019. in 2018, la independiente had a stand in which 46 peruvian independent publishers from 9 regions from all over the country (lambayeque, ancash, lima, huanuco, junin, cusco, arequipa, puno and moquegua) were grouped. in 2019, the stand of "la independiente" brought together 48 publishers from 9 regions of peru (ancash, arequipa, cusco, huanuco, junin, lima, loreto, piura and puno) and the implementation unit 003 of the ministry of culture - caral archaeological zone.
Financial Ressources: Approximately usd 31,641.8 per year
Recommandations: The data generated by the participants or attendees to la independiente allowed us to prepare a profile and a characterization of the peruvian publisher, which is currently in progress and under evaluation. likewise, one of the tasks in progress is the positioning of the fair as a central activity in the publishing industry calendar, providing a greater number of dates that stimulate the activity of the sector throughout the year, and not only in limited occasions. finally, another challenge for the next years is to strengthen the use of virtual platforms and digital tools, thus promoting a space called "la independiente digital", which shall broaden the participation of publishers and citizens' access to goods and services.

Title EN: “positioning the country as a film destination, a commitment of the film commission of chile”.
Goal: Achieve A Balanced Flow Of Cultural Goods And Services And Increase The Mobility Of Artists And Cultural Professionals
SDG: SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 10 - Reduce inequality within and among countries,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Flow of cultural goods and services,Flow of cultural goods and services
Agency Implementation: Ministry of cultures, arts and heritage (mincap), through the fcch.
Main Feature: The chilean film commission is a specialized office dependent on the council of art and audiovisual industry of the ministry of cultures, arts and heritage. its objective is to contribute to the development of the national audiovisual industry by promoting chile and its various locations as a film destination on the international scene, increasing the cultural, social and economic impact of our country. in coordination with public and private organizations, they work to improve social and economic conditions, facilitating the development of national and foreign productions throughout the country. the commission provides leadership and coordination among government agencies, service providers, businesses, and others. at the national level, it works to promote and disseminate the work of the audiovisual industry. it offers intergovernmental coordination with all entities that influence audiovisual production processes. in addition, it provides information on locations, entry of people and goods into the country, permits to film and installed capacities (technicians, professionals and companies related to the audiovisual industry). at the international level, its focus is the promotion and diffusion of chile as privileged places to film international productions: feature films, commercials, television programs, among others. it acts as a facilitator for those foreign productions that want to know the national audiovisual offer and develop their projects in a simple and effective way. specifically: coordinates different actors, both nationally and internationally, to facilitate the development of productions in our country; offers as hosts for foreign productions that come to film in chile, providing technical assistance, all the necessary and specialized information, as well as contact with those institutions that provide filming permits; coordinates actions at the national level so that chile is an increasingly friendly country to film, so that the different actors in the industry can enhance their work and offer better conditions for the realization of productions; y, works through strategic alliances with national and international events, with a view to promoting chile as a filming destination. in 2014, the commission began the implementation of the "chile film friendly program", which ensures better conditions to carry out productions, through standardized protocols for granting filming permits, friendly rates, and facilitation of information in the development of filming, and productions in the territories. within this framework, a series of local agreements were created with various communes at national level, which undertake to offer better conditions to carry out productions.
Results: Through the chile film friendly program, the film commission of chile (fcch) has managed to articulate a protocol of service to productions, maintaining a link in the municipalities in charge of issuing permits. these agreements to date have been signed with: valdivia, santiago, providencia and concepcion. it is expected to add 4 municipalities a year. it is important to understand that in 2019, the production promotion corporation - corfo generated a call for support to regional film commissions, where regional film commissions projects from the regions of antofagasta, atacama, biobio, coquimbo, los lagos, aysen and magallanes, could apply to be benefited with technical and financial support for 9 months (from december 2018), for their operation, development or improvement of their management model, action objectives and leading therefore, a collaboration alliance with the fcch, to strengthen regional capacity based on the chile film friendly regional plan. the beneficiaries should respond to relevant information requirements in order to know their programming and management capacity in relation to the regional plan of the fcch. in turn, the projects must maintain constant coordination of the culture series corresponding to the region and fcch for the execution and promotion of their activities.
Financial Ressources: Budget 2019*: clp$8.958.162.000.-/usd$11.491.157. ** annual budget allocated to the audiovisual development fund, the program in which the fcch is hosted as a component of it.
Recommandations: If there is no formal evaluation of the measure, in 2019 the directorate of budgets - dipres dependent of the ministry of finance, drawn up a final report on the evaluation of the audiovisual development fund program, whose component no. 6 is the "national and international positioning and visibilization of the audiovisual field" and which includes the work that the film commission of chile carries forward. available at: https://www.dipres.gob.cl/597/articles-189316_informe_final.pdf

Title EN: “preparation of a first participatory public account of a ministerial nature”.
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture,Integrate Culture In Sustainable Development Frameworks
SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: National sustainable development policies and plans,Partnering with civil society
Agency Implementation: Ministry of cultures, arts and heritage (mincap).
Main Feature: The citizen participation mechanism called "participatory public account" is established in law no. 20.500 of 2011, on "associations and citizen participation in public management". it is a process that provides spaces for dialogue and exchange of opinions between the institutions, their respective authorities and the community, with the purpose of publicizing the management to subsequently evaluate it, promote transparency, generate conditions of trust and guarantee the exercise of citizen control over public administration. during these instances there is the possibility of formulating questions and comments, which must be officially answered; citizen control and co-responsibility is also promoted, guaranteeing standards of transparency and public probity in accordance with law no. 20,880 on "probity in public function and prevention of conflicts of interest". along these lines, said law also considers the participation of the council of civil society as an institutional instance, destined to present observations to the public account document, regulating the form and terms. mincap has this council by provision of law no. 21,045, which establishes the national council of cultures, arts and heritage and assigns it in turn the quality of council of civil society. the structure of the participatory public account 2018-2019 of mincap considered 5 axes of reportability, which, in turn, correspond to the objectives that guide the actions of the institution in the long term. these are: "decentralization and citizen participation", "art and creativity in education", "creation and creative freedom for artists", "enhancement of heritage" and "installation of the new ministry of cultures, arts and heritage".
Results: The activity that took place in may 2019 was attended by national and regional authorities, led by the minister of cultures, arts and heritage, consuelo valdes chadwick. 172 people participated in the exhibition phase of the activity, where just over a third declared to live in the commune of casablanca (34%), where the activity was located; 26% in valparaiso and vina del mar. seen as a whole,valparaiso region accounts for 60% of attendance at the activity. in relation  to other regions of the country, it is relevant to say that the second with the largest presence was the metropolitan, in particular the commune of santiago, with 15%. regarding the composition of the total attendees according to sex, 44% corresponded to men and 56% to women. when analyzing participation according to belonging to institutions or organizations, it is observed that 42% work in the public sector, counting 57 mincap officials among them. on the other hand, 37% of the total participants declare that they belong to institutions and civil society organizations, while 21% do not belong or do not declare. similarly, 53% of those attending do not participate in cultural organizations, in contrast to 28% who do, while the remaining 19% do not specify it. in the face-to-face activity after minister consuelo valdes's presentation, roundtables were held, in which 54 people participated,of which 67% were women and 33% men. as can be seen in graph 4, the table that aroused the most interest was that of "value enhancement of assets", which comprised 41% of the total number of participants; the round table "decentralization of culture, arts and heritage" concentrated 20%; "art and creativity in education" 19%, the "cultural participation" table at 13% and, finally, the "creation and creative freedom" table, which brought together 7% of those who attended the activity. additionally, it is relevant to note that the expository phase of the participatory public account 2018-2019 was followed by 647 users through streaming. in the "participatory public account report 2018-2019", a complete and detailed synthesis of the public account of mincap, made by minister consuelo valdes, is offered. through this document, the institution responds to the commitment established with the participating people, both in presence and virtual ways, referring to the return and answering your comments and questions. available in:	https://www.cultura.gob.cl/cuentapublica/wp-content/uploads/sites/28/2019/07/informe_cpp_mincap_2018-2019.pdf.
Recommandations: If there is no formal evaluation of these processes of preparing the public account, it is important to mention that for the periods 2016 and 2017, the former cnca (today, mincap) was awarded by the division of social organizations dependent of the segegob, thanks to its excellent performance of the participatory public account process, which involves a process that provides instruments and dialogues in spaces of dialogue instruments its respective authorities ,and the community, with the purpose of making knowledge of the management, to later evaluate it and guarantee the exercise of the citizen control over the public administration.

Title EN: “the sea, a successful collaboration work at different levels and with different actors”.
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture,Integrate Culture In Sustainable Development Frameworks
SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: National sustainable development policies and plans,Cultural and creative sectors
Cultural Domain: Cinema and Audiovisual Arts,Music,Performing Arts,Visual Arts
Agency Implementation: Ministry of cultures, arts and heritage (mincap), through the department of education and training in arts and culture, dependent of the undersecretariat for cultures and arts.
Main Feature: The arts education week (sea), is an international celebration, promoted by unesco that seeks to "sensitize the international community about the importance of arts education; and promoting cultural diversity, intercultural dialogue and social cohesion". in chile, it has been celebrated since 2013 and is aimed at boys and girls and young people of school age, a stage of education where the development of the arts and creativity play a fundamental role in generating freer and more aware subjects of their environment. during the specific days of the celebration, the participants of the network are invited to make visible their experiences and artistic projects, around the theme, which the sea guides each year. the 2020 motto is "transform the present, dream the future" and it is an invitation to promote and enhance the protagonism of children, girls and young people (nnj) through collaborative artistic experiences that develop and make visible their ideas, likes, interests, actions and concerns. in addition, it invites the adult world to recognize and value it. the realization of artistic projects is proposed as an effective support for transforming participation, capable of plasming the dream of a different world that modifies present realities. to participate, institutions must register on the institutional page of the mincap: http://semanaeducacionartistica.cultura.gob.cl/ . this platform provides tools to plan activities and allows the different collaborating institutions to share materials, news, disseminate their activities and report on specific calls for each region. during sea, educational establishments are opened to receive art and culture, inviting artists and cultors to carry out talks, actions, tours and/or workshops open to the educational community that generates a memorable and understanding artistic experience contributes art to education. if an artist wants to participate in this celebration, they can access this platform and review the schools and liceos of their locality that are adhered to the sea and who wish to be contacted by an / a artist or cultor.
Results: After 7 years of experience, the sea in our country has stopped being an isolated landmark and has become a permanent platform to disseminate artistic education experiences and favor collaboration networks between schools, cultural spaces, playschools, universities, artists and cultors. through the web page http://semanaeducacionartistica.cultura.gob.cl/ which remains active throughout the year, the different institutions that register can contact themselves, share news, videos, related art pages, education pages. during the specific celebration days, the network participants are invited to visibilize their experiences and artistic projects, around the theme, which each year guides the sea. during the present year and in the context of the health crisis, it is important to understand that the sea has kept all its platforms active to offer online activities to the diverse educational communities that require it today. in this way, the call was made for cultural spaces, universities, educational establishments to continue to register and actively participate in the web platform, relating to it as an important element of dissemination and exchange of article practices.
Financial Ressources: Budget 2019: clp$70.000.000.-/usd$90.000.- *annual budget.
Recommandations: Although there was no formal evaluation of the program, we can mention some elements that have allowed the consolidation of the sea model in chile: -	collaboration at different levels and between different actors: the sea is installed on the premise of collaboration, as one of the characteristics of quality artistic education. in this sense, it is organized by an executive board in which different actors linked to artistic education converge: unesco, mincap, mineduc, university of chile and balmaceda young art - baj. the articulation of actors also supposes a second benefit: economic sustainability, since, in a logic of network, interaction and interdependence, the management of these projects or programs involves resources beyond their own or assigned ones. -	art as a way of knowing: sea is a privileged moment to make visible the contributions of art in education and to position art education as a way of understanding the complexity of the current world. in this context, during these 6 years of travel, the sea has emphasized in relieving art as a way of knowing, without reducing it to a mere doing. to achieve this, each year, a different theme is defined that guides the celebration, inviting teachers, artists, educators and students to reflect and develop projects on contemporary issues. -	consolidation of a flexible celebration model: the celebration model is articulated around an official program, led by the executive board and the regional secretaries of culture and a program self-managed by local cultural agents (schools, cultural spaces, universities, from the executive table, a theme is proposed, guiding documents are prepared for each of the summoned agents (schools, cultural spaces, universities, artists), with the aim of encouraging participation, making the emphasis of each celebration and contribute with pedagogical suggestions articulated from 4 fundamental axes of artistic education: the reflective process, the creative process, the link with the context; and, the visibility and enhancement of the processes developed. -	institutionalization of the artistic education week: a highly relevant element in the consolidation of the chilean sea model has been the institutionalization of this initiative, through different instruments of public policy. for example, from the mincap, in the 15 regions of the country, tables of artistic education have been formed that favor collaborative work between institutions, educators, artists and groups that develop training processes in art and culture. since 2016, the regional celebrations of the sea have been promoted as part of the work plan of these tables.

Main Feature: During the prague quadrennial 2019 the georgian national pavilion pursues the goal to document transformation of aesthetics of georgian theatre and demonstrate political context, communication culture and interaction of artistic reflections. modern practice of georgian theatre focuses on a wide range of dialogues, reflections on the essence and opportunities. the subjects of the dialogue unite local and global identities including wider paradigms and groups representing subcultures and gender. the dialogue consists of diverse elements and vectors giving the theatre a role of a universal medium that should foster a complex process, identify the problems and support the involved sides in renewal of their identities, “create” a common knowledge through communication. under the circumstance of the shift of paradigm the process of search of renewed identity, which unites confrontational and communicative aspects, becomes especially active. during the pq19 exposition of the georgian national pavilion “the unlocked circle” will resonate with the newest theatrical trend. it is based on the dialogue and is especially visible in the works of the young directors who attempt to represent social, cultural and political contexts that give birth to the changes of a paradigm, start transformation of the language of georgian theatre (among them through formation of so called “new theatre of sensitivity”). it is important that the “new theatre of sensitivity” documents the recent history as part of a “dialogue”.
Results: The result of the project is the popularization of georgian scenography and theater and other georgian arts.  the project presented the current changes in the georgian theater and scenography in 2013-2019, the reflection of the creators on modern political and social processes.  participation in pq19 became an opportunity for georgian artists to find new partners, plan future projects and most importantly, the participation of professionals in oistat forums. rallies was a good opportunity to establish active contacts and expand cooperation within this international network.

Agency Implementation: Društvo za razvoj trajnostnega oblikovanja TRAJNA
Main Feature: Krater is an emerging production space for transdisciplinary practices, which sprouted from the neglected, crater-resembling construction site near the city center of Ljubljana. By exploring the potential for world-making projects on the lands of anthropogenic ruins, Krater acts as the situated prototype of a terraforming agency. Site-specific production stations (papermaking workshop, wood workshop and myco-design lab) which consist of open access, ever-evolving workshop spaces, are set to create a dialogue with the impoverished crust of earth colonized with invasive and other feral plants.The urban laboratory Krater is opened with the aim of establishing a unique polygon for researchers from the fields of design, ecology, biology, architecture, landscape architecture, law, performing arts, and other scientists and cultural creators. Although Krater is accessible to the general public who can freely roam the location in the presence of contract signatories or participate in numerous curated programs for all generations, it is extremely important to emphasize that the contract with the Ministry has enabled the situated establishment of a research institute for the younger generation, which does not have many opportunities to work outside the established market-defined positions of their professions. Atthe Crater, through interdisciplinary collaborations, offers an exceptional model of coexistence taking care of urban ecology, research of biomaterials, creation of public programs, and production of new jobs.This is also evidenced by the exceptional support that the collective receives for its operation on pioneering projects in regenerative design and urban ecology from international institutions: 	Het Nieuwe Instituut in Rotterdam, 	University of Sheffield, 	University of Amsterdam, 	Floating University in Berlin, 	Atelier Luma in Arles, 	Master in Architecture in Luxembourg, 	European Center for Research on the Impact of Creative Practices CIRCE in Berlin, 	The Savannah Center for Contemporary Art in Tamale SCCA (Ghana), 	and many other cultural and educational institutions. Therefore, this is not a space that offers accessibility only to the local public, but a space that represents a pioneering example of a new urban typology in European dimensions, admired, researched, co-created, and supported by a wide international (professional) audience. This is supported by  mass requests for guided tours, and numerous invitations forpartnerships in European projects. Regardless, the Krater and its user community remain dependent on obtaining public funds for designing programs and activities on site, so the schedules and rhythms of opening the space and activities on it depend on successful applications.
Results: Creatives at the Krater are involved in numerous internationally acclaimed, award-winning initiatives in sustainable design and ecology. This year, Krater was recognized as the official exhibition space for the 35th Ljubljana Graphic Biennial, won the Plečnik Medal for best public space (2023), and was a finalist for the New European Bauhaus Award (2022) and the European Prize for Urban Public Space (2022). Its caretakers aim to welcome a diverse audience, having engaged over 4200 citizens and 600 school children in educational programs, making the space accessible to an international audience as well.The Krater's ecosystem serves as a research environment for international experts in law, ecology, architecture, and design, focusing on climate-resilient urban futures and critically addressing greenwashing. It's a topic of doctoral dissertations and master's theses across various fields, and has hosted interns from design schools in France, the Netherlands, Estonia, and the UK. Krater's community outputs span from conferences, roundtables, documentary films, music events, performances, and prototypes for sustainable materials and techniques. Its commitment to using natural materials earned the Made in Slovenia certificate for product design.This initiative has introduced new discourses into culture, design, and architecture, gradually gaining prominence in the local educational landscape, partly due to our efforts. The European project Future DiverCities recognized our unique experience, inviting us to design a curriculum on ecological regeneration for cultural organizations across Europe. We have hosted debates on cultural policies, sustainable construction, and spatial planning, attracting ministry representatives and other state institution leaders, offering a unique service of caring for discarded plants, and conducting weekly tours for a wide range of academic and professional visitors.Our project research and international collaborations over the last three years have highlighted the Krater as a pioneering ecosystem in Ljubljana, a self-sustaining biodiversity reserve that demands reevaluation in the face of climate change. Future interventions in this space will be informed by our findings, aligning with European standards for a climate-resilient future.

Main Feature: Considéré comme un monde parallèle, immersif, en trois dimensions, un monde virtuel mais aux interactions bien réelles, le Metaverse est un monde où chacun peut évoluer, à travers un avatar ou un hologramme. Un monde virtuel dans lequel on pourra travailler, se divertir, voyager, consommer, étudier, retrouver des proches…Curiosité supplémentaire, il est au cœur du numérique du futur et à l’interconnexion de l’industrie créative (3D, animation, jeu vidéo, VR, AR, design architectural…) et des technologies (IA, Blockchain, IoT, 5G…). Le Metaverse se nourrit donc de technologie et de contenus…La plupart des projets viennent essentiellement des États-Unis, de Chine, de Corée, du Japon et d’Europe.Dans l’espace Africain et plus spécifiquement en Tunisie, l'objectif étant de ne plus être uniquement des consommateurs, mais d'être acteur, influenceur, s’approprier la technologie, et penser son futur, et celui de l’humanité, et de la jeunesse. Donc il s'avère crucial de veiller à ce que la première ressource de l’Afrique, la jeunesse, puisse s’adapter véritablement et efficacement alors que le Metaverse va redéfinir les compétences d’avenir.Alors comment penser la transformation digitale, au service des populations (notamment des jeunes et des femmes), de la diversité culturelle et linguistique, de la démocratie sans répondre à l’émergence de ces mondes virtuels, du Metaverse ?C'est ainsi que le TICDCE propose de mener une réflexion et des expérimentations (à travers des conférences, des ateliers, du réseautage, des expositions) pour identifier, évaluer les problématiques, les enjeux liés afin d’élaborer des propositions, imaginer des solutions pour se projeter vers un futur numérique meilleur.
Results: - Organisation d’une conférence consacrée au « Metaverse et Industries Créatives Culturelles à l’heure de la francophonie numérique » le 18 novembre 2022. Et ce en marge du 18ème sommet de la Francophonie Djerba 2022. Sous le slogan : « Imaginons la Francophonie numérique d’Après » Créons un futur qui nous ressemble, qui nous rassemble, qui nous unit. La conférence a réuni 23 experts du monde Francophone avec la présence de 2 Ministres Tunisiens (affaires Culturelles / Economie et planification). Ce sommet était le point de départ et était l’initiateur pour placer la thématique au cœur des travaux du gouvernement à l’occasion des workshops des « Assises de l’Innovation ».- Exécution du projet « Africa Metaverse » qui est une initiative lancée par le DigiArtLivingLab (DALL) (Tunisie), Laboratoire d'innovation sociale et ouverte de l'école d'Art et de Technologie NET-INFO (Tunisie) et Lancé par l’Africa Metaverse Summit du 1 au 3 Juin 2022 (sommet virtuel lancé de la Tunisie). Ce projet a mis en place « l’Académie Africaine de la Metaverse » avec plusieurs partenaires publics (tel que le TICDCE), privé et OSC. Ce projet a permis de Créer une plateforme de type Metaverse africain qui a réuni la communauté du numérique Africain et la communauté africaine du Gaming, de la VR & AR, des Comics, de l'Art digital, et autres ... autour de la culture et du patrimoine africain. L’objectif étant de développer un nouveau narratif, un nouveau «storytelling» sur une Afrique, qui innove et qui gagne.- Plusieurs projets Metaverse ont été développés par des startups soutenues par le TICDCE tels que le projet « Digital twin de Ribat de Sousse »…

Main Feature: The belize international music and food festival was conceived as a dynamic platform 1) for belizean artists to showcase their creative expressions and musical talent; 2) to serve as a space for belizeans artists to foster connections within the music industry; 3) and to bring visibility to belize’s creative industry. first launched in 2022, the festival supports the growth and development of belize’s orange economy, particularly the music sector. the two-day festival is a space to showcase the breadth of musical talents from every corner of the country. it is also an opportunity for belizean artists to enhance their performing skills through stage performance training that is offered as part of being enlisted as a performer. artists can also share new music and gain international and local exposure through the marketing initiatives to promote the festival, carried out by the belize tourism board. the festival also aims to boost belize’s tourism traffic during a traditionally slow time of the year for tourism by serving as a highly anticipated and signature event.  the festival features belizean and international performers and is complemented by a vibrant culinary landscape. the second festival will be held july 28 and 29, 2023.
Results: The first festival was a success with close to 9,000 persons in attendance over the two days. the festival fueled economic activity and boosted tourism activity on the island of san pedro, ambergris caye where it was held. a profit of $ 25,798 usd was also generated. this was used to create two state-of-the-art recording studios in the northern and central parts of belize.  the second festival will result in a greater number of belizean performers with more than 50 musicians and djs scheduled to participate along with international performers from the caribbean and the usa. a wider range of music genres will be featured including traditional and indigenous music such as paranda, punta, and brukdown. the belizean performers for the 2023 festival also represent different geographic areas, performing experience, age categories, and include males and females.
Financial Ressources: Financial resources allocated in usd $433,354.
Recommandations: The first edition of the belize international music and food festival contributed to the strengthening of the creative skills of the local performers and increased their visibility. the festival provides a much needed platform for cultural expression and exposure for belize’s cultural and creative industries. belizean artists were able to enhance and share their craft, reaching new audiences.  the profits from the first festival was used to create an orange economy fund. this will bring together belize’s creative talents and strengthen the local economy.

Title EN: Commemorating the 50th anniversary of the martyrdom of novelist ghassan kanafani
Goal: Achieve A Balanced Flow Of Cultural Goods And Services And Increase The Mobility Of Artists And Cultural Professionals

Area of Monitoring: Flow of cultural goods and services,Mobility of artists and cultural professionals
Agency Implementation: Ministry of culture
Main Feature: The ministry of culture organized a series of activities and events to commemorate the 50th anniversary of the martyrdom of novelist ghassan kanafani. the policy/measure was initiated after several meetings with civil society organizations (csos) to promote palestinian literature and the need to share it with the world. the main activities of the anniversary included: 1. seminars and festivals held in various locations such as the west bank, jerusalem, and 48 lands to commemorate the anniversary. 2. a narrative conference held in jordan with the participation of writers and novelists from seven arab countries. 3. another narrative conference held in gaza at al azhar university with the participation of academics, writers, and artists from gaza. 4. the launch of the ghassan kanafani novel prize for youth to encourage the writing of the best novel. through these activities, the ministry of culture aimed to promote palestinian literature, preserve the legacy of ghassan kanafani, and encourage young writers to contribute to the palestinian narrative. to commemorate the fiftieth anniversary of the martyrdom of ghassan kanafani, a series of cultural events and seminars were organized in amman and gaza with the participation of writers and critics from palestine and abroad. additionally, a book about his life was published for both children and adults, along with a podcast magazine that explored his life and work. in collaboration with the tamer foundation, a play and a comic book based on his famous work "men in the sun" were also created. furthermore, a summary of the conference held in gaza, amman, and ramallah was printed and distributed. finally, the ghassan kanafani prize for arabic fiction was established to recognize and encourage new writers in the field.
Results: 1. increased awareness among the youth and general public about the importance of palestinian narrative and the legacy of ghassan kanafani as a prominent novelist. 2. the organization of successful seminars, festivals, and conferences commemorating the anniversary in various locations, including the west bank, 48 lands, jerusalem, jordan, and gaza. 3. the establishment of the ghassan kanafani novel prize for youth, which encourages and recognizes young writers for their contributions to the palestinian narrative. 4. encouragement of learning and improving the best ways of narrative in literature and other forms of creative writing. 5. the prize for the best writer is now an annual event, which provides a continuous platform for promoting and encouraging the development of palestinian literature and narrative.
Recommandations: 1. make efforts to make the next project in palestine. 2. make efforts to call for experts for next activity 3. the experts must be 7 years’ experience in the field

Title EN: Culture sector working group meetings (cswg)
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture
SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Partnering with civil society
Agency Implementation: Ministry of cultue
Main Feature: The main feature of the policy/measure is the establishment of a culture sector working group (cswg) that meets regularly to promote effective and coordinated implementation of culture programs in palestine. the cswg consists of 8 members and is headed by the ministry of culture and its deputy, the norwegian kingdom, while the technical advisor is the unesco office in the state of palestine. the group's purpose is to strengthen sector-specific and technical policy dialogue and exchange of information between all relevant stakeholders, ensuring adherence to the national plans and priorities. the cswg is a platform for policy dialogue, information sharing, and achieving set milestones in the sector strategies, which will assist in the overall achievement of the palestinian national development plan and the national strategy for culture sector 2020-2022. the specialized sector working group in culture brings about improvements in program alignment and harmonization, coordinating investments, creating synergies, promoting results-based management, and creating mutual accountability through timely and transparent information sharing. the cswg also helps to face the most prominent challenges and weaknesses of legislative structure in the cultural sector, poverty of infrastructure, poor coordination between partners working in cultural affairs, financial crises, and the modesty of the status of women and their contribution to the making of culture. such huge challenges require the establishment of a specialized sector working group that can work accordingly and in a timely manner to make sure that a good strategy is in place to face these challenges. in conclusion, the culture sector working group is a crucial measure to ensure effective and coordinated implementation of culture programs and to face the significant challenges faced by the cultural sector in palestine. through policy dialogue, information sharing, and mutual accountability, the cswg aims to strengthen the sector-specific and technical policy dialogue and exchange of information between all relevant stakeholders, thus promoting the growth and development of the culture sector in palestine.
Results: The implementation of the culture sector working group (cswg) has resulted in several positive outcomes. these include the compilation and sharing of data on ongoing and planned projects in culture between all members, as well as input to relevant culture sector plans and gap reports. the cswg has also supported the submission of project plans by the ministry/agency and provided a statement of progress towards aid effectiveness goals. additionally, the group has issued statements on innovative aid delivery practices trialed in the sector and contributed to national cross-sector issues and discussions. it has also issued statements on key issues such as human rights, climate, and gender. ongoing discussions between all donors of the sector about the current and future of the sector have been facilitated by the cswg, leading to a more coordinated and effective approach to supporting the culture sector in palestine.
Recommandations: The cswg has a core group that meets before and after meetings to prepare the agenda for the next meetings and evaluate and follow up on the outcomes. after each meeting, the core group puts forth its recommendations, which include: 1. inviting new donors and private sector institutions to deliver presentations on their work in the culture sector to expand support for the sector. 2. following up on the decisions made during cswg meetings. 3. activating the presentation of new studies about culture during cswg meetings. 4. activating members to share their plans and strategies for the sector with cswg. 5. focusing on proactive discussion and feedback from invitees that can contribute to the deliberations of the sector strategy for 2024-2029. 6. establishing a culture thematic working group to discuss specific technical issues.

Title EN: Memory code
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture
SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Digital environment
Agency Implementation: Ministry of culture
Main Feature: The memory code project is a policy initiative that seeks to enhance the visual digital content about all palestinian national figures. it aims to produce a group of short films in different languages that display visual digital content through a barcode that is carved into a screen. the project also includes placing a work of art (interpenetration of races) in different places in cities, town camps, and villages. the primary aim of these codes is to make the short films available anytime and anywhere through a barcode that can be scanned via a mobile device. this means that workers in the cultural sector will have access to all the digital content they need. the project seeks to make the rich history and cultural heritage of palestine easily accessible to anyone, anywhere in the world, and to preserve it for future generations.
Results: He results achieved so far through the implementation of the memory code policy/measure are: - the initiative has successfully reached out to all palestinian intellectuals and artists living in villages, camps, and marginalized places, making it possible to capture and preserve their knowledge and experiences. - the project has succeeded in making palestinian culture more accessible and modern by digitizing it and using barcodes to display the visual digital content. - the program has been instrumental in introducing and promoting the use of digital technology to preserve and share cultural heritage. palestinian youth, in particular, have been able to benefit from this program and develop their knowledge and skills in this area. overall, the memory code policy/measure has been successful in its aims of promoting palestinian culture and preserving it for future generations. the use of digital technology has allowed for wider access to this rich cultural heritage, and the project has helped to empower marginalized communities and individuals by giving them a platform to share their experiences and knowledge.
Recommandations: After evaluating the memory code policy/measure, we have reached some conclusions and recommendations. our recommendations are that while the project has shown promising results, it is not easy for everyone to use. the project requires a digital mobile device and a digital barcode, which could limit access for some individuals. we have held meetings with our partners to evaluate the first phase of the project and are currently waiting for the next phase to begin. we recommend that further efforts be made to increase accessibility and expand the reach of the project to ensure that more people can benefit from it. in conclusion, while the memory code policy/measure has shown potential in preserving and promoting palestinian culture, it needs to be made more accessible and user-friendly. we recommend that efforts be made to improve the technology and infrastructure needed to use the project and to engage with communities to ensure that they can fully benefit from this initiative.

Cultural Domain: Performing Arts,Visual Arts,Music,Publishing,Design,Cinema and Audiovisual Arts,Media Arts

Main Feature: It is the definitive document on matters of policy orientation and operationalization on the management and use of arts and culture in the gambia. in this policy, culture is defined as “set of distinctive spiritual, material, intellectual and emotional features of society or a social group, and that it encompasses in addition to art and literature, lifestyles, ways of living together, value systems, traditions and beliefs”. (source: unesco universal declaration on cultural diversity adopted in 2001). the policy is the guiding document on matters pertaining to arts and culture and has been developed through rigorous public participation to ensure sustainable management and use of the arts and culture of the gambia for the benefit of her people. it has been developed through intensive and inclusive stakeholder participation, updating the first national cultural policy developed in 1988, and the use of a unesco funded international consultant. the process was spearheaded by the national centre for arts and culture (ncac), under the aegis of the ministry of tourism and culture, as the government coordinating agency for the management, promotion and development of the arts and culture sector. the process involved many stakeholders through consultative meetings, site visits, workshops and the development of needs assessments based on swot (strengths, weaknesses, opportunities and threats) analysis. there were subsequent stakeholders’ consultative meetings culminating in a two-day national stakeholders’ validation forum that adopted the draft text of this policy. a select team of stakeholders was set up by the forum to further vet the first draft in line with the decisions adopted. the policy is formulated to address the management and use of cultural heritage resources for the benefit of the country and its people. the policy is consistent with the constitution of the gambia, and other related national legislations dealing with management and use of arts and culture heritage resources. the process was supported by the government, unesco and other national partners. finally, as part of the realization of the policy commitments made herein, the government of the gambia through the ministry responsible for arts and culture and the national centre for arts and culture immediately upon approval of this document shall develop a strategic plan and business plan as may be applicable to start the process of implementation.
Results: 1.	passing of a copyright regulation 2018 and the establishment of the collecting society of the gambia (csg). 2.	establishment of the artistic associations- music, film, theatre, fashion, visual arts, writers, book publishers, models and photographers. 3.	creative business enterprise training, mentoring and funding support programme established to focus on youth development 4.	introduction of 70 percent local content in radio and tv stations throughout the country 5.	the gambia government in 2020, disbursed 60, 000 us dollars as covid-19 relief fund for 3000 individual artists and artists groups
Recommandations: •	the mandate of the ncac was widened to include the administration of copyright •	the organogram was restructured from a division to a directorate system •	a special directorate was created to manage the 2005 convention domain •	the gambia has benefitted from the unesco-aschberg funding for 2022/23 to improve the status of female artists and cultural professionals

Title EN: Playwrights workshop trinbago (pwt)
Goal: Integrate Culture In Sustainable Development Frameworks
SDG: SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Cultural and creative sectors
Agency Implementation: National drama association of trinidad and tobago (ndatt)
Main Feature: The playwright’s workshop trinbago (pwt) was initiated in 2003 by theatre icon, actor, playwright, director, producer and lecturer, tony hall (1948-2020) with support from trinity in trinidad study away programme of trinity college, hartford, c.t. lordstreet theatre’s jouvay institute and the national drama association of trinidad & tobago. pwt is a collective of playwrights, theatre practitioners and enthusiasts working together to make plays for stage, screen, street and radio. the pwt has spawned numerous projects including the monthly readers theatre series (mrts), the new play festival (npf) and the pwt circle. since 2009 and continuing throughout this reporting period, during the mrts, playwrights, theatre practitioners and enthusiasts meet on the first wednesday of every month at 7 pm to listen to a cold reading of the selected script(s) and participate in a discussion to assist the playwrights with the further development of the scripts. some sessions featured readings of multiple plays, with scripts written by playwrights from trinidad and tobago, jamaica, the us, the uk, and nigeria. the readings are advertised on social media platforms and through newspaper articles. the playwrights are present to observe the reading and discussion and make a few opening remarks. as part of the capacity building the playwrights are encouraged to take notes from the discussions and consider the feedback received in their writing process. the feedback includes playwriting notes given by veteran playwrights and directors present at the sessions. this programme also offers playwrights valuable insight into how audiences will perceive their story, characters, and plot before the play is produced on a stage. readers are cast from regular attendees to the sessions, who see the script for the first time on the day of the reading or the day before in certain instances. this activity builds the capacity of readers, especially actors who are able to improve upon their script analysis and cold reading skills, and build their networks of fellow actors, playwrights, directors and producers. some actors who have read in the mrts were selected to participate in the npf where they received further training in the playbuilding workshops, as well as an income earning opportunity. the playwrights are also offered the opportunity to have their script considered for the npf, which takes three plays which would have been read in the mrts and further develops them in a five-phase process leading to a full staging of the finished play. playwrights and actors are provided training in workshops, panel discussions and online seminars through interaction with veteran theatre practitioners functioning as dramaturges and directors. during the covid-19 pandemic, the pwt and its activities were taken online via the zoom platform, which allowed greater access to local, regional and worldwide participants and audiences. in 2020 and 2021, the pwt circle transitioned to online and held weekly sessions on wednesdays to practice and enhance cold reading and script analysis skills. in april 2023, the mrts evolved into a hybrid form featuring in-person and online components. the sessions have been held at queen’s hall, port of spain and via zoom. the online component was maintained in an effort to continue building the existing and new online audiences. through the use of multimedia and other visual and audio equipment, playwrights, readers and audiences participate both in-person and online.
Results: From january 2019 to may 2023, the mrts has featured the reading and discussion of 64 scripts by more than 73 playwrights. four sessions featured scripts written by playwriting students at the department of creative and festival arts, the university of the west indies, st augustine. since the transition to online platforms in april 2020 in response to the nationwide shutdowns due to covid-19, 37 scripts have been read online, featuring playwrights from the us, jamaica, barbados and nigeria. since 2019, npf has workshopped 10 new plays, engaged 11 playwrights, 7 dramaturges, 8 directors and more than 85 practitioners as cast, crew and festival production team. in 2019 npf workshopped 3 new plays by 3 playwrights, and engaged 3 directors, 3 dramaturges, 17 actors, and 5 people crew and festival production team. in 2020 no festival was held due to the lockdown imposed as part of the covid-19 pandemic. in 2021, the play development workshop phase facilitated by the bangalore little theatre, india, developed 5 new plays written by 6 playwrights all of which had dramatic readings performed online. two plays were further workshopped, filmed at a performing arts venue and aired on online platforms for viewing and panel discussion to audiences from trinidad and tobago, as well as india. the festival also engaged 2 dramaturges, 5 directors, 49 actors, and 16 people as crew and the festival production team. in 2022, the festival ended after the 2nd phase due to scheduling conflicts of the playwrights with the reopening of theatres and other work-related activities. the festival to that point had engaged 2 playwrights, 2 dramaturges, and 2 people from bangalore little theatre, india. some readers and actors who attend the mrts and playwrights circle have transitioned from reading in the sessions to becoming playwrights themselves. in the reverse, playwrights who have had their plays read in the mrts have returned as readers and in some cases become actors. actors who consistently take part in the sessions have shown great improvement in their reading ability, script analysis skills, and delivery on stage. due to its recognition as working with contemporary playwrights, pwt was asked to perform two in-person dramatic readings of excerpts from plays by local playwrights at the ngc bocas literary festival. these readings took place on april 29 and 30 at the national library, port of spain.

Title EN: Promoting the respect and appreciation of uganda’s indigenous ethnic minority communities through cultural entrepreneurship
Goal: Integrate Culture In Sustainable Development Frameworks
SDG: SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: National sustainable development policies and plans
Agency Implementation: Cross cultural foundation of uganda (ccfu)
Main Feature: In uganda, there are about 21 indigenous ethnic minority groups (imgs) whose combined total population is not more than 1 million people. they are among the most marginalised categories of people in uganda. women and young people from img communities are doubly marginalised. some of them such as the benet, bagabo and bakingwe are not recognised in the national constitution while others appear with either derogatory names or names they do not associate with as a people. imgs are less represented in leadership structures and access to basic social services is hampered by limited access to national identity cards that allow them enjoy the services. owing to this, ccfu engaged with imgs through use of creative arts to create awareness about and promote the rights of imgs while improving their livelihood.  ccfu identified and worked with 6 women and 4 young people’s groups to engage them in cultural entrepreneurship projects. small seed grants based on 2 year plans were to target beneficiaries to purchase raw materials for making art and crafts and music instruments. some of the products were sold to earn income to the imgs while others were linked to close-by community museums to include in the artefacts that demonstrate the habitats of the communities. through advocacy, imgs were also supported to showcase their products at various events (both local and national) and demonstrate the identities of these imgs. ccfu supported the formation of 2 regional advocacy platforms for imgs (one in the rwenzori and another in the karamoja regions). the capacities of imgs to lobby and advocate for their rights were built through trainings and joint activity implementation for mentorship. others were supported to express themselves through their traditional music and dance. documenting oral history of imgs and disseminating it at national and local levels was done to increase written evidence and information about their ethnicity and support as an advocacy tool. central and local government leadership, parliamentarians and other human rights organisations were engaged in sensitisation and dissemination events about the existence and rights violations faced by imgs.
Results: Indigenous ethnic minority people have been recognised and their cultural, social and political rights respected at the local levels (district). owing to the advocacy engagements where indigenous people showcased their culture through creative arts, they have been included in local leadership structures. some are now heading sub counties, others district sector committees, school management committees while others are on the local council leadership committees the equal opportunities commission picked interest in the plight of imgs and are leading the process of redressing their violated rights through development of national action plans and ensuring their inclusion in annual plans and budgets of the different government ministries. there is also improved knowledge level about the existence of imgs by the different majority ethnicities in uganda. ccfu in collaboration with the national coalition on the rights of imgs celebrates the world day of indigenous persons (4 years in a row now) and this has provided an avenue for advocacy.  information and education materials have been produced and are providing a resource base for the population as learning materials.

Title EN: Radio programs
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture
SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Media diversity
Agency Implementation: Minsitry of culture
Main Feature: The main features of the policy/measure are: - a one-hour weekly radio program that focuses on cultural issues, promotes culture and arts, talents, intellectuals, and various initiatives. - the program is broadcasted on five radio stations in gaza and palestine and reaches marginalized areas in remote areas of palestine. - the program is also available on all social media platforms for the ministry and the partner radios, which include 24 fm, mawwal radio, hebron radio, shabab fm, and zaman fm. - the ongoing program has interviewed tens of players in the sector, leaders, youngsters, and foreign intellectuals in the years 2021 and 2022. - the program promotes cultural diversity and raises awareness on international cultural topics.
Results: The weekly radio program focusing on cultural issues has been highly successful in its efforts to reach marginalized areas in palestine. through its broadcasts on five different radio stations, including 24 fm, mawwal radio, hebron radio, shabab fm, and zaman fm, the program has been able to bring cultural awareness and promotion to even the most remote corners of palestine. one of the key successes of the program has been its ability to reach marginalized groups, particularly youth and women. by promoting youth initiatives, experiences, and talents, the program has been able to inspire and motivate the younger generation to get involved in the cultural sector. women have also been given a voice through the program, which has helped to break down gender barriers in the cultural sphere. in addition to reaching marginalized areas and promoting youth initiatives, the program has also been successful in covering activities in the cultural sector. by interviewing leaders and players in the sector, as well as foreign intellectuals, the program has brought attention to cultural diversity and international cultural topics. this has helped to broaden the cultural horizons of listeners and promote understanding and appreciation of different cultures. overall, the radio program has been an effective tool for promoting and supporting the cultural sector in palestine. its ability to reach marginalized areas and promote youth initiatives and talents has helped to ensure that the sector remains vibrant and relevant, while its coverage of activities and promotion of cultural diversity has helped to broaden the cultural horizons of listeners.
Recommandations: It was concluded that the online cultural streaming series, including tallat thakafya, al-ta’lileh, little tales, and hashtag your_homeland_your_health, had a positive impact on palestinian society during the pandemic. the streaming series helped reach out to palestinian intellectuals and artists living in palestine and the diaspora, building a bridge between those living in different areas and enabling them to share their experiences. the online programs also provided an opportunity to present the experiences of palestinian intellectuals and artists to the palestinian community and society. furthermore, the streaming series created a dialogue between young people and professionals, acting as excellent examples and role models in various cultural fields. it was recommended that the ministry of culture continue to develop similar online cultural programs in the future, as it had proven to be an effective and popular tool for sharing and promoting palestinian culture. additionally, the ministry should consider ways to further promote the streaming series on its social media platforms, increase audience engagement, and continue to build trust with the community. finally, it was recommended that the ministry explore the potential of a virtual fund, as opposed to a physical one, to support future cultural initiatives.

Results: Currently, the film commission has two full-time employees and a long-term goal is to generate sufficient revenue to become self-sustaining.
