Le projet priorise les femmes/filles vivant dans les quartiers précaires, tout en basant sur le principe de non-discrimination entre les personnes en situation de handicap et non handicap. Le projet a facilité aux bénéficiaires des ateliers de production et d’apprentissage, des activités de valorisation et de gestion de leurs carrières par l’entremise d’un Start Up s’hébergeant à la fois dans un espace numérique et physique. Ce projet a mis en avance des valeurs d’égalité, de diversité, de rentabilité économique et de responsabilité sociale liée à l’engament citoyen pour la réduction de déchets solides. Sont réalisés sur le projet un site web, des comptes médias sociaux et des ateliers sur la création de marché en ligne, d’appui à la vente de leurs productions et à l’évolution de leurs carrières centrées sur les économies verte et circulaire. Les objectifs spécifiques de l’initiative sont : ⮚ Permettre aux groupes cibles (parties prenantes) le développement et la gestion des canaux de communication sur le projet (ODD 17) ; ⮚ Initier quarante (40) femmes/filles en création d’entreprises, en production des oeuvres d’art/d’artisanat de récupération et des nouvelles technologies de l’information et de la communication et gestions de leurs agendas (ODD 4) ; ⮚ Accompagner quarante (40) femmes/filles à la valorisation de leurs carrières d’artistes et artisanes de récupération sur une plate-forme virtuelle en portfolio et d’autres outils numériques (ODD 9) ; ⮚ Favoriser quarante (40) femmes/filles les moyens et outils nécessaires de gestion de leurs carrières d’artistes et d’artisanes de récupération des déchets solides (ODD 8 et ODD 13) ; ⮚ Assurer le suivi-évaluation conformément aux stratégies de gouvernance fonctionnelle du projet par l’entremise des parties prenantes (ODD 17). Les modalités de mise en oeuvre des actions se présentent en trois (3) parties : la mise en place, la mise en oeuvre et l’évaluation. La dernière est transversale dans tout le processus d’action en diverses sous-parties : un diagnostic (évaluation ex-ante), des évaluations concomitantes et l’évaluation finale. Concernant la mise en place, les co-partenaires assurent une gouvernance fonctionnelle pour une meilleure gestion des ressources humaines, logistiques et financières. En matière de mise en oeuvre, nous visons quatre (4) étapes : les formations, le montage des canaux de communication (site internet et la création des comptes 169 sur les réseaux sociaux), l’accompagnement des artistes/ artisanes et nouvelles femmes/filles dans ces filières de métiers en ateliers de production et la promotion/valorisation de leurs carrières dans les foires inter/nationaux. Pour faire suite, chaque étape de la mise en oeuvre nécessite au moins une (1) évaluation concomitante. Les rôles des co-partenaires se déroulent ainsi : - C3D est le porteur du projet et assure son exécution. - Tenant compte de l'expertise de EFED dans le champ environnemental en général et la question de genre en particulier, un accord de partenariat sollicité par l'Association Culture en Trois Dimensions (C3D) autour du projet intitulé: "Accompagnement managérial des femmes et filles (Formation, promotion et autonomisation) en art et artisanat de récupération des déchets solides dans l'aire métropolitaine de Port-au-Prince (En provenance des quartiers en situation de vulnérabilité) a donc été établi entre EFED et l'Association Culture en Trois Dimensions (C3D). Cet accord de partenariat assigne à l'Engagement des Femmes et des Filles pour l'Environnement et le Développement Durable (EFED) un double rôle technique et financier. Sur le plan technique, il s'agit pour EFED de définir et d'assurer le plan de marketing social et numérique du projet. D'un point de vue financier, EFED assurera la gestion administrative du projet (Validation des rapports, hébergement et décaissement des fonds) ; - Fenêtre des enfants-ASSITEJ Haïti assume deux grands rôles : la gestion des activités des filles artistes et artisanes et la coordination des foires et d’autres formes d’expositions dans ce projet. Les procédures en matière de suivi-évaluation sont diversifiées en outils et méthodes d’applications. Pour les premiers, nous utilisons : les rapports techniques et financiers. Pour les seconds, nous appliquons la cartographie des incidences pour appliquer le suivi-évaluation conformément aux stratégies définies par les groupes cibles pour les bénéficiaires, et, le changement le plus significatif (CPS) pour évaluer la durabilité et l’impact des bénéficiaires même après l’implémentation du projet. Les composantes des ressources humaines sont : chargé(e) de projet (1), chargé(e) de communication (1), webmaster (1), consultants en suivi-évaluation (2), chargé(e) de marketing culturel et social (1), gestionnaire des médias sociaux (1) et formateurs/formatrices (3) (en récupération des déchets solides (1), management des entreprises culturelles (1) et nouvelles technologies de l’information et communication et gestion d’agenda (1)).
Results: Grâce cette initiative nous avons atteints beaucoup de résultats, voici quelques-uns : - Trente-cinq (35) femmes et filles répertoriées à travers neuf (9) associations de base ; - 60 participants/es et une vingtaine de personnes (physiques et morales) des ressources humaines rencontrés ; - Quinze (15) femmes et filles initiées en création d’entreprise (Start up) et sont bénéficiaires des stages en cours au sein du Centre d’art à Port-au-Prince ; - Un autre groupe de 19 femmes et filles initiées en production d’oeuvres d’art et artisanat de récupération de déchets solides et sont bénéficiaires des stages pratiques dans 5 ateliers d’artistes et artisans/es à Port-au-Prince ; - Les trente-quatre (34) femmes et filles sont initiées en Nouvelles Technologies de l’Information et de la Communication et en gestion d’agenda : Création d’entreprise, finalités de l’entreprise, classification des entreprises, environnement de l’entreprise, caractéristiques de l’entrepreneur, étude de Marché, stratégie de marketing, le Marketing Mix, chiffre d’affaires, étude financière, étude juridique ; - Cinq (5) idées d’entreprise culturelle sont conçues et sont et développes par cinq (5) groupes de participantes avec le coaching de la C3D. - Un site web et un compte Facebook, un compte Twitter, un compte Instagram et un compte Youtube créés ; - Une vingtaine d’articles de presse et vingt (20) autres textes (curriculum vitae, portfolio, biographie, portraits d’artistes, monographie, articles de presses et/ou scientifiques et rédactions de nouveaux projets) conçus et montés pour le site et les comptes médias sociaux ; - Une soixantaine d’oeuvres vendues. etc.

Title EN: Prix du « Meilleur artisan entrepreneur » Haïtien
Goal: Integrate Culture In Sustainable Development Frameworks
SDG: SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: National sustainable development policies and plans
Agency Implementation: HAITIAN CRAFT CREATORS
Main Feature: Haitian Craft Creators ou HaiCraft est une Marque fille de CZart, une entreprise artisanale, fondée en Haïti le 1er Février 2016 par Caroline Zéphir dans le but de promouvoir l’artisanat haïtien et d’aider les jeunes haïtiens et haïtiennes à développer leurs compétences et à leur fournir un métier manuel capable de leur générer des revenus. CZart est enregistrée en Haïti (CZart Haïti) et également aux USA (CZart LLC) elle produit des accessoires artisanaux pour revendre aux collectionneurs et collectionneuses de produits artisanaux et aux touristes locaux et internationaux mais elle forme également les jeunes grâce à une initiative baptisée «WEEK-END DE L’ARTISANAT» que l’équipe a lancée depuis 2017 qui Consiste à former à travers des ateliers de formation sur l’artisanat de nouveaux artisans entrepreneurs haïtiens en Haïti et en République Dominicaine. CZart vend aussi des cours en ligne via leur plateforme 172 en ligne www.czartcraft.com Haitian Craft Creators (HaiCraft) est une structure haïtienne lancée en novembre 2022 dans le but de promouvoir, mettre en réseau et renforcer les capacités des créateurs d’art haïtiens. Notre vision est d’oeuvrer pour un monde où l’artisanat est au coeur du développement durable et une communauté haïtienne où les métiers de la main sont des vecteurs de changements positifs. Nos actions sont orientées vers trois (3) grands axes: la promotion de l’artisanat, le réseautage, et le renforcement de capacités. Pour marquer la journée mondiale de l’Art (15 avril) et la journée du travail (1er mai) deux journées extrêmement importantes pour les créateurs d’art, HaiCraft a réalisé un concours dénommé: PRIX DU «MEILLEUR ARTISAN ENTREPRENEUR HAÏTIEN». Un concours organisé pour rappeler aux artisans qu’ils sont aussi des entrepreneurs et qu’ils doivent tout faire pour garder en vie leur entreprise malgré la conjoncture sociopolitique extrêmement chaotique d’Haïti. Face à ce contexte difficile, les artisans sont obligés de faire preuve de résilience et se battre quotidiennement pour la survie et le maintien de leur passion ou de leur entreprise. De ce fait, pour les récompenser et pour renforcer notre mission de contribuer à la valorisation de l’artisanat haïtien le réseau Haitian Craft Creators – HaiCraft a décidé de réaliser la première édition du concours “MEILLEUR ARTISAN ENTREPRENEUR HAÏTIEN” du 15 avril au 1er mai 2023 pour honorer les trois (3) meilleurs artisans qui jouent un rôle déterminant dans l’économie nationale et qui méritent d’être reconnu. Ce n’était pas un concours pour sélectionner les meilleurs oeuvres des artisans mais pour récompenser les artisans qui sont aussi de vrais entrepreneurs qui gèrent leur entreprise et leur équipe même en temps de crise. Un jury de 3 membres a été constitué pour évaluer les dossiers présentant les entreprises créatives participantes pour ensuite procéder à la sélection les artisans gagnants. Ce concours était un moyen de les booster, les encourager, les aider et renforcer leur entreprise. HaiCraft a offert aux gagnants les prix suivants: 1. 1erprix: $500USD + Plaque d’honneur + Formation 2. 2eprix: $250USD + Plaque d’honneur + Formation 3. 3eprix: Kit de matériels + Plaque d’honneur + Formation. Pour plus d’infos: 1. https://belidemag.net/czart-llc-et-haicraft-vous-presentent-le-prix-du-meilleur-artisanentrepreneur- haitien/ https://belidemag.net/les-grands-gagnants-du-prix-du-meilleur-artisan-entrepreneur-haitien-sont-connus/
Results: ● Récompenses et Reconnaissance : Trois (3) artisans entrepreneurs gagnants ont reçu des récompenses telles que des prix en espèces, des trophées, des formations. Cela offre une reconnaissance officielle de leurs compétences et de leur créativité ; ● Le premier gagnant a reçu montant de 75,000.00 gourdes ($500 USD) ; ● Le deuxième gagnant a reçu montant de 37,500.00 gourdes ($250 USD) ; ● Le troisième gagnant a reçu un kit de matériels pour renforcer son travail ; ● Visibilité et Promotion : Les trois (3) artisans lauréats ont bénéficié d'une visibilité accrue grâce à la promotion de leurs produits et de leurs réussites via les réseaux sociaux de HaiCraft et d’autres médias en ligne comme BÈLIDE magazine. Le concours a attiré l'attention des médias, des acheteurs et des clients potentiels ; ● Confiance Renforcée : Le concours a renforcé la confiance des artisans entrepreneurs en leurs compétences et en leur potentiel ; ● OpportunitésCommerciales:Lesgagnantsontreçuplusieursopportunitésdeventee tdedistributionélargiespourleursproduits ; ● Sensibilisation : Le Prix du meilleur artisan entrepreneur a contribué à sensibiliser le public à l'importance du secteur artisanal, à la culture locale et aux traditions artisanales ;

Title EN: Lancement de la rubrique de promotion « Men Kreyatè ».
Goal: Promote Human Rights And Fundamental Freedoms
SDG: SDG 5 - Achieve gender equality and empower all women and girls,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels
Area of Monitoring: Gender equality
Agency Implementation: HAITIAN CRAFT CREATORS
Main Feature: Haitian Craft Creators ou HaiCraft est une Marque fille de CZart, une entreprise artisanale, fondée en Haïti le 1er Février 2016 par Caroline Zéphir dans le but de promouvoir l’artisanat haïtien et d’aider les jeunes haïtiens et haïtiennes à développer leurs compétences et à leur fournir un métier manuel capable de leur générer des revenus. CZart est enregistrée en Haïti (CZart Haïti) et également aux USA (CZart LLC) elle produit des accessoires artisanaux pour revendre aux collectionneurs et collectionneuses de produits artisanaux et aux touristes locaux et internationaux mais elle forme également les jeunes grâce à une initiative baptisée «WEEK-ENDDEL’ARTISANAT» que l’équipe a lancée depuis 2017 qui haïtiens en Haïti et en République Dominicaine. CZart vend aussi des cours en ligne via leur plateforme en ligne www.czartcraft.com Haitian Craft Creators (HaiCraft) est une structure haïtienne lancée en novembre 2022 dans le but de promouvoir, mettre en réseau et renforcer les capacités des créateurs d’art haïtiens. Notre vision est d’oeuvrer pour un monde où l’artisanat est au coeur du développement durable et une communauté haïtienne où les métiers de la main sont des vecteurs de changements positifs. Nos actions sont orientées vers trois (3) grands axes: la promotion de l’artisanat, le réseautage, et le renforcement de capacités. 1- Lancement de la rubrique de promotion «M en Kreyatè» Notre rubrique "MEN KREYATÈ" est un espace en ligne dédié aux artisans en particulier les femmes créatrices du réseau HaiCraft dans le but de célébrer et promouvoir le talent artistique et l'artisanat exceptionnel provenant de diverses styles et domaines. "MEN KREYATÈ "signifie « Voici un/e créateur/trice ». "MEN KREYATÈ " signifie aussi « Mains créatrices ». Nous croyons fermement à la valeur des compétences artisanales et à leur contribution à la richesse culturelle et à l'innovation. À travers cette rubrique en ligne, nous mettons en avant les artisans en particulier les femmes artisanes entrepreneures et leurs créations, tout en racontant leurs histoires uniques. Notre objectif ultime avec la rubrique "MEN KREYATÈ" est de mettre en avant la diversité culturelle et la créativité dans le monde de l'artisanat. Nous souhaitons offrir une plateforme où les artisans surtout les femmes peuvent être sous les projecteurs grâce à leur travail et peuvent briller, partager leur passion et inspirer d'autres personnes à s'engager dans des pratiques artisanales. En connectant les amateurs d'artisanat et en favorisant la compréhension interculturelle, nous espérons contribuer à la préservation du patrimoine culturel et à la croissance du secteur artisanal. Nous publions la photo des artisans accompagnée de leur biographie détaillée pour permettre aux publics de faire leur connaissance, de connaitre leur parcours dans le domaine. Ensuite, les oeuvres de l’artisan sont publiées pour assurer leur visibilité être renforcer leur réseau de vente. En somme, cette rubrique de promotion dédiée aux artisans et à leurs oeuvres offre bien plus qu'une simple vitrine pour les créations artisanales. C'est un moyen de reconnaître, célébrer, inspirer et préserver, tout en ayant des retombées positives sur l'économie, la culture et la société dans son ensemble Consiste à former à travers des ateliers de formation sur l’artisanat de nouveaux artisans entrepreneurs.
Results: Nous sommes ravis de partager les résultats remarquables que notre initiative a déjà apportés au secteur culturel. Ces résultats qualitatifs et quantitatifs démontrent l'impact positif que la rubrique a pu réaliser jusqu'à présent : ● 35 créateurs d’art dont 31 femmes créatrices et leurs oeuvres ont été présentés à travers les réseaux sociaux et valorisés grâce aux publications en ligne de la rubrique MEN KREYATÈ ; ● La confiance et l’estime de soi des créatrices ayant participées à la rubrique ont été augmentée ; ● Le taux d'engagement, mesuré par le nombre de commentaires, de partages et de likes sur les articles et les créations présentées, ont augmenté progressivement, atteignant un taux moyen de 5 à 10% ; ● En facilitant les échanges et les interactions sur le travail des artisans, l’activité a contribué à élargir la communauté artisanale en ligne ; ● Le réseau HaiCraft est de plus en plus connu au niveau local et international et contribue à l’atteinte de notre mission de rehausser l’artisanat haïtien au niveau international ;

Title EN: Cultural Awards
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture
SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Cultural and creative sectors
Agency Implementation: Dubai Culture and Arts Authority, Community Development Authority Dubai, Sultan Bin Ali Al Owais Cultural Foundation, Dubai Media City, Dubai Executive Office, Fujairah Culture and Media Authority, Sharjah, Department of Culture and Information
Main Feature: Over the years, the private and public sector in the UAE have launched several cultural awards to encourage and promote artists and creators and to provide support in the form of exposure and financial reward. Some of the awards that are currently active in the UAE are the following:   •	Arab Social Media Award: The Award, launched in 2014 by Dubai Executive Office, highlights the most important initiatives of social media in the Arab world and honors individuals and institutions that have creatively used social media channels to increase awareness of issues of concern to the Arab community and have had a positive impact on the development and prosperity of the community. There are 20 categories for the award, including categories for arts, media, youth, tolerance, and technology. •	Arab Journalism Award (AJA): Launched in 1999, is the region’s most prestigious award recognizing journalistic excellence. The award’s main goal is to reward talent, inspire, and stimulate creativity and enhance the constructive role of the press in serving the community. It rewards talent under 13 categories including investigative reporting; young talent in journalism; photojournalism; economic journalism; outstanding cartoon artwork; sports journalism; best press interview; best columnist; media personality of the year; political journalism; cultural journalism; smart journalism and humanitarian journalism. The award’s main goal is to reward talent, inspire, and stimulate creativity in journalism.  •	Sheikh Zayed Book Award: The Sheikh Zayed Book Award is organized by the Department of Culture and Tourism in Abu Dhabi and is presented annually to outstanding writers, intellectuals and publishers, as well as young talent whose writing and translation enriches the Arab intellectual, cultural, literary and social life. Each prize consists of a gold medal bearing the Sheikh Zayed Book Award logo, a certificate of merit, and a cash reward, comprising a total prize value of seven million UAE Dirhams (US $1.9m) annually. The Cultural Personality of the Year receives a prize of one million UAE Dirhams, while the winners of the other categories receive 750,000 UAE Dirhams each.   •	International Prize for Arabic Fiction (IPAF): IPAF is supported by the Department of Culture and Tourism in Abu Dhabi and was launched in April 2007. It is the most prestigious and important literary prize in the Arab world, and if often referred to as the “Arabic Booker Prize”. Its aim is to reward excellence in contemporary Arabic creative writing and to encourage the readership of high-quality Arabic literature internationally through the translation and publication of winning and shortlisted novels in other major languages. One of the main aims of the IPAF is to encourage the translation of Arabic literature into other languages. The shortlisted authors each receive $10,000 US. The winning author goes on to receive a further $50,000 US, with a commitment that IPAF will meet the cost of translation of the winning novel into English. Novels associated with IPAF can look forward to increased readership and sales both within the Arab world and internationally through translation.  •	Little Writer Competition: The competition is organized by the Department of Culture and Tourism in Abu Dhabi. It is a series of competitions for children called ‘Little Writer’ which focuses on the Arabic language as an intellectual and cultural component that support social values. The winning stories are included in a volume called “Little Writer in the Big Book” which is distributed to all schools’ libraries and MAKTABA’s branches across the Abu Dhabi. •	Sheikh Mohammed bin Rashid Patrons of the Arts Awards: The awards is organized by Dubai Culture and Arts Authority honor and recognize individuals, business, organizations, and government entities that have provided financial and in-kind support for the promotion of artistic activity in Dubai. Contributions are recognized in the visual arts, film, literature and performing arts. •	Mansoor Bin Mohammed Award for Short Films: The Community Development Authority in Dubai delivers this award, and its objective is to encourage creativity and innovation among young people. The Award aims to (1) raise community awareness of human rights issues, (2) encourage youth to employ creative skills to portray human rights and thus to develop their creative artistic capacities and (3) to promote the values of tolerance, cultural diversity, and to combat discrimination and extremism. To date 30 films have won this award.  •	Jameel Prize for contemporary artists and designers: Organized by the Victoria and Albert Museum, London, in partnership with Art Jameel, the vision of the Jameel Prize is to recognize the influence of Islamic tradition on contemporary culture and celebrate contemporary practitioners inspired by Islamic design and visual culture. The artists and designers short-listed for the Jameel Prize are invited to show examples of their artwork in a special exhibition, which debuts either at the V&A or another notable international museum, before travelling to other venues around the world. •	Sharjah Prize for Arab Culture – UNESCO: Funded by the Department of Culture in Sharjah, the award was established under the directives of His Highness, Ruler of Sharjah, in cooperation with UNESCO, when Sharjah was named Capital of Arab Culture in 1998. The award is given in recognition of the efforts of cultural figures, or institutions that contribute to the intellectual and artistic promotion of Arab culture and its appreciation and understanding around the world.   •	Sharjah Award for Theatre Creativity: The Department of Culture in Sharjah organizes the Award, which was established in 2007. The Award encourages and honors Arab playwrights who have shown their dedication to theatre over the years and created effective platforms for Arab theatre.   •	Sharjah Award for Arab Creativity: The annual Sharjah Award for Arab Creativity is brought by the Department of Culture in Sharjah and was established in 1996. It supports talented writers in the UAE and across the Arab world. Categories of the award are short stories, poetry, playwriting, children's literature, and essays.   •	Sharjah International Prize for Cultural Heritage: A merit award established in 2016 and granted annually by the Sharjah Institute for Heritage to individuals, groups, or projects in honor of the efforts made in the field of heritage preservation and has completed its third cycle. The award works to appreciate the various efforts exerted at the local, Arab and international levels in the field of heritage preservation and documentation of successful experiences and practices in order to ensure its continuity. The award aims to spread the spirit of theoretical and practical scientific competition between those interested and working in the field of scientific and field research in preserving and codifying heritage. The award also honors human treasures and emphasizes the effective role of narrators carrying oral literary masterpieces, traditional knowledge and craft skills in preserving the cultural heritage of man and ensuring its permanence.   •	Sharjah International Book Fair Awards: The annual Sharjah International Book Fair Awards which is brough by the Sharjah Book Authority, promotes the production of good quality publications and recognize and appreciate distinguished individuals and organizations for their contribution to the social, cultural and literary fields. The breakdown of the awards include: Turjuman Award, Award for an Emirati Book, Award for the Best International Book, Award for the Best Arabic Novel, Publisher Recognition Award, and Cultural personality of the Year Award. •	Sharjah Award for Artistic Criticism Research: The Sharjah Award for Artistic Research places artistic and visual research at the forefront, emphasizing the contributions of writers, critics, and academics as a parallel creative process to the artistic one. It seeks to attract insightful efforts and ideas, aiming to stimulate specialized critical research in the fields of visual and fine arts. The award highlights the role of creators, follows artistic trends, documents them, and strives to establish a common language between critics and readers. Participants are encouraged to innovate their tools to achieve the desired goal of presenting any topic. •	Sharjah Award for Arabic Poetry: The Award was launch in 2011 under the patronage of His Highness Sheikh Dr. Sultan bin Mohammed Al Qasimi, a member of the Supreme Council Ruler of Sharjah, to honor pioneers of Arabic poetry. Each year, the award honors a local personality and another Arab Figure. •	The Sharjah Award for Theatrical Composition - Theatrical scripts for Adults: In confirmation of the importance of theatrical writing and composition in fostering cultural and theatrical activity, the Department of Culture in Sharjah established the Sharjah Award for Theatrical Composition in 1996, specifically during the seventh edition of the Sharjah Theatre Days Festival, based on the recommendations approved by the committees arising from the events of the Sharjah Theatre Days Festival. Considering that theatre reflects society, it is crucial that the reality of society is reflected on the local theatre stage. Therefore, these recommendations align with the noble visions and directives of His Highness Sheikh Dr. Sultan bin Muhammad Al Qasimi, Member of the Supreme Council of the Union, Ruler of Sharjah, emphasizing the necessity of supporting and encouraging local talent and fostering communication to sustain their creativity and engagement with the cultural and theatrical community. The inaugural launch of the Theatrical Composition Award in 1996 was a tribute and appreciation to the playwrights and theatrical creators from the United Arab Emirates and citizens of the Gulf Cooperation Council countries. •	Sharjah Award for School Theatrical Composition: The Theater Department at the Department of Culture in Sharjah presents the Sharjah Award for School Theatrical Composition as a means of encouragement and motivation for the children of the United Arab Emirates, citizens of the Gulf Cooperation Council countries, and residents, to submit their creative works, develop their abilities, encourage talent, and elevate it, as well as to provide the school library with distinctive theatrical texts. The competition is classified into two categories: Teacher’s category, Students category. •	The Sharjah Award for Arabic Poetry Criticism: Under the guidance and patronage of His Highness Sheikh Dr. Sultan bin Muhammad Al Qasimi, Member of the Supreme Council and Ruler of Sharjah, the Sharjah Award for Arabic Poetry Criticism was launched to support and nurture Arab critics and enthusiasts interested in studies focused on Arab poetic experiences. The award focuses on literary criticism directed towards Arabic poetry, aiming to broaden the research horizons for Arab critics to serve the Arab creative landscape. •	Sultan Bin Ali Al Owais Cultural Award: The Sultan Bin Ali Al Owais Cultural Award is granted to several outstanding Arab innovators and intellectuals in recognition of their significant contributions in the following categories of (1) poetry (2) short story, novel and drama (3) literary studies and criticism (4) humanities and future studies.   •	Fujairah International Monodrama Festival Awards: The Fujairah International Monodrama Festival Awards was established in 2003 and brought by Fujairah Authority for Culture and Media. It aims at encouraging the presence of Monodrama in the Arabic theatre in general, and in Emirati theatre in particular, and supporting the young and talented artists who can contribute to its growth.   •	Fujairah Photography Award: Brought by the Fujairah Culture and Media Authority and established in 2007, the Award was launched with the aim of upgrading the intellectual, cultural and aesthetic scene in Fujairah in particular, and the UAE in general. It also aims at presenting creative works that reflect reality, spark the creative interest and curiosity of the public and enrich the world of visual arts.
Results: The implementation of various cultural awards in the UAE has achieved significant results, profoundly impacting the country’s cultural landscape. These awards have played a crucial role in promoting artistic excellence by recognizing outstanding achievements in literature, calligraphy, and other artistic fields. They have enhanced the UAE's global visibility, positioning it as a key player in the international cultural arena and attracting global participation. By providing substantial support and recognition, these awards have nurtured emerging talents, offering financial rewards and career-boosting opportunities
Recommandations: The implementation of cultural awards in the UAE has yielded significant results, profoundly impacting the country's cultural landscape. These awards have effectively promoted artistic and literary excellence, enhanced the UAE's global visibility and positioning it as a key player in the international cultural arena. They have provided crucial support to emerging talent, offering financial rewards, recognition, and career-boosting opportunities, while also contributing to the preservation and innovation of cultural heritage. Title EN: : Film policy 2024-2027: A strong film nation
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture
SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Media diversity
Agency Implementation: Danish Film Institute
Main Feature: The film policy 2024-2027 focuses on securing Danish film and content production in all types of productions and formats.  The policy has a special focus on ensuring the production of quality Danish content targeted at children and young people. As part of this, a strategy will be developed for supporting content targeted at children and young people, and there is a special focus on ensuring good and safe working conditions for children and young people when they take part in film and TV productions. At the same time, the policy focuses on the film talent, and securing the right educational offers. Not least the film agreement focuses on the Danish regional film funds and equal film distribution everywhere in Denmark. The regional film funds receive a government grant and also provide support for film productions. The cooperation between the state, the Danish Film Institute and the regional funds must be well-functioning and transparent.  In addition and as a part of the new film policy, e.g. subsidies are provided to secure that students and school children can go to the cinema as part of their education, and historical films are digitized and made available throughout the country. Also subsidies are provided to a film trial scheme for people with dementia, called “Memory Cinema”, where people with dementia can watch historical films from their hometown. The film policy also has a focus on people with a visual disability as it imposes on all Danish films, that receive state support and have a Danish cinema premiere, must be made accessible to people with a visual disability through visual interpretation.
Results: The new film policy 2024-2027 has not been evaluated so far, but it will be evaluated at the end of the period. The measures set out in the policy will be evaluated at that time.
Financial Ressources: Financial resources allocated to the film policy 2024-27 is in total 90,4 mio. USD.

Title EN: Decision No. 188/QĐ-TTg dated on February 09, 2021 of the Prime Minister on the amendment and supplement several articles of Decision No 844/QĐ-TTg dated on May 18, 2016 of the Prime Minister approving the Project to Support the National Innovation and Cr
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture
SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Cultural and creative sectors
Cultural Domain: Design,Performing Arts,Media Arts,Cinema and Audiovisual Arts,Music,Publishing,Visual Arts
Agency Implementation: The Ministry of Science and Technology
Main Feature: Decision No 844/QD-TTg, implemented over a five-year period from 2016 to 2021, has yielded remarkable results. These include the initial establishment of several primary platforms for Viet Nam's startup ecosystem, the formation of organizations supporting startup companies, the integration of business startups into educational programs, the development of capacity for ecosystem actors, the initial proposal, and the construction of various policies and mechanisms that foster favorable conditions for innovative startups. Based on these achievements, the Government Office proposed to the Prime Minister to approve Decision No 188/QĐ-TTg on the amendment and supplement several articles of Decision 844/QĐ-TTg. Decision No 188/QĐ-TTg aims to accelerate and enhance network activities, develop in-depth, and establish new centers of technology and strategic technology. The decision also adjusts and expands Decision No 844/QĐ-TTg’s project, focusing on solutions to attract domestic and international resources from corporations, experts, and universities to create a more favorable environment for innovative startups. One of the newly added objectives is to establish a national system of innovation startup centers within various ministries, sectors, and local authorities, resulting in a comprehensive nationwide network of innovative startup ecosystems. This initiative involves the construction of a system of innovation centers, including three national centers of innovation startup support located in Hanoi, Da Nang, and Ho Chi Minh City, as well as innovation startup centers in other localities, ministries, sectors, and institutions. The vision for 2030 is for Viet Nam’s startup ecosystem to be ranked among the top 15 emerging ecosystems in the Asia-Pacific region. Additional provisions also include the formation and support for the development of the National Innovation Startup Network, with financial backing for the following activities: - Building and fostering networks of innovative startup organizations and individuals, investors, experts, consulting organizations, training and coaching services, media, and services catering to innovative startups at local, regional, and national levels; participating as members in regional and global networks to attract international resources supporting domestic innovative startups. - Collaborating with international experts and organizations in training, coaching, communication, organizing scientific seminars and conferences, and conducting innovation startup journeys both domestically and internationally. This also includes consulting on technology transfer, investment, market development, conducting research, surveys, evaluation reports, and advising on the improvement of policies and institutions to support innovative startups. Additionally, invite successful Vietnamese experts from abroad to provide regular consultancy and services for centralized innovation startup support zones at sectoral, regional, and local levels. - Organizing annual national and international scientific conferences and the High-level Forum of the Innovation Startup Network to facilitate dialogue and exchange at both national and international levels.
Results: As of the end of 2020, Decision No. 844/QĐ-TTg (also known as Project 844) has supported the organization of 244 training courses and workshops on innovative startups for more than 23,000 individuals involved in the startup ecosystem. Among these, the group of individuals and startup enterprises accounted for 36% of the total participants in the training courses; local government officials, political-social organizations, educational institutions, and incubation centers accounted for 30% of the total participants; the remaining percentage comprised trainers and innovative startup advisors. From 2016 to 2021, Viet Nam had approximately 1,000 organizations capable of supporting innovative startups, 79 incubators, 39 business accelerators, 202 co-working spaces, and 217 venture capital funds, of which 37 had Vietnamese legal status. By 2023, the private sector, public sector, and international organizations had established numerous entities nationwide, supporting innovative startups under various models. Across the country, nearly 20 localities had established or were in the process of establishing innovative startup support centers; around 100 incubators and business accelerators were in operation; and many international innovation startup centers had opened branches or collaborated to establish innovation spaces in Viet Nam. Additionally, 60 out of 63 provinces and cities had issued decisions approving the implementation plan of Project 844 locally; approximately 20 localities had established or were in the process of establishing Innovative Startup Support Centers; and 84 incubators and 35 business accelerators were operational nationwide. In 2023, various international startup support centers had opened branches or collaborated to establish innovation spaces in Vietnam, such as the "Da Nang-Seoul Innovation Startup Space" in Da Nang and the K-Startup Center under the Korea SMEs and Startups Agency (KOSME) in Ha Noi. Furthermore, 208 venture capital funds have operated and invested in Vietnamese startups, including nearly 40 domestic investment funds. The number of angel investors was also gradually increasing, with the three most active organizations being the Vietnam Silicon Valley Accelerator, the CLAS Expara Vietnam Accelerator, and the Vietnam Startup Acceleration Fund.  Various universities have established innovation hubs to foster a conducive environment for students, faculty, and alumni to transform ideas into valuable products or services, foster an innovative culture, and establish robust innovation communities. These innovation hubs also serve as venues for training courses, workshops, and events to equip participants with the necessary knowledge and skills for innovation and entrepreneurship, providing technical support, consultancy, and essential resources for developing new technologies and products from ideation to commercialization, expanding cooperation opportunities, and attracting investment through networks connecting innovators, businesses, and financial organizations. Some active innovation hubs include the Viet Nam National University, Ha Noi, and the RMIT University Innovation Hub (VNU-RMITINNOHUB), which was launched and operated in Hoa Lac to connect scientific talents and promote innovation activities between universities and enterprises in Vietnam and Australia; the University of Science and Technology of Hanoi Innovation Hub (UIH); and the Entrepreneurship and Innovation Centre at Dong A University, Da Nang, among others. Many cities have established innovation hubs, networks, and centers, including the Vietnam Innovation Hub complex in Da Nang, the Da Nang Innovation Startup Support Center, the Network of Innovation Complexes in Da Nang and the Central Region, the Saigon Innovation Hub in Ho Chi Minh City, among others. These initiatives have contributed to the creation and orientation of the Innovative Startup Ecosystem, international integration, the connection of public-private resources, and the sharing of support for the community to access resources for innovation.
Recommandations: Viet Nam have established a comprehensive support system for startups from the central to local levels, which includes key activities such as acting as the focal point for providing, guiding, and supporting innovative startups; organizing regional and local events for these startups; commissioning innovative startup communities to address local government challenges; and promoting, honoring, and rewarding national innovative startup support activities at the local level. However, the next phase requires the further refinement of policies and legislation regarding innovative startups in a comprehensive, synchronized, and unified manner. This includes developing the ecosystem in-depth by sector, field, and locality, and utilizing the system of innovation startup support centers and innovation centers as the core of development. Clarifying the concepts of innovation and innovative startups, issuing regulations on the types of organizations, their functions, tasks, and related activities is a priority in terms of policy. Focused preferential policies and incentives should be proposed to promptly address the difficulties and obstacles faced by innovation organizations and innovative startups in ministries, sectors, localities, educational institutions, political-social organizations, businesses, and corporations comprehensively, synchronously, and uniformly. Mechanisms and policies to attract venture capital, provide direct incentives, and unlock available financial resources from both domestic and foreign sources should be developed. Efforts to enhance investment connection activities, attract investment resources from individuals, organizations, and venture capital funds domestically and internationally, particularly Vietnamese investment funds and foreign investment funds operating in Viet Nam, should be intensified. It is essential to provide swift identification and proposal of solutions to overcome challenges in venture capital investment activities in Viet Nam. Specific financial mechanisms for training and incubating innovative startups should be established. An open innovation system should be promoted, sector-specific ecosystems should be developed, and a controlled experimental legal framework for certain areas should be created for innovative startups. Additionally, a detailed legal framework for managing entities within the innovative startup ecosystem (defining entities, stipulating functions, and tasks for support units, etc.) should be established. Furthermore, enhancing coordination mechanisms between ministries, sectors, and localities from the central to the implementation level is crucial to unify directions and share appropriate resources for the innovative startup ecosystem. The established national, regional, and local innovation startup support centers should function as the central hub for linking and directing the execution of related activities. There should be continuous study, implementation, or adjustment in line with the development of the ecosystem in the current phase regarding programs and projects of ministries, sectors, and political-social organizations, with timely reports to the Government and the Prime Minister for issuance in the near future. It is particularly important to promote the innovative startup ecosystem in various industries and fields, associated with the state management role of specialized ministries in promoting the formation and development of ecosystems with different characteristics and components in various fields. Strengthened coordination, streamlining, and attraction of resources in terms of capital, finance, infrastructure, and expertise from the public sector, private sector, and overseas Vietnamese experts are necessary for the advancement of innovative startups.

Agency Implementation: National Library of Colombia - Ministry of Cultures, Arts, and Knowledge.
Main Feature: The purpose of the “I read life” National Plan for Reading, Writing, Orality and Libraries (PNLEOB) is to contribute to the care, protection, and dignity of the lives of people and communities in the different territories of Colombia, based on the reading, writing, orality practices and public, community and popular libraries. The Plan is based on territorial, differential population and intersectoral, rights and justice approaches; In accordance with this, it develops differential actions, according to the particularities of each territory, aimed at ensuring educational and cultural rights, especially of populations excluded in economic, social, and cultural terms.                   The PNLEOB includes reading, writing, orality, and libraries based on the multiplicity of uses and sociocultural meanings that they acquire in social and individual life. In relation to the Colombian context and history, the Plan contemplates reading, writing, and orality as conduits for the construction of different ways of processing conflicts, as alternatives to war and expressions of a culture of peace. Therefore, it seeks to strengthen libraries and other spaces in which these practices occur, beyond the traditional spaces intended for education and culture, contribute to the strengthening of networking and the social appropriation of the Plan, in pursuit of its sustainability in time.                   The Plan contemplates three strategies: the first, “Creation, production, intercultural dialogue, and knowledge”, is a commitment to promote the creation of content and artistic creation through the oral and written word, the production of new multimedia narratives and accessible content, to put them into circulation and promote the necessary dialogues between knowledge and cultures. “Pedagogical mediations and lifelong learning”, the second strategy aims to strengthen the educational role of culture, and contribute to the training of reading, writing and oral mediators who carry out their work in spaces other than formal education. The commitment to literacy of people and communities who, due to social, cultural, and gender factors, have been denied the appropriation of the alphabetic code is a priority in this area, in a country in which around 5.3% of the population is not literate (DANE, 2018). Far from understanding the literacy process as the imposition of a code, at the expense of the denial of language practices and people's prior knowledge, the Plan proposes a literacy exercise based on the recognition, dialogue, and revitalization of one's own languages and cultures.                   The third strategy, “Social appropriation of knowledge, knowledge, and memories”, works for the incorporation of reading, writing, orality, literature, and oralitura in daily life. For the word in all its manifestations to gain meaning and purpose for people and communities, it must be appropriate and integrated into decision-making with public impact and problem-solving. This area includes initiatives of community science and culture of peace and the creation of the National System of Oralities, made up of a network of practitioners of the different expressions of orality present in the country, the mapping of these agents and their practices and the creation of a national oral library.                  From these strategies, the Plan is committed to contributing, from its scope, possibilities and specificities, to the project of building a fair country for a dignified life. For life to persist in being, for it to reproduce and produce, it is necessary that equitable conditions exist for its deployment in the world. The commitment to generating these material, social, and cultural conditions gives meaning to this Plan: one that contributes to the construction of a fairer country, in which the power of life can continue to be; a country in which the different forms of knowing, knowledge, memory, language, and words are recognized and can be appropriated by all people. In this horizon of meaning, reading, writing, and orality constitute conduits and conditions of possibility for effective participation in society, culture, and lifelong learning.
Results: The “I read life” National Plan for Reading, Writing, Orality, and Libraries (PNLEOB), of the National Library of Colombia – Ministry of Cultures, Arts, and Knowledge, began its implementation process in 2024, after a formulation phase in which around 400 agents from the reading, writing, oral, and library sectors participated. The agents participated in advanced dialogues in different regions of the country, in accordance with the territorial and differential population approaches, and with the consideration of population and cultural diversity as a guiding principle of the Plan.                   To date, as part of the Plan's commitments, the implementation of the “Arnoldo Palacios” Departmental Plan for Reading, Writing, Orality, and Libraries of Chocó has been formulated and begun, which has a presence in all the municipalities of the department and with a team made up of people from the territory. For the implementation of the Plan in the department of Chocó and in other prioritized territories, territorial characterization exercises have been carried out that allow defining, in a differential and participatory manner, the strategies of the Plan that will be developed in each territory. The Plan has managed to articulate with other areas of the Ministry of Culture, Arts, and Knowledge, with other sectors of the national government and civil society, in accordance with its conception of reading, writing, and orality as practices linked to all dimensions of the lives of people and communities.                   At the end of 2024, the systematization and evaluation of the results of the first year of implementation of the PNLEOB will begin.
Recommandations: Although an evaluation of the measure has not been carried out because it is in its first year of implementation, the following recommendations have been identified to take into account in this process:         ●	Cultural public policies are called to incorporate territorial and differential approaches, which allow the diversity of cultural practices and practitioners to be recognised, integrated and put into dialogue. Assuming these approaches implies understanding them as guidelines for action and translating them into projects, programs, and concrete actions.          ●	The sustainability of public policies largely depends on their decentralization and their appropriation by civil society. In this sense, it is essential to incorporate, in the formulation and implementation of policies, strategies for their social appropriation and for the strengthening of networks made up of civil society agents.          ●	Access, use, and appropriation of reading, writing, and orality are part of the exercise of educational and cultural rights, and are conditions of possibility for the exercise of other rights. In this sense, policies aimed at strengthening the reading, writing, oral, and library sector contribute to generating favorable conditions for the development of the potential of people and communities and, therefore, for the dignity of their lives.

Title EN: Austrian Eco-label for cultural institutions
Goal: Integrate Culture In Sustainable Development Frameworks
SDG: SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: National sustainable development policies and plans
Agency Implementation: Federal Ministry for Climate Action, Environment, Energy, Mobility, Innovation and Technology
Main Feature: The Austrian Eco-label has been awarded since 1990. In addition to products, services, schools and educational institutions, the label was recently extended to the certification of cultural institutions, including museums, theatres and cinemas.  Museums: The umbrella organizations of the museum sector in Austria, ICOM-Austria and Museumsbund Österreich, have created a "museum seal of approval" that offers a quality standard. In addition, museums can apply for environmental certification under the Austrian Eco-label. The museum-specific environmental criteria include minimizing the use of chemicals in conservation or restoration work, the sustainable handling of exhibits during transport and storage, the choice of materials in the construction of exhibitions, and the consideration of sustainable development goals in the context of educational work.  Theatres: As of 2022, the Austrian Eco-label can also be awarded to theatres and musical theatres. Environmental management and social responsibility of theatres can thus be recognized. The core criteria of the Eco-label guidelines for theatres relate to areas such as management, energy, cleaning and food. Other criteria cover programme, content, and events, ticketing and communications, props, costumes and make- up. Theatres benefit from certification not only through cost savings and quality improvements, but also through increased awareness among their patrons.  Cinemas: Starting in 2022, cinemas also have the opportunity to become Eco-label certified. Criteria for cinemas to be awarded the Eco-label include offering drinks in reusable systems, offering regional drinks and food, avoiding portion packs, taking measures to avoid disposable tableware and communicating alternative mobility concepts for travel.  Film industry: The Austrian Eco-Label is awarded to specific film productions, not to a single production company. The ecological requirements along the entire production chain of a film production must be met. A film production is defined as follows: the production of cinematographic, commercial, documentary or television films, series, shows (if the aspect of recording is in the foreground) or reports, which is divided into the phases of project development, pre-production, filming, post-production, and film exploitation. For the specific film production, the Guideline includes criteria in the areas of mobility and climate protection, set, materials for buildings, set design and props, costume and makeup, technology, catering, and accommodation. Although the specific film production is awarded, there are also criteria that must be met by the production company. These must be proven during the initial Eco-label assessment. Among other things, the production company must appoint a Green Producing Officer, adhere to environmentally friendly office management, and motivate its employees to environmentally friendly mobility.
Results: As of May 2024, 44 museums and galleries (including all federal museums and the Austrian National Library) have been awarded the Austrian Eco-Label. 10 theatres have been awarded so far, including Burgtheater Wien, Austria’s largest theatre. Furthermore, five cinemas have been awarded so far.

Title EN: “Women in Music”: a project focused on increasing gender equality in DR’s music content across all channels and platforms

SDG: SDG 5 - Achieve gender equality and empower all women and girls,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels
Area of Monitoring: Gender equality
Agency Implementation: Danish Broadcasting Corporation
Main Feature: DR works continuously to promote diversity and to create and support a broader representation in public service content. The basis for DR’s efforts to promote diversity is that all users should be able to recognize themselves as well as learn something new about others when watching, listening to, or otherwise engaging with DR’s public service content. This includes, among other things, measures to support the recognition and advancement of women as artists, cultural professionals and/or creative entrepreneurs. For example, in 2021, DR initiated a project called “Women in Music”, which aimed to increase female representation in artists played on DR’s platforms through monitoring, playlist rotation and internal training courses on bias and discourses. The project included several initiatives, including an annual music summit in close collaboration with the music industry, which was held for the first time in 2022. At the same time, DR has increased editorial focus through for example various workshops for employees focusing on bias and restricting narratives. In addition, the proportion of women and mixed bands on all music channels and at DR’s concerts is continuously monitored and followed up on. Together with other stakeholders in the music industry, DR mapped the representation of women throughout various stages of the “food chain” within the music industry and uncovered different barriers for women through interviews with many female artists and musicians in Denmark. More information can be found in the following article: https://www.dr.dk/presse/ny-rapport-viser-hvilke-barrierer-kvinder-moeder-i-den-danske-musikbranche (The article is in Danish).
Results: As a result of DR’s active efforts in connection to the “Women in Music”-project, the proportion of Danish music with a female lead artist or female representation in bands or orchestras played on DR's platforms has increased from 35% to 46% percent within only two years.  https://www.dr.dk/presse/presse-koncern/dr-loefter-sloeret-et-staerkt-og-mangfoldigt-musikaar

Title EN: « Dream city » un festival à ciel ouvert en faveur de la mobilité artistique et la diversité culturelle
Goal: Achieve A Balanced Flow Of Cultural Goods And Services And Increase The Mobility Of Artists And Cultural Professionals
SDG: SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 10 - Reduce inequality within and among countries,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Mobility of artists and cultural professionals
Agency Implementation: Association L’Art Rue
Main Feature: Depuis sa création en 2007, le festival Dream City, initié par les artistes Selma et Sofiane Ouissi et porté par l’association L’Art Rue, joue un rôle central dans le développement de la scène culturelle et artistique en Tunisie, ainsi que dans le soutien aux artistes tunisiens, de la région MENA, d’Afrique et d’Europe.  1.	Programmation et Méthodologie La programmation de Dream City se construit en moyenne deux ans avant l'édition avec, comme pour chaque édition, des œuvres créées qui se nourrissent du monde actuel, de ses enjeux et défis en dialogue avec des œuvres invitées. Dream City se distingue par sa méthodologie singulière : inviter des artistes tunisiens et internationaux à inventer et créer contextuellement en s’engageant avec la cité et ses habitants. C'est aussi un festival engagé sur la durée qui accompagne les artistes invités et leur offre un temps long de création (allant de 1 à 4 ans) pour pleinement appréhender les spécificités et les réalités sociales et politiques. Enfin, c'est un festival à part qui investit les espaces informels de la médina de Tunis (café, rue, maison abandonnée, place…). Dream City aborde et traite les réalités sociales et politiques de la Tunisie dans un contexte mondial fragile. Des thématiques telles que la question de la démocratie et de la citoyenneté, le vivre-ensemble, les droits humains mais aussi les questions relatives à la gouvernance, aux problèmes environnementaux et à la mémoire sont au cœur de ce festival.  2.	Dream City 2022 Pour sa 8ème édition en 2022, Dream City a présenté durant 10 jours, 55 œuvres, dont 12 nouvelles créations et 2 étapes de travail, mettant en avant 58 artistes. Parmi eux, 45 étaient tunisiens et 13 provenaient d'Afrique. Cette diversité géographique favorise un échange culturel riche et varié, permettant aux artistes de partager leurs perspectives et d'enrichir leurs pratiques artistiques. Les collaborations artistiques incluaient 64 performeurs et experts tunisiens, dont 19 issus de milieux défavorisés, incluant des personnes handicapées et des femmes. Cette inclusion sociale témoigne de l'engagement de Dream City à intégrer diverses voix et à créer des opportunités pour des groupes souvent marginalisés.  3.	Dream City 2023 Pour sa 9ème édition en 2023, elle s’est tenu durant 17 jours, avec 43 œuvres dont 11 nouvelles créations réalisées par 15 artistes, incluant 8 tunisiens. En tout, 87 artistes ont participé, accompagnés de 187 collaborateurs artistiques et experts de 10 nationalités africaines différentes. L'inclusion de 17 performeurs amateurs tunisiens issus de groupes défavorisés dans une des œuvres souligne l'importance accordée à l'inclusion sociale et à l'engagement communautaire.  4.	Plateforme de Réseautage et d’Echange de Connaissance Dream City est également une plateforme de réseautage et d'échange de connaissances. Lors des éditions 2022 et 2023, 156 professionnels de la culture ont participé à des discussions approfondies sur les enjeux artistiques et culturels dans la région. Ces discussions favorisent le partage d'expériences et de compétences, renforçant ainsi le réseau des professionnels de la culture nationale et internationale, leur permettant de collaborer sur des projets futurs. À travers ses diverses initiatives, le festival contribue non seulement au développement culturel de la Tunisie, mais également à l'enrichissement de la scène artistique locale et internationale.
Results: Le bilan Dream City 2022 et 2023 totalise : -	47 447 visiteurs sur les deux éditions du festival -	23 nouvelles créations artistiques développées -	27 artistes en créations  -	139 artistes invités -	88 artistes Tunisiens -	81 artistes internationaux -	Plus que 30 espaces de la Médina et de Tunis investis pour le festival -	311 enfants ont participé à "Kharbga City" -	260 bénévoles travaillant sur le festival -	156 professionnels de la culture de différentes nationalités  -	157 jeunes de la Médina ont assuré la sécurité du festival -	Plus que 350 personnes ont travaillé sur l’organisation du festival

Title EN: •	The Act on Equal Treatment and Protection against Discrimination (Anti-discrimination Act)
Goal: Promote Human Rights And Fundamental Freedoms
SDG: SDG 5 - Achieve gender equality and empower all women and girls,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels
Area of Monitoring: Gender equality
Cultural Domain: Design,Performing Arts,Media Arts,Cinema and Audiovisual Arts,Music,Publishing,Visual Arts
Agency Implementation: Ministry of Culture of the Slovak Republic
Main Feature: Gender equality
Results: 1.	Legislative measures: •	Slovak law guarantees equal right for women and men, including the right to equal opportunities in culture. •	The Act on Equal Treatment and Protection against Discrimination (Anti-discrimination Act) includes provisions against discrimination on the basis of sex, which contributes to equal access to cultural activities and positions. 2.	Support of cultural organizations and projects: •	Ministry of Culture of the Slovak Republic and other cultural institutions support projects and organisations that focus on supporting women in culture. This includes funding for programs supporting women´s work in art, literature, film and other fields of culture. •	Grant schemes and scholarships are often aimed at supporting women-led projects or projects that reflect women´s perspectives and experiences. 3.	Awareness-raising and education initiatives: •	Various organisations and initiatives, such as the Slovak National Centre for Human Rights, organise campaigns and educational programmes to raise awareness about gender equality in culture. •	Workshops, seminars and conferences are aimed at empowering women in the cultural sector and supporting their professional growth and development. 4.	Equality of opportunities at work: •	Many cultural institutions and organisations are adopting equal opportunities principles in the workplace. This includes measures to promote equal pay, promotion and representation of women in leadership positions. •	Programs of mentoring and couching often specialize in supporting women in cultural professions. 5.	Surveys and statistics: •	Regular surveys and statistical analyses regarding the participation of women in cultural life provide important data for the formulation of policies and measures. •	The data help to identify barriers and areas where more support and intervention is needed. In Slovakia, there are a number of ministries, government and parliamentary bodies responsible for gender equality issues. These institutions play a key role in the formulation and implementation of policies aimed at promoting gender equality and combating gender discrimination. Ministries and government bodies  1.	Ministry of Labour, Social Affairs and Family of the Slovak Republic: •	This Ministry is one of the main bodies dealing with gender equality issues. It is responsible for the preparation and implementation of policies and measures to promote equal opportunities for women and men. •	The Ministry coordinates and implements various programs and projects aimed at improving the status of women in society, labour rights and combating discrimination. 2.	Ministry of  Justice of the Slovak Republic: •	The Ministry of Justice deals with legislative issues relating to equality before the law and the protection of human rights, including gender equality. •	The Ministry of Justice works to develop and implement laws and regulations that promote equality between men and women. Government and parliamentary bodies  1.	Government Council for Gender Equality: •	The Council is an advisory body to the Government of the Slovak Republic on gender equality issues. Its aim is to promote the integration of gender equality in all areas of public life. •	The Government Council for Gender Equality provides recommendations and advisory opinions to the Government in the development and implementation of policies aimed at gender equality. 2.	Committee for Gender Equality of the National Council of the Slovak Republic: •	The Committee for Gender Equality is a specialised committee of the National Council (Parliament) of the Slovak Republic, which deals with issues of gender equality and equal opportunities. •	This Committee works on drafting laws and legislative initiatives that promote equality between men and women and oversees their implementation. 3.	Slovak National Centre for Human Rights: •	The Centre is an independent institution that monitors and promotes the protection of human rights and fundamental freedoms in Slovakia, including gender equality. •	The Slovak National Centre for Human Rights conducts research, educational programmes and campaigns to promote gender equality and fight discrimination. These bodies work together to ensure equal rights and opportunities for all citizens, regardless of gender, and their work is key to advancing gender equality in Slovakia.

Title EN: Abu Dhabi International Book Fair 2020-2024
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture
SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Cultural and creative sectors
Agency Implementation: Abu Dhabi Department of Culture and Tourism
Main Feature: The Abu Dhabi International Book Fair, established in 1981, has evolved into one of the premier literary events in the Middle East. From 2020 to 2024, the fair continued to enhance its stature as a significant global literary platform. In 2020, despite the challenges posed by the COVID-19 pandemic, the fair adapted by incorporating a hybrid model, which saw participation from over 1,000 publishers and over 500 authors, with virtual events reaching an estimated 300,000 attendees worldwide. The 2021 edition expanded on this approach, offering virtual author talks and panel discussions that drew more than 400,000 viewers and included 1,200 exhibitors from 80 countries. The 2022 fair saw a return to in-person events, featuring an extensive lineup of international authors and publishers, with over 1,500 exhibitors and approximately 350,000 visitors attending. This edition emphasized the importance of physical interaction while integrating digital features to enhance the visitor experience. By 2023, the fair had further embraced technological advancements, such as augmented and virtual reality, showcasing thematic content and regional literature. This year’s event attracted over 1,800 exhibitors and welcomed around 400,000 visitors. By 2024, the Abu Dhabi International Book Fair had firmly established itself as a leading global literary event. The fair celebrated a diverse array of genres and authors, with participation from over 2,000 exhibitors and attendance exceeding 450,000. The event not only supported the growth of the publishing industry but also fostered cultural dialogue and literacy promotion on an international scale, continuing to integrate digital transformation to meet the evolving needs of the literary community.
Results: The Abu Dhabi International Book Fair has made substantial contributions to the publishing industry and community development through its implementation. By bringing together over 2,000 exhibitors and facilitating interactions between industry professionals from around the world, the fair has significantly supported the growth and evolution of the publishing sector. It provides a vital platform for publishers to showcase their work, forge new business partnerships, and explore emerging trends and innovations, thus driving the industry's development. Additionally, the fair’s embrace of digital innovation, such as virtual author talks and augmented reality experiences, has expanded its reach and accessibility, making it easier for global audiences to participate and engage with the literary community.  In terms of community development, the fair plays a crucial role in promoting literacy and education by featuring a diverse array of books and educational resources. It organizes various programs and workshops that encourage reading and enhance literary skills among participants of all ages. Furthermore, the event fosters cultural exchange and understanding by highlighting literature from different cultures and regions, thereby enriching the community’s cultural fabric. Title EN: A new structure for media subsidies
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture
SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Media diversity
Agency Implementation: Swedish Agency for the Media (Mediemyndigheten, earlier called the Swedish Press Broadcasting Authority)
Main Feature: A new structure for media subsidies (mediestöd) was launched in January 2024, replacing earlier subsidy schemes (stemming from the 1970:s). The government saw the need to modernize and further develop a system better adapted to the digital environment. The earlier main Press subsidy scheme was rights-based, while a parallel needs-based support system had also been introduced.   The new main Media subsidy scheme has been developed to be fully technically neutral and is open to general news media regardless of form of distribution. The overall aim of the subsidy scheme is to promote a diversity of high quality news media throughout the country, and thus strengthen the democratic infrastructure and promote democratic participation. The scheme therefore specifically targets local and regional news media.   Subsidies can be received by news media in need of financial support that engage in news reporting and are published regularly. The editorial content should primarily be self-produced and focus on news and investigative journalism (there are specific requirements on editorial content, self-produced content and periodicity). Media eligible for support should be generally accessible and work to ensure that people with disabilities can access the content. There is also a requirement that the journalistic activities should not significantly undermine fundamental democratic values.   Four support schemes are included. Starting with the main scheme:  1) General support for news media, with a focus on local and regional media.  2) Extended support for news media covering geographical areas with a lower media coverage or news media in national minority languages.  3) Support for the distribution of printed newspapers.  4) A temporary transitional support scheme (ending in 2028) for newspapers that used to receive “operational support” within the previous subsidy schemes.
Results: The structural changes of the support schemes were launched only this year, and no results have yet been reported. The new law on media support and the new support schemes are based on a government inquiry which was presented in 2022 (“Ett hållbart mediestöd för hela landet Ds 2022:14”). The government inquiry included an evaluation of the necessity and proportionality of a media aid as such which resulted in the proposal to retain support which was deemed to have served to uphold media plurality in Sweden. However, the report also pointed to the need for reforms. The report was submitted to a consultation procedure which gave both public sector, private sector and CSO actors the possibility to give their views on the proposals presented. The aims of the reform have been to adapt the support to new techniques and meeting the needs of smaller news media actors.
