Title EN: Accessibility of media services
Goal: Promote Human Rights And Fundamental Freedoms
SDG: SDG 5 - Achieve gender equality and empower all women and girls,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels
Area of Monitoring: Gender equality
Agency Implementation: Council for Electronic Media
Main Feature: At the end of 2020. The Broadcasting Act has been amended to transpose the provisions of Directive (EU) 2018/1808 of the European Parliament and of the Council amending the Audiovisual Media Services Directive. Media service providers should ensure that content on their services is progressively made accessible to people with visual or hearing impairments. Means of making audiovisual media services content accessible include, but are not limited to, sign language interpretation, subtitling for the deaf and hard of hearing, speech subtitling and audio description.  Radio service providers shall make programmes and broadcasts accessible to the visually or hearing impaired via the internet, mobile applications or other technical means at their disposal.  The law provides specific obligations for certain persons: - for public service media providers: to produce and make available for distribution news and current affairs television programmes in accordance with technological developments and economic opportunities in a way that makes them accessible to people with visual or hearing impairments. Public service providers should plan to subtitle all television programmes with language content such as news, current affairs, films, series, etc., gradually extending to relevant non-linear on-demand services.  - for commercial media service providers with national coverage and digital terrestrial broadcasting of television programmes with a poly-thematic or informative programming profile and an average daily audience share of more than 20 per cent, as well as the television programmes of BNT: to provide mandatory Bulgarian sign language translation of at least one of their news broadcasts in the range 19:00 - 23:30.    The accessibility measures and actions cover all audiovisual media service providers registered and licensed by CEM. The accessibility requirements are largely measurable for television programmes with a poly-thematic and informative profile, while in Bulgaria a large number of providers create and/or provide for distribution music, film and other niche channels that imply other types of accessibility requirements - such as audio dubbing in Bulgarian and due to the mandatory requirement for translation into Bulgarian.
Results: After the entry into force of the amendments to the RTS Act related to the accessibility of media services, providers had to submit three-year plans to the regulator within eight months. It should be noted that the implementation of accessibility measures requires financial resources, human labour, the application of artificial intelligence, the introduction of innovative technologies, Internet applications, the introduction of subtitling systems, and this involves financial resources.  Most of the commercial media service providers are members of the Association of Bulgarian Broadcasters – ABBRO. This is the largest and most representative organisation that unites most of the radio stations and includes the five largest TV providers.  ABBRO has submitted an Accessibility Plan, which is comprehensive and includes not only ABBRO's member radio stations but also major television providers with large audiences, who have submitted as separate applications their percentages or volume in hours for each individual programme, on an annual basis, for the three-year period 2022-2024. 11 more commercial providers have subsequently joined ABBRO's Accessibility Plan. There are another 28 non-ABBRO providers who have submitted plans. A crucial aspect here is that some of the Accessibility Plans are more modest and implementation is staggered over time, as the new obligations are linked to investments (financial, human, technological).  The Bulgarian National Television has also presented an Accessibility Plan, which outlines achievements and upcoming steps to increase accessibility. BNT provides sign language interpretation by professional interpreters for the Around the World and at Home central news bulletin at 8 p.m. and also for the 6 p.m. news bulletin. Also, at briefings and press conferences of important institutions on topical issues. Since November 2022, a sign language interpreter has also been provided during the More of the Day daily journalistic programme - topical journalism. The BNT 1 programme also provides scrolls during news broadcasts. Sign language interpreters for the deaf are also provided for election campaign periods - for election debates and other forms of campaigning. Sign language interpretation is also provided for live broadcasts of religious services. BNT provides on its website the option HEAR THE NEWS - the programme is based on an e-reader which converts written text, with a female voice, into audio. At first the voice interpretation has problems with intonation and getting the accents right, but this is improving over time due to the self-learning artificial intelligence and is a very important part of improving access to information content for blind people: https://bntnews.bg/listen. BNT provides continuity of the introduced BETA BNT SUBTITLES option - also accessible from the website, with this option subtitles are included in real time of the viewing time - http://tv.bnt.bg/, and these subtitles are included for all types of programmes. BNT1 broadcasts a programme for people with hearing impairments, WORLD OF GESTURES, once a week. In BNT2 - sign language interpretation is provided in the programme Knowledge.BG.  The Accessibility Plan of the Bulgarian National Radio commits that BNR will prioritise the accessibility of media services for people with disabilities in its programming, digital and technological development. It explicitly sets out a number of specific activities:  BNR to focus on the development of its web portal www.bnr.bg, by introducing technology for adding subtitles to audio content; also, a section on the BNR portal to enable people with disabilities to send complaints, recommendations and questions related to the accessibility of the services offered by the public broadcaster. BNR informed that it is working on these obligations. Additional means of accessibility are being introduced, for example, functionalities are already available for some articles and sound files, e.g.: https://binar.bg/bnr-novini/. Much of the audio content is also available as text files, on the BNR website, in various subdirectories. At the end of 2021, the BNR has acquired software that will be the basis for building a national newsroom. In mid-2022, the software was upgraded with additional capabilities, including automatic subtitling of sound files and automatic dubbing of texts. In the meantime, Bulgarian National Radio has started negotiations with specialists in the field of sign language interpretation, and through the BNR's Facebook profile will be offered the possibility of presenting one newscast per day via a video with sign language interpretation. On the BNR web portal is available the functionality to enlarge the font size of the articles at the user's request. There is also a functionality for submitting alerts through a special Submit an alert button on the homepage, enabling people with disabilities to send complaints, recommendations and questions related to the BNR and other institutions. BNR also draws attention to the problems of people with disabilities as part of its on-air programmes. As a major challenge, the national public service broadcaster notes that funding for the medium continues to be tied solely to linear content, and that accessibility measures can only be implemented for non-linear services provided via the internet and social networks.  In June and July 2022, The Council for Electronic Media carried out a focused monitoring of audiovisual content for the fulfilment of the obligations to ensure the accessibility of 12 programmes insofar as they are of providers with a large public impact and audience. The monitoring of distributed media content aimed to identify the presence or absence of subtitles, sign language and/or running captions, short excerpts from news headlines, various scroll bars, etc. The monitored programmes were selected according to their profile, either poly-thematic or specialised, in order to confide what kind of content is accessible to audiences with special hearing needs. Polythematic programmes are BNT1, BNT2 (implemented in the field of culture and education), BTV, NOVA TV, BULGARIA ON AIR. The specialised ones - BTV LADY (aimed at the female audience), BTV CINEMA, DIEMA FAMILY, KINONOVA (film), EUROCOM (news and information), NATIONAL GEOGRAPHIC (documentary), 7/8 TV (entertainment and information). Key findings: the focused ten-day monitoring of the accessibility of the distributed TV content is limited in time (for the period 6-15 June 2022), limited in scope (checking only 12 TV programmes), limited in type of accessibility - for people with hearing difficulties.  The data obtained is a snapshot for a 10-day observation period and shows that of the five selected poly-thematic programmes, the first place in the amount of subtitles (8.2%) is held by BULGARIA ON AIR, followed by BNT2 and BNT1. In terms of the amount of content with sign language interpretation, BNT1, BNT2 and BTV recorded the highest amount. The highest number of running captions/scrolls was in BNT1, followed by BULGARIA ON AIR and BNT2.  Of the specialised programmes, EUROCOM has the most subtitles and captions, while the other specialised programmes - mainly film programmes - do not have accessibility for the hearing impaired, as they rely on subtitling in Bulgarian. The resulting accessibility values (for people with hearing problems) of the 12 TV programmes show both positive trends for some programmes and very unsatisfactory trends for others. This suggests a need for further efforts by providers to increase the amount of accessible content for people with hearing impairments, which the CEM will continue to monitor.   More information on accessibility can be found in the CEM report on the implementation of the accessibility requirements for media services (Article 8a of the Law on Radio and Television) - https://www.cem.bg/activitybg/2253
Financial Ressources: The financing of this measure for the public BNT and BNR is from the general maintenance funds provided by a subsidy from the state budget. Funding for implementation by commercial providers is at their own expense.

Goal: Integrate Culture In Sustainable Development Frameworks
SDG: SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: International cooperation for sustainable development
Cultural Domain: Design,Performing Arts,Media Arts,Cinema and Audiovisual Arts,Music,Publishing,Visual Arts
Agency Implementation: European Commission (Directorate General for International Partnerships) Organisation of the African, Caribbean, Pacific Group of States
Main Feature: The programme intends to boost the potential of the cultural and creative sector and its contribution to the social and economic development of the ACP countries, aiming at: ·	Encouraging entrepreneurship and cultural innovation, as well as the participation of the youth ·	Creating new jobs and increasing artists’ and cultural professionals’ revenues ·	Raising the quality of the ACP cultural productions, ·	Valorizing the cultural productions and artists from the ACP countries on international markets.
Results: Through a cascading grant system implemented by intermediate organisations to gain proximity to sectoral needs and increase efficiency, the following results have been achieved: 272 cultural and creative industries  projects spread over the ACP countries have been supported and more than 140 feature films, documentaries and series projects have received an ACP bonus.   Numerous promotion, training, and capacity-building activities have been offered to subgrantees and film professionals, enabling them to improve the quality and sustainability of their projects.   The credibility of ACP Culture has also helped cultural organisations on the ground to conclude longer-term partnerships with other institutions.   Film makers gained an increased international recognition: African films supported by the programme were screened in prestigious film festivals in Europe and Africa, where they won several prizes and special mentions.
Financial Ressources: Aprox. USD 44 million [EUR 40 million]
Recommandations: Main conclusions drawn from the mid-term evaluation for the period 2019-2022:   -	The tripartite approach of the ACP-EU Programme (financing, nourishing capacity, and networking) is confirmed to be largely relevant.  It has encouraged organisational growth and South-South, North-South collaborations with a unique and broad transnational/transregional approach, while accompanying the market  opportunities offered by the digital transition. -	The Programme has yet to adequately develop complementarities and/or synergies with other relevant ACP or regional programmes, allowing to coordinate/share cross sectoral knowledge, essential to address the development of the creative economy. -	There are indications that CCIs and Audiovisual operators have gained experience in grant delivery, organizational management and SME development which strengthen their future prospects. A dialogue has been initiated with and among the main stakeholders in order to promote the continuity of some post-project benefits.   Recommendations include:  -	Advance at the political level by using the ACP-EU Culture Programme as a platform and facilitator for that exercise. -	Focus on and foster intra-ACP networking, and knowledge generation and management. -	Engage with international, regional, and national cultural agencies to develop an ‘alliance’ for ACP culture that would share information on current and upcoming developments. -	Promote linkages between the CCIs and the tourism sector, and encourage cross–sectoral exchanges among the grantees working in different subsectors . -	Develop mentorship among grantees to spread experience to youth. The more experienced and mature of the grantees could become mentors for younger creatives .   Link: https://www.acp-ue-culture.eu/en/feature-update/supporting-culture-and-creativity-in-acp-countries-harnessing-the-mid-term-evaluation-of-the-acp-eu-programme/

Title EN: Act Out – Tour und Residency Funding Programme
Goal: Achieve A Balanced Flow Of Cultural Goods And Services And Increase The Mobility Of Artists And Cultural Professionals
SDG: SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 10 - Reduce inequality within and among countries,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Mobility of artists and cultural professionals
Agency Implementation: Federal Ministry for European and International Affairs, IG Freie Theaterarbeit
Main Feature: ACT OUT is an international tour and residency funding programme for independent theatre and performance artists and groups from the genres: Drama theatre, Musical theatre, Children’s and youth theatre, Dance and performance, New Circus and Contemporary Circus, Street art/performance, Object and puppet theatre. ACT OUT is funded by the Federal Ministry for European and International Affairs and administrated by IG Freie Theaterarbeit (“Austrian Association for Independent Performing Arts”).In addition to the residency funding programme, ACT OUT online offers an online-video platform on Vimeo where artists / theatre groups can upload recordings of their stage productions. ACT OUT online serves, among other things, as a selection catalogue for Austrian Cultural Forums who are interested in streaming Austrian stage productions. Tour and residency funding is available for all countries, but the focus lies on other European countries. Guest performances or tours within Austria are not supported.  The maximum amount of funding for international guest performances is EUR 12,000. Support is provided for costs for travel, transportation, accommodation and translations as well as fees for artists, technicians and production management. The maximum funding amount for international residencies of up to 5 persons is EUR 4,000. Support is provided for travel and accommodation (up to a maximum of 21 days) as well as artists fees.  The project aims at: •	Supporting cross-border artistic work •	Enabling the expansion of international networks •	Developing new mediation formats (see video platform in particular)  Between 2021 and 2023 EUR 65,000/year have been allocated to the programme by the Federal Ministry for European and International Affairs.

SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Partnering with civil society
Agency Implementation: Abu Dhabi Music and Arts Foundation ADMAF
Main Feature: A professional development program for cultural professionals from diverse disciplines, designed to instill skills and build networks for long-term creative partnerships across the UAE, with practical experience working across rapidly changing fields. Tandem believes that the burning cultural and social questions of our times can be addressed much more creatively and effectively through inspiring learning experiences when working with new organizations and across new localities. Tandem Al Emarat is an initiative of the Abu Dhabi Music and Arts Foundation, European Cultural Foundation and MitOst. This cultural program offers a space to build real, meaningful and sustainable relationships that can grow through shared artistic interests, enthusiasm for creative discovery and the joy of making things happen together. The program also allows cultural professionals from many different disciplines to acquire skills required for engaging in long-term partnerships. The Tandem process provides hands-on possibilities for getting real insights into the cultural scenes in the 7 Emirates. Participants gain practical experience by collaborating within rapidly changing fields in the UAE.
Results: The program successfully established a network of cultural managers across the seven Emirates. By focusing on local collaborations, Tandem Al Emarat facilitated the creation of robust partnerships among cultural professionals within the UAE. Additionally, they also brought in several collaborations and funding from several international foundations. Participants gained valuable skills and experience through hands-on projects and workshops. These activities provided practical insights into managing cultural projects and navigating the rapidly changing cultural landscape in the UAE. The program's structure, which includes partner forums, kick-off meetings, and final presentations, ensured comprehensive professional development for all participants.

Title EN: Addis Jazz Festival and African Day Celebration
Goal: Achieve A Balanced Flow Of Cultural Goods And Services And Increase The Mobility Of Artists And Cultural Professionals
SDG: SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 10 - Reduce inequality within and among countries,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Mobility of artists and cultural professionals
Agency Implementation: Selam Ethiopia
Main Feature: Addis Jazz Festival Mulatu Astatke's pioneering work in the 1960s, blending Ethiopian melodies with jazz harmony, gave birth to the vibrant tradition of Ethio-jazz. While this unique sound has been celebrated worldwide, its prominence within Addis Ababa itself has grown only recently. Recognizing this rich heritage and its untapped potential, Selam has established the Addis Jazz Festival as a premier event in the city. Despite other cities like Cape Town and Nairobi boasting established jazz festivals, Addis Ababa has lacked a flagship event that reflects its historical, cultural, and political significance. The Addis Jazz Festival aims to fill this gap by providing a platform for local and international talent, fostering intercultural exchange, and celebrating the global jazz community's spirit. As Ethiopia's largest jazz festival to date, the Addis Jazz Festival features both emerging stars and established legends, showcasing the rich diversity of the jazz scene. Beyond music, the festival offers a dynamic experience with food, drinks, circus performances, cultural product markets, and art exhibitions. Following successful inaugural editions in 2019 and 2023, the 2024 festival, in collaboration with African Jazz Village, promises an even grander experience. Held at the iconic African Jazz Village at Ghion Hotel, the festival aligns with Africa Day celebrations, echoing themes of unity and diversity—values deeply embedded in the improvisational spirit of jazz.  Goals and Objectives Goals: Establish a world-class jazz festival in Addis Ababa. Celebrate African unity, diversity, and culture, amplifying the impact of the Connect for Culture Africa (CfCA) program through strategic partnerships.  Schedule The 2024 Addis Jazz Festival was organized over three days: Day 1: May 24 Day 2: May 25 Day 3: May 26 Why these dates? The festival is scheduled in May to maintain seasonal consistency and align with Ethiopia's festive season post-Easter and Ramadan, traditionally marked by social gatherings and celebrations. Additionally, coinciding with Africa Day, the festival leverages this timing to advocate for cultural demands and showcase Africa's vibrant arts sector. By providing a platform for artists in the capital of Africa, the festival becomes a dynamic celebration of Africa Day and a testament to cultural diversity. Venue Selection for Addis Jazz Festival 2024 Location: African Jazz Village, Ghion Hotel Significance of the Venue The decision to hold the Addis Jazz Festival at the African Jazz Village, located within the Ghion Hotel, is both strategic and symbolic. This venue is renowned for its deep-rooted connection to Ethiopia’s rich musical heritage. It has hosted numerous legendary performances and recordings that have significantly shaped Ethiopian jazz. The African Jazz Village, under the ownership and promotion of the renowned musician Mulatu Astatke, stands as a testament to the country’s musical legacy and innovation. Symbolic Value Hosting the festival at this iconic location is a tribute to Ethiopia’s cultural and artistic history. It elevates the festival's prestige and allure, transforming it into a revered space where artists and jazz enthusiasts gather to celebrate the fusion of Ethiopian melodies and jazz harmonies, a tradition pioneered by Astatke. This choice aligns with the festival’s objectives of celebrating African unity, diversity, and culture, particularly as the event coincides with Africa Day celebrations. Thus, the venue choice underscores the importance of preserving and promoting Africa’s cultural heritage.   Achievements in Celebrating Africa Day The Addis Jazz Festival successfully celebrated Africa Day on May 25th, extending the festivities through May 24th and May 26th as well. The event featured a diverse lineup of artists from various African countries, including Ethiopia, Uganda, Zambia, and Zimbabwe. Key highlights included: Showcasing Ethiopian Jazz and African Music: The festival highlighted the rich traditions of Ethiopian jazz alongside a variety of other African musical genres, offering attendees a deep dive into the continent's vibrant musical landscape. Promoting Cross-Cultural Exchange: Through its diverse lineup, the festival fostered cross-cultural exchange and unity, bringing together musicians and audiences from different backgrounds to celebrate African heritage. Educational Platform: The event served as a platform for the education and appreciation of African heritage, with performances and activities designed to enhance understanding and appreciation of the continent's cultural richness. Solidarity and Celebration: The festival fostered a sense of solidarity among attendees, encouraging a shared celebration of African identity and culture. Overall Festival Production Despite facing challenging conditions, including uncertainty regarding the festival venue and financing, the Addis Jazz Festival was executed with a high level of professionalism. The organizing team demonstrated flexibility and resilience, ensuring the festival's success under less-than-ideal circumstances. Although the original plans for the festival envisioned a different scenario, the execution remained strong and adaptive. The team effectively navigated unforeseen challenges, maintaining the festival's core mission and delivering a memorable event that aligned closely with its strategic goals.
Results: Showcasing Ethiopian Jazz and African Music: The festival highlighted the rich traditions of Ethiopian jazz alongside a variety of other African musical genres, offering attendees a deep dive into the continent's vibrant musical landscape. Promoting Cross-Cultural Exchange: Through its diverse lineup, the festival fostered cross-cultural exchange and unity, bringing together musicians and audiences from different backgrounds to celebrate African heritage. Educational Platform: The event served as a platform for the education and appreciation of African heritage, with performances and activities designed to enhance understanding and appreciation of the continent's cultural richness. Solidarity and Celebration: The festival fostered a sense of solidarity among attendees, encouraging a shared celebration of African identity and culture.

Title EN: Decision No. 1909/QĐ-TTg dated on December 11, 2021 of the Prime Minister approving the Cultural Development Strategy to 2030
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture
SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Cultural and creative sectors
Agency Implementation: Government, Ministry of Culture, Sports and Tourism, Ministry of Education and Training, Ministry of Information and Communications, Ministry of Science and Technology, Ministry of Home Affairs, Ministry of Finance,  Ministry of Foreign Affairs, others
Main Feature: This strategy is dedicated to mobilizing all development resources to ensure that culture becomes a true inner strength, a driving force that significantly fosters patriotism, national pride, belief, and the aspiration to build a prosperous and happy nation. It aims to position Vietnamese people at the center, as the subject, the most important resource, and the goal of development.  The strategy emphasizes proactive cooperation and the promotion of Vietnam’s cultural values internationally, enhancing cultural soft power. It significantly contributes to the overall strength of the entire political system, elevating the country's international standing, fostering a peaceful environment, firmly defending the Fatherland, and ensuring sustainable development and international integration.  Specific objectives to be achieved by 2030 include:  - Ensuring that 100% of provincial administrative units have three types of cultural institutions, including a cultural center, a museum, and a library.  - Guaranteeing that at least 75% of the population in remote, border, and island areas and 80% of communes in ethnic minority and mountainous areas can enjoy and participate in cultural activities. - Annually publishing 10–15 high-quality research and critical theory works on culture and the arts; achieving 2 ASEAN literary awards; and producing approximately 20–25 cultural and historical works on national history, revolutionary struggles, and national renewal.  - Striving for the added value of cultural industries to contribute 7% of GDP, with an average annual growth rate of 7% in GDP value, and having 1-3 creative cities participating in the UNESCO Creative Cities Network.  - Increasing investment in culture to a minimum of 2% of the total annual budget expenditure.  The strategy includes 11 groups of tasks and solutions: - Raising awareness and promoting cultural development.  - Improving institutions, policies, and legal frameworks.  - Building the Vietnamese people with comprehensive development.  - Creating a healthy cultural environment, creating the driving force for socio-economic development, and international integration.  - Enhancing the quality and effectiveness of cultural activities.  - Protecting and promoting national cultural heritage.  - Completing the market mechanism in the cultural sector, with a priority on developing certain cultural industries. - Actively integrating and enhancing cultural cooperation and exchange.  - Creating breakthroughs in human resource development in the field of culture and arts.  - Promoting scientific research, technology, and digital transformation in the cultural sector.  - Effectively utilizing investment resources and developing the cultural sector.
Financial Ressources: The resources for implementing the Strategy include state budget, enterprise capital, and other legitimate support, sponsorship, and mobilized sources

Title EN: Adoption of the initiative by the Islamic World Educational, Scientific, and Cultural Organization (ISESCO) aimed at including culture as a standalone goal within the Sustainable Development Goals.
Goal: Integrate Culture In Sustainable Development Frameworks
SDG: SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: International cooperation for sustainable development
Cultural Domain: Design,Performing Arts,Media Arts,Cinema and Audiovisual Arts,Music,Publishing,Visual Arts
Agency Implementation: -Ministry of Culture - Islamic World Educational, Scientific, and Cultural Organization (ISESCO)
Main Feature: This initiative was presented by the Islamic World Educational, Scientific, and Cultural Organization (ICESCO) on the occasion of the State of Qatar hosting the 12th Conference of Culture Ministers in the Islamic World, held in Doha on September 25-26, 2023, under the theme "Renewing Cultural Action in the Islamic World," and making it a tributary for sustainable development (Annex No. 19). The State of Qatar adopted this initiative following the meeting. The initiative calls for taking the necessary measures to: -	Preserve and revive traditional knowledge, indigenous cultures, and ancestral cultural practices. -	Promote cultural diversity, dialogue, and respect. -	Support policies and investments based on cultural indicators for sustainable development. -	Ensure equal access for all to various forms of cultural expression, artistic activities, and cultural resources, with a focus on marginalized groups.
Results: On September 25, 2023, the 12th The 12th Conference of the Ministers of Culture in the Islamic World commenced under the theme "Renewing Cultural Work in the Islamic World" in Doha, the State of Qatar, with the participation of delegations from 44 countries, 12 international and regional organizations, and 12 ministers from various Islamic countries around the world. The conference resulted in the adoption of several recommendations relevant to the scope of this report, as follows: -	Working on incorporating culture as the 18th Sustainable Development Goal. -	Developing cultural policies in Member States to strongly address the economic and developmental dimensions of culture. -	Developing programs for Cultural Capitals in the Islamic World. -	Working on implementing the Cultural Index Project in the Islamic World. -	Developing a strategy to combat the illicit trafficking of cultural property in the Islamic world.
Financial Ressources: Information not available

Title EN: AG culturel | Kultur-GA
Goal: Integrate Culture In Sustainable Development Frameworks
SDG: SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: National sustainable development policies and plans
Cultural Domain: Performing Arts,Cinema and Audiovisual Arts,Music,Visual Arts
Agency Implementation: Association AG culturel | Kultur-GA
Main Feature: Ce projet d’abonnement, élaboré en collaboration avec les cantons romands, permet aux jeunes jusqu'à 26 ans de profiter de l'offre culturelle la plus étendue de Suisse. L'AG culturel est un abonnement qui permet à son détenteur ou sa détentrice d'accéder librement, pour le prix de 110 dollars américains par an, à tous les lieux culturels ayant signé la convention de partenariat.  L'AG culturel est valable dans les cantons de Fribourg, Neuchâtel, Jura, Valais et Berne. L'AG culturel compte plus de 290 lieux partenaires, ce qui fait des milliers d'événements (concerts, spectacles, expositions, festivals et films.) accessibles gratuitement. Parce que la culture est un moteur de créativité et d'échanges, l'association veut contribuer à l'accès facilité aux événements culturels, toutes disciplines confondues et permettre ainsi aux jeunes de découvrir autrement le monde qui les entoure et de le/se questionner.  L'AG culturel est né de la volonté de favoriser la pratique culturelle en Suisse par la mise en réseaux des lieux et par une offre libre et illimitée. Le prix étant défini par avance, cet abonnement encourage la multiplication des sorties et la prise de risques culturels. Ouverte à tous les arts et à toutes les institutions culturelles établies sur le territoire de validité et proposant une programmation professionnelle, cette initiative donne accès à la culture sous toutes ses formes et dans toute sa diversité.
Results: L’abonnement est né en 2012 en Valais. En 2018, il s’est étendu aux cantons suivants : Fribourg, Neuchâtel, Jura et Berne (Jura bernois, Seeland et Bienne). En 2021, l’AG culturel a étendu son offre en Suisse alémanique par une adhésion de la ville de Berne. En 2022, le nombre d’abonnés (1514) a plus que doublé en comparaison avec l’année précédente (627). La progression est encore plus marquée si on compare avec les chiffres de fin 2019, soit avant la pandémie ; puisque le nombre d’abonnements a triplé par rapport à cette période (395). Au 22.12.2023, il y avait 1803 abonnées et abonnés. Pour l’ensemble de l’année 2022, les lieux partenaires ont comptabilisé près de 5325 entrées réalisées par les abonnés de l’AG culturel. Ce chiffre est trois fois plus élevé que celui pour 2021 (1549). Les chiffres pour l’année 2023 seront connus début 2024 mais les prévisions laissent à penser que le nombre d’entrées va doubler par rapport à 2022. En fin 2023, 290 lieux sont partenaires de l’AG culturel. Ce chiffre n’a cessé de croître ces dernières années : 213 en 2020, 237 en 2021, 258 en 2022.
Financial Ressources: Soutien des cantons partenaires, de la Conférence des Présidents des Organes de répartition de la Loterie romande CPOR pour la période 2018-2020 et 2021-2023, et soutien de la Confédération (Office fédéral de la culture OFC, soutien à la participation culturelle) pour l’extension en Ville de Berne.
Recommandations: Le rapport d’activités est régulièrement évalué par les cantons romands (CDAC CIIP). L’association poursuit son travail de communication vers les potentielles futures personnes abonnées.

Results: ●A total of 18 spaces for training with a decolonizing approach were promoted (workshops, discussions, forums, meetings and exchanges of knowledge and talks), and a total of six (6) research projects were developed at the national level on the decolonization of thought for the liberation of peoples, under this concept a total of 86 decolonizing articles were published in digital format, In turn, a total of six (6) decolonizing books were edited, published and baptized, all of this as a spearhead towards the affirmation of identity, as well as the scope of cognitive sovereignty and historical-cultural awareness of the Venezuelan people, with direct and indirect benefit of a total of 51,356 people, with an investment of USD 5,090.40.         ● The Foundation "International Center of Studies for the Decolonization Luis Antonio Bigott" (CIEDLAB), developed a total of nine (9) investigations on the decolonization of thought for the liberation of peoples, equivalent to 90% of the programmed goal (10 investigations). These investigations were carried out at the national level, benefiting a total of 4,574 people, including researchers, teachers and students, 2,360 (52%) women and 2,214 (48%) men, with an investment of USD 1,196.10 (US$).
Recommandations: Identity, cognitive sovereignty and cultural historical awareness. Take into account organizations, institutions and services dedicated to local studies, heritage recovery, the construction of narratives and the preservation of collective memory.

Title EN: African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA)
Goal: Integrate Culture In Sustainable Development Frameworks
SDG: SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: National sustainable development policies and plans
Cultural Domain: Design,Performing Arts,Media Arts,Cinema and Audiovisual Arts,Music,Publishing,Visual Arts
Agency Implementation: Department of Trade, Industry and Competition (DTIC).
Main Feature: The African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA) was established through a series of significant steps and milestones. The idea for the AfCFTA was first proposed during the 18th Ordinary Session of the Assembly of Heads of State and Government of the African Union (AU) in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia, in January 2012. The session adopted the decision to establish the AfCFTA and the Action Plan for Boosting Intra-African Trade. Formal negotiations began in 2015, focusing on creating a single market for goods and services across Africa. These negotiations were conducted in phases, covering various aspects such as trade in goods, trade in services, and dispute settlement mechanisms. The AfCFTA Agreement was signed by 44 of the 55 AU member states on March 21, 2018, in Kigali, Rwanda. This marked a significant step towards the realization of the AfCFTA. The AfCFTA officially entered into force on 30 May 2019. Trading under the AfCFTA regime officially began on 1 January 2021. This marked the start of a new era for intra-African trade, with the aim of creating a single, liberalized market for goods and services across the continent, including cultural goods and services. The AfCFTA is one of the flagship projects of the AU’s Agenda 2063, which envisions an integrated, prosperous, and peaceful Africa. The African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA) has several key objectives aimed at transforming the economic landscape of Africa as follows: Create a Single Market: The AfCFTA aims to create a single market for goods and services across the continent, facilitating the free movement of people and investments. This is in line with the Pan African Vision of “An integrated, prosperous, and peaceful Africa” as outlined in Agenda 2063. Boost Intra-African Trade: By eliminating tariffs on 90% of goods and reducing non-tariff barriers, the AfCFTA seeks to significantly increase trade within Africa. This is expected to boost intra-African trade by over 52%. Enhance Competitiveness: The agreement aims to enhance the competitiveness of African economies by promoting industrial development, diversification, and regional value chain development. Economic Growth and Development: The AfCFTA is designed to contribute to sustainable and inclusive socio-economic development, gender equality, and structural transformation across the continent. Global Trade Position: Strengthening Africa’s common voice and policy space in global trade negotiations is another key objective, aiming to improve Africa’s trading position in the global market. These objectives collectively aim to create a more integrated and prosperous Africa, enhancing economic growth and development across the continent
Results: The African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA) is expected to bring about several transformative results for the continent: Poverty Reduction: The AfCFTA has the potential to lift around 30 million people out of extreme poverty and raise the incomes of 68 million others who live on less than $5.50 per day. Economic Growth: By creating a single market for goods and services, the AfCFTA is expected to increase Africa’s income by $450 billion by 2035. This will be driven by trade facilitation measures that cut red tape and simplify customs procedures. Increased Trade: The agreement aims to boost intra-African trade by over 52% by eliminating tariffs on 90% of goods and reducing non-tariff barriers. This will deepen continental integration and increase productivity. Job Creation: The AfCFTA is expected to create better jobs and increase employment opportunities across the continent. This will be particularly beneficial for women and youth, who are key drivers of economic growth in Africa. Investment Attraction: The agreement is anticipated to attract significant foreign direct investment (FDI), with estimates suggesting an increase of between 111% and 159%. Competitiveness: By enhancing the competitiveness of African economies, the AfCFTA will help diversify exports and accelerate growth. Shared Prosperity: The overall goal is to increase shared prosperity across Africa, making the continent more competitive on the global stage. These results collectively aim to transform Africa’s economic landscape, fostering sustainable development and inclusive growth

Main Feature: MEASURE 2- DNC Agreement, MEC-INEFOP-ASU, Uruguay Ilumina During 2020, the Department of Creative Industries (DICREA) of the National Directorate of Culture (DNC) begins dialogue with two civil society organizations: the Association of Sound Technicians (ASU) of Uruguay and the Uruguay Ilumina collective. In May 2020 - within the framework of the pandemic - Uruguay illuminates presented a national professional lighting training project to the DNC. The generation of job sources for professionals in the field was identified as a need, as well as the need for professional training throughout the national territory. From these first dialogues, articulation work begins between Uruguay Ilumina, the ASU and DICREA in the development of a proposal for the professionalization of the occupations of sound technicians and illuminators, including both training and certification of skills. It is presented to the National Institute of Employment and Vocational Training (INEFOP), which in October approves the project and the signing of an agreement for these purposes. This dialogue process culminated in the joint design by the three parties (civil society, DNC, and INEFOP) of a project to develop cultural and creative industries throughout the national territory. The agreement was signed in February 2021 and the calls and project activities also began that year. For this purpose, a monitoring commission was created made up of the four parties and two specialized work tables for sound engineers and lighting engineers respectively with the presence of the aforementioned social organizations, in which the terms of the calls to be made were jointly defined. During the years 2022 and 2023, lighting and sound courses continued to be developed nationwide within the framework of this project. Financial resources allocated to the policy/measure in USD  Through an agreement between the Ministry of Education and Culture (MEC) through the INAE, the National Directorate of Culture together with the Dance Association of Uruguay (ADDU), the Eastern Regional University Center of the University of the Republic and the National Institute of Employment and Vocational Training (INEFOP) opened the Management and production of sustainable and inclusive cultural projects program in 2022, which involves training for the development of the dance sector in Uruguay. The training was aimed at 50 dance agents from all over the territory. The training program was addressed in three semesters, working transversally on the theoretical-practical approach. The training included, among others, the following contents: Rights, diversity and equity and inclusion of people with disabilities.

Main Feature: The airBurgenland artist-in-residence programme was launched in 2023. The programme offers up to 50 residencies for artists, writers, academics and curators annually. The main objective of the programme is to strengthen the impact of contemporary art in Burgenland as well as its impact on society in general. In order to promote transnational exchange and the mobility of artists, airBurgenland cooperates with art institutions and platforms throughout Europe. Besides inviting international artists to Burgenland, airBurgenland also provides opportunities for Burgenland artists to take part in international activities, thus establishing sustainable relationships between international artists and local communities.  Support is provided for: accommodation, studio and workshop space, mentoring, connections to local communities and artists, connections to international institutions and partners, venues for exchange and presentation of work, per diems, local transport. The programme aims at: •	Strengthening the presence and impact of contemporary art in Burgenland •	International networking •	Establishing lasting relationships between international artists and local communities
Results: In 2023 - the first year of the project - 43 artists (27 female, 16 male) from 14 countries and seven disciplines were invited as artists in residence as part of the airBurgenland programme. In addition to the artists, eight curators worked within the framework of the project. The presence of the artists in residence allows to build sustainable networks. First and foremost, it creates a dialogue between the invited artists, their communities and their audiences. In addition, the simultaneous presence of several artists from different countries also creates various cross-border-networks.

Title EN: andererseits – Magazine for Disability and Society
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture
SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Media diversity
Agency Implementation: Medienhaus andererseits GmbH
Main Feature: andererseits is an independent, inclusive magazine founded in 2020. Its aim is to tell socially relevant stories from diverse perspectives. A special focus lies on the perspectives of people with disabilities. As a digital-first publication, andererseits is not only committed to high journalistic standards, but also works innovatively with digital tools and social media. Since March 2024, andererseits also publishes a print magazine. Andererseits’ products (magazine, website, newsletter, social media) all facilitate different dimensions of accessibility. A main goal is to provide information in plain language and thus creating a source of information for the approximately 700,000 people in Austria who use plain language and therefore have limited access to information. andererseits provides copies of the print magazine free of charge or at a reduced price for e.g. to persons with learning difficulties, senior citizens, people with German as a second language and young people.  The ethical principles of andererseits are based on the Code of Ethics for the Austrian Press and are inspired by other media, including the BBC's Editorial Guidelines.  Journalists with and without disabilities work for andererseits – equally, critically and paid fairly. Although 15-20 percent of people living in Austria have a disability, there are very few journalists with disabilities. andererseits thus creates an environment in which people with and without disabilities work together.  Journalistic texts are often created in teams, either in the form of co-authorship or in the form of supported authorship. A similar model applies for graphic design processes. There is also participation of people with disabilities at a strategic level; the management is advised on budget planning and strategic issues by an inclusive advisory board.  andererseits mission and impact include:  Outreach: andererseits reaches several hundred thousand social media accounts across the German- speaking world every month. Numerous media have already taken up investigative research by andererseits. Readers without disabilities are thus sensitized to the topic of inclusion, and fears of contact are reduced. This effect is measured by andererseits in quarterly user surveys.  Awareness Raising and Advocacy: andererseits is also actively committed to awareness raising and advocacy. The project serves as a good practice example and case study within the media sector itself and has also received attention at the political level in Austria.  Empowerment: andererseits achieves its greatest impact through the direct empowerment of people with disabilities. Journalists who work for andererseits are increasingly receiving external assignments. About 15 young journalists with disabilities have been enabled to enter the professional media sector.

Title EN: Art, Culture and Diverse Finland: The Ministry of Education and Culture's action plan to promote diversity in the field of arts and culture (June 2023)
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture
SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Cultural and creative sectors
Cultural Domain: Design,Performing Arts,Media Arts,Cinema and Audiovisual Arts,Music,Publishing,Visual Arts
Agency Implementation: Ministry of Education and Culture
Main Feature: The Ministry of Education and Culture's action plan to promote diversity in the field of arts and culture is based on the final report of a working group appointed by the Ministry (2021). The action plan aims to take into account the increasing diversity of the Finnish population in the planning and decision-making procedures in arts and cultural policy. The action plan's cross-cutting principles are to promote the realisation of equity and equality, to recognise the diversity of cultural heritage and strengthen intercultural dialogue, and to provide everyone living in Finland with the opportunity to increase their knowledge and skills and to utilise them at work and in leisure activities.   The action plan contains six sets of measures that promote cultural diversity, equity and integration in cultural policy work (strategies, financing, performance and target guidance), in the agencies of the Ministry's branch of government, in the national art institutions, and in the cooperation carried out with cultural communities. Strengthening the knowledge base and carrying out measures within the Government are an important part of the action plan.
Results: Performance guidance agreements for the period of 2024-2027 have been made with agencies, which include concrete objectives and measures concerning enhancement of diversity and competence building in this sphere. Target guidance negotiations have taken with three national art institutions with concrete objectives and measures for enhancement of cultural diversity.  Dialogue cards are a tool developed by the Ministry of Education and Culture and the Arts Promotion Centre Finland (June 2023). The cards enable organisations in the arts and cultural sector make their activities more equal and sustainable. Communities and municipalities in the arts and culture sector all over Finland have ordered more than 1000 dialogue cards in the last six months. The dialogue cards are available free of charge. Dialogue cards: https://www.taike.fi/en/dialogue-cards/dialogue-cards   The Ministry of Education and Culture is developing criteria that support responsible activities, which will be used to promote and monitor the implementation of good governance, equality and non-discrimination, cultural diversity as well as sustainable development in the activities of communities. (2023–2025)   The Ministry of Education and Culture is participating in the implementation of the “National Dialogues” operating model by organising dialogue events. The model is coordinated by the Ministry of Finance. National Dialogues help to build an understanding of different societal phenomena, challenges and opportunities in cooperation between citizens, communities and authorities. The National Dialogue model is not a political process and it does not aim for unanimity or decision-making. The aim is to gain as extensive an understanding as possible of people’s experiences and the economic, social and ecological challenges at hand. The aim is to strengthen social inclusion, cohesion and the ability of Finnish society to change through social dialogue. The operative core group ensures that the summary and the communications spearheads included in it reach the relevant parties in central and local government administration. Ministry organised in 2022 Migration Dialogue, in 2023 Together and Alone Dialogue, which compiled a picture of communities and encounters in today's Finland in the field of arts and culture , in 2024 National dialogue on security and trust in the field of arts and culture.    The Ministry of Education and Culture is taking part in planning and organising the “Y-festivaali” (“Y Festival”) cultural and human rights event of the Ministry of Justice, which will take place in September 2024.    The Center for Cultural Policy Research Cupore: Artists with foreign background in Finland. Diversity Report 2023 was published in the beginning of 2024.
Financial Ressources: Ca. 736 000 USD per year. Arts Promotion Centre Finland´s Subsidies for Promoting Cultural Diversity and Combating Racism. These subsidies are intended for communities to support inclusion and participation in culture, as well as intercultural dialogue.

Title EN: An example of general support for public cultural institutions at local level: public institutions in the Municipality of Celje
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture
SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Cultural and creative sectors
Agency Implementation: Municipality of Celje
Main Feature: The following public cultural institutions operate in Celje: Celje Central Regional Library, Celeia Celje Institute for Cultural Events and Tourism, Celje Regional Museum, Celje Museum of Recent History and the Celje City Theatre. The main funder of the Celeia Celje Institute for Cultural Events and Tourism and the Celje Central Regional Library is the Municipality of Celje. The Celje Regional Museum, the Celje Museum of Recent History and the Celje City Theatre are largely financed by the Ministry of Culture. This exceeds 70 % of the total income of all three institutions and exceeds the total municipal expenditure on culture. The state co-financing brings robustness and stability to the cultural ecosystem and at the same time has a positive impact on the development of creativity, professional priorities and mobility of cultural workers in the city. State funding also means that Celje is not only a local or regional cultural centre, but also a national one in certain areas.
Results: The city of Celje creates a stimulating cultural environment in which creativity, diversity and cooperation are encouraged. Through a balanced system of public cultural institutions and private cultural institutions, it ensures a stable cultural ecosystem in which cultural content and cultural innovation can be maintained.
Financial Ressources: approx. 14,8 million USD
Recommandations: Cultural funding is the most direct instrument available to a municipality to support cultural activities. The overall volume of funding and the structure of the cultural funding system are important. It is worth focusing on two structural questions in particular: What is the optimal ratio of funding between public and private cultural institutions and, secondly, how should funding be allocated between personnel costs, general material costs, program costs and investment costs? It is important to recognize that some of these categories are relatively fixed and externally regulated, which means that the municipality has limited control over them. It is therefore of the utmost importance that the question of the optimal structure of the funding system is sensibly addressed several years in advance, as this is the only way to achieve real cost containment.

Main Feature: The workshops were part of the 3 year Malawi National Commission of UNESCO project on "Strengthening Institutional Capacities in implementing the Malawi Cultural Policy in line with the UNESCO 2005". They aimed at discussing and making recommendations on activities to protect and promote artistic freedom. Two training workshops were therefore organised, in December 2021 and February 2023, for government officials, cultural practitioners and civil society organizations. Area of Monitoring: National sustainable development policies and plans
Agency Implementation: CULTURAL FOUNDATION OF THE CENTRAL BANK OF BOLIVIA - NATIONAL MUSEUM OF ETHNOGRAPHY AND FOLKLORE
Main Feature: The Annual Meeting of Ethnology (RAE) is framed within the institutional objective that mandates to investigate, analyze, dialogue, reflect and develop processes in relation to Bolivian cultural heritage and cultural diversity, throughout the national territory with an open participatory character of the general population, which through short-term actions or institutional policies seeks to develop, recover and disseminate knowledge and research of a cultural nature;  Promotes cultural activities of training and/or non-formal education and spaces for dialogue and reflection from diversity, interculturality, decolonization and depatriarchalization.  This measure has become a space for reflection, dialogue and exchange of knowledge that has been in force uninterrupted for 38 years; generating each year debate under a specific topic such as water, music, food and for the following year the territory.  It has become a national and international reference in the social and human sciences, promoting interdisciplinarity and the recognition of local and indigenous knowledge, all as sources of knowledge and valid in scientific interpretation.  Gradually adapted has to new forms of knowledge transmission, not only with lectures, but also with audiovisual displays, performances and the participation of the cultural diversity of dances and music of indigenous nations and peasant peoples from different latitudes of Bolivia.
Results: In recent years the following data have been obtained: 2022: "Crieanza Mutua y Alimentación" (Mutual Parenting and Feeding), 4 cities (La Paz, Sucre, Santa Cruz, Cochabamba), 231 exhibitions, 1,159 registered, 4,554 attendees, 1 catalogue, 2 volumes of RAE memoirs. 2023: “Sonidos, músicas y espacios" (Sounds, music and spaces), 4 cities (La Paz, Sucre, Santa Cruz, Cochabamba), 217 exhibitions, 787 registered, 7108 attendees, 1 catalogue, 2 volumes of RAE memoirs. 2024: “Agua los flujos de la vida" (Water the flows of life) (preliminary), 4 cities (La Paz, Trinidad, Sucre, Cochabamba).
Financial Ressources: $us. 82,370.42 (versions from 2022 to 2024)
Recommandations: As a space for dialogue, respect for all types of thoughts is prioritized, without having one predominant one, since everyone contributes to the construction of interculturality and freedom of expression around the proposed topics. This has made the event an interdisciplinary and plural space with the participation of professionals, academics, students, civil society, indigenous peoples, related institutions and anyone who wishes to participate as exhibitors and attendees. With a proposal that changes every year, the scientific heritage (academic and local) is kept up to date in favor of the dissemination and democratization of knowledge.

Title EN: Appel à projets « Découvertes culturelles »
Goal: Integrate Culture In Sustainable Development Frameworks
SDG: SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: National sustainable development policies and plans
Agency Implementation: Service de la culture – Ville de Lausanne
Main Feature: À fin 2020, la Ville de Lausanne a proposé aux structures d'accueil de l'enfance des secteurs du préscolaire, du parascolaire et du socioculturel lausannois, une programmation de découvertes culturelles. Suite à un appel à projets ouvert, 18 propositions artistiques ont été retenues dans les domaines du théâtre, de la danse, du cirque, de la musique et de l’art du récit. Jouées entre quatre et huit fois chacune, elles ont fait l’objet au total de 80 représentations en 60 lieux d’accueil différents. Le Service de la culture a assuré la sélection et l’organisation de ce projet en collaboration avec le Service de la petite enfance, le Service des écoles et du parascolaire, la Permanence Jeunes Borde ainsi que la Fondation pour l’animation socioculturelle lausannoise (FASL). Une attention particulière a été accordée à la pluralité des formes, des esthétiques, des écritures et des parcours artistiques pour départager les 62 candidatures déposées. Les représentations ont eu lieu de mi-mai à fin novembre 2021 au sein des centres de vie enfantine, des APEMS, des structures d’accueil du parascolaire, des centres socioculturels et des maisons de quartier. Cette mesure a eu pour objectif d'offrir des rendez-vous culturels aux enfants et aux jeunes qui fréquentent ces lieux, et donner aux artistes et aux équipes artistiques l’opportunité d’explorer de nouvelles possibilités de jeu en dehors des lieux de culture institutionnels. Elle s’inscrit également dans la volonté affirmée de la Municipalité de renforcer l’accès à la culture pour toutes et tous, dès le plus jeune âge. Par cette démarche, la Ville souhaitait également soutenir dans le cadre de cette reprise de la vie culturelle le secteur professionnel lausannois avec des contributions financières directes. 45 artistes ont ainsi bénéficié de ce soutien.
Results: Ces rendez-vous destinés aux enfants et aux jeunes ont permis aux artistes de se produire en dehors des lieux de culture institutionnels. Ils ont créé du lien et de nouvelles synergies avec les lieux de vie de l’enfance. 45 artistes ont bénéficié d’un soutien financier par cette mesure qui a fait l’objet d’un appel à projets. Les Découvertes culturelles ce sont : -	18 spectacles : chant, cirque, conte, danse, musique, performance, théâtre -	80 représentations dans 60 lieux de vie de l’enfance à Lausanne : •	30 représentations dans 13 crèches et garderies  •	30 représentations dans 30 APEMS et UAPE (parascolaire)  •	20 représentations dans 17 Centres d’animation socioculturels  -	Spectatrices et spectateurs : 2553 enfants, accompagnantes et accompagnants
Recommandations: La qualité du contact avec le public, l’interaction et la proximité avec les artistes sont des composantes qui ont favorisé la réussite du projet dans son ensemble. La mesure a permis d’explorer de nouveaux canaux de diffusion. Présentées in situ, les propositions artistiques ont privilégié des formats adaptables, simples de mise en œuvre et pensés pour un public susceptible de circuler par moment. Un point d’attention est la participation et l’engagement des équipes éducatives dans la mise en œuvre du projet. L’accompagnement d’actions de médiation « Avant – pendant – après » a permis d’ancrer plus durablement l’expérience, d’encourager des collaborations avec les équipes éducatives et d’approfondir la découverte culturelle.

Title EN: Approval of Presidential Decree 198/2021 National Program for the Advancement of Women. (Regulatory framework)
Goal: Promote Human Rights And Fundamental Freedoms
SDG: SDG 5 - Achieve gender equality and empower all women and girls,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels
Area of Monitoring: Gender equality
Cultural Domain: Design,Performing Arts,Media Arts,Cinema and Audiovisual Arts,Music,Publishing,Visual Arts
Agency Implementation: Cuban Women Federation
Main Feature: The National Program for the Advancement of Women summarizes the sentiment and political will of the Cuban State and constitutes the cornerstone in the development of policies in favor of women, while providing continuity to the advancement and development of gender equality. in the country. It promotes actions aimed at achieving greater comprehensiveness and effectiveness in the prevention and elimination of manifestations of discrimination against women, as well as strengthening the mechanisms and professional capacity of public officials to incorporate gender issues in the elimination of inequalities.
Results: The Commission for Attention to Youth, Children and Equal Rights of Women, of the legislature of the National Assembly of People's Power, systematically analyzes the implementation of the Presidential Decree 198/2021 Program, with the participation of the Vice Prime Minister, the Secretary general of the Federation of Cuban Women and the Minister of Education, along with other Cuban authorities. The progress of the State in carrying out legislative work, the use of communication in favor of equality, as a fundamental tool is highlighted. The Program highlights the prevention and confrontation of violence. The need for men and women to work together for these purposes is highlighted, with a multisectoral perspective and with greater sensitivity in all organizations, since it cuts across the labor and social spheres, which is why it is considered a priority for the population. The participation of women in the cultural and creative sectors is increasing, for example: statistical data show the degree of superiority of the number of women who occupy management positions in museum institutions compared to men. Networks and platforms have been created in work environments and in other cases promoted by CSOs that work on issues of gender equality, women's empowerment, discrimination, and violence against women. From the cultural and creative sectors, scholarships, awards, contests, and participation programs have been promoted to which women have equal opportunities; many of them stand out in audiovisual production, photography, literature, and music. Progress of women is shown in the equal rights, opportunities and possibilities endorsed in the Constitution of the Republic.
Recommandations: The systematic analysis must continue from parliament to compliance with the Program and society must have greater accessibility to information about it through the media. We must delve deeper into the obstacles that affect the economic, political, social and family spheres. Strategies must continue to be established to achieve articulations that contribute to the economic empowerment of women and their representation in the media, in legislation and in the law around equity. Incentives should continue to be created aimed at women creators, artists, entrepreneurs and managers of projects and experiences from the cultural and creative sectors. New museological and museographic projects must take into account this indicator whose representation must offer greater opportunities for creation, dissemination and participation in museum spaces whose interpretation resources must be multisensory from individual and collective enjoyment.
