Title EN: Approval of the Regional Culture Plan 2022-2030 Junín, and the Provincial Culture Plans of Huancayo, Jauja and Tarma to 2030
Goal: Integrate Culture In Sustainable Development Frameworks
SDG: SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: National sustainable development policies and plans
Cultural Domain: Design,Performing Arts,Media Arts,Cinema and Audiovisual Arts,Music,Publishing,Visual Arts
Agency Implementation: Decentralized Directorate of Culture Junín; Provincial Municipality of Huancayo; Provincial Municipality of Tarma; Provincial Municipality of Jauja; Junín Regional Government
Main Feature: On December 7, 2022, through Regional Ordinance No. 361-GRJ/CR, the Regional Government of Junín approved the Regional Culture Plan for 2022-2030, becoming the first regional public policy at the national level on culture. The Regional Culture Plan is a territorial management instrument whose purpose is to guide the public action of the regional government in matters of culture. Likewise, its design responds to the need to address culture as a development factor due to the growing demand of indigenous peoples to meet their particular needs; cultural agents and art workers whose economic income depends on the value chain of cultural and creative industries and the vulnerable situation of the cultural heritage of the department. This situation warrants the implementation of regional policies that contribute to closing gaps in the exercise of cultural rights. The aforementioned Plan has strategic objectives, including stimulating the economic development of the value chain of cultural industries (artists), benefiting cultural agents. In addition, strengthen institutional capacities and programmatic and regulatory frameworks to reduce discrimination rates. Finally, develop mechanisms that help strengthen the existing cultural diversity in the Junín region. In the same line as the Regional Government, the provincial municipalities of Huancayo, Jauja and Tarma, approved their Provincial Cultural Plan for 2030, through Ordinance No. 663-2021 MPH, Ordinance No. 010-2022 MPJ and Ordinance No. 043-2022 MPT, respectively. For the preparation of each of the culture plans, there was technical assistance from the Decentralized Directorate of Culture of Junín, complying with guideline 6.4 of the National Culture Policy: “Implement sectoral, intersectoral and intergovernmental articulation mechanisms, to the development of cultural policies throughout the national territory”.
Results: Three provincial culture plans approved in the Junín region. The implementation of policies, programs and activities that promote the development of the value chain of cultural industries, the recognition and value of cultural diversity, the enhancement of cultural heritage and the strengthening of a governance system.
Recommandations: Culture has been identified as an axis of development, an economically active sector that lives off culture and that strengthens the identity processes of the residents of the Junín region has also been made visible, allowing them to exercise their cultural rights. Recommendations: Support from the central and regional government the processes of developing management instruments that allow culture to be installed as an axis of development.

Title EN: Appui au développement culturel
Goal: Integrate Culture In Sustainable Development Frameworks
SDG: SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: National sustainable development policies and plans
Agency Implementation: fondation H
Main Feature: La Fondation H, créée à Antananarivo en 2017 à l’initiative de l’entrepreneur et mécène Hassanein Hiridjee, est reconnue d’utilité publique depuis 2018. La Fondation H opère des programmes dédiés à l’accompagnement des artistes d’Afrique et de ses diasporas dans leur carrière, facilite l’accès des publics à l’art. La Fondation H travaille ainsi à faciliter la participation à la vie culturelle et l’accès à des expressions et des équipements culturels, notamment en répondant aux besoins des groupes défavorisés ou vulnérables. Elle a ainsi mis en place un ensemble de programme demédiation à destination de tous types de publics notamment les plus vulnérables et éloignés des espaces culturels.  L’accès à toutes les offres culturelles de la fondation H est gratuit. Chaque visiteur est accueilli au sein de nos espaces pour être accompagné, s’il le souhaite, dans sa visite de l’exposition. Nous proposons par ailleurs des visites adaptées aux différents types de publics répondant à leurs besoins et spécificités : handicap physique, mental, éloignement géographique, condition financières et sociales précaire... Le format de la visite est adapté en fonction du public et du temps dont il dispose. Le programme Hay, dédié au jeune public (2-20 ans), propose des visites et des ateliers sur-mesure et par groupe d’âge, en lien avec les expositions présentées au sein des deux espaces à Antananarivo et à Paris. Hay est un mot malgache qui signifie appris ou acquis. C’est dans cette optique de découverte et d’apprentissage que le programme est mis en place. Chaque matinée ouvrée, tout au long de l’année, la Fondation H accueille des groupes d’enfants via des partenariats de long terme noués avec différentes structures (écoles primaires et secondaires, ONG, associations d’aide à l’enfance). La Fondation H propose l’organisation d’un minimum de trois visites sur l’année pour chaque groupe d’enfants. Les jeunes sont ainsi en mesure de vivre cette expérience plusieurs fois, au fil des différentes expositions de la Fondation H et de découvrir divers ateliers et activités. La Fondation H prend en charge l’intégralité des coûts associés à ces visites (transport, goûters, ateliers, etc.). Chaque mercredi après-midi, tout au long de l’année, des ateliers Hay, toujours gratuits, sont par ailleurs proposés au grand public. Nous organisons tous les samedis un événement à destination d’un public spécifique afin de permettre à toutes et tous d’avoir accès à l’art contemporain et à la culture.
Results: Le programme de médiation culturelle proposé par la Fondation H permet l’ouverture plus large de l’accès à la culture et aux expressions artistiques au plus grand nombre. La gratuité et l’adaptation des programmes aux différents types de public à permis à la Fondation H en 15 mois d’ouverture d’accueillir près de 150000 visiteurs dont les plus éloignés de la cultures (population vulnérables, handicapés physiques, mentaux…).

Title EN: Arab Reading Challenge
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture
SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Cultural and creative sectors
Agency Implementation: Mohammed bin Rashid Al Maktoum Global Initiatives
Main Feature: The Arab Reading Challenge is the region’s biggest knowledge initiative that aims to spark passion for knowledge and foster the habit of reading among the young generation to broaden horizons and boost critical, analytical and creative skills. The Arab Reading Challenge was launched under the umbrella of the Mohammed bin Rashid Al Maktoum Global Initiatives, a UAE-based foundation that combines wide-ranging humanitarian, social, development and empowerment entities and programmes. The reading competition kicked off its first edition in the 2015-2016 academic year when His Highness Sheikh Mohammed bin Rashid Al Maktoum, Vice President and Prime Minister of UAE and Ruler of Dubai, challenged Arab school students to read and summarize 50 books a year. Since then, the Challenge has been drawing participations from millions of Arab students residing in the region and the world who stock their shelves with a diverse range of books every year, gaining knowledge and demonstrating excellent critical thinking skills and ability to engage in constructive discussions at an early age.  The Challenge implements Sheikh Mohammed bin Rashid Al Maktoum’s vision that “reading is the first step towards a better future driven by knowledge and learning. Nations that read will lead the future. “The Arab Reading Challenge encourages students from grade one to 12 to read in the Arabic language, promoting the use of their mother tongue in their daily lives and highlighting the aesthetics of the rich language across science, literature and other areas of study. By introducing students to different cultures and customs through books, the Challenge seeks to highlight the importance of reading in building self-learning skills, promoting open dialogue and fostering the values of tolerance, coexistence and acceptance of differences. Reading builds enlightened and healthy minds capable of engaging with the world and driving positive change in their societies. One Arab Reading Champion is selected after elimination stages that start at class level, then school level, proceeding to the level of the educational district, directorate or governorate, leading up to the selection of the top 10 students from each country before filtering down the national winners. In a ceremony that takes place in Dubai in October/November, finalists compete for the grand prize that leads up to the winner announcement. Participation in 2024 edition has seen a 13.7% increase compared to last year's figures, when 24.8 million students competed in the challenge, 229,000 schools from 50 countries are taking part in this year's challenge, with 28 million students, supervised by 154,000 supervisors. “Students need to read and summarise the content of 50 books to compete in the qualifying rounds that move up from the class and then school levels up to the country level. Outstanding reading champions outstanding schools on the country level are selected based on rigorous criteria that closely evaluates all aspects of the participation. Specialised committees work closely with the Arab Reading Challenge committees to select winners at the education zone and governate levels. The top 10 reading champions and a Champion from each country are selected, and they then move to the final qualifying stage to win the Arab Reading Challenge title. The winner of the Arab Reading Champion title receives an award of AED500,000 to continue their journey of knowledge, broaden their horizons, and advance their experiences. ED 1 million is presented to the outstanding school, helping improve its capabilities to invest in further driving the practice of reading as a daily habit. Another AED300,000 award is presented to the outstanding supervisor so they can continue to inspire and mentor future generations. The reading champion selected at the community champions will be awarded AED100,000. This category is open to Arabs living abroad and non-Arabs learning the Arabic language.
Results: The constant increase in participation numbers is clear evidence the initiative has succeeded in reaching all students across the Arab world as well as Arab communities abroad. At the same time, it was noticed that in 8 years, the challenge has exceeded all expectations in terms of participation or its community impact, as it continues to instill a love of reading and knowledge among the new generation Year after year, the Arab Reading Challenge continues to attract larger numbers of students. The first edition in 2015 saw the participation of 3.6 million students from 19 countries, while the 7th edition in 2023 attracted 24.8 million students from 46 countries.
Recommandations: The Arab Reading Challenge has served to garner excitement around reading and strengthen the culture of reading Arabic literature among students. The initiative is in line with the UAE’s goals of building knowledge-based societies, promoting and protecting the Arabic Language and of removing barriers between cultures through understanding. The UAE will continue to build on the previous successes of the initiative to further encourage reading amongst children, youth, and different segments of society.

Title EN: Argentina unida se muestra en Tecnópolis
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture
SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Cultural and creative sectors
Agency Implementation: Secretary of Culture of the Nation
Main Feature: During the months of July, August and September, the Coordination Directorate of the Federal Council of Culture held weekly regional meetings with authorities and teams from the cultural agencies of the provinces in order to organize and coordinate the exhibition.   The exhibition also counted on the contribution made by each province to carry out the activities related to its participation in the exhibition. This joint work made "Argentina Unida se Muestra "an authentic federal space in Tecnópolis and one of the most relevant attractions of the park.   Planned within the framework of the celebration of the 10th anniversary of Tecnópolis, "Argentina Unida se Muestra" was carried out thanks to the joint work between the Ministry of Culture of the Nation, through the Secretariat of Cultural Development, and the Federal Council of Culture (an organization composed of the highest authorities in the area of Culture of the 23 provinces and CABA) represented through its regional entities, which also articulated with the Market of Argentine Cultural Industries (MICA).   The purpose of the exhibition was to promote cultural industries and knowledge economies applied to culture, with the idea of fostering the projection and multiplicity of federal productions, thus generating the visibility of our identity and diversity of cultures.
Results: Argentina Unida se Muestra was made up of four (4) spaces through which different activities were offered for visitors to enjoy different experiences.  During 11 consecutive weekends and 23 days of activity, nearly 200 activities were presented (including music recitals, theater and dance performances, lectures, workshops and discussions, among other experiences), receiving the visit of more than 140,000 people who participated in the various proposals.  Permanent exhibition:  It was the first federal and national exhibition, with contents defined by each of the provinces in a national park (Tecnópolis), which brought together productions in the areas of art, science, technology and innovation and was proposed as a meeting place from which to witness the work of Argentine artists and share the country's cultural diversity. The exhibition also aimed to promote cultural industries and knowledge economies applied to culture.  It was presented in the form of a dynamic tour through regions, in a large space of 900 m2, using the most varied graphic, photographic, sound, audiovisual and interactive resources. Exhibits ranged from works of art, sculptures, typical fabrics and historical garments to audiovisual and interactive content in which the public could learn, for example, about the manufacture of biodiesel, learn about the culture of water or see robots at work. The spatial design was configured, at the same time, as a didactic instrument and a transit through multiple emotional and sensory experiences.   GASTRONOMIC STREET  Gastronomy is another of the forms of our culture. There, the provinces will present their diverse gastronomic proposals generating the intersection between tradition and innovation. In individual boxes, regional producers will exhibit their most representative gastronomy through packaged products, beverages and handicrafts related to gastronomy to be sold to the public.   FEDERAL PATIO  Each weekend one of the six cultural regions of our country will be the exclusive protagonist of the artistic program of more than 100 shows. There will be an exchange between music, dance, performing and visual arts, as well as the crossing of generations in different disciplines. Thus, during  A federal program produced by the provinces and the contribution of the Mercado de Industrias Culturales de la Argentina (MICA) will be held for 14 days.   MULTIPURPOSE AUDITORIUM  Auditorium where activities generated by the National Ministry of Culture, the Federal Council of Culture and the Cultural Industries Market (MICA) will be programmed, following the same rotating schedule by regions proposed by the exhibition. An area for talks, exhibitions, discussions and shows related to the themes presented in the exhibition.  The public was invited to observe, interact and interact with numerous contents specially selected by each province to showcase the richness of  The material, cultural and human resources that inhabit them, without falling into commonplaces or stereotypes, from a contemporary perspective attentive to diversities.  Governors, provincial and national secretaries and ministers visited and participated.
Financial Ressources: Signing of the Collaboration Agreement between the Ministry of Culture and the Federal Council of Culture for an amount of 150,672 usd ($14,414,400) to carry out Argentina Unida se Muestra en Tecnópolis.

Title EN: Argentinean participation in the programmes of the Ibero-American cultural area
Goal: Integrate Culture In Sustainable Development Frameworks
SDG: SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: International cooperation for sustainable development
Agency Implementation: Secretariat of Culture
Main Feature: These Ibero-American cultural programmes are aimed at the development of specific cultural and creative industries and are part of Argentina's strategic cooperation plan with other regions of the world for the visibility and internationalization of cultural industries. These Ibero-American cooperation programmes seek to strengthen public policies focused on these industries. It is both technical and financial cooperation, designed to respond to the needs and development of each of the cultural sectors. Furthermore, the objectives of these programmes are aligned with the 2030 agenda.   It should be noted that Argentina has been one of the main promoters of Ibero-American cooperation in the region and actively participates in all these programmes with a representative in the Intergovernmental Council and also, in some cases, with the work of the Technical Unit.   Ibermúsicas Programme Ibermúsicas' mission is to contribute to the musical development of the Ibero-American region. It is a multilateral programme of Ibero-American cooperation that promotes the presence and knowledge of cultural diversity in the music arts, encouraging the formation of new audiences and expanding the labor market for professionals in the sector. It also includes Ibero-American music in its broadest sense, covering the whole range of musical genres. Iber-Rutas Programme: Strengthening routes of rights and interculturality in Ibero-American migration This programme, implemented for the first time in 2010 at the proposal of Argentina, aims to promote cultural diversity in Ibero-America through the implementation of competitions, aid funds, calls for proposals and research linked to the rights of migrants from an intercultural point of view. It should be noted that its Technical Unit has been operating since 2011 under the auspices of the Secretariat of Culture of the Argentine Nation in the National Directorate of Federal Integration and International Cooperation. Ibercocinas Programme - Tradition and Innovation  This programme was a proposal made by Argentina, Colombia, Mexico and Peru in 2015, and seeks to design and promote policies, programmes, strategies and cultural initiatives for the dissemination and popularization of gastronomic strengths, to promote spaces for education and training related to cuisine, gastronomy and the production of traditional and artisanal foods in the Ibero-American space, as well as research and preservation of traditional and popular gastronomy. It also seeks to delve into the history of food in the region, to highlight the contributions to the world of traditional cuisines, the creation of gastronomic registers and collections, patent and marketing policies, designations of origin, as well as to contribute to the design, implementation and evaluation of public policies to promote culinary culture.  Ibercultura Viva Programme  The Cultura Viva programme, created in Brazil in 2004, and the Puntos de Cultura programmes launched in Argentina (2011), Peru (2012), Costa Rica (2015) and Uruguay (2017). However, there are several governmental initiatives in Ibero-America that are committed to culture as a fundamental link to transform realities and seek to recognise and strengthen the cultural initiatives of the communities in the places where they take place. The concept of ‘living culture’ emerged with the Brazilian experience of the Pontos de Cultura, but has existed in practice for decades in thousands of communities in Ibero-American countries. Cultura viva comunitaria is, therefore, an expression created to give name, meaning and visibility to cultural dynamics that have emerged in the region. Why alive? Because it is pulsating, mutant, and diverse. Why communitarian? Because it is where it is born, where it is organized. And because the idea is to give priority to benefiting peoples, groups and communities in situations of social vulnerability and with reduced access to the means of production, recording, enjoyment and cultural dissemination.

Title EN: Art Jameel Pavilion: Tarabot - Weaving a Living Forum 2023
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture
SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Partnering with civil society
Agency Implementation: Art Jameel
Main Feature: The Art Jameel pavilion, "Tarabot: Weaving a Living Forum," is a significant cultural project that exemplifies the integration of art, sustainability, and community engagement. Here are the key features that highlight its contribution to cultural diversity and social inclusion: � Innovative Architectural Design: The pavilion, designed by Lebanese practice theOtherDada, features a fractal, domed structure that combines traditional architectural techniques with modern technology. This innovative design approach highlights the blending of cultural heritage with contemporary practices, promoting cultural diversity. � Sustainability and Re-use: A core aspect of the pavilion is its commitment to sustainability. By using recycled waste materials and integrating indigenous plants, the project emphasizes the importance of environmental responsibility. This approach aligns with the global push towards sustainable development and cultural practices that respect and preserve natural resources. � Interspecies Habitat: The pavilion is designed to create a new interspecies habitat, fostering biodiversity and ecological balance. This aspect of the project underscores the interconnectedness of human and non-human life, promoting a holistic view of cultural and environmental sustainability. � Community Engagement: Art Jameel, through this pavilion, aims to engage the local community and promote a dialogue about sustainability and reuse. The pavilion serves as a platform for discussions and activities that involve the community, enhancing social inclusion and cultural participation. � Collaboration and Interdisciplinary Approach: The project involves collaboration between architects, scientists, and conservationists. This interdisciplinary approach enriches the cultural expressions involved in the project and promotes a comprehensive understanding of sustainability and design. � Educational and Inspirational Role: By showcasing sustainable architectural practices and the re-use of materials, the pavilion serves as an educational tool and an inspiration for future projects. It encourages artists, architects, and the public to consider sustainability in their work and daily lives. � Promotion of Cultural and Environmental Awareness: The pavilion�s design and its associated activities aim to raise awareness about the importance of sustainability in cultural and urban settings. This focus on environmental consciousness enhances cultural awareness and responsibility among the public. � Integration of Traditional and Modern Elements: The use of traditional techniques alongside modern technology in the pavilion�s construction reflects a respect for cultural heritage while embracing innovation. This integration supports the preservation and evolution of cultural expressions. � Focus on Local Context: The pavilion is tailored to the specific environmental and cultural context of the Jaddaf Waterfront Sculpture Park in Dubai. This localization ensures that the project is relevant and beneficial to the local community, promoting cultural diversity and inclusion. � Symbolic Representation: The name "Tarabot," meaning "weaving together" in Arabic, symbolizes the project's aim to integrate various aspects of architecture, urbanism, ecology, and human-centered design. This symbolic representation highlights the project's cultural significance and its commitment to fostering a diverse and inclusive environment. In summary, the Art Jameel pavilion "Tarabot: Weaving a Living Forum" promotes cultural diversity and social inclusion through its innovative design, sustainable practices, and community engagement. The project exemplifies how art and architecture can contribute to a culturally diverse and environmentally sustainable future.

Main Feature: The goal of the funding programme “Art for Well-being” is to promote the accessibility of culture and the arts to socially and culturally excluded groups in society, with a view to the positive impact of the arts on people's personal well-being and health.  Main activities funded by the programme: 1. Projects ensuring accessibility of professional arts and culture to groups in society (in particular social and cultural exclusion groups) who, for objective reasons (e.g. health), have limited or no access to culture. 2. Projects ensuring cooperation with all categories of health and social services and making professional arts and culture accessible to users and providers of these services. 3. Creative projects that address the problems of social and cultural exclusion for the well-being or health of the individual.  In this way the programme seeks to address social problems, i.e. ageing population, social exclusion etc. and achieve a positive impact of art on human health and well-being.  Prior funding pilot projects, since 2022 the programme shifted to financing long-term (3-year) projects focusing on the accessibility of art in healthcare facilities.

Over the past years, our NGO has undertaken various initiatives to promote and showcase the  diversity of cultural expressions. We actively organise art sessions, seminars, meetings, leadership courses and capacity-building  events for artists and individuals seeking to pursue art professionally or as a source of support in  both good and challenging times. Our initiatives include organizing art competitions and art camps for children and artists. We  aim to promote creativity and cultural expressions as essential elements for the sustainability of  mankind. To achieve this, we collaborate with other NGOs and community centers. Our upcoming intervention at an  international conference in South Korea in September 2024 will explore the theme âArt &  Human Rights: Another Nexus,â celebrating Womenâs Rights Announcement Day (September  1) and Gender Equality Week. In October 2025, we will host a symposium in Mauritius. 150 artists from around the world will  participate in a residency with the theme "Cultural Horizons: The Future of Art, Culture, and  Heritage."We organise meetings, retreats, exhibitions, and discussions, and we share stories and  experiences, thus preserving traditions for future generations. We have established student social clubs in schools to offer young people the chance to engage  in social and cultural activities that meet the needs of our local communities, foster critical  thinking, and develop problem-solving skills. Additionally, these clubs aim to encourage  exploring new perspectives, as well as embracing innovation and progress. Our efforts address the needs of vulnerable groups and facilitate the inclusion and participation  of women in cultural life, ensuring they have access to diverse cultural facilities and  expressions. Our NGO also conducts art and music therapy and self-leadership sessions in  womenâs prisons and uses art as a therapeutic tool that promotes emotional resilience and wellbeing. Through our work, we aim to empower individuals on a journey of leadership and self discovery, harnessing the healing power of art and culture.
Results: Carpe Diem Art Therapy NGO is committed to promoting a deep appreciation for art and culture and creating opportunities for individuals and communities to engage with these essential elements. Our dedicated  efforts aim to support artists and individuals expressing themselves in the art world across diverse cultures, while also addressing the needs of vulnerable groups. We are focused on facilitating the inclusion and participation of inmates, women, and senior citizens in cultural life, and we have seen significant positive outcomes. Our initiatives have made a meaningful impact on the lives of individuals and communities, particularly in the  following areas: • Our self-leadership sessions have empowered women to take charge of their lives, build  self-confidence, and develop leadership skills. Many participants have expressed a renewed sense of purpose and direction, enabling them to envision and pursue positive futures. • Art and music therapy sessions have provided a therapeutic outlet for women in prisons, helping them to cope with stress, trauma, and emotional challenges. Main Feature: During the last four years, Ceibal, a public center for educational innovation with digital technologies, continued to develop its Artistas en el aula program, aimed at primary and secondary education groups whose objective is to bring different artistic expressions closer to students through direct contact with artists and their works. Starting in 2020, the program was adapted to a 100% online format, within the framework of the COVID-19 pandemic. Each instance of this proposal is developed with an artist who proposes a work process using Ceibal's CREA platform - which serves as a virtual classroom - to bring participants closer to the creative process. Title EN: ARTISTIC TRAINING AND DISSEMINATION PROCESS IN THE SANTA CLARA NEIGHBORHOOD OF THE RURAL PARISH OF IZAMBA
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture
SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Cultural and creative sectors
Agency Implementation: JULIA SUSANA MAYORGA MOREJÓN juliateatro1971@gmail.com  teléfono 593 998959947  MARÍA SOL BARRAGÁN MAYORGA sisainti@hotmail.com  teléfono  593 992625296
Main Feature: This process is developed in the Santa Clara neighborhood in the rural parish of Izamba in the city of Ambato and consists of running permanent arts workshops for children from the neighborhood and surrounding areas in the areas of theater, cooking, creative literacy and music (batukada). Each workshop has a minimum of 10 and a maximum of 20 participants, children and adolescents between 5 and 18 years of age.  Each workshop has a duration of 10 months divided into five levels of two months each, with a frequency of five hours of class per week. The teachers who share the workshops are inhabitants of the sector or people directly related to the neighborhood, artists and professionals. The instructors prepare the pedagogical and didactic guide for each area, which allows planning the knowledge according to the group and assessing progress through bimonthly evaluations of each group. The evaluations are indicators that allow monitoring the progress of the planning and at no time determine the permanence or not of the workshop participants; they are not qualification instruments but rather a measurement of the results proposed for each level. Five evaluations are carried out during the annual process.  Every two months, once the activities planned for each level have been completed, there is a public display of what has been learned, in a popular festival held in the Santa Clara neighborhood park with the participation of the workshop groups and invited theater, music, cooking and creative reading and writing groups, who share experiences with each group in training. The park is a space for community gathering and to be considered and used as a space for the arts.  The public showcase is held on a Sunday afternoon every two months and the invited artistic casts do workshops in the morning for the members of the project's workshops.  These activities in the neighborhood have been taking place since 2018 at the Arriba el Telón Cultural Center located in Santa Clara, this whole process of artistic training and dissemination is executed freely in the space of the neighborhood's recreational park. Santa Clara is a rural neighborhood with the particular characteristic that for 25 years it was a market and is currently rebuilding its community social fabric in the space transformed into a recreational park, which again motivates the joint work and neighborhood relationship around the care of this space.  The neighborhood is a reference of Ambato's gastronomy, here are located the famous hueca de las habas chumadoras that summons a large number of diners on weekends, but it is also characterized as a dangerous neighborhood in the conflictive map of the city of Ambato. A large number of children come to the park to play and use its services. Through this process we seek to strengthen neighborhood organization and participation, the cultural use of public space and the artistic development of children between 5 and 18 years of age, school children, who live in the sector and surrounding areas. Since 2018 the community has found in these artistic training workshops safe spaces for their sons and daughters to develop talents and skills through art, it has also brought artistic expressions closer to territory, managing to democratize cultural dissemination by reaching the sector where people live, activities that otherwise could not be enjoyed by the neighbors of the neighborhood. Several theater, dance, music and reading mediation groups have met in the sector to disseminate their production and the population, especially children, has approached the exercise of art.  This project is developed by the Cultural and Pedagogical Foundation Arriba el Telón, by the Semillero Lector project and by the neighborhood's Legal Committee. The community is involved in the project by participating in the workshops with the assistance of their children, providing the necessary elements to carry out the respective activities of each workshop, supporting the organization of public exhibitions, and taking care of the public space used in each cultural activity.  The project has been developed continuously, with a short interruption period in 2020 due to the health situation.  During the time that this process of training and dissemination in the arts has been developed, it has been executed with contributions from parents, with voluntary payments to attend the performances, with barter, with the collaboration of artists and casts that have presented themselves voluntarily and with the participation of young cultural managers of the sector. Santa Clara is a neighborhood with a mestizo campesino ethnic majority. Currently Santa Clara is a more organized space, from 2018 to 2020 the project worked with the difficulty of the physical presence of the market that complicated the circulation and the public space was disordered.   From mid-2021 to July 2022, the recreational park was built and the space was not usable. At present there is the possibility of taking advantage of the renovated space for the implementation of socio-cultural activities so that everything that was done in an independent space is transformed into a community process that develops activities in the park.  This process is projected as a great cultural center with a training offer that increases the number of artistic areas to 10, that manages to build classrooms for all areas and that the artistic diffusion is sustained and self-sustainable with different cultural options.  We hope that the artistic movement generated will function as a pole of economic development for the people of the sector who no longer have the market to trade, generating a large artistic and artisan market in the diffusion space. We aspire to form audiences for the performing arts, music, reading and writing, to have a permanent batukada that represents the community in different events that can generate economic resources, that the cooking workshops also generate income for each member and that the children are able to create literary and scenic works that can be marketed and are also an option for economic production to sustain the family and community space.
Results: 60 children and adolescents between 5 and 18 years of age trained in the arts in permanent art workshops in the Santa Clara neighborhood, a batukada group. A mobile library in permanent work of reading mediation. A community formed around artistic activities.

Title EN: Artistic Residency Program for Artists from Ukraine
Goal: Achieve A Balanced Flow Of Cultural Goods And Services And Increase The Mobility Of Artists And Cultural Professionals
SDG: SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 10 - Reduce inequality within and among countries,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Mobility of artists and cultural professionals
Agency Implementation: The Zbigniew Raszewski Theatre Institute
Main Feature: The Artistic Residency Program for artists from Ukraine was initiated less than 10 days after Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine.  Its primary goal was to ensure the safety of people in the Ukrainian theater, support at the level of humanitarian aid, but also - which is extremely important for psychological well-being - the opportunity to continue professional work. The aim of the program was to enable residents to work creatively by implementing a specific project or looking for new inspirations under the artistic supervision of Polish theaters and other cultural institutions, as well as to create conditions for establishing permanent cooperation between Polish cultural organizations/institutions (and their teams) and representatives theater competitions from Ukraine
Results: Since March 2022 until now (the program is ongoing), 187 artists from Ukraine have participated in residencies.  More than 100 Polish cultural institutions spread over 12 cities expressed their willingness to accept Ukrainian residents into their teams. In 2022-2023, thanks to the Program, performative projects of high artistic value were carried out by creators of independent Ukrainian culture in several dozen Polish theaters and cultural institutions from the non-governmental sector.  Several of them participated in international festivals and shows.  Thanks to an intensive language course and substantive, legal and psychological support provided by the Theater Institute, the residents of the Program have the opportunity to stay in Poland and work related to their profession
Recommandations: The evaluation showed great potential for intercultural rapprochement resulting from the Program. The opportunity for cooperation and exchange of experiences between Polish and Ukrainian theatre people was appreciated.  The recommendations focused on developing the training component, so that residents could achieve independence faster in the previously unknown formal and cultural realities of Poland/European Union.

Title EN: Arts education digital repository. “Obra gruesa” – Art, education and culture.
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture
SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Digital environment
Cultural Domain: Design,Performing Arts,Media Arts,Cinema and Audiovisual Arts,Music,Publishing,Visual Arts
Agency Implementation: Ministry of Cultures, Arts and Heritage.
Main Feature: “Obra Gruesa. Art, education and culture", is a digital repository of the Ministry of Cultures, Arts and Heritage of Chile, developed by the Department of Education and Training in Arts and Culture with the support of UNESCO, that holds public information and documents (archives, publications and audiovisual media), as well as academic and theoretical material developed and shared by public and private institutions, and by members of civil society related to the arts education field.  Its purpose is to provide for the citizens in general and academic and student world in particular, free and transparent access to primary-source information, which nourish research processes and generating useful knowledge from programmes and public policies on this matter, as well as accessing the knowledge obtained through specialised research studies and publications, among others.  This repository holds publications, reference texts, magazines, audiovisual content, academic articles, among many archives related to mediation and arts education. Access is open and free for the general public. Following the monitoring framework of the 2005 Convention, this measure is placed in the "digital environment" area of monitoring, responding to the "measures and policies that facilitate access to diverse cultural expressions in the digital environment" indicator.
Results: In "Obra Gruesa" there are currently 1,307 indexed items whose formats are diverse, including JPG, PDF, DOCX, among others. In the other communities section, there are 116 entries with web links. Additionally, there are 800 items under the "Centros de Creación" Fund, which is part of the website redesign. This number is for reference only, as new items are periodically added.  Regarding users and stakeholders, this platform is designed for audiences, whose interest would be public information and documentation in Arts education, coming out of the MINCAP Department of Education and Training in Arts and Culture, as well as academic and theoretical material developed and shared by public and private institutions and by persons from civil society related to the area of Arts Education.  Therefore its potential users are: academics, researchers, undergraduate and graduate students, allied academic institutions, other institutions related to arts education, artists, collaborators and arts collectives, interdisciplinary groups and the general public.
Recommandations: For the future of the measure, updating and improving the "Obra Gruesa" platform is sought, which is based on the Law on Digital Transformation of the Administration, Law nÂº 21.180. The platform has been entirely reorganised so that in the future it functions as a thematic digital Documentation Centre, that enables the storing of programmes, archives, documentary collections, bibliographic collections, different types of publications, articles, among others, in different formats, utilising online digital technologies.   In this manner, the programmes, funds and all the areas that will be part of the new structure of "Obra Gruesa" digital Documentation Centre will allow taking on the organisation of all the current sections and new ones, classifying each associated document.

Title EN: MECANISME DE FINANCEMENT MIS EN PLACE PAR LE MINISTERE EN CHARGE DE LA CULTURE ET LE MINISTERE EN CHARGE DE LA JEUNESSE  EN COLLABORATION AVEC L'AGENCE EMPLOI JEUNE : Initiative Fin Culture
Goal: Integrate Culture In Sustainable Development Frameworks
SDG: SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: National sustainable development policies and plans
Cultural Domain: Design,Performing Arts,Media Arts,Cinema and Audiovisual Arts,Music,Publishing,Visual Arts
Agency Implementation: Ministère  de la Culture et de la Francophonie/Direction du Partenariat et des Relations Extérieures
Main Feature: Selon les derniers chiffres de l’Organisation Internationale du Travail, le taux de chômage en Côte d’Ivoire est le plus élevé au sein de la tranche âgée de 35 ans et moins, qui représente 77% de la population nationale. Les défis de l’insertion professionnelle de cette jeunesse reposent avant tout sur la facilitation de l’accès au financement pour le soutien de leurs projets entrepreneuriaux, mais également, la formation et l’encadrement professionnel. Or la culture et l’insertion professionnelle des jeunes sont les piliers de la stratégie de croissance inclusive de la Côte d’Ivoire, inscrits dans les ambitions du Plan National de Développement.  Afin d’adresser ces défis, Birimian et Orange Bank Africa ont souhaité étendre leur partenariat noué en septembre 2022, à la création du Guichet Fin Culture. Doté d’une enveloppe de 1 milliard de francs CFA (1,5 millions d’Euros) abondé par l’Agence Emploi Jeunes, émanation du ministère de la promotion de la jeunesse et de l’emploi des jeunes, le Guichet Fin Culture a pour but de financer 100 projets par le biais de prêts bancaires d’un montant compris entre 1 et 20 millions de Francs CFA.  Le guichet unique « Initiative Fin Culture » est un programme qui est exécuté par l’Agence Emploi Jeunes (AEJ) et le Ministère de la Culture et de la Francophonie (MCF) en lien avec le Partenaire financier Birimian. De façon générale, il vise à soutenir les acteurs du secteur culturel par le financement de leurs projets à hauteur de 1 000 000 à  20.000.000 FCFA.  En effet, ce guichet a pour cibles, les entreprises du secteur de la culture (mode et design, arts du spectacle, arts plastiques et visuels, livre, cinéma/audiovisuel) dirigées par un jeune ou collectif de jeunes caractérisés par les critères suivants : -Être de nationalité ivoirienne ; -Être âgé(e) de 18 à 55 ans au 31 décembre de l’année de dépôt du dossier (pour les entreprises dirigées par un collectif de jeunes, le demandeur principal est tenu de respecter le critère d’âge) ;  -Résider en Côte d’ivoire ; -Avoir une activité ou un projet de développement d’activité correspondant à un besoin réel ; -Avoir un besoin de financement n’excédant pas les fourchettes indiquées ; -Justifier d’une qualification et/ou expérience pertinente dans le secteur d’activité indiqué ; -Présenter un dossier complet (Voir Etape 1 : Soumission des plans d’affaires).  En ce qui concerne le processus de soumission, les jeunes/entreprises devront obligatoirement disposer d’un numéro AEJ donc s’inscrire sur la plateforme de l’Agence (www.agenceemploijeunes.ci). A l’issue de cette identification, le promoteur pourra se présenter sur la plateforme dédiée aux guichets de financement (https://projets.agenceemploijeunes.ci/ ) afin d’y soumettre son plan d’affaires ainsi qu’un ensemble de pièces jointes permettant de faciliter la prise en charge de sa demande. Il s’agit notamment, de la copie de sa pièce d’identité (CNI, Attestation d’Identité ou Passeport) ; le registre de commerce de l’entreprise (pour les projets en développement) et sa Déclaration Fiscale d’Existence (DFE)pour les projets en développement. Le promoteur pourra également bénéficier de l’appui et des orientations du Ministère de la Culture et de la Francophonie impliqués dans la présente initiative. En effet, la Direction du Partenariat et des Relations Extérieures qui est le point focal du Ministère de la Culture et de la Francophonie à la possibilité de visualiser les dossiers soumis et en cours de traitement par les équipes de l’Agence Emploi Jeunes afin de faciliter le suivi. Notons que le programme couvre l’ensemble du territoire.
Results: Le projet a démarré le samedi 20 avril 2024. En effet, 100 projets sont attendus pour financement d'ici la fin de l'année.

The actions set out in the Audiovisual Action plan are being delivered across Government by relevant Departments and their agencies. The initiative aims to deliver improvements for the audiovisual sector across the following eight policy areas: 1.	Oversight 2.	Section 481 Film Tax Relief 3.	Strategic Review of Feature Film Funding 4.	Funding 5.	Skills Development 6.	Regulatory Reform 7.	Marketing 8.	Other supports and reforms Since its launch in 2018, there has been widespread cooperation across Government on the plan.
Results: The Second Progress Report on the Implementation of Audiovisual Action Plan was published in August 2021.  The AV Action Plan was launched in June 2018 and delivers on the commitment in Pillar 4 of the Creative Ireland Programme to deliver an industry-wide plan to make Ireland a leader in the audiovisual sector with the actions set out in the plan being delivered across Government by relevant Departments and their agencies.   Many of the recommendations within the Audiovisual Action Plan have been achieved and the Audiovisual Steering Group will meet later his year (2024) to decide on the next steps required. Second Progress Report on the Implementation of the Audiovisual Action Plan: https://www.gov.ie/en/publication/de571-implementation-of-the-audiovisual-action-plan-second-progress-report/

Title EN: Bajo Cauca Film Festival
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture
SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development

Main Feature: The Bajo Cauca Film Festival was created with the intention of generating a space to talk about what cannot be talked about, a space so that filmmakers from Bajo Cauca can make their cinematographic and performing arts works visible.          The Bajo Cauca is an area that has historically been affected by the armed conflict, so this space lends itself to telling stories through the arts as historical memory of a territory that has been plagued by violence due to the existence of mines of gold that attract the presence of legal and illegal armed groups.
Results: This space has 10 editions (counting the one that will be held in 2024) and has been a place where year after year between 45 and 60 regional cinema short films produced in the six municipalities of Bajo Cauca have been received. It is a great achievement that there are new filmmakers in the region and that there are more people telling their story.          Additionally, through the audiovisual production workshops taught at the festival, several participants have been encouraged to study cinema or social or audiovisual communication in cities such as Medellín and Bogotá.

Cette structure devait lui permettre de s’inscrire dans le mouvement et l’effort à déployer afin d’organiser ou soutenir toute initiative audiovisuelle et culturelle concernant la Centrafrique et la Diaspora Centrafricaine, afin de contribuer à : l’éducation, la sensibilisation, l’information de la population ; et, promouvoir, la culture de la paix, la démocratie, le civisme, les droits de l’homme, la protection de l’environnement, le développement économique, social et culturel, ou bien encore, le panafricanisme en tant que concept d’intégration du Continent africain. C’est ainsi qu’en 2020, grâce à son association, Sylviane GBOULOU va mettre en place le festival Bangui Fait Son Cinéma (BFSC), festival international de films africains et Afro-descendants de Bangui.
Results: Le festival est à sa troisième édition consécutive.  La quatrième édition est en préparation. Le festival est ouvert aux cinéastes de tous  les nationalités et âges. On y projette des films de fiction de courts et  de longs métrages, de Centrafrique et d’ailleurs.

Title EN: Formation et Renforcement des capacités des acteurs aux arts du cirque / YIRIWA
Goal: Integrate Culture In Sustainable Development Frameworks
SDG: SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: International cooperation for sustainable development
Agency Implementation: Centre Culturel Franco-Guinéen (CCFG)
Main Feature: YIRIWA, qui signifie « croissance, expansion », est le nom donné en langue sousou à la composante 1 de la Création Africa Guinée. Ce projet est un incubateur pour les compagnies de cirque guinéennes. Il est financé par le Ministère de l’Europe et des Affaires étrangères pour une période de 1 an, de septembre 2023 à septembre 2024. Le Centre Culturel Franco-Guinéen (CCFG) est l’opérateur du projet YIRIWA, en coordination avec Circus Baobab et R en Cirque. Il vise à favoriser l’insertion des acteurs/ créateurs dans des filières économiques. En Guinée le Cirque a un fort impact dans l’évolution sociale de ses acteurs. Souvent issus des couches les plus défavorisées de la population, les acrobates peuvent voir leurs conditions de vie exceptionnellement améliorées grâce aux tournées internationales. Ce programme vise à outiller les compagnies (artistes, administrateurs et techniciens) pour permettre le développement de leurs projets tant en Guinée qu’à l’International dans la filière du spectacle vivant. YIRIWA appuie des formations, de la dotation de matériel, l’accès à des services de scénographie et création de décors dans le cadre de l’appui à l’entreprenariat culturel. Le programme YIRIWA a été pensé pour les compagnies de cirque guinéennes, en préfiguration de l'École Nationale du Cirque, porté par la compagnie Circus Baobab, dont le projet architectural est soutenu par l’AFD avec le Ministère de la Culture du Tourisme et de l’Artisanat et le Ministère de l’Enseignement technique de Guinée   Ces formations  portaient sur : -	technique de cirque main à main ; -	techniques d’éclairages lumière pour les spectacles ; -	technique de la bascule coréenne ; -	techniques du fouet et du mât chinois ; -	mise en piste ; -	dramaturgies ;  -	maquillage de spectacle ; -	création de costumes de cirque ; -	techniques aériennes ; -	 « De l’idée d’un projet à sa 1ère représentation » ; -	Santé et sécurité ; -	droits des artistes ; -	pédagogie de l’initiation aux enfants ;  -	jonglage ; -	danse contemporaine et acrobatie ; -	plan stratégique de développement local et international ; -	techniques acrobatiques.
Results: -	21 acrobates des 6 compagnies de cirque de Conakry ont été formés en technique de cirque main à main, dirigée par Céline Sommer, du 10 au 17 octobre 2023. Chaque bénéficiaire a reçu un certificat de participation à l’issue de la formation ; -	Les capacités de deux régisseurs du CCFG, du Palais du Peuple et 6 techniciens des compagnies de cirque ont été renforcées en techniques d’éclairages lumière pour les spectacles, du 6 au 15 décembre 2023. La formation a été donnée par Jean-Marie Prouvèze, éclairagiste ; -	52 acteurs du cirque ont été formés en technique de la bascule coréenne par Yann Ecauvre, du 22 au 31 janvier 2024 ; -	29 acteurs du cirque ont été formés en techniques de fouet et du mât chinois par Julie Delaire, du 22 janvier au 2 février 2024 ;  -	30 acteurs du cirque ont été formés en mise en piste par Yann Ecauvre, du 1er au 12 février 2024 ; -	22 acrobates ont été outillés en dramaturgies par Bilia Bah, du 12 au 26 février 2024 ; -	15 femmes des compagnies de cirque ont été formées en maquillage de spectacle par Rayhanna Diallo,  du 11 au 22 mars 2024 ;  -	5 costumiers ont été formés en création de costumes de cirque par Solène Capmas, du 2 au 13 avril 2024 ; -	6 compagnies de cirque et 5 opérateurs culturels ont bénéficié d’une formation sur la thématique « De l’idée d’un projet à sa 1ère représentation » par Camille Zunino, du 6 au 11 mai 2024 ; -	6 compagnies de cirque ont été formées en santé et sécurité (premiers gestes de secours en cas de chute, les notions essentielles d’hygiène, la préparation aux entraînements et aux spectacles) par Isabelle Sage, du 13 au 18 mai 2024 ; -	6 compagnies de cirque et 5 opérateurs culturels ont été formés en droits des artistes par Kankou Fofana, du 23 au 29 mai 2024 ; -	6 compagnies de cirque ont été formées en pédagogie de l’initiation aux enfants (l’hygiène à respecter avec un public jeune, les gestes et paroles à éviter, la gestion d’un groupe de petits et la responsabilité vis-à-vis des parents, etc.), du 1er au 3 juillet 2024 et 30 enfants d’un orphelinat, entre 6 et 15 ans, ont été invités au Studio de Circus Baobab pour leur initiation au cirque (acrobatie, jonglage, trampoline) afin de mettre en pratique les notions acquises, le 13 juillet 2024  ; -	6 compagnies de cirque ont été formées en technique de jonglage par Olivier Conrard, du 4 au 20 juillet 2024 …
Financial Ressources: 187 133 euros soit 197 620 USD
Recommandations: A l’issue du renforcement des capacités des acteurs du cirque, il a été demandé à chaque groupe participant de monter un spectacle de cirque portant sur le thème rapatriement des biens culturels guinéens spoliés. Après trois (3) semaines de création, les résultats ont été présentés dans les différentes communes de Conakry.
