Title EN: Beauty in Unity Exhibition
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture
SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Cultural and creative sectors
Agency Implementation: Dubai International Art Center
Main Feature: The "Beauty in Unity" exhibition at Gallery 76, Dubai International Art Centre (DIAC), showcased nearly 500 pieces from over 45 artists. The event, celebrating artistic diversity and unity, featured a vibrant array of artworks from various nationalities, fostering a collaborative spirit. The policy aims to promote cultural diversity and artistic collaboration. It provides a platform for artists to showcase their work and engage with the community, emphasizing the importance of unity in art. The exhibition highlights diverse artistic expressions and fosters cultural exchange and dialogue.
Results: The exhibition successfully brought together a diverse group of artists, enhancing cultural understanding and appreciation. It provided a platform for emerging and established artists to display their work, contributing to the cultural vibrancy of Dubai. The event also facilitated the sale of numerous artworks, reflecting the resonance of the theme and the skillful execution by the artists.
Recommandations: Celebration of Diversity: The exhibition successfully highlighted the richness of cultural diversity, showcasing various forms of art that reflect different traditions and perspectives. Artistic Collaboration: The show emphasized the importance of collaboration among artists from different backgrounds, fostering a sense of unity and mutual understanding through their shared love for art. Cultural Awareness: By featuring artists from multiple cultures, the exhibition promoted cultural awareness and appreciation, encouraging viewers to explore and understand different cultural narratives. Aesthetic Harmony: The curation of the artworks demonstrated a harmonious blend of styles, techniques, and mediums, creating a visually cohesive and engaging experience for the audience. Recommendations for Future Shows Expand Artist Participation: Increase the number of participating artists to include a wider range of cultural backgrounds and artistic styles, further enriching the exhibition’s diversity. Interactive Elements: Incorporate interactive elements or workshops that allow visitors to engage more deeply with the art and the artists, fostering a more immersive and educational experience. Community Engagement: Strengthen community engagement by involving local schools, universities, and cultural organizations in the planning and execution of the exhibition, enhancing its reach and impact. Marketing and Promotion: Enhance marketing efforts through social media campaigns, collaborations with influencers, and media partnerships to increase visibility and attract a larger, more diverse audience.

Title EN: Beyond Emerging Artists 2024
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture
SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Cultural and creative sectors
Agency Implementation: Abu Dhabi Art Fair
Main Feature: The annual initiative provides three emerging artists in the UAE with a platform to develop their practice and realize ambitious art projects. The selected artists participate in a year-long program curated by a guest curator, receiving critical feedback and support throughout the process. The program culminates in a group exhibition at the Abu Dhabi Art Fair in November, with the works remaining on public display in Abu Dhabi for several months beyond the fair dates and later exhibited internationally. Supported by Friends of Abu Dhabi Art since 2021, the initiative showcases artists from diverse backgrounds and experiences, reflecting a cosmopolitan vision of the Gulf region. The participating artists navigate a unique path between historical issues and contemporary matters, exploring the interplay between private and public spaces, as well as subjective and collective memory. Although each artist's work is distinct, they collectively investigate the new dialectics of daylight and nocturnal spaces, proposing a speculative realism in response to global challenges such as climate change. The program offers a platform for three commissioned emerging artists in the UAE, providing funding and curatorial support to create or develop new works. These commissioned pieces are first exhibited in Abu Dhabi and then showcased internationally in diverse locations each year. Since its launch in 2017, the initiative has supported emerging talent, allowing them to realize ambitious art projects under the guidance of a guest curator. Eligible artists must be long-term residents in the UAE or UAE Nationals, with a demonstrable commitment to their work and ties to the local art community.
Results: Some of its key achievements include providing a platform for emerging artists to showcase their talents and express their cultural diversity in an artistic format annually, which would further allow them to develop their practice and realize ambitious art projects. Additionally, selected artists participate in a year-long program of workshops and studio visits guided by a guest curator. This leads the artists to create new projects for the same program but with different artistic capabilities. The artists also experience exposure as their artworks are first showcased in Abu Dhabi and then in diverse locations which provides them with recognition and the motivation they need to continue with their artwork. The program has fostered artistic growth and international exposure.

Title EN: Billets solidaires
Goal: Integrate Culture In Sustainable Development Frameworks
SDG: SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: National sustainable development policies and plans
Agency Implementation: Direction du Département de la culture et de la transition numérique de la Ville de Genève
Main Feature: En collaboration avec un réseau d’associations et organismes à caractère social, le Département de la culture et de la transition numérique (DCTN) de la Ville de Genève gère des invitations qui permettent chaque année à environ 2000 spectatrices et spectateurs d'assister gratuitement à des spectacles dans une vingtaine de lieux culturels (théâtre, danse, cinéma, opéra). L'intérêt et la particularité de cette mesure résident dans l'accompagnement qu'offrent ces organismes sociaux à leurs bénéficiaires. Ces organismes œuvrent dans des domaines très variés et en faveur de publics désavantagés, discriminés, rencontrant des difficultés de toutes natures.
Results: Un réseau de 50 partenaires issus du domaine social. Une moyenne de 1200 usagères et usagers par an.
Financial Ressources: 55 360 USD en moyenne
Recommandations: Plusieurs organismes sociaux relèvent que pour certaines usagères et certains usagers les horaires des représentations en soirée peuvent être problématiques et être perçus, (pour des raisons de fatigue, d’insécurité, etc.), comme un frein pour une sortie culturelle. La langue de la représentation, le type de spectacle, la communication des programmes sont considérés comme peu accessibles. Le prix du billet de transport peut également être un frein à leur sortie. Certains organismes sociaux mentionnent que leurs usagères et usagers ne sont pas assez autonomes ou ne se sentent pas légitimes pour sortir seules et seuls au spectacle et auraient besoin d’un accompagnement personnalisé. Pour rappel, les billets solidaires bleus et rouges sont transmis par le DCTN aux organismes sociaux partenaires en début de chaque année. Malheureusement il n’y a, à l’heure actuelle, aucune communication en cours d’année sur les billets qui ne seraient pas utilisés. Ainsi, en fin d’année, certains organismes ont été à court de billets solidaires alors que d’autres ont en trop reçu et les détruisent sans les avoir utilisés. Certaines associations demandent si une bourse aux billets pourrait être mise en place.

Title EN: Bilateral agreements on cooperation in culture, cultural industries, and culture and creativity
Goal: Achieve A Balanced Flow Of Cultural Goods And Services And Increase The Mobility Of Artists And Cultural Professionals
SDG: SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 10 - Reduce inequality within and among countries,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Treaties and agreements
Cultural Domain: Design,Performing Arts,Media Arts,Cinema and Audiovisual Arts,Music,Publishing,Visual Arts
Agency Implementation: The Ministry of Culture, Sports and Tourism of Viet Nam and signing partners
Main Feature: This measure mentions bilateral agreements signed between the Government of Viet Nam or the Viet Nam’s Ministry of Culture, Sports and Tourism with foreign governments and relevant ministries and agencies in culture and cultural industries with the goal of promoting the exchange and cooperation in culture and cultural industry, strengthening relations between Viet Nam and other countries, promoting the country's image; at the same time, contributing to the development of culture, creativity, and cultural trade of each side. Some main contents of those bilateral agreements are as follows: (i) Encouraging the parties to exchange and cooperate in organizing and sending representatives to participate in cultural events, performing arts, exhibitions, photography, cinema, fashion, cuisine, etc. which are held at each country;  (ii) Enhancing the exchange of artists, experts, and high-quality human resources in the cultural and creative fields; organizing seminars, conferences on information sharing policies and experiences in cultural development, creativity, copyright protection and related rights; cooperating in human resource training, etc.  (iii) Encouraging and facilitating the development of trade in cultural goods and services in each country's cultural industries, etc.  (iv) Increasing support and facilitate the implementation of cultural exchange and promotion activities of one country in another country on the principle of consensus and reciprocity;  (v) Implementing cooperation within the framework of treaties, agreements, and international working mechanisms related to culture and cultural industries of which the parties are members;  (vi) Actively calling for participation and cooperation between cultural enterprises of the parties. During the period 2020 - 2023, Viet Nam has signed 18 cooperation agreements at the government or ministerial level with international partners in the field of culture and cultural industry including: 1. Cultural Cooperation Program between the Ministry of Culture, Sports and Tourism of Viet Nam and the Ministry of Human Resources of Hungary for the period of 2020-2022 2. Plan for Cooperation in Culture, Arts and Tourism between the Ministry of Culture, Sports and Tourism of Viet Nam and the Ministry of Information, Culture and Tourism of Laos for the period of 2021-2025 3. Memorandum of Understanding on Cultural Cooperation between the Ministry of Culture, Sports and Tourism of Viet Nam and the Ministry of Culture of Thailand 4. Memorandum of Understanding on Cooperation in the field of Culture between the Ministry of Culture, Sports and Tourism of Viet Nam and the Ministry of Culture and Youth of the UAE 5. Cultural Exchange Program between the Ministry of Culture, Sports and Tourism of Viet Nam and the Ministry of Culture, Sports and Tourism of Korea on activities to celebrate the 30th anniversary of establishing diplomatic relations between Viet Nam and Korea in 2022 6. Cultural Cooperation Program between the Ministry of Culture, Sports and Tourism of Viet Nam and the Ministry of Culture of Russia for the period 2022-2024 7. Memorandum of Understanding on Cultural Cooperation between the Ministry of Culture, Sports and Tourism of Viet Nam and the Ministry of Culture of Mongolia. 8. Memorandum of Understanding on Cooperation in the field of Culture between the Ministry of Culture, Sports and Tourism of Viet Nam and the Ministry of Culture of Cuba 9. Cultural and Tourism Cooperation Plan between the Ministry of Culture, Sports and Tourism of Viet Nam and the Ministry of Culture and Tourism of China 10. Memorandum of Understanding on Cooperation between the Ministry of Culture, Sports and Tourism and the American Chamber of Commerce in Viet Nam 11. Memorandum of Cooperation between the Ministry of Culture, Sports and Tourism of Viet Nam and the Ministry of Culture, Sports and Tourism of Korea for the period 2023-2025 12. Cultural Exchange Program between the Ministry of Culture, Sports and Tourism of Viet Nam and the Ministry of Culture of India for the period 2022-2025 13. Cultural and Artistic Cooperation Plan between the Ministry of Culture, Sports and Tourism of Viet Nam and the Ministry of Culture and Arts of the Kingdom of Cambodia for the period 2023-2027 14. Cooperation Program in the field of Culture between the Ministry of Culture, Sports and Tourism of Viet Nam and the Ministry of Culture of Belarus for the period 2023-2025 15. Memorandum of Understanding on Cooperation in the field of Culture and Tourism between the Ministry of Culture, Sports and Tourism of Viet Nam and the Government of Wakayama Prefecture, Japan for the period of 2023-2025 16. Agreement on Cultural, Sports and Tourism Cooperation between the Ministry of Culture, Sports and Tourism of Viet Nam and the Kanagawa Prefectural Government for the period 2023-2025 17. Cooperation Program in the field of Culture between the Ministry of Culture, Sports and Tourism of Viet Nam and the Ministry of Culture of the Republic of Bulgaria for the period 2024-2026 18. Memorandum of Cooperation in the field of Copyright and Related Rights between the Ministry of Culture, Sports and Tourism of Viet Nam and the National Copyright Office of the People's Republic of China.
Results: 1. Every year, bilateral cooperation agreements have served as one of the important foundations for the Vietnamese Cultural Week and Cultural Day program and activities to promote and introduce Viet Nam's country, people, traditions, and culture abroad.  Vietnamese Cultural Weeks and Days abroad are elaborately organized with many diverse art forms, aimed at the general public, international friends, and oversea Vietnamese communities, such as performing arts (ethnic music, traditional, classical arts combined with contemporary arts), painting and photo exhibitions, museum displays, Vietnamese film screenings, fashion shows, Vietnamese cuisine introductions, etc. These events have successfully attracted the attention of the audience in the host countries, presenting to international friends the image of a beautiful Viet Nam with friendly people and a rich culture, while at the same time delivering a message about Viet Nam's development and international integration orientations, especially in the fields of culture and creativity. Vietnamese Cultural Weeks and Days abroad are especially meaningful when they take place in new or geographically distant areas that do not have many cultural cooperation relations with Viet Nam.  Some specific examples include:  After COVID-19, the Ministry of Culture, Sports and Tourism in collaboration with relevant domestic and foreign agencies have organized of a series of Viet Nam Cultural Weeks and Cultural Festivals abroad, in which various events have created significant impact on the international community such as Viet Nam Cultural Week in Laos and Lao Cultural Week in Viet Nam (2022) taking place at the same time to celebrate the 60th anniversary of the establishment of diplomatic relations between Viet Nam and Laos and the 45th anniversary of the signing of the Treaty of Friendship and Cooperation between the two countries; Viet Nam Cultural Week in Cambodia and Cambodian Cultural Week in Viet Nam (2022) to celebrate the 55th anniversary of the establishment of diplomatic relations between the two countries and welcome the Viet Nam-Cambodia Friendship Year 2022; Cultural and artistic program, exhibition, and introduction of Viet Nam’s martial arts in Japan on the occasion of the Viet Nam President's visit to Japan on the occasion of the 50th anniversary of establishing diplomatic relations between Viet Nam and Japan (2023); Viet Nam Cultural days in Cuba, Argentina, Uruguay on the occasion of the official visit to the three Latin American countries of Viet Nam National Assembly’s Chairman (2023); Vietnamese Cultural Day in UAE (2023), etc.  According to the signed cooperation agreements, Viet Nam’s Tourism and Cultural Festivals in Japan and South Korea have been organized annually by Viet Nam’s Ministry of Culture, Sports and Tourism with the support of South Korean and Japanese partners. The festivals taking place in many cities across South Korea and Japan have successfully attracted hundreds of thousands of visitors, promoting Viet Nam’s culture to Japanese and South Korean audiences while also making an important contribution to attracting tourists from two countries to Viet Nam.  2. Based on international bilateral cooperation agreements at the government and ministry levels, various cooperation programs have also been signed and implemented between the Ministry of Culture, Sports and Tourism or agencies under the Ministry with international partners in specific areas aiming at deep and substantive cooperation such as cooperation in preserving works of art and displaying exhibitions between museums, art training cooperation between professional art schools, cooperation to support film promotion and production between film management agencies, and cooperation to promote creative cultural products and services with foreign cultural centers, foreign business councils in Viet Nam, etc.  Some specific examples include:  Regarding cultural investment, a number of large Korean corporations have actively invested in Viet Nam's cultural sector. Kumho Asiana Group has made many contributions to Viet Nam - Korea cultural cooperation and exchange. Every year, the Kumho Asiana Viet Nam Cultural Scholarship Fund awards a variety of scholarships to students majoring in Vietnamese culture and arts. In 2023, Samsung Viet Nam Group awarded 80 scholarships to Bac Ninh University of Physical Education and Sports and Viet Bac College of Culture and Arts, as well as sponsoring the Viet Nam Tourism and Cinema Forum in Nha Trang. The CJ CGV Group has actively invested in Viet Nam's film industry, organizing the CJ Short Film program and sharing experiences on how to strengthen the cooperation between Viet Nam and South Korea in cinema.  Netflix, the world's leading company in providing online entertainment and content creation services, has successfully worked with Viet Nam’s Ministry of Culture, Sports and Tourism in a variety of activities, such as Viet Nam Film Week at EXPO 2020 Dubai, Viet Nam Film Festival, Ha Noi International Film Festival, and various programs on capacity building for the film industry and supporting vulnerable people, including the 2021 Magic Voice dubbing contest, the initiative "Cinematic Beauty Fund: Creative Economy,"  and the workshop "Viet Nam’s creative economic industries in the digital era." The movie "A tourist’s guide to love" (2023), invested by Netflix and filmed entirely in Viet Nam, has been ranked as the world’s most-watched English movie on Netflix, reaching the Top 10 movies in 89 countries across the Americas, Europe, Asia, Oceania, and Africa, and peaking No. 1 in 19 countries after just 10 days of release (April 21–30, 2023),  3. Bilateral agreements have also been the platform for cultural exchange activities between Viet Nam and the world to be successfully organized in Viet Nam. Every year, foreign diplomatic missions and international organizations in Viet Nam organize foreign cultural and artistic activities in Ha Noi, Ho Chi Minh City, and many other localities of Viet Nam. The events range from traditional and contemporary art performances to film screenings, exhibitions, book introductions, cuisine festivals, seminars, and many more. These diverse activities have attracted the interest of a large Vietnamese audience. Notably, in addition to the international factors, most of the activities have involved Vietnamese artists, art practitioners, and cultural experts. These are opportunities to interact and exchange professional experiences, expand creative inspiration, seek cooperation potential, and contribute to enriching cultural life in Viet Nam. The Vietnamese public and art professionals eagerly anticipate annual events like the European Film Festival, European Music Festival, European Documentary Film Festival, International Yoga Day, Korean Cuisine Festival, and Toyota Concert, among others.  Besides, many cultural and artistic events in Viet Nam have reached regional and international levels, such as the Ha Noi International Film Festival, the International Circus Festival, the International Dance Festival, the International Puppet Festival, etc., especially attracting the participation of famous artists and art troupes from countries that have signed the cooperation agreement with Viet Nam.
Recommandations: The implementation of Viet Nam's bilateral cooperation agreements on culture, cultural industry, and creativity with foreign partners is reviewed, reported, and evaluated annually. Currently, the Vietnamese Government has established a Working Group that meets regularly to urge, monitor, and evaluate the implementation of international cooperation agreements. Some recommendations are as follows:  - Actively expanding cultural cooperation with other countries and international institutions related to culture and cultural industry, diversifying forms of cooperation, and bringing international relations into depth and substance in order to achieve practical results.  - Proactively developing short-term and long-term plans to implement international commitments, especially bilateral cooperation commitments with specific, creative, and diverse content with the participation of artists and people, etc.; actively implementing proposed commitments; setting out measures to monitor and evaluate implementation efficiency; and promptly delivering measures and improvement plans in case implementation activities do not achieve expected results.  - Actively participating and playing an active role in international cultural forums and organizations, appointing people to work and run for leading positions at professional agencies of organizations.  - Increasing Viet Nam's presence at international cultural, sports, and tourism events; establishing favorable conditions for countries, international organizations, and foreign cultural and tourism agencies to organize cultural promotion, cooperation, and people-to-people exchange activities in Viet Nam; actively inviting international artists, experts, and art and culture workers to attend international cultural and art events held in Viet Nam and participate in cooperation activities with Vietnamese partners, etc.

Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture
SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Cultural and creative sectors
Agency Implementation: Miguel Ricardo Velasco Zabala EMAIL: miguel.velasco@vrealitybolivia.com  PHONE: 78862064
Main Feature: The Global Game Jam is a collaborative event that seeks to invite people of all ages, from 18 years old, to experiment, share and create a video game or board game in a hackathon of a few hours (usually 48 hours) without necessarily having the knowledge to do so, since one of the objectives is to learn by doing.  The event is launched simultaneously worldwide on the same day in January and with the headquarters in La Paz, Bolivia, it seeks to consolidate the small scene that currently exists in the country to create an industry that also brings together all the disciplines, specialties and professions needed to create a video game from music and sound effects, graphic design, illustration, narrative, 3D modeling, animation and the technological areas of programming and others. Since 2016, this event has been taking place year after year in Bolivia in different cultural or academic spaces, as well as online during the pandemic years. Video game development is a collaborative space that is growing very slowly in the country, while in neighboring countries it is an entire industry that has events that generate local, national and even global economic movement. For example, EVA in Argentina or Gamescom Brazil (formerly Big Festival) are large cultural movements that bring together thousands of people from their respective countries and also from all over the world around the development of these interactive, playful experiences.
Results: Among the results obtained are the formation of video game development teams, networking that allows participants to have a radar of people who have the necessary skills to be able to collaborate on the projects they may have. The academic sector has been involved through different universities to be more open to the development of video games and to see it as an important area with unique characteristics that has a lot of potential. We have managed to connect different cultural spaces, as well as municipal governments, to support fans and professionals in video game development to have spaces where they can experiment, learn about and explore this industry.

Title EN: BOLIVIA: STIMULATING INCLUSIVE GROWTH THROUGH THE CREATIVE ECONOMY
Goal: Integrate Culture In Sustainable Development Frameworks
SDG: SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: National sustainable development policies and plans
Cultural Domain: Design,Performing Arts,Media Arts,Cinema and Audiovisual Arts,Music,Publishing,Visual Arts
Agency Implementation: CERES (Center for studies of economic and social reality) EMAIL: santiagolaserna@gmail.com PHONE: (+591 – 4) 4799365
Main Feature: It is a three-year project to promote the creative economy in Bolivia, with an emphasis on Cochabamba, which seeks to meet three main objectives annually:  1. Conduct, publish and disseminate academic research on the creative economy in Bolivia. We do this in partnership with the Institute for Business Economic Progress of the Franz Tamayo University (IPEE) and we have covered diverse topics, from a status report on the creative economy in Bolivia, observing the characteristics of Bolivian workers who benefit from the creative economy in the country, to a survey of cultural consumption in the key cities of Bolivia.  2. Train creative entrepreneurs with the necessary tools so that they can improve their ventures and become stronger democratically and with a gender focus. To this end, we have designed, in conjunction with the Franz Tamayo University, the first Diploma in Orange Economy in the country, offering a special scholarship package for women. We have also developed a series of free workshops (some virtual, others in person) specifically designed for women entrepreneurs, entitled Mujeres Inspirando Mujeres.  3. Finally, we seek to have an impact on the promotion of the creative economy and the appropriate public policies to promote it, through alliances with the public and private sectors, associations and institutions. We have achieved this through talks, special events, and an annual creative economy forum held on the UNIFRANZ campus, with the presence of high-profile international guests, including Felipe Buitrago, who will come to Cochabamba in November 2024.  One of the most interesting incidents we have achieved this year is getting the former Minister of Culture of the city of Buenos Aires, Enrique Avogadro, to advise Congresswoman Samantha Nogales with his team on a proposed law on Patronage, which is currently being evaluated by the Congresswoman's team.
Results: Bolivia: Stimulating Inclusive Growth through the Creative Economy project has promoted multiple initiatives to strengthen the creative economy sector in the country, promoting public policies, academic training and the active participation of actors in the creative sector. One of its main achievements is the publication of the book Economía Creativa en Bolivia, by Santiago Laserna and other authors, available through Editorial Plural. In addition, a public policy bulletin was produced that offers proposals for the promotion of the creative economy, a product of the first year of work and the Creative Economy Forum (EMPRENDEFEST) 2023. In the educational field, the project launched the first diploma in orange economy in Bolivia, with more than 13 graduates in its first edition, while the second edition has more than 30 enrolled.  Additionally more than 8 workshops of the Women Inspiring Women program were held, with the participation of more than 60 students, promoting female leadership and empowerment in the creative sector. The project has also had an impact on the regulatory framework, offering advice for the development of a Patronage Law project and supporting the Municipal Law on Creative Economy of Cochabamba, with the inclusion of two members of the project in the ad hoc committee for its implementation.  The project proposals were also presented to the Commission for Territorial Organization of the State and Autonomies of the Plurinational Legislative Assembly and to more than 60 members of the departmental assembly of Cochabamba. In addition, more than 5 entrepreneurship courses have been taught for high school students in peri-urban areas of Cochabamba, and more than 5 discussions have been held on key topics of the creative economy in Bolivia.  The presentation of a survey of cultural consumption for the central axis of the country represents another significant effort to understand the dynamics of the sector and guide effective policies.

Title EN: BZ48H – short film contest
Goal: Achieve A Balanced Flow Of Cultural Goods And Services And Increase The Mobility Of Artists And Cultural Professionals
SDG: SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 10 - Reduce inequality within and among countries,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Mobility of artists and cultural professionals
Agency Implementation: Cooperativa 19
Main Feature: BZ48H, an acronym for Bolzano in 48 hours, is a short film competition that challenges artists and filmmakers to create a short film in 48 hours, from conception to post-production. The main objective is to tell the story of the city of Bolzano through their films, restoring its soul and atmosphere. The challenge is open to everyone: professionals, students and amateurs, both local and from other national and international cities. The short films must be written, shot and post-produced within 48 hours in Bolzano, have a maximum length of 8 minutes (excluding opening and closing credits) and respect 3 clues given by the organisation at the start of the competition.  Bolzano is transformed into an open-air stage, representing the arena in which the filmmakers' stories will be set.   The diversity of the participants' backgrounds extends the project beyond the city's borders, in order to promote the encounter between forms of expression rooted in the culture of the region and those of the national and international territory. BZ48H aims to bring together young people who want to approach the world of storytelling through images and creative people who want to experiment with new forms of expression. This is one of the reasons why the project wants to leave freedom in the choice of the genre to be represented, so as not to limit the possibilities of collaboration in the creation of one's own team. This openness has on many occasions made it possible to see crews at work made up of members from different regions (e.g. a director from Bolzano, a sound engineer from Trento, an actor from Innsbruck), groups of creatives who have met at film schools, thanks to workshop experiences, or simply through the most popular online communities today, which allow for sector networking that transcends all geographical boundaries.  Another important feature, in line with the nature of the South Tyrolean territory, is linguistic inclusiveness. The short films produced during the 48-hour competition will be able to be produced in any language, and this means giving value to different cultural traditions, points of view and identities through the stories told. This will be possible by investing in ensuring that resources and support for production (subtitling, translation, interpretation services) are available to ensure an inclusive and collaborative experience for all participants.  For young creative people, often from outside Bolzano, participation in this project is not only a professional challenge, but also an opportunity to understand and enhance the cultural and social richness of the region. The direct contact with the local community and the possibility to contribute to the creation of cinematic works that are unique in the South Tyrolean context stimulate a sense of belonging and connection with the host territory. In conclusion, the production of short films in Bolzano is not only a filmmaking experience, but also a discovery, a collaboration and an integration that unites talents.
Results: Now in its eighth edition, BZ48H has consolidated its presence with over 170 film crews and a total of around 1,500 participants. The strategy adopted in recent years has been to intensify the participation of young filmmakers from South Tyrol, on the one hand, and to facilitate the participation of young creators from all over the country and abroad, on the other. The offer "Vieni da fuori" (Come from Outside), conceived in synergy with the Bolzano Tourist Board, continues to be a valuable incentive to reach Bolzano from the most diverse cities of origin and to receive free accommodation in selected hotels.  This opportunity has won the loyalty of some film crews from Northern and Central Italy and has opened the way for the participation of filmmakers from Northern/Eastern Europe (Poland, Austria, Germany).

Area of Monitoring: Cultural and creative sectors
Cultural Domain: Design,Performing Arts,Media Arts,Cinema and Audiovisual Arts,Music,Publishing,Visual Arts
Agency Implementation: Ministry of education, science, culture and sports of the Republic of Armenia
Main Feature: The department of contemporary arts of the Ministry of education, science, culture and sports of the Republic of Armenia regularly announces annual calls for providing financial support to cultural programs and projects within the fields of contemporary arts. The call is intended for projects that contribute to the attainment of the general interest in culture, to encouraging the development of creative industries and includes a wide range of fields corresponding to all four goals of the 2005 Convention (ranging from creating conditions for contemporary arts development, ensuring availability of cultural contents, encouraging innovation and creativity, professional research in culture, to applying new technologies in the field of culture, creating conditions for the unhindered flow of information and exchange of cultural expressions, supporting international and intergovernmental cooperation, and encouraging artistic activities of socially vulnerable groups). The call is announced in the form of 8 separate lines corresponding to areas of culture:  1. Literature and Publishing – events, periodicals related to arts and culture, capital works in the field of culture, published in Armenian, as well as valuable literary works, both by national authors and in translation to Armenian. 2. Music (creative process, production, interpretation)  3. Arts, applied arts, visual arts6. Theatrical arts (creative process, production and nterpretation)  4. Artistic dance – classic ballet, folk dance, contemporary dance (creative process, production and interpretation)  5. Cinematic arts and other audio-visual creative activities  6. Cultural activities of national minorities in the Republic of Armenia 7. Cultural activities of persons with disabilities 8. Cultural activities of children, as well as for children and youth  The general goal of the call is to harmonize the cultural development of the Republic of Armenia through creating an encouraging environment for the advancement of all areas of artistic expression, as well as providing conditions for the availability of cultural contents and audience development (specially in socially vulnerable groups). The call relate also to support to women’s cultural activities and the promotion of gender equality in the area of contemporary arts. For each listed artistic field a professional commission is formed. Project proposals evaluation is based on the Regulation on the Criteria, Standards, and Selection of Projects in Culture that are financed and co-financed from the budget of the Republic of Arrmenia. The right to participate in the call is granted to institutions, artist associations as well as other associations registered for carrying out cultural activities, individuals (artists, assistants, i.e. professionals in culture), and other subjects in the field of culture and cultural institutions founded by the Republic of Armenia.
Results: From 2020 to 2023, a total of 320 project proposals were submitted within all call lines, and a total of 260 projects were approved for funding.
Financial Ressources: In the period 2020-2023 a total of around 4,250,000 USD (1,700,000,000 AMD): every year 1,062,500 USD (425,000,000 AMD)
Recommandations: Evaluations were carried out based on the reporting of the funds recipients, as well as on direct monitoring, following, and analyzing the implemented project activities. It was found that the implementation of the contemporary arts call procedurally met all legally defined criteria. The outbreak of the COVID-19 pandemic caused changes in the structure of the call: new investments were introduced through new call lines intended for online creative activities and online placement of artistic expressions and products. Additional improvements of human rights and artistic freedom were achieved through introducing new project propositions with a view to support of socially vulnerable groups.

Title EN: Cambodian arts and crafts
Goal: Integrate Culture In Sustainable Development Frameworks
SDG: SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: National sustainable development policies and plans
Agency Implementation: Satcha Cambodian Handicraft Incubation Center
Main Feature: B.R.B. Cambodia was created by Pierre-André Romano, Chairman of the Board, and 3 other founders Khmer and foreigners with a common passion for Cambodian craftmanship and social enterprises, to promote Cambodian arts and crafts and facilitate the access to domestic and international markets for artists, craft-people, and producers. In 2022, 6 more shareholders joined to help funding Satcha, the new art and craft center in Cambodia, with 60% of the funds being brought by Cambodian individuals willing to support our mission.  Today 100% of our team is Khmer, under the leadership of the founder who is strongly involved in Cambodia development. Believing in the young generation of Khmer managers, he hired a team of 8 leaders (7 women and 1 man) working together in a flexible organisation, where he fosters creativity and accountability instead of a strict hierarchy. We host 52 master craft-people where we provide them with workshop, tool, raw materials and training, in a single location open to public where visitors can learn about Cambodian skills and talents, and can buy the artworks.  A hybrid social business model An incubation center where we provide for free a 3-years full set of hard/soft-skill entrepreneurship training class. A co-op where we commit to buy all their production during these 3 years to guarantee their income and sustain their living. A socially oriented shareholder agreement where all the partners commit to give back 2/3 of our net profits to the incubated craft people in social benefit, extra training, and entrepreneurship support.  We Act Encouraging responsible consumption and production by offering meaningful and high-quality handcrafted products. Preserving, promoting, and supporting Cambodian tradition, culture and know-how, through excellence in craftmanship.  Providing sustainable careers for this industry and generating a positive impact on social, environmental, and economic development in Cambodia. For a Better Future To highlight the pride of craftmanship as one of the main pilar of Khmer National Identity by creating incubation and training centers in every province, by promoting a lively culture with a modern vision inspired by strong traditional foundations, and by showcasing Cambodia as an exemplary model of responsible and sustainable consumption and production.
Results: Since the opening of Satcha in March 2023, we hosted 59 craft people with 12 different skills. They already benefit from language classes (Khmer writing and reading, basic English), art history and design, and creative thinking classes.   Although the entrepreneurship program is for 3 years, 2 of them already left to create their own company and we support them as Satcha’s subcontractors for special projects. In the field of artistic creativity, they started to create their own design, mixing inspiration from contemporary art and patrimonial ornaments. We also foster cross-skill collaboration to create mixed-material decorative items such as ceramic and rattan, fabrics and water hyacinth, paintings and leather carving, … Beside the main site opened since the beginning of the program, we already opened 2 more sites, one in Siem Reap with 8 more carvers and ceramists, and one in Kulen with 10 weavers.

Title EN: Campagne Objectif Culture 2030
Goal: Integrate Culture In Sustainable Development Frameworks
SDG: SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: International cooperation for sustainable development
Agency Implementation: Conseil international de la musique
Main Feature: La campagne ObjectifCulture2030 (#culture2030goal), portée conjointe par un groupe d’OSC, est formée par plusieurs réseaux culturels mondiaux unis pour défendre le rôle de la culture dans le développement durable. Elle est la continuation de la campagne #culture2015goal, créée en 2013 pour demander que la culture soit incluse dans l’Agenda 2030 des Nations Unies pour le développement durable (et les ODD) qui a été adopté en septembre 2015.  La campagne est axée sur le système des Nations Unies. Celui-ci comprend des organes centraux comme l’Assemblée générale des Nations Unies et le Conseil économique et social (ECOSOC), ainsi que des agences ayant des mandats thématiques pertinents, à savoir l’UNESCO, le PNUD ou l’ONU-Habitat.   Les objectifs :  -	Une place plus importante pour la culture dans la mise en œuvre de l’actuel programme de développement mondial (l’Agenda 2030 de l’ONU); -	L’adoption de la culture comme objectif distinct dans le programme de développement post-2030; -	L’adoption d’un agenda global pour la culture. Les activités impliquent de :  -	Participer aux forums politiques de haut niveau des Nations Unies et à d’autres événements intergouvernementaux pertinents, notamment en organisant des panels de haut niveau ; -	Soutenir le plaidoyer aux niveaux national et régional en faveur de l’intégration de la culture dans la planification du développement, par le partage d’outils et d’informations ; -	Développer et mettre en œuvre des méthodologies pour le suivi et l’engagement d’examens nationaux et locaux volontaires, y compris par le biais de rapports alternatifs, afin de maximiser la reconnaissance de la culture; -	Influencer et façonner le discours par la publication de déclarations et d’autres rapports, notamment en formulant ce à quoi pourrait ressembler un objectif culturel (avec mention des droits culturels, du patrimoine matériel et immatériel, de l’accès, de la diversité, de la créativité, etc.); -	Établir des liens avec diverses autres parties prenantes et faire converger les campagnes. La campagne est en échange direct et régulier avec le Secteur de la Culture de l’UNESCO, notamment l’Unité des politiques culturelles et développement.
Results: Durant les 4 dernières années, la campagne a réalisé :  -	Rapport « La culture dans la localisation des ODD », une analyse des rapports volontaires locaux : lien ici (lancé le 21 décembre 2021) -	Débat ResiliArt x Mondiacult : 28 février 2022 o	Intitulée « Vers un objectif culturel dans l’agenda du développement durable », la campagne #culture2030goal ResiliArt x Mondiacult a exploré la question : comment pouvons-nous assurer une plus grande place à la culture dans l’agenda, et ainsi déclencher le nécessaire changement de paradigme ? Il a souligné la nécessité d’une priorisation explicite de la culture pour faire la différence et a donné un aperçu de la manière dont nous pouvons faire mieux aujourd’hui, à la fois dans la conception de politiques culturelles qui soutiennent le développement durable et dans la conception de politiques de développement durable qui intègrent pleinement la culture. o	Lien ici  -	Avant-projet d'un futur objectif culturel : lien ici. Basé sur les contributions d'experts et une enquête auprès des acteurs du domaine, le projet d'objectif devrait recentrer les efforts visant à garantir que la culture prenne sa place au cœur de la planification du développement. -	Document « La culture dans les examens nationaux volontaires de 2022 », mettant en évidence certaines des différentes manières dont la culture est abordée dans ces examens, célèbre les bonnes pratiques et indique les domaines nécessitant une attention accrue. -	Événement au Centre de partenariat (Partnership Hub) de la Conférence générale de l'UNESCO, 15 novembre 2023 -	Panel au Sommet Culture de CGLU, novembre 2023, Dublin -	Intervention orale lors de la consultation des parties prenantes de la société civile à l'ONU, décembre 2023 -	Contribution écrite au Pacte des Nations Unies pour l'avenir, décembre 2023 -	Webinaire « Objectif Culture 2030 - Regard vers l'avenir » (23 janvier 2024)  Déclarations :  -	Déclaration sur l’absence de la culture dans le projet de déclaration finale du Sommet sur les ODD, 7 June 2023 -	Déclaration sur la reconnaissance croissante par le gouvernement du rôle de la culture dans le développement, 24 octobre 2023 -	Déclaration « Pas d'avenir sans culture » sur la publication du premier projet du Pacte pour l'avenir, 2 février 2024 Résultat : Le projet révisé du Pacte pour l’avenir, contient dans l’Action 7 une forte expression en faveur de la reconnaissance du rôle de la culture pour le développement et une référence à un objectif culture dans l’Agenda après-2030.

Title EN: Canada and the Government of Quebec’s support for the Coalition for the Diversity of Cultural Expressions
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture
SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Partnering with civil society
Agency Implementation: Department of Canadian Heritage
Main Feature: The Coalition for the Diversity of Cultural Expressions (CDEC) is a non-profit organization that brings together over 50 professional associations representing more than 360,000 creators, artists, performers, and professionals and more than 2,900 entities working in production, distribution, publishing and distribution in the sectors of literature, cinema, television, new media, music, performing arts and visual arts, in Quebec and across Canada.  Canada and the government of Quebec are historic partners of the CDCE since they participated in its financing since its launch, in 1998, by the main Canadian and Quebec professional associations in the cultural sector. Remember that it is in concert with the CDCE that Canada and Quebec succeeded in promoting the cause of the diversity of cultural expressions and the adoption, by UNESCO, of the Convention on the Protection and Promotion of the Diversity of Cultural Expressions (hereinafter “2005 Convention”).  The CDCE therefore represents a privileged interlocutor of Canadian Heritage and the Ministry of Culture and Communications of Quebec (MCC) in the matter of the diversity of cultural expressions and plays a vital role in relaying the concerns of its members to the governments, particularly in the negotiation of commercial agreements, the diversity of cultural expressions in the digital space as well as to promote the actions and positions of civil society at UNESCO.  Since its creation, the CDCE has been supported on a recurring basis by the MCC for carrying out activities considered normal and regular, associated with their daily operations. For its part, Canadian Heritage supports the CDCE for research activities, its participation in the governing bodies of the Convention, and in its function as Secretariat of the International Federation of Coalitions for Cultural Diversity (IFCCD).
Financial Ressources: Between 2020 and 2024, Canadian Heritage paid a total of CAD 545,000 (approximately USD 397,470).  Between 2019-2020 and 2023-2024, the total contribution of the MCC to the CDCE amounts to CAD 1,205,000 (approximately USD 87,643,241).

Title EN: Canada and the Government of Quebec’s Support to Vues d’Afrique International Film Festival
Goal: Achieve A Balanced Flow Of Cultural Goods And Services And Increase The Mobility Of Artists And Cultural Professionals
SDG: SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 10 - Reduce inequality within and among countries,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Mobility of artists and cultural professionals
Agency Implementation: Cultural Business Development Corporation (SODEC) Ministry of International Relations and La Francophonie (MRIF) Department of Canadian Heritage Telefilm Canada
Main Feature: Vues d’Afrique festival:  Serving as a showcase for great African and Creole filmmakers, this festival aims to raise awareness of the realities and culture of African countries by focusing more on the French-speaking diasporas. In addition to actively contributing to the discovery of African and Creole cultures, this festival allows the development of multiple partnerships between Quebec (Canada) and the countries of the South. Vues d'Afrique already celebrated its 40th edition in 2024; it is through general public activities that the organization promotes the culture of the African continent. The festival is held once a year in April.  Support from SODEC: Since the 2018-2019 financial year, SODEC has offered its support to the organization with variable funding over the years.  Support from the Minister of International Relations and La Francophonie (MRIF):  Essentially, since 2021, the MRIF has offered its support to the organization with its programming and its adjacent activities such as a recognition awards ceremony which took place among others on April 30, 2023. During this edition in 2023, the ministry had allocated funding of CAD 4,000 in addition to participating in the ceremony directly by making a speech during the awards ceremony.  Support from the Government of Canada: The Department of Canadian Heritage also supports the Festival annually through its Canada Arts Presentation Fund for a total of CAD 381,780 for the period 2020-2024.
Results: In 2023, for example, Vues d'Afrique International Film Festival hosted an international academic conference themed: “Marginality and Fragility in African Cinemas.”  The 2023 edition focused on crucial and current themes for filmmakers. These are subjects such as: global ecological fragility, the marginalization of vulnerable populations, the search for new forms and expressions in the cinemas of Africa and its diaspora as well as methods of decolonization of research relating to the festivals which were addressed during the conference. In addition, it explored the networks, channels, partnerships, and distribution circuits of their films on a global scale.  Alongside the festival activities, this conference was held at the Moroccan Cultural Center in Montreal (Canada). It brought together several critics, filmmakers and cinema professionals from the four corners of the world (Africa, Brazil, Canada, United States, Europe) and working in the field for decades. In collaboration with the festival, this event was the ideal opportunity to encourage exchanges, debates, updates and promotion of various projects.
Financial Ressources: SODEC  SODEC supports the event annually. Since the 2018-2019 financial year, it has supported the festival for a total amount of CAD 188,70 (approximately USD 137,125) since 2019.  MRIF:  Like SODEC, MRIF supports the event annually. Between 2021 and 2024, the MRIF supported the festival for a total amount of CAD 19,149 (approximately USD 13,928).  Canadian Heritage:  The Department of Canadian Heritage supports the Festival annually with a contribution of CAD 381,780 for the period 2020-2024 (approximately USD 278,127).
Recommandations: The festival promotes a balanced cultural exchange and facilitates the mobility of artists and cultural professionals. The 2023 edition was a prominent example of this contribution, allowing filmmakers from various countries to promote their films in Canada.

Title EN: Canada Council Granting Programs: Arts Across Canada and Arts Abroad
Goal: Achieve A Balanced Flow Of Cultural Goods And Services And Increase The Mobility Of Artists And Cultural Professionals
SDG: SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 10 - Reduce inequality within and among countries,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Mobility of artists and cultural professionals
Cultural Domain: Design,Performing Arts,Media Arts,Cinema and Audiovisual Arts,Music,Publishing,Visual Arts
Agency Implementation: Canada Council for the Arts
Main Feature: The Canada Council’s Arts Abroad Program celebrates the creativity, innovation, and excellence of Canadian artists by helping to bring Canadian works to the world. This program supports artists, arts professionals, groups, and organizations to enhance international exposure, undertake artistic exploration or exchanges with international colleagues, and nurture new and existing art markets in a global context. This program includes six components:  1.	Travel: Project grants for artists, arts professionals, groups and organizations to travel abroad to network, collaborate, and build the international profile of Canadian arts practice. 2.	Representation and Promotion: Project grants to support Canadian organizations that represent Canadian artists to travel to develop international markets and promote work abroad. 3.	Translation: Project grants for Canadian or foreign organizations to translate Canadian literary and dramatic works for publication or presentation abroad. 4.	Circulation and Touring: Project grants for Canadian artists, groups and organizations to circulate exhibitions and tour internationally. 5.	Residencies: Project grants for artists, arts professionals, artistic groups and arts organizations to participate in residencies abroad. 6.	Co-productions: Project grants for Canadian artistic groups and arts organizations to be partners in international co-productions of new work or exhibitions.  The Canada Council’s Arts Across Canada Program fosters meaningful relationships and exchanges between artists and the Canadian public. Artists, arts professionals, groups and arts organizations can apply to present and share artistic work with diverse communities across the country, engage more deeply with the public and develop a stronger national profile. Festivals and other presenters can apply to highlight the work of Canadian and international artists and contribute to the growing dialogue and exchange on arts in Canada. The program includes seven components:  1.	Travel: Project grants for artists, arts professionals, groups and organizations to travel within Canada to network, collaborate and build national profile. 2.	Representation and Promotion: Project grants for organizations that represent artists to travel to develop markets and promote work within Canada. 3.	Translation: Project grants to support activities linked to the translation of Canadian literary works or dramatic works into French, English, an Indigenous language, American Sign Language (ASL), Langue des signes québécoise (LSQ), or any other regional Canadian or Indigenous sign language for Canadian publication or presentation. 4.	Circulation and Touring: Project grants for Canadian artists, groups and organizations to circulate exhibitions and tour in Canada. 5.	Foreign Artist Tours: Project grants for Canadian arts organizations to host tours of foreign artists in Canada. 6.	Public Outreach: Project or composite grants to support activities that contribute to public appreciation of the arts in Canada. 7.	Arts Festivals and Presenters: Core grants to support Canadian organizations that strengthen artistic practice through the presentation and exhibition of Canadian and international work.
Results: Arts Across Canada & Arts Abroad 2020-21:  •	CAD 26.8 million total awarded  •	674 arts organizations supported (CAD 23.3 million awarded)  •	68 groups supported (CAD 1.4 million awarded)  •	207 artists supported (CAD 2.1 million awarded)   2021-2022:  •	CAD 35.4 million total awarded  •	790 arts organizations supported (CAD 29.6 million awarded)  •	115 groups supported (CAD 2.3 million awarded)  •	467 artists supported (CAD 3.5 million awarded)   2022-2023 •	CAD 51.1 million total awarded  •	927 arts organizations supported (CAD 37.9 million awarded)  •	231 groups supported (CAD 5 million awarded)  •	1,118 artists supported (CAD 8.2 million awarded)

Title EN: Canada Council for the Arts’ Northern Co-delivery Partnerships
Goal: Integrate Culture In Sustainable Development Frameworks
SDG: SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: National sustainable development policies and plans
Cultural Domain: Design,Performing Arts,Media Arts,Cinema and Audiovisual Arts,Music,Publishing,Visual Arts
Agency Implementation: Canada Council for the Arts
Main Feature: To better serve northerners in the arts, the Council has launched three co-delivery partnerships in the North. Co-delivery partnerships are a new way of working for the Council that allow the partner organization to support artists and arts workers in the North on their own terms, according to their realities and priorities for making and sharing arts and culture, and strengthening the Council’s presence and relationships in the North, and meeting the region’s unique and varied cultural realities for making and sharing arts and culture. Three measures are underway to cover the breadth of art practices in northern Canada:  •	The Council and the Government of Yukon (one of the three territories) partnered to support Yukon's emerging Indigenous artists and cultural carriers. The partnership grows out of a shared desire to develop new ways of supporting Indigenous artists and arts workers with strong Indigenous leadership and impact. The Government of Yukon’s Tourism and Culture Department recruited an Indigenous Outreach and Program Officer, based in the territorial capital of Whitehorse, who supported Indigenous artists to apply for arts funding from both territorial and federal sources. The Officer engaged and supported Indigenous artists to help build their capacity to create, perform, and export. The co-delivery partnership with the Government of Yukon also supported an Indigenous Outreach Liaison position and provided micro grants to Indigenous artists and cultural carriers.  •	The Council has partnered with the Inuit Art Foundation to launch a new national, Inuit-specific funding pilot program in the spirit of self-determination. Grounded in Inuit traditional knowledge, this program is shaped by community feedback from Inuit across their homelands in northern Canada, and those residing in southern Canada, to ensure it meets the needs of all artists. The program also offers capacity building opportunities for Inuit in the program delivery.  •	The Council and the Government of the Northwest Territories (GNWT) have set up a three-year co-delivery agreement for the period of 2023-2026. It is aimed at addressing both Indigenous and non-Indigenous arts organizations and focused on supporting capacity building and sector development. Through this partnership, the Council will provide the GNWT with a financial contribution of CAD 750,000 over three years. The activities will be co-developed with community input and delivered by the GNWT. They include the recruitment of a full-time Arts Advisor located in the Northwest Territories to help build the capacity of arts and culture organizations in the grant application process and at large. In addition, a dedicated funding program focuses on meeting the needs of Indigenous community organizations outside of the territorial capital, Yellowknife. Outreach sessions will offer capacity-building opportunities for arts and culture groups and organizations across the territory and help to increase their access to funding provided by the Council.
Results: Yukon Partnership CAD 200,000 over 2 years (2022-2023 & 2023-2024):  Based on the partnership’s first six months, it has resulted in a significant increase in engagement with its intended communities across the Yukon. The partnership is allowing Council funding to reach a number of new recipients.   Inuit Art Foundation Partnership CAD 180,000 (2022-2023): The Inuit Art Foundation successfully piloted its Inuit-specific grant funding initiative and marked the initiative’s first year. The program was designed to lower barriers that Inuit face to accessing public funding. In total, 40 artists from across all regions of Inuit homeland were supported, many of them previously not reached by the Council.  Northwest Territories Partnership CAD 750,000 over 3 years (began in 2023): Too early in the partnership to have results described.
Financial Ressources: USD 815,000 (CAD 1.1 million) Note: This reflects the combined total of all three partnerships

Title EN: Canadian Commission for UNESCO’s Cultural Resilience Project
Goal: Integrate Culture In Sustainable Development Frameworks
SDG: SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: National sustainable development policies and plans
Cultural Domain: Design,Performing Arts,Media Arts,Cinema and Audiovisual Arts,Music,Publishing,Visual Arts
Agency Implementation: Canadian Commission for UNESCO (Canada Council for the Arts)
Main Feature: In the summer of 2021, the Creative City Network of Canada, in partnership with CCUNESCO, asked Canadians to share stories of culture organizations that improved their dire circumstances resulting from the COVID-19 pandemic to keep their art on offer, to maintain revenue and audiences, or to find new audiences. In total, over 200 such stories were collected by Hill Strategies Research from all provinces and two territories. The final report documents how artists and organizations stabilized revenue, maintained audiences, or created new streams of revenue during the pandemic.   This short-term plan aided in paving the way for building resilience while ensuring equitable distribution and access to resources and cultural expressions.
Results: The measure led to a Phase Two project, in which new professional development tools for cultural and creative industries were developed in collaboration with project partners, the Cultural Human Resources Council and Les Arts et la Ville. An interactive 3-hour training workshop toured Canadian municipalities in 2022 and 2023 and was delivered in both official languages to arts and culture organizations across the country, available through virtual event and live streamed to YouTube.
Recommandations: 12 interrelated themes were highlighted in the final report:  1.	Innovation works best when customized: Though innovation often involves technology, many of the stories involved changes in organizational processes. Some innovations were both technology and process based.  2.	Flexibility and adaptability needed: Flexibility and adaptability of mindset, objectives, and resource allocation were key ingredients for innovation and resilience.  3.	Support is varied but crucial: Whether through financial or in-kind support, every innovation relied on staff, collaborators, and a range of funders to pitch in.  4.	Digital, organizational, and financial challenges: All innovations faced incredible challenges during the pandemic. Artists, arts managers, and heritage workers overcame key digital, organizational, and financial barriers in implementing changes.  5.	Small can be mighty: Many innovative ideas got off the ground with very few resources, and some of the smallest organizations were able to be very nimble. 6.	Partnerships can extend capacity and reach: For many innovators, partnerships were essential to their resilience.  7.	Equity bolsters resilience, and resilience enhances equity: The hard work of creating equity can contribute to resilience, which, in turn, influences equity.  8.	Sometimes, just jump: The organizations and artists who responded particularly well identified opportunities and, in many cases, took a big leap of faith.  9.	Prioritizing and connecting with artists: A common theme among organizations and artists who had success during the pandemic was that they prioritized the community’s artists and developed new projects according to artists’ ideas and needs.  10.	Short-term innovations can lead to longer-term changes: Most pandemic-related innovations were focused on short-term goals such as creating works and employing artists, but a number of artists and organizations also turned their attention to long-term applications of their innovations.  11.	Important places of exchange: Artists and cultural organizations are often at the forefront of engaging in dialogues about the compelling histories, stories, issues, and ideas that exist in every community.  12.	Redefining the arts and heritage: Some pandemic innovations have pushed the boundaries of artforms or of the presentation of gallery and museum collections.

Title EN: CELEBRATION DE LA JOURNEE MONDIALE DE LA PROPRIETE INTELLECTUELLE EN COTE D'IVOIRE
Goal: Promote Human Rights And Fundamental Freedoms
SDG: SDG 5 - Achieve gender equality and empower all women and girls,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels
Area of Monitoring: Artistic freedom
Agency Implementation: Office Ivoirien de la Propriété Intellectuelle (OIPI)
Main Feature: La célébration de la Journée Mondiale de la Propriété Intellectuelle 2024 en Côte d'Ivoire vise à sensibiliser le public et les acteurs du secteur culturel à l'importance de la propriété intellectuelle (PI) pour la protection et la valorisation des œuvres et innovations. L'événement comprend des conférences, des ateliers, des expositions et des performances artistiques. Les activités visent à informer les créateurs, les entrepreneurs et le grand public sur les droits de propriété intellectuelle, les mécanismes de protection disponibles, et les avantages économiques et culturels de la PI.  Le 26 avril de chaque année est décrété « Journée Internationale de la Propriété Intellectuelle (JMPI) ». Le thème mondial de cette année est « La propriété intellectuelle dans les Objectifs de Développement Durable : construire notre avenir commun grâce à l’innovation et à la créativité ». La Côte d’Ivoire n’est pas restée en marge de cette journée. Ainsi le 26 avril 2024 à 10h30mn, a eu lieu à l’hôtel "Le Vaisseau", la célébration de cette journée organisée par L’Office Ivoirien de la Propriété Intellectuelle (OIPI). Le thème retenu par l’OIPI est « Promouvoir la propriété intellectuelle pour stimuler l’entrepreneuriat et l’innovation en Côte d’Ivoire dans la perspective de la réalisation de Objectifs de Développement Durable ».Plusieurs activités ont animé ce forum de réflexion : -Une conférence introductive ;  -Un panel ; -Echanges et synthèses des axes de solutions. Après une série de questions des participants, des axes de solutions ont été trouvés pour atteindre les Objectifs de Développement Durable d’ici à en 2030, ce sont : - diminuer de la consommation des énergies ; - réduire le cycle de vie des objets et encourageant le recyclage ;  - valoriser les déchets qui sont des opportunités d’emploi pour les jeunes.
Results: Les précédentes célébrations ont réussi à augmenter la compréhension et l'intérêt pour la propriété intellectuelle parmi les artistes, les entrepreneurs et les innovateurs en Côte d'Ivoire. Elles ont également contribué à une meilleure reconnaissance des droits de PI et à une augmentation des enregistrements de brevets, marques et droits d'auteur auprès de l'OIPI. De plus, elles ont favorisé des collaborations entre différents acteurs du secteur culturel et technologique.
Recommandations: L'évaluation a montré que la Journée Mondiale de la Propriété Intellectuelle a considérablement sensibilisé sur l'importance de la PI, mais a également mis en lumière la nécessité de renforcer les capacités locales pour l'application des droits de PI. Les recommandations incluent l'intensification des campagnes de sensibilisation, l'amélioration de l'accès aux services de protection de la PI, et la promotion de l'innovation locale à travers des initiatives de formation et de soutien aux créateurs et innovateurs.

Une autre caractéristique majeure de cette grande manifestation est la collaboration étroite avec les associations culturelles locales.
