Title EN: Chile's participation in the Ibero-American cultural space. Iber Programmes.
Goal: Integrate Culture In Sustainable Development Frameworks
SDG: SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: International cooperation for sustainable development
Cultural Domain: Design,Performing Arts,Media Arts,Cinema and Audiovisual Arts,Music,Publishing,Visual Arts
Agency Implementation: Ministry of Cultures, Arts and Heritage (MINCAP) Ministry of Foreign Affairs (MINREL)
Main Feature: Co-operation is a fundamental pillar of the work carried out by the Ibero-American Conference, following its formation in 1991, and over three decades of its history, Chile has always been a committed partner and actor in the strengthening and development of Ibero-American co-operation.   In the Ibero-American Cultural Space, Chile has an extensive participation through its active presence in eleven programmes: Iberartesanías, Ibercultura Viva, Ibermedia, Ibermúsicas, Iberorquestas Juveniles, Iberrutas, Iberbibliotecas, Iberarchivos, Ibermuseos, Iberescena.   All of them are related to Chile through MINCAP and the Network of Ibero-American Diplomatic Archives (RADI) coordinated by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs (MINREL). During 2023, in order to promote coordination, coherence and consistency in institutional participation in Iber Programmes, a series of meetings were held with representatives of these programmes to hear their opinions on the gaps that need to be addressed and then reduced, and possible synergies and opportunities that can be harnessed by MINCAP in its activities.   The Iber Programmes are situated within the indicator “co-operation strategies for development that include action lines to support diverse cultural expressions”, from the 2005 Convention monitoring framework.
Results: (a) IberArtesanías: participation in the programme enables access to information and training resources that serve the purpose of strengthening public policy towards the sector. It also provides access to resources from an annual competitive fund.   (b) IberOrquestas: taking part in this programme has enabled participation in the development of the study for shaping the Atlas de Buenas Prácticas (Atlas of good practices) for musical groups - instrumental and vocal - members of the associated systems and foundations.   (c) IberMúsicas: to date, participation in the programme has enabled the allocation of resources directly to 68 Chilean projects in the artist mobility, festival and composer residency categories.   (d) IberEscenas: participation in the programme has enabled access to financing for national performing arts projects in the creation residence, performing arts show coproduction, festivals and performance spaces for show programming categories. To date, 33 projects have benefitted, in these categories.   (e) IberMedia: participation in the programme has enabled access to financing for fiction and documentary genre films in coproduction with countries from Ibero-America, audiovisual projects with development finalised with countries from Ibero-America.   (f) IberCultura Viva: the programme enabled the implementation of the digital platform, physical publications also available in digital format, Ibero-American community living culture centres, IberCultura Viva collection and community culture ideas. At the same time, the Diploma Course on Community-Based Cultural Policies (free translation) has been implemented in coordination with Flacso Argentina.   (g) IberRutas: the programme enabled the publication (in digital format) of the International Seminar on Interculturality and Migration(free translation) held in Chile.   At the same time, the “Ibero-American Register of Migration Researchers” (free translation) takes place. In addition, “Maleta Abierta” and “Miradas de Iberoamerica” competitions were held, whose goal is to contribute to guarantees of respect of cultural rights of individuals and peoples, regardless of their migratory status, as well as to encourage reflection through photography of migrants in different situations that testify and illustrate the enrichment that interculturality means for Ibero-American peoples, as well as the integration processes that it implies.
Recommandations: Ibero-American co-operation has several advantages, concentrating its management as a support mechanism for strengthening public policies in the region and in the best interests of Chile. It promotes the exchange of experiences and promotes the articulation and synergies within the Ibero-American System and with external partners. Chile's presence in Ibero-American Co-operation has been constant, with the participation of ministries, public and civil society entities.   It is a way to provide spaces and generate broader and cross-cutting interaction activities for sustainable development, such as sharing of thoughts and cross-cutting action plans within this framework for collaboration. Beyond the achievements among peers, trust has been gained and some synergistic bonds have been created between people and places, which would undoubtedly have been slower in absence of political will for this concerted effort at governmental level.   Chile can affirm that this Ibero-American co-operation space has been and still is a virtuous bridge for creating or deepening more networks, which constitute an active contact platform and a showcase of human talent, enhancing our personal and institutional capacity to learn in an environment of richness and a diversity of nuances that this shared culture has.   Participating as a country has benefitted public and civil society entities, allowing them to share experiences, obtain skills and generate knowledge networks, which has been beneficial for the participating institutions. Similarly, the country's different regions were included through the cultural programmes, strengthening and benefitting local and regional projects, as well as different communities from the world of culture (artists, musicians, artisans, audiovisual producers, among others).   The balance of the past 30 years has been positive for our country. However, there are many challenges ahead, both in the area of internal coordination as well as the need to provide more visibility to the effects of participating in this multilateral space, where co-operation plays a very important role.

Title EN: Chile's strategy for achieving Sustainable Development Goals Participative dialogues for the  implementation of the 2030 Agenda.
Goal: Integrate Culture In Sustainable Development Frameworks
SDG: SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: National sustainable development policies and plans
Cultural Domain: Design,Performing Arts,Media Arts,Cinema and Audiovisual Arts,Music,Publishing,Visual Arts
Agency Implementation: Ministry of Foreign Affairs (MINREL).
Main Feature: Within the framework of Chile's 2030 Agenda implementation strategy34, the National Council, in its first session held in May 2023, agreed to propel implementation and adoption of the 2030 Agenda and its Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). In this context, it was decided, together with reactivating state bodies associated with the 2030 Agenda, to initiate a process to design a National Implementation Plan for the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) in Chile.   The design process considered several participation mechanisms that included representatives from different sectors of society. Based on this premise, regional dialogues were organised all over the country: dialogues with excluded social groups; dialogues in the social, economic and environmental working groups; interviews and/or workshops with key informants; self-organising dialogues and dialogues with the Red Nacional Agenda 2030 national network.   Through these activities, the participation of more than 2,000 people was observed all over the country, generating with these inputs, the first draft of the Strategy Proposal for the Implementation of the 2030 Agenda, which was sent out for public consultation, receiving back more than 1,000 comments on the different chapters of the strategy. During the dialogues, the importance of encompassing intercultural relationships and promoting peace and intercultural coexistence also stood out, emphasising necessity of benefiting from local and ancestral wisdom.   The necessity of addressing the historical conflict between the State and indigenous communities through dialogue was specifically suggested. Also, to provide social services that respect and take into account the cultural particularities and specific needs of these groups was identified as one of the main challenges of the State. Finally, this strategy reports on indicator on “national sustainable development policies and plans that include action lines to support diverse cultural expressions”, from the 2005 Convention monitoring framework.
Results: One of the main results of the Chilean strategy to address the 2030 Agenda and, at the same time, the 2005 Convention on cultural diversity, is the importance of promoting peace and intercultural coexistence, highlighting the need to make the most of local and ancestral wisdom of indigenous peoples. In this manner, to provide social services that respect and take into account the cultural particularities and specific needs of these groups was identified as one of the main challenges for the State.   These premises implicate Chile and its commitment to comply with the SDGs through the inclusion of initiatives for the promotion and protection of cultural diversity.
Financial Ressources: Without funding.

Area of Monitoring: Cultural and creative sectors
Agency Implementation: Ministère de la Culture et Centre du cinéma et de l’image animée (CNC)
Main Feature: La chronologie des médias fixe le délai d’exploitation des films par les différents diffuseurs selon des fenêtres successives. Elle est déclenchée par la sortie de l’œuvre en salles en échelonnant, 4 mois plus tard, les diverses fenêtres d’exploitation d’une durée prédéfinie et dont l’enchainement total s’étend sur une durée de 36 mois. Les œuvres qui sont directement diffusées sur une plateforme ou une chaîne de télévision sans sortie en salle de cinéma n’y sont pas soumises.  La chronologie des médias poursuit deux objectifs d’intérêt général :  •	Protéger l’exploitation des films en salles de cinéma.  •	Assurer le préfinancement des œuvres cinématographiques en France en garantissant à chaque diffuseur une visibilité maximale des œuvres qu’il exploite sur sa fenêtre dès lors qu’il dispose d’une exclusivité sur celle-ci. Sur ce point, la chronologie des médias fonctionne de façon incitative en accordant des fenêtres d’exploitation plus ou moins attractives en fonction du degré de contribution des éditeurs de services dans la production d’œuvres.  La chronologie des médias résulte des dispositions du code du cinéma et de l’image animée (CCIA) qui prévoient directement le délai applicable à la vidéo physique (4 mois sauf dérogation pour les films les moins vus en salle) et renvoient à un accord professionnel de plusieurs années pouvant être étendu par le ministre de la Culture à l’ensemble des diffuseurs s’agissant des autres délais (télévision, service de médias audiovisuels à la demande).  L’accord actuel a été conclu le 24 janvier 2022pour une durée de trois ans puis a été étendu par arrêté du 4 février 2022.
Results: En complément des données chiffrées d’ores et déjà décrites en mesure 2, en ce qui concerne plus spécifiquement la salle de cinéma, on relèvera que :  •	Le nombre d’entrées en salle s’établit à 181 millions d’entrées cinéma en 2023 avec une part de marché de 40 % pour les films français ; il s’agit du 1er marché de l’Union européenne en termes de fréquentation ;  •	8 593 films sont projetés en salle dont 681 inédits et 403 films recommandés Art et Essai en 2022 ;  •	60,4 % de films inédits projetés sont des films français en 2022 ;  •	2 061 établissements cinéma actifs et 6 298 écrans actifs en 2022 ;  •	11 films français dépassant le million d’entrées, dans des genres très variés (Anatomie d’une chute, Tirailleurs, Les 3 mousquetaires, Alibi.com 2).
Recommandations: La chronologie des médias participe, aux côtés des obligations de financement directes (mesure 1) et des taxes affectées au CNC (mesure 2), des performances du système français.

Cultural Domain: Performing Arts,Media Arts,Cinema and Audiovisual Arts,Music,Publishing,Visual Arts
Agency Implementation: General Directorate of Cultural Industries and Arts (Ministry of Culture)
Main Feature: “Citizen participation in cultural industries and the arts” is an initiative that aims to expand citizen participation in decision-making in the arts and cultural industries sector, as well as in strengthening transparency. of public management. In compliance with Guideline No. 6.5 “Implement citizen participation mechanisms in the development of cultural policies”, the General Directorate of Cultural Industries and its line directorates have implemented a series of mechanisms that ensure this participation and thereby guarantee the sustainability of cultural governance, Priority Objective No. 6 of the National Culture Policy for 2030. The objectives to be achieved are:  Ensure transparency and citizen control over public policies and services regarding cultural industries and arts. ●	Improve and expand spaces for citizen participation in the cultural industries and arts. ●	Strengthen the capacities of civil society for the adequate exercise of its citizen participation in the design, execution and evaluation of public policies and services in the field of cultural industries and arts. The main actions contemplated by the strategy are: 1.	The development of the Public Account in Cultural Industries and Arts. This is a transparency tool. Its objective is to be accountable to citizens regarding the use of public resources for the implementation of policies and services in cultural industries and arts. 2.	Implementation of citizen participation mechanism. For this, the following have been defined and implemented: informative talks, dialogue tables, technical tables, work tables, citizen meetings, committees, work groups, spaces for citizen consultation, as well as mechanisms for attention and information to citizens. Depending on their scope, these can be at the local, regional, macro-regional or national level, and due to the nature of their application, they can be sectoral or multisectoral in nature. 3.	Generation and dissemination of citizen participation information mechanisms. A web space of the Ministry of Culture has been implemented, through which monthly and annual reports are made in which the spaces for dialogue and information implemented by the DGIA with the agents of the sector and civil society in general are reported. This initiative seeks to expand transparency about the interaction between public servants of the Ministry of Culture and citizens. Each report collects information on the participation mechanisms implemented, which can be informative talks (sectoral or regional), dialogue tables (sectoral, regional, technical and permanent), advisory committees or working groups.
Results: From 2020 to 2023, 808 participatory mechanisms have been implemented, achieving the participation of more than 17,400 citizens, including cultural agents, artists and public servants. Among the main results obtained, we can mention: -	Within the framework of the health emergency caused by Covid19, measures and mechanisms were implemented to mitigate the economic effects on the culture sector produced by the pandemic. The bases of Emergency Decree 058-2020, the lines of economic support and content acquisition, as well as the health protocols by sector, were discussed through dialogue tables and informative talks as part of the citizen participation mechanisms. of the General Directorate of Cultural Industries and Arts, obtaining, during 2020, a total of 265 spaces implemented: 96 dialogue tables (between regional, technical and sectorial), and 169 informative talks (sectoral and regional). -	“Towards a new Law of the Artist”. Law No. 28131 of the Artist, Interpreter and Performer was enacted 17 years ago, prior to the approval of the Convention for the Diversity of Cultural Expressions of 2005, and prior to the National Culture Policy for 2030, therefore from the Ministry of Culture, work was undertaken to update it. For this process, between March and December 2021, a total of 18 technical dialogue tables were held (including 2 tables in indigenous languages and one table in sign language), with agents from the sector in the 25 regions of the country. -	“Recovery Plan for cultural industries and arts”, for the preparation of this document (in 2021), 59 participation spaces were implemented at the national level (including 3 tables in indigenous languages and one table in sign language), in which 1,278 cultural agents, public servants, and citizens participated, receiving 1,913 contributions that were finally made visible and incorporated into the Recovery Plan. This process included the formation of a Consultative Committee made up of representative cultural agents, academia, and the public sector. -	Sectoral Working Group: “Listen to you working group for the promotion of the artistic sector”, created with Ministerial Resolution No. 000297-2023-MC (08/07/2023). This temporary group aimed to propose measures and strategies for the strengthening, reactivation and operation of the artistic sector. As part of this mechanism, they formed 3 working subgroups: subgroup of the music sector, subgroup of the theater and circus sector, and subgroup of the traditional art sector. Within the framework of this mechanism, 6 informative talks and 7 meetings with subgroups were held. 688 artistic agents from the 25 regions of the country participated, obtaining: i) a list of challenges categorized by priority level and ii) a matrix of contributions to the Draft Law for the Promotion of the artistic sector. -	Within the framework of the launch of the Economic Stimuli for Culture, each year a Sectoral Working Group is formed, of a temporary nature, in charge of formulating technical and financial proposals for the stimulus lines for the preparation of the Annual Economic Stimulus Plan for Culture. the Promotion of Cinematographic Activity, guaranteeing the participation of the actors who make up the cinematographic and audiovisual activity in the country and of citizens in general. -	For the approval and subsequent socialization of the National Reading, Book and Library Policy, the Directorate of Books and Reading (approved on 07/13/2022), implemented spaces for dialogue and citizen consultation with the purpose of incorporating the contributions and recommendations coming from citizens and the publishing sector. -	To date, 2 Public Accounts have been published in cultural industries and arts, as well as 3 annual citizen participation reports.

The renewed framework will be anchored in self-determinacy and in the spirit of reconciliation, and will support the creation, presentation, and discoverability of Indigenous content throughout the broadcasting system. The co-development process includes a public consultation on how the broadcasting system in Canada can best promote the interests and needs of Indigenous Peoples.   Following the public consultation, the CRTC will work with Indigenous representatives and participants to co-develop a proposed policy and to further comments on the potential impacts of the new policy.
Results: The CRTC’s three-phase proceeding to co-develop the new Indigenous Broadcasting Policy began in 2019 and is ongoing. The first phase, which focused on early engagement with Indigenous Peoples, is completed. The information captured during the engagement sessions, and consolidated in the What You Said Report, has helped to establish the conduct and scope of the next phases of policy development. The second phase will be launched in 2024, and will include a public consultation in collaboration with First Nations, Inuit and Métis peoples on how the broadcasting system in Canada can best promote the needs and interests of Indigenous Peoples. The final outcome will be a co-developed Indigenous Broadcasting Policy building towards a renewed relationship and shared governance.

Title EN: Comité Visas Artistes
Goal: Achieve A Balanced Flow Of Cultural Goods And Services And Increase The Mobility Of Artists And Cultural Professionals
SDG: SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 10 - Reduce inequality within and among countries,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Mobility of artists and cultural professionals
Agency Implementation: Zone franche, le réseau des Musiques du Monde
Main Feature: Zone Franche défend l’idée que l’accueil des artistes et professionnels étrangers en France est un élément indispensable à la construction d’une politique culturelle tournée vers la diversité et les échanges interculturels. La France a un rôle majeur pour les Musiques du Monde en Europe : elle en est une plateforme majeure et la circulation des artistes intervient comme levier économique et de développement, dynamisant les scènes émergentes du monde entier.  Le Comité Visas Artistes a été initié en 2009 pour réagir face aux difficultés croissantes relatives à l’octroi de visas, rencontrées par les organismes professionnels du secteur musical, travaillant à un niveau international. Il a pour vocation de soutenir les professionnels du secteur musical quand ceux-ci rencontrent des difficultés dans l’obtention de visas et la résolution de situations de blocages. Avec un périmètre d’action qui concerne tout le champ du spectacle vivant, ce comité représente les professionnels du secteur : producteurs, labels, tourneurs, artistes, programmateurs (festivals, salles de spectacles, collectivités territoriales…) et artistes. Il est régulièrement consulté et reconnu pour son expertise et son caractère exemplaire en tant que plateforme informelle. Zone Franche, le réseau des musiques du monde, en est le pilote.  La triple mission du Comité Visas Artistes  1)	Agir : intervention auprès des ministères concernés dans les cas de difficultés d’obtention de visas ou de blocage. A noter ici l'efficacité de la procédure d'alerte mise en place depuis 2015 en partenariat avec le MEAE et la Sous-Direction des Visas (SDV) du ministère de l'Intérieur qui permet de régler aujourd'hui la majorité des blocages dans des délais rapides. 2)	Conseiller : le montage des dossiers étant complexe et évoluant rapidement, il est difficile pour les petites structures de suivre l’évolution des démarches à suivre. Pour cela Zone Franche a constitué un réseau de structures et personnes ressources aidant à répondre à des questions parfois très spécifiques et très techniques. Afin de rendre lisibles et accessibles les procédures et démarches liées à l'obtention des visas, le comité édite également le Guide pratique des visas. 3)	Préconiser : la tâche du Comité consiste enfin à collecter des cas pour identifier les raisons de blocage ou de mise en difficulté les plus fréquentes, en vue de produire des recommandations auprès des autorités publiques afin d'améliorer les procédures. Ce travail de préconisation du CVA est accompagné par le plaidoyer de Zone Franche sur la mobilité des artistes, une valeur essentielle pour le réseau. Zone Franche réunit 2 fois par an les membres du comité. Il est composé du le CNM, du FNSAC, de l’UPFI, du SNAM CGT, du SFA, du PRODISS, de l’UFISC, du SMA, de l’ONDA, de l’Organisation Internationale de la Francophonie, de l’Institut Français, de De Concert!, de Mobiculture, de la Cité internationale des arts et des trois ministères concernés : Europe et des Affaires étrangères, Culture et Intérieur. Les réunions du comité sont l’occasion de faire un bilan des situations d’urgence gérées par Zone Franche tout au long de l’année concernant les refus de visas, le retard dans le traitement des dossiers, etc… Il est aussi le moment où se construit le dialogue sur les problématiques repérées, les points à valoriser, le plaidoyer à mener, etc…   Zone Franche publie deux documents dans le cadre de cette activité :  -	Le Guide pratique des visas : il vise à rendre plus lisible la réglementation en vigueur, encourager les bonnes pratiques, aider les professionnels à se repérer dans les étapes de leur "parcours visas" avec un outils ressource spécifique au secteur culturel ; -	Libre circulation des artistes : de la théorie à la réalité : il s’agit d’un document de plaidoyer qui part du corpus juridique international, européen et national, fondant la libre circulation des artistes, pour aller jusqu’aux réalités concrètes (voire systémiques) des situations de refus, de blocage. Il plaide pour une meilleure effectivité du droit des artistes à se déplacer.
Results: Chaque année, Zone Franche traite en moyenne 80 dossiers, pour 150 artistes (un dossier pouvant représenter un ou plusieurs artiste-s) avec un taux de résolution moyen de 70% (c’est-à-dire que pour 70% des cas, le refus se transforme en acceptation, le blocage enlevé, le retard dans le dossier accéléré, etc…).   L’analyse des données relatives à chaque cas permet à l’association de faire une typologie moyenne des pays de provenance des artistes concernées, des problématiques rencontrées, etc… Par le traitement des dossiers Zone Franche développe une vue d’ensemble des dysfonctionnements systémiques et des entraves à la libre circulation des artistes.  Enfin, du fait de son expérience, voire de son expertise, Zone Franche organise ou participe à de nombreuses rencontres professionnelles et / ou scientifiques, autour de la libre circulation des artistes ; l’association s’implique dans les travaux d’enquête ou autre sur ce sujet, etc…

Title EN: Copyright in the education sector. Literary Rights Society.
Goal: Promote Human Rights And Fundamental Freedoms
SDG: SDG 5 - Achieve gender equality and empower all women and girls,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels
Area of Monitoring: Artistic freedom
Agency Implementation: Literary Rights Society (SADEL), National Union of Artists (UNA).
Main Feature: The Literary Rights Society (SADEL) is a non-profit entity for the management of intellectual property, created under the scope of the Law Nº17.336 on Intellectual Property, dedicated to safeguarding the copyright of writers and publishers. It was formally created in 2000, but since 2008 it has been collectively managing the copyright of its members.   In accordance with the Law, SADEL is authorised to grant licenses and establish rates for the partial reproduction of works, with the sole purpose of collecting and distributing the earnings among the copyright owners. One of its fundamental purposes has to do with copyright in woks utilised by tertiary education establishments.   This has to do with Chilean universities paying for works that are used in their study resource and photocopy centres in order to photocopy, digitise, upload to their virtual classrooms and send by email, up to 15% or an entire chapter of each of the books represented, both from the national catalogue as well as from those with international agreements with other rights-management entities, paying a low cost rate. In 2016, SADEL decides to take legal action against universities which violate copyright by not signing this agreement.   As a result of these legal actions, a milestone was reached with a change in how universities are transitioning from a system where copyright is not respected to a system where they have progressively began to respect the rights of the owners of moral and economic rights of the works utilised in the educational process, with even some study centres who are very committed to excellence to reach out, voluntarily, in order to obtain a license.   We currently represent a large number of authors and publishers, both national and international, as we have reciprocal representation agreements with rights management organisations, like ours, from Spain, Mexico, Argentina, Colombia, United States of America and Australia.   The money collected is distributed among all our members and behind SADEL there is a team that works every day, committed to creating change in the cultural paradigm in Chile and for the work of authors and publishers to be respected, as occurrs in developed countries such as Germany, France, Italy, Norway, England, etc.   Finally, in line with the monitoring framework of the 2005 Convention, this measure falls within the indicator on "policies and measures that promote and protect the social and economic rights of cultural professionals".
Results: To date more than 17 licenses have been signed with universities and study centres. Respect and promotion of copyright are key pillars for cultural development. Through the payment for use of the workds, academic and scientific activity is precisely rewarded for the effort made by its authors, makes the creation and dissemination of knowledge sustainable.

Title EN: Competency-Based Education Framework
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture
SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Cultural and creative sectors
Agency Implementation: Ministry of Education
Main Feature: National Goal One of Education advocates for national unity and a sense of identity among its diverse population through education.   Goal 6 targets to promote respect for and development of Kenya’s rich and varied cultures. It recognizes that Education should instill in the youth an understanding of past and present cultures and their valid place in contemporary society be guided to blend the best of traditional values with the changing requirements that must follow rapid development to build a stable and modern society values, moral principles, and a sense of integrity among its citizens that aims at developing responsible citizens who make ethical choices and contribute positively to society.  The Ministry of Education implements Competency-Based Education (CBE) that promotes diversity and culture by recognizing and valuing individual differences, accommodating diverse learning needs, and creating inclusive learning environments that celebrate cultural diversity and promote equity in education.  The Competency Based Curriculum framework provides for The Arts and Sports Science pathway which provides opportunities for self-realization and expression as well as for individual development and fulfilment. It is envisaged that about 15% of learners in the senior school will take up this pathway and build on the skills already acquired at junior Secondary. The Arts and Sports Science Pathway has three tracks; Visual Arts, Performing Arts, and Sport Science. In all the tracks, the learner is expected to learn core subjects as well as choose options including Legal and Ethical issues in Arts, Communication Skills, Performing Arts, Music, Dance, Theatre and Elocution, Visual and Applied Arts including Fine Art, Applied Art, Time Based Media. The Arts and Sport pathway is aimed at enabling the learner to develop an understanding and appreciation of artistic and cultural expression through music, bodily movement, choreography, acting, improvisation, interpretation of contextual drama, scripting, elements of stage techniques, creative writing, and public speaking, whilst also using a variety of texts and contexts. It is envisaged that through the Competency-Based curriculum, 5% of learners will take up the Performing Arts Track in senior secondary school and another 5% will take up the Visual and Applied Arts. The Physical Education and Sports Policy 2022 was developed to fast-track the actualization of competency-based education. CBE also encourages the integration of arts and cultural themes across various subjects, not just confined to Arts as a learning area for instance History, Literature, and Poetry. This interdisciplinary approach ensures that arts and culture are not isolated but instead woven into the fabric of students' overall learning experiences, promoting a holistic understanding and appreciation of cultural diversity. Teaching of Indigenous languages are also part of the curriculum. In addition, the curriculum recommends language of instruction in Early Years of Education to be the language of the catchment area which is greatly indigenous language. This amounts to preservation and promotion of indigenous culture. Indigenous languages are as well a learning areas among other options such as the Kenya Sign Language.  Beside mainstreaming culture and art in the formal curriculum, the ministry promotes culture through co-curricular activities. There is established programs that promote cultural and artistic expression through the Music, Drama, and Film Festivals held annually. This serves to nurture the learners abilities and talents, in line with the mission and vision of competency based education  ‘’Nurturing every learners Potential’’  To actualize this aspiration, Schools and colleges have established Clubs to showcase individuals diversity including culture  through inter-school/ colleges forum. Over one Million learners participated in the Kenya National Drama and Music Festivals every year within the reporting period. This strategic plan has been formulated to reposition Kenya’s education system by making it more responsive to current and emerging issues in education.  It actualizes implementation of the Competency-based education at all levels that support identifying and supporting gifted and talented people to attain their full potential. This provides students with opportunities to develop their artistic talents and appreciate cultural expressions from an early age.  It takes cognizance of the need to allocate resources for training teachers in and for additional infrastructure to meet the needs of new learning areas under CBC which include but are not limited to Art and sport pathway.  The Plan encourages partnerships between schools and local communities through Community Service Learning (CSL). The NESSP acknowledges Recognition of Prior Learning (RPL) through the KNQF policy framework that targets individuals in society seeking access to recognition of competencies regardless of their educational background, age, status, disability gender, race religion, or nationality.
Results: Recognition of Prior Learning (RPL) through the Kenya National Qualification Framework (KNQF) policy framework.  Increased participation in Kenya national music, drama, and film festivals  Increased support from partners

Title EN: Consolidation de la gouvernance et de la décentralisation des organisations professionnelles de la culture
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture
SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Cultural and creative sectors
Cultural Domain: Design,Performing Arts,Media Arts,Cinema and Audiovisual Arts,Music,Publishing,Visual Arts
Agency Implementation: CONFEDERATION NATIONALE DE LA CULTURE CNC
Main Feature: La mise en place en 2015 de la Confédération nationale de la culture (CNC) a suscité un grand espoir au sein de la société civile culturelle car étant l’aboutissement d’un long processus de structuration des acteurs des secteurs culturels et créatifs. Aussitôt, l’organe dirigeant, le Bureau exécutif s’est trouvé confronté à diverses difficultés liées entre autres à l’acquisition d’un siège fonctionnel, à la limite juridique des textes fondateurs, à l’inexistence de sections et de coordinations sur l’étendue du territoire national et à la représentativité dans diverses instances.   En vue d’améliorer la participation de la société civile culturelle à la gouvernance du secteur, le Ministère de la Communication, de la Culture, des Arts et du Tourisme a accordé un appui à sa structuration à travers un financement du Programme d’Appui aux Industries Créatives et à la Gouvernance de la Culture (PAIC-GC). Cet appui vise une meilleure organisation et mobilisation des sections dans toutes les régions ainsi que leur implication dans la mise en œuvre des politiques publiques au niveau national et décentralisé.    Conformément à son plan d’actions 2021-2023, plusieurs actions ont été menées.    Du 25 octobre au 18 décembre 2023, dans la perspective d’une meilleure appropriation des textes et d’un constat de la vitalité des instances fédérales sur le terrain, la CNC a procédé à l’organisation d’ateliers de capitalisation et d’appropriation du processus de structuration à Koudougou et à Bobo-Dioulasso. Elle a aussi entamé la consolidation des organes dirigeants des fédérations (dans les 6 filières) et de ses coordinations régionales et a procédé à l’élaboration d’un plan d’actions pour chacune des six (06) fédérations. La mise en œuvre de ce plan d’actions s’est faite en plusieurs phases :   la phase préparatoire qui a permis d’assainir l’environnement de mise en œuvre physique des actions. Il s’est agi d’organiser des rencontres de concertation en vue d’aplanir les différentes divergences qui minaient le fonctionnement de certaines fédérations, de mobiliser les différentes cibles, d’identifier les formateurs, de formaliser des contrats et des collaborations et d’élaborer les modules de formation ;    la phase exécutoire qui a porté sur l’organisation de deux (02) sessions de formation au profit des membres des associations s.
Results: La mise en œuvre de cette initiative a permis le renforcement de la démocratie et de la décentralisation des fédérations et de la CNC à travers :   la relecture des textes juridiques des fédérations et de la CNC ;   l’installation des coordinations fédérales et confédérales dans les 13 régions administratives du Burkina Faso ;   l’organisation des assemblées générales fédérales et confédérales ;   l’élaboration d’un répertoire des associations culturelles ;   l’élaboration de plans d’actions pluriannuels au sein de chaque fédération ;    la consolidation du plan d’actions triennal de la CNC ;   le renforcement de la collaboration avec les structures déconcentrées de l’administration publique;   la légitimation des coordinations régionales de la CNC et des fédérations auprès des collectivités territoriales.   Coût total de l’initiative : 64 599,5 USD   Partenaires: Ministère de la communication, de la culture, des arts et du tourisme, l’Union Européenne

Title EN: Consolidation des droits des femmes dans les milieux professionnels, judiciaires  et familiaux au Togo
Goal: Promote Human Rights And Fundamental Freedoms
SDG: SDG 5 - Achieve gender equality and empower all women and girls,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels
Area of Monitoring: Gender equality
Cultural Domain: Design,Performing Arts,Media Arts,Cinema and Audiovisual Arts,Music,Publishing,Visual Arts
Agency Implementation: Ministère chargé de la promotion de la femme
Main Feature: La mesure visant à renforcer les droits des femmes dans les milieux professionnels, judiciaires  et familiaux s’est concrétisée par révision en novembre 2022 de 4 lois : - modification de la loi portant code de sécurité sociale ; -modification de la loi portant code des personnes et de la famille en république togolaise;  - modification de la loi portant nouveau code pénal et  - modification de la loi portant code du travail. Ces lois ouvrent de nouvelles perspectives à la promotion des droits humains notamment en ce qui concerne l’égalité des genres.
Results: Grace à la présente mesure, le statut civil, les droits matrimoniaux, le positionnement familial et social de la femme sont améliorés au Togo à travers : - la protection de la femme y compris les femmes âgées et les handicapées contre le harcèlement physique, moral et économique ;  - la protection de l’emploi de la femme salariée pendant la période de grossesse, de d’accouchement, du congé de maternité et de l’allaitement ; - la garantie du droit aux conditions égalitaires de remariage de la femme divorcée ou de la veuve.

Title EN: Establishing management skills through the Creative Ecosystems Promotion and Development Programme.
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture
SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Cultural and creative sectors
Cultural Domain: Design,Performing Arts,Media Arts,Cinema and Audiovisual Arts,Music,Publishing,Visual Arts
Agency Implementation: Ministry of Cultures, Arts and Heritage, Department of Promotion of Culture and Arts, Executive Secretariat of Creative Economy.
Main Feature: The current measure, the Creative Ecosystems Promotion and Development Programme, seeks to increase involvement opportunities for cultural agents in their professional arenas. This measure is proposed as a support system that seeks to generate more sustainability in the cultural activities carried out by cultural agents, and to increase their involvement, implication and impact in the creative, artistic and cultural development of the communities they are part of.   The programme seeks to generate more integration between creators, managers, associations, enterprises and institutions to produce cultural goods and services, with the goal of having a better impact in a particular territory. The aformentioned aims to be a broader solution, working with multple approaches, like empowerment/strengthening and sustainability in their processes while/as long as they create economic well-being, social cohesion and territorial development. In practice, this measure is implemented through the following actions:   (1) Training in creative economy: training, practical workshops, classes, courses and supporting learning materials on topics such as design and preparation of projects, communication, promotion and commercialisation in culture, administration and finance in culture, measuring objectives and social impact in culture, heritage in cultural projects, among others.   (2) Initiatives for strengthening the value chain in cultural processes: financing for cultural agents that develop projects for public space reactivation and improvement through cultural activities, with the involvement of local communities.   (3) Promotion of association and networks within culture: funding for cultural agents that develop and implement management processes through asociation or networks at different stages of the cultural value chain and at different territorial levels (neighbourhood, commune, region, national, international or others).   (4) Promotion of participation by and valuing of the creative economy in the territories: funds for implementing gatherings, fairs, seminars, reports and publications, participatory laboratories and other activities for connecting with the sector. In accordance with the monitoring framework of the 2005 Convention, this measure is part of the actions that "support the development of dynamic cultural and creative sectors".
Results: For the 2023 call for projects of the programme for promotion and development of creative ecosystems, 148 projects applied for funding, 41 of those from the Metropolitan Region (27.7% of the total) and 107 from other regions of the country (72.3% of the total). There were 59 selected projects, and taking into account the project teams, the number of direct beneficiaries reached 840. In terms of regional coverage, all of the country's regions are represented, reaching 58 communes.   The regions representing the least number of projects are Tarapacá, Antofagasta, Coquimbo, Aysén and Magallanes (one project), and the regions representing the most number of projects are Santiago Metropolitan Region (20 projects), Valparaíso (six projects), Arica and Araucanía (five projects). It should be noted that the projects supported focused on gender, such as the “Feria de Artes y Oficios Lunisolar. Mujeres creadoras IV”, internationalisation through, for example, the “Valdivia International Film Festival” project or events that connect culture and tourism like the “Birds, Crafts and Tourism Festival" in Curaco de Velez (Chiloé).   Lastly, interdisciplinary and/or intersectoral initiatives across the whole territory were financed, in order to boost economic growth, community impact and the strengthening of local creative ecosystems. At the same, funding is sought for complementary activities at events such as festivals, fairs, meetings, markets, or similar, in the creative economy field, that take place in different regions of Chile.
Financial Ressources: 2023: USD 1,600,000 (annual budget).

Title EN: Content diversity in mass media. Regulation for mandatory cultural programming in free-to-air television.
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture
SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Media diversity
Agency Implementation: National Television Council (CNTV).
Main Feature: According to the dispositions of Article 19 Nº 12 of the Political Constitution of the Republic of Chile, and in Law Nº 20.750, part of the importance of television and as mass media, is its capacity to grow and develop culture and knowledge, as well as value of heritage and the national and universal identity of Chile. In this context, the National Television Council (CNTV), in the exercise of its constitutional and legal authority, agreed on the "Normas sobre la obligación de los servicios de televisión de transmitir un mínimo de programas culturales a la semana" ("Regulations on the obligation of television services to broadcast a minimum of cultural programmes per week").   This regulatory definition, from October 2014, with its modification in May 2015, establishes that "the concession licensees of limited television services, will be obliged to boradcast at least four hours of cultural programmes per week" (free translation). At the same, it establishes that "cultural programmes shall be understood to be those that refer to values that emanate from existing multicultural identities in the country, as well as those related to civics, those destined for strengthening national, regional or local identities, such as holidays and cultural celebrations and those destined to promote universal heritage and, in particular, national heritage" (free translation).   Regarding the broadcast time-slot, the regulation indicates that "at least two of the four hours of cultural programming must be broadcast in prime time slots, which are laid down in these regulations, with the day and time within the aforementioned time slots subject to each television service's own criteria" (free translation). This measure is part of the "policies and measures that promote and protect freedoms of creation and expression and participation".
Results: In general, positive change has been observed since the implementation of the regulation, both from the perspective of the cultural programming on offer, and its consumption by the audiences. Comparing 2013, the year prior to the implementation of the regulation, with 2016, when it comes into force, an increase of more than four percent is observed in cultural programme viewing time on free-to-air television.   At the same time, in general it can be seen that the channels broadcast more hours of cultural programming than those required by CNTV. It is specially useful to acknowledge that the television industry has made efforts in programme innovation in order to offer audiovisual cultural content, a demonstrating important progress as a result of the implementation of the current applicable regulation.
Financial Ressources: No budget.
Recommandations: The CNTV Department of Studies prepares the “Balance de Programación Cultural” each year, with systematised statistical information on the application of the regulations related to this type of programming. For 2022, the folowing data stands out.   (1) The cultural offering stays around 7% of total programming. The channels broadcast more hours of programming than those required by CNTV. At the same time, the television industry efforts to innovate in the cultural content offering in audiovisual format, are evident.   (2) Although the reception and reach of these programmes show a continous decline in the last four years, mirroring a general tendency in free-to-air television, the time people dedicate watching this type of programmes, has constantly and significantly increased during the period, which indicates an interest in the cultural content offered by television.   (3) The data shows that cultural content surpasses the four hours established by the regulation and that this content, associated with clear and defined time-slots, build engaged and established audiences.   (4) According to profiling data on television audiences, with this measure it has been possible to create cultural content that enable reaching diverse audiences

Title EN: Co-production of an Italian classic play a Servant to Two Master
Goal: Achieve A Balanced Flow Of Cultural Goods And Services And Increase The Mobility Of Artists And Cultural Professionals
SDG: SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 10 - Reduce inequality within and among countries,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Flow of cultural goods and services
Agency Implementation: Ethiopian National Theatre
Main Feature: Introduction The Italian Institute of Culture in Addis Ababa and the National Theater of Ethiopia embarked on a significant cultural collaboration to bring Italian theatrical expertise to Ethiopia. This initiative resulted in the production and presentation of the Italian classic Commedia dell'Arte play, A Servant to Two Masters, for an Ethiopian audience. The project not only showcased Italian art but also served as a platform for cross-cultural exchange and artistic development.  Key Contributors A team of experts from Italy, including a theater director, scene designer, stage construction specialist, costume designer, and choreographer, was brought in to lead the production. Their involvement was crucial in ensuring that the play maintained its authentic Italian roots while being adapted to resonate with the Ethiopian audience.  Objectives The primary objectives of the collaboration were:  Cultural Exchange: To foster mutual understanding and appreciation between Italian and Ethiopian cultures through theater.  Exposure to Global Performing Arts: To expose Ethiopian performers and audiences to global trends in performing arts, particularly Italian theater traditions.  Experience Sharing: To create a platform for Ethiopian and Italian theater practitioners to exchange knowledge and experiences.  Capacity Building: To provide Ethiopian theater professionals with hands-on training through workshops focused on Italian comedic techniques, specifically the nuances of Commedia dell'Arte.  Production and Performance The play A Servant to Two Masters was staged at the National Theater of Ethiopia for six months. The extended run allowed a broad audience to experience the production, thereby maximizing its cultural impact. During this period, workshops and interactive sessions were held, providing Ethiopian theater practitioners with valuable insights into Italian theatrical practices.  Conclusion This collaboration between the Italian Institute of Culture and the National Theater of Ethiopia stands as a testament to the power of cultural exchange. Through the shared language of theater, both nations were able to celebrate their rich artistic traditions while learning from one another, fostering a lasting relationship between Italian and Ethiopian cultural communities.
Results: The partnership between the Italian Institute of Culture and the Ethiopian National Theater marked a significant milestone in cultural exchange, focusing on the introduction and adaptation of Italian theatrical traditions to the Ethiopian stage. The collaboration centered around the production of the Italian classic Commedia dell'Arte play A Servant to Two Masters, which was presented to Ethiopian audiences with the involvement of Italian theater experts.  Knowledge and Skills Transfer Through this partnership, Ethiopian theater professionals, particularly those affiliated with Addis Abeba Theaters, gained new insights into Italian humor and acquired specialized skills in staging plays. The Italian team, comprising a theater director, scene designer, stage construction specialist, costume designer, and choreographer, provided in-depth training and workshops, enabling local professionals to enhance their technical and artistic capabilities. This training included aspects of Italian comedic techniques, stage design, and costume creation, significantly broadening the participants' understanding of global theater practices.  Cultural Exchange and Impact The collaboration facilitated a dynamic cultural exchange between Italy and Ethiopia, allowing Ethiopian theater enthusiasts to experience a new style of play that blended Italian traditions with local interpretations. This exchange not only introduced Ethiopian audiences to the rich heritage of Italian theater but also encouraged the appreciation of diverse international art forms. The project successfully bridged cultural gaps, fostering a deeper understanding and respect for the performing arts across borders.  Achievement of Objectives The partnership effectively achieved its objectives, particularly in strengthening cultural ties between the two nations. Ethiopian performers and theater professionals benefited from unique learning opportunities that expanded their artistic horizons and improved their technical skills. The production was well-received by the general public, enjoying a six-month run at the Ethiopian National Theater, which underscored its success in engaging and educating audiences about the art of Commedia dell'Arte.  In conclusion, this collaboration not only enriched the Ethiopian theater landscape but also solidified the cultural relationship between Italy and Ethiopia. The successful integration of Italian theater practices into the Ethiopian context has left a lasting impact, providing a foundation for future cultural exchanges and collaborative artistic endeavors.

The project was launched on the island of Sal with the aim of distinguishing the city of Santa Maria as the first copyright-friendly city in the world. Since its launch, the @ Flabel program has distinguished the Santa Maria Festival with its first Copyright Friendly Seal. With this example, the project spread to other Cape Verdean municipalities and music users. Area of Monitoring: Cultural and creative sectors
Cultural Domain: Media Arts,Cinema and Audiovisual Arts,Music,Publishing,Visual Arts
Agency Implementation: Kenya Cultural Centre
Main Feature: Kenya Cultural Centre incorporating the Kenya National Theatre in partnership with the Kenya International Theatre Festival Trust with support from the Sports, Arts and Social Development Fund (SASDF) implemented a capacity building and competition program, ‘County Theatre Fiesta’, for grassroot theatre companies/groups in the following counties; Mombasa, Kiambu, Embu, Nakuru, Kisumu and Uasin Gishu. County Theatre Fiesta was implemented through the government’s Talanta Hela Initiative. County Theatre Fiesta aimed at building the capacity of upcoming theatre practitioners to create professional theatre pieces and perform theatre production in a professional way hence improve the quality of the productions, economically empower the artists and broaden the entertainment scope for Kenyans. The program used competition to train all theatre companies that registered for the competition by holding a 10-day training in each county before the main competition. The registered theatre companies were trained on how to produce professional theatre productions. They also had an opportunity to use a professional theatre space as most of the groups/theatre companies use schools, churches and social halls
Results: Creation of new markets for local theatre companies/groups, Creation of job opportunities for Kenyan youth with acting talent both locally and internationally; Expansion of audiences for Kenyan theatre productions; and the exportation of Kenyan theatre to international platforms, improving our visibility; Promotion of theatre going culture at the counties

Title EN: Cultural strategies by Federal States and municipalities
Goal: Integrate Culture In Sustainable Development Frameworks
SDG: SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: National sustainable development policies and plans
Cultural Domain: Design,Performing Arts,Media Arts,Cinema and Audiovisual Arts,Music,Publishing,Visual Arts
Agency Implementation: City of Vienna, Federal State of Styria; City of Salzburg, Federal State of Vorarlberg, Federal State of Lower Austria
Main Feature: Culture and Arts Strategy 2030 – The Future of Culture and Arts in the Federal State of Styria From spring 2021 to May 2023, the “Culture and Arts Strategy 2030 – The Future of Culture and Arts in the Federal State of Styria” was developed in a far-reaching artistic, cultural and participatory process. The process started out with round tables and discussions among representatives of large Styrian cultural institutions and shareholders of the Province of Styria, the Styrian festival landscape, the interest-based community, and the culture and arts committee. In addition, preliminary round tables were held in the seven Styrian regions and Graz involving persons engaged in the cultural sector of all disciplines and regions as well as regional managers and persons engaged in the areas of education, social services and society. These initial steps created the basis for a far-reaching discussion process which was aimed at the status quo and the requirements for culture and arts in the future. Five main fields of future action were identified: funding and fair pay; regional profiles and cooperation between initiatives and institutions, cultural hubs in the regions; interdisciplinary and interdepartmental work; workshops for the future. For all of those fields, recommendations were developed that will determine the framework for the implementation of cultural–political guidelines for a future-oriented arts and culture sector in Styria.  Cultural Strategy Salzburg 2024 Under the slogan Kultur.Leben.Räume (“Culture.Life.Spaces”), the City of Salzburg, in cooperation with representatives of civil society (Salzburg 2024 Initiative) developed the Cultural Strategy Salzburg. Representatives from the arts and cultural sector, the city and Federal State of Salzburg, the (creative) business community, tourism, science, education as well as social work were involved in the process. The process furthered a broad understanding of culture, based on the existing heterogeneity of the sectors and society. The initiative was launched in 2018 and runs until 2024. The final report entails short-, medium- and long-term recommendations, that will shape cultural policy measures in the coming years.  Cultural Strategy Vorarlberg 2023 (Update): In 2023, the existing cultural strategy of the Federal State of Vorarlberg was comprehensively updated. The update was based on a multi-stage participatory process that included, among other things, a Kulturenquete (conference format, 2022). In the framework Kulturenquete the existing cultural strategy was discussed and fundamental positions for the strategy updated were outlined. The results of the Kulturenquete formed the basis for the work of a strategy group consisting of six experts responsible for drafting the update. As a result, the 2023 cultural strategy focuses on areas such as fairness and fair pay, diversity and cultural participation, cultural work for and with young people and young adults as well as environment, climate and sustainability.  2nd Cultural Programme Federal State of Upper Austria The 2nd Cultural Programme of the Federal State of Upper Austria defines the strategic fields of action of cultural policy in Upper Austria (creating art in the 21st century, communicating; laboratories of the future; our values (cultural heritage, popular culture); fostering new talent; art as an internal driving force and external messenger). Art and culture are no longer discussed on a sectoral basis, but rather following important areas of action. The implementation process is based on two pillars: a) a new, annual series of cultural policy-oriented events (starting in 2021) and b) starting in 2022 and every three years thereafter, "implementation reports" to the Upper Austrian Parliament.  Revision and Re-publication of the Cultural Strategy of the Federal State of Lower Austria (2021) In 2021, the Federal State of Lower Austria adopted a revised cultural strategy. This strategy follows four guidelines: 1) Participative - Cultural participation for everyone, 2) Creative - New approaches through innovation, 3) Cooperative - Strengthening the power of networking, 4) Diverse - Living diversity and equality. Substantively, five key areas of action are defined: 1) Create new possibilities for cultural participation for families, 2) Harness the opportunities of digitalization, 3) Live sustainably & climate responsibly, 4) Develop culture & tourism as a holistic experience, 5) Create model regions for art and culture.

Agency Implementation: Federal Ministry for Arts, Culture, the Civil Service and Sport; Federal Ministry for Labour and Economy, Federal Ministry of Finance, Covid-19-Finanzierungsagentur des Bundes GmbH (COFAG)
Main Feature: The culture and arts sector in Austria was severely affected by the (health policy) measures implemented to combat the COVID-19 pandemic. All cultural institutions suffered from a major loss of revenues (e.g. from ticket sales or rental of venues). The loss of income posed an existential threat to many freelance artists, cultural operators and NGOs in the field of culture. Starting with March 2020 the Federal Government adopted a series of general and sector-specific measures to support the cultural and creative sectors (see below). Moreover, various relevant measures were implemented by regional governments (see separate measure). Several times, the measures were extended and the budgets increased. The Federal Ministry for Arts, Culture, the Civil Service and Sport launched a hotline, a mailbox and regularly updated FAQs on the website. In addition to the regular culture budget, the Austrian federal government has supported the arts and culture sector with around 450 million euros in additional funding in 2020 and 2021 (designed specifically to combat the effects of the COVID 19 pandemic). Furthermore, actors and institutions in the arts and culture sector also benefited considerably from funding measures not designed specifically for the sector.  The measures in detail:  COVID-19 Fund In order to (partially) compensate loss of income, the COVID-19 Fund was set up in the framework of Künstlersozialversicherungsfonds (KSVF; “Artists' Social Insurance Fund”) in March 2020 to supplement previously available support options. The COVID-19 Fund of the KSVF was set up as a culture-specific support option to compensate for loss of income due to closures, postponements and cancellations. This fund initially provided support of EUR 1,000 to artists and was then continued as an instrument for those who did not qualify for either the “bridge financing fund for self-employed artists” (see below) or the “hardship fund” (see below). In addition to artists, cultural mediators were eligible. The COVID-19 fund was endowed with up to EUR 50 million until 31 December 2022 and was intended to ensure rapid assistance.  Bridge Financing Fund for self-employed artists The Bridge Financing Fund for self-employed artists was available to persons who create, practise, communicate or teach art and culture and who are insured with the Social Insurance for the Self-Employed (SVS). The total volume of the fund amounted to EUR 175 million on 31 December 2022 and was administered by the SVS. Benefits from this fund could also be drawn in 2022; applications were possible until 30 April 2022.  Hardship Fund for self-employed artists and cultural workers The Hardship Fund, administered by the Austrian Federal Economic Chamber, was designed to support self- employed artists and cultural workers (micro-enterprises, EPUs, freelancers, newly self-employed) in the event of loss of income. Applications had to be submitted on a monthly basis. Compensation was paid for 80% or 90% of the net loss of income. Benefits from this fund could also be claimed in 2022; applications were possible until 2 May 2022.  Non-Profit Support Fund (NPO-Fund) The fund for non-profit associations and organizations, established by the Federal Ministry for Arts, Culture, the Civil Service and Sport in July 2020 and administered by austria wirtschaftsservice (aws), provided cost subsidies for non-profit organizations to cushion the loss of income caused by the COVID-19 crisis. Applicants could receive subsidies for 100% of fixed costs and a flat rate for maintenance costs. In addition, an NPO lockdown grant was made available, which was structured in the same way as the lockdown revenue replacement (see below) and was paid out in 2021. A total of EUR 829.2 million was granted, EURO 121.5 million of which for the arts and culture sector.  Protective Shield for events in the field of culture and sport The protective shield for events, handled by the Austrian Hotel and Tourism Bank, offered grants for financial disadvantages resulting from a COVID-19-related cancellation or significant restrictions on events. Eligible costs were non-cancellable expenses for third-party services in the value chain (e.g. suppliers, technology, artists, florists, venues, etc.). Under the protective shield for events (grant model I) funding was provided for up to 90 per cent of the eligible costs (max. EUR 2 million). In a further step, the protective shield was extended as a liability model with a maximum liability assumption of EUR 10 million per organiser ("protective shield for events II"). This involved liability for up to 80 per cent of the proven financial disadvantage. A total of EUR 300 million was made available for this purpose.  Fixed Cost Subsidy for Companies The fixed cost subsidy was open to all profit-orientated companies, i.e. also commercial cultural enterprises or companies as well as Single-Person Businesses (EPUs); applications were accepted via FinanzOnline and processed by the Austrian Covid-19 Funding Agency (COFAG). Fixed costs were reimbursed up to 100% (depending on the loss of income). In addition, a default bonus was created, which was paid out in 2021. Various costs were eligible.  Lockdown revenue compensation (directly / indirectly affected) To provide rapid support to the business sectors in Austria that have been directly or indirectly affected by the lockdown / measures to prevent the spreading of the COVID-19 disease, lockdown revenue compensation was introduced as an immediate grant. In 2020, cultural businesses directly affected were reimbursed 80% of their turnover for the lockdown in November and 50% in December. Those indirectly affected (e.g. artists) were recognised with the same thresholds and payments were made in 2021. The fund was processed by COFAG.  Comeback Grant for film and TV productions The Comeback Grant, implemented by the Federal Ministry of Labour and Economy and the Federal Ministry for Arts, Culture, the Civil Service and Sport, enabled independent film production companies to continue filming cinema and TV productions that had been interrupted or postponed due to the COVID-19 pandemic. The grant could be applied for until 30 June 2022 from the occurrence of an actual interruption or short-term postponement due to COVID-19-related measures, for the additional expenses incurred as a result. A total of up to EUR 25 million in funding was made available for this purpose.  Neustart Kultur (“Restart Culture”) With the Neustart Kultur (“Restart Culture”) programme launched in March 2021, the Federal Ministry for Arts, Culture, the Civil Service and Sport offered a support package that helped Austrian artists and cultural institutions to resume and continue their artistic and creative activities and contributed to their economic resilience. The aim was to support the arts and culture sector on its way back to normality. A total of around EUR 20 million was paid out in five calls for proposals: Package # 1: “From stage to video”, for the realisation and accessibility of stage formats via video stream. Volume EUR 2 million  Package #2: “Perspectives.Innovation.Art”, for new artistic formats that did not fit into any of the conventional funding schemes, Volume EUR 2.6 million.  Package #3: “Fresh air. Funding for outdoor projects”, Volume EUR 2 million   Package # 4: “Funding for investments” to finance measures to modernise rooms, technical equipment, digital investments that help make cultural institutions fit and attractive for the coming years, Volume: EUR 9.40 million  Package # 5 “Audience development” for measures to retain and increase the participation of existing and new audiences, Volume: EUR 4 million  Structural support programme The Structural Support Programme was a special funding programme in accordance with § 2a of the Arts Promotion Act and was available in 2021. Its aim was to support cultural institutions or individuals working in the arts that, despite the utilisation of all possible aid measures, continued to face existential economic difficulties. The structural support programme was endowed with EUR 10 million. The Federal Ministry for Arts, Culture, the Civil Service and Sport awarded special funding of up to EUR 50,000 per application as part of the structural support programme to maintain diversity in the cultural sector. A total of EUR 2.978 million was paid out in 2021.  VAT Reduction VAT for art and culture has been reduced from 10% and 13% respectively to 5% applied from 07/2020 until 12/2021.
Results: The Ministry for Arts, Culture, the Civil Service and Sport responded immediately to the COVID-19 health crisis with a mix of measures to combat the effects of the coronavirus on the arts and culture sector. The measures alleviated the economic hardship caused by COVID-19 for artists, cultural workers and cultural institutions.
Financial Ressources: s. above
Recommandations: All measures were evaluated quantitatively, some of which were also subjected to a qualitative evaluation. An audit was also carried out by the Austrian Court of Audit
