Main Feature: Describe the main features of the policy/measure:  Description of the procedure for the exchange  accessible format copies of certain works and other subject-matter protected by copyright and related rights for the benefit of persons who are blind, visually impaired or otherwise  print disabled text (hereinafter – the Description) was prepared to ensure the requirements of Regulation (EU) 2017/1563 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 13 September 2017 on the cross-border exchange between the European Union and third countries of accessible format copies of certain works and other subject matter protected by copyright and related rights for the benefit of persons who are blind, visually impaired or otherwise print-disabled and also implementing provisions of Article 25 of the Law on Copyright and Related Rights (for more detail: https://e-seimas.lrs.lt/portal/legalAct/lt/TAD/28bbb420560611e485f39f55fd139d01?jfwid=bkaxlpm8). The purpose of the Description is to determine the procedure for the exchange of accessible format copies of works or other objects  protected by copyright and related rights intended for persons with print disabled by authorized entities operating in the territory of the Republic of Lithuania with the 2013 June 27 Ratified parties (hereinafter referred to as parties to the Marrakesh Treaty), authorized entities and disabled beneficiaries of the Marrakesh Treaty to Facilitate Access to Published Works for Persons Who Are Blind, Visually Impaired, or Otherwise Print Disabled (https://www.wipo.int/wipolex/en/text/301016). Pursuant to regulations of the Description, the Lithuanian Audiosensory Library coordinates the activities of Authorised Bodies established in the Republic of Lithuania.
Results: A favourable legal environment enables cooperation between the Lithuanian authorized institution, the Lithuanian Audiosensory Library (LAB), and foreign partners. LAB has signed a cooperation agreement with the WIPO platform Accessible Books Consortium (ABC) for the exchange of publications in accessible formats, and cooperates and provides its readers with access to the Bookshare platform.  In 2023, 55 accessible format publications from ABC and 1358 publications from Bookshare platforms were downloaded, most of them in English, Russian and Polish languages.  4 LAB publications have also been submitted to the ABC platform after receiving requests from authorized authorities in the US and India.

Agency Implementation: Lithuanian Council for Culture
Main Feature: The main objective of the measure is to increase Lithuanian businesses' competitive advantage, social responsibility and added value through design solutions based on the principles of innovation, the digital and circular economy, involving cultural and creative sectors that were affected by the COVID-19 pandemic.  Design Wings involved companies from all over Lithuania, for which design solutions are developed by emerging design professionals and supervised by experienced mentors — highly skilled design experts. Participating companies develop design solutions for a product, for communication design (images, messages), or processes, services and interfaces.  Measure was initiated by the Ministry of Culture of the Republic of Lithuania and Innovation Agency, implemented by the Lithuanian Council for Culture.
Results: This project connected business people, designers, and mentors – with different skills and experiences from all parts of the country.   The apprentice designers who completed their studies in 2018-2022 were invited to participate in the project as the employees of the creative segment, as they were affected by the COVID-19 pandemic and lost their income and the possibility to improve their professional skills. During the project, they received scholarships, improved their professional skills while collaborating with the enterprise. One of the benefits was that Lithuanians who graduated abroad were welcomed to return home and work for a local business. The other group benefiting from the project were representatives of small and medium-size businesses who did not have the possibility to employ designers paying them adequate market price for their services.  All the project participants had the possibility to communicate with one another online and during live meetings where they shared their experiences and ideas. The work regarding design solutions was carried out on an inclusive basis: designers could receive assistance or advice from professionals from different design branches (graphic, product, service, fashion, or UX) in case it was necessary. Design solutions corresponded to the principles of circular economy and digitalization, i.e., they were environment-friendly and aspired not to cause consequences for future generations and nature. The fundamental Design Thinking principles were constantly in use.  Outcomes of the project:  Young designers affected by the pandemic financially and professionally improved their skills, acquired new knowledge, and established new contacts.  Small and medium-size enterprises acquired theoretical knowledge and received tangible design solutions created according to their needs. Professional design solutions created during the project helped to increase the enterprise's competitiveness and expand the business by offering new or improved products and services.  During the project, 34 design solutions meeting sustainability and circular economy principles were created that are simultaneously commercialized, adapted for production, and realized.

Area of Monitoring: Cultural and creative sectors
Agency Implementation: Phare Ponleu Selpak
Main Feature: Describe the main features of the measure/initiative (800 words):  Develop targeted community outreach and engagement activities to create more meaningful social impacts and play a bigger role in arts & culture education, promotion and development through conducting of arts and cultural events and festivals is one of the goals in the PPSA’s 5 years strategic plans that contains several objectives to be achieved: -	Deeper engagement with alumni to ensure their success and increase their contribution to the school. -	Create an artist incubation program with a fund to provide support to emerging artists’ creations. -	Engage wider local community with targeted arts awareness and education programming on campus, through satellite programs. -	Bring “Phare in the City” through a location suitable to engage community in the arts at many levels while creating a space for shows to generate revenue for the school. -	Profile Phare’s performing and visual arts, engage local artists and create opportunities for collaboration with other organizations and foreign artists through festivals (Tini Tinou, S’Art Urban Art Festival…etc.). -	Support the development of communities by addressing social issues using art (social circus, forum theatre, art therapy). -	Increase the targeted areas where our child protection program provides a safety net to the most vulnerable children and families. The following programs have been designated to implement the above objectives: 1- Artistic Programs Artistic training is the main program at PPS consisting of a Performing Arts School (PAS) and a Visual and Applied Arts School (VAAS).  A- Performing Arts School (PAS): The goal of the performing Arts School is to provide performing arts skills including circus, dance, music and theatre to children and young people for future employment opportunities in culture and arts industry. Performing Arts School has four main disciplines: Circus, Theatre, Music, and Dance. The PAS in charge of performing at the events and festival.  B- Visual and Applied Arts School (VAAS): The Visual and Applied Art School in Phare Ponleu Selpak is a first of its kind, high-quality, vocational art school offering everything from leisure children art classes to professional training in graphic design, visual arts, and animation. VAAS seeks to contribute to a successful shift between the current agricultural economy to a tertiary-based economy of Cambodia’s future. VAAS offers graphic design, animation, and visual arts. The VAAS in charge of decorating and make the events a spectacular.  2- Social Support and Students Development Programs Socia Support and Students Development Program plays a big role when come to an organization of a community-based event and festival. They communicated with the local authorities and families for the events and festival. Also, they in charge of students’ and artists’ safety and security  3- Community Outreach and Engagement (COE) While PPS plays a big role as a sustainable economic agent for the surrounding communities providing jobs, training the young generation and attracting visitors in Battambang and aims to play an ever more proactive role in the community through the following activities the COE plays the bigger role.  Arts & Culture Promotion Phare Ponleu Selpak is one of the main artistic influencers in Cambodia and contributes to the dynamism of Cambodian arts and culture. PPS is also a well-known tourist attraction, giving foreigners an opportunity to experience traditional dances through the student shows. PPS aims to play a bigger role in bringing arts to the communities by more arts education programs aimed at the local residences. PPS believes the sustainability, growth and evolution of the various art forms will only happen if the local communities build a deeper appreciation and take an active role for the arts and culture.  Alumni Relations & Artistic Incubator Changing lives through the arts doesn't stop as soon as our students graduate. PPS keeps close relationships with its alumni and artists and supports them to start their artistic careers and get visibility thanks to many collaborations, exhibitions, tours, local performances, workshops and gainful employment through Phare Performing Social Enterprise. PPS aims to strengthen its alumni engagement and support their initiatives through an Artistic Incubation Program.  Collaborations with NGOs PPS works closely with many arts and non-arts NGOs based in Battambang and other provinces. PPS continues to collaborate with Epic arts, Cambodian Living Arts etc. in promoting arts and hosting activities together. PPS also works closely with Child Rights and Protection NGOs and many community- based organizations to provide integrated social support services and spread the access of arts.
Results: What are the results achieved so far through the implementation of the measure/initiative? (400 words)  Within the past four years in implementing the “Develop targeted community outreach and engagement activities to create more meaningful social impacts and play a bigger role in arts & culture education, promotion and development through conducting of arts and cultural events and festivals” Phare Ponleu Selpak managed to conduct 3 festivals, ROS’ Battambang, Tini Tinou International Circus, and S’Art Urban Art Festival.  ROS’ (taste in Khmer) Battambang Festival – is the food and arts festival initiated in 2020 just right before Covid-19 hit Cambodia hardly. It gathered students and artists of performing arts and visual arts together with local food vendors to make the festival a spectacular bringing in thousands of audience members to experience different performances of various arts forms while tasting local foods at the same time. In the original plan, this festival meant to be held as an annual festival, but due to Covid-19 and resources, we could not make it until today.  Tini Tinou (here and there in Khmer) International Circus Festival – is a biennial festival that conducts every even year. 2022 marked as its 12th edition after silenced for many years due to pandemic and resources. The festival brought many foreign circus artists from Europe and Asia to have workshops, exchanges and showcase with the Cambodia’s circus artists. The artists performed their mixed discipline to the publics as the results of the exchange and workshop. The festival brought in many local and international audiences to experience different performances from different countries.  S'Art Urban Art Festival - is a biennial festival that conducts every odd year shifting with Circus Festival. 2023 marked as its 3rd edition after its soft launched in 2018 at PPS compound and the city-wide in 2019; the festival was cancelled in 2021 due to the pandemic. The festival in 2023 was comprised many activities like, hip hop workshop, showcase and battle, giant puppet workshop and creation, various art workshops, exhibition, mural painting and graffiti, after-dark showcase and activities, artists talk, panel discussion, and finale arts parade and concert. This year, the festival invited the artists for mural and graffiti from Indonesia, Malaysia, Thailand, Taiwan, Vietnam, France, Canada, and Cambodia. Also, the professional breakers from Vietnam, Laos, and Cambodia. The festival brought in more than 7000 people to engaged and attended. The mural paintings on the historic building’s wall of Battambang city have brought in tourists to Battambang which contributing to its economic growth.

Title EN: Developing a road map for the Nakuru creative city
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture
SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Digital environment
Cultural Domain: Design,Performing Arts,Media Arts,Cinema and Audiovisual Arts,Music,Publishing,Visual Arts
Agency Implementation: Creative Economy Structure
Main Feature: Describe the main features of the measure/initiative (800 words): The Creative Working Group & Creative Economy Structure put forward a timely suggestion to effectively identify the cultural hot stops in the city by developing a digital application that guides anyone interested in visiting our great city. The digital application will also take cognizance and develop an artiste database/index guide for the Nakuru Cultural Ecosystem. This was a welcome idea as the same was also a potential project by the Nakuru City Board in their Strategic Plan after Nakuru was awarded a city charter.It was also proposed that the mapping of the creative hubs shall incorporate the pop-up spots that were identified in around the city neighbour-hoods such as Racecourse, Rhonda, Kivumbini, London, Free Area and many more through the Reggae For Peace organized by Nakuru Players Theatre in conjunction with Mystic Band over the December holidays. The initiative sought to have musical concerts within these grassroots and hard to reach areas to help the communities therein to reimagine their surroundings and spur development through creativity and culture. The Working Group proposes that the mapping of our great city should be given priority and preferably be conducted within two financial years (F.Y 22/23 and 23/24).In a bid to support Nakuru’s local creative communities to develop an encouraging policy and economic environment, and further connect creative professionals and local creative businesses to international networks and platforms, the Task Force proposed the need for a culture policy. Taking into account that the formulation and enactment of any public policy involves extensive public participation, engagement with relevant stakeholders, intense lobbying and positive political goodwill, the Task Force suggested that the two financial years preferably (F.Y 22/23 and 23/24) can be sufficient in achieving this great feat. The team unanimously agreed on the need for immediate and intensive sensitization programme of the status of Nakuru City. It was observed that most people were not aware of Nakuru City as a UNESCO creative city, the obligations and perks it had for its people. It was agreed that these workshops shall not only aim to inform but also used to source and identify relevant stakeholders who would help out in this noble course. The stakeholders herein include the following (but not limited to): Nakuru County Government, Nakuru City Board, Museums and Historic sites (Hyrax Hill and, Kariandusi prehistoric sites, Lord Egerton Castle, Elsa House, Utamaduni and Eagle Point museums and historic sites), Libraries(Kenya National Library Service), Nakuru Players Theatre Institutions of learning, Creative Communities and Groups(Council of International Organizations of Folk Festivals), Community Based Organizations(Honeymoon Hill CBO and Njoki Karuoya creative and media centre), parastatals, private companies and the general public. These workshops would be conducted by The Creative Economy Working Group in partnership with the City Board which has internalized the subject matter herein and can disseminate the same effectively. The timeline for the aforementioned workshops shall be ongoing Between March and November when the city shall be commemorating the attaining of the UNESCO Creative City status.
Results: The Creative Economy Working Group milestones achieved by Nakuru City since acquiring of the status of a UNESCO Creative City: Mapping and identifying the pop-up spots in and around the city neighbour-hoods such as Racecourse, Rhonda, Kivumbini, London, Free Area and many more through the Reggae For Peace organized by Nakuru Players Theatre in conjunction with Mystic Band over the 2022, 23 December holidays. The initiative sought to have musical concerts and street festivals within these grassroots and hard to reach areas to help the communities therein to reimagine their surroundings and spur development through creativity and culture. The other initiatives are offering spaces to photographers visual artists to express and grow their art for economic development. Great support and political goodwill from County Government of Nakuru in this worthy venture. The Working Group has been having planning meetings which formed part on the development agendas as by the City Plans and the CIDP with the confirmation of and support His Excellency the Governor of Nakuru H.E Susan Kihika  The formation of the roadmap of Nakuru City as a UNESCO Creative City which featured the development of the policy . The Working Group was able to bring together stakeholders and creatives for public sensitization and participation  through the support of Twaweza Communications. This has so far gained momentum in developing the The Culture & Creative Economy Policy for the City which has assist both the city and creative practitioners in developing programs and plans.

Title EN: Developing the young public for music, particularly classical music, and creating playing fields and long-term, sustainable development opportunities for young and independent artists, serving as a bridge to bring renowned international classical artists
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture
SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Partnering with civil society
Agency Implementation: Viet Nam Youth Music Institute
Main Feature: The Viet Nam Youth Music Institute is a non-profit social organization with a mission to inspire young people to build long-term relationships with music, especially classical music, while creating playing fields, long-lasting and sustainable development opportunities for young artists, independent artists, and bringing renowned classical artists and experts from around the world to Viet Nam. The Viet Nam Youth Music Institute is currently operating as a legal entity as a Social Enterprise, dedicating itself to a series of diverse artistic performance activities, classical music festivals for everyone, educational programs, and cultural and artistic exchanges domestically and internationally with an aim of bringing classical music - a rich art form of the world closer to numerous Vietnamese audiences through major initiatives: Viet Nam Youth Orchestra (VYO): As the first multinational youth orchestra in Viet Nam, the VYO provides a place for young people who love classical instruments to practice with leading artists in Viet Nam and meet, interact, and engage in weekly cultural and artistic activities together. The VYO has explored masterpieces of world classical music and performed works featuring diverse cultures such as the Northwestern Highlands and Central Highlands and the Hue royal court of Viet Nam (Tran Manh Hung: Symphony "Thien Thanh"), English folk songs (Vaughan Williams: English Folk Song Suite), melodies and harmonies using traditional Japanese musical instruments (Yuzo Toyama: Rhapsody for Orchestra), etc. Open Dialogue and Concert Series and Triangle Concert Series: These are two chamber music concert series held in Ha Noi, creating performance venues for artists, especially young and independent artists. Artists have a chance to listen and realize their own concerts with a professional event organizing team, providing an open, intimate, and fully equipped space for working, creating, and performing with the support of experienced artistic curators & education curators. The Open Dialogue and Concert Series and the Triangle Concert Series have successfully organized debut stages and supported many new artists/artist groups in the classical music community. Viet Nam Classical Music Festival 2024 (VCMF): Lasting for 8 days including various artistic performances such as chamber music, opera performances, art exhibitions, symphonic orchestra performances, symposia to connect with specialists, masterclasses, and workshops held at various indoor and outdoor venues in Da Lat City, the Viet Nam Classical Music Festival is the first large-scale classical music festival successfully organized in Viet Nam. With the participation of 135 artists from both North and South, veteran artists, promising young artists, and big names in the world classical music market, the Viet Nam Classical Music Festival is a vibrant cultural and artistic exchange event between regions of Viet Nam and especially between Viet Nam and the world. VYO Exchange Program: This is one of the annual projects of the Viet Nam Youth Orchestra, aiming to bring talented young orchestras from abroad to Viet Nam and vice versa. In 2024, the VYO Exchange Program is planning to bring a world-renowned conductor and a string orchestra known as prodigies to perform in Viet Nam.
Results: - Starting from late 2021, the Viet Nam Youth Music Institute has successfully organized 11 Chamber Music Concerts, 3 Symphony Concerts, 2 Educational Concerts, a series of 4 Community Concerts, 2 Classical Instrument Exhibitions, and a 8-day Viet Nam Classical Music Festival, comprising a total of 19 performances, combined with diverse cultural and artistic activities, not to mention various workshops and music appreciation sessions for students and audiences of all ages. - The intensive and diverse forms of cultural and artistic programs and events by the Viet Nam Youth Music Institute have provided opportunities for young artists in Viet Nam to perform and attracted international artists from around the world, as well as cultural and artistic experts, to Viet Nam for cultural exchanges with the public. The VYMI has successfully hosted 51 international artists (from Germany, the United States, Taiwan (China), and Japan), organized events, provided creative spaces for over 200 artists, assisted 4 young artists/artist groups debut to the public, and operated an independent Youth Symphony Orchestra with 63 members from 11 different nationalities (Republic of Korea, Japan, Germany, Viet Nam, the United Kingdom, the United States, Canada, Switzerland, New Zealand, France, and Russia) at the current time. - In addition to art performance programs, educational concerts, and a series of workshops, open days on musical instruments, and music appreciation sessions for students aged 6 and above, young audiences, families, and adults are regularly organized by the Viet Nam Youth Music Institute. Furthermore, all VYMI concerts are accompanied by educational and artistic curators. VYMI projects have successfully attracted public interest and drawn nearly 10,000 audiences to explore classical music. - In addition to possessing a high-quality art performance space with full facilities to support artists throughout the process of creation, practice, and performance, the Viet Nam Youth Music Institute continues to explore and organize events at various venues, including cultural and public spaces such as the 22 Hang Buom Culture and Arts Center, Bac Tu Liem District Cultural Center (Ha Noi), AEON Mall Ha Dong, Da Lat Art Boulevard, concert halls such as Phố Bên Đồi Creative Studio, the Grand Concert Hall of the National Academy of Music, and theaters such as the Hanoi Opera House, Ho Guom Theater, and Da Lat Theater, etc.

Area of Monitoring: Cultural and creative sectors
Cultural Domain: Design,Performing Arts,Media Arts,Cinema and Audiovisual Arts,Music,Publishing,Visual Arts
Agency Implementation: Arts Council England
Main Feature: Grant funding (£2,000-£12,000) to support individuals who are cultural and creative practitioners and want to take time to focus on their creative development.
Results: The period of 2018-2022 saw over 11 rounds of funding. DYCP received over 18,000 applications, of which 3,713 (20%) were successful, receiving £33m across 3,670 individuals.
Financial Ressources: The June 2023 funding round saw a total of $5,560,415.53 awarded to 401 people.
Recommandations: An evaluation from March 2022 found that the DYCP programme is a good way to fund individuals. It helps them to build new contacts and skills. People were happy with the chance to try out new things and found that being chosen for funding made applicants feel good about themselves and their work.    However, the report also recognised some improvements for the DYCP programme. The report highlights a desire to have more applications from Museums and Libraries, to make the application process easier to use and follow, to give more feedback if someone does not get the funding so they can understand why and to do more with the data and information we collect.

Title EN: Développement de plateformes numériques : des contenus culturels digitalisés et plus accessibles
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture
SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Digital environment
Agency Implementation: Le Ministère des Affaires Culturelles (MAC) Le Centre des Musiques Arabes et Méditerranéennes (CMAM) La Bibliothèque Nationale de Tunisie (BNT)
Main Feature: La numérisation des contenus culturels fait partie intégrante des orientations stratégiques du Ministère des Affaires Culturelles (MAC). L’objectif étant, notamment, d’investir dans le patrimoine (en tant que source de développement) en créant des mécanismes de travail et des instruments de valorisation en symbiose avec les nouvelles exigences liées aux nouvelles technologies de l’information et de la communication (NTIC). Dans ce cadre, le MAC s’est lancé dans un projet de numérisation à travers le développement de plateformes numériques : •	Musika.tn   Soutenu par le programme « Tfanen » -Tunisie créative  ( avec un financement de 230.000 DT) et en collaboration avec l’Organisme Tunisien de Protection des Droits d’Auteurs et droits Voisins - OTDAV (qui repose sur l’encouragement de l’offre légale à travers une convention d’autorisation et d’exploitation, établie entre les deux institutions concernant les œuvres musicales diffusées dans la plateforme et l’application « musika », garantissant ainsi les droits matériels et moraux des ayants droit) et la Société ARCHIMED, le Centre de Musique Arabe et Méditerranéenne (CMAM) a développé la plateforme numérique « Musika.tn » afin d’assurer la diffusion et la valorisation de ses archives musicales. Les principaux objectifs de la plateforme de diffusion dédiée à la musique sont : -	Diffuser en streaming le fond sonore du CMAM (produit à forte valeur identitaire) -	Renforcer la visibilité et l’identité du CMAM notamment à l’aide d’un portail documentaire riche et mettant en valeur l’ensemble de la collection. -	Créer une référence du son tunisien à l’échelle nationale. -	Attirer et fidéliser le grand public et particulièrement les jeunes. -	Consommer légalement le répertoire musical tunisien en tant que produit culturel à forte valeur identitaire. La plateforme musika.tn est à la fois :  -	Une plateforme institutionnelle offrant accès en mode web aux experts, usagers, chercheurs avec toutes les métadonnées de références. -	Une plateforme mobile permettant un accès léger et en streaming aux fonds et la distribution numérique de la musique tunisienne en service d’écoute instantanée.  Afin de rapprocher la musique tunisienne aux différents groupes d’âge au niveau national et international  et en raison  de la domination des plateformes de streaming numérique dans la consommation et la numérisation de la musique et des œuvres musicales dans le monde et de l’énorme flux de leurs revenus , et pour éviter le piratage dont souffre le secteur musical tunisien et pour assurer l’accès légal aux œuvres musicales tunisiennes sur les plateformes de streaming populaires (Amazon-Apple music-Spotify-Deezer) et les réseaux sociaux (YouTube-Twitter-Instagram- Tik Tok et autres), le CMAM a annoncé un avis d’appel à partenariat avec une société de distribution digitale de la musique. •	La plateforme numérique de la Bibliothèque nationale de Tunisie (BNT) : Projet réalisé par le Ministère des Affaires Culturelles et la Bibliothèque Nationale avec le partenariat de « Beit Al Hikma » et du groupe Archimède. C’est un portail dédié à la valorisation des collections numériques et / ou numérisées de la Bibliothèque Nationale de Tunisie (BNT) offrant un accès gratuit au patrimoine écrit tout en respectant les lois de la propriété intellectuelle. Cette plateforme dont le lancement été célébré le 29 mai 2022 vise à :   -	Valoriser et exploiter le patrimoine culturel tunisien en utilisant les méthodes modernes de gestion et de marketing.  -	Contribuer à la démocratisation de la culture et la transmission du savoir, d’autant plus que BNT, outre sa contribution à la recherche scientifique, universitaire et académique, joue un rôle-clé dans la préservation de la mémoire collective et la documentation du patrimoine commun (il importe de souligner que la BNT fondée en 1885 contient aujourd’hui 2 millions de livres, 16 .000 périodiques et 24.000 manuscrits (40. 000 titres)) -	Consolider le principe de la décentralisation culturelle et mettre à disposition des bases de données et de ressources qui aident à la recherche scientifique et à la préservation des documents menacés de dégradation. -	Mettre en place l’infrastructure logistique et technique liée à la numérisation conformément aux normes internationales en matière de traitement des fonds et documents spécifiques ainsi que la gestion du contenu numérique de diverses sources (numérisation-téléchargements-archivage électronique-dépôt légal numérique.) -	Faire découvrir la richesse de la documentation de la BNT et proposer des contenus alternatifs permettant de conserver les documents originaux et de les rendre accessibles au public, tout en tenant compte du respect des droits d’auteur et des droits voisins. -	Contribuer directement à créer un dynamisme économique autour des Industries Culturelles et Créatives.  Par ailleurs, la BNT a lancé un projet « Ouïe-livre » en partenariat avec la « Fondation Abdelwaheb Ben Ayed » (FABA) qui consiste en la création d’un studio sonore au Sein de la Bibliothèque Nationale permettant de produire des copies sonores d’un ensemble d’ouvrages-destinés prioritairement aux malvoyants et non-voyants ainsi qu’aux personnes handicapés mais aussi à tous les citoyens désirant écouter des livres lus.  •	Le Ministère des Affaires Culturelles travaille actuellement sur deux autres plateformes dédié à : -	La gestion du Fonds National des arts plastiques ayant pour objectif de promouvoir le fonds national ainsi que les artistes plasticiens appartenant aux diverses écoles d’art. -	La gestion et le suivi des subventions publiques qui permettra d’assurer une meilleure gouvernance des financements publics (budget : 462 milles dinars/ taux d’avancement du projet : 70%)
Results: •	La création d’une plateforme numérique de musique tunisienne avec le nom propriétaire de « musika.tn » permettra de rendre accessible au grand public un patrimoine musical exceptionnel valorisé à l’échelle locale et internationale. Il s’agit pour le CMAM d’être acteur dans la diffusion numérique du patrimoine musical tunisien et créateur de changements à impact positif pour les artistes et les opérateurs du secteur musical, en travaillant sur la documentation des supports numérisés (catégories, genres, mots clefs, identification des compositeurs, interprètes, etc.) et en développant une application mobile de streaming audio et vidéo « musika ». La nouvelle application Musika.tn devait proposer, à son lancement, près de 5.000 œuvres tunisiennes. •	La plateforme (www.bibliotheque.nat.tn) comprend un système d’information documentaire multilingue pour le traitement des collections. Ce système contient plus de 500.000 notices de différents documents (livres, périodiques, manuscrits…) et 10.000 documents numérisés, et un portail documentaire de diffusion et de recherche du contenu et des ressources de la bibliothèque en ligne ainsi que les ressources fédérées et agrégées. Le portail fournit quatre sous-portails interconnectés de manière structurée et systématique qui bénéficient tous d’un accès commun à la même base de données documentaire et numérique de manière transparente et unifiée : -	Le portail général qui sert de site,   -	Le catalogue général contenant près de 500 000 enregistrements de documents divers,  -	« Al Khaldouniya » numérique qui valorise les 10 000 documents numérisés pour les lecteurs et les chercheurs,  -	L'espace des jeunes qui convient à leurs besoins.   Le portail propose également un accès à la plateforme du «Musée du Patrimoine Écrit (MPE)» de la BNTet au projet «Ouïe Lire» (production de livres audio). Title EN: Diagnostic/assessment of Law 41-00 (Culture Law), that creates de Secretariat of State for Culture (now Ministry of Culture)
Goal: Integrate Culture In Sustainable Development Frameworks
SDG: SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: International cooperation for sustainable development
Cultural Domain: Design,Performing Arts,Media Arts,Cinema and Audiovisual Arts,Music,Publishing,Visual Arts
Agency Implementation: Ministry of Culture, its dependencies and descentralized subsidiaries
Main Feature: The organic law creating the now Ministry of Culture, definig its structure and competencies, and gathering fundamental cultural rights dates back to the year 2000. In the past 20 years the State has undergone important transformations through the promulgation of laws focused on making the government more modern, efficient and transparent, rendering some provisions from Law No. 41-00 obsolete, and even in some instances, inapplicable. In mid 2023 the Ministry of Culture identified the need to start the works of diagnostics and assessments of Law No. 41-00, and to that effect received support from UNESCO through its regional office in Havana, providing the services of two international consultants: Nelson (Nilson) Acosta and Lazaro Israel Rodriguez Oliva. Both consultants delivered their respective final reports, which together constitute the diagnostic for Law 41-00, concurring in the need to make a new norm. The Ministry is currently drafting the index for a new law, to be presented to the National Culture Council, the sectoral advisory body, in its next session (it meets every 6 months), so as to gather feedback and proposals for the subsequent drafting of the preliminary bill to modify Law No. 41-00.
Results: 2 diagnostic reports by UNESCO’s international consultants
Financial Ressources: N/A (services provided through UNESCO)

Title EN: DicoLab Cultura al digitale
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture
SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Digital environment
Agency Implementation: Fondazione Scuola Beni Attività Culturali
Main Feature: The National Plan for the Digitization of Cultural Heritage, a strategic vision document with which the Ministry of Culture promotes and organizes the digital transformation process, entrusts training with the task of triggering change in people to foster value-generating organizational change.         It is from this assumption that, with the Ministry of Culture - Digital Library, the Foundation works so that the broader process of digital transformation of cultural institutions is a collective and shared project, firmly based on common languages and visions and widespread awareness.         The educational offerings of "Dicolab. Culture to Digital" is aimed as much at organizations, with specific orientation and assistance actions, as at individuals in various capacities involved in the processes of production, use, and governance of digital cultural heritage (managers, directors, administrators, technicians, expert specialists, undergraduates, postgraduates, doctoral students, and researchers), with custom-designed refresher courses.         "Dicolab. Culture to Digital" thus reaches out to staff of the Ministry of Culture and other public administrations; companies in the cultural sector; students (undergraduates and postgraduates) and researchers; cultural institutions, public and private; professionals and experts.
Results: Already 400 hours of training have been produced, with 40,000 users and 100 online training products to their credit.          To support the process of digital cultural transformation in the territories, moments of listening and dialogue, organized on a territorial basis, with representatives of the culture system, regions, local authorities, cultural institutes, and businesses have been promoted already at the planning stage.          Throughout the country, decentralized branches of the training program have been set up to activate processes of listening, engagement and territorial animation: up to 10 hubs distributed throughout the country
Recommandations: The success of Dicolab.Culture to Digital, from the conception of training offerings to their production, relies on tireless work in building partnerships, networks, synergies and collaborations.         The planning of educational offerings is shared with the Central Institute for the Digitization of Cultural Heritage - Digital Library of the Ministry of Culture and implemented in some cases in collaboration with other central and peripheral institutes of the Ministry of Culture.         In the implementation of the project, the Foundation School of Cultural Heritage and Activities involves all the protagonists of the digital transformation, interacting with entities, organizations, qualified and leading realities in the field and aiming increasingly at the creation of synergies and the enhancement of know-how in the field of digital cultural heritage.

Title EN: DigitACT - Developing Digital Skills for Young Actors and Young Performing Arts Technicians in the era of Pandemic
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture
SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Digital environment
Agency Implementation: Center for Social Innovation  Mitos Centre of Performing Arts and other partners from EU countries
Main Feature: “DigitACT: Developing Digital Skills for Young Actors and Young Performing Arts Technicians in the era of Pandemic”  ) is a transnational ERASMUS+ project which aims at intervening in the pandemic aftermath situation in performing arts. Specifically the project aims at supporting young performing arts professionals and technicians to adapt to the digitalization needs and evolution of their field as a means of setting up a sustainable and durable professional path for themselves and their working ecosystem. The two main pillars of the project are: a. creating advanced digital skills to both target groups in relation to digital broadcasting of their activity and work b. boosting personal digital promotion skills for young professionals.  Young actors and technicians who are about to enter the respective job market or have just entered it, are facing huge difficulties in adapting to these new circumstances for which they were probably not sufficiently trained in their drama schools and faculties. In many countries, lots of plays were streamed through the web in very low quality, thus degrading the image of the artistic product and the artists themselves. On the other hand, young actors, who are now trying to build their professional profile, meaning their web presence (professional platforms, digital portfolios, digital networking spaces, digital CVs, audition videos, self-presentation during online interviews/auditions) will have to upgrade their digital skills as a manner of boosting their personal digital marketing skills, thus, enhancing their career development. DigitACT project addresses the above-mentioned needs helping young actors and young technicians to be better included in the performing arts job market which is undergoing a dramatic transformation.  The project is carried out simultaneously in 5 EU countries: Cyprus, Greece, Lithuania, Portugal, Italy.  DigitACT is led by MITOS organization (Cyprus) and its duration is 24 months starting from May 2021.   OBJECTIVES •	To equip young professionals in the field of performing arts, namely actors and technicians, with specialised digital skills in order to permit them to adjust their work methodologies and outcomes to the pandemic conditions and to upgrade their professional digital presence as a means of more efficient cyber networking (aligned with “Economic Dimension” priorities of the New European Agenda for Culture adopted by the European Commission in 2018) •	To encourage the mobility (meaning the capacity of being virtually present wherever it is needed) of young professionals in the cultural sector and remove obstacles to their mobility, especially the ones imposed by the pandemic ( “Social Dimension” of New European Agenda for Culture) •	To boost job retention, job creation, career development and life-long learning for young professionals in the performing arts •	To spread the message of the urgent need for adapting to the new conditions among the culture and art sector and encourage stakeholders to take relevant initiatives in the partner countries. •	To support culture as an engine for sustainable social and economic development (“External Dimension” of the New European Agenda for Culture) •	To foster the cultural capability of all Europeans by making available a wide range of cultural activities and providing opportunities to participate actively ( “Social Dimension” of the New European Agenda for Culture)  Direct beneficiaries/participants: •	Young actors •	Drama school graduates (about to enter the respective job market) •	Drama school students •	Young theatre and performing arts technicians •	Graduates of technical schools/faculties who wish to enter the performing arts sector •	Technical schools/faculties students who wish to enter the performing arts sector  Indirect beneficiaries/participants: •	Theatre and performing arts associations, organisations and institutions •	Drama schools, performing arts training centres and trainers •	Cultural policy makers •	Performing arts audience •	General public
Results: •	Extensive qualitative and quantitative research with the participation of performing arts professionals The research will lead the partnership to identify the new needs of this target group throughout the changes that the pandemic imposed. •	1 training curriculum for actors •	1 training curriculum for technicians •	1 training curriculum for Young Ambassadors (performing arts young professionals who will spread the project’s message in the sector) •	5 workshops with 100 actors and 4 workshops with 50 technicians in total across the 5 partner countries •	1 “DigitACT Pros” mobile app which will help professionals obtain a smart portfolio app to promote their work in different contexts. •	5 National Pools and 1 EU pool of DigitACT Young Ambassadors •	1 EU Charter for Digital Skills in Performing Arts (coalition for the promotion of digital skills within the performing arts sector) •	1 international conference at the end of the project

Title EN: Digitalization of cultural content in the Republic of Belarus
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture
SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Digital environment
Cultural Domain: Design,Performing Arts,Media Arts,Cinema and Audiovisual Arts,Music,Publishing,Visual Arts
Agency Implementation: Ministry of Culture of the Republic of Belarus  Minsitry of Communications and Informatization of the Republic of Belarus
Main Feature: The modern policy of the Republic of Belarus in the field of digitalization prioritizes ensuring innovative development of the national economy through the introduction of technologies, improving the public administration system and developing information and communication infrastructure, developing electronic services, as well as ensuring competitiveness. The main emphasis in the development and implementation of digital technologies has been made towards the creation of an information and communication infrastructure and conditions for electronic communication between the government bodies, business community, and citizens. In Belarus, as of December, 2021, 98% of the population are Internet-users. The total number of mobile subscribers in Belarus is 11.76 mln (127%), and 98,4% of the subscribers have access to 3G and 4G networks.  Digitalization has affected all areas of social life, including culture. The State Program "Digital Development of Belarus" for 2021-2025 provides for the implementation of measures to develop a modern information and communication infrastructure, implement digital innovations in various industries and "smart city" technologies, as well as ensure the information security of such solutions. In the sphere of culture and mass-media the State Program emphasizes the following key technological trends : growth of digital materials, growth of the number and diversity of digital online content producers; online format of interaction with consumers of services (virtual excursions, concerts, exhibitions, performances, etc.), use of virtual and augmented reality, virtual assistants; digitalization of historical and cultural funds; electronic format of interaction between employees of the cultural sphere. In the current realities, the digital transformation of culture should take into account the problems of preserving national cultural values ​​and cultural identity and actively involve the population in the digital cultural environment. Thus, within the framework of the digital development of culture and the media, it is necessary to ensure: quality control of content, fully or partially created by modern digital technologists, prevention of the dissemination of inaccurate and harmful content on the Internet; systematized collection and digitization of information on historical and cultural values, creation and development of digital funds (text, photo, video, audio), development and updating of electronic catalogs, ensuring the safety of materials in digital form; use of modern ICT to demonstrate cultural heritage - use of ICT as auxiliary and independent elements in exhibition, cultural and educational, restoration, scientific and stock and other areas of activity; use of platform solutions (including the development of services of the digital platform "Smart City (Region)") to involve citizens in the cultural life of cities and regions, organizing online broadcasts and virtual concert halls to demonstrate cultural events held by museums and theaters, concert halls and libraries. The State Program provides for measures to form "smart city" technologies and information and communication infrastructure, implement digital innovations, as well as ensure the information security of such solutions. Belarusian IT companies are involved in the implementation of the activities outlined in the program. In particular, a number of companies provide services in the field of digitalization of culture. Thus, the beCloud company co-organized the fourth #GBCregions and presented technological projects of a country-wide scale in the field of culture to the participants of the regional forum in Vitebsk. Today beCloud is implementing several projects for cultural organizations and institutions, offering a wide range of opportunities, solutions and products for the digital transformation of the industry (Museum, large projects with the Belarusian State Archive of Film, Photo and Sound Documents (BSACFPD) and the National Library of Belarus, storage on the Republican cloud platform). Particular attention is paid to the formation of electronic information resources. In 2023, active work was carried out to develop the automated system "Electronic Library" and include it in the State Program "Digital Development of Belarus" for 2021-2025." All regional libraries have purchased scanning and server equipment for digitizing regional collections. In the future, the regional digital content created will become part of the National Electronic Library. The access to the documentary, library, and museum collections is provided through open online resources: the electronic library catalog (https://e-catalog.nlb.by) and the State Museum Collections Catalogue of the Republic of Belarus (https://www.dkmf.by/about). There are also databases of tangible immovable cultural property, intangible cultural heritage (www.living-heritage.by), archaeological monuments.
Results: The digitalization of culture and cultural resources is an important element of the country's cultural policy. During the reporting period, the following was achieved: 1) the number of internet-users significantly increased; 2) tthe catalogues of museums items and cultural heritage items were seriously improved; 3) the infrastructure of electronic libraries and the digitization of materials stored in the National Library of Belarus have been improved; 4) joint environment is being developed for managing and accessing information related to culture and historical and cultural heritage.
Financial Ressources: The data are not available
Recommandations: To continue digitalization of cultural products within the state programme 'Culture of Belarus for 2021-2025'

Title EN: Distribution and access to Chilean Audiovisual Content "Ondamedia" Chilean film platform.
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture
SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Digital environment
Agency Implementation: Ministry of Cultures, Arts and Heritage.
Main Feature: Ondamedia is a video streaming platform of the State of Chile, created by MINCAP, with the goal of promoting national cinema and audiovisual culture to the public, and reducing access barriers for this type of cultural content. The platform offers all film genres (dramas, documentaries, comedies, horror, short films) organised in categories and collections like memory and Human Rights, indigenous peoples, gender diversity and social marginalisation.   It also offers conferences in the sciences, arts and humanities. In 2017, Ondamedia came to being as an initiative of the National Council of Culture and the Arts (now MINCAP) in order to encourage the consumption of Chilean films at a national level, as well as support for the creators through payments for the right to exhibit their works. That same year, the National Council of Culture and the Arts launched a beta version of Ondamedia with a catalogue of 40 fiction films, 41 documentaries, 20 short films and 394 science, arts and humanities clips, allowing a maximum of eight viewings per month.   In March 2020, ondamedia enabled unlimited access to its feature films, documentaries and short films, without viewing restrictions. That same year, as a result of compulsory co-financing for COVID-19, Ondamedia reached 2,200,000 views, six times its audience of the previous year. In 2023, the films from the catalogue had on average 15,000 viewers.
Results: The platform has more than 455 thousand registered users, from many of the communes of Chile, which has enabled access to Chilean film for a much of the population within the national territory that does not have other means of access. This implies the promotion of consumption of diverse audiovisual productions, ensuring the diversity of cultural expressions from different periods.   In turn, more than one million films are played annually, contributing in great measure to addressing the low national film consumption happening in Chilean cinemas. For 2022, this platform had more than 2,000 audiovisual works. It should be noted that during that same year, 65 new inclusive subtitles have been added to feature films for deaf and hearing impaired people, totalling 127 titles to date.

Title EN: Directive No. 25-CT/TTg dated on September 10, 2021 of the Prime Minister on accelerating the implementation of Viet Nam's External Cultural Relations Strategy
Goal: Achieve A Balanced Flow Of Cultural Goods And Services And Increase The Mobility Of Artists And Cultural Professionals
SDG: SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 10 - Reduce inequality within and among countries,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Treaties and agreements
Cultural Domain: Design,Performing Arts,Media Arts,Cinema and Audiovisual Arts,Music,Publishing,Visual Arts
Agency Implementation: The Ministry of Culture, Sports and Tourism presides over and coordinates with ministries, branches, localities, socio-political organizations, unions, people's organizations and businesses to organize the implementation of this Directive.
Main Feature: This is a directive document of the Prime Minister requesting Ministers, Heads of ministerial-level agencies, Heads of Government agencies, Chairmen of provincial and municipal People's Committees to promote the implementation of Viet Nam's Foreign Cultural Strategy, with specific tasks and solutions, as follows: 1. Continue to cultivate communication, acquire a thorough understanding, and heighten awareness of the role and importance of culture in general, external cultural relations in particular, and the perspectives and goals of Viet Nam's External Cultural Relations Strategy in the context of globalization and international integration.  2. Strengthen the implementation of Viet Nam's External Cultural Relations Strategy from now to 2030, promoting the development of cultural industries in Viet Nam and integrating foreign information work into our overall foreign policy, socio-economic development, and national defense; promote the development of digital culture, focusing on the application of science, technology, and the achievements of the Fourth Industrial Revolution; and enhance the implementation of external cultural relations activities after the COVID-19 pandemic.  3. Build and simultaneously improve the legal and policy system, promoting the negotiation, signing, and implementation of international treaties and agreements to support external cultural relations activities in the new period including the fundraising policies and guidelines to attract both domestic and foreign resources generating new motivation for sustainable cultural development.  4. Strengthen the work of preserving and promoting cultural and human values and promoting the country’s image abroad in many diverse forms and methods of expression; promote communication and promotion on mass media, digital platforms, social networks, the exchange of reporters and press groups, and cooperation with international film crews.  5. Continue to strategically construct Vietnamese Cultural Centers and Vietnamese Language Teaching Centers abroad, taking into account the needs, political, economic, and cultural relations between Viet Nam and the host countries, as well as the development conditions of Viet Nam; improve the quality of staff and operational efficiency of Vietnamese Cultural Centers abroad.  6. Continue to promote external cultural relations activities closely linked with the Vietnamese community abroad, contributing to preserving and promoting the Vietnamese language, cultural identity, and national traditions, and attracting high quality resources abroad, which contributes to the sustainable development of the country.  7. Actively implement foreign cultural activities at national and local levels in the land border areas between Viet Nam and neighboring countries through culture, sports, and tourism exchange programs and regular exchange activities, contributing to the effective protection of national territorial sovereignty and enhance exchanges and mutual understanding among people in border areas.  8. Actively integrate internationally, making effective use of multilateral cooperation, and further promoting the role of external cultural relations activities at important multilateral mechanisms and forums such as UNESCO, ASEAN, ASEM, IFACCA, WIPO, etc.  9. Actively absorb and selectively introduce the quintessence of human culture to Vietnamese, while at the same time, hosting and organizing large-scale and prestigious international events, and developing quality festival brands, festivals, and cultural and artistic events in Viet Nam.
Results: By the end of 2023, 59 agencies and localities in Viet Nam had issued their own plans to implement Prime Minister's Directive No. 25-CT/TTg on accelerating the implementation of Viet Nam's External Cultural Relations Strategy. In 2022, the Ministry of Culture, Sports and Tourism of Viet Nam signed 12 international agreements on culture and art cooperation. In 2023, Viet Nam's Ministry of Culture, Sports, and Tourism signed another 15 international agreements on culture, sports, and tourism cooperation, establishing a legal framework to effectively implement cultural and external cultural relations activities. In addition, many localities have also signed and implemented international agreements with other countries' local authorities.  Viet Nam has also proactively and actively participated, emphasizing its role in major international mechanisms and forums:  - At the World Exhibition EXPO 2020 Dubai (October 1, 2021 to March 31, 2022), the Viet Nam Pavilion, hosted and operated by the Ministry of Culture, Sports and Tourism, attracted 700,000 visitors, welcoming more than 30 delegations of Heads of State and Heads of International Organizations. Viet Nam also won the Bronze Prize for "Theme Interpretation" awarded by the Bureau International des Expositions (BIE) and the First Prize in the category of Valuable Initiatives, Ideas, and Products for Foreign Information of the 8th National Award for Foreign Information.  - Within the ASEAN framework, Viet Nam’s Ministry of Culture, Sports and Tourism fully participates in ASEAN culture, sports, and tourism cooperation mechanisms, performing the role of coordinating ASEAN-Korea cultural cooperation during the 2021–2024 period and actively enhancing ASEAN values, awareness, identity, and people-to-people cultural connections in the ASEAN Community through implementing the Plan to Implement the Goals of the ASEAN Cultural-Social Community to 2025. Viet Nam also hosted the 2022 ASEAN Music Festival in Hoi An City, Quang Nam Province and organized the 2022 ASEAN Film Week on the occasion of the 55th anniversary of the founding of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations and ASEAN Traditional Costume Exhibition in Hue City (2022), etc.  - Within the framework of the Federation of Arts Councils and Cultural Agencies (IFACCA), representatives of the Ministry of Culture, Sports and Tourism have affirmed Viet Nam's role through exchanging and developing policies and IFACCA’s general programs, fully participating in events such as the 9th World Summit on Culture and Arts organized by IFACCA and the Swedish Arts Council and meetings of the Executive Council; co-chairing the 18th regular meeting of the Asia-Pacific group of countries.  - Within the framework of UNESCO, in 2023, Viet Nam was elected Vice President, representing the Asia-Pacific region at the Intergovernmental Committee of the 2005 Convention. The Ministry of Culture, Sports and Tourism coordinated with the local authorities of Hoi An City and Da Lat City to prepare dossiers, and successfully supported the two cities to become the official members of the UNESCO Creative Cities Network, etc.
Recommandations: - Continuing to negotiate and sign treaties and agreements on culture, sports, and tourism with other countries.  - Continuing to proactively implement the Plan to Implement Directive No. 25-CT/TTg of the Prime Minister on accelerating the implementation of Viet Nam's External Cultural Relations Strategy, giving priority to organizing Viet Nam Culture and Tourism Weeks and Days abroad, as well as cultural and artistic programs celebrating even years of diplomatic relations.  - Maintaining an effective presence in multilateral frameworks at international organizations like ASEAN, APEC, UNWTO, UNESCO, IFACCA, ASEM, OIF, GMS, APEC, UNWTO, etc.  - Engaging actively in activities within the ASEAN framework, taking on the role of chairing the ASEAN Sports Ministers' Conference for the 2024-2025 period, taking part in the ASEAN Culture Ministers' Meeting in Malaysia, the ASEAN Tourism Ministers' Meeting in Laos, and coordinating the cooperation between ASEAN and Korea on culture and tourism.  - Creating favorable conditions for countries and international organizations to introduce culture and tourism in Viet Nam, ensuring effective management of foreign cultural centers in Viet Nam, as well as coordinating with countries to organize foreign cultural weeks in Viet Nam.  - Coordinating with ministries, branches, and localities in foreign affairs and organizing cultural, sports, and tourism events both domestically and internationally;  - Supporting localities to build and submit dossiers to join the UNESCO Creative Cities Network.

Title EN: Dirsi tutto, sinfonia di corpi in movimento - 2022
Goal: Promote Human Rights And Fundamental Freedoms
SDG: SDG 5 - Achieve gender equality and empower all women and girls,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels
Area of Monitoring: Artistic freedom
Agency Implementation: Università degli Studi di Padova - UNESCO Chair Human Rights, Democracy and Peace
Main Feature: This event, organized in partnership with the Municipality of Padova, is part of the initiatives to commemorate the 40th anniversary of the Human Rights Centre of the University of Padova, founded by Professor Antonio Papisca in 1982.  The great ideals of freedom, peace and solidarity are on everyone's lips today. As is the growing awareness of the need to defend human rights. But the difference between abstract concepts and reality lies in the concrete emotions we feel, in our lived lives.  Dirsi tutto - Sinfonia di corpi in movimento has this purpose: to transform the broadest ideals into an engaging performance, capable of conveying its message directly, without veils, to the hearts and minds of the audience. To make bodies and movements, musical sounds and human voices translate into emotion, participation and moral stance. Not with the intention of embellishing or ennobling reality, but to reveal it to us all, awakening us from the spell of repetition, habit, everyday conformity. Because all rights are based on freedom, and freedom on courage, and courage on faith in the possibility of improving the world, representing it in its most engaging and evocative forms.
Results: The results achieved by the initiative respected the purposes of it, which were the visible and emotionally vivid rendering of the messages supported by human rights, with a focus on the concept of freedom and courage in improving the world's worst situations.

Main Feature: DISEÑARTE-BOLIVIA is a content platform that promotes Author Design, art and fashion through an International Fashion Meeting that integrates conferences, discussions, workshops and laboratories. It takes place from September to November in the city of La Paz, as it is a multicultural and diverse city, the epicenter of national culture. As a breeding ground and observatory, Diseñarte disseminates emerging design, values networking and the interaction of related disciplines; promotes the opening, visualization and integration of art and fashion, contributing to the collaborative construction of knowledge and being a showcase for the creative industry of fashion design. It is carried out in coordination with the Bolivian Association of Design and Fashion ABOMODA and has the institutional support of CONPANAC and ALADI. It contributes to the construction of the Creative Fashion Design industry within cultural industries for Bolivia and the world, contributing to the construction and consolidation of a platform that involves Design, Art, Fashion, fostering the articulation of knowledge and collaboration through conferences, discussions, Fashion laboratories, spaces for dialogue and a catwalk of laboratory results where emerging authors share a platform with renowned authors.  The Diseñarte experience allows the participation of various Bolivian and foreign cultural actors with valuable careers. Thus, democratizing fashion and giving value to each cultural actor. Diseñarte offers: Creativity and Design laboratories and workshops, 20 talks, 10 conferences, 5 design experiences, 1 Fashion Illustration contest, 12 photographic productions and 1 collective catwalk. All the contents of DISEÑARTE are aimed at creators of visual and textile art, designers, plastic artists, lovers of design, art and the general population, and especially young people who seek to reaffirm their identity for themselves and for society through clothing. We had activities open to the public free of charge that presented themes of identity, history, art and fashion. Each year's creative process has a theme that is the guiding thread of the fashion laboratories where the production chain of fashion design is strengthened, seen as part of creative and cultural industries. We value design from the idea, conceptual work, the application of visual elements for fashion design such as illustration, drawing, color, pattern making, tailoring, photographic production, and many other aspects. We believe that promoting, affirming and sharing knowledge with new generations, contributing to the training of audiences and designers with awareness and criteria regarding their identity and context, as well as the interaction of related areas, is a premise of DISEÑARTE.
Results: The DISEÑARTE BOLIVIA Meeting has had 10 editions to date, which have allowed for the integration, articulation and linking of all its actors and the project itself. As well as making National Fashion Design visible inside and outside the country. Diversity of cultural expressions was achieved. Value was given to each cultural actor involved and to the aspects of Fashion Design that have been part of Diseñarte. Revalue textiles, techniques and textile customs, as well as value the articulation of areas such as pure arts, drawing, painting, photography with visual and contemporary arts such as illustration, installation and fashion production. He is a promoter of the diversity of these expressions and has contributed to a collaborative constitution of the knowledge from exhibition spaces, discussions, conferences, and has also achieved institutional alliances that support the meeting. He has been a promoter of the creative cultural sector of Fashion Design and the diversity of cultural expressions through: The platform and its content spaces promoted new authors, it was a breeding ground for creativity and a space for growth for each area of Design, Fashion and Production. This comprehensive approach has led to many projects being carried out and linked through the platform today. Forming audiences, new creatives and connecting areas that were not previously connected to each other.

Title EN: Diwaniya Art Gallery

Main Feature: Diwaniya Art Gallery est une galerie d'art située à Cheraga, dans la banlieue ouest d'Alger. Fondée par le plasticien algérien Hamza Bounoua en septembre 2020, la galerie se consacre à l'art contemporain du monde arabe en général, et l'Afrique du Nord en particulier. Bounoua ambitionne d’enrichir le débat artistique, de promouvoir le mouvement artistique algérien et de développer le marché de l’art algérien, à travers des expositions collectives et individuelles, en galerie et ailleurs, la participation à des foires internationales et des expositions virtuelles sur des plateformes spécialisées et reconnues. L’inauguration de la première exposition était prévue pour le mois de mars 2020, mais en raison de la situation sanitaire liée à la pandémie de COVID-19, l’ouverture officielle a été reportée en mois de septembre avec des mesures sanitaires strictes, à travers la limitation du nombre de visiteurs et autres mesures.  La galerie a ouvert ses portes avec l'exposition collective intitulée "Massarat" ou « Parcours » qui présente les œuvres de plusieurs artistes : Thilleli Rahmoun (Algérie) : Œuvres intitulées "Syndrome de Stockholm", utilisant des collages et des techniques mixtes sur le thème de la liberté, Rachida Azdaou (Algérie) : Collection "Depressed", photographies et vidéos de performances de l'artiste Toufik Kara, Lulwah Al Homoud (Arabie Saoudite), Mohamed Ibrahim El Masry (Egypte), Ghada Zoughby (Liban), Rashid Diab (Soudan), Mohamed Al Ameri (Jordanie), Mohamed Abou El Naga (Egypte), et Shadi Talaei (Iran) : Œuvres variées, incluant des perspectives contemporaines sur la calligraphie et des travaux sur les thèmes culturels et sociaux. Une œuvre de la plasticienne algérienne Baya Mahieddine a été également exposée en hommage à cette grande figure de l'art algérien. L'exposition "Massarat" était accessible au public jusqu'au 13 janvier 2021. Diwaniya Art Gallery à la Foire d'art Intersect 21 de Chicago La galerie d'art algérienne Diwaniya Art Gallery a représenté six artistes algériens et étrangers lors de l’édition virtuelle de la foire d'art Intersect 21 de Chicago. La galerie a présenté les œuvres des artistes suivants : Thilleli Rahmoune (Algérie), Ali Boukhalfa (Algérie), Mustapha Nedjai (Algérie), Lulwah Al Homoud (Arabie Saoudite) et Mohamed Ibrahim El Masry (Egypte). Objectifs et ambitions de Diwaniya Art Gallery La galerie a pour ambition de représenter l'art algérien et artistes étrangers dans divers événements internationaux, offrant une vitrine professionnelle sur la scène artistique mondiale. Diwaniya Art Gallery à la 2ème  édition de Égypte Int'l Art Fair La Diwaniya Art Gallery représente quatre artistes algériens et étrangers à la deuxième édition de la foire d'art Égypte Int'l Art Fair qui s’est tenue du 26 au 28 février 2021 au Caire, Égypte, présentant les œuvres de : Rachida Azdaou (Algérie), Ghada Zoughby (Liban), Rashid Diab (Soudan) et Mohamed Ibrahim El Masry (Égypte).  Exposition "Jussur" d'Ali Boukhalfa à Diwaniya Art Gallery Première exposition individuelle "Jussur" (Passerelles) de l'artiste peintre et sculpteur Ali Boukhalfa, qui s’est tenue jusqu'au 23 juin 2021.  Exposition virtuelle "Al Basma" sur la plateforme new-yorkaise Artsy Diwaniya Art Gallery est la première galerie d'art algérienne à collaborer avec Artsy. Cette collaboration vise à offrir de nouvelles opportunités sur le marché de l’art en ligne et à représenter des artistes algériens et étrangers sur la scène artistique internationale. La Diwaniya Art Gallery a organisé une exposition virtuelle intitulée "Al Basma" en partenariat avec la plateforme new-yorkaise Artsy. Cette exposition s’est tenue du 20 juin au 20 octobre 2021 et a convié des artistes d'Algérie, du monde arabe et de la Méditerranée à présenter leurs œuvres. L'objectif étant de créer une mosaïque pour promouvoir la culture algérienne et favoriser les échanges entre artistes et collectionneurs. Cette exposition a connu la participation des artistes suivants : Adlène Samet (Algérie), Hassen Drici (Algérie), Tayseer Barakat (Palestine), Patrick Altes (Franco-Espagnol), Ghadah Alkandari (Koweïtienne), Vincent Abadi (Zepha) (Français), Emna Zghel (Tunisienne), Shakir Alousi (Irakien). Exposition virtuelle "Asdiqa" sur la plateforme Artsy L'exposition virtuelle "Asdiqa" (amis) s’est tenue sur la plateforme new-yorkaise d'art moderne et contemporain Artsy du 25 octobre au 25 décembre 2021. Cette exposition a regroupé sept (07) artistes du Maghreb, notamment de l'Algérie, de la Tunisie et de la Libye. Cette exposition a connu la participation de : Hicham Belhamiti (Algérie), Fatima Chafaa (Algérie), Jamal Matari (Algérie), Ranou Kadi (Algérie), Myriam Dib (Algérie), Mohamed Dhahbi (Tunisie) et Mariam Abu Bakr El-Assad (Libye),  Le commissaire de l'exposition, Zoubir Hellal, a souligné l'importance de créer des ponts au-delà de la distanciation sociale imposée par la pandémie de COVID-19, il a insisté sur la nécessité de maintenir des relations d’amitié non conditionnées.  Diwaniya Art Gallery à la vente aux enchères d'Al Bahie à Doha Diwaniya Art Gallery a participé à la vente aux enchères d'art moderne et contemporain qui a été organisée par Al Bahie le 4 décembre 2021 à Doha au Qatar. Cet événement a célébré "80 ans d'art en provenance du monde arabe". Diwaniya Art Gallery propose les œuvres de quatre artistes : Ali Boukhalfa (Algérie), Vincent Abadi Hafiz (Zepha) (France), Rashid Diab (Soudan), Mohamed Ibrahim El Masry (Égypte).   La participation à cette vente aux enchères a été une occasion pour promouvoir les œuvres et les artistes algériens, de définir la cotation des œuvres et de suivre la dynamique du marché international de l'art.

Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture
