Area of Monitoring: Cultural and creative sectors
Agency Implementation: Ministry of Economy
Main Feature: The Ministry of Economy (MOE) has launched the Economic Content Creators Program in collaboration with the Dubai Media Council. This initiative is designed to enhance the skills and capabilities of content creators and journalists in the UAE, with a specific focus on economic and financial reporting. The program aims to improve the quality and depth of economic media coverage, thereby supporting the broader goal of sustainable economic development. The primary objective of the Economic Content Creators Program is to build a cadre of highly skilled media professionals capable of delivering in-depth analysis and high-quality reporting on economic and financial matters. This will enhance the media's role in informing the public and stakeholders about economic policies, developments, and opportunities. The program provides comprehensive training to participants, covering various aspects of economic reporting. This includes modules on analyzing economic events and their impacts on the local and global economy, discussing challenges and opportunities in key sectors such as energy, technology, and tourism, examining economic policies and their effects on businesses and consumers, and understanding global economic transformations, including international trade, technological innovation, green economy initiatives, and sustainability. The initiative is a joint effort between the Ministry of Economy and the Dubai Media Council, leveraging their combined expertise and resources to deliver effective training. The collaboration aims to align media content with the UAE’s economic vision and strategic priorities. The program is designed to equip journalists and content creators with advanced analytical skills and tools necessary for high-quality economic reporting. This includes training on the use of data analytics, economic indicators, and digital platforms for effective content dissemination. By focusing on enhancing the quality of economic and financial reporting, the program seeks to raise the standards of journalism in the UAE. This will contribute to a more informed and engaged public, fostering a transparent and vibrant economic environment. The program emphasizes the importance of sustainability and innovation in economic reporting. It encourages journalists to cover topics related to the green economy, sustainable development, and technological advancements, aligning with the UAE's long-term economic goals. Improved economic reporting will support the UAE’s efforts to attract foreign direct investment (FDI), promote entrepreneurship, and stimulate economic growth. By providing accurate and insightful economic information, the media can play a crucial role in shaping investor confidence and public perception.
Results: Since its implementation, the Economic Content Creators’ program has successfully nurtured a diverse pool of content creators specializing in economic topics. The program has facilitated the production of high-quality content that has reached a broad audience, increased public engagement and understood economic issues. Moreover, several content creators who have participated in the program have reported significant growth in their professional skills and network, leading to better career opportunities and collaborations. The program has also contributed to the visibility of economic discourse in various media platforms, promoting informed discussions on economic policies and trends.
Recommandations: The Economic Content Creators’ program has demonstrated a positive impact on both content creators and the wider public’s understanding of economic matters.

Title EN: Droits d’auteurs et droits voisins en Algérie
Goal: Promote Human Rights And Fundamental Freedoms

Agency Implementation: Office National des Droits d’Auteurs et des Droits Voisins (ONDA)
Main Feature: L'Office National des Droits d'Auteur et des Droits Voisins (ONDA) est un établissement public créé en 1973 et placé sous la tutelle du Ministère de la Culture et des Arts. Il a pour mission de protéger les droits moraux et patrimoniaux des auteurs, des titulaires des droits voisins et de leurs ayants droits, tout en assurant la gestion collective d’œuvres littéraires et artistiques et de prestations de toute nature. L’Office est le seul organisme habilité en Algérie en matière de gestion collective des droits d’auteur et des droits voisins. Il est chargé de recueillir les redevances dues à l’exploitation publique des œuvres de l’esprit, des prestations et de la répartition des droits d’auteur et droits voisins au nom des ayants droits en Algérie. A noter que l’Algérie est signataire de plusieurs accords internationaux relatifs aux droits d’auteurs tels que la Convention universelle sur le droit d’auteur (UNESCO), la Convention de Berne pour la protection littéraire et artistique, etc.  L’office a toujours encouragé la création individuelle dans différents modes d’expression et œuvré au développement de l’industrie des arts. Il joue un rôle essentiel dans le soutien de la création en Algérie, en encourageant la diversité culturelle et en contribuant au développement du secteur artistique et culturel du pays.   L’ONDA offre différentes formes d’aides à la création qui peuvent varier en fonction des domaines artistiques et des critères établis. Parmi les types d’aides possibles figurent les subventions financières.  Cet office contribue également à l’aide sociale à travers le Fond Social des Droits d’Auteur, qui constitue un mécanisme visant à soutenir les artistes et les créateurs dans des situations spécifiques, et ce en fournissant une aide financière supplémentaire aux créateurs qui font face à des difficultés sociales ou économiques particulières.  Le Fond susmentionné peut être utilisé pour venir en aide aux créateurs qui rencontrent des problèmes de santé, des difficultés financières, des situations d’urgence ou d’autres circonstances défavorables. Il peut être un soutien financier temporaire ou à court terme pour les créateurs qui font face à ces mêmes difficultés. La mission et l'impact de l'Office National des Droits d'Auteurs et des Droits Voisins (ONDA) en Algérie sont indéniables. Depuis sa création en 1973, il a joué un rôle crucial dans la protection des droits de créateurs et dans la promotion de la diversité culturelle. En tant qu'unique organisme habilité à gérer collectivement les droits d'auteur et les droits voisins dans le pays, il a œuvré pour encourager la création individuelle et soutenir l'industrie artistique dans son ensemble. Une collaboration avec des organisations internationales telles que l’IFFRO (International Fédération of Reproduction Rights Organisations), la CISAC (Confédération Internationale des Sociétés d’Auteurs et Compositeurs) a été initiée et la signature de plus de cinquante-quatre (54) conventions de réciprocités avec les sociétés de gestion collective à travers le monde pour promouvoir et protéger les droits d’auteur

Title EN: ECONOMIC STIMULI FOR CULTURE
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture
SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Cultural and creative sectors
Agency Implementation: General Directorate of Cultural Industries and Arts (Ministry of Culture)
Main Feature: The Ministry of Culture has a financing policy for cinematographic and audiovisual projects, as well as the performing arts, visual arts, music, books and the promotion of reading with the aim of promoting a wide diversity of cultural expressions.  Law No. 29565, Law creating the Ministry of Culture, establishes that the Ministry of Culture is an organization that constitutes the State's budget statement. In that sense, according to literal c) of article 7 of Law No. 29565, among the exclusive functions of the Ministry of Culture is “promoting the arts, creation and artistic development through the organization, leadership, supervision and evaluation of public actions aimed at such purposes, promoting the presence of different cultural organizations, facilitating the population's access to them and promoting private initiatives that contribute to the fulfillment of the goals of the sector", in this line the awards are granted economic stimuli.
Results: The main results are the following:   ARTS:   During the first 6 editions of the Economic Stimuli for Culture (2018-2023), a total of 7,504 applications have been received, of which 789 cultural projects in the sectors of performing arts, visual arts and music at national level have been financed worldwide, granting the total sum of S/ 17,244,050 (seventeen thousand two hundred and forty-four thousand and fifty with 00/100 soles). Likewise, the amounts allocated for the delivery of economic stimuli have increased by 35% (2018-2023); However, the demand for applications received has increased by 212% (2018-2023).  BOOK AND READING:  En the last six editions, have been financed with S/ 7,698,458.21 (seven million six hundred and ninety eight thousand four hundred and fifty eight with 21/100 soles) for the implementation of 586 cultural projects in the book and reading sector nationwide, out of twenty-two (22) regions of the country.  The demand for applications has increased by 122% compared to the first edition of the economic stimuli. Likewise, the demand covered with respect to the number of applications has remained at 20% on average year after year. Although it is true, there was a reduction in the number of beneficiaries compared to the 2018 call, the average of the amounts awarded to the winners has remained above the initial amount in subsequent years, which translates into a greater number of financing to each of the declared beneficiary projects.   CINEMA:    In the last five editions, S/ 136,928,887.80 have been financed for the implementation of 1,321 cultural projects in the cinematography and audiovisual sector nationwide, 833 from Lima and Callao, 472 from regions of the country and 16 from Peru domiciled abroad. Likewise, there has been an increase in applications from regions outside Metropolitan Lima and Callao, going from 20.81% to 41.04% from 2018 to 2023. Regarding other gaps such as gender, in the last two years, reservations have been applied for female filmmakers in the feature film development and production contests, as well as in the short film production contest, in order to encourage greater participation of women. Meanwhile, results have been obtained such as that in the Exclusive Fiction Feature Project Contest for the regions of the country (except Metropolitan Lima and Callao) they increased from 1 application to 6 from 2018 to 2023.
Financial Ressources: Año 2023. Total:  USD 8 891 421
Recommandations: According to the Evaluation Report of the National Culture Policy for 2030 corresponding to 2023 (June, 2024); the factors that influenced the performance of the services provided within the framework of the provision of economic stimuli for cinema include the holding of informative talks, the dissemination of calls through social networks and the action of giving back to citizens carried out by the beneficiaries. In addition, access to the internet and digital tools, as well as the ability to formulate viable projects, affect the application process. Evaluation criteria that encourage gender parity in projects were applied and reservations were made for female directors in competitions with greater demand.

In this way, artists, entrepreneurs, companies and groups of cultural industries and the arts throughout the country benefited. Through Ministerial Resolution No. 151-2020-MC dated June 11, 2020, the “Guidelines for the application of buffer mechanisms to mitigate the economic effects in the Culture Sector produced in the context of the Health Emergency due to the COVID-19, within the framework of Emergency Decree No. 058-2020.”  *By Ministerial Resolution No. 072-2021-MC dated March 26, 2021, the “Guidelines for the granting of economic support were approved within the framework of Emergency Decree No. 027-2021, Emergency Decree that establishes extraordinary measures in economic and financial matters to mitigate the socioeconomic effects in the Culture Sector produced in the context of the Health Emergency due to COVID-19.”

Title EN: Educational, cultural and children's television. NTV public channel.
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture

Area of Monitoring: Media diversity
Agency Implementation: National Television of Chile (TVN), University of Chile.
Main Feature: NTV is a Chilean public television channel, with educational and cultural programming, aimed at child and youth audiences. It is public property through the National Television of Chile, having began its broadcasts in August 2021. Even though it has its history is directly related to "TV Educa Chile", a Chilean children's free-to-air television channel, following an agreement between the National Television Association (Anatel), the Ministry of Education (MINEDUC) and the National Television Council (CNTV), it begins broadcasts with the ai of supporting the child and youth educational processes in the context of the COVID-19 pandemic.   This public cultural channel was announced by the former president Michelle Bachelet in her 2015 Public Account and in 2018 the Law 21.085 on public TV was adopted, which established the legal basis for this new television channel.Although it is a channel that does not allow advertising (unlike the main channel), the public resources assigned are not permanent nor stable over time.   The NTV programming begins at 6 in the morning and ends after midnight, from Monday to Sunday. Its programming schedule consists of various time slots and types of series devoted to children, youth and families, split into age groups. We can consider this cultural channel within the monitoring framework of the 2005 Convention, as part of the "policies and measures that support diversity of content in the media" indicator.
Results: In its first year of broadcasts, the NTV channel premiered 184 programmes, equalling 742 hours of programming in its various time slots. Of those, 89% (164 programmes) refer to national productions and 11% to international productions (20 programmes). Audiovisual content is divided according to its origin. Thirty four percent are programmes specially produced for NTV (internal and external productions, co-productions), 21% are domestic licenced content (paid exhibition licences), 17% belong to the children's programming catalogue produced by the regulating television body, 16% represent donations (specially produced for, but at no cost to the channel) and 12% are TVN's prior productions.   Of the 742 hours of programming in its first year on air, 522 hours (70%) represent family and 220 hours (30%) children's programmes. NTV has had a significant impact on the audiences as, since its launch until june 2023, it has positioned itself as the most viewed channel among cultural channels and, in the same period, it is the third most watched children's channel.   During these two years, more than 12 million people have tuned into NTV, giving an impulse to live and diverse programming, fostering cultural, social, artistic and scientific development, strengthening identity and reflecting diversity in all its dimentions.

Les Cantons et la Confédération ont soutenu des « projets de transformation » proposés par des entreprises culturelles pour s’adapter au nouveau contexte provoqué par l’épidémie de COVID-19. Il s’agissait de les aider dans une réorientation structurelle ou à regagner des publics. Visarte Vaud a bénéficié d’un soutien financier du Canton de Vaud et de la Confédération pour élaborer un projet de transformation.   Projet soutenu par le Canton de Vaud (projet de transformation 2022) En 2022, l’enquête menée par Visarte Vaud visait à identifier grâce à des méthodes qualitatives (rencontres en face à face) les besoins et manques des artistes visuelles vaudoises et visuels vaudois dans le contexte de la pandémie et à pouvoir mettre en place des projets concrets pour y pallier. Les entretiens approfondis, complétés par des focus groups, des groupes de travail, des tables rondes ainsi que des observations sur le terrain des arts visuels, ont donné la possibilité à Visarte Vaud de réunir tout d'abord des informations nombreuses et précieuses sur la situation des artistes locales et locaux. Visarte a pu rassembler des recommandations de la part des plasticiennes et des plasticiens en vue de mises en œuvre concrètes visant deux objectifs principaux en lien avec deux problématiques transversales fondamentales :  1) La mise à disposition de ressources et d'outils facilitateurs de la gestion professionnelle d'une carrière d'artiste  2) La fédération des autrices et des auteurs des arts visuels, notamment via la conception d'un événement sous forme de Forum des arts visuels qui a eu lieu à Lausanne en septembre 2023.   La nécessité de se fédérer est apparue comme la condition primordiale permettant d'atteindre le but de cette recherche : la reconnaissance du statut et la dé-précarisation des artistes visuelles et visuels.  Ce projet de transformation visait à générer plus de cohésion interne dans le milieu des plasticiennes et des plasticiens mais aussi plus de lien avec la société pour une meilleure compréhension du monde artistique particulier des artistes visuelles et visuels.
Results: Dans le cadre de ce projet, nous avons établi des collaborations avec les artistes participantes et participants au projet et les autres actrices et acteurs du secteur des arts visuels vaudois, ainsi qu'avec les sections valaisannes et genevoises de Visarte œuvrant dans les mêmes buts.   Tout ce travail a permis à Visarte Vaud de déposer un nouveau dossier de demande de fonds pour la réalisation d’un Forum Des Arts Visuels sur deux journées afin de permettre d’aborder les différentes thématiques qui touchent le statut de l’artiste.

Title EN: Enactment of the Te Ture mō te Hararei Tūmatanui o te Kāhui o Matariki 2022 | Te Kāhui o Matariki Public Holiday Act 2022
Goal: Integrate Culture In Sustainable Development Frameworks
SDG: SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development

Cultural Domain: Design,Performing Arts,Media Arts,Cinema and Audiovisual Arts,Music,Publishing,Visual Arts
Agency Implementation: Manatū Taonga Ministry for Culture and Heritage Ministry for Business, Innovation and Employment Te Arawhiti Office for Māori Crown Relations
Main Feature: Matariki is the Māori name for Pleiades, which is an open star cluster within the constellation of Taurus. For many Māori, the eastern pre-dawn appearance of Matariki in the winter sky, during the last quarter of the lunar month of Pipiri, marks the beginning of the Māori New Year. Some iwi use the heliacal rising of other stars, such as Puanga – as their marker of the Māori New Year.  In April 2022 Te Ture mō te Hararei Tūmatanui o te Kāhui o Matariki 2022 | Te Kāhui o Matariki Public Holiday Act 2022 was passed. The Act that was drafted in both Te Reo Māori and English, which is only the fifth legislative Act in New Zealand to have this feature. The Bill was introduced in all three readings through speeches that were in Te Reo Māori by the then Minister for Arts, Culture and Heritage Hon Kiritapu Allan.  The passing of the legislation acknowledges the importance of celebrating cultural diversity and the importance of traditional knowledge systems.  Since April 2022, Matariki has been celebrated and honoured as a nation through hautapu ceremonies including a national broadcast of a hautapu hosted by different iwi each year. International interest in Matariki has grown considerably as the same star cluster has significance to communities from the Pacific Islands to Australia, Asia, the Americas, Europe and Africa. Other nations are now exploring how they can also revive traditions associated with these stars.  Since the Te Ture mō te Hararei Tūmatanui o te Kāhui o Matariki 2022 | Te Kāhui o Matariki Public Holiday Act 2022 was passed into law, a Chief Advisor to the government position has been established, to provide advice on Matariki.   The inaugural nationally broadcasted Hautapu ceremony in 2022, hosted at Museum of New Zealand Te Papa Tongarewa, New Zealand’s national museum alongside mana whenua and the Right Honourable Jacinda Ardern (Prime Minister at the time). The nationally broadcasted Hautapu ceremony has since been hosted in 2023 by Ngāti Whakaue in Rotorua, and in 2024 will be hosted by Kāi Tahu in Wanaka, Otago.
Results: Most New Zealanders (87%) are aware of Matariki and more than half (57%) understand what it is and why we celebrate it in Aotearoa New Zealand.  For many New Zealanders, Matariki is about connection and national identity:  •	Nearly 3 in 4 New Zealanders (70%) think Matariki is a chance to celebrate the culture, people, and stories of Aotearoa New Zealand  •	2 in 3 (66%) think Matariki is for all New Zealanders  •	72% see it as an opportunity to connect with Māori culture  •	68% think it brings people and communities together  •	65% see it as an opportunity for intergenerational storytelling and knowledge sharing  •	55% feel Matariki encourages people to do something to connect with the natural environment   Six in 10 New Zealanders celebrated Matariki in 2023, and while the ways of celebrating varied, getting together with friends and whānau for kai and going outside to view the Matariki star cluster were the most popular activities.  The Matariki public holiday also encouraged various activities over the long weekend for 64% of New Zealanders from spending time with friends and whānau, going out for a meal or drink, attending an event, festival, or concert (Matariki and non Matariki specific), to shopping, day trips, and getting away for the long weekend.  There is currently no specific evaluation for the Matariki public holiday. However, the Ministry for Culture and Heritage is preparing to release two reports on Matariki 2023, which include consumer spend report and a national attitudes/behaviour report.

Main Feature: The Arts Council’s Equality, Diversity and Inclusion (EDI, formerly separate Equality Scheme and Disability Action Plan format) Policy is developed on the basis that everyone in Northern Ireland has an equal right to engage with and participate in the arts, regardless of age, marital status, having dependants, disability, sex and gender identity, race, religion, political opinion, sexual orientation, or socioeconomic status.
Results: As part of the delivery of the outgoing Equality Action Plan, delivered between 2019 and 2024 ACNI have provided opportunities for older people, many of whom have a disability, to engage in the arts via the Arts and Older People Programme, a programme designed to reduce loneliness and isolation. ACNI have also delivered a young people and wellbeing programme (ARTiculate) to improve the emotional, physical and social wellbeing of young people. ACNI have delivered a Creative Schools Partnership programme within designated Urban Village areas – a government initiative designed to improve community relations in areas of Northern Ireland where there has been a history of poor community relations, deprivation and tension. ACNI implemented a schools lending programme. They also undertook an audit of inequalities to monitor engagement in the arts by Section 75 Groups. ACNI improved visibility of Section 75 groups by promoting positive imagery through ACNI media releases. They provided equality training to all Arts Council staff (including Board members). ACNI liaised with two deliberative forums – rural and minority ethnic/global majority artists and organisations. Minority ethnic mentoring and residencies programme  has been mainstreamed as part of SIAP. ACNI have delivered a premium payment programme to support 375 groups to access the arts.    As part of the delivery of the outgoing Disability Action Plan, delivered between 2019 and 2024, ACNI have delivered disability and neurodiversity training to staff helping to increase awareness and confidence. ACNI have improved their monitoring and evaluation systems to, more accurately measure, the extent to which disabled people are represented in our audiences, as participants and within our workforce. ACNI supported the careers of disabled artists through providing grants (SIAP), improving access to the application process and funding key arts and disability organisations. They participated in research to establish the feasibility of a national disability access card. A Ministry of Understanding was drawn up with the University of Atypical to support D/deaf, neurodiverse and disabled artists applying for Arts Council investment.
Recommandations: The EDI Plan will be monitored by an internal Working Group and progress reviewed at Arts Council board meetings on an annual basis. ACNI will regularly publish updates, using its various channels of communication, outlining how specific issues are being addressed. We will report on progress of this plan annually as part of our submission to the Equality Commission of Northern Ireland.     The EDI Policy recognises that while ACNI have supported and promoted developmental initiatives over many years, our work in advancing change still has a long way to go. We are all too aware that many inequities still exist in the arts and that there is a substantial number of people who continue to experience barriers to engaging with and participating in the arts. We believe that through promoting equality, diversity and inclusion, we can benefit from high quality art that is relevant and more reflective of our society today.    The EDI Plan has identified a number of actions to complete going forward, including but not limited to: completing an Equality, Diversity and Inclusion Audit, monitoring key audience indicators, introducing new measures of diversity to strengthen the evidence ACNI have to inform decisions, liaising with strategic partners towards encouraging greater diversity on Arts sector Boards, continuing to report on equality, evaluating key EDI programmes, as well as maintaining and creating new EDI advisory groups.

The OSMR Act 2022 was enacted on 10 December 2022. The OSMR Act 2022 amended the Broadcasting Act 2009 to establish Coimisiún na Meán and dissolve the Broadcasting Authority of Ireland (“BAI”).  In addition to undertaking the functions of the BAI as the regulator for broadcasting in Ireland, Coimisiún na Meán is to establish a regulatory framework for online safety, update the regulation of television broadcasting and audiovisual on-demand services, and transpose the EU’s revised Audiovisual Media Services Directive into Irish law.  Coimisiún na Meán carries out a range of activities to support Ireland’s media sector and help develop content for Irish audiences that reflects and shapes Irish society. It runs funding schemes to support the production and preservation of culturally valuable broadcast content, and in 2024, is prioritising developing a Local Democracy Reporting Scheme and a Courts Reporting Scheme, to stimulate the provision of high quality, diverse and innovative news and comment on current affairs.  It also supports the development of the media sector and related events and activities through sponsorship and the implementation of sectoral learning and development programmes. Media literacy initiatives, and support of Media Literacy Ireland to make sure that people can critically understand and interact with media and make informed choices about what they see, read and share online. It also aims to promote high standards of environmental practices in the media sector, through the Broadcasting Sustainability Network.  In addition, An Coimisiún’s Gender, Equality, Inclusion and Diversity Strategy, due to be published in 2024, will be an important step to help ensure that the media is appropriately diverse, accessible, inclusive, and representative of contemporary Ireland.  Coimisiún na Meán’s regulatory functions also include: •	Licensing radio and television services additional to those provided by RTÉ, TG4, the Houses of the Oireachtas Channel and the Irish Film Channel.  •	Regulating TV and radio services and audiovisual/video on-demand services established in Ireland. •	Having overall responsibility for the regulation of Irish public service broadcasters. •	Devising and implementing codes and rules for programme content on Irish broadcasting services. •	Handling complaints from viewers and listeners concerning content broadcast by licensed and public service broadcasters and made available on video on-demand services. •	Implementing a range of plurality activities, including providing advice to the Minister is respect of media mergers.  Coimisiún na Meán is also is responsible for Ireland’s Online Safety Framework. This framework makes digital services accountable for how they protect people, especially children, from harm online.  Broadcasters in the State must be licenced by Coimisiún na Meán. The Broadcasting and Other Media Regulation Acts 2009 to 2022 provides the statutory framework for licencing and regulation of broadcasting services and obliges Coimisiún na Meán to ensure the provision of open, inclusive and pluralistic broadcasting and audiovisual media sectors.

Title EN: EU support for the recovery of the CCSIs in the wake of Covid-19, the digital and the green transitions
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture
SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Cultural and creative sectors
Cultural Domain: Design,Performing Arts,Media Arts,Cinema and Audiovisual Arts,Music,Publishing,Visual Arts
Agency Implementation: European Commission, Ministries of EU Member States
Main Feature: The Cultural and Creative Sectors and Industries (CCSIs) have been dramatically hit by the Covid-19 crisis, especially in the case of activities based on venues and visits, performing arts, music and ‘heritage’ sectors. According to available data, music venues reported a 76% drop in attendance and museums lost up to 75-80% of their revenues (in popular touristic regions). The crisis exacerbated even more the structural weaknesses of the sector. The pandemic, followed by the energy crisis and high inflation, caused an overall slowdown in investments in the cultural and creative industries, which face additional difficulties to access debt and equity due to their characteristics (micro-size enterprises, intangible intellectual property assets, etc.). In this context, public investment keeps playing an important role in financing cultural and creative industries.  Hence, to support Member States’ actions, the European Commission has taken a set of measures to tackle the consequences of the coronavirus outbreak on the cultural and creative sectors.  As already detailed in the previous UNESCO 2021 report, the Commission issued the EU guidelines on the safe resumption of activities in the cultural sector in June 2021. The Commission has also published the first interactive EU funding guide for Culture (CulturEU) to help the sector navigate through various funding opportunities.  Furthermore, an impressive amount of funding has been mobilised to support the recovery of the sectors. EU financial support to cultural and creative sectors has been substantially increased, with almost EUR 2.5 billion from the Creative Europe programme, for the programming period 2021-2027, (increased by more than 60% compared to the previous programme 2014-2020). Moreover, at least EUR 2.28 billion have been allocated in the newly created cluster dedicated to culture, creativity and inclusive society in Horizon Europe, the EU funding programme for research and innovation.  Additionally, the cultural and creative sectors have also benefited from significant investments from the Recovery and Resilience Facility (RRF), the EU plan for emerging stronger from the COVID-19 crisis and the key instrument at the heart of NextGenerationEU.  The RRF entered into force on 19 February 2021. It finances reforms and investments in EU Member States made from the start of the pandemic in February 2020 until 31 December 2026.  18 Member States have included in their recovery and resilience plans a range of reforms and investments to support the resilience of the cultural and creative industries and to drive their green and digital transition. Overall, total estimated expenditure in the cultural sector amounts to EUR 11.7 billion, across 18 Member States, which corresponds to 1.8% of the total expenditure in the plans. This expenditure is matched with 141 measures across these 18 Member States.  Among the most relevant reforms, various Member states have planned legislation to improve the status of artists and cultural workers, embrace digital and greening opportunities or adjust funding schemes. Investments include, for instance, support to the production and distribution of digital content, digitisation of cultural heritage, acquisition of digital skills, renovations to increase appropriate energy efficiency in cultural buildings, safeguarding of cultural heritage sites against climate change, and green and climate-friendly projects by cultural actors.  Other measures target the competitiveness, innovation and internationalisation of CCSIs, training and capacity building, the accessibility of content, access to finance, intellectual property management, arts education and research, attractiveness of territories, cultural tourism, among others. Some Member States have planned innovative actions to harness the power of culture for social cohesion and well-being. In addition, the cultural and creative sectors will also benefit from horizontal measures for all sectors. For instance, green construction will increase demand for architectural services. Support for the digitalisation of small and medium-sized enterprises or digital skills will usually also be open to CCSI professionals and companies as well as increase demand for their services.

Therefore, through the artistic programme, the city is led away from its prevailing public perception as a disadvantaged industrial city and into its next phase, strengthening its position on the cultural map at a regional, national, and international level. This is being realised through wider synergies within the national and international contemporary cultural field, turning the city into a thriving cultural destination, one undoubtedly remarkable for the visitor.  By becoming the European Capital of Culture, Elefsina is joining an ECoC family of over 70 European cities that have held the title so far. Elefsina is the fourth European Capital of Culture hosted in Greece, after Athens (1985), Thessaloniki (1997), and Patras (2006). In 2023, the city of Elefsina is not celebrating alone, as the title of European Capital of Culture is being hosted together with our partner cities, Timișoara in Romania and Veszprém in Hungary, forging close links, exchanges, and collaborations between the three cities.

Title EN: Exhibition of photographs "Sons of a Lesser God. Stories of Palestinian girls and boys arrested by the Israeli army", Padova, 3-18 July 2021
Goal: Promote Human Rights And Fundamental Freedoms
SDG: SDG 5 - Achieve gender equality and empower all women and girls,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels
Area of Monitoring: Artistic freedom
Agency Implementation: Università degli Studi di Padova - UNESCO Chair Human Rights, Democracy and Peace
Main Feature: From 3rd to 18th of July 2021, in the Cortile Pensile of Palazzo Moroni of Padova took place the Photo exhibition "Sons of a Lesser God. Stories of Palestinian girls and boys arrested by the Israeli army", by Roberto Brancolini.  Roberto Brancolini's photographs told us the experience of Palestinian adolescents arrested by the Israeli army in the Occupied Territories, the areas of Jerusalem, Ramallah, Nablus and Hebron. Every year, Israel prosecutes 500 to 700 minors in its military courts, who are arrested, interrogated and detained by the Israeli army. It is estimated that Israeli authorities have arrested, tried and detained approximately 13,000 Palestinian minors since 2000.  Under international law, the detention of minors should be a measure of last resort and last for the shortest possible time. Civil law protects minors arrested in Israel, however, in the Occupied Territories of the West Bank, it applies the law of war and military courts operate. In addition, according to the complaints of many observers, Palestinian boys and girls are frequently subjected to arbitrary arrest and detention. The most common charge brought against them is stone-throwing. The penalty for this offence can be up to 20 years in prison.  Roberto Brancolini, a freelance photographer, specialises in news and reportage. He has followed the development of anti-globalisation movements in Italy, the events of the indigenous people of Chiapas in Mexico after the Zapatista revolt and the Gezi Park protests in Turkey. More recently, he carried out photographic research on women migrating from Eastern Europe, known as caregivers. Since the construction of the separation wall in the West Bank, he has been recording the deterioration of the living conditions of Palestinian civilians. He also collaborates with Tavola della Pace and with national agencies, magazines and newspapers.  The event was organised by L’Osteria volante, Group InScialla, Labiba Network, AssoPace Padova, in collaboration with Padova municipality, Municipal Department of International Cooperation, Archive Peace and Human Rights and the Human Rights Centre “Antonio Papisca”, University of Padova.
Results: Through a visual exposition the photographer was able to show the underlying contradiction between the sources of international law and Israel's conduct in violation of those laws. Thanks to the photos, victims are not simply data in international reports, but people, in this particular case, children, with their own lives and histories.  The visitor can then establish an emotional connection with the photo subjects, becoming aware of another injustice perpetrated against innocents.  The photo exhibition is still touring Italy and it was also shown in other european countries.

Title EN: Evaluation de l’impact socioéconomique du secteur culturel dans l’atteinte des cibles des ODD du Burkina Faso
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture
SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Cultural and creative sectors
Cultural Domain: Design,Performing Arts,Media Arts,Cinema and Audiovisual Arts,Music,Publishing,Visual Arts
Agency Implementation: Ministère de la Communication, de la Culture, des Arts et du Tourisme (MCCAT)  Commune de Ouagadougou
Main Feature: Au Burkina Faso, comme dans la plupart des pays du Sud, l’insuffisance d’informations quantitatives et qualitatives due à l’indisponibilité et/ou à la fragmentation des données statistiques culturelles ont conduit à un faible financement de la culture dans les stratégies et politiques de développement nationales et locales. Cet état de fait reste un frein majeur pour une meilleure prise en compte du secteur culturel dans les stratégies de développement malgré que celui-ci soit constamment cité comme secteur prioritaire de développement dans les discours politiques. Il est donc plus qu’essentiel et urgent de rassembler les données et de mettre en place des systèmes de mesure plus fiables pour mieux comprendre les multiples contributions de la culture aux dimensions économiques, sociales et environnementales du développement durable.   Ainsi, en vue de pallier l’absence de données sur la contribution du secteur de la culture au développement social et économique et de mieux orienter les décideurs, le Ministère en charge de la culture a engagé au cours des dernières années des initiatives en vue du renforcement de son système de production et de diffusion de données statistiques culturelles. Cette action a été possible grâce à la réalisation de l’étude pilote d’évaluation des Indicateurs Culture|2030 de l’UNESCO. Il s’agit d’une méthodologie innovante développée par l’UNESCO afin de mesurer et évaluer le rôle de la culture dans la réalisation des ODD. Dénommés Indicateurs thématiques de la culture 2030, ce cadre est bâti autour de vingt-deux (22) indicateurs regroupés en 4 dimensions thématiques transversales à savoir : (i) Environnement et résilience, (ii) Prospérité et ressources, (iii) Connaissances et compétences, (iv) Inclusion et participation.     Cette étude a consisté à mobiliser l’ensemble des sources et ressources informationnelles disponibles au niveau sectoriel (études sectorielles et annuaire statistiques ministériels, rapports d’activités, etc.) extra sectoriel et macro (rapport d’enquête nationaux de l’INSD) pour évaluer et analyser les vingt-deux (22) indicateurs selon les dimensions concernées.    La réalisation de l’étude pilote a également été un tremplin de sensibilisation et de plaidoyer auprès des parties prenantes (Administrations publiques, OSC, PTF, Secteur privés, Institut national des Statistiques, Universitaires, etc.) sur les défis et enjeux liés à la production et de la diffusion régulières d’informations statistiques exhaustives sur le secteur culturel. A ce titre, le lancement de l’étude intervenue le jeudi 07 octobre 2021, a été placé sous la coprésidence du Ministre en charge de la culture et du Maire de la Commune de Ouagadougou et a connu la participation de plus d’une centaine de participants provenant d’horizon divers.    Dans le cadre de ladite étude, une équipe pluridisciplinaire issue du Ministère en charge de la Culture, de la mairie de Ouagadougou, de l’Institut national de la Statistique et de la Démographie (INSD) et des personnes ressources a été mise en place par un arrêté ministériel. Cette équipe a été assistée par un expert sous-régional mis à disposition par l’UNESCO assurant l’interface entre l’équipe nationale et l’équipe de coordination de l’UNESCO.   Dans le cadre de cette opération, le Burkina Faso, s’est appuyé sur les acquis de son système de statistiques culturelles en exploitant les données des différentes études déjà réalisées. Ainsi, elle a permis au pays de tester la qualité de son système de production de statistiques culturelles et d’en tirer les leçons pour son renforcement
Results: La réalisation de l’étude pilote a permis au Burkina Faso d’actualiser l’évaluation de certains indicateurs d’impact clés du secteur culturel, de mettre en lumière les faiblesses du dispositif de collecte et de production de données statistiques et de mener des analyses qualitatives;    l’évaluation des indicateurs clés réalisée en 2021 a permis l’actualisation de la situation d’indicateurs d’impacts que sont : le PIB culturel évalué à 3,4% en 2019, la proportion d’emplois culturels estimée à 3,5 % en 2019, le taux d’exportation de biens estimé à 0,01% en 2020 et la proportion de la dépense des ménages adressée au produits culturels estimée à 1,6% en 2018;     l’étude a permis de mettre en lumière la capacité du secteur culturel à apporter des réponses efficaces, durables et inclusives aux principaux défis de développement actuel du Burkina Faso :   En effet, il apparait qu’en dépit d’un contexte social et sécuritaire difficile, les bases du vivre ensemble des Burkinabè restent assez solides car 95,8% des personnes enquêtées dans le cadre de l’étude, tolèrent d’autres cultures dans leur espace et 56% de personnes interrogées sont contre toute discrimination basée sur le genre. Toutefois, le pays doit faire des efforts en matière d’éducation culturelle et environnementale dans les politiques publiques tant aux niveaux national et local.

Main Feature: The "Everyday Ethiopia" photo exhibition was a traveling showcase organized by Gerar – The Creative Hub, in collaboration with the Addis Abeba Professional Photographers Association and supported by the USAID Ethiopia Support Program. The exhibition aimed to present the diverse cultural tapestry of Ethiopia through the lens of fifteen established and emerging photographers. It was held in four major Ethiopian cities: Addis Ababa, Bahir Dar, Hawassa, and Dire Dawa.  The collaboration demonstrated a shared commitment to preserving and celebrating Ethiopia’s cultural heritage. The exhibition featured a wide range of photographic works, including candid portraits, cultural celebrations, and market scenes. Objectives  The primary objectives of the "Everyday Ethiopia" exhibition were:  1. To promote youth dialogue for peace-building processes. 2. To illustrate the power of art in bringing people together and enhancing social cohesion. 3. To engage youth in the creative sector and promote the establishment of civil societies.  Activities and Engagement  The exhibition included a series of complementary activities aimed at engaging youth and the wider community. These included: - Close and Open Dialogue Sessions: Facilitated discussions aimed at promoting peace and social cohesion. - Workshops and On-the-Job Training: Practical training sessions in photography and exhibition management, designed to enhance skills and encourage youth participation in the creative industries.

Title EN: Example of an individual measure at local level: Knjigobežni.ce project – construction and installation of outdoor reading sheds to promote reading in Celje

Agency Implementation: Municipality of Celje Celje Central regional library
Main Feature: The Municipality of Celje, in cooperation with the Secondary School of Civil Engineering and Environmental Protection, has installed 19 reading sheds with a large selection of books in public places in all parts of Celje. Financing was provided by the Municipality of Celje. The public company Zelenice was also involved in setting up and installing the sheds. The city administration presented the installation of the reading sheds to the public during a five-day event entitled Knjigobežni.ce, which it organised together with the Celje Central Regional Library and the Celeia Celje Institute for Cultural Events and Tourism. Visitors were welcomed in cafés and restaurants in the city centre with a variety of books to browse through and take home if they particularly liked them. The books were accompanied by bookmarks presenting the Knjigobežni.ce project. The promotional event ended with an afternoon of storytelling, where Anja Štefan, a well-known writer and storyteller, told fairy tales to inspire and encourage children and adults alike to read.+§%
Results: The city of Celje is working to improve access to books. It promotes the improvement of existing forms of accessibility through regular monitoring of user needs and the development of new forms of access to knowledge.  19 reading sheds have been set up in public spaces in all districts of the city. The reading sheds make it possible to store and exchange books with a wide variety of content. They appeal to young and disadvantaged groups and promote reading among all generations.
Recommandations: This activity makes the Municipality of Celje one of the "Reading Friendly Municipalities" for the period 2022-2025, which is a special certificate that can be awarded to municipalities that are committed to improving reading literacy, promoting reading and developing a reading culture.

Title EN: Exonération des droits de douane sur les produits culturels dans la politique commerciale du Bénin
Goal: Achieve A Balanced Flow Of Cultural Goods And Services And Increase The Mobility Of Artists And Cultural Professionals
SDG: SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 10 - Reduce inequality within and among countries,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Flow of cultural goods and services
Cultural Domain: Design,Performing Arts,Media Arts,Cinema and Audiovisual Arts,Music,Publishing,Visual Arts
Agency Implementation: MINISTERE DE L’ECONOMIE ET DES FINANCES (MEF)
Main Feature: Au Bénin, les produits culturels bénéficient d'une exonération partielle de droits de douane, conformément à la politique commerciale du pays. Ils sont classés comme des biens essentiels sociaux et sont par conséquent soumis à un taux de droit de douane de 0%. Cette exonération vise à promouvoir le développement du secteur culturel au Bénin en facilitant l'importation et la distribution de produits culturels tels que les livres, les films, la musique et les œuvres d'art. Cela permet aux Béninois d'avoir un accès plus large à une variété de produits culturels à des prix abordables, tout en stimulant la croissance de l'industrie culturelle locale. Il est important de noter que cette exonération ne s'applique pas à tous les produits culturels. Certains produits, tels que les produits audiovisuels et les jeux vidéo, peuvent être soumis à des droits de douane à des taux réduits.  Pour plus d'informations sur la politique commerciale du Bénin relative aux produits culturels, les sources suivantes sont disponibles : Rapport d'Analyse sur la Politique Commerciale du Bénin : https://instad.bj/images/docs/rapports/Rapport%20d'Analyse%20sur%20Politique%20Commerciale.pdf   Site web du Ministère du Commerce et de l'Industrie du Bénin : https://commerce.gouv.bj/
Results: -	Accessibilité accrue des produits culturels :  La réduction ou la suppression des taxes à l'importation a permis de rendre les livres, films, instruments de musique et autres produits culturels plus abordables pour le public béninois. Cela a facilité leur diffusion et leur consommation. -	Développement des industries culturelles locales : Les exonérations ont aidé les créateurs, artistes et entreprises culturelles béninoises à se procurer plus facilement leurs intrants de production. Cela a soutenu la compétitivité et la croissance des filières culturelles nationales. -	Diversification de l'offre culturelle : Avec des produits culturels importés plus accessibles, les consommateurs béninois ont pu bénéficier d'un éventail plus large d'œuvres et d'expressions artistiques, favorisant la diversité culturelle.
Financial Ressources: Non estimées

Design Thinking Workshop (DTW);  6. Road to Creative Media Exhibition (Pameran Jalan Menuju Media Kreatif, JMMK);  7. Music Without Borders (Musik Tanpa Batas, MTB);  8. Kriya Expo;  9. Minang Film Festival (MIFFEST);  10. Mini-Seminar Series: Meeting of Minds;  11. Animakini Festival (Animasi Cikini); and  12. Branding Indonesian MSME Products.   FKI is a biennial arts festival initiated by BKPTSI, which includes ISI Denpasar, ISI Surakarta, ISI Yogyakarta, ISBI Bandung, ISBI Aceh, ISI Padangpanjang, ISBI Tanah Papua, IKJ, and STKW Surabaya with support from Kemendikbudristek. This festival aims to showcase the practices, discourses, and achievements of art-design works from students, lecturers, and selected educational staff from higher education institutions of the arts in Indonesia. ISI Denpasar hosted the 2023 FKI with the theme “Samudra-Rakta-Samasta” (Maritime Power in Contemporary Art Creation), highlighting dwipantara maritime affairs from time to time.  These higher institutions of the arts also individually organize various arts events at the national and international levels. One is ISI Surakarta, which organizes World Dance Day and the Blora Market Cultural Festival. ISI Surakarta organizes World Dance Day by holding a 24-hour non-stop dance performance. This event's 17th year of organization was in 2023, which brought dancers, choreographers, art groups, art institutions, and cultural figures from within and outside the country to perform together in several collaborative dance performances.  Meanwhile, the Blora Market Cultural Festival is an event initiated by ISI Surakarta in collaboration with the Blora Regency Government and several artists from Blora. This festival is research presented as an arts and culture festival to develop the arts and culture potential of Blora. This research was funded in 2023 by the Kedaireka Matching Fund Program, Kemendikbudristek, in cooperation with the Blora Regency Government. This festival was held on September 16, 2023, in Blora, Central Java. The main theme of this festival is a combination of Blora's identity, Blora's artistic potential, and socio-cultural harmony in Blora. It showcases Blora's culture advancement objects, such as teak forests, barongan art, and the Blora traditional market.  ISI Yogyakarta also organizes several arts events at the national and international levels, such as the International Jogjakarfest, DTW, and JMMK. The Karawitan Department organizes the International Jogjakarfest under the official name "International Yogyakarta Karawitan Festival." This annual event presents musical performances and international online webinars. The musical performances showcase the beauty of musical art, both live and virtually, from musical groups within Indonesia and abroad.  Meanwhile, DTW has been held since 2014 through collaboration between ISI Yogyakarta and Hochschule Hannover University of Applied Sciences and Arts (HsH) Germany. This workshop is one of ISI Yogyakarta's annual activity agendas, held every May by the Interior Design Study Program with Prof. Gunnar Spellmeyer and the Nextars HsH Team as the main convenors. Through DTW, Indonesian participants gain experience collaborating with foreign participants from HsH in problem-solving using the Design Thinking method. It is hoped that ISI Yogyakarta students can use this experience to complete their assignments.  JMMK is an annual exhibition of visual arts photography, film screenings, and television animation, which has been organized since 2008 by the Faculty of Recorded Media Arts. This event is a forum for students and lecturers from the Photography, Film, and Television Study Program and the Animation Diploma Study Program to exhibit and showcase their works of art. This exhibition aims to present learning outcomes in the field of recorded media arts, as well as a tool to measure the quality of education at the Faculty of Recorded Media Arts. The works on display include photography, television programs, video/film, and animation. This exhibition gives participants freedom of theme on the condition that the works exhibited do not contain elements of discrimination to specific ethnicity, religion, race, and inter-group relations or pornography. Apart from being a forum for displaying works of recorded media art, this event is also a forum for dialogue and discussion that enriches thinking about recorded media art in the general context of the creative industry and society.  Another higher educational institution of the arts that organizes arts events at the national and international levels is ISI Pandangpanjang. The three events that have been organized are MTB, Kriya Expo, and MIFFEST. MTB is a program that has become the hallmark of the Karawitan Arts Study Program. Since 2013, MTB has become a routine activity carried out by the Karawitan Department Student Association and occurs four times a year, every three months. This program is a milestone activity that creates new creative spaces for expressing audio arts. MTB also has a significant impact on improving the quality of learning in the field of music composition. This program is a means of sharing knowledge and skills among students and a constructive learning medium. This initiative has played a role in improving learning outcomes in the Karawitan Arts Study Program. During the 2020 pandemic, MTB was held online and reached a broader audience in Pekanbaru, Yogyakarta, Bandung, and Surakarta.  Next is the Kriya Expo, an annual exhibition organized by the Craft Arts Study Program to display artworks with practical value and beauty. This exhibition involves MSMEs engaged in the crafts field to promote MSME products through exhibitions. Apart from exhibitions, seminars, and workshops in the crafts field, these are also part of the series of events. The 4th Kriya Expo in 2021, with the theme "Sustainability of the Creative Economy in the Crafts Field in the Pandemic Era," showed how the creative industry sector survived during the pandemic. The 6th Kriya Expo in 2023, with the theme "Creativity & Innovation Towards Sustainable Crafts Work," had two main activities, namely an exhibition of the best works of art by students and lecturers curated by national curator Dr. Arif Suherson, M.Sn from ISI Yogyakarta and an art market (bazaar) with the participation of MSMEs in the city of Padangpanjang and its surroundings.  Furthermore, MIFFEST is an annual student film festival the Television and Film Study Program has held since 2017. This event aims to be a medium of appreciation and education for students and the community to create a vibrant film ecosystem in West Sumatra. Initially, this event only included participants from West Sumatra, but after three years, its scope was expanded to become national.   The last higher educational institute of the arts whose program is to be reported is IKJ. The three programs this institute holds at the national or international level are the Mini-Seminar Series: Meeting of Minds, Animakini, and the Branding Indonesian MSME Products activities. IKJ initiated the Meeting of Minds amid the COVID-19 pandemic to build an atmosphere of scientific discussion and resilience amidst the challenges the world community was experiencing at that time. The Meetings of Minds has been held 3-4 times yearly since 2021, filled with discussion activities in the campus environment and involving the public, with resource persons from internal IKJ and also external (art experts, cultural experts, or national or international academicians). Topics of discussion included (1) Betawi culture as an iconic institution and its relationship to urbanity; (2) research and innovation topics that refer to the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals as a blueprint for achieving a better and more sustainable future for all; (3) Culture Advancement as an effort to increase cultural resilience and the contribution of Indonesian culture amidst world civilization through protecting, developing, utilizing, and fostering culture; and (4) other topics related to culture and creative industries.  Meanwhile, the Animakini festival has been held every year since 2017 by IKJ with support from the government through the Creative Economy Agency, Jakarta Arts Center Taman Ismail Marzuki (Provincial Government of DKI Jakarta), Indonesian Institute of Sciences, National Film Production, and also non-government parties, such as Ainaki. This festival focuses on providing a forum for actors in the animation ecosystem with the aim of (1) socializing the main strategies of Indonesian animation and formulating a road map for developing the animation creative economy; (2) introducing current animation developments in the education sector and distribution industry; and (3) collaborating to create inter-regional working networks through animation business incubators that bring together parties, academics, industry, government, communities, and the media. Collaborative activities to strengthen the animation ecosystem include seminars, talk shows, masterclasses, exhibitions, workshops, and competitions to increase the competitiveness and quality of animation. In 2020, the festival was held online during the pandemic with the theme "Even though you are far away, you still move" with a three-day highlight event that included a 3D modeling workshop, production processes at TV stations, academic and industrial seminars, as well as watching animated works together for a month. Then, in 2021, the festival was also organized online with the theme "Collaboration and Exploration" and emphasized serving as a meeting forum for animation ecosystem players in Indonesia, final project collaboration, 3D modeling and motion graphics workshops, music videos, presentations on Indonesian animation studies, and sharing session with actors in the animation industry. In 2022 and 2023, the festival was held back to normal at Taman Ismail Marzuki, Jakarta.   Lastly, the Branding Indonesian MSME Products program was collaboratively initiated between the UNESCO Jakarta Office and the Architectural Documentation Center through the Jakarta Old City Creative Youth program in 2019. The Visual Communication Design Study Program helped develop the branding of 13 MSMEs around the Old City of Jakarta in 2019-2020. With support from MSME development institutions, namely the Indonesian Culinary Alliance and Selow Food, student groups were able to collaborate in product branding of selected MSMEs, starting from identity development, packaging, promotional media to marketing media, which these MSMEs can directly utilize to increase their product value. In 2021-2022, exhibition and seminar activities were held online with the theme "Branding Ceria UKM Gembira," In 2022-2023, it was held in person with the theme "Joy Collaboration.”   In general, exemplary higher education institution initiatives that support the mobility of artists and cultural professionals are aimed at contributing to achieving the following agenda(s) of the National Strategy for Culture: 1. Provide space for the diversity of cultural expressions and encourage cultural interaction to strengthen the inclusiveness of culture (Agenda 1); 2. Protect and develop values, expressions, and practices of traditional culture to enrich national culture (Agenda 2); and 3. Develop and utilize cultural resources to strengthen the position of Indonesia internationally (Agenda 3).
Results: 2023 World Dance Day: One hundred forty dance performances were performed and documented on the YouTube channel, and as many as 20 MSMEs benefited from this activity.  2023 FKI: The 12th FKI involved art institutes in Indonesia and collaborations with maestros, artists, designers, and professional artists. It also gathered world art institutes such as Lasalle Arts College Singapore, The Western University of Australia, Masarakam University of Thailand, and Malaya University of Malaysia.  International Jogjakarfest: Throughout the implementation from 2020 to 2022, at least 76 performances of musical works, both classic and contemporary compositions, were presented, which can also be accessed on the YouTube channel. Every year, at least participants from 5 friendly countries, such as Singapore, Germany, Russia, Thailand, and New Zealand, take part.  DTW: Through a rigorous selection, an average of 50 participants attend DTW yearly. These consist of students and lecturers from 3 study programs in the Design Department (i.e., Interior Design, Visual Communication Design, and Product Design), students from HsH, and general participants such as professional designers, practitioners/experts, and MSME representatives.  JMKK: Throughout its implementation from 2020 to 2023, more than 100 works have been exhibited. This exhibition and screening involved participants from various art colleges that are members of BKSPTSI as well as guest participants from overseas campuses such as Universitas Teknologi Mara (UiTM), Malaysia; Royal Melbourne Institute (RMIT), Australia; University of Tasmania, Australia; and Canberra Institute of Technology, Australia. In 2020-2021, the exhibition was held online due to the COVID-19 pandemic, while in 2022-2023, the exhibition was held back to normal, with an average of 50-75 visitors per day.  MTB: This program has created several talented young composers from West Sumatra who have now achieved recognition at the national and international levels, such as Canda Suara, Gubuk Kopi, Taman Bunga, Jumaidil Project, Marawa, Ethnic Percussion, Karak Trondol, Agung Perdana Project, Avant Garde Dewa Gugat (AGDG), and Darak Badarak.  Mini-Seminar Series: Meeting of Minds: In 2021, the seminar was held online with 168 participants. Meanwhile, in 2022 and 2023, the seminar was held back to normal with 209 participants (including 4 participants from Singapore) and 160 participants (including 1 participant from Australia), respectively.  Animakini: 1. In 2020, it was held online, involving 30 institutions. 2. In 2021, it was held online, involving around 1000 participants, including representatives from 48 vocational schools from Medan to Sumbawa, 17 study institutions and corporations from all over Indonesia, and 91 campuses from Banda Aceh to Papua, and even from Nanjing, China. 3. In 2022 and 2023, it was held back to normal again, involving around 300 participants yearly.  Branding Indonesian MSME Products: 1. In 2021-2022, 24 working groups (90 students and six lecturers) for 24 MSME brands presented the final rebranding results under the guidance of the WomenPreneur Indonesian Culinary Alliance and SelowFood, in collaboration with IKJ.   2. In 2022-2023, 21 working groups (80 students and six lecturers) for 21 MSME brands presented the final rebranding results under the guidance of the WomenPreneur Indonesian Culinary Alliance.  3. In 2023-2024, 28 working groups (105 students and nine lecturers) for 28 MSME brands presented the final rebranding results.
Recommandations: Internal evaluations of the programs reported in this section by ISI Surakarta, ISI Yogyakarta, ISI Padangpanjang, and IKJ generally resulted in the following conclusions. 1. The use and utilization of technology and social media, especially during the COVID-19 pandemic, has allowed the programs to be accessed by many participants and spectators from outside the region and abroad, expanding their reach. 2. Many people are generally interested in participating in the programs; therefore, good selection and curation are needed to maintain their quality. 3. Implementation of activities is often hampered by funding because most activities still depend on funding from study programs at the relevant institutions. 4. Cooperation with domestic and international partners needs to be strengthened, especially regarding promotion and financial support for activities from third parties. 5. The members of the organizing committees are generally students, so the regeneration of the committee members in carrying out activities each year is a challenge.

Title EN: Film and Culture Policy Evaluation
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture
SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Cultural and creative sectors
Cultural Domain: Design,Performing Arts,Media Arts,Cinema and Audiovisual Arts,Music,Publishing,Visual Arts
Agency Implementation: Ministry of Culture and Sport
Main Feature: The Ministry of Culture and Sport in Ethiopia manages four key policies: Culture, Film, Language, and Sport. While the Culture and Creative Industry sector has successfully implemented the Culture and Film policies.  In alignment with the 2005 UNESCO Convention on the Protection and Promotion of the Diversity of Cultural Expressions, the Ministry has conducted thorough evaluations of the Culture and Film policies. These evaluations follow established procedures to ensure that the policies meet international standards and effectively support the cultural and creative sectors.  The objectives of these evaluations are threefold: 1. Assess Policy Effectiveness: To evaluate how well the Culture and Film policies have been implemented and their impact on the cultural and creative industries.  2. Identify Areas for Improvement: To highlight any gaps or challenges in the current policies and recommend necessary adjustments.  3. Ensure Compliance with International Standards: To verify that the policies align with the principles of the 2005 UNESCO Convention.  This evaluation process is essential for enhancing the effectiveness of cultural policies and promoting the growth of Ethiopia's creative industries.
Results: The policy evaluation process for the film and culture policies has been designed to address existing gaps and enhance the effectiveness of these policies. The evaluation involved a comprehensive stakeholder consultation process to identify priority areas and address gaps in policy implementation.  Key components of the evaluation included: Stakeholder Consultation: Engaging various stakeholders through consultative workshops to gather insights and define key areas that need improvement. This process ensured that the concerns and suggestions of relevant parties were considered in the policy revision.  Policy Alignment: The evaluation aimed to ensure that both the film and culture policies align with other national policies. This alignment is crucial for creating a cohesive policy framework that supports the broader cultural and creative sector.  Participation of Civil Society and Private Sectors: The evaluation emphasized the need for active participation from civil society organizations (CSOs) and private sector entities. Their involvement is vital for a holistic review process and for integrating diverse perspectives into the policy framework.  Digital Culture Integration: Recommendations were made to incorporate digital culture aspects into the policies. This includes adapting the policies to address the challenges and opportunities presented by the digital environment.  The policy evaluation process has provided valuable recommendations to strengthen the film and culture policies, ensuring they are more effective and relevant to the current cultural and creative landscape.

Title EN: Expanding Enhancing international cultural cooperation
Goal: Achieve A Balanced Flow Of Cultural Goods And Services And Increase The Mobility Of Artists And Cultural Professionals
SDG: SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 10 - Reduce inequality within and among countries,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Treaties and agreements
Cultural Domain: Design,Performing Arts,Media Arts,Cinema and Audiovisual Arts,Music,Publishing,Visual Arts
Agency Implementation: Ministry of Education, Science, Culture and Sport of the Republic of Armenia
Main Feature: For the purpose of ensuring the right of artists to free movement and opportunity to directly cooperate, the right to interact with the Armenian culture and that of the peoples of the world, the Ministry of Education, Science, Culture and Sport of the Republic of Armenia has initiated and continued to implement measures for consistent amendment, update of the legal and contractual basis and attracting special-purpose investments. Importance is attached to the consolidation of diversity of cultural expressions presented by different countries and individuals, ensuring the participation of Armenia in significant humanitarian and cultural activities carried out by international organizations, expanding the cooperation with the international network of non-governmental organizations in order to enhance institutional and management capabilities, promoting the integration of culture into sustainable development policies, etc.
Results: As a result of a consistent policy, we had the opportunity to establish cooperation with more than 60 states, covering almost all the continents. Such agreements provide Armenian artists with the opportunity to participate, under preferential conditions, in events organized in different countries and organisations. The signed international agreement enabled the implementation of major programs, by re-equipping a number of cultural organizations and reconditioning many monuments.
Recommandations: The established legal and contractual basis allows to expand the geography of cooperation, create preferential conditions for theatre and concert organizations, individual creatives, as well as create prerequisites for attracting additional funds from foreign countries. At the same time, divergence in interpretation of the provisions of the Convention and the low level of public awareness pose obstacles to the comprehensive cooperation. In this context, we recommend carrying out works for raising public awareness.

Title EN: Export Licences
Goal: Achieve A Balanced Flow Of Cultural Goods And Services And Increase The Mobility Of Artists And Cultural Professionals
SDG: SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 10 - Reduce inequality within and among countries,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Flow of cultural goods and services
Agency Implementation: Department for Culture, Media and Sport; Arts Council England
Main Feature: Arts Council England has launched Export Licensing Online in August 2024, a brand-new digital portal for issuing export licences. Some cultural goods – including works of art, antiques and archaeological finds – need a licence to be exported from the UK because of their age and monetary value. They will need a licence whether they are being exported permanently or temporarily. The Arts Council issues these licences on behalf of the Secretary of State for Culture, Media and Sport.    The export control system gives the UK the chance to keep cultural goods from being exported that are judged by experts to be of outstanding national importance. It also provides a guarantee that cultural goods are being exported legally. The system is designed to strike a balance, as fairly as possible, between the various interests concerned in any application for an export licence. Those interests might include the rights of the owner, in the case of a sale any buyer, and the heritage of the UK.
Results: The portal is now live and ready to accept applications. Two webinars have been hosted to showcase valuable insights and practical knowledge about how to navigate the online portal.

Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture
SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Cultural and creative sectors
Agency Implementation: Federal State of Upper Austria, KUPF Oberösterreich (“Culture Platform Upper Austria”)
Main Feature: In 2021, the Federal State of Upper Austria in cooperation with KUPF Oberösterreich (“Culture Platform Upper Austria”) launched the funding programme "EXTRA". A call for proposals is planned biennially.  The 2021 call was themed Neustart ("Restart"). Cultural initiatives and collectives were invited to submit projects developing ideas and proposals to promote a vibrant cultural sector after the COVID-19 pandemic. 12 projects were funded with a total EUR 95,000. In 2023, the call was themed Heimat and focused on a (critical) examination of the concept of “Heimat” and (social) identities, particularly regarding marginalised social positions. 8 projects were funded with a total of EUR 100,000.
Results: The programme has gathered attention also outside of Upper Austria and enabled the implementation of innovative projects. Most projects were developed specifically in response to the funding calls, and their realization would not have been possible without the funding due to the lack of other financial resources. As the programme was developed in close cooperation between KUPF Oberösterreich (Culture Platform Upper Austria) and the Federal State of Upper Austria, it also contributes to strengthening the cooperation mechanisms between Civil Society and the Federal State government.
