Title EN: Fashion Association Botswana support and empowerment of the Fashion Industry
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture
SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Cultural and creative sectors
Agency Implementation: Fashion Association Botswana
Main Feature: The Fashion Association Botswana (FAB) is a pivotal organization dedicated to nurturing and promoting the fashion industry in Botswana. It focuses on advocating for fashion designers, models, photographers, and other stakeholders within the fashion ecosystem. This initiative plays a crucial role in representing these professionals in policy-making processes, advocating for their rights, and ensuring they have a voice in various decision-making forums. Below is a comprehensive description of the key features of this initiative. Mission and Objectives The primary mission of FAB is to support and empower fashion industry professionals in Botswana. The association aims to create a thriving environment where creativity can flourish, and local talent can be showcased both nationally and internationally. The core objectives of FAB include: 1.	Advocacy and Lobbying: FAB advocates for favorable policies and regulations that support the growth and sustainability of the fashion industry. This includes lobbying for financial support, infrastructural development, and regulatory frameworks that protect the interests of fashion professionals. 2.	Representation: The association represents fashion designers, models, and photographers in various forums, ensuring their voices are heard in decision-making processes that affect the industry. 3.	Promotion of Cultural Diversity: FAB promotes the rich cultural heritage of Botswana through fashion. It encourages the integration of traditional elements into modern fashion, thereby preserving cultural identity while fostering innovation. Key Initiatives and Activities 1.	Policy Advocacy: •	FAB engages with government bodies and policymakers to influence the development of policies that benefit the fashion industry. This includes advocating for tax incentives for fashion businesses, grants for emerging designers, and the establishment of fashion hubs. •	The association also works to ensure that fashion industry professionals are included in national cultural and economic strategies. 2.	Capacity Building: •	Training and Workshops: FAB organizes training sessions and workshops to enhance the skills of fashion designers, models, and photographers. These sessions cover various aspects of the industry, including design techniques, business management, marketing, and photography. •	Mentorship Programs: The association runs mentorship programs where experienced professionals mentor emerging talents, providing guidance and support to help them navigate the industry. 3.	Networking and Collaboration: •	Events and Exhibitions: FAB organizes fashion shows, exhibitions, and networking events to provide a platform for designers to showcase their work. These events attract industry stakeholders, including buyers, investors, and media, providing exposure and business opportunities for local talent. •	Partnerships: FAB collaborates with local and international organizations, including fashion schools, industry associations, and cultural institutions, to create opportunities for cross-border collaboration and knowledge exchange. 4.	Promotion and Marketing: •	Branding and Public Relations: The association undertakes various promotional activities to raise the profile of Botswana’s fashion industry. This includes managing public relations campaigns, participating in international fashion events, and leveraging social media to highlight the work of local designers and models. •	Showcasing Talent: FAB ensures that local talent is showcased on national and international platforms, helping designers and models gain recognition and access new markets. 5.	Support Systems: •	Financial Assistance: FAB provides financial assistance in the form of grants, loans, and sponsorships to help fashion professionals develop their businesses. This financial support is crucial for covering production costs, participating in events, and expanding operations. •	Legal and Professional Support: The association offers legal assistance and professional advice to its members, helping them navigate contracts, intellectual property rights, and other legal matters related to their work. Impact on the Fashion Industry and Community The initiatives undertaken by FAB have had a significant impact on the fashion industry in Botswana. Some of the notable impacts include: 1.	Economic Empowerment: By providing financial support and business development services, FAB has empowered many fashion professionals to establish and grow their businesses, contributing to the local economy. 2.	Cultural Preservation: Through the promotion of culturally inspired fashion, FAB has played a crucial role in preserving Botswana’s cultural heritage. This has not only enriched the local fashion scene but also helped in maintaining cultural identity. 3.	Increased Visibility: FAB’s efforts in promoting local talent have increased the visibility of Botswana’s fashion industry on the international stage. This has opened up new opportunities for designers and models, attracting international collaborations and investments. 4.	Community Building: The association has fostered a sense of community among fashion professionals, encouraging collaboration and mutual support. This has created a vibrant and supportive ecosystem where creativity and innovation can thrive.
Results: The key achievements resulting from the implementation of Fashion Association of Botswana's initiatives:  Improved Compensation for Models One of the significant achievements of FAB is the successful negotiation of better payment rates for models in Botswana. Historically, models were compensated at very low rates, which undervalued their contributions and discouraged many talented individuals from pursuing modeling as a career. FAB's persistent advocacy and dialogue with industry stakeholders have led to the establishment of fairer and more competitive rates for models. This not only ensures that models are adequately compensated for their work but also raises the overall standards and professionalism within the industry.  Support for Local Fashion Designers in Uniform Production In a landmark achievement, FAB has effectively lobbied the government to halt the importation of uniforms from other countries and instead commission local fashion designers to produce uniforms within Botswana. This initiative addresses several key issues:  	Economic Empowerment: By sourcing uniforms locally, the initiative provides a steady stream of business for Botswana's fashion designers, boosting their income and supporting the growth of local businesses. 	Job Creation: The increased demand for locally produced uniforms has created new job opportunities within the fashion industry, from design and tailoring to distribution. 	Sustainability: Local production reduces the environmental impact associated with importing goods and supports sustainable practices within the industry. 	This policy change represents a significant win for local designers and showcases the potential for homegrown talent to meet national needs effectively. Government Collaboration with Local Designers The Ministry of Youth, Sports, and Culture has initiated the collection of garments from local fashion designers, a direct result of FAB's advocacy efforts. This initiative highlights several important outcomes: 	Recognition and Validation: By showcasing garments from local designers, the government publicly recognizes and validates the creativity and talent within Botswana's fashion community. 	Increased Visibility: This collaboration provides designers with a platform to display their work, increasing their visibility and enhancing their reputations both locally and internationally  Impact on the Fashion Industry and Community The achievements of FAB have had a profound impact on the fashion industry and the broader community in Botswana: 	Economic Impact: The increased demand for locally produced garments and the improved compensation for models have provided significant economic benefits, contributing to the financial stability of fashion professionals. 	Professional Development: The establishment of fair payment standards and government collaboration have raised the professional standards within the industry, encouraging more individuals to pursue careers in fashion. 	Cultural Impact: By promoting the work of local designers and supporting traditional designs, FAB has played a crucial role in preserving Botswana's cultural identity. This has fostered a sense of pride and community among fashion professionals and the public.

Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture
SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Partnering with civil society
Cultural Domain: Design,Performing Arts,Media Arts,Cinema and Audiovisual Arts,Music,Publishing,Visual Arts
Agency Implementation: Federal Ministry for Arts, Culture, the Civil Service and Sport
Main Feature: In 2021, on behalf of Secretary of State Andrea Mayer, the Federal Ministry for Arts, Culture, the Civil Service and Sport started a national arts and culture strategy process. The aim of this process is to establish a regular, structured and open exchange between stakeholders from the arts and Culture sector. From the outset, stakeholders were invited to discuss future issues in the field of art and culture. In addition to the learnings from the COVID-19 pandemic, preliminary work at the federal level, the cultural strategies and mission statements of individual federal states and municipalities, as well as national and international examples of good practice were used as a basis for discussion.  Regular exchange was initiated with the members of the Austrian National Assembly’s Culture Committee, representatives of the media and civil society as well as the entire interested public. In 2022, key topics such as ecology, innovation and digitalization, innovation, fairness, gender equality, diversity, accessibility, internationalization, cultural education / outreach, cooperation and cultural heritage were examined in dialogue groups held in Federal States.  In 2023, the first Forum Kultur, a public event on the cultural strategy process, took place in Vienna. Furthermore, the joint work of the federal government and the Federal States was continued in 2023: events on audience development were organised in cooperation with the Federal State Governments of Carinthia and Upper Austria. Specificities of cultural work in a rural environment and the relation to the urban space were highlighted within these events.  All in all, the Ministry for Arts, Culture, the Civil Service and Sport collected extensive feedback from stakeholders in the arts and culture sector on various levels within the process – online and at in person events – and then processed it in a structured way. This feedback forms the basis for the creation of federal cultural policy guidelines, which were initiated in 2023 and published in June 2024. The guidelines outline the areas of action including the necessary measures (existing and future) of the Ministry’s art and cultural policy. They further highlight Austria’s sustainable development as a location for art and culture in a European and international context. The Ministry for Arts, Culture, the Civil Service and Sport implements a policy of openness, participation, by strengthening dialogue structures as well as by taking into account multiple perspectives of artists, cultural institutions and civil society.  The process is financed through the regular budget of the Ministry for Arts, Culture, the Civil Service and Sport.  With regard to the reporting framework of the 2005 Convention, this measure is also relevant for Goal 3 (Integrate Culture in Sustainable Development Frameworks).
Results: •	Permanent dialog structures between the Ministry for Arts, Culture, the Civil Service and Sport, the Federal States and various civil society actors in Austria have been established. •	Numerous new formats and instruments of participation were introduced and relevant studies presented (e.g. on audience participation). •	As a result of the dialogue processes, among other things, important cultural policy measures were initiated, for example regarding fair pay, audience development, cultural participation and on early access to art and culture for young people. •	Development of federal cultural policy guidelines (presentation 2024)
Financial Ressources: s. above

Title EN: Felega: Bringing Back Azmari’s to the Creative Platform
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture
SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Cultural and creative sectors
Agency Implementation: Theater Arts Professional Association
Main Feature: The TAPA Theater Arts Association has played a pivotal role in preserving and advancing Ethiopia's rich traditional arts, which have flourished for over 3,000 years. Their recent project exemplifies their commitment to cultural, economic, and human rights through theater.  The project engaged 120 members aged 18 to 35 from Addis Ababa and 11 regional areas. It aimed to raise awareness about their experiences and challenges while fostering sustainable financial growth by monetizing their artistic talents. This initiative not only helps maintain Ethiopia's vibrant cultural heritage but also boosts the confidence and support of the theater community.  The association conducted four-day-a-week workshops that provided technical training on various traditional instruments and performance techniques. These sessions also offered practical experience through performances at diverse events organized by TAPA, allowing the trainees to showcase their skills to varied audiences.  The performances integrated multiple aspects of cultural expression, including theater, Theater for Development (TfD), election awareness, dance, and contributions to peace and security. Events were held at prominent venues such as Alliance Ethio-Française, the National Theater, Cultural Centers, and in various regions of Ethiopia, including international locations like China and Kenya. This extensive outreach attracted over 21,500 attendees, significantly broadening the impact of the project.
Results: The recent workshop organized by the TAPA Theater Arts Association has yielded significant results across various dimensions.  Awareness and Cultural Expression: The workshop successfully heightened awareness about the artistic and theatrical contributions of Ethiopian culture. It provided TAPA members with numerous opportunities to showcase their talents, fostering both pride and confidence in their performances.  Economic Impact: The initiative has created income opportunities for TAPA members, contributing to their financial stability. Additionally, the workshop has facilitated the enhancement of ethical and professional standards within TAPA.  Social Impact: By addressing poverty and raising awareness about societal issues, the project has made notable progress in improving the lives of participants and the broader community.  Media and Documentation: The workshop gained considerable attention through press coverage and an hour-long documentary that documented the project's process and outcomes.  International Recognition: The workshop received certification from Chinese and Kenyan cultural tourism authorities and involved visits to 26 provinces in China, engaging with diverse ethnic groups.  Election Awareness: The project also included efforts to increase awareness of election-related issues within Ethiopian society.

Signature d’une convention entre le Festival International de la Bande Dessinée d'Alger (FIBDA) et l’Ecole Supérieure des Beaux-Arts d’Alger au profit de ses étudiants dans le volet formation et production culturelle.

Main Feature: In 2021, the IG Bildende Kunst (Association for Visual Artists) has established the Working Group “Focus: Senior Artist”. This working Group is dedicated to the situation of ageing, older and senior artists, as well as issues and needs in these phases of (professional) life. Special emphasis is put on working conditions and social realities of senior artists. The main goals are to improve working conditions as well as the social and economic situation of old(er) artists and to raise awareness for the challenges that artists face over the course of their lives.  In a first phase, the Working Group carried out extensive research on the (social and economic) situation of ageing artists in Austria and organised a series of public discussions as well as the exhibition "alter|n|ative: Erfahrene Subjekte in Resonanz”. Title EN: FÔLEGO
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture
SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Cultural and creative sectors
Cultural Domain: Performing Arts,Media Arts,Cinema and Audiovisual Arts,Music,Publishing,Visual Arts
Agency Implementation: Cultural Heritage, IP and DGARTES - Directorate General of Arts
Main Feature: Fôlego was a more than two year artistic programming and intervention project with an impact on the development of performing arts’ audiences in five Portuguese municipalities: Mação, Oleiros, Proença-a-Nova, Sertã and Vila de Rei. Bringing closer together and strengthening the relations between their populations privileged artistic intervention methodologies that come from working with the communities, promoting the sharing of experiences between the populations in this region and artists and cultural actors through the thematic lens of Climate Change. Arts become the inspiring catalyst to motivate communities in valuing their territory and its inhabitants. Fôlego operated in a coordinated effort between multiple local, national, and international institutions, both governmental and nongovernmental.
Results: Access and support to/for contemporary arts in low-density municipalities through, inter alia: programming of artistic productions, involvement of residents in creative processes and audience development activities. The project focused on close relations with the local communities in five Portuguese municipalities, strengthening and promoting the mobility of artists and audiences between them. During its activity period, Fôlego was able to establish a wide network of local agents from several areas. These connections were the starting points of the project’s artistic initiatives, enhancing resources and drawing on diverse traditions, especially at regional and national level. The project contributed to bridge the gap between expert knowledge and local knowledge, facilitating a creative dialogue between artists, regional authorities, scientists, local citizens, and others, based on resources essential to the territorial economy. The international partnerships established within the scope of the project, contributed, inter alia, to the mobility of artists and cultural professionals. When it comes to programming activities with foreign partners, Fôlego followed a job-shadowing logic, promoting the exchange of knowledge with local artistic agents, involving the scientific and school community. Through a programme focused on sustainability and climate change, the project contributed to social and cultural development in the region. It impacted also in the regions’s economy, trough, inter alias, job creation. Fôlego produced (i) a handbook/good practices guide on sustainability - gathering an extensive description of all the activities and knowledge exchange during the project and (ii) a Sustainable Business Guidance Manual - resulting from the ‘Sustainable Business’ workshop developed within the scope of the project, both available on the projects website, with no costs associated.

Agency Implementation: DJ SCHOOL ABIDJAN,AGENCE EMPLOI JEUNES, RYTHMIK ACADEMY (PARIS) , GROUPE KIBIO, DMC WORLD DJ TRACE CÔTE D’IVOIRE,Caisse Nationale de Prévoyance Sociale (CNPS)
Main Feature: La structure DJ SCHOOL ABIDJAN a été créée en Juin 2022. Elle a pour objectifs : la formation, la vente d’équipements Disc- Jockey (DJ) et l’événementiel. Au niveau de son secteur formation, elle propose des formations qualifiantes d’une durée allant de 03 à 09 mois (selon le type de formation) en animation musicale et scénique (Disc-Jockey). Elle est la 1ère structure ce de type en Afrique francophone. Elle a pour mission de mettre ses compétences à la disposition de DJs professionnels par la formation continue mais également les amateurs de musique qui souhaitent avoir les bases de ce noble métier. Nos formations sont les suivantes : Animation Musicale et Scénique, M.A.O (Musique assistée par ordinateur), Music business (Industrie musicale), Sonorisation, Lumières.  Elle entend se positionner comme le hub de la formation de l’animation musicale en Afrique francophone. Elle dispose de professionnels aguerris et disponibles pour une formation de qualité. Elle dispose de l’appui institutionnel du Ministère de la Culture et de la Francophonie et de l’UNESCO ainsi que la reconnaissance du Ministère de l'enseignement technique et de la formation professionnelle. Cette formation inédite a un intérêt spécial. Il s’agit d’une innovation en termes de formation en Côte d’ivoire car DJ SCHOOL ABIDJAN est pionnière dans le domaine de l’ingénierie de l’animation musicale et scénique en Côte d’Ivoire. On dénombre plus de 30 000 DJs en Côte d’Ivoire dont 90% d’amateurs selon une étude en cours de réalisation par DJ SCHOOL ABIDJAN en partenariat avec le BURIDA (Bureau ivoirien des droits d’auteurs). Tous ces acteurs ont appris sur le tas. De plus, cette formation méconnue du grand public, de l’administration et même des acteurs est une source de revenus fiable dans le domaine du divertissement. Il faut également noter le caractère indépendant qui peut découler de ce métier ; créant ainsi de véritables entrepreneurs culturels, contribuant ainsi à l’élargissement de l’assiette fiscale, à l’auto emploi et donc à la réduction du chômage des jeunes. Pour information, un DJ en côte d’ivoire touche entre 150 000 Fcfa et Un million de franc par mois.
Results: Les résultats atteints par cette initiative sont :  - création d'un écosystème relatif au domaine de l’Animation Musicale et Scénique (AMS) - Création de filière AMS par la mise en place d'une maquette pédagogique adaptée aux réalités. Reconnaissance et Habilitation par le Ministère de l'enseignement technique et la formation professionnelle  - 150 apprenants dont 12 filles, et 1 personne en situation handicap avec un taux d'insertion professionnel de 90% - création d'une agence de booking chargée de l'Insertion Professionnelle post formation.  - création de la branche Afrique de l'ouest du championnat mondial de DJ (DMC) gérée par DJ SCHOOL ABIDJAN  - Mise en place d'un cluster en vue de la structuration des acteurs et l'accès au financement en partenariat avec l'agence emploi jeune et ORANGE BANK.

Title EN: FORMATION EN MODE ET COUTURE DES JEUNES FILLES VULNERABLES DU DISTRICT D’ABIDJAN
Goal: Integrate Culture In Sustainable Development Frameworks
SDG: SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: National sustainable development policies and plans
Agency Implementation: Etablissement MOMO CHE Bureau UNESCO ABIDJAN MINISTERE DE LA CULTURE ET DE FRANCOPHONIE  UNICEF  PNUD
Main Feature: Dans le cadre de la mise en œuvre du Programme de Consolidation de la Paix, l’établissement MOMO CHE a contribué à la mise en œuvre du projet PBF « Les jeunes comme moteurs de prévention des discours de haine et des conflits socio-politiques et communautaires », dans le cadre d’un partenariat avec le Bureau UNESCO Abidjan. Ce projet visait à contribuer à réduire les risques de violences liées aux discours d’incitation à la haine et à la diffusion de fausses informations à travers une implication active des jeunes (hommes et femmes) dans la prévention et la résolution des conflits.  En outre, Il met un accent particulier sur la promotion des principes des droits de l’homme liés à la liberté d’expression et la lutte contre les discours de haine dans les communautés et sur les réseaux sociaux ; et sur les mécanismes locaux d’alerte précoce,  les mécanismes traditionnels basés sur les alliances interethniques mis en place dans le cadre des interventions PBF en Côte d’Ivoire, ainsi que des forums intercommunautaires pour une gestion pacifique des conflits, la réinsertion sociale et l’autonomisation des jeunes filles vulnérables du district d’Abidjan. Au nombre des activités décrites dans ledit projet, s’inscrit l’activité de mentoring et de formation de 30 jeunes filles vulnérables dans le district d’Abidjan, membres et leaders d’organisation de jeunesse dans le domaine de la mode et du design dont la formation s’est tenue sur sept (07) mois. L'Etablissement MOMO CHE a mis en œuvre le mentoring et la formation de 30 jeunes filles vulnérables dans le district d’Abidjan, membres et leaders d’organisation de jeunesse de la mode et du design pour une période de sept (07) à compter du 23 octobre 2020 au 30 avril 2021 dans le district d’Abidjan. Ce projet a mis en avant les industries culturelles et créatives (ICC) en l’occurrence la mode et le design comme vecteur d’autonomisation des jeunes filles vulnérables, de réinsertion sociale et de création d’emplois durable.
Results: À l'issue de cette formation de 07 mois, les apprenantes ont pu réaliser des tenues vestimentaires pour des défilés de mode de haut niveau. Elles ont confectionné des vêtements pour des personnalités influentes du pays et de la sous-région. Les apprenantes ont participé à la création des collections pour plusieurs événements, notamment le Gala de l'Association des Créateurs de Mode de Côte d'Ivoire (ACMCI), l'AFRIK FASHION SHOW et le FIMA au Niger. Nous espérons que ce projet s'inscrira sur le long terme afin de permettre à un plus grand nombre de jeunes filles vulnérables de devenir autonomes et de contribuer de manière constructive à la cohésion sociale. Nous souhaitons accueillir encore davantage de jeunes filles pour leur offrir une formation qualifiante en techniques de couture. L'augmentation du nombre de bénéficiaires contribuera à réduire le taux de chômage et à favoriser une insertion socio-professionnelle durable de ces jeunes filles, ce qui participera également à la lutte contre les violences verbales de toute nature et à la consolidation de la paix.

Students receive extensive information, by keynote speakers and develop a proposal, under the guidance of professionals in the field of culture and entrepreneurship. Title EN: Freedom for diverse cultural expressions. Intercultural and migrant inclusion programme.
Goal: Promote Human Rights And Fundamental Freedoms
SDG: SDG 5 - Achieve gender equality and empower all women and girls,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels
Area of Monitoring: Artistic freedom
Cultural Domain: Design,Performing Arts,Media Arts,Cinema and Audiovisual Arts,Music,Publishing,Visual Arts
Agency Implementation: Ministry of Cultures, Arts and Heritage (MINCAP).
Main Feature: The measure Intercultural and Migrant Inclusion Programme (PIIM) is an initiative whose purpose is to make visible the cultural expressions of migrants who live in our country, which involves working directly with the migrant artists and/or communities who reside in Chile. Thus, its main lines of action are:   (1) access to interculturality, centred on the design of regional projects, prepared by the Regional Ministerial Secretariats (Seremis) together with miagrant and/or pro-migrant artist civil society groups,   (2) regional migrant projects, an action that seeks for regions to develop actions for raising awareness and appreciation of migrant cultural expressions. The methodology focuses on the participation of the public, through a joint effort together with the Seremis, with a working group or opportunity that leads to the selection of a focal point and a project to be developed on a regional level. These projects could be implemented in the areas of reserach, presentation and dissemination,   (3) intercultual stage “Winnipeg-Rockodromo”, aims to be a meeting place  between different cultures, through different creative cultural activities, such as theatre, dance, music, talks, crafts presentations, gastronomic presentations, as well as artistic expressions from different countries, etc.   (4) fostering interculturality, focused on the promotion of the work of migrant artists in cultural centres,   (5) migrant artists in cultural centres, which aims to circulatecontent by migrant artists in the same spaces where content by Chilean artists circulate,   (6) platform for raising awareness, to support different projects and activities by civil society on migrant themes in the areas of culture, art and interculturality,   (7) Días D: During Días D, the programme seeks to postition content and programming of migrant artists and projects in the celebrations of the international days recognised by MINCAP,   (8) catalogue of migrant artists, an offering of migrant artists and projects, consisting of all the artists with whom a connection has been established,   (9) capacities for interculturality, whose goal is to raise awareness of the contribution of migrant artistic and cultural organisations in the cultural sector, as well as to provide tools to eliminate all forms of discimination and racism in cultural and/or educational spaces,   (10) debates around migration and culture, dissemination of different cultural expressions and contributions from collectives of resident immigrants in Chile through the organising national opportunities for discussion with civil society, such as colloqiums, talks and/or public forums, and   (11) migrant artist conferences, whose purpose is to create a meeting point for migrant artists residing in Chile.   Lastly, from the monitoring framework of the 2005 Convention, this measure is part of the indicator on "policies and measures that promote and the social and economic rights of cultural professionals".
Results: In relation to the quantitative data that reports on the implementation of this measure and according to different actions described, we can highlight that in 2022, 47 artistic and cultural activities took place on a national level, in order to showcase migrant expressions.   Regarding the audiences who benefited, for the same year, the numbers reached 303 people throughout Chile, encompassing the vast majority of the regions. In turn, visibility was given to 508 migrant artists throughout the country through their different interventions.   Lastly, in 2022 the third update of the migrant arts catalogue was carried out, where already more than 90 projects have been registered, in theatre, music, film, poetry, dance, workshop, among other artistic manifestations and expressions. At an international level, it should be noted that this measure is part of the Iber-routes programme, strengthening the rights and interculturality of Ibero-American migration.   Finally, MINCAP represents this programme in MERCOSUR's Commission for Cultural Diversity, taking an active part in its meetings and participating in its different actions.
Recommandations: Even though there has not been a formal evaluation of the programme, in general terms we affirm that the migrant artist and practitioners awareness has steadily grown in Chile, to a large extent because of the access to their expressions and new dissemination spaces.   This progress, without a doubt, contributes to the diversity of cultural expressions, in line with the 2005 Convention, as well as to fostering the country's interculturality. MINCAP programmes such as Interculturality and Migrant Inclusion, strongly propel these objectives.

Le programme inclut différentes activités et réunions visant à encourager les lecteurs et accorder une attention particulière aux écrivains. Le programme du ministère comprend une série de réunions axées sur le livre, pour que les auteurs et écrivains participent à la vente par signature et présentent ainsi leurs dernières publications. La première édition de ce forum du livre a été organisée du 01er octobre 2023 au 23 mai 2024, en l’honneur de l’écrivain et académicien Abdelmalek Mortad, et la seconde, frappé du slogan « Influence des chercheurs algériens sur la culture humaine », a été organisée du 24 mai jusqu’à la fin 2024.

La deuxième édition de l’événement intellectuel national du forum du livre a enregistré les activités culturelles suivantes  - des expositions de livres en braille,  - des rencontres de poésie, - des rencontres littéraires : lectures et discussions sur les publications locales ou nationales, séminaires, concours intellectuels et littéraires,  - des activités culturelles et éducatives destinées aux enfants, - des expositions de livres pour le fonds documentaire des bibliothèques et expositions de livres d’écrivains,  - une vente par signature de livres,  - une récompense accordée à deux mille quatre cent sept (2407) entre invités et écrivains.

Title EN: Free entrance to national/central museums
Goal: Integrate Culture In Sustainable Development Frameworks
SDG: SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: National sustainable development policies and plans
Agency Implementation: The museums involved (museums receiving direct funding from the government)
Main Feature: To facilitate access to arts and cultural heritage and broaden participation the government introduced free entry to museums financed within the state budget during 2005-2006, which was then reintroduced in 2016-2022. In many cases an entrance fee was still needed for temporary exhibitions. From 2023 free entrance is still valid för children and young people up to 19 years of age, but entrance fees were reintroduced for other groups.
Results: The results show that the introduction of free entrance is associated with increased participation in the form of more visits to the museums that introduce it. It is doubtful, however, that the reform led to broader participation (see evaluation below), which was one of the reasons for the government to limit the free entrance to only apply to children and young people up to 19 years.
Financial Ressources: 7900 USD (80 million SEK) per year
Recommandations: The results show that the introduction of free entrance is associated with increased participation in the form of more visits to the museums that introduce it. Museums in general see a larger increase in visitor numbers during the years when free entrance is introduced, compared to other years. The museums that were part of the free entrance reform saw a considerable increase directly after the introduction not seen in any other year, or in other, similar museums. The increase amounted to about one million exhibition visits (i.e., visits to the cafés and restaurants located in the museums have been excluded). The accuracy of this figure is debatable, but it is highly unlikely that the increase would be unrelated to the reform.  It is doubtful, however, that the reform led to broader participation. The proportion of the Swedish population that visited a museum at least once during the last 12 months (i.e., not only the museums included in the reform) did not increase in connection with the reform – not even in Stockholm, where most of the museums included in the reform are located. The clearest increase in Stockholm was rather in the group that visits museums at least once every quarter. This suggests that the increase mostly consisted of people who already visited museums at least once a year starting to visit them more often. An analysis of audience surveys finds no increase in the proportion of visits by unaccustomed visitors to museums with free entrance as a result of the reform. The proportion of visits by certain underrepresented groups (men, the elderly, and people living outside of the region where the museum is located) also remained the same.  These findings of a clear increase in participation, but absence of, or unclear evidence regarding broader participation, are in line with what studies of free entrance in other countries have found.  The evaluation report concludes with a discussion of possible explanations of why the  reform did not have the effects the government hoped for. Among the possibilities discussed are that the objectives regarding broader participation were not clear enough; that the reform was resource-demanding in a way that may have crowded out other measures to broaden the audience; that free entrance came to include only the permanent exhibitions; and that the  museums included in the reform were concentrated in Stockholm to such a  large extent.  (Fri entré till museer Effekter på antal museibesök och museibesökens sammansättning, Myndigheten för kulturanalys/Swedish Agency for Cultural Policy Analysis, Rapport 2023:1)

Title EN: Free Museum Visits (since 2018)

Area of Monitoring: National sustainable development policies and plans
Agency Implementation: Ministry of Culture of the Republic of Lithuania
Main Feature: Free Museum Visits Programme started in 2018 as the initiative, which aimed to provide the opportunity for the schoolchildren to visit national and state museums free of charge. Since 2019, Free Museum Visits Programme has been extended to provide the opportunity for everybody, regardless their age or socio-economic status, to visit national and state museums, which are under the Ministry of Culture, free of charge every last Sunday of month.   The aim of this extension was to strengthen the cultural identity of Lithuanian citizens, to develop their habits of independent cultural knowledge and experience by ensuring the accessibility and openness of the museums. This initiative contributes to encouraging public to choose museums as places to spend their leisure time with the expectation that visits to the museums will become their usual habit.   Development of cultural habits must be consistent and resources of museums must be used for the development of creative environment. Free access to the permanent exhibitions of national and state museums is particularly important for people with low incomes, who, due to their limited financial resources, are unable to visit museums frequently.  Ukrainian citizens can visit free of charge all national museums and state museums (Lithuanian Sea Museum offers discounts for admission tickets) outside the realm of this Free Museum Visits Programme.
Results: According to the statistical data, in 2020 over 198 600 visitors took the opportunity to visit museums free of charge last Sunday of each month. Meanwhile, there were more than 200 600 visitors in 2021, more than 336 250 visitors in 2022 and over 510 700 visitors in 2023, accordingly. The decrease in the number of visitors in the years 2020-2021 was due to the pandemic and various restrictions caused by Covid-19. Meanwhile, in the first half of the year 2024, about 222 000 visitors visited museums free of charge on the last Sunday of each month and it shows an increasing interest of the public in museums. According to The Survey on Participation in Culture and Satisfaction with Cultural Services in Lithuania (2023), the share of residents who visited a museum in Lithuania or abroad at least once has increased significantly  from 40% to 60% (for more detail information: https://www.kulturostyrimai.lt/visos-temos/kulturos-politika/gyventoju-dalyvavimas-kulturoje-ir-pasitenkinimas-kulturos-paslaugomis-2020/.  Three most popular museums of Free Museum Visits Programme are National Museum – Palace of the Grand Dukes of Lithuania, National Museum of Lithuania and Lithuanian Sea Museum.
Financial Ressources: A total of more than USD 1, 5 million (EUR 1 400 000) was allocated annually for Free Museum Visits Programme.

Title EN: Funding of public cultural institutions
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture
SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Cultural and creative sectors
Agency Implementation: Ministry of culture
Main Feature: The Ministry of Culture regularly, i.e. every year, funds 144 cultural institutions (in addition to many others that it funds occasionally or through public calls). Most of them are public institutions established by the state and municipalities, but some private organisations performing a public service or particularly important activities in the public interest also receive regular financial support. For some institutions/organisations, the state finances most of their costs (programmes, salaries, equipment and other costs necessary for their operation), while for others only the costs related to their public service activities are covered. Annually, the following institutions are allocated funding:  - 28 national public institutions (museums and galleries, theatres, archives, opera and ballet, philharmonic, cultural centre, national library, cinematheque, film studio, arboretum, theatre institute, Public Institute of the Republic of Slovenia for Cultural Heritage, Mercury Heritage Management Centre), - 3 public institutions (Slovenian Film Centre, Slovenian Book Agency, Republic of Slovenia Public Fund for Cultural Activities), - 104 municipal public institutions (museums and galleries, craft centre, theatres, public libraries), - 2 institutions of the Hungarian and Italian ethnic groups 7 private organisations, including 3 church archives, a museum run as a business and 3 NGOs.
Results: Culture and arts multiply the potential of living together in a sustainable and socially just community, which is only possible if culture is understood as a public good and is integrated into society. It must be accessible to all, regardless of their status or personal circumstances. It therefore urgently needs stable public funding and support. The distribution of public funds permits the production of art that is both independent and unrestricted.The allocation of public funds has been shown to result in a substantial and varied array of cultural events and assets. Survey data from the Statistical Office of the Republic of Slovenia (SURS), which covers all public cultural institutions and not only those that receive financial support from the Ministry of Culture, show a steady growth in cultural offerings on the one hand and cultural consumption on the other. The data on visitor numbers to museums and galleries show fluctuations and recovery trends in visitor numbers over the years and illustrate the impact of external factors such as the COVID-19 pandemic and the subsequent recovery. In 2019, museums and galleries in Slovenia recorded a total of 2,800,899 visitors. However, the outbreak of the COVID-19 pandemic in 2020 led to a drastic drop in visitor numbers to just 989,311 visitors. This downward trend continued in 2021, albeit with a slight improvement to 1,295,548 visitors. Encouragingly, the data for 2022 shows a notable recovery with 2,176,114 visitors, indicating a resurgence of public interest in cultural activities and the resilience of these institutions. The data for attendance at stage performances also shows a significant recovery after the pandemic and underlines the importance of funding to support these institutions in difficult times. In 2019, a total of 4,453,642 people attended stage performances in Slovenia. This figure fell to 1,492,240 in 2020 due to the impact of the pandemic. In 2021, attendance figures improved slightly to 1,899,654, reflecting a gradual recovery. By 2022, the number of visitors had risen significantly to 3,631,185, approaching pre-pandemic levels. This recovery underlines the important role of public institutions in cultural life and the need for sustainable funding to maintain their operations and offerings. In 2022, there were 58 public libraries in Slovenia, including 283 local library branches and 13 mobile libraries (bibliobuses). These libraries operated in 205 municipalities. A total of 411,627 members were registered in the libraries, which corresponds to 19.4% of Slovenia's population. These members visited the libraries 7,615,451 times. The public libraries had a total of 12,119,083 items in their collections, which were borrowed 19,660,882 times in 2022. The libraries employed 1,212 full-time staff and had total operating expenditure of 59.8 million euros in that year. In addition to the number of visitors, the number of performances and festivals organized by public institutions also reflects their dynamic contribution to cultural diversity and richness. In 2022, there were 24,347 performances and 187 festivals organized by public institutions in Slovenia. These figures underline the large scale and diversity of cultural events supported by public institutions and the role they play in promoting a vibrant cultural landscape. The ability to organize such a high number of events despite the challenges posed by the pandemic demonstrates the commitment and ingenuity of these institutions. The analysis of the SURS data clearly shows that public institutions play an essential role in the cultural sector, with high visitor numbers and a wide range of offerings, even in the face of challenges such as the COVID-19 pandemic. The recovery in visitor numbers and the continued high volume of cultural events underline the importance of funding these institutions to ensure their sustainability and the continued enrichment of cultural life. Therefore, continued and increased funding of public institutions is not only justified, but also necessary for the cultural well-being of society.
Financial Ressources: approx. 660million

Title EN: Funding scheme (governmental) for arts schools at a municipal level (continued measure)
Goal: Integrate Culture In Sustainable Development Frameworks
SDG: SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: National sustainable development policies and plans
Agency Implementation: Swedish Arts Council
Main Feature: The Government’s fundamental view is that all children, whatever their background, are to be given an opportunity to engage in the arts. Municipally or privately run arts schools on a municipal level reach a substantial number of children and young people and give them an opportunity to perform and create, thus developing their creative abilities and cultural, social and intellectual skills. One of the challenges of the arts schools is to reach children and young people of all backgrounds – children from rural areas or socioeconomically disadvantaged areas are underrepresented. The government has therefore continued its funding (which was first set up in 2016) aiming at developing the work of the art schools in various ways, for example by broadening participation by introducing new ways of working, new subjects and courses in order to attract new target groups.
Results: 256 out of 290 municipalities have applied for funding. According to representatives from the art schools and municipalities the government funding has been crucial to enable many of the projects, to introduce new subjects or new methods, as scarce municipal resources often limit the capacity to renew the ways of working. The funding was mainly used to: - introduce new subjects - introduce new and developed ways of working - such as “open art school” initiatives or to enable one-to-one tuition (as oppose to only group tuition) - enable advanced courses - Reach underrepresented groups such as children in rural areas or socioeconomically disadvantaged areas - continuing education of teachers. (Uppföljning av de statliga insatserna till stöd för den kommunala kulturskolan 2020-2022, by Ramboll)  The cooperation between different municipalities and art schools has most probably improved as e result of the reform, as project funding could involve more than one municipality. The projects reports show that the funding has resulted in an increased range of subjects and educational methods in the arts schools. In year 2021/2022 - 62 000 “new” children attended the art schools, children who had not attended courses earlier (the total funding was 200 mnkr). In year 2020/2021 - 33 000 “new” children attended the art schools, children who had not attended courses earlier.  (Vad går bidraget till? Redovisningar av utvecklingsbidraget till kulturskolor 2020/2021; 2021/2022, Swedish Arts Council, Statens kulturråd)
Financial Ressources: 10 869 565 USD (100 million SEK ) per year in 2020 and 2023; 19 754 101 USD (200 million SEK) per year 2021 and 2022
Recommandations: The Swedish Arts Council has a national Art School Centre – a centre which distributes the funding but also offers other kinds of support measures to the municipal arts schools. Even though a large majority of the art schools do apply for funding, the evaluation report recommends the centre to look further into the reasons for some art schools not applying and to better understand their needs of support.   Also the evaluation recognizes the dependency of national funding, as many municipalities report difficulties in finding the possibilities of funding new ways of working, introducing new subjects etc within their municipal budgets.     (Uppföljning av de statliga insatserna till stöd för den kommunala kulturskolan 2020-2022, by Ramboll)

Title EN: Gender Equality Policy
Goal: Promote Human Rights And Fundamental Freedoms

Main Feature: The Porto Municipality commits to promoting gender equality by integrating it into its values and publicly disclosing this commitment internally and externally through various channels like the company website, intranet, and emails. Good management practices in gender equality are also shared. An Internal Task Force was established to oversee gender equality initiatives, and mechanisms were created to encourage employee suggestions in areas such as recruitment, performance assessment, and career progression. Job advertisements are reviewed to ensure they are free from gender bias. The annual training plan includes modules on gender equality, covering topics like stereotypes, inclusive language, parenting protections, work-life balance, and harassment. Regular meetings are organized to discuss performance evaluation, career progression, and the representation of women in decision-making roles. A salary table is transparently disclosed, and information on local resources for work-life balance will be provided. Flexible working arrangements are promoted, and campaigns to disseminate a code of good conduct and reporting procedures for harassment and other offenses were launched and communicated through various channels. This policy ensures that women, who represent a significant portion of cultural creators and consumers, have equal opportunities and are not subjected to discrimination. Such a workplace contributes to a more inclusive environment where diverse cultural expressions can thrive. It promotes awareness and advocacy while integrating gender equality into cultural policies reflecting a holistic approach to cultural governance.
Results: All the different aspects of the described policy were implemented. The Porto Municipality is still implementing the organization and holding of meetings with workers and/or their representative structures to address issues related to performance evaluation, career progression, and development policy (including the appointment and participation of women in top decision-making and management positions).
Recommandations: The implementation of policies and measures aimed at promoting work-life balance, preventing, and combating workplace harassment, demonstrates a significant commitment from the company to the well-being and safety of its employees. The dissemination of clear information and procedures for reporting inappropriate behaviour is essential to create a safe and respectful work environment. Recommendation: - To ensure the ongoing effectiveness of these policies and measures, it is recommended to: - Periodic Evaluation: Conduct regular assessments to measure the effectiveness of implemented policies, including organizational climate surveys and employee feedback. - Continuous Education: Provide ongoing training on gender equality, harassment prevention, and work-life balance policies for all employees. - Monitoring and Updating: Monitor closely employee trend and need regarding work-life balance, adapting policies as needed to better address evolving demands. - Transparency and Communication: Maintain open and transparent communication with employees about assessment results and any updates or changes to related policies and procedures. - These recommendations aim to continuously improve the work environment and foster an inclusive and respectful organizational culture, where all employees can thrive and contribute positively to the company's success.

Title EN: Gender mainstreaming in government agencies (Jämställdhetsintegrering I myndigheter JiM).
Goal: Promote Human Rights And Fundamental Freedoms
SDG: SDG 5 - Achieve gender equality and empower all women and girls,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels
Area of Monitoring: Gender equality
Agency Implementation: Swedish Arts Council
Main Feature: JiM is a government programme involving a number of government agencies within all policy areas and aims to strengthen the agencies work on gender mainstreaming. The Swedish Arts Council is one of the agencies. The programme was initiated in 2013 and continues during years 2020-2025.  Gender mainstreaming is the government's main strategy for achieving the equality policy goals. Gender mainstreaming involves (re)organizing, improving, developing and evaluating the decision-making process, so that an equality perspective is incorporated into all decisions, at all levels and all stages of processes. The purpose is to contribute to meet the goals of gender equality policy goals that concern women and men having the same power to shape society and their own lives. This in turn is structured as six sub-goals: • An even distribution of power and influence. • Financial gender equality • Equal education • An even distribution of unpaid domestic and care work. • Equal health • Men’s violence against women must cease
Results: The government programme has resulted in an increased focus on gender mainstreaming within the work of the agency at all levels, even though gender mainstreaming and gender equality has long been part of the work of the agency. The programme has also lead to increased exchange of experiences and good practices between government agencies within different policy areas.
Financial Ressources: No additional resources allocated, within the regular budget of the agency.
Recommandations: An evaluation of JiM during 2013-2018 by the Swedish Agency for Public Management (Statskontoret) shows that several authorities have changed their working methods, thereby increasing equality for their target groups. The Swedish Agency for Public Management also observes many examples of results with weak connections to actual gender equality issues in the operations or society. Therefore, The Swedish Agency for Public Management assesses that the government could contribute even more to achieving gender equality policy goals if the guidance provided to authorities regarding gender mainstreaming integration were more comprehensive. A recommendation made was that the government further should specify the gender mainstreaming missions of the agencies by breaking down the gender equality policy sub-goals into operational goals that specify what each agency should achieve. The government could also clarify which gender equality issues at the societal level they expect each agency to address or contribute to solving (Statskontoret Utvärdering av regeringens utvecklingsprogram för jämställdhetsintegrering i myndigheter, report 2019:14). No evaluation has been made for the current period 2020-2025. No separate evaluation has been made of the agencies working within culture, arts and media.

Title EN: Integrate culture in sustainable development frameworks
Goal: Integrate Culture In Sustainable Development Frameworks
SDG: SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: National sustainable development policies and plans
Agency Implementation: PATH
Main Feature: The Measures and initiatives implementation promote the inclusion of creativity and cultural expressions as strategic elements in national sustainable development plans, that support regional equity in the distribution of cultural resources and facilitate inclusive access to such resources.  ●	Support cultural industry-based regeneration projects at the regional, urban and/or rural levels, including community-based initiatives ●	Facilitate participation in cultural life and access to diverse cultural facilities and expressions, notably addressing the needs of disadvantaged or vulnerable groups. ●	Integrating culture into sustainable development frameworks, as advocated by UNESCO and other international bodies, offers several key benefits:  1. Preservation of Heritage: Incorporating cultural aspects ensures the safeguarding of diverse cultural expressions, traditions, and languages, promoting cultural diversity as a vital component of sustainable development.  2. Enhanced Social Cohesion: Culture fosters social inclusion, identity, and belonging, which are critical for building resilient communities. Embracing cultural diversity can mitigate social tensions and enhance community resilience.  3. Local Knowledge and Innovation: Indigenous and local knowledge systems embedded in cultural practices often offer sustainable solutions to environmental challenges. Integrating these insights into development strategies promotes innovation and sustainability.  4. Economic Opportunities: Cultural industries, such as crafts, tourism, and creative arts, can stimulate local economies and generate employment, contributing to poverty reduction and economic growth in sustainable ways.  5. Environmental Conservation: Many cultural practices emphasize respect for natural resources and ecosystems. Integrating these values into development frameworks encourages sustainable environmental management and biodiversity conservation.  6. Policy Effectiveness: Recognizing cultural dimensions improves the relevance and effectiveness of policies and interventions. Tailoring development strategies to local cultural contexts enhances their acceptance and long-term impact.  7. Human Rights and Ethical Considerations: Cultural rights are human rights. By integrating cultural perspectives, development frameworks uphold the dignity, identity, and rights of individuals and communities, promoting ethical development practices.  In essence, integrating culture into sustainable development frameworks enriches approaches with diverse perspectives, promotes resilience, and ensures development that is both sustainable and inclusive.
Results: Integrating culture into sustainable development frameworks is crucial for fostering inclusive and resilient societies. Recognizing cultural diversity enhances policy effectiveness and promotes community engagement. Key achievements include: - Policy Integration: Many countries have embedded cultural considerations into national sustainable development strategies, promoting cultural heritage conservation and indigenous knowledge. - Community Empowerment: By valuing local traditions and practices, sustainable initiatives gain community support and participation, ensuring their long-term success. - Global Recognition: UNESCO's efforts in promoting cultural sustainability have raised awareness worldwide, emphasizing culture as a driver of sustainable development. - Innovation and Resilience:*Cultural integration fosters innovative solutions rooted in local knowledge, enhancing resilience to environmental and social challenges.  These achievements highlight the transformative potential of integrating culture into sustainable development frameworks, paving the way for more inclusive and holistic approaches to global challenges.

ECCD Chair, Carole Tongue, was attending in person and in her speech â" that was applauded loudly by the participants- she highlighted the necessity  to  â¢ implement transparency principles for generative A.I,  â¢ not use the TDM exceptions enshrined in the 2019 Copyright directive  as they are not practicable and turn copyright on their head against  creator rights holders â¢ Avoid AI companies getting their raw materials for free from creators.  Therefore there must be fair remuneration through licensing or other  methods â¢ More transparency of algorithms needed for both users and creators She urged the Commission to reflect on a new model (potentially licensing)  and a legislative proposal specifically addressing the impact of A.I for culture.  Strong collective bargaining for creative workers also necessity to avoid  actors/artists having to give away image rights. AI companies do not : â¢ Respect for the work of publishers:  â¢ Indicate (in their role as search engines) the sources of the content they  generate which they propose to users â¢ Amplify Disinformation  â¢ Do not provide transparency What do we do if nothing tomorrow in the news will be credible ? She called for transparency requirements regarding generative A.I.s,  She warned about the replacement of professionals in journalism (Axel  Springer fired over 200 journalists, editors and chief editors). Main Feature: The Icelandic Film Fund has supported Icelandic film production since it was established in 1979. The Fund’s primary focus is financially supporting filmmakers in Iceland in creating films that have cultural and societal relevance in Iceland. The Fund emphasizes the development of the Icelandic film culture and supports various forms of films at several stages of film production, from script writing to production and promotion. It engages in activities such as promotion of the films within Iceland or in foreign countries, in addition to supporting local film festivals, seminars and workshops where local and foreign professionals, as well as aspiring filmmakers, are given the opportunity to form connections with one another and exchange information. The Fund has also placed particular emphasis on supporting production of children’s material, aiming to ensure that at least one project specifically aimed at children be produced each year, as per the policy of Icelandic filmmaking for the years 2016-2019. The same policy also emphasizes continuing support specifically for individuals new to the industry. Formulation of the Icelandic filmmaking policy for 2020-2030 is currently in progress. This will be the first time in Iceland that a comprehensive policy and a plan of action on its basis is formed. The policy will address the role of filmmaking in Icelandic culture, film education on all levels, promotion of Icelandic films and support in the production of films.
Results: The Icelandic Film Fund has been instrumental in supporting Icelandic film makers in completing their film related projects. This adds depth to the cultural landscape in Iceland as well as increasing awareness of Icelandic culture in foreign nations where the films may be viewed. In the year 2019, a total of 180 applications for some form of support were received by the Fund, with 92 of those projects receiving funding, a 51% success ratio. That same year, 10 Icelandic films and 6 Icelandic documentaries premiered in theatres. Numerous films supported by the Icelandic Film Fund have been selected to participate in various international film festivals. Fiscal support by the Icelandic Film Fund allows Icelandic filmmakers the opportunity to create culturally relevant and meaningful material to enhance the local culture. This equally gives foreign individuals in other countries further opportunities to be introduced to Icelandic culture and expand their own personal cultural scope.

Agency Implementation: Ministry of Cultures, Arts and Heritage, Department of Promotion of Culture and Arts, Executive Secretariat of Creative Economy.
Main Feature: The measure seeks to improve the different dimensions that impact on the working conditions of cultural workers in Chile. Precarious work is defined as a multi-deminsional phenomenon related to a general defenceless work situation, that considers a way of relating to the workplace and social world, creating precarious work (Ministry of Labor, 2011).  Within this context a need is born for establishing a measure for the promotion and strengthening of cultural work. To this effect, precarious work is understood as a phenomenon that affects the formality of work, employment stability and income or salaries that derive from the work, association and work skills of cultural workers.   In practice, the measure looks to contribute in the improvement of problems such as informality, multiple jobs, low salaries, social insecurity and gender gaps. Its aim is to reduce the level of job insecurity of cultural workers, in order to contribute to the improvement of the different dimensions that impact on the working conditions of cultural workers.   The aforementioned is based on 5 lines of action:   (1) Formality in cultural work: to provide specific knowledge to the sector on matters around formalisation, labour law and social security, and copyright, among others, from a cultural worker perspective.   (2) Promotion of cultural internships and placements: to contribute to job placements of cultural workers and to promote their employability opportunities, through internships and placements that foster cultural employment.   (3) Technical assistance for cultural work co-operatives: to provide technical assistance to cultural workers on matters of creating co-operatives and pre co-operatives, for the development of this type of association.   (4) Skill and trade certification: To certify technical and trade skills of cultural workers.   (5) Raising awareness around cultural work: To make visible and to raise awareness of the value of cultural workers. In accordance with the monitoring framework of the 2005 Convention, this measure is part of the actions that "support the development of dynamic cultural and creative sectors" through the "job creation and entrepreneurship measures" indicator.
Results: The measure, implemented since 2023, to date does not have results of the implementation.

The program supports Indigenous projects in any audiovisual format such as film, television, and video games, as well as sector development activities. The ISOP is delivered by the Indigenous Screen Office corporation (ISO), an independent Indigenous-led organization with a mandate to support and advance self-determination and narrative sovereignty within the Indigenous audiovisual sector.   ISOP supports Indigenous creators and professionals in Canada in the development, production, marketing and distribution of Canadian audiovisual content in any format for any distribution platform. Moreover, support is provided to projects that increase Indigenous participation, visibility and representation within the audiovisual sector.
Results: Since 2021, the ISO has delivered over CAD 23.4 million in direct contributions to Indigenous creators through ISOP funding, helping to realize the completion of critically acclaimed projects such as Bones of Crows (a film and television miniseries), Night Raiders (film), and Slash/Back (film), among others. Moreover, in fiscal year 2022-23, ISO invested CAD 1 million to support the creation of a production studio in Nunavut, the first studio of its kind. This northern studio will create economic development opportunities for Nunavut's film and TV industry and be shared for broad community use.  While current ISOP funding sunsets on March 31, 2024, the 2021 Mandate Letter to the Minister of Canadian Heritage committed to providing the ISO with additional ongoing funding so that authentic Indigenous stories can be told and seen. The policy provides tools for the development of projects such as the production of phonograms, concerts, tours, audiovisuals, press actions, among others. Each call has its own Rules and Conditions, but all of them are aimed at music groups and soloists previously registered with INAMU, and who are developing a musical project. There are several lines of annual promotion that differ in the form of distribution, the destination, the amount of benefits, the amounts and the evaluating entity. Those who receive the aid are requested to render the amount spent according to what is established in the terms and conditions of each line of call. For the rendering of production vouchers, the assigned supplier company will keep a copy of the material produced. In addition to the obligation explained above, a social compensation must be made within the framework of the Social Cultural Circuit. INAMU set up this Circuit so that musicians who have received a benefit can make a social compensation in the way they prefer (giving a talk, singing live, performing a technique clinic, providing some knowledge or educational tool, workshop, or others), with the aim that sectors of society that have difficulty accessing cultural events can participate in some musical activities. Area of Monitoring: Media diversity
Agency Implementation: GEPAC - Cultural Strategy, Planning and Assessment Bureau-Ministry of Culture
Main Feature: The State's incentive regime for the media in Portugal consists of a set of measures and financial support designed to promote the sustainability and diversity of the media, especially those at a regional and local level. These incentives aim to ensure that communities have access to diverse, plural and quality information, contributing to social and territorial cohesion. This regime arose in response to the need that was then noted to reinforce the support mechanisms for regional or local media bodies towards their entrepreneurialization, as the results obtained with the application of previous regulatory frameworks on the ground had proven to be insufficient. The previous regime focused the incentives framework on supporting initiatives that aimed to invest in improving the technical and operating conditions of the media. Incentives can be granted through various types of support, such as direct subsidies, tax exemptions, and specific programs to support the production of informative and cultural content. Furthermore, there is specific regulation to ensure transparency and equity in the allocation of these incentives.
Results: The main objectives of this policy currently are the support for technological modernization by facilitating the transition to new digital technologies and the modernization of infrastructures; fostering media literacy by promoting initiatives that increase citizens' media literacy, helping them to better understand and use the media. It also permitted the economic sustainability of local and regional media by offering direct financial support to help the media face economic challenges, especially in crisis contexts and thereby promoted the diversity and pluralism of content and pluralism of opinions, especially in regions where the supply of information is more limited.
Financial Ressources: Year 2023: 946.928,56 USD (general budget) = 433,950 USD (North) + 226,270 USD (Alentejo) + 153,560 USD (Center) + 90,640 USD (Algarve) + 57,070.15 USD (Lisbon Region)
Recommandations: A set of project measures are intended to support the development of regional newspaper and radios. Of the total budget of almost 947k USD, support is chiefly allocated to Technological modernisation (30%) and digital transformation159 (53%) with smaller allocations for Media literacy related projects (4%) and support for media accessibility (11%). Funds are also available for employment and professional training. It was implemented a new fundamental pillar which consists of creating an incentive for literacy and education for the media, involving, for the first time, at an inter-municipal level, educational establishments, media bodies and local authorities. This innovation recognizes the great importance of the theme of literacy and inclusion in the field of media and the digital agenda and seeks to continue the initiatives already developed, among other entities, by UNESCO.
