Main Feature: The policy of integrating culture as an economic asset involves a series of interrelated practical steps, including: First: Conducting necessary studies to identify the elements of economic potential in the cultural sector and how to invest them to diversify national income sources by the end of 2019. Second: Establishing a strategic partnership framework with the private sector based on the identified economic potential elements by the end of 2019. Third: Putting in place necessary guarantees to simultaneously preserve identity and enhance citizenship and cultural communication through: -	Developing and implementing mechanisms that encourage increasing knowledge levels and promoting reading habits by the end of 2019. -	Establishing mechanisms that support distinguished national cultural production by mid-2019. -	Developing and implementing attractive cultural programs that help promote citizenship, Qatari values, and cultural communication by the end of 2022. -	Developing and implementing a plan to enhance knowledge of immigrant cultures and interact with them by the end of 2022. -	Establishing and implementing necessary mechanisms to protect and develop Qatari cultural heritage by the end of 2022.
Results: The outcomes of the policy aiming to integrate culture as an economic asset in the development strategy include: -	Reviewing regulatory frameworks, laws, policies, and sectoral strategies related to culture, especially Emiri Order No. (3) of 2020. -	Designating the culture sector with its own ministry to oversee its operation, devising its policies, and making appropriate decisions under Emiri Order No. (4) of 2021. -	Implementing measures to promote reading and increase knowledge, by supporting authors, expanding distribution channels, and ensuring the dissemination of cultural production domestically and internationally. -	Supporting outstanding national cultural production financially and artistically, similar to initiatives by Qatar Museums like the "Doha Design" initiative or the Doha Film Institute's community program "Made in Qatar." -	Enhancing the talents and productivity of artists through initiatives like the "Zwara" exhibition residency program and training workshops. -	Encouraging and guiding students towards majors in cultural fields, including providing financial grants or government scholarship privileges. -	Linking with the private sector and civil society to enhance productivity in the cultural sector through various initiatives, events and effective partnerships through specialised cultural centers, such as open calls for artistic intervention. -	Promoting the integration of resident communities by enabling them to exercise their cultural rights through various means such as allocating cultural spaces or establishing radio channels in their languages, or even enabling them to open schools for communities. -	Fostering openness to others by organizing cultural weeks and enhancing cultural year programs. -	Strengthening communication with international organizations and regional bodies active in the cultural field through the establishment of an international cooperation department within the Ministry of Culture. -	Establishing coordination mechanisms within all relevant State institutions responsible for implementing these measures to ensure planning, quality, and innovation, acting as a link between these institutions and the National Planning Council.
Financial Ressources: Not available
Recommandations: The positive indicators accompanying the policy of integrating culture as one of the economic asset have led to the continuation of this policy at the level of outlining the Third National Development Strategy (2024-2030) to achieve "Qatar Vision 2030" while enhancing:  -	Increasing awareness of national identity and celebrating it. -	Increasing the production and consumption of local cultural content. -	The Ministry's participation in various seminars and workshops aimed at making culture an asset for the economy, similar to the training workshop entitled "Cultural Index in the Islamic World" (December 2023) in coordination with the Islamic Educational, Scientific, and Cultural Organization (ISESCO).

SDG: SDG 5 - Achieve gender equality and empower all women and girls,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels
Area of Monitoring: Artistic freedom
Cultural Domain: Design,Performing Arts,Media Arts,Cinema and Audiovisual Arts,Music,Publishing,Visual Arts
Agency Implementation: Koalisi Seni sekretariat@koalisiseni.or.id +62811177450
Main Feature: Artistic Freedom Monitoring System in Indonesia by Koalisi Seni with the support of UNESCO IFCD As one of the member states that has ratified the UNESCO Convention 2005 on the Protection and Promotion of the Diversity of Cultural Expressions, Indonesia is obliged to report the situation of artistic freedom in the QPR. However, in both QPR 2016 and 2020, Indonesia did not fulfill its obligation to report the situation of artistic freedom.  There was very limited data on artistic freedom in Indonesia. Cases of violations tended to be reported by several human rights organizations under a broader category: violations of freedom of expression. Until 2020, there were no organisations that made it their priority to investigate or analyse artistic freedom.  In 2020, Koalisi Seni collaborated with UNESCO Jakarta to initiate research on the situation of artistic freedom spanning from 2010 to 2020. We analyses patterns of violations, motives, victims, and perpetrators. We concluded that Indonesia needed a more systematic monitoring system for artistic freedom. To follow up the research recommendation, Koalisi Seni submitted a proposal to UNESCO IFCD and the Aschberg Programme to establish a monitoring system prototype. The proposal was granted and we started to build the prototype in 2022.  With the support of UNESCO, we established: ● A web-based artistic freedom monitoring system and help desk ● A monitoring network consisting of human rights CSOs and art organizations, including CSOs that provide assistance to the victim. We also established a forum with this network to evaluate the system  We also published: ● A practical handbook for artists to mitigate risk ● 2023 annual report (preceded by two annual reports in 2021 and 2022)  Lastly, to strengthen network and build capacity within the communities, we organised: Series of workshops and public discussions to disseminate the knowledge
Results: a. 197 violations, 252 victim entities and 258 perpetrators were documented, occurring from 2010 to 2023. This database is accessible to the public via http://kebebasanberkesenian.id and is updated regularly. i. Of 252 victims, 217 were not rehabilitated, 12 were partly rehabilitated, 17 were unknown. 180 were artists, and 33 were others. ii. Of 258 violators, 126 were police, 43 were mass organisations, 42 were local government officials.  b. Along with the database, we have published: i. 4 annual reports, detailing patterns of violations and policy recommendations. ii. 1 practical handbook for artists to mitigate risk, know their rights and whom to contact when attacked  c. 6 CSOs and 1 corporate entity committed to joining the monitoring network. They are: i. YLBHI (Indonesia Legal Aid Foundation) ii. SINDIKASI (Indonesia Creative and Media Workers Union) iii. KAKG (Gender Equality Advocates Collective) iv. Digital rights defenders v. SAFEnet vi. Taskforce KBGO vii. Hukum online and its legal consultation subsidiary, Justika  d. 9 media were interested in joining the monitoring network. i. Tempo ii. Kompas iii. The Finery Report iv. Hukum online v. The Conversations Indonesia vi. Project Multatuli vii. Narasi TV viii. Art Calls ix. Konde  e. Over 60 participants attended 3 workshops, online and offline f. Over 200 participants attended 3 public discussions g. International CSO network formed, including Freemuse, Arts Equator, Nhimbe Trust, PEN International, Artigo 19, PEN Belarus.

Pour atténuer les effets des crises multidimensionnelles en général et celle sécuritaire aux plan national et local en particulier, le Burkina Faso, à mi-parcours du deuxième Plan national de développement économique et social (PNDES) 2021-2025 ,a adopté, en sa session du Conseil des ministres du mercredi 25 janvier 2023, le Plan d’action pour la stabilisation et le développement (PA-SD) 2024-2026 comme outil opérationnel programmatique physique et financier autour de quatre (04) piliers devant répondre aux nouvelles orientations de l’action gouvernementale parmi lesquels figure la réponse humanitaire inscrite au Pilier 3 dudit référentiel national de développement. Title EN: Institutionnalisation des semaines artistiques et culturelles (SAFRA) entre les communes rurales de Guinée, de Guinée-Bissau (Gabou), de Gambie (Bassi), du Sénégal (Tambakounda), du Mali (Nkaye) et de la Mauritanie (Seribabi)
Goal: Achieve A Balanced Flow Of Cultural Goods And Services And Increase The Mobility Of Artists And Cultural Professionals
SDG: SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 10 - Reduce inequality within and among countries,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Flow of cultural goods and services
Agency Implementation: Communes rurales de Guinée, de Guinée-Bissau (Gabou), de Gambie (Bassi), du Sénégal (Tambakounda), du Mali (Nkaye) et de la Mauritanie (Seribabi)
Main Feature: Les échanges culturels décentralisés entre les communes rurales de Boké (Guinée), de Gabou (Guinée-Bissau), de Bassi (Gambie), de Tambakounda (Sénégal), de Nkaye (Mali) et de Seribabi (Mauritanie) sont encadrés par un comité de coordination basé au Sénégal, suivant une convention d’organisation des échanges culturels annuellement dans une commune d’un de ces pays. L’objectif est d’institutionnaliser un cadre d’échanges culturels et artistiques entre les différentes communes rurales de ces pays.  C’est un fort outil de mobilisation des acteurs culturels de ces communes autour des arts de scène et de musique dans les disciplines artistiques et culturelles suivantes : -	Le ballet ; -	La percussion ; -	La poésie ; -	Le chant  -	Les orchestres modernes ; -	Le théâtre ; -	Les expositions littéraires et de produits de l’artisanat d’art ; -	Les défilés de mode ; -	la soirée culturelle comprenant des prestations d’artistes modernes et traditionnels.  Suite à des années de représentations artistiques et culturelles, les acteurs et les professionnels de la culture ont échangé autour des techniques de promotion, de valorisation et de diffusion de leurs œuvres artistiques et culturelles.  Ces échanges culturels et artistiques ont favorisé une forte mobilisation des élus locaux, des artistes et des organisations de la société civile culturelle dans sa mise en œuvre. La semaine de l’amitié et de la fraternité (SAFRA) dans toutes ses éditions a favorisé des échanges culturels et artistiques de façon structurée entre les artistes et les professionnels de la culture de ces communes de manière à valoriser les expressions culturelles et artistiques, à créer les conditions favorables aux échanges culturels et à l’établissement des relations de partenariat entre les professionnels de la culture des différentes collectivités locales.  Chaque 2 ans, de manière alternée, la semaine est organisée par une commune rurale d’un de ces pays. La mise en œuvre de la mesure est assurée principalement par les budgets des communes, l’accompagnement de l’Etat et les partenaires techniques et financiers. Toutes les éditions organisées en République de Guinée sont supervisées par un comité national d’organisation, mis en place par le Ministère en charge de la Culture. Des campagnes de communication et d’information ont été faites en direction des différents publics à travers les radios rurales, communautaires et les réseaux sociaux.
Results: Durant la semaine organisée en 2020 à Tambakounda (Sénégal) : -	120 artistes, danseurs de ballet ont démontré leurs talents dans les pas de danse, chorégraphie, rythme de leurs différentes communautés ; -	90 percussionnistes ont valorisé leurs instruments traditionnels à travers les différents rythmes de leurs localités ; -	24 poètes ont acclamé sur les thèmes liés à la protection de l’environnement, de l’amitié et des violences faites aux personnes vulnérables ; -	30 chanteurs vedettes des communes ont véhiculé des messages d’amitié, de fraternité, de solidarité, de paix et de cohésion sociale;  -	72 artistes des orchestres modernes ont présenté des répertoires musicales de leurs collectivités ; -	42 artistes de théâtre ont présenté des pièces théâtrales conformément au thème retenu par édition ; -	48 stands ont été aménagé pour l’exposition des œuvres littéraires et des produits artisanaux des différentes collectivités ; -	48 stylistes et créateurs de mode venus des différentes communes rurales ont présenté leurs collections.

Title EN: INSUL’ARTS
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture
SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Cultural and creative sectors
Agency Implementation: Cultural Heritage, IP and DGARTES - Directorate General of Arts
Main Feature: Insul’arts seeks to create a new artistic and cultural dynamism in the Autonomous Region of Madeira through the development of a programmatic offer in contemporary arts. Madeira is a Portuguese island territory and as such suffers from all the social, economic, logistical, and cultural constraints that are characteristic of these spaces. “Ser Ultraperiférico” (“To be Ultraperipheral”) is a social and cultural trace of the Madeiran population and life, which occupies in its spirit a feeling of unreachability and inaccessibility. The steep mountains and the extensive sea that make up the landscape of this beautiful island, is embodied in its population austerity and lack of opportunities. Insul’arts emerges as a rupture from this austerity, having in its foundations (i) Equality and participation: enjoyment of shows and artistic activities by the populations living in peripheral spaces within the Island; (ii) Training and sustainability: development and training of young artists and regional structures to work arts and culture nationally and internationally, fostering artistic employability in insular spaces; (iii) Creation and transformation: contributing to the transformation and future of the insular space in an ideal place for work, professionalization and artistic consumption, aiming at bringing together the arts and closer to the different social, educational and cultural systems that exist in the territory.
Results: Access and support to/for contemporary arts in low-density municipalities through, inter alia: programming of artistic productions, involvement of residents in creative processes and audience development activities. The main aim of the Insul'arts project was to contribute to change the paradigm regarding the relation between public and institutions and performing arts, creating a new ideal and perception of their importance in all their different forms, thus developing and enriching the human and social capital of the outermost regions. In this sense, the activities carried out have enabled the engagement of different sectors of the Autonomous Region of Madeira, ranging from the training of local artists (including a scholarship program), teachers, and educators, building relationships between audiences on the outskirts of Madeira 30 and the creations and artistic programming defined. The decentralization of activities and the need to reach audiences in rural municipalities whose art consumption habits are not regular or even non-existent was a major concern within the plans defined, reflected, inter alia, in the spaces programmed. Reconciling the relationship between the arts and the education sector was reinforced, particularly through the partnership with DybwikDans, raising awareness of the importance of the arts in the human and creative development of babies and children. The international partnership also contributed to the mobility of artists. The project also questioned different ways of using the concepts "difference and "inclusion", especially when it comes to artistic works involving artists with disabilities, promoting actions, nationally and internationally, to share knowledge and train artists and producers with and without disabilities in the areas of creation, production, dissemination, logistics and professionalization of inclusive companies. All in all, by programming a cycle of shows in Madeira's different cultural centers, using artists with nationally and internationally recognized careers and activities that encourage the development and professional training of young regional artists, the project paved the path to positive and innovative results, felt not only within its lifetime, but medium to long term.

Title EN: Intercultural artistic relations
Goal: Promote Human Rights And Fundamental Freedoms
SDG: SDG 5 - Achieve gender equality and empower all women and girls,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels
Area of Monitoring: Gender equality
Agency Implementation: Swedish Performing Arts Coalition
Main Feature: Swedish Performing Arts Coalition promotes gender equality by actively supporting the implication of women as cultural professionals, experts and artists. Their board is represented by a significative number of women. In all their projects and activities, women have access to key roles, as decision-makers, producer etc. All the executive team - director, project manager, operations coordinator and head of member service - is composed of women. Swedish Performing Arts Coalition are working with women producers for their festivals. More female representation and implication is one of the criteria when planning artistic collaborations and projects. Women are fully included at any level in their daily work. Swedish Performing Arts Coalition actively supports LGBTQIA+ rights and freedoms. Every year the queer Proud Performing Arts in Sweden, an exclusive free festival is produced. It presents only queer performances in order to largely increase the visibility of LGBTQIA+ representation in the cultural and artistic field and to give access to it for everyone into the Swedish public sphere. Diversity and LGBTQIA+ representation and implication is another one of the criteria when planning artistic collaborations and projects.   Swedish Performing Arts Coalition is one of the core organizations in the forming of the network Freemuse Global LGBT Action Group. Together with colleagues from all over the world they will put special focus on threats and punishment aimed at queer performers. Swedish Performing Arts Coalition promotes the fundamental rights and freedoms of all human beings. They are committed to support minorities and indigenous people participation and representation. The geographical and ethnical identity of the artists in another important criteria in projects and to represent all the diverse identities. They decided to get even more involved in the promotion of human fundamental rights and freedoms by focusing their next biggest international event, the Swedish Biennial for Performing Arts, on minorities and indigenous people arts in order to actively support and promote their representation and implication in the international artistic and cultural scene.   Swedish Performing Arts Coalition actively defends the fundamental rights and freedoms by supporting threatened artists. The project ”Colleagues in crisis” is an important part of their work. They prioritize and shred light on questions concerning freedom of expression, by supporting performance artists who live in conflict zones/are threatened by oppression or persecution, by using our broad network to help those who want to come to Sweden, or for creating a new context for those who live in Sweden in exile. Moreover, they are currently participating to the ”TRIANGLE FOR UKRAINIAN ARTISTS”. This project is a collaboration with partners in Ukraine, Poland and Sweden to support Ukrainian playwrights to continue working during the current war of aggression. As an International Theatre Institute, they are member of the ”Action Committee for Artists Rights” which collects, proves, analyses and makes public cases of violation of the rights of theatre artists and the right to free artistic expression. The cases are addressed to politicians on a formal political level in the name of ITI, according to ACAR’s reaction scheme. ACAR cooperates with other Human and Artists Rights organizations and networks worldwide.

Main Feature: The Government of Timor-Leste actively seeks opportunities for bilateral and multilateral cooperation to create opportunities for training, financing and international exposures for actors in Culture sector.  It has developed regular partnership with the Indonesian Cultural Center in Dili to promote exchange of students, artists and academics and PROCULTURA, a project cofounded by the European Union and Calouste Gulbenkian Foundation and administered and co-financed by Camões, I.P. to support job creation in Culture sector
Results: -	The cooperation with the Indonesian Culture Center has provided scholarship to significant number of Timorese students, including artists, to study in the academic institutions of Indonesia.  From 2016 to 2021, a total of 619 students were beneficiaries of the scholarship program; 176 students accessed the scholarship in 2022 and 117 students in 2023.  The impact of such regular scholarship is yet to be assessed, but is expected to contribute significantly to the diplomatic relationship between the two countries and the quality of human resources in Timor Leste including culture sector. -	PROCULTURA provides grant for small-scale cultural projects, scholarships for undergraduate and master course in the field of music and performing arts and for art residencies, and offers intensive training on cultural entrepreneurship and financing.  In the last four years, 6 projects were selected from Timor-Leste, for a total amount of around 62.000€ (USD 67.580), in various areas of the cultural sector such as gastronomy, children's and youth literature, handicrafts, multimedia and arts education.  In 2023, Timor Leste submitted 9 project proposals aimed at supporting development of film production, participation in international exhibitions or residencies, and creation of music studio, amongst others.  While the impact of PROCULTURA to Timorese culture scene is yet to be assessed, the existing of program has encouraged culture sector actors to develop skills in project proposals writings.

Title EN: International Fund for Cultural Diversity. Fostering youth empowerment.
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture
SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Cultural and creative sectors
Agency Implementation: Balmaceda Young Art Cultural Corporation (BAJ)
Main Feature: Balmaceda Young Art (BAJ), in its 30-year history, has established itself as an important space for cultural participation and social integration of youth, recognised for promoting personal and social transformation through art.   Today, the cultural corporation confronts the challenges of the times, integrating a focus on cultural diversity in its practices through "Fostering Cultural Diversity through Youth Empowerment" (free translation), a project  awarded by the International Fund for Cultural Diversity - UNESCO, whose general goal is to promote the diversity of cultural expressions, strengthening this focus in informal arts education practices (workshops) in the regions of Chile where Balmaceda Young Art can be found, with the aim of increasing tolerance, respect and recognition of diversity as value, among active and empowered youth.   This initative connects a local experience of informal arts education with the interpretative frameworks of the 2005 Convention, through evaluative research with aim of contributing to the design of cultural and education policies that contribute in that regard to cultural diversity.   The experience lasts 18 months and manifests itself through the following 4 components: In the first place, there is the training component with the purpose of instilling skills related to the objectives and guiding principles of the 2005 Convention for Diversity of Cultural Expressions and associated content, among artists-educators that catty out workshops in Balmaceda Young Art and teachers and cultural agents not associated with the institution, for its implementation in educational settings.   For this purpose, between December 2022, January and March 2023 a virtual training took place for 20 artists-educators affiliated with BAJ, regarding content related to interculturality and intersectionality, contemporary didactics on the arts and qualitative research, seeking the inclusion of a cultural diversity approach in the artistic training workshops.   In second place, the arts training component took place through a programme offering 20 arts workshops with a focus on cultural diversity, oriented towards youth between 14 and 19 years of age, that took palce at the BAJ centres in the Antofagasta, Valparaíso, Metropolitan, Biobío and Los Lagos regions. The third component refers to research on evaluation of the results on the inclusion of content around the goals and guiding principles of the 2005 Convention and the focus on Cultural Diversity in arts education workshops.   In terms of methodology, qualitative information production techniques were employed, specifically though the focus group and participant observation, looking to analyse the effect that the inclusion of content related to Cultural Diversity (Interculturality and inter-sectionality) and the interaction of youth from diverse backgrounds within the workshops, has in the dynamics of the workshops and in the creations or artistic processes that emerge from them.
Results: Within the results, we can highlight that 20 artists-educators, affiliated with BAJ, receive training around the 2005 Convention and other related topics such as interculturality, intersectionality, contemporary arts pedagogy and qualitative investigation.At the same time, 15 BAJ emplyees receive training on the 2005 Convention and the cultural diversity approach.   Ninteen arts workshops took place with a cultural diversity focus for youth in the regions where BAJ operates (Antofagasta, Valparaíso, Metropolitan, Biobío and Los Lagos). In the Antofagasta, Valparaíso, Metropolitan, Biobío and Los Lagos regions, 288 youths take part in the arts education workshops with a focus on cultural diversity.   Regarding the profile of the young participants, 81% are women or diversities, 21% belong to indigenous peoples and 9% are migrants. A series of 10 artistic mediation events with a focus on cultural diversity took place in the Biobío Region.   Qualitative evaluative research was carried out, as a pilot to understand how preparing and incorporating content that addreses the goals and guiding principles of the 2005 Convention in the BAJ arts workshops impacts on the cultural diversity knowledge and practices within the space. A publication about the formative arts workshop model with a focus on cultural diversity is prepared and disseminated through the BAJ website.

Title EN: INTERNATIONAL HUMAN RIGHTS FILM FESTIVAL “BAJO NUESTRA PIEL”
Goal: Promote Human Rights And Fundamental Freedoms
SDG: SDG 5 - Achieve gender equality and empower all women and girls,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels
Area of Monitoring: Artistic freedom
Agency Implementation: Bajo Nuestra Piel  EMAIL: festival@bajonuestrapiel.org PHONE: (+591) 77703196
Main Feature: The “Under Our Skin” International Film Festival on Human Rights is an act of opposition to all forms of discrimination and works to promote respect for human dignity, freedom, solidarity, social justice and equality in all areas through national and international cinema.  Since 2016, it has sought to disseminate, inform and raise awareness in society about the importance of Human Rights through the powerful tool of cinema, audiovisual artistic representation in documentary, fiction and animation formats, contained in the production of quality cinema with social commitment, with its own innovative methodology. We want to form new audiences with a critical sense and active participation, who get involved in citizen mobilization activities and/or the dissemination and promotion of the defense of Human Rights, based on the generation of spaces for debate, dialogue, awareness and reflection with the public present at our screenings and training workshops. To this end, we work to create cultural spaces with greater reach and impact, with actions that allow society to visualize and become aware of the exercise of our Human Rights, generating dialogue, interacting with adolescents and young people, opinion leaders, public figures invited to our events and the general population, and creating greater interest in cinema from the Global South, as an alternative to popular and more commercial productions, exploring films that show the realities of unknown countries and their situation in terms of Human Rights. The logic of local organization, that is, the formation of local work teams, seeks the long-term institutionalization of the festival in each department with the generation of resources and own funds that allow them to continue the activities, mainly through the construction of alliances with governmental and non-governmental entities. Based on extensive year-round collaborations with local and international human rights organizations and activists, the most pressing human rights issues are assessed and defined for each location individually. Content is then created around these themes through constant cultural exchange between the artists and filmmakers working on the films we screen, and local artists and filmmakers, and the public, through thematic workshops, spaces for dialogue, and the award-giving process for film selection. Our events consist of community film screenings (short, feature-length), followed by panel discussions, community dialogues, and interactive workshops. Priority is given to activities that have the greatest reach, engagement, and impact. The public part of the festival is presented in the cultural spaces of each locality, as well as in alternative exhibition places: public squares, schools, prisons, nursing homes, etc., without any entrance fee. We work in the field of Human Rights and Civil Society. Human Rights are the fundamental axis of Bajo Nuestra Piel's work, from the rights of children to those deprived of liberty who face complex situations and violations of their fundamental rights. The defense of a life free of violence for all has a privileged space in our project. And of course, from the use of cinema as the main tool for transformation. An essential part of this is the festival’s travelling stage. By visiting rural destinations, the festival reaches out to remote and underprivileged villages to reach an audience that generally lacks access to cinema, let alone cinema that touches on human rights issues and/or includes unconventional artistic content. Younger generations shape our future and tend to be more open to new and possibly innovative ideas. Therefore, we recognize the potential power of youth to influence and drive change. As an organization, we are especially committed to educating new and young audiences through advocacy, empowerment and mentoring to help create an inclusive and prosperous society. To have a strong reach to people between 12 and 25 years old, educational screenings are organized for youth and teenagers that take our film programming and workshops to their universities, schools and special screenings are shown in (juvenile) prisons, indigenous communities, police and military student schools in the effort to open a space for information exchange and discussion for the most vulnerable and least visible in the country. There is no doubt that women continue to be a population group that is highly vulnerable in the full exercise of their rights. This is why we always have a wide variety of films and shorts that address gender issues from different perspectives, and we work to generate deep reflection and debate on the subject with our public.
Results: Since 2016, we have reached more than 40,000 people with our public screenings within the framework of the Film Weeks in 6 of the 9 departments of Bolivia, covering both urban and rural areas, where more than 250 feature and short films from 48 different countries have been screened. We have also developed 5 educational process projects with specific populations such as prisoners, social reintegration centers for minors, soldiers in training, women victims of violence and high school students in their educational units. This international project, based and originating in Bolivia, is currently being developed in more than 50 locations in the country, Ecuador, Peru, Chile and Kenya, with plans to extend to other countries in the South American region, as well as in East Africa. However, it is not simply transported from one city to another. Each activity is carefully selected and adapted, thanks to the creation and management of local coordination teams and volunteers.

Title EN: Joining international treaties and commitments on copyright and related rights
Goal: Achieve A Balanced Flow Of Cultural Goods And Services And Increase The Mobility Of Artists And Cultural Professionals
SDG: SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 10 - Reduce inequality within and among countries,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Treaties and agreements
Cultural Domain: Design,Performing Arts,Media Arts,Cinema and Audiovisual Arts,Music,Publishing,Visual Arts
Agency Implementation: Ministry of Culture, Sports and Tourism and other ministries and branches; provincial and municipal People's Committees, etc.
Main Feature: During the period 2020 - 2023, Viet Nam has joined three new WIPO international treaties on copyright and related rights.  - WIPO Copyright Treaty (WCT) and WIPO Performances and Phonograms Treaty (WPPT), officially taking effect in Viet Nam from February 17, 2022 and July 1, 2022, respectively: These are two treaties related to the protection of works and the rights of authors in the digital environment. Joining the WCT and WPPT affirms Viet Nam's commitment to implementing new generation free trade agreements, creating a legal foundation, contributing to the effective and transparent protection of copyright and works in cyberspace, strengthening international exchanges and cooperation in culture, introducing Vietnamese culture to the world, and bringing human cultural quintessential features to Viet Nam.  - The WIPO Treaty on creating conditions for persons with visual impairments, persons with disabilities who cannot read print, and other persons with disabilities who cannot read to access works to read in the usual way (Marrakesh Treaty), taking effect in Viet Nam from March 6, 2023: The treaty allows people with disabilities and people who raise and care for people with disabilities to copy, distribute, perform, and communicate works across borders in an accessible copy format of the original or copy of the work. In addition to facilitating easier access to publications for people with disabilities, the Marrakesh Treaty also creates a reasonable balance between protecting copyright and protecting the public interest. Joining the Treaty will greatly assist the disabled community in accessing a richer and more diverse source of work, as well as exercising equal rights to cultural and creative enjoyment for all groups of people.  In 2023, the Ministry of Culture, Sports and Tourism of Viet Nam and the National Copyright Administration of the People's Republic of China signed a Memorandum of Cooperation in the field of copyright. According to the Memorandum of Cooperation, the two sides strengthen cooperation and regularly exchange legal and technical information in the field of copyright and related rights. The Memorandum also encourages the two countries to engage in copyright and related rights training and expert exchange activities.
Results: To ensure the implementation of international commitments, contributing to the effective execution of copyright and related rights in Viet Nam, in the period from 2020 to 2023, Viet Nam has conducted many diverse activities and achieved many positive results, as follows:  (i) Improving the law and enhancing the efficient management and enforcement of copyright and related rights  - On June 6, 2022, the National Assembly of Viet Nam officially passed and promulgated the Law amending and supplementing a number of articles of the Intellectual Property Law. Among the three amendments and supplements to a number of articles of the Intellectual Property Law, this amendment and supplement is considered the largest and most comprehensive, covering many issues, including copyright and related rights content.  - On April 26, 2023, the Vietnamese Government issued Decree No. 17/2023/ND-CP detailing a number of articles and measures to implement the Intellectual Property Law on copyright and related rights.  - Implementing a complete review, proceeding to issue a decree stipulating penalties for administrative violations of copyright and related rights, and organizing the development of a draft decree amending and supplementing a number of articles of Decree No. 21/2015/ND-CP regulating royalties and remunerations for cinematographic, fine arts, photography, theater works, and other types of performing arts.  - Digitizing copyright assets and related rights and strengthening copyright protection in the internet environment.  - Improving the openness and transparency in the activities of collective representative organizations of copyright and related rights.  (ii) Promoting and education on copyright and related rights  The Ministry of Culture, Sports and Tourism, the agency directly responsible for the implementation of policies on copyright and related rights, has chaired or coordinated to organize many seminars and conferences, competitions, events, etc. to disseminate and provide training on copyright and related rights in general and the three newly joined WIPO international treaties in particular. The subjects of these conferences and workshops are very diverse, including representatives of state management agencies, rights holders, collective representative organizations of copyright, related rights, businesses, etc. Events includes the Conference to disseminate the basic contents of WCT Treaty and WPPT Treaty (September 2022), Training Conference on the Marrakesh Treaty and copyright exceptions for people with disabilities (September 2022), online competition on copyright and related rights, Workshop on copyright and related rights protection in cyberspace (December 2022), Viet Nam and Korea Copyright Forum (April 2023) and Discussion on "The role of women in promoting innovation, creativity, and creating intellectual property" (2023), etc.  (iii) The increasing role of collective management organizations of copyright and related rights  Collective management organizations of copyright and related rights not only collectively represent the author community, protecting the rights and cooperative interests of authors, but also at the same time contribute to reducing the burden on the state for copyright protection tasks that exceed the management activities of competent authorities. In Viet Nam, collective management organizations have gradually promoted and asserted their indispensable role in copyright and related rights. In addition to previously established organizations, in the period 2020–2023, a number of additional organizations have been founded, such as the Viet Nam Creativity and Copyright Association (VCCA), the Viet Nam Digital Content Creative Alliance (DCCA), etc.

Area of Monitoring: Cultural and creative sectors
Cultural Domain: Media Arts,Cinema and Audiovisual Arts,Music,Visual Arts

Main Feature: The Film Commission’s particular focus covers both the film and animation industry. The Film Commission’s main target areas related to these specific screen-based industries involves advocating policy as well as liaising between government departments, private sector companies and agencies to facilitate production as well as acting in an advisory capacity for these productions. Included also in this function is the facilitation of film and animation productions, arrangement and processing immigration, permits, licenses, registration and tax requests.   Promotion is also a large part of what is done at The Film Commission. This involves promoting Jamaica as a film location, promoting local productions and also promoting the export and investment opportunities in our film and animation industry.  The Commission is  also tasked with ensuring that film and animation as local industries are able to grow and develop and meet the standard of international markets. For this reason The Film Commission is also involved in developing various initiatives to increase and improve business and performance in these two particular industries.
Results: The main incentives available to filmmakers and content creators for production through the Film Commission are:   The Employment Tax Credit (ETC) which reduces Corporate Income Tax liability. ETC provides for a maximum of 30 percent credit for local companies’ Pay As You Earn (PAYE) obligations, which can reduce income tax liability to as low as 17.5 percent.  Bond Waivers for foreign productions. Foreign producers who register their productions with the Film Commission can access bond waivers on all approved equipment being imported temporarily. Duty-free importation on Equipment and Machinery and Productive Incentive Relief (PIR). The PIR allows filmmakers to import products for use in your productions without an import duty charge being applied. Musicians and filmmakers are the main beneficiaries of this incentive and can access it by signing up online for The Entertainment Registry. The Entertainment Registry lists creatives in the music and film industry which allows for confirmation as an industry professional. The PIR exemption however doesn’t preclude production companies from customs duty and Additional Stamp Duty. Under this incentive programme some of the types of goods that may be imported are tools of trade for the film and music industry. For more details on what goods and incentives are covered under the PIR visit Jamaica Customs. Double Taxation Avoidance Agreements (DTAAs), which govern the levying of taxes, by two or more jurisdictions, on the same asset or income.

Agency Implementation: National Centre on Sexual Education(CENESEX)
Main Feature: Facilitate the effective exercise of the rights of LGBTIQ+ people, through comprehensive sexuality education. Facilitate the guarantee of the sexual rights of all people and especially LGBTIQ+ people, in the family, social and community settings. Carry out activities in virtual and in-person spaces, ranging from academic dialogue and social activism, to artistic, community and communication actions. Raising awareness among the population regarding respect for family plurality, equality education, non-discrimination based on sexual orientation and gender identity, as well as the promotion of a legal culture around family law. Celebration of the International Transidentities Gender and Culture Colloquium with themes focused on health. Debate on bioethics, on how to guarantee the rights of the LGTBIQ+ community from the Cuban public health sector, as well as on trans and intersex childhood and adolescence, in all of which experiences from gender medicine are present.
Results: Joint collaborative work has been done with the Ministry of Culture and its institutions. Every year an Artistic Gala is held in which professional artists who feel identified with the defense of the rights of the LGBTIQ+ community participate. An example of this is the participation of renowned artists such as the singers Vania Borges and Haila María Monpie, among others, in many of the activities organized by CENESEX. The Trans community currently has a choir that has been advised by teacher Digna Guerra, a renowned singing artist. The plan of activities throughout the country in the celebration of the Conference each year was broad and comprehensive, since scientific actions and programs are also carried out in different locations coinciding with May 17, International Day against Homophobia and Transphobia. The country has significant advances that can be celebrated, such as the enshrinement in the Constitution of the Republic and the Family Code of the right of all people to build a family, based on diverse relationships of affection, and to live with full dignity, without discrimination of any kind. At the end of November 2023, 1,333 same-sex marriages had taken place in the country (806 between men and 527 between women), to which 85 de facto unions were added.

Main Feature: The Karama International Human Rights Film Festival, established in Jordan in 2010, is the first of its kind in the country. With a 14-year track record of cultural impact, it immerses audiences in a unique cultural and cinematic experience through screenings, workshops, and events that employ multimedia methods. The festival sparks critical thinking and fosters understanding of human rights issues through powerful cultural events.Held annually in Amman, the six-day international festival remains attuned to the intellectual, moral, and creative issues in the MENA region and globally. Through films, visual arts, music, seminars, forums, and art exhibitions, the Karama Film Festival promotes dialogue, engages in debates, builds capacity, and launches high-impact programs adressing pressing human rights topics.Over the past fourteen years, Karama HRFF has showcased more than 850 films from over 66 countries, including documentaries, feature fiction, short fiction, and animation. The festival aims to advocate for human rights, stimulate debate, encourage critical thinking and civic engagement, and foster democratic dialogue on human rights issues among international, regional, and local institutions, organizations, and the broader public.

Engagement of audiences is also an ongoing process. We however witness an increased awareness and understanding of the human rights issues. Compared to our first edition where the festival’s objective was to introduce the notion of human rights in Jordan’s artistic rhetoric, we have reached an advanced phase.  Result 1. Result 2. Increase belief in the importance on youth as cultural and artistic members of the community promoting human rights values and ethics.  Result 3. Better connections, enhance collaboration, and better access to information and resources amongst young artists, as well as giving them platforms to express and shape their societies.   Result4. All participants of panels, discussions will want to pursue their engagement and social activism through their own platforms as networks.   Result 5. Shedding light on the importance of the results of last decade of political and social change on the current generation and opening the discussion on the issues faced today. Title EN: Key to the City
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture
SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Cultural and creative sectors
Agency Implementation: TrAP - Transnational Arts Production
Main Feature: Key to the City is a project that helps to achieve TrAP's goal of a representative and diverse cultural life in the future. The background for the project is that fewer people with minority backgrounds choose a career in cultural life because they lack opportunities in the form of information and networks - not because they lack talent or interest. The way this is done is by reaching out to young people and putting them in contact with art and cultural institutions. The young people are also employed by the various institutions for a limited period. Through Key to the City, the young people get to help shape the work they will do in the company they are employed in for a shorter period. By allowing the young people to participate in these decisions and step into work roles that they find exciting and challenging, the young people will have a taste for more and perhaps want similar work in the future. We think it is important to also reflect the field of art and culture by giving young people experience with different types of jobs within the field. A major focus in Key to the City is to break in young people's prejudices about art and cultural work and show that it is more than just work as an artist or museum host. Many young people often have this impression, and do not see this work as relevant if they are not "artistically gifted", this shows the importance of opening up the field. Key to the City reaches out to young people in districts with a perceived distance from cultural life and puts them in contact with art and cultural institutions. The young people are employed by the various institutions for a limited period. Most of the jobs we create do not require professional expertise, and then we select those who show the greatest interest and curiosity for the job. It is appropriate for us to give the jobs to those who have not had similar jobs before, and who do not already have a large network in the field of art and culture. In this way, we believe that we can reach the right target group for the project - namely those who have little or no contact with the art and culture field. Although these are important to reach, we also want to help young people who already have an interest and perhaps experience in the art field, but who have not yet developed a network. Therefore, we also create jobs that are more subject-specific. In this way, we get applicants who would like a path into an art field and want to build a network and good work experiences. We recruit young people between 16-25 years, through Instagram accounts open calls. Keys to the city has also turned out to be quite beneficial to the art institutions in Norway (Particularly Oslo), due to the focus on youth-involvement and the lack of experience of recruiting this group into the arts. Since we started in 2019, we have been able to offer jobs at the Oslo Philharmonic, the National Museum, the Ultima Festival, Fotogalleriet, Kunstnernes Hus, Musikkfest Oslo, Ultima, UKS, Kunsthall Trondheim, Det Norske Teatret, Atelier Nord, the project Makingsensetogether, Intercultural Museum, Oslo Open, Nitja Centre for Contemporary Art.
Results: What we see as a result of the project is that the path to the creative sector for young people in working class neighbourhoods is made more accessible. Not always because of our intended efforts, this is also a product of unplanned impacts like for instance that the youngsters in our programs get to know each other and back each other up. This is one of the strongest ways in which a good outcome is secured for our participants. Not only can they unpack and understand the different experiences but also help describe the potentials and barriers they encounter when entering the arts scene. Finding the way is something we do collectively. Although our program is directed towards individuals, we make sure that the different participants can meet each other so that this aspect of the program can unfold.

Title EN: Key to the City
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture
SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Partnering with civil society
Cultural Domain: Media Arts,Cinema and Audiovisual Arts,Music,Visual Arts
Agency Implementation: House of Arts
Main Feature: Key to the City is a multi-stakeholder movement that integrates creativity and cultural expressions in development strategies and frameworks related to SDG 3 on good health and wellbeing. Through partnerships with various ministries, youth-led organisations, local councils and the police, the initiative addresses mental health and substance abuse challenges through creative expressions such as performing arts, music, radio programming, podcasting and visual arts. Target groups are school drop-outs, young people with disabilities, recovering addicts, school going youth, teenage mothers and youths in marginalised communities. Their access to and participation in cultural life is facilitated through trainings on creative entrepreneurship, awarding of micro-grants, and interaction with psychotherapy support extended by established artists and cultural professionals through various artforms. The desired outcome of these interventions is the realisation of inclusive and participatory cultural policy making through the amplification of social change art, art for development and raising youth understanding of their unique role in development, while simultaneously ensuring that these youths practice mindfulness and prioritise their mental well-being.  Some community-based projects of the initiative, as driven by recipients of micro-grants include but are not limited to:  •	Bootcamps: focusing on mindset shifting, with creative expressions as a conduit  •	Colouring your trauma: a visual art project that challenges the stigma of vocalising and expressing emotion  •	Art-therapy sessions for girls: a woman-only programme that encourages school-going girls to communicate their fears, challenges and aspirations on canvas, in a safe environment  •	Dance it off: established by a consortium of youth-based organisations to promote dance as a form of exercise and source of mental welfare
Results: The initiative has demonstrably increased youth knowledge of mental health and wellness, through providing a creative platform of expression. This has been evidenced by a significant drop in reported cases of drug and substance abuse.  As of December 2023, the initiative had benefited 9 982 youths through the grant-making strand, with a total of 107 979 individuals cumulatively reached through online arts programming.  Overall, the initiatives’ use of arts and culture programming has strengthened capacity of youth-led organisations to engage in mental health action and advocacy; strengthened community awareness and action on mental health in vulnerable urban communities, and further improved access to services for youths affected by mental health problems in vulnerable communities.

Main Feature: Visarte Vaud, s’engage pour que la création artistique ait lieu dans de bonnes conditions et conseille les artistes. Elle se donne pour tâches de faire progresser la reconnaissance de la profession et la sécurité sociale de ses membres, de défendre leurs droits, d’encourager la solidarité entre les professionnelles et les professionnels, d’aider les membres en matière juridique, financière et sociale, de traiter des questions pertinentes et de les diffuser sur diverses plateformes.  Visarte Vaud a mis en place en novembre 2023 un premier atelier/workshop sous la forme de boîte à outils ou de « kit de survie » en collaboration avec le Bureau Culturel Vaud, à l'attention des artistes visuelles et visuels. Le titre de l’atelier était : « Les arts visuels au travail : Enjeux de la professionnalisation et kit de survie. »  Le but de l’atelier/workshop est de présenter un panorama des enjeux auxquels sont confrontées et confrontées les artistes visuelles et visuels au sortir de l’école, au début ou au cours de leur vie professionnelle. La seconde partie de l’atelier dédiée à des questions/réponses, partages d’expériences, de documents et d’informations a pour objectifs de répondre aux questions telles que : -	Comment accéder à des ressources et à du matériel sans l’aide d’une institution ? -	Quelles sont les stratégies de parcours à prendre en compte, où appliquer et quand ? -	Comment mettre en avant son travail ? -	Quelle forme administrative et juridique adopter dans sa pratique artistique ? -	À quoi sert et comment monter une association ? -	Quels sont les droits et devoirs en matière de conditions de travail ? -	À quelle rémunération prétendre ?
Results: Ces ateliers « kit de survie » seront pérennisés les années prochaines sous forme de série d'ateliers thématiques. Ceux-ci seront complétés par un guichet-permanence à l'attention des artistes visuelles et visuels au sein de leurs nouveaux locaux dans la Maison Gaudard, devenue la nouvelle Maison de la culture et de l'innovation numérique à Lausanne.

L’intégration de la perspective de genre au sein du processus budgétaire vise la promotion de l'équité et l'égalité entre les sexes. Cette approche ne se traduit pas par l'élaboration de budgets distincts ou spécifiquement axés sur les femmes, mais plutôt par l'assurance que les budgets reconnaissent et répondent aux priorités et besoins parfois différenciés de divers groupes, qu'ils soient constitués de femmes, d'hommes, de filles ou de garçons. Le budget national, qui traduit les priorités gouvernementales en détaillant les dépenses prévues sur une période donnée, est traditionnellement présenté sans faire référence à la population bénéficiaire ventilée par sexe. Dans cette apparente neutralité subsiste toutefois une réalité bien différente, car les décisions budgétaires entraineront des répercussions distinctes sur les femmes et les hommes. Ignorer ces disparités risque donc d'entretenir, voire d'aggraver, les inégalités existantes. C'est ici que l'intégration de l'approche genre au processus budgétaire, à travers l'adoption de la BSG, prend tout son sens : elle ambitionne de réformer la gestion des finances publiques pour assurer une mise en œuvre plus effective des engagements en matière d'égalité femmes-hommes. Elle contribue à plus de pertinence des actions de l’État et ainsi à une meilleure performance des politiques publiques. La Tunisie s'est résolument inscrite dans cette dynamique internationale en instaurant une budgétisation sensible au genre, notamment en intégrant ces questions au sein de son cadre normatif. La Loi Organique du Budget (LOB) n°15 du 13 février 2019 a marqué une réforme significative en faveur de l'égalité entre les femmes et les hommes en insufflant une dimension genre au processus budgétaire. Son article 18 stipule d'ailleurs que : « Le responsable de programme œuvre à la préparation du budget suivant des objectifs et des indicateurs garantissant l’équité et l'égalité des chances entre les hommes et les femmes et d’une manière générale entre les différentes catégories sociales, sans discrimination, et qui feront l'objet d'une évaluation sur cette base. ». La BSG en Tunisie s'inscrit au cœur des réformes budgétaires en cours, notamment en lien avec la gestion budgétaire par objectifs (GBO). L’intégration de l’approche Genre dans le processus budgétaire, vient non seulement compléter les efforts de l’Etat en matière de l’égalité des genres, mais joue également un rôle central et structurant en matière de confirmation de la crédibilité de ces efforts. En effet, le budget n’est jamais neutre. Il constitue un instrument qui traduit les politiques publiques et les stratégies sectorielles. De ce fait, un Budget Sensible au Genre a une portée structurante et stratégique du fait qu’il répond à des objectifs aussi bien politiques, économiques que sociaux et culturels. Dans cette optique la BSG constitue l’un des : • Outils de concrétisation des droits de l’Homme et de réduction des inégalités. • Instruments renforçant la logique axée sur la performance dans la gestion publique. Ainsi la nouvelle approche budgétaire axée sur la performance et intégrant la dimension genre permet le passage des intentions exprimées vers des mesures concrètes ayant un effet tangible. • Outils fondamentaux pour assurer la transparence du budget • Mécanismes de réalisation de l’équité, de l’égalité et de la justice socio-culturelle. • Outils de renforcement des liens entre les impacts sociaux, économiques et politiques dans une optique de développement durable.  La BSG cherche en outre à faire évoluer la gestion du budget de l’Etat dans le but de garantir la pleine réalisation des engagements en matière d’égalité Femmes/Hommes.
Results: Le système de gestion des finances publiques en Tunisie s'efforce de répondre aux objectifs des politiques publiques visant à reconnaitre les besoins différenciés des femmes et des hommes, et à favoriser l'égalité des sexes. Ainsi, l'intégration de la dimension genre est devenue une exigence pour toutes les missions et les programmes, avec l'obligation d'incorporer cette perspective dans leurs processus de planification et de budgétisation. Pour ce faire, depuis l’élaboration du budget 2020, les circulaires budgétaires exigent de chaque mission (y compris la mission culture) la prise en compte du genre dans les politiques publiques et le budget. Le ministère des finances via l’Unité Centrale de la Gestion Budgétaire par Objectifs (UCGBO) a élaboré une note d’orientation sur la BSG ayant pour objectif de proposer un cadre de référence unifié aux chefs de mission, aux responsables de programme et à tout autre acteur intervenant dans la mise en œuvre de la démarche BSG. Le ministère des Finances a introduit deux outils spécifiques dans la budgétisation qui augmentent significativement la prise en compte du genre dans les programmes et le budget des ministères couvrant l'ensemble de la chaine allant de la planification à l'évaluation créant ainsi un environnement propice à sa mise en œuvre au sein des politiques publiques. L'objectif est de veiller à la prise en charge des besoins spécifiques des femmes et des hommes, tout en réduisant les disparités. Il s’agit des fiches genres jointes dans le Projet Annuel de Performance (PAP) et de la fiche de restitution annexée au Rapport Annuel de Performance (RAP) des ministères. Cela constitue un apport important de la Tunisie à l’institutionnalisation de l’approche genre dans le budget. Ces deux fiches font l’inventaire des engagements visant la promotion de l’égalité entre les femmes et les hommes de chaque ministère. Elles soulignent les écarts et contribuent à aligner les programmes sur les effets annoncés dans le Plan d’Action national pour l’Intégration et l’Institutionnalisation du Genre (PANIIG). Elles traduisent les besoins et les actions prévues en objectifs et indicateurs opérationnels. En annexe du RAP, la fiche-genre restitution établit le bilan des efforts fournis. Avec ces annexes, dans chacun des documents mentionnés ci-haut, les fiches genre reprennent systématiquement les programmes et les apprécient à la lumière des engagements à l’égard de l’égalité femmes-hommes, ainsi, la préoccupation d’égalité et d’équité est introduite à deux moments cruciaux de la budgétisation. En 2022, le Ministère des Finances, en partenariat avec l’UNICEF et Genesis Analytics, s’est lancé dans la mise en place d’un référentiel de déploiement des nomenclatures sensibles au genre et à l’enfant. Le but de ce référentiel est de rendre intelligible la mise en œuvre de la nomenclature sensible au genre et celle sensible à l’enfant, en mettant à la disposition de toutes les parties prenantes, qu’ils soient, responsables au sein de la chaine managériales, financiers ou administrateurs de budgets, un guide pratique pour faciliter l’intégration des questions du genre et de l’enfant dans la classification du budget de l’État. L’objectif général du référentiel est d’appuyer les acteurs clés d’affecter correctement les dépenses dédiées à la promotion de l’égalité de genre et droits des enfants dans le système d’information de la gestion financière et d’assurer leur suivi et leur analyse.
Recommandations: L'institutionnalisation de la budgétisation sensible au genre nécessite un engagement ferme et une approche globale pour que la perspective de genre soit adéquatement intégrée au processus budgétaire. Des conditions facilitantes sont importantes pour une mise en œuvre réussie de la BSG : • engagement politique : il est essentiel que les plus hautes instances gouvernementales affichent un engagement fort en faveur de l'égalité des sexes. Les décideurs•euses politiques doivent reconnaitre l'importance de l'intégration de la perspective de genre dans le budget et être prêt•es à soutenir les changements nécessaires ; • cadre légal et politique solide : l’adoption d’une vision stratégique, d’une politique nationale claire en matière de genre et d’une législation correspondante sont grandement facilitantes à l’atteinte de l’égalité entre les femmes et les hommes; • analyse de genre : la réalisation d'une analyse de genre approfondie est la première étape pour comprendre comment les politiques publiques et le budget affectent différemment les femmes et les hommes. Cette analyse doit être intégrée dans le processus budgétaire ; • données et statistiques sexospécifiques : il est essentiel de disposer de données sexospécifiques de qualité pour étayer la budgétisation sensible au genre. Les données sur les indicateurs de genre doivent être collectées et utilisées de manière régulière ; • capacité institutionnelle : les organismes gouvernementaux doivent disposer du personnel formé et compétent pour réaliser une budgétisation sensible au genre. La formation et le renforcement des capacités sont donc essentiels ; • participation des parties prenantes : les groupes de femmes, les organisations de la société civile, les chercheur•euses et d'autres parties prenantes doivent être consulté•es et impliqué•es dans le processus budgétaire. Leurs perspectives et leurs connaissances sont précieuses pour identifier les besoins et les priorités de genre ; • budget transparent et accessible : assurer la transparence du processus budgétaire et rendre les informations budgétaires accessibles au public renforcent la reddition de comptes et permettent aux citoyen•nes de suivre l'utilisation des ressources ; • suivi et évaluation : la mise en œuvre de la budgétisation sensible au genre doit être suivie de près et des mécanismes d'évaluation doivent être mis en place pour évaluer l'impact des politiques budgétaires sur l'égalité des sexes ; • collaboration intersectorielle : les ministères et les organismes gouvernementaux doivent travailler ensemble de manière coordonnée pour garantir une approche cohérente de la budgétisation sensible au genre ; • durabilité à long terme : la budgétisation sensible au genre ne devrait pas être considérée comme une initiative ponctuelle, mais comme un processus continu et durable. Elle doit être intégrée dans la culture organisationnelle et institutionnelle à long terme. En résumé, l'implantation de la budgétisation sensible au genre nécessite un engagement politique, un cadre légal solide, des compétences techniques, la participation des parties prenantes et une approche globale pour intégrer la perspective de genre dans tout le processus budgétaire de manière soutenue et durable.

Title EN: la création de la Centrale de Matériels d’Appui aux Industries Culturelles
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture
SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Cultural and creative sectors
Agency Implementation: Ministère en charge des Arts et de la culture
Main Feature: La Centrale de Matériels d’Appui aux Industries Culturelles, créée par Décret n°15.301, du 6 Aout 2015, a pour objet, l’acquisition, la gestion, la sauvegarde et la mise à disposition de matériels, équipements et logistique appropriés et destinés à la création, la production et la commercialisation des œuvres artistiques pour la promotion des industries culturelles en République Centrafricaine. La Centrale de Materiels est un organe à caractère public et professionnel, placé sous la tutelle du Cabinet du Ministère en charge des Arts et de la Culture. Elle dispose d’une autonomie de gestion administrative et financière. Le fonctionnement de la La Centrale de Materiels  (CMAIC) est régi principalement par son Arrêté de fonctionnement n°908/MTACA/DIRCAB/DCMAIC, du 7 Mars 2016, depuis l’article 4 à l’article 36. Ils parlent du Comité de Gestion, de la Direction et ses Services, des ressources, des dispositions financières et comptables, de l’organe de contrôle, du personnel et des dispositions finales. De manière plus spécifique, à l’étape de la création, la La Centrale de Materiels est appelée à soutenir les artistes et les créateurs dans leurs efforts pour créer des activités, biens et services culturels. A l’étape de la production, elle appui le développement d’activités, biens et services culturels en favorisant l’accès aux mécanismes de production et en favorisant le développement d’entreprises culturelles. A l’étape de la distribution ou diffusion, elle promeut les possibilités d’accès dans la distribution d’activités, biens et services culturels, par le biais de canaux publics, au niveau national, régional et international. A l’étape de l’accès, la Centrale de Materiels est appelée à fournir de l’information sur l’offre des activités, biens et services culturels nationaux ou étrangers disponibles, grâce à des incitations appropriées, et à développer la capacité du public à y avoir accès.
Results: La Centrale possède un bureau principal pour l’administration et deux (2) unités de prestation et de production artistique : un magasin des matériels et équipements de sonorisation et de production musicale et un studio d’enregistrement sonore. Les forces de l’organisme sont les suivantes : •	Les institutions publiques et les Artistes ou Groupes artistiques sont les clients potentiels de la CMAIC ; •	L’existence d’une note fixant la tarification des prestations de service de la Centrale. Une tarification jugée abordable et promotionnelle ; •	Une expérience en matière de contractualisation des prestations de service ; •	L’offre de trois services au public : 	Location des matériels de sonorisation de haute gamme pour les productions scéniques ; 	L’accueil en résidence de création musicale ; 	La production phonographique en disposant un studio d’enregistrement sonore.  •	Le recrutement d’un Technicien de son de niveau professionnel ; •	L’existence d’un cadre règlementaire ; •	La localisation de la CMAIC en plein milieu artistique, administratif et d’un accès facile au public.
Recommandations: Vu les faiblesses, les menaces et les difficultés rencontrées, nous suggérons les idées suivantes : •	Le renforcement du cadre normatif de la CMAIC en élaborant un projet de lois spécifiques régissant les sous secteurs des industries culturelles et créatives en République Centrafricaine ; •	La mise en place du Comité de Gestion en vue de renforcer le cadre institutionnel et  de gouvernance ; •	Concevoir, élaborer et publier des outils de gestion administrative, financière, comptable, communicationnelle et logistique de la CMAIC ; •	La mise en place d’un programme de formation et de perfectionnement du personnel et des acteurs du secteur ; •	La garantie du financement publique par la création de nouveaux crédits dans la loi des finances de l’Etat ; •	Le renforcement du dispositif de sécurité et de sureté sur les matériels et les installations de la CMAIC ; •	La diversification, le renforcement, la structuration et la décentralisation des offres de services et de biens de la CMAIC ; •	La mise à disposition d’un site domanial autonome pour abriter l’administration et le centre des opérations de la CMAIC ; •	L’adoption de la stratégie de Partenariat Public-Privé (PPP) en vue de renforcer et garantir le financement croisé des actions de la CMAIC ; •	La mise en place d’un cluster culturel. C’est un cadre de discussion, d’échange et de renforcement des capacités inter organisme public de la culture et du tourisme.

Title EN: La Lanterne Magique / Die Zauberlaterne / La Lanterna Magica
Goal: Integrate Culture In Sustainable Development Frameworks
SDG: SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: National sustainable development policies and plans
Agency Implementation: Association Suisse La Lanterne Magique ASLM, Neuchâtel
Main Feature: La Lanterne Magique invite tous les enfants de 6 à 12 ans à découvrir 9 films par année, à un prix qui permet à toutes et tous de faire partie du club, et selon une démarche unique en son genre. Quelques jours avant chaque séance, les enfants reçoivent un journal illustré qui leur présente le film. Avant la projection, un spectacle amusant et interactif joué par des animatrices et des animateurs, des comédiennes et des comédiens les prépare encore à la découverte du cinéma. Sans leurs parents mais entourés d’adultes responsables, les enfants apprivoisent les grandes émotions du cinéma et partagent des moments privilégiés avec des camarades de leur âge, tout en aiguisant leur sens critique. La Lanterne Magique propose chaque année un nouveau programme de films qui montrent le meilleur du cinéma dans toute sa diversité, offrant ainsi une éducation à l’image de qualité.  La Lanterne Magique a bénéficié du soutien de l’Office fédéral des assurance sociales OFAS avec les aides financières aux organisations particulières selon l’art. 7 al. 2 de la loi sur l’encouragement de l’enfance et de la jeunesse LEEJ.  La Lanterne magique a également bénéficié d’un soutien de l’Office fédéral de la culture OFC, dans le cadre du soutien à la médiation cinématographique pour les enfants et les jeunes, par le biais d’une convention de prestations pour la période 2020-2024.
