Title EN: La nouvelle politique culturelle de la République de Guinée.
Goal: Integrate Culture In Sustainable Development Frameworks
SDG: SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: National sustainable development policies and plans
Cultural Domain: Design,Performing Arts,Media Arts,Cinema and Audiovisual Arts,Music,Publishing,Visual Arts
Agency Implementation: Ministère de la Culture, du Tourisme et de l’Artisanat
Main Feature: En 2018, la République de Guinée a adopté une nouvelle politique culturelle. Cette politique se fonde à la fois sur la révolution culturelle socialiste (1967-1984), les principes définis dans la Constitution et les Lois organiques du pays, mais aussi dans des Conventions internationales auxquelles la Guinée est partie prenante. Au titre des Conventions Internationales, il faut notamment citer la Déclaration Universelle des Droits de l’Homme et le Pacte International relatif aux Droits Economiques, Sociaux et Culturel dont les dispositions sont rappelées et précisées dans des conventions africaines : • la Charte Africaine des Droits de l’Homme et des Peuples, • la Charte de la Renaissance Culturelle Africaine de l’Union Africaine (2006), • le Plan d’action de l’Union Africaine sur les industries culturelles et créatives en Afrique, connu sous le nom de Plan d’action de Nairobi (2008) ; • la Déclaration et Plan d’action de Dakar pour la promotion des cultures et des industries culturelles ACP (2003). Elle s’inscrit dans le Plan National de Développement Economique et Social (PNDES) 2016-2020, en tant que cadre de cohérence temporelle, sectorielle et régionale à moyen terme et première phase quinquennale d’opérationnalisation de la Vision à long terme « Guinée, 2040 ». La Nouvelle politique Culturelle est en cohérence avec le Document de Stratégie de Réduction de la Pauvreté (DSRP). Dans ce cadre, elle vise les objectifs suivants : • Reconnaître, illustrer, protéger et promouvoir la culture nationale : La Guinée met un accent particulier sur la reconnaissance et l’illustration de son identité culturelle nationale en considérant le pluralisme culturel, le droit à la différence et le respect réciproque des cultures des communautés composant la nation comme un facteur de paix, d’équilibre, d’équité et de cohésion sociale.  • Démocratiser l’accès à la culture : elle favorise la liberté de création et d’expression des créateurs et l’épanouissement culturel de chaque individu. • Promouvoir une culture novatrice, scientifique et technique : elle s’appuie sur la capitalisation des savoirs locaux pour produire une sensibilité, une culture et des pratiques de l’innovation. Attentive aux rapports qui existent entre la société, la culture, la science et les technologies, elle met un accent particulier sur les Technologies de l’Information et de la Communication (TIC) comme outil de développement et de promotion des cultures locales et de la culture nationale. • Contribuer à la réduction de la pauvreté et au développement durable : considérant le caractère transversal de la culture, la Nouvelle Politique Culturelle contribue de façon significative à l’atteinte de l’ensemble des Objectifs du Développement Durable (ODD), et plus spécifiquement aux sous-objectifs portant sur l’éducation. Elle appuie la promotion des industries culturelles pour produire de la richesse, offrir des revenus, générer des emplois et promouvoir des innovations et des connaissances.  • Participer à l’édification d’un monde de paix, d’entente entre les nations, plus équitable et plus prospère : elle contribue à renforcer et à dynamiser sa participation à la construction de l’espace culturel de la Communauté Economique des Etats de l’Afrique de l’Ouest (CEDEAO) et de l’Union Africaine (UA). Ce document d’orientation est articulé autour de trois (3) axes stratégiques prioritaires, parmi lesquels deux (2) concernent directement la protection et la promotion de la diversité des expressions culturelles : - favoriser et appuyer la créativité, les innovations et la diversification des expressions artistiques et culturelles en dotant les institutions, les organisations et les artistes de ressources appropriées (axe 2) ; - Renforcer les capacités des institutions publiques et des autres acteurs du secteur de la culture en matière de gouvernance et de management du secteur de la culture (axe 3). Aussi, plusieurs actions prioritaires visant à protéger et à promouvoir la diversité des expressions culturelles ont été identifiées dans le document. La finalité de cette politique vise à optimiser la contribution de la culture à la cohésion nationale, à la démocratie, à l’émancipation sociale, à la construction d’un citoyen libre et responsable et au développement durable de la Guinée.
Results: Les résultats suivants ont été obtenus, à savoir : -	La Bibliothèque Nationale de Guinée (BNG) créée par décret du 9 août 2023, fixant les missions et son organisation. Cette initiative marque une étape significative dans la conservation et la promotion du patrimoine culturel et documentaire du pays. Elle fonctionne conformément à ses missions ; -	21 préfectures sur 33 sont dotées de bibliothèques de lecture publique (2022 et 2023), avec un personnel formé en bibliothéconomie et dont les fonds sont renouvelés et actualisés chaque année ; -	10 communes rurales isolées ou constituant des lecteurs potentiels sont dotées de 8  Centre de Lecture et d’Animation Culturelle (CLAC) (2022, 2023 et 2024) avec un personnel au nombre de 40 formés en animation/médiation culturelle et dont les fonds sont renouvelés et actualisés chaque année ; -	Dotation des CLAC en engins roulants (Pick up) (2022, 2023 et 2024) ; -	23.571 lecteurs sont abonnés au niveau des bibliothèques de lecture publique (2022, 2023 et 2024) ; -	14.412 lecteurs sont abonnés au niveau des CLAC (2022, 2023 et 2024) ; -	3.024 animations sont réalisées dans les Bibliothèques de Lecture Publique (2022, 2023 et 2024) ; -	6.456 animations sont réalisées dans les CLAC (2022, 2023 et 2024) ; -	13 bibliothèques numériques équipées de 78 ordinateurs sont créés et fonctionnelles (2022, 2023 et 2024) ; -	Acquisition de 12.143 livres d’auteurs guinéens en faveur des 21 bibliothèques de lecture publique (2022, 2023 et 2024) ; -	Les ouvrages d’auteurs guinéens figurant dans les programmes scolaires et universitaires :  -	Littérature : Enfant Noir de Camara Laye, le cercle des tropiques d’Alioune N’Fan Touré, les écailles du ciel de Thierno Monenembo, Jeune homme du sable de William Sassine… ; -	Science exacte : Séries de collections avec l’INRAP ; -	Séries scientifiques : CIAM 11ème, 12ème, terminale, mathématique physique et chimie. -	Quatre (4) éditions « Des 72 heures du Livre » ont été accompagnées par le gouvernement guinéen en tant qu’évènement de promotion du livre et de la lecture publique ; -	Quatre (4) éditions de la quinzaine artistique et du festival national des arts et de la culture (2017, 2018, 2022 et 2023) ont été organisées avec la participation des artistes des quartiers, des communes, des sous-préfectures, des préfectures et des régions ; -	Des évènements artistiques et culturels d’envergure nationale ont été organisés avec l’appui du gouvernement : -	Mamaya (Kankan), 3 éditions (2021, 2022 et 2023) ; -	Kania soly (Kindia), 2 éditions (2023 et 2024) ; Title EN: Laboratory Humour and Human Rights - Humour, a less explored tool to advance human rights - 2023
Goal: Promote Human Rights And Fundamental Freedoms
SDG: SDG 5 - Achieve gender equality and empower all women and girls,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels
Area of Monitoring: Artistic freedom
Cultural Domain: Performing Arts,Media Arts,Cinema and Audiovisual Arts
Agency Implementation: Università degli Studi di Padova - UNESCO Chair Human Rights, Democracy and Peace
Main Feature: The Lab is part of the project The Road Less Traveled, initiated by the Human Rights Center of the University of Padova, and done in cooperation with Global Campus of Human Rights. The project explores how graduates from human rights masters use their knowledge and their skills by taking less usual career paths.   Humor is one of the less explored tools to advance human rights. The aim of the lab was to discuss with a group of interested individuals( human rights advocates/academics/practitioners, comedians, cartoonists,…) how to use more and more efficiently to advance human rights. In particular, this two-day laboratory has the potential of humor as a tool for: Educating about Human rights,Communicating human rights, Advocating for human rights, Building communities centered on human rights.   In preparation for the lab was also organized a webinar where experts shared their experience is using humor to advance human rights
Results: Some of the participants accepted to be interviewed and shared what they learned and some tips on using humor to advance human rights in their different fields of work. One of the participants managed to create and develop a board game on the freedom of movement “Ticket to Safety". Moreover, former participants, part of RED NOSES International, recorded a podcast episode on the theme of humor and human rights, inviting some of their fellow peers.

Title EN: Policies and Measures that Support the Development of the Film Industry
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture
SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Cultural and creative sectors
Agency Implementation: 1. Ministry of Education, Culture, Research, and Technology  2. Ministry of Financ  3. Ministry of Tourism and Creative Economy/Tourism and Creative Economy Agency  4. Ministry of State-owned Enterprises  5. Financial Services Authority
Main Feature: In the past four years, policies and measures that support the development of the film industry include:  1. Law 20 of 2003 on the National Education System (Sistem Pendidikan Nasional) (Law on Sisdiknas);  2. Law 13 of 2003 on Manpower (Law on Manpower);  3. Law 33 of 2009 on Film (Law on Film);  4. Law 6 of 2023 on the Stipulation of Government Regulation in Lieu of Law 2 of 2022 on Job Creation into Law (Law on Job Creation);  5. Draft Law on Amendments to Law 20 of 2003 on the National Education System (Sistem Pendidikan Nasional) (Draft Law on Sisdiknas);  6. Draft Law on Amendments to Law 13 of 2003 on Manpower (Draft Law on Manpower);  7. Draft Law on Amendments to Law 33 of 2009 on Film (Draft Law on Film);  8. Minister of Education and Culture Regulation 30 of 2019 on the Prioritizing Indonesian Films and Prioritizing the Use of Domestic Resources;  9. Financial Services Authority Regulation 57/POJK.04/2020 on Securities Offering through Information Technology-Based Crowdfunding Services;  10. Indonesian Film Agency (Badan Perfilman Indonesia, BPI);  11. Regional Film Commission (Komisi Film Daerah, KFD);  12. Indonesian National Work Competency Standards (Standar Kompetensi Kerja Nasional Indonesia, SKKNI);  13. National Economic Recovery Program (Program Pemulihan Ekonomi Nasional, PEN);  14. Dana Indonesiana;   15. Indonesia Film Financing (IFF);  16. Indonesia Film Facilitation Portal (IFFa);  17. Indonesiana Film;  18. Indonesia Film Content Academy (IFCA);  19. Participation in the ASEAN International Film Festival and Award (AIFFA);  20. Balinale International Film Festival (BIFF); and  21. Indonesia Film Festival (Festival Film Indonesia, FFI).  Several policies and measures reported in the 2020 QPR, namely: (1) Law on Film; (2) Minister of Education and Culture Regulation 30 of 2019 on the Prioritizing Indonesian Films and Prioritizing the Use of Domestic Resources; (3) BPI; (4) KFD; (5) SKKNI (see Goal 1, Policies and Measures for Education and Training Programs in Culture and Creative Economy Sectors); and (6) BIFF, are still valid/ongoing at the time of drafting this report. As additional information, the Minister of Education and Culture Regulation 30 of 2019 has encouraged significant rejuvenation of the SKKNI for film workers in Indonesia. Then, for BIFF, even though it was not held in 2020 due to the COVID-19 pandemic, starting in 2021-2023, it returned to normal.  In the latest developments, BPI has completed: (1) preparation of professional certifications and standardized mechanisms in the film sector (with the Ministry of Manpower and Kemendikbudristek); (2) implementation of FFI (with Kemendikbudristek); (3) Law on Film (with Kemendikbudristek); (4) preparation of the National Film Master Plan (with Kemendikbudristek); (5) organizing the AKATARA Indonesian Film Market & Business Forum (see Goal 1, Policies and Measures that Encourage Job Creation and Entrepreneurship in Culture and Creative Economy Sectors); (6) preparation of Guidelines for the Establishment of a Regional Film Commission (with Kemenparekraf); and (7) research and development.  Furthermore, after pilot efforts in Bandung, Bojonegoro, Siak, Banyuwangi, and Yogyakarta, Kemenparekraf expanded the KFD to three other areas, namely Banda Aceh, Singkawang, and Jayapura. However, due to constraints from several regulations, the only active KFDs left are in Banyuwangi and Yogyakarta, with some new ones in Batam and Jakarta. Now, BPI is trying to continue this program by changing the function of KFD into an association of production service companies.  Meanwhile, the One Stop Bekraf program has been discontinued since 2019 in line with changes in internal policies at Kemenparekraf. Apart from that, the Law on Film, which was previously the primary legislation that specifically regulated the film sector, as reported in the 2020 QPR, has now had several regulations changed with the enactment of the Law on Job Creation (see Goal 1, Policies and Measures that Encourage Job Creation and Entrepreneurship in Culture and Creative Economy Sectors). This law has simplified the licensing flow in the film process through One Single Submission. Previously, film business permits had to be processed at the Ministry of Trade and then at Kemendikbudristek. But now, just one step is enough. Regarding regional levy taxes, the Law on Job Creation gives the Central Government the authority to intervene in the amount of regional levy taxes.   The development of the film industry cannot be separated from the quality of education and training. As explained in Goal 1, Policies and Measures for Education and Training in the Culture and Creative Economy Sectors, the Law on Sisdiknas and the Law on Manpower underlie the education and training sector in Indonesia, including higher education and job training for artists and film activists. As industry and society's demands for the education and training sector develop, stakeholders have identified a real need to update the Law on Sisdiknas and the Law on Manpower, along with updating the Law on Film. Even though the Draft Law on Sisdiknas, Draft Law on Manpower, and Draft Law on Film have been registered with the National Legislation Program, they have not been prioritized for completion in 2024.  In the past four years, several new policies that support the development of the film industry were issued, including the PEN stimulus fund program for the film subsector, specifically aimed at restoring the Indonesian economy in the film subsector. This is mainly due to the closure of cinemas and the reduced number of film productions in 2020-2021. The focus on improving the film subsector was also carried out with the issuance of the Financial Services Authority Regulation 57/POJK.04/2020 on Securities Offerings through Information Technology-Based Crowdfunding Services. This regulation has opened wider opportunities for the public to actively participate in financing Indonesian films through the Securities Crowdfunding (SCF) financial technology platform. SCF can be used as an alternative film industry financing with permission from the OJK. Apart from that, funding for the film industry is also provided through (1) Dana Indonesiana (see Goal 1, Measures that Provide Funds for CSO Capacity Development) and (2) IFF (see Goal 1, Measures that Provide Funds for CSO Capacity Development).  The facilitation needed by the film industry is not only limited to funding. Several new activities are being done to advance the film industry in the digital era, such as creating the IFFa portal. Kemenparekraf, PFN, and Telkom (through its subsidiary Nuon Digital) developed this portal. IFFa makes it easy for film producers to quickly access the desired shooting locations, including shooting permits, creating harmonious collaboration between producers and location owners, and expanding partnerships with stakeholders in this sector. Meanwhile, some examples in education and training include the Indonesiana Film workshop and IFCA activities (see Goal 1, Policies and Measures for Education and Training Programs in Culture and Creative Economy Sectors).  Lastly, several major film festivals have not yet been reported in the 2016 and 2020 QPRs. First, Indonesia's participation in the biennial AIFFA activity, a collaboration among ASEAN countries in the cultural sector to introduce Southeast Asian films to international markets and broader audiences. AIFFA aims to advance ASEAN filmmaking by inspiring and championing the work of screenwriters, filmmakers, and all artists who use the language of film to tell stories. AIFFA also provides a forum for artists, cinematographers, screenwriters, and film professionals to promote collaboration and networking within the ASEAN film industry and from ASEAN to the world. After not being held in 2021 due to the COVID-19 pandemic, AIFFA resumed normally in 2023 in Sarawak, Malaysia.  The second is FFI, which was pioneered by Usmar Ismail and Djamaluddin Malik in 1955 and, since 2014, has been organized by BPI. Even though it has faced various complex problems in its long journey, this festival continues to survive and, in recent years, has become more established and developed. In general, there are three categories assessed, namely: (1) feature films, including 17 awards; (2) non-length feature films, including four awards; and (3) special/other, including five awards. The winners received awards in the form of the "Citra Cup", "Vidia Cup" (Widya) for electronic cinema, "S. Tutur Cup" for film posters, and "Mitra Cup" for film criticism. In the past four years, this festival has taken place every year in Jakarta.  In general, policies and measures that support the development of the film industry are aimed at contributing to achieving the following agenda(s) of the National Strategy for Culture:  1. Provide space for the diversity of cultural expressions and encourage cultural interaction to strengthen the inclusiveness of culture (Agenda 1);  2. Develop and utilize cultural resources to strengthen the position of Indonesia internationally (Agenda 3);  3. Utilize objects of culture advancement to improve people’s welfare (Agenda 4);  4. Institutional reform and culture budgeting to support the culture advancement agenda (Agenda 6); and  5. Strengthen the role of the government as a facilitator of culture advancement (Agenda 7).
Results: SKKNI: There are 15 new SKKNI related to film that have been produced in the 2020-2023 period, namely for (1) film censorship personnel, (2) film directing, (3) film acting, (4) film camera setup; (5) film sound system; (6) film editing; (7) film artistic design; (8) writing film scenarios; (9) film production management; (10) film casting; (11) action choreographer; (12) film lighting; (13) grips; (14) visual effects; and (15) film marketing.  The List of SKKNI related to Culture and Creative Economy per Main Group in the Annexes section provides a complete list with document links.  PEN: A total of 56 recipients of government assistance for Indonesian film production have been selected, representing 23 production houses and 33 film communities consisting of 29 films selected for the short film category and 27 films chosen for the short documentary film category. These films have passed the assessment by a team of curators, where each received stimulus assistance of IDR 250 million per film title.  BIFF: 1.  In 2021, 49 films from 24 countries were screened. 2. In 2022, 63 films from 26 countries were screened. 3. In 2023, 45 films from 13 countries were screened.  Participation in AIFFA:  1. 34 films were screened out of 120 films submitted to the committee during the screening event. Indonesian films included "Before, Now, and Then" by Kamila Andi and "The Woman Crowned With A Crescent Moon (Cinta Bete)" by Roy Lolang.  2. Of the 14 award categories, Indonesia brought three trophies, namely for the film "Before, Now, and Then" in the Special Jury Award category, the film "The Woman Crowned with a Crescent Moon" in the Best Cinematography category, and the Best Actor category for Datuk Ahmad Tarmimi Siregar, a Malaysian actor with Mandailing blood in the Indonesian-Malaysian joint film "Perjalanan Pertama".
Financial Ressources: PEN Film Subsector: Stimulus funds amounting to IDR 136.5 billion. / 8.364,979,35 USD  Dana Indonesiana: See Goal 1, Measures that Provide Funds for CSO Capacity Development.  IFF:  See Goal 1, Measures that Provide Funds for CSO Capacity Development.

Main Feature: Le projet L’ART AU FEMININ a pour objectif général de promouvoir le rôle et la place de la femme dans les corps de métiers artistiques et culturelles. A cet effet il célèbre l’excellence de la femme du secteur des arts et de la culture à travers le Prix des Arts au Féminin (PAF). Cette activité offre une plate-forme de formation et d’expression à la femme en vue de son émancipation et son autonomisation. Les domaines concernés par ce projet sont : le théâtre, la danse, la musique, la mode, les arts visuels, la littérature, la production audiovisuelle et le mécénat. La première édition sera consacrée essentiellement à la célébration des femmes pionnières qui ont tracé les sillons et qui constituent des mémoires collectives dans le domaine des arts et de la culture en Côte d’ivoire. Elles méritent d’être sorties de l’oubli, d’être honorées afin qu’elles soient des modèles pour les jeunes générations. Elle a eu  lieu du 21 au 28 Juin 2024. Les sites proposés sont le Centre d’Action Culturelle d’Abobo (CACAB) et le Palais de la Culture d’Abidjan. Un jury constitué d’experts de haut niveau dans le domaine artistique et culturel a eu  la responsabilité d’identifier ces femmes dans chacune des disciplines précitées. Un comité scientifique composé de praticiens et d’enseignants-chercheurs sera mis sur pied pour élaborer les termes de référence, validé la documentation générale et consigné toutes les productions intellectuelles qui ressortiront de l’exécution du projet.  Les objectifs spécifiques :	 -Honorer les femmes du secteur artistique et culturel de Côte d’Ivoire ; -Former l’échantillon qui interagira avec le projet.  -Inciter de plus en plus de femmes à pratiquer les métiers artistiques et culturels ; -Développer la coopération intellectuelle, artistique et culturelle entre les femmes d’ici et d’ailleurs ; -Créer des opportunités de rencontres et d’échanges ; -Remettre des prix et récompenses aux pionnières identifiées (performance et qualité de travail évaluées). Les activités : -Cérémonie d’ouverture ; -Exposition photos et d’œuvres des femmes pionnières  -Journée scientifique ; -Ateliers de formation maters-class (spécifiques) : -Ateliers de renforcement des capacités (ouverts) ; -Spectacle de distinction et de prestations artistiques.  La cible :  -Les femmes évoluant dans les domaines ou disciplines du projet ; -Les professionnelles et amatrices ; -Les promoteurs et consommateurs de produits artistiques et culturels ; -Les établissements de formation du secteur des arts et de la culture ; -Les partenaires au développement.  Impact et valeur ajoutée : -Existence d’un cadre de promotion et de formation de la femme du secteur artistique et culturel ; -Financement de projets féminins de création artistique ; -Création d’un réseau de chercheurs dans les arts et la culture ; -Les travaux faisant objet de publications ; -Eclosion de jeunes talents artistiques féminins ; -Création d’opportunités pour les femmes artistes.
Results: Les résultats atteints par la mesure sont remarquables. En effet, ce projet constitue une main forte contributrice pour les projets de promotion et d’émancipation du genre féminin. Il a été donc très bien accueilli sur le terrain par les populations ; - ce projet est également une main forte contributrice pour les partenaires au développement humain et durable ; - les partenaires gouvernementaux et publiques se sont engagés dans l’aspect pratique et financier ; - l’impact à long terme le plus pertinent demeure les compétences que ces femmes ont acquises  lors des formations.

Title EN: Law on culture /revised/
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture
SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Cultural and creative sectors
Agency Implementation: Ministry of Culture
Main Feature: The law specifies that the Government should not solely finance the activities of the cultural sector or provide social guarantees. Instead, it advocates for developing the cultural sector as a creative economy, focusing on producing products and services in subsequent stages. The law consists of 16 articles, 26 sections, and 22 clauses that delineate the convention's objectives, principles, scope, as well as the rights and obligations.
Results: The Ministry of Culture is implementing a comprehensive system for managing the cultural field across all 21 provinces and in the capital city, Ulaanbaatar. Since its establishment in 2020, the cultural sector's budget has grown significantly from 180.8 billion MNT to 397.7 billion MNT by 2024, marking a 2.2-fold increase. This allocation now constitutes 0.5% of GDP and 1.4% of state budget expenditures, demonstrating a 1.2-fold increase over the past five years. The operating budget for the cultural sector in 2021 was 115.5 billion MNT, which has risen to 242.8 billion MNT by 2024 through a new budget allocation strategy based on achieved results. This expansion includes financial support for cultural institutions, extending to 421 organisations. These institutions now have opportunities to finance their initiatives based on effective evaluation. In 2023, the budget for the activities of 333 national-level cultural centres was 1.4 billion MNT, with an approved increase to 7.0 billion MNT in 2024. Capital investment expenditure, which amounted to 92.8 billion MNT in 2021, increased to 154.8 billion MNT by 2024. This investment has facilitated the introduction of large-scale cultural productions in the country and the addition of 3.705 million square metres of cultural space, benefiting 1.7 million people in the capital city.

Title EN: Law on the Status of Creative Persons and Professional Creative Organisations
Goal: Promote Human Rights And Fundamental Freedoms
SDG: SDG 5 - Achieve gender equality and empower all women and girls,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels
Area of Monitoring: Artistic freedom
Cultural Domain: Design,Performing Arts,Media Arts,Cinema and Audiovisual Arts,Music,Publishing,Visual Arts
Agency Implementation: Ministry of Culture of the Republic of Latvia, the Council of the Creative Unions of Latvia.
Main Feature: The purpose of this Law is to promote the development and strengthening of professional artistic and scientific creations by determining the status of creative persons and professional creative organisations and the support measures. Section 3 defines that professional creative organisation could be establish and register in a Register of Professional Creative Organisations if it protects the professional and social rights of creative persons. Section 10 also defines that professional creative organisation has right to create social security and benefit funds and disburse to its members the benefits and grants specified in the articles of association. In accordance to the Section 14 of the Law the programme of support measures for creative persons is an aggregate of measures to be carried out in order to provide support to creative persons. The Council of Creative Unions of Latvia helps to implement Programme of Support Measures for Creative Persons by providing consultations for creative persons in order to get apply for support at State Cultural Capital Foundation or to help to obtain the status of a creative person for persons who do not belong to any professional creative organization.
Results: The Law on the Status of Creative Persons and Professional Creative Organisations has come intoforce on 01.01.2018. The Council of Creative Unions of Latvia has been delegated the state administration task of granting the status of a creative person to persons who are not members of any creative professional association.  The following performance indicators were achieved within the framework of the performance of the state administration's task: For example 26.04.2023 – 25.04.2024: 1. Consultations provided to persons who are members of professional creative organizations - 615; 2. Consultations provided to persons who are not members of professional creative organizations - 193; 3. Applications for the status of a creative person were evaluated and administrative acts issued on granting or denying the status of a creative person - 32; 4. Granted creative person statuses – 18; 5. Remote Zoom consultations/seminars – 11; 6. Written consultations – 21; 7. Individual remote video consultations - 23.
Recommandations: The performance of the task of the state administration is ensured in accordance with the law on the status of creative persons and professional creative organizations, and the allocated funding is used in accordance with the purpose provided for in the delegation agreement.

Title EN: le programme de lecture  publique et d’animation culturelle
Goal: Integrate Culture In Sustainable Development Frameworks
SDG: SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: International cooperation for sustainable development
Agency Implementation: Ministère chargé des Arts, de la Culture et du Tourisme
Main Feature: Par Décret du 27 juillet 2011, il a été créé en République Centrafricaine, en application de la Convention de partenariat signée entre l’Organisation Internationale de la Francophonie et la République Centrafricaine, un Réseau de Centres de Lecture et de l’Animation Culturelle, en abrégé (CLAC).  Le Réseau de Centres de Lecture et d’Animation Culturelle constitue un programme de développement de la lecture publique et de l’animation socioculturelle. Le premier réseau est composé de dix centres, essentiellement en milieu rural.  En vue de remplasser et élargir le mandat du réseau sur toute l’étendue du territoire en multipliant les réseaux, un autre Décret °17.314 du 04 Septembre 2017 a été pris pour créer le Centre National de Lécture Publique et d’Animation Culturelle, en abrégé, CENALEPAC. En effet, le CENALEPAC a pour mission principale de mettre en œuvre la politique nationale de lecture publique et d’animation culturelle. A ce titre, il est chargé entre autres de : 	Créer et coordonner les centres culturels publics ; 	Contribuer à la promotion et à la diffusion des œuvres et auteurs nationaux ; 	Développer la coopération avec les ministères techniques concernés par la lecture publique ; 	Identifier appuyer les collectivités locales qui désirent bénéficier des centres de lecture publique ; 	Mettre à disposition les fonds d’ouvrages et le materiels d’animation et de gestion ; 	Appuyer les bibliothèques associatives ; 	Favoriser le désenclavement des communautés, notamment rurales, en y créant des structures d’accès aux livres et aux moyens actuels d’information ; 	Développer les foyers d’échange et de formation, notamment dans les domaines de l’éducations, de la santé, de la promotion sanitaire et du concept genre ; 	Soutenir l’épanouissement et la préservation de la culture locale.  Cette mesure volontaire et incitative vise donc à soutenir les acteurs publics et privés du livre et à favoriser l’accès aux pratiques culturelles autour du livre et de l’audiovisuel et à leur développement. Elle contribue également au renforcement de la presse écrite, à la liberté d’expression ainsi qu’à la diversification des journaux. Elle implique, dans sa mise en œuvre, les collectivités territoriales notamment les communes abritant des CLAC (centres de lecture et d’animation culturelle). Elle se fait sous forme de financement direct et indirect (don de livres et de matériels audiovisuels).
Results: Au vue des difficultés liées aux différentes crises, trois centres sont opérationnels à savoir : Bangui, Damara et Sibut.

Title EN: Lithuanian Council for Culture and Arts
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture
SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Cultural and creative sectors
Cultural Domain: Design,Performing Arts,Media Arts,Cinema and Audiovisual Arts,Music,Publishing,Visual Arts
Agency Implementation: Ministry of Culture of the Republic of Lithuania
Main Feature: The Lithuanian Council for Culture and Art is a group of experts formed by the Ministry of Culture of the Republic of Lithuania with the right of an advisory vote to analyse, evaluate and assist the Minister of Culture of the Republic of Lithuania in the formulation of the cultural policy.  The main task of the Lithuanian Council for Culture and Art is to make proposals to the Minister of Culture on the formulation of cultural policy. In carrying out this task, the Council shall perform the following functions:  -	analyse cultural and artistic processes and the most pressing problems of cultural policy. -	examine the need for laws and other legal acts regulating the field of culture or having an impact on cultural processes, and the improvement of existing legal acts. -	submit proposals on the guidelines for the submission of projects financed by the Press, Radio and Television Support Fund, the activities of the Lithuanian Council for Culture and the Culture Support Fund. -	on the proposal of the Lithuanian Council for Culture, coordinate the description of quotas for the establishment of grants for artists and culture professionals. -	submit proposals on the composition of the Commission for Lithuanian National Culture and Art Prizes, and in cases provided for by legislation, submits proposals on the composition of advisory councils in the field of culture and expert commissions. -	in the cases provided for by legislation, submit proposals on the awarding of prizes to persons meritorious in the field of culture and art. -	delegate candidates to the Joint Expert Group of the Lithuanian Council of Sciences. -	submit proposals for the approval of the composition of the assembly of members of the Lithuanian Council for Culture. -	discuss other cultural policy issues referred to the Council by the Minister of Culture, and others.  The decisions of the Lithuanian Council for Culture and Art are of a recommendatory nature.  The new wording of the Order of the Minister of Culture of the Republic of Lithuania No ĮV-194 of 17 March 2020 has changed the principle of the composition of the Council: The Council is composed of a representative delegated by the Minister of Culture and one representative delegated by each of the Advisory Councils working at the Ministry of Culture in various fields: Lithuanian Design Council, the Council for Cultural Education, the Lithuanian Visual Arts Council, the Lithuanian Library Council, the Lithuanian Film Council, the Council of Museums,  the Council of Professional Performing Arts Institutions, the Lithuanian Council for Architecture, the Lithuanian Council for Digitisation of Cultural Heritage, the Council for Cultural Centres, the Council for Ethnic Culture and Intangible Cultural Heritage, the Council for Archives. In addition, there are representatives from the National Gallery of Art (Chair of the Board) and the Expert Commission for the Protection of the Immovable Cultural Heritage.  The Council also includes representatives from the Youth Council, the Council for the Disabled Persons, the Council of Non-Governmental Organisations, and the Association "College of Cultural Self-Government".
Results: The Council analyses issues related to specific cultural sector and contribute to the formation of cultural policy guidelines.
Financial Ressources: Depending on the amount of the meetings attended, members of the Council are remunerated from the budget of the Ministry of Culture of the Republic of Lithuania.

Main Feature: Under Law N° 19,889 (article 220) promulgated on July 9, 2020, five institutes aimed at promoting the arts and disseminating culture were institutionalized within the orbit of the National Directorate of Culture of the Ministry of Education and Culture, strengthening from the from an institutional point of view, pre-existing areas within the aforementioned state agency. The creation of the National Institute of Music, the National Institute of Letters, the National Institute of Visual Arts was established, as well as the legal status was granted to the already existing National Institute of Performing Arts and the National Institute of Cinema and Audiovisual. Through this institutional framework, the National Directorate of Culture carried out, throughout the four-year period, a wide variety of cultural activities reaching the entire national territory, as well as various public calls aimed at granting financial support to artists and creators, disseminating their works at a national and international level, offer them training proposals and recognize their work through different awards.
Results: 41 public calls were implemented for various purposes in the field of performing arts, music, visual arts, literature and audiovisual. A total of 651 beneficiaries were selected through this mechanism. Likewise, a total of 361 awards were awarded through the calls for the different annual national awards as well as specific prizes that were awarded for a certain year of the four-year period. A total of 30 open windows were implemented: 10 in 2021, 8 in 2022 and 12 in 2023. By institute there were 12 INLET, 7 INMUS, 6 INAE and 5 INAV. 411 projects were selected through this mechanism.
Financial Ressources: The figures correspond to the sum of the budget n the 4 years between 2020 and 2023. (Official quotation of 29 December 2023) Instituto Nacional de Artes Escénicas (INAE): 1.707.868 USD; Instituto Nacional de Música (INMUS): 647.347 USD; Instituto Nacional de Letras (INLET): 400.047 USD; Instituto Nacional de Artes Visuales (INAV): 664.387 USD. Title EN: Living Spaces of the Arts
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture
SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Cultural and creative sectors
Agency Implementation: Ministry of Cultures, Arts, and Knowledge
Main Feature: With the purpose of strengthening the processes of training, creation, research, artistic interpretation, and circulation, the Directorate of Arts of the Ministry of Culture, Arts, and Knowledge has been designing and implementing the adaptation of spaces that have benefited the pedagogical and artistic processes of local schools and art groups.                  Likewise, calls have been generated for the strengthening of already existing spaces, such as the Circus Tents and Theater Rooms. Their positioning as living scenes of art and culture in the territories makes them fundamental places for strengthening the sector from the relationship with the human environments that surround them.                  In the process of developing spaces for artistic practice, the following strategies are worked on.         1. National Program of Concerted Rooms:         This program of the Ministry of Culture, Arts, and Knowledge seeks to strengthen and financially support theater and performing arts venues throughout the national territory, giving them the opportunity to consolidate themselves as outstanding cultural platforms for artistic expression. This program supports the processes and spaces of the country's theater infrastructure, to contribute to the consolidation of democratic cultural citizenship, which promotes the right of citizens to both expression through the performing arts, and access to artistic and theatrical activities in a free and guaranteed manner.         2. Circus tent circulation         For its part, the circus as an artistic spectacle where various circus artists perform to convey different emotions to the public through the exhibition of their skills and abilities. They have an itinerant vocation, moving through different cities, municipalities, townships, and villages, bringing circus shows to the entire population. To this end, they require a large investment of financial and administrative resources that allow them to rent spaces for the installation of the tent and that adapts to the needs of the public and its artists. In this sense, financial resources are provided to support the processes of itinerant circulation of the Colombian circus tents.         3. Law on Public Entertainment of the Performing Arts (Law 1493 of 2011) – LEP in Spanish.         Based on the needs identified in the cultural industries market, as well as strengthening the cultural offer and facilitating the population's access to artistic and cultural activities, the Ministry of Culture, Arts, and Knowledge, defined in 2011 a legislative agenda in which one of its priority projects was the formulation, consensus and issuance of Law 1493 of December 26, 2011.         In this sense, the law seeks the formalization of this sector throughout the country, the promotion of the industry through tax incentives and the generation of resources for the improvement of the infrastructure of the stages for the presentation of live performing arts: music, magic, circus without animals, dance, and theater.         Regarding the formalization and implementation of the Single Portal for Public Performances of the Performing Arts –Pulep in Spanish-, more than 531 performing arts stages have been registered and the Ministry of Cultures, Arts, and Knowledge has authorized 35 companies as online ticketing operators for public performing arts shows as of April 30th.         4. Dance and Movement Centers         Promote a Culture of Peace in the national territory, strengthening dance organizations, through the formation of networks, support for management and cross-sector associativity, expanding the impact of resources and sustainability.         The CDM strategy is configured as a structure made up of CULTURAL NETWORKS AND ASSOCIATIVE PROCESSES that recognizes all agents in the sector and its various forms of organization, where the financial, technical, and systemic support and strengthening of the different agents allows a greater impact for the sector and cultural citizenship in all its dimensions.
Results: • 218 theaters dedicated to the promotion, circulation, creation, training and dissemination of the performing arts, financially supported to nourish artistic programming and audience development.         • 135 circus tents supported with financial resources for their itinerant circulation processes of circus tents         • 30 nodes of Dance and Movement Centers         • 134 stages for the circulation of performing arts built, improved, or adapted thanks to the Public Entertainment Law

Title EN: Library on Wheels" initiative
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture
SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Cultural and creative sectors
Agency Implementation: Abu Dhabi Department of Education and Knowledge
Main Feature: The "Library on Wheels" initiative by the Abu Dhabi Department of Education and Knowledge (ADEK) is a policy measure designed to promote literacy and a love for reading among students by bringing library resources directly to schools and communities. The main features of this initiative include mobile library units equipped with a diverse collection of books, digital resources, and interactive reading activities. These mobile units visit various schools and neighborhoods, making access to educational materials convenient and engaging for students who may not have easy access to traditional libraries.
Results: The results achieved so far through the implementation of the "Library on Wheels" initiative have been promising. The initiative has successfully increased reading engagement among students, with many reports enhanced reading habits and a greater interest in literature. Schools have observed a positive impact on students' reading skills and overall academic performance. Additionally, the initiative has fostered a community spirit around reading, involving parents and community members in the educational journey of children.
Recommandations: The main conclusions from this initiative indicate that mobile libraries highlight the importance of innovative approaches to education that go beyond traditional methods. Recommendations for the future include expanding the fleet of mobile libraries to reach more areas, incorporating more technology-based learning tools to complement physical books, and conducting regular assessments to tailor the book selections to the evolving interests and educational needs of students. Additionally, increasing community involvement through volunteer programs and reading events can further enhance the impact of the initiative.

Agency Implementation: China Writers Association
Main Feature: China Writers Association (CWA), in collaboration with major literary publishing houses and journals, book companies, film and television companies, and online literature platforms, has established a coordination mechanism for the implementation of the Literature Summit Plan for a New Era. The plan aims to facilitate regular recommendations and nominations of high-quality topics by institutional members to CWA and coordinate efforts in literature creation, editing and publishing, promotion and publicity, results transformation as well as Chinese literature translation and promotion overseas so as to foster exceptional literary works.  The sub-program “Sailing Project - Translation and Promotion of Works” in Literature Summit Plan for a New Era aims to establish a comprehensive “going global” mechanism centered around the core elements of “translation, introduction, dissemination, and broadcasting.” It involves the selection of overseas translators, identification of suitable foreign publishers and book fair platforms, and establishment of an overseas social media matrix to form international convergence media promotion channels for Chinese literature.  The sub-program “Literature Picturized Project” aims to recommend literary works with potential for film adaptation and provides a platform for collaboration and incubation purpose.
Results: The Literature Summit Plan for a New Era has reviewed and approved 47 creative projects, among which, 31 literary works have been published. Through the implementation of “Sailing Project - Translation and Promotion of Works”, nearly 60 contracts have been concluded with over 40 overseas publishers, covering almost 30 different languages.

Title EN: Map of flexibilities to copyright in Latin America
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture
SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Partnering with civil society
Cultural Domain: Design,Performing Arts,Media Arts,Cinema and Audiovisual Arts,Music,Publishing,Visual Arts
Agency Implementation: Karisma Foundation
Main Feature: The agenda of exceptions and limitations to copyright has been defended by civil society organizations for several years. In the Colombian case, this political advocacy by the Karisma Foundation has focused on calling for the holding of the Public Hearing contemplated in Article 17 of Law 1915 of 2018, according to which, through the participation of civil society, should periodically establish the necessary modifications and updates to the copyright system and the expansion of its flexibilities in favor of the scientific and cultural development of Colombian citizens. In the context of these efforts and joining forces with Latin American civil society organizations, the Karisma Foundation participated in the preparation of the report on copyright flexibilities in Latin America carried out by the Latin American Civil Society Alliance for Fair Access to Knowledge. In this report, a comparative study was presented in a general way between Latin American copyright legislation and the advance and scope of exceptions and limitations to it in ten (10) Latin American countries. The objective of this study was to analyze the state of the situation of the copyright regulations of each country from the point of view of the balance of rights and, on the other hand, provide a useful tool for educational institutions, as well as for teachers, research teams, library staff         and archives, and for citizens in general, which allows understanding the scope of the national copyright regulations and detect the presence or absence of flexibilities. The report also sought to be useful for people interested in public policies in the region, especially for those who carry out these policies and must analyze and propose adjustments to copyright regulations to keep them updated and in line with the public interest. Additionally, the project carried out by the alliance also developed an interactive web page for consultation on the report that brings the discussion closer to Latin American citizens.
Results: As a result we have a document that will be released in the second half of 2024 that analyzes         the impact that the lack of these flexibilities in the digital environment has for the activities of         libraries, archives, and museums in Colombia. The mapping of flexibilities has served as input to show international organizations such as the World Intellectual Property Organization (WIPO) the need to promote standards that support access to information, knowledge and culture for Latin American citizens. In the Colombian case, the mapping carried out serves as input for the design of copyright policies and legislation that align with the most advanced countries in the region in this matter and also makes it possible to compare exceptions and limitations between the countries of Latin America.

Pour corriger cet état de fait, la compagnie artistique et culturelle Arenk Théâtre de Guinée a entrepris un vaste programme de rassemblement des professionnels du théâtre (femmes et filles).  Dans le but d’éliminer ce climat d’inégalité, les femmes/filles de la compagnie Arenk Théâtre de Guinée ont organisé un atelier dont le thème est « lutte contre l’inégalité basée sur le genre en milieu artistique et culturel » qui a été une opportunité de faire des représentations artistiques à travers une pièce de théâtre intitulée « la scène au féminin ». Les objectifs de cet atelier visent à : -	Favoriser à part égale les opportunités de promotion  et de représentativité des femmes et filles dans le milieu artistique et culturel ; -	Accroître le taux de visibilité des œuvres artistiques et culturelles des femmes et filles dans les évènements (expositions, festivals, etc.) ;  -	Mener des campagnes de sensibilisation pour informer le public et les professionnels sur les enjeux du genre et équité ; -	Encourager la participation et l’implication des femmes aux activités artistiques et culturelles des faitières ; -	Responsabiliser les femmes et filles dans les organes de décision des faitières (OSC culturelles).
Results: De 2020 à 2021, les résultats suivants ont été atteints : -	4 sessions de formation ont été organisées à l’intention de 50 femmes/filles de la compagnie  en leadership ; -	10 campagnes de sensibilisation pour 250 femmes/filles  ont été organisées pour les mobiliser et informer de leur participation aux activités artistiques et culturelles ; -	2 pièces de théâtre entièrement réalisées par des femmes ont été diffusées lors des  journées internationales des droits des femmes ; -	12 femmes/filles de la compagnie ont participé à des évènements artistiques et culturels sur les plans sous régional, régional et international.

Agency Implementation: Мinistry of Culture of the Republic of Belarus  Commissioner for Religious and National Affairs Belarusian Center of National Minorities
Main Feature: In accordance with the Law of the Republic of Belarus On National Minorities (adopted in 1992, latest revision of 2007), all the citizens of the Republic of Belarus, regardless of their nationality, shall enjoy the protection of the State on an equal basis (Article 13). They shall have equal political, economic and social rights and freedoms (Article 6). Representatives of 141 nationalities live in the Republic of Belarus, 213 public organizations and their branches of 27 nationalities function, which, as a rule, carry out activities active cultural and educational activities. In order to provide support and coordination of this activity, organizational and methodological and practical assistance to national cultural and educational associations in the implementation of their statutory activities, the Ministry of Culture issued Order No. 291 of 22 December 1994 establishing the “Republican Center for National Cultures”. The public associations of Azerbaijanis, Armenians, Afghans, Greeks, Georgians, Dagestanis, Jews, Kazakhs, Koreans, Lithuanians, Moldovans, Germans, Palestinians, Poles, Russians, Tatars, Bashkirs, Turkmens, Ukrainians, Gypsies, Chuvashes, Estonians actively, initiative and successfully work with the Center. The Center for National Cultures is the organizer of the Belarusian Festival of National Cultures, which has been held in Grodno every 2 years since 1996 and gathers more than 1000 participants — representatives of about 40 nationalities residing in the Republic of Belarus or invited as guests of the festival. The Center also contributes immensely to the support of the Belarusian diaspora abroad: it organizes trips for Belarusians abroad to their homeland, their creative team performances in Belarus, collaborates with the Belarusian schools and gymnasiums in Lithuania, Latvia, Poland, organizes summer camps and Belarusian language courses for children of Belarusians residing abroad An example of constructive interaction and cooperation of national associations with each other and government bodies, as well as the democratic nature of these relations, is the Consultative Council of National Communities at the Center. The Council at the Center has been operating for more than 20 years. It includes 21 representatives of national national-cultural public associations in Belarus. The form of such self-government speaks about the absence of confrontation between the nationalities living in the republic, gives them the opportunity to form their own public activities, participate in the socio-cultural life of the republic, jointly consider and solve emerging issues. The Commissioner for Religious and National Affairs and his staff is a republican body of state administration that coordinates the activities of state administration bodies of the republic and implements state policy in the sphere of interethnic and interfaith relations in the country. In addition, the Law of the Republic of Belarus "On Belarusians Abroad" assigns a number of tasks to the Commissioner for interaction with compatriots abroad. These areas are the basis of the work of the Commissioner and the staff of his staff.
Results: Increasing the tolerance, integrating national minorities into the Belarusian society, supporting the cultural diversity and promoting intercultural dialogue, educating young people and adults.

SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Partnering with civil society
Cultural Domain: Design,Performing Arts,Media Arts,Cinema and Audiovisual Arts,Music,Publishing,Visual Arts
Agency Implementation: Ministère de la Culture et des Arts
Main Feature: En vertu de la loi n°12-06 du 12 janvier 2012 relative aux associations et dans le cadre de l’aide aux associations culturelle et artistique, le Ministère de la Culture et des Arts consacre annuellement un chapitre n°43-04 intitulé « Mécanisme d’encouragement aux associations à caractère culturel » et géré par la Direction de l’Organisation de la Diffusion du Produit Culturel et Artistique (DODPCA). Il encourage la société civile dans la diffusion et la promotion de l’action culturelle et artistique, notamment le développement et la promotion de la culture locale. Les entités concernées par ce chapitre sont : •	Associations culturelles nationales, •	Associations culturelles locales.	 A l’ouverture de la session au mois de janvier, les associations postulantes sont appelées à présenter leurs programmes culturels annuels accompagnés d’un dossier technique, en plus de l’estimation financière. 	Une commission ministérielle pluridisciplinaire évalue les programmes dépose et statue sur les propositions sous forme de délibération (au mois de mai), les programmes novateurs et diversifiés qui se vouent à la promotion culturelle locale sont les plus encouragés et subventionnés. A l’issue de la réalisation des actions le subventionnées, un bilan moral et physique est obligatoirement déposé auprès des services de la (DODPCA) au Ministère de la Culture et des Arts, auquel sont annexés tous les documents attestant de la réalisation et du financement du programme.
Results: Associations culturelles et artistiques ayant bénéficié des subventions au titre des années 2020/2021/2022/2023 : •	2020 : 64 •	2021 : 100 •	2022 : 101 •	2023 : 130 Soit un total de 395 associations
Recommandations: Promouvoir l’action culturelle et artistique à caractère associatif ; •	Diversifications culturelles et artistiques dans les projets ; •	Redéploiement géographique plus étendu à travers une délocalisation du champ d’intervention de ces associations et festivals vers les régions dites éloignées ; •	Amélioration des prestations et de l’organisation des évènements culturels.

Title EN: Mise en place du Fonds d’Appui au Développement des Médias (FADEM)
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture
SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Media diversity
Cultural Domain: Performing Arts,Cinema and Audiovisual Arts,Music,Publishing,Visual Arts
Agency Implementation: Direction Générale du Fonds d’Appui au Développement des Médias (FADEM)
Main Feature: Dans le but de diversifier les sources d’information de qualité et de favoriser les conditions d’exécution des missions des médias publics et privées, l’Etat guinéen a jugé nécessaire d’apporter une aide financière aux médias afin d’assurer leur bon fonctionnement et de moderniser leurs infrastructures et équipements.  C’est ainsi que l’Etat guinéen a créé par le décret D/2022/0553/PRG/SGG du 24 novembre 2022, le Fonds d’Appui au Développement des Médias (FADEM). Ce décret met en place les organes d’administration et de gestion de l’établissement : le Conseil d’administration, la Direction Générale et l’Agence Comptable. Le Fonds d’Appui au Développement des Médias (FADEM) a pour attributions le financement, le développement et la promotion des médias en République de Guinée. A ce titre, il est particulièrement chargé : -	de mobiliser des fonds pour le financement des projets de développement des médias ; -	d’élaborer et mettre en œuvre le mécanisme d’octroi des subventions de l’Etat aux médias et de veiller à la conformité des projets de développement des médias aux critères d’éligibilité du fonds ; -	de veiller à la bonne exécution des projets financiers et assurer le suivi-évaluation ; -	de soutenir l’amélioration des conditions de vie des acteurs de la presse ; -	de contribuer au renforcement des relations avec les partenaires techniques et financiers ; -	de faciliter l’accès aux emprunts par les entreprises et organes de presse auprès des banques et établissements de microfinance ; -	de participer aux rencontres nationales, sous régionales, régionales et internationales traitant des questions de financement et de développement des médias ; -	de participer à l’élaboration des textes législatifs et règlementaires dans le domaine du financement des projets des médias ; -	de contribuer au financement des activités liées à la formation et à l’équipement des médias et d’en assurer le suivi.  Ainsi, ce fonds permet aux médias de faire la promotion des industries culturelles et créatives à travers le contenu de leurs programmes artistiques et culturelles (contenu local guinéen). Ce fonds n’est pas destiné au fonctionnement des médias publics et privés, mais plutôt au financement d’investissements structurants pour assurer leur viabilité et développement. Le processus de sélection des projets à financer annuellement est piloté par le Comité technique et se déroule comme suit : lancement de l’appel à projets ; réception et étude technique des dossiers ; sélection des projets ; financement des projets ; suivi des projets.
Results: -	Un projet pilote de Formation de 50 journalistes contre les discours violents et de haine a été organisé dans les régions de Kankan, Labé, N’Zérékoré et Conakry, du 5 au 29 octobre 2024 ; -	Un atelier de réflexion sur les contraintes de la presse écrite à l’ère du numérique a été organisé en faveur de 30 journalistes, du 23 au 24 juillet 2024 ; -	la convention collective des acteurs professionnels des médias a été élaborée et validée en collaboration avec le Bureau International du Travail (BIT), 2024 ; -	une formation de 45 journalistes basée sur le genre à Mamou, Kindia et Conakry, 2024 ; -	un siège combiné de la radio rurale de Guinée, du FADEM et de l’AGP a été mis en place en 2024 ; -	une formation de 400 journalistes de la radio rurale de Guinée en matière de gestion, activité environnementale, traitement des sujets sensibles, animation a été réalisée, sur la période 2023-2024.

Title EN: Mécanisme institutionnel d’aide à la diffusion du produit culturel et artistique
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture
SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Cultural and creative sectors
Agency Implementation: Ministère de la Culture et des Arts
Main Feature: Dans le cadre de l’aide aux projets et à la diffusion de l’action culturelle et de son budget de fonctionnement, le Ministère de la Culture et des Arts consacre annuellement un chapitre n°37-04 intitulé « Organisation de manifestations culturelles et cinématographiques », et géré par la Direction de l’Organisation de la Diffusion du Produit Culturel et Artistique (DODPCA). A ce titre, il soutient les festivals et acteurs de la société civile dans la diffusion et la promotion de l’action culturelle et artistique, notamment le développement et la promotion de la culture locale.  Les rubriques concernées par ce chapitre sont : A°- Les grands évènements culturels prévus par le Ministère de la Culture et des Arts : •	les festivals culturels internationaux, •	les festivals culturels nationaux, •	les festivals culturels locaux. B°- Les Acteurs culturels porteurs de projets : •	les associations culturelles (nationales, locales), •	les coopératives artistiques, •	l’action culturelle du Ministère de la Culture et des Arts présentée par les établissements sous-tutelle (CADC, AARC, ONCI, Théâtre national et les Théâtres Régionaux, Opéra, etc.). A l’ouverture de la première session au mois de janvier, les organismes postulants ont été appelés à présenter leurs projets culturels accompagnés d’un dossier technique et d’une estimation financière.  Une commission ministérielle pluridisciplinaire a évalué les projets déposés et statué sur les propositions au moyen de délibérations. Les projets novateurs et diversifiés voués à la promotion de la culture locale sont encouragés et subventionnés.  La deuxième session a eu lieu au mois de septembre. A l’issue de la réalisation des projets, les bilans moral et financier ont été déposés auprès des services de la (DODPCA) du Ministère de la Culture et des Arts, auxquels ont été joints tous les documents attestant de la réalisation et du financement des projets susmentionnés.
