Title EN: Mécanismes en faveur du renforcement des échanges de biens et services culturels :
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture
SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Cultural and creative sectors
Agency Implementation: Le Ministère des affaires culturelles
Main Feature: En tant que département chargé de concevoir et exécuter la politique publique de l’Etat Tunisien en matière culturelle, le ministère des affaires culturelles (MAC) s’est fixé des objectifs clés afin de promouvoir le secteur culturel et créatif. Ces objectifs s’inscrivent dans le cadre des orientations stratégiques nationales pour le développement notamment la vision Tunisie 2035 et le plan de développement 2023-2025 fixant des objectifs alignés sur les objectifs du développement durable (ODD) dont notamment la promotion de la culture nationale dans sa diversité et le développement des produits culturels nationaux porteurs de forte valeur identitaire comme outil de développement durable. Ces orientations stratégiques s’articulent autour des axes suivant : •	Les ICC sont un levier de développement global durable et un catalyseur d’investissement, •	Une infrastructure et un contenu culturel plus développés et attractifs au soutien d’une culture intégrée et solidaire, •	Les domaines artistiques et créatifs sont un élément essentiel pour un modèle de développement basé sur la créativité, l’innovation et la création de la haute valeur ajoutée, •	Les services culturels numériques basés sur les principes de la gouvernance et les bonnes pratiques dans les secteurs culturels,  •	Un cadre juridique qui instaure et favorise un secteur culturel développé et structuré, •	Promouvoir la diplomatie culturelle et le rayonnement de la Tunisie à l’échelle régionale et internationale.  Ainsi, un certain nombre d’incitations financières et fiscales sont mises en place dont notamment : Suppression des autorisations administratives relatives à l’importation des films par décret présidentiel n°2022-317 du 8 avril 2022 modifiant et complétant le décret gouvernemental n°2018-417 du 11 mai 2018 relatif à la publication de la liste exclusive des activités économiques soumises à autorisation et de la liste des autorisations administratives pour la réalisation de projets, les dispositions y afférentes et leur simplification (article 6 et 8). Afin de promouvoir les ICC et de soutenir l’investissement privé dans de domaine culturel et dans le cadre de la loi de l’investissement , les ICC ont été incluses parmi les secteurs prioritaires dans le but de soutenir les initiatives individuelles et celles des OSC pour développer et mettre en place des projets culturels à forte valeur ajoutée et à forte employabilité dans les secteurs artistiques et culturels tout en adoptant le principe de discrimination positive pour les régions les plus défavorisées selon des critères de développement (les régions de l’intérieur et les quartiers populaires) . Les secteurs prioritaires sont les secteurs caractérisés par leur vocation stratégique et leur capacité à augmenter le rythme de la croissance et qui jouissent d’une priorité conformément aux plans de développement.  Les incitations financières sont : •	Une prime de l’augmentation de la valeur ajoutée et de la compétitivité : 15% du cout d’investissement approuvé avec un plafond d’un (01) million de dinars. •	Une prime de développement de la capacité d’employabilité au titre de la prise en charge par l’Etat de la contribution patronale au régime légal de la sécurité sociale au titre des salaires versés aux employés de nationalité tunisienne recrutés pour la première fois et d » une manière permanente pour les trois premières années à partir de la date d » entrée en activité effective. •	Une participation au capital pour les entreprises créées et les investissements d’extension dont le volume de l’investissement ne dépasse pas 15 millions de dinars et ce comme suit : -	Un taux de 60% du capital pour les projets dont le coût est inférieur ou égal à 02 millions de dinars. -	Un taux de 30% du capital pour les projets dont le coût dépasse 02 millions de dinars et inférieur à 15 millions de dinars. •	Décret gouvernemental n°2018-824 du 9 Octobre 2018 fixant la liste des équipements, matériels et articles destinés aux activités culturelles bénéficiant de l’exonération des droits de Douane et de la taxe sur la valeur ajoutée et les procédures d’octroi de ces avantages.  •	La révision des cahiers des charges relatives à la création d’institutions culturelles privées pour qu’ils soient adaptés à la législation en vigueur en matière d’investissement. Entre 2020-2024 le nombre des cahiers des charges octroyées s’élève à 546.

Title EN: Mécanismes institutionnels d’aide à la création artistique, la production culturelle et la diffusion
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture
SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Cultural and creative sectors
Cultural Domain: Design,Performing Arts,Media Arts,Cinema and Audiovisual Arts,Music,Publishing,Visual Arts
Agency Implementation: Ministère de la Culture et des Arts
Main Feature: Le FNDATICPAL (Fonds National pour le Développement de l’Art, de la Technique et de l’Industrie Cinématographique et de la Promotion des Arts et des Lettres) a été clôturé par la Loi de Finance de 2021 (loi n°16-20 du 31 décembre 2021), et deux chapitres ont été affectés au budget de fonctionnement du Ministère de la Culture et des Arts, en remplacement, à savoir :  •	Chapitre n°43-05 intitulé « Aide de l’Etat à la promotion des arts et des lettres, à l’édition du livre et au cinéma »,  •	Chapitre n°44-33 intitulé « Contribution au profit du Centre Algérien du Développement du Cinéma dans le cadre de l’aide de l’Etat au développement de l’industrie cinématographique ».  Deux commissions souveraines composées de compétences culturelles et artistiques nationales, nommées par la Ministre de la Culture et des Arts, sont chargées, chacune en ce qui la concerne, de l’examen des dossiers de demandes d’aide l’une pour les projets cinématographique, l’autre pour les projets littéraires et artistiques. Les catégories bénéficiaires des deux (02) chapitres sont les artistes, les auteurs, les producteurs, les éditeurs ainsi que toutes les entités morales œuvrant dans le domaine de la création et de la production artistique, littéraire et cinématographique.  Les deux (02) chapitres visent respectivement à soutenir la production artistique dans les domaines des arts et des lettres, et les projets cinématographiques (longs et courts-métrages, fictions ou documentaires et films d’animation) ainsi que des projets qui répondent aux normes de création. Les principaux domaines d’intervention des deux chapitres sont : •	l’écriture littéraire, la traduction de et vers la langue nationale, l’édition, l’impression et la promotion d’œuvres littéraires, ouvrages et travaux de recherche dans les domaines des arts et des lettres, sur tous supports existants ou à venir, •	l’édition, l’impression et la promotion de publications périodiques spécialisées dans les domaines littéraires et artistiques,  •	la publication d’ouvrages destinés à la jeunesse et de bandes dessinées sur tous supports existants ou à venir, •	la participation à des ateliers et résidences dans tous les genres littéraires en Algérie et à l’étranger, •	l’organisation d’hommages et de commémorations aux personnalités et aux évènements littéraires, ainsi que de prix et concours dans le domaine des arts, •	l’écriture, la production, la distribution, la diffusion et la promotion de pièces de théâtre et de spectacles artistiques, •	l’enregistrement, la production, la distribution, la diffusion et la promotion d’œuvres, de création ou de patrimoine musical et lyrique et de clips musicaux sur supports sonores et visuels,  •	la production, la distribution, la diffusion et la promotion d’œuvres chorégraphiques,  •	la réalisation de projets regroupant plusieurs domaines artistiques, de prototypes dans le domaine du design et de création plastique, •	l’organisation et la promotion d’expositions d’œuvres artistiques et l’acquisition de matériel servant à leur réalisation, •	l’édition et l’impression de catalogues d’expositions et d’évènements artistiques, •	la mise en œuvre et le développement d’un projet artistique, d’un concept ou d’un travail de recherche servant un projet d’art visuel. •	l’aide au financement de la production, de la coproduction et de la postproduction,  •	l’acquisition de droits de distribution et d’exploitation de films en Algérie et à l’étranger,  •	l’aide à l’écriture et à la réécriture de scénario de films, •	la distribution, l’exploitation et la promotion d’œuvres cinématographiques,  •	la préservation du patrimoine filmique par la numérisation et/ou le tirage de copies,  •	l’organisation d’ateliers et de résidences de formation dans tous les métiers du cinéma,  •	l’acquisition d’équipement,  •	la réalisation, la réfection, l’amélioration d’infrastructures cinématographiques, la modernisation des équipements des structures cinématographiques et des techniques du cinéma non prévues dans le budget « équipement ».  Au titre de ces dotations, les établissements culturels et autres entités morales peuvent également en bénéficier dans le cadre de leurs activités.

Title EN: Media and Publishing Forums in Belarus
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture
SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Media diversity
Agency Implementation: Ministry of Information of the Republic of Belarus
Main Feature: A number of media and publishing forums are held annually in Belarus. They contribute to the promotion of various media, their evaluation, and the broader participation of civil society in the discussion of the role and importance of modern media for society in the Republic of Belarus. These forums include: - Forum of the media community of Belarus - Belarusian international media forum "Partnership for the Future" - Forum of young journalists - Minsk international book exhibition and fair. The recent Forum of the media community of Belarus was organized in May, 2024. The participants of the media forum were heads and employees of mass media, bloggers and experts, representatives of specialized universities and ideological activists, press secretaries of republican government bodies, organizations, as well as representatives of government agencies supervising information policy issues. The program of the event was planned to be intense: speeches by heads and representatives of republican and regional media, work of experts in the field of communications, discussion of current issues in the industry, exchange of opinions. A bright and memorable final accent was the award ceremony for the winners and laureates of the XX National Competition "Golden Letter". The Ministry of Information annually holds the Belarusian Information Forum, which is an important event in the socio-political life of the country, aimed at solving the problems of state information policy. The main goal of the event is to concentrate the efforts of the international journalistic community in developing a positive view of the Belarusian reality, to include leading journalists from the post-Soviet space and far abroad in covering the processes of sustainable development of the country and to increase the public interest of foreign countries in the Republic of Belarus, to establish Belarus as a sovereign state pursuing an open and honest policy, defending the principles of good neighborliness, peace and mutual understanding, to focus the attention of the world community on the issues of preserving historical memory, to consolidate the expert and media community in confronting modern challenges and threats. The 10th Forum of Young Journalists “Journalism Today: Territory of Responsibility” was held in Minsk on December 15, 2024. More than 200 young journalists from state republican and regional media took part in the Forum. On March 14–17, 2024, the 21st Minsk International Book Fair was held in Minsk. The central themes of the fair were the 80th anniversary of the liberation of Belarus from the Nazi invaders, 30 years since the first presidential elections in the history of sovereign Belarus, the 30th anniversary of the adoption of the Constitution of the Republic of Belarus, the Year of Quality declared in the Republic of Belarus in 2024, and anniversaries of classics of Belarusian literature. The exhibition featured 452 exhibitors from 21 countries. Over the four days of its work, the exhibition was visited by a record number of people – more than 62 thousand people. A special place in the country’s annual calendar of events is occupied by the Day of Belarusian Literature – a holiday dedicated to national culture, literature and the printed word. Traditionally, it is held in the historical centers of culture, science, 16 of 55 literature, and printing. The main idea of the holiday is to preserve and develop the spiritual heritage of Belarus, promote national cultural traditions, show their ties with the Slavic origins and modern times. The program includes an international roundtable discussion held with the participation of foreign writers, the Republican contest of young readers ‘Zhivaya Klassika /Living Classic’, a scientific and practical conference devoted to the history of the city – the holiday's capital entertaining quizzes, quests, and the Book and Press Festival
Results: presentation of the national media and publishing achievements;  • establishment of the discussion platform and involvement of youth and the broad public in the process of discussion of the national media and publishing strategy.
Financial Ressources: The data are not available
Recommandations: The Forums contribute to the cooperation between the government and various mass media

Title EN: Media Development and Diversity Agency (MDDA)
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture
SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Media diversity
Agency Implementation: Media Development and Diversity Agency
Main Feature: The MDDA, is a statutory development agency for promoting and ensuring media development and diversity, set up as a partnership between the South African Government and major print and broadcasting companies to assist in (amongst others) developing community and small commercial media in South Africa. It was established in 2003, in terms of the MDDA Act No. 14 of 2002 and started providing grant funding to projects on 29 January 2004. The agency’s mandate is encapsulated in Section 3 of the MDDA Act of 2002, from Section 16 and 32 of the Constitution Act No. 108 of 1996, thereby providing for freedom of expression and access to information. The MDDA facilitates the growth of the community broadcast, print and digital sectors in several ways, the biggest part of its mandate is to encourage the ownership, control, and access to media by historically disadvantaged communities as well as by the historically diminished Indigenous language and cultural groups. The agency assists with training broadcasters, publishers, and journalists and by speaking out on behalf of community media and its importance to this country. The Media Development and Diversity Agency (MDDA)’s mandate is to: •	Create an enabling environment for media development and diversity that reflects the needs and aspirations of all South Africans. •	 Redress exclusion and marginalisation of disadvantaged communities and persons from access to the media and the media industry. •	Promote media development and diversity by providing support primarily to CSCM projects. •	Encourage ownership and control of, and access to, media by historically disadvantaged communities as well as by historically diminished indigenous languages and cultural groups. •	Encourage the development of human resources and training, and capacity building, within the media industry, especially among historically disadvantaged groups. •	Encourage the channeling of resources to the community media and small commercial media sectors. •	Raise public awareness regarding media development and diversity issues.  The key concepts in the agency’s mandate that makes up its name are defined in the Act as follows: •	Media – means all forms of mass communication, including print, publications, radio, television and new electronic platforms for delivering content. •	Development – means the development of media and infrastructure so that historically disadvantaged communities and persons have access to media as owners, managers, producers, and consumers of media. •	Diversity – regarding media, means access to the widest range of sources    and information, as well as equitable representation within the media in general. •	Agency – media development and diversity agency established by section 2 of the Act.
Results: The agency provides grant funding support, research and training, as well as media education to local community operators and the public at large. By supporting the establishment and development of community and small commercial media, both through funding and capacity building support, the agency ensures that there is sufficient dissemination of credible news to South African communities, taking indigenous languages into consideration to accommodate scores of audiences served. In the 2021/22 fiscal year, the Presidency worked with the agency to launch 12 brand new state-of the-art digital studios in community radio stations across all the nine provinces of South Africa. This new technology helps to elevate the quality of broadcasting and open up the airwaves for these sometimes-remote radio stations. This has led to the increase of community radio listenership. According to Radio Info Africa Community radio listenership in South Africa garners roughly 8 million people.  Since its inception the agency has funded a total number of 586 community media projects. This number includes 321 community broadcast projects in the form of community radio and community TV stations, and 185 community print projects in the form of community newspapers, community magazines and small commercial print projects.  To mark this significant milestone, celebrations were held through a variety of events. These celebrations highlighted the importance of quality ethical journalism, community media sustainability, the advancement of social-cohesion and human rights by community media; and different critical media-related topics and issues. Monthly events were hosted by the Agency from June to November 2023 under the theme of “Democracy & Diversity: Celebrating 20 Years of Access to Information and Media Freedom through community media” and targeting different parts/ stakeholders of the community and small commercial media sector.  In January 2023, the MDDA Board approved the final report of the Community and Small-Commercial Media Sustainability Model research. The main objective of the sustainability research was to develop a South African Sustainability Model for the CSCM sector which categorises the sector according to their ability to self-sustain, partially sustain; and the inability to self-sustain to allow for focused, responsive and proactive support. The findings of this research will significantly influence how the Agency advocates for the sector and the implementation of the MDDA funding strategy going forward.

Title EN: Member States’ expert group on the governance of EU's International Cultural Relations
Goal: Integrate Culture In Sustainable Development Frameworks
SDG: SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: International cooperation for sustainable development
Cultural Domain: Design,Performing Arts,Media Arts,Cinema and Audiovisual Arts,Music,Publishing,Visual Arts
Agency Implementation: The European Commission (DG Education, Culture, Youth and Sport) and EU Member States
Main Feature: The EU Work Plan for Culture 2023-2026, under priority D ‘Culture for co-creative partnerships: strengthening the cultural dimension of EU external relations’, provides for the creation of a short-term group of Member States’ experts focusing on the governance of the EU strategic approach to international cultural relations (ICR). The group started its activities mid-2023 and is expected to issue its recommendations by end 2024.   The group focuses on the governance of the EU strategic approach to ICR by outlining possible ways for improving working structures and methods, including approaches for cultural heritage in conflicts and crises and culture in development cooperation. Its proposals should allow for the effective bridging of gaps between administrations responsible for foreign affairs, cultural affairs and development cooperation policies. The aim of these improved working structures and methods should be to:  i) Strengthen cross-sectoral cooperation and synergies between activities undertaken by the EU and its Member States with non-EU countries, including with UNESCO and the Council of Europe;  ii) Promote coherent, well structured, prepared and implemented EU policies relating to ICR, based on grass-roots level cooperation and a co-creative partnership logic;  iii) Foster the capacity of the EU and its Member States to actively contribute in a collaborative way to relevant culture-related multilateral policy processes, in particular as regards the 2030 Agenda and the sustainable development agenda beyond 2030.
Results: The final report from the group is expected by end-2024. It will compile recommendations for a cross-cutting, inclusive and more effective policy approach, including proposals for improved working structures and methods.

Title EN: Mercosul Audiovisual Platform
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture
SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Digital environment
Agency Implementation: Audiovisual Secretariat of the Ministry of Culture
Main Feature: Launched in March 2023, the Mercosul Audiovisual Platform was created by the Specialized Meeting of Mercosul Cinematographic and Audiovisual Authorities (RECAM), which includes Argentina, Brazil, Paraguay and Uruguay. The Platform aims to expand the viewing windows for regional short film audiovisual production, as well as access possibilities for all audiences. With the intention of reaching a more diverse audience, the platform has a special interest in improving audiovisual accessibility conditions for blind and deaf people, as provided for in the agency's Work Program. From the beginning, the platform was developed seeking to provide viewing tools for works that have accessibility features (sign language, descriptive subtitles and/or audio description). To achieve this, we received advice from blind and deaf people who are experts in audiovisual accessibility. Furthermore, with the aim of promoting the circulation of regional cinema in general, the platform also makes room for works that do not have audiovisual accessibility resources. An indication of available resources can be found on each film page.
Results: Two cycles of public calls for works to be made available on the Mercosul Audiovisual Platform have already been published, resulting in two exhibition cycles. The cycle of short films for children resulted in the availability of 12 films covering different themes, territories and languages of Mercosur, contributing to the construction of the region's own imaginaries. The short film cycle “Territories in Transformation” explores the relationship between places, people and cultures. It offers four short films that invite us to reflect on how spaces and homes are fundamental elements in the constant evolution of our lives and environments. A special highlight of the Mercosul Audiovisual Platform is the presentation of the Paraguayan animated short “They are not alone”, by Mathias Maciel, which has, as a landmark in the region, audio description and subtitles for the deaf in Spanish, Portuguese and Guarani. The piece was produced in Encarnación in honor of indigenous artists who seek to raise awareness in society about caring for the Earth.

Title EN: Mera Gaon Meri Dharohar
Goal: Integrate Culture In Sustainable Development Frameworks
SDG: SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: National sustainable development policies and plans
Agency Implementation: Indira Gandhi National Centre for the Arts (IGNCA)
Main Feature: Mera Gaon Meri Dharohar  (MGMD) project, part of the National Mission on Cultural Mapping (NMCM) and undertaken during the Azadi Ka Amrit Mahotsav, aims to map 6.5 lakh villages across India, documenting their geographical, and demographic profiles, and cultural assets. This extensive cultural mapping includes recording oral histories, belief systems, traditional knowledge, customs, festivals, rituals, local religious practices, and various art forms such as folk songs, dances, tales, and handicrafts. Each village is categorized under specific themes like Arts and Crafts Village, Ecologically Oriented Village, Scholastic Village, Historical Village, Architectural Heritage Village, and Epic Village, among others. The project also includes the establishment of the National Cultural Work Place (NCWP), an online platform for cultural service providers. This platform allows artists to register and showcase their work, provides unique identification codes for artists, links to government welfare schemes, and offers facilities for uploading and editing village data, performances, and exhibitions. Other features include a virtual living museum, a village travel passport, and digital badges for online village travel. The MGMD project is designed to preserve, safeguard, and disseminate India & rich cultural heritage, creating a national database through extensive surveys and documentation, while promoting cultural vibrancy and self-reliance in rural economies through digital platforms and outreach activities.
Results: Since its implementation, the "Mera Gaon Meri Dharohar project has successfully initiated the mapping of numerous villages, bringing to light the rich cultural tapestry of rural India. The project & engagement with local communities has fostered a deeper understanding and appreciation of their cultural heritage, while also providing a platform for artists and cultural practitioners to showcase their talents and gain recognition. This initiative has also facilitated the integration of culture and tourism, enhancing the visibility of these villages and promoting cultural tourism. Through the NCWP, artists have gained access to various government welfare schemes and unique identification codes, ensuring better support and recognition for their work. The Project and its efforts in documenting and preserving traditional knowledge and art forms have contributed significantly to the revitalization of rural economies, promoting self-reliance and sustainability. The creation of a virtual living museum and other digital tools has further amplified the reach and impact of these cultural initiatives, making the rich heritage of Indian villages accessible to a global audience and setting a strong foundation for future cultural mapping and preservation efforts.

Title EN: Mercado de Industrias Culturales del Sur - MICSUR
Goal: Achieve A Balanced Flow Of Cultural Goods And Services And Increase The Mobility Of Artists And Cultural Professionals
SDG: SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 10 - Reduce inequality within and among countries,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Flow of cultural goods and services
Cultural Domain: Design,Performing Arts,Media Arts,Cinema and Audiovisual Arts,Music,Publishing,Visual Arts
Agency Implementation: Secretariat of Culture
Main Feature: As part of the initiatives for the promotion and internationalization of Argentina's cultural and creative industries, the Secretariat of Culture of the Nation participated in the IV Edition of the Market of Cultural Industries of the South (MICSUR) held in the city of Santiago de Chile, from April 17 to 20, 2024. Comprised of 9 South American countries (Argentina, Brazil, Bolivia, Chile, Colombia, Ecuador, Uruguay, Peru and Paraguay), MICSUR aims to consolidate a platform for the knowledge, dissemination, promotion, circulation and commercialization of goods and services generated by small and medium-sized enterprises entrepreneurs in the cultural and creative industries, as well as to strengthen existing regional ties that link the cultural ecosystem throughout South America. MICSUR is understood as a space for the commercialization and exchange of cultural products and services from South America, where business roundtables are held, stands are set up, showcases, parades and seminars are held aimed at the commercial integration of South American nations. In addition, in its trade fair dimension it counts on the participation of delegations of buyers and sellers of the sector, including extra-regional buyers. The first meeting was held in 2014 in the Argentine city of Mar del Plata and presented a challenge and an unprecedented experience for the countries of the region. Given the success of that first meeting, it was decided to give continuity to the meeting, consolidating it as a State policy of the countries of the expanded MERCOSUR. MICSUR is currently part of the work program of the MERCOSUR Cultural Arts and Cultural and Creative Industries Commission (CAICC). MICSUR has three previous editions: Mar del Plata (2014), Bogota (2016) and Sao Paulo (2018). The Argentine Delegation that participated in MICSUR Chile 2024 was made up of cultural companies characterized by their commercial experience and capacity to invest in their own logistics expenses.  These projects have a strong presence in international markets and have a profile in the MICA Platform, and have been part of business rounds in the Cultural Industries Market of Argentina (MICA) and the Cultural Industries Market of Brazil (MICBR) in their 2023 editions. The delegation had a commercial agenda prepared in collaboration with the National Directorate for the Promotion of Tourism, Sports, Cultural Industries and Knowledge-Based Services (DNTEC) and the Argentine Investment and International Trade Agency of the Argentine Foreign Ministry. In addition to the commercial and institutional delegation, Argentina participated in the showcase spaces, with a guaranteed place for a representative project from each participating area: music, fashion and performing arts. As part of the preparations for the participation of the Argentine Delegation, the National Directorate of Federal Integration and International Cooperation launched a series of training courses on the internationalization of cultural goods and services and participation in business rounds. These tools were very useful to strengthen the experience of Argentine cultural enterprises in the various activities carried out at MICSUR. Among them we can mention: Pitching training for business rounds in MICA Platform; How to internationalize my business in the cultural industries sector.
Results: Argentina's participation in each edition of MICSUR has varied according to the country's context and cultural policy objectives. Mar del Plata (2014): Argentina organizing country, more than 300 entrepreneurs participated. Bogota (2016): 60 entrepreneurs. São Paulo (2018): 67 entrepreneurs. Santiago de Chile (2024): 9 entrepreneurs.
Recommandations: Over the years, MICSUR has become a regional public policy recognized as a platform for opening commercial opportunities and consolidating ties with business and institutional entities of the MERCOSUR countries in a market in continuous expansion. Based on this recognition, the Meeting of MERCOSUR Ministers of Culture has ensured the continuity of the initiative with the designation of Asunción, Paraguay and Quito, Ecuador, as venues in 2026 and 2028 respectively.

Title EN: Midundo Online Radio Programming
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture
SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Digital environment
Agency Implementation: Culture and Development East Africa (CDEA)
Main Feature: Midundo Radio is an innovative online platform dedicated to showcasing the talents and creativity of East African artists and innovators. Unlike traditional radio stations, Midundo Radio operates exclusively online, leveraging digital technologies to reach a global audience. Through its digital media content, Midundo Radio aims to amplify the voices and talents of both upcoming and A-list  East African creatives, providing them with a platform to share their work with the world. One of the key features of Midundo Radio is its focus on creating an online marketplace for creative content producers. By curating and showcasing a diverse range of programmes, including Utamaduni Express; an edutainment social justice programme aimed at providing information on cultural matters ,Haki za Msanii; programme that highlights the rights and duties of all stakeholders in the art sector, Mpiga Debe; a vox pop programme aimed at highlighting the connection of art and climate change and lastly Binti Longa :a programme curated to engage in matters of Women and the girl child. Midundo Radio represents a dynamic and forward-thinking initiative that harnesses the power of digital media to promote and support East African creativity. By providing a platform for artists and innovators to showcase their work and connect with stakeholders.
Results: Through Midundo Radio's initiatives, significant achievements have been realized in empowering East African artists and fostering creative collaboration. By using the online platform, the radio has facilitated broader access to diverse programming, allowing artists to reach a bigger audience and expand their fan base. This increased visibility has led to enhanced recognition and opportunities for artists to showcase their work on an international scale, potentially resulting in collaborations and partnerships with artists and industry professionals. Additionally, Midundo Radio's programs, such as the Binti Longa program and the Haki za Msanii program, have shown tangible outcomes. The Gender Forum initiated by the Binti Longa program has provided a space for discussions and initiatives focused on gender equality and women's empowerment within the creative industry. This forum has contributed to increased awareness and advocacy for gender issues, fostering a more inclusive and equitable environment for artists of all genders.  Furthermore, the Haki za Msanii program's creative hook-ups have offered artists valuable training on their rights, branding, and other relevant topics. These sessions have equipped artists with the knowledge and skills necessary to navigate the industry effectively, assert their rights, and build sustainable careers. As a result, artists have experienced improved professional development opportunities, increased confidence in their work, and enhanced networking prospects, ultimately leading to greater success and impact within the East African creative community and beyond.

SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Partnering with civil society
Cultural Domain: Performing Arts,Media Arts,Cinema and Audiovisual Arts,Music
Agency Implementation: Ministry of Culture and its dependencies
Main Feature: The policy consists on the standardizing of the mechanism for temporary use of cultural spaces, including theatres, cultural centers and open spaces, through the implementation of the protocol (which did not exist prior to 2024). The objective of this protocol is to regulate the use of infrastructure and cultural spaces under the stewardship of the Ministry of Culture and its dependencies as a measure for efficiency, control, transparency and security. The protocol includes temporary and permanente spaces for cultural events such as fairs, congresses festivals, and other events where it is applicable due to their cultural nature. The protocol does not apply to museum spaces within their institutional and missional role, such as in temporary or permanent exhibitions; or to infrastructure or spaces formally on loan for a period over 30 days. There is also a public rate table for the use of this cultural service, and currently the Ministry is working on the automatization of the service through the institution’s service portal: https://cultura.gob.do/index.php/servicios
Results: The policy was issued on April of 2024, so results will be available from 2025 onwards. But the standardization of services fulfils governmental strategies included in the Government Plan for the period 2020-2024.

Title EN: Mimeta Cultural Development program
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture
SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Partnering with civil society
Agency Implementation: Mimeta
Main Feature: Mimeta is a recognised international player in the field of artistic rights, serving as a development partner, contributor to policy dialogues, and a member of the donor community engaged in this sector. Since its inception in 2008, Mimeta has played an important role in supporting infrastructure organisations (NGOs in the cultural sector) advocating for artists and cultural actors within civil society. This network of organisations now serves as the platform for cultural, developmental, and cultural-political/activist collaboration in the countries concerned. They also play a central role in the international discourse on artistic rights, as representatives of the global south. Supporting the establishment of such organisational structures has been Mimeta's strategic focus since its inception. Mimeta’s program for cultural development focuses on strengthening the idea of artistic rights and artistic freedom, primarily in the Middle East and Sub-Saharan Africa. Mimeta’s vision for cultural development is dependant on local ownership of the issue and context-sensitive solutions, which is why Mimeta’s local partnerships are fundamental to its work.  The vision of Mimeta is to GIVE PEOPLE THEIR RIGHT TO FREE CREATIVE EXPRESSIONS, created on free terms and presented by independent institutions. The mission is to support and protect those who want to enhance a culture by aesthetic or intellectual means. Both vision and mission highlight the impact arts and creativity have on developing open societies, including the culture itself. The long-term impact is to provide free artistic practice to individuals. To achieve the intended impact, Mimeta focuses on outcomes that ensure protection for artists, storytellers, producers, and their works against abuse, censorship, legal or social persecution, and outcomes that increase accessibility for people to participate in artistic practice. These two outcomes constitute Universal Artistic Rights (ref. art 27 of the Universal Declaration of Human Rights) Mimeta’s Human Rights Approach is founded on three human rights, Freedom of Assembly, Freedom of Association and Freedom of Expression are all interlinked in the work with artistic freedom and artists' rights. On the strategic level, Mimeta is achieving results by supporting organisations and individuals who work on behalf of the arts and media, to improve the sectors´ position on rights issues, in political and legal matters, professionalism and skills, the distribution of the free expression and - in the end - the sustainability of the sector. Thus, Mimeta works with partners that address these issues on behalf of their sectors. At the same time, we see that changes cannot be achieved unless the need for change is understood, embraced, and advocated for by a community wider than the practitioners themselves, turning the stories into a widely adopted narrative for change. Storytelling is in this context also a tool for change. In this way, we work both for the universal rights that belong to the practitioners, and we see their free storytelling as a prerequisite for making change in societies. Mimeta is particularly concerned with building capacity for the partners, contributing to the growth of strong and meaningful local institutions while remaining aware of the local context. The value of developing strong local partners is immeasurable. Mimeta’s vision and goals of long-lasting effects are dependent on local ownership and knowledge. The capacity building includes reporting and knowledge building, which in turn drives learning and innovation. These concepts, coupled with Mimeta’s experience and expertise in fund management and impact management position Mimeta uniquely in the sector. Mimeta operates with a commitment to compliance, pro-activity, and an orientation towards continual learning. Our approach is characterised by a reputation for being knowledgeable and systematic doers, allowing us to navigate complex landscapes with effectiveness and impact for the constituencies we serve. These are our values.
Results: The implementation of Mimeta’s mission and program in this last QPR period was strongly aligned with goal 1 – Support Sustainable Systems of Governance for Culture. Through its partnerships, Mimeta seeks to strengthen cultural infrastructure and cultural ecosystems. This has resulted in a plethora of activities, including information and awareness-raising activities, such as conferences and capacity building and training for artists and cultural professionals. This vision to develop the cultural sector and contribute to a diverse cultural expression manifests differently in Mimeta’s partner organisations. One example is Ettijahat, a civil society cultural organisation based in Lebanon and Belgium, working to promote independent culture across the Arab world, with some emphasis on Syrian culture both in Syria and Syrians in exile. Ettijahat work includes a specific program, Life, which supports smaller creative enterprises. The organisations targeted by the Life Initiative and their beneficiaries play a vital role in the Syrian arts and culture sector and contribute to the establishment of a diverse, inclusive, and robust civil society both in the region and in the diaspora. Given the near-total lack of freedom of expression in Syria and the restrictions Syrians face across the Arab region and elsewhere, this initiative is rare and enables cultural practitioners to exercise their rights to free expression. Many of Mimeta’s partners create spaces for artistic and media activities which promote the diversity of cultural expressions. One example would be L'Art Rue, which is a Tunisian cultural non-profit organisation which hosts a large bi-annual cultural festival called Dream City. L'Art Rue seeks to put the artists and their creative work at the heart of a larger civic project and the democratic transition process of Tunisia. L'Art Rue’s stated mission is to innovate through arts, culture, education, and cross-sectoral collaboration for social change and a more equal and open society. Dream City has become a cultural arena which presents a diverse cultural expression to its audience, emphasising the often neglected voices in society. Mimeta’s partners in this QPR period have also included organisations focused on media and media freedom. One example relevant to goal 1 is Febrayer, a media network based in Berlin which works in and for media outlets in the Arab region and the Arab communities in the diaspora. Febrayer is able to provide capacity-building activities for its member organisations and cultural professionals. This includes providing organisations with technological labs and other forms of support that is needed by its members: social media lab, business lab and educational structures for journalists from Arabic-speaking countries. The abovementioned examples highlight how Mimeta supports initiatives with activities which promote the diversity of cultural expressions, in media and the culture and creative sectors. Mimeta has seen cultural development as contributing to the cultural ecosystem at multiple levels to bring effective and sustainable change towards a stronger cultural ecosystem, be it at an individual, organisational or sector level.

Title EN: Minority Language Broadcasting
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture
SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Media diversity
Agency Implementation: BBC, S4C, MG ALBA, Ofcom, Northern Ireland Screen
Main Feature: Legislative framework - The Media Act 2024 requires that PSBs must collectively contribute towards minority language broadcasting as part of the remit and will be held accountable for their delivery by the independent regulator, Ofcom.
Results: S4C - S4C is the UK’s only dedicated Welsh language broadcaster. Since 1982, it has delivered news, stories and programming. S4C is also committed to making the Welsh language accessible to everyone. Since 2022, S4C has been wholly funded through the BBC licence fee. S4C offers the opportunity for all ages to hear and enjoy the Welsh language, but they are committed to attracting younger audiences to encourage interest in Welsh from an early age.     BBC - The BBC is a British Public Service Broadcaster (PSB), founded in 1922. The BBC’s Royal Charter, which sets out the BBC’s responsibilities, contains a duty to regional and minority languages within the BBC’s general duties, with a further set of responsibilities provided in the Framework Agreement. This sets out the expectation that the BBC must support the provision of output in the Welsh language in Wales, the Gaelic language in Scotland and the Irish language and Ulster Scots in Northern Ireland, on television, radio and online.    MG ALBA - Through its partnership with the BBC to form BBC ALBA, MG ALBA has been delivering Gaelic language content for audiences since the channel’s launch in 2008. In addition to providing content designed to inform and entertain those already fluent in the Gaelic language, MG ALBA is committed to supporting all levels of Gaelic learners to gain confidence in speaking Gaelic.    There is an obligation in the BBC’s Framework Agreement which states that the BBC, in partnership with MG ALBA, must continue to provide a television service supporting MG Alba’s function of securing that a wide and diverse range of high-quality programmes in Gaelic are broadcast or otherwise transmitted so as to be available to persons in Scotland.    Support for Irish language and Ulster Scots - The Irish Language Broadcast Fund and Ulster Scots Broadcast Fund provide high quality content for audiences in Northern Ireland, and to support Northern Ireland’s independent production sector. Funding for the Northern Ireland digital terrestrial television multiplex that has carried RTÉ and TG4 services to Northern Ireland since 2012 supports cross-border broadcasting on the island of Ireland.
Recommandations: An independent review of S4C was published in 2018, Building an S4C for the Future. It made a number of recommendations to ensure the broadcaster can adapt to technological and market changes, thereby safeguarding the continuation of its unique cultural contribution.      The Media Act 2024 includes provisions to update S4C’s public service remit, including providing greater clarity on its ability to invest and generate commercial revenue; giving new unitary board and audit arrangements a statutory footing; and allowing S4C and the BBC to agree alternative arrangements for the BBC supporting S4C.     The parliaments/assemblies of the UK nations have conducted work to consider the provision of minority language broadcasting, for example the Welsh Senedd, State of Play: Public Service Broadcasting in Wales (2024) - this found a lack of market provision with regard to the provision of Welsh language content. It said that the regulator’s powers in relation to the Welsh language should be enhanced to allow it to require Welsh language provision on commercial radio services in Wales. Title EN: Misogyny in Music
Goal: Promote Human Rights And Fundamental Freedoms
SDG: SDG 5 - Achieve gender equality and empower all women and girls,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels
Area of Monitoring: Gender equality
Agency Implementation: Women and Equalities (Select) Committee; House of Commons
Main Feature: The Women and Equalities Committee examines the work of the Government Equalities Office and holds the Government to account on equality law and policy, including the Equality Act 2010, and cross Government activity on equalities. It also scrutinises the Equality and Human Rights Commission. The Committee published the Misogyny in Music report in January 2024. This report identified that women working in the music industry face limitations in opportunity, a lack of support, gender discrimination and sexual harassment and assault as well as the persistent issue of unequal pay in a sector dominated by self-employment and gendered power imbalances.
Results: A report has been written highlighting the problems of misogyny within the UK�s music industry. The Women and Equalities Committee held oral evidence sessions with academics, industry bodies, festival representatives, record label executives, artists and government and met privately with women from a diverse range of professional backgrounds from across the industry. They have issued a number of recommendations for industry bodies to respond to.
Recommandations: The report set out a number of recommendations based on their findings. Firstly, there are legislative steps that the UK Government can take to help tackle some of these concerns identified. The Equality Act should be amended to ensure freelance workers are provided with the same protections from discrimination as employees, section 14 of the Act should be brought into force to improve protections for people facing intersectional inequality. The Government should legislate to impose a duty on employers to protect workers from sexual harassment by third parties. The report outlined evidence on the impact of non-disclosure agreements on victims of discrimination, harassment and abuse. The report recommends that the Government should urgently bring forward legislative proposals to prohibit the use of non-disclosure and other forms of confidentiality agreements in cases involving sexual abuse, sexual harassment or sexual misconduct, bullying or harassment, and discrimination relating to a protected characteristic. They also suggested that the Government should consider a retrospective moratorium on NDAs for those who have signed them relating to the issues outlined above. The report also recommends that additional requirements should be placed on areas in the industry in which harassment and abuse are known to take place. Studios and music venues and the security staff that attend them should be subject to licensing requirements focused on tackling sexual harassment. Managers of artists should also be licensed. The Office for Students has proposed a new condition of registration and potential sanction for educational settings aimed at improving protections for students. They urge the OfS to implement its proposals swiftly and to enforce them robustly. They state that the establishment of a new authority, the Creative Industries Independent Standards Authority (CIISA) will help to shine a light on unacceptable behaviour in the music industry and in doing so, may reduce the risk of further harm. Crucially, it will be a single, recognisable body that anyone in the industry can turn to for support and advice. Music colleges, conservatoires and other educational settings need to do more to address the gendering of instruments, roles and genres and improve the visibility of and support for female role models. The Government and industry bodies should offer increased, funded and targeted opportunities for women and girls to study subjects and to engage in training in areas of the music industry that remain male-dominated and where women are made to feel unwelcome. Pathways to careers for women working in the sector must improve, particularly in key gatekeeping roles such as A&R and other male-dominated areas including sound engineering and production. The report also highlights that the main problem at the heart of the music industry is none of these; �it is the behaviour of men. � While necessary, preventative measures risk normalising behaviours and place the responsibility on women as potential victims rather than men as potential perpetrators. Educating boys and men on misogyny and consent, how to respect and better support women and to recognise the additional challenges they face will be more transformative than any of the measures set out in this report. They urge the UK Government to develop and introduce a new strategy in schools, aimed specifically at boys on issues of misogyny, sexual harassment and gender-based violence.

Title EN: Modernization of Canada’s Broadcasting Act through the Online Streaming Act
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture
SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Digital environment
Agency Implementation: Department of Canadian Heritage
Main Feature: The modernization of Canada’s Broadcasting Act seeks to ensure that online streaming services operating in Canada support and contribute to the production and discoverability of Canadian and Indigenous content, including content in English, French, and Indigenous languages. The reform further seeks to ensure that the broadcasting system reflects Canada’s diversity, ensuring that Canadians have more opportunities to see themselves in what they watch and hear.  The recent modernization of our legislative framework is an important facet of the federal strategy to support Canadian creators and ensure the long-term success of our creative industries and the influence of our culture. It ensures lasting support for Canadian music and stories, including original French-language content.
Results: With respect to the legislative process, the Online Streaming Act received Royal Assent on April 27, 2023. In November, the Government of Canada released policy directions to the Canadian Radio-television and Telecommunications Commission (CRTC), as Canada’s broadcasting regulator.   The regulatory implementation of the amended Broadcasting Act began in May 2023. The CRTC published a regulatory plan, launched four public consultations and published two initial decisions. It held a major public hearing in autumn 2023 on what base contributions online services must make to support the Canadian broadcasting system. As part of its multi-year plan, the CRTC will hold a series of public consultations over three phases that will cover a wide range of issues, including the definitions of Canadian and Indigenous content and accessibility for persons with disabilities. The CRTC is currently conducting public proceedings to implement these new objectives, which should be completed in 2025.   It is still too early in the process for the implementation of the amended Broadcasting Act to have been evaluated. The Broadcasting Act includes a five-year review of the amendments made by the Online Streaming Act.

Title EN: Mondo Crafts
Goal: Promote Human Rights And Fundamental Freedoms
SDG: SDG 5 - Achieve gender equality and empower all women and girls,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels
Area of Monitoring: Gender equality
Agency Implementation: NGO Mondo
Main Feature: Mondo has been engaged in social entrepreneurship since 2013, when we brought the first baskets from Ghana, jewelry from Uganda and Kenya, and beautiful embroidered products from Afghanistan to Estonia, and sold them in the pop-up shop of the Telliskivi Creative Campus during the Christmas period. We received a very positive response and experienced that Estonian people want to buy a product with a story, it is important for them that the products are bought directly from artisans, whom Mondo often even knows by name, and to contribute to their better livelihood through their purchase. Since the first shop, we have come a long way: we have sent Estonian volunteer designers to the communities to develop products, we have supported the concentration of craftsmen in cooperatives in order to manage themselves better and grow - to take on new students and develop quality. We have invested in setting up a shea butter factory and getting basket weavers their own building in Ghana and setting up a shop-sewing workshop in Uganda.  Why women? We have focused on women in our business, because research shows that a woman invests 99% of her income in the family, while a man invests 30-40%. We believe and see how a stable income allows artisans to improve their lives, take care of themselves and their family's health, and educate their children longer. All this increases self-esteem and confidence. Mondo supports local artisans both in product development and honing quality, as well as in finding foreign markets for their products. And often the biggest help is having someone believe that they can do it, that they can grow their businesses and be respected in the community for doing so.   Our principles: 1. We operate on the principles of fair trade, i.e. we pay fair wages to producers and take care of their good working conditions. 2. A social enterprise must be self-sustaining - therefore the entire price paid for the product does not go directly to the craftsman, but the price also includes costs related to transport and taxes, labelling, sales and marketing. 3. The profit from the sale of the products is channelled back to support the self-sustainability of the communities that made the handicrafts - to expand entrepreneurship and improve the communities' self-sufficiency.  Origins of products:  Congo village, northern Ghana Yen Pang Basket Weavers cooperative was born in Congo village in 2014, when Mondo offered village women the opportunity to learn basket weaving. The cooperative, which originally started with 8 women under a mango tree, has now doubled in size, and with the help of Mondo, they have adapted a small house where they go knitting together. In 2015, they already sent 350 baskets to Estonia. About half of the weavers are widows, whose position in society is low, the majority of women are illiterate. In the fall of 2014, designer Triin Kordemets was in the village of Kongo as a Mondo volunteer, and a year later Anne-Liis Leht, whose cooperation with local craftsmen resulted in the baskets available for sale.  In the shea butter production center built in the village of Kongo, shea butter is made by nearly 100 women who are gathered under the Congo Community Development Widows Association cooperative, this cooperative produces 1.5-2 tons of shea butter per year, which is sold to Germany, Canada and the United States in addition to Estonia.  In addition, in 2022, a group of Yakoti weavers with eight members, whose training Mondo contributed to a few years ago, started operations again in Ghana. The cooperation with the latter is smaller than with the main group, but hopefully the skills of the group members will increase in the future - at the moment, the weavers are able to weave only simpler models.  Kampala Disabled Initiatives, Uganda Kampala Disabled Initiatives was established in December 2014 with the support of the NGO Mondo as an organization for women with special needs that produces sewing and handicrafts. The Estonian designer Liina Viira helped improve women's sewing skills, who developed a series of KDI bags to stand out on the local market. A volunteer Eve Kislov also worked with the communities in February-October 2022, teaching group members the basics of entrepreneurship and practical skills. The groups mainly dealt with product development and marketing.  Istanbul, Turkey In January 2022, Mondo representatives visited the Small Projects Istanbul organization in Turkey, where the Muhra group of refugees from Syria makes various handicrafts, mainly jewelry. As novelty products, necklaces and macrame wall decorations were brought for resale in Estonia.  Afghanistan and Lebanon Due to the deep domestic crisis, the ordering and transportation of goods from the Tahaddi group from Lebanon and the Silk Road Bamiyan Handicrafts group from Afghanistan have stopped at the moment. A Mondo Crafts representative is in regular contact with both groups of artisans and is ready to place new orders as soon as possible.
Results: Mondo develops direct trade with its communities, i.e. all products come directly from artisans and their cooperatives, which makes it possible to know the exact origin of the product and to pay the women a fair price. We see every day how the opportunity to earn money with work and provide a better life for your family increases self-confidence and self-esteem.  By increasing livelihoods in local communities, we do our part to alleviate global inequality. Thanks to the income, it is possible for women to support their children's education and access to medical care, supporting the sustainability of communities' livelihoods. Empowering women through new knowledge and skills (handiwork, entrepreneurship) helps to increase their independence.  Our focus is therefore broadly on achieving sustainable development goals - one side of social entrepreneurship empowers communities in partner countries, while the other side increases awareness of responsible consumption in countries where products are resold (global educational activities).
