Workshops, Dialogue, and Conferences: ·         Workshop on Rice Cultures in Assam was organised in collaboration with local colleges, village representatives and Leiden and Ambedkar Universities, focussing on the rich cultural significance of rice. ·         A joint workshop with Rajiv Gandhi University, Arunachal Pradesh, engaging in dialogues with diverse communities in Arunachal Pradesh to understand the challenges faced in preserving intangible heritage. ·         In ajoint projectwith Ambedkar University, the Shillong International Conference on “Oral Traditions: Continuity and Transformations in Northeast and Southeast Asia” was conducted. ·         The Agricultural Heritage MuseumsConference (CIMA 23) – was organised to explore and engage on educating the public through Agriculture Museums on the significance of agriculture to human society, and to explain the many ways that agriculture has evolved. It was meant to facilitate dialogue between museums across the globe about agricultural heritage topics and discoveries. ·         Manjusha Art Workshop – A workshop on Manjusha craft was organisedwhere students were taught the art form; the workshop was aimed at promoting the art form and its learning and transmission process. ·         A collaborative Himalayan Heritage National Conference with the UNESCO C2C at the Wildlife Institute of India, Dehradun, was organized on the intangible culture of the Himalayan regions. The aim is to establish links between scholars, communities, and government/non-government bodies, to further the efforts of safeguarding intangible andlived heritage, and to explore itsconnections with economic regeneration. ·         “This is Dahanu”, a locally conducted project by the INTACH Dahanu chapter created an E-Newsletter and a video project. The initiative encouraged students from diverse backgrounds, languages, and educational levels to contribute articles, artwork, and essays focusing on their local heritage. This mentorship aimed to help students achieve a satisfactory standard in their work, fostering a deeper understanding and appreciation of Dahanu's cultural heritage. ·         A Patna Kalam workshop organised by the INTACH Patna Chapter, was an initiative to promote and preserve the unique Patna Kalam style of painting. The hands-on training by skilled artists included lectures, demonstrations, and interactive sessions. The goal was to encourage new generations to appreciate and continue this traditional art form.   4.     Films and Audio- Visual documentation: ·         Award-winning film made on the Kumbh mela, KUMBH – THE NECTAR OF FAITH, looks at the ethos of the Maha Parv Kumbh. Inscribed by UNESCO on the Representative List of Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity, this event witnesses the largest peaceful gathering of devotees in the world, embodying the true spirit of inclusiveness. They congregate at four locations in India in the designated six-year cycle (Ardh Kumbh) or the twelve-year cycle (Maha Kumbh) with a single purpose – a dip in the nectar of faith. The film explores its deep significance for the people of the sub-continent. ·         The Ramayana Project: VIGNETTES OF RAMAYANA To review the transmission, mobility, adaptation and concrete expressions of the Rama theme among different communities and regions in India, and to study at close quarters the power of the ‘oral word’, a series of films have been made under the Ramayana Project. The 34 short films were made to understand and capture the ethos of the Ramayana. They portray how the story in the epic has changed to include local flavour without losing the central theme and message. The films, through experts, bring out the nuances of the distinct forms of the Ramayana as performed in different parts of India.                                                                                                                                                                                            ·         Film on the River Ganga: A LOVE BEYOND REASON The documentary film highlights the lesser-known ICH elements, including Indigenous knowledge systems, folklore, performing arts, oral history, fairs, festivals, crafts, and culinary traditions of communities and regions along the river Ganga. The documentary showcases the above-mentioned living cultural treasures, and how the people of the country engage with the river and get impacted by it. ·         Documentary on the RAAS (RAAX) MAHOTSAV OF MAJULI, Assam, outlines aspects of the Raas festival held at Majuli in Assam and its significance in the life of the people of the world’s largest river island. The film looks at four Satras—Uttar Kamalabari Satra, Dakshinpat Satra, Samaguri Satra and Garamur Satra—and the Missing Community’s celebration of this festival. ·         Film on Gaya Pitrapaksha traditions: GAYA: STRINGS OF FAITH. 5.     Social Media and YouTube ·         The Instagram handle of the ICH Division @intach_myheritage has been active in spreading awareness of Indian cultural and artistic traditions. The team has employed the approach of creating visual articles to educate and introduce the complex intangible processes underlining Indian art and culture to a general audience. As a result, the newly started Instagram handle has seen consistent growth in followers and visibility. ·         The documentary films and audio-visual documentation have been uploaded on the INTACH YouTube platform for wider dissemination. 6.     Museum Work ·         RSSM – The Museum has been set up at Jabalpur with building restoration, design, development of content, and creation of AV documentaries on the life of great Gond Raja Shankar Shah and his son Raghunath Shah depicting their heroic life and death during the Mutiny of 1857. ·         Virtual Experiential Museum at Man Mahal (an ASI Building), Dashashwamedha Ghat, Varanasi, was set up by INTACH to showcase the rich cultural heritage of Kashi. 7.     INTACH’s Heritage Craft and Community Division Work ·         HCCD and the INTACH Aurangabad Chapter has restarted the tradition of handmade paper-making in Kagzipura, Maharashtra, to revitalise its paper-making craft, combating extinction with workshops, making it into a craft village and successfully creating sustainable livelihoods for the Kagzi Community there. Also recognized at G-20 – W20, Kagzipura paper products are gaining international acclaim. Future plans include a Paper Museum, Kagzipura Lake rejuvenation, and global handmade product promotion. ·         The Kerang fabric (made from the bark of a tree) revival project was executed with the INTACH Orissa-Koraput Chapter. Through skill-upgradation and design implementation workshops and awareness campaigns, the project aims to revitalize the demand for Kerang fabrics both locally and globally. INTACH is in the process of applying for the GI Tag for Kerang. Recognizing the significance of preserving indigenous crafts and empowering local communities, the Government of Orissa is in discussions to formalize a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) with INTACH for the phase 2 of promotion and revival of Kerang fabrics.   ·         The Sacred Waste Training Programme – a pan India project - provides training for converting flower waste into incense sticks and cones. The project, besides providing a sustainable solution for tackling pollution, also provides a livelihood for the marginalized sector (especially women). The first Scared Waste training programme was held in Maihar, MP, and adopted by various INTACH Chapters like Jammu, Ayodhya, Sekhawati, Vishakhapatnam and Shivpuri.
Results: The activities conducted by INTACH are deeply researched and are backed by in depth, comprehensive fieldwork, which is why they lend credibility to the organisation and its work in this sphere. INTACH’s activities have been widely appreciated. The dissemination programmes and workshops have effectively raised awareness about lived and practiced heritage, provided exposure to heritage under threat and to the livelihoods of communities engaged in cultural activities or creative economies. The use of social media has further amplified the impact by reaching a wider audience. Additionally, the successful screening of numerous films at various locations, resulting in National and International Awards, is a testament to the success of the initiatives. Collaborationson ongoing discourse and dialogues with government bodies, scholars, universities, and cultural organizations have been instrumental in establishing valuable connections that help in safeguarding the living cultural traditions.

Title EN: MUNICIPAL CULTURAL WORKING DAYS OF LA PAZ
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture
SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Partnering with civil society
Cultural Domain: Design,Performing Arts,Media Arts,Cinema and Audiovisual Arts,Music,Publishing,Visual Arts
Agency Implementation: MUNICIPAL AUTONOMOUS GOVERNMENT OF LA PAZ – MUNICIPAL SECRETARIAT OF CULTURES AND TOURISM
Main Feature: The Cultural Working Days of the Municipality of La Paz are an open participation event for workers in the arts and cultures with the objective of evaluating the application of the Municipal Autonomous Law No. 265-319 on the Promotion; Safeguarding; Development and Promotion of Cultures and the Arts, as well as the strategic planning in cultures and arts for the planning of the cultural policies of the municipality.  Since 2005, the Autonomous Municipal Government of La Paz has organized five Cultural Working Days. The first and second versions of the Cultural Working Days had the purpose of developing the five-year planning process of the cultural sector of the Autonomous Municipal Government of La Paz through the proactive participation of all the cultural actors of the city, validating, complementing and incorporating their demands in the plans, programs and projects in the Municipal Development Plan, as well as in the cultural agendas within the framework of the appointment of the Municipality of La Paz as the Ibero-American Capital of Culture and as part of the celebrations of the Bicentennial of the Revolution of 1809. The III Cultural Working Days in 2015 was focused on diagnosing the state of cultural development in the municipality and the main needs and demands of the different sectors to identify, complement and prioritize the main actions, programs and projects to be implemented as part of the Cultural Development Program 2015-2020, within the framework of the Government Plan 24/7 and the Plan 2040 "The La Paz we want". At this time, the Intercultural Citizen Council for the Planning of Cultures and the Arts (CONCIPCULTA) was renewed.  In 2020, the IV Cultural Working Days of the Municipality of La Paz were held, with the aim of establishing a participatory space for both the evaluation and the planning of the municipality's cultural policies and to renew the Intercultural Citizen Council for the Planning of Arts and Cultures. In 2023, the V Cultural Working Days of the Municipality of La Paz were held, which resulted in the renewal of both CONCIPCULTA and the Territorial Councils of Cultures, the adjustment and design of strategic planning guidelines and the review and proposed adjustment and modification of Municipal Autonomous Law No. 265-319 on the Promotion; Safeguarding; Development and Promotion of Cultures and the Arts.
Results: The development of the Cultural Working Days contributed to the proactive participation of cultural workers, to the diagnosis of the situation of the cultural sector in the Municipality and to the incorporation and agreement of proposals in the planning processes of the Autonomous Municipal Government of La Paz, as well as in the cultural agendas of the municipal cultural management system. On the other hand, the Cultural Working Days were established as the articulating body with cultural workers for the formation of citizen representation organizations that strengthen the processes of co-responsibility in the design of cultural policies and thereby strengthen governance and citizen participation. The development of the Municipal Strategic Plan for Arts and Cultures is one of the main results arising from the Cultural Working Days held in 2020, capturing in a document the strategies for the promotion of cultures and arts in the Municipality of La Paz, strategies developed within the framework of cultural rights under the conception of the contribution of cultures to the care of life as the fourth pillar of development.
Financial Ressources: DOES NOT INCLUDE BUDGET
Recommandations: The development of Cultural Working Days should strengthen dialogue not only with workers in the arts and cultures, but also with the planning processes that should be extended to inter-municipal areas, incorporating sectors such as health, education and the environment, among others, so that this articulation promotes the design of policies that respond to sustainable social, environmental and cultural development.  Citizen participation should be strengthened with dialogue and planning processes at the macro-district level, considering indicators of previously recorded cultural processes.

Title EN: Multiplex cinématographique TMV du centre commercial GARDEN CITY

Main Feature: L’intérêt du public algérien pour le cinéma se manifeste essentiellement par sa demande sans cesse croissante pour des lieux de projection modernes et accessibles. Les salles de cinéma, anciennement des espaces de réunions sociales, continuent de jouer un rôle important dans la vie culturelle du pays. Les cinéphiles algériens expriment un désir constant de découvrir une variété d’œuvres cinématographiques, à la fois locales et internationales. Pour ce faire, le Multiplex cinématographique TMV est venu répondre aux besoins suscités, il est composé de quatre (04) salles de cinéma d’une capacité globale de quatre cents (400) places, équipées des dernières technologies en termes de son et de projections, situé à Alger au Centre Commercial GARDEN CITY. Le multiplex a été inauguré le 1er octobre 2023, il ouvre ses portes tous les jours jusqu’à vingt-trois heures (23:00), pour 10 séances de projection/jour. Le prix moyen du ticket est de l’ordre de 850,00 DA (soit USD 6,29).

Recommandations: Les Multiplex cinématographiques contribuent à stimuler l’économie locale en créant des emplois et en générant des revenus. L’essor de ces nouvelles installations permettra de mettre en valeur les talents du cinéma algérien en offrant des plateformes de diffusion pour leurs créations. Ces nouvelles installations de projection garantissent aux générations futures l’accès à leur héritage culturel, tout en favorisant un sentiment de fierté nationale et d’appartenance en préservant le patrimoine cinématographique et en le mettant en avant.

Area of Monitoring: Cultural and creative sectors
Agency Implementation: AUTONOMOUS MUNICIPAL GOVERNMENT OF LA PAZ – MUNICIPAL SECRETARIAT OF CULTURES AND TOURISM
Main Feature: The enactment of Municipal Autonomous Law No. 265-319 on the Promotion, Safeguarding, Development and Promotion of Cultures and the Arts is one of the most important measures in the municipality of La Paz. Provides the necessary framework for the development of policies and strategies that respond to the exercise of individual, collective and community rights and duties in the field of cultures and the arts, to safeguard, preserve, strengthen, promote, disseminate and develop cultures and the arts, the protection of cultural heritage as well as establish mechanisms for co-responsible and decentralized participation, as well as a plural vision based on the recognition and appreciation of diversity and sustainable development It is the first autonomous law in Bolivia that addresses the cultural issue. It consists of 120 articles and 3 final provisions. One of its most important aspects is that the Municipal Autonomous Government of La Paz (GAMLP) must allocate 3.5% of its income to the cultural area. The construction of this regulatory framework responds to a participatory process of public and private actors.
Results: 	Stablished basis of consideration and regulation of cultures as a municipality of La Paz 	It became as a reference to promote a process of analysis at a national level generating a debate on municipal cultural regulations in other municipalities 	It made possible to allocate 3.5% of municipal income to the cultural field 	Promoted a policy that provided stability and continuity to measures and actions for the promotion of cultures, including Municipal Competitions and the Municipal Competitive Fund for Cultures and the Arts, among other aspects provided for in the same regulations.
Financial Ressources: DOES NOT INCLUDE BUDGET
Recommandations: The same law establishes the evaluation mechanisms to be carried out every two and a half years through public calls for Cultural Working Days (Jornadas Culturales). The Cultural Working Days (Jornadas Culturales) should have the open participation of all workers in the arts and cultures, cultural institutions, groups and interested people with the objective of evaluating the application of the Municipal Autonomous Law No. 265-319 on Development; Safeguard; Development and Promotion of Cultures and Arts. Up to the present administration, five versions of the Cultural Working Days have been developed as instances of evaluation of this regulatory framework, in which there is a proposal to modify and update the Law.

Title EN: MUNICIPAL PROGRAM FOR THE PROMOTION AND STRENGTHENING OF CULTURAL AND CREATIVE ECONOMIES OF THE CITY OF LA PAZ
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture
SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Cultural and creative sectors
Cultural Domain: Design,Performing Arts,Media Arts,Cinema and Audiovisual Arts,Music,Publishing,Visual Arts
Agency Implementation: MUNICIPAL AUTONOMOUS GOVERNMENT OF LA PAZ
Main Feature: The Autonomous Municipal Government of La Paz, in compliance with the Municipal Autonomous Law 265-319 on the Promotion, Safeguarding, Development and Promotion of Cultures and the Arts since 2017, has made progress in the implementation of a Municipal Program for the Promotion, Promotion and Strengthening of Cultural and Creative Economies, with the purpose of contributing to the strengthening and visibility of cultural and creative economies through institutional conditions for their development, improving the capacities of cultural workers and dynamizing spaces oriented to the generation of resources and jobs that allow the gradual self-sustainability of the cultural sector and the increase in the quality of life.   To this end, the Municipal Program for the Promotion, Promotion and Strengthening of Cultural and Creative Economies is composed of the following components:  Optimal Institutional Conditions: This consists of proposing actions in three areas: a) Institutional Strengthening of the Municipal Secretariat of Culture and Tourism (SMCyT) to be able to implement the Program, b) Regulatory Management, identifying needs for adjustments such as proposals for new regulations as well as regulatory procedures to promote cultural and creative economies, and c) Infrastructure to establish municipal spaces that allow hosting actions to promote cultural ventures, such as laboratories, coworking spaces, etc.  Relationships and strategic alliances: It aims to identify actors and institutions not only in the cultural field and propose alliances such as generating agreements and joint work with the aim of positioning the importance of cultural and creative economies and strengthening cultural enterprises. These can be cultural enterprises, international organizations (OEI, AECID, IDB), banking entities (Banco Sol), copyright management societies (SGAE, SOBODAYCOM), the National Chamber of Commerce, the Federation of Entrepreneurs, as well as local, national and regional festivals, networks and circuits.  Spaces for training, development and innovation: Aimed at proposing actions for discussion, training, education and collaborative work, but also for training audiences with the aim of improving the business skills of the cultural sector and encouraging cultural entrepreneurship in alliance with other GAMLP bodies and external entities. They include awareness and training courses, the development of laboratories and project incubators, implementation of seedbeds, among others. It includes the development of two areas: Training and Skills and Innovation and Entrepreneurship Processes.  Incentives for Cultural Economies: This is focused on proposing the generation of different incentives such as funds or competitions, aimed at promoting the development of cultural and creative economies, providing resources for the development of cultural ventures aligned with the objectives of municipal management and supporting the realization of meetings, festivals, training processes and civil society initiatives. The approach is not only focused on allocating municipal resources but also on other public and private entities doing the same, and for this reason it initially involves two areas: municipal incentives and inter-institutional management.  Linkage, Markets and Fairs: Aimed at carrying out different linkage activities between cultural enterprises and potential applicants for cultural goods and services. The applicants may be: companies, institutions, socio-cultural organizations and citizens. Linkage activities may be cultural markets, cultural entrepreneurship fairs, business meetings - show cases, cultural showcases, workshops, auctions, among others.  Cultural information monitoring and management platform for the municipality of La Paz: This consists of a proposed cultural information system, with the aim of centralizing, generating, processing and permanently monitoring information related to cultural and creative economies. It involves mapping, creating databases of cultural ventures, and surveys on cultural consumption within the framework of the creation of a Cultural Observatory of La Paz.
Results: Among the most relevant results that show that the municipality is on its way to generating a policy to promote cultural and creative economies are:  Incubator Projects: These have been carried out since 2016 in six areas: 1) performing arts, 2) musical arts, 3) audiovisual arts, 4) video games, 5) plastic arts, and 6) crafts and fashion design. The projects were selected through public calls, supporting more than 260 proposals, benefiting 900 cultural actors, 120 beneficiaries of the digital marketing specialization course, 58 beneficiaries of the art criticism course, and 63 beneficiaries of the art pedagogy course.  Market for Cultural and Creative Industries (MICC 360) In 2018, the first Market for Cultural and Creative Industries (MICC 3600) was created as a platform for linking and training between proponents and demanders of cultural artistic products and services, whether at local, national or international level.  Sami Q'athu: Created in 2019, the Sami Q'athu (Color Market) or plastic arts market as part of a program of local cultural markets aimed at public and private institutions, organizations, companies and the general population for the acquisition of cultural goods and services.  Around 50 artists participate in each edition, offering more than 200 works in the specialties of painting, sculpture, drawing, engraving, artistic ceramics and mixed techniques, available for public purchase.  Q'athu del Libro: In 2020, coordinated work was carried out with the Municipal Secretary of Economic Development called "Q'athu del libro" where more than 135 authors were able to upload their works to the network to be marketed in the virtual entrepreneurial showcase that was promoted with an agenda of activities that was seen by more than 350,000 people on the networks.  Craft fairs: In different specialties, the work and manual skill of Bolivian artisans reaffirms the tradition of fairs that host these products, whether utilitarian or decorative. With an annual average of 30 of these small spaces for supply and demand of crafts, this sector is perfecting its techniques, which allows it to maintain a constant dynamic, since even during the pandemic the fairs continued with all biosecurity measures.  The Chola Paceña Fashion Show, our tradition: The elegance of the chola from La Paz was reversing those notions that being a chola represented subordination. In the annual show, also taken with great success to Spain and Chile, the manifestations of the urban chola are exhibited in new contexts and new spaces, highlighting the pollera as a symbol of identity.  Design and fashion: The Municipal Department of Culture has promoted around twenty fashion design initiatives that propose a new conception of fashion and design. Among these proposals, the following can be highlighted: Fashion and Author Design Laboratory (Diseñarte), Chukuta Moda, Fashion with Cultural Identity, the First Fashion Days/Fashion Week, Asian Fusion Project, Bolivia Fashion Show, Bolivian Design and Authors , 100 Years of Fashion in Bolivia and La Paz Diseña.  “La Paz Filma” Film Commission: This is a project – the first of its kind in the country – that seeks to position the city as a filming location. To this end, it creates an institutional commission to strengthen the promotion of the territory and offer it as an ideal filming space, generate income from services and sources of work, as well as promote tourism. The program strengthens the realization of local film projects, both in the country and abroad, and facilitates the necessary logistical and technical services. To date, more than 300 products have been supported, in different formats, themes, length and difficulty, these were the result of an institutional artistic-cultural creation policy.  Surveys on Cultural Perception, Participation and Cultural Consumption: The Survey of Perception of Cultures, Participation and Cultural Consumption of the Municipality of La Paz was conducted on two occasions.  The first was in 2015 through a project coordinated by the Municipal Secretariat of Cultures, the Institute of Theoretical and Applied Statistics of the UMSA Statistics Department and the Spanish Cooperation, with a pertinent district and macro-district disaggregation, obtaining information on practices and consumption in arts, cultural heritage, technical and artistic training, municipal spaces, perception of municipal management, among others. This survey pursued the additional objective of knowing the perceptions of the population in order to prioritize the actions and projects to be executed in the following five years within the framework of the five-year program, mainly in relation to cultural infrastructure and heritage.
Financial Ressources: DOES NOT INCLUDE BUDGET
Recommandations: With regard to the achievements made in strengthening cultural and creative economies, it is important to continue developing activities to make visible the effective contribution of artistic-cultural production to the traditional economic sphere, as well as to other alternative and/or community economic dynamics. This implies making it clear in different public and private spheres that economic activity is not dissociated from cultural development, which is a fundamental component for the historical, social, productive and economic progress of municipalities and in this way dignifying the work of cultural workers and promoting the improvement of their working conditions and the quality of cultural services and products.  Finally, it is essential to continue conducting Surveys on Cultural Perception, Participation and Cultural Consumption, in order to have useful information for decision-making and to be able to make visible the contribution of cultures to sustainable human and social development as well as to the economic growth of the municipality, with the perspective of generating a Satellite Account at the local level.

Agency Implementation: Arts and Culture Norway
Main Feature: The Norwegian Museum sector is large and diverse. Some museums have several hundred employees, while others are small and have a few employees. Many receive operational support from the Ministry of Culture, while others receive operating support from other sources, like municipal museums, university museums or private museums. Arts and Culture Norway has several tools and tasks in the field of cultural heritage and a main responsibility for the development of the museum sector. This is done through advice and concrete development measures. The report to the Norwegian Storting (white paper) Meld. St. 23 (2020-2021) Musea i samfunnet – Tillit, ting, tid [The Museum in Society – Trust, Things, Time] underlines the important role of museums in society. Museums are important institutions for the production and preservation of knowledge, and have the power to define historic value, historic relevance, contemporary relevance and perspectives on truth. Museum policy therefore deals with fundamental social values since the museums help to shape these values through their activities and endeavours. Museums are expected to play an active role in society. This entails, for example, questioning accepted truths, challenging power structures, enabling new voices to be heard and presenting a nuanced and balanced picture of society.  To contribute to the development of the museum sector, ACN invites applications for financial support for three-year development programmes. These funds are also intended to encourage projects that promote collaboration, competence development, methodologies and strategies for museums’ efforts in the area of sustainable development. The programme focusses on: •	Digitization – diversity, dialogue and cooperation •	Research – research expertise, collaboration and infrastructure •	Museums as social actors - diversity, relevance and sustainability
Results: In the period 2021–2023, 17 museum projects across the country received grants. The various projects that have received support so far have shed light on social and cultural sustainability through the presentation of new and relevant knowledge about the use of nature and climate change. The manner in which gender and diversity are represented in museum collections is also highlighted, as is their role as arenas for debate and the expression of views on controversial topics in a local community. The programmes are also intended to help strengthen the museums’ capacity for prioritisation, dialogue and critical reflection, and have transferable value for the rest of the museum sector.

Title EN: Museums for Human Wellbeing (Research and Programme)
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture
SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Cultural and creative sectors
Agency Implementation: The Ministry of Culture of the Republic of Lithuania
Main Feature: In 2022–2023 initiated and commissioned by the Ministry of Culture the research sought to assess how Lithuania’s museums and their activities contribute to the development of the public’s psychosocial and spiritual wellbeing, looking at this phenomenon through the prism of the accessibility of culture to all. One of the key objectives – to draft recommendations for the development, improvement and expansion of the system of Lithuanian museums’ services for people with disabilities. It also identified the experiences and attitudes of people with disabilities towards accessibility of Lithuanian museums, and assessed the experiences, attitudes, needs and expectations of Lithuanian museum staff, education, health and social services professionals and representatives of organisations representing people with disabilities.  The recommendations laid out in the form of practical advice aimed at the main directions for improvement of museum accessibility for people with disabilities were as follows: adopting museum accessibility policy and its implementation; cooperation with people who have a disability and the organisations that represent them, health, education and culture professionals, other museums in Lithuania and abroad; presenting information about museum accessibility on their websites; adaptation of museum access routes and premises for people with disabilities; increasing the accessibility of museum content; and the training of museum staff to work with people who have a disability.
Results: The analysis of methodological material related to the accessibility of cultural institutions for persons with disabilities showed that Lithuania has a complete legislative framework for the accessibility of museums for persons with disabilities. A number of studies have been carried out and excellent guides for museums have been produced, providing recommendations on how to make museums accessible to persons with disabilities. However, the study showed that there is a lack of a single document that addresses the various aspects of making a cultural organization accessible, adjusting its work to different forms of disability.  The analysis of quantitative and qualitative research results allowed to assess the current situation of accessibility of Lithuanian museums for persons with disabilities, the attitudes of Lithuanian museum staff and visitors with disabilities towards the accessibility of physical and informational (content) infrastructure of museums, their expectations, and to identify the main directions of improving the accessibility of museums for persons with disabilities and the tools that can be used.  The research results and recommendations were useful in forming culture, health and social services policy provisions for the functioning and activity organisation of Lithuania’s museums, seeking to ensure the social and cultural needs of people with disabilities are satisfied by creating the conditions for proper involvement in cultural activities and making the most of cultural services. After conducting this complex research, recommendations were prepared for how to increase the accessibility of museums.   Furthermore, in 2023, three pilot museum projects were carried out with the main aim of developing and testing museum services for people with disabilities with a view to ensure their access to museums.  In 2024, the Ministry of Culture of the Republic of Lithuania allocated financial support to 7 national, state and municipality museums projects, targeted at ensuring that social and cultural needs of people with disabilities are met through access to museums.
Financial Ressources: Financed from the Progress program of the Development of Culture and Creativity of the Ministry of Culture of the Republic of Lithuania for 2021-2030 approx. USD 834 300 ( EUR 750 000)

Title EN: Music and Movies Digitalization and Streaming
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture

Area of Monitoring: Digital environment
Agency Implementation: Ethiopian Copyright and Neighboring Rights Collective Management
Main Feature: The Ethiopian Copyright and Neighboring Rights Collective Management has undertaken a significant initiative to promote the digitalization and global dissemination of Ethiopian music and movies. This initiative aims not only to preserve Ethiopia’s rich cultural heritage but also to provide Ethiopian artists with opportunities to reach a broader international audience. The following report details the key aspects and achievements of this initiative.  Promoting Digitalization of Ethiopian Arts The project has focused on the digitalization of Ethiopian music, movies, and other art forms, making them accessible to a global audience through various digital platforms. This effort is vital for preserving cultural works and ensuring they are available to future generations. The digital format also provides greater flexibility in accessing and enjoying these works, increasing their reach beyond traditional boundaries.  Enhancing Artists’ Income and Revenue One of the primary goals of this initiative is to improve the financial well-being of Ethiopian artists. By facilitating global access to their work, the project has opened up new revenue streams, allowing artists to earn income not only from local sales but also from international markets. Additionally, the initiative has supported the production of high-quality art products, further boosting the earning potential of creators.  Addressing Market Gaps in the Music Industry The Ethiopian music industry has long faced challenges related to market gaps and the underproduction of high-quality content. This initiative has provided financial support for the production of quality music, helping to fill market gaps and raise the overall standard of music production in Ethiopia.  Advertising and Promotion of Artists The initiative has also focused on promoting Ethiopian musicians and performers both locally and internationally. By utilizing mainstream media and social media platforms, the project has significantly increased the visibility of artists, helping them grow their fan base and enhance their market value. This promotional effort has been instrumental in elevating the status of Ethiopian artists on the global stage.  The efforts of the Ethiopian Copyright and Neighboring Rights Collective Management have marked a transformative step in the digitalization and global dissemination of Ethiopian music and movies. By promoting digitalization, enabling global access, and supporting the production of quality content, the initiative has provided Ethiopian artists with unprecedented opportunities for growth and international recognition. The ongoing efforts to advertise and promote these artists further solidify Ethiopia’s presence in the global arts community, ensuring that Ethiopian culture continues to thrive in the digital age.
Results: The initiative focuses on establishing a robust and effective streaming platform for music and movies, providing opportunities for both Ethiopian and international audiences to access Ethiopian art. The platform ensures fair compensation for artists while promoting Ethiopian culture on a global scale.  By enhancing the visibility of Ethiopian arts in international communities, the initiative helps address market gaps by creating a conducive environment for investors to enter the Ethiopian music and film industries. Moreover, the platform supports all associated costs, from production to marketing and advertising, thus supporting the complete lifecycle of content creation and distribution.  This comprehensive approach helps promote Ethiopian artists, elevates the quality of their work, and increases their reach and market value globally.

Main Feature: During 2022, the Culture Observatory of the Ministry of Cultures emphasized the creation of national and international knowledge management networks, with the implementation of the following actions:         ▪	Analysis of agreements with actors of the quadruple helix for the constitution of territorial observatories in the country.         ▪	Definitions of regions for the creation of new territorial observatories at the national level.         ▪	Methodological document that establishes the route for the creation of economic and cultural observatories, understanding the dynamics of each of the regions and how this would connect the networks of existing observatories and the future ones to be created.         ▪	Support to boards of directors in terms of structuring research products, obtaining funding sources, and development of events and/or initiatives of each observatory         ▪	Recommendations to overcome bottlenecks experienced by territorial observatories         ▪	Accompany the international network of observatories in its creation, implementation and achievement of early victories         ▪	Identify and establish alliances with other Latin American countries to form the network of observatories from an international perspective, under the leadership of the Colombian Observatory of Culture and Economy         ▪	Propose a roadmap with the strategy that allows the Colombian Observatory of Culture and Economy to be positioned as the leader of a network of international observatories.                   Derived from these actions, on July 7, 2022, in the context of the Second Meeting of Cultural and Creative Economy, a Declaration was signed in which Colombia and five (5) countries in the region (Ecuador, Mexico, Uruguay, Argentina, and Brazil) began the network of international observatories. In this declaration they commit to:                  1.	Recognize the work from different countries and institutions to observe, systematize, and present to society the results of their analyses in the interrelation between culture, economy, and development.         2.	Express the importance of recognizing culture as one of the bases of human development, of its capabilities, manifestation of its identity and search for the freedom that its full expression generates; and the role that cultural policy and economics observatories play in collecting and disseminating them.         3.	⁠ ⁠Highlight that culture has a high potential to promote sustainable development and that observatories of cultural policies and economics can provide a significant contribution to our societies.         4.	Promote networking between the observatories that we currently represent within the framework of the "International Network of Observatories and Researchers of Cultural Policies and Economics" that is established, in order to generate synergies, share methodologies, carry out joint research, promote meeting spaces, and jointly disseminate the results of the research carried out.         5.	⁠Participate in the creation of the roadmap for the development of this network and initiate actions that allow its implementation and consolidation.                  For its part, the national observatory network is made up of seven (7) observatories throughout the territory. These observatories arise from territorial initiatives in which the Ministry advised on their constitution through a route for the creation of observatories, understanding the dynamics of each of the regions.                  The first observatories to be established were those of the cities of Cali and Medellín (2021), followed by the observatories of the cities of Barranquilla, Cartagena, Pasto, Ibagué, and the Metropolitan area of Medellín.
Results: The consolidation of a national network made up of seven (7) observatories throughout the territory. Area of Monitoring: Cultural and creative sectors
Agency Implementation: British Phonographic Industry
Main Feature: The Music Export Growth Scheme is designed to make available grants ranging from £5,000 - £50,000 to UK-registered independent music companies to assist them with marketing campaigns when looking to introduce successful UK music projects overseas.
Results: Through 22 rounds over the last ten years, the scheme has invested over £6 million in British music, leading to an estimated £55.5 million financial return to the UK economy and a return on investment of nearly £14 for every £1 received from the Government.
Financial Ressources: A further $4.13m in committed funding has been allocated from 2023-25 to enable emerging artists to break into new international markets.
Recommandations: The Music Export Growth Scheme is playing its part promoting British artists. Along the way, MEGS has helped the likes of BRITs winners Catfish & The Bottlemen and Mercury Prize recipients Young Fathers, Dave and Wolf Alice on their musical journeys to international success.     Since MEGS launched in January 2014, over 240 applications have been supported with investment totalling nearly £3.8 million. This has generated a 12 : 1 return on investment, with some £36 million generated for the UK music economy.    In addition to its excellent financial returns, the Scheme has an important cultural impact, helping to promote British culture overseas and extend the UK’s soft power. With the UK now looking to develop new international trading relationships, not least in rapidly emerging markets across Asia, Africa and South America, the need for MEGS is arguably greater than ever.

Main Feature: As a specific action within the EU’s Music Moves Europe initiative, the European Union seeks to highlight and promote the diversity of the European repertoire with a European Union Prize for popular and contemporary music: The Music Moves Talent Awards.   The annual Music Moves Europe Talent awards celebrate emerging artists who represent the European sound of today and tomorrow.   The Music Moves Europe Talent Awards aim to put a spotlight on the most interesting new European talents – and to showcase the richness of the European music industry. Outstanding European emerging artists will receive a Music Moves Europe Talent Award in recognition of their growing international success. They are given the opportunity to perform at the Eurosonic Festival (ESNS) and receive on top of that a prize package, including a training programme and financial support for touring and promotion. The nature of the Prize affirms a shared commitment to helping emerging artists to break through in Europe and beyond.  The Prize is implemented by Eurosonic Noorderslag (ESNS) in partnership with Reeperbahn Festival and co-funded by the Creative Europe programme. It gets the support of a unique alliance of European music industry partners, including:  Digital Music Europe (DME),  European Broadcasting Union (EBU),  European Music Exporters Exchange (EMEE),  Independent Music Companies Association (IMPALA),  International Music Managers Forum (IMMF),  The live music platform for new European talent (Liveurope), The European network of music venues and festivals (Live DMA), and  European Festival Association (Yourope).
Results: Each winner receives a prize package worth €10,000 split into two parts: touring and promotional support, and business training. In addition, they are offered a range of networking, broadcasting and recording opportunities from the live sector and recorded music industry.   Winners of the Music Moves Europe Talent Awards during the reporting period can be found here: https://mmeawards.eu/en/mme_artists/

Main Feature: In May 2023, the European Commission launched a new dialogue with the music sector under the Music Moves Europe initiative, covering the period 2023-2026. A consortium of well-established European music conferences/festivals ((Eurosonic Noorderslag (the Netherlands), ARTmania (Romania), Linecheck (Italy), MaMa (France), Reeperbahn Festival (Germany) and Tallinn Music Week (Estonia)) is organising a series of 10 specific structured dialogues at music conferences. Moreover, two EU-level conferences on music will take place in the period. The structured dialogue with the music sector aims to raise awareness on the specific needs of the music sector and to identify possible fields of EU action with clear added value at the European level.
Results: Four dialogue sessions will have taken place by end-2024: One on the challenges of the music ecosysem, at Tallin Music Week (May 2023), one on how to support new talents in the music ecosystem at Linecheck (Nov 2023), one on greening the music ecosystem at Eurosonic (Jan 2024), and one on fair remuneration of artists at Reeperbahn (September 2024). In addition, the first EU-level conference took place on 22 February 2024, allowing an exchange between policy makers, EU institutions and the music sector on these issues.

In addition to an orchestral introduction, the composition has three main elements: the dialogue between baritone-chorus-reciting voices, which makes explicit the meaning of faith in peace (a cappella choir and orchestra, recitative and aria for baritone etc.); the intervention of children's voices (three interludes for treble voices and instruments in different styles); the final prayer of St. Francis of Assisi with the choral intervention of all: soloist, voices and instruments. Main Feature: Since 1979, Nordic Anthropological Film Association (NAFA) has organized this international event. In 2018, Lisbon was chosen to host in 2020 the 40th Festival. The Festival brings films from all over the world that relate with different cultures and societies. It is an excellent opportunity to have an overview of contemporary ethnographic film. NAFA, based in Norway, is a non-commercial, non-profit educational and research association 8 working to promote the ethnographic film and visual anthropology. The main objectives of this bilateral initiative were i) to enlarge and reinforce the relations between PT and NO institutions and persons, ii) production, distribution and awareness of ethnographic film to the specific target groups and other audience, iii) the training of filmmakers, and developing new uses of electronic and interactive visual media, iv) to set an international network on ethnographic film. The films focus on different themes: traditions, ecology, personal family stories, music, ethnic minorities, etc. All screenings were planned to take place at the Museum of National Ethnology, except for the opening planned for central Lisbon. It was estimated that around 20 filmmakers that would be presenting their films, a conference on visual archives, workshop, meetings and social events. Tangible results from this event were expected such as to promote new concepts on the relation between cultures, languages and traditions, to celebrate an informal encounter between students, academics and other public enhancing institutional relations between Museums and Research Unities from both countries and creating scientific cooperation and networking for future and better bilateral interconnections between Portugal and Norway.
Results: The initiative consisted in organizing the 40th Edition of the NAFA International Ethnographic Film Festival, in Lisbon, from 29 September to 2 of October 2021. The event aimed to promote a platform and opportunity for reflection on major cultural diversity, human rights, ecology and immaterial and material immaterial and material heritage, among other values. The Festival took place at the National Museum of Ethnology and the programme included the participation of twenty-three films from different parts of the world, recording the diversity of cultural practices cultural practices that cross the contemporary world. Along with the official selection of the festival, the initiative's activities also involved the organization of workshops and conferences. The event allowed to celebrate an informal meeting between students, academics and other public and to promote new concepts about the relationship between cultures, languages and traditions. In this way contributed to a better humanitarian understanding of other cultures, their habits and traditions, focusing on different themes: traditions, ecology, personal family stories, music, ethnic minorities, among others. The initiative also allowed to develop production strategies to work together with Third World countries, where a large number of these films take place, and to improve the practical strategies of production, distribution and awareness-raising of ethnographic films for specific target groups and other audiences.

Cultural Domain: Design,Performing Arts,Media Arts,Cinema and Audiovisual Arts,Music,Publishing,Visual Arts
Agency Implementation: Lên Ngàn - a multidisciplinary cultural, artistic and creative platform
Main Feature: Lên Ngàn, established in 2019, aims to develop local culture and arts in Viet Nam and bridge the gap to the international arena. Its purpose is to narrow the distance between the public, contemporary art, and local cultural heritage, and diversify forms of experience. Lên Ngàn operates as a platform for exchanging cultural and artistic experiences, becoming a space where artists, cultural experts, researchers, businesses, and others can experiment with ideas or interact with various audiences. It also provides the public with knowledge and understanding of cultural heritage, culture and arts, and a deepened affinity with the brand of businesses or public entities. Furthermore, Lên Ngàn promotes activities with partners to explore Viet Nam's social and cultural aspects.  Lên Ngàn initiates and coordinates cultural and artistic projects with numerous Vietnamese and international partners, manages stakeholders’ collaboration to act as an intermediary connecting between social resources, including the state, enterprises, cultural entities (artisans/artists/creators), and the public. Lên Ngàn's curatorial approach focuses on a model that utilizes diverse resources and is community-oriented. It engages in activities contributing to society, including initiating cultural, artistic, educational, media, and research projects. Lên Ngàn focuses on the relationships between creativity and social change; creates an interdisciplinary ecosystem. In addition to activities developing local culture and arts and contributing to the indigenous community, Lên Ngàn provides services to businesses, artists, museums, and collectors.  Lên Ngàn promotes the work of Vietnamese artists and cultural experts, as well as international artists connected to Viet Nam, thereby expanding the understanding of “art from Viet Nam”. Instead of limiting itself by defining artists based on nationality, Lên Ngàn emphasizes practice, experimental spirit, and critical thinking in art as prerequisite factors. By connecting artists with the Vietnamese cultural landscape, Lên Ngàn creates opportunities for artists to pursue experimental creativity and encourages them to continue exploring their personal art fields, thus driving innovation and growth and contributing to the diverse cultural and artistic landscape of Viet Nam.  The community of Lên Ngàn includes fields such as contemporary art, heritage, anthropological research (cultural and social anthropology), cinema, performing arts, visual arts, history, literature, media and others, together explore creative and cultural practices across Viet Nam. With the aim of contributing to the artist community and serving the community, strengthening the connection of cultural experiences and promoting commerce inspired by culture, Lên Ngàn has focused on quality, initiating, and managing diverse projects to make Viet Nam's cultural and artistic life more vibrant and serve as a bridge to the region.
Results: Lên Ngàn has created several breakthroughs, evocative, and highly inspirational projects and works that have had a direct impact on the local community. The projects by Lên Ngàn are a synthesis of various components, materials, and media, including video, performing art, painting, sculpture, poetry, public art, etc. These projects provide a reference platform for governance, management, and leadership within the art and cultural community while also preparing basic skills for future young leaders in the creative and cultural sectors. Lên Ngàn promotes experimental creativity, and encourages artists to continue exploring their personal art within their respective fields, realizing their imagination and reflecting social issues, and contributes to enhanced training through the direct transmission of experience in art, culture, and creative business in Viet Nam.  Specific activities include:  - The performance "Cõi Thinh Không" - a borderless world reviving traditional Vietnamese theater. It is inspired by various musical elements throughout time and history, explores the concepts between "East" and "West," cultural identity, and "genre" through both original compositions and adaptations from traditional music. The project fosters an open learning environment among traditional artists and other art areas such as experimental contemporary, contemporary dance, hiphop, etc. The performance, supported and sponsored by the Hanoi Department of Culture and Sports, premiered at the Innovation and Creativity Week 2021 organized by the Hanoi People's Committee and UNESCO.  - "The Sound-Color" Project: Contemporary music and performing art. Lên Ngàn initiated the "Sound-Color" project in 2020, collaborating with Kongo Gallery Viet Nam, S&S Group, and 84NOISE to provide artists with opportunities for a creative exploration journey. The works are experimental and innovative, demonstrating that even the oldest art forms in Viet Nam can be preserved by developing and blending with contemporary music while retaining their unique identity. The first performance in 2020 was sponsored by Rolls Royce Motor Car Ho Chi Minh City. The work "Sóng Ngầm Sông Hồng" (The Subsurface Waves of the Red River) was one of three performance series of the project, archived by Exeter University (UK) in the digital library of the Institute of Ethnology on the theme of femininity in contemporary music.  - The Thanh Cảnh (Sound-Scenery) Cultural and Artistic Initiative 2023: In 2023, Lên Ngàn, along with AC Project/Counterflows, UK, initiated the Thanh Cảnh Cultural and Artistic Initiative with the support and sponsorship of the British Council under the UK/Viet Nam Season 2023 program. Thanh Cảnh was founded on the idea of professional artists working, guiding, and advising new artists in a practical environment. The Thanh Cảnh project included two phases in June and September 2023, involving six artists from different cultural and artistic spaces. In phase 1, Thanh Cảnh developed a rich dialogue among artists from different generations, cultures, and principles. Thanh Cảnh focused on creative processes, collaboration, and the development of local materials, aiming to enhance diversity, equality, and accessibility. The series of events included sound fieldwork, themed research related to audience development, studio opening with ideas for work development, and concert programs. Phase 2 involved selecting the most promising works for presentation at the Counterflows Festival UK 2024, with the aim of advancing the development of indigenous Vietnamese art in the international arena. The project engaged over 400 on-site audiences and generated over 600,000 interactions on social media platforms.

Title EN: National Policy on Culture and Heritage
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture
SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Cultural and creative sectors
Agency Implementation: State Department for Culture, The Arts and Heritage
Main Feature: The National Policy on Culture and Heritage is anchored on the Constitution of Kenya, Vision 2030, and the regional and international legal instruments that promote culture as a pillar for national cohesion and development.  The first edition of the National Culture and Heritage Policy was approved by Cabinet in the year 2007 and consequently implemented. However, because of the new constitutional dispensation that came into effect in 2010, it was necessary to have it reviewed and aligned with the Constitution after extensive stakeholder consultations. The reviewed National Policy on Culture and Heritage was approved by the Cabinet in the year 2021 paving way for its dissemination and implementation. The Policy was developed in a multi agency approach where State agencies, private sector, CSOs and the academia participated. The Policy is premised upon the Constitution which recognizes culture as the foundation of the nation and as the cumulative civilization of the Kenyan people and the nation. The government is, thus, committed to supporting its implementation as a way of broadening the options for every citizen to contribute to the socio-economic and political development of the nation. It also accords them opportunities for the betterment of their lives. The Policy provides an enabling environment for appreciating, protecting, safeguarding and promoting the culture of the people of Kenya as well as reinforce national unity and pride while stimulating creativity and innovation. Most importantly, the Policy provides direction for the implementation of cultural programmes at National and County level taking into cognizance that the management of culture is a devolved function.  The Policy also plays a key role in  fostering collaboration and partnership at the regional and international levels. Its implementation is the basis for all national strategies and programmes  for culture and arts in the country. The activities are implemented in partnership with the County Governments, Civil Society organizations among other stakeholders . Two notable programmes implemented in the reporting period include  the National Visual Artist in residence programme in June 2021 that brought together  40 up coming artists for a two week training and mentoring workshop under the leadership of older and more experienced pioneers in the industry. The works produced were showcased in a national exhibition- The Marejeo exhibition, at the National Museums of kenya. It served a dual purpose of nurturing artistic as well as reviving the conversation on the need for a national art gallery. A national Crafts fair showcasing handcrafted products from the 47 counties themed ' ’Our heritage of Splendour’’ was held in February 2021  where representatives of craft groups in the Counties showcased and sold crafts dominant in their Counties at a national platform.
Results: County Goverments have picked que form the National Policy on Culture and Heriage and developed similar policy documents to guide the development of the Culture sectors at the local level. There is also Improved participation in culture and arts programme both at National level and County Governments.

Title EN: National Film Board of Canada’s Commitment to Gender Parity
Goal: Promote Human Rights And Fundamental Freedoms
SDG: SDG 5 - Achieve gender equality and empower all women and girls,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels
Area of Monitoring: Gender equality
Cultural Domain: Performing Arts,Media Arts,Cinema and Audiovisual Arts,Music
Agency Implementation: National Film Board of Canada (NFB)
Main Feature: In 2016, the NFB became one of the first cultural agencies in the federal public service to make specific commitments regarding gender parity when it announced that by 2019, it would achieve and maintain a 50:50 gender balance in: the number of productions in progress directed by women; and the proportion of the production budget allocated to works created by women. In 2017, the NFB pushed this commitment further by setting the goal of achieving gender parity by 2020 in key creative positions in its documentary, animation, and interactive productions. In this case, the fields targeted included editing, cinematography, screenwriting and musical composition, along with other creative activities related to animation and immersive storytelling, in which women were still prominently a minority. Further, in 2021, the NFB signed up for the 50-30 Challenge, an initiative led by the Government of Canada, Canadian businesses and diversity organizations. One of the goals of this program is to challenge Canadian organizations to achieve gender parity on their boards of directors and in senior management. By taking on these various commitments, the NFB has helped to increase women’s representation and has proven itself as a leader in the industry in Canada.   The NFB seeks gender parity* both in the percentage of completed productions and in the allocation of its production budgets. These two performance indicators are an integral part of the NFB’s annual accountability reporting.  *Gender parity means equal representation of men and women. It is important to understand that the target is not exactly 50%, but the achievement of a parity zone that comes close to the indicator for the works completed at the NFB.   Staunchly feminist projects Here are a few examples of projects developed at the NFB in recent years that give voice to women:   23rd edition of the Cinéaste recherché(e) competition   In the Cinéaste recherché(e) competition, run by the NFB French Program’s Animation Studio, the winner receives the opportunity to create their first professional work at the NFB. In 2018, the Studio gave concrete expression to the NFB’s commitment to gender parity by making the 23rd edition of this competition open to women only, to support and increase the presence of female animation filmmakers. The winner of this competition was Véronique Paquette, and her animated film Loca will be completed in 2024.  Lab on women and the creation of images  In September 2023, the NFB’s Quebec, Canadian Francophonie and Acadian Documentary Studio held a creative lab at the NFB’s offices, on the theme of women and the creation of images. Attended by 15 women from Black communities, the event examined the place that female creators occupy in the cultural and artistic spaces of the Canadian Francophonie.  Otherly  Premiering on Instagram Stories, Otherly was a series of seven short documentaries on the theme of belonging. The series showcased the perspectives of filmmakers from whom little is heard in social media: female, non-binary, and genderqueer creators.  A Return to Memory  This medium-length documentary by Donald McWilliams, scheduled for completion in 2024, rediscovers the women of the NFB, sometimes known as the “Grierson Girls,” who helped lay the groundwork for Canadian documentary film during the Second World War and the years that followed.
Results: Seven years after making its original commitment, the NFB continues to meet its goals for gender parity both in number of productions and in production budgets. It has also met or exceeded its goals for most of the key creative positions (screenwriting, editing and musical composition) and achieved notable improvement in cinematography.  In 2022–23, among all the NFB works that were in some stage of production:  -	64% were directed by women; -	60% were written by women; -	66% were edited by women; -	32% had women as their cinematographers; -	20% had musical scores composed by women.  Parity Certification  The efforts that the NFB has made to achieve gender parity over the past several years have been recognized with six Parity Certifications awarded by Women in Governance (most of them at the Gold Parity or Platinum Parity level). Women in Governance is an organization founded in 2010 to support women in advancing their careers and securing seats on boards of directors, and to support organizations in working to close the gender gap in their workplaces.
Financial Ressources: In 2022–23, 66% of the NFB’s production budgets were allocated to works by women.
Recommandations: It was by adopting clear and measurable objectives in 2016 that the NFB became one of the first cultural organizations to have made formal commitments in terms of gender parity and the first public cultural institution to receive certification Parity from the Canadian organization Feminine governance. The NFB has been a pioneer and is pleased to see that other organizations in the audiovisual sector have followed suit. The initial 2016 commitments made over a three-year period are now an integral part of the NFB’s culture. Constant work and renewed measures allow the organization to ensure equitable representation of women both in front of and behind the camera.

Title EN: National Living Culture Policy
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture
SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Partnering with civil society
Cultural Domain: Design,Performing Arts,Media Arts,Cinema and Audiovisual Arts,Music,Publishing,Visual Arts
Agency Implementation: Ministry of Culture
Main Feature: The National Living Culture Policy is a public State policy managed in a shared manner by the Ministry of Culture in intergovernmental partnerships and with state, district, municipal governments, cultural groups and institutions, cultural managers and producers and civil society, to articulate, train and encourage actions carried out by entities, collectives and cultural agents in their communities, as well as supporting, valuing, recognizing, dimensioning and disseminating cultures and cultural actions in their different territories. It emerged with the Cultura Viva Program, created in 2004, and its origin dates back to the Federal Constitution of 1988, which establishes the duty of the State (Public Power of all spheres) to guarantee citizens the full exercise of cultural rights and access to sources of national culture, in addition to promoting, valuing and encouraging the production, dissemination and circulation of knowledge, the universalization of access to cultural goods and services and cooperation between federated entities, public and private agents operating in the cultural area, among others (CF/88, art. 216-A, § 1, items I to IV). Thus, established through Law No. 13,018, of 7/22/2014, the National Living Culture Policy is characterized as the first community-based policy of the National Culture System, and reaches a large national and international dimension, currently being a reference for community-based cultural policies in several Latin American countries. An example of this is the Ibero-American cooperation program IberCultura Viva, created in 2014, which was based on Brazilian policy, and already brings together 13 countries. Designed to value community-based culture, network articulation and shared management, based on the principles of autonomy, protagonism and empowerment of civil society, the Cultura Viva Policy encompasses initiatives linked to the solidarity economy, urban and peripheral cultural production, culture digital, popular culture, the cultural expressions of indigenous communities, quilombolas, those of African origin, the segments of childhood and youth, covering all types of artistic and cultural language such as: music, performing arts, visual arts, cinema, circus, literature and crafts, among others. The objective of the policy is to promote the network articulation of these initiatives, in addition to contributing to social inclusion, the fight against prejudice and all forms of discrimination and intolerance, the recognition and appreciation of Brazilian cultural diversity and the full exercise of rights cultural. In addition to ensuring the continuity of actions at national and international levels, the Living Culture Law creates other forms of financial support for cultural initiatives, simplifies and reduces bureaucracy in accountability processes and the transfer of resources to civil society organizations. Different from the idea that the State should “take” culture, the Cultura Viva policy is based on enhancing the cultural groups and agents that already exist in the country's territories and communities and that promote the population's access to cultural goods and services in territories and communities where they operate – with cultural training, in the aesthetic dimension, with the creation, production and/or dissemination of artistic languages and symbolic expressions, in guaranteeing and promoting accessibility and equity, and in reducing inequalities and combating economic violence, gender, race/ethnicity and sexuality, among other social oppressions. When recognized, these groups receive the name “Culture Points”. The policy also recognizes other institutions, called “Pontões de Cultura”, which develop, monitor and coordinate cultural activities in partnership with regional, identity and/or thematic networks of Pontos de Cultura.
Results: Currently, the National Culture Policy is present in 27 Brazilian states, in around a thousand municipalities and abroad, being a public policy with great reach and visibility of the Ministry of Culture. In 20 years, around 3,500 Cultural Points and Pontoons were supported, recognized in more than 1,400 municipalities, in all 27 Federative Units of the country. These Points and Pontoons are georeferenced on the Cultura Viva Network Map.

Title EN: National Lottery Arts and Older People Programme
Goal: Integrate Culture In Sustainable Development Frameworks

Agency Implementation: National Lottery; Arts Council of Northern Ireland
Main Feature: National Lottery Arts & Older People Programme aims to strengthen the voice of older people and promote positive mental health and emotional wellbeing through the arts.  The proposed projects should reflect the partnership approach with the target groups they plan to engage with and have the support from them in the delivery.     The Arts & Older People Programme was set up to increase opportunities for older people to engage with the arts. It achieved this by providing funding to arts-based projects that addressed related social issues such as poverty, isolation and loneliness, as well as promoting positive mental health. The design of the Programme was informed by the Arts & Older People Strategy which was undertaken by the Arts Council in July 2010.
Results: Applications for the most recent programme have now closed and the projects are currently underway.     ACNI awarded £216,571 to 29 projects during 2022/23. Seven of the organisations funded were new to the programme. A total of 2,173 participants took part and 1,542 contact hours were delivered by arts organisations.
Financial Ressources: Applicants could apply for grants between $1286.68- $12866.80.
Recommandations: The 2022-2023 Arts and Older People Programme (AOPP) has been evaluated. The most recent programme will be evaluated after completion.     The October 2023 roundtable symposium and subsequent meetings with the office of COP resulted in very productive discussions and information exchange. Sharing learning from the AOPP on an annual basis through these could be beneficial and enhance dissemination of learning from the programme. Reconvening the AOPP steering group could also help to shape the programme and focus for evaluations.    The AOPP has been successful in enabling participants to become socially included. Greater emphasis on elevating those voices through perhaps an initiative like AOPP champions.     The success of the AOPP is dependent on the highly skilled artists that have been involved with it. To ensure that the richness of the AOPP model continues capacity development of artists across NI is vital. This could include formal training on issues such as ageing, dementia, person centred care. It could also include shadowing of or mentoring by established AOPP artists. The piloting of ‘an artist in residence’ could provide powerful learning.    The AOPP is a public health intervention that is focused on primary and secondary prevention of ill-health. As such the total impact is likely underestimated. A cost benefit analysis could yield powerful evidence of the far-reaching impact of the arts in alleviating social isolation and loneliness, supporting cognitive health and wellbeing, and combatting frailty. This information could strengthen advocacy for investment in the arts as being financially expedient.

Goal: Promote Human Rights And Fundamental Freedoms
