Agency Implementation: Ministry of Labour and Social Policy (MLSP)
Main Feature: The policy on equality between women and men in the Republic of Bulgaria is a horizontal policy, in the implementation of which a number of institutions and organizations are involved according to their competences. The country pursues a coherent policy on gender equality, which is in line with national specificities and commitments under international treaties to which it is a party, including as an EU Member State. The legal guarantees for equality and equal treatment of women and men are contained in the Bulgarian legislation in force - the Constitution of the Republic of Bulgaria, the Labour Code, the Law on Protection against Discrimination, the Law on Equality of Women and Men (LWEM) and a number of other special and sectoral laws. According to the provisions of the law adopted in 2016. The Council of Ministers (CoM) determines the state policy on gender equality, as well as adopts a national strategy on gender equality and plans for its implementation. The Minister of Labour and Social Policy directs, coordinates and supervises the implementation of the State policy on gender equality. The Minister also chairs the National Council for Equality between Women and Men under the Council of Ministers (the National Council), which is a body for consultation, cooperation and coordination between the central and territorial executive authorities and civil society structures. The Council is composed of representatives of all ministries (incl. The Council includes representatives of the Council of Ministers (the Ministry of Culture), various state and executive agencies and other bodies established by law (the Council for Electronic Media, the Commission for Protection against Discrimination (CPD), the SACP, the SAB, the NSSI, the NSI, the Ombudsman of the Republic of Bulgaria, the NKBTH and BAS); the representative organisations of employers and employees at national level; the National Association of Municipalities in the Republic of Bulgaria; and non-profit legal entities whose object of activity is in line with the priorities of the state policy on gender equality. The National Council provides opinions on draft strategic documents and normative acts that contain provisions related to equality between women and men beforetheir submission to the Council of Ministers; participates in the development of the provisions of the Law on Equality between Women and Men (LWEM), the National Strategy on Equality between Women and Men is the main programming document that contains the objectives for achieving equality between women and men, the bodies and priority areas for achieving the objectives, etc. The National Strategy for Gender Equality; proposes measures to promote public policy in this area; and participates in the development of the quantitative and qualitative indicators needed for the gender equality monitoring system. The National Strategy for the Promotion of Gender Equality for 2016-2020 identifies the following as priority areas: increasing women's participation in the labour market and equal economic independence; reducing gender pay and income gaps; promoting equality between women and men in decision-making processes; combating gender-based violence and protecting and supporting victims; and changing existing gender stereotypes in society in various spheres of public life. The Strategy is available at: https://www.mlsp.government.bg/ckfinder/userfiles/files/Strategy_Gender%20Equality_201 6(2).pdf. The strategy is implemented through plans that include activities, responsible authorities, financial means, etc. In the National Action Plan for the Promotion of Gender Equality for 2018 and the National Action Plan for the Promotion of Gender Equality for 2019-2020, the competent authority, the Ministry of Culture (MoC), has set out the following measures under the priority area of 'Changing existing gender stereotypes in society in various spheres of public life': • Stimulating talented children of both sexes in the arts, science and sports through the Programme of measures for the protection of children with outstanding gifts from public, municipal and private schools; • Support of creative projects related to the expression, creative development and participation in cultural life, in compliance with the principle of equality between women and men - development of creative potential in the field of performing arts through creativeprojects, in compliance with the principle of equality between women and men and nondiscrimination on the basis of gender; development of creative potential of women and men in the field of amateur creativity, which is carried out through support of projects, in compliance with the principle of equality of women and men. The legislation in force in Bulgaria contains provisions prohibiting discrimination on a number of grounds, including gender (Art. 6 of the Constitution, Art. 3 of the Labour Code and Art. 1 of the Law on Protection against Discrimination) and requiring equal remuneration for equal or equivalent work (Art. 243 of the Labour Code and Art. 14, para. 1 of the Protection against Discrimination Act).  The national action plans for promoting equality between women and men adopted over the last four years have included a number of measures in the priority areas of Reducing gender pay and income gaps and Promoting equality between women and men in decision-making.
Results: o Promoting gender equality. o Reducing the gender pay gap in the economic activities 'Culture, sport and entertainment'. o Stimulating talented children of both genders in the arts. o Annual support for creative projects related to the expression, creative development and participation in cultural life, respecting the principle of equality between women and men.

Title EN: National Policy Framework on Culture, Climate and Creativity

Agency Implementation: Department of Tourism, Culture, Arts, Gaeltacht, Sport and Media
Main Feature: In 2023, the Minister for Culture announced new funding and plan to support cultural organisations to reduce carbon emissions, setting out the vision for the cultural sector to become a leader on climate action in Ireland. At the core of this vision is the preparation of a new national policy framework on culture, creativity and climate action.  The development of a National Policy Framework on Culture, Creativity and Climate Policy represents a world first in bringing together these policy areas, continuing Ireland’s leadership in national policy and legislation for climate action.  The National Policy Framework will provide a responsive framework for action across the culture and creative sectors, taking into account progress to date as well as sectoral ambitions and requirements. To support its development, the department has undertaken an international literature and policy review in this area, engaging in initial internal and external stakeholder consultation. In June 2023, a consultation event with stakeholders from the National Cultural Institutions, arts and cultural organisations from across Ireland, other Government Departments, and local authority representatives took place. The Department also launched a stakeholder survey aimed at the cultural sector, which requested feedback on the policy objectives that should be prioritised in the framework.   Following the event and survey, the Department undertook in-depth one-to-one engagement with stakeholders to identify the specific challenges that the sector faces in regard to climate change and to discuss potential solutions.   In March 2024, the Department conducted wider public consultation to gain the public opinion on the role of the culture and creativity sector in climate action. The survey received a total of 118 responses.   This research base and engagement has suggested that the creation of the national policy framework will: 1. Encourage the cultural sector to take climate action 2. Provide guidance and support to the sector on climate action 3. Provide a structure that enables coordination, monitoring and evaluation of sectoral climate action 4. Embed climate considerations within sectoral decision-making 5. Utilise the unique qualities of culture in the effort to combat climate change 6. Reduce the emissions of the culture sector in support of national targets  It is proposed to structure the policy framework under the three key headings of embedding climate action at the core of culture and creativity, enhancing the sustainability of the Culture and Creativity Sector and Engaging society through culture and creativity.  The Cultural Capital Scheme is provided by the Department of Tourism, Culture, Arts, Gaeltacht, Sport and Media. In line with the Government's action on climate change, this scheme provides funding for projects that reduce an organisation’s carbon footprint and will, for the first time, include funding for organisational energy audits. Projects that provide additional capacity for artists and artistic production, as well as those that address access issues, will also be supported. https://www.gov.ie/en/publication/46f4f-creative-arts-grants-and-funding/
Results: The policy framework is still in development and is due to be published later in 2024

The National Theatre School, turning its attention to the area of artistic promotion and understanding that every training process must necessarily be linked to its innate relationship with an audience, decided that part of this training process would also be accompanied by processes of assembly and exhibition of the results and shows that serve as a platform for learning and at the same time socialize the products of academic training by sharing the works produced with the population. In this way, the training process does not develop in a theoretical or encapsulated environment, but rather confronts its exploration with spectators who will enable feedback and therefore an evaluation of the same process.
Results: The National School of Theatre (ENT) has made a significant impact on the artistic and cultural development of Bolivia, especially in Santa Cruz de la Sierra. Since its creation, the National School of Theatre has trained approximately 2,000 young people in various areas of theatre, of which 250 have graduated, becoming actors, playwrights, directors, technicians and set designers who nourish the local cultural scene.  The National School of Theatre training program has reached an audience of approximately 200,000 spectators through plays produced by its students, consolidating theatre as an accessible and enriching experience for the community.  In addition, the  National School of Theatre has received multiple awards from the Senate and the Municipality of Santa Cruz, in recognition of its contribution to art and culture.  The National School of Theatre has also promoted professional development through international agreements, enabling its stable cast, Amassunu, to perform in countries such as France, Spain, Switzerland and Chile, bringing Bolivian talent to the international stage and promoting cultural exchange.  As part of its focus on artistic employability, the National School of Theatre has organized specialized workshops in scenography, lighting and sound, training young people in technical skills that allow them to access job opportunities in the sector.  Also has trained 250 teachers in theater, expanding artistic education nationwide.  At the community level, the National School of Theatre has contributed to cultural access in peripheral areas of Santa Cruz through theater festivals with Educational Units, promoting inclusion and cultural development in areas with fewer resources.  The National School of Theatre has established itself as a benchmark for training and promotion of theater in Bolivia, generating a cultural ecosystem that enriches artistic life and provides opportunities for the professional growth of young people.

Agency Implementation: Ministry of Cultures, Arts, and Knowledge, in coordination with the Ministry of National Education
Main Feature: The National System of Artistic and Cultural Training and Education for Coexistence and Peace - SINEFAC is understood as: "the set of relationships between agents and actors of an institutional and particular; public, private or mixed order; of norms, resources (physical, financial and other), policies, programs, projects, plans, and practices, which have to do with or have a specific and recognizable function in the field of artistic and cultural education and training, at all levels and modalities of education and that tend to be strengthened in terms of supply, quality, coverage, relevance, and access, under conditions of equality, as away to strengthen the comprehensive education of subjects and as a guarantee of exercise of cultural and educational rights" (Mincultura, Sinefac Base Document).                  This definition includes the different structural and functional elements of the system. Sinefac is part of the National Education System and the National Culture System and is associated with the Science, Technology, and Innovation system. Furthermore, the System covers all levels and modalities of education.                  The general and complementary purposes of the System are:                  a)	The strengthening and development of artistic and cultural education at all levels and modalities contemplated in the educational system          b)	Every inhabitant of the country must have access, through intentional offer, to quality, timely and relevant artistic and cultural education and training processes, throughout their life, as part of the exercise of educational and cultural rights and as a fundamental element in their comprehensive training. Title EN: New Zealand Screen Production Rebate – Domestic
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture
SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Cultural and creative sectors
Agency Implementation: Ministry for Culture and Heritage Ministry of Business, Employment and Innovation New Zealand Film Commission
Main Feature: The New Zealand Screen Production Rebate – New Zealand (NZSPR) supports the domestic film industry and the development of New Zealand creatives. It provides eligible productions, which must have ‘significant New Zealand content’, a rebate of 40% on Qualifying New Zealand Production Expenditure (QNZPE). This is capped at $6 million per production (that is, of QNZPE up to $15 million) unless the production qualifies for an Additional Grant (up to $20 million), which is available to productions that meet additional criteria. Rebate provisions were reviewed under the Review of Government Investment in the Screen Sector in 2022, with changes announced and implemented in 2023. Changes included allowing domestic screen productions to access the NZSPR alongside other government funding, the introduction of interim rebate payments, the introduction of a cap (25%) on above-the-line costs, and changes to the market attachment requirements in the NZSPR’s criteria.  The Economic Trends in the New Zealand Screen Sector reporting is the second edition of this series, reporting data and insights on the screen sector in New Zealand for the most recent year available (year ending March 2021). This reporting series continues and expands on reporting that was previously undertaken by Statistics NZ (which ended in 2019).
Results: Domestic productions accessing the rebate spent around $608 million in New Zealand from 2014 to 2022, including on local jobs, hospitality, building and construction. This represents a significant investment into New Zealand’s economy and far outweighs the cost of the domestic rebate over the same period of around $245 million. Alongside the immediate benefits of productions’ direct spending, there are wider benefits of supporting screen productions. Economic benefits include skills development, attracting tourism, and contributing to New Zealand’s goal of becoming a high-wage, low emissions economy. Cultural benefits include showcasing our unique New Zealand stories, perspectives, and identity on screen.
Financial Ressources: The NZSPR – New Zealand (and associated monitoring, reporting and evaluation) is funded through a Multi-year Budget Appropriation, providing grant assistance to screen productions. The appropriation for the period FY24/25 to 25/26 is around USD$50 million (NZD$80 million) Funding is reviewed through annual budget processes.

It aims to provide opportunities for youth to develop their skills in filmmaking and support emerging talent through grants, training, and resources. The programme includes workshops, mentorship and funding opportunities for film projects.
Results: The NFVF Youth Filmmaker Project has demonstrated significant achievements since its inception:  •	Film Production: The project has successfully facilitated the production of over 50 short films created by young filmmakers. •	Awards and Recognition: Several films have garnered awards at local and international film festivals, highlighting the talent and potential of the participating youth. •	Skill Development: Participants have reported substantial improvement in their filmmaking skills, including technical proficiency and storytelling capabilities. They have been able to successfully apply for funding independently after the programme and some have been identified and hired to work in different productions.  •	Audience Engagement: With the SABC partnership the films produced have reached diverse audiences, contributing to the cultural dialogue and broadening the visibility of emerging filmmakers.
Recommandations: The evaluation of the NFVF Youth Filmmaker Project has yielded several key conclusions and recommendations: Strengths: The project has successfully nurtured emerging talent and produced high-quality films that have received notable recognition. The educational and mentorship components are well-regarded by participants. Areas for Improvement: Some challenges identified include limited funding for production and post-production phases, which could impact the quality and scope of the final projects. The project is very demanding on the participants and we should consider introducing mental health experts for their well-being.  Recommendations: More funding is required. Increased collaboration with industry partners could also provide more comprehensive support for participants.

Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture

Agency Implementation: Ministère chargé des Arts et la Culture
Main Feature: Le document de Politique Nationale de la Culture de la République Centrafricaine est élaboré en vue de permettre au Ministère en charge de la Culture de :  - concevoir et de mettre en œuvre des plans d’actions coordonnés pour le développement harmonieux et soutenu du secteur ;  - mobiliser les moyens indispensables pour la préservation et la promotion de la Culture nationale en conjuguant les efforts de tous les acteurs et des partenaires aux niveaux national et international ;  - disposer d’un plan d’actions à court et moyen terme (2021-2025) devant servir d’appui à l’action de plaidoyer à mener en faveur du renforcement de la place de la culture dans les stratégies et plans de développement et dans la mobilisation d’investissements privés, ainsi que dans la recherche de nouveaux partenariats.  En effet, la vision de la Politique Nationale de la Culture consiste à faire du secteur une ressource importante au service de la cohésion sociale, de la paix, de la promotion de la créativité, de la création de richesses, en vue du développement, de l’épanouissement intégral de l’Homme et de la Nation centrafricaine, dans une optique de préservation de nos valeurs ancestrales et de leur enrichissement à travers un dialogue permanent avec les autres Cultures du monde. De façon générale, la Politique Culturelle Nationale prend en compte toute la « chaine des valeurs » des fonctions structurant la filière, qui permet d’ajouter de la valeur économique aux créations artistiques et aux ressources issues du patrimoine culturel. Art. 6 Quotas are guaranteed in all promotion notices carried out with resources from Law No. 14,399, of 2022, of at least: (...) III – five percent for people with disabilities.  CHAPTER VII - AFFIRMATIVE ACTIONS FOR PEOPLE WITH DISABILITIES AND ACCESSIBILITY MEASURES Art. 16. Public selection procedures may provide for measures that contemplate and encourage the protagonism of cultural agents with disabilities, as provided for in Law No. 13,146, of July 6, 2015 - Brazilian Law for the Inclusion of Persons with Disabilities (Statute of the Person with Disabilities), through the adoption of affirmative actions referred to in art. 2nd, with a view to promoting cultural projects: I - carried out by individuals with disabilities; II - carried out by legal entities that contain people with disabilities in positions of creation, direction, production, coordination and creative management of the project; III - with themes related to accessibility and people with disabilities; IV - focused on training actions on accessibility; or V - aimed at the professional qualification of people with disabilities in cultural production chains.  Art. 17. The following are considered accessibility resources implemented in the publication of notices: I - formats accessible by screen reader software or other assistive technologies, allowing reading with synthesized voice, character enlargement and different contrasts; II - formatting with basic marking elements, such as title, paragraphs and lists; III - simple language, with clear and understandable information, avoiding complex languages and acronyms; IV - textual description of images; V - use of the Brazilian Sign Language - Libras.  Art. 18. Public selection procedures must provide that the project, initiative or space competing in public selection offers architectural, communicational and attitudinal accessibility measures compatible with the characteristics of the products resulting from the object, in order to include: I - in architectural accessibility measures: accessibility resources to allow access for people with disabilities, reduced mobility or elderly people to places where cultural activities take place and to accessory spaces, such as bathrooms, eating areas, circulation, stages and dressing rooms; creation of reserved parking spaces; forecast of duly identified preferential queues; II - in communicational accessibility measures: accessibility resources to allow access by people with intellectual, hearing or visual disabilities to the content of cultural products generated by the project, initiative or space, with reserved spaces for deaf people, preferably at the front from the stage where the sign language interpreters are located; It is III - in attitudinal accessibility measures: the hiring of sensitized and trained professionals to assist visitors and users with different disabilities and for the development of accessible cultural projects from their conception, including the participation of consultants and collaborators with disabilities and representation in the teams of cultural spaces and in the themes of exhibitions, shows and cultural offers in general.  Art. 19. Resources from: I - architectural accessibility: a) accessible routes, with maneuvering space for wheelchairs, including on stages and dressing rooms; b) tactile floor; c) ramps; d) elevators suitable for people with disabilities; e) handrails and guardrails; f) women's and men's bathrooms adapted for people with disabilities; g) parking spaces for people with disabilities; h) seats for obese people, people with reduced mobility, disabled people and elderly people; i) adequate lighting; j) other resources that allow access for people with reduced mobility, elderly people and people with disabilities; II - communicational accessibility: a) Brazilian Sign Language - Libras; b) Braille system; c) tactile signaling or communication system; d) audio description; e) subtitles for the deaf and deaf; f) simple language; g) texts adapted for screen reader software; It is h) other resources that allow accessible communication for people with disabilities; III - attitudinal accessibility: a) training of teams working on cultural projects; b) hiring professionals with disabilities and professionals specialized in cultural accessibility; c) training and awareness raising of cultural agents, the public and everyone involved in the cultural production chain; It is d) other measures aimed at eliminating ableist attitudes .  Art. 20. The project, initiative or space that competes in public selection resulting from the provisions of this Normative Instruction will offer accessibility measures compatible with the characteristics of the object and will provide for measures that contemplate and encourage the protagonism of cultural agents with disabilities, under the terms of § 5 of art. 9th of Decree No. 11,740, of 2023. Single paragraph. The resources to be used in accessibility measures will be included in the costs of the project, initiative or space, from its conception.  Art. 21. The promotional materials for cultural products resulting from the project, initiative or cultural space will be made available in formats accessible to people with disabilities, will contain information about the accessibility resources made available, and universal symbols that indicate the accessibility available of express and visible form.”

Title EN: Nouvelle loi relative à l’industrie cinématographique
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture
SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Cultural and creative sectors
Agency Implementation: Ministère de la Culture et des Arts
Main Feature: La promulgation de la loi n°24-07 du 29 avril 2024 relative à l’industrie cinématographique, fixe les dispositions applicables à l’industrie cinématographique notamment celles relatives à la production, à la distribution, à l’exploitation des films cinématographiques et à leur promotion par tous supports, ainsi que l’organisation des activités y afférentes. Elle inscrit, à ce titre, l'Algérie dans une nouvelle ère de son histoire culturelle et artistique de sorte à ce qu’elle concrétise :   •	la relance des industries culturelles et cinématographiques, à travers des incitations et la garantie d’un climat favorable aux producteurs ; •	l’encouragement de l'investissement ; •	la libération des initiatives en vue d’ériger l'Algérie en pôle régional et international de production cinématographique. Cet intérêt particulier accordé à l'industrie cinématographique témoigne de la place qu'occupe ce secteur dans la stratégie du développement durable du pays, mettant en avant "la nécessité de rassembler tous les acteurs, chacun en ce qui le concerne, autour de l’enrichissement et l’élaboration de ce texte juridique, qui a permis de développer une loi intégrée qui tend vers : •	la mise en place de bases et de mécanismes répondant aux aspirations des professionnels et conformes aux choix économiques du pays, •	la relance cinématographique majeure en adéquation avec les grands défis qui attendent le pays ; •	la protection de l'identité culturelle algérienne, d’autant que le cinéma est de taille à façonner, à valoriser et à développer cette dernière ; •	la réalisation du rayonnement culturel du pays à l'étranger ; •	la promotion de la diplomatie cinématographique comme l’un des outils les plus performants sur lequel misent les pays pour la promotion de leur culture et la réalisation de leurs intérêts stratégiques. Cette loi, qui constitue un cadre juridique pour cette industrie, permet entre-autres :  •	de s’adapter aux grandes mutations que connait le monde, notamment numériques et technologiques, •	d'asseoir des bases et des mécanismes, adaptés aux choix économiques du pays, à même de répondre aux aspirations des professionnels de cette industrie,  •	de définir avec précision les règles essentielles de la pratique des activités relatives à l'industrie cinématographique,  •	de consacrer la liberté de pratiquer différentes activités cinématographiques dans le respect de la Constitution, des lois de la République, des valeurs et constantes nationales, de l'islam, du référent religieux national ainsi que d'autres religions, de la souveraineté et de l'unité nationales, de l'intégrité territoriale, des intérêts suprêmes de la Nation, des principes de la Révolution du 1er  novembre 1945, de la dignité des individus, en plus de bannir le discours de discrimination et de haine. Une lecture de cette loi permet de faire ressortir quatre (04) axes majeurs : 1°- Une redéfinition précise des différents concepts et métiers de l’industrie cinématographique à savoir : l’industrie cinématographique, le service cinématographique, l’audiovisuel, le film cinématographique, le film de court métrage, le film de long métrage, le film documentaire, le film amateur, le générique, la production cinématographique, la coproduction, le producteur, le producteur associé, le producteur délégué, le producteur exécutif, le réalisateur, la distribution cinématographique, le distributeur, l’exploitation cinématographique, l’exploitant, l’établissement d’exploitation cinématographique, la plate-forme électronique, les services concernés sous tutelle du Ministère chargé de la Culture, le visa culturel. Ce sont là autant de concepts et de métiers qui ont été adaptés aux différents changements et mutation qu’a connu le monde d’une manière générale et l’Algérie en particulier, de sorte à garantir le renouveau insufflé et voulu pour l’industrie cinématographique en Algérie. 2°- L’exercice des activités relatives à l’industrie cinématographique : il s’agit d’un recadrage de l’exercice des activités relatives à l’industrie cinématographique, d’une pratique régie dans un cadre réglementaire soucieux de préserver les droits inhérents aux acteurs de l’industrie cinématographique et à leurs créations notamment en matière de production cinématographique, de distribution cinématographique, d’exploitation cinématographique dans les salles, multiplex de salles de cinéma et espaces de projection publics, ou par supports d’enregistrement, procédés de diffusion télévisuelle et plates-formes électroniques. 3°- Les visas d’exploitation : cet axe traite justement des visas d’exploitation et fixe les cadres réglementaire et juridique régissant leur délivrance, un cadre qui se veut garant de l’équité et de l’égalité des chances et des genres. 4°- Le registre public du cinéma, le dépôt légal et la conservation des archives cinématographiques : cet axe traite de la tenue du registre public du cinéma, du dépôt légal et de la conservation des archives cinématographiques et ce, par la création du registre public du cinéma tenu par les services concernés sous tutelle du Ministère chargé de la Culture et de l’obligation faite aux producteurs de s’y enregistrer. Il traite, en outre, du dépôt légal et la conservation des archives cinématographiques et ce, en prodiguant une garantie de non exploitation des copies déposées pendant toute la durée de leur protection, ainsi que de la protection et la préservation des archives cinématographiques. 5°- Les métiers du cinéma et la déontologie de l’activité cinématographique : cet axe traite des métiers du cinéma à travers notamment une redéfinition technique de ces derniers qui s’adapte au mieux aux exigences contemporaines et technologiques. Il traite, en outre, de la déontologie notamment en élargissant les domaines de compétence et les attributions des contrôleurs et inspecteurs du cinéma, faisant que leurs missions périodiques soient des plus efficaces. Cette démarche s’inscrit dans le cadre de la protection des droits et de la liberté de la création.
Recommandations: Dans ses recommandations, la Commission chargée de l’élaboration, la promulgation et le suivi de l’application du texte a appelé à : •	accélérer la promulgation des textes d’application de cette loi, •	établir un lien entre l'industrie cinématographique et les startups,  •	créer un fond de financement sans intérêt pour motiver les jeunes à produire en la matière et enrichir la scène cinématographique en Algérie,  •	Inciter à produire des films ayant trait à l'Histoire de l'Algérie.

Title EN: Obligations de diffusion : quotas d’exposition et mise en valeur des œuvres cinématographiques et audiovisuelles
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture
SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Digital environment
Agency Implementation: Autorité de régulation de la communication audiovisuelle et numérique (ARCOM)
Main Feature: La loi du 30 septembre 1986 et ses décrets d’application imposent aux services de télévision ainsi qu’aux services de médias audiovisuels établis en France, publics comme privés, des quotas d’exposition d’œuvres européennes et d’expression originale française (EOF). L’objectif est en particulier de préserver la diversité culturelle et de soutenir les industries du cinéma et de l’audiovisuel. Ces quotas s’appliquent respectivement pour les deux couloirs, cinéma et audiovisuel, à hauteur d’au moins :  •	60% d’œuvres européennes ;  •	40% d’œuvres d’EOF.  Ces pourcentages s’appliquent sur le contenu annuel des catalogues de ces services. Les éditeurs de services devant répondre à ces obligations sont définis en fonction du nombre ou de la proportion d’œuvres diffusées sur leurs canaux. Par exemple, les services de médias audiovisuels établis en France soumis à cette obligation sont ceux dont l’offre comporte annuellement au moins dix œuvres cinématographiques de longue durée ou dix œuvres audiovisuelles.  En outre, conformément aux dispositions de l’article 29 du décret n°2021-793 du 22 juin 2021, les éditeurs de services de médias audiovisuels doivent réserver à tout moment une proportion substantielle des œuvres dont la mise en valeur est assurée autrement que par la seule mention du titre, à des œuvres européennes ou d’EOF. Le décret fixe plusieurs moyens de mise en avant pouvant en particulier être utilisés par l’éditeur : mise en avant sur la page d’accueil, dans les recommandations de contenus, dans les recherches de programmes initiées par l’utilisateur et au sein des campagnes promotionnelles du service.
Results: La mise en œuvre de cette politique est évaluée chaque année, d’une part, de façon globale dans le rapport annuel de l’ARCOM et, d’autre part, dans des bilans individuels par éditeurs de services. Au global et au surplus, on relèvera que les films français représentent 17% du temps de visionnage de films sur les plateformes de vidéo à la demande.
Recommandations: Les films français sur les plateformes de vidéo à la demande représentent la proportion la plus élevée de visionnage de films nationaux étudiée par l’OEA dans 9 pays européens (cf. SVOD Usage in the European Union, European Audiovisual Observatory, décembre 2023).

Title EN: Observatorio de Género y Diversidad “Territorio por la igualdad”
Goal: Promote Human Rights And Fundamental Freedoms

Agency Implementation: NATIONAL THEATER INSTITUTE
Main Feature: The Observatory of Policies for Gender Equality and the Eradication of Violence and Inequalities towards Women and LGBTIQ+ Persons of the National Theater Institute, is composed of women and LGBTIQ+ persons from the provincial representations and the headquarters of the agency. In line with the transversal policies proposed by the Ministry of Women, Genders and Diversity, this Gender Observatory of the National Theater Institute organized during 2020 -a year in which gender policies were often relegated- several activities that strengthened its recognition and visibility: “Nochecitas de Conversa: Teatro y Géneros” was a cycle of virtual meetings between theater professionals from different regions to reflect on theatrical practices from a gender perspective.  Another of the activities promoted by this Observatory promoted by the INT were the regional meetings “Teatro Territorio por la Igualdad” (Theater Territory for Equality). This consisted of a series of virtual meetings held among representatives, groups, groups, representatives of the regions and people linked to the performing arts throughout the national territory. The objective was to present this new institutional space and establish the first contacts with the regional communities, as well as to open and strengthen channels of territorial communication on issues related to equality and the performing arts   ideology -political action, criticism, education and reflection- of gender and theatrical activity, culture and society in the different regions. In an unprecedented meeting held within the framework of “Teatro Territorio por la igualdad”, the Observatorio de Políticas para la Igualdad de Género del Instituto Nacional del Teatro met with authorities of the Subsecretaría de Abordaje Integral de las Violencias por Razones de Género del Ministerio de las Mujeres, Géneros y Diversidad and the Dirección de Planificación y Seguimiento de Gestión del Ministerio de Cultura. At the meeting, ideas, proposals and projects were analyzed and shared to articulate actions in the provinces for the prevention and eradication of gender-based violence and to receive guidance in relation to protocols on violence and the filing of complaints.
Results: In Argentina, according to the survey Trayectorias laborales presented in 2018 by SAGAI -Sociedad Argentina de Gestión de Actores e Intérpretes-, in which 1116 people participated, two out of three actresses and one out of three actors declared having been sexually harassed at some point in their career. Six percent of those who reported having suffered harassment were minors at the time of the event. 38% of those surveyed witnessed situations of sexual harassment of third parties. 54% of the actresses surveyed performed simulated sex scenes, and of this percentage, 50% said they felt uncomfortable doing them. As for the actors, 51% performed sex scenes, but only 17% said they felt uncomfortable. The coordination of intimacy is a new disciplinary field from which to rethink the working and production conditions of scenes of intimacy, nudity, simulated sex and scenes of physical contact. The advent of it allows not only to enable a space for institutional dialogue, where the affections and emotions regarding intimacy scenes are expressed by all the people who collaborate in their production, but also to experiment new modalities and techniques to increase the feeling of trust, predictability, and consequently the comfort of the workers without losing verisimilitude in the scene. This new approach to stage work evidences the primacy of production processes and conditions over the artistic or aesthetic results of the stage statement. All of them arrive at the rehearsal room with a biography that in the vast majority of cases no one knows. In this sense, coordinating a scene of intimacy implies coordinating the sensitive. In commemoration of LGTBIQ+ Pride Month, a meeting called “Theater, gender: Is there a queer theater?” was proposed to accompany the LGTBIQ+ community and continue thinking about how we imagine the relationship between gender and theater, exchanging different experiences, both from artistic practice, theoretical thinking and policy design in relation to the issue.

Title EN: On the Road Again
Goal: Achieve A Balanced Flow Of Cultural Goods And Services And Increase The Mobility Of Artists And Cultural Professionals
SDG: SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 10 - Reduce inequality within and among countries,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Mobility of artists and cultural professionals
Agency Implementation: Federal Ministry for European and International Affairs, Künstlerhausvereinigung Vienna
Main Feature: In 2021, the section for International Cultural Affairs in the Federal Ministry for European and International Affairs and the Austrian Cultural Forums in cooperation with the Künstlerhaus association in Vienna launched an international call for submissions on the general theme of transformations in society and ecology. Artists from the fields of visual arts and media art were invited to submit works related to the general theme of the call to one of the 23 destinations of the Austrian cultural forums (Arad (Tel Aviv Cultural Forum), Belgrade, Berlin, Bratislava, Bucharest, Budapest, Istanbul, Krakow, Kyiv, Ljubljana, London, Mexico City, New York, Prague, Rome, San Francisco, Sarajevo, Tehran, Tianjin (Beijing Cultural Forum), Tokyo, Warsaw, Washington, and Zagreb). The project was created to provide international perspectives to help local artists survive the COVID-19 crisis through art. The idea was to use the cultural network of the Austrian Foreign ministry and its resources for a post-COVID initiative to encourage artists to start new projects around the world. The overarching theme centred around upheaval in society and the environment, and the way that artists address realities that affect everyone around the world. Our society is changing, as is the economic and political environment in which we live. The Russian attack on Ukraine has brought war back to Europe. And the world itself is changing, not least because of humanity’s careless actions.  The project was continued in 2023 with a second call, focusing on «Climate Dignity». The starting point for the call is a broad understanding of DIGNITY which is not limited to the dignity of human beings, but also considers the dignity of nature and its species. CLIMATE DIGNITY means, on the one hand, that all people have the right to live in a sustainable world in which their health, freedom and livelihood are not adversely affected by climate change. In the spirit of climate justice, this applies specifically to people, communities, and countries that are or will be most affected by the consequences of climate change and are therefore particularly in need of protection. CLIMATE DIGNITY emphasizes, on the other hand, that the impact of human-induced climate change and the intertwined loss of biodiversity not only threatens human dignity, but also endangers nature and its flora and fauna. The “more-than-human” concept of CLIMATE DIGNITY thus focuses on the interdependence between humans and nature in all its manifestations. The 2023 call is an invitation for artistic collaboration between artists living and working in Austria and artists living and working outside of Austria. Results: The CEM maintains up-to-date data in a public register, which has five separate sections with detailed information on all radio and television programmes distributed on the territory of the Republic of Bulgaria by cable, satellite or analogue terrestrial or digital broadcasting networks, as well as on non-linear media services and video sharing platforms. Main Feature: The Piedmont Cultural Observatory (OCP) was founded in Turin in 1998 by Fondazione Fitzcarraldo and other public and private partners, it is ruled an Agreement renewed periodically. The mission of OCP is to collect and analyse data about culture in the Piedmont region. It conducts research to support decision makers and other cultural stakeholders. It offers business intelligence through the time series, analysis of data and information on consumption, economic resources and employment, production and cultural supply focused on Museums and cultural heritage, cinema, performing arts, libraries and publishing. The Piedmont Cultural Observatory accomplishes its mission by two different activities: the institutional activities, the core of our work that guarantee the time series of cultural indicators, and the special research projects, defined yearly or upon request by OCP partners to study specific topics. Some of our main outputs regard statistical reports published on website monthly or annually and the Annual Report realised since 1998 that photographs, highlights and analyses the main factors related to the field of culture in Piedmont, also in relation to the national and international context. We use surveys and interviews to create a report enriched by a set of information, statistical data and insights. Not just a collection of data, but a dashboard to understand trends aimed to help policy makers, cultural operators, researchers and students. ArtLab. Territories, Culture, Innovation is the most important independent Italian event dedicated to innovation in cultural policies, programmes and practices, providing space for structured dialogue between stakeholders from the creative and cultural ecosystem and in dialogue with other sectors, in a cross-sectoral and transnational perspective. Since 2006 ArtLab represents the most significant advocacy activity of our foundation and aims to contribute to the development and strengthening of the role of cultural and creative sectors in society, economy, and institutions; promote the recognition of their contribution to the creation of social and economic value; and develop strategic guidelines and operational indications for professional communities and stakeholders. ArtLab is an annual itinerant project: consisting of two main events, one in a city in the North and one in the South of Italy, along with several satellite events. The project is led by Fondazione Fitzcarraldo ETS, but the contribution to its design and development involves an increasing and diverse network of national and international partners, including over 40 European networks, agencies, and cultural institutes from different countries, public administrations, territorial agencies, foundations, businesses, institutions, universities, and professional organizations. Around ArtLab, an online community has formed, which currently boasts approximately 5,500 registered users through the web platform. This community includes operators, organizations, policymakers, public administrators, banking and philanthropic foundations, freelancers, institution leaders, and stakeholders from the cultural and entrepreneurial worlds.
Results: OCP over the years, thanks to its research and analysis initiatives, contributed to understanding the behaviours and the trends of cultural participation, to the evaluation of the economic and social effects of the initiatives and events financed by our partners. It also contributed to the setting of regional laws about the cultural sector, supported public bodies and banking foundations in the definition of economic measures and interventions dedicated to cultural operators and organizations. In the last few years, ArtLab has promoted and hosted several important national and international discussions on key topics, including: special public-private partnerships for the cultural enhancement of public assets in accordance with Article 151 of the Public Procurement Code; meetings between representatives of the Culture Committees of the Chamber of Deputies and the Senate and the cultural sector regarding various legislative proposals over the years concerning cultural and creative enterprises; the expansion of audiences; training, new skills, and enabling conditions for digital transition; the role of cultural and creative enterprises in the National Recovery and Resilience Plan (PNRR) and cohesion policies; cultural welfare and the role of culture in the well-being of communities and territories.

In addition, biannual working plans have also been designed and implemented with binding participation, and in dialogue with regional cultural policies. On the other hand, and using the study “Systematisation of working plans of the 2020 Arts Education Working Groups, evaluation 2019, projection 2020-2021” (free translation), the following results were obtained: diversity of participants, corresponding to actors from central institutions of the State of Chile, such as MINEDUC, National Youth Institute (INJUV), National Service for Minors (SENAME), among others, and local ones, such as Municipal Education Departments (DAEM) or educational establishments with an arts emphasis or an arts specialisation. Therefore, it is essential that the work they do has a purpose that mobilises different actors and is actually carried through and included in all their actions. Title EN: Partenariat avec la société civile pour l’organisation du symposium Littéraire International  du Togo en vue de la contribution de la littérature africaine  à l’atteinte des ODD
Goal: Integrate Culture In Sustainable Development Frameworks
SDG: SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: National sustainable development policies and plans
Agency Implementation: Association des Écrivains du  Togo (AET)
Main Feature: Le symposium littéraire est une importante mesure illustrant le partenariat entre les autorités publiques et la société civile en matière de promotion de la diversité culturelle.  Afin de relever le rôle de la littérature dans la réalisation des ODD, ce symposium s'est fixé comme objectifs de :  -	Rassembler les éditeurs, écrivains, libraires, universitaires, critiques, journalistes culturels, promoteurs, partenaires nationaux et internationaux ;  - éditer et diffuser les actes du symposium de 2022 et de 2024 - créer une maison de l’écrivain au Togo ;  - recruter un personnel ; - former des jeunes dans différents domaines de la littérature ;   - rendre régulièrement compte des activités littéraires aux autorités et au public ;  - organiser à l'intention des femmes des résidences d'écriture littéraire  et des formations au leadership.
Results: Les résultats obtenus sont : - un cadre biennal de discussion sur la littérature comme un instrument clef pour l’atteinte des ODD est créé au Togo ; - la réflexion et les échanges ont lieu sur les défis de la production, de l’édition et de la diffusion des  œuvres littéraires ; - les œuvres togolaises sont inscrites au programme d’enseignement scolaire ; - les réflexions sont en cours pour la mise en réseau des acteurs de la chaîne du livre au Togo.
Recommandations: A l’issue de la mise en œuvre de cette initiative, la principale conclusion à laquelle les acteurs sont parvenus, est que, le sous-secteur de la littérature et de l’édition peine à impacter significativement la société togolaise et à booster le développement durable. Ainsi, sa contribution à l'atteinte des ODD reste faible.   Pour combler cette insuffisance, la présente mesure a formulé les recommandations/résolutions suivantes : - renforcer le plaidoyer pour la mise en œuvre effective du statut de l’artiste au Togo ; - multiplier les séances de sensibilisation des artistes/écrivains sur leurs droits ;  - créer des réseaux de thématiques littéraires ou sociales ; - rendre opérationnelle la maison de l’écrivain.

Title EN: Participatory cultural policies in Chile. Regional Quinquennial Strategies and National  Quinquennial Strategy.
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture
SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Partnering with civil society
Cultural Domain: Design,Performing Arts,Media Arts,Cinema and Audiovisual Arts,Music,Publishing,Visual Arts
Agency Implementation: Ministry of Cultures, Arts and Heritage (MINCAP).
Main Feature: The Law N° 21.045, that creates MINCAP, states that "the National Quinquennial Strategy for Cultural Development, (...) shall be understood [as] the definitions of strategic objectives for cultural development country as a whole, based on studies and diagnoses of the various areas of cultures, arts and cultural heritage carried out by MINCAP, considering  the contribution of the Regional Quinquennial Strategies for Cultural Development".   In turn, "the Regional Quinquennial Strategy for Cultural Development, (...) shall correspond to the definitions of strategic objectives for regional cultural development, in all its areas, formulated on the basis of studies and diagnoses carried out by MINCAP on the reality of the sector, and considering the particularities and identities of the region. The Regional Quinquennial Strategies must be considered for the purposes of preparing the National Quinquennial Strategy".   The participatory process of these strategies, that began in 2022, is the first of its kind since MINCAP was established, because it involves civil society in the preparation of the primary road map of culture, the arts and heritage in Chile. One of the main differences from the former policies, is that these strategies describe how the actions will be implemented in matters of culture, providing an operational blueprint of the policies for the institution.   Another relevant point is that the "bottom-up" methodology ensures at the regions are those who inform the National Quinquennial Strategy, with the territorial component being one of its specific approaches and, therefore, also for the diversity of cultural expressions. With regard to the monitoring framework of the 2005 Convention, these strategies respond to the "measures that strengthen the skills and capacities of civil society" indicator.
Results: Specifically, in the participatory process, to date, between 70 and 275 people have taken part in the in-person meetings throughout all the regions of Chile. At these meetings, diagnoses were carried out and solutions were proposed for the following topics: "Participation and access to cultural life", "Artistic and heritage training and awarenessraising for the public", "Creative ecosystems and promotion of the cultures, the arts and heritage", "Memories, identities and sustainable management of heritage", "Habitability and management of spaces for artistic, cultural and heritage use" and "Institutionality, governance and citizen participation in public management".   This measure or policy supports equity in the distribution of cultural resources and inclusive access to them as it is based on a "bottom-up" methodology where regions, in a decentralised manner, carry out their own participatory processes and prepare their own Regional Quinquennial Strategies, these being the ones that inform the National Quinquennial Strategy and not the other way around.   Apart from this orientation from the territories, these processes benefit from the participation of cultural agents, unions and associations, which means an involvement of civil society in the institutional strategy planning.
Recommandations: Even though the preparation process of the Regional Quinquennial Strategies has not finished yet and, thus, cannot be evaluated, there are some conclusions and/or recommendations that can be cited from the previous process. Specifically, the absence of an information system that reports on policies, is the reason that monitoring, tracking or evaluation of these instruments are not feasable. In this regard, it was observed that in the previous process, the indicators on all levels of the instruments were absent.   Furthermore, the current instruments related to the national and regional policy did not have an operational blueprint that would connect these instruments with ministerial work. In this sense, connecting the cultural policies with the plans and programmes is necessary, as operational means for their implementation. In turn, diagnoses as stages of the process of policy or strategy renewal, have not been considered and, consequently, are left out when preparing these instruments.   Lastly, monitoring requires establishing clear and previously defined roles and functions, something that was not seen during the previous process.

Title EN: PARTICIPATORY SPACES FOR COORDINATION, EVALUATION AND PLANNING OF CULTURAL POLICIES: CULTURAL WORKING DAYS AND CULTURAL COUNCILS
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture
SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Partnering with civil society
Cultural Domain: Design,Performing Arts,Media Arts,Cinema and Audiovisual Arts,Music,Publishing,Visual Arts
Agency Implementation: MINISTRY OF CULTURES, DECOLONIZATION AND DEPATRIARCHALIZATION
Main Feature: Supreme Decree No. 064 of 2009 is approved to create instances of citizen and state participation for the development of the cultural sector, within the framework of the Political Constitution of the State and the National Development Plan “Bolivia Dignified, Sovereign, Productive and Democratic to Live Well”, and determine the regulatory framework for its operation.  Its objectives are:  Generate democratic processes of citizen participation that propose, evaluate, plan and exercise social control over the development of the cultural sector. Establish national and departmental bodies that propose public policies for the development of cultures, with the participation and consensus of representatives of social sectors. Decentralize and territorialize cultural management towards artists and cultural managers from all departments of the country. Strengthen the direct and equitable participation of artists and cultural managers in the cultural development process.  The Plurinational Council of Cultures is the instance of social participation, of a proactive, consultative and control nature of the cultural sector, at the national level. It is made up of different ministries related to the cultural field, representatives of the Autonomous Departmental Governments, the Federation of Municipal Associations, the Departmental Councils of Cultures, and representatives of organizations of indigenous, native, and peasant peoples.   Its powers are: a) Evaluate and exercise social control over the management of the Departmental Culture Councils. b) Approve the proposals regarding national cultural policies of the cultural sector to be presented to the Ministry of Cultures. c) Deliberate regarding the diagnosis of national cultural development needs. d) Issue the policy guidelines to be executed in the next management of the Plurinational Council of Cultures. e) Define the proposal for a National Plan for the Development of Cultures to be presented to the Government. f) Present cultural projects, to be managed before the Ministry of Cultures and their registration in the Annual Operating Plan and Budget. g) Prepare its Statutes and Internal Regulations.  The Departmental Councils of Cultures in the 9 departments are bodies of social participation, with a propositional, consultative and cultural sector control character, at the departmental level.   They are made up in each Department by delegates from each thematic table of Departmental Cultural Days, a delegate of representatives of the Departmental Autonomous Governments and of the Departmental Association of Municipalities.   Among their main responsibilities are organizing and convening Cultural Days, outlining proposals for cultural policies within the framework of the results of the days, proposing, following up and socially controlling the cultural projects presented to the municipal governments and the departmental government.  These Councils functioned, especially at the departmental level, on an almost regular basis until 2020 before the 2019 Covid Pandemic and the changes of government at both the national and local levels, becoming an important experience of articulation between public institutions and civil society for the discussion, evaluation, planning and even monitoring of public cultural policies, programs and projects.  Another measure of coordination with civil society implemented within the framework of this policy by the Central Government was the holding of Cultural Working Days at the departmental level, also within the framework of Supreme Decree No. 064 of 2009.  Cultural Working Days are spaces for dialogue, discussion and initiatives on municipal policies and activities related to culture and the arts, considering the opinion of society, which should be held every two years. They consist of the formation of two days of thematic worktables in which any interested citizen can participate openly, only having to register and attend.  They generally have two stages: the first is intended to evaluate the current state of the cultural field established by each thematic table, while the second is aimed at carrying out a biannual strategic planning and the election of delegates to the Departmental Council of Cultures. The results of the Departmental Cultural Days, in terms of evaluation and strategic planning, must be systematized and reflected in a Report to be presented to the Plurinational Council of Cultures.  It should be noted that although it is not established in Supreme Decree No. 064, several Municipal Autonomous Governments, mainly in the main cities of the country, held Cultural Days on a more regular basis and based on them formed their Municipal Cultural Councils, as is the case of La Paz (2005, 2007, 2015, 2020 and 2023) and Sucre (2024) since they are established in their laws for the promotion of cultural development and other municipalities, carried them out or generated similar spaces for planning and discussion with civil society for specific issues, such as the case of the Municipality of Tarija in 2021.
Results: The generation of experiences of coordination and joint work between the State and civil society, especially in the cultural sector. The creation of spaces for discussion, evaluation, planning and even monitoring of public cultural policies, programs and projects at the departmental level. Strengthening public cultural management at State levels where there has been a commitment to encourage participation, through involvement either through the Cultural Councils, but above all through Cultural Working Days in the planning and evaluation of cultural policies. The reduction of levels of mutual distrust and the creation of experiences of responsible co-management between the State and civil society in places where the Councils of Cultures have worked best and where cultural events or other similar spaces have been held regularly.

Title EN: Particular Universal
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture
SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Cultural and creative sectors
Agency Implementation: Cultural Heritage, IP and DGARTES - Directorate General of Arts
Main Feature: Particular Universal was a two-year project, centered on the Municipality of Castro Marim (southeast Portugal), based on artistic co-creations linked to the themes of identity, memory, and landscape. The project included different work modules around complementary concepts and strategies, such as, among others, the creation of a sound archive, a community archive for “Vozes da Memória” (“Voices of Memory”) and several thematic artistic residencies targeted at Portuguese, Norwegian and international creators for the production and presentation of theater plays, new music and sound art. The methods used were closely linked to concepts such as immersion, documentation, inspiration, and collaboration, and translate into the involvement of the local population, through workshops and interviews leading to the production of community theater works, sound recordings, installation, acoustic and electronic composition and presentation, exchanges, and mentoring.
Results: Access and support to/for contemporary arts in low-density municipalities through, inter alia: programming of artistic productions, involvement of residents in creative processes and audience development activities. The activities that made up the Particular Universal project contributed to the following specific objectives: strengthening and diversifying the cultural offer in the Municipality of Castro Marim, based on the development of artistic works that were, on the one hand, designed specifically for local communities as direct participants/audiences, and, on the other, created in dialogue with the material and immaterial identity of the region; training and development of local audiences and capacity building in the artistic field, through the workshops held and the skills developed through the active participation of the local community in creative processes; differentiated artistic opportunities, in terms of creation and presentation, for a multitude of national and international artists, promoting a deepening of their careers through immersion in new contexts; direct creation of jobs over the months of the project; development of relationships and partnerships with an international organization of reference in contemporary art and with other artistic organizations associated with it; international visibility for the region and the artists involved through the activities held in Norway. The project impacted on the region's economy (inter alia, its activity reflected in the hotel industry), in the articulation with tourist and heritage areas and in the visibility provided to the region among communities linked to contemporary creation. In terms of sustainability, long-lasting effects are expected from the Castro Marim Sound Archive and the ‘Voices of Memory’ Community Archive, as instruments that will remain available to the public (and added to the municipality's fixed cultural and tourist offer) after the project's completion period, with the training given to the local community aimed at their continued participation, operation, maintenance and expansion, and the acquisition of skills in the area of sound capture, editing software and community organizational practices.
