Title EN: Policies on Sustainable Medium- and Long-term Culture Development Plans
Goal: Integrate Culture In Sustainable Development Frameworks
SDG: SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: National sustainable development policies and plans
Cultural Domain: Design,Performing Arts,Media Arts,Cinema and Audiovisual Arts,Music,Publishing,Visual Arts
Agency Implementation: 1. Ministry of National Development Planning/National Development Planning Agency 2. Ministry of Education, Culture, Research, and Technology 3. Ministry of Tourism and Creative Economy 4. Coordinating Ministry for Human Development and Cultural Affairs
Main Feature: In the past four years, policies on sustainable medium- and long-term culture development plans include: 1. Law 25 of 2004 on the National Development Planning System;  2. Law 17 of 2007 on the 2005-2025 National Long-term Development Plan (Rencana Pembangunan Jangka Panjang Nasional) (RPJPN 2005-2025);  3. Draft Law on Amendments to Law 25 of 2004 on the National Development Planning System;  4. Draft Law on the 2025-2045 National Long-term Development Plan (Rencana Pembangunan Jangka Panjang Nasional) (Draft Law on RPJPN 2025-2045);  5. Presidential Regulation 59 of 2017 on the Implementation of Achieving Sustainable Development Goals;  6. Presidential Regulation 18 of 2020 on the 2020-2024 National Medium-term Development Plan (Rencana Pembangunan Jangka Menengah Nasional) (RPJMN 2020-2024);  7. Minister of Education, Culture, Research, and Technology Regulation 13 of 2022 on Amendments to the Minister of Education and Culture Regulation 22 of 2020 on the 2020-2024 Ministry of Education and Culture Strategic Plan; and  8. Minister of Tourism and Creative Economy Regulation 11 of 2022 on the 2020-2024 Ministry of Tourism and Creative Economy/Tourism and Creative Economy Agency Strategic Plan.  Several policies reported in the 2020 QPR, namely (1) RPJPN 2005-2025, (2) Presidential Regulation Number 59 of 2017 on the Implementation of Achieving Sustainable Development Goals, and (3) RPJMN 2020-2024, are still valid at the time this report was drafted. As the 2005-2025 RPJPN expires, the Central Government and the House of Representatives have drafted the Draft Law on RPJPN 2025-2045. From the draft that can be accessed, the Draft Law on RPJPN 2025-2045 places the Golden Indonesia Vision 2045 as a blueprint for making Indonesia a developed country by 2045, the 100th anniversary of Indonesia's independence. Overall, the Draft Law on RPJPN 2025-2045 seeks to create a cultural ecosystem that is resilient, inclusive, and adaptive to changing times while maintaining the noble values ​​of Indonesian culture. Some of the main focuses of the Draft Law on RPJPN 2025-2045 related to implementing the Convention based on policy directions in cultural resilience, digitalization, tourism, gender equality, and youth empowerment include the following.  1. Cultural Resilience: It is essential to maintain and strengthen socio-cultural resilience by preserving, developing, and utilizing local socio-cultural values. This is done through various community-based activities, including community-based tourism, which aims to maintain local socio-cultural dynamics.  2. Digitalization: Digital transformation is integral to increasing the effectiveness of governance and innovation in various sectors, including culture. This includes using technology for documentation, preservation, and promotion of culture and improving the digital accessibility of cultural information.  3. Tourism: Community-based tourism development is a strategy to increase regional socio-cultural resilience. This tourism model actively involves local communities, especially young people, in managing and developing tourist destinations based on local wisdom and cultural values.  4. Gender Equality: The focus should be on increasing women's role in various social, economic, and cultural aspects. Gender equality is an essential indicator of a more just and inclusive society.  5. Empowerment of Youth: Young people are considered essential actors in various cultural initiatives. They are empowered through their active participation in developing and preserving local culture and involvement in creative and innovative initiatives that support sustainable development goals.  Meanwhile, regarding the 2020-2024 RPJMN, which will also expire, even though technocratic drafts of the 2025-2029 RPJMN have already begun to be formulated, access to them is still limited. Further access to the technocratic drafts is pending till the official start of the term of office of the new President and Vice President and their government cabinet. The target is to enact the 2025-2029 RPJMN through a Presidential Regulation no later than January 2025. Then, reporting on the Presidential Regulation on Annual Government Work Plans starting from the 2024 QPR will no longer be continued because, after being reconsidered by the Drafting Team, it is deemed irrelevant for this section.  Another policy reported in the 2020 QPR but has expired is the Head of the Creative Economy Agency Regulation 8 of 2017 on the 2015-2019 Creative Economy Agency Strategic Plan. This regulation has been replaced by the enactment of the Minister of Tourism and Creative Economy Regulation 11 of 2022 on the 2020-2024 Ministry of Tourism and Creative Economy/Tourism and Creative Economy Agency Strategic Plan. Kemendikbudristek also has a strategic plan, which was not reported in the 2020 QPR. The strategic plan of Kemendikbudristek at the time of drafting this report is contained in the Minister of Education, Culture, Research and Technology Regulation 13 of 2022 on Amendments to the Minister of Education and Culture Regulation 22 of 2020 on the 2020-2024 Ministry of Education and Culture Strategic Plan.  One of the policies related to planning for continued cultural development which has not been reported in the 2020 QPR is Law 25 of 2004 on the National Development Planning System. This Law is the main foundation that provides the structure for national development planning. In this Law, it is stated that the National Development Plan consists of development planning prepared by the Central Government in an integrated manner by Ministries/Agencies and development planning by regional governments under their authority, producing long-term, medium, and annual development plans, respectively. At the Ministry/Agency and Regional Work Unit level, each is required to develop strategic plans and work plans that refer to and are in line with national and regional development plans. Furthermore, this Law also regulates the preparation steps, the person responsible for each step, the implementation time, the form of regulations for determining each type of plan, and several other work mechanisms. When this report was drafted, the Draft Law on Amendments to Law 25 of 2004 on the National Development Planning System had been registered in the National Legislation Program. Still, it has not yet become a priority for completion in 2024.  In general, policies on sustainable medium- and long-term culture development plans are aimed at contributing to achieving the following agenda(s) of the National Strategy for Culture: 1. Provide space for the diversity of cultural expressions and encourage cultural interaction to strengthen the inclusiveness of culture (Agenda 1);  2. Protect and develop values, expressions, and practices of traditional culture to enrich national culture (Agenda 2);  3. Develop and utilize cultural resources to strengthen the position of Indonesia internationally (Agenda 3);  4. Institutional reform and culture budgeting to support the culture advancement agenda (Agenda 6); and  5. Strengthen the role of the government as a facilitator of culture advancement (Agenda 7).

Title EN: Policies that Ensure Transparency in Decision-Making related to the Provision of Funds and Grants by the Government
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture
SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Cultural and creative sectors
Cultural Domain: Design,Performing Arts,Media Arts,Cinema and Audiovisual Arts,Music,Publishing,Visual Arts
Agency Implementation: 1. Ministry of Education, Culture, Research, and Technology 2. Ministry of Tourism and Creative Economy/Tourism and Creative Economy Agency 3. Ministry of Finance
Main Feature: In the past four years, policies that ensure transparency in decision-making related to the provision of funds and grants by the government include:  1. Presidential Regulation 111 of 2021 on the Endowment Funds in the Field of Education;   2. Minister of Tourism and Creative Economy Regulation 7 of 2022 on Second Amendments to Minister of Tourism and Creative Economy/Head of the Tourism and Creative Economy Agency Regulation 10 of 2020 on General Guidelines for Distribution of Government Assistance within the Ministry of Tourism and Creative Economy/Tourism and Creative Economy Agency;   3. Creative Economy Agency Regulation 4 of 2018 on Technical Instructions for Research Incentive Programs for Creative Economy Actors;   4. Director General for Culture Regulation on Technical Instructions for Government Assistance to Facilitate the Field of Culture;   5. Facilitation for the Field of Culture (Fasilitasi Bidang Kebudayaan, FBK); and  6. Dana Indonesiana.  Creative Economy Agency Regulation 4 of 2018 on Technical Instructions for Research Incentive Programs for Creative Economy Actors was reported in the 2020 QPR and is still valid when drafting this report. The same conditions apply to the annual policy of the Director General of Culture Regulation on Technical Instructions on Government Assistance to Facilitate the Field of Culture for 2021 and 2022. The FBK itself was formed to explore an integrated grant scheme using a recipient selection method specifically designed to accommodate the characteristics of arts and culture actors in Indonesia. The 2021 FBK category includes documentation of the maestro's work/knowledge, creation of innovative-creative works, and utilization of public spaces, while for 2022, only documentation of the maestro's work/knowledge and utilization of public spaces. FBK recipients in 2021 were individuals, cultural communities, and social institutions/organizations operating in the cultural sector, while in 2022, only cultural communities and social institutions/organizations were recipients. The FBK theme for 2021 was "Cultural Resilience," while for 2022, it was "Local Wisdom (Clothing, Food, and Shelter) for the Present and Future."  As additional information, the FBK initiated efforts to establish a cultural endowment fund. In the two years of its implementation, FBK succeeded in becoming a prototype of a new management method for government grants in the cultural sector, which later became the forerunner of the Dana Indonesiana program (see Goal 1, Measures that Provide Funds for CSO Capacity Development).  One of the other policies that was reported in the 2020 QPR is of the Head of the Creative Economy Agency Regulation 19 of 2016 on the General Guidelines for Distribution of Government Assistance within the Creative Economy Agency. Since its issuance, this regulation has been replaced several times, most recently with the enactment of the Minister of Tourism and Creative Economy Regulation 7 of 2022 on Second Amendments to Minister of Tourism and Creative Economy/Head of the Tourism and Creative Economy Agency Regulation 10 of 2020 on General Guidelines for Distribution of Government Assistance within the Ministry of Tourism and Creative Economy/Tourism and Creative Economy Agency. Meanwhile, another policy reported in QPR 2020, the 2019 Creative Economy Agency Government Assistance Technical Instructions, is no longer valid.  One new policy in the past four years is Presidential Regulation 111 of 2021 on the Endowment Funds in the Field of Education, which is the basis for the formation of the cultural endowment fund (now Dana Indonesiana; see Goal 1, Measures that Provide Funds for CSO Capacity Development). Establishing a cultural endowment fund is part of the mandate of the Law on Culture Advancement (see Goal 1, Specific Policies that Regulate Culture and/or Creative Economy Sectors). Based on PR 111 of 2021, the cultural endowment fund, the research endowment fund, and the higher education endowment fund are part of the education endowment fund. The Education Fund Management Institution carries out the overall management of the endowment funds under the Kemenkeu, while the management of service programs for beneficiaries is handed over to the relevant ministry.   In general, policies that ensure transparency in decision-making related to the provision of funds and grants by the government are aimed at contributing to achieving the following agenda(s) of the National Strategy for Culture: 1. Provide space for the diversity of cultural expressions and encourage cultural interaction to strengthen the inclusiveness of culture (Agenda 1);  2. Institutional reform and culture budgeting to support the culture advancement agenda (Agenda 6); and  3. Strengthen the role of the government as a facilitator of culture advancement (Agenda 7).
Results: Dana Indonesiana: See Goal 1, Measures that Provide Funds for CSO Capacity Development.

Title EN: PROJET UN JEUNE, UN AVENIR
Goal: Integrate Culture In Sustainable Development Frameworks
SDG: SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: National sustainable development policies and plans
Agency Implementation: ONG SPORTS SANS FRONTIERES Bureau UNESCO ABIDJAN MINISTERE DE LA CULTURE ET DE FRANCOPHONIE  UNICEF  PNUD
Main Feature: Le projet cible essentiellement des jeunes de Yopougon, amateur de football, déscolarisés et sans emploi. Certains ne possèdent pas d’extrait de naissance, ni de jugement supplétif. Ils n’ont donc pas accès aux services sociaux de base (éducation, santé, etc.). Le projet a organisé des rencontres avec 150 les jeunes autour des mécanismes endogènes de gestion des conflits pour leur rappeler les fondamentaux de la vie africaine pour qu’ils prennent conscience de leur place dans la société et qu’ils communiquent ses valeurs dans leur environnement immédiat. Ils seront formés en alphabétisation fonctionnelle numérique et passeront des messages de Paix et de cohésion sociale dans les quartiers au cours d’un match de football qui a été organisé à cet effet. Les jeunes ont bénéficié d’une formation par le Centre Technique des Arts Appliqués (CTTA) de Bingerville, en art plastique, en design/mode, en sculpture/céramique. Ils ont appris également un métier du secteur des Industries Culturelles et Créatives (ICC) dans le domaine des arts, de l’artisanat et de la mode, ont été insérés professionnellement via le tutorat à travers l’Association des créateurs de mode de Côte d’Ivoire (ACMCI) pour ceux qui opté pour le design et mode. De manière pratique, ils ont continué leur formation dans le domaine du football et ont suivi une formation qualifiante concomitamment dans les métiers des arts les cours dans le même centre.  Les jeunes sont aujourd’hui résilients face aux fléaux de l’immigration clandestine et de l’extrémisme violent et contribuent au mieux à la cohésion sociale au sein des communautés et sont autonomes.
Results: Grâce à ce projet  qui lie sport, culture et éducation dans le but de lutter contre les violences et l’immigration clandestine, 150 jeunes vulnérables ont bénéficié d’une formation dans les métiers des Arts précisément en technique d’impression (Design textile, batik, sérigraphie), Staff en bâtiment, tapisserie (formation de lisser), décoration intérieure, design. A ce jour, 65% sont à leur propre compte et 15% sont dans recrutés dans des entreprises en décoration et peinture en Côte d’Ivoire, 10% sont reste au CTTA pour une formation académique diplômante et 5% travail avec leurs amis qui sont à leur compte.

Area of Monitoring: Cultural and creative sectors
Agency Implementation: Pomeranian Film Foundation in Gdynia
Main Feature: The Festival allows for an open confrontation of the film work with the audience, film life observers and participants, as well as journalists. The event is attended by approximately 2,000 professionals each year. Gdynia hosts Polish and international guests: filmmakers, actors, producers, festival programmers. It is the most important Polish film event, thus, a significant part of the accompanying events, such as fora, conferences, presentations or workshops, are addressed to this group of participants. Year after year, due to the development of infrastructure and the growing popularity of the event, the number of attendants increases. Polish Film Festival is the most important Polish film event, holding the status of the national film festival, which clearly contributes to the popularisation of film culture, the promotion of Polish film achievements, and the establishment of the position and reception of Polish cinema.
Results: The Gdynia Festival not only offers a comprehensive programme of panel discussions, consultations and networking meetings addressed to film industry representatives, but also helds activities that serve to define problems and search for systemic solutions.   One of them was developement of environmentally-friendly solutions and joining the signatories of the Culture for Climate declaration, a grassroots initiative for the ecological functioning of cultural institutions. Since then the Festival establishes only responsible partnerships with the companies environmentally oriented. By choosing the services of local companies, the Festival aims to reduce its carbon footprint and support businesses in Gdynia. The Festival promotes less plastic and waste, waste recycling, sustainable means of transportation, and promotion of eco-solutions.  The festival is conducting research into the Profile of a Film Festival Attendee, co-financed by the Polish Film Institute. The Pomeranian Film Foundation in Gdynia and the Department of Socio-Economic Geography and Spatial Management at Adam Mickiewicz University in Poznań are involved in the project. The study measures the impact of film festivals on local development, the profile of the average festival attendee and festival tourist, and describes their cultural preferences.  It also analyses: new media, new ways of participating in culture and changing communication channels in the marketing of cultural goods and services. The reports are published annually.

Title EN: POTOSÍ INTERNATIONAL FESTIVAL

Area of Monitoring: Flow of cultural goods and services
Cultural Domain: Performing Arts,Cinema and Audiovisual Arts,Music,Visual Arts
Agency Implementation: MUNICIPAL AUTONOMOUS GOVERNMENT OF POTOSÍ
Main Feature: The Potosí International Culture Festival was inaugurated in 2009, with the aim of celebrating and promoting the region's rich cultural heritage. This event has become an important space for artistic and cultural expression, seeking to highlight the diversity and heritage of Potosí, a city with a rich history and a significant cultural legacy. The festival's objectives are to highlight and celebrate the traditions, music, dance and art of Potosí; to facilitate the meeting between local and international artists, promoting dialogue and mutual learning; and to contribute to regional development through culture, generating a positive impact on the local economy. The festival is held annually and features a wide variety of activities, including: •	Concerts by national and international artists •	Exhibitions of traditional and contemporary crafts •	Workshops and conferences, with spaces for training and the exchange of knowledge on various cultural expressions.  Since its inception the festival has grown in terms of participation and diversity of activities, attracting an ever-growing audience, characterised as an event of this magnitude that requires considerable investment in logistics, promotion and remuneration to artists. To date, 15 versions have been held, and the festival has continued annually, with the latest version mentioned in 2023, highlighting the participation of national and international artists and a varied cultural program.
Results: Among the results, it has managed to position itself as a key event in the cultural calendar of Potosí, which generated a significant impact in the promotion of culture, attracting the attention of media and visitors, and a boost to the local economy. Likewise, the Festival managed to strengthen its cultural identity, contributing to the revaluation of the traditions and customs of Potosí, promoting local pride and interest in culture. From 2005 to 2023, the presence of national, international and local groups was achieved. There were also exhibitions, conferences, cast theatre, seminars, dances, films, videos, paintings, etc. The support of artists from Potosi, most of whom performed without receiving any remuneration, as did some national groups, will allow a large number of events to be free of charge and to take place in open places such as parks and plazas.

Title EN: Promoting connection and empathy between artists and the community, between art and local life, building sustainable communities in creative practice and art enjoyment, and supporting diverse expressions in artistic creation.
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture
SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Partnering with civil society
Cultural Domain: Performing Arts,Media Arts,Cinema and Audiovisual Arts,Publishing,Visual Arts
Agency Implementation: A Sông Art Club
Main Feature: A Sông is an independent and non-profit artistic collective, founded and organized by artists, mainly operating in Da Nang and Quang Nam in Central Viet Nam. The purpose is to nurture the local community in Central Viet Nam through education and encouragement activities on the arts, such as community gatherings, creation residencies, workshops, presentations, and discussions, while honoring the intersection of artistic and non-artistic aspects in life. A Sông regularly organizes the following main programs: The Cinema Con Nha Ngheo (Cinema CNN) (Cinema of the Peasants), a community screening and discussion program focused on the field of moving images curated by independent filmmaker Mai Huyen Chi and co-curated by Le Ngoc Duy. With activities revolving around film screenings, talks, workshops, and guidance, Cinema CNN promotes the work, practice, and artists on moving images in genres ranging from fictional and non-fictional films to experimental films and other forms of video art. The project aims to (i) provide independent films, artworks of moving images, and discussions on cinema and art for audiences in Central Viet Nam, and (ii) nurture and support local filmmakers and artists on moving images as a way to promote diversity and integration. The Program Cùng ăn cơm (CAC) (Eating together), organized and led by artist Hoang Anh, includes visits to the homes or studios of local artists. Activities include conversations, studio visits, communal cooking, and discussions about artistic practices. The purpose of eating together is to create a deep and intimate connection between artists and participants, establish a safe space for interaction and observation, and facilitate exchanges between artists and audiences. Instead of somewhat distant encounters in an art space or museum, this program brings the audience closer to the lives of the artists. The Artist in Residence program, coordinated and guided by artist Xuan Ha, provides opportunities for interdisciplinary artists, researchers, and art practitioners to explore and learn more about the history, culture, and society of Central Viet Nam. The program encourages research and creative experimentation, creating a space for artists within and outside the region to meet, exchange ideas, and develop their projects. The main purpose is to promote understanding and honor the unique cultural values of Central Viet Nam, while also supporting diversity and creativity in art. In addition to the three main programs initiated and organized by A Sông, we also collaborate with other programs, events, and cooperative projects. Due to limited financial and human resources, combining and collaborating on meaningful projects from other areas to implement in Central Viet Nam is also another field of our operation. This collaboration not only stimulates the region’s art scene, but also promotes the exchange of knowledge and working experience between artists, practitioners from other regions and local people. These collaborative projects create opportunities for artists from all regions to meet, learn from each other, and build a richer and more diverse artistic community in Central Viet Nam.
Results: A Sông was founded in September 2019 by artist Xuan Ha. From 2019 to the end of 2022, she, along with many other colleagues, organized about 15 large and small events in Da Nang and Quang Nam, despite facing extremely challenging pandemic periods. Among these were 4 exhibition events, 2 music and performance events, 4 screening and discussion events, 4 workshop and field visits, and 1 residency program. Through these years of persistent activity, A Sông has become an indispensable name in the Central Viet Nam art community, promoting the participation of numerous local artists in exhibitions, performances, artistic activities and bringing art closer to local audiences. During this period, A Sông also introduced and connected Central Viet Nam artists to events outside the region, such as artist/filmmaker Mai Huyen Chi participating in the Month of Arts Practice - MAP 2020 Heritage residency program initiated and organized in Ha Noi; artist Mi Fa holding a solo exhibition at Mơ Art Space (Hanoi) and participating in the Month of Arts Practice - MAP 2022 residency program; two photography projects by Pham Ba Linh and Nguyen Dinh Phong participating in the 2022 Nổ Cái Bùm art festival (Dalat), etc. Since the start of 2023, A Sông has officially welcomed new members and operated as an art collective. With the addition of new members, A Sông has deepened exchanges and contributed to more constructive activities for the community, initiating three main programs organized regularly: Cinema Con Nhà Nghèo (Cinema CNN), the progam Cùng Ăn Cơm (CAC), and the Artist in Residence program (A.I.R.) From 2023 to mid-2024, we have successfully implemented three Cinema CNN programs, three CAC programs, and three Artist in Residence programs. Through these activities, we have fostered direct and profound dialogues with local audiences, attracted over 5,000 audience arrivals, and clearly demonstrated their desire to access art in their locality. In 2023, in addition to the main programs organized in Da Nang-Quang Nam, A Sông was also trusted and invited to participate in projects outside the region, such as: (i) being invited by the British Council as the representative of the Central region to Belfast city for the 25th anniversary celebration of the signing of the Belfast/Good Friday Agreement (GFA) in Northern Ireland; (ii) being invited as curators for a screening program at the Overshare Video Festival organized by Garden Reflexxx and recess, at Testing Grounds, Melbourne, Australia; (iii) co-organizing and curating the "Lives Adrift" screening and discussion event in Phnom Penh, Cambodia; and (iv) being invited to present at the Southeast Asian Art Forum at the Nanyang Academy of Fine Arts (NAFA), Singapore. This has contributed to building trust for A Sông and has somewhat positively impacted various community groups, not only within but also outside the region. Through vibrant and positive activities, A Sông and its members have been honored and recognized by Hanoi Grapevine’s Finest 2023-2024 as follows: - A Sông was selected for recognition in the Active Organisers/New Organisers category. - Mai Huyen Chi was selected for recognition in the Active Curators/Producers category. - Cinema Con Nhà Nghèo (Cinema CNN) was selected for recognition in the Finest Projects category. - Nguyen Hoang Anh was selected for recognition in the Finest Artists category.

Title EN: Programmation en expositions
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture
SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Cultural and creative sectors
Agency Implementation: FONDATION H
Main Feature: La Fondation H, créée à Antananarivo en 2017 à l’initiative de l’entrepreneur et mécène Hassanein Hiridjee, est reconnue d’utilité publique depuis 2018. La Fondation H opère des programmes dédiés à l’accompagnement des artistes d’Afrique et de ses diasporas dans leur carrière, facilite l’accès des publics à l’art, et participe activement au développement et à la structuration de la scène artistique dans l’océan Indien.La Fondation H travaille ainsi sur la promotion du secteur des arts visuels via :  -	Une programmation d’expositions d’art contemporain La Fondation H a organisé depuis l’ouverture de son premier espace en 2019, une vingtaine d’expositions individuelles et collectives et accueilli jusqu’à ce jour 13 artistes internationaux en résidence de recherche et de création à Antananarivo.  -	Un programme de formation et de renforcement de capacité des artistes visuels malgaches à travers le programme Ainga Lancé en avril 2022 par la Fondation H, Ainga vise à offrir aux artistes de l’océan Indien des bases théoriques et pratiques solides pour se projeter dans leur carrière artistique et la développer. Ainga est un terme polysémique malgache. Il prend ses racines des termes fibatana renvoyant à "soulever", fialana signifiant "départ", hevitra mitombina iaingana se traduisant par "principe de base", mandeha évoquant le fait de partir, et encore tombon-dalana aussi compris comme avoir l’avantage dans une course. Ainga est la combinaison de toutes ces notions et prend forme dans le contexte de la Fondation H par un accompagnement dans la carrière des artistes de l’océan indien à travers l’organisation de workshops intensifs et professionnalisant organisés régulièrement à Antananarivo. Le programme Ainga est entièrement gratuit. Depuis 2023, la Fondation H est un organisme de formation agréé par l’État malgache. Cela lui permet, en l’absence de formations liées au métier d’artiste à Madagascar, de remettre des attestations de formations certifiées par l’Etat aux artistes participants aux différents modules de Ainga. -	Un programme de soutien à la création contemporaine à travers le prix Paritana Depuis sa création en 2017, le Prix Paritana soutient la scène artistique malgache (artistes de nationalité malgache ou résidant à Madagascar) en organisant un prix d’art contemporain, remis chaque année à trois artistes. Son ambition est de mettre en lumière l’émulation créative de la scène contemporaine malgache, et de l’accompagner. Ouvert à tous les artistes évoluant sur la scène artistique malgache et à tous les médiums (peinture, sculpture, vidéo, photographie, installation…), le Prix Paritana encourage le dialogue entre les cultures et rend possible la construction et la diffusion de projets artistiques à Madagascar et à l’international. -	Un ensemble de programme de médiation à destination de tous types de publics  La Fondation H accueille au sein de ses deux espaces, à Antananarivo et à Paris, des expositions temporaires tout au long de l’année ainsi que des évènements organisés en rapport avec ces expositions (conférences, visites commentées, rencontres avec les artistes, etc). Notre équipe de médiation culturelle est toujours présente et disponible. Chaque visiteur est accueilli au sein de nos espaces pour être accompagné, s’il le souhaite, dans sa visite de l’exposition. Nous proposons par ailleurs des visites guidées en équipe, des visites de groupes ainsi que des visites privées en dehors des horaires d’ouverture classiques de nos espaces. Le format de la visite est adapté en fonction du public et du temps dont il dispose. Le programme Hay, dédié au jeune public (2-20 ans), propose des visites et des ateliers sur-mesure et par groupe d’âge, en lien avec les expositions présentées au sein des deux espaces à Antananarivo et à Paris. Hay est un mot malgache qui signifie appris ou acquis. C’est dans cette optique de découverte et d’apprentissage que le programme est mis en place. Chaque matinée ouvrée, tout au long de l’année, la Fondation H accueille des groupes d’enfants via des partenariats de long terme noués avec différentes structures (écoles primaires et secondaires, ONG, associations d’aide à l’enfance). La Fondation H propose l’organisation d’un minimum de trois visites sur l’année pour chaque groupe d’enfants. Les jeunes sont ainsi en mesure de vivre cette expérience plusieurs fois, au fil des différentes expositions de la Fondation H et de découvrir divers ateliers et activités. La Fondation H prend en charge l’intégralité des coûts associés à ces visites (transport, goûters, ateliers, etc.). Chaque mercredi après-midi, tout au long de l’année, des ateliers Hay, toujours gratuits, sont par ailleurs proposés au grand public. Nous organisons tous les samedis un événement à destination d’un public spécifique afin de permettre à toutes et tous d’avoir accès à l’art contemporain et à la culture.
Results: Quels sont les résultats atteints jusqu’à présent grâce à la mise en œuvre de la mesure/l’initiative ?  L’existence d’initiatives privées, depuis ces 4-5 dernières années sur le paysage artistique malgache – agissant pour la promotion de la diversité des expressions artistiques et culturelles - a permis une visibilité accrue de l’art contemporain donnant la possibilité aux artistes de créer, de se montrer et surtout au public d’accéder à une grande diversité des expressions artistiques.  Depuis l’ouverture du nouvel espace de la fondation H (de fin avril 2023 à juin 2024), nous avons accueilli près de 150000 visiteurs dans nos expositions.

Agency Implementation: Centre national du cinéma et de l’image animée (CNC)
Main Feature: Le programme DEENTAL-ACP (« DEENTAL » signifie « ensemble » en peul) a été lancé en juillet 2020 par le CNC avec la collaboration financière de l’Union Européenne et le support de l’organisation des états ACP (Afrique, Caraïbes, Pacifique), pour une durée de 4 ans et un budget total de 3 M€.  Il a pour objectif de soutenir la structuration de l’écosystème audiovisuel des pays ACP et agit sur trois axes :  •	L'amélioration des conditions de création et de production d'œuvres audiovisuelles dans les pays ACP ;  •	La mise en place d’actions de formation à destination des acteurs du secteur audiovisuel des Etats ACP ;  •	Un accès accru aux marches nationaux, régionaux et internationaux et une meilleure circulation de ces œuvres à travers la coproduction ACP-UE ;  Ce dispositif permet :  •	D'accorder des bonus financiers aux projets en provenance des pays ACP bénéficiaires de l’Aide aux cinémas du monde (cogérée par le CNC et l’Institut français) et/ou du Fonds pour la jeune création francophone en Afrique subsaharienne et Haïti (fonds abondé par 12 partenaires de pays francophones du Nord dont le CNC et ses homologues wallon, luxembourgeois, canadien et québécois et administré par le collectif Génération Films au Burkina Faso).  •	De mettre en place des actions en renforcement des capacités pour soutenir la structuration du secteur audiovisuel dans les pays ACP.
Results:  Bilan positif :  •	Depuis son lancement, 46 projets de 14 pays différents ont bénéficié de ces bonus. Un second volet du programme comprend la mise en place d’actions en renforcement des capacités : des dispositifs ad hoc sont construits en lien avec des festivals en Europe (Cannes, Séries Mania, etc.) et dans les pays ACP (à Dakar, Nairobi, Saint-Domingue, etc.) afin de permettre à des professionnels ACP de travailler sur leurs projets avec des mentors expérimentés, d’approfondir leurs connaissances du secteur et de construire un véritable réseau international. •	En 2022, le CNC a remporté un second appel européen lui permettant, d’une part, de prolonger de deux ans le programme DEENTAL-ACP (2024-2025), et, d’autre part, d’intégrer deux partenaires internationaux dans le programme pour la période 2022-2025 : le Fonds de Promotion de l’Industrie Cinématographique et Audiovisuelle (FOPICA) du Sénégal et l’East Documentary Film Fund (DOCUBOX) du Kenya. Des bonus peuvent désormais être appliqués sur certains appels à projets de ces fonds, et des actions en renforcement des capacités peuvent être menées par ces partenaires.
Financial Ressources: 3,2 millions pour 4 ans (2020-2023)

Title EN: Programme for Artistic Freedom
Goal: Promote Human Rights And Fundamental Freedoms
SDG: SDG 5 - Achieve gender equality and empower all women and girls,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels
Area of Monitoring: Artistic freedom
Cultural Domain: Design,Performing Arts,Media Arts,Cinema and Audiovisual Arts,Music,Publishing,Visual Arts
Agency Implementation: Swedish Arts Council
Main Feature: The Programme for Artistic Freedom contributes to strengthening artistic freedom globally, through knowledge transfer and collaboration related to the role of culture in international development cooperation and strengthening artistic freedom globally. Over all, the program contributes to promoting culture’s role in freedom of expression and democratisation on the international stage. The intended outcomes of the programme are: •	Improved conditions for artists to work without being subject to threats or harassment •	In cases where an artist is unable to work in his or her own community, increased opportunities to access a safe haven •	Increased number of countries with legislation that provides improved conditions for artists to freely create, display and distribute their work without being exposed to various forms of censorship •	Increased capacity and networking on an international level, the development of a shared understanding, and knowledge of how the conditions for artists to work can be improved •	Increased capacity of relevant actors to strengthen women’s opportunities to be artistically active  The direct target group of the programme is organisations who work to promote artistic freedom in countries that are classified as countries eligible for Official Development Assistance (ODA) by the Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development's Development Assistance Committee (OECD/DAC).  The programme has 11 civil society partner organisations listed below. One of these is ICORN (International Cities of Refuge Network) within which several Swedish municipalities host artists and writers at risk in two-year residencies.   The Swedish Arts Council also has a continued government remit to support and promote the Cities of Refuge Network in Sweden.
Results: The programme has led to increased support for threatened artists, including legal protection. Partner organisations have worked on establishing safe havens and residencies in various countries in the global south, providing legal assistance and protection. Workshops, seminars, networking meetings and conferences have also been organised to address issues related to artistic freedom and the situation of artists worldwide. Online forums such as digital censorship maps and anonymous chat rooms for persecuted artists have also been established. The programme partners include both cultural and human rights organisations. Some of these operate globally, with a presence in various regions while others work regionally.  Partners have not yet reported results for 2023, but some results from 2022 are as follows:  117 artists from the global south given access to SafeHavens abroad within the Programme for Artistic Freedom (during 2022 alone).   24 lawyers and civil society representatives have been trained to increase their competence to defend cultural rights and cultural actors.   More than 30 legal cases of individual artists have been managed by human rights lawyers, an additional 60 individual have received legal consultation   5 legal cases of individual artists in national courts have been tried   1 case of individual artist were litigated in the European Court of Human Rights  21 artists at risks were given customized training in physical and digital security, advocacy work and well-being  More than 600 cases of censorship, violations and harassments against artists were documented
Financial Ressources: Approximately 5 440 000 USD between 2021 and 2023 (extended to June 2024)
Recommandations: A mapping and needs analysis, including partial evaluation of the programme so far, concludes that current developments in society impact artistic freedom. Trends like shrinking democratic spaces, authoritarian regimes, populism, and conservative values pose challenges for artists to express themselves freely. Global crises and wars add further strain. The pandemic’s continued effects, including restrictive legislation in some countries, continue to negatively affect artistic freedom. Despite these challenges, attention to artistic freedom has grown, and digitalization provides new networking opportunities. However, artists, especially women and minorities such as LGBTQIA+-persons, face increased online threats and persecution. Efforts to support artistic freedom remain crucial, including supporting organisations that raise awareness and enhance understanding of artists’ situations. Protecting persecuted artists and addressing mental health is also essential.  The mapping and needs analysis identifies the need to continue collaboration with a variety of organisations, including those based in the global south, and incorporating administrative support and capacity development into future programs to promote artistic freedom.

Main Feature: In the past four years, programs and events to increase participation in and access to the diversity of cultural expressions include: 1. Facilitation for the Field of Culture (Fasilitasi Bidang Kebudayaan, FBK);  2. INDONESIANA.TV;  3. Culture Advancement of Villages;  4. Movement for Artists to Enter Schools (Gerakan Seniman Masuk Sekolah, GSMS);  5. National Culture Week (Pekan Kebudayaan Nasional, PKN);  6. House of Indonesian Culture (Rumah Budaya Indonesia, RBI);  7. Blora Market Cultural Festival; and  8. Appreciation Program for Cultural Practitioners.  PKN (see Goal 1, Measures that Facilitate Dialogue Mechanisms between CSOs and the Government regarding Policies) and RBI were reported in the 2020 QPR and are still ongoing at the time of drafting this report. In the latest development, RBI has developed a digital platform that allows global audiences to interact directly with Indonesian culture without being physically present. RBI's digital platform includes a virtual cultural festival, webinar, and workshop that anyone worldwide can access. This allows broader participation and facilitates worldwide conversations and discussions between cultural figures, researchers, and the general public. Meanwhile, the Indonesiana Platform, also reported in the 2020 QPR, is no longer operating after the COVID-19 pandemic in 2020 until this report was drafted.  Several measures are relevant and have been reported in the 2020 QPR but have not been declared as programs that increase participation in and access to a diversity of cultural expressions, namely the FBK program (see Goal 4, Policies that Ensure Transparency in Decision Making related to the Provision of Funds and Grants by the Government) and GSMS (see Goal 3, Policies and Measures for Culture Regeneration). As an additional note, GSMS is one of Kemendikbudristek's priority programs in the field of culture, which supports the Merdeka Learning Program.  One of the new programs that has not been reported in the 2020 QPR is INDONESIANA.TV. This program covers a cable television network, website, and mobile application that broadcasts the production of knowledge and information about culture in the form of audiovisual and text content. Hopefully, this program will play a role in building a cultural ecosystem that unites the Indonesian people in diversity, joy, openness, and equality. All INDONESIANA.TV channels are under the management and ownership of the Cultural Media Center, a technical implementing unit under the Directorate of Film, Music, and Media, Kemendikbudristek.   Another new program is the Culture Advancement of Villages program, which results from the collaboration between Kemendikbudristek and Kemendes PDTT. This program is a joint work platform to build independent villages through increasing cultural resilience and the contribution of village culture amid world civilization. This program is one of Kemendikbudristek's priority programs to support the process of cultural advancement and realize related initiatives through empowering village communities. This cultural advancement initiative is hoped to be expressed in the Village Culture Advancement Document, which will then become the basis for preparing the Village Medium-term Development Plan (Rencana Pembangunan Jangka Menengah Desa). The criteria for villages to be included in the Village Culture Advancement program include (1) villages that are located around national cultural heritage areas or have designated intangible cultural heritage; (2) villages around the spice route point, National Park Hall (Balai Besar Taman Nasional), underdeveloped to developing types of villages; (3) villages included in national priority areas; and (4) villages whose regencies or cities have prepared their Regional Culture White Papers (see Goal 1, Measures that Support CSO Participation in Policy Design).  Furthermore, the Blora Market Cultural Festival is held at the Sido Makmur Market, Blora City. This festival manifests the community's efforts to express their creativity and utilize the market as an economic and cultural activity center. The festival emphasizes various important market aspects, including financial, historical, ritual, tourist, and learning values. This festival is a real example of how traditional markets can be revived and empowered through creative collaboration between the community, government, and other stakeholders to maintain cultural heritage, encourage local economic development, and promote sustainable tourism.  Finally, there is the Appreciation Program for Cultural Practitioners (see Goal 4, Policies and Measures that Protect the Social Rights of Artists), specifically organized as government assistance for arts and cultural workers during the COVID-19 pandemic.  In general, programs and events to increase participation in and access to the diversity of cultural expressions are aimed at contributing to achieving the following agenda(s) of the National Strategy for Culture:  1. Provide space for the diversity of cultural expressions and encourage cultural interaction to strengthen the inclusiveness of culture (Agenda 1);  2. Protect and develop values, expressions, and practices of traditional culture to enrich national culture (Agenda 2);  3. Develop and utilize cultural resources to strengthen the position of Indonesia internationally (Agenda 3);  4. Institutional reform and culture budgeting to support the culture advancement agenda (Agenda 6); and  5. Strengthen the role of the government as a facilitator of culture advancement (Agenda 7).

Title EN: Project Diamond
Goal: Promote Human Rights And Fundamental Freedoms
SDG: SDG 5 - Achieve gender equality and empower all women and girls,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels
Area of Monitoring: Gender equality
Agency Implementation: Creative Diversity Network
Main Feature: Project Diamond is an industry-wide diversity monitoring system for TV created by the Creative Diversity Network (CDN). It provides a single online system used by the BBC, ITV, Channel 4, ViacomCBS, UKTV and Sky to gather diversity data on programmes they commission. The initiative is managed by the Creative Diversity Network (CDN) on behalf of the broadcasters. With the support of production companies via the Silvermouse platform, Diamond collects diversity data directly from cast, contributors and crew (Actual data about individuals� characteristics) and production companies (Perceived data about how individuals on-screen might be perceived by viewing audiences). Diamond was designed to answer two questions. Firstly, does the workforce on UK productions, both on and off-screen, reflect the diversity of the UK population? Secondly, are audiences seeing themselves reflected on screen?
Results: There have been six reports published since its launch in August 2016. Their sixth annual report has provided updated statistics for programmes broadcast across the Diamond channels between 1 August 2021 and 31 July 2022. Over those 12 months, they collected nearly 54,000 diversity forms relating to more than 1.1 million TV production contributions4. The proportion of off-screen contributions made by disabled people and those over-50 has been increasing slowly year on year, but these groups remain under-represented compared to population statistics. There has also been an increase in those who identify as Black, Asian and Minority Ethnic - in particular people who identify as Black and those who identify as being of mixed ethnicity. Overall, representation by people who identify as lesbian, gay or bisexual (LGB) is strong, compared to population estimates. Representation is particularly strong for those who identify as a gay man. The proportion of off-screen contributions made by people who identify as transgender has increased in each of the last three years. Overall, on screen, there is balanced representation of gender and good representation by those who identify as transgender. Overall, those who identify as LGB or Black, Asian and Minority Ethnic are strongly represented on-screen. On-screen representation by those over 50 has also been increasing, although this group is still under-represented compared to population statistics. Overall, the greatest area of concern for the industry is diversity off-screen. Over-50s and people who identify as disabled are still very under-represented in many off-screen roles, and progress is slow. The proportion of contributions made by disabled people in senior roles is very low compared to population statistics. Females are making fewer contributions off-screen than they were four years ago, driven by a reduction in the percentage of contributions made in a senior role � from 50.4% in 2018-19 to 45.4% in 2021-22. The sharpest decline in female contributions coincided with the Covid-19 pandemic and the first UK lockdown, which occurred during the 2019-20 reporting period. Female representation is particularly low in the important roles of Writer (32.4%) and Director (25.3%). Many craft roles remain highly gendered, with females heavily outnumbering males in Hair and Make-Up and Costume and Wardrobe, while males remain dominant in Camera, Sound and Lighting. With the exception of Commissioning Editor, those who identify as Black, Asian and Minority Ethnic are still under-represented in all senior roles. Among craft roles, representation by people who identify as Black, Asian and Minority Ethnic is particularly low in Lighting and Sound. Representation by people who identify as South Asian not only remains very low across many roles, it is falling. Disabled people continue to be under-represented on-screen. Contributions made by disabled people have been static over the past three years. The proportion of on-screen contributions made by people who identify as South Asian is not only low, it continues to fall.
Recommandations: The ambition for 2022-2025 is to continue to grow their data collection and reporting, but they also believe it is more important than ever to focus efforts on ensuring that the insights they have developed and shared so far continue to drive effective and pervasive change across the industry. CDN wants to improve Diamond, the �tool�, to increase both the quantity and scope of data collection and reporting. This will include reviewing the survey questions in the context of available benchmarks and to ensure maximum utility of the data. They want to develop Diamond as a driver for change by developing more detailed reporting outputs and data analysis. CDN want to work with the industry to develop and agree priorities and common goals and build a collective understanding of good practice that can drive measurable progress (and also eliminate any ineffective initiatives).

Title EN: Projects for the promotion of cultural participation and regional development through arts and culture: 1.	Kultursommer Wien 2.	Communale OÖ 3.	Supergau 4.	YUKUMOOKT
Goal: Promote Human Rights And Fundamental Freedoms
SDG: SDG 5 - Achieve gender equality and empower all women and girls,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels
Area of Monitoring: Artistic freedom
Cultural Domain: Design,Performing Arts,Media Arts,Cinema and Audiovisual Arts,Music,Publishing,Visual Arts
Agency Implementation: 1.	City of Vienna, 2.	Federal State of Upper Austria 3.	Federal State of Salzburg 4.	Federal State of Tyrol
Main Feature: Cultural participation as well as regional development through arts and culture are important elements of cultural policies in Austria, not only on the Federal Level but also for the Austrian Bundeslaender (Federal States). The following projects serve as good-practice-examples in this respect:  1.	Kultursommer Wien (Cultural Summer Vienna) has been established in 2020. The original intention was to support artists as well as the audience during the COVID-19 pandemic by providing a cultural programme in different outdoor locations all over Vienna. The project has been continued since then. Its main aim is to provide vast opportunities of cultural participation for different audiences (for example families, children, older generations) at different locations (e.g. public parks and places, retirement homes). With Kultursommer Plus a participatory approach is established through workshop and other formats that allow for audience participation. Kultursommer Wien aims at providing barrier-free, inclusive possibilities for cultural participation for all people living in Vienna. It, thus, also serves as an important cultural policy tool for the City of Vienna.  2.	Communale Oberösterreich is a festival-like format that aims at community building through arts, culture and education. Cultural and artistic projects are developed in and for rural areas of Upper Austria, focusing on the intersection of culture and society. Communale Oberösterreich promotes cultural participation and education as well as (artistic) experimentation. Communale Oberösterreich contributes to regional development through a diverse, participatory and interdisciplinary programme, involving regional artists, cultural initiatives and the local population. An important pillar of the project is to provide educational opportunities for people living in decentralized and rural areas, focusing on social learning and political education. Special emphasis is placed on programmes for children and youth.  3.	Supergau Festival in the Federal State of Salzburg was established in 2021. Artists from various disciplines are invited to show with their works that rural regions can be extraordinary places for contemporary art. The countryside becomes an art space that unfolds in a complementary way to the existing art spaces in the city. The aim is not to compete with the city, but to expand the field of artistic activity. Through the cooperation of municipalities, residents and artists, Supergau, a new artistic district in the province of Salzburg, is created for the duration of 10 days. Supergau is organised by the Federal State of Salzburg and contributes to the implementation of the cultural development plan of the Federal State of Salzburg. The province of Salzburg is thus expressly committed to the promotion of contemporary art production, with which new approaches are developed, realised and shown. The project is funded with EUR 600,000 per festival.  4.  YUKUMOOKT (Yunges Kulturmonat Oktober) was launched by the Federal State of Tyrol in 2023. The project aims at strengthening cultural participation of young people, promoting their interest in arts and culture and encouraging them to get involved in artistic projects. Children, families, schools and youth centres are invited to discover their (cultural) environment and develop projects together with (local) artists and architects. The direct exchange between artists, architects and young people makes the creative potential of young people visible while at the same time strengthening cultural participation. Additionally, the project provides opportunities for cultural institutions to develop cultural participation programmes for a young audience and thus strengthen their outreach to this target group. In 2023, a total of 803 children and young people participated in cultural programmes in 16 one-day and multi-day events at 13 different locations throughout Tyrol. A total of 25 artists and architects were involved in the projects. The project is a first step to establish a network and platform for cultural education (focusing on young people) and will be continued in 2024.

Title EN: PROMOCIÓN QHAPAQ ÑAN
Goal: Integrate Culture In Sustainable Development Frameworks
SDG: SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: International cooperation for sustainable development
Agency Implementation: MINISTRY OF FOREIGN AFFAIRS
Main Feature: In 2024, we celebrate the Decade of the Qhapaq Ñan or Andean Road System, which was inscribed on the UNESCO World Heritage List, in the Cultural Itinerary category, on June 21, 2014, during the 38th Meeting of the World Heritage Committee of the United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organization (UNESCO). This commemoration of the integration with a strong cultural and historical legacy of six Latin American countries including: Argentina, Bolivia, Chile, Colombia, Ecuador and Peru, is a common heritage of exceptional value for the Andean peoples. To promote and disseminate the wealth of World Heritage, it was published on the digital platforms of the Embassies and Consulates, and the official website of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, in “Commemoration of the Decade of the Qhapaq Ñan, Andean Road System”. The Bolivian Mission in the Republic of Peru participated in the commemorative events for the Andean Road System. The Representative of Bolivia at UNESCO developed an activity together with his peers from countries that share the Inca Trail in order to safeguard this World Heritage Site.
Results: The Qhapaq Ñan not only represents a historical legacy of the Andean peoples, but is also a symbol of cooperation and unity among the nations that share it, highlighting the importance of its preservation and promotion in the global context. UNESCO has supported exhibitions celebrating the Qhapaq Ñan, highlighting its role as a meeting place for diverse cultures. These initiatives seek to make cultural diversity visible and reflect on the history of interaction between Andean peoples.

In this context, various artistic groups have been formed, such as folk dance, contemporary classical dance, a charango and guitar orchestra, and a choir. Title EN: Promote the development of tools to strengthen public cultural management.
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture
SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Cultural and creative sectors
Agency Implementation: General Directorate of Cultural Industries and Arts (Ministry of Culture)
Main Feature: In order to contribute to the fulfillment of Priority Objective No. 6 of the National Culture Policy for 2030, which is “Ensure the sustainability of cultural governance”, the General Directorate of Cultural Industries and Arts of the Ministry of Culture has undertaken the work of designing and promoting management and information instruments for the implementation of public policies and services in favor of cultural industries and arts in the territory. Within the framework of the health crisis, caused by the pandemic, spaces were opened to identify existing problems and gaps. Public cultural managers at the national level participated in these spaces, where they expressed the need to strengthen their capacities in cultural policies, cultural management and design, formulation and implementation of cultural projects to facilitate the institutionality of the sector. Already in the challenges identified in the CPI Peru 2016-2019, a challenge was posed to strengthen public management in cultural material at the local level. Therefore, prioritizing the development of tools to strengthen public cultural management became a priority for the General Directorate of Cultural Industries and Arts. These tools are not only instruments that guide the work of those in charge of public cultural management at the regional or local level, but they also fulfill the function of training public managers in cultural management and cultural managers in public management. To date, there are 3 guides prepared, after the presentation of each of these, a stage of socialization, subsequent training, and in some specific cases, the technical assistance service is implemented for its implementation.
Results: During the period between 2020 and 2023, we highlight the main results: 1. “Guide for the promotion of the arts, cultural industries and community culture in public spaces”, whose objective is to provide mapping tools, analysis and action strategies, which allow the accompaniment and promotion of artistic-cultural activities in communities . 2. “Practical guide for the prevention of gender violence: Sexual harassment in artistic activities”, aims to provide guidance, approaches, recommendations and tools to identify, make visible, prevent and eradicate practices and relationships that reproduce gender violence in the type of sexual harassment in the artistic sectors of the performing arts, visual arts and music. 3. “Guide for the preparation of culture plans in regional and local governments”, approved in June 2020. It is a methodological tool that allows designing the cultural development strategy of a territory.

Title EN: PROMOTE THE INCLUSION OF CREATIVITY AND CULTURAL EXPRESSIONS AS STRATEGIC ELEMENTS OF SUSTAINABLE DEVELOPMENT PLANS AND STRATEGIES
Goal: Integrate Culture In Sustainable Development Frameworks
SDG: SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: International cooperation for sustainable development
Cultural Domain: Design,Performing Arts,Media Arts,Cinema and Audiovisual Arts,Music,Publishing,Visual Arts
Agency Implementation: Ghana Culture Forum
Main Feature: •	The Ghana Culture Day celebrations have been successfully held by GCF in March every year since its inception. The event features two key activities namely; Interschool Debate and Symposium.  The 2023 edition coincided with the National Delegates Conference of the GCF during which seven Functional Executive Committee members were elected to lead the organization for the period 2023 to 2027. •	GCF collaborated with UNESCO to hold the World Day for African and Afro descendant Culture which took place at the Conference Hall of the Accra Metropolitan Assembly on 24th January 2022. It featured a three-part colloquium under the theme “African and Afrodescendant culture for peace and sustainable development”.  •	GCF collaborated with the National Folklore Board to organize the Highlife Music Stakeholders Conference at the Accra Tourist Information Centre in Accra on Friday, March 4, 2022.   •	With facilitation from the EU Delegates in Benin, Togo and Ghana, GCF participated in the study which was carried out simultaneously within the three countries. The first phase of the study sought to source information to prove or otherwise whether there exist cultural commonalities. GCF was also invited to the validation roundtable which took place on 16th June, 2022 in Lomé, Togo. •	GCF collaborated with UNESCO to conduct a Regional Workshop on Advancing the Anti-Racism and Anti-Discrimination agenda to ensure Social Inclusion and Promote Regional Integration at the Accra Tourist Information Centre on 7th October, 2022. This event featured a constructive and transformative dialogue between Ghana and the African Diaspora on issues concerning racism and discrimination, strategies to ensure social inclusion and integration between people of African descent.  •	A 3-day Strategic Planning Retreat was organized by GCF to develop the Work Plan and administrative framework for the four-year term of the Functional Executive Committee. All seven members of the committee together with the GCF National Secretariat’s Administrator were present at the retreat which took place from 11th – 13th May, 2023. •	GCF’s Functional Executive Committee members paid curtesy visits to key stakeholders in the culture sector including – GCF Co-Conveners/Founders; Ministry of Tourism, Arts & Culture; Ghana Tourism Authority; National Commission on Culture; National Theatre of Ghana; Ghana National AfCFTA Coordinating Office; High Commission of Barbados and the European Union Delegation in Ghana. •	GCF has participated in several key cultural sector events including, Presidential Summit on Tourism (30th – 31st May, 2023); Tourism for Economic Growth and Job Creation Summit; UNESCO-Aschberg Project Stakeholder Consultative Meeting (27th Nov. 2023).
Results: •	The annual celebration of Ghana Culture Day has resulted in improved appreciation of culture among students and youth as well as increased dialogue towards strengthening the cultural and creative sector for socio-economic development.  •	Development of a roadmap towards enlisting highlife music as UNESCO’s Intangible Cultural Heritage of Ghana resulting from the holding of the highlife music stakeholders conference in Accra. •	Increased intellectual discourse towards the incorporation of African history and culture into education among cultural experts from different parts of Africa and across the diaspora resulting from the World Day for African and Afro-decent culture event.   •	Establishment of clear policy strategies towards pursuing anti-racism and anti-discrimination agenda and on promoting regional/national integration resulting from the Regional Workshop on Advancing Anti-racism and Anti-discrimination.   •	The GCF-FEC Strategic Planning Retreat has resulted in the development of a Road Map towards effective leadership in the implementation of the 2005 UNESCO Convention. This includes the development of a Work Plan, activation of the National Steering Committee, formation of the Task Teams and appointment of Domain leaders/coordinators. •	Advocacy visits conducted by GCF in addition to the participation in key national and regional cultural meetings has resulted in a strengthened bond of cooperation between GCF and key stakeholders including - Ministry of Tourism, Arts & Culture; Ghana Tourism Authority; National Commission on Culture; National Theatre of Ghana; Ghana National AfCFTA Coordinating Office; High Commission of Barbados as well as the European Union Delegation in Ghana

Title EN: Promoting access to museums for disadvantaged groups
Goal: Integrate Culture In Sustainable Development Frameworks
SDG: SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: National sustainable development policies and plans
Agency Implementation: Ministry of Culture
Main Feature: The national public service is provided by 46 museums and galleries set up by the state or local communities. The Ministry of Culture, which funds this service, recommends that museums and galleries offer at least one project (exhibition, digitization, educational program, etc.) per year for disadvantaged groups (e.g. people with mobility and sensory impairments, people with dementia). The museums report annually on the implementation of these projects, both in terms of content and funding.  The museums strive for a gradual and comprehensive adaptation of permanent exhibitions for disadvantaged groups and address specific visitor target groups with individual, tailor-made projects. The aim is to make museums permanently accessible to disadvantaged groups.
Results: The measure is effective. In 2020, 20 museums had adapted permanent exhibitions, and by 2023 this number had risen to 33. At least one exhibition was adapted for visitors with sensory impairments by 17 museums in 2020 and 21 in 2023. The number of publications on websites adapted for visitors with sensory impairments and inclusion of vulnerable groups is also gradually increasing. Not all museums keep statistics on visitors from disadvantaged groups. For those that do record admissions, the proportion of visitors from disadvantaged groups does not even reach 1% of the total number of visitors. In 2023, 8 national museums ran 568 accompanying programs for children, of which 40 were adapted for disadvantaged groups; 29 out of 336 programs were adapted for young people and 43 out of 706 accompanying programs were adapted for adults. Six museums are part of UNICEF's Safe Places for Children network and four are part of the Dementia Friendly Points network. The permanent exhibitions in the museums are adapted for visitors with limited sensory abilities, and access is also regulated (elevators, ramps, induction loops). Accessibility is also ensured by sensory-friendly museum websites and free general admission on the first Sunday of every month in all national museums.

Title EN: Promotion des instrumentistes d’Afrique à travers le festival des Meilleurs Instrumentistes d’Afrique

Main Feature: Le projet d’ « appui à la promotion et à la valorisation des musiciens instrumentistes africains » a pour ambition de célébrer les instrumentistes du continent à travers plusieurs offres d’activités capables de les aider à mieux se professionnaliser pour se révéler davantage performants et gérer convenablement leur carrière. Il a commencé en 2014 en République du Bénin et prend en compte les professionnels des autres pays du continent et de la diaspora.  Le but fondamental du projet est de créer une saine émulation entre les instrumentistes du continent en tissant des liens interrelationnels et intergénérationnels pour maintenir la flamme du savoir-faire des instrumentistes face à la montée en puissance des programmes de composition assistée à l’Ordinateur ; une réalité qui met en péril le métier d’instrumentistes sur le continent et par ricochet met aussi  le patrimoine matériel et immatériel des Communautés sur le Continent, faute de transmission des savoir-faire dans ce secteur.  Au-delà des instrumentistes, le projet prend en compte toute la chaîne de la logistique événementielle à travers la promotion et le renforcement de capacité des différents acteurs des corps de métiers de la logistique du spectacle vivant : régisseurs son et lumière, monteur de scène, décorateurs, costumiers animateurs et présentateurs live, opérateurs de prise de vue, chefs plateau, réalisateur de scène, vendeurs et fabricants d’instruments de musique,  etc.  Pour mettre tout ce programme en orchestration, le programme lance annuellement un festival de musique live, intitulé Festival des Meilleurs Instrumentistes d’Afrique (Festival MIA) pour offrir aux musiciens instrumentistes du continent africain, une tribune d’expression et de distinction.
Results: Après 09 éditions le festival des meilleurs instrumentistes d’Afrique le palmarès se présente comme suit :  -	20 artistes instrumentistes internationaux sont honorés -	30 instrumentistes lauréats sont primés et promus  -	10 orchestres de la musique traditionnels sont programmés et promus  -	200 orchestres reçus à Cotonou venant du Bénin, Togo, de la Côte d’Ivoire, du Burkina Faso, du Niger, du Mali, du Sénégal, du Congo et de la diaspora -	12 Tables-rondes sur les thématiques relatives à  la promotion des carrières artistiques sont organisées avec la participation des acteurs culturels et les professionnels des médias -	20 sessions de formation en régie son et lumière et logisticien de la scène sont organisées  -	07 éditions du Salon de la logistique événementielle et de l’audiovisuel sont organisées -	05 orchestres pépinières sont créés pour assurer la relève au niveau du secteur  -	01 étude dans le but de réaliser une cartographie des instrumentistes à vent du Bénin est en cours
