Advocacy meetings with the members of the Constitution and Legal Affairs Committee,   5. Meetings with legislators on the need to Amend the National Arts Act.No 23 of 1984.

Title EN: Promoting the Creative Development of Young People
Goal: Integrate Culture In Sustainable Development Frameworks
SDG: SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: National sustainable development policies and plans
Agency Implementation: Ministry of Culture
Main Feature: The Ministry of Culture operates to promote the creative development of young people, including children and school students from ethnic communities.  During the 2020- 2023 period, annual scholarships and one-off financial support have been provided by the Ministry of Culture, the Ministry of Education and Science, the Ministry of Youth and Sports and municipalities.  Each calendar year these Programmes provide USD 1,041,624 from the central budget for scholarships and one-off grants to over 1000 children and school students with evident talents who study at public, municipal and private schools. In 2023, the funds have been increased for the first time to USD 1,106,440. The number of children has gradually increased over the years and by 2023 there are 1,330 children assisted.  There is regular institutional and financial support for the exposure and development of young talents directed at organising festivals, gatherings, contests, exhibitions, performances, and other events that enable appearance and development of young talents. The events are supported by contest sessions run by the Ministry of Culture in the fields of theatre, music and dance. They are organised by art schools, community centres, other non-governmental organisations, often with assistance from municipal administrations. Part of the consistent policy for encouraging, preserving and promoting cultural diversity is the annual selection and presentation of key events and festivals of the Roma community throughout Bulgaria as genre highlights in the Cultural Calendar with national coverage prepared by the Ministry of Culture.  Another area of this policy is providing contemporary conditions to implement a quality educational process and to prepare highly qualified professionals in the arts and culture field. In this respect, the Arts and Culture Training Programme provides support and methodological guidance to 23 arts and culture schools. Schools conduct training in professions, which are of strategic importance for the country, and in majors related to preserving national identity, traditions and culture, providing personnel with artistic and creative potential, developing Bulgarian culture and arts, and implementing the cultural policy of Bulgaria.
Results: During the 2020-2023 period, annual scholarships and one-off financial support have been provided by the Ministry of Culture, the Ministry of Education and Science, the Ministry of Agriculture and Foods, the Ministry of Youth and Sports and municipalities.  Each calendar year these Programmes provide USD 1,041,624 from the central budget for scholarships and one-off grants to over 1000 children and school students with evident talents who study at public, municipal and private schools. In 2023, the funds have been increased for the first time to USD 1,106,440. The number of children has gradually increased over the years and by 2023 there are 1,330 children assisted.  At the same time, integration processes are being implemented and conditions are being created for non-formal and informal lifelong learning, for equal access to human knowledge, for communication and awareness, for promoting cultural diversity, for overcoming discrimination, racism and intolerance, and for intergenerational continuity.  Activities focused on children and young people promote the diversity of cultural expression forms.
Financial Ressources: From the state budget - USD 1 041 624 per year - from 2023 - USD 1 106 440 per year
Recommandations: The measure is highly assessed, it has contributed over the years, and tends towards expanding.  Website – mc.government.bg, “Protection of Children with Evident Talents” section.

Title EN: Promoting wellbeing for the elderly through culture
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture
SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Cultural and creative sectors
Cultural Domain: Performing Arts,Media Arts,Cinema and Audiovisual Arts,Music
Agency Implementation: Arts Promotion Centre
Main Feature: Arts and culture have an impact on the wellbeing, functional capacity and health of elderly people. The key impact objective of the measure was to target preventive measures that improve functional capacity of the older population.  As part of the National Programme on Ageing 2030: For an age-competent Finland Arts Promotion Centre implemented project entities, which aimed at promoting well-being for elderly through culture. The objective of the project entities was to strengthen the cultural wellbeing activities of various actors and regions. The projects directly or indirectly also promoted the employment of artists in the sector of culture for health and well-being.   In the projects operating models for cultural broadcasting and outreach cultural work were developed. The projects focused on cooperation between wellbeing services counties and municipalities in the promotion of health and wellbeing. The results of the projects included good practices in artistic activities and coordination, quality recommendations for well-being of elderly people through culture and the recommended measures for the Finnish model for culture for health and well-being aimed at the ageing population  The project entity was part of the national age programme administered by the Ministry of Social Affairs and Health (MSAH). The programme extensively prepares for the ageing of the population. The programme's projects encourage people to ensure that older people are as functional as possible. One of the objectives is an economically and socially sustainable service system.
Results: The implementation of the measure has resulted in a recommendation for a Finnish model of cultural services for older people. The recommendation state that high-quality services for the elderly population include culture. An example of an operating model that promote that objective is the operating model of outreach cultural work for older people that promotes older people's functional capacity and inclusion through arts and culture.
Financial Ressources: 2,1 million USD
Recommandations: Developing the operating conditions of artists working with cultural wellbeing for the elderly calls for improvements in the basic, general conditions for cultural wellbeing activities. Accordingly, we have presented recommendations in six interconnected categories:    1) objectives, strategies and influence,    2) funding,    3) coordination,    4) understanding and competencies,    5) operating models, and    6) effectiveness and information needs.     The recommendations can be summarized as follows: cultural wellbeing needs to become a fixed element in decision making and steering systems and its significance should be made clearer to the decision makers especially in the context of wellbeing services counties; permanent funding solutions where the health and social services sector has a stronger role should be developed; cultural wellbeing activities should be coordinated more effectively especially at regional level, commissioning competencies in the sector need developing; and actors in the sector need a better understanding of the impacts and significance of cultural wellbeing activities.   The operating models should be consistent, scalable and at the same time flexible enough to take local specificities into account. In the context of impacts and information needs, existing data collections should be utilized and applied more effectively and collaboration structures should be created to develop concepts, methods and technical solutions as a whole.    Focus should be placed not only on the general conditions for cultural wellbeing activities but also more specifically on them as an operating environment for artists. The objectives of Arts Promotion Centre (Taike), especially, aim to strengthen the position of artists in the production of cultural wellbeing. In the project funding channelled by Taike, special attention has been given to operating models and the formulation of quality recommendations. These can have an impact on broader structural factors, but their impact can also be seen in the concrete development and systematization of artists’ work.    One should however note that the Promoting wellbeing for elderly through culture -programme has been implemented as a part of broader changes that might be beyond its reach of influence. It is important to maintain the will to keep developing cultural wellbeing activities also along with the health and social services reform, since despite the basic problems there has been steady progress.    Consequently, it would be good to reassess the operating conditions of artists as a part of the development of cultural wellbeing activities also after the situation of change caused by the reform has stabilized.

Main Feature: This policy constitutes a tool to promote the diversity of cultural expressions in the municipality and the dynamization of creativity and innovation in the artistic and cultural proposals in the municipality. This is linked to the strengthening of diversity and the establishment of intercultural dialogue as guiding principles of municipal cultural policies, based on the promotion of cultural processes or projects that can be incorporated into the cultural and artistic life of the municipality and reverse processes of exclusion, segregation and inequality in its various forms.  Since 2018, the Municipal Competitive Fund for Culture and the Arts has been implemented (FOCUART), which is a milestone of this administration and the first of its kind at a national level, with the aim of making transparent the allocation of resources for different cultural areas in six lines of strengthening related to the arts and new technologies, living community culture, cultural spaces and cultural heritage, research and training in arts and cultures, the development of networks, mobility and cultural circulation, and audiovisual production.
Results: 492 beneficiary projects supported by FOCUART from 2018 to August 13, 2024 In 2022, 53.8% of the projects were developed in the Centro macro-district, while in 2023 the most benefited macro-districts were the Cotahuma macro-district with 18%, Sur with 17% and max Paredes and Centro with 16% each, which shows a greater decentralization of the Fund in those two years. In 2022, it was recognized that 74% of the projects applied some practice of creative cultural economy and reciprocity, mainly ayni, minka and the exchange of goods and services. In 2022, it was recorded that the capacities for the formulation of cultural projects increased from 21% to 28% during the development of the projects. In 2022, the areas of project development are the promotion of creative cultural economies with 26%, followed by strengthening cultural diversity with 23% and the promotion of cultural rights with 15%.  In 2022, the projects were developed mainly with youth populations at 54%, and in 2023 the population most benefited by the projects was children and adolescents with 25%, followed by people with disabilities with 16% and older adults with 13%. In 2023, 43% of the Fund's winners are between 25 and 35 years old, and 61% of the winners are women.

It is suggested that the proposal for the following managements considers the policies linked to sustainable development from the cultures, the actions oriented to the Project Consulting Office are strengthened, as well as the increase in the budget.

Les méthodes de dialogue entre la Haute Autorité de l'Audiovisuel et de la Communication (HAAC) et les organisations faîtières des médias au Bénin incluent : Élections de représentants : Les professionnels des médias élisent leurs représentants pour siéger à la HAAC, ce qui garantit une représentation directe et une participation active des médias dans les processus de décision. Main Feature: In order to promote an improvement in the economy of artisans, Mincetur assigned an economic subsidy to those living in poverty and extreme poverty, benefited by DU 029-2023 and, in addition, granted competitive funds to the winners of the "We Are Crafts" contest.  The National Contest “We Are Crafts” is a Mincetur initiative that allows, through the delivery of non-refundable resources, to strengthen the workshops dedicated to craft activity in the country.  The aforementioned Contest is directly aimed at artisans and associations of artisans, companies linked to the artisan activity or artisan cooperatives that are registered in the National Registry of Artisans (RNA) and the Single Taxpayer Registry (RUC) with the status and condition of taxpayer active and existed.  In addition to this contest, artisans benefit from the income tax deduction in accordance with the provisions of the Second Complementary Provision of Law No. 31103, which declares the reactivation of the tourism sector of national interest and establishes measures to its sustainable development (12/30/2020); and DS No. 432-2020-EF, for the application of the Second Final Complementary Provision of Law No. 31103 referring to the additional deduction of expenses from Fourth and Fifth Category Income (12/31/2020).  In order for financial subsidies and tax exemptions to be granted, the following actions have been developed:  ●	Approval of Emergency Decree No. 029-2023, “Emergency Decree that establishes extraordinary measures in economic and financial matters to promote the reactivation of the family economy and the reactivation of the tourism sector and dictates other provisions” (7/25/2023 ). ●	Approval of Law No. 31103, Law that declares the reactivation of the tourism sector of national interest and establishes measures for its sustainable development (12/30/2020). ●	Approval of SD No. 432-2020-EF, Standard for the application of the Second Final Complementary Provision of Law No. 31103 referring to the additional deduction of expenses of Fourth and Fifth Category Income (12/31/2020) which regulates, among other aspects, the deduction of income tax in accordance with the Second Complementary Provision. ●	Approval of the National Classifier of Artisanal Lines- CLANAR, with RM n° 084- 2021- MINCETUR (6/30/2021). ●	Approval of new formats for registration in the National Registry of Artisans, through RVM n° 0009- MINCETUR/VMT (7/15/2021). ●	Approval of Supreme Decree No. 007-2021-MINCETUR, which modifies the Regulations of Law No. 29073, Law of the artisan and the development of artisanal activity, approved by Supreme Decree No. 008-2010-Mincetur (2/5 /2021).  Likewise, to stimulate employment and promote improvement in the economy of artisans, Mincetur held the national fairs "De Nuestras Manos", "Arte Nativa", macro-regional fairs and decentralized craft fairs, implemented the commercial platform "Artesanías del Peru", among other actions.
Results: Since 2021, through Somos Artesanía, Mincetur has received the application of 10,157 artisanal economic units and delivered a total of S/ 18,984,670 ($5,089,724 dollars) to 3,602 beneficiary winners, mainly artisans located in rural areas from the country.  Puno is the region that registers the highest number of beneficiary winners, with a total of 600. Cusco continues on the list, with 445 artisans; Arequipa, with 348; and Piura, with 345. Along these lines, it is important to highlight that 78% of winners are women who have basic education, earn income up to the minimum living wage and are dedicated to crafts as their main economic activity.  Regarding the registration of artisans, to date, 65,201 artisans are registered in the National Registry of Artisans (RNA) monitored by Mincetur.

Title EN: Promotion of gender equality and actions against any type of discrimination.
Goal: Promote Human Rights And Fundamental Freedoms
SDG: SDG 5 - Achieve gender equality and empower all women and girls,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels
Area of Monitoring: Gender equality
Agency Implementation: National Institute of Fine Arts and Literature (INBAL)
Main Feature: The National Institute of Fine Arts and Literature (INBAL) actively promotes gender equality and staunchly opposes all forms of discrimination as integral components of its artistic initiatives. The institute has developed a comprehensive schedule of activities guided by a policy of substantive equality and the advancement of women's rights. Notably, women artists are prominently featured across all artistic disciplines, as well as in conferences, colloquiums, and workshops. Additionally, INBAL prioritizes artistic programming with a gender perspective.  Each year, in celebration of International Women's Day on March 8, INBAL work centers prepare extensive programs throughout the month, fostering a conducive environment for promoting this focus area. The National Coordination of Visual Arts organizes discussions, colloquiums, exhibitions, panels, workshops, and conferences, specifically highlighting the contributions of women who, despite their significant role in Mexico's cultural history, are often overlooked.  Furthermore, INBAL collaborates closely with other organizations and institutions dedicated to providing platforms for female artists, such as the International – Ibero-American Meeting of Women in Art organized by the Women in Music Collective A.C. and ComuArte.
Results: From 2019 to 2023, over 2,500 activities have been conducted to promote gender equality, reflected through four key approaches: •	Promoting the participation of women artists and cultural agents to institutionalize gender parity throughout the artistic process, from conception to presentation and dissemination. •	Programming actions or activities that address or are centered around gender equality themes. •	Highlighting the work of female creators such as composers, playwrights, and writers. •	Addressing and eliminating gender-based violence in educational settings, casts, technical teams, and other contexts.  From December 2018 to 2023, nearly 400 activities have been implemented focused on combating homophobia and supporting the LGBTQ+ community. These initiatives span various disciplines including theater, dance, literature, opera, and visual arts. INBAL also promotes anti-homophobia actions and supports the LGBTQ+ population through its programming. These efforts contribute to challenging traditional masculinities and rethinking the implications of historical gender inequalities and entrenched machismo within a hegemonic heteropatriarchal context from an artistic perspective. These activities encompass a diverse spectrum of gender identities and expressions with which artists and participants identify, including man, woman, non-binary, transgender, cisgender, queer, genderqueer, and non-conforming identities, among others. They are part of the National Day to Fight Homophobia, Lesbophobia, Transphobia, and Biphobia (declared in 2019) and International Pride Day.  The National Institute of Fine Arts and Literature (INBAL) undertakes actions across multiple fronts to uphold its commitment to integrate gender perspective as a cornerstone of its daily operations. This commitment extends beyond its cultural offerings to encompass internal labor relations and its role as a public advocate of gender equality. The Directorate of Institutional Liaison and State Engagement systematically records and analyzes actions with a gender perspective, with indicators from INMUJERES (National Institute for Women) providing significant metrics. These indicators measure the percentage of actions or activities addressing gender equality, its implications, opportunities, and challenges.

Main Feature: This measure is a national competitive fund, implemented in a decentralised manner by CONADI on a national level, that is to say, throughout Chile. Its objective is to support the creation and continuity of diverse artistic and cultural forms of the country's indigenous peoples in traditional or contemporary spheres.   Indigenous expressions are financed in the areas of visual arts, photography, theatre, traditional or contemporary dance, music, oral and/or written expression creations, that help to generate knowledge, training and awareness of traditional knowledge such as poetry, stories, storytelling, traditional indigenous arts and techniques such as textile arts, pottery, jewelry, basket weaving, recreational expressions, strengthening of processes and collective practices, traditional cultural, conmemorative and/or festive expressions that contribute to reviving cultural customs, festivities or traditions such as "Willka Kuti", "Inti Raymi", "Wetxipantu", or the conservation and protection of cultural heritage, preparation of community museums, archelogical sites, indigenous cultural innovation, projects that contribute to generating technological innovation with identity such as websites with indegnous cultural content, mobile applications that promote indigenous culture or language, as well as its traditions, or projects that promote the revival of archaeoastronomy or astronomy, among others.   This measure contributes to artistic freedom as it promotes cultural expressions of indigenous peoples in Chile, within their aristic and cultural manifestations. In turn, it supports re-shaping cultural heritage through works with local sensibilities and roots.
Results: In the last call of the competitive fund in the programme “Fondo para iniciativas artístico y culturales indígenas” ("Fund for indigenous artistic and cultural initiatives"), 128 initiatives  were funded, of which three belong to indigenous associations, 11 are from indigenous communities throughout Chile, 64 women and 50 men, with a total investment of 295,000,000 pesos for 2023, the last call for this contest.   This considers beneficiaries from different regions of the country such as Arica and Parinacota, Tarapacá, Coquimbo, Continental Valparaíso, Metropolitan, O'Higgins, Biobío, Araucanía, Los Ríos, Los Lagos and Magallanes.

Main Feature: The Book and Reading Directorate has been developing the Freedom of the Word program since 2016 to benefit populations in situations of vulnerability or social exclusion through the planning and development of book circulation actions and the promotion of reading and writing. Likewise, it promotes reading in other prioritized groups such as girls, boys, young people and older adults.  In addition, civil society, through cultural managers benefiting from economic stimulus competitions, among others, develop projects in favor of the promotion of reading in vulnerable populations such as those developed in prisons, children, native communities, and the LGBT population. Some of them, such as the program "Remembrances of a life behind bars" implemented in the Santa Monica prison, had as a final product a book, which will be presented at the Lima International Book Fair in 2024.
Results: In 2023, the reading promotion programs, “La Libertad de la Palabra” (LP) and “Reading in Early Childhood” (LPI) have benefited more than 6,700 people, including children, young people, and older adults.    In the case of the LP program, in 2023 it benefited penitentiary centers, residential care centers and youth centers in 19 regions of the country: Lima, Callao, Ica, Loreto, San Martín, Huancavelica, Ayacucho, Arequipa, Moquegua, Tacna, Puno , Piura, Lambayeque, La Libertad, Huánuco, Ucayali, Cusco, Apurímac and Junín. Furthermore, in 2023, the program managed to integrate 18 additional Reading Spaces: 3 residential reception centers; 2 family community centers; and 2 INABIF family recreation centers; and 11 ONP pension homes). With the readers' club activities, family reading and appropriation of the text. With respect to the LPI program, children from 5 regions have benefited: Loreto, Junín, La Libertad, Huánuco and Lima through the activity of “The hour of singing and lullaby”; “Story time”; “Family reading”; and “Appropriation of the text.”

Title EN: Promouvoir l’accès au marché culturel suisse, aux réseaux professionnels, au public et renforcement des capacités des cinéastes du Sud et de l’Est : Project Open Doors – Film Festival Locarno
Goal: Integrate Culture In Sustainable Development Frameworks
SDG: SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: International cooperation for sustainable development
Agency Implementation: Direction du développement et de la coopération DDC
Main Feature: Composante essentielle de l’aide au développement durable, la culture occupe une place de choix dans les concepts stratégiques de la Direction du développement et de la coopération (DDC), en accord avec l’art. 13 de la Convention UNESCO de 2005. Outre la promotion de la culture dans les pays de développement, la DDC soutient spécifiquement l’accès des artistes professionnelles et professionnels d’Amérique latine, d’Afrique, d’Asie et d’Europe de l’Est (à l’exception des État-membres de l’UE) au marché de l’art et de la culture en Suisse. Cette intervention a pour but de renforcer le secteur culturel local dans les pays d'origine. Dans ce contexte, la DDC a établi des partenariats stratégiques avec des organisations professionnelles du secteur culturel suisse. Un accent tout particulier est mis sur le secteur cinématographique, où ce soutien se déploie sur plusieurs niveaux. L'un de ces partenariats est celui conclu avec le festival du film de Locarno, qui réalise le projet Open Doors. Le projet Open Doors est né conjointement entre le Festival du film de Locarno et la Direction du développement et de la coopération (DDC) en 2003. Open Doors soutient la création cinématographique indépendante des régions où la Suisse est engagée dans le cadre de sa coopération internationale. Le projet crée des ponts pour la coopération cinématographique au-delà des régions, des pays et des continents. Open Doors vise à renforcer les industries cinématographiques émergentes de la région et à contribuer à leur développement en tant qu'industries durables et indépendantes, en permettant aux cinéastes disposant de peu de ressources d'accéder au programme. Open Doors facilite les liens entre les cinéastes, avec et entre les institutions de la région concernée - qui sont rares pour de multiples raisons - ainsi que les connexions avec l'industrie cinématographique internationale et européenne, donnant aux cinéastes des perspectives plus larges sur la manière dont une industrie cinématographique peut être construite. Pour atteindre plus efficacement cet objectif, Open Doors a adopté depuis 2016 une approche plus approfondie : l'initiative concentre son travail sur une seule région pour une période de trois ans (remplaçant le format précédent d'un an). Cela permet de capitaliser sur les connexions créées, en construisant un réseau vertueux plus fort et plus articulé. Les régions ciblées pour la période couverte par le rapport ont été l'Asie du Sud-Est et la Mongolie (2019-2021) et l'Amérique latine et les Caraïbes (2022-2024). Depuis 2020, Open Doors est actif tout au long de l'année, à travers une gamme diversifiée de programmes en ligne et en personne. Il propose aux cinéastes à différents stades de leur carrière plusieurs activités professionnelles et publiques, où elles et ils peuvent accéder à des ressources, des formations, de l'inspiration créative et des contacts, afin de créer, financer, promouvoir et distribuer leurs œuvres, de développer leurs compétences et, en fin de compte, de contribuer au développement de leur communauté cinématographique. Open Doors accorde une grande attention aux cinéastes qui débutent leur carrière. Toutefois, pour une expérience d'apprentissage mutuel, la ou les sélections comprennent généralement un équilibre entre les cinéastes ayant réalisé des courts métrages ou leur premier long métrage et les cinéastes avec plus d’expérience. Cependant, plus spécifiquement, Open Doors a mis en place de nouveaux programmes visant directement à soutenir les jeunes talents dans leur développement professionnel, en leur donnant accès à l'information et aux outils de travail (y compris par le biais de plates-formes numériques), à la formation et aux services de conseil.
Results: Depuis sa création, nombre de cinéastes et de professionnelles et professionnels du cinéma de plus de 80 pays ont pu participer au programme Open Doors. Elles et ils ont pu y accéder à des formations, des ressources créatives et un réseau international pour développer leurs projets professionnels.  Pendant les années de la pandémie de COVID-19 (2020 et 2021), les programmes Open Doors ont été transférés entièrement ou partiellement en ligne, avec des programmes de formation et de rencontre se déroulant sous forme numérique, ainsi que des projections de films. La pandémie a accéléré certains développements qui étaient déjà prévus pour Open Doors, comme une utilisation plus large d’internet et de la technologie numérique pour atteindre une plus grande base de cinéastes, afin de répondre à des besoins et des demandes plus variés, par exemple en offrant en ligne des consultations artistiques et de carrière avec des experts, ainsi qu'une plateforme web interactive gratuite avec des outils et des ressources pour les réalisateurs de films. La participation pendant le COVID-19 est restée constante et les projets ont pu être menés à bien malgré le blocage mondial.   Pour la période 2020-2023, les chiffres suivants peuvent être annoncés :  En termes de mobilité des artistes, 14 réalisatrices et 18 réalisateurs ont participé au programme, ainsi que 20 productrices et 14 producteurs représentant 32 projets de films (24 participantes et participants à Locarno, 8 en ligne uniquement à cause du COVID-19).  En outre, 35 productrices et producteurs ont participé au programme de développement de carrière (24 à Locarno, 9 en ligne ; 20 femmes et 15 hommes).   En outre, 35 réalisatrices et 45 réalisateurs ont représenté 78 films des pays concernés qui ont été projetés au festival du film de Locarno (58 sur place à Locarno et 20 en ligne uniquement à cause du COVID-19).   Les courts métrages de chaque édition ont également été programmés en ligne gratuitement pendant ou après le festival, afin de les rendre accessibles à un public régional plus large qui n'aurait pas eu la possibilité d'accéder aux projections du festival.   En termes de « mobilité » en ligne et d'accès aux ressources, 79 projets de films ont été soutenus grâce à des consultations spécifiques avec des expertes et experts de l'industrie cinématographique. Dont 49 femmes réalisatrices ou productrices et 74 hommes réalisateurs ou producteurs. En outre, l'équipe artistique d'Open Doors a fourni des conseils artistiques et/ou professionnels et un retour d'information à 360 projets et talents.   La plateforme d'apprentissage en ligne de Open Doors s'est également développée pour devenir un réseau de 2096 membres de 107 pays à ce jour, dont 828 femmes / 1215 hommes / 53 autres ou non communiqué.   En termes de mobilité régionale, environ 8 événements publics en ligne ont été organisés (dont plusieurs restent disponibles sur la plateforme web publique de Open Doors) ; environ 25 collaborations avec des organisations locales pour des événements destinés aux cinéastes de la région ; touchant environ 1000 talents.   Les résultats qualitatifs peuvent être mesurés en particulier à travers les trajectoires professionnelles et les développements pour les professionnels du cinéma : achèvement et circulation des films, développement de carrière, développement d'initiatives qui ont émergé sur le terrain et la coopération régionale.  La participation aux Open Doors a permis à plusieurs cinéastes de réaliser des longs et courts métrages et de les diffuser dans les grands festivals internationaux (Cannes, Venise par exemple) en collaboration avec des coproductrices et coproducteurs internationaux ayant participé aux Open Doors. Plusieurs films ont également pu être réalisés grâce à des coproductions dans la région concernée, ce qui a souvent ouvert la voie à une collaboration entre ces pays pour la première fois.  La visibilité et les ressources mises à la disposition des professionnelles et des professionnels du cinéma ont également contribué à la reconnaissance des représentantes et des représentants de l'industrie cinématographique par les autorités et à un dialogue plus étroit entre les deux parties. Pour nommer quelques exemples concrets, la Mongolie a réussi à élaborer la loi sur le cinéma mongol (annoncée en juillet 2023) et les Philippines ont ouvert de nouvelles lignes de financement pour les coproductions en Asie du Sud-Est et avec l'Europe (France). D'autres anciennes participantes et anciens participants ont profité du réseau et des ressources acquises pour créer ou renforcer des initiatives visant à former et à mettre en relation des professionnelles et professionnels du cinéma au niveau local et/ou régional, contribuant ainsi à un accès plus local et diversifié à la culture et aux ressources nécessaires.  Un exemple vertueux est le Circulo de Industria : un atelier de formation et un événement de rencontre pour les professionnelles et les professionnels du cinéma des pays méso-américains, avec un accent sur la coopération régionale entre les pays concernés ; les anciennes et les anciens élèves ont confirmé qu'elles et ils utilisaient les ressources de la boîte à outils pour enseigner dans leurs cours et leurs écoles respectifs.  En outre, le projet Open Doors offre aux cinéastes la possibilité d'apporter leur point de vue sur des questions sociales et mondiales dans un contexte international à travers leurs films.
Recommandations: Le partenariat DDC-Locarno Open Doors a été évalué et couvre la période 2012 - 2020. Les principales conclusions et recommandations sont les suivantes : La collaboration DDC-Open Doors est décrite comme très ciblée et la valeur ajoutée de la coopération comme importante : la DDC dispose d'un partenaire solide doté d'une grande expertise professionnelle, le festival gagne en internationalité et élargit ses contacts avec les futures et futurs cinéastes. Quant aux cinéastes, elles et ils ont accès à la scène cinématographique internationale, tout en bénéficiant d'un programme adapté à leurs besoins. Compte tenu de la bonne réalisation des objectifs d'Open Doors, des réactions positives des participantes et des participants – cinéastes, productrices et producteurs, de l'impact considérable (sur les cinéastes mais aussi dans les pays d'origine) et de la grande valeur ajoutée (pour Open Doors, les cinéastes du Sud et de l'Est, le Festival du film de Locarno et la DDC), il a été recommandé à la DDC de poursuivre son partenariat avec Open Doors.

Title EN: Promouvoir un égal accès aux responsabilités et opportunités professionnelles ainsi qu’aux financements –conditionnement des aides publiques versées par le CNC à l’observation de la parité dans les équipes
Goal: Promote Human Rights And Fundamental Freedoms
SDG: SDG 5 - Achieve gender equality and empower all women and girls,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels
Area of Monitoring: Gender equality
Agency Implementation: Centre National du Cinéma et de l’image animée (CNC)
Main Feature: Le CNC applique depuis le 1er janvier 2019 un bonus de 15% au soutien financier mobilisé pour les films dont les principaux postes artistiques et techniques respectent la parité, c’est-à-dire qui comptent au moins autant de femmes que d’hommes dans les postes clés de la production et de la création d’un film. En octobre 2022, le CNC a apporté plusieurs aménagements à ce bonus, entrés en vigueur dès le 1er décembre 2022 : le poste de compositrice a été intégré dans le barème de calcul du bonus parité ; les postes de post-production son (monteuse son et mixeuse) font désormais parties également du barème de calcul ; le terme de producteur est accolé à celui de représentant légal afin de prendre en compte le rôle du producteur qui incarne la société de production, développe les projets et cherche les financements ; et deux barèmes distincts pour le secteur de l’animation ont été créés, un pour la 2D et un autre pour la 3D. En 2022, la part des films éligibles au bonus parité était de 32% pour les films de fiction, 35% pour les films documentaires et 25 % pour les films d’animation, soit 32,5 % des films d’initiative française agréés en 2022. De plus, le conseil d’administration du CNC a voté le 8 décembre 2022 une mesure pionnière en matière de conditionnement des aides à l’égalité : en effet, les aides sélectives ou automatiques à la production d’œuvres audiovisuelles sont désormais conditionnées au dépôt, par les demandeurs d’aides, de données relatives au nombre d’hommes et de femmes occupant des postes clés dans la production de l’œuvre. Ainsi, depuis du 1er janvier 2023, un formulaire spécifique précisant l’identité et le genre des personnes occupant ces fonctions est systématiquement intégré dans les dossiers de demande d’autorisation préalable, d’autorisation définitive et de demandes d’aide à la préparation. Par ailleurs, la ministre de la Culture Rima Abul-Malak a annoncé fin 2023 l’extension de cette mesure de conditionnalité à la formation de tous les membres des équipes de tournage.
Results: Un quart des films agréés ont bénéficié de ce bonus en 2019, et un tiers en 2020 et 2021.

Title EN: Protection of Ukrainian artists at risk or in exile
Goal: Promote Human Rights And Fundamental Freedoms
SDG: SDG 5 - Achieve gender equality and empower all women and girls,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels
Area of Monitoring: Artistic freedom
Agency Implementation: Association of Polish Artists and Designers (ZPAP)
Main Feature: In the wake of the outbreak of war in the Ukraine, the Association provided assistance to artists from the Ukraine by making available their own houses and the properties of the ZPAP districts in all major Polish cities. Integration and access to galleries was provided. Studios were created and made available to them. Certificates were implemented to enable the transport of artworks. Thanks to close relations between ZPAP and the Association of Ukrainian Artists, information is being verified in order to prevent fraudulent activities that may occur during the war conflict.
Results: Amongst others, the residents assisted and recommended by the Association could obtain the Gaude Polonia scholarship from the Ministry of Culture and National Heritage, which allows them to continue their work. Through the Association, some artists can benefit from studios at the Academy of Fine Arts.

Title EN: READ PERU FESTIVAL
Goal: Integrate Culture In Sustainable Development Frameworks
SDG: SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: National sustainable development policies and plans
Agency Implementation: Book and Reading Direction - Mnistery of Culture
Main Feature: The Read Peru Festivals are cultural events of a temporary nature that promote the social appropriation of reading in the population through recreational, educational and/or artistic processes that prioritize the promotion of legal and sociocultural approaches to reading.  The cultural programming of the Read Peru Festivals allows the celebration of the various ways of reading, the meeting and recognition of the agents of the sector and bibliodiversity, axes that aim to challenge the population in relation to both the collective identities that are formed through the book object and orality, as well as the identification of roots, interpretations and future projections in each individual.  The cultural programming of these festivals is prepared from two inputs: 1) the survey of needs of the school public (children and youth), the public with disabilities and older adults, 2) the survey of experiences of agents in the book sector and reading in each targeted region. In this way, we seek to promote the creativity of local agents when designing and proposing activities related to books and reading in their localities.  The Read Peru Festivals are part of a sustained cultural policy with growing impact on the book and reading ecosystem, as they seek to energize the offer related to books, reading and orality through coordinated work with institutions in the regions where it is implemented, and where they are still incipient.
Results: Since 2020, these festivals have been held in the regions of Áncash, Arequipa, Ayacucho, Huánuco, Ica, Lambayeque, Loreto, San Martín, Tacna and Tumbes.  In 2023, 4 reading festivals were held in the regions of San Martín, Tacna, Tumbes and Lambayeque, registering a total of more than 9 thousand citizens participating in person and more than 140 thousand citizens who participated simultaneously through the platforms and channels of the Ministry of Culture.  Additionally, to date we have achieved the inclusion of 2 Peruvian sign language interpreters in each festival and the participation of people with visual, hearing, cognitive and motor disabilities in the different editions.

International artistic mobility, the exchange of experience, exhibitions, online courses, and artistic mobility have been favored. Agreements have been signed between cultural institutions. The provision of dedicated spaces has facilitated greater public engagement and networking opportunities, contributing to a more vibrant and active civil society landscape. Additionally, the measure has fostered stronger partnerships between NonBenefit Public Associations and governmental bodies, enhancing the overall impact of civic initiatives.

Main Feature: Forty-four accessible format version service providers (including cross-border exchange organizations) in four provinces, including Beijing, Hebei, Jiangxi and Hainan, provide or produce accessible format editions of works for people with print disabilities in order to ensure that people with disabilities participate equally in cultural life and share the fruits of civilizational development.

Title EN: Public consultation for the Law on the Status of the Artist (2024)
Goal: Promote Human Rights And Fundamental Freedoms
SDG: SDG 5 - Achieve gender equality and empower all women and girls,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels
Area of Monitoring: Artistic freedom
Cultural Domain: Design,Performing Arts,Media Arts,Cinema and Audiovisual Arts,Music,Publishing,Visual Arts
Agency Implementation: Deputy Ministry of Culture
Main Feature: The Deputy Ministry of Culture announced a public consultation on the Draft Law entitled "On the Creation of the Register of Artists and Establishment of Artistic Sponsorship Law of 2024", which aims to institutionalize the social and professional status of the artist and invited anyone interested to send οpinions/comments/observations through an electronic platform. The purpose of the bill is to define the terms and conditions for registration in the Register of Artists and the Register of Associations of Artists. The drafting was completed by the Deputy Ministry of Culture and the Office of the Commissioner of Legislation, according to information accessed on the Commissioner's website.   The Law aims to register all artists as well as artists' associations that meet the requirements set out in the law, something that will allow them to have access to "artistic sponsorships". Cultural Domain: Design,Performing Arts,Media Arts,Cinema and Audiovisual Arts,Music,Publishing,Visual Arts
Agency Implementation: Indian Ocean Commission
Main Feature: 1.	Regional workshop on UNESCO Culture|2030 indicators  To emphasize the importance of CCIs in the economic development of countries, the IOC held a regional training workshop on the UNESCO Culture|2030 indicators, from December 11 to 13, 2023.  The indicators respond to a thematic approach to the role of culture in the 2023 Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs).  The training was led by UNESCO and organized in synergy with the project "Review of Cultural Policy" in collaboration with COMESA.   2. Review of the legal and policy frameworks for the Cultural and Creatives industries (CCI)   IOC has developed a new framework to measure the policy’s improvement and business regulations to foster creative economy in the region.   As main findings, the study highlighted the following:  1) Development Planning: Most MSs have incorporated CCIs development in National development Strategies affirming that creativity is linked to sustainable development and can contribute towards attainment of SDGs. 2) Public Funding: There is a weak funding and capitalisation for the CCIs in all the countries under investigation, though this varies from one Member State to another. 3) CCI strategies: Significant number of Member States do not have stand-alone CCIs strategies which are address the specific needs of CCIs and strategically position them towards the creation of wealth, employment and export. 4) Digital capacities: Weak digital capacities and infrastructure across MSs limits the ability of the digital economy to transform CCIs at every level of the value chain. 5) Cross border IP Protection: Weak IP regimes for cross border IP protection mechanisms and protection of works in the digital space has wide consequences for copyright, digital rights management across the MSs and the COMESA region. 6) Taxation: High tax and regulatory burdens on the CCIs (film, music, fashion, craft etc.) and limited access to business incentives. 7) Visa regulations: Participation of CCIs in regional and international trade tends to be limited by challenges such as lack of mobility funding and visa requirements across all Member States.  8) Business regulation: There are different regulatory frameworks and institutional frameworks for administering business regulations in each MS. 9) Institutional frameworks: Institutions for supporting CCIs also differ from country to country. 10) National Statistical Systems: Disparity and major gaps in the national cultural statistics systems, resulting in either a diversity of existing data or a quasi-absence of data on the cultural and creative industries sector.
Results: 3-day training course completed with the participation of 30 people (50% women) from 11 countries: Burundi, Ethiopia, Kenya, Madagascar, Mauritius, Mozambique, Ouganda, Seychelles, Somalia, Sudan and Union of Comoros  Study published including recommendations to strengthen the policy framework of the CCI within Indianoceanie.  9 Mauritian Artists have benefited from the Fund - Ale Vini (International Travel)

Title EN: REACT  (“Enhancing Albanian and Italian Youth to Support Disadvantaged Communities to become Climate Change Resilient through Art and Culture”)

Main Feature: REACT Project aims to strengthen the climate change resilience and transform the communities’ lives, by enhancing the youth through an international education program based on culture and art. This project will enable the emergence of fresh, youth-led activists, who will become youth as agents of change in their community and will promote climate change resilience, advocate solutions to local authorities, and will support the disadvantaged communities, like the Roma minority in Albania and Miglionico community in Italy, in making positive changes to their way of life and mitigate the effects of climate change.                   The main activities of this project are:                   • To create the Academy for Climate Ambassadors, with an international education training program based on culture and art, in which will be trained 40 youth, 20 youngsters from Albania and 20 youngsters from Italy, between the age of 13-30 year’s old, will be trained to become agents of change and learning about the impact of the climate change in the vulnerable communities, such as the Roma minority in Albania and the Miglionico community in Italy. During the Academy’s international education program, the youth activists will learn more about the theory and practice of green economy, circular economy, and how to use art and cultural games for climate change advocacy. 20 Italian youngsters and 1 representative from APS Giallo Sassi will travel to Albania and will participate to the 2-days training event of the Academy for Climate Ambassadors and 1 day of field advocacy in the community in Durres (Albania) together with Albanian youngsters. Also, 20 Albanian youngsters and 1 representative from IRCA will travel to Italy and will participate to the 2-days training event of the Academy for Climate Ambassadors and 1 day of field advocacy in the community in Miglionico (Italy) together with Italian youngsters.                   • To organize a series of 16 open lectures in secondary schools and universities of the respective countries, entitled “Climate Talk”, where trained Climate Ambassadors, climate activist, university professors, and active citizens will discuss about the effects of climate change in their community and suggest solutions to support the disadvantaged communities to transform their living and deal with the climate change effects in their community.                   • To organize a competition with secondary school and university students on climate change, with prizes for three best art works.                   • To organize an exhibition of artworks in Matera (Italy) and in Tirana (Albania) on climate change created by the Climate Ambassadors and climate activists of the communities.                   • To organize in their respective countries 3 days of community work to planting trees and greening the environment, raising awareness to not planting near the rivers, and to support the community with practical solutions to develop.                   • To organize mediatic visibility presence through participation of 2 speakers (1 in Albania and 1 in Italy) in television programs and the writing of 10 (5 in Albania and 5 in Italy) news articles from journal writer about the promotion of the climate change resilience actions needed to be taken to support disadvantaged communities.                   • To arrange 4 (2 in Albania and 2 in Italy) meetings with the local government representatives of the respective countries to advocate for the local government cooperation in implementing practical solutions for supporting the disadvantaged communities to combat the consequences of climate change.                   • To produce a documentary on the consequences of climate change in Albania and in Italy.                   • To organize a closing event at Reja (Cloud) installation in the center of Tirana (Albania) to gather youth, Climate Ambassadors trained by the project, climate activist, journalists, and active citizens to discuss about climate change effects and solutions to be implemented by all of us.                   • To organize a closing event in Matera (Italy) to gather youth, Climate Ambassadors trained by the project, climate activist, journalists, and active citizens.                   This project facilitates knowledge transfer and exchange of experience between Italians and Albanians in working with youngsters to develop climate changes to multicultural communities, disadvantaged groups, and enabling them to adapt their lives to climate changes.                    REACT project is in response to the continued changing climatic landscape which requires a shift in the way disadvantaged communities live in Italy and in Albania.
Results: The Project dealt with raising awareness of climate change and environmental protection among local and Albanian youth through various training and dissemination phases, which took place in both Italy and Albania, involving experts in the field at various levels and 50 Albanian and Italian youth who were involved in a residential experience in the two countries between June and July 2023.

Title EN: Reading for Pleasure Initiative
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture
SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Cultural and creative sectors
Agency Implementation: Emirates Literature Foundation
Main Feature: The Emirates Literature Foundation (ELF) has launched the "Reading for Pleasure" initiative to foster a love for reading among children in the UAE. This initiative underscores ELF's commitment to making literature accessible and engaging for students, particularly through the promotion and preservation of the Arabic language. The primary objectives of the initiative are to promote reading in Arabic, enhance access to diverse literature, and cultivate lifelong reading habits among young students. By encouraging reading in Arabic, the initiative aims to preserve the language as a mother tongue and foster a deeper cultural connection among young readers. Additionally, the initiative seeks to make a wide range of books, including regional stories and translated works, available to students, ensuring that they have access to diverse and age-appropriate reading materials. As part of the implementation, ELF has partnered with Al Hudhud Publishing, an Emirati publishing house known for its diverse Arabic children's stories. The initiative, launched in 2023 and set to run for five years, involves six schools and three universities in the UAE. Over the next four years, Al Hudhud will continue to donate books, and participating universities will evaluate the program's impact on students. The partnership also includes training and awareness sessions for teachers and parents to support a culture of reading beyond the classroom. By involving parents, the initiative aims to create a supportive reading environment at home, thereby reinforcing the habit of reading and ensuring a comprehensive approach to children's literacy development. In alignment with the United Nations' Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), the initiative supports SDG 4 (quality education) by ensuring inclusive and equitable quality education and promoting lifelong learning opportunities for all, and SDG 10 (reduced inequalities) by addressing educational disparities within the UAE. The project also includes providing access to authors, events, fairs, and festivals focused on books and authors, working with schools to integrate regular reading habits, and collaborating with university research teams to gather evidence on the impact of reading for pleasure. This comprehensive approach aims to nurture a generation of avid readers empowered by the knowledge and imagination found within the pages of books, ultimately contributing to a more literate and empathetic society.
Results: The Reading for Pleasure Initiative from The Emirates Literature Foundation has achieved significant results since its inception. The program has notably increased reading engagement among students and the wider community by fostering a culture where reading is valued for enjoyment rather than solely for academic purposes.
Recommandations: The Reading for Pleasure Initiative has demonstrated that a well-rounded and inclusive approach to promoting reading can lead to substantial improvements in literacy and a love for reading among young people.

Area of Monitoring: National sustainable development policies and plans

Main Feature: The Pontos de Leitura Award was launched in 2023, through a public notice, and aims to recognize and reward community libraries that develop actions to promote reading. Among the selection criteria, projects that aimed at digital empowerment of libraries and that strengthen or develop activities related to information and communication technologies – ICTs were highlighted.
Results: 300 community libraries were awarded for carrying out reading activities in their spaces. The awarded projects are diverse and cover different audiences and territories. Among them are community libraries located in indigenous villages, quilombola territories, rural settlement areas and urban outskirts. Each award-winning library received US$6,053.5131 (R$30,000.00).

Title EN: Reading promotion
Goal: Integrate Culture In Sustainable Development Frameworks
SDG: SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: National sustainable development policies and plans
Agency Implementation: Swedish Arts Council
Main Feature: During the years 2022-2024 the government has introduced and has continued the funding of several measures within reading promotion, both funding schemes targeting municipal libraries and other reading promotions initiatives run by the Swedish Arts Council.   - “Stronger libraries” (2018-2023). Funding for municipal libraries to improve the accessibility to libraries throughout the country. Libraries play a crucial role to promote reading particularly among children and young people, and also to promote the knowledge and use of national minority languages. (150 million SEK in 2021, 75 million SEK in 2022, 75 million SEK in 2023)    - Reading Promotion Boost for Public Librarians 2021–2023 (Läsfrämjandelyft för folkbibliotekarier). Funding for training for librarians (municipal libraries) within reading promotion focusing on children and young people, particularly boys, and also people with disabilities in need of alternative materials and methods. (15 million SEK in 2021, 30 million SEK in 2022, 30 million SEK in 2023)    - A range of reading promotion initiatives run by the Swedish Arts Council, one of these is Book Start (Bookstart) which has received additional funding during these years. Funding can be applied by libraries for Bookstart-projects targeting children between 0-3 years and their parents/other adults with a close relationship to the children. The aim is to stimulate linguistic development through books and reading. The projects involve both local libraries, the children´s local health service and nursery schools and thus also promotes cross-sectorial cooperation. (15 million SEK in 2021 and 20 million SEK yearly from 2022 as additional funding)    - “Läsrådet”/A National Reading Council, with experts appointed by the government covering different aspects of reading and reading promotion, established within the Swedish Arts Council.  The aim of the council being coordination on a national level of initiatives focusing on reading promotion for children and young people within both government agencies, civil society organisations, organisations within “folkbildning” (Swedish folkbildning is the collective name for the activities conducted by the country’s folk high schools and study associations, adult education), books shops, publishing houses and other actors from the private sector. (10 million SEK per year)
Results: The Stronger libraries programme (2018-2023) has played a crucial role in enhancing the range of materials, services, and programs available and improving accessibility in public libraries. A final report of the years 2021-2023 will be published by the end of the year by the Swedish Arts Council.   The Reading Promotion Boost for Public Librarians 2021–2023 has focused on the first steps of building an infrastructure for professional development within the library sector through collaborative efforts and partnerships. There was great interest from both regions and municipalities to apply for funding, which shows the needs within the sector.
Financial Ressources: The government has set aside 5,2 million USD (SEK 55 million in 2021) and 7,1 million USD (SEK 75 million) annually in 2022–2023 to promote increased reading. The investment is permanent and amounts to 4,3 million USD (SEK 45 million) from 2024 onwards.  In 2024-2026, 3,78 million USD (SEK 40 million) per year will be set aside for public libraries' work to promote reading.
Recommandations: Av evaluation of Bookstart was published in 2020. According to the report government support has undoubtedly been significant in getting Bookstart underway in many places across the country. A continued support could allow ongoing projects to grow and/or provide more municipalities with the opportunity to initiate Bookstart. Bookstart is however dependent on funding within the municipalities. Also its success depends on the multilevel cooperation between the Swedish Arts Council, the regional level (child health care) and the municipal level (public libraries and preschools).   Even though many would hope for a nationwide implementation, a more reasonable approach for further development of the Bookstart model seems to be organic growth based on the positive experiences gained from ongoing projects. However, this assumes that knowledge and experiences are disseminated, by both national and regional actors. Enhanced collaboration a national level between government agencies would also benefit the further development of Bookstart.   (Bokstart i Sverige – en uppföljning, by Governo, 2020)

Title EN: RESILIENCE (Santa Cruz)
Goal: Integrate Culture In Sustainable Development Frameworks
SDG: SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: National sustainable development policies and plans
Agency Implementation: Mary Carmen Monje  EMAIL: marycarmen2moon@gmail.com PHONE: 726 11654  Alessandra Abruzesse  EMAIL: ales1@hotmail.com PHONE: 65898386  Valeria Catoira EMAIL:valeriacatoira@gmail.com PHONE: 76009425
Main Feature: RESILIENCE was born in 2018 in the city of Santa Cruz de la Sierra, as a critical response to the cultural stagnation of Santa Cruz, the cancellation of the visual arts biennial and the demand for a decent budget for art and culture by the mayor's office. RESILIENCE proposed actions with different time frames, short, medium and long term. In the short term and almost immediately, they are ARTISTIC MANIFESTATIONS, forms of protest that speak from what we know, from ART. At least 5 mobilizations were carried out, each with a concept and collective work of production and convening. In the medium term, the ALTERNATIVE ITINERARY OF ART AND CULTURE was considered first, which was presented not as a "counter-biennial", leaving aside Western terms that do not apply to our society, but an ITINERARY in which art forms, not only conventional ones but those often alienated, are part of a time of visibility, considering the existence of routes and, above all, trying to avoid simultaneous events, a problem that all cultural centers currently face due to the lack of a common, established, complete and serious cultural agenda. In parallel, work was done on information and training on laws, actions, or municipal possibilities for artists, managers and cultural spaces. Access to information is a very important deficiency, so the long-term objective was to make a proposal for the constitution, drafting and application of the Law on Art, Culture and Heritage. For this purpose, a methodology and a working group were created that worked together with the Municipality to make an initial assessment of the sectoral demands, in order to prepare the progress towards the law that can respond to each sector. A proposal for a Municipal Law on Arts, Culture and Heritage was drafted, which was carried out in an open and inclusive manner for all cultural sectors and citizens, but which did not make any further progress due to a lack of political will. El DEBER awarded “Resiliencia” the “Patuju de Bronze” recognition, 	for the work and social impact that was achieved in a short time.
Results: At least 5 mobilizations with the participation of at least 100 people from different art groups. Art and Culture Itinerary, with self-managed spaces and artists with more than 60 activities and the attendance of at least 700 people Thanks to the Solidar Switzerland fund, the creation and printing of the “Manual of good practices in visual arts” was possible. The process of drafting the proposed law was carried out with the Ministry of Culture, working in roundtables with artists and citizens in general, in a transparent manner and with an open invitation. An information booklet was produced on the process of constructing the proposed Municipal Law on art, culture and heritage. A bill was drafted, but it was never enacted.

Title EN: Recommendations for democratisation of the media. Report "More breadth, more voices,  more democracy. Contribution for the Communications of the Chile that is coming”
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture
SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Media diversity
Agency Implementation: University of Chile, University of La Frontera, University of La Serena, Ministry General Secretariat of Government.
Main Feature: The goal of the document "More breadth, more voices, more democracy. Contribution for the Communications of the Chile that is coming”, whose content was gathered in 2022, was to make a series of recommendations available for the Ministry General Secretariat of Government and the citizens, that consider a revision of previous reports, international jurisprudence in order to gather suggestions and experiences of the national sectors involved in the debate around the democratisation of media.   This was carried out through a dialogue process with multiple sectors involved as a defense of the freedom of expression and a pluralist exercise of media in Chile, oriented towards promoting the development of a national information industry, that encourages pluralism of voices and diversifies the circulating discourse, that strengthens community and indigenous media, that values public print, radio and television platforms in the public, educational and cultural spheres.   Among the topics covered, there were: interculturality, gender perspective and education as across the board issues; right and access to information; media and democratic systems; journalism work and media professionals; media ethics; social networks; technological development and democratisation. Following the monitoring framework of the 2005 Convention, this research excercise is part of the "policies and measures that support diversity of content in the media" indicator
Results: Even though, the suggestions of the document, have not been implemented to date, the main result of this measure is the prepation of the report itself, understood as actions and recommendations for pluralising cultural media and content.
Recommandations: Even though the document "More breadth, more voices, more democracy. Contribution for the Communications of the Chile that is coming” has not been evaluated in terms of the implementation of its results, it proposes a series of recommendations on diverse areas for the media.   These take into cosideration cross-cutting issues on matters of, for example, interculturality, gender perspectives, education and media, rights and access to information, systems of media and democracies, public media, community media, journalism and communications, media ethics, social networks and technological development and democratisation. For each of these issues, a series of recommendations was developed with contributions from the participants of the group interviews and focus groups. The details of the recommendations are found in the report.

Title EN: Re-defining Cypriot Fashion Heritage through sustainable fashion and art
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture
SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Cultural and creative sectors
Agency Implementation: Fashion Heritage Network Cyprus
Main Feature: The Fashion Heritage Network Cyprus (FHNC) was founded in July 2022. It consists of a group of young Cypriot fashion designers and creators who aim to explore the beauty and uniqueness of Cypriot fashion heritage through zero-waste and sustainable fashion designs and art pieces. The FHNC is all about stimulating and re-discovering elements of Cypriot Fashion Heritage and communicating these creative shifts in a sustainable manner to a wide audience. The network consists of 40 members volunteering in various departments such as fashion design, heritage, events, social media, etc.  Among other objectives, the FHNC is committed to creating designs that are environmentally friendly and zero-waste in order to have the minimum impact on the environment. Furthermore, Cypriot Fashion Heritage is classed as sustainable, as fashion sustainability tactics (i.e reuse, natural dyes, repair, upcycle) were generally used in the past.   FHNC is an inter-communal project, that brings together young Cypriot fashion designers and artists from different communities and gives them the opportunity to work together collaboratively, exchange ideas, and showcase their work. Moreover, the network also organizes educational workshops and seminars for its members as well as the chance to present their work on both local and international platforms and network with industry professionals. Through art, we can create dialogue and create bridges.  The network aims to raise awareness about its objectives through: •	Fashion show/exhibition with creative sustainable fashion designs as well as educational information about sustainability and cultural heritage •	Upcycling and Educational Videos •	Fanzine •	Interactive workshops •	Educational Social Media Posts •	Panel discussions •	Participating in related events, conferences
Results: What are the results achieved so far through the implementation of the measure/initiative? (400 words)   Revive CYPRUS, May 2023: This event showcased a collection of 12 exquisite pieces of sustainable fashion and art inspired from Cypriot cultural practices and traditions. The venue for this event was the Gardens of the Future, and we were humbled by the attendance of 700 esteemed guests. The opening night was graced by the High Commissioners of Great Britain and Australia, who delivered welcoming addresses as our principal sponsors. The event spanned four days and included an array of engaging activities.   Revive London, September-October 2023: We had the honour of presenting our REVIVE fashion and art exhibition at the Cyprus High Commission in London for two weeks. The exhibition was a massive success and was visited by several prestigious guests from the world of fashion, culture, and the Cyprus diaspora. Notably, this was the embassys first-ever contemporary and sustainable fashion exhibition inspired by Cypriot cultural heritage.  Culture and Art Award, March 2024: Fahion Heritage Network Cyprus director, Chritina Dymioti, was awarded with the "Culture and Art" award at the Cypru Diapora Forum in Limassol.    Cyprus Fashion Film Festival, June 2024:   We had the pleasure of being the co-organizers of the first ever Cyprus Fashion Film Festival (CFFF), held in Limassol. It was a resounding success, captivating audiences with a unique blend of fashion and film. The event, showcased the creativity and innovation of Cypriot and international designers and filmmakers. The event was fully booked, reflecting its immense popularity and the strong interest in the fusion of fashion and film. During CFFF, we showcased an exclusive fashion show which featured 14 emerging Cypriot designers, the show highlighted sustainable fashion inspired by Cypriot architecture. This marked the first-ever bicommunal fashion show in Cyprus, celebrating cultural heritage and eco-conscious design. This event marks a significant milestone for Fashion Heritage Network Cyprus (FHNC), solidifying its commitment to preserving and promoting Cypriot cultural heritage through sustainable and contemporary fashion  The Cyprus Fashion Film Festival was held under the auspices of the Municipality of Limassol and the Deputy Ministry of Culture, with support from UNFICYP, Home For Corporation and many more. We also had the honour to have RIK and  LIFE.COM.CY as our Media Sponsors.    Moreover, we will be featured in the second edition of the book  Sustainability in Fashion: A Cradle to Upcycle Approach (Hardback) Claudia E. Henninger (editor), Panayiota J. Alevizou (editor), Helen Goworek (editor), Daniella Ryding (editor) which will be published this winter.

Title EN: Réduction de la TVA sur les produits culturels
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture
SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Cultural and creative sectors
Cultural Domain: Design,Performing Arts,Media Arts,Cinema and Audiovisual Arts,Music,Publishing,Visual Arts
Agency Implementation: La Confédération Générale des Entreprises du Maroc, CGEM
Main Feature: Au Maroc, des efforts significatifs sont déployés pour démocratiser l'accès à la culture. La proposition de réduire la TVA sur les produits culturels de 20 % à 10 % est avancée pour encourager la promotion de la culture. Youssef Mouhyi, membre du groupe parlementaire de la CGEM à la Chambre des conseillers, explique que cette initiative vise à rendre les produits culturels plus accessibles à la population et à dynamiser le secteur culturel. Cet amendement est discuté lors des délibérations du Projet de Loi de Finances (PLF) 2019 en commission des Finances de la deuxième chambre. Une proposition similaire avait déjà été soumise par le patronat lors de l’adoption du PLF 2018, mais n’avait pas été retenue à l’époque.  La réduction de la TVA permet de diminuer les prix des livres, des billets de cinéma, des œuvres d'art et d'autres produits culturels, favorisant ainsi une plus grande consommation et un soutien renforcé à la production culturelle locale. Les partisans de cette mesure estiment qu'elle pourrait également contribuer à une meilleure démocratisation de l'accès à la culture en rendant les produits culturels plus abordables pour une plus grande partie de la population.
Results: Cette mesure a stimulé la consommation culturelle, encourageant ainsi une augmentation de l'accès à la culture pour les Marocains de tous horizons économiques.  En parallèle, la politique a soutenu la croissance du secteur culturel local en augmentant la demande pour les productions artistiques et littéraires marocaines. Les initiatives de promotion culturelle ont également bénéficié d'un soutien accru, favorisant la diversité et la richesse de l'offre culturelle disponible dans le pays.  Sur le plan économique, la réduction de la TVA a contribué à dynamiser le marché des produits culturels, renforçant ainsi leur rôle dans l'économie nationale. En fin de compte, cette politique a non seulement abaissé les barrières économiques à la participation culturelle, mais elle a aussi renforcé l'identité culturelle du Maroc en valorisant et en promouvant ses nombreuses expressions artistiques
