Title EN: Safe Environment in the Film Industry (since 2019)
Goal: Promote Human Rights And Fundamental Freedoms
SDG: SDG 5 - Achieve gender equality and empower all women and girls,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels
Area of Monitoring: Gender equality
Agency Implementation: Lithuanian Film Centre under the Ministry of Culture of the Republic of Lithuania
Main Feature: In 2019, The Lithuanian Film Centre, together with the Centre for the Development of Equal Opportunities and the Lithuanian Centre for Human Rights, implemented a project on prevention of sexual harassment in the film industry. During the project, experts from the Centre for the Development of Equal Opportunities and the Lithuanian Centre for Human Rights carried out the first anonymous electronic survey on the prevalence and recognition of sexual harassment in the film industry. The results of the survey revealed that sexual harassment practices are widespread in the Lithuanian film industry and not all forms of sexual harassment are equally well recognised.  The electronic survey showed that in the Lithuanian film industry: - Between 24% and 41% of respondents said they had experienced unwanted behaviour; - Women are 3-6 times more likely than men to experience it; - 71% of cases of sexual harassment are perpetrated by a person in a higher position; - Actors are the most likely to experience sexual harassment (43%); film industry participants under the age of 30 are more likely to experience sexual harassment than older respondents.  For more detail on the results of the survey: https://www.lkc.lt/docs/Apklausos-rezultatu-apzvalga.pdf  Based on the results of the survey, trainings were conducted to directors and producers on the recognition of sexual harassment and on possible measures to set a creative and working environment in the film industry that is intolerant to sexual harassment. The training was implemented by specialists from the Centre for the Development of Equal Opportunities and the Lithuanian Centre for Human Rights.  Based on the survey data and the results of the training, the organisations made recommendations on further actions that could be taken by the Lithuanian Film Centre to ensure that the film industry is safer environment for all those involved in it. Recommendations: https://www.lkc.lt/docs/Rekomendacijos-del-seksualinio-priekabiavimo-prevencijos.pdf.  The problem of sexual harassment is multi-layered and needs to be tackled further to encourage responsible behaviour. Therefore, in order to contribute to creating a safer environment for all those involved in the film industry, since 2020 The Lithuanian Film Centre has launched a safe working environment information section, accessible to all, which brings together knowledge on the extent of the problem of sexual harassment, how to recognise it, where to find help and encourages film companies to become responsible and share good practice examples.
Results: As a good practice example was developed framework 'Memorandum of Mutual Understanding of '[the title]' Film Team', the document signed by the actors and the members of the film's team aimed to avoid misunderstandings, promote a culture of communication based on trust, openness, and respect, and help to resolve problems promptly and manage tense situations effectively.  The purpose of this Memorandum is to establish a framework of cooperation in the film production process. This Memorandum is intended to:  - ensure a positive and emotionally supportive work environment respecting the physical and psychological integrity of the person; - promote a communication culture based on trust, openness and respect; - prevent abusive or disrespectful behaviour, sexual and other harassment; - solve arising problems promptly and manage tense situations effectively; - prevent and effectively respond to workplace discrimination.  The provisions of the Memorandum are announced and applied to everyone working on the film set well as all participants of the pre-production and post-production processes, including, but not limited to, actors, crew members and technical staff.  Team leaders are encouraged to implement the provisions of this Memorandum during the entire process of film production by actively engaging to manage situations of potentially inappropriate behaviour.  The following behaviour is considered to be inappropriate: - Unwanted physical contact, sexual or other harassment; - Unwanted repetitious flirting or other romantic attention of a sexual nature, including unwanted texting e-mails, notes, comments about a person’s physical appearance; - Disrespect for a person’s decision to break a voluntary romantic relationship with a colleague; - Intentionally abusive comments about a person's race, nationality, citizenship, language, origins, social status, beliefs or views, age, disability, ethnicity, religion, gender, sexual orientation, sexual identity and/or appearance; - Recruitment and division of work among employees and volunteers based on a person's race, nationality, citizenship, language, origins, social status, beliefs or views, age, disability, ethnicity, religion, gender, sexual orientation, sexual identity and/or appearance when not objectively justified.  The developers of the Memorandum invite all those who wish to make use of the example but encourage to redesign and update the agreement each time, taking into account own circumstances and capacities.  In 2021, “Memorandum of Mutual Understanding of '[the title]' Film Team” was updated.
Financial Ressources: No data available

Title EN: Safe to Create
Goal: Promote Human Rights And Fundamental Freedoms
SDG: SDG 5 - Achieve gender equality and empower all women and girls,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels
Area of Monitoring: Artistic freedom
Cultural Domain: Performing Arts,Cinema and Audiovisual Arts,Visual Arts
Agency Implementation: Department of Tourism, Culture, Arts, Gaeltacht, Sport and Media
Main Feature: Safe to Create Safe to Create is a Dignity at Work programme funded by the Department of Tourism, Culture, Arts, Gaeltacht, Sport and Media whose aim is to impact change on the culture and practices of the arts and creative sectors in Ireland to provide safer working conditions for all workers.  This programme is managed by the Irish Theatre Institute, on behalf of the Department and in partnership with the Arts Council, Screen Ireland and Minding Creative Minds.    Through the Safe to Create programme, the Government of Ireland is looking to transform culture and practices through training, information, resources, research, voluntary compliance and certification and provide key support for victims/survivors in the areas of reporting, counselling and legal advice.    S2C Research Ongoing research has been a key focus of the Safe to Create Programme.    Influencing Change: Pathways to Dignity at Work Through Good Governance In November 2023, Safe to Create undertook a piece of research entitled ‘Governance and Dignity at Work in Ireland’s Arts & Creative Sectors’. The aim of this research was to identify the barriers to good governance and dignity at work in Ireland’s publicly funded arts and creative organisations, and called on those in charge to provide insight into what is working and what needs to change so perpetrators of poor and harmful behaviour can be held to account.    The insights gathered from this survey were recently launched as Influencing Change: Pathways to Dignity at Work Through Good Governance  https://www.safetocreate.ie/wp-content/uploads/2024/05/ITIS2C_InfluencingChange2024_Report_Final_WEB.pdf   Broader Research focusing on experiences of disabled artists, members of the LGBTQIA+ community, and artists and arts/creative workers from a minoritised racial or ethnic background  After the Speak Up report was published, it was recognised that the initial research did not adequately capture the experiences of certain communities within the arts/creative sector. As a result, qualitative and quantitative research was undertaken to gather as much intersecting information as possible, focusing on experiences of disabled artists and arts workers (including those with intellectual disability), members of the LGBTQIA+ community, and artists and arts/creative workers from a minoritised racial or ethnic background. This research was developed in consultation with individuals and organisations from these communities. Findings from this research will be announced in July 2024.     Minding Creative Minds Minding Creative Minds (MCM) is part of the Safe to Create Programme and is Ireland’s first 24/7 mental health and wellbeing support programme for the Irish Creative community. With increased funding from the Department of Tourism, Culture, Arts, Gaeltacht, Sport and Media, MCM has continually improved its services.   In 2024, MCM is focusing on the following:  1.	Establishing a HR, Legal, Finance, Mediation focused Advisory Service for creatives in Ireland to address specific, complex and challenging career concerns in a confidential manner. It is intended to provide this new additional service in consultation with other bodies and associations ensuring to avoid any duplications of services.  2.	Establishing a career service encompassing workshops, masterclasses, 1:1 mentorship programmes, tutorial, industry specialist Q&A’s and jobs boards.  3.	Creative Art Therapies; providing music, drama and art therapy sessions as creative art therapies for adults within the creative community. These forms of therapy can have numerous mental, emotional and social benefits for participants.
Results: Through the Safe to Create programme, ITI will continue to work with the Department of Tourism, Culture, Arts, Gaeltacht, Sport and Media, its existing partners Minding Creative Minds, Screen Ireland and the Arts Council. They anticipate a growing team of partners working towards improving conditions for arts and creative sector workers across the island of Ireland.   In the first instance, they will: •	Continue to develop and expand the resources and information available on this website •	Undertake a dedicated campaign to build partnerships and collaborations across artforms to embed a commitment to Dignity at Work for all artists and arts workers in Ireland •	Collaborate with artform resource organisations to provide access to the necessary supports, advice and practical help to address Dignity at Work issues •	Conduct a ‘roadshow’ to build understanding of the issues, to share knowledge on dealing with problems and to embed the Code of Behaviour in the funded arts sector •	Provide training programmes and resources on key Dignity at Work issues •	Develop a mediation service •	Work in partnership with appropriate agencies, including the Arts Council, Screen Ireland and the Department, to improve accountability and compliance, building effective monitoring and oversight mechanisms for Dignity at Work issues •	Undertake further research to monitor the impact of measures taken  Recognising that committed and meaningful leadership is key to the success of Safe to Create, in 2022 the Department of Tourism, Culture, Arts, Gaeltacht, Sport and Media has established a Working Group to oversee and inform the programme. The group brings a broad and diverse range of expertise, experience and influence that reflects the programme’s purpose. They are committed to a shared way forward towards creating a safe and respectful environment for all working in the arts and creative sectors.  SAFE TO CREATE WORKING GROUP MEMBERS Department of Tourism, Culture, Arts, Gaeltacht, Sport and Media (Chair) Irish Theatre Institute Minding Creative Minds Screen Ireland / Fís Éireann The Arts Council / An Chomhairle Ealaíon  Other organisations, informant groups and workplace change specialists will be asked to join the Working Group as required.  WORKING GROUP TERMS OF REFERENCE Primary purpose: to have overall responsibility for the oversight and development of the Safe to Create programme and online platform. To act as custodians of the core purpose of Speak Up: A Call for Change report and to guide the implementation of its recommendations; To oversee delivery and communication of all aspects of the Safe to Create programme; To monitor progress and share insights and learning; To engage specialist consultants to support the work of the group as necessary; To engage with stakeholders; To meet at least three times yearly; and To make progress reports to the Minister on a regular basis.
Financial Ressources: In 2023 €782,000 (approx. $849,799.40 USD) and in 2024 €996,484 (approx. $1,082,879.16 USD) was allocated to ITI and MCM

Title EN: SAMI Q'ATHU – VISUAL ARTS MARKET (Collaborative and Community Economies)
Goal: Achieve A Balanced Flow Of Cultural Goods And Services And Increase The Mobility Of Artists And Cultural Professionals
SDG: SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 10 - Reduce inequality within and among countries,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Flow of cultural goods and services
Agency Implementation: MUNICIPAL AUTONOMOUS GOVERNMENT OF LA PAZ
Main Feature: Created in 2019, the Sami Qhatu (Color Market) or plastic arts market was held three times (in person the first time and in virtual and semi-face-to-face formats in subsequent versions), as part of a program of local cultural markets aimed at public and private institutions, organizations, companies and the general population for the acquisition of cultural goods and services.  Its objective is to promote and encourage the sale of works by visual artists and, to a lesser extent, artisans through exhibitions in municipal halls, social networks and cultural and artistic platforms, so that the public can access the purchase of the works presented for two to three weeks.  Approximately 50 artists participate in each version, mainly from La Paz and El Alto, but also from the interior of the country and even from border cities in Peru and Chile, selected from public calls. Each one presents between 6 and 10 works at an affordable cost to the public in the following specialties:  -	Painting: oil, watercolor, acrylic, tempera, pastel and others. -	Sculpture and Artistic Ceramics: wood, stone, metal, fiberglass and others. -	Drawing: charcoal, pencil, graphite, sanguine and others. -	Engravings: woodcut, lithography, chalcography, etching, aquatint, drypoint, silkscreen and others. -	Other Media: digital arts (photography), textile art, mixed media.  For the purchase/sale of works, the interested person comes into direct contact with the artist, in order to agree on prices, payment method and delivery of the work, therefore, the transaction is the sole responsibility of the artist and the buyer.  The programme includes exhibitions in municipal halls, virtual showcase demonstrations and auctions, as well as training spaces, discussions or akullis, sales of supplies and materials, and tours of artists' workshops, both in person and virtually.  It is worth noting that since the pandemic, a virtual space with galleries has also been implemented. according to discipline, on the virtual platform.
Results: Sami Qhatu is a space that aims to democratize the population's access to works by Bolivian visual artists through their purchase at affordable prices and break the stigma that art is only for the wealthy sectors.  Around 50 artists participated in each edition, offering more than 200 works in the specialties of painting, sculpture, drawing, engraving, artistic ceramics and mixed techniques, put up for public consideration for purchase.  Each edition includes more than 10 complementary activities related to training, discussions, conferences, demonstrations and visits to artists' workshops. In addition, a catalogue of the works that are being sold is designed and published virtually.
Financial Ressources: $us. 2,500 in each version

Title EN: Samudra Art Prize & Local folktales
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture
SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Cultural and creative sectors
Agency Implementation: Caudan Arts  Centre
Main Feature: The first of these initiatives was to collaborate with and host the Samudra Art Prize, which is mainly a Fine Arts project. This year will be the 2nd edition. Two years back, we started the first edition which focused on the Ocean (Samudra is a Sanskrit word for Ocean). The idea behind Samudra Art Prize is to celebrate art and raise awareness and different calls were out out for participation of artists (mainly Fine Arts). The first edition saw the participation of 300 artists and artworks that were on display in different parts of the arts centre. There were 800 applicants and artworks that were submitted for selection. The focus this year is on Flaura and Fauna and an equally enthusiastic response is expected.  In relation to our goal to develop awareness for environment and sustainability, we also participated in an international project entitled ‘Climate Change & Other Small Talk’. There were 8 theatre groups across the world that participated in creating theatrical podcasts around Climate Change. Ours was entitled ‘To Best the Beast’ – a satire on green washing. It was written, recorded and involved participants of the theatre group of Caudan Arts Centre.  Another endeavour that is of importance for us is local Folktales: we have noticed that the interest in local folktales is dwindling and getting lost with the new generation. Over the past 2 years, we have adapted a number of tales which have been presented to young audiences. The tales include: The legend of Pieter Both, Tizan Gato Kanet, and many other Indian tales.    We have also curated and hosted an exhibition of a great Mauritian artist who passed away: Vaco Baissac. His last remaining works are exhibited and they centre around 3 themes: womanhood, nature and the creole language. This 10 month long exhibition has also hosted talks around arts as well as 15 workshops on Vaco’s painting style, open to children and adults.
Results: There have been more than 1500 young students who have attended the shows on the folktales and we have helped to broaden cultural horizons, and bring to life stories that the parents of the children knew.   The Samudra Art Prize has received widespread success and participation – as seen by the fact that this project is being held for the second year, with a view to increasing the number of selected participants. The final exhibition will also be held over one month.    Vaco’s exhibition has been very popular and there were also a number of school visits organised in order to disseminate Vaco and his style to the younger generation. Both public and private schools have been invited for guided tours.

Title EN: Screening of the documentary Pray the Devil Back to Hell (2008) by Gini Reticker - 2023
Goal: Promote Human Rights And Fundamental Freedoms
SDG: SDG 5 - Achieve gender equality and empower all women and girls,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels
Area of Monitoring: Gender equality
Agency Implementation: Università degli Studi di Padova - UNESCO Chair Human Rights, Democracy and Peace
Main Feature: The screening of the documentary is promoted as part of the project " Transforming the future: Youth, Women and Students in Dialogue for Peace and the Protection of Girls in Italy and Georgia", implemented by the Human Rights Centre "Antonio Papisca", in collaboration with the Civilian Defence Research Centre, with the support of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation, in support of Italy's 4th National Action Plan on "Women Peace Security" (2020-2024) and the dissemination and implementation of the corresponding International Agenda "Youth Peace and Security" with the aim of recognising the positive role of women and youth as agents of change in peace processes.  Pray the Devil Back to Hell chronicles the remarkable story of the Liberian women who came together to end a bloody civil war and bring peace to their shattered country. Thousands of women - ordinary mothers, grandmothers, aunts and daughters, both Christian and Muslim - came together to pray for peace and then staged a silent protest outside of the Presidential Palace. Armed only with white T-shirts and the courage of their convictions, they demanded a resolution to the country's civil war. Their actions were a critical element in bringing about an agreement during the stalled peace talks.  A story of sacrifice, unity and transcendence, Pray the Devil Back to Hell honors the strength and perseverance of the women of Liberia. Inspiring, uplifting, and most of all motivating, it is a compelling testimony of how grassroots activism can alter the history of nations.
Results: The screening was open to the public and was attended by 120 people, including some of the beneficiaries of the other project activities (university and high school students and their teachers). It was a concrete testimony of non-violent resistance, grassroot activism, and a successful peace process, thanks to the fundamental work of Liberian women. Moreover, it spread the history of Liberia, of the peace process and the work of Leymah Gbowee, Nobel Peace Prize laureate.

Main Feature: In operation since 2010, the Technical Secretariat of MERCOSUR Cultural (STMC) is a permanent technical body that provides specialized advice for the countries participating in the work agenda of the Meeting of MERCOSUR Ministers of Culture (MERCOSUR Cultural).  Based in Argentina since 2014, the STMC is responsible for ensuring the implementation of regional activities, projects and programs agreed upon by the different specialized commissions of MERCOSUR Cultural, including: commission on cultural diversity; commission on arts, cultural and creative industries; commission on cultural heritage; cultural information system of the south.  As a permanent program under the National Directorate of Federal Integration and International Cooperation of the National Secretariat of Culture, the STMC contributed to the consolidation of the region's cultural agenda by developing activities related to the promotion and dissemination of the region's cultural assets and manifestations.  Among the main activities promoted between 2020 and 2024 we can mention:  -Creation and implementation of the MERCOSUR Cultural Virtual Library. -Promotion of the Project: Evaluation of the impact of COVID-19 on the cultural and creative industries: a joint initiative of MERCOSUR, UNESCO, IDB, SEGIB and OEI”. -Inter-institutional cooperation for the macro and microeconomic estimation of the impact of the restrictions imposed by the COVID 19 pandemic on the Cultural and Creative Industries. -Holding of three editions of the MERCOSUR Cultural Diversity Seminar. -Conducted seminars on export and import control in MERCOSUR. -MERCOSUR Film Festival -Organization of the MERCOSUR University Arts Festival. -Organization of the COMER Festival. MERCOSUR Cuisines Festival
Results: The progressive consolidation of the STMC agenda has been based on the commitment of the region's countries, which have tended to build a regional identity that encourages regionalist thinking in recognition of the fact that cultural complexity can only be addressed in an integrated manner in a complex and changing world.  This convergence promoted fruitful debates, projected concerted positions and made possible the realization of long-delayed projects. This would not have been possible without the development and strengthening of state cultural institutions. It would have been difficult for the regional sphere to move forward with weak and/or disjointed national institutional processes.   Financial resources allocated to the policy/measure in U.S. dollars usd 20,000
Recommandations: Thirty years after the creation of MERCOSUR, new social and economic dynamics announce different challenges and opportunities for the countries of the region. The impact of the health crisis caused by COVID-19, changes in the global economy and new technologies, the challenges caused by climate change, and the need to address the challenges of the global economy and new technologies are all factors that are affecting the region.   The climate change that affects the world of cultural work, among other phenomena, calls for a prompt readjustment of the objectives and priorities of MERCOSUR's cultural integration, based on an inclusive approach, which should deepen, among others: (i) the cross-cutting nature of culture for the achievement of the Sustainable Development Goals; (ii) the fundamental role of the State as articulator of resources and promoter of opportunities for the strengthening and reactivation of the cultural sector; (iii) the implementation of regional projects with a comprehensive perspective and approach; (iv) the adoption of its own mechanisms for the financing of projects; (v) the promotion of measures to facilitate the circulation of cultural goods, services and agents.

Cultural Domain: Design,Performing Arts,Media Arts,Cinema and Audiovisual Arts,Music,Publishing,Visual Arts
Agency Implementation: European Commission
Main Feature: Two EU-funded actions in the Western Balkans are currently implemented in the field of culture.  The first action (Culture and Creativity for the Western Balkans (CC4WBs)) aims to improve the performance of the cultural and creative sectors in order to enhance skills, knowledge, and access to financial aid to increase competitiveness and sustain co-production and circulation of goods and services in the Western Balkans. This systemic and people-centred approach to development is intended to deeply embed progress across the sector, while ensuring ownership and engagement as key requirements for local sustainability. Overall, the CC4WBs Action aims to promote intercultural dialogue and enhance the socio-economic impact of the cultural and creative sectors in the Western Balkans in line with the guiding principles of international normative instruments, including the 1972Convention Concerning the Protection of the World Cultural and Natural Heritage, UNESCO 2005 Convention on the Protection and Promotion of the Diversity of Cultural Expressions, Convention for the Safeguarding of the Intangible Cultural Heritage, the 1980 Recommendation concerning the Status of the Artist, the 2015 Recommendation concerning the Protection and Promotion of Museums and Collections, and the 2021 Recommendation on the Ethics of Artificial Intelligence as well as the MONDIACULT 2022 Declaration with a view to foster reconciliation, peacebuilding and sustainable development in the region. It has a duration of 4 years and will finish in April 2026.  The second action addresses the illicit trafficking of cultural goods in the region. It will be finished by 31 May 2025.  In addition, the European Commission is organising a Ministerial Meeting on Research & Innovation, Education & Youth, and Culture in the Western Balkans every two years, as part of its commitment under the Western Balkans Agenda on Innovation, Research, Education, Culture, Youth and Sport. The first edition took place in June 2022 in Tirana (Albania). The next one is scheduled for 29 Sept – 1 Oct 2024, in Skopje (North Macedonia).
Results: Through the funding of projects on the ground in the context of the CC4WB action, over 800 partnerships amongst CCIs and Cultural Institutions and CSOs were forged in the context of several calls for projects that were launched in the region. CSOs are the main beneficiary of the funding.   Both projects mentioned above (CC4WB and Illicit trafficking) place significant emphasis on capacity development.  The Ministerial Meetings on Culture in the Western Balkans are a unique opportunity for the ministers in the region to sit together and exchange views on topical issues in the field of culture.
Financial Ressources: Aprox. USD 11.8 million for both actions

Title EN: SIGNATURE DU CADRE DE COOPÉRATION DES NATIONS UNIES POUR LE DÉVELOPPEMENT DURABLE 2023-2027
Goal: Integrate Culture In Sustainable Development Frameworks
SDG: SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: National sustainable development policies and plans
Cultural Domain: Design,Performing Arts,Media Arts,Cinema and Audiovisual Arts,Music,Publishing,Visual Arts
Agency Implementation: Ministère des Affaires Etrangères, de la Coopération Africaine et des Marocains Résidant à l'étranger
Main Feature: Le Maroc signe un Cadre de coopération des Nations Unies pour le Développement Durable (CCDD) 2023-2027. Ce cadre est l'instrument de référence pour la planification et le suivi des activités des Nations Unies au Maroc, visant à atteindre les objectifs du Programme de développement à l'horizon 2030. Élaboré conjointement par le gouvernement marocain et le Système des Nations Unies, le CCDD 2023-2027 est le fruit de consultations avec divers acteurs, notamment les départements ministériels, les institutions nationales, la société civile, le secteur privé, le monde académique, ainsi que les partenaires sociaux et financiers. Ce cadre a été conçu dans le contexte de la refonte du modèle de développement marocain, impulsée par Sa Majesté le Roi Mohammed VI, en réponse aux répercussions de la pandémie de COVID-19. Le CCDD 2023-2027 s'articule autour de quatre axes stratégiques : 1.	Transformation économique inclusive et durabilité : o	Intégration des secteurs productifs dans les chaînes de valeur internationales. o	Promotion de l'écosystème entrepreneurial, notamment en appuyant les TPE et les entreprises sociales et solidaires. o	Soutien à la stratégie écologique et à l'économie circulaire à faible émission de carbone. o	Investissement dans l'innovation et le développement en recherche et développement. 2.	Développement du capital humain : o	Accès équitable et de qualité à l’éducation, à la santé et à la culture pour tous. o	Renforcement de la santé publique avec une approche holistique, inspirée des leçons de la pandémie. o	Amélioration des performances éducatives, du préscolaire à l'université, et promotion de la culture comme vecteur de développement durable. 3.	Inclusion et protection sociale : o	Généralisation des mécanismes de protection sociale pour renforcer la résilience des familles et des populations vulnérables. o	Promotion de l'inclusion des jeunes pour transformer la fenêtre démographique en dividende. o	Réduction des inégalités territoriales entre les zones urbaines et rurales. 4.	Gouvernance, résilience et développement local : o	Harmonisation des cadres juridiques avec la Constitution et les engagements internationaux du Maroc. o	Appui à la réforme du système judiciaire et à la promotion des droits humains. o	Renforcement de la gouvernance, de la transparence et de la digitalisation de l’administration. o	Promotion de l’efficacité des politiques publiques au niveau local et régional. o	Soutien à l'émergence d’écosystèmes locaux, notamment en milieu rural et dans les petites et moyennes villes. Ce cadre s’aligne avec les objectifs du Nouveau Modèle de Développement du Maroc et les stratégies sectorielles, traduisant l’engagement du Maroc envers les objectifs de développement durable (ODD). Il marque une étape cruciale dans le partenariat entre le Maroc et le Système des Nations Unies pour le développement, visant à approfondir la coopération et à contribuer aux chantiers de développement du Maroc avec des approches innovantes et des solutions durables.
Results: La mise en œuvre du Cadre de coopération des Nations Unies pour le Développement Durable (CCDD) 2023-2027 au Maroc est encore dans ses premières phases, mais plusieurs résultats notables ont déjà été atteints grâce à cette politique. Voici quelques-uns des principaux résultats obtenus jusqu'à présent :  Renforcement de la coopération internationale :  Le partenariat entre le gouvernement marocain et le Système des Nations Unies a été consolidé, facilitant une collaboration plus étroite et une meilleure coordination des initiatives de développement. Appui à l'entrepreneuriat et à l'innovation :  Des programmes ont été lancés pour soutenir les très petites entreprises (TPE) et les entreprises sociales et solidaires. Ces initiatives ont permis de renforcer l'écosystème entrepreneurial, facilitant la création d'emplois décents, en particulier pour les jeunes et les femmes. Promotion de la durabilité environnementale :  Des projets visant à promouvoir une économie circulaire et à faible émission de carbone ont été mis en place. Ces projets ont contribué à la sensibilisation et à la mise en œuvre de pratiques écologiques parmi les entreprises et les collectivités locales. Amélioration de l'accès aux services sociaux de base :  Des efforts significatifs ont été déployés pour améliorer l'accès à l'éducation, à la santé et à la culture. Des programmes spécifiques ont été conçus pour les populations les plus vulnérables, notamment dans les zones rurales et marginalisées. Renforcement de la protection sociale :  La généralisation des mécanismes de protection sociale a progressé, avec une couverture sociale et médicale étendue à une plus grande partie de la population. Des initiatives ont été mises en œuvre pour améliorer la gouvernance et la soutenabilité financière de ces systèmes. Promotion des droits humains et de la bonne gouvernance :  Des réformes ont été entreprises pour harmoniser les cadres juridiques avec les engagements internationaux du Maroc. Des programmes de formation et de renforcement des capacités ont été mis en place pour les institutions nationales, améliorant ainsi la promotion et la protection des droits humains. Développement local et régional :  Des initiatives pour renforcer les capacités des administrations locales et des collectivités territoriales ont été lancées. Cela a permis une meilleure cohérence et efficacité des politiques publiques à l'échelle locale et régionale, avec une attention particulière à la réduction des inégalités territoriales. Mobilisation de partenariats multi-acteurs :  La mise en œuvre du CCDD a favorisé la mobilisation de partenariats multi-acteurs et multisectoriels, impliquant le secteur privé, la société civile et les partenaires internationaux. Ces partenariats ont été cruciaux pour la réalisation des objectifs du cadre de coopération. Ces résultats montrent que, bien que la mise en œuvre du CCDD soit encore en cours, des progrès significatifs ont été réalisés dans divers domaines stratégiques. La coopération renforcée entre le gouvernement marocain et les Nations Unies continue de jouer un rôle crucial dans le soutien au développement durable et inclusif du Maroc.

Title EN: Social Prescription Initiative (since 2023)
Goal: Integrate Culture In Sustainable Development Frameworks
SDG: SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: National sustainable development policies and plans
Cultural Domain: Design,Performing Arts,Media Arts,Cinema and Audiovisual Arts,Music,Publishing,Visual Arts
Agency Implementation: Initiative is a joint project of the Ministry of Culture of the Republic of Lithuania and the Ministry of Health of the Republic of Lithuania
Main Feature: This is an activity of the Ministry of Culture of the Republic of Lithuania Programme for the Development of Culture and Creativity for the period 2021-2030, Progress measure No 08-001-04-01-01 "Increasing Access to High Artistic Value, Diverse and Inclusive Cultural Content" (for more detail look: https://www.e-tar.lt/portal/lt/legalAct/7f512000fae211eeb884ddd8796e2c7b).   The Social Prescription Initiative is dedicated for people who have reached the age of retirement (65+) with mild symptoms of anxiety or depression with the aim of improving their psychological well-being and mental health through their inclusion in long-term free activities in the field of culture, wellness, non-formal education or other activities available in the community and municipality. Cultural services include cultural visits, participation in thematic clubs, discussions with artists, cultural education, art workshops, etc. All services aim at expanding the diversity of cultural experiences and promoting social contact.   This initiative is a joint project of the Ministry of Culture and the Ministry of Health, which started in 2023 with an initial pilot phase and will continue in 2024-2030. Participation in the Social Recipe Initiative activities is free of charge. Activities are coordinated by municipal public health offices. Cultural organisations such as libraries, museums and performing arts organizations, also NGOs provide services tailored to seniors.  The initiative is based on the good practices of the United Kingdom, Canada, Norway and other countries (for more detail look: http://kurklt.lt/projektai/socialinis-receptas/).  Description of the procedures for implementation of social prescription act was initiated within a ministerial legislative act of a broader scope – Lithuanian Health Strategy 2014-2025. Social prescription aims to implement the principle of the Health strategy – “health in all policies”, which emphasizes the need of facilitating the convergence between health and culture by using the potential of the culture and arts, to promote activities that contribute to the positive impact on human mental and physical health.  Description of the procedures for implementation of social prescription act is also seen as enactment of another goal outlined in the Health strategy – to increase cross-sectoral cooperation between   primary health care specialists and other health care specialists, employees of social security and education, cultural sectors and artists, NGOs, local communities.
Results: In 2023, the Social Prescription Initiative was piloted in four Lithuanian municipalities: Kaunas, Šiauliai, Vilnius and Klaipėda district. The pilot project involved 21 cultural and arts organizations under the Ministry of Culture (museums, libraries, performing arts organizations) providing cultural and artistic services to the target group on a voluntary basis, offering a total of almost 60 cultural activities. 731 seniors participated in the Social Prescription Initiative (660 women and 71 men). For more details look: https://www.hi.lt/uploads/Institutas/2023/Socialinio_recepto_iniciatyvos_suvestine_metine_ataskaita_2023.pdf. Experience of participants shows that such initiatives are of great importance and benefit to the community of seniors, encouraging their active lifestyles, lifelong learning and self-improvement.  In Sept. 2024, 50 Social Prescription projects received funding of  approx. USD 172 000 (EUR 155 000).
Financial Ressources: A total of more than USD 10 million (EUR 9 million) is planned until 2030.

From the Training, Production and Circulation line, in the context of the training, production, and circulation actions of cultural content representative of the territories, 60 people were trained in the production of convergent content, 20 convergent products were made, of which 15 products are representative of the regions participating in the laboratories and 5 products are presentation of the methodological proposal, productions carried out and reports of the training process. Likewise, within the framework of actions from trajectories, experiences, paths, and learning traced by community radio, there were 40 participating stations with 21 convergent products created (10 infographics and 11 narrative podcasts) and put into circulation.         Finally, from the Stimuli and Circulation line, 134 sound resources were made available to the Content Bank as a result of the 2022 Stimulus Grants in the categories of Sound Narratives of rural Colombia (50 resources), Citizen Radio Strips (54 resources) and Digital sound creation Podcast (30). 40 descriptive sheets and 1 document Knowledge of community radio: Modules for reflection and action.

The key features of this agreement include the facilitation of joint cultural programs, art exhibitions, and music performances, promoting cross-cultural dialogue and understanding. The measure also emphasizes knowledge-sharing between institutions in both cities, focusing on enhancing artistic and cultural development. Additionally, it creates opportunities for artists and cultural professionals from both regions to collaborate, enhancing the mobility of creative talent.

Joint exhibitions and performances have been successful in building cultural bridges and increasing the visibility of Emirati and Korean artists on international platforms. The partnership has also led to enhanced knowledge exchange between cultural institutions in both cities, strengthening their respective cultural infrastructures. It emphasizes community engagement, offering workshops, talks, and interactive activities to foster a deeper connection between artists and the public. The festival also integrates innovative digital elements, such as virtual tours and online exhibitions, to broaden its reach

It has also fostered a sense of cultural pride and identity, encouraging both artists and audiences to explore and celebrate the rich artistic heritage of the UAE.

The festival has also facilitated cultural exchange by highlighting diverse artistic expressions and fostering dialogue among artists, audiences, and international visitors. Community engagement has been a central focus, with a range of interactive workshops, exhibitions, and performances designed to involve the public and enhance their appreciation for art and design. Main Feature: Dans un contexte international marqué par une forte dynamique d’innovation des technologies numériques, le Burkina Faso s’est engagé dans la réduction de la fracture numérique en développant des infrastructures de soutien de base afin de donner de nouvelles opportunités aux secteurs de croissance dont celui de la culture.    L’amélioration de la connectivité filaire 5G consécutivement à l’interconnexion des 13 chefs-lieux de région et de 34 chefs-lieux de province a renforcé l’accès des populations à Internet avec un taux de pénétration de 75,81% des populations burkinabè (Annuaire statistique 2022 du MTDPCE). De facto, cela a contribué ainsi à créer un environnement numérique favorable à la création et à la diffusion de biens et services culturels. Dans ce cadre, le Gouvernement a facilité le développement de plateformes de diffusion et de distribution de contenus culturels (cinéma et audiovisuel, arts de la scène, arts visuels, design et services créatifs). Dans la même lancée, des procédures administratives de l’administration culturelle ont été digitalisées. Toutes ces initiatives ont permis d’améliorer l’accès des artistes et des opérateurs culturels au marché des biens et services culturels et des usagers aux services administratifs.
Results: Les principaux résultats de la mise en œuvre de la mesure sont :   la promotion du e-commerce à travers l’appui pour le développement de vingt (20) plateformes de distribution et de diffusion en ligne des produits culturels dont entre autres :    Mamboné Distribution, Mamzik, Innovartiste, Visas scène dans le domaine des arts de la scène ;    Digit’Radikal’ Art dans le domaine des arts visuels ;   Aiguille virtuelle, Pagne d'or et Mode chez nous dans le domaine de la Mode et du Design ;   Yennenga Movies, Vibes et Fastream dans le domaine du Cinéma et de l'audiovisuel ;       la dématérialisation de la procédure de délivrance des agréments et licences des entreprises culturelles (Licence A et B d'entrepreneur de spectacle) ;    La dématérialisation de la vente de tickets d’entrée aux évènements culturels majeurs (SNC, SIAO, FESPACO, etc.) ;     la réalisation d’un portail culturel de la Région des Hauts-Bassins en vue d’assurer la promotion culturelle au niveau déconcentré.

Area of Monitoring: Media diversity
Agency Implementation: Ministry of the Presidency / Vice Ministry of Communication
Main Feature: The radios of the native indigenous nations and peoples are means of communication aimed at working from and for the community, having elements such as community self-management, their location in the indigenous communities themselves, the use of a native language, broad and permanent participation of listeners. Before the 2019 coup d'état, Bolivia had 105 radio stations in operation. During the irregular government these radio stations were closed and victims of destruction and looting. In 2020, only 18 Radios remained in operation.  Currently there are 58 Radios in operation nationwide.
Results: 58 radios were installed, aimed at working with and by native indigenous nations and peoples, granting them community self-management, location in the indigenous communities themselves, the use of a native language and promoting the broad and permanent participation of local listeners.

Recommandations: It is concluded that the work carried out by the Ministry of the Presidency, through the Vice Ministry of Communication, has resulted in the promotion and encouragement of access to technology for native indigenous nations and peoples, ensuring free expression, access to information, as well as the exercise of journalistic activities. On the other hand, it is concluded that the National System of Radios of the Indigenous People (RPO's) encourages the development of skills and abilities in the field of communication, as well as radio production.

Main Feature: The Republic of Kenya participated in two editions of the International African Textile Exhibition- Système d’Identification et de Traçabilité des Produits Textiles Africains’ (SITA). The Festival brings together players in the textile industry in Africa. Since 2009, SITA has been committed to promoting African textiles, supporting farmers, and encouraging environmentally friendly production methods.  SITA aims to promote the authenticity and legitimacy of African textiles worldwide. By establishing rigorous quality standards and distinctive labels, it seeks to safeguard intellectual property, guarantee fair production standards, and oppose counterfeiting. The initiative also seeks to strengthen the textile economy in Africa by encouraging recognition and appreciation of African textile products, while ensuring appropriate protection of the rights of designers and producers. The festival comprises a training segment where players in the fashion value chain are trained in a given area such as dyeing or weaving techniques. A parade of African Traditional and industrial outfits, an Exhibition sale to discover and buy unique Creations directly from the artisans, Fashion show- presentation of creations by African designers, A tourist excursion an international conference discussing issues and perspectives in African textile led by experts, E-Commerce Training to get advice, sell products online and reach the global market and an awards segment where best actors in African Textiles are honored. Kenya supported 8 fashion designers in the textiles value Chain to participate in the 8th edition held in Lome, Togo, and the 9th  edition held in Conakry, Guinea.
Results: Peer learning and networking with leading African textile enterprises Strengthening of Kenyan Textile entrepreneurs In 2019, SITA launched "Textile Mag", a magazine available in print and online, which highlights African textiles and creates a link between producers, designers and consumers  This event is now one of the major events in the field of textiles in Africa.

Title EN: Sostegno alla micro-imprenditoria femminile ambientalmente sostenibile nel settore turismo rurale finalizzata alla resilienza dei settori vulnerabili
Goal: Integrate Culture In Sustainable Development Frameworks
SDG: SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: National sustainable development policies and plans
Cultural Domain: Design,Performing Arts,Media Arts,Cinema and Audiovisual Arts,Music,Publishing,Visual Arts
Agency Implementation: Università degli Studi di Torino - Sviluppo Sostenibile e Gestione del Territorio
Main Feature: The project aims to improve living conditions in the marginal rural areas of the Republic of Cape Verde, supporting the resilience of the most vulnerable people with particular attention to female empowerment, gender equality and environmental sustainability. Specifically, it plans to promote the resilience of vulnerable families and their inclusion in the growth dynamics of rural tourism development, respecting environmental sustainability and safeguarding biodiversity in three highly marginal areas. The goal will be achieved by offering quality services related to the preservation and enhancement of the environmental and cultural resources of the territory through support for micro-entrepreneurship, especially for women.  According the Chair’s aim, a positive change can be achieved through the enhancement of the environmental heritage and the promotion of mountain tourism and of the tools identified in the interinstitutional collaboration. It focuses on a permanent support network, female entrepreneurs, and permanent financial support (guarantee fund) for the start-up and tourist offers activated with consequent integration of agricultural income and greater resilience of families through the definition of “Guidelines for the development of sustainable rural tourism”.  The planned actions aim to achieve the following expected results: 1. Establishment of a network of local stakeholders with the aid of international excellence expertise to improve inclusive and sustainable approaches, with a focus on benefiting vulnerable sectors through a gender-based perspective; 2. Availability of targeted tourist proposals that safeguard and enhance the environmental, economic and cultural resources, and that ensure a positive impact on the inhabitant people in terms of increasing their resilience in the areas of residence and in their traditional activity, while preserving the social network; 3. Activation or establishment of decentralized economic entities to ensure the sustainability of offers for the benefit of the people, within a framework of economic, environmental and gender sustainability.

Title EN: Soutenir les travailleurs freelances dans les secteurs créatifs en Tunisie
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture
SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Partnering with civil society
Cultural Domain: Design,Performing Arts,Media Arts,Cinema and Audiovisual Arts,Music,Publishing,Visual Arts
Agency Implementation: réseau des freelances et professionnels tunisiens qui regroupe les talents de l'informatique, du design, de l'audiovisuel, de l'art, du multimédia, de l'édition et de bien d'autres secteurs.
Main Feature: Les travailleurs freelances représentent la principale force de production et de développement des secteurs créatifs en Tunisie. Ce mode de travail indépendant leur offre non seulement un moyen d'expression et de création, mais aussi leur principale source de revenus et souvent leur seule opportunité d'emploi. En revanche, ces travailleurs opèrent dans un cadre informel, souvent non réglementé, en raison de l'inadéquation des législations et des lois avec ce nouveau mode de travail. Cette informalité influence profondément le secteur créatif en Tunisie et expose les freelances à des risques majeurs : absence de statut, absence de protection des droits d'auteur, concurrence sur le marché international, précarité et marginalisation.  Les mesures prises par le projet visent à mobiliser les freelances afin qu'ils se regroupent au sein d'une structure représentative (Tunisian Freelancers COOP) et à encourager les décideurs administratifs et politiques à développer des lois et des législations permettant d'intégrer ces travailleurs dans les circuits formels, tout en conservant les avantages du travail freelance dans les secteurs créatifs.
Results: - Création d’une communauté de freelances dans les secteurs créatifs à travers une série de rencontres appelées « les cafés des freelances ».  - Établissement de partenariats avec les ministères et les administrations publiques en vue de répondre aux problématiques de l’informalité du travail freelance dans les secteurs créatifs.  - Ouverture d’un débat national sur le travail freelance en Tunisie.  - Révision des lois et des législations en rapport avec le mode de travail freelance en Tunisie dans les secteurs créatifs, comme la loi de l’auto-entrepreneur et le statut de l’artiste.

Title EN: Soutien à la mise en œuvre de projets structurants des opérateurs culturels à travers des programmes cofinancés par l’Etat et ses partenaires
Goal: Integrate Culture In Sustainable Development Frameworks
SDG: SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: National sustainable development policies and plans
Agency Implementation: Ministère de la Communication, de la Culture, des Arts et du Tourisme (MCCAT)   Bureau de Coopération Suisse (BUCO)   Conseil Régional des Hauts-Bassins
Main Feature: Dans le cadre de sa politique de soutien au secteur de la culture, le Gouvernement du Burkina Faso a entrepris, à partir de 2015, une révision de ses référentiels de planification sectorielle en vue de mieux définir le rôle, la contribution et les moyens d’actions de la culture dans les processus de développement national tels que contenus dans les référentiels nationaux de développement notamment le Plan national de développement économique et social (2016-2020) et le Référentiel national de développement (2021-2025). Cela a été également l’occasion pour le pays d’internaliser un ensemble d’orientations et d’objectifs de développement assignés au secteur de la culture par les instances internationales et sous-régionales. Il s’est agi de la prise en compte des objectifs sectoriels de l’Agenda 2030 visant à améliorer les conditions de vie des hommes et des femmes dans toutes leurs dimensions y compris le secteur culturel ainsi que la directive de l’UEMOA portant harmonisation de la loi de finances au sein des pays membres, qui consacre le passage du budget objet au budget programme. Dans cette dynamique, un nouveau référentiel de développement du secteur culturel à savoir la Stratégie nationale de développement de la culture et du tourisme (SNCT) a été adoptée pour la période (2018-2027) avec comme innovation majeure l’approche programme guidée par les principes de la Gestion axée sur les résultats (GAR) et la mise en place de systèmes et mécanismes participatifs et inclusifs d’élaboration, de suivi et d’évaluation de la mise en œuvre des politiques publiques.    Cette volonté politique clairement inscrite dans les priorités des référentiels de développement a favorisé la mise en place de programmes de développement prévoyant de booster les principaux maillons de la chaîne des valeurs des Industries culturelles et créatives (ICC). Ainsi, sur la période (2020-2024), le soutien au développement du secteur culturel national, a été fortement marqué par l’opérationnalisation de deux programmes majeurs que sont le Programme d’appui aux industries créatives et à la gouvernance culturelle (PAIC-GC, 2018-2024) et le Programme d’appui au secteur de la culture, phase 5 (PASEC 5, 2019-2022) cofinancés par l’Etat et ses partenaires techniques et financiers (PTF) notamment l’Union Européenne (UE) et le Bureau de la coopération Suisse et agence consulaire au Burkina Faso.   Les programmes ont été initiés en vue de contribuer à l’atteinte de l’objectif général de la Stratégie nationale de la culture et du tourisme (SNCT) à savoir : Créer une dynamique de développement culturel et touristique, fondée sur les valeurs communes propres aux Burkinabè, les capacités entrepreneuriales et la créativité des acteurs, en vue de l'épanouissement économique et social des populations du Burkina Faso.    De façon spécifique, le PAIC-GC vise les objectifs suivants :    améliorer la création d’emplois dans les filières prioritaires, moteur des industries culturelles ;   contribuer au renforcement de la gouvernance culturelle du Ministère  en charge de la culture, des arts et du tourisme (MCAT) et de la décentralisation culturelle au niveau régional.   Quant au PASEC  5, sa mise en œuvre vise :    les opérateurs culturels, qui avec le soutien du programme, participent par la création/production et la diffusion d’œuvres de qualité à la construction de la citoyenneté, de la bonne gouvernance, de la cohésion sociale et de la paix ;    les opérateurs culturels partenaires soutenus par le programme améliorent leurs capacités de gestion et diversifient leurs ressources pour assurer leur pérennité ;    le partenariat avec l’État et le fonds de développement culturel et touristique renforce l’offre d’appuis techniques et financiers adaptés aux besoins des opérateurs culturels, en particulier pour les initiatives artistiques des jeunes et des femmes.
Results: La mise en œuvre du PAIC GC et du PASEC 5 a créé un intérêt auprès de l’ensemble des acteurs culturels du Burkina Faso et particulièrement ceux des filières prioritaires concernées (le cinéma et l’audiovisuel, les arts de la scène et les arts visuels). Les résultats de la mesure se présentent comme suit :   la gouvernance du secteur culturel renforcée. Les interventions ont permis de renforcer la capacité d’action du Ministère de la communication, de la culture et des arts et du tourisme (MCCAT), du Conseil Régional des Hauts Bassins (CRHB), au plan institutionnel, organisationnel et logistique. Au total, 224 agents publics ont pris part à divers programmes de formation initiés dans le cadre du PAIC-GC (90 agents formés dans le cadre du Programme Transversal de Formation, 09 agents au titre de la formation certifiante, 18 enseignants d’art et culture et 07 autres agents de l’Administration publique centrale et déconcentrée). En outre, les capacités opérationnelles des structures centrales et déconcentrées du MCCAT, du CRHB et du Fonds de développement culturel et touristique (FDCT) ont été renforcées grâce à la dotation en moyens roulant, en matériels informatiques et en mobilier de bureau. Ces structures sont aujourd’hui plus aptes à initier, à mettre en œuvre et à évaluer des actions de promotion du secteur. Par ailleurs, les capacités techniques et opérationnelles du principal instrument de financement du secteur culturel au niveau national (FDCT) ont été renforcées. Cela s’est matérialisé à travers entre autres, une évaluation des process et du profil des agents du FDCT, d’une part et d’autre part le recrutement de profils spécifiques manquants mais également par la formation ciblée des agents sur des thématiques comme la gestion du cycle du crédit, l’analyse des demandes de financement et le suivi-évaluation des projets financés, toute chose qui contribue à renforcer le principe d’équité et de transparence dans les processus d’appel à projets du FDCT.    En somme, la mise en œuvre des programmes a été un tremplin pour renforcer les capacités des administrations publiques en charge de la culture, consolider le mécanisme national de financement du secteur culturel et renforcer le processus de planification culturelle au niveau local. Les initiatives développées par les bénéficiaires dans le cadre desdits programmes ont parfaitement intégré l’atteinte des objectifs de développement de la SNCT qui vise à créer une dynamique de développement culturel, fondée sur les valeurs communes propres aux Burkinabè, les capacités entrepreneuriales et la créativité des acteurs.     Les capacités technique et opérationnelle des acteurs culturels renforcées : les acteurs culturels ont bénéficié de formations à travers un programme spécifique dédié. Les actions de formation inscrites dans le cadre du PAIC GC ont permis de toucher plus de 500 professionnels des filières du cinéma et de l’audiovisuel, des arts de la scène, des arts plastiques y compris le design. Cela a favorisé l’appropriation du processus créatif et de mise en marché des différentes filières et donné une nouvelle orientation à leurs actions à travers les projets financés. Plusieurs organisations sont en mesure de monter des projets structurants pour la recherche de financement auprès d’institutions financières nationale et internationale. A travers les projets financés, les organisations bénéficiaires se sont dotées de moyens techniques de production modernes pour l’amélioration de la qualité des œuvres. Certains de ces projets ont permis de renforcer les capacités techniques des acteurs culturels des maillons faibles de la chaine de valeurs. C’est notamment le cas de la mise en marché, du digital et des curateurs, ce qui devrait se traduire par une réduction des coûts de production et une amélioration de la compétitivité des produits d’origine burkinabè ;   l’accès des acteurs culturels au financement amélioré :  Sur la période 2020-2024, la mise en œuvre des deux programmes a favorisé la mobilisation des ressources financière au profit des opérateurs culturels, cela a permis d’octroyer des soutiens financiers structurants aux acteurs des filières culturelles prioritaires, pourvoyeurs d’emplois et de revenus pour l’économie nationale. En effet, plus de 279 structures (entreprises et associations) ont bénéficié de financement pour la mise en œuvre de leurs projets grâce au programme PAIC GC et du PASEC 5. Au-delà des appuis financiers directs aux opérateurs, les programmes ont permis de renforcer la structuration du secteur culturel dans une logique entrepreneuriale ;   le processus de la décentralisation culturelle dans la région des Hauts-Bassins consolidé :  après le transfert des compétences et des ressources en 2014, les attentes des Collectivités territoriales (CT) étaient la mise en œuvre d’actions opérationnelles concrètes au niveau décentralisé. En effet, la quasi-totalité des ressources allouées au secteur culturel était gérée au niveau central, toute chose qui ne facilitait pas l’accès aux financements des opérateurs culturels locaux. Pour changer cet état de fait, des actions spécifiques ont été initiées à l’adresse des collectivités territoriales dans la mise en œuvre des deux programmes.  A ce titre, le volet appui au renforcement de la décentralisation culturelle dans les Régions des Hauts-Bassins et du Centre-Ouest soutenu respectivement par le PAIC-GC et le PASEC 5 a permis aux autorités des CT desdites Régions de se doter de stratégies de développement de la culture et de l’économie culturelle des collectivités. En outre, la Région des Hauts-Bassins a également bénéficié d’un portail culturel et d’une enveloppe financière dédiée aux financements des besoins spécifiques des acteurs culturels locaux à hauteur de 647 286 USD (345 689 339 FCFA) dont 33 162,7 USD (17 710 839 FCFA) comme contribution du CRHBS, destiné à la promotion des filières culturelles et du tourisme culturel ;    la contribution du secteur culturel à l’économie nationale améliorée : plus de 2 000 emplois directs et indirects ont été générés par les activités des deux interventions. Faisant passer le taux d’accroissement des emplois culturels de 11% en 2018 à 11,30% en 2021. Quant au taux d'accroissement du nombre d’entreprises culturelles formelles, cet indicateur a enregistré une évolution satisfaisante entre 2019 et 2020 (+7,32 points). Cette performance correspond aux résultats attendus de la Stratégie nationale de la culture et du tourisme (SNCT). Elle résultait de l’effet de l’augmentation des financements publics aux opérateurs, du renforcement des capacités en matière de formalisation et d’une meilleure capitalisation des données culturelles et touristiques par l’INSD.

Title EN: Soutien annuel de l'Union Nationale des Femmes au Maroc
Goal: Promote Human Rights And Fundamental Freedoms
SDG: SDG 5 - Achieve gender equality and empower all women and girls,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels
Area of Monitoring: Gender equality
Cultural Domain: Design,Performing Arts,Media Arts,Cinema and Audiovisual Arts,Music,Publishing,Visual Arts
Agency Implementation: Ministère de la Jeunesse, de la Culture et de la Communication-Département de la Culture
Main Feature: L'Union Nationale des Femmes du Maroc (UNFM), fondée en 1969 par Feu Sa Majesté le Roi Hassan II, œuvre depuis plus de cinquante ans aux côtés des femmes et des jeunes filles. Grâce à une multitude d'actions concrètes et convergentes, l'UNFM s'attache à garantir les droits des femmes, à les protéger contre toutes formes de violences, et à favoriser leur pleine participation au développement. Dans cette optique, l'UNFM se positionne comme un levier essentiel pour une croissance plus inclusive et durable, déployant une multitude d'initiatives destinées à promouvoir la capacitation des femmes et des jeunes filles. Parmi ces initiatives, le partenariat annuel avec le département de la culture occupe une place prépondérante, apportant une contribution significative à l'accomplissement de la mission de l'UNFM. Chaque année, l'UNFM collabore étroitement avec le département de la culture à côté des autres départements ministériels pour mener à bien divers projets et activités culturelles. Ce partenariat stratégique joue un rôle crucial dans l'émancipation des femmes et des jeunes filles, en leur offrant des plateformes et des ressources pour développer leurs talents et renforcer leur présence dans le secteur culturel. Grâce à ce partenariat, des événements culturels, des expositions artistiques et des festivals sont organisés régulièrement pour mettre en lumière les talents féminins. Ces événements permettent aux femmes artistes de s'exprimer librement et de sensibiliser le public aux enjeux de genre à travers des œuvres culturelles et artistiques. Le partenariat permet également la mise en place d'ateliers et de formations dans diverses disciplines artistiques et métiers de la culture. Ces programmes offrent aux femmes et aux jeunes filles l'opportunité d'acquérir de nouvelles compétences, de se former en gestion culturelle et de se préparer à des carrières dans le domaine culturel. En collaboration avec le département de la culture, l'UNFM établit et renforce des bibliothèques et des centres de lecture dans plusieurs régions du Maroc. Ces infrastructures fournissent un accès précieux à des ressources éducatives et culturelles, favorisant ainsi l'alphabétisation et l'éducation continue des femmes et des jeunes filles. Des campagnes de sensibilisation sont menées pour promouvoir les droits des femmes et combattre les stéréotypes de genre. Des conférences et des débats sont organisés pour discuter de thématiques culturelles et sociales, sensibilisant ainsi le public aux questions de genre et encourageant une société plus inclusive. L'UNFM et le département de la culture apportent un soutien financier et logistique à des projets culturels initiés par des femmes. Cela inclut la production de films, la publication de livres et d'autres initiatives créatives, contribuant à la visibilité et à la valorisation des femmes dans le secteur culturel. Ce partenariat annuel entre l'UNFM et le département de la culture renforce la mission de l'organisation en offrant aux femmes et aux jeunes filles des outils et des opportunités pour s'émanciper et s'épanouir. En intégrant la dimension culturelle à ses actions, l'UNFM touche un public plus large et instaure un changement durable dans les mentalités et les pratiques sociétales. En somme, le partenariat avec le département de la culture illustre parfaitement comment la collaboration entre différents acteurs peut aboutir à une croissance plus inclusive et durable. Il permet aux femmes de jouer un rôle actif et reconnu dans le développement de la société, contribuant ainsi à la réalisation des objectifs de l'UNFM pour un avenir meilleur et plus équitable pour toutes et tous.

Title EN: Soutien aux parents pendant les résidences et les voyages de recherche
Goal: Achieve A Balanced Flow Of Cultural Goods And Services And Increase The Mobility Of Artists And Cultural Professionals
SDG: SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 10 - Reduce inequality within and among countries,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Mobility of artists and cultural professionals
Agency Implementation: Fondation suisse pour la culture Pro Helvetia
Main Feature: Les artistes dont les enfants sont mineurs (moins de 18 ans) et qui participent à une résidence ou à un voyage de recherche mis au concours par la Fondation suisse pour la culture Pro Helvetia peuvent demander un soutien financier supplémentaire pouvant atteindre 1107 dollars américains par mois de voyage. La contribution financière peut cofinancer les frais suivants liés à la résidence ou au voyage de recherche : frais supplémentaires de garde d'enfants à destination ou au domicile, frais de voyage supplémentaires pour les enfants et/ou une personne de garde qui les accompagne, frais d'hébergement supplémentaires liés aux enfants et/ou à une personne de garde.
Results: Depuis juin 2022, 45 artistes soutenus avec enfant(s) ont bénéficié de cette mesure. Les retours sont généralement positifs. Les artistes apprécient le soutien financier supplémentaire qui peut être utilisé de manière très flexible et adaptée aux besoins individuels de la famille.
Recommandations: L'évaluation est encore en cours, mais les premières conclusions montrent que la mesure est bien accueillie. La communication proactive du soutien aux parents lors de la promotion des résidences et des voyages de recherche, ainsi que pendant le processus de candidature, est particulièrement appréciée.

Title EN: Soutien de l’Agence française de développement (AFD) aux ICC
Goal: Integrate Culture In Sustainable Development Frameworks

Main Feature: L’AFD s’est vu confier en 2018 un nouveau mandat afin de soutenir le secteur des ICC. En 2022, l’agence a engagé près de 36,1 millions d’euros dans le développement des ICC, dont 56% en Afrique. Les projets soutenus par l’AFD ont pour objectifs :  •	La professionnalisation des acteurs de la culture, le développement de l’entrepreneuriat et la promotion d’un tourisme durable.  •	Le renforcement de l’égalité d’accès des femmes et des hommes aux biens et services culturels.
Results: À travers le lancement d’appels à projets, l’AFD soutient la société civile et les entrepreneurs culturels afin d’accompagner la structuration de l’écosystème culturel et créatif et favoriser l’émergence d’actions à fort impact social. Deux programmes phares sont ainsi déployés en Afrique depuis 2019 : Accès Culture et Afrique Créative. •	Accès Culture (3 M€) : mis en œuvre en partenariat avec l’Institut Français, le dispositif vise à financer des projets culturels à fort impact social portés en binômes par des associations africaines et françaises. •	Afrique Créative (2 M€) : ce dispositif d’incubation vise à soutenir l’entrepreneuriat créatif à travers un accompagnement technique et financier. Ces deux programmes ont permis, depuis 2019, le soutien d’une centaine de projets ICC dans 30 pays africains.
