Title EN: Soutien du secteur culturel en tant que partie de la coopération internationale de la Suisse : « North Africa Cultural program »
Goal: Integrate Culture In Sustainable Development Frameworks
SDG: SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: International cooperation for sustainable development
Cultural Domain: Performing Arts,Cinema and Audiovisual Arts,Music,Publishing,Visual Arts
Agency Implementation: Direction du Développement et de la Coopération DDC
Main Feature: Le thème « Culture et développement » fait partie de la stratégie de coopération internationale de la Suisse. L’agence gouvernementale suisse pour le développement, la Direction du développement et de la coopération (DDC), utilise une partie de ses fonds pour l’art et la culture dans ses programmes nationaux de coopération au développement (environ 1 % du budget consacré à un pays partenaire). La Suisse soutient la culture en tant que droit humain. Par ailleurs, un secteur culturel dynamique et indépendant est un moteur de changement social, qui promeut la liberté d'expression et la participation démocratique, et qui constitue la base d'une société civile forte. En outre, les échanges et le dialogue interculturels peuvent constituer la base d'une coexistence pacifique en renforçant la confiance entre les communautés et en promouvant la tolérance et la solidarité.  Le programme culturel régional en Afrique du Nord en est un exemple. L'objectif général de ce programme est de renforcer le dialogue interculturel, la solidarité et les moyens de subsistance, en particulier chez les jeunes femmes et les jeunes hommes, et d'encourager l'expression créative en tant que vecteur de changement. La promotion des arts et de la culture est un moyen supplémentaire pour atteindre les objectifs de la Suisse en Afrique du Nord en termes de stabilité politique, de prospérité économique et de gestion des migrations, en encourageant le dialogue et la compréhension entre les peuples de la région et en prévenant la violence.
Results: À travers « North Africa Cultural program », la Suisse a pu promouvoir, entre 2020 et 2023, la diversité des expressions culturelles dans la région de l’Afrique du Nord, en appuyant plus de 50 organisations et espaces culturels en Tunisie, en Algérie, en Égypte, en Libye et au Maroc, mais aussi au niveau d’autres régions, dont le moyen orient et l’Afrique subsaharienne, en appuyant la coopération sud-sud entre les organisations basées en Afrique du Nord et leur voisinage.  Le programme renforce la résilience des organisations culturelles indépendantes en Afrique du Nord et offre la possibilité aux jeunes artistes de promouvoir leurs compétences et d’échanger entre elles et entre eux, en facilitant ainsi le réseautage et la mobilité des artistes dans la région, qui a connu des défis importants surtout durant la pandémie du COVID-19.  En outre, le programme offre un appui structurel et programmatique aux organisations qui interviennent dans plusieurs domaines culturels, tels que les arts visuels, la musique, la production cinématographique, les arts de la scène et les arts numériques.  Le programme a opté pour une approche inclusive et de proximité, ce qui a permis d’atteindre plusieurs jeunes artistes dans les zones rurales où l’accès à la culture n’est pas forcément acquis. C’est le cas du Centre culturel des arts et métiers de la montagne de Semmama, un espace conçu pour les enfants, les jeunes et les adultes essentiellement originaires des zones rurales et défavorisées, dans le but d’encourager « l’action culturelle et sportive » à travers des clubs de cinéma, de théâtre, de cirque, de musique et d’activités sportives afin de les sensibiliser à la culture et au sport à l’aide d’une programmation culturelle de proximité, et ce dans un cadre d’action difficile dans une zone frontalière connue par plusieurs mouvements des groupes terroristes dans les montagnes de Kasserine et notamment dans la montagne de Semmama. Le programme a permis d’ouvrir des formations à des jeunes artistes et à des femmes de milieux ruraux, et de les inclure dans un écosystème de production et de « branding » des produits artistiques de la région, permettant ainsi l’autonomisation financière d’un nombre de jeunes et de femmes dans la région de Semmama.  La fin de l’année 2023 a connu la confirmation d’une nouvelle phase de ce programme qui va continuer jusqu’en octobre 2027.
Recommandations: Le renforcement organisationnel et structurel des structures culturelles leur a permis de faire preuve de résilience face aux conséquences économiques liées à la pandémie du COVID-19 et elles sont ainsi sorties plus fortes de cette crise.  L'évaluation a recommandé que, dans la perspective d'une éventuelle nouvelle phase, la théorie de changement soit développée conjointement avec l'organisation chargée de la mise en œuvre et que les indicateurs concrets soient optimisés. En outre, il est nécessaire de développer un plan de renforcement des capacités et de réseautage pour une éventuelle phase 2, et de formaliser des protocoles d’entente entre l'organisation chargée de la mise en œuvre et les représentations suisses dans les pays ciblés par le programme.

Title EN: SPECIAL PROGRAM IN CULTURAL PUBLIC MANAGEMENT
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture
SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Cultural and creative sectors
Agency Implementation: General Directorate of Cultural Industries and Arts (Ministry of Culture)
Main Feature: The Special Program for Cultural Public Management (PEGPC) is organized jointly with the National School of Public Administration – ENAP, belonging to the National Civil Service Authority (SERVIR) and the General Directorate of Cultural Industries and Arts of the Ministry of Culture, with the support of the UNESCO Office in Lima. ENAP is the public entity in charge of providing training for managers and training for Peruvian public servants on public administration and management issues. The PEGPC is the first program that trains and certifies public servants in cultural public management.  The Cultural Public Management Program, in virtual mode, is aimed at those responsible for the cultural units or areas of local governments, for which a space is opened for 35 people for each course, with the intention of working on the contents in class. of each session. The Program lasts 3 months and has a total of 100 teaching hours, which is structured as follows: 1.	Course 1: Cultural management for generation of public value (32 hours) 2.	Course 2: Strategic negotiation in cultural public management (32 hours) 3.	Course 3: Processes approach and permanent improvement in cultural public management (32 hours) 4.	Conference of experts (4 hours) This program was launched for the first time in 2020, by 2023 it has had 5 editions, one per year, except for the first year when two editions were held. The Diagnosis on the impact of Covid19 on the cultural industries and arts, identified as one of the problems the weakness of subnational governments in matters of public cultural management generated, among other causes, in the lack of capabilities of the public servants in charge. Although this problem is not a direct consequence of the pandemic, given that this weakness already existed previously, it did, however, exacerbate the gap. For this reason, the implementation of the PEGPC responds to the need to strengthen cultural governance, identified in the NCP and in the IPC 2016-2020.
Results: A total of 559 public servants applied, benefiting a total of 179 cultural leaders in subnational governments from all regions of the country.
Recommandations: The need to expand the training offer has been identified so that it reaches more public servants, not only those in leadership positions but also middle management and cultural promoters. It is necessary to implement a monitoring system in order to measure the impact on the participants and the territories where they operate.

Title EN: Status of Cultural Professionals
Goal: Promote Human Rights And Fundamental Freedoms
SDG: SDG 5 - Achieve gender equality and empower all women and girls,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels
Area of Monitoring: Artistic freedom
Cultural Domain: Design,Performing Arts,Media Arts,Cinema and Audiovisual Arts,Music,Publishing,Visual Arts
Agency Implementation: Ministry of Culture (Directorate General for Books, Archives and Libraries and General Inspection of Cultural Activities)
Main Feature: The Statute for Professionals in the Cultural Area was approved by the Decree-Law no. 105/2021. This law applies to professionals in the performing arts, audiovisual, visual arts and literary creation, who carry out an authorial, artistic, technical-artistic or cultural mediation activity. In order to cover all the employment relationships that are established within the culture sector, as well as the respective social protection regime, the Statute is divided into three essential parts: (i) the register of professionals in the field of culture (RPAC), (ii) the employment contract and service provision regime; and (iii) the social protection regime. In addition to the individual identification of cultural professionals, the purpose of the Statute is to structure and statistically identify the cultural sector in order to define public policies for professional and technical development, support and other public benefits. Although registration is optional, only those who are registered benefit from the special contributory scheme provided for in the Statute. Secondly, and with the aim of being broad and comprehensive, the Statute regulates the various ways of providing cultural activity, including both employment contracts and contracts for the provision of services.
Results: In addition to the creation of the new subsidy for the suspension of cultural activity, the Statute includes other measures, namely: Extending social protection to all eventualities (suspension, parenthood, illness and occupational diseases); Adoption of the presumption of an employment contract in the culture sector, with different contribution rates being created to discourage the signing of more precarious contracts; Combating false green receipts through the creation of a new contribution rate to be paid by entities that choose to enter into service provision contracts, accompanied by a new declarative obligation to justify this option; Establishment of a specific inspection regime for situations involving service provision contracts; Simplification of the delivery of contributions through the figure of withholding tax and the possibility of, in cases where this is not possible, the cultural professional making the payment through the entity benefiting from the benefit. The Decree-Law No. 25/2024, of April 1, makes the second amendment to the Statute of Professionals in the Area of Culture, as foreseen and after an initial period of validity and integrating contributions from the sector.

Mongolia has implemented progressive measures to enhance regulation of the creative economy sector, focusing on state support across various domains: Cinema, sound arts; Visual arts; Songs and music; Fashion; Digital content and game development; Literature, books, and publications.
Results: "Cultural Creative Month" campaign was held annually from 2021 to 2023 to promote 12 domains of cultural and creative industry, organising a total of 9,003 cultural and artistic events nationwide and supporting over 350 enterprises and artists. Drawing inspiration from France's "Culture Pass" program, implemented in over 50 countries, Mongolia conducted a study in 2023 involving 51,128 teenagers to enhance access to cultural services. To enhance the global visibility and competitiveness of Mongolian visual artists' intellectual works, the Mongolian pavilion was successfully showcased at the 59th and 60th Venice Biennale of Fine Arts. Mongolian artists also participated in the "On the Move" (MOVE) exhibition in Qatar and the NordArt International Fine Arts Exhibition in 2022 and 2024. Title EN: Statut de l’artiste
Goal: Promote Human Rights And Fundamental Freedoms
SDG: SDG 5 - Achieve gender equality and empower all women and girls,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels
Area of Monitoring: Artistic freedom
Cultural Domain: Design,Performing Arts,Media Arts,Cinema and Audiovisual Arts,Music,Publishing,Visual Arts
Agency Implementation: Présidence de la République Ministère de la Culture et des Arts Conseil National des Arts et des Lettres (CNAL)
Main Feature: La promulgation du décret présidentiel n° 23-376 du 22 octobre 2023 portant statut de l’artiste, est l’aboutissement de nombre de concertations avec les différents acteurs du secteur culturel et artistique consistant en : Trente-six (36) rencontres avec artistes et acteurs du mouvement associatif au nombre de dix mille huit cent (10800) à travers les cinquante-huit (58) wilayas (départements) ont eu lieu du 24 septembre 2022 au 24 novembre 2022 conférant ainsi une dimension nationale à ces consultations, animées par, entre autres,  -	un représentant du Conseil National des Arts et des Lettres (CNAL -	un représentant de la Direction de Développement et Promotion des Arts (DDPA), -	 les directeurs de la Culture des Wilayas, un représentant de l’Office National des Droits d’Auteurs et Droits Voisins (ONDA), -	 un représentant des Directions des Wilayas chargées de l’Emploi et de la Sécurité Sociale (DESS),  -	des représentants de wilayas de la Caisse Nationale des Assurances Sociales des Travailleurs Salariés (CNAS) et des représentants de wilayas de Caisse Nationale des Assurances Sociale des Travailleurs Non-Salariés (CASNOS), -	des représentants de wilayas de la Caisse Nationale des Retraites (CNR) ; -	des représentants de wilayas de l’Inspection du Travail.  Mise en ligne d’un questionnaire sur les plateformes du Ministère de la Culture et des Arts dans l’objectif d’élargir les consultations à plus grande échelle notamment pour les artistes et hommes de lettres établis à l’étranger. Ce questionnaire a permis la collecte de près de mille trois cents (1300) avis éclairés à l’intérieur et à l’extérieur.   La lecture et l’analyse des différentes données collectées à l’issue de la mise en ligne du questionnaire ont été confiées à une équipe d’experts en analyse de données statistiques en ayant recours au Logiciel d’Analyse Statistique (SPSS). En date du 24 décembre 2022, tous les résultats obtenus (rencontres et questionnaires) ont été remis au Président de la Commission chargée de la rédaction du projet de loi portant Statut de l’Artiste en l’occurrence Monsieur Missoum LAROUSSI, commission composée d’experts pluridisciplinaires (juristes et artistes)  pour présentation à Madame la Ministre de la Culture et des Arts à la date du 29 mars 2023. La Commission chargée de la rédaction du projet de loi portant Statut de l’Artiste a enregistré la participation d’artistes et professionnels du cinéma et spectacle vivant au cours de ses vingt-trois (23) séances tenantes, lequel projet dans sa première mouture a été soumis pour lecture aux acteurs concernés dans le cadre d’une rencontre nationale qui s’est tenue en date du 9 mai 2023, ayant regroupé quatre cent soixante-dix (470)  intervenants entre artistes et associations professionnelles, ce qui a donné lieu à l’enrichissement du projet de loi en question pour une mouture finale.  Ce projet de loi ainsi présenté en la forme du décret présidentiel susmentionné, fixe les droits et obligations de l’artiste, en s’inscrivant dans la diversité culturelle prônée dans les recommandations de l’UNESCO sur la condition de l’artiste en date du 27 octobre 1980.  Il définit le cadre juridique dans lequel l’artiste doit évoluer et exercer son métier en toute sécurité et dans la garantie de la préservation de ses droits les plus fondamentaux notamment ses libertés d’expression et de création. Ce statut s’articule autour de trois (03) axes principaux : Une redéfinition précise des différents métiers de l’artiste et concepts à savoir, technicien d’œuvres artistiques, administrateur d’œuvres artistiques, auto entrepreneurs activités artistiques, création artistique, contrat artistique, contrepartie artistique, métiers artistiques et établissements artistiques. Ce sont là autant de métiers et de concepts qui ont été adaptés aux différents changements et mutation qu’a connu le monde d’une manière générale et l’Algérie en particulier, de sorte à garantir le renouveau insufflé et voulu par le pays. Une définition des droits et obligations de l’artiste, tant matériels que moraux, une mise en place de dispositions relatives respectivement aux enfants et aux personnes à besoins spécifiques, aux artistes étrangers en situation régulière, à la protection sociale de l’artiste, le tout à travers une carte dite « carte d’artiste » qui confère à ce dernier sa qualité d’artiste et par conséquent tous les droits prévus par la législation et règlementation en vigueur. Une définition du cadre réglementaire propre à la pratique de l’activité artistique de sorte à garantir à celui-ci une protection juridique à l’exercice de son art et des modalités de sa rémunération dans le respect des lois et de la dignité qui lui est due. Cet axe met en place une nomenclature de métiers artistiques, définit les établissements artistiques et traite, en outre, des modalités de promotion de l’activité de l’artiste. In fine, ce statut a impliqué une large consultation avec différents partenaires et acteurs de l’industrie artistique et a été conçu de sorte à répondre aux différentes attentes et aspirations du monde artistique.
Results: Un (01) texte d’application est en cours d’élaboration en rapport avec la création d’un mécanisme de remboursement des artistes, techniciens d’œuvres artistiques et administrateurs d’œuvres artistiques en cas d’arrêt involontaire de l’exercice de l’activité artistique.   Deux (02) textes d’application ont été élaborées à savoir ceux en rapport avec les modalités de création et de gestion des coopératives artistiques ainsi que la nomenclature des métiers artistiques auprès des services du Ministère chargé de la culture, nomenclature ayant recensé deux cent vingt et un (221) métiers artistiques regroupés en neuf (09) domaines artistiques à savoir : les arts littéraires, les arts dramatiques, les arts musicaux, les arts du spectacle, les arts chorégraphiques, les arts visuels, les arts cinématographiques et de l’audiovisuel, les arts de la rue et les arts numériques.  A ce jour, douze mille six cent quatre-vingt-seize (12696) cartes d’artiste ont été délivrées.

Title EN: Stellar Program
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture
SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Cultural and creative sectors
Agency Implementation: Unlimited A.C.M
Main Feature: The Stellar Program, established in 2019 by UAE Unlimited, is an ongoing educational initiative designed to support emerging artists in the United Arab Emirates. The program spans 6-8 months and includes mentorship sessions, guest artist tutorship, and practical workshops aimed at enhancing the artists' education beyond traditional art school curricula. The program is divided into three main sections, running concurrently with the planning and production of the exhibition. Each year, a guest artist provides mentorship, guiding the artists through proposal development, production planning, and the execution of their final artwork. Offering insights into art theory, criticism, and practice, providing feedback and advice on the artists' concepts and techniques. Additionally, four day-long workshops cover key skills such as artwork photography, media relations, art writing, and art business, led by leading arts professionals from the UAE. The Stellar Program is led by engaging tutors, advisors, and artists, equipping participants with the tools and techniques to excel in their professional artistic careers.
Results: Through comprehensive mentorship, intensive sessions with established artists, and practical workshops, participants have gained invaluable knowledge and skills. These initiatives have enhanced the artists' understanding of contemporary art, improved their technical abilities, and prepared them for successful careers. The program has fostered a supportive and dynamic artistic community, promoting cultural production and artistic excellence in the UAE. Through these efforts, UAE Unlimited has reinforced its commitment to nurturing emerging talent and contributing to the broader cultural development goals of the region. The Stellar Program continues to be implemented, ensuring ongoing support and development for the UAE's emerging artists.
Recommandations: The UAE Unlimited Stellar Program is a notable initiative designed to support and nurture emerging artists from the UAE. It offers a platform for young artists to develop their skills, collaborate with established professionals, and present their work in significant exhibitions. The program emphasizes mentorship and professional development, providing resources and opportunities to help artists reach their full potential. Recommendations for enhancing this program include expanding its outreach to a wider range of disciplines and integrating more technology-based art forms to keep pace with contemporary trends.

Title EN: Strategy for Arts Council Norway and the Norwegian Cultural Fund   2021–2024
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture
SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Cultural and creative sectors
Agency Implementation: Arts and Culture Norway
Main Feature: In 2021, Arts Council Norway adopted a new four-year strategy for the period 2021–2024. The strategy focuses on two key areas that the Council believes must be prioritized during this time: 1.	Diversity – New Voices, Expressions, and Aesthetic Practices: The Council recognizes that many artists and actors do not apply for participation in the Cultural Fund’s schemes and projects. Structural elements, such as language and scheme design, may hinder new applicants. The Council aims to foster conversations and learning from perspectives that have previously been underserved and marginalized.  2.	More Space for Differing Expressions – Uncongenial Fellowship: Through various schemes, Arts Council Norway defends artistic and cultural expressions as free forms of creativity. They strive to create vibrant and critical public audiences that strengthen the position of arts and culture in society. The Council encourages a climate of expression where organizers, producers, and artists can take risks. To achieve its purpose and primary objectives during this period, the Council has implemented several measures: •	Prioritizing broad representation and expertise when appointing peers to committees. •	Raising awareness about the importance of terminology and language in reaching new groups. •	Providing specific guidance to underrepresented stakeholders and communities in the arts and culture sector. •	Prioritizing schemes aligned with the strategic focus areas.
Results: One tangible result of the Council’s work on its strategic focus areas is a significant rise in the number of applications received by the Cultural Fund. The largest increase occurred in 2023. This substantial rise in new applicants has, in turn, led to an increase in grants awarded to artists and participants from underrepresented groups, fostering greater diversity and breadth in the artistic and cultural expressions receiving financial support from the fund.

Title EN: Strategy on the performing arts
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture
SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Cultural and creative sectors
Agency Implementation: Norwegian Ministry of Culture and Equality
Main Feature: Over the last 10-15 years the performing arts field in Norway has grown and the infrastructure in the field is inadequate and outdated. The strategy aims to set a new course for the performing arts field from 2021-2025.   The strategy has four focus areas/measures:  1.	A cultural life with a diversity of actors who create and offer varied experiences to as many people as possible. 2.	Professional performing arts of high quality are accessible to a broad and diverse audience throughout Norway. 3.	Predictable conditions for the production and dissemination of performing arts. 4.	The professional performing arts field should be competitive and sustainable.  The strategy presents measures to ensure that there are more performances, more stages and that the performing arts can thus reach a wider audience. It proposes measures to improve the infrastructure for the performing arts, as well as ensure predictability for independent performing arts groups.
Results: -	Since 2022, an extra NOK 10 million has been allocated annually to various performing arts initiatives to meet goals in the strategy. -	A new subsidy scheme has been established for independent performing arts groups with an allocation of NOK 26 million. -	Dance centres across the country have received increased subsidies

Title EN: Support for the production of audiovisual works (film and television)/production incentives
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture

Area of Monitoring: Cultural and creative sectors
Agency Implementation: The Swedish Agency for Economic and Regional Growth (Tillväxtverket)
Main Feature: The film industry constitutes a central part of the cultural and creative sectors in Sweden, creating positive effects for both regional development and Sweden´s competitiveness. Most European countries offer production incentives for the audiovisual sector. These incentives allow film and TV productions to receive tax reductions or financial compensation for their costs. This fact has put Sweden at a disadvantage in the competition for international production locations, also leading to more Swedish film productions being shot abroad. The production incentives can both attract for film foreign films to Sweden, create better conditions for national film production and safeguard expertise and capacity within the Swedish film industry. This, in turn, can contribute to job opportunities and regional growth in Sweden.  The incentives were introduced in 2022 and total 100 million SEK (9 877 050 USD) per year. Support can cover up to 25 percent of eligible costs, i.e. costs generated by the production within the country («production rebate »). Eligible costs are costs that are necessary to carry out the production in Sweden and that relate to the production and post-production phase. Eligible costs are salaries paid to individuals who pay tax in Sweden and the purchase of goods or services from companies that are obliged to pay taxes in Sweden. Companies whose main activity is the production of audiovisual works can apply for support. Both national and international companies can apply.
Results: The incentives were welcomed by the film sector and there has been a great demand to apply for the support. The sector also assesses that the incentives already have made a certain difference. There are for exemple several examples of Swedish film productions that have been shot in Sweden during these years as a result of the incentives, which otherwise would have been shot in other countries. However the sector simultaneously argues that the total amount should be significantly higher to achieve the expected effect.
Financial Ressources: 9 877 000 USD (100 million SEK) per year from 2022

Title EN: Structuration des acteurs en faitières (organisations de la société civile) pour l’amélioration de la gouvernance du secteur culturel en République de Guinée
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture
SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development

Cultural Domain: Design,Performing Arts,Media Arts,Cinema and Audiovisual Arts,Music,Publishing,Visual Arts
Agency Implementation: -Fédération des Entrepreneurs Culturels et Economiques de Guinée (FECEG) ; -Union Nationale des Artistes Musiciens de Guinée (UNAMGUI) ; -Association des Editeurs de Guinée ; -Association des Ecrivains de Guinée.
Main Feature: En République de Guinée, les organisations de la société civile ont eu  un rôle croissant dans le processus du développement économique, social et culturel au cours de ces dernières années.  Les différents accords et traités signés durant la période 2020-2024 entre les partenaires évoluant dans le secteur culturel (OIF, Agence Française de Développement, Enabel, le Système des Nations unies) ont contribué largement à la reconnaissance des statuts d’acteur culturel et de bénéficiaire, du rôle et de l’apport des organisations de la société civile au processus de développement socio-économique et culturel tant aux niveaux national que local à travers leurs actions, leurs propositions et leurs capacités de transformation quantitative et qualitative. A cet effet : •	Les faitières culturelles qui les regroupent, développent régulièrement des plaidoyers en faveur de la gouvernance et de leur participation au développement des activités du secteur culturel ;  •	Les recommandations des organisations faitières de la culture contribuent  à l’amélioration de la gouvernance du secteur de la culture guinéenne. La Nouvelle Politique Culturelle adoptée en 2018 marque l’avènement d’un nouveau document cadre du développement national de la culture sur le plan économique et social consacrant cette participation.  Le Programme cadre d’appui au secteur de la culture (PASEC) érige la culture en secteur de croissance et de développement en lien avec les objectifs de développement durable (ODD). Les faitières, durant les années 2020-2024, ont développé un système de plaidoyer pour leur meilleure implication dans le processus d’élaboration des programmes, des projets culturels et de leur mise en œuvre. Ces plaidoyers visent essentiellement la prise en compte de leurs préoccupations dans le programme cadre d’appui au secteur de la culture (PASEC).  Par ailleurs, à titre d’illustration, lors des différentes rencontres, notamment les Journées de réflexions sur la restructuration des ensembles artistiques nationaux (du 30 août au 1er septembre 2023), l’Atelier d’élaboration du plan stratégique de relance des ensembles artistiques nationaux (du 15 au 17 octobre 2023), l’Atelier de validation des avant-projets de lois du secteur de la culture (du 12 au 16 septembre 2023), ... les représentants des organisations faitières ont plaidé pour la prise des mesures destinées au renforcement de leurs capacités structurelles et opérationnelles. Les propositions étaient relatives :  -	à la mise en œuvre des différents projets de lois du secteur culturel en République de Guinée ;  -	au renforcement des capacités des faitières afin de poursuivre leur organisation, leur structuration et de favoriser leur contribution au développement ;  -	à l’augmentation annuelle des ressources allouées au Fonds de Développement des Arts et de la Culture (FODAC) pour mieux répondre aux besoins de financement des acteurs culturels ;  -	à l’élaboration d’un cadre légal des structures faitières ;  -	à la réalisation des infrastructures culturelles et artisanales.  Le Président de la République de Guinée, dans son programme de réformes intérimaires (PRI) 2022-2027, place la culture comme l’une des préoccupations nationales à prendre en compte pour le développement socio-économique.
Results: Les résultats atteints sont les suivants : -	l’organisation des sessions de formation en technique d’élaboration et de financement des projets artistiques et culturels, sur la période 2020-2024 ; -	les consultations ont été réalisées, sur la période 2020-2024, pour intégrer les opinions et préoccupations des faitières (OSC) dans le plan annuel du travail du Ministère ; -	des séances de restitution ont été organisées pour informer les faitières sur les dispositions prises pour la mise en œuvre des différents mécanismes de restructuration ; -	la soumission pour adoption des six avant-projets de lois du secteur de la Culture au Conseil National de la Transition, 2023-2024 ; -	la participation régulière des OSC au Cadre sectoriel de Dialogue, lieu d’examen et de validation de la mise en œuvre des programmes et politiques sectoriels de la culture dans leurs domaines d’intervention ; -	la réalisation des plaidoyers sur la période 2020-2024, a permis à l’Etat de prendre les mesures visant l’augmentation du budget annuel du FODAC, de 1 159 420 USD à 28 985 507 USD au compte de l’année 2025 ; -	la réalisation de 12 projets de construction d’infrastructures culturelles et artisanales (4 villages artisanaux, 2 centres multiculturels de la Mamaya à Kankan et du Dounounba à Kouroussa, l’abri du Sosso bala à Niagassola, etc.) en faveur des artistes et acteurs de la culture ; -	des études architecturales sont en cours pour la construction d’un palais de la culture.

Title EN: Study "Gender Inequality in the Cultural Sector: Economic and Emotional State of Female Artists" (2022)
Goal: Promote Human Rights And Fundamental Freedoms
SDG: SDG 5 - Achieve gender equality and empower all women and girls,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels
Area of Monitoring: Gender equality
Cultural Domain: Design,Performing Arts,Media Arts,Cinema and Audiovisual Arts,Music,Publishing,Visual Arts
Agency Implementation: Lithuanian Council for Culture
Main Feature: Conducted in 2022, this study aimed to discover how and why female artists’ economic and emotional state differs from that of male artists; to identify measures to improve female artists’ economic and emotional state and strive for greater gender equality in cultural and creative sectors.  Objectives of the study: -	to analyse the economic state of artists; -	to assess the emotional state of artists; -	to assess gender equality regarding leadership and recognition (awards); -	to reveal the causes and triggering factors of gender gaps; -	to provide recommendations on possible ways to address the gender inequality issue in the cultural sector and proactively integrate the gender equality principle in developing and implementing cultural policy in Lithuania.
Results: The study concluded that there is a problem of gender inequality in the cultural and creative sectors, which manifests itself in unequal economic and emotional state of male and female artists. In other words, the economic and emotional state condition of male artists is, on average, better than that of female artists. In addition, men’s creative work is often more appreciated than that of women, which also contributes to a more significant gap between men’s and women’s emotional and economic state.
Financial Ressources: The study has been executed by the staff of the Lithuanian Council of Culture and Head of Creative Europe Desk LT

Main Feature: The Swedish Arts Grants Committee promote artistic development and innovative culture, monitoring and analysing the economic and social conditions of professional artists. The government also appoints special monitoring missions concerning specific questions on artists’ working conditions, for example analyse and promote artists opportunities in the cultural and creative sectors with a special focus on business development policies and measures. Results: The report shows that there are several complex consequences for artists’ working conditions due to the imbalance on the global market where multinational companies set the normative practices on the markets. Title EN: Study on Media Concentration and Diversity of Media Content in Finland
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture
SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Media diversity
Agency Implementation: Ministry of Transport and Communications
Main Feature: The one-year research project started in March 2023 and was financed by the Prime Minister’s Office. It investigated in particular the state of news media concentration and its effects on the content offerings as well as the regulation of concentration. The research project was carried out by media scholars from Tampere University and University of Turku.       The main goal of the project was to find out what the current state of concentration of media ownership in Finland is. Moreover, the study empirically examined how the concentration of news media has affected the diversity of media content and considers the consequences of concentration in terms of equality of information and freedom of speech.      At the same time, the goal was to map what kind of effects concentration has been found to have on media content internationally and how concentration has been tried to be curbed in key reference countries. The further goal is to use interviews and surveys to find out how the media industry itself and other experts in the field see the effects of concentration on media diversity, equal access to information and freedom of speech. The report is in Finnish, but some of the results may be published in academic publications in English.
Results: The research reveals that national players continue to have a crucial role in the Finnish media. While digital platforms are growing, traditional distribution channels still have a role to play. The concentration of the news media industry is evidenced by increased cooperation within and between news media groups, as well as shrinking editorial organisations.      The degree of concentration varies among media branches, and they have been partly developing in different directions in this regard. The radio and television sectors have evolved towards increased competition, while the earlier abundance of newspapers has decreased towards a more concentrated industry structure. This concentration has granted increased resources for producing quality media content, while increased cooperation within media groups seems to narrow down the news offer. The findings of the report reflect the overlap and distribution practices within media groups.   Based on our survey and interviews, editors see a continuing trend of ownership concentration. Views on whether the media offer sufficient diversity of content options were divided, as were views on the need for sector-specific regulation.

Task I - LOCAL INITIATIVES directed at animation activities, aimed at direct and close cooperation with representatives of the local community. The main emphasis is to maintain permanent relations with the inhabitants of the localities. Discovering talents and strengthening social potential is expected to result in the creation of joint initiatives for the benefit of local communities and public space. Agency Implementation: Pukañawi Cultural Management Center EMAIL: cinetecadederechoshumanos@gmail.com  PHONE: +59172890872
Main Feature: The International Human Rights Film Festival “EL SEPTIMO OJO ES TUYO” (FESTIMO) is defined as a cultural action and its general objective is linked to strengthening intercultural dialogue, education in human rights and the training of audiences through cinema as a free expression of peoples. FESTIMO is responsible for organizing, promoting, and disseminating quality cinema and reflecting on the situation regarding human rights. It develops and implements educational and analytical cycles with film screenings for neighborhood councils, schools, communities, and vulnerable social groups. It also informs, educates, and communicates to young people of both sexes about the areas of cinema, especially about audiovisual production in the so-called School of Nature.  Finally, it is responsible for creating, generating, and strengthening institutional alliances for the construction of the infrastructure of the Human Rights Film Library “School of Nature” located in the P'ajchiri urbanization, intended for the service of training, production, dissemination, and preservation of art cinema, memory cinema, and cinema for human rights. FESTIMO consists of seven days of screenings, organized by a jury of filmmakers and human rights defenders, three international, three national and three locals. It awards the Pukañawi – Red Eye Award to ten award-winning films. Its audience has reached more than twenty thousand participants in person and online. FESTIMO practices cinema as a human right and has thus defended its free entry into theaters since its first edition. The selection of films is the result of a call for entries that is launched on December 10th of each year. The screenings take place at three times: 10:30, 16:00, 19:00, and itinerant screenings are also organized in other cities and communities. The film company produces a catalogue, program, posters, and audiovisuals for TV and social networks. It develops exhibitions, academic meetings, and the Latin American Forum for Cinematographic Integration between filmmakers and the general public. It promotes the construction of the Human Rights Film Library and promotes co-production projects.
Results: The FESTIMO in its last 19th edition offered 58 films in total, of which 51 films were in competition for the 2023 Pukañawi Award, 17 films in the short film category, 16 films in the medium-length film category and 19 films in the feature film category. 10 co-productions were presented, 7 films from Chile, 4 films from Brazil, 3 films from Spain and Argentina, 2 films from Colombia, France, Peru and Bolivia and one film each from Malaysia, Greece, Sweden, Qatar/Sudan, India, Russia, Iran, Nicaragua, Germany and Ecuador. For the 2023 Pukañawi Award, 2 productions from 2021, 32 productions from 2022 and 9 productions from 2023 were submitted. There were three parallel exhibitions: Godard in Sucre, Museum of Memory and rescued cinema. Productions from 1965, 1967, 1968, 1984, 1989, 2003, 2010, 2013, 2019 were appreciated. Between film productions and co-productions, there was representation from 30 countries. More than 10 award-winning films, more than 20,000 participants in person and online, screenings at 3 times: 10:30, 16:00. 19:00 in 5 locations, free of charge. A 170-page catalogue, a programme, a poster and audiovisuals for TV and social media have been produced. Exhibitions, academic lectures and the IX Latin American Forum against impunity were held through the eyes of women. The efforts to build the Human Rights Film Library continued this year at the Ministry of Culture, and a campaign was launched to promote the project at film festivals in Europe and Africa.  FESTIMO is currently preparing to celebrate its 20th anniversary in August 2024, and due to its characteristics, this edition will give way to the creation of the Invisible Film Biennial, a space to unite the cinemas of the Quechua Nation (Bolivia, Peru, Ecuador, southern Colombia and northern Argentina) with the cinemas of Africa, and its execution time will be six weeks between August 2024 and August 2025. The Invisible Film Biennial will be held to commemorate the Bicentennial of Bolivia, and its activities include the Meeting of Human Rights Film Festivals (HRFN) of Latin America and a symposium on Stone Sculptures in the Park of Memory and Ancestral Knowledge, the site of the Human Rights Film Library “School of Nature.”

Title EN: Sultanate of Oman hosting the Aga Khan Awards for Architecture and Music 2022.
Goal: Achieve A Balanced Flow Of Cultural Goods And Services And Increase The Mobility Of Artists And Cultural Professionals
SDG: SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 10 - Reduce inequality within and among countries,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Mobility of artists and cultural professionals
Agency Implementation: Ministry of Culture, Sports, and Youth
Main Feature: The Sultanate of Oman hosted the awards ceremony for the winners of the 2022 Aga Khan Award for Architecture and Music in its forty-fifth anniversary, with the participation of 463 competing projects at the 15th edition of the Award from 29 to 31 October 2022. The celebrations were held at the House of Musical Arts at the Royal Opera Muscat in the presence of a number of Their Highnesses and Excellencies Ministers and Undersecretaries, as well as a group of Omani architects and musicians, in addition to nearly 250 international guests from around the world, members of the Steering and Judging Awards Committee, finalists and winners of the Architecture and Music Awards. The number of winners reached 15 winners from different countries of the world:  •	Indian Zakir Hussain for Lifetime Achievement •	 Malian "Afel Bokom" for his exceptional contributions to Mali's musical culture as a leading performer, composer and producer. •	 Indian "Asin Khan Langa" for his interest in preserving and reviving the traditions of Sarangi Sindh through his performance. •	 Mauritanian "Combana Mint A'la Warkan" to preserve and spread traditional Agaouine music in Mauritania. •	 Afghan Daoud Khan Saduzai for his commitment to the highest standards of playing the Afghan Rabab and spreading it around the world. •	 Indonesian Benny Chandra Rennie for adopting new creative styles in Indonesian music inspired by tradition and blending them with innovative styles. •	 British Shumek Data for his ongoing efforts in documenting marginalized and endangered musical traditions in the Indian subcontinent. •	 Tanzanian "Yahya Hussein Abdul Allah" for his artistic prowess and outstanding imagination as a performer and musician. •	 Iranian "Yasmin Shah Hosseini" for her exceptional artistic achievements in expanding the musical language by playing the oud. •	Pakistani Zarsangha for her lifelong dedication to Pashtun music performance and preservation. •	 Indian "Dilshad Khan" for preserving and developing the arts of playing the sarangi instrument.  Omani artist Musallam bin Ahmed Al Kathiri received a special award for excellence in serving Oman's musical heritage. The closing ceremony of the Sultanate of Oman hosting of the Aga Khan Awards for Architecture and Music witnessed a musical performance by the leading musicians of the Aga Khan Music Programme with the participation of Yurdal Tukan, one of the most famous Turkish oud players and a video of the Aga Khan Award for Architecture for the 2022 edition. HE Undersecretary of the Ministry of Culture, Sports, and Youth Saeed bin Sultan Al Busaidi delivered a speech in which he said: "The Sultanate of Oman's hosting of the Aga Khan Awards for Architecture and Music and its accompanying events is in support of the objectives of the cultural strategy, which calls for an open identity to the cultures of peoples, and an affirmation of its continuous support for culture, literature and arts, and to achieve one of its most important theme, which is to enhance cultural communication, highlight the role of the Sultanate of Oman in building the global cultural scene, as well as emphasize partnership and integration with local and international institutions in the cultural fields. This hosting also fully confirms the ability of the Sultanate of Oman and its capabilities to host such international events, and to achieve the cultural vision of making the Sultanate of Oman a cultural destination with a solid identity." His Excellency also explained that the presence of this distinguished elite of participants, winners, senior invitees, and artistic cultural figures to attend the awards ceremony, viewers who will follow these events through various media platforms, will achieve an intellectual and tourism dimension, activating the cultural promotion of the Sultanate of Oman and its multiple vocabularies in the tourism, economic and scientific fields, and translating one of the most important themes of the cultural strategy and its executive plan, which is cultural openness to the world and the export of Omani cultural identity.  The Sultanate of Oman is the first country to host- for three days- the Aga Khan Award for Architecture and Music. The winners of the Aga Khan Music Awards were crowned, represented by the "Lifetime Achievement" Award and the special award received by the Omani music researcher Muslim bin Ahmed Al Kathiri for his contributions to preserving the Omani musical heritage. The Aga Khan Award for Architecture 2022 Winners Symposium was also held, in which the most important experts, academics and architects in the international community and the Sultanate of Oman participated. Its sessions focused on the infrastructure and social impact of architecture in the Sultanate of Oman. The Aga Khan Award for Architecture started in 1977 and seeks to identify, encourage and promote building concepts that successfully meet the needs and aspirations of societies in which Muslims are present in a large number since its launch 45 years ago. 128 projects have received the award and about 10,000 building projects have been documented.
Results: - Omani artist Mussallam bin Ahmed Al Kathiri was awarded a special award for excellence in promoting Omani musical heritage. - 15 winners from different countries of the world. - A symposium for the winners of the Aga Khan Award for Architecture for the 2022 session, which included two sessions, the first entitled Infrastructure and Adaptive Reuse and the second entitled The Social Impact of Architecture. - Launching postage stamps representing the Omani architectural and musical style. - A huge flow of information related to the Omani cultural scene. - The number of followers, listeners and viewers of media institutions reached nearly 100 million followers. - Extensive media coverage in various languages, Arabic, English and other Semitic languages. - The presence of a distinguished elite of participants, winners, senior invitees and international cultural and artistic figures at the ceremony.
Recommandations: o	Getting to know the winners from different countries of the world, the works accompanying the distribution ceremonies and building a database of them. o	Continuing to enhance the Omani cultural scene and its integration with different countries of the world,  o	Continuing to enhance community awareness of participation in these global awards. o	Hosting the ceremony makes the Sultanate of Oman a destination for global awards and organizations and an incubator for many upcoming international cultural events. o	Attracting more unique events that promote the cultural and tourism scenes.

Title EN: Summer Camp

Area of Monitoring: Cultural and creative sectors
Agency Implementation: Ministry of Culture in partnership with federal, local and private institutions in the UAE.
Main Feature: The Summer Camp’ is an important annual event organised by the Ministry of Culture. This year, the camp will run throughout the month of July, starting from July 1st until the end of the month, featuring a diverse set of programmes, including workshops, discussions, cultural and artistic performances, training courses, and guided tours. These activities will be conducted in partnership with top institutions and organisations, as well as experts and specialists from different fields. The Summer Camp is aligned with the UAE’s national goals for investing in the country's youth. Its participants will have an opportunity to learn new skills and broaden their horizons, keeping up with the latest knowledge trends. The camp also aims to reinforce the participants’ national identity based on Emirati culture and works towards strengthening their contribution to shaping the future of the UAE. Showcasing the Ministry of Culture’s commitment to providing a stimulating and supportive environment for individuals of all ages, from 6-year-olds to senior citizens over the age of 60, the 2024 edition of the Summer Camp will focus on three main tracks: •	Skill development of participants, aiming to equip talented individuals with advanced skills aligned with the UAE's centennial plan. •	Raising community awareness about the fundamentals of different sectors, national priorities, and educating communities about future trends. •	Instilling Emirati values in community members, introducing them to the core components of the Emirati identity and culture.
Results: The Ministry of Culture of the UAE organizes an annual summer camp that plays a crucial role in promoting cultural engagement and personal development among youth. The summer camp, designed to provide educational and recreational activities, caters to a wide range of interests, including arts, culture, and science. In recent years, the summer camp has seen robust participation, with approximately 1,500 to 2,000 students engaging each year. This reflects a growing interest in the camp's diverse offerings and its importance in the cultural calendar.The camp features a variety of programs, including workshops in traditional arts, creative writing, performing arts, and STEM (Science, Technology, Engineering, and Mathematics) activities. These programs are designed to develop both cultural appreciation and practical skills.The camp has received positive feedback from participants and parents, highlighting its effectiveness in fostering creativity, teamwork, and a deeper understanding of cultural heritage. Surveys and evaluations indicate high satisfaction rates and a strong impact on the participants’ personal and academic growth.
Recommandations: The summer camp organized by the Ministry of Culture has had a notable positive impact on youth development, effectively fostering creativity and cultural appreciation through its diverse range of activities. Participants and parents have expressed high satisfaction with the camp's programs and facilities, highlighting its success in providing meaningful and enjoyable experiences.

Title EN: Support for cultural and creative sectors to overcome the effects of Covis-19
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture
SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Cultural and creative sectors
Agency Implementation: Ministry of Education and Culture
Main Feature: Since the beginning of the Covid-19 pandemic, the Ministry of Education and Culture initiated multiple recurrent modes of support to tackle the effects of the pandemic to working conditions and structures for agencies in the creative field.  During 2020–2022, the Arts Promotion Centre distributed a total of 130 000 000 euros (ca. 141 400 000 USD) as grants, or Covid-19 Support, to professionals in the creative field, including artists, private traders and sole proprietors, and art associations, in order to maintain working conditions during and over the pandemic.  Subsidies granted by the Ministry of Education and Culture before the pandemic were re-evaluated and their purposes of use and planned timetables changed and extended.  In addition, businesses and singular entrepreneurs in the cultural field could apply for additional funding from the Ministry of Economic Affaris and Employment, the Centres for Economic Development, Transport and the Environment, as well as financial support from Business Finland.  The Ministry of Education and Culture gathered data in multiple ways on the impact of the Covid-19 pandemic from the beginning to further enhance dialogue with the creative field and to react to the effects of the pandemic. Arts Promotion Centre maintained a dialogue with the creative field in order to enhance straightforward grant application processes.
Results: The Covid 19 pandemic presented an unforeseen challenge for the creative sector, and the evaluation on the impact of the pandemic with regards to funding structures is still discussed in and by the creative field in Finland.  In August 2021, then Minister of Science and Culture Antti Kurvinen appointed a working group to solve the issues in the cultural and creative field. In 2023, on the basis of the conclusions drawn by the working group, a report on cultural policy was initiated to further clarify and produce a vision of the national cultural policy's impacts and longevity.

Title EN: Support for Cultural Diversity Preservation and Intercultural Dialogue

Agency Implementation: Ministry of Culture
Main Feature: Supporting cultural diversity preservation and intercultural dialogue is an essential element of international cultural relations and an asset for the countries involved during this globalisation age. Cultural diversity is a factor for sustainable development.  International cooperation is carried out in line with the policy of the Bulgarian state regarding international relations, the priorities for developing Bulgarian culture and in compliance with the existing legal and legislation norms. It includes: - promoting the values of cultural diversity;  - promoting Bulgarian cultural achievements overseas and foreign culture in Bulgaria; - building a positive image of Bulgaria as a stable partner in international cultural policy and international relations through consistently conducted policy of active cultural relations development based on mutually agreed contractual relations; - affirming Bulgarian presence and status of Bulgarian culture; - participation of Bulgarian artists in the art market abroad, supporting the free movement of artists, cultural values and cultural products;  - exploring opportunities for promoting and disseminating Bulgarian culture abroad through participation in various international events, contests, festivals, exhibitions and other appropriate forms, as well as for international events taking place in Bulgaria;  - organising international bilateral events in the country and abroad;  - planning, coordinating and controlling the activities of Bulgarian Cultural Institutes abroad; - opening new cultural institutes based on bilateral international agreements; - establishing the role and mission of culture as a means of preventing and overcoming crisis situations and conflicts.
Results: Participation in international organisations and platforms for cooperation and implementation of bilateral and multilateral cooperation agreements in the fields of culture and audiovisual arts. This is a prerequisite for establishing intercultural dialogue and encouraging the development of friendly and mutually beneficial relations with other countries around the world.  Integration of Bulgarian culture into cultural diversity and cultural processes on a global scale; expanding the influence scope and intensity of Bulgarian and international cultural achievements by attracting new audience.

Title EN: Support for Mexico's artisanal sector
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture
SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Cultural and creative sectors
Agency Implementation: National Fund for the Promotion of Artisanal Creation  /  Fondo Nacional para el fomento de las Artesanías (FONART)
Main Feature: FONART is a Public Trust of the Federal Government, constituted in 1974 by mandate of the Federal Executive and incorporated into the Ministry of Culture as of 2020. Its objective is to promote, support, foster and disseminate the country's artisanal activity. In order to fulfil this purpose, it carries out the necessary acts for the acquisition and commercialisation of the country's artisanal products; it provides technical and administrative assistance to artisans; it promotes artisanal production, and supports creators by acquiring the necessary inputs for their artisanal production.  Furthermore, through the collection of handcrafted pieces that are exhibited in Fonart's shops, the public can purchase them and learn first-hand about the country's handcrafted production, which, in addition to commercialisation, strengthens the dissemination of handicrafts.  Also, the craftsmanship is disseminated and publicised through the workshops that make up the "Artisan Corridors" and other strategic projects, in which visitors will learn directly from the artisans, the raw materials they use, the techniques they develop and the handcrafted objects they make, as well as the use they make of them. This promotes the knowledge and recognition of craft knowledge as a fundamental part of heritage and of artisans, as well as creators, as bearers of this knowledge inherited from generation to generation.  With these actions, craftspeople are comprehensively attended to in order to provide the tools that facilitate their integration into economic, social and cultural development as a result of the exercise of their activity, as well as their insertion into the markets.
Results: Through the National Fund for the Promotion of Handicrafts (FONART), the artistic and cultural meaning of handicrafts has been promoted and disseminated through the 259 competitions held throughout the country, in which 45,573 artisans have participated, with 9,758 winners, 5,527 women and 4,231 men, and a total of 63,951 pieces have been received from the various branches of handicrafts.  The sum of these results is to have reliable information on what happens in popular art, year after year, throughout the country (craft techniques, raw materials used, preservation and / or innovation of the type of piece that is made).  This makes it possible to direct support for the provision of raw materials, tools, training and occupational health care, actions that promote craft production and thus strengthen the knowledge that is the country's cultural, tangible and intangible heritage.

In this way, the state actively promotes the development of creativity and innovation while pursuing the goal of increasing the qualifications, knowledge, skills, competences and mobility of cultural professionals and strengthening equal opportunities and social cohesion. Title EN: SUPPORT FOR SELF AND TEAMWORK
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture
SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Cultural and creative sectors
Agency Implementation: he Polish Filmmakers Association
Main Feature: he Polish Filmmakers Association is the largest organization of film people in Poland. Since 1966, he has been continuously caring for the interests of creators and the film community. SFP has an extremely wide scope of operation. From the protection of filmmakers and film professions, through collective management of copyrights, to the promotion and dissemination of film culture in Poland and abroad, as well as film production. Today, the Polish Filmmakers Association has approximately 1,800 members. The basic, primary task of the Association is to protect film people and film professions. This applies primarily to people at the beginning of their professional career as well as older people. Young members of the Association can operate within the structures of the Munk Studio and apply for creative scholarships, thanks to which they have the opportunity to prepare their debut in comfortable conditions. Elders – gathered in the Senior Circle – attend meetings and film screenings every month. Medical and sanatorium care, which is also supported by SFP, is particularly important for them. The Association operates one of the most effective organizations for collective copyright management - ZAPA, i.e. the Association of Audiovisual Authors and Producers. ZAPA operates under a license from the Minister of Culture, which SFP received in 1995. ZAPA represents directors, screenwriters, cinematographers, set designers, costume designers, sound operators, editors and producers of audiovisual works.
Results: The self support for the film industry is particulalry important in Poland. The Polish film industry has been waiting for many years for legislation to be adapted to modern models of distribution of works. Legislative neglect makes Poland the last country in the European Union that has not implemented the DSM Directive. Deprived of royalties for online exploitation, Polish filmmakers are irretrievably losing not only their due remuneration, but also their international competitiveness and presence on equal terms in the global audiovisual market.  During the pandemic period, the Association of Polish Filmmakers provided support to members of the Association (lunches, shopping, financial aid etc.).  Assistance to war refugees from Ukraine (providing accommodation, food, access to culture, assistance in finding jobs).  The Scenario Program (support for the development of screenwriting creativity: financial, legal, creative).

Title EN: Support granted by Polish Film Institute for initiatives related to film production, promotion and dissemination of film culture indirectly impacting exchange of cultural goods and services with developing countries
Goal: Achieve A Balanced Flow Of Cultural Goods And Services And Increase The Mobility Of Artists And Cultural Professionals
SDG: SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 10 - Reduce inequality within and among countries,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Flow of cultural goods and services
Agency Implementation: Polish Film Institute
Main Feature: The Polish Film Institute carrying out its statutory tasks in the field of cinematography provides co-financing of the projects related to film production, film promotion and dissemination of film culture within the scope of PFI Operational Programmes. An application for co-financing of a project may only be submitted by an entity originating from Poland, another member state of the European Union, the Swiss Confederation or a member state of the European Free Trade Agreement (EFTA) - a party to the agreement on the European Economic Area, therefore the subjective criterion excludes the possibility of providing direct support to entities originating from outside the abovementioned territories, including the countries qualified as developing.   Nevertheless, the support provided by the Polish Film Institute in some cases may have an indirect impact on the cultural and economic exchange with developing countries, as the beneficiaries of the support are often collaborating with entities from developing countries or undertake projects related to such countries, e.g. engaging in international film co-productions, organizing an industry event presenting or promoting the cinematography of developing countries.
Results: 1.	The Polish Film Institute supported the production of films co-produced with developing countries. Between 2020 and 2023, approximately 28 grants were awarded for projects involving these countries. The most frequently collaborating country was Ukraine (15), while other countries involved in supported co-productions included: Malaysia, Indonesia, Nigeria, Vietnam, Serbia, North Macedonia, Montenegro, Lebanon, Palestine, Albania, and Mexico. Please note that data presented above does not include projects supported within PFI Operational Programme VI – Polish-Ukrainian Film Initiatives in 2022-2023, which are described in Objective 11: Artistic Freedom.  2.	In the period of 2020-2023 21 initiatives organized on the territory of developing countries have been granted support by the Polish Film Institute.
