Main Feature: Support to contemporary arts (theater arts, cinema/audiovisual arts, music, dance, visual arts, cultural education) “Law on Audio-visual Media" was adopted in 2020. Amendments to the “Law on Audio-visual Media" in 2022, 2023, 2024 "Law on Cinematography" was adopted in 2021. Amendments to the "Law on Cinematography" in 2023 “Strategy  of promotion, preservation and development of culture in the Republic of Armenia for 2023-2027” in 2023  Amendments to the “Law on the Fundamentals of Cultural Policy” in 2024  “Law on museums” in 2024 Amendments to the “Law on Libraries and Library Affairs” in 2024 Amendments to the “Law on state awards and titles” in 2020, 2024 Amendments to the “Law on Charity” in 2023, 2024 Relevant Draft Legislation Draft Law on Equality and Protection from Discrimination Draft Law on National Minorities  The amendments to the above laws, as well as the newly adopted laws, aimed to develop the sectors of contemporary art and the creative industry, book publishing, mobility and the status of independent and self-employed artists, to expand international cooperation, develop joint film production, introduce cashreback mechanism, etc. The approved Strategy identifies the following key objectives: preserving cultural diversity, strengthening intercultural dialogue, strengthening the potential of culture and its connections with other fields (education, science, tourism, youth and others), as well as the integration of cultural development into the long-term socio-economic development of a democratic society, the promotion of international development and exchange in the field of culture, the stimulation of creativity and innovation of cultural agents.
Results: The measure pointed out the importance of connecting culture with other sectors and drew attention to the vital role of culture in the sustainable development of society. In the reporting period, in the field of:  Performing Arts/Theatre: 70 dramatic, opera, ballet, musical, comedic, marionette, puppet and pantomime performances have been staged for various layers of society, audiences and people of all ages within the framework of creative orders; 6 dramaturgical works has been obtained; participation of all 11 Armenian state theaters (operating under the ministry) and other theatrical troupes and 16 individuals every year has been ensured in 20 international festivals and projects.   Music: obtainment of musical works, new adaptations and musical arrangements; ensuring of participation of Armenian music and dance groups and individual performers in international music festivals. In the same period, 50 works by more than 30 Armenian authors were obtained, new adaptations and musical arrangements of 71 works were made, 5 albums were published. The participation of 15 Armenian music groups and 70 individual performers in 90 international music festivals and projects was ensured.  Cinema/Audiovisual arts: nearly 123 full-length and short-length films, 23 documentaries, 26 animated films have been produced, including 30 debut programms and support has been provided for the issuance of 3 film magazines and for the development of 30 draft scripts and film projects of individual filmmakers.  Every year, the participation of Armenian films and individual creators in 60 international film festivals, film markets and forums has been ensured. During the Covid-19 period, Armenian filmmakers participated in 20 film festivals. In 2023 11 Armenian films were presented at different film festivals and won 32 awards. One of the most important achievements of Armenian cinema is that in 2023, for the first time, Michael Gyurjian's film “Amerikatsi (The American)”, made with state funding, was included in the shortlist of Oscars among the 15 best international feature films. Furthermore, in 2023, Armenia and the world celebrated the 100th anniversary of the foundation of Armenian cinema. This event was included in the UNESCO list of significant anniversaries․ Publishing:  The role of the RA Ministry of Education, Science, Culture and Sports in the field of book publishing is the coordination and regulation of the field. While developing and implementing the policy of the sector, the Ministry is guided by the belief that the development of each link is equally important. In this field, our programs are aimed at solving the following problems: equal development of all aspects of the literary field, preservation, development, dissemination and popularization of literary-cultural heritage through literary products, formation of civil society, reproduction and development of society's creative potential, international cooperation in the field of book distribution creation of favorable conditions. In the field of publishing Armenian publishers are supported through grants programs.  These are: “Translation programs and support for creators and researchers”, “Armenian lite-rature in translations”, “Publication of non-state press”, “Support for the popularization of literature, participation in international book exhibitions”, “Literature publication” and “Printing of books in Braille for visually impaired people, making notebooks and recording services of "Talking books”. Through the "Translation Programs and Support for Creators and Researchers" initiative, the Ministry supports translation works, cultural studies, literary and literary criticism projects. With this event, in 2020-2023 124,695.2 thousand AMD (USA $ 296893 for 4 years) was allocated for the implementation of 128 creative, research and translation projects, among which 54 books of Armenian classical and modern literature were translated into more than 20 languages and published in foreign countries. The goal of the "Non-State Press Publishing" program is the dissemination of national-civili-zational values, the appreciation of Armenian cultural traditions and new achievements, the deve¬lopment of modern creative approaches, and the professional assessment of new and creative art born in Armenia. Allocations under the program also provide an opportunity to support the activities of printed and electronic periodicals published in Armenia for national minorities. Those periodicals cover the cultural transition of the community, public life. Thanks to the project, these communities are able to preserve their national language, folklore, culture, and traditions.  Within the scope of the program in 2020-2023 293,729.0 thousand AMD (USA $ 699355 for 4 years) was allocated to the projects of 119 printed and electronic periodicals (35 periodicals of 11 national minorities living in Armenia: Yezidi, Kurdish, Greek, Assyrian, Ukrainian, Hebrew, Russian, Georgian etc.). With the program "Support for popularization of literature, literary programs and participation in international book exhibitions", the Ministry supports our country's participation in republican literary programs and international book exhibitions aimed at promoting reading and popular-rizing literature. 2020-2023 With the support of the Ministry, Armenia participated in the Frankfurt International Book Exhibition with a national pavilion. At the same time, the Yerevan International Book Festival was also held, in which dozens of writers from Armenia and abroad, more than fifty publishing houses, booksellers and literary agencies participate every year, dozens of presentations, speeches and other programs are held, we have 15,000 visitors. The Yerevan International Book Festival, which has been held since 2017 in September, greatly contributes to the development of the publishing sector. In 2022, 60 events took place as part of the festival. Representatives from France, Italy, Russia, Georgia, Slovenia and Cyprus took part in the festival. The goal of the "Literature Publishing" program is to present the historical and cultural heritage of Armenia and the Armenian people in a foreign language, which will later be provided to 500 foreign libraries. As part of the festival, a literary competition was organized in 4 categories: “Fiction”, “Poetry”, “Dramaturgy”, “Children’s Literature”. The purpose of the "Literature Publishing" program is to publish foreign language literature representing the historical and cultural heritage of Armenia and Nagorno-Karabakh, Armenian carpet art (also other manifestations of intangible cultural heritage), archaeological and architectural heritage of Armenia, and repleni-shing foreign libraries with these books.  The program "Printing of books in Braille for visually impaired people, making notebooks and recording services of "Talking books"" ensures the right of cultural education of the mentioned people, to receive information through the publication of books in Braille, recording of audio books, etc. With this program in 2020-2023 34,253.1 thousand AMD (USA $ 81555 for 4 years) were allocated for the publication of 389,061 pages of books and magazines in Braille, and for the recording of 480 hours of audio books.  Visual arts: support has been provided to the organisation of 12 individual exhibitions, the participation of young creators in 12 international biennales, exhibitions and innovative programmes; 2 visual arts works have been obtained.   Dance: in the reporting period, 16 new dances have been choreographed; support has been provided to the participation of 2 state dance ensembles (operating under the ministry) and 2 other dance ensembles and 9 individual performers in 14 international festivals and competitions; 2 international festivals have been held.   Cultural education sector: The educational programme for the national, string and brass instruments in music and art schools (each year: 1181 schoolchildren of 145 community schools, including 648 national instruments, 350 string instruments and 183 brass instruments). “Acquisition of musical instruments for music and art schools” (each year 35 musical instruments of 10 types) within the scope of the programme. The “Educational-Methodical and Practical Assistance” programme, which was held with the participation of 29,545 schoolchildren and 5,449 pedagogues of music, art, fine arts and dance schools of the republic. “Teacher Training” programme, which was held with the participation of 2,075 pedagogues of the aforementioned schools. “Organising of master classes in Armenia by foreign specialists and support to participation of gifted musicians and performers in master classes and creative camps abroad” programme, which was held with the participation of 400 gifted schoolchildren and 200 pedagogues of music and art schools of the republic. “Target programme for development and improvement of talented teen musicians and performers in the Republic of Armenia” programme, within the scope of which individual lessons and master classes were given to 15 gifted teen musicians and performers (classical music instruments: piano, violin, cello). Out of the gifted teen musicians involved in the programme, 15 of them participated in over 150 different events, including competitions, festivals and concerts. Мost of them received laurels at republican and international competitions. In the reporting period, through the “Development and publication of new curricula, textbooks and methodical manuals for music, art and fine arts schools” programmes, 50 educational-methodical manuals in 11,700 copies were published and distributed free of charge to educational institutions providing cultural education in the republic. “Philharmonic of Schoolchildren” programme, within the scope of which 108 lesson-concerts were organised and held with the participation of nearly 43,420 children and teens of the republic. The program "Quyr dprocner" (sister schools) subscription system which carried in Yerevan and all regions of Armenia for all schoolchildren of Armenia (aged 10-14) studying at middle classes․  In the same time, for supporting the tradition of access of children to cultural institutions, the ministry is realized the new program – “Subscription program”, which is implemented in Yerevan and all regions of Armenia for middle school students (10-14 years old), including Syrian-Armenian children, children of Nagorno-Karabakh and children of orphanages in Yerevan and Gavar. In the framework of this program, around 440000 beneficiaries have the possibility to visit 2 museum and 1 theater each year. The participats of the program regularly visit all Armenian cultural institution (the National Gallery of Armenia, the Komitas Museum-Institute, the History Museum of Armenia, the Hovhannes Tumanyan Museum, the National Academic Theatre of Opera and Ballet named after Alexander Spendiaryan and attended the concert programme of Armenian State Honored Ensemble of Song and Dance named after Tatul Altounyan and State Ensemble of Armenian Folklore Music and other). Visits to Tsitsernakaberd [Armenian Genocide Memorial Complex], “Mayr Hayastan” [Mother Armenia] Memorial and Komitas Pantheon were also organised for the children. By selection of profession, support has been provided to 120 individual performers and 1 choir for participation in 40 international child and youth competitions, festivals and master classes. From 2020 to 2023, in the field of cultural education, other educational and cultural projects have been implemented for schoolchildren in public schools (660 school, 21000 children), the number of which currently amounts to 18 projects, including the target programs “Class A”, “Your art at school” and “Class + classic”, “Meknark”, “Zardagir”, “Dasarvest”.
Recommandations: Due to the work done over the past four years, tangible results have been recorded in terms of revitalisation of cultural life, proportionate development of the sectors of contemporary arts (cinema/audiovisual arts, theatre arts, visual arts, music, dance, cultural education), improvement of the activities of individual creators and creative groups, identification of the potential of young creators and promotion of activities and awareness-raising of Armenian contemporary arts in the republic, as well as expansion of international partnerships and internationalisation of Armenian contemporary arts. This was achieved through the reorganization, optimization, professional training and improvement of theater, concert and cultural institutions. Alongside this progress, nevertheless, the imperfection of the legal-contractual field remains a major issue, and as a result, this does not clearly ensure the legal relations between the State and creators.

Main Feature: Tales of EUkraine (TEUk) is an opportunity for European publishers to support their Ukrainian counterparts and to display their solidarity to the most vulnerable victims of the conflict by doing what they do best: publishing books. This project will bring together European and Ukrainian publishers to deliver bilingual children’s books to several communities hosting Ukrainian refugees, fostering integration and mutual understanding. Title EN: Tax incentive for financing projects associated with arts, cultures, and heritage in Colombia.
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture
SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Cultural and creative sectors
Cultural Domain: Design,Performing Arts,Media Arts,Cinema and Audiovisual Arts,Music,Publishing,Visual Arts
Agency Implementation: Colombia Crea Talent Corporation – CoCrea
Main Feature: Article 180 of Law 2277 of 2022 establishes the tax incentive for the financing of cultural, artistic and heritage projects in the country, where in its regulatory decree the incentive of 165% is proposed, which means that for every 100 pesos that If the taxpayer contributes to a project within the framework of this mechanism, he or she may deduct 165 pesos in the tax base of the income tax return for the fiscal year in which the contribution was made.         The Colombia Crea Talent Corporation – CoCrea is responsible for the implementation of this tax incentive, which is done through a public and open call, which seeks to select projects related to arts, cultures, and heritage, so that they are susceptible to receive investments or donations that grant their contributors the right provided for in article 180 of Law 2277 of 2022.         CoCrea makes the call, evaluates the projects, delivers the guarantees that certify that said projects are cultural, artistic, or heritage and that they are also technically and financially viable, monitors the execution of said projects and certifies their compliance with the Ministry of Cultures, Arts, and Knowledge. The Ministry provides contributors with an investment or donation certificate through which the deduction established in article 180 of Law 2277 of 2022 is made.
Results: To date, the implementation of the tax mechanism has allowed the development of 221 projects related to arts, cultures, and heritage in Colombia. The total value of these projects has been COP$497,629 million, of which $385,438 has been financed. The remaining value corresponds to compensation from the project owners. 26 of Colombia's 32 departments have been impacted with the implementation of these 221 projects.         Year after year, the tax incentive is leveraged on the tax quota established by the Superior Council of Fiscal Policy (CONFIS in Spanish). The tax quota establishes the maximum amount of investments or donations that can be made within a period of time and that is susceptible to the tax incentive that is managed by the Corporation.         The fiscal quota approved for each term and its use to date have been the following:         Year	2020	2021	2022	2023	2024         Approved tax quota	$300,000	$600,000	$207,800	$200,000	$200,000         Use	$30	$18,282	$62,658	$120,097	$14,860         Percentage	0.01%	3.04%	30.15%	60.04%	7.43%         Data in millions of pesos                  It is important to highlight that the percentage of use of the fiscal quota has increased significantly year after year, which has allowed us to position a fiscal quota of $200,000 million pesos in recent years. By 2024, it is expected to reach 89.47% of the quota approved for the validity period.                  On the other hand, during the period included in this report, the Corporation's associates have contributed $7,498 billion pesos to support the implementation of the tax incentive.

Title EN: Telefilm’s Equity, Diversity, and Inclusion (EDI) Action Plan
Goal: Integrate Culture In Sustainable Development Frameworks

Area of Monitoring: National sustainable development policies and plans
Agency Implementation: Telefilm Canada
Main Feature: Telefilm Canada is a Government of Canada Crown corporation in the Canadian Heritage portfolio. It aims to support the development, production, promotion and distribution of the screen-based industry in Canada.  Telefilm launched its Equity and Representation Action Plan in July 2020. The Action Plan, aimed to better support Racialized (Black and People of Colour) creators, as well as filmmakers from 2SLGBTQIA+, Persons with Disabilities, and Official Language Minority communities, is based on the foundation of four key pillars: 1.	Reviewing the policies at Telefilm; 2.	Improving Telefilm’s hiring, staffing and training practices (both in terms of new hires and retention and promotion of current employees); 3.	Funding through Telefilm’s various programs; 4.	Engaging in continuous dialogue with filmmakers and industry members.  Equity, Diversity and Inclusion Plan 2022-2024 Following the implementation of the first phase of the Equity and Representation Action Plan in July 2020, Telefilm Canada renewed its engagements for Equity, Diversity, and Inclusion in alignment with the 2022-2024 Corporate Plan. This continues its commitment to an industry that reflects a culture of mutual respect, dignity, and inclusivity.  Aligned with Telefilm’s Corporate Plan, the EDI Action Plan sets out new equity-building actions to further integrate EDI reflexes into daily work at Telefilm. This plan will enable Telefilm to deliver practical, measurable results in support of the audiovisual industry. It is based on four pillars: 1.	Strengthen Telefilm Canada’s inclusive culture through greater equity in access to all programs and a representative portfolio. 2.	Expand Equity, Diversity and Inclusion-informed decision-making based on data and business intelligence. 3.	Uplift, amplify and empower as an Ally of Choice to the industry. 4.	Support a strong sense of belonging at Telefilm through leadership accountability.
Results: Telefilm created a development stream for Black Creators and Creators of Colour (first named the Racialized stream).    New inclusion roles were created to better connect with the industry and evolve Telefilm’s programs (including a Vice-President EDI), with hiring objectives for all levels of staffing. There is also dedicated funding to better educate staff to appreciate cultural expression.    There is set targets and objectives for investments focused on underrepresented communities and their stories.    Telefim has financed and partnered with newly formed groups to support their growth, their exposure and their presence in the industry nationally and internationally.    Further, access for underrepresented groups have been improved. The efforts made through the Equity, Diversity, and Inclusion (EDI) Action plan focused on eliminating barriers and improving access for filmmakers traditionally disadvantaged by systemic barriers, including women, Indigenous People, People, official language minority communities (OLMC) members, Black people and people of colour, people with disabilities and members of 2SLGBTQIA+ communities. Telefilm has improved access by rethinking its programs and funding allocations, working in collaboration with the industry.   Data collection  Telefilm introduced new practices including self-identification. The collected data has served to improve the representation of members of equity-seeking Canadian communities, including women in key roles, to achieve parity in its programs, to monitor the fulfillment of Telefilm’s commitment to Indigenous creators, and to adopt more targeted measures for Black people and people of colour.   In 2022-23 Telefilm announced that it will finance films in all languages expanding past French, English and Indigenous languages and has subsequently funded films in more than 10 other languages.   New Dawn fund  Telefilm’s corporate priorities and modernization in Canada resonated abroad, which led to an international invitation for Telefilm to join with nine European film institutes and funds to launch the New Dawn Fund aimed at increasing diversity in the global film industry.   Accessibility plan:  In December 2022, Telefilm launched its 2023-2025 Accessibility Plan, which sets out steps Telefilm plans to do over the next three years. Among other actions, Telefilm will ensure that people with disabilities have better access to its funding programs; it intends to better meet their accessibility needs in interactions with Telefilm which will help increase visibility and opportunities for creators with disabilities and will improve the self-identification process as part of the recruitment process so that more people with disabilities are hired and promoted.   People, official language minority communities (OLMCs) Telefilm developed program objectives and guidelines to support creative teams from OLMCs and from regions outside the main production centres of Toronto and Montréal by means of, for example, more flexible eligibility criteria or specific streams that facilitate applicants’ access to certain programs. In addition to this, Telefilm supported the professional development project Élan, with the Alliance des producteurs francophones du Canada, Netflix and the Canada Media Fund. This initiative aimed to encourage professional development and the execution and recognition of Canadian Francophonie projects.

Title EN: TEMPORADAS/Seasons
Goal: Integrate Culture In Sustainable Development Frameworks
SDG: SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: International cooperation for sustainable development
Cultural Domain: Design,Performing Arts,Media Arts,Cinema and Audiovisual Arts,Music,Publishing,Visual Arts
Agency Implementation: Cultural Heritage, IP and DGARTES - Directorate General of Arts
Main Feature: Temporadas (seasons in Portuguese) was a programming project for Vaga - a new cultural space in Ponta Delgada (São Miguel Island, Azores). It aimed to organize and present new art projects and expand references in the broad field of arts and foster collaborations between artists, agents, and organizations in the Azores and in relation to other geographies, specifically Iceland and Norway. Temporadas was the context for a practical exercise on curatorial models and processes of commonality and shared agency, assuming Vaga as a place of experimentation for future formats. Temporadas invited groups of artists to explore an anchor theme, which unfolded in a program of activities that included exhibitions, installations, performances, meetings, investigation, and research; while also allowing for spontaneous programming contexts, responding to the stimuli of the moment and to the encounters and synergies that arose between participants.
Results: Access and support to/for contemporary arts in low-density municipalities through, inter alia: programming of artistic productions, involvement of residents in creative processes and audience development activities. Temporadas was organized to mobilize various players to build a synergetic and healthy ecosystem. The project involved direct investment in the local economy, namely through the sharing and distribution of financial resources among the various agents involved in the activities. It has enabled a new mapping of the cultural territory and became as to the production of culture content (informal intersection between artists and different communities, involvement of local agents, creating movements and flows between different areas and audiences in the city of Ponta Delgada, collaboration between partners of different scales and geographies, to sustain new artistic centralities). The project contributed to the consolidation of a medium to long-term development strategy for the Vaga space in São Miguel's cultural sector and its audiences, having reached people who don't usually attend the cultural circuit and built a network of national and international artistic, professional, and institutional collaborations. The activities of the first three Temporadas were accompanied by Labtempo – a collective of young people resident on the island of São Miguel, who co-curated and developed the final and fourth Temporadas, thus actively involving the younger layer of the population in creative processes.

A living space of constant updating, whose data will be linked to the Cultural Information System of Paraguay (SICPY).
Results: After the conclusion of the second period enabled for the registration of artists, managers and cultural workers on the Téra platform, the National Secretariat of Culture (SNC) completed the processing, verification and cross-referencing of data, totaling 12,172 registered in both stages. The subsidy granted by the Executive Branch was equivalent to 25% of the current legal minimum wage, which would be G. 548,210. “This benefit could be granted up to 4 (four) times for the same amount,” says the law promulgated on August 17.
Financial Ressources: The measure was designed and implemented with the technical team of the SNC and the advice of the Ministry of Information and Communication Technologies (MITIC) and the Ministry of Culture of Ecuador

In the first phase, the registration of artists, managers and cultural workers in the natural person category was enabled, within the framework of the implementation of the Artist Subsidy Law, and at the same time, a database was generated as a fundamental tool. for the construction of cultural policies. « Téra allowed 3,000 workers to receive this subsidy. Subsequently, the second stage was enabled so that registered workers could update their data or enrich their profiles, but also for those who were unable to register in the first stage.

Title EN: The 1st Da Nang Asian Film Festival 2023 (DANAFF 2023)
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture
SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Partnering with civil society
Agency Implementation: Da Nang City People’s Committee, Viet Nam Film Development Association (VFDA), Da Nang City’s Department of Culture and Sports
Main Feature: The 1st Da Nang Asian Film Festival 2023 (DANAFF 2023), taking place on March 19–23, 2023, was the first international film festival in Da Nang City with the aim of selecting and honoring outstanding cinematic works rich in human values and unique artistic expressions. It sought to encourage new talents in Vietnamese and Asia-Pacific cinema, introduce Vietnamese audiences to new, high-quality cinema works from Asia, and contribute to the development of cinema as a significant cultural industry that positively impacts the cultural, economic, and social development of the city. This festival marked the first time a local authority collaborated with a civil society organization to host an event in accordance with Viet Nam’s revised Cinema Law 2022. The main program of the DANAFF 2023  included the Opening Ceremony and the Closing Ceremony - Awards Ceremony for the Asian Film and Vietnamese Film Competitions, featuring valuable prizes; the "Vietnamese Cinema Today" Program showcasing selected and newly produced Vietnamese films; the "Da Nang Film Selection" Program; the National Cinema Focus program; screenings of films by renowned international guests; outdoor screenings of selected Vietnamese and international films; international seminars and discussions on significant topics related to the film industry; artists meet and greet; the "Nurturing Talent" workshop, offering basic and advanced acting classes for students selected through casting rounds in major Vietnamese cities, led by foreign experts; and tours of historical sites and scenic spots promoting film locations etc.
Results: The 1st Da Nang Asian Film Festival 2023 attracted around 800 delegates and guests both domestically and internationally, including artists, actors, directors, film producers, and film experts, drawing significant attention from Da Nang citizens and film lovers. A total of 36 films (26 Vietnamese and 10 international films) competed in two categories: the "Asian Film Award" and the "Vietnamese Film Award." The jury, comprised of experts in Vietnamese and international cinema, evaluated and selected 12 official awards. Additionally, the festival's international partner, the Network for the Promotion of Asian Cinema (NETPAC), presented the NETPAC Award for the Best Vietnamese Film, and the audience selected the Audience Award for the Most Popular Vietnamese Film. Besides the competition films, the festival featured many notable activities, including six film screenings with interactions with film crews at local theaters; three outdoor film screenings; and two seminars on "Developing the Film Industry - Building a Favorable Filming Environment in Da Nang" and "Japanese Cinema - Successful Stories and Cooperation Directions with Vietnamese Cinema." The film festival has become a cinematic bridge between Viet Nam and other countries in the region, connecting Da Nang's audience with the participating countries. The 2nd Da Nang Asian Film Festival will take place in July 2024, building on the success of the first film festival.
Recommandations: Despite being its inaugural edition, the 1st Da Nang Asian Film Festival 2023 demonstrated professionalism in its organization. Title EN: The National Strategy of Human Rights
Goal: Integrate Culture In Sustainable Development Frameworks
SDG: SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: National sustainable development policies and plans
Cultural Domain: Design,Performing Arts,Media Arts,Cinema and Audiovisual Arts,Music,Publishing,Visual Arts
Agency Implementation: The Goverment of Georgia
Main Feature: On September 5, 2022 the Government of Georgia approved the second National Strategy for the Protection of Human Rights in Georgia for 2022-2030. The new comprehensive Strategy addresses all fundamental human rights and freedoms and puts a special emphasis on the protection of the rights of vulnerable groups. At the onset of 2023, the Strategy was adopted by the Parliament of Georgia.   National Strategy includes specific goals and objectives to strengthen freedom of speech, media and expression. The state is obliged to protect the freedom of speech, media and expression, as established by the Constitution of Georgia and international human rights standards, and to ensure the protection of media representatives. A free environment in which freedom of speech, media and expression is guaranteed significantly contributes to raising citizens' awareness. An informed society, in turn, contributes to the formation of an informed electorate, which is essential for ensuring a stable democracy. To further strengthen the existing guarantees, the human rights strategy envisages the improvement of the mechanisms for the protection of freedom of expression and is aimed at better protection of freedom of expression and access to information in the country, as well as internet access and media pluralism guaranteed by the Constitution.  On December 28, 2023 the Government adopted the 2024-2026 Action Plan for implementing the Human Rights Strategy. The action plan has a separate chapter on Freedom of Speech, Media, and Expression, which aims to ensure rights and freedoms of expression and access to information, including access to the Internet and media pluralism.  Apart from this, as part of the action plan, objective 15.3 focuses on further improving intellectual property rights protection mechanisms. This involves working on amendments to the Law of Georgia "On Copyright and Related Rights" to align it with EU standards and best practices. These proposed amendments, which address issues related to intermediary service liability, will be presented to the Government of Georgia for initiation, reflecting a commitment to strengthening the legal framework in line with international norms.

Main Feature: Between Sunrise and Sunset, curated by Maya Allison for Biennale Arte 2022, is an immersive installation by Emirati artist Mohamed Ahmed Ibrahim. The exhibition features dozens of human-sized, biomorphic sculptures arranged in an undulating display of color and movement, evoking the transition from sunrise to sunset. The sculptures suggest bodies, trees, metamorphosis, and mutation, reflecting the artist's deep engagement with his materials and environment. Ibrahim's process involves building up papier-m�ch� over loose skeleton structures, incorporating natural elements like earth, leaves, tea, coffee, and tobacco. The resulting textures and colors of the sculptures derive from these raw materials, creating a visceral connection to the natural world. The installation transforms the pavilion into a dynamic landscape that evolves as viewers move through it. Ibrahim is a key figure in the UAE's contemporary art scene, known for his prolific experimentation and production over nearly 40 years. He is a core member of a group of conceptual artists who have significantly influenced the Gulf arts scene since the 1980s. The exhibition is the fifth collaboration between Ibrahim and Allison, and it is accompanied by a monograph titled Mohamed Ahmed Ibrahim: Between Sunrise and Sunset / Works 1986 � 2022, co-edited by Allison and Cristiana de Marchi, and published by Kaph Books. This publication is the first comprehensive study of Ibrahim's work, contextualizing his artistic journey within the broader cultural and artistic developments in the UAE.
Results: The Between Sunrise and Sunset exhibition has successfully highlighted the UAE's contemporary art on a global stage, contributing to the international recognition of Mohamed Ahmed Ibrahim and the UAE�s vibrant art scene. Key achievements include: � International Recognition: The exhibition has garnered significant attention at La Biennale di Venezia, one of the world's most prestigious art platforms, enhancing the visibility of Emirati art. � Cultural Exchange: By participating in an international event, the exhibition has fostered cultural exchange and dialogue, showcasing the UAE's unique artistic expressions and perspectives. � Educational Impact: The accompanying monograph provides an in-depth study of Ibrahim's work, serving as a valuable resource for scholars, students, and art enthusiasts interested in Middle Eastern art. � Artistic Innovation: The use of natural materials and the transformation of the pavilion space have demonstrated innovative approaches to art-making, aligning with contemporary global trends in sustainability and materiality. Overall, the initiative has reinforced the UAE's commitment to supporting and promoting its artists, while contributing to the global discourse on contemporary art.

Title EN: The Cultural Capillaries
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture
SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Partnering with civil society
Agency Implementation: Ideell kulturallians
Main Feature: The Cultural Capillaries is a project by Ideell kulturallians (Non-profit Cultural Alliance with 20 member organizations, CSOs within the cultural sector) with funding from Postkodstiftelsen (The Swedish Postcode Foundation). It is called “the Cultural Capillaries” because the local non-profit cultural associations oxygenate the entire cultural life of Sweden. The project has been implemented in two rounds in 2021 to 2022 and 2023 to 2024 with the aim of giving local non-profit cultural associations the opportunity to apply for open project support based on the needs of the business. All associations affiliated with one of the member organisations of Ideell kulturallians were allowed to apply. A total of 1,350 organisations submitted applications, and SEK 16 million was allocated to 400 different cultural projects. Applications were received from 233 of Sweden's 290 municipalities.   Nonprofit cultural organisations play a significant role as a dynamic force in cultural life. Thousands upon thousands of associations together carry out a rich and varied range of activities throughout Sweden and create the basic conditions for artistic development. These organisations contribute a large part of the physical infrastructure or cultural life, such as stages premises and technical equipment and are an important player in creating meeting places that promote social development and democracy.  Through the rich activities of the associations and various events, opportunities have opened up for people, regardless of background or financial circumstances, to take part in cultural experiences. Through meetings, togetherness and understanding of people's differences up a promoted. In our time of rapid change and unrest in both Sweden and the world, culture can be a way to gain strength to process and gain perspective. The community in an organisation can be the decisive key to personal development, strength and self-esteem and increased participation.  In addition to many local cultural projects, Ideell kulturallians has organised 16 regional collaboration meetings where local and regional cultural associations gathered to exchange experiences, discuss common challenges and strengthen their networks. Based on applications, project reports, regional cultural meetings and discussions with associations we have obtained a solid knowledge base that describes the associations irreplaceable work for the society, the individual, and for artistic development. In September 2024 we will organise a major conference about the Cultural Capillaries and a report on the project will be published in connection about the conference.
Results: It has shown that non-profit organised culture can take any form. It emerges locally and local initiative creates great diversity. An association can bring people together around the broad and popular, as well as the advanced and experimental. Anything is possible: shadow play performances, in depth study folklore painting tradition, Lessons in the oud string instrument, development of Japanese popular culture, physical theatre. The many different activities, which may be specialised or narrow in scope, together form a varied and complex fabric.  The non-profit cultural sector plays a crucial role in making art and culture accessible to everyone – regardless of background residence or financial circumstances. Non-profit organisations are found all over the country from big cities and urban areas to rural areas and suburbs. By organising everything from performances, concerts and exhibitions to workshops, meetings and lectures around the country, the associations help more people to participate in cultural life in many different roles – as audience organised co-creator and cultural practitioner. Nonprofit organisations are often the first encounter with culture for children and young people outside the home. Many associations take great responsibility for creating participation among this particular target group, including through outreach work.  Associations also invite people to co-creation. By providing platforms for participation in arts and culture, nonprofit cultural organisations open doors to both creativity and civic engagement. When people are not just spectators but active participants in society, not only democratic values are promoted, but also the self-esteem of the individual. They are empowered, given a voice and a place to express themselves. This work is visible in organisations across the country but is perhaps particularly important in areas of low employment and social economic deprivation.  The growing problems of social exclusion and mental illness are high on the agenda of many politicians. Here the non-profit cultural sector plays a crucial role – Not least in areas such as sparsely populated areas and suburbs where institutions often do not reach. Through their important meeting places where people can explore new interests, associations contribute to meaningful leisure time and promote health.  Participation is also crucial for to foster creativity and new ideas. When people from different backgrounds and experiences are given the opportunity to contribute their thoughts and perspectives, the potential for innovation and cultural development increases.

Title EN: The Design Fund

Area of Monitoring: Cultural and creative sectors
Agency Implementation: Ministry of Culture and Business Affairs Iceland Design and Architecture
Main Feature: The Design Fund allocates grants to diverse projects in the field design and architecture in Iceland: development, research, production, marketing and travel.  The role of the Design Fund is to promote innovation and value creation in the field of design and architecture with financial support and advice, and facilitate promotion and marketing abroad that enhances the export of Icelandic design.  The Design Fund adheres to the Ministry of Culture and Business affairs, and its annual balance is determined by parliament.  The Design Fund’s aim is to strengthen the knowledge, employment opportunities and value creation in the field of design and architecture with direct financial support and consultation. The Fund also supports promotional and marketing activities abroad, which promotes increased exports of Icelandic design. The Fund is overseen by the Iceland Design and Architecture center which is under the supervision of the Ministry of Industries and Innovation. The fund is divided into four categories with different emphases: development and research grants; project grants; marketing and promotional grants; and travel grants. The categories are interlinked in such a way that a project could receive funding at multiple different stages of development and promotion. Development and research grants support innovation through funding the research and development of new designs and ideas. With a developed idea, project grants may be applied for to implement the idea. Marketing and promotional grants may be applied for once a product has been implemented, to support fully developed projects in entering the market. Travel grants are intended to increase the opportunities that designers and architects have in terms of collaboration and participation in promotional projects overseas, such as exhibitions, events, conferences, or business meetings. The board of the Fund is comprised of five individuals, one nominated by the Ministry of Education, Science and Culture, three by Iceland Design and Architecture and one appointed without nomination. The board reviews applications to the Fund with consideration of the quality and status of the project; the professional background of applicants; that the financial basis of the project is satisfactory; and the value and importance of the project for Icelandic design and architecture.
Results: Since the Fund was established in 2013 it has provided various projects with numerous grants. The Fund’s website displays information regarding projects funded.  Since its establishment, the Fund has supported numerous projects in various sectors of design. The Fund provides a well-structured environment for designers and architects to seek and receive fiscal support at all stages of idea creation, supporting innovation and diversity in the industry.
Financial Ressources: In 2924 579.042 USD was allocated to the Design Fund (80.000.000 ISK)

Title EN: The designation of the cultural space "Beit Al-Sulaiti" for events and activities of the expatriate communities residing in the State of Qatar.
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture
SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Cultural and creative sectors
Agency Implementation: Ministry of Culture
Main Feature: Following the measures adopted by the State of Qatar to encourage Arab and foreign communities to hold their events, these communities were in 2022 allocated “Beit Al-Sulaiti”, one of the spaces belonging to the Ministry of Culture. It is a spacious traditional Qatari house built in the late 19th century and completed by the State. The Minister of Information and Culture officially handed it over in 1990. The space is equipped with all the necessary facilities for such activities. Various communities can use it free of charge to express their customs, traditions, and cultural features. It is worth noting that the State of Qatar, through its various cultural institutions, has adopted the principle of specialization since the 1980s to enable Arab and foreign communities residing in the country to open educational schools following the same curricula as their countries of origin. This approach helps them preserve their distinctiveness and facilitates their integration into Qatari society. For instance, the Tunisian School in Doha was established in 1988 for the Tunisian community and other Maghreb communities.  Additionally, the measure of allocating a space for communities to practice their cultural activities is similar to another relatively older measure, which also exceeds the time frame covered by this report. This is the “Artist in Residence Program” overseen by the cultural center named “Fire Station”. The center is dedicated to creativity and aims to provide an appropriate space for artists who wish to practice or develop their creativity through residency programs (https://firestation.org.qa/ar), such as the New York Art Residency for 2024. It also attracts local community members in the State of Qatar through events and opportunities offered by the center, including involving them in artistic and cultural exhibitions
Results: Since the State’s allocation of “Beit Al Sulaiti” in 2022 for different expatriate communities to express their diverse cultures, more than 25 cultural events have been held by over 15 Arab and foreign communities. These events have included artistic and musical performances, singing and dancing, culinary traditions, and traditional clothing displays. Each community is usually given a specific day to showcase its culture.
Recommandations: Upon evaluating the initiative of allocating a space for expatriate communities to express their customs, traditions, and cultural diversity, the Ministry of Culture, as the supervising authority of this space, has recognized the success of this initiative. This success is particularly shown in the significant number of events held.  In terms of recommendations, the department within the Ministry of Culture responsible for managing this space is studying mechanisms to expand the participation of communities. This includes allocating budgets to help cover the needs of some events on the one hand, and facilitating procedures for using the space and obtaining financial support on the other hand.

Main Feature: Darat al Funun – The Khalid Shoman Foundation, is a home for the arts and artists from the Arab world. It is the first of its kind non-profit private initiative in the region. It was founded and led by artist Suha Shoman, to support the arts and Arab artists mainly in the conflict zone of Bilad al Sham.Today, Darat al Funun is housed in six renovated historical buildings and warehouses dating back to the 1920s and 1930s. Our location includes a restored archaeological site of a six-century Byzantine church built over a Roman temple in our garden. We bring together visual arts with other forms of artistic expression by hosting innovative performances, film screenings, concerts, and cultural events. Our vision of a home for the arts and artists from Jordan and the Arab world develops and evolves in parallel with the changing art scene and the needs of the artists. The houses that form Darat al Funun were built by Jordanian, Palestinian, Syrian, and Lebanese families, and they are a living memory of the history of Jordan and the shared history of the Levant region (Bilad al Sham). Today, Darat al Funun is an oasis for the arts overlooking the crowded downtown area of the old city of Amman. Visitors come to admire Amman's traditional architecture, attend events in the archaeological site, read a book in our art library, or take a walk in our gardens. Darat al Funun actively pursues its mission of providing a platform for contemporary Arab artists. We support art practices and artistic exchange, stimulate critical discourse and research, and host visiting and resident artists who produce and show their work. Academics and artists give talks or workshops, and The Lab is open to projects by emerging artists. We also program educational activities for young people and students. Our art library, publications, films, and digital archives are open for research and documentation. In 1988, establishing a home for the arts was a challenge, to say the least. By salvaging and restoring abandoned traditional buildings and antiquities, Darat al Funun contributed to preserving Jordan's architectural and cultural heritage. By rehabilitating them and dedicating them to contemporary arts, Darat al Funun brought together the old and the new, the past and the present, tradition and modernity. Over the years, "Art, Architecture, Archaeology" became the symbol of the Darat al Funun. It is the only site in Amman where archaeological remains and traditional historical buildings stand side by side in a space dedicated to contemporary Arab arts.
Results: Our initiative covers the following programs: Artists-in-Residence: Through this program, we aim to create a productive environment for artistic exchange.  Over the years, we have had many artists stay in residence at Darat al Funun, including Etel Adnan & Simone Fattal (Lebanese), Farid Belkahia (Moroccan), Marwan Kassab Bachi (Syrian), Rachid Koraichi (Algerian), Mona Hatoum (Palestinian, Lebanese), Amal Kenawy (Egyptian), Tarek Atoui (Lebanese), Wael Shawky (Egyptian), and Emily Jacir (Palestinian).  Artists stay in residence to produce works for their exhibition at Darat al Funun, to give talks or workshops, and to engage with our activities and the local art scene in Amman.  Many of these artists had their first solo exhibition in the region at Darat al Funun. 	  Residency Exchange Program: We have since 1999 also collaborated with international institutions in exchange residencies programs. We have had residency agreements with: UNESCO-Aschberg “Bursaries for Artists” Program which lasted from 1999-2007. It gave the opportunity to young artists from all over the world to be in residency at Darat al Funun (countries: Pakistan, the UK, the Czech Republic, Spain, Bulgaria, South Africa, Mexico and Belgium) Pro Helvetia, Switzerland (2004-2012): Over the years, young artists from Jordan including Oraib Toukan, Ala’ Younis and Raed Ibrahim spent time in residence in Aarau, Switzerland, and we hosted several Swiss artists in return. Nuova Icona, Venice (2014):  Mohammad Hawajri from Gaza spent time in residency in Venice, while we hosted his Italian counterpart, Lorenzo Maneti.  Fondazione Fotografia di Modena in Italy (2014-2019): This program gave the opportunity to young photographers from Jordan to follow lectures while in Modena. We hosted students from their photography program as part of their studies. (Nadia Bseiso, Mohammed Zakaria, Mo’Awia Bajis)  The residency exchange program gives young artists the opportunity to find inspiration from the city of Amman, and from places such as the Dead Sea, Petra and Wadi Rum, engage with our activities and the local art scene, give talks, and produce art in a new context. Fellowship: Our Ph.D fellowship encourages research on art in the Arab world.  In 2011 we established the Darat al Funun Dissertation Fellowship for Modern and Contemporary Arab Art to encourage research on modern and contemporary art of the Arab world.  The fellowship provides financial support to one or two Ph.D. candidates per academic year. They stay between 4-6 months in Amman. Fellows get the chance to pursue their own research, to use our archives and our collection, and to write their dissertation.   Fellows are expected to give at least one public lecture, and participate in our cultural and artistic activities. It is the first existent fellowship in the region exclusively designed to advance scholarship in the field.  Summer Academy: Through this program, we aim to develop practice within a critical setting through experimentation.  In 1999 we launched our Summer Academy, which provided a key opportunity for emerging artists to study and work under supervision of the late Berlin-based Syrian artist Marwan Kassab Bachi.   From 1999-2003 over 60 artists from Jordan, Palestine, Syria, Lebanon, Egypt and Iraq attended the academy. For many of these artists it was a formative experience in their career.  In 2019, Darat al Funun relaunched the Summer Academy with a new concept, offering 10-15 participants from the region the space to develop their practice within a critical setting that encourages experimentation, knowledge-sharing, and communal learning.  The Lab: for young emerging artists who are participating in our At the Lab program. We hold an annual open call for innovative projects by young artists at our experimental space The Lab that engage with the community or interact with the public, through workshops, discussions, public contributions, or otherwise. Artists at The Lab coming from outside Amman also stay in our residency building.  We also strongly encourage and support local artists to incorporate environmental themes into their work. For example, in a recent exhibition titled "Re-rooting," which featured works by 21 local young artists and environmental activists, many of the projects addressed ecological concerns. This group exhibition highlighted various projects that shed light on the three most pressing concerns in Jordan today: water politics, agro-ecology, and extractive building practices. Several featured projects in the exhibition examined building practices that often disregard the destruction of habitats, the existence of other species, and the ecological damage caused by such practices. For instance, Tayyun Research Studio's "Insect Hotel" presented a unique perspective on city living by proposing structures for interspecies coexistence. In contrast, Abeer Seikaly's video, "Matters of Time," drew comparisons between temporary and permanent architecture in desert environments, highlighting the use of natural renewable resources such as goat hair in tent-making, as opposed to non-renewable materials and building practices that harm the landscape. Overall, the "Re-rooting" exhibition raised awareness of these pressing issues and offered creative solutions to mitigate their impact.

By bringing together the most dynamic and representative modern and contemporary masterpieces of over 200 artists from more than 20 countries and regions, the event allowed the public to experience the breadth and depth of art while embarking on a grand aesthetic journey.  The CAB has been actively encouraging local non-profit cultural and art groups and individual performers to participate in the creative process, soliciting more creative productions with local characteristics, developing a larger showcase platform for local performing arts, and, moreover, inviting overseas performing groups and artists to perform in Macao. Title EN: The President’s Special Fund for the Support of Talented Youth
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture
SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Cultural and creative sectors
Cultural Domain: Design,Performing Arts,Media Arts,Cinema and Audiovisual Arts,Music,Publishing,Visual Arts
Agency Implementation: The Council of the President’s Special Fund for the Support of Talented Youth  Ministry of Culture of the Republic of Belarus
Main Feature: The special fund of the President of the Republic of Belarus for the support of the talented youth was set up in accordance with Decree No.18 of the President of the Republic of Belarus of 12 January 1996 “On the special fund of the President of the Republic of Belarus for the support of the talented youth.” The operation and goals of the special fund of the President of the Republic of Belarus for the support of the talented youth are regulated by Decree No.429 of the President of the Republic of Belarus of 16 December 2022 “On the operation of special funds of the President of the Republic of Belarus”. The resources of the fund are generated from the allocations from the reserve fund of the President of the Republic of Belarus, voluntary contributions from the citizens of the Republic of Belarus, foreign citizens and stateless persons, as well as legal entities, and etc. The Council of the Fund manages the fund's resources. The Council consists of the leading cultural and art workers, representatives of the Presidential Administration of the Republic of Belarus, the Office of the Council of Ministers of the Republic of Belarus, interested state bodies and institutions, creative unions, and other public associations. The Fund Council, in accordance with the proposals from state bodies, institutions, public associations and the recommendations of the expert and art commission of the fund, encourages talented students, teachers, young artists and cultural workers with creative achievements. The Fund seeks to create conditions to discover young talents and unlock the potential of young people and provide opportunities for their professional growth and development. The Fund pays talented young people scholarships, grants and bonuses, provides them with financial assistance for internship participation, to conduct master classes by leading artists. The Fund resources are allocated for creative projects and meetings with recognized artists of various countries. They are also sent for the organizing contests, festivals, concerts, exhibitions, publications and other events as well as to identify and promote young talents and their creativity; ensuring the participation of creative youth in international competitions, exhibitions, symposiums and other actions in the field of culture and art aimed at the development and mutual enrichment of national cultures; the acquisition of musical instruments, stage costumes, materials and equipment for art classes. In order to improve the activities of the special funds of the President of the Republic of Belarus for the social support of gifted pupils and students, for the support of talented youth, on December 16, 2022, the Head of State signed Decree №429 «On the activities of the special funds of the President of the Republic of Belarus». The document is aimed at providing state support for the best representatives of gifted and talented youth, creating favorable conditions for the further development of their scientific and creative potential, and stimulating youth initiatives. Annually, about 150 people are planned to be encouraged by the awards of the Fund for the Support of Talented Youth. Also, in addition to Decree №429 «On the activities of special funds of the President of the Republic of Belarus», the Ministry of Culture of the Republic of Belarus has developed a roadmap for accompanying talented young people, which allows providing educational and professional support for young people who are included in the database of gifted and talented youth. Providing state support for gifted and talented youth makes an important contribution to the achievement by the Republic of Belarus of Sustainable Development Goals 4, 8 and other SDGs. Over the years the special fund has provided financial assistance to 4,518 citizens and 359 groups. In line with Decree No. 429 signed by the President of Belarus on 16 December 2022, the Culture Ministry operates a data bank of talented youth. This data bank features people included in the special fund of the President of the Republic of Belarus for the social support of gifted students.
Results: The activity of the The President’s Special Fund for the Support of Talented Youth provides the tremendous assistance in the formation and development of a creative person. It stimulates the motivation of talented young people to achieve a high creative performance, and supports teachers, state and non-governmental organizations of culture and art, universities and the children's educational institutions in the art sphere.
Financial Ressources: Around 3mln BYN which is 850 th. USD
Recommandations: he Fund’s activities (operational and financial) are monitored annually by the Fund’s Council. Based on monitoring, the measures and recommendations are being taken to improve the management of the Fund and increase its potential.

Main Feature: Describe the main features of the measure/initiative (800 words):  THE ROYAL FILM COMMISSION - JORDAN (RFC) was established with a vision to develop an internationally competitive Jordanian film industry. Founded in accordance with the Royal Film Commission Law No. 27 for the year 2003, approved by Law No. 22 issued by the Parliament in 2008, the RFC is a financially and administratively autonomous Jordanian public organization led by a Board of Commissioners, chaired by HRH Prince Ali Bin Al Hussein. The RFC is a member of the Association for Film Commissioners International (AFCI). The (AFCI) is the official professional and educational organization for film commissions. AFCI Members assist feature, television, commercial, industrial and stills production throughout the world. For more information about (AFCI) www.afci.org What we do  Production Services We provide producers with comprehensive services, such as assistance in obtaining filming permits, location scouting, custom clearance and much more. Education & TrainingWe develop learning environment in cinematic arts across Jordan and establish programs that address the need for new and innovative methods of communication. Fostering Film Culture in Jordan The RFC organizes thematic screenings throughout the year all over the country, thus enriching the film culture in Jordan. Funding The Royal Film Commission – Jordan (RFC) supports the activities and programs that develop the potential of the independent local film industry, as well as its economic viability and continuity. To that end, the Jordan Film Fund (JFF) has been established to enable filmmakers to tell their stories, especially in Jordan.
Results: In the twentieth year since the establishment of the Royal Film Commission (RFC-Jordan), the most important achievements of the Commission are summarized as follows:     Designing and implementing an integrated strategy aimed at building and strengthening the film and television production sector by working on five main axes:    Filming in Jordan     The Commission provides integrated production services for film and television productions filmed in the Kingdom. Filmmakers can obtain comprehensive information about filming in Jordan through the commission, as well as the necessary filming permits, equipment entry facilities and site surveys.    Over the past sixty years, huge films have been shot in the Kingdom such as "Lawrence of Arabia" to contemporary commercial films, such as "Dune", "Star Wars: Episode Nine", "Aladdin" and "Mars Man", as well as television series and advertisements. Jordan is an attractive location for filming due to its variety of locations, availability of 300 sunny days a year, presence of professional crews, and financial incentives. To enhance production facilities in Jordan, a new studio has been built in Amman, including two 1,500-square-meter cameras.    A total of 143 feature films shot in Jordan include 31 Jordanian films and six co-productions  Total foreign series filmed in Jordan 29   Productions benefiting from the incentive system (financial response) 31  Number of beneficiaries of the production sector 133.966 job opportunities    Jordan Film Fund    The Commission supports activities and programs that develop the local independent film industry, taking into account its economic feasibility and sustainability. To this end, the Jordan Film Fund was established in 2011 with the aim of enabling filmmakers to tell their stories, especially in Jordan.     The projects supported by the Fund participated in the most important Arab and international festivals, many of which won valuable awards, and Jordan was represented at the Oscars twice. This is in addition to the screening of commercially supported films, especially recently, in Jordanian, Arab and international cinemas, in addition to online platforms such as Netflix and Shahid.

Main Feature: 1.)	The Roots of Dance (2021 – 2022) was an international and multi-cultural arts project aimed at young dancers and choreographers. Its goal was to stimulate the artists' imagination by returning to the roots of dance and looking for inspiration in local culture in order to develop contemporary dance and enrich dance culture in the world. The stimulus for this search was the traditional Polish culture.  2.)	“PolandDances / Tournée” (2022, annually thereafter) was a program that subsidized the presentation of Polish dance performances internationally. This program served to present and promote Polish dance artists to foreign curators, presenters, producers and audiences.
Results: 1.)	The Roots of Dance - Over the course of two years, online and live workshops and meetings took place. Contemporary dance, dance and traditional music artists from Poland conducted workshops with participants from schools and dance companies in Georgia, Mexico, Canada, Croatia, USA, India, China and Malaysia. On one hand, the foreign dancers learned about Polish dance traditions, while on the other hand, the Polish artists showed them tools for building contemporary dance based on the traditions of their own country. The culmination of the project was a study visit by the foreign participants to Silesia, Poland, where they first learned about the traditional cultures of Podhale and Beskid Żywiecki through field visits. Then, together with Polish contemporary dance artists and students, they worked on choreographic etudes that were a fusion of many dance and music traditions and many cultures and ways of thinking with the body. 2.)	“PolandDances / Tournée” - Three organizations took part in the Program so far, exporting Polish dance culture abroad and cooperating with international Partners. Main Feature: The state program is aimed at implementing the priorities of the social and economic development of the Republic of Belarus for 2021-2025 and solving the problems of state policy in the sphere of culture. Within the framework of the State Program "Culture of Belarus" for 2016-2020, a number of measures have been implemented to preserve the historical memory of the Belarusian people, their national and cultural identity and traditions, to actively involve citizens of Belarus into the cultural life of the country, to realize the creative potential of the nation, to ensure high-quality formation, preservation and use of documents of the National Archival Fund of the Republic of Belarus as part of the information resource of the country, as well as to promote  the preservation of the national and cultural identity of the Belarusian diaspora. Important achievements in the development of the cultural sphere in the last five years are associated with the improvement of legal regulation, optimization of the network of cultural institutions, intensification of activities to protect the historical and cultural heritage, accelerating the pace of informatization of the cultural sphere, as well as with increasing the demand by the Belarusian citizens for services provided by cultural organizations.   The main directions of cultural development in the medium term will be associated with solving such pressing problems as: improving the quality and ensuring the maximum availability of cultural services, which will be possible thanks to the introduction of various forms of public service using modern technologies, the development of national cultural brands and their integration into the international cultural space, the development of cultural industries, folk crafts and trades. An important problem at the present stage is the improvement of the infrastructure and digitalization of the cultural sphere. Work will continue on the construction, restoration, reconstruction, major repairs of cultural infrastructure facilities, including architectural monuments, updating and modernizing the material and technical base of cultural organizations. It is planned to form digital cultural content, create electronic catalogues of historical, cultural and natural monuments of the Republic of Belarus, digitize the funds of museums, libraries, film funds, and intangible cultural heritage sites. The goal of the State Program is to create conditions for the effective functioning of the network of cultural organizations and the active involvement of Belarusian citizens into the cultural life of the country. The implementation of the State Program will contribute to the achievement at the national level of the Sustainable Development Goals for the period up to 2030, contained in the resolution of the United Nations General Assembly of September 25, 2015, including ensuring openness, safety, resilience and environmental sustainability of cities and settlements, promoting progressive, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all.
Results: 1. legal and social protection of cultural workers has been ensured and remuneration system has been improved; 2. the program has contributed to the preservation, use and ensuring great access to the historical and cultural heritage of the country; 3. the cooperation between cultural institutions and their audience has been strengthened, the attendance at cultural events and the number of the amateurs have increased; 4. the program has contributed to the development of international relations and inter-cultural communication through the implementation of international agreements of the Republic of Belarus and celebrating the days of the Belarusian culture abroad; 5. cultural education programs have been created in various fields of culture and harmonized with the requirements of the labor market; higher education institutions of culture and art offer high-quality and competitive education, and their research centers deal with important research cultural issues; additional professional education of cultural workers is developing; 6. multilateral communication with compatriots abroad has been ensured through the implementation of numerous cultural and educational initiatives, including festivals, exhibitions, organization of the Belarusian language courses for the Belarusian diaspora, publishing and research projects, and activities in support of the common heritage. 7. conditions for better mobility of the Belarusian artists and for the export of cultural products in such industries as cinema, visual arts and design, performing arts, librarianship and museum affairs have been created.
