Title EN: Theater in Krisen- und Konfliktgebieten – Travail théâtral dans les zones de crise et de conflit - Workshop
Goal: Promote Human Rights And Fundamental Freedoms
SDG: SDG 5 - Achieve gender equality and empower all women and girls,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels
Area of Monitoring: Artistic freedom
Agency Implementation: SWISS ITI
Main Feature: Swiss ITI est le centre suisse de l’Institut International du Théâtre-ITI, qui est une ONG partenaire de l’UNESCO. L’ITI, fondé en 1948, comporte 80 centres nationaux dans le monde, c’est la plus grande organisation mondiale des arts du spectacle. L’ITI promeut les objectifs de l’UNESCO pour la compréhension mutuelle et la paix et préconise la protection et la promotion des expressions culturelles, indépendamment de l’âge, du sexe, de la religion ou de l’origine ethnique. L’ITI travaille au niveau international et national pour l’accomplissement de ces missions dans les domaines de l’éducation artistique, de la collaboration et des échanges internationaux, la mobilité des acteurs et actrices de la culture.  Dans le cadre des Rencontres suisses de théâtre 2021 à Fribourg, Swiss ITI a organisé et réalisé une table ronde sur le thème « Theatre in conflict zones ». Des professionnelles et professionnels du théâtre ont parlé de leur travail théâtral pratique dans des zones de conflit et des artistes des pays concernés ont décrit de leur point de vue leurs conditions de travail et les restrictions dans leur pays ainsi que leurs expériences dans le cadre de coopérations internationales. O'tooli Mazanza-Haase (Malawi), Homan Wesa (Afghanistan), Anina Jendreyko (Suisse/Irak), Thorleifur Örn Arnarsson (Islande/Irak) ont participé à cette table ronde.  L'attention et l'accent mis sur les difficultés, les possibilités et les restrictions liées au travail théâtral dans les régions en crise ont pu ainsi être présentés à un large public grâce au cadre des Rencontres théâtrales suisses.  Dans le cadre des Rencontres théâtrales suisses 2023, Swiss ITI a organisé un atelier sur le thème « Travail théâtral dans les zones de crise et de conflit ». Daniel Bausch (Professeur, Accademia Dimitri) et deux étudiantes formées dans le cadre du CAS Resilient Stages (Accademia Dimitri) ont présenté leurs expériences pratiques de travail scénique dans le nord de l'Irak et ont donné au public un aperçu du travail théâtral pratique dans les zones de conflit.   L’attention des jeunes professionnelles et professionnels de la scène a ainsi été attirée vers l’existence d’une formation académique qui fournit des bases pour le travail théâtral dans les zones de crise. Swiss ITI, membre de faîtière internationale « ITI-Institut International du Théâtre » est en relation avec ses homonymes dans les zones de conflits et favorise les contacts nécessaires, ou intervient directement sous forme d’atelier dans des camps de réfugiés ou de présentation de performances et spectacles.
Results: La possibilité de suivre la formation CAS « Resilient Stages » devenu CAS « Intercultural Theatre Practice in Conflict Zones » de l'Accademia Teatro Dimitri a été présentée à un large public.  Ce programme de formation offre une occasion unique d'expérimenter le travail interculturel dans des zones de conflit et de crise locales et internationales et d'utiliser des approches basées sur le théâtre pour faire face à des réalités difficiles. Le programme de ce CAS (Certifcate of Advanced Studies) se compose de trois modules qui s'appuient les uns sur les autres et combinent connaissances théoriques, exercices pratiques et réflexion.   Les participantes et participants apprennent comment le travail théâtral peut être utilisé pour activer les forces vitales, renforcer la conscience de soi et le sentiment de communauté. Elles et ils apprennent à réfléchir à leur propre situation de départ et développent une conscience de l'inégalité et de la discrimination. Elles et ils analysent leur motivation et acquièrent des compétences et des aptitudes leur permettant de se positionner dans des coopérations interculturelles.   La participante ou le participant s'engagera dans une expérience inspirante et transformatrice. Un échange avec des personnes de théâtre des régions kurdes d'Irak et/ou de Syrie est proposé. Elle et il sera possible d'expérimenter comment le théâtre peut contribuer à vivre la diversité comme une richesse en apprenant les uns des autres. Le travail théâtral dans les régions en crise est une création culturelle tournée vers l'avenir.

These performances will be followed by interactive sessions with the audience, allowing for open discussions and reflections on the themes presented. These sessions will be designed to impart knowledge on Switzerland's approaches to GBV prevention and to enhance participants' skills in using theater as a medium for social change. Community leaders, women’s organizations, and other stakeholders will be involved in the planning and execution of the theater projects. Title EN: T-Levels and the TLTP
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture
SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Cultural and creative sectors
Agency Implementation: Department for Education
Main Feature: The TLTP is a level 2 one-year, 16-to-19 study programme that provides a route to T levels.   T Levels are level 3 classroom-based technical alternatives to A Levels, designed with employers to deliver the skills they need, combining classroom learning with a substantial industry placement.   These courses will provide students with the core knowledge and skills needed for entry to a range of occupations in the creative industries including Jeweller, Costumier, Stage Technician and Broadcast Assistant.
Results: Digital Production, Design and Development was among the first T Levels launched in September 2020, providing a route into the video games sector. The Craft and Design and Media, Broadcast and Production T Levels will be taught for the first time from September 2024.       The Ofsted report evaluating T-levels found the following: ‘Most students who remain on a T-level course achieve the qualification successfully. Around two thirds of respondents to our 2022 questionnaire told us that they felt well prepared for their next steps. However, many leave before the end of the course, and the number of students who progress to the second year of T-level courses is low in many providers. In at least one provider, no students progressed from the first year of the T-level course to the second year.    Students who complete T-level courses generally move on to employment, apprenticeships or higher-level study, including degree courses. In some cases, students who wanted to go to university are surprised and disappointed that T-level qualifications are not always accepted as a valid entry qualification.’
Financial Ressources: The Government provides $698.36 per student for the industry placement element of the T Level programme. A total of nearly $1,003,094,600.00 million in funding has been allocated to the delivery of T Levels, across three main areas: capital funding (over $637.87 million), the T Level Professional Development Programme for teachers (nearly $50.79 million) and the Capacity and Delivery Fund for employers ($317.43 million).
Recommandations: The Department for Education (DfE) commissioned Ofsted to carry out a thematic review of T-levels and the TLTP across 2021/20223 to assess the early implementation of the new qualifications. The report writes the following:   ‘There remains considerable work to do to improve the quality and effectiveness of T-level courses and the TLTP, to make sure that they fulfil their potential and can be offered at scale.  T levels and the TLTP have been implemented with varying degrees of success. In the best providers, they have been adopted after extensive engagement with employers and as part of a well-considered curriculum planning process.    Students’ experiences on T-level courses and on the TLTP vary considerably. At their best, T levels provide an opportunity to combine high-quality study of theory with excellent development of practical skills. At worst, courses are not at all what students expected, and many students reported being misled and ill informed about their content and structure.    Initial assessment of students’ abilities at the start of their T-level courses and on the TLTP is weak in most providers. Teachers do not assess effectively enough what students know or can do in relation to their chosen pathway. They do not identify gaps in students’ knowledge and understanding precisely enough to inform curricular planning and make sure that students make secure progress. Where initial assessment is more comprehensive, teachers do not always use the information to plan and sequence the curriculum.    The physical resources used to support the teaching of T-level courses and the TLTP are good in most providers. Providers have used capital funding appropriately to invest in high-quality, up-to-date resources. Teaching resources, including specimen assessment and examination materials, are not of such good quality. The very limited resources available from awarding organisations to support the teaching and assessment of T levels are underdeveloped. Providers do not collaborate to share resources and best practice.    The practical aspects of courses are generally taught well. However, vocational teachers often struggle to teach theoretical content in sufficient depth or to set work that is appropriately challenging. The theoretical content of T-level courses is often more complex and demanding than that of similar courses. Many providers have experienced difficulties in recruiting and retaining staff who have the required experience and expertise.    Teachers expressed concern about the high volume of content in T-level courses. They are particularly concerned about the assessment requirements and the length of the industry placement, both of which limit the available teaching time. On some T-level courses, teachers and students are concerned about the amount of assessment and the appropriateness of assessment methods. On the health and science T level, the quantity and complexity of the science content make it particularly hard to teach everything in the time available.    The quality of industry placements varies considerably across individual providers and on different T-level courses. Finding suitable placements is a barrier to increasing the number of T-level places available in many providers. The number of suitable placements is often limited in any given area because of the specific employment sector where the placement is required and the length of time students are required to attend.    Often employers are poorly informed about the content and structure of T levels. In these cases, activities that students complete on industry placements are not well aligned with the T-level course content. In some instances, industry placements are not appropriate for the pathway that students are on. However, the best industry placements do provide a very beneficial opportunity for students to develop relevant knowledge and skills.    Staff in providers are concerned that the T-level ‘brand’ is not well known. They are concerned that parents and school staff do not understand T-level qualifications. They are also worried that the brand’s reputation has been damaged by problems with T-level examinations in 2022 and delays in rolling out new T levels in craft and design, media, broadcast and production, hairdressing, barbering, hospitality and catering.    TLTP curriculums have generally improved since our first visits. The best TLTPs include a relevant technical or vocational qualification and a range of activities, including work placements, that prepare students to move on to an appropriate T-level pathway. On the most effective TLTPs, students benefit from valuable work-experience opportunities that are tailored to their development needs and the learning aims of their programmes. Such placements enhance the TLTP curriculum and are a positive and popular aspect of courses.    However, the least effective TLTPs are not fit for purpose. They do not include work experience and do not prepare students to move on to a T-level course. In cases where students are on work-experience placements, these are not sufficiently tailored, and students do not benefit from activities as much as they should. For some students, the TLTP results in no meaningful outcome after a year on the programme. Across all providers, few students on the TLTP move on to a T-level course.’

Enhanced Local and International Collaboration: - Jazz Festival in Dili: Supported by France, ArtEmpreender organized a Jazz Festival that fostered youth engagement, cultural diversity, and local artist promotion, highlighting Timorese talent on a global platform. - Duo Cziffra Concert: In partnership with the Institute Français, ArtEmpreender facilitated a classical music concert and workshops, enriching local musicians’ skills and encouraging cross- cultural musical exchanges. 2. Promotion of Artistic and Cultural Development: - Workshops and Master Classes: The week-long event featuring Duo Cziffra included various workshops and master classes in Dili, enhancing the artistic capabilities of local musicians and connecting traditional Timorese music with classical genres. - Fashion Week Participation: ArtEmpreender members participated in CPLP Fashion Week in Lisbon, showcasing Timorese fashion and music, thereby promoting cultural richness and diversity on an international stage. 3. Fostered Entrepreneurship: - Training and Capacity Building: Regular training programs and mentoring sessions have equipped cultural entrepreneurs and artists with essential skills for professional growth and sustainability. - Networking Opportunities: Establishing connections with international artists and       8              organizations has expanded market access and created new opportunities for Timorese artists. 4. Facilitated Mobility and Exchange of Cultural Professionals: - Exchange Programs and Residencies: Artists and cultural entrepreneurs have participated in international residencies and fellowships, fostering professional development and cultural exchange. These experiences have enriched local practices and expanded the global reach of Timorese art. - Travel Grants: Financial support for attending international events has enabled Timorese artists to gain exposure, network, and collaborate with global peers. 5. Increased Visibility and Awareness: - Media Campaigns: Strategic use of traditional and social media has raised the global profile of Timorese art and culture, attracting international interest and appreciation. - Publications and Reports: Documenting and promoting successful collaborations and exchanges have showcased the vibrant cultural landscape of Timor-Leste. These efforts by ArtEmpreender have nurtured the local artistic community and positioned Timor- Leste as an active participant in the global cultural arena. The initiatives have led to meaningful cultural exchanges, professional growth for artists, and a strengthened socio-economic fabric through art and entrepreneurship.

Title EN: Un programme national pour l'entreprenariat féminin et l'investissement sensible au genre « Raidet »
Goal: Promote Human Rights And Fundamental Freedoms
SDG: SDG 5 - Achieve gender equality and empower all women and girls,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels
Area of Monitoring: Gender equality
Cultural Domain: Design,Performing Arts,Media Arts,Cinema and Audiovisual Arts,Music,Publishing,Visual Arts
Agency Implementation: Ministère de la Famille, de la Femme, de l'Enfance et des Personnes âgées (MFFEPA)
Main Feature: L’égalité des genres est une priorité globale de l’Unesco préconisé par la convention de 2005 dans son article 7 qui stipule que les états parties sont encouragés à « tenir dument compte des conditions et des besoins des femmes ». Elle fait partie aussi des priorités stratégiques de la Tunisie fortement engagée dans la mise en œuvre de stratégies nationales alignées sur les objectifs de développement durable. La promotion de l'égalité des genres présuppose la mise en place de mesures permettant l’instauration et le développement d’une culture d’autonomisation des femmes et ce dans le cadre d’une approche intégrée de développement durable en vertu de laquelle les droits économiques sociaux et culturels des femmes sont en interaction et appréhendés de manière globale. Ainsi l’accès de la femme à l’offre culturelle, sa contribution en tant que praticienne de la culture au niveau des différents maillons de la chaine des valeurs véhiculée par la convention de 2005 à savoir la création, la production et la diffusion reste d’une manière ou d’une autre fortement tributaire du degré de son inclusion sociale et son autonomisation économique. Dans cette perspective et afin de développer une politique publique d’autonomisation économique des femmes incluant la promotion de l’investissement et le renforcement des capacités entrepreneuriales des femmes un programme national pour l'entreprenariat féminin et l'investissement sensible au genre « Raidet » est lancé le 8 mars 2022 ayant pour objectif principal de soutenir l'initiative privée des femmes, en particulier les femmes et les filles innovantes dans les secteurs porteurs dans tous les gouvernorats, dans les zones prioritaires et dans les quartiers populaires à forte densité de population, en plus de soutenir des projets spéciaux ciblant des groupes spécifiques de femmes en situation de vulnérabilité. La mise en œuvre de ce programme s'étend jusqu'à l'année 2026 et pourra créer 3000 projets féminins, à raison de 600 projets chaque année, avec des fonds estimés à 50 millions de dinars du budget de l'Etat. Le programme cible les femmes tunisiennes âgées entre 18 et 59 ans, de toutes les catégories et niveaux d'éducation (des femmes analphabètes jusqu’aux titulaires d'un doctorat), et inclut les femmes et les filles des zones rurales et urbaines. Les femmes souhaitant financer leurs projets doivent posséder les qualifications suivantes : • Être titulaire d'un diplôme universitaire ou d'un diplôme équivalent. • Certificat de formation des centres de formation professionnelle. • Certificat de capacité professionnelle. • Tout certificat de formation reconnu. Il vise à renforcer le rôle des femmes dans le développement et l’économie et à encourager les femmes et les filles à lancer leurs propres projets d’investissement, en fournissant 7 lignes de financement pour accorder des micro, petits et moyens prêts à des conditions différentielles et concessionnelles, et avec un plafond de financement de 300 milles dinars. Le MFFEPA met en œuvre le programme national « Raidet » à travers des conventions de partenariat avec 03 institutions bancaires partenaires :  Financement des projets des femmes à travers la ligne de financement créé avec la Banque Tunisienne de Solidarité • Financement de la création de micro-projets dont le coût ne dépasse pas 10 mille dinars pour un projet, sans autofinancement et sans excédents, qui sont restitués sur une période ne dépassant pas 48 mois, y compris un différé d'amortissement ne dépassant pas 12 mois, selon le type d'activité. • Financement de la création de microentreprises dont le coût est supérieur à 10 mille dinars et inférieur à 150 mille dinars pour un seul projet sans nécessiter l’autofinancement de la part du bénéficiaire, cela est réalisé par l'affectation d'un crédit qui doit être restitué dans les conditions suivantes : - Montant des crédits : 20% du coût du projet sur les ressources de la ligne de financement sans emploi des excédents. - Une période de remboursement ne dépassant pas cinq (5) ans, compte tenu d'un délai de grâce de trois ans. - La banque affecte le reste du financement (80% du coût du projet) sous la forme d'un prêt à moyen terme aux conditions applicables à la Banque Tunisienne de Solidarité  Financement des projets des femmes à travers la ligne de financement créé avec la Banque de Financement des Petites et Moyennes Entreprises • Les petites et moyennes entreprises féminines sont financées avec un plafond maximum de 300 000 dinars, individuellement ou dans le cadre du financement participatif (deux entrepreneures ou plus), tout en respectant les conditions suivantes : - Montant des crédits : 30% du coût du projet dans le cadre de l'autofinancement, réparti comme suit : - 25% des ressources de la ligne de financement du Ministère de la Famille, de la Femme, de l'Enfance et des Personnes âgées, sans emploi des excédents - Contribution de 5% de l’entrepreneure et de ses partenaires - La banque affecte le reste du financement (70% du coût du projet) sous forme de prêt à moyen ou long terme, selon les conditions applicables à la banque, avec un taux d'excédent estimé à 7,25% - Des avis sont émis sur les demandes d'obtention d'un prêt de contribution et attribués par le comité d'animation du programme « Raidet ». Le prêt à moyen ou long terme est accordé par le Comité Interne de Crédit de la Banque, selon les conditions applicables à la Banque. Le délai de grâce : Maximum quatre (04) ans. - Période de Remboursement : Un maximum de dix (10) ans, y compris le délai de grâce estimé à quatre ans. - Assurer l'accompagnement et l'encadrement des femmes qui souhaitent lancer des projets au niveau national et régional.  Financement des projets des femmes à travers la ligne de financement créé avec la Banque Nationale Agricole • Financer, développer et/ou élargir les petites et moyennes entreprises féminines dont le coût est supérieur à 100 000 dinars et inférieur à 300 000 dinars. • La Banque nationale agricole affecte jusqu'à 80 % du coût du projet sous forme de prêts à moyen ou long terme. - Montant des crédits : 20% du coût du projet sur les ressources de la ligne de financement du Ministère de la Famille, de la Femme, de l'Enfance et des Personnes âgées. - La banque cède le reste du financement (80% du coût du projet) sous forme de prêt à moyen terme aux conditions applicables à la banque. - Une période de remboursement ne dépassant pas 12 ans et un délai de grâce ne dépassant pas 3 ans, - Assurer l'accompagnement et l'encadrement pour celles qui souhaitent lancer des projets, dans les limites des capacités de la Banque.
Results: Depuis son lancement le 8 mars 2022 et jusqu’à fin 2023, le programme « Raidet » a permis le financement de 3.679 projets de femmes avec des fonds supérieurs à 35.6 millions de dinars, qui ont contribué à la création de 50605 emplois dont 3266 micro-projets. Les dossiers de financement enregistrés sur la plateforme numérique « Raidet » ont atteint 15000 dossiers.
Financial Ressources: 50 millions de dinars du budget de l'Etat

Title EN: Women in Power
Goal: Promote Human Rights And Fundamental Freedoms
SDG: SDG 5 - Achieve gender equality and empower all women and girls,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels
Area of Monitoring: Gender equality
Agency Implementation: MOMIX (Moris Music Expo)
Main Feature: WIP by MOMIX Reduce inequality and professionalise women in the music industry of mauritius.  WIP is a program to promote the integration and professionalisation of women in the music industry of Mauritius. This program is part of the dynamics MOMIX in its role as a structure dedicated to a sustainable development of a Mauritian music industry, both viable and inclusive.   To date, there is no modus operandi in the music industry system in Mauritius, and even less considering the integration of the professional woman. Based on two directives of WIP program, namely: (i) the professionalisation of women who are already active in the industry, and (ii) the awareness-raising of women who want to start in the music industry, and then it will be possible to use research to propose coherent and effective cultural actions.  It is necessary to understand the opinions of women on the subject, as well as to work on the actual percentage of women in the industry.   In this way, the program Women In Power (WIP) by MOMIX aspires, on one hand, to understand the motivations and demotivation of women to settle in the industry, and on the other hand, to professionalise the women who are already active in this industry.  This is a support program based on these two types of interventions so as to reduce the inequality in terms of opportunities to women and to optimise their access to the professional world of music.
Results: Women	In Power by MOMIX	@	IOMMa	& Sakifo	2024  Two women (Carole	& Kimberly)	from the programme WIP by MOMIX	have successfully participated	in the biggest festival	& the biggest Music Conference in	the	Indian Ocean. She had the opportunity	to master her skills and	learn the technical stage	 practices for	Sakifo. She succeeded	to fulfill her duties and came	back	to Mauritius with such great experiences.  Kimberly from MOMIX Few months ago, the IOMMa	team	contacted Kimberly so as to be part of	the	INTERNATIONAL  IOMMA	JURY, in	order to	select, among	other jury members,	the	suitable	performances for IOMMa	2024. Kimberly also participated as	moderator in a conference on merging musical styles in the Indian Ocean.  Moreover,	she  participated	in One-to-One Meetings.  WIP by MOMIX	provides support	and	assistance to  women in the programme who are	already active	in the music industry of Mauritius. Thus, it will enable them	to explode	that glass ceiling in this industry.

Title EN: Training actions of the Cultural Diversity Observatory
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture
SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Cultural and creative sectors
Cultural Domain: Design,Performing Arts,Media Arts,Cinema and Audiovisual Arts,Music,Publishing,Visual Arts
Agency Implementation: Cultural Diversity Observatory
Main Feature: The Cultural Diversity Observatory (ODC) is a non-governmental organization whose central objectives are to produce and disseminate qualified information, develop research that generates critical knowledge, carry out training processes and provide consultancy in the interdisciplinary field of protection and promotion of cultural diversity and its interfaces with cultural policies, cultural management, mediation processes, memory and heritage, education, health, environment, etc. To this end, the Observatory develops training, research, information dissemination and consultancy projects and actions. In the period from 2020 to 2023, the Observatory's main achievements were:  ODC Dialogues: This is a communication action that also functions as a training action, bringing together experts and the general public to discuss current issues from the perspective of promoting cultural diversity. The activity takes place online, in the format of a live broadcast, being broadcast on the ZOOM platform and made available on the Observatório da Diversidade Cultural - ODC YouTube channel:  Participatory Mapping of Cultural Diversity Workshop The Cultural Diversity Observatory carried out a training action aimed at young people, with the aim of preparing cultural agents and managers, teachers and members of cultural groups and movements to carry out participatory research to map cultural diversity at a micro-regional level. The workshop included conceptual and methodological training and had the following topics: 1) Training and Conceptual Deepening (Experimentation and Experiences) • Cultural Diversity and Local Development (10 class hours) – dedicated to reflection on the concepts under study, with an emphasis on the text of the Convention on the Protection and Promotion of the Diversity of Cultural Expressions. It addresses cultural diversity and its interfaces with local, regional and national development. • Education for Diversity (10 hours/class) - Reflects on educational processes and their fundamental importance for guaranteeing Cultural Diversity, understood as collective and collaborative work whose responsibility Both teachers, students and the community in general participate. Discusses the possibilities and limits for building shared knowledge and practices in cultural diversity. 2) Mapping Diversity in Terms of Subjects, Practices, Spaces • Preparation to deal with a virtual environment (10 class hours) – Social Networks and connections; Internet; Principles of working with wordpress, free media and free software; principles of community communication; study and sharing of cases; Production of a follow-up and update blog. • Construction of cultural diversity maps (30 class hours) – based on the survey and analysis of data relating to the city, participants are supported in the preparation of a map of cultural diversity in the municipality and a table of alternatives to promote diversity culture in the most different parts of the city. Systematization of mapping information to create a multimedia catalog of the community's artistic and cultural practices.  Cultural Management Course for Community Leadership Training aimed at young people that aims to give them opportunities for reflective experiences to build an environment where diversity, knowledge, respect for themselves and others enhance collective work in favor of transforming the daily conditions of communities, carrying out a training action to initiate cultural management aimed at community leaders. Among the topics covered in the training are: how communities can act in a network and in solidarity to recognize and strengthen local cultural practices and give them visibility; perspectives for developing and building collective and community projects; the different central elements in the construction of cultural projects from the perspective of vulnerable and decentralized groups; how costs are collected in cultural projects; and how to build spreadsheets that portray the proposed action.  SDG and Cultural Diversity Workshop Training activity aimed at institutional and individual agents and managers of cultural, socio-environmental and economic and social development policies, programs and projects, in order to train participants to understand and use the SDGs and their interface with the field of cultural diversity. The key points of the discussion were: people as a central element of sustainable development; the best use of renewable sources and all available resources; improving people's quality of life; smart, inclusive cities and urban arrangements with urban designs thinking of everyone; the appreciation of people and local dynamics. During the workshop, four groups of actions were discussed that can be adopted at the local level to promote cultural diversity and sustainable development: promoting creativity, fostering innovation, actions in public and training spaces and qualification of urban policies and services in the urban environment.
Results: ODC Dialogues In the period from 2019 to 2023, eight editions of ODC Diálogos were held, on the themes: Diversity and Sustainability; Diversity, local and peripheral heritage; Cultural Borders; Art and Public Space; Culture and the Covid19 Pandemic in Brazil; Cultural Emergency Laws and the Institutionality of Culture; Cultural Diversity and Biodiversity; Education, Memory and Cultural Heritage. All of them are available for free access on the YouTube platform, through the address:  Mapping Workshop Two cultural diversity mapping workshops were held in the municipalities of Betim and Santa Luzia, both in the State of Minas Gerais. The results were the training of a group of approximately 20 local cultural agents in the methodology of participatory cultural mapping. The results are available at:   Cultural Management Course for Community Leadership The Observatory found a great demand for training cultural managers, especially when taking into account that the existing training offers for cultural managers are very focused on operational issues, project development and other day-to-day topics in the management of cultural spaces. There is no training offered with an emphasis on issues of protecting and promoting cultural diversity or valuing vulnerable cultural groups. Therefore, the cultural management courses offered by the Cultural Diversity Observatory to train community leaders in the cultural area have achieved positive results.  SDG and Cultural Diversity Workshop Training actions were carried out in five municipalities. In evaluating the results achieved, we verified an increase in the objective engagement of civil society organizations and the school environment in promoting aspects of cultural diversity and sustainability in everyday life. We believe that this action must be more systemic so that the results are incorporated more broadly, both by school communities and by users of cultural equipment in municipalities, as well as public health equipment. The perception we have is that, in general, when talking about the SDGs of the UN 2030 Agenda, teachers, cultural equipment technicians, health or social assistance professionals only imagine actions linked to composting or waste treatment, recycling manuals, or even reducing water consumption. Very few understand other aspects linked to our daily practices or cultural aspects.

Title EN: Training and professionalisation of the visual arts sector. Pedagogical programme "Escuela  sin escuela".
Goal: Integrate Culture In Sustainable Development Frameworks
SDG: SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: National sustainable development policies and plans
Agency Implementation: SACO Cultural Corporation.
Main Feature: The SACO pedagogical programme, created in 2012, unites and consolidates diverse activities in the training and professionalisation areas in the visual arts field, in a desert territory and isolated as the Antofagasta Region is (internationally known for its extracte mining industry, being the most important and lucrative one in the country) in the north of Chile.   A city that, despite its economic impotance, is a territory isolated from the important national artistic centres, even being closer to other Andean Plateau countries such as Bolivia or Peru, or north-east Argentina. The measure "Escuela sin escuela" (School without school) seeks to promote artistic development in the north of Chile, and the growth of the local creative scene, with the aim of changing the previously mentioned context and to combat centralisation that exists in the Chilean and Latin American territories.   Through this programme, the goal is for new artists, managers, curators, mediators, among other cultural practitioners, to emerge from the Antofagasta Region, without having to go through the filter of the capital, Santiago. For the implementation "School without school", novel methodologies and technologies are utilised, and experts are brought in from different parts of Chile and the world.   The majority of the exponents at the biennial, are asked to offer a pedagogical opportunity for the local community, as a symbolic and effective act of retribution towards the territory from which it receives nourshment. With regard to the use of new technologies, since 2021 SACO works with advanced 360o virtual reality hardware, in order to take diverse projects to neighbourhoods and communities far away from the urban centres, including, among others, arts exhibitions and world-views of the first inhabitants of the Atacama desert.   Both events have mediation programmes, through which creativity and the ability to express the participants' own stance and preferences are developed. Some of the main pedagogical projects in SACO's history have been presented in a published format, with the aim of presenting them to a wider audience and to serve as an archive and study material for future initiatives, both internal and external, that take plase in similar contexts.
Results: Since 2012 the SACO Corporation carries out informal educational activities within the region, with SACO4 “Between the Form and the Mold” (2015) standing out: a festival where 84 students from different cities in the north of Chile took part in a one-week camp of artistic education with Latin American teachers.   In 2016, a refresher and creative stimulus workshop on for teachers of visual arts took place with the aim of revising strategies in the classroom. That same year, and also in 2018, the two editions of Intervened Deserts took place, a pedagogical programme that called upon creators from the northern macro-area to traverse the desert, in groups led by renowned artists, generating arts creation laboratories.   The programme took place in Paposo, Quillagua, Ayquina, Taltal, Ollagüe and Pedro de Valdivia. In 2019, "Burying Flags in the Sea" was implemented, a project by the artist Miguel Braceli, who worked his exhibition together with middle-school students from the Juan José Latorre Benavente Educational Complex in Mejillones, turning them into co-authors of a work of art of an international standard.   In 2020 and in 2022 a Diplomado Microdurías (Mocrocuration certification) took place. In 2020, as a rehearsal and a trial run of a content programme contextualised and designed to be used under specific conditions of field research, responding to the requests of various Latin American countries. This programme, only two weeks long, has been transformed into a full seven-month-long diploma in 2022, that culminated with 18 new Latin American curators after a processes of co-construction of virtual and in-person learning, together with thirty teachers from different areas.   The admission process for the 3rd edition of the diploma will commence in October 2023. This is in addition to the virtual reality projects: Bienal en el maletero (Biennial in the Trunk), an initiative that presents a selection of the exhibitions of the biennial through a curatorial journey, and paseo Interestelar (Interstellar Walk), a proposal that places value on the Andean world-view, through an animation created with a basis in the ancestral knowledge of the Andean Plateau cultures.   To date, the programme "School without school" has reached 50 educational establishments and civic organisations, in different cities and villages in north of Chile. Apart from children and youth, the main audience of this programme are senior citizens and self-taught artists. According to measure and evaluation schemes based on surveys, participant lists and photographic and audiovisual records, the SACO Corporation, through its pedagogical workshops, talks and events on a larger scale, reaches approximately five hundred participants, annually.

Title EN: TV 2 recruitment diversity initiative
Goal: Promote Human Rights And Fundamental Freedoms
SDG: SDG 5 - Achieve gender equality and empower all women and girls,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels
Area of Monitoring: Gender equality
Agency Implementation: TV 2 Denmark
Main Feature: In 2023 TV 2 Denmark has increased efforts regarding diversity in recruitment, seeking to improve diversity in gender, age, and ethnicity in the company workforce. Detailed initiatives include: Cross-company workshops, webinars for leaders and nudging strategies in HR-tools for recruitment. 2023 also saw the introduction of the tool Develop Diverse, which runs job postings (and other external communication) through an AI-based filter, to remove unconscious biases, and ensure a higher degree of diversity in these texts. A recent pilot project has tested blind recruitment, i.e. recruitment processes in which the job interviewer does not know the gender, age or ethnicity of the interviewee. Going forward, AI tools will assist in these processes.
Results: Blind recruitment pilot tests are currently being evaluated.

Main Feature: Under the Act the objective of the Academy shall be to promote excellence in the design field of fashion and textile, graphic and multimedia, built in and architecture, jewellery and arts and crafts. Moreover, the Academy aims at promoting multisectoral design fields. The Academy aims at providing educational, research, consultancy and training facilities and services in the design field.
Results: The Academy of Design and Innovation has participated in the Dubai Expo in March 2022 that included a two fashion shows, an international conference on design and an exhibition. The Academy has participated in the Salon Internationale du Textile Africain(SITA) since 2021. Title EN: Training young and professional artists
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture

Area of Monitoring: Cultural and creative sectors
Cultural Domain: Performing Arts,Cinema and Audiovisual Arts,Music,Visual Arts
Agency Implementation: Al Balad Theater EMAIL:info@al-balad.org PHONE: (06) 465 2005
Main Feature: Al Balad Theater, established in 2005, is a nonprofit, multi-purpose performing arts venue located in Amman. The theater serves as a hub for local and international artists, offering rehearsal and performance spaces for theater, dance, urban arts, and music. It also organizes three major annual festivals: Al Balad Music Festival, Baladk Street and Urban Art Festival, and Hakaya Storytelling Festival. In addition to these events, Al Balad Theater conducts performing arts workshops, supports independent artistic production, and encourages regional and international artistic exchanges. Operated by a dedicated core team, eleven board members, and a network of volunteers, Al Balad Theater partners with various organizations locally, regionally and internationally, including Amman Municipality, Tamasi, the Swedish Institute, and the Arab Education Forum, to enrich Jordan's cultural landscape and provide a supportive environment for independent artists.  Since 2016, Al Balad Theater has systematically worked on an initiative aimed at training young and professional artists, particularly focusing on the Syrian community. This initiative was made possible through our the theater’s work with a large number of local organizations and CSOs in Jordan and the region. This initiative encompasses three main areas designed to build the capacity of professional artists, enhance social cohesion, and promote cultural expression and diversity:  Filmmaking Workshops for Young Women: These workshops are designed to empower young women to use filmmaking as a tool for self-expression. Covering essential skills such as story development, camera usage, editing techniques, and teamwork, these workshops have been held annually across various locations in Jordan, including camps. Each year, more than 60 young women participate, culminating in the production of their own fictional or documentary films. Participants are mentored by inspiring filmmakers from the region, providing a robust learning experience.  Storytelling Performances: Aimed at fostering social connections through storytelling, this activity has reached over 50 locations across Jordan, including underprivileged areas and refugee camps. Storytellers engage local communities and Syrian refugees by sharing traditional stories, followed by discussions and reflections. This initiative has successfully enhanced community bonds and provided a platform for cultural exchange.  Music Workshops: These workshops offer professional musicians from Syria and Jordan the opportunity to collaborate on projects related to Syrian musical heritage. Participants work on writing and transforming musical ideas into notation, developing musical embellishments and harmony, refining performance skills, and producing collaborative musical pieces. These sessions not only preserve and celebrate Syrian musical traditions but also foster professional growth and cross-cultural collaboration among musicians.  Through these initiatives, Al Balad Theater continues to uphold its mission of enriching the cultural fabric of Jordan and providing a nurturing environment for independent artists.
Results: Filmmaking workshops: 24 5-day long filmmaking workshops for young women across Jordan. 20 Short films produced 360 young women participated in the workshops.  Storytelling Performances: ≈10,500 audience members reached mainly children and young people.  More than 50 locations in Jordan with solid partnerships formed between Al Balad Theater and other local CSOs working in the humanitarian field. Music Workshops 8 music workshops for young Syrian and Jordanian musicians or professional musicians early in their careers.  Composing, producing and recording more than 50 pieces of music across the years.  These results demonstrate the significant impact of the initiative, showcasing the engagement and empowerment of young women through filmmaking, the broad reach and community connection through storytelling performances, and the creative output and professional development facilitated by the music workshops.

Main Feature: Le Traité d’Amitié et de Coopération (TAC) Ivoiro-burkinabè vise à renforcer les liens culturels, économiques et politiques entre la Côte d'Ivoire et le Burkina Faso. Ce traité établit un cadre de collaboration pour la promotion des échanges culturels, la préservation du patrimoine commun, et le soutien aux industries culturelles et créatives. Les deux pays s’engagent à organiser des événements culturels conjoints, à faciliter la mobilité des artistes et des professionnels de la culture, et à coopérer dans la numérisation et la conservation des archives culturelles.
Results: Le TAC a conduit à l’organisation de plusieurs festivals culturels et artistiques conjoints, favorisant une meilleure compréhension mutuelle et la célébration des cultures respectives.  Des initiatives de formation et de renforcement des capacités ont été lancées pour les jeunes artistes des deux pays.  Le traité a également facilité la mise en place de projets de numérisation des archives culturelles et la conservation du patrimoine commun, renforçant ainsi la coopération culturelle transfrontalière.
Recommandations: L'évaluation a montré que le TAC a considérablement renforcé la coopération culturelle entre la Côte d'Ivoire et le Burkina Faso. Il est recommandé de continuer à soutenir les initiatives conjointes et d'accroître les investissements dans les infrastructures culturelles. Il est également suggéré de développer davantage de programmes de mobilité pour les artistes et les professionnels de la culture, et de renforcer les mécanismes de suivi et d’évaluation pour mesurer l’impact des projets culturels réalisés dans le cadre du traité.

Title EN: Transition écologique de la Culture: « Guide d’inspiration et d’orientation pour la transition écologique de la culture"
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture
SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Cultural and creative sectors
Cultural Domain: Design,Performing Arts,Media Arts,Cinema and Audiovisual Arts,Music,Publishing,Visual Arts
Agency Implementation: Haute-fonctionnaire transition écologique et développement durable (MC/SG/MTEDD) - Ministère de la Culture
Main Feature: Un ministère de la Culture résolument engagé dans la transition écologique (dans ses trois piliers, changement climatique, biodiversité, sobriété de ressources), engagé pour lui-même et pour l’ensemble des secteurs culturels, que le ministère de la Culture accompagne, informe et incite. Cet engagement est formalisé dans un « Guide d’inspiration et d’orientation pour la transition écologique de la culture » (cf. liens ci-dessus), rendu public par le ministère à l’automne 2023. Ce guide, élaboré avec les différentes composantes du ministère, s’appuie sur un triptyque de leviers : mesurer les impacts environnementaux pour les réduire (par exemple bilan carbone) ; former et informer sur la transition écologique ; financer le changement. Il met en lumière de nombreuses bonnes pratiques, dans le champ de la sobriété énergétique, et plus largement, dans tous les secteurs, émanant d’acteurs publics et privés.  Le guide s’articule autour de 5 axes de transition écologique pour le secteur culturel :  -	Créer autrement : de nouvelles pratiques durables  -	Développer un numérique culturel sobre  -	Inventer l'architecture, les territoires et le paysage de demain  -	Préserver, conserver et sauvegarder pour demain  -	Repenser la mobilité des publics pour une culture toujours accessible  S’agissant des principaux sujets, le guide pose des cibles à atteindre, à l’horizon 2027, afin de s’assurer de l’effectivité de la transition écologique du ministère de la Culture et des filières culturelles, ces objectifs sont répartis dans le temps, de 2023 à 2027 et concernent l’ensemble des thématiques.
Results: Chantier en cours pour former à la transition écologique, notamment dans les écoles d’enseignement supérieur pour l’inclusion obligatoire d’ici 2026 de la transition écologique dans les cursus initiaux des écoles (architecture, patrimoine, création, cinéma) est dans sa phase de lancement et diagnostic, la dynamique est engagée. La sensibilisation des cadres supérieurs (100% d’ici fin 2024), et la formation des dirigeants d’établissements publics et de structures labellisées (100% d’ici 2025) sont des objectifs en cours de concrétisation. Elles s’appuient sur le plan interministériel pour l’encadrement de l’État et sur une mobilisation des secteurs professionnels.   Plusieurs chantiers, dans un état d’avancement divers selon les filières, sont en cours, pour décarboner les modèles de production et de diffusion de la culture :  « Plan Action ! » du CNC pour le cinéma et l’audiovisuel, qui depuis 2023 prévoit de conditionner les aides aux tournages à la réalisation de bilans carbone (engagement sur les moyens à ce stade) ; dimension écologique du plan « Mieux Produire, Mieux Diffuser » pour le spectacle vivant et les arts visuels, avec le l’expérimentation en 2024 d’un pacte d’engagement des structures labellisées, dans une logique de plancher écologique qui remonte progressivement ; objectif d’une couverture de l’ensemble des secteurs culturels par des référentiels carbone débouchant sur des plans d’actions, champ du spectacle vivant presque intégralement couvert en 2024. En cours, la mise en place d’un référentiel carbone des musées en 2024-2025, avec l’idée de doter la filière d’une stratégie collective de décarbonation.  Actions concrètes pour concilier protection patrimoniale et transition écologique, exemple réalisé en 2022-2023 pour le déploiement des énergies renouvelables (photovoltaïque, éolien…) : le 9 décembre 2022, les ministres de la Culture, de la Transition écologique et des collectivités territoriales, et de la Transition énergétique ont signé une circulaire conjointe, suivie à l’automne 2023 de la publication d’un guide sur l’implantation des panneaux solaires dans un contexte patrimonial. Ces publications visent à un traitement pertinent et homogène sur le territoire.
Financial Ressources: Financement de la transition écologique dans les lieux culturels : 42 M$  / Programme Alternatives vertes : 26 M$
Recommandations: Evaluation continue, au fur et à mesure de l’atteinte des cibles. Plan d’action structuré fin 2023.

Title EN: TRANSITIONAL REGULATION FOR THE AUTHORIZATION OF THE TEMPORARY EXPORT OF CULTURAL GOODS
Goal: Achieve A Balanced Flow Of Cultural Goods And Services And Increase The Mobility Of Artists And Cultural Professionals

Area of Monitoring: Flow of cultural goods and services
Agency Implementation: MINISTERIO DE CULTURAS DESCOLONIZACION Y DESPATRIARCALIZACION (MINISTRY OF CULTURES, DECOLONIZATION AND DEPATRIARCHALIZATION)
Main Feature: The Plurinational State of Bolivia, through a Ministerial Resolution, approves the regulations that establish the requirements for the authorization of temporary export of cultural goods. Through this measure, the Ministry of Cultures, Decolonization and Depatriarchalization authorizes the temporary exit of cultural goods, justifying the reason for the transfer of the cultural good, its description, destination and the length of stay of the good outside the country.  These exchanges of cultural goods or services are carried out either for an exhibition or artistic presentation abroad, and allow them to be protected from possible loss or other mishaps whose absence from registration would not allow knowing about their destination. The objectives of the measure are to provide technical and legal security for the export of cultural goods, regulate the requirements for export authorization, prevent the export of cultural goods as a strategy to prevent illicit trafficking of cultural goods, and have control and statistics on the export of cultural goods. This measure, like any other, contains an administrative procedure that is outlined below: •	Authorization request note addressed to the Highest Executive Authority of the Ministry of Cultures, Decolonization and Depatriarchalization, justifying. •	Report on the state of conservation of the cultural asset to be transferred outside the country, issued by the entity or institution in charge of its custody, including a photographic sample of the same. •	Copy of the relevant regulations of the cultural asset of the material cultural asset to be transferred out of the country, where applicable. •	Request from the requesting country or foreign institution or location of the stay. •	Written authorization from the owner or custodian of the cultural heritage assets for temporary export, in accordance with the protocols of the Ministry of Cultures, Decolonization and Depatriarchalization.
Results: In 2024, the departure of 149 cultural assets (paintings) has been recorded, of which 90 went to the USA, 23 to Spain, 14 to Mexico, 10 to Russia, 5 to Chile, 2 to France, 2 to Germany, 1 to Poland, 1 to Italy and 1 to Colombia.

Title EN: Virtual Dubai Calligraphy Biennale

Area of Monitoring: Cultural and creative sectors
Agency Implementation: Dubai Culture and Arts Authority
Main Feature: The Dubai Culture and Arts Authority launched the Virtual Dubai Calligraphy Biennale, expanding on the success of its inaugural event. This virtual edition features 19 art exhibitions showcasing works by over 270 local and international artists. It offers a 360-degree viewing experience, allowing visitors to explore and purchase artworks. The biennale includes diverse cultural designs and calligraphy in more than eight languages, providing accessibility and engagement for a global audience, including people of determination.
Results: The inaugural Dubai Calligraphy Biennale, held in October 2023, garnered over 1,000 participation requests from around the globe through an open call by Dubai Culture earlier in the year. This virtual biennale showcased the works of more than 270 local and international artists, representing a diverse array of cultural calligraphic expressions. The biennale's extensive programming featured over 150 workshops and more than 25 talks, alongside 19 exhibitions spread across 35 locations. The virtual format allowed art collectors to explore and purchase artworks, enhancing accessibility and engagement with the artistic community. Designed with inclusivity in mind, the virtual biennale ensured access for people of determination, making diverse creative expressions accessible to all. It activated over 35 heritage and cultural sites, enriching the spectrum of available programs and enhancing public engagement. The biennale underscored the importance of calligraphy as a cultural expression, promoting both traditional and contemporary styles in over eight languages. This initiative supported Dubai Culture's mission to enrich Dubai’s cultural and creative landscape by harnessing innovative digital capabilities.
Recommandations: The high number of participation requests and the involvement of over 270 artists from around the world underscore the biennale's success in attracting and engaging a global audience. The diverse programming, including workshops, talks, and exhibitions, significantly contributed to the event’s success and its appeal to a wide range of participants. The biennale effectively showcased the diversity of calligraphic art, presenting works from different cultures and languages, thus promoting cultural exchange and understanding. The inclusion of both traditional and contemporary calligraphy highlighted the dynamic nature of the art form and its relevance in the modern cultural landscape. The use of a virtual platform allowed for innovative presentation and greater accessibility, enabling a wider audience to engage with the biennale's offerings. The initiative ensured inclusivity by making the virtual biennale accessible to people of determination, enhancing their cultural experience. Future editions should continue leveraging digital technologies to expand the reach and impact of the biennale. Enhanced virtual reality and interactive elements could further enrich the user experience. Maintaining and expanding the diverse programming of workshops, talks, and exhibitions will keep engaging the community and fostering a deeper appreciation for calligraphy and cultural arts. Implementing a robust feedback mechanism to gather insights from participants and visitors can inform improvements and innovations in future editions.

Title EN: VIRTUAL PROGRAM OF ARTISTIC PRESENTATIONS
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture
SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Digital environment
Agency Implementation: MINISTERIO DE CULTURAS DESCOLONIZACIÓN Y DESPATRIARCALIZACIÓN  (MINISTRY OF CULTURES, DECOLONIZATION AND DEPATRIARCHALIZATION)
Main Feature: The Program was born in 2021 whose objective was the recovery of the cultural sector after the devastating effects on artists due the pandemic. Has searched to alleviate the deteriorated economy and combat the difficulties suffered by the quarantine.  Support was provided via a digital environment, achieving a significant impact on the participation of artists. Each artistic initiative has benefited from an approximate amount of $us. 600. Also searched to create greater accessibility and visibility, democratising the participation of artists from different regions of the country and without the geographical limitations that always exist.  This measure has made it easier for emerging and lesser-known artists to show their work to wider audiences, both nationally and internationally, since in some cases the live broadcasts and recordings had international access or circulation. Direct real-time interaction between artists and their audiences has also been discovered through live streaming events, which has enriched the cultural experience and fostered a sense of community.  The experience has also opened the door to new forms of artistic expression, such as digital art, augmented reality and digital music.  This has allowed artists to experiment with innovative techniques and expand their creative repertoire, which has enriched the cultural landscape and promoted the exchange of ideas and styles.
Results: In addition to supporting cultural sectors within the framework of the Cultural Industries, economic sustainability was sought from the post-pandemic perspective, which led to results related to new business models.  Digitalization has allowed artists to explore alternative business models, such as the sale of works through online platforms and the monetization of digital content. This has contributed to the economic sustainability of their projects, especially in a context where live performances may be limited. Digital platforms offered artists tools to analyze their audience behavior, allowing them to make informed decisions about their career and adapt their marketing strategies. Certainly, challenges and considerations have arisen from the experience regarding competition and saturation of the market.  While digitalisation has expanded opportunities, it has also increased competition. Title EN: VULGARISATION DU DÉCRET N° 2021-624 DU 20 OCTOBRE 2021 PORTANT STATUT DE L’ARTISTE
Goal: Promote Human Rights And Fundamental Freedoms
SDG: SDG 5 - Achieve gender equality and empower all women and girls,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels
Area of Monitoring: Artistic freedom
Cultural Domain: Design,Performing Arts,Media Arts,Cinema and Audiovisual Arts,Music,Publishing,Visual Arts
Agency Implementation: Direction des Affaires Juridiques et de la Coopération (DAJC) ;
Main Feature: Le décret n° 2021-624 du 20 octobre 2021 portant statut de l’artiste a pour objet: -l' exercice libre de la profession d’artiste ; - l'Inscription et immatriculation au registre national des artistes ; - la sécurité sociale de l’artiste ; - les droits et obligations de l’artiste ; - les sanctions relatives aux non-respect des dispositions du décret. Ce nouveau statut de l'artiste a fait l'objet d'un atelier le vendredi 27 janvier 2023 au Musée des Civilisations de Côte d'Ivoire pour vulgariser ce texte auprès des acteurs concernés. Cet atelier a été présidé par la  Ministre de la Culture et de la Francophonie. Cette étape importante pour tous les artistes prend son essence officielle avec la signature du décret n° 2021-624 du 20 octobre 2021 portant statut de l'artiste, par le Président de la République. Pour la promotion de ce décret auprès des acteurs concernés, un partenariat multi-acteurs a été établi entre l'ONG Culture et Développement, le Bureau des Arts et de la Communication et le Ministère de la Culture et de la Francophonie à travers la Direction de la Réglementation et du Contentieux, la Direction des Industries Culturelles et Créatives et le BURIDA. Un appui financier de l'Organisation Internationale de la Francophonie a permis à ces équipes d'organiser des ateliers destinés aux artistes à Yopougon, Korhogo et Yamoussoukro afin de les informer, les sensibiliser et de mieux comprendre le décret. Plus de 400 artistes y ont participé en présentiel ou par le biais des réseaux sociaux. Ce partenariat multi-acteurs a également permis de créer un tiers-lieu innovant, le programme Yop-Crealab, une première en Côte d’Ivoire. Il faut retenir entre autres que «Le décret n° 2021-624 du 20 octobre 2021 portant statut de l’artiste apparaît comme le mécanisme de protection à la fois des activités artistiques et de l’intégrité des artistes comme pour tout travailleur professionnel protégé. Le texte vient donc formaliser et professionnaliser le secteur artistique en vue de créer un environnement propice à l’exercice de la profession d’artiste. Enfin, le décret prévoit des mesures prises par l’État pour garantir la sécurité sociale des artistes y compris ceux qui sont en situation d’handicap».Il faut noter que cette restitution a été suivie d'un atelier pratique sur "la découvrabilité des contenus cultuels Ivoiriens en Ligne".
Results: La vulgarisation du décret portant statut de l'artiste a permis de : 	une protection des activités artistiques en général et surtout de la protection de l’intégrité des artistes comme tout travailleurs professionnels protégés à cet effet par les lois et règlements en vigueurs en Côte d’Ivoire ; - Un encadrement juridique et normatif du secteur artistique. en outre, le secteur artistique a été formalisé et professionnalisé en vue de créer un environnement propice à l’exercice de la profession d’artiste, pour le  plein épanouissement des artistes. - une reconnaissance du statut des artistes .
Recommandations: Cet décret  fait de l’artiste, un travailleur légal. C’est un changement capital pour le quotidien de l’artiste et pour les opportunités qu’il offre au secteur de la Culture. Cette reconnaissance du statut de l'artiste est liée à l’importance que la Côte d'Ivoire accorde aux Industries Culturelles et Créatives (ICC). D'autres actions vont se poursuivre avec plusieurs partenaires l''AFD, l' OIF et l''UNESCO  à Abidjan et également à l'intérieur du pays.

Title EN: White Paper on Artist Policy: Artist conditions. Report no. 22 (2022-2023) to the Storting (Meld. St. (2022-2023) Kunstnarkår)
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture
SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Area of Monitoring: Cultural and creative sectors
Agency Implementation: Norwegian Ministry of Culture and Equality
Main Feature: The white paper outlines the government’s ambitions for the national artists policy for the forthcoming years and establishes the overarching objectives for this policy. It examines the present state measures in cultural policy and the general conditions under which artists operate nationally and internationally, while suggesting modifications and refinements. The white paper's primary objectives are: 1. Enhancing Opportunities: Furnish artists with ample opportunities to work both nationally and internationally. 2. Fair Compensation: Ensuring that artists receive equitable remuneration for their artistic work and are explicitly incorporated into other relevant policy domains 3. Nationwide Impact: Supporting artists in working throughout the country.. The government advocates for the state artists' policy to be grounded in the following three fundamental principles: 1. Arm’s Length Principle and Peer Review: Ensuring a separation between government and artistic decisions, facilitated by peer review. 2. Artistic Freedom and Freedom of Expression: Preserving artistic freedom and the right to free expression. 3. Transparent Administration: Ensuring equal treatment, impartiality, and transparency in the administration of support schemes.  The white paper proposes 50 distinct measures aimed at fortifying the position of art and artists. It advocates for a strategy and value principles geared towards fair remuneration for artistic work. State-funded artist grants will see an increase, and the age limit for eligible recipients will be raised from 67 to 70 years. State-financed arts and cultural institutions will also be required to report on their utilization of, and compensation for, self-employed artists. Furthermore, the white paper examines other policy areas pertinent to artists’ working and living conditions, such as labor and welfare policies, pensions, taxation, and business policies. It also suggests measures to optimize and enhance social rights for freelancers and self-employed artists.
Results: The white paper was approved by the Norwegian Parliament on 19 March 2024 and the measures have therefore not yet been implemented.

Its core features include:  • Access to Support: Facilitating pathways for women to access government resources and departmental support for their creative initiatives. • Experience Sharing: Creating a safe space for women to discuss their experiences, challenges, and successes in the industry. • Addressing Systemic Barriers: Highlighting the historical and ongoing challenges women face due to patriarchal norms and societal constraints, including the legacy of apartheid and restrictive cultural practices. • Combating Gender-Based Violence (GBV): Raising awareness about GBV and its impact on women’s participation and self-expression in the arts.
Results: The Women In Arts Imbizo has yielded several positive outcomes, including: Feedback Mechanisms: Establishing feedback loops with organizations to continually assess needs and improve support. Encouraging Participation: Actively promoting the involvement of women in various creative and cultural sectors. Empowerment Platforms: Facilitating information sharing and skill development workshops to empower women artists. Balanced Representation: Working towards a more equitable creative landscape with equal opportunities for all genders. Funding Opportunities: Successfully raising funds from governmental sources, private entities, and philanthropists to support women-led programs. Health and Wellness Initiatives: Prioritizing the mental and physical well-being of women in the arts through wellness programs. Skill Development Programs: Implementing training sessions aimed at enhancing women’s skills in various artistic disciplines. Job Creation: Fostering employment opportunities and entrepreneurial ventures for women, enabling sustainable livelihoods.
Recommandations: As no formal evaluation has been conducted, specific conclusions remain unavailable. However, ongoing dialogues and stakeholder feedback suggest the need for enhanced support structures, increased funding opportunities, and broader engagement strategies to address the unique challenges faced by women in the arts. Title EN: Work Plan for Culture 2019-2022
Goal: Support Sustainable Systems Of Governance For Culture
SDG: SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all,SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all,SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels,SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development

Agency Implementation: Council of the European Union, European Commission, EU Member States
Main Feature: EU Member States define their priorities for cultural policy making at EU level in multi-annual Work Plans for Culture adopted through conclusions of the Council of the European Union. Two Work Plans were in place during the period covered by this report.    This section describes the 2019-22 Work Plan for Culture, published here: https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:52018XG1221(01),  and its amendment in 2020 available here:  http://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/PDF/?uri=uriserv:OJ.C_.2020.193.01.0020.01.ENG   The 2019-2022 Work Plan for Culture defines six priority areas (A-F) for action (originally five, to which a sixth – sustainable development - was proposed in a Council Resolution of November 2019 and formally added in May 2020) A) Sustainability in Cultural Heritage  B) Cohesion and well-being  C) An ecosystem supporting artists, cultural and creative professionals and European content  D) Gender equality  E) International cultural relations  F) Cultural dimension of sustainable development.  Several policy cooperation actions were undertaken for each priority, including Member States’ expert groups under the open method of coordination (OMC), a light but structured method EU Member States use to cooperate at European level, for example in the field of culture. It helps create a common understanding of challenges and helps to build consensus on solutions and their practical implementation. Through an exchange of good practices between EU Member States, it contributes to improving the design and implementation of policies, without regulatory instruments. It can be regarded as a form of ’soft law’.
Results: The following achievements were notable in the different priority areas:  A) Sustainability in Cultural Heritage •	Peer-learning project ‘Cultural Heritage in Action’ launched in 2019. •	Group of EU Member States’ experts on ‘Strengthening Cultural Heritage Resilience for Climate Change’ and the report published in July 2022. B) Cohesion and well-being  •	Group of EU Member States’ experts on High-quality architecture and built environment, with its report ‘Towards a shared culture of architecture – Investing in a high-quality living environment for everyone’ and report published in October 2021. •	Workshop with Member States’ experts on Culture for Social cohesion in November 2020. •	Report from the stakeholders’ dialogue on Understanding digital audiences. C) An ecosystem supporting artists, cultural and creative professionals and European content  •	The Commission published a study on the status and working conditions of artists and cultural and creative professionals in December 2020, and a stakeholders’ dialogue was launched on the same topic.  •	Group of EU Member States’ experts  on the ‘Status and working conditions of artists and cultural and creative professionals’ ran between 2021 and 2023 and published its report on the topic.  •	Group of EU Member States’ experts on Audiovisual Co-productions published its report ‘Co-productions that shine’ in March 2022. •	Group of EU Member States’ experts on Multilingualism and translation published its report in February 2022.  D) Gender equality  •	Group of EU Member States’ experts on gender equality in the cultural and creative sectors issued its report in June 2021.  E) International cultural relations  F) Cultural dimension of sustainable development. •	EU Member States experts’ report on Cultural dimension of sustainable development was published in September 2022, and was preceded by a stakeholders’ dialogue on the topic of culture and SDGs (with its corresponding report).  All reports can be found on the following page: https://culture.ec.europa.eu/policies/cultural-policy-cooperation-at-the-eu-level/cooperation-with-the-eu-countries
Recommandations: The European Commission surveyed Member States and produced a report on implementation of the Work Plan for the Council Cultural Affairs Committee, which can be found here: eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=CELEX:52022DC0317.  According to the report, all actions were implemented as planned. Delivering this high number of planned outputs within a short timeframe and during COVID-19 was considered a ‘remarkable achievement’.
